reviews.comment: She gave me detailed, excellent feedback on my Personal Statement for medical school and helped me take it from early draft to finished product.

Profe. Anghel is a super kind and helpful professor that truly wants her students to succeed. I originally had her for 303, and she later helped me with fellowship applications by providing valuable feedback on my essays. She gives very detailed and constructive feedback on writing that helped me better develop my narrative.

Pretty safe choice for tech writing even though there are certainly better options. She is definitely open to criticism which is very commendable. If you put in the effort w her, you will certainly get an A

This professor truly cares about giving meaningful feedback to her students about their writing, and is always making sure that they understand the course material and feel they are writing about something meaningful to them! The course material was also interesting, current, diverse, and helped facilitate a greater understanding of latin culture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Profesora Anghel's class and it was my favorite Spanish class I've taken. She created a collaborative class environment and supported student participation. She had a deep understanding and passion for topics relating to gender equality and cultural studies and taught us how to properly convey our thoughts in essays. Very kind and helpful.

At first I did not like that she lets students speak english in class. I felt awkward when I would decide to try speaking spanish to practice but she slowly learned her teaching style (it was her first semester teaching) and became much more strict (in a motivating way). Loved the content and discussions, she makes participating easy.

Great professor! Class usually consists of small group discussions about whatever the homework material is. Homework is definitely mandatory and a little bit heavy but it's always things like watching a movie or reading a book. Would 100% take again. Prof. Anghel was amazing and learned a lot from this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Office hours with Anghel were always constructive. Discussion-based class format; she values analysis and understanding over rote learning of content. Detects specific weaknesses in class and consciously makes an effort to strengthen them. I suspect she would teach a class with less predefined of a schedule than 303 even better. Great overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: test dont approve
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The sweetest professor, always accommodating to students. She really takes the time and effort to help you out and make sure you're getting the most out of her class. Regardless of your comfort level with Spanish, if you have the opportunity to take a class with Anghel, I highly recommend it.

I took Spanish 102 with Professor Anghel. She is always available and willing to help students. I love that she put an emphasis on lots of interaction between classmates, as that really is the best way to learn and improve your Spanish.
Shirley was a great assistant professor in the class I took. She offered helpful feedback on homework and was always friendly.

Shirley was the TA for a major seminar I was in and she was always so kind and helpful! I had several great discussions with her when we were paired up to talk during class. Her comments and corrections on homework were thoughtful and helpful. When she led the class she encouraged participation but didn't pressure students.

Professor Anghel taught my first Spanish class at WashU and was helpful to me as a beginner, including time outside of class. She's very nice and teaches as well as anyone I've had in the Spanish department here. I definitely felt comfortable participating in her class, which is important in any language class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Although Shirley was the TA for this class, she really helped in making it engaging and easy to follow as it was a new course at WashU. Shirley was great in giving feedback that allowed for improvement, and never shut down a student. Instead, she worked to help us understand our mistakes so we could correct them in the future.

The poor rating on here does not accurately reflect Anghel's class at all but of 202 in general. Mine was a 7 person class... of course you can't skip class! Anghel creates a fun learning environment without the pressure to feel like you should be at a level you are not. I felt comfortable speaking up because she corrects you in a supportive way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 1-Has lost my grade- twice 2-Required a meeting outside of class so I set up a meeting with her around lunch time. She cancelled on that morning via email because she 'didn't anticipate being so busy' 3- Is one of the last ones to 9am class, but will dock you for coming late 4-Has missed class 3 times- fails students for missing more than 3 times

Dr. Bednarski is a good lecturer but moves a little fast, so it can be challenging to take notes.  WAY more engaging than Hafer.  I wish Bednarski taught every lecture instead of switching with Hafer every few weeks.  Course was challenging but fair.

Definitely loves what she does, but the lectures are too fast with too much information thrown at you. Class is clearly just memorization, so save your time and skip the lectures. You'll probably do just as good as if you went.
Super nice and very clear. She is a sweetheart and her lab is great!

Bednarski is very sweet, like a kindergarten teacher. She really takes her time on the lab introductions/summaries each class, but she's a good professor. Tries her best to help you and doesn't make you feel bad if you have questions.
Probably the least knowledgable bio prof I've had here. Doesn't explain procedures well and does not convey what is expected of students on lab reports.

Dr. Bednarski was a nice person, but the grading in the lab section of this course is done very poorly. Points are deducted without reason and denied being regraded. Dr. Bednarski is not knowledgable of the material and merely reads off slides for lab presentations. Do not recommend.
She may be nice but she isn't a good lecturer. She has a lot of umms in her lectures and basically reads slides word for word.... I finally had to start reading the textbook because of her.

Professor Bednarski is a very relatable and personable teacher. She makes the material manageable and is able to teach the concepts in such  way that makes it interesting and fun. I highly recommend you to take her subsection for lab.
Super nice and helpful! 10/10 would recommend

There are two exams, 1 paper, a presentation and no quizzes. The class is taught discussion style. Paper and exams were FAIR, not tough and not easy. Study and you'll get an A. This class doesn't require you to break your back.
Really friendly. Very relaxed. Super sweet. Made my lab experience positive.
I don't know why she's labelled in chemistry because I had her as a bio lab TA, but she's AWESOME! She's probably one of the nicest people I've ever met in the bio department, very helpful too!
Prof Bednarski is great at explaining complex concepts and making them easy to understand.  Her lab section is the funnest.

Take MEC2900 w/ Gray. He is knowledgeable, will stop and answer your questions in class or outside of class, and is a great lecturer. The class is difficult with hard exams, but Gray gives you everything you need to be able to succeed in the class. There is an Olin curve for every test. Study the slides/practice exams heavily and you will do fine.

Andrew Gray is a great lecturer and individual. He was very accessible outside class and genuinely wanted his students to do well. Much of the course is determined by whether you beat the average on the exams. It is hard to get an A- or A if you do average on the exams, even with 100% in everything else. Difficult class but great professor.
MEC290 is just a hard class, period. Gray is a decent professor but you will need to work hard in the course.
His lectures are long and boring. The exams are so hard. I've heard he's the better option though.

Great professor, very caring, and explains everything in detail. Easy to reach and ask questions, the lectures are interesting. Try to understand everything in-depth, because the material by itself is quite hard. All exams open notes, but nothing extraordinary. If you attend every lecture and do all your homework, you should be ready.

Andrew Gray is an amazing professor. Genuinely cares about students and works to make sure everyone grasps the material. He does teach very difficult classes, hence the difficulty rating; however, he does his best to convey all of the material to students in an easy-to-understand manner.

Gray is consistently amazing at what he does. He is a great professor that wants everyone to succeed. MEC370 is challenging for sure, but office hours are very helpful. He is open to scheduling additional times if weekly ones don't work. Problem sets are participation-based, just study hard for those exams. Would highly recommend Gray.

Great lecturer, made the game theory topics very clear. Office hours times were a bit inconvenient for me, but he made himself available whenever I emailed and provided pretty quick help every time. Made sure everyone understood and welcomed questions. Exams were all fair, and Prof. Gray was very knowledgable about the topics.

I love him and his class. MEC 290 is definitely notorious in Olin but I liked it and it was my favorite course. Taking MEC 290 with him made me want to go to every single class, review on time, and study hard for the exams. One thing is that the engagement grade is not only based on poll eve but also on how active you are in the classroom.
Gray is a chiller. Game Theory is an interesting course - just prepare to get really good at being efficient at test taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gray is probably the only professor you want to take MEC 290 with. The material can be difficult to understand in the beginning, but towards the end, the topics get more clear. He allows cheat sheets for the exams and is super kind, caring, and will offer additional office hours if you ask. I would say office hours are a must for this class.

I heard MEC was tough when I went in, and the concepts were indeed tough at times. Gray explains them concisely and clearly, and his lectures add genuine value. I would not take MEC290 with anyone else besides Gray. Problem Sets and cooperative exercises are mostly easy A. Exams are curved to average of 85. He also actually cares about your success

Took this over the summer and he is great. Definitely the best professor for MEC 290 by far from what I've heard. Super accessible for help even though it was asynchronous and seems like a good lecturer. I would definitely recommend taking it with him over anyone else.

Would have struggled more if I had taken this with another professor. He makes the material manageable and is good at explaining things in plain English. We also got unlimited cheat sheets which was a lifesaver as someone who doesn't care about economics or know what I was doing. Go to lecture!! He says things not on the PPT notes that are helpful
I found this class super interesting. Gray makes it easy to follow and the exams are easier than other Econ Strat classes. I always looked forward to this class
Good professor, the course is tough though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Clear lectures and material that has a straightforward style and occasional dry humor. Everyone dreads mec290, but I felt like Gray is the exception.

Great professor! I was really scared of Game Theory because it is a hard course, but he taught it so well, everything made sense. Tests were really fair, lectures were engaging, and office hours were always open and helpful. I would definitely take this class again!

Andy Gray is straight up the best professor I've had in Olin so far. Unbelievable lecturer, nicest guy, and he cares so much. He's like that guy who is really cute but doesn't even know it--but with teaching. He has such a gift for teaching, but also the mentality of someone who is trying to improve themselves every day. It's so inspiring.

Professor Gray's class is designed for you to learn. The lectures are clear, concise, and well planned and you can tell that he cares about and understands on a high level the material being taught. Semi-weekly problem sets helped ensure I was understanding and engaging with the material so I didn't have to study as much when the exams arrived.

Translates material very well, very reasonable, teaches and lectures well. Is always available to help and seems to have great expertise in the material. Would recommend. An upper division class, so obviously expect some more work (weekly Problem Sets) but very manageable overall if you put in the effort.

For all the horror stories of Mec 290, a very straightforward and good lecturer. Show up, take detailed notes, and ask questions when you get confused, and you will get AT LEAST a B. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gray gives clear, concise lectures that make micro concepts easy to understand. The content itself is not too difficult, and Gray makes sure that the problem sets are similar to tests. Gray seems to be the best MEC 290 teacher.
imo Gray is the best prof for mec 290. In general, it's a difficult course, but he really cares about teaching the material and making sure it gets understood.

Professor Gray is honestly the best professor that you can have for MEC 290. He explains the concepts really well and is willing to help the students. As long as you do the practice materials, you will PASS.

MEC290 is a pretty boring class to take, and the concepts are hard to digest sometimes, but Gray is a great lecturer who helps his students understand the topics well. Exams are open notebook and curved generously, and problem sets are graded for completion unless you really mess them up. MEC290 will suck, but take it with Gray if you can.

Micro is boring but Gray does a pretty good job of explaining the concepts. Sometimes his answers to people's questions can get a little long winded but other than that, lectures are useful to attend in person in case you have questions. Would strongly rec going to his office hours. Problem sets are fine, go to TA office hours if you need help.

Professor Gray is a great person and lecturer who genuinely cares about each of his students and makes himself available to help. Class is pretty lecture heavy, grade is determined mostly by two midterms and a final; there's also 6 problem sets and a case competition that's 10% of the course grade (case competition is completely outside of class).

Micro is really a boring class by nature. 1.5hr lectures feel like 2+hrs every time. Prof Gray is a personable guy who does about as good as a job as I'd hope for a professor in this class. His office hours are great, exams are open note and curved ~87, problem sets are helpful, and he gives a TON of practice exams. Nice guy if you get to know him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Decent lecturer (econ isn't the most exciting topic to teach and he does not change this but doesn't do a bad job either). Concepts are hard to understand and tests are hard (but curved)

While loved by a lot of students, I found that he was very condescending, and it almost felt like he was not rooting for our success. He rarely did examples in class that followed exam format, and there were very little practice questions on the HW and in the textbook. Moreover, the exams are VERY difficult. Please take Hynes for your own sanity.
One of my favorite WashU professors, if you're going to take physics I would highly suggest him or Hynes!!

His teaching style is very engaging and he has a great personality. At first I was a bit of a hater because of how enthusiastic he was but his personality and teaching style really grew on me. He also writes the exams so he teaches exactly what you need to know for the exams

He's very loud (in a good way) and talks in a way to keep your attention. He explains things pretty well, responds to emails quickly, and tries to engage people by calling on different parts of the room, which sometimes means he takes a long time waiting for someone to volunteer. It's a big class, so there's only so much he can do. Pretty decent.
Prof. Medeiros is very enthusiastic about Physics, which is good for learning but not so much for my ears.

His lectures are very interactive, and I personally love that because it keeps me engaged. I think physics is that type of class where if you don't understand every step, it will be very difficult to understand the overall concepts. They also provide a lot of resources to study.
This professor was demeaning when questions were asked.

This professor uses a condescending tone with students. When asked for help, he often talks in circles without providing any help or insight. Additionally he assumes students don't know anything and often explains things in a manner which thus simply confuses students further.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy.

Professor Medeiros is the best! If you can take his specific section for physics, you should! He's always willing to stay after class and answer questions and just in general, you can see that he's super passionate about the subject and about helping students. Easiest 5 stars ever given :)

His lectures are passionate, interactive, and dense in content, but might not be suited for everyone. If you prefer to have more conceptual explanations, a slower pace in lecture, and slides that are organized so can be directly used for your notes, take Professor Alford or watch his recordings.

Very passionate and caring professor. Enthusiastic about teaching and understanding about anything you might not get. Very good lectures with my only problem being that at times some parts of the solving process were unexplained or glossed over, though this is an issue with many professors. Would definitely take a class from him again.

He is very funny and energetic during lectures. Clearly puts a lot of effort into making the class interesting and engaging. He explains things in a clear and understandable manner, and is available after and outside of class

He is very passionate about physics but he presents the material at a level higher than the rest of the physics 191 professors. If you have a good physics background already, you will love Medeiros. I struggled a lot because the pace of this course was not suitable for me (as someone with no physics background)

Very passionate about physics and it comes through in lectures. Seems like a nice guy. Tests are kind of tough, but the TAs generally do a poor job departmentwide of grading them -- be ready to submit regrade requests. He does a solid job of teaching but if you took AP physics you can sleep through the lectures.

Very good professor and great at explaining topics but the class is very participation-heavy and if you do not understand a topic you will be called out for not joining in with the class. The only thing that bothered me about his lectures is that he would allow someone to explain something wrong so I did get confused by that.
He is a very interesting teacher, but he doesn't always include many practice problems during his lectures which would help, especially for more difficult topics.

Dr. Medeiros is an amazing lecturer who really makes you appreciate physics. Electricity and magnetism is very challenging without a doubt, but Dr. Medeiros made it manageable. He can teach in a way that holds your attention for an entire 80 minutes, which is really hard to do. In-lecture demonstrations are always a classic.
When I had him as a professor he had a lot of enthusiasm and energy and clearly cared a lot about the subject. Would highly recommend his lectures.

Solid professor that was available for his students, whether that was through Piazza or office hours. Could've done more practice problems in class on the last exam's material rather than doing demos for every single concept, which I found was a little unnecessary. Had a strong understanding of the material.

Professor Medeiros presents lecture material clearly and concisely and always answers questions with detail and clarity. He creates a great classroom environment where he engages students with eye-opening demos related to physics concepts and encourages everyone to participate in discussions and ask questions.

Very very enthusiastic and energetic. Seems to genuinely care about how you're doing, always scans the room for questions and answers them thoroughly. At certain points the pace could feel a little slow (i.e. only doing 1 or 2 problems all of class), but otherwise, he made lectures clear and mostly engaging. In-class demos were also pretty cool.
Passionate in teaching, caring for students, one of the best professors I've ever had.

Medeiros does a really good job of making lectures engaging & interesting. The course is really well-structured and grading expectations are fairly straightforward. There were 3 online tests, each 4 hours long (no cumulative final) but I heard tests might be moving to in person next semester. There are several opportunities to pad/boost your grade.

Class is always engaging and interesting with Gus. He shows that he cares for indvidual students and wants each person to learn. Classes are always a conversation and also available outside of class to help.
One of the best professors I've ever had. Kind, caring and always responsive to students' questions. His enthusiasm in teaching makes this class whole lot easier.

Unintentionally hilarious. He fell off a chair and broke a clock without trying. Loves physics but obviously physics didn't love him. Will shout at you every day to have a good afternoon and says you signed a contract to answer questions. We love professor Medeiros!

Very enthusiastic and engaging lectures! His demos really helped me apply concepts and understand why this all matters. He always encourages participation and questions, but never cold calls or makes anyone feel stupid. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to make sure we are all understanding the material

Professor Medeiros is a brilliant Professor. He knows how to engage students. I hate physics, but I still enjoy going to class because of him. He's super understanding and responsive outside of class. I recommend 100%
awesome dude! super excited to be teaching and he definitely cares about his students. class isn't too hard as long as you keep up with the course.

The class was pretty unorganized all semester. Long time to get exam grades, not much clarity in the scope of each exam, assignments often posted late/same day as the deadline, many questions left unanswered on Piazza, lots of grading complications after the semester ended. Stopped attending lectures very early on since I didn't find them helpful
3407 was the most unorganized class I've ever been in, apparently it's usually not this bad so hopefully it's better in the future.
Her class is ran by TAs, 0 communication between professor and students.

Only half way thru the semester but I NEED TO VENT. This professor DOES NOT reply to piazza posts. It's been more than A MONTH since our 1st exam and WE STILL DON'T HAVE THE GRADES. It's 4 days away from the 2nd exam and she never gave us the scope of the exam nor any logistical information about it. If you can, DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When I did the pre-lecture video, pre-recitation videos, tried in recitation, then attempted the homework (with AI), I did do above average on the exam. But, this takes easily 12 or 15 hours a week, so I couldnt keep up the whole semester. The prof is insanely out of touch from the class, and the notes/examples she provides are insanely unhelpful.

This class has the trifecta. Lectures that are confusing and often contain incorrect or contradictory information. TA's that are unhelpful at discussing potential solutions and really only serve to spoonfeed you the rubric answers. Exams that are long and ask you to either memorize or copy answers from previous problems. Disappointingly bad course.

Goes through material very fast, does not host office hours, not accessible through email or piazza. In terms of lecture, Agrawal is an okay professor. Wish she would be more patient and explain things more thoroughly given that the material is very challenging.

Agrawal runs 347 like she's going through the motions. "Lectures" are not lectures. You watch years-old lecture videos, some made by other teachers, and then watch examples on the board during the lecture slot. The syllabus has no grade scale, and she avoided all questions about what it is. Would never take this class if it wasn't required. 0/5

Professor Agrawal makes lectures interactive and clearly walks though multiple examples for every topic. The course schedule with videos, lectures, and recitation is tough, but it helped me learn the material well for exams.

Not really a fan of Agrawal. Her lectures were all over the place, with convoluted explanations of content and poorly organized structure. Her grading criteria was often unclear, and I never really felt comfortable approaching her for help outside the class. Her only saving grace is that her exams weren't terribly difficult.

Easily the most heartless prof Ive ever had. Lectures were so confusing, and she makes notoriously hard exams. Not to mention, so many people were confused that they had to resort to using extra materials or working with each other and instead of passing people (in a pandemic???), she reported them all for academic integrity, so theyre facing Fs.

She is one of the best cs prof I've ever met. She explains the concepts clearly and very responsive to students. She doesn't rly reply to emails but very helpful in piazza and question sessions. Also, overall class structure was fair. Homeworks and exams were doable if u put some effort, and grading system was also fair. Really enjoyed this class.
Professor Agrawal is such an amazing instructor. She gives very clear lectures and very doable homework & exams. Really enjoyed taking her class!
Just reading MIT papers and so on. She cannot remember whole concepts that she uses in class. I did all my homework and paper reviews as best as I could but she graded me B.
She explains things well and is responsive to questions in class.
She's very good about answering questions in lecture and explains algorithms quite clearly.

This professor cannot clearly explain the knowledge. She used many MIT course materials, even for the homework. And she seldom replied students' email. I highly recommend MIT online courses instead of her course.
Completely unavailable to students. She should forward her paycheck to MIT because their videos were the only way I learned the material.

She basically follows the MIT open course for her lecture, and most of her homework. The lab instructions are not clear, which makes students hard to test the correctness of their code. The average test scores is about 50%.  Just avoid her section if you are not really necessary to take her class.
Terrible professor. Incoherent accent, primarily talks to the board. Spends too much time on complex proofs. Seems nice enough as a person, but she has moments where you question that as well
Loved her! great professor, requires you to focus a lot but its so worth it!

I think 241 is one of the hardest classes you can take at WashU. It's really interesting material, just hard. She does a pretty good job explaining it and she covers everything, but it's heavy stuff and you have to work hard in the class. I tried taking 241 with Bueller and she was far better.

I took her class two years ago and quickly dropped it. She has improved a lot. Her lectures now make way more sense and she is better at explaining material. The class is really hard but incredibly curved. I would avoid the class unless you have to take it, but it is less painful than I feared.

Unhelpful, class average was in the 40s, didn't seem to care whether anyone was failing or not, took weeks to respond to emails.  She only seems to be here because she does "exciting" research, as she really can't teach.
He was a fine prof. Classes are optional to attend and honestly quite dull, but the homework isn't too much and the exams are really easy (and 70% MC). Definitely serviceable
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i want to like this guy more than i do. when i meet with him in office hours, he's meow personable and friendly. but during lecture it feels like he's going thru the motions. i don't usually understand things during class the first time he lectures - i have to teach myself during recitation or homework. i would recommend solving textbook problems
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture material and homework assignments are difficult, but Stern is really accessible outside of class. His explanations are so clear and is always willing to help, no matter how confused you are. Class content is difficult, but his exams are, in my opinion, pretty fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For advanced math classes Stern is really great. Clear explanations, super available, really friendly and supportive in office hours, enthusiastic in lecture. One of my fav math profs I've ever had. Exams are not too easy but are very fair, easier than the homeworks. All the bad reviews on here must be Calc 2 students who don't want to do proofs.

Good lecturer and knowledgeable about the material. Wants proofs done his way. Success in his class feels rewarding. Publicly berated a student for coughing during lecture and gave death stares the rest of the semester per cough - don't sneeze/cough even with a mask on. Impersonable but strong academic. Take the class pass/fail or not at all.

Professor Stern is fantastic! His lectures are fast but easy to follow and delivered with enthusiasm. Don't be afraid to ask questions during class. He is tremendously helpful in office hours, too. So if you are stumped on a homework problem - and you will be - show up and he will clear up anything that's puzzling you. And he's a metalhead \m/ !

This class was ridiculously hard for the type of material covered. Professor Stern stood in front of the board reading the textbook proofs to us, answering no questions, and then expecting us to be capable of the hardest problems on WebWork and Crowdmark. Worst professor ever. Failed the final after getting As all semester. Do not take.

Wow, this guy was bad at his job. Made my life awful for a semester. Horribly difficult homework and bad teaching don't mix well, but you will have to learn to cope in any Stern class. Showed up to every single class, did every homework, and went to review sessions but was lost the whole time and didn't learn a thing. Hard not to hate this guy.

Stern is by far one of the worst professors that I have taken at WashU. Every class day, you will spend the entire hour rushing to copy notes while retaining no knowledge. His lectures are almost entirely theoretical and he will spend so much time writing down tedious proofs that have no application for homework, recitation, and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ari Stern is the worst professor I've ever had. He spends the majority of his lectures on useless proofs and theoretical concepts and then only does a few incredibly basic and unhelpful problems. The WebWork and Crowdmark are far more difficult than anything in class, which makes them much more difficult to do than should be necessary for Calc 3.

Professor Stern is a great lecturer. I struggle with math, but I've been able to stay engaged and understand his lectures. He does a really great job explaining and providing different ways to visualize difficult concepts. You'll need to study a lot outside of class, since it is a tough subject, but Prof. Stern makes it more approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I LOVED calculus until I took it with Stern. Don't waste your time taking it with Stern because you'll need to teach yourself the material anyway. His lectures are messy and very theoretical so you won't even get any formulas needed to work through the problems. It is also nearly impossible to hear him because he always speaks facing the board.

Awful professor. Goes way too fast in lecture, and makes the tests insanely hard. The averages in Calc 3 this semester speak for themselves, and show that he is truly not up to par. Better off watching review videos on YouTube than wasting your time in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Stern doesn't teach concepts very well, and also doesn't go over very many examples in class. Definitely a quantity over quality kind of teacher. Even in WashU's lacking math department, he stands out as significantly below average.
The math department is lucky to have him. Stern is a fantastic and devoted teacher
He is one of best professors I ever had. He is young, smart, and cool. His lecture is never boring.

So so so helpful. I had already taken this class in high school, but just wanted to make sure I had a solid base before moving on to calc 2. Super nice, always helpful at office hours, and doesn't get frustrated even if you have dumb questions. His tests are pretty easy if you study, he doesn't try to confuse you or give you unnecessarily hard qs.

Alyssa is the best professor I had at Olin! I appreciate how the course blended theory with application, helping me understand the dynamics of power, influence, and organizational politics in a practical way. The frameworks are highly actionable. I can immediately apply in team settings, career planning, and complex stakeholder environments.

I thoroughly enjoyed the content in this course. The class discussions were particularly impactful, and I feel that I got a lot out of them. They allowed me to expand my knowledge, interact with my peers, learn from the professor's experience, and put course concepts/ideas into practice.

What I liked most was how practical the course felt. The frameworks for understanding influence, power, and stakeholder dynamics were so useful, and I found myself using them right away. The case discussions also made the concepts come alive and helped me think more strategically about how work actually gets done in organizations!

I enjoy Prof Liang's energy and delivery. You can just tell that she is a subject matter expert by her responses to questions. It was a pleasure to learn from one of the best in the OB field. The content is transferable to any industry, and I was able to use some of the frameworks at my job while still taking the course.

If you can take OB 360 w/ Liang please please do it. She is so kind and her lectures are not only engaging, but include a lot of activities that can make it easier to remember key concepts for the exams. Overall, the content is not hard and if you have a good group, the class can be really enjoyable. She is one of the best professors I have had!

Professor Liang is a great professor. She really cares about students and the material she teaches. The class itself is pretty easy - it's a lot of psychology. The tests are more application based but nothing too hard.

Prof. Liang was one of my favorite lecturers so far in the b school. Passionate about OB and cares about her students. She'll change some topics based on class interest. Group work was tough due to a bad group, but not her fault. Two exams both very easy, only given as people wouldnt show up otherwise. Maybe studied for 30mins each.

She is a really good lecturer and clearly knows her stuff. Sometimes what she wants on tests can be slightly confusing but overall it is fine. She has super clear rubrics. She seems to love her job, has great energy, and can be pretty funny sometimes. Nice professor and the day to day work of the class is not bad at all, overall pretty easy.

I came into this class not knowing what it would be about or how much I would like it. However, I am really happy I took it. I learned a lot! Professor Liang has been one of my favorite professors at WashU. She is very engaging in class. And she makes it easy to understand and apply concepts.

Professor Liang is the best professor I've had at WashU. Her classes are really engaging, with lots of peer discussions, group activities, and case examples. And she deeply cares about her students. She makes sure everyone feels safe to participate in class, and she provides individualized feedback to everyone. I highly recommend her course!

Prof. Liang is knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. And she engages students with lots of activities, discussion questions, and business examples. Sometimes she can be intense and harsh, but she cares about students. She provides insightful feedback on your strengths and weaknesses based on your personality and career aspiration.

In previous years, this class was easy, but now it's difficult. No one showed up to the lecture, which made her mad, so she made the tests impossible. Lectures are very boring. Tests used to be online, now in person. Rude to all students when she realized people took this class for an easy A. Don't take this class anymore.
This class was ridiculously hard. Slideshows were boring and extremely long and exams were impossibly hard.
No longer an easy A. Very difficult exams and quizzes.

Unresponsive and incredibly boring lectures. You will not be able to find out your grade until it is posted with no class structure available on canvas. Easy class but would not take, far to great of a headache than its worth.

Great lecturer! But, the quizzes are very difficult and annoying, with required readings and quizzes for each class. Expect 3hrs of work per week just on these quizzes. Then there are discussions. Also exams are heavily content based. This is not free credit, but the subject is fascinating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Syllabus has changed it is no longer an easy A. Two midterms are hard as hell. A lot of things to memorize and SB just want her students to suffer. I don't know why she make this course from doing fun labs to memorize bullet point from slides that we will never use again. If you can, try ur best to avoid this class and SB.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She never respond email and she looks like do not want to talk with students.

Baitzel is very knowledgeable and passionate, not an easy class, but does give the benefit of the doubt and she makes the content very interesting.  She adds fun activities into class in a way I haven't experienced in college.

Make sure you keep up with assignments, but she is very understanding. Not a blow of class but worth it.
Kind of monotonous lecturing and not that cohesive but she tried her best to keep everyone engaged.

A lot (!!!) of little assignments and grading could be harsh, but it was all pretty straightforward and lots of drops. I didn't do great on all the assignments but still got an A+. Baitzel's lectures weren't super engaging and I didn't usually go (most people didn't) but she is really nice and caring. Content was usually pretty interesting.

Professor Baitzel is friendly and passionate about archaeology. Each lecture has associated readings and a short quiz, and each week of material has a short discussion assignment. There are 4 reflection papers, 3 "lab" assignments, and a final project. Baitzel is great at posting everything on Canvas and keeping it organized.

I don't know how this professor sets up the grading rubric. This class is not beginner friendly, she would take points off for going over a 300-word limit for a discussion response that asks to list and explain more than 6 factors clearly. This class is definitely not fun. Take the other two intro courses if you can.

Took ANTH 3095 01 last semester and ANTH 190B this spring. Professor Baitzel's classes usually have heavy workload but if you follow the lectures everything will work out just fine. There are several papers and projects but they are not hard. Also she is very very caring and she offered me several accommodations. Nice and sweet prof!
I loved Prof Baitzel for Into to Arch, shes incredibly kind and genuine and really has a passion for her work and research and is caring towards her students.

She's nice and not monotone or boring to listen to, but her lectures were quite disorganized (especially the slideshows themselves), and quizzes, discussion posts, and reflection papers were often confusing to follow. Discussion posts had many requirements but a very tight word limit, which was a bit unreasonable. Quizzes were often convoluted.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Baitzel is relatively new and not a great teacher yet. However, she cares about her students and is great about receiving feedback! This class was fascinating, but hard. The quizzes are very hard, harshly graded, and the class moves extremely quickly. Only take if you are very interested in osteology or have prior experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Yes some of his teaching isn't the best but as long as you go over the slides, homework, quizzes, class tasks, etc. then you will be fine. He really does want his students to do well and is very helpful in office hours. He cares and wants you to succeed!

DON'T TRUST SLANDER! People rating Nazmul low have clearly never taken a class in the rest of the Econ department; he is one of the best we have to offer. I have taken 2 classes with him, and he is kind and an easy grader. He knows every single person's name. Sends reminders out before every class. Passionate and responds to emails within 10m.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is not the best professor ever in terms of teaching, but the contents are relatively easy to understand and easy to get an A (he gives out a lot of extra credits). Homework are not long, and he gives reasonable time to complete it. Exams are not super difficult and very similar to practice exams and in class activities.

For the love of god please save yourself. He is a nice person, sure, but he does not understand the material he's teaching and makes countless mistakes during lecture. He takes long pauses to understand the slides and is authoritative. Do not go to class it will make things astronomically more confusing than it needs to be. Worst professor to date.
Very knowledgeable professor who conducts the course at a great pace. He comes off as very thoughtful and truly wants his students to succeed.
very boring lectures hard to stay involved, gives a lot of extra credit at the end to boost grade. Tests are fair but challenging

I don't understand the other half of the ratings for this professor on this site. His teaching of ECON 1502, at least, should be rated nowhere near a 5. When students ask him questions after class, his explanations are always unclear and sometimes even incorrect. He tries to include some jokes in class lectures, which sometimes backfire.

I've learned close to nothing from his lectures. Do NOT take this course with this professor unless you want to self study his hundreds of slides before exams. I don't even think this professor has the knowledge capable of teaching the materials to students.

His lectures are extremely confusing. He is failing to reach the bare minimum of teaching extremely easy concepts. He also frequently makes mistakes that cause students to cast doubt on their understanding of the material.

His lectures are extremely boring and sometimes confusing. He is not great at explaining concepts or answering questions, but he's pretty funny and nice to students. The class material itself is pretty easy but it felt like I had to self-teach the course because the lectures are so bad.

This class was genuinely unenjoyable. Lectures were confusing and difficult because the professor often seemed unsure of what he was teaching. Mistakes were common, which made everything more frustrating than it needed to be. I would strongly advise waiting to take this course in the spring with a different professor for an easier experience.

His lectures are extremely boring and often confusing due to frequent mistakes in class and on exams. Students regularly have to correct him, and he often pauses to stare at his own graphs because he seems unsure of what he is explaining. While the exams are not difficult, they consistently contain errors, making grading frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nazmul is hilarious and truly cares about students, especially ones who put in effort in lectures. I was able to get on a first-name basis with him pretty quickly in a large lecture. Good professor, easy class.

Do NOT take his class. Lectures are very boring, and he cannot articulate concepts clearly. Exam questions are so confusing with multiple correct answers. Nevertheless, this class is extremely easy as long as you self-study and review the slides and homework.

This course was frustrating from start to finish. The professor gives exam questions that almost nobody gets right, including ones with multiple correct answers after telling us there would only be one. Explanations in class are unclear, and the lectures are copied slides with very little time spent on the concepts that actually matter.

Nazmul is a great professor. You can tell he is passionate about his subject. The class has a textbook but you don't really need to read it. There are quizzes that are worth not much of your grade, homework with unlimited attempts that are worth more, and heavily weighted tests. If you pay attention and take notes (office hours too) you'll be fine.
Class was a really easy A. He was a chill guy, but sometimes he would use dad-joke-style analogies and class would be a little awkward.

I have took 352 with him, and now Im taking his 413. Really a caring person who tried hard to explain things, but he speaks word by word which may find hard to understand sometimes. Homework and tests are easy, so many extra points to pump your grade and many of them are grade on completion. Also he replies email really fast! Nice prof overall.
Nazmul is an interesting guy and sometimes lectures are not the most useful; however, overall, I learned quite a bit from his course and would definitely take a class with him again.

Lecture material and homework assignments are quite easy. The final project is long and time-consuming, but is largely graded on completion, so it's not too bad. Prof is extremely nice and helpful. This is definitely not a difficult class to get the grade you want.

Good lecturer overall but a bit disorganized. Tried to highlight important concepts and was very patient. Cherry-picked info from pre-made slides, probably because it was his first semester here. 50% of the grade is hw. Very easy first exam (~90 average) / slightly harder 2nd exam (~80 average) + extra credit. Pretty easy to get the grade you want.

Very good professor, humorous and definitely knows what he's talking about. Homework is worth 45% of the final grade, so as long as you do the homework and go to most of the lectures you will get an A.

Professor Sinclair is a great person and is clearly passionate about her work, but the way she ran the class was frequently frustrating. The readings were unrealistically long and would often be posted late, leaving essentially no time to read them, and grades were returned weeks later, after we had already taken the next exam.
Amazing class with great lectures but grading took forever to be released and the class was kind of disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Sinclair is stellar! She is passionate and well-spoken. She loves to hear from her students and encourages great dialogue in class. She will tailor the class - to an extent - to the students' interests. There's no textbook but there are many academic publications or books to read. However, it is totally fine to skim.

Professor Sinclair was an awesome prof. She's an expert in her field and always knew what she was talking about. The class was very reading heavy but you could always get 100% on the quizzes if you just read the abstract or skimmed. Sinclair was very passionate about politics and was very encouraging of participating at a grass roots lvl
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Made the coursework and materials very hard but very good lecturer and I learned a lot. Tests were fair relative to the study materials.

The GOAT! The best professor at WashU, without a doubt. You will learn so much. He's not "overly difficult," a good class SHOULD be challenging. If all your classes are easy A's, you're probably not learning much. I mean this with my whole heart, if you have the opportunity to have him, take it!!! It will be so worthwhile. And go to office hours!

GOAT! The best professor at WashU without a doubt. You'll learn so much. It's not "overly difficult," a good class SHOULD be challenging. If all your classes are easy A's, you're probably not learning much. I mean this with my whole heart, if you have to opportunity to have him, take it!!! It will be so worthwhile. And go to office hours!
This guy is the best.

Sign up for a class with Dr. Foster right now! Highkey the goat of the math department at WashU. Linear Algebra was hell! But there were plenty of resources and extra credit assignments to make up for it. On top of that you get a professor that actually cares about his students and makes an effort meet everyone where they're at.

Honestly, Prof. Foster hit it out of the park. I'm pretty sure this was his first class at WashU too. Do not expect an easy class but do expect to learn a lot. Show up to office hours, stack up the extra credit when you can (he provides plenty) and you are guaranteed to do well in this class.

The class is very difficult, and it's a lot of work. The homework is hard, and so are the tests. Frequent assignments with the PCRQs. He means well but has not learned how to effectively teach or run a class. Would recommend taking the class with a different professor but he cares.

Definitely demanding but much rewarding class at WashU. You would learn most of linear algebra you needed as an undergraduate student. Since there are tons of extra credits, it's not that difficult to get an A. Definitely worth taking.
Overly difficult

He is a nice guy, but prepare for larger workload than other professors. He gives problem set and webwork at the same time, and 80% grade depends on exams (although he also gives a lot of extra credit). You will learn a lot in his class.

Difficult class and you would probably need to spend a lot of time reviewing; tests take up 80% of the grade but he gives a TON of extra credit for both hw & the final. He has recordings for every lecture which is super helpful and oh can be very helpful.

Great job for his first time at WashU. He genuinely cares and gives tons of extra credit. He assigns more work than the other sections, but you get a way better understanding of the material. Knows his stuff and is a chill dude.

Overall great, but need to WORK. There are tons of homework including webwork, written ps, and optional ps. Get prepared to spend more time that you imagined. Attend his oh which is helpful. He gives extra credits which boost my grade a lot.
Difficult compared to the other section. Be prepared that you will need work hard for this class and really try to understand the concepts (for True-False questions). Gave extra credit opportunities.

Ben Foster is a cool dude and he seems like he cares about his students a lot. He loves what he teaches, but it doesn't help that his class is significantly difficult. If you're not a master at math, prepare to pour most of your semester into the class. It was his first year teaching so there were quite a few lumps, but overall it's doable.
DO NOT TAKE FOR AN EASY A! But you'll learn a lot, and good to take if you are a math major

Definitely not an easy A class, content is significantly harder than other matrix classes and lots of homework. But I can tell he is a really nice person and always answer questions promptly and detailedly in Piazza or during/after class.

Professor Foster is an absolute goat. While this class was quite intense at times, its grading was always fair, often generous. There was tons of extra credit offered, and exams were designed to fairly test your understanding of the content. You would only lose one point if you got the wrong answer with the right process. TAKE THIS MANS CLASS!!!

He let us out of class late every single time and it seemed like his lectures progressively got more rushed as class went on. He assigned lots of homework and the exams were much more work and difficult than the other Matrix section. With that said, Foster gave us tons of extra credit, cares about his students, and gives lots of resources to help.
Professor Rodgers gave good engaging lectures, and focused heavily on understanding and not just memorization. The tests have a lot of multiple choice and were not too hard.
Prof. Rogers taught micro well. He makes funny jokes during lectures, but I don't even think he's trying to be funny. Definitely knows his stuff and an interesting person to talk to.

You need to teach yourself the material. Exams are extremely difficult, and class averages are low. Grading system is weird, so the final can make or break you. If no micro background, don't take it because you'll be very stressed when tests come around. Wish he taught actual tough stuff more than rambling for the entirety about stupid concepts.

Prof. Rogers is a good person but lectures are him mansplaining simple topics. While I appreciate the detail, we never get to actually difficult content, and the tests are literally testing on stuff we didn't learn in class and had to self-teach via textbook. For those taking micro for the first time, you need to read and practice on your own.

Rogers is an engaging lecturer. The content is interesting and he gives lots of examples of the theory taught. Ultimately he docked my final grade without responding to my email asking for an explanation and scores back on final project. Disappointing ending to an otherwise great semester.

A majority of your grade comes from your exam grades (80%). Rogers is a boring lecturer (although it seems like he tries his best) and his class lectures cover a fraction of the info he expects us to know. He relied on the textbook to teach us, and I think the textbook was terrible. A lot of self-teaching is required to pass this class.

He's fine but I found lectures boring and rambly. Very kind and understanding, really wants people to succeed, but overall I don't think the class was set up too well. Almost no homework aside from occasional open-note quizzes, which is nice because it's a light workload but not great for knowing things when the tests come

Hilarious guy, took Econ404 with him. Tries to get students to understand the logic instead of making them do excruciating math. The problem sets are straightforward and attending his office hours is extremely helpful. Safe to call Econ404 an easy A.
A huge chiller. So funny. Very kind. Super nuanced and deep.

definition of a chiller. took AP Micro in HS and this was the same level of difficulty (although that does mean I was kinda familiar with the subject coming in). But class felt very reasonable and you could get help if you needed it
I love Professor Rogers. He's such a cutie and is very nice. Very receptive to questions, and the exams are not too difficult.

Tries his best to keep class fun, but tends to spend class going over easy problems in too much detail and not discussing harder concepts. Make sure to read the textbook and do the problems, it's very helpful. If you don't already have an understanding of micro, don't skimp out on the readings and study consistently, otherwise, you'll be lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very funny and quirky and does his best to keep everyone engaged in-class lectures. With that being said, he does ramble a bit and can go on long tangents. I would highly recommend doing the practice problems in the textbook for exam prep. Exams are not meant to trick anyone and your grade generally reflects your level of understanding

Rogers is a straightforward guy who is fairly to-the-point and clear about his expectations. Doing the textbook readings and end-of-chapter problems are very helpful towards mastering basic concepts, as his lectures can sometimes gloss over things or mention something important in passing. Overall, he's a fine pick for the intro to micro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He rambles on in lectures, and only really covers the simple parts of topics, while the tests cover much more in-depth material. I ended up not paying any attention in the lectures and teaching myself everything though Khan Academy. I'd recommend not taking his class if you don't already know what the class covers.

A really nice guy, but his lectures are way too simplistic comparing to his exams. Sometimes he would spend too much time on basic concepts and never talk about the more in-depth stuff that is covered on the exams.
Waste of time. Lectures were boring and didn't teach micro that well.
Claimed he would curve the class the whole semester, then never did. Also made the final really hard. Avoid Rogers if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's not a good professor, not sure why his reviews are so high. Made the final pretty hard, and rambles on in lecture. His slides were overly simplistic and didn't explain micro very well.

Brian wants to be a cool econ professor. and he really tries his best. He can be funny but often just ends up rambling about the same thing he's been talking about for half the lecture. Also, his voice kinda sounds like Pleakley from "Lilo and Stitch" which is entertaining.

Brian Rogers is amazing. His lectures are clear and extremely helpful. You will want to show up for class because you will honestly enjoy it. He is extremely funny. Absolutely rocks athleisure. Truly cares about students, even going so far as to host extra office hours near exams and a full hour and a half review session for the final.

Brian is the definition a superstar. I adore showing up to class each day because he's informative, thoughtful and hilarious. He's dramatic in the most understated way possible, and he rocks athleisure like no one else. Class is well-paced, and he obviously cares about his students and their success. His explanations are clear and helpful. Rock on.
Very clear and engaging lecturer - uses simple examples to explain complex topics and really seems to put a lot of thought into each lecture. Definitely take him if possible.
Really awesome at explaining - pretty engaging for a big lecture intro class. Seems to put effort into preparing concise and easy to understand lectures and also seems very passionate about econ.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Rogers is a good young professor who has a sense of humor and respects his students.  His intro micro class is pretty easy (about equivalent to AP micro or maybe a bit easier) but still pretty entertaining.  I would recommend this class to just about anyone.

Rogers is engaging in lectures and very clear with examples. He is funny and a nice guy, willing to help during his open office hours. Definitely recommend taking his intro to micro class, it inspired be to pick up an economics major
Really enjoyed his lectures. He moves at a fast pace but doesn't sacrifice clarity. Young guy with a good sense of humor.

took intro psych freshman fall with him and he was great! engaging lecturer, cared about his students, easy to understand and follow and outlined the class very clearly. Go to class or if you skip lecture honestly just study vocab terms from the textbook and you will be fine. easy A with a little effort
Love Bergstrom, really fair on exams and just a good guy
Prof Bergstrom is super engaging, his lectures are always interesting, and he explains things clearly. I would definitely recommend him for intro to psych.
explains super well and keeps students engaged in lectures through videos and examples. if you study the terms on the slides you will do good on the exam.

Bergstrom is an awesome professor. His lectures were always interesting, and I enjoyed the analogies and historical stories he would tell. The workload was light, assignments were straightforward, and overall, a great introductory class, given that you do the work and reading.
Made sure lectures were interesting and content was understandable

Loved this class! Bergstrom was a great professor and made the lectures not boring. Attendance is not really mandatory if you want to do well on the exams, since you could honestly just study the slides and do fine, but I would recommend going because it was interesting.

Bergstrom was a great professor, everyone loved him. Just make sure you memorize the key information on the slides and you'll be completely fine for the tests. Lectures were a lot of fun and the class was relatively easy.

Pretty interesting guy, and made the test material clear. His lectures were often quite interesting and included some funny bits that kept me engaged. Honestly it was a pretty easy class and I stopped going at some point.
Dr. Bergstrom's lectures were pretty interesting! You could tell he was very enthusiastic, but he did go on tangents often.

I love Bergstrom! Compared to the other intro psych professor, his exams had higher averages (lol) and were highly reflective of the retrieval questions he provided. I liked his style of lecturing w his humor and real-life examples. Reading the textbook isn't required; just memorize the key information from slides and lectures.

Bergstrom was the best teacher I had my freshman year first semester. His lectures were great and helped explain concepts, and he made the material engaging. He is also just a very sweet guy and clearly cares about his students as well.
Love Berg!
Took this class in Fall of 2024. My second favorite psychology professor. Very clear lectures and straightforward exam.

Class is not difficult, but you really need to put in the work and study for exams. Dr. Bergstrom is a really great and caring professor! If you study, pay attention in class, and take good notes, you'll definitely pass.
His slides are helpful, and if you pay attention in class it is not hard to do well.

Dr. Bergstrom is an amazing professor and I really enjoy his lectures. He incorporates many engaging videos during his lectures that keep me focused, and he's a very funny lecturer. I hope to take another class with him in the future.
Amazing lecturer and good slides
amazing lecturer

Super friendly and an amazing prof. Lectures were always entertaining, super lively and definitely enjoys teaching. Studying tests was very straightforward; the book has underlined terms and definitions that makes making quizlets/notecards really easy.

Loved Prof. Bergstrom. Outside of class he was incredibly kind and cared about students. Not the typical professor. Really knew the content, wasn't challenging to understand. Shared his own stories, didn't just read off slides. Great guy - HIGHLY recommend.

Dr. Bergstrom is very funny and makes content that could be boring very interesting. If you took AP Psych in highschool It's basically the exact same concepts. I didn't need to read the textbook and missed a few lectures and was perfectly fine. The 1st exam wasn't difficult and I expect the second to be the same. Definitely recommend the class!
He was a great lecturer who always made the lectures interesting and funny. He explained the concepts very well, and the tests were straightforward

I was worried I'd struggle in BioPsych since I don't have science background, but it ended up being incredibly manageable. Straight forward tests (study the homework quizzes and you'll do well) and interesting lectures. Passionate and gives interesting lecturers. Only problem was that it was sometimes difficult to communicate outside of class.

Insanely detailed in lecture and really cares about the subject. If you need examples and visual aides to learn content, he is the professor to go with. Really enjoyed his class and teaching style. Would recommend.

Brian Bergstrom is my GOAT. I love that man. He's an amazing lecturer, he's funny, and his tests are incredibly fair. Four tests per semester...drop lowest grade. Gives comprehensive practice quizzes that if you do well on you will do well on the test. Vocab/concept heavy. Start studying 4+ days in advance. Explain concepts aloud. Make connections.

Dr. Bergstrom is a good lecturer, he can be a bit boring at times, but fairly covers and explains all the content he expects you to know. The tests are fair, the only content on them is what he has covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bergstrom is very patient and can articulate difficult concepts clearly with real-world examples. His exams cover only what is learned in class and provide slides and practice quizzes to aid learning.
A very nice professor!

For a class that could become very easily muddled, Dr. Bergstrom does an amazing job of simplifying and clarifying the course material. Truly is an extremely caring professor, so I strongly recommend taking Psych 301 with him!
Super funny and great lectures. Posted lot's of retrieval practice questions, making it easy to study. He made the already interesting class even more fun

I don't usually write reviews for professors, but I loved Bergstrom. He is an absolute king. For this being a tough class, he made it so much better. He is so accessible outside of class, and you can tell he really cares about his students. He is probably my favorite professor at WashU. I highly recommend him!
He gives really clear lectures and materials. Always willing to help and support. He's the best professor I ever had.
Very nice and good at giving examples for psychological concepts.

Bergstrom is an amazing professor and also a really nice guy! He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Very humble, and admits when things are wrong / need changes. There is a lot of textbook reading assigned in this class, but as long as you read them and pay attention in class, you'll do fine. Really enjoyed 100B!

He's the best professor I've ever had here. He's passionate about everything he teaches and you can tell he knows what he's talking about. He makes it really easy to get a good grade. The class is mostly based on quizzes and exams. He lets you drop an exam and on top of that, the final is optional. He also gives you 3 attempts per review quiz.

Hands down best professor I've ever had at WashU. For a 2 hour class twice a week, he kept it engaging and made sure to give breaks. Prof Bergstrom is very caring, accommodating, and truly wants students to learn and succeed. For one of the hardest psych classes, he made it less of a burden which we were all so grateful for.
Sometimes I would get lost in lectures, just because he would deviate from the slides a lot. But, overall, if you are in tune, he is an awesome professor!

Love love loved Bergstrom! He was super flexible and understanding about us having other stuff outside of his class and would always change deadlines to give us more time. Really appreciated him this semester

Was my favorite of the 3 Intro to Psych professors. Tests can be a little tough but you should do very well if you pay attention in the lecture and look at the slides. Nice sense of humor in lectures.

I love this man, and if I could, I would take the rest of my psych classes with him. Amazing professor and genuinely cares not only about his work but also his students. Can be pretty late with grading things, but more than makes up with be super understanding and flexible with you.

Lectures can be a little boring, but he truly cares about the success of his students. Powerpoints are largely based on the textbook and offers optional practice quizzes to test our learning. Lectures are funny and interesting if you pay attention.

Professor Bergstrom is the best professor I have had at WashU. He makes the class incredibly engaging, he gives very detailed instructions, and he is incredibly understand. Even though Experimental Psych is known to be one of the more difficult classes and work heavy classes in the Psych Department, Bergstrom made the class incredibly manageable.

He is just the best! He truly cares about his students in and out of the classroom and only wants to see them succeed. This class can be very content-heavy, but he moves through it well and in an engaging manner. Definitely one of my favorite professors!

I love Professor Bergstrom!! He is so engaging and considerate to his students. He loves to chat with you in or out of class and is a great resource. The few lectures we had were very entertaining and informative. It is clear he wants his study to do well and be healthy. Very awesome would highly recommend him.
Bergstrom was so nice and so funny! Very engaging and really cares about you as a student. He's been my favorite professor at WashU so far! 10/10 recommend.

Dr Bergstrom is awesome! He is a great lecturer and is funny. He gives good feedback on papers and allows you to do corrections. Regarding the research paper, he is instrumental in helping you develop your idea and offers great insight. Take experimental psych with him! Trigger warning though: this class is a lot of work.
Exam is too content heavy and given the subjectivity of the material it was difficult to prepare for the exam compared to traditional ones. Grading can also be a little harsh.

I couldn't really connect with her and she had clear favorites in class. Exams are worth a lot and my grade is honestly a reflection of the effort I put in. Group projects are fun. She just tends to feel like she's right all the time and doesn't explain concepts clearly when asked questions

I really enjoyed taking OB with Birnbaum. She makes the class very engaging with many interactive classes and group activities. The exams in this class are content-heavy but doable if you prepare them beforehand.

One of my favorite core classes. Birnbaum is a great lecturer and is good at responding to feedback. I learned a ton in this class, and have already started using the info IRL. Assignments and exams were straightforward with articulated grading criteria, which apparently is not the case with the spring prof. Her research is also super interesting.

This individual does not understand WashU values. The lack of being able to think for yourself and bring in outside materials shows a lack of openness to learning from students on his part. An only use my lectures slide mentality is not a WashU value.  As a student who loves rigor, this class is unchallenging and lacks depth of learning.

(This is for 4030) The materials are crazily difficult compared to SDS 3030, and his lecturing styles make it worse. Going to lectures are highly recommended (self-taught is impossible). Homework are long but doable because you can copy codes from lecture slides. Exams are similar to practice exams, but still difficult to do in 50' and take 50%.

Singlehandedly the worst professor I've had at WashU. While the content was quite manageable, I cannot overemphasize how unreasonably difficult his exams were. The lectures were 0 help, as he just read directly off of the slides. Prof Katsianos singlehandedly made me not want to do a stats minor, or ever take a stats class again. Avoid at all costs

The way he respond in piazza is not helpful. Students asked question about which method should use, and he responded as "you can use whatever you want as long as it is correct". And this class has no replace in midterms which have lots of percentage, make it almost impossible to get an A if you did bad in one midterm....
Super nice and responds really fast on piazza! Assigns a lot of homework questions but is not a harsh grader (on homework and on exams). highly recommend taking a class with Bill!!

Bill was a good teacher throughout this semester, I honestly felt like I learned in his class. There were 2 exams both 25% of your grade, so if you messed up a little bit your grade suffered greatly. He graded nice on the exams though, in my opinion. He gave such long homework though, make sure you start a couple days prior to the due date.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very difficult class, especially if you miss class, good luck understanding the slides. Lectures are boring and hard to follow. Topics are taught at a high level without much intuitive explanation
Unhelpful office hours

Professor is very nice and helpful when asked questions, but exams are 70% multiple choice which does not provide a lot of room for error given that the class is mostly graded on exams. Really nice professor though, but mainly just writes down and teaches the slides exactly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams in this class were quite difficult and often had a curve, and though I enjoyed the content, I think the lectures/teaching could have been better.

Very passionate professor, and he cares about his students' success. The exams are mostly multiple choice (each question is 4 points) with no partial credit, so little room for error. The difficulty in content increases quite steeply after the first exam. Go to office hours and ask question- he is very accessible if you just make the effort to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bill has good slides and lectures overall. Homework is a little time consuming but is fair. Exams are generally fair but a little hard to do in the 50 min time frame and have some tricky questions. The final project which in theory should boost your grade is graded incredibly harshly on top of being time consuming which is rather counterintuitive.

He makes good slides, but the exams are UNREASONABLY HARD. For the second midterm that counted 25% towards the final grade the average before curve is 63% (he curved 10 points, but it is useless). For the final, he said it was really easy and it turned out that the average before the curve is 70% (he curved 5 points up).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course starts off fairly easy for the first month, but immediately gets more difficult until Exam 2. The slides and notes are incredibly useful. Bill teaches really passionately, but is a bit slow-paced. Be prepared for calculation-heavy homeworks and exams.
Bill is very chill, and his exams are sometimes hard, but he also gives out extra credit sometimes.
Really kind and caring professor that gives fair exams, it isn't difficult to do well if you do the homeworks and study

493 Probability is a hard class. Bill is a new instructor, obviously he needs more effective teaching methods instead of just copying from the slides. The slides he provides are clear and you can basically learn by yourself. Tests and hw are not easy. But Bill tries hard to raise the average, such the nicest grader ever. The final is easy.

Really good professor who takes the time in class to not only teach concepts clearly, but go over plenty of proofs and examples in class. He does a great job of teaching you the concepts underlying everything, but not demmanding perfection on the exams. He is a very fair grader and puts out practice exams which are reflective of the real exams.
exams are a lot easier than hw, both are pretty reasonable. grading is fairly lenient imo, also he's hot

The averages on the midterms were 89% and 84%, grading was very lenient and the exam Qs were very easy compared to the HW and content covered in lectures. Bill is a very intelligent and caring teacher and imo this class is only slightly harder than SDS3211. If you are paying attention in class and not ChatGPT-ing the HW you will probably get an A.
Professor Sanz was an angel! PLEASE take the FYO: Conservation and Research in Zoos and Botanical Gardens. It was such an engaging class and was a nice break from the hectic school life.

TAKE THIS CLASS! Prof Sanz is so nice and funny! Every week was a fieldtrip to a different place, and the only work is 3 questions each week and 3 reflection essays. She is super understanding and accommodating with deadlines. This class feels like a break from school and every place we went had a different expert speaker. LOVE LOVE LOVE THIS CLASS

Professor Sanz is the kindest and generous instructor yet! She always gives excellent feedback and checks up on each of her students. I would recommend this first-year opportunity for first-year students.

I had her for the first year program with research conservation in Zoos and Botanical gardens. She is an extremely kind , interesting and engaging professor who cares deeply. Class was super fair not time consuming at all.

Dr. Sanz is one of the best professors at WashU! She is so caring and invested in each of her students and their projects. She is accessible outside of class and goes out of her way for students. Only problem is that she is so enthusiastic about the course that she sometimes cuts off students when they are speaking in order to give a comment.

i loved this class and crickette! she is so sweet and is really passionate - this class was the reason i decided to become an anthro major.
