I didn't have access to backfiles but I studied for a few days before the exams and got solid As on them. don't have to read the textbook or go to class. definitely a lot of memorization, but HIGHLY recommend

Easy class to get science credit out of the way, but super memorization heavy.  Slides are posted after lectures so you can easily skip, but trying to review all lectures in one weekend can take HOURS.  Exam averages are so high because so many people have access to backfiles, but if you want to authentically do well, you'll have to study VERY HARD
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was disappointing. She just reads of the slides so a majority of students just don't attend. Her tests can be tricky -- you pretty much have to memorize the entire primate table + all the random facts she spews out. Easy class if you like to just sit an memorize all weekend. Would not recommend.
She makes a boring topic really interesting and is invested in making sure you get a high grade.
Really easy class and really interesting

She talks really quickly in lecture and overplans  a bit, but she always posts all of the slides online which makes it easy to study for this class. The tests are really straight forward and she tells you what information to know so you won't be overwhelmed. A great class to take if you need science credit but don't like science! Would take again.
Talks really fast in lecture, but posts all lecture slides online so you can catch up what you miss. Don't need to read the textbook because all information on tests are given in lecture.
Really nice and super intelligent but lectures are super fast and you'll need to do a lot of reviewing on your own time. Exams are fair but hard!
Phenomenal Calc 3 professor. Her lectures were very well placed and she explained things very clearly. She was also so warm, kind, and willing to help any student with questions. Highly recommend
Her lectures are extremely fast for such a higher level math course, nearly impossible to follow

Wonderful professor! She provides a lot of examples with different scenarios for each theorem, which helps a lot with my understanding of how to apply. She explains the theorem in a clear way which fits our current level of math. Very friendly at questions and wonderful graphs drawn when explaining.
Somewhat hard to understand at times due to microphone issues and accent, but very sincere and understanding teacher who wants the best for her students.

Beheshti is great in my opinion. I seriously have loved Calc III with her this semester.
She clearly knows her stuff about math and is very caring in the lecture hall; always answers questions kindly and clearly and I have always felt well prepared for the class after watching her lectures.
Slight (middle-eastern?) accent but no issue there.

Beheshti is a truly knowledgeable and down to earth professor who knows how to teach the material in an effective and clear way. The tests were fairly straightforward and covered the content at the same level of difficulty as recitation problems, examples from lecture, and homework problems did. Basically, if you do the work you should be fine.

Someone down there said it best. In most classes I do well, and I've always felt like I could succeed if I put enough effort it. However, this class has been a completely different story. The tests are SO HARD. Behsheti teaches calc and knows her stuff., but the tests are incredibly advanced and nothing like anything we learn.

Great lecturer. Draws intuitive diagrams to illustrate calculus concepts. She knows what she is doing. In my opinion, people who give her bad ratings on RateMyProfessor either don't attend lecture or don't read the textbook, etc.. As long as you are attentive, you will get the grade you want. Thanks for a great semester.

Not a fan. She knows what she's talking about and is helpful in office hours but simply doesn't know how to teach. Her lectures are almost useless; she moves super fast, makes errors, doesn't post slides, and makes you feel dumb for asking a question. I had straight A's my whole life and a 36 on the ACT but I think I'm going to get a B or C.
not curve and very tough

Difficult, but very fair class.  Exam questions are based off homework + lecture examples, so it's good to go to lecture if you're not a calculus wiz! One of the better professors in the math department at WashU
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Beheshti is a very fair professor, definitely one of the better math professors at Wash U. She really tries to explain concepts in class rather than just write out a formula and tell you to memorize it. As long as you memorize how to do the example problems in class and in the homework, you're golden.

She's awesome. She doesn't come off as super nice or friendly, but once you talk to her she's really nice and wants to help you. Exams aren't easy, but they are fair. Gives you lists of problems from old exams to study which are really helpful.
she's super sweet. I wish I had appreciated her while I had her because now I've had such horrible math professors.

Lectures are really nice and clear. Homework challenging but helpful for exams. She will give you lots of tips on study material for exams -- old homework, extra problems, past exams. Exams can be hard but are very fair -- no surprise or impossible problems. She also just seems like a genuinely nice and dedicated professor. I'd for sure take again.
Solid teacher, some people find her hard to understand because of accent. Tests are pretty easy to prepare (just do the past tests on math department site). All in all, a solid class.
Beheshti is awesome. Recommend her class.

She speaks very quickly in her lectures.  The Webassign problems teach you just as much as she does, so you if you skip a few lectures it's fine.  Very intelligent woman and her tests are pretty easy.

I adore Beheshti. I don't think her accent is that difficult to understand and her tests are pretty easy. She is a good lecturer, but she doesn't stop for anything between "Good morning everyone" and "I'm out of time," sometimes not even to breathe. Lectures aren't taped though, so go to class.

Excellent professor!  Very clear and actually tests on what she teaches.  She is very helpful to students and I would highly recommend her.  Tests are all multiple choice , but as far as I know, the average grade for the class is pretty high.
Her lectures were pretty clear. Tests are really easy, straight from homework and suggested problems (average was a 80). Make sure to learn how to do the Webassign problems. (solutions are posted)

Behesthi has really good intentions of being a good lecturer, but intentions don't always match outcome. Her accent is very hard to understand for a lecture, but she will be very sweet and helpful in office hours.I decided to never attend class and just teach myself from the textbook and managed to get an A. Overall easy and helpful, very nice lady
Straightforward course. She is nice in office hours.
Professor Beheshti is extremely caring and genuinely wants all of her students to do well! The tests were fair, but the material was tough.
Her exams were way too easy
Her notes were very clear, and going to her office hours helped me a lot.

I thought she was fine, but I'm also pretty good at figuring out concepts on my own. Plenty of people never went to class and found reading the book to be more worthwhile. Don't bother asking questions in class; you probably won't understand her answer. Exams varied in difficulty but were overall pretty fair.

Incomprehensible. Doesn't teach basic calc, but rather expects you to easily understand her obscure examples. LAUGHS WHEN YOU GET A QUESTION WRONG. Unapproachable and intimidating.  Very intelligent, clearly bored with the subject.

Had her for both 429 Linear Algebra and 430 Modern Algebra.  Very straightforward and clear in her lectures.  And if you are confused by something, the class atmosphere is very accommodating to asking questions.  Lectures closely but far from exactly follow textbook - helped me to have the book open during class to compare.

Beheshti seems to be an excellent mathematician who is bored silly teaching Calculus. Her lectures are mind-numbingly dull and consist mostly of example problems. Her tests are much harder than the practice quizzes, often including twists and complications that she never showed us in class. The TA was a much better teacher than she was.

She is unbelievably difficult to understand when you can actually hear her. She just does examples from notes, and is very poor at answering questions. The tests are unreasonably hard and require tricks to do several problems. The TA was a much better teacher than her. "xesquared pi half"

Dr. Campbell would get grades back relatively quickly and was willing to meet and help you outside of class, but his grading was picky and we had more assignments than other equal classes. He cares about his students, but he also picks on them a bit, and the way he explains things can often make things more confusing rather than clearing things up.
I don't understand the hate! If you aren't social, he WILL pick on you, but I love the guy. He's a GOAT. Very passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Personally, I don't understand the bad ratings. Mr. Campbell was an amazing teacher who is passionate about writing and wants to see his students succeed. He cracks a lot of jokes and tries to connect with the students in a light-hearted manner. He can take a while to grade and not everyone clicks with his personality, but he is amazing overall.
I don't know why people don't like him. I suck at writing, but got an A.

The professor bases all your subsequent grades on your first paper. If you get a B on the first assignment, that is what you will get for every paper after it. He takes a long time to grade and ends up providing little to no feedback. He also goes off topic a lot and it distracts students from learning.
Great professor. Would absolutely take again. Gives great feedback.

Dr. Campbell is an amazing teacher who gives amazing feedback. He is very kind and a good listener. He even had my class over for dinner (great cook). I definitely became a better writer because of this class. My only heads up is to participate in the class discussions, it is super important for both your grade and your writing development.

Without getting too much into details of what happened in our class, it is important to note that reports were filed against Dr. Campbell this semester(FL23). He would take a long time to get our essays back to us. When he would get them back to us, the feedback he would give wasn't helpful. Our averages for each assignment were in the low B range.
Gives an okay amount of feedback, but the number grade doesn't match the feedback he gives. Lectures mostly about history because that's what he's more interested in. Takes forever to return papers.

Yes Dr. Campbell was a tough grader sometimes, but setting up one on one meetings for feedback and ideas on papers was extremely helpful. He also is very experienced in academia with so much knowledge that he is so willing to share if you ask. I definitely became a better writer due to his class.

If you dont want a miserable college writing experience I would avoid him. He can be extremely rude to students at times and was an extremely harsh grader for my class. We usually had our average essays in the C+/B-/B range. Also took months to return essays sometimes. Really disappointed.

The only thing that got me through this course was knowing how to write from my high school English classes. Dr. Campbell's lectures were very meandering and never really seemed to have a point to them. He also picked on individual students and was very condescending at times. Never took points off for me turning papers in late though.

Professor Campbell was a funny professor, but most times the lectures were unhelpful and irrelevant. While he was accessible outside of class, he didn't give great or constructive writing feedback, and often interrupted students. Very flexible with deadlines.
Amazing teacher makes an attempt to relate to students on a genuine level. You will look forward to this class.

Professor Campbell is an interesting teacher. If youre looking for writing skills and tips, you wont find them here beyond a vague cater to your audience repeated every class. His lecture style is engaging and fun, but his grading process is unclear and contradicts itself. He is also messy with due dates and communication - super frustrating.

Prof. Campbell is great!! His lectures are so much fun; you'll actually want to go to class. The readings were really interesting and the papers weren't hard at all. He's a really funny guy and I would definitely take a class from him again. I had him for College Writing: Writing Identity.
Campbell was amazing. Super chill guy and very flexible with due dates. Classes were super entertaining and he was always getting everyone engaged. Had him for college writing writing identity.
Good professor, everything besides the final is take-home, tries to give a lot of partial credit on homeworks
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Chi is extremely knowledgeable, and you can be confident that he'll be able to explain any topic you bring to him clearly and in depth. I'd often had questions or problems I wanted to work through after class, and he'd often stay to answer them for well over an hour. Overall an extremely caring, dedicated, and proficient professor.
his explanations are confusing sometimes and its fine all semester cause its take home stuff until the final then you need to teach yourself everything
Lectures are a little too free-flow for my liking.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I stopped going to class after ~a month. He is a good, caring person, but lectures tend to go off on tangents and his explanations are... interesting. He tries to make sure you understand the broader concepts but Thornton did not structure the curriculum for that, so he's usually behind the other profs, lol. Teach yourself first if going to lecture

you'd think it's his first time teaching the class bc he has no outline of the content anywhere, doesn't use online tools (besides canvas) for anything, rambles at the board, and makes tons of mistakes. you'll end up having to teach yourself everything at the end of the semester for the final, but you probably won't know what to study

He is a very poor lecturer. However, he has ~4 homework assignments, a take-home midterm and an in person final with a 5x8 (front & back) cheat sheet. You will likely have to teach yourself the content and how much time you spend studying for the final exam will likely determine your final grade. He is more helpful during OH than in class.

Chi is a really nice guy and gives a pretty decent lecture on matrix algebra. The course is just designed incredibly poorly where students are graded on 5 homeworks before taking a final worth 35% of their grade. Makes most of the semester very easy, but you have to learn an entire semester of matrix during reading week to do well.

Lectures were very bad, he constantly makes mathematical mistakes. The take home midterm and homework are very easy. For the final, since I didn't go to class and just studied for a day, the grade is what I expected.

Chi gets a lot of hate but honestly, he is a wonderful guy. Only 4 HW assignments (all problems from the textbook), a take-home midterm, and a final. He can be a little disorganized and confusing, but read the textbook, spend time on the homework, and watch videos to help you understand! He was always willing to answer questions too!

Full disclaimer: I'm don't like math too much. So I found his lectures to be a bit dry and long-winded, but given the context of Zoom classes, he really made a strong effort to explain the bigger concepts while using concrete examples which i appreciated. Best thing about him is that he held multiple office hours a week and was extremely accessible

I would avoid taking Chi if possible. Tests were very difficult, nothing like lecture at all. When asked if there would be any sort of grade adjustment due to class being moved online because of Covid, he dismissed the question and compared getting an A to being a Navy SEAL.
He doesn't know how to explain concepts and gets really off track during class. Hard to understand. Emailed him about grading and responded rudely. I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: the professor cannot explain things clearly, not a great experience being in his classes.

Tests are hard. He knows what he's talking about, but the homework is unrelated and so are the test. He is also very uncaring. I feel like I could get run over by a car and he wouldn't give any special accommodations.

Great professor! This class is very cool, with interesting proofs and a broadening of horizons when it comes to math. If you do not like proofs, that's all this class is, so don't complain if you don't like it. Chi is a very nice professor, not a tough grader. There are only two exams, and they're take-home. Great class, 10/10 recommend.

I initially had an idea that math courses with take-home exams is a joke, which was harshly challenged by this professor last semester. You will never survive this course unless you are a mathematical genius or visit all his office hours after carefully taking all the notes from the lecture. He is responsive to questions via email, though.
sooo good !!! He is the best teacher I have ever had. Just make sure you studies after class .

Quo-Shin Chi is the definition of a bad professor.  he is hard to understand, his lectures are despicable and horribly organized, and he does not seem to care about his students or how well they can understand the material.  Do not take him at all costs.

Chi tries really hard to provide advice to students and seems enthusiastic about teaching. However, his lectures are very difficult to understand and I got lost very quickly- I ended up mostly learning from the textbook. He also is much more interested in theoretical math and proofs, not applications.

Incredibly boring, incredibly confusing. Clearly does not know how to connect with students. Often goes from one topic to the next without any resolution or clear transition. Luckily, all the assignments are take home, including the tests, so you can use the textbook to help you heavily with your grade. Avoid him if you aren't a math major

He is the most boring professor in the world.  I had to stop coming to class because it was too painful.  Luckily, the textbook explains the material way better than he does, so the class was fine.  Exams were take-home, which was great.
I had a lot of trouble understanding and following him, mainly because he is pretty animated and this made some of the material harder to understand

Chi was a decent professor. His lectures were sometimes confusing and not applicable to a calculus 1 course - but he knows his stuff. He is very approachable and easy to reach through email or office hours. His tests are confusing and hard - but once you understand how he writes them... they aren't that bad.

Great guy, and very accommodating.  Had him for both 302 Geometry and 3351 Number Theory.  Thoroughly knows the subject matter, though at times sloppy at the board, sometimes to the point of losing his train of proof completely.  Basically teaches straight from the books, but you should definitely go to class - especially for Number Theory.
Easy if you get the solution manual. Difficult if you don't. You can download the manual here: lol jk...use google

Professor Chi is, by far, one of the most helpful teachers I have had at WashU.  He is extremely quick to respond to emails with questions and is very generous with help in office hours.  For the upper level classes, he only uses take-home exams and homeworks, which makes these difficult classes much less stressful.  Super nice, highly recommended!

The only problem I had with Chi was 53% average he gave on the final exam in order to lower the average final grade. Go to class because the textbook is confusing as hell. Do hw with friends because half of them will be impossible and you'll just end up copying the answer manual. Pay attention in lectures or you'll fall behind within seconds.

Chi is a very nice guy and his lectures are generally well organized and clear, although somewhat dry. He does have a bit of an accent but that doesn't hamper his ability to deliver a clear lecture. Homeworks and test fairly straightforward, and he's helpful in office hours.

Super nice guy.  Super helpful in office hours.  Pretty dry lecturer, and kind of confusing.  Just walks in and writes proofs on the board for an hour, doesnt stop for people to ask questions.  Not too hard though and once again a super nice, helpful guy.
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Chi's lectures tend to be hampered by a sense of disorganziation, but his coverage of material is good.  Both the midterm exam and final were take-home, and he was generous with hints both in class and in office hours.

Highly recommend this course for anyone interested in neuro. As a neuroscience major, I found the curriculum to be a solid mix of essential refreshers and new, niche insights into specific areas of the field. To succeed, make sure to attend every lecture and take detailed notes—the exams are heavily weighted toward the slide content.

BIOL 4114. Quizzes are fair and directly based on slides and lecture content. The professor uses very clear, easy-to-understand drawings to explain complex molecular concepts. Lecture pace is just right. Usually ends class a little early. Highly recommended.

I took the Bio 411 neuroplasticity class and enjoyed it. The content can be dense but much of it is discussed during the class. He does a good job of making his lectures engaging by including interested stories about his research experience. 
It's important to review the notes from previous lecture because these will be on the in-class quizzes.

Poor grammar in English, extremely thick accent to the point he is NOT understandable (mainly due to extremely poor grammar)-- takes FOREVER if at all to respond to emails. DID NOT even know when we would have the final and it was a week before classes were supposed to end. Lectures are DENSE + POOR GRAMMAR, JUMP EVERYWHERE (I WISH I could give ex)
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overly strict at the beginning of the semester, lectures hard to follow. You have to study on your own from a text book to get high results from quizzes. There is very little overlap of material covered in class and questions on the test. Not invested in students success. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was a very good class. Enjoyed learning new and interesting materials. Many interesting topics of Neuroscience were covered.
Thoroughly enjoyed the class. Exams were given from his lectures and power points. It was a great class! Thanks Dr. Chowdhury!!!

What a joke. This guy just changes multiple test questions during the exam, which is fun. There are also quite a few exam questions that make no sense at all. Asks you to give a presentation with no guidelines whatsoever. Does not respond to emails or help with anything. Most frustrating class I have ever taken. Never take any of his classes!!!!

Actual student here: if you read a review on this site that says "good" it is actually the PROFESSOR writing reviews about HIMSELF. You will note various grammatical mistakes that indicate his poor speaking and writing.

I must say he is an excellent professor and wonderful person. Dr. Chowdhury genuinely cares the students. he and his exams are very fair. Almost all of his exam  question are from his lecture and power point. If you don't miss class you will do good. Interesting and need neuroscience topics are discussed. I would say take his class.

Just finished with a good grade. This class was well planned and diversified. Many interesting events of ongoing neuroscience research on sensory field were discussed. Class covered a lot. Have to memorize everything on the slides however, you don't need the textbook. So not really a lot. enjoyed this class.

His speech is difficult to understand due to a thick accent.  His slides are hastily prepared and sometimes incoherent due to poor grammar.  The tests are a combination of ridiculously easy, average, and very randomarcane questions.  He's not very responsive to emails, but generally replies eventually.

I enjoyed this sensory neuroscience class. Professor covers many aspects of sensory neuroscience from philosophy to plasticity. Biology background is needed to understand the materials. Very interesting class. learned a lot!!!
Bad Awful  Doesn't speak english Makes up ratings on this website Avoid at all costs
Best professor i have had in a long time
Highly recommend! would take again any day for sure. best professor I have had in a long time
Great teacher. Best in his field.
Very enthusiastic. Presents the topic in an interesting ways. He has a very good grasp on the subject matter. He is a great professor!
Great teacher. Very clear perception, can make the materials interesting. Great class!!!

The grading policy is very unbalanced and unfair. I think the retake policy is really ridiculous. Students who underperformed are given a chance to retake the exam, while students around the median, or even in the upper quartile, are stuck with 75% scores because they did poorly on the coding section, for which very little practice was provided.
The class was very poorly designed. However, he was really accessible outside of class and always willing to help. He does pay attention to whether or not you care about his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: worst professor at WashU. Worst syllabus.
Bad lectures, bad syllabus, worst class ever taken
Avoid this professor

Worst class at WashU (Spring 26). It has way to many assignments, harsh grading, cant miss ANY assignments, hard exams. They're trying to force mastery based learning on a huge class where it doesn't work. Professor unhelpful and not have empathy for students. DO NOT TAKE.

Very kind professor but his lectures were not great. If you're trying to learn beyond Zybooks or are confused, always skip lecture to study, go to his office hours instead. (Also the new bucket grading system is one of the worst things I've ever seen)
I don't think there has ever been a worse grading policy
Worst grading policy I have ever experienced. Do bad on 1 assignment? Forget about getting an A
Most ridiculous grading policy. Pretty boring lectures
Horrible lecturer although passionate in a 1-on-1 setting. The class just happens to have enough resources for people to succeed, but NOT as a result of  the professors.

He was really helpful during studio and lecture when you needed him. The content in this class is difficult but since the exams in the class only count 10% each, it's not hard to get an A. Lecture wasn't necessary to attend and I didn't pay attention in studio and just read the studio summaries. I definitely learned a lot in this class.
Terribly unfair with final grade. Miscommunication on assignments.

Prof. Cole lectures were not very good. He used the same plain black slides with white text for the whole semester. His voice is very monotone and lectures are very fast, often going through 100 slides a class. However, you can teach yourself the content from the textbook and studio summaries. Class is easy to get an A even if you don't understand.

Just finished this course. Prof. Cole was really a nice person, and he cared about his students' thoughts. The most important tip was GO TO THE OFFICE HOUR! Exams might be difficult, but only take up 30% of the final grade. Be serious about the labs and Zybook. Extra credits are a huge surprise.

I stopped going to lectures mid semester as I could not pay attention in class. I think the content of the class is better learned using the book and online resources. Some aspects of the class are poorly managed in my opinion but getting a good grade in the class is highly achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ngl I only saw him once all semester but the class wasnt hard just do the extra credit. good ass beard tho he kinda looks like the lumberjack from clash royale.

Professor cole seemed like a really nice person, lectures don't help that much in this class, I wouldn't recommend attending. Do the extra credit, it isn't too difficult, and will really boost your grade. Nice prof, but didn't interact that much. The content is pretty challenging, but stay on top of your work and you will do fine in the class.
Cole is so nice and accommodating, he is a lovely man. The class is super interesting but he's not the best lecturer. Lectures didn't help anyway though.

Professor Cole is very caring and always happy to help, but lectures are somewhat boring and the pacing is way too fast. It would be more helpful if there were two 80-minute lectures per week instead of blowing through 70-100 slides in a little over an hour, or just have students watch Professor Siever's videos instead. Very kind person regardless.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are terribly boring and not coherent, I don't recommend going to class since attendance is not tracked and such a waste of time. Seems like TAs are more in charge of the course. If you read and try to understand the textbook, you should do fine. The professor is super nice but doesn't explain the materials well.

The class itself is manageable if you put in the time, but lectures are not worth attending in my opinion. Lots of homework and exams are tough, but can be done utilizing Office Hours. The professor himself is really nice though, and regularly came to studio to answer any questions students had about content in general.

This class teaches important concepts of algorithms and DS needed in the real world and the class does well in teaching those concepts. However, do not go to lectures, so incredibly useless no offense. Assignments are fair in my opinion and exams are not too bad. However extra credit in this class is insane, do the extra credit readings DO THEM

Lectures are incredibly boring and disorganized. Material is primarily taught through TAs in studio or office hours. That being said, Cole did do a good job listening to student feedback, which helped the course.
Honestly it's 247 you probably already know what you're signing up for.

He actively tries to make his process better over time. Solicits students feedback and makes considerable changes to listen to it. His lectures are mostly review of the book, but his explanations are very helpful.

Very nice guy; checks in on his students, gives them opportunities to ask questions, and listens to/implements feedback. However, incredibly boring and hard to follow lectures. It's a straightforward class though so as long as you do the required work you should survive.

Super boring lecturer. But incredibly nice, always willing to answer questions (though not necessarily well) and much more helpful one-on-one. 

As a class, 247 is a slog but doing the readings and going to OH to check homework before turning it in will mean you'll probably pull off a good grade and get a reasonable understanding of content.

Prof Cole is very kind - his piazza posts are so sweet! The class also has a lot of extra credit, which is really nice. The only thing is that his lectures put me to sleep. However, everything else makes up for it!

Really nice guy, but a terrible lecturer. So bad in fact that I never went to class after the first two weeks. It is nearly impossible to stay up as he lectures. Easy exams, good grading, interesting course material, nice homework, but terrible lectures.
Never saw the guy. Only thing I know about him is that he has a beard. A class where you can learn nothing and still get a 100.

Kind & solid professor. Lecture is not necessary and somewhat hard to follow/focus on, but sometimes it can be helpful just to familiarize yourself with the material. Take notes on reading due before lecture and try to attempt the studio to understand the material. Homework can be tough so use OH. Exams are fair, with few difficult questions.

He's a really nice professor! His lectures aren't necessary but when I did go because a prelecture had an unclear topic he made it understandable. 247 is not easy material but he wants his students to succeed and makes the class doable. I will say he and his TAs are pretty bad at answering on piazza but office hours are almost always happening!
Lecture is often an unnecessary and dull repeat of the pre-lecture assignments. Otherwise, an ok professor.

Dr. Cole makes CSE247 well-organized. This course includes reading, lab, lectures, and studios, which greatly helps students to strengthen their understanding of concepts. Exams are fair, and it's an easy A class because there are 5% extra credits. Dr. Cole is also accessible outside class as long as you reach out to him on Piazza.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved having Dr. Cole, he was incredibly caring, and knew all the students in his class by name despite it being a larger lecture class. The class was difficult, but very interesting and rewarding. Cole really wants his students to succeed and will help you if you need it. I recommend doing what you can to get Cole if you want to take 247.
great beard

Cole was great for 247. He clearly cared about teaching the content and beyond that, he cared to learn each student's name that he talked to in a large lecture class.

247 is very manageable the only downside of the class is how long it takes for important assignments to come back however that is on the class and TA's more so than Cole.

Cole is a great professor. His lectures aren't the most engaging, but he is very caring for students and encourages participation. He is very caring and answers any questions thoroughly and really makes sure the students learn from his class.
Lecture hard to understand...

This class is known to be a doozy, but Professor Cole made it approachable and enjoyable. Assignments and exams are difficult but the TAs were amazing; go to TA hours for the assignments before they get busy! I learned so much from the class and feel like Professor Cole works hard to explain concepts as many ways as students need.
Cole is a really great guy. I wouldn't say 247 is like impossible, but a lot of the tests are poorly worded and grades ultimately don't come down to whether or not your know the material.

Cole was a great lecturer, but, more importantly, a personable professor. He answers questions with great detail at office hours, is always at studios, and really cares about how students are doing with the material. The 247 material can get a little dry, but he does his best to keep it as engaging as possible. Can't go wrong taking his class.

Dr. Cole is super wholesome. A good professor to learn from and a person to know. He will answer questions online ASAP, but don't expect him to give you the complete answer; most times he'll lead you in the right direction and you must get to the conclusion yourself, which isn't a bad thing anyways.

Cole is a very caring professor. He is humble and understanding. However, the TA's for 247 can be annoying as their mindset while grading is negative, think they r god. They try to find every possible way to deduct points rather than finding possible ways to give more points. I would definitely take him again. Just hope the quality of TA's improves

Cole is a great guy who genuinely cares about his students. He constantly seeks out feedback on his lectures and content, both of which are engaging and reasonable. He's not like the greatest teacher on earth but he's understanding and approachable and the class itself is fairly easy and interesting.

Super awesome guy. Not always the most engaging lecturer but really goes out of his way to try to help everyone succeed. Super respectful and just overall a really caring and great person. Plus his exams, while not easy, aren't above expectation and are very fair. Definitely would take another class with him.
Amazing teacher. Acts like a cheerleader.

Megan Daschbach is my role. model. Although I couldn't go to her lectures, I went to every single one of her help sessions. Let me tell you: each week, her teaching was a MONUMENTAL lock in moment. I can tell how hard she works for the class & is willing to help students. She is nothing short of phenomenal. Words don't do it justice.

Undoubtedly amazing lecturer who aced in teaching. However, tests are extremely hard and take up a large portion of ur grade. She always asserts that she wants to help develop applied problem solving skills, but ironically you can only get a good grade if you practice a lot of exam-like questions instead of actually developing ur thought processes.
love this prof

Literally the most amazing professor ever. If you can't learn from Dr. Daschbach, you have no hope of learning general chemistry because she makes everything so digestible and easy to understand, and always answers questions so thoroughly and is so knowledgeable about what she is teaching. She is so so good. One would regret not taking her class.

Good class and good teacher. Very organized and she really tried to connect with the students. In the end, I just did not find the material as exciting as 1701. Sorry classmates, but in a sick way, I like that the exams are not just memorizing old problems.

Daschbach really knows the material. She lectures way fast and they can be tough to follow live. Spend the time to watch the lecture videos. Exams are hard as &*^^ but the grade lines are generous. Overall, quality person and professor and a very good class.

Professor Daschbach is an AMAZING professor, so enthusiastic and great lecturer.  However, her class is way too hard, significantly harder than Gen Chem at other schools. The exams are way too hard and you can study so much, go to office hours, and do everything right, and still do poorly on the exams because of the absolute curveball questions.

one of the best professors i've ever had. although the material is extremely difficult and different from high school chem classes, she does a great job at getting people to understand conceptually (also through office hours). her lectures are so engaging too- i love her and wish she taught more

Daschbach is known as one of the best lecturers at WashU; she paces lectures well, explains tough concepts well, and is very enthusiastic. Exams are tough, but she provides lots of extra support and practice. Tough class, but very rewarding and very good teaching and learning support. This made me more interested in taking more chemistry classes.
for such a large lecture, she keeps me interested throughout. definitely a hard class but she breaks things down well. great great professor
She is a great professor and her lectures are amazing.  She explains things very well.  Be prepared for a difficult class with a lot of hours and extra work that needs to be put in to do well.
Tests she created were very nit-picky with taking off points, placing an emphasis on optimizing procedures rather than depth of understanding. good lecturer and explanations, a little loud.

Amazing lecturer, she truly cares about all her students. Keeps millennial humor in the class to make sure everyone is engaged, which was a plus. If you study, it is possible to do well in the class, but note the exams are quite difficult and the final is no easier.
Daschbach is the best! Su8per difficult material but she explains it as well as it could be. Be ready to work hard in 1701, PLTL is a must, but Daschbach is so funny and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Funny, knowledgeable, and kind professor, not much more you could ask for. The class itself is a bit test heavy, but I think it helps you stay on track. I didn't think the content was too hard but even if you do the cutoffs are super generous (you basically need 80% on tests and quizzes).
She is the best!!! Exams not really that hard so long as you do the practice problems and pltl carefully.

Professor Daschbach is an amazing professor, despite Gen Chem having some content that may be difficult for some students. However, she does a great job of presenting the material and is always available for help sessions and advice.

Best lecturer I have this year. An incredibly smart, talented, and kind professor. She REALLY knows her stuff, and is very enthusiastic in her lessons (Harry Potter, iykyk). Highly recommend. With this course, you need to put in work, but if you do put in work you can learn a great deal. So glad to have had Daschbach.
Phenomenal. Made difficult concepts easy to grasp. Insane tests though with tight timing.
Absolutely adore her. Her lectures are so interesting and it genuinely seems like she loves to teach. So lucky to have her!

She's so incredible. She's so energetic and her passion for the subject is truly infectious. She's so easy to approach and genuinely cares for each student. Don't get me wrong, the class is difficult, but she makes it so worth it. Highly highly highly recommend

Truly an incredible professor who cares about students. Her lectures are unbeatable. They are entertaining but she also has a clear commitment to making sense, which not many chem professors do. Started in Mabbs but learned SO much more going to Daschbach. She is so helpful, kind, and encouraging in a tough subject. Truly one of the best at Washu.

Her genuine excitement and enthusiasm for the subject of chemistry was infectious. It was hard to not get embarrassingly invested in the “story of the electron,” and there was never a dull moment in class (an outstanding achievement given the subject matter). Low amount of homework, but difficult exam. The best intro to Chem I could've asked for.
This class is so hard but Daschbach is such a good teacher.  Her lectures are so good and she is so helpful in office hours.

She is really such an amazing person and really caring about every student that takes the class. The subject material can be difficult if you get behind or maybe skip a few lectures, but it is possible to catch up. I'd recommend going to every lecture (attendance is marked and will go towards your grade) and doing all the optional homework
Amazing. That's all I gotta say.

Truly the best and clearest lectures I've ever witnessed. So engaging and concise. She got a standing ovation at the end of the semester for no other reason than she is just *that* good. One of the best professors ever, too bad I hate chem because I genuinely found this course so interesting and rewarding. I regret not attending more help sessions!

Professor Daschbach puts a lot of effort and thought into lectures, teaching directly to what you need to know for exams. She cares a lot about making the material accessible and answering questions whenever she can. Super enthusiastic and amazing lecturer.
she is incredible. switching my major to chemistry

Professor Daschbach had the best lectures. She was very clear and has a way of explaining things in a manner that is incredibly comprehensible. Additonally her office hours are incredibly helpful. Great teacher and a great class even though the class was very rigorous it was incredibly fulfilling.

Amazing professor and mentor. I learned how to learn and study from her. If you are struggling, talk to her about how to study better and those skills will help you all of college. Go to her weekly help sessions.

Amazing for grabbing your attention during lectures, and overall a wonderful, dedicated, and inspiring person. Class overall was tough - do the non-graded homework sets and PLTLs, they will save your life.
Dr. Daschbach is the best lecturer I've ever had. She understands the material so well and just presents everything perfectly.
She's really nice and has great lectures. even though chem111 is pretty tough, she explains things really well

You do not realize how good Loombach is until you take other courses. The team is incredible and passionate. They just know how to teach. They have remained my biggest mentors at WU. I will miss them.

Professor Daschbach is the best at what she does. I have never met someone so organized and capable of explaining concepts. Anyone will tell you she is the glue of Chem 111-112 and the person who makes Gen Chem the best intro sequence at Washu by far.
Best professor I've ever had!! Every lecture was so clear and well thought out. Class material is difficult... but if you attend lecture and work hard, you will get the grade you want!
The goat
She is amazing

LOVE Daschbach's teaching. I prefer her more than Loomis because she gives better foundational explanations imo. Really well structured class but NEED to study for tests (they are very hard). Engaging lectures that use PollEverywhere to track attendance. Hard class, but great experience with a lot of help options.

Prof Daschbach is an incredible lecturer! You can tell that the presented material is thoughtfully curated and she truly loves chemistry. The exams are hard and the time limits make things stressful, but if you're willing to put in the time to study you'll get the grade you want. Although the course is tough, I feel like I've grown so much from it!

I love professor Dashcbach so much, if you have any interest in chemistry or science you must take a class with her. She cares about her students and wants them to learn the material, and even though the class is very tough, her positive attitude gets you through it.

Loomis + Daschbach = Best class ever!! They will push you, but you will learn. D is great w/ notes and details. L is great w/ explaining concepts and real life connections. If they ever teach together again, you must take this class.
An amazing professor that helps students understand challenging concepts. The class is structured for students to be successful.
Her Chem 111 class is no joke as far as difficulty goes, but she really does try to make it as simple and understandable as possible. Very helpful outside of class too. 100% would take her again!

While the tests are the hardest thing I have ever done, Professor Daschbach is incredible. She is very engaging, funny, and makes the material as understandable as possible. She turned a difficult subject into a puzzle to be solved and inspired me and my friends to work hard. The content is hard, but studying and going to office hours/PLTL helps.
very solid teacher, clear lecturing, straight forward and stays on topic.
Absolute legend!
She clearly loved chemistry so much and made the whole class love it as a result. I was so glad I took this class with her.

One of the nicest and most supportive professors at washu. I love that she loves chemistry and helping students to love chemistry. Lectures were really well organized and given. Chem 111A was a tough class, but both Dashbach and Loomis were really accessible and enthusiastically willing and able to help.

Professor Daschbach is genuinely one of the best professors at WashU. She takes extremely difficult material and makes it accessible to all students. The class is very hard, but she teaches students how to develop the work ethic to succeed in this class and others. She will always meet with students outside of class and is a very caring person!

The class is tough, but the professor is amazing. If you really care about achieving a good grade there are more than enough materials to do so. It is obvious Daschbach really cares about her students.

i love her. so enthusiastic and happy to help students. you can tell she genuinely loves what she teaches and wants students to succeed (as long as they put in the effort!). genchem is difficult, but it's very doable if you use your resources. she's always happy to stay after class/stay on zoom to answer everyone's questions. daschbach i <3 you
Amazing lecturer, her drawings/diagrams are the best by far. Very accessible outside of class, but the class is hard so be ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Chem 111 with Daschbach and Loomis is such a well-run class. The lectures are incredible, and the tests really push your understanding of the content to the limits. Daschbach is very kind, explains things very well, and is accessible "backstage" after class if you have the time. All around a top-tier professor.

Dr. Daschbach is the best professor I've ever met in WashU. She's an amazing lecturer explaining chemical concepts in a straightforward manner and caring her students. Importantly, she encourages students to collaborate with each other instead of competing negatively. You would enjoy the exploration in chemistry after taking this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Daschbach is a queen. She is magnetic and passionate. Incredibly hard class, but teaching caliber is top tier. Plenty of opportunities to practice difficult material. Participation questions have to be done in class, so go to lecture. Best way to learn. Get ready to hate your life frequently, but be really proud of yourself when you're done.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dashy is ok, and she has been teaching this course forever. Overall, an ok class and semester. I did find it annoying how she constantly tried to convince us the material was amazing. We did not come to Wash U for a cheerleader. Please just teach. Also, tone the exams down a bit. They don't have to be that hard.
I did not love professor Daschbach's teaching style. PLTL was generally unhelpful for me.

Important to note that Chem 111A is very difficult, especially coming from HS chem. However, Dr. Daschbach is a wonderful instructor. Lectures are interesting, office hours and review sessions are frequent and helpful. You can tell she really loves the content. One con-$95 textbook that was never used. Overall great instructor tho.
Loved Professor Daschbach, she was so passionate about teaching and so excited every day to talk with students, the class was very difficult though, be ready

she is one of the best professors I've ever had. always extremely excited to talk about chemistry in class and out of class. always accessible and super flexible. the gen chem class in general is kinda difficult, but she tries to make it really simple and clear. she's literally teaching quantum mechanics like its 1+1

Makes a story out of the material, time passes quickly in class, lectures become very interesting. Extremely good at teaching and a god at orgo. Knows the material extremely well and can answer any question .
Very difficult class but Dashbach is great! Funny, engaging, and easy to listen to and take notes from.
There is nothing bad here.
Dr. Daschbach has been the best professor I've ever had. She is amazing at teaching really tough material, and she always makes sure all her students feel comfortable and included.
Daschbach was a good lecturer and good at answering questions!! She explains concepts very well and clearly understands how to teach. Would take her again if she taught higher-level courses!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Daschbach is an amazing professor. She genuinely cares about her students and thoroughly explains materials so that the students all understand it. She is super approachable and works really hard to help students outside of class. I would definitely take a class of hers again.
Way too optimistic, but overall a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Daschbach clearly explains the material necessary for the quizzes and exams. She encourages students to use the resources like PLTL, recitations, etc. and it has helped me be successful in the class.

Dr. Daschbach is a master of Chemistry, and can explain anything from Quantum to Organic. I bet during normal semesters, she is even more of a rock star. Unfortunately, she seemed tired and exhausted much of the semester. I think this wore on her patience a bit for some of the students. Overall, good person and challenging course.

Daschbach is simply amazing. Great engaging lecturer and explains material very well while being both thorough and efficient. The class is hard but Daschbach is really helpful with study tips and with her help sessions. She really cares about students and passionate about the class.
Professor Daschbach was great and genuinely cared about her students. She was a fantastic lecturer and explained all the material very well.

Just finished the best class I probably will ever take. Daschbach (and Loomis) made 111 a great learning experience, even with Covid and Zoom. I just wish we could have done the course in person. Incredible dedication to teaching and the students. Great team.

Simply an incredible class. The material is taught in a way that is interesting and straightforward. Daschbach makes complex ideas seem simple and easy to learn. The material is still difficult, so study your lecture notes. The most amazing professor.

Dr. Daschbach is one of the best lecturers you will find at WashU. She explains complex theories in a style that makes the material easier to process. If you attend lecture and review your notes, you can do very well in this class. Problem sets and PLTL packets are also very useful.

Daschbach is great and incredibly encouraging. However, based on all of the reviews below, you may think that everyone gets an A, which is really false. Most people get Bs, so be ready to put in the work.

I love Professor Daschbach! She explains things in a clear and organized way. Also, the lecture notes that she writes on the board are very useful for exam preparation. There are a lot of available resources like help session, PLTL, outside of the classroom. The exams are a lot harder than the homework and lecture materials, but it's expected.
Such a great teacher really knows how to keep students engaged
Daschbach was my favorite professor first semester. She keeps everyone super engaged and the material interesting and easy to understand

She is the best professor ever! Super caring, knowledgeable, and simply extraordinary at teaching. She makes learning the infamously difficult WashU Gen Chem rather easy and interesting. And - she is an awesome life coach who inserts life wisdom sporadically in her lecture slides. Make sure to go to class - watching videos won't provide much fun!

She's very passionate and knowledgeable about chemistry. There are tons of resources outside of class that can help you solidify your understanding. It's fast-paced and challenging, but the grade cutoffs are very generous. The main issue I have is that grading criteria for +/- on letter grades are NOT disclosed ever, which I find unsettling.

Daschbach is an incredible teacher (the best Ive had so far at WashU)! She explains difficult concepts very well, and her enthusiasm makes you excited to learn chemistry. If youre going to take Chem 111, do it with Daschbach. Go to lecture and take good notes, and youll do more than fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Would take again

reviews.comment: I don't care when your other classes are, if you can, TAKE DASCHBACH'S SECTION. She goes out of her way to make the notes organized and visually clear, and she was the first instructor I've had who said "you have to understand the concepts" and actually stood by it. Doesn't mean it's an easy class, but you'll learn and grow a lot from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Daschbach is an incredible lecturer and human being. Gen Chem at WashU has such a scary reputation, and she's the perfect person for the job. She's super approachable, and explains really difficult concepts in a clear, and very exciting, manner. DO NOT READ THE BOOK. Lecture is your main source of material 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Daschbach is solid, and he tries very hard to keep the students excited. I felt sorry for her sometimes when she was trying to get us jazzed up about orbitals and "quantum weirdness". Overall, it was a hard, but good class. I think you will learn from any of the instructors they put in there.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Daschbach is simply the best. Take her Chem 111 section if you are taking the course. She makes the material easy to understand and fun to explore. Exams are tough, sure, but that's to be expected - it's chemistry. She will be clear to emphasize important things in lecture. Show up to class, take GOOD NOTES, and you'll do great.
Professor Daschbach  made learning chemistry enjoyable.  She made difficult material more interesting and could always crack a joke to lighten the mood.

Daschbach is by far the best chem professor Washu has to offer. She cares about the content and my test grade raised 40 points when I switched to her lectures. She's the reason I pulled an A in the class.

She is really passionate about Chemistry and really tries to explain stuff well. However, sometimes she does not really explain the main points and instead focuses on irrelevant details, which can be misleading when studying for exams. the exams are a lot harder than the material presented. She is an okay professor but I have had better
DaschBAE is the best Chem teacher of Wash U. You have to listen to lecture and study hard, but you can succeed!!

Professor Daschbach is hands down the best Professor I have ever had. She was an amazing introduction to college, and made me excited to learn chemistry. You can tell that she loves teaching and is passionate about the material and wants to see students success. She is funny enough to be enjoyable, but serious enough to teach the material well.

His class is overrated. Not that easy of a class as people make it seem. Your grade is only based on three challenging tests. Didn't know how to study for the test, as "anything said in lecture was fair game". Lectures are boring, makes it up with some humor. Took Fall 2025.

definitely very entertaining for the content. i did not enjoy the content very much as it felt repetitive and very memorization based. the grades are basically based on exams only. professor strait however was very passionate, caring, and told funny stories, i just wish the content was more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The goat. I'm not studying anthro but loved this class. Take it!
Do not miss lecture!! 90% of grade is tests, get ready to study.
I mean, if you want to talk about legendary professors, David might be the GOAT. He's witty, funny, and he teaches with passion. He's the type of guy you'd ask to be your best man at your wedding.
I don't know how he made a class about primates so engaging

I highly recommend taking this class if you are a first-year student who is vaguely interested in anthropology, evolution, or human anatomy. Prof. Strait covers a large volume of information in one semester, and it was an accessible yet challenging class that is definitely memorization-heavy. Attending/viewing lectures is essential for success.

Dr. Straight is an amazing lecturer. Even though attendance wasn't mandatory and recordings of the lectures were posted to Canvas, I still enjoyed attending the lectures in person because of how funny/entertaining he is. This course requires a LOT of memorization to do well on the exams (which make up 90% of your grade).

RUN NOW WHILE YOU HAVE THE CHANCE!!! if you'd like to stay up late hours of the night cramming 40 hours of content, just to be asked how many neanderthal toenail clipping were found neander valley 150,000 years ago on an exam worth 40 percent of your grade this class is for you! if you value your time, sanity, and sleep don't take this class.

Intro to Human Ev. is fun and engaging with hilarious Dr. Strait, but it's tough. You must learn tons of primates and anatomy. No homework, optional readings, and 3 fair but intense exams. Final is on the last day. Take laptop notes. Look at past Quizlets and StudCo before adding to your schedule. Prof. claims it's not memorization, but it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher, but the amount of material tested for on the exams are absurd. Also, the TAs are useless.

I loved this class! Dr. Strait makes it so engaging, both in his explanation of the course content and the anecdotes that he tells about his life. There is a lot of material, but if you don't procrastinate your studying, you can do very well on his exams. If you have the chance to take this course, I would absolutely recommend it!

This class is on the tougher side because of how much content is covered; however, Prof. Strait's lectures make it an enjoyable experience. He shared many stories to make the lectures more interesting, and he did a great job covering all the content. I learned a lot and would recommend taking this with Prof. Strait if you have the time to study.

Anatomy is a ton of memorization to begin with and the lectures were packed with material. However, he is very passionate about the material, kind, funny, and understanding. I loved taking the course!

Professor Strait is incredibly passionate and entertaining in class. The grades are based on 3 exams that are all very memorization based, so make sure to know literally everything he says in class and puts on the slides.

Dr. Strait is so funny, it is obvious how deeply he cares for both his students and subject matter. He translated topics into relatable stories and incorporated humor in his lectures. There is no homework, just test-based. He was accommodating to me when I had a traumatic injury and worked to come up with a new grading scale to adjust accordingly.
Strait is awesome and so is this class. The most caring and funny professor you'll have at WashU. Graded on 3 big tests, so just take good notes cause his slides are mostly pics.

Super knowledgeable, interesting lectures and he includes many stories (makes it more entertaining and can help drive the point home). Anatomy is a tough class, there's a LOT of content but he's an AMAZING professor! You will have to study a lot (so i don't recommend taking it unless u need it), but his exams are very fair (if you've studied).

Probably one of my favorite professors at WashU so far! Lectures are very entertaining and make sense. He gives weekly readings, but they are not required, just supplementary. Class is graded mostly on three exams that are very memorization-heavy (it's a lot), so as long as you prepare well for those, you'll be fine.

Prof Strait is generally an enthusiastic and chill guy! The first two midterms and labs were fine. However the final was really hard and def required detailed memorization! A lot of memorization so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing guy who does his best to make learning interesting and enjoyable. Lectures can often go into detail far beyond what's covered in the exam, though. Memorization heavy for sure

STRAIT IS THE BEST! He is so knowledgeable about what he teaches. The lecture are very engaging and interesting (even if you aren't anthro major). Only assigns optional reading homework. Everything about class is great except for the fact that everything is graded by 3 MC exams, don't underestimate difficulty, lost of memorization and details.

Not much work other than studying for the exams. Labs are simple. Prof. Strait plays music before class and tells stories/jokes during lectures! His office hours are the best time to contact him and it is worth it--he is very kind and patient
Rants during lectures. Moves too quickly. Assigns additional lectures to watch before exams since he doesn't plan well enough to get through the necessary material before an exam.

Lectures are relatively enjoyable, but they can also be found online from when it was still online class. Professor Strait is a very knowledgeable and qualified lecturer, and can make lectures funny and interesting. Graded mostly by just 3 tests. The final unit is the most difficult and is weighted the most, but little time is spent on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Strait is a true gem. He's a sweetheart and clearly loves his job. Always comes into class with a smile on his face ready to blast his favorite delta blues songs at deafening volumes. Lectures are straightforward and he does post the slides on canvas which is helpful.

Dr Strait is incredible; his class was by far my favourite this year and potentially of my time at WashU. His lectures were engaging and his ability to work humour and sincerity into his lectures made coming to lecture the highlight of my day. The only downside was that we were graded mainly on three exams, two of which were difficult to study for.
He's aight
I absolutely love Dr. Strait. He is really funny and interesting. The class is fascinating.

Dr. Strait is a great lecturer who clearly cares about his students. He tries to keep his lectures entertaining by infusing them with humor and is very inspiring to listen to. He knows exactly what to say and when to say it to make a big impact on his students; his lectures on climate change were very moving. Take a class with him if you can.

An absolute gem!! One of the best professors at WashU. He plays music at the beginning of every class and tells stories and cracks jokes throughout his lectures to keep people engaged. Professor Strait is a really entertaining and sweet professor who cares about his students and the topics he teaches a lot.
its literally impossible to hate this man

I thought Anatomy was quite difficult this semester, as exams were moved back in person and closed note (exams are 90% of your grade). Prof. Strait is an ANGEL though, as he made our final online, open-note, and unlimited time at the last minute (literally in the exam room before the final). He's a great prof, just be prepared to memorize a TON.

Dr. Strait is an incredibly thoughtful, engaging professor whose love for what he teaches is contagious. Human ev is SO interesting (made me want to switch majors). He says it's not memorization heavy but sometimes you just have to sit down and grind flashcards. It becomes a lot easier if you find trends and understand the logic behind them.
Very funny and engaging lectures. Only had 3 labs and 3 tests that made up the grade. If you memorize the lectures, the tests are easy (also didn't need the textbook but he said to get it).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Human evolution was the only biology/anthropology class I've taken at WashU. Even in my senior year, Dr. Strait had me interested in the material and the class. He is a phenomenal person, accomplished but humble and kind. He is an excellent, patient professor, and goes out of his way to try and make class interesting and fun. 10/10

Great professor and a super loveable guy that makes anthropology very interesting with his use of videos but he can be a bit fast when explaining things and powerpoints are more so visual than summarizers of content. Grades in this class consist of 3 chunkey tests and 3 labs, if you suck at tests (me) make sure you study and take really good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor Strait's lectures on Human Evolution are entertaining. He is occasionally humorous and tells personal stories. He conveys passion for the material.

There is no homework in the class; there are a few multiple choice exams.

I love Dr.Strait, he is a fantastic professor and he clearly is very passionate about both teaching and the subject he teaches. One of my favorite profs at WashU and I certainly won't forget him and my experience in his class for a long time.
was unclear on directions to print skeleton diagram. had to manually draw the diagram.

Dr. Strait is the best professor I've had at WashU so far! Not only are his lectures interesting and funny, but he truly cares about his students and it shows. He is an incredible man and I am so sad that I'm done taking HumEv. If you show up to class and take good notes, you're golden.

One of the most engaging lectures I've ever had! I also loved how he plays music before every lecture to help set the mood, and also just for the sake of it. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and even said at the beginning of the semester that he doesn't care if all of his students get A's.

Dr. Strait is a funny professor who gives solid lectures and is generally accommodating. While Covid is still a problem, this class is a guaranteed A. Open note, take-home exams are only grades, besides extra credit.

Best professor. Very engaging lectures that were recorded if you had to miss them. Offered extra credit with 10-minute "labs" where you examined actual human skulls and other fossils brought from the Med School campus. Exams all multiple choice 40 questions with 50 minute time limit. Easy clear questions, no surprises. Saw many fun videos in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Strait is a hilarious and caring professor who has electric and dynamic lectures. The best class I've ever taken - and it's very easy as well.

I took Prof. Strait's class just as a science credit for an engineering major, but it was one of my most interesting classes. The classes were all video lectures given the time we were in, but they were unique and easy to watch/complete. He made jokes often and offered music just because. Grades were also easy MC quizzes. Textbook use was optional
My favorite professor at WashU so far! He's very engaging and really cares about what he teaches. It really shows in class (or on video for my case).

He is one of the most caring professor I have encountered at WashU. The content of this class is very fun if you enjoy anatomy and I can feel that he cares about his student even though this is a fully asynchronous and online class.
The literal best professor at Washington U. Very engaging, very clear guidelines for assessments.

Pros: a fantastic introduction course to paleoanthropology, because the professor breaks down concepts so that even those without prior knowledge of paleoanthropology can easily understand course content  lecture content balances information with fun facts, keeping you interested  very empathetic professor
he is probably the most engaging and fair professor i have had at wash u so far and i am a senior. would highly recommend.
he's actually incredible. happy, genuine professor. very knowledgable. love his course so far.

His anatomy and development class is hard, absolutely. BUT he's probably my favorite prof that I've had at Wash U. He's funny, engaging, and clearly passionate about what he does. Material and tests are hard, but he makes class fun and worth it. Also, if you're pre-med, it's helpful content for the MCAT.

I took Human Evolution with him during my freshman first semester and he was literally my best teacher. He is so kind and funny and makes the learning experience very personal and easy. By far one of my best teachers so far and I would 100% take his class again.
Very nice professor who is willing to help. Your ability to succeed in human evolution is dependent on how well you memorize. This class is almost entirely memorization, so get ready for this
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Strait is by far one of the best professors I've had at WashU. I never found myself counting the minutes until the end of his lectures but was instead immersed completely in what he was telling us. It's obvious that he really cares about what he teaches and about his students as well
Dr. Strait is so sweet and understanding and if you are having trouble with anything, he is very accessible and will work with you to make sure you succeed in his classes

an amazing guy and an amazing professor. very passionate about what he is interested in and that is clear in his lectures. although the content is difficult and not very interesting, he keeps the class energized with his jokes. if you want a good grade, do not skip class because certain slides are not uploaded. he plays fun music before class too!

Great professor, actually cares about you, willing to accomodate, super chill. The tests aren't easy unless you know the material well, so get ready to memorize. But, this has been my favorite class at WashU so far, both because of the material and the professor.

Dr. Strait is so great! He's so funny and such a great teacher. His work is very straightforward and if you study, you will likely do well (in this class there was quite a bit of memorization). My friends and I all found his class really engaging and interesting. Ten out of ten!

Professor Strait doesn't believe in textbooks, so there is no required reading except for the short articles that he posts online every other day. Lectures and slides are right to the point, and it is somewhat easy to predict what will be on exams. Exams are not super easy but if you studied then you can maybe figure them out. Still a great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: LOVED professor Dan-Cohen's. Awesome lecturer and even better person. Class itself was very easy and the only things that were graded were the 4 noncumulative online midterms throughout the semester. Would recommend this course to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She was the worst at responding to emails.

Professor Talia is a very caring professor, very accessible outside classroom, offers coffee chat hours just for random questions. However, the course content is a lot. As a non-anthro major, I found the pace of the course to be extremely fast. I once took 12 pages of notes for a single lecture. It's not hard to get an A. But it isn't that chill.

Professor Cohen is so nice and cares about her students personally and academically. The class is an easy A if you go to most of the classes. If you don't go to class, you could still get an A- if you're locked for exams. All exams are online and open note so it's pretty easy if you use the slides and go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Talia is a great professor and her class was very easy. However, some of her guest lecturers insulted conservatives and it was clear that the class had a bias. Thankfully, the tests are objective and test you objectively on the course content from the unit based on her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She truly cares so much. People don't go to class.
online exams
Great intro anthro class. Easy to manage exams and not too hard. Exams match class lectures

Only graded on 3 online exams. This year you could drop 1, except the final. 
She's an excellent lecturer, but they took me a while to get used to. She speaks incredibly fast so there is no way to take notes from the slides and pay attention to what she's saying. But she does explain the concepts amazingly and really knows what she's talking about.

The only grades are the 3 online exams (drop worst), and online final exam. All multiple choice. The content is fairly interesting, but you could literally never showup and still do good on the exams. Requires maybe 10 hours of your time outside of class.

Overall a pretty easy class but still lots of interesting course content in my opinion. Dan-Cohen also brought in a few guest lecturers that I really enjoyed listening to. She also really cares about her students. Content from readings/homework was interesting and appears on quizzes. Take-home quizzes are pretty straightforward.

Prof. Dan-Cohen did a great job providing clear, helpful and relevant information that consistently aligned w/ the exam questions.  The class was pretty interesting, too; I didn't even really know what anthro was to this, now I'm planning on taking 2 anthro courses next semester.  It was graded by 4 exams (lowest is dropped), which imo is good.

Dr. Dan-Cohen has taken past criticism (like her lecture speed) into account and now makes an active effort to check in with her students every lecture to check her pace. She genuinely is so excited about anthropology and wants her students to succeed. I would totally take another class with her!

Dan-Cohen's the best lecturer I've had at WashU--she's very engaging, and the course content is super interesting. You get a nice overview of the entire field of cultural Anthropology. She loves talking to students about course material. 160B is an easy A, but I suggest doing the readings and attending lecture when you can, they're fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dan-Cohen is a really engaging lecturer and her class is super interesting. Intro to Cultural Anthro is graded super easily based off 4 open-note quizzes. Readings are interesting and deal with a lot of different topics. Class was definitely on the easier end but still engaging and I thought I got a lot out of it!

Prof Dan-Cohen has been great. Her lectures are energetic, and lively. I took this as a humanities requirement but it has probably been my most interesting class this year!
Class is graded based completely on 4 "quizzes" with one dropped. these are online and open note/all resources available. Her class is fairly easy, and is shes a great lecturer!

Dan-Cohen is pretty decent but nothing great. She gives standard lectures with a lot of reading off her slides and it gets kind of monotonous. Grades are only comprised of midterms. She does post lecture recordings though, which is helpful for reviewing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures were great; she got better at pacing as the semester progressed, and she was very engaging and easy to listen to. I could tell she really cared about us learning the material and enjoying the class.
