Although the structure of the class itself is flawed (big lecture, not geared for discussions), it was a pleasure to have her teach us.
Engaging and pointed discussions that managed to involve everyone. Truly a pleasure to take this class.

Durai was very nice and loved to talk to him, but the lectures were slow and dragged. The class is pretty boring to begin with. The class was known to be super easy in previous years. Two tests, 1st one was extremely easy, 2nd one was impossible, ruining everyone's grades. Was told they increased the difficulty bc they realized it was too easy.

Professor Sundaramoorthi is by far one of the most caring and kind professors at WashU. He is always willing to help students if they ask for it, and he is a hilarious person. Every exam (including the final exam) is extremely similar to the past exams. As long as you actually practice the exams, you will be more than ok in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Great teacher

Durai is one of the best professors I've had at WashU. In a statistics class, it's easy for a professor to just teach the problems, but he takes time to explain the concepts behind them engagingly. He is also always willing to chat to discuss position in the class, and makes strong efforts to be equitable across students. Super caring, 10/10.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS. ABSOLUTELY UNFAIR FINAL EXAM. WORST CLASS EVER

reviews.comment: Strong lecturer, even though he could be somewhat difficult to understand from time to time. Always made the content entertaining and was easy to talk to.

reviews.comment: Super great professor, he gives dad energy in the best way and is intentionally and unintentionally funny. Exams are usually the same as past practice exams, the questions are often repeated. Lectures are easy to follow and the homework assignments are pretty easy as well. Has occasional pop quizzes that are mostly for attendance purposes.

Lectures were slightly repetitive but clear. Exams are identical to practice exams and homework. Super nice guy who wants his students to succeed. Gives out pop quizzes but usually gives answers for students who are present. If you took AP Stats or just do the homework, you should not have much trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His exams are not hard, but his lectures are long. I took AP Stats and this class is way easier, but his explanations are confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was consistently impressed by his ability to break down complex concepts into easily understandable components. His teaching style is engaging and methodical, ensuring that students of all backgrounds can grasp even the most challenging material.
Great professor, highly recommend.
Professor Durai's class was a transformative experience. His unique teaching style fostered a dynamic atmosphere that sparked my intellectual curiosity and inspired me to think more critically.

Professor Durai's class was truly inspirational. He presents complex concepts in a way that is both accessible and engaging, making every lesson valuable. It was an enriching experience, and I am grateful for the opportunity to learn from him.

Professor Durai is an exceptionally caring and supportive professor. He consistently goes above and beyond to help students succeed, offering guidance and encouragement at every step. His approachability and dedication make him stand out as one of the most helpful professors I have had the pleasure of learning from.

1.easy to follow. 2. core concepts are clearly explained. 3. easy to get an A grade. 4. professor is so supportive
This course is suitable for business students.

Great Professor! He supported a lot in understanding basic concepts and replied to questions really fast. He also provided me with lots of supportive career advice which really helped shape my future career.
Sad to see he got hate reviews because of students who just didn't want to learn and expected good grades.

1.He clearly says that while he teaches both Machine Learning concepts and R practice, only concepts are included in exams.
2.The course can be challenging for those study at the last moment. My way to get an A is by answering Qs in the course to ensure I don't misunderstand the concept, and he always provide great feedback even if I was wrong.

reviews.comment: Don't take his class, such a nightmare.

reviews.comment: The video posted basically taught nothing and is hard to understand, and lab session in person also taught nothing. What only matters is the attendance. The most ridiculous part is that the closed-book final exam counts for 50% and coding is not on the test, only conceptual and calculations were in the exam. No curve on the exam. Avoid his lessons!
Very ridiculous class, R's in class but not on the test. 50% of the test and no curve. please avoid if you can.

Final exam weights 50% of your total grade, he taught coding during class and the exam tests your conceptual knowledge and calculation. Those lecture videos he posted each module has nothing to do with the exam. I would rate less than 1 if I can!!
Amazing professor. Great patience.

What a gem. Professor Durai brings in real world problems. He focuses on breadth rather than depth, and you learn R coding rather well. The expectations are clearly laid out from day one and you can watch the lectures at your own pace. The final project is challenging but is one of my main talking points in data science interviews. Good TA support.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Durai is an excellent teacher I have seen in WashU. He is patient enough to answer all of your questions. The structure of content in his lecture is really clear,making it easy for me to review whenever I forget something. Therefore, I highly recommend this professor and this course.

He does not know what he is talking abt. expect u to know everything by yourself. he just put up the code and wont tell you what it does and what it means to the whole thing. worse data teacher ever met
Durai's notes are very easy to follow. His tests essentially mirror the previous tests that he posts on Blackboard.

Notes are clear but material is boring. For quizzes/tests you can no longer use cheat sheets. He reproduced past exams and quizzes for future ones and expects memorization. Just talks at students for 1.5 hour lectures and overall disappointed. I don't look forward to his class. 25/46 students usually go.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor, very clear lectures and small amount of homework is easy and prepares you well for the tests. Additionally, he uploads all his past exams which are essentially the same as new exams so tests are easy if you study these. You don't have to go to class - he uploads videos online but there are pop quizzes based on attendance basically.
Just show up to class, pay attention, receive A
Durai hooks you up. Gives you videos of him doing lectures and how to do stuff in excel. He also explains things clearly and actually cares if you know the stuff.

Durai is a truly amazing professor. You can tell he puts a lot of time into creating helpful notes, loves the material and is very clear in explaining it. Also extremely available outside of the classroom! However, beware on falling behind. The class is very easy if you do a little bit every week, but I feel some students got overconfident
Great professor! He tests directly from the notes and is very clear on what he wants. He is very helpful and nice!

NOT open book nor open note.  Dr. Durai has a generous cheat sheet policy though.  Great organized notes, very easy to follow.  So smart, and a great teacher!  He gets a lot of test/quiz questions from the book.  Really concerned about students and their feedback.

Notes are very clear and straightforward.  Material is a bit boring but he does what he can.  The quizzes/tests you get cheat sheets, not open book nor open note.  He loves students' feedback and actually does adjust his course in response to it.  I really liked him and thought he was a great teacher compared to Prof Snir.
Extremely dull and boring. However, if you put in the effort in, then it is a very easy class. To be fair, Durai does care about the students and loves to hear feedback.
Dr. Durai does a great job of teaching this intro stats course. His notes are very clear and he really tests from the notes. Never used the book at all.

This class is very easy since all the exams are open note and open book. His notes are summaries of the chapters in the book and are extremely helpful. I am keeping them to use for my other stats classes. Durai is also very easy to reach and forgiving about late homework. Take this class!

The notes are given to us with blank spots to fill in during lecture.  The homework is a sort of WebWork format. The exams are open note, open book, and open computer. In short, this the easiest class I've taken in the business school. Take it before he gets more difficult!

Subpar instruction, an angry and snarky vibe from the instructor. I am going to retake the class, which feels like a waste of a credit. Hoping to learn something with a different professor. Strongly recommend against taking any class with this guy.

Progressively got more irritable as the semester went on. Extremely harsh essay grader (Class average was a 70%). Lectures/Rambles for like 45 minutes every class and takes meticulous attendance/participation scores. Not sure how I got the grade I did, but he probably had to round up because everyone was flunking if not.

reviews.comment: The previous reviews are correct that this guy has fragile ego and you better always stay with his opinion. Office hours are not helpful. His opinion on your work is inconsistent. Stay away from this guy if you still want a happy first year at washu, please.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Condesending, always in a bad mood. Every class is a presentation that he says in monotone. For class discussions, he is not open to contradicting opinions. With essays, he's always throwing out academic violation accusations. If you dont hate yourself, try to get a different teacher.
Fragile ego. Grades based off how easily you submit to his opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: It was hard to know what Dr. Iler wanted out of you, grading felt very inconsistent and office hours were not helpful because he'd tell you one thing and then not stay consistent. Also, it did not feel like feedback was constructive because even if you edited it accordingly, it wouldn't change the end result.

Earned around an A− on each essay. Tips: Iler prioritizes thesis specificity & counterarguments. He was very chill with me, but not with everyone—some peers faced academic integrity accusations and rough grading (60s/70s for essays). Honestly not sure how I made it through unscathed, make an effort to get on his good side
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's so cool and chill. it was a blast having him. just put some effort, be honest in your work, and it'll pay off
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Iler made college writing very interesting! I enjoyed his lectures and learned a lot. He is very accommodating when scheduling times to meet with him outside of class. Honestly, just don't use AI, and he will respect you for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Whatever kindness he once had must've evaporated over summer. You could genuinely attend every office hour knowing that he will tell you your work is amazing, then fail you. You will leave this course feeling hopeless and disillusioned. I genuinely pity anyone taking him next semester, his RateMyProfessor score does NOT match the reality. Good luck

Avoid Dr. Iler at all costs. Several of my friends in easier college writing classes have been able to cruise by, while Dr. Iler has much stricter policies and grading methods than any other College Writing professor. He is often condescending, and though he offers some help at office hours, it is often misleading, vague, and unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a fun and important class. The content was super engaging and made me think differently about conspiracy theories, how we process information, and talk about big issues. I learned a lot. The professor is kind, supportive, and really values what students have to say. Highly recommend.

I didn't expect to enjoy this class as much as I did, especially since it only meets once a week, but it quickly became one of my favorites. Iler is so nice, incredibly understanding, and always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Iler is awesome, my actual GOAT. I wouldn't say he's an "easy" A, but he's a very fair graders and care a lot about your effort, so he's quite literally an "A for effort" grader. Workload is pretty light, and he gives super clear feedback and instructions. Take him if you want to really improve your writing without sacrificing your GPA.

Dr. Iler isn't very warm or welcoming to students in general. He also makes you read your entire essay out loud in front of the class, which is not true of other college writing professors. In most college writing classes, you are guaranteed to get a good grade if you put in effort, Iler seems to be much less willing to give A's than most

I was not looking forward to taking this class because I needed to fulfill the writing requirement, but Dustin Iler made the class a lot better than I thought it would be. He brings a great energy to the class and is incredibly clear about the criteria on assignments. He is also incredibly open to help if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mandatory class, and the topic wasn't the most interesting. Go to office hours if you want to improve your writing/get a good grade.

I received an F and failed Technology and Selfhood, which was my fault. There were resources I could have utilized and help I could've looked for. However, Dr. Iler was always empathetic, tried his best to help me, and always offered help and time to work with me. Do yourself a favor and take your writing class with him. He does care.

Most of the works are completion grades, even essay drafts. He's so opened for feedbacks and ideas and encourage you to contribute to the class. He doesn't give a lot of homework compared to other College Writing class. Also allow you to resubmit if there is something wrong with your format, citation,... and still give full credit.

College Writing is a well-recognized grinding course at WashU, but taking the course with Dr. Iler would surely alleviate such pain to some degree. Everyone has to take CWP, so be nice to yourself and choose Dr. Iler as your instructor.
DUDE'S SO NICE JUST TAKE HIM
around 30% of the work is graded on completion. Needs to participate in class. Easy to reach out outside the classroom
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hes overall good. he grades pretty tough compared to other college writing professors but a better professor to relate to and become close with. I have largely no complaints other than the lack of rubrics for assignments and no clear guidelines for what is considered enough participation

This is my second course with Iler, I also had Tech and Self w/ him and knew I wanted him again. Argumentation was more than I ever expected - the course is open ended and I found myself writing about a range of topics and exploring new techniques. Iler pushes you to do your best and is very helpful on feedback. Facilitates such amazing discussions

Dr. Iler is one of my favorite professors at WashU. He really cares about his students and helped me become a much better writer. He's an honest grader but is helpful and if he sees improvement will give you good grades. Participation is important but he will not call you out. If you're taking college writing I highly highly recommend Dr. Iler!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Iler was an amazing professor who truly cares about what he is teaching. He is also very open to you coming up with your own topic - I ended up writing about memes for one paper and Minecraft for another. He wants to make the material engaging for everyone. Readings can be a bit long but all were interesting. He will help if you reach out

Such an amazing professor! He really helped me with my writing coming to WashU. There are a lot of readings but theyre interesting in my opinion. Very helpful at office hours & encouraging. He really listened to me during the lecture when we discussed readings, different from the large classes I was enrolled in. I wish every class was like this!!
Dr. Iler is great. Writing Technology is a really interesting class and his feedback on papers is very helpful. Revisions/drafts for papers are a good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dustin is a great dude. Really cares about the students and gives great feedback on papers.

So glad I met Dr. Iler. He made my summer amazing. I knew that he is a great person on the first day of class because he remembered everyone's name immediately and never forgot or called a wrong name. During lectures, he asks lots of thought-provoking questions, encourages discussions and provides insightful opinions. Love him a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome writing teacher; gives you the freedom you need to find your own writing voice while keeping the class structured enough to develop your skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Iler was the best English teachers I have ever had! Writing has always been a struggle for me and he made it so understandable and very helpful towards his students I could email him at anytime and get a respond great professor!

I love Dr. Iler! He is so sweet and helpful, I was dreading Writing 1 but he made that class my favorite my first semester. He managed to make the readings interesting, and he never forced participation but still got to know you well. An easy grader but also helped me improve my writing significantly, and he is hilarious. Take him if you can!

I came into college very intimidated by writing and dreaded taking writing 1, yet Dr. Iler made this class my favorite class my first semester freshman year. He makes a mandatory course fun, interesting, and actually taught me how to significantly improve my writing. Would love to take another course he teaches.
Good lecturer. Mostly busy work graded by TAs. Make sure to follow the rubrics and you should be fine.

Professor Dohrman was a decent professor, but the class was not my favorite. Her lectures were usually organized, but they could feel dry at times, and some material was harder to follow than it needed to be.
Passionate professor, repetitive class and pop quizzes are tough. Many busy work assignments all graded by TA's. 1 case compeition group project which is alot of work. Easy class though

So strict and if you don't follow exactly what she says you will get a bad grade. Super harsh on rules (and there are lots). Constantly trying to penalize students grades. Don't take this class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Dohrman. If you get to know her and share your story, she makes sure to remember it and invests a lot in her students. She is a great person to have in your network, and I really encourage speaking with her one-on-one if you can. She really is rooting for everyone as long as you are putting your best foot forward. Class is busy work.

Dohrman is really excited and cares about the career growth of her students. MGT201 is a lot of busy work, but it can be very helpful with the right attitude. Your experience could depend on whether you are interested in consulting or not, as lots of resources revolve around it. If you invest in Dohrman, she will invest back.
As this is a public speaking type class, Dohrman makes it a more fun and chill environment, 10/10 recommend

Dohrman is a fine lecturer and a good person but the class sucks. So much of it is busy work and she assigns so much of it that it can get annoying with other assignments. As long as you follow the rubric, you should get a A's on the assignments.

MGT 201 is definitely a useful class, considering that it gives you great experience in real-life consulting. There are no tests; it is mostly project- and presentation-heavy. Dohrman grading is super inconsistent; her instructions for many of the assignments are confusing. Go to the TA; they do most of the grading and know more.

Dymek is a passionate and kind professor. Make sure to have a genuine interest in the subject, otherwise it is hard to learn anything from the class. I got sleepy so many times. You do get a cheat sheet on the exams but there is way too much information.

Tests are all brute memorization, requiring you to put in tremendous amounts of time. Lecture was interesting but got monotonous very fast. I understand that Professor Dymek wants to make this class seem like it's a class worth taking but it's not. Be prepared to put in more time in this class than your other classes combined. Do not recommend.

Prof. Dymek is very knowledgable about the subject, however the content gets rather monotonous rather quickly, making skipping lectures all too appealing. The tests are more of a measure of how good you can make a cheat sheet, so see to it that you make yours thorough.

While the phrase is a bit trite, I genuinely believe Professor Dymek is the best I have had at WashU. Aside from his playing music during lectures, encyclopedic knowledge, and whimsical anecdotes and turns of phrase, he exudes a passion that everyone should aspire to emulate in their lives. I'm honored to say I was able to take a class with him.

Really kind, excited about his subject. The class has a lot of work that requires menial effort. Everything is open book so quizzes are super easy, lab can have quite a bit of work every now and then. Content can get really boring at times and you def need to bring coffee to class or you'll fall asleep.

The class was taught asynchronously, but the lectures were still really interesting. Lots of interesting material in there. I do think that the organization of the lectures could be a little bit more clear, but it didn't really negatively affect my experience of the class. Quizzes and homeworks weren't too challenging. Awesome guy!

The lectures were really fun, especially before we went online for the second half of the semester. He cares a lot and the parks are beautiful; grading criteria aren't very clear though, and I didn't find the lectures well organized in terms of argument, themes, concepts, etc. Rocks (and national parks) are rly cool though!

Interesting class- Dymek is incredibly knowledgable about the topics and is a fun, engaging lecturer. However, this class is basically a straight geology class with a bit of environmental science (climate change) at the very end. The labs were pretty killer, being difficult and requiring a lot of time and effort. Do all the extra credit you can.

Geology of National Parks with Prof. Dymek is great.  He knows everything there is about geology of the US and accompanies his lectures with his own photography.  He also plays music along with slideshows and gives a letter grade to National Park signs.  Overall, great class, but there is lots of material.  Dymek is the man.

Dymek is very passionate about the subject, but it is very geology heavy. Be prepared to do lots of work. Although it is not difficult, it seems to be more than the course is worth. There are SmartWorks quizzes, readings, 2 novels, and a weekly 2 hour lab with lab reports--all in addition to lecture reading.

In Aloe Blacc's song "I'm the Man," I'm 99% confident he is referring to Professor Dymek! He always adds a little humor while discussing the geology of national parks. FRESHMAN: I know very little about science and I'm on track to get a A-/B+ in this class with very minimal effort.  Work hard on homework assignments and you'll be fine!

The professor had a tendency to go on tangents in lecture, but had a fun, if bizarre, sense of humor.  Lectures were generally enjoyable;  exams were very difficult and often focused on small details or specific examples from class.  The professor did, however, offer help with exams and gave a lot of extra credit to soften the blow.

If you have ever been on a hike, or have even the least interest in being outside, this is a fantastic class. There are music/photo montages for each of the parks. Visually interesting with simple explanations of common geological processes. Tests are easy and a cheat sheet is allowed. Very clear and the class is actually fun to attend.

Tests are insanely difficult.  He means so well, but this class is just too big. Questions don't feel welcomed, and he doesn't have office hours.  There is not a study guide or list of recommended things to study. You are on your own in this class.  It is possible to get an A if you are willing to work like it's a 300 level course (it's 118).

Easiest class I ever took. To be completely honest I never cracked the spines on my books and I never actually sat down to study for a test. Final was extensive but as long as you have your Powerpoint slides in order and well organized it is not hard at all. Anyone can get an A in this class. Great professor

Very interesting class, I learned a lot from him.  He went beyond just talking about geology, and into the politics of the national parks and problems with the system.  He was also very obviously passionate about the subject, which was nice.

Exams were not overly difficult, he is a big, funny and jolly man, but his jokes can fall flat. The subject is interesting, but there was a lack of depth in the coverage much of the actual geology, but it's survey course. The slides are pretty, and its pretty brainless if you've study earth processe
his exams are extremely tough. if you're not quite interested in geology, don't take his class
No Comments

This class was extrememly difficult for a 100 class.  Even with open notes.   One large part of exam 1 consisted of one page from the text (out of hundreds read)that you were to identify specific rocks ids. I would not recommend to non science majors.
good, smart professor, but his geology of national parks class is hard as hell for a non-science major, 100-level class. his tests are open notes but tests are hard even if you take good notes.

Geology of National Parks was quite difficult for a 100 level non-science major class.  Tests are open notes, but beware, you can't possibly take enough notes in class anyway.  Class is graded on a big curve though so the bad raw scores don't matter in the end.

Dr. Elise is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students and their success. She never fails to have a smile on her face and always to encourage students to try their best. She conveys information really well and helps break down complex bio topics into smaller, more understandable chunks. Would 100% recommend taking 2960 with her.

I didn't have Dr. Elise (I had Hanes), but my goodness, this woman is amazing. She cares SO MUCH for students, evident in the her teaching approach & the effort she puts into class materials. She even prepares questions for students to ask during office hours. Lowk got 3 on the AP, but with Dr. Elise's unwavering support, I was able to get an A+ :)

Great professor. Loved her class. The course is well-designed to make sure you actually learn stuffs and not worrying too much of your grade. Exams are really hard and detailed, but they only take up a limited portion of the total grade. Also made a lot of friends in this group-discussion styled class. Really enjoyed it overall.

this lady is my queen. bio 2960 is not a weed out in the small section AT ALL compared to chem. the content isn't necessarily super simple but she breaks it down really well and is super accessible outside of class for extra questions. the small section saved my grade and i cannot recommend this professor enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I have ever had

I was part of the small section for Bio 2960 and it was amazing. There was a lot of content so it was difficult but if you stay on top of things and ask for help you can get and A in the class. Lab helps a lot and is 25% of your grade so make sure to remember that. Dr. Elise is so kind and caring, definitely take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor! Bio 2960 is hard—it covers a lot of material and is taught at a fast pace. However, Dr. Elise is so enthusiastic and sweet and genuinely wants us learn. Even if you've taken AP or IB bio, I still recommend applying to be in the small section with her!

Dr. Elise is hands-down the most wonderful and impactful professors I've ever had. She knows and cares about each individual student and really wants everyone to succeed. The Bio2960 content can be heavy/challenging, but she breaks it down and presents it in a digestible and engaging way. She's super accessible and supportive outside of class.

Take Dr. Elise if possible. If not, try to get in her lab section. She is so caring and friendly in addition to explaining the materials extremely clearly. The course is structured as group discussions + prelecture recordings. Be ready to do more work than the other section but the take away is huge and cooperative learning experience is fantastic.
Never seen someone care for their students' success so much. If you have the chance, take BIO2960 with Dr. Elise.

Dr. Walck-Shannon (who prefers to go by Elise) is a very caring and down-to-earth professor. I had her for 2970 Lab; she truly cares about student success. I learned early on that she is the only lab professor who creates additional material to help students understand course content. She is truly one of the best professors at WashU.

Professor Walck-Shannon is one of my favorite profs at WashU. She is extremely caring, and an amazing lecturer. She takes the time to learn everyone's name in Bio 2960's special sections (around 80 kids), and knows everyone individually, which is incredible. Definitely take a class with her if you can.

A hidden gem at WashU, one of the most genuinely caring professors at this school, and a phenomenal instructor. She explains the concepts very clearly and makes them super approachable. She is extremely clear in her expectations for students. A professor I highly recommend every student take.

Dr. Elise is absolutely amazing. I had her for 2970 lab and she helped make the 2970 material so much more understandable. She is one of the most caring and enthusiastic professors at WashU, and if you can take a course with her definitely do!
She was an amazing lab instructor and was very caring and accommodating. She also made sure that the content and labs were easy to understand. Amazing overall!
One of the best instructors in the BIOL department. If you can take section three with her; DO IT. She is so sweet and her enthusiasm got me through the Dark Ages my second semester.

Dr. Elise is one of the most transformative professors at WashU. She deeply cares about her students' success and mental well-being, building lasting relationships. She goes beyond teaching, ensuring we fully understand the material, and offers incredible support and resources. I highly recommend her—she will change how you approach learning!

The sweetest, most enthusiastic professor ever. Her redesign of 2960 evidently required enormous amounts of work, and she handled the new semester extremely well. Her teaching style is good, but the class structure is great. As long as you consistently actively engage with the material, it is very possible to do well in this course.
She's so sweet and amazing.
Elise is awesome, very accessible. Give very deep explanations.

Dr. Shannon really cares her students and explains concepts clearly during lab sections. Biology department should let Dr. Shannon to be the lecturer for Bio2970 rather than Dr. Barton whose brain often stops working. I would recommend others taking lab section with Dr. Shannon for Bio2970.
Very sweet prof.
Lectures felt like a waste of time and the grading scale was unfair despite your effort.

Thimsen is overhated. He is not a friendly or flexible guy but teaches in a very logical manner. Lectures are easy to follow which I appreciated. Homework is very tough and you'll never know what you got wrong since even the TAs don't get an answer key. However, exams were graded fairly and I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy is clearly smart, but has absolutely no idea how to present material to undergrads in an engaging way. He is the typical "got a PhD to do research but this school is forcing me to teach stuff to a bunch of dumb undergrads ughh" guy, making him sound condescending in his lectures. Grades are only based on exams and HW (graded on accuracy).
Worst class I have ever taken. Absolutely hated this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cannot believe I pay 80k a year to be taught by this man.

I took the class a year ago. I heard different feedbacks for him. Prof Thimsen is very smart. I heard that year SP2018 were insanely hard which the homework is 24 hours/week. In our year(SP2019), he teaches clearly on the concepts, some of which overlaps with GenChem. However, his homework and final are really hard. Ready to learn during exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: very passive aggressive! whenever you speak up in class and she didn't agree with what you said you will be shut down immediately. additionally i felt like she was very demeaning if u spoke out in class and she didn't agree w u + made it very hard for me to speak up after being belittled in front of the whole class. change ur cw teacher if u can.

unnecessarily tough grader for a freshman writing course. Graded us like we were scholars and wasn't the best at giving advice/feedback to students in a receivable manner. She challenged me as a writer and had to visit her office hours for every assignment- she did make me a better writer but if you're just looking for a easy CW section avoid her

She gives out grades within like a 5 point range for every student in the class. You have to tailor your writing to EXACTLY how she wants it to get a DECENT grade; highest score for nearly every assignment in the entire class was a 93. If she doesn't like your topic or agree with it, you're getting a bad grade. Take another CW class or theme.

G'Sell wants you to write the way she would write. She has an idea in her head of how an essay should be, and if your idea is not hers, your grade will reflect that. Get ready to be constantly interrupted and misunderstood in class and during office hours. She picks favorites, and if you aren't one, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: annoying, irritating, save me, help me, release me

Don't try to have your own ideas, interests or thoughts, it'll cost you. Make sure whatever you're writing is interesting to HER, what you think doesn't matter all that much. She's also the supreme lord of passive aggressiveness.
Overall extremely passive aggressive, does not provide insightful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very passive-aggressive

My writer's voice would be nowhere near as strong as it is today had I not encountered Prof. G'Sell by chance for a required first-year course. She genuinely engaged the small class's identified interests, often tailoring the syllabus and readings to our research topics. Her feedback was always thorough, and she made the editing process rewarding.

Prof. G'Sell is one of the most caring, genuinely interested, professors I have encountered at WashU. She genuinely wants her students to become not only better writers, but thinkers, and is incredibly invested in student success. She is readily accessible out of class and gives outstanding feedback. Overall, anyone would be lucky to be her student

Confined by rhetoric I don't get to choose,
Eileen G'Sell controls my moods.
Wielding the gradebook like a sword,
Each B- tells me that there is nothing to work towards.
My words drowned out,
Steamrolled by a supposed guide,
Who would rather deride.

Judged by how well you suck up,
Your grade is basically luck.

She is a very tough grader. She is also passive aggressive and if your writing or a comment in discussion does not follow her personal opinion she disregards it. A good quality of this professor is that she gives great feedback on your writing.
HARD TEACHER

For your understanding !!!! Please read this before you make a decision! 

The teacher is a tough grader! Lots of homework, and paperwork, and she does not allow being on the good grades! 

Do not recommend!

If you want an easy A, I would suggest taking CW with a different professor. G' Sell is a very tough grader and has high expectations for all her students. She is professional and can be very passive-aggressive about minor human errors. She gives constructive, logical, and thorough feedback on assignments (explaining some of the good reviews).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor G'Sell is kind and overall a good teacher. As long as you show her that you are putting in effort, you should be fine. There is a good amount of reading but it's not necessary as long as you can participate otherwise. She gives very long and elaborate feedback that can be a bit confusing but she is VERY responsive via email.

Ms. G'Sell is an excellent teacher. The lectures were fun and easy to grasp. The first reading of the class was a bit of a chore, but I didn't do it and was fine.  

The rubric of this class is a bit vague, so I advise going to Eillen's office hours and finding a thesis that interests her or something she doesn't know much about.

I took the Modern Media Ampersand with Eileen and really enjoyed it. The lectures and readings were really informative. The problem that I had with her/this course is that the written briefs of the assignments for projects and papers are not in line with her actual expectations for what she wants included in the projects. Office hours are helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Eileen had obvious personal judgements against students, particularly female students whom she did not think were similar to her. I do not recommend taking any of her classes.

A delight to have as a college writing professor. A lot of people dread CW, but with her I highly enjoyed it and feel that I grew as a writer, thinker, researcher, and overall student under her professorship. She supports and challenges ideas in fascinating ways & gives INCREDIBLE feedback. With her as a professor, you're sure to be a better writer

G'Sell is an effective professor for skill improvement. Offers prompt and constructive feedback, is supportive during office hours, and fair in grading. Not an easy A, but reasonable. The readings in Power and Commodity are interesting; participation and effort are key for success despite the initial reading load.
If you actually interested in becoming a good writer take her class. If not drop the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor G'Sell helped me grow tremendously as a writer. She definitely does not let you take the easy was out, but makes you so much better for it. Such a caring teacher and very understandable.
Eileen G'sell is a nice professor; however, if you want an A in this class, I would recommend taking this class with a different professor.
I highly recommend switching out of this class if you have this teacher. Even if that means that you have take citizen scientist; don't have Eileen G'Sell as your teacher!
Also, her office hours were in-person at 8:30 in the engineering-part of campus. That says enough.
Eileen Gsell can not teach and is the harshest grader. Don't take any class with her.

G'sell cares a ton about her students and her work. You need to grind to get an A, so get ready to meet with her consistently in her office hours. But, if you put in the work, you will be rewarded. She is very attentive to students needs and super accessible outside of class. She has a habit of talking over students in class at times though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a tough grader, but she is EXTREMELY HELPFUL and caring! Take Professor G'Sell's class, you will work your butt off, but it will be worth it!
Extremely caring. Super funny. I recommend Power & Commodity Culture to all.

Professor Eileen G'Sell is a highly respectable professor. She leaves paragraphs of meaningful feedback on every assignment you hand in and is always accessible outside of class to talk further. You need to WORK in her class. Professor G'Sell has made me think in ways I've never thought before and broadened my imagination through her wisdom.

She's obviously passionate and really believes that what she's doing is important. However, she constantly interrupts students and fails to listen to their ideas, asserting her own before she even truly understands what her students are trying to say. She needs a reality check so that she can use her passion for teaching in a more productive way.

Impossible to get a good grade if you have differing opinions from G'Sell. She will destroy your thoughts if she disagrees on a personal level and the grade represents this. Office hours are useless: she rarely answers the questions asked and will just criticise your individual opinions/thoughts. Prefers to talk over students than listen to them.

She constantly interrupts students, will destroy your opinion if it doesn't align with hers. Most unhelpful person during office hours, won't directly answer any questions/will talk about something unrelated. Will talk over you and is a harsh grader if your opinions aren't the same as hers. Has taught me nothing about being a good writer.

Professor G'Sell is truly one of a kind. She is incredibly accessible outside of the classroom and truly is invested in each of her student's success. I would not be the writer I am today without her guidance, support, and input. Her courses are the perfect mix of structure and independence. I wish I could take another course with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor G'Sell is a knowledgeable instructor who is willing to take the time to provide you with detailed, constructive feedback on your writing. Power and Commodity culture had some really interesting readings that were not inaccessibly difficult to grasp, and I would highly recommend it to freshmen for their writing requirement!
Great teacher. Tough grader and isn't afraid to critique students, but I genuinely cared about what I what I learned in her class. Learned a lot and overall had a great experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: I think that Professor G'Sell's teaching style is tailored to those who intend to truly grow in their writing abilities from this course. Not only are her expectations and feedback clear, but she also rewards those who take an active effort to improve as the semester progresses. Put in the effort and attend office hours, and you'll be rewarded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have ever taken. I have always excelled in writing and came as an English major. She crushed this dream. I have never met someone so condescending, passive aggressive, and pretentious. If your ideas are even slightly off from hers, good luck doing well in this class. I would rate her a 0 if I could

Professor G'Sell is the least helpful professor I've had, and she comes off as condescending both in class and office hours. She never answered my questions in office hours and always rushed through our meetings. She only values your paper if you make points that line up with her opinions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I felt that every original thought I put in this class, was put down. Tough grader and passive-aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor G'Sell is the best! She gives amazing feedback and really went out of her way to make our online course fun, interactive, and impacting. Power and Commodity Culture is an exciting and rewarding theme for freshman writing -- highly recommend!

Eileen is a funny, smart, and dedicated teacher. She was very personable (remembered people's interests, and was excited about the wide range of topics we selected to write on. She gave thoughtful feedback, graded fairly, and was clear with her expectations. She hosted frequent and helpful office hours. A fascinating course w/ great professor!

I dread having to go to Professor GSells class every week. She is not helpful at all even when going to her office hours. She is pretentious and knocks down any idea or opinion you suggest. If your writing style doesnt align with what she likes then good luck with getting an A.

Professor GSell is quite possibly the worst instructor Ive ever had. Not only is she unclear and inconsistent with her criteria, she is extremely rude and abrasive. Additionally, if you do not write exactly how she wants with all of her opinions, she does not give your paper the time of day. She does not care how your writing progresses AT ALL.

Professor G'Sell was one of the best instructors I have had at WashU. Her teaching style is collaborative, inclusive, and insightful and the individualized care she gave made the class so enjoyable. She gave great feedback and accommodated my busy schedule by oftentimes meeting with me three times a week at 8:30AM!

She provides very vague feedback and does not seem to appreciate writing styles that are different from her own expectations. I met with her to review all my papers and did not feel like I learned anything new from her by the end of the semester. Instead, I felt I had to change my writing style to fit what she wanted, which did not stick long term.

Eileen is a great professor! Very good at leading discussions, providing feedback, and helping you during office hours (also very responsive to email). Fair grader, too. You get the grade you deserve. Participate in class discussions, do the best you can, and work the hardest you can. I kinda slacked near the end and ended up with a B+.

I thought she did a great job of trying to make everyone a better writer no matter where they started. If you want to do well, set up appointments with her to revise/ discuss papers. She might be a hard grader, but she rewards thoughtful input. She's interesting and funny, so going to class (which is definitely required) isn't bad at all.

I took Writing I with Eileen last fall and can safely say that she has had in immense effect on my style and ability. She is extremely helpful and will make you a better writer. However, she is a fairly hard grader, but it's well worth the effort.

I really enjoyed my class with her. Great discussion leader. Good sense of humor. Cares for her students, and really gets a sense for them through their writing styles. She also as a interesting/good taste in clothing.

Helpful teacher!  Grading procedure is relatively hard, but she'll write mini-novels in the margins of your papers so you'll know EXACTLY how to fix it.  Very approachable and available outside of class as well.

For Math 310. Do not take this class with Dr. Evans!!! Brutal grader. He is just asking way too much, and other teachers are significantly easier. I also felt like I was treated differently, almost like he had it out for me, which made the experience even more frustrating. Save yourself and take Foundations for Higher Math with someone else!

Dr. Evans is a kind and supportive professor who brings enthusiasm to his lectures. His office hour availability can be limited and the class pace sometimes falls behind, but overall he creates a positive learning environment and remains one of the strongest instructors I've had at WashU.

Lectures were well organized, and he made the content easy to understand. He truly cares about students learning the material and will give you the help you need during his office hours. Also, he's quite funny.
Had him for Calc 3. Super nice guy, great lecturer, clearly enjoys teaching.
Had Evans for Calc III. Funny guy, clear lectures, and good office hours / review sessions. Don't be annoying and he will be nice.

He is a fantastic Professor, gave me multiple extensions on assignments and always cared about my mental health. Too be fair, he was a bit of a boring lecturer, and he did spit on my little brothers grave, and he would get angry when people would pack up early. Professor Evans made all of the content much easier then other teachers would.
He do lectures with humor and will explain any topic on the subject when asked.

This won't let me select any other class than 131 but I had Professor Evans for Calc 3(Math 2130). He is an amazing professor, tho he did spit on me grandmother's grave, and all of his lectures were easy to follow. This class is not easy if you can't visualize 3D shapes or suck at vectors but the way Evans teaches made it easy.

Took Calc III with Evans. Great professor, explains things very well, and makes difficult concepts relatively understandable. Very open to helping students if they show that they are willing to learn math. 
Did spend the first week of the semester to go and spit on my ancestors' graves. Very Icky, but understandable. Overall, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Evans does go fast in lectures, but as long as you're not trying to mark down every last word he says/writes, then he's pretty easy to keep up with. Also, very good 1-on-1 outside of class, so if a lecture seems overwhelming, just go to office hours.

Easy to reach outside of class and personable, but tests were hard and made to be confusing on purpose. Some of the homework took extremely long, and even the math help room couldn't help me. Very frustrating trying to do your best, as the only way to do well on tests was to learn the theory behind the math, not just doing the problems correctly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not as hard as people perceive it to be. A lot of opportunities to raise your grade, review homework & past exams, go to office hours, and review lecture notes. One class was group work. If you don't have pre calculus understanding the class covers a bit at the beginning but it'll pick up. Ppl complained bc they thought it'd be like HS math lolz.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take this course if you have never taken Calculus, this is a fast-paced course with no time to ask questions. Whenever a student has asked questions he will make you feel embarrassed in front of the whole class. He writes notes extremely fast and, he expects you to know Calculus, this class should be a review for people who have taken calc.

Evans is a terrible. He talks really fast, and its obvious he's passionate about math, but his lectures are so confusing and all over the place. During one of our Monday lectures, he started doing Wednesday's lecture and stopped himself midway and was like, "whoops! I'm sorry! Let me go back and do Monday!" It is not worth it to go to lecture.

My message to washu students is that while johnson may be superior for 131, I think that Evans is underrated and a passionate teacher who will teach the content just fine. Goes a bit fast in lecture but the lecture notes posted in study hub are VERY useful. In lecture focus on watching and understanding content instead of writing notes.

I loved Professor Henriksen's passion for physics. I can tell he truly enjoys teaching and cares for his students. The class itself is difficult which might be discouraging but his lectures kept me engaged. He does cold call which kept me focused.
Henriksen is such a weird dude. He made a terrible class fun with his demos and quirkiness. Would highly recommend him as a professor since the rest of the course is absolute hell.

One of the best Intro Physics professors for sure. He's super funny in lecture, and does a good job teaching the material. Physics 198 is a really difficult class, but Henriksen makes it much more enjoyable! He also does amazing demonstrations in class. Would highly recommend.

Professor Henriksen is my favorite professor in the physics department.  I don't really like physics, but he somehow makes his lectures SO interesting and fun.  Students really respect him and vice versa -- this makes for a great class.  The exams are challenging, but he prepares his class well for them (he doesn't write the exams).  He is great!

Excellent lecturer who does a great job of explaining difficult concepts. You do best if you read the book in depth beforehand, because his lectures will help you understand the concepts but leave it up to you to learn how to solve individual problems. Brilliant, helpful if you ask for it, always open and respectful of student opinions.

Professor Henriksen is legitimately the only reason I passed electronics lab. His lectures are clear and concise, he is constantly available during lab to offer his help, and he offers you opportunities to learn rather than just giving you the answers. Also he teaches skills that transfer across fields, useful since I also study art. Hawt too.
One of my favorite professors ever. He is so clear and really wants everyone to know the material. I would definitely recommend him. Also he is hot and has his tongue pierced.

Really cares about teaching, lectures make a lot of sense (they clarify exactly what it says in the textbook). Exam prep for students is nonexistent, and will sometimes lead you in the opposite direction of what is on the exam (or maybe the exam itself is just too difficult)
Very caring teacher and nice person. Inspired me with regards to physics.
Loveeeeeeeeee
Very nice and passionate!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Esparza made WGSS so interesting and every lecture was captivating. He uses a combo of lecture and activities in class. Every reading connected to the topics (even if they were long). We covered so many topics and it touches on so many current issues. There is nightly readings/videos but they all can be used in the few papers he assigns.

I had Dr. Esparza last semester for Intro to WGSS and he is an amazing professor. He is very patient with all the students and mindful of the different perspectives and places that students hold. He is very informative and willing to help people grow and understand different intricacies. I recommend his Intro to WGSS class for anyone interested!

This was my first time taking a WGSS course, and I absolutely loved it because Esparza did such a good job at introducing the course material. I learned so much in this class. Esparza is a great professor who approached even the toughest topics with respect and perspective. Grading was overall clear, and he was open to any additional questions.

I learned so much in my Sex in the City class this semester! I'm so grateful to have had Esparza as a professor. He was very knowledgeable and passionate about the topic and kind to students. I would recommend this class and prof to everyone!
The content in Intro to WGSS was incredibly interesting and Esparza did an amazing job with the lectures. Provided a lot of relevant examples and was very respectful and patient in discussions.

I took Racial and Sexual Politics of Public Health with Dr. Esparza and loved it! The class was both interesting and horrifying (not his fault, it's the content). Class consisted of attendance, participation, 3 essays, and a final project. Readings were long but never felt irrelevant and the essays were graded fairly with feedback.

I had Esparza for Intro to WGSS and Sex in the City (online bc of covid) and enjoyed the courses and him! Esparza did a great job of exploring all the aspects of WGSS and I benefited from all the readings and assignments. Esparza is a bit dry but it is super easy to receive an A and he left lovely comments on all my work. Recommend WGSS and him!
Class is ridiculously hard for an introductory statistics course
Rude professor, ridiculously hard introductory statistics course.

reviews.comment: The content of the class is repetitive. Annoying pop quizzes. You do get 3 cheat sheets on midterm/final.

I personally had a good relationship with Professor Snir, but I also made an effort to build one. He definitely seems to have favorites, so I can understand why some students had tougher experiences. The exams are challenging too. Still, if you attend class, pay attention, and pick a solid group for the final project, you should be fine overall.

I personally had a good relationship with Snir, but I also made an effort to build one. He definitely seems to have favorites, so I can understand why some students had tougher experiences. The exams are challenging too. Still, if you attend class, pay attention, and pick a solid group for the final project, you should be fine overall.

This class is really repetitive and cummulative material on every exam/quiz. Lots of group projects, good professor but boring. Random pop quizzes every week for attendance, great B school curve at the end of semester. Snir is flexible but is strict with some things. TA's grade almost everything. Exams were kinda hard but you get 3 cheat sheets.
An evil man tbh
so far so good?

I had a decent experience with Snir, but I understand how others could have terrible ones. He gets a lot nicer if you get to know him and if you express interest in being a TA. His exams are difficult, especially the final. We had pop quizzes for attendance which was annoying, but participation is small. Good luck. He is what you make of him.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's ruthless, terrible lecturer, doesnt care, he inspires me to quit my career plans. Love this guy. Also sexist and racist :)

Least favorite class I've taken at Olin. Lectures are boring and we learn outdated statistical methods. Most of the class material and project work is in Excel, but the tests are on completely different topics and done on paper. He's not an easy person to get along with and doesn't seem interested in helping students. Wouldn't recommend.

Least favorite professor of all time. Clearly did not like certain students in class. Lowered my grade from an A to B+ just because the believed that I didn't do enough work on the final project even though I helped my group a lot. Wrote him an email asking about it and did not want to discuss anything. Would not recommend getting on his bad side.

Snir is a great teacher. Sometimes, the lectures can be a bit boring, but that's more on the material than the professor. If you can pay attention in class and do the homework on time, then you should succeed in this class.

The final is unexpectedly nasty and stats is tuaght in an old fashioned way, students have to handwrite proofs and many statistical figures. We are not taught efficient or modern stats technologies. TAs CARRIED this class for me, thanks guys! Prof Snir made me uncomfortable when I asked questions because he does not like talking with students.

Snir does a great job organizing his class and gives plenty of practice tests before exams. However, his tests are graded quite harshly and are a large portion of our grade. Snir can come off caring one moment and condescending the next, and I never felt comfortable asking for help. Lectures were also quite dull and lack engagement.

I really enjoyed the class. Lectures cover all the material you need to know for the group projects, quizzes, and exams. As long as you understand the content well, I think the exams were very fair. He also gives a bunch of practice quizzes and exams which are super helpful if you actually do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The midterm and quizzes were fair but the final was cruel. I studied a lot and failed the exam (literally), but since I did well on the midterm and other stuff, I walked away with a B. Expectations for the final were unclear. His lectures are boring, but informative. Seems like a chill guy. Exams are graded harshly, so pay attention in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: midterm and quizzes are easy and then the final comes out of nowhere. terrible lecturer, very hard to learn from him

He honestly has taught me so much and prepared me so well for statistics. His class is running really well and he makes it VERY easy to be prepared for tests just do all his practice exams. His pop quizzes are really easy and honestly just for attendance. He is a nice guy and I learned a lot from him, lectures can be dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's a good lecturer, offers guided notes, hw has unlimited attempts, and theres plenty of TA OH. Quizzes & midterms resemble past ones (he provides many past examples). The final is tough though, so stay focused and dedicate some time to studying. Overall the class is fair and expectations are pretty clear, you more or less get what you put in.

Snir is a really good lecturer and professor, but he is not a good person. He is very condescending when answering questions and makes it uncomfortable for students to ask. That said, he teaches content really well (just not a great person).

Snir is a decent lecturer and fair grader, he makes sure all grading criteria are known well ahead of time for assessments... he is pretty boring but mainly because of the material.
This class is hard not because of the statistical material but because you must do the procedure correctly, label everything, put stats in context to get full credit.

Dr. Snir is such a caring professor. I love his lectures; he does the problems with you in class on the board. I really like how his tests, and classes are set up. His homework is a little hard. Make sure to have a study group for the homework or get a tutor. Overall, it was an enjoyable class.

Dr. Snir is a kind professor. His lectures always use real world application and the project is quite fun. It is an easy course due to the fact that every test and quiz comes with numerous practice exams. If you can commit the time to do these, you can easily obtain a high A in the course. Regrades during my semester boosted grades too.

He is easily the least compassionate person who is so absolved in themself that it is amazing that the school allows this man to keep teaching this class aside to stroke his own ego. This man is a testament to the tenure system and its flaws, It is the WORST and LEAST INTERESTING CLASS IN BUSINESS SCHOOL BY FAR.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I found this class to be a bit challenging- the homework takes a bit of time and the tests included processes we don't cover in class. Class is focused on the Excel processes; meanwhile, the tests are handwritten problems- just practice the past exams to get used to it. He is super nice and cares about his students. Great guy.

Great guy and pretty good professor. Interacting with him is often very easy as he's quite nice and rather enjoyable to talk to, but the lectures can definitely get boring quickly. You do have a term paper, a poster (based off of the term paper), and a final exam all due/held within 1-2 weeks of each other, so this class's workload is pretty high.

Professor Snir is a great professor and he cares about his students a lot. He holds plenty of office hours and are more than willing to answer students' questions. He instilled a new policy where you can earn up to 50% of the points missed on exams and quizzes.

Snir is a great professor; his lectures are straightforward and organized and he sets clear expectations for the class at the beginning of the semester. DAT121 can be a bit boring in terms of content at times, but Snir always incorporates examples that makes things easy to understand. Definitely cares about his students success!

Professor Snir is great. While the lectures can be boring (its Managerial Stats what can he do) he is really straight forward about what we need to know and is eager to help if we had any questions. The grade is focused mostly in the Final and the Midterm, but you get 6 cheat sheets, so like just study and put in the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Probably the least helpful professor I've had at WashU. Always tried to get help from him outside of class but he never was willing. His lectures are dry and uninteresting. I know it's statistics, but you can at least try to gather student attention.

Snir is as straight-forward as it gets. DO the homework, show up to class, take some notes ON HIS PRINTED OUT NOTES THAT HE GIVES YOU LOL and you'll be just fine.

The pop quizzes are really easy and more for attendence. They're also open book and literally have direct answer choices usually based on the notes that, again, HE prints and gives.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: ENOUGH with the Snir slander. Snir is a great professor!! He prints out all the notes for students in advance, and makes complex topics easy to understand. The course is very well organized. Classes went at a good pace and I always felt engaged. He does a really good job explaining the core concepts, and is super helpful outside of class!!

This class is fine if you do the homework and show up to class. Just know this man is an absolute snoozefest and his tests are way too hard. He curves the class and he is genuinely pretty understanding, just super boring. But, he was the only DAT121 professor so I guess if you don't have a choice, you will get through it.

You get in what you put out in Snir's class. Lectures are a bit slow, but if you sit through them, take notes, and put in the effort you'll do well. Unfortunately, I did none of those things. Great teacher all around though.

Snir is a nice person and makes the content easy to follow. Yes, they may not be the most exciting lectures in the world, but we're learning stats -- give him a break. If you follow the lectures or literally just read the lecture notes, you should generally be fine for the quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Eli Snir is prob the best professor I've had at WashU. he rewards good grades for those who have paid attention and come prepared to class no matter the exam grade that they get. Plus his exams are great because they are well structured and never deviate from the structure and difficulty of past exams. Awesome prof and even better person.
The final exam was just bizarre and unnecessarily obscure and hard. The grading in this class is just so inconsistent with no leniency. The professor was also just unhelpful most of the time.

This man has no business teaching undergraduates. I feel like a lot of topics he just covers as if we already learned them--it feels like he doesn't understand that him knowing the concepts doesn't mean everyone knows them. Lectures are pretty bland and often difficult to follow. He's a nice guy, but please stay away if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is human before he is a professor, something a lot of professors lack. He may seem intimidating at first but he's very accommodating and makes an effort to help you.

I had Snir the previous year for a non-business class, and took him again for DAT121. His lectures are kind of boring but he a nice person in general. Very accommodating regarding tests and interviews and is willing to work with you if you bring up concerns. For homework I would stick to the TAs as he is very busy. Exams are average difficultly.

His class is alright, it can get a little bit dry at times in lecture. There's a lot of homework, most of them aren't very hard but there a couple that are really hard. TA help sessions were really helpful for me to get through them. The exams are worth a lot of your grade, but there's a final project that can be helpful to improve your grade.

The professor seems bothered when you seek help outside of class. The lectures are boring, but you have to know absolutely everything that is covered- so going to class feels draining. You are required to use SPSS software for the final project, but the whole class is conducted in Excel. Each exam is worth a huge part of your grade. Stressful!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had at WashU- and I've had some bad ones. Snir had no compassion in helping his students. I asked for help a couple of times and was shut down immediately. Especially during COVID, he made us even more stressed than we already were during a pandemic. WashU, you need to reevaluate Snir- he should just stick to research.

DAT 121 is a very boring class. Prof Snir tries really hard to make it engaging, but it just doesn't work. He cares a lot about the class, but it is a dreadful experience. Snir isn't terrible by any means, just isn't great.
Two exams where the average was in the 70s. No curve in the course. 60% of the class is in the B/C grade range, and he mumbles to himself in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Snir's lectures tend to be boring and drag on. The most useful things in the class are learning how to use Excel and how applicable stats is in the real world. The content of the class is fine, it's just that Snir doesn't do a great job at teaching it. Keep your expectations low.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I had in WashU. I think Professor Snir is very nice and helpful. His classes are well-organized. You need to prepare well in order to get a better grade. He likes to talk with his students and give them constructive advise. I will recommend him to every WashU student.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Pretty boring lecturer and doesn't teach very well

Absolutely one of the most boring lecturers at Wash U. I had to fight to stay awake every class. Terrible at answering questions, not that anyone really ever asked anyway because most were completely lost. I did all my learning by looking at the practice tests. I like statistics but I hated this class. Sorry excuse for a "professor".

Kind of boring and not entirely informative, but turned out fine. My favorite part of the class was an independent project where we had a lot of freedom to choose whatever topic we wanted, and was graded pretty leniently.

Not a super nice/friendly guy but his material is well organized and easy to follow.  Exam grading is super specific -- you need to word things super specifically and follow the rules just as he likes them for full credit.  Study hard and early and it will absolutely pay off.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class itself isn't too bad. The only thing that bugged me was that his grading was very subjective and stingy. He tries to take points off and doesn't like regrades. As a person, he's just a boring, bland guy. Nobody really likes him, he's not hated, he's just an awkward guy.  I'd recommend taking the class with another professor, but he's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The term paper and presentation can help if you mess up on the midterm. If you go over past homework and go to class and actually pay attention, then every quiz and exam is fair and doable.

One of the best professors I had in the school. The lectures are highly organized and even if some concepts are not explained clearly, he is always there for you to answer any question you might have. Very quick in replying emails.  You can truly learn a great deal if you care about this course and attends lectures.

Snir has a sarcastic sense of humor, which I liked but some do not. As a teacher, he is fantastic. Gives us notes for every lecture and goes over things clearly. There is many opportunities for extra credit and the final term paper is graded easily. I would recommend.

Nice guy, but notes/lectures are often unorganized and confusing.  Not as clear as Dr. Durai, and has more strict 'cheat sheet' policy. Never used book, attendance optional and not needed, easier to learn on your own. Final project, pretty easy.

He actually cares about the class and having kids learn, which is great.  He doesn't require attendance, so most people do not show up.  The classes are pretty interesting though and have cool real life examples.  He is also a pretty nice guy.
Does not teach very well / does not take attendance, resulting in no one ever going to class
Very interesting and funning professor. Odd in a good way. Very helpful and engaging on teaching.

The course is easy, however the professor sometimes explains things in an unclear manner. I feel like some of the statistics concepts were simple in theory, but explained in a way that made it appear more complex or difficult to understand. You can get a good grade easily, but I don't feel I actually learned much of value.

Great professor that cares about her students. Grading is clear and she is very open to meeting outside of class. I wish more professors cared about their students and actually knew what they were talking about like she does. Also, very quick with email responses, even on the weekends. Would definitely recommend her!

Overall good, but be prepare for group work--find a good member pleaseeeeee. Do not expect for office hour, she is always absent for it--at least when I go to her office everytime she is late, and her door is locked. She does not reply to email very quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Samira is a pretty good stats professor. The class is pretty easy as long as you pay attention. Lectures are recorded so attendance isn't really important but she likes participation. All the quizzes are online and open note and she gives lots of time to do them. The only thing is that an A is an 95% (not 93% like other classes)

Office hours and textbooks fill in learning gaps. Be careful of participation grade, because there's a quick assignment every lecture! Another user seems to imply Fazel's non-American accent is hard to understand. In my experience Fazel slows down her speaking, has very clear slides to follow, which accomodates many types of learners. Caring prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is sweet, always answers emails, and is available during office hours. Paying attention in lectures isn't necessary since the slides will be more than enough to do the quizzes and homework. However, there is a class participation quick assignment every lecture, so paying attention in class won't hurt.

She is incredibly sweet, and perhaps it's just the format of the class, but I don't think I learned much in the course. I came in with strong excel skills that allowed me to handle all the course's content, and they didn't really improve throughout the semester. Lectures were boring, and quizzes were so easy you don't need to pay attention.
Samira is the nicest ever. She will make sure you get a good grade on things if you ask for help.

Dr. Fazel is amazing! All you have to do is pay attention in class and fill in the guided notes, and you will do great. She explains the concepts extremely well, and her lectures were very organized and straightforward. If you have any questions definitely go to her office hours. She is always willing to help! This class is an easy A/A+.

Prof. Samira is such a kind, caring, and respectful professor. Yes, the statistic topics can become a bit dry at times, but she does her best to engage students in class, as well as give plenty of opportunities to get help. The exam is very easy if you use the past exams and study guides to help. Don't take an easy professor for granted! So kind!!

A really nice professor. Always willing to answer questions. Lots of practice quizzes and exams available and the course content was extremely easy so it's pretty much an easy A. Definitely take DAT 120 with her.

The class content is boring, but Samira does her best to make it engaging. She always finds ways to relate it to the real world. Lots of practice problems in class. She fills in guided notes that have everything you need to get 100% on exams and quizzes. Homework is very easy, usually just using Excel to solve a problem. Very kind and caring prof.

Class is not that hard, especially as homework is easy. Midterm is in-person in class and it is pretty easy. Final is a take-home, during which he created an AI cheating scare mass-email that got people concerned for no reason, and did not release grades for a long time.

He was a good professor overall. His lectures were well aligned with the labs and homework assignments. While some homework rubrics were occasionally vague, this did not significantly detract from the overall learning experience.
