He also provided extra credit opportunities, allowing students to improve their performance and succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class work does not help those without prior coding experience enough to meet his expectations. Very stubborn and threatened us all with AI use and then waited days to release grades to scare us. Released fina grades and then refused to answer emails.
Not a hard class if you submit labs. I had no prior coding experience. Feldman is very fair

Prof. Fleury is very kind and knowledgable; not an exaggeration to say that he renewed my interest in film. Intro to Film is very doable content wise and is genuinely interesting. Lectures are clear and coherent, and he gives great feedback during office hours if you seek guidance on your shot analysis exercises.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Had him for the First year seminar, horror across media. Considering a Film minor because of him and looking forward to taking intro to film with him next spring. His lectures are fun and engaging. He's a very genuine person and gets to know the class. He likes to do small class lectures to really emphasize that component.

Had him for Horror Across Media. Amazing professor. Very passionate in what he does and the screenings were always very fun. One relatively easy assignment was due each week, and the midterm was pretty easy if you memorized the slides.

I took Fleury for the Horror Across Media first year program. Could not recommend this guy enough. Genuinely cares about the subject matter, as well as the input that students put in. Every assignment is meaningful and never seems like busy work. Actually the GOAT.
love him but intro film was tough (its intro!)

Great professor all around. Challenges you to your highest ability through his lectures and deep knowledge of Cinema studies. The class is difficult and make sure to start your papers not the night before the deadline. But strongly recommend because he's very passionate and is engaging within his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Fleury is the best professor I've ever had. Usually, I can never stay awake in lectures, but he makes class so fun that I was not only awake the whole time, but actively participating. He's extremely passionate about what he teaches and kind towards everyone. He lays out clear, fair expectations and if you follow them, you'll do great.

Taking his first-year seminar Superhero Media was one of my favorite courses of the semester. His interest alone makes you want to be interested, but regardless the content is great and easily engaging. There's some group projects, but they're a breeze. You literally get to watch superhero movies and shows for a class, what more could you want?

Professor Fleury is always prepared and friendly. His class is very organized, engaging, and entertaining. He grades quickly and efficiently with detailed feedback. I thoroughly enjoyed video game studies. Wish all professors were like this!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very engaging and sweet professor. The lectures almost always held my interest and prepared me very well for the exams. Nothing bad to say about her!

She is the sweetest! Even brought her daughter and a dog into class to demonstrate course concepts. Her lectures are great but the slides are often confusing when using them to study. Exams are pretty specific but all multiple choice. She's really nice and a great for intro to psych!
Not a fan of her teaching style just not engaging what so ever
Never really gave good feedback, also get ready for the tests as one bad quiz will set your grade back to be almost unrecoverable. Be weary going into this teachers class.
Run.                   .

She is a great professor, but her classes are pretty test heavy. Your grades on the exams basically dictate your overall grade. However, she is an awesome professor and she knows what she is talking about. Her lectures are very understandable and she explains things in multiple ways so that every gets it. She also gives great in person feedback.

Dr. C-S is fantastic! She is really nice, always available for questions, and grades like she wants students to succeed. Be warned, her slides don't make much sense if you've missed class, so make sure to be there. Otherwise, a great NSM credit for non-math people.

Dr. CS was a very passive aggressive teacher. she did not really provide much help with studying for exams and office hours are extremely vague. She is very passive aggressive. When you have questions about content from class she is extremely passive aggressive.

She's amazing! I loved her for Psych Stats and she's very supportive and encouraging and understanding. She will help you with anything and even just re-explain things if you don't get it right away. Amazing and hilarious individual!

I was nervous going into this class because I hadn't done any math in a bit, but Dr. CS was an amazing professor and made it one of my favorite classes. Topics were presented clearly and she spent extra time on things that were more confusing. Lectures were engaging with lots of examples. Exams are straight-forward and not surprising.

Took Psych Stats w/her and was really impressed. The Canvas was extremely organized, expectations clear, and pretty solid lectures. Never really too much HW at all, and although I never talked with her 1-on-1, she seems super approachable and friendly. Not too difficult of a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: wasn't clear about grading format and has a different grading point system. tests are pretty straightforward
Her lectures were clear and provided relevant examples which helped me understand the content better

I loved professor CS! The content for this course was relatively difficult but very light compared to something like Calc II. If I were to take this class again I would make sure to have stayed on task and focused a little more. The earlier section in the day tend to do better than the later section; its a hr,20min class so make sure to stay awake!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: pretty easy course, Dr. CS makes it easy to succeed -- exams are pretty much just the slides. Psych Stats is NOT common sense tho, so u will need to study on ur own to do well. Class is built similarly to a high school course, content-wise. Very doable, just a bit boring.
Great lectures with lots of examples. Took time to make sure people understood the topics and gave lots of examples. Love her.

Dr. Cohen-Shikora is amazing at lecturing and tries to add humor to lectures as well. Although few exam materials, she did provide a practice exam and was available for questions if you had any after class. Overall an amazing professor, definitely would take her again.

Dr. CS was a nice teacher. However, she did not really provide us with much study tools for our exam. She was really vague on what to study for, so it was really hard for me to pinpoint exam material. Not an awful prof, but definitely could be better.

Dr. C-S is my absolute favorite professor at WashU! She is incredibly kind, cares about students, and is a great lecturer. Experimental psych with her was great. She gave good feedback and had high expectations, but the class never felt wildly overwhelming. She is a wonderful person and professor.

I would rate 6 stars if I could! Dr. CS really has a gift for breaking down complicated topics into understandable terms. I'm not a math person but did well. She has a positive attitude and there are lots of ways to boost your grade.

Professor CS was amazing! I thoroughly enjoyed this class and wished I would have stayed on top of attendance. Though the content can be confusing at times, she does a very good job at explaining things and reviewing them along the way before exams. Not a lot of work outside of class if you attend it! Love professor CS!!

The tests are really hard for this class. She is an interesting lecturer. It was fine just not worth the effort the tests require (over 25 hours of studying the weekend before a test). It was tough but she is an interesting teacher.
She seems like a good person, but she is very unforgiving on deadlines.

Prof. C-S is a very caring professor. Her lectures are clear and engaging. She's very accessible both in and out of class, responds quickly to emails, and answers questions clearly and concisely. Workload is quite reasonable.

My only complaint is that she didn't do more of the lecturing in the FYP!

Prof Cohen-Shikora was great in psych stats. A good AN class for non math people. Lectures are easy to follow, recorded, and slides posted. Lots of little assignments and quizzes that are easy 100s if done on time, can be easy to forget. Prof wants students to succeed and is available outside of class. Would recommend.
Easy A. I stopped going to lectures after a while, and studied the slides that she posted. Great teacher based on the lectures I did attend. Four tests overall, and they are pretty straightforward.

The lectures were okay but she had little information on the slides and skipped through them sometimes, regardless I felt as though I had taken thorough notes but the quiz questions were ridiculously difficult compared to the other lecturers. Take this class in the fall if you plan on taking it.
Great professor that is engaging and delivers clear, concise lectures. The class was relatively difficult, but she made it manageable for everybody. Highly recommend her.
Dr. Cohen-Shikora is a great professor, her lectures are engaging and she makes it clear as to how you can succeed in the course.

She loves talking about her own kids and connecting them to themes in the class. Do not hesitate to ask questions, she is pretty engaging. What worked for me to really listen is to sit in front because it is easy to turn this class into background noise.

I would never take this class again. Everyone in 100B said it was really easy first sem. The quiz averages were high 90s and it was interesting. Professor CS's lectures were pretty good. BUT it seemed to be her goal to keep grades low. The quiz averages were low 80s, and are 90% of your grade. I got a 5 on AP psych, and still had to P/F this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cohen-Shikora was doing too much at 10am.  Her poll everywheres never related to lecture, and then she would end up having to skip over slides for time.  The slides were never good, and didn't reflect what was in the textbook.  She said quizzes wouldn't be cumulative and then asked mainly questions from early lectures on later quizzes.

My inspiration, my muse, my campus celebrity, my why washu. Dr CS is the dopest, illest, kindest, loveliest, dankest professor I have ever had at this university. She deserves the world. Very interesting lectures, very engaging, very compassionate. Love her

Excellent professor! Lectures are clear and engaging, and she somehow manages to make stats a bit fun. Pace is very slow at first (spends 2 weeks explaining means), but speeds up by the end. Don't bother with reading textbook - just take notes and do assignments, and she makes it quite easy to get an A! Exams are easy as long as you study.

I love Dr. CS! She's fun, engaging, and makes the material very understandable. I had her for the paired stats-experimental classes, and I highly recommend it. Made stats 100% easier (I dropped it last semester), and experimental was easy but rewarding. Very complex ideas made to feel super simple because of how well they were explained.

Was a clear lecturer and made psych interesting and engaging. The structure/format of her lecture slides made navigating my notes for quizzes easy. Outside of class, she's super sweet and cares about her students.

Dr. CS is very sweet and truly cares about her students. Her lectures are clear, engaging, and easy to follow. Her quizzes were also easy and written well. She is accessible in office hours and answers Piazza consistently. Highly recommend!

Cohen-Shikora is one of the kindest and most genuine professors at WashU. I've had her for multiple semesters, and she's engaging, smart, and grades very fairly. She also goes out of her way to help students. Experimental psych isn't easy, but it's also a very reasonable class if you keep up with the workload.

ECS is in general a poor lecturer. Skips through the slides way too quickly to take good notes. Then she does not post the slides and makes you sift through the videos. Questions on quizzes are very specifically worded and have lots of technicalities or inconsistencies. Complains about her kids all the time as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cohen-Shikora was the saving grace of FYP. Her lectures were the only ones that made sense and kept me engaged. She seems very nice and her discussion sections were pretty fun. The feedback she gives on papers is kinda unhelpful but besides that she's a fine professor for lectures/ tests. I think she would do really well in a different class.

She's an amazing lecturer and really tries her best to make sure students fully understand the material. She even reviews topics from the previous lecture in almost every new lecture, and offers extra credit to help boost your grade! One of the best professors I've had so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. C-S is such a kind, caring professor. Stats isn't the most thrilling class, obviously, but she tries her best to make it as engaging as possible. Dr. C-S thoroughly explains each concept and does lots of helpful example problems in class. She's really dedicated to setting students up to succeed and is always ready to help in office hours!
you get out what you put in. not the most interesting class you will ever take, but you will definitely do well if you put in the work

She's a nice lady and is very helpful. Follows the textbook pretty closely but gives us recommended problems which is nice. She works out problems by hand in front of the class which is helpful as well. The latter part of the class I felt was a bit rushed. I would recommend taking her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She goes over easy material in excruciating detail and rushes through the difficult content, but does make herself accessible outside of class if you need help. This is about as good as it gets for a required class for a major.

A very rote-memorization professor. Puts in effort to drum up enthusiasm, but definitely falls flat often. That being said, basic statistics isn't the most abstract and conceptual subject, and I walked away knowing how to conduct hypothesis testing and such. Existence of 5 midterms are really annoying, but it's hard to fail the class.

Cohen- Shikora does a good job of making a pretty boring subject matter somewhat interesting. Her class is test heavy, 5 test including the final, and also has 3 computer assignment and chapter quizzes. You can not go to the class and survive but going to the lectures and doing the quizzes is the best way to do well.

Experimental is kind of boring, but she does her best to make it interesting, and the experiment we performed as a class was pretty neat.  Schedule for the class is weird - no work for weeks at a time and then you're suddenly swamped.  She's a good lecturer and explained things very well.

Pretty good class, kind of boring, not too much else to say.  Beware, the class starts out VERY slow (as in how to calculate a mean) but it ramps up to a normal level by the 3rd exam.  Definitely take it with Cohen-Shikora if you can, very nice, gives good examples, recognizes most people don't really like stats that much.

Dr. Finneran cares about her students and gives extensive feedback so that each student can improve. It seems that students either love her or hate her, which I think depends on how invested you are in the subject of the class (because yes, she does assign a lot of reading and writing). In my experience, she is not a tough grader.

Dr. Finneran is a very interesting person and a great professor!  Sometimes she will talk about things that don't make sense or feel relevant, but overall she gives great insight and leads good discussions about the readings.

She assigns a lot of readings, and even more supplementary readings, which are irrelevant in class. She has us read aloud the paragraph or two that she deems important from 27 page articles to discuss, and we all just ignore the rest. She is also a very tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Finneran doesn't really care about teaching. She only really cares about her books. And she expects you to know as much as her after decades. Its preposterous.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I will never take another course with her again. I seriously considered dropping the ampersand class I was in because of her as a teacher. Avoid her if you know what's good for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She doesn't care if you succeed. She just wants to further herself. She expects students to know the texts to the same degree that she does, regardless of the fact that we have 3 days to read it and she has had 30+ years to teach the same text.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hardly gives any feedback on assignments. Assigns an unmanageable amount of work for each class (reading 500+ pages per class)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is horrible. I don't want to sound mean, but she is the one teacher in all of my time as a student who really didn't like teaching or want to help students learn.
avoid her. she doesn't care about teaching
She gave random tests and quizzes contradictory to the syllabus and didn't really care about us learning, more about her telling us about what she thinks of the way we should think. This isn't psych.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really didn't like Dr. Finneran. She taught my Ampersand Ireland course, and she was horrific. She assigned a random pop quiz, which then translated to 3.33% of the final grade on the first day of a module, even when the syllabus says that we only have written assessments (i.e. papers). Avoid her at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Finneran didn't actually teach anything, she just told us her opinions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Erin Finneran is a horrific teacher. She is very opinionated and keeps going off on tangents in class about pop-culture references. I do not recommend in the slightest. If you have an opportunity to take your class with a different professor, seize the opportunity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Read everything if you want to do well, you have to be more insightful that her, which will go poorly if you disagree with her. Very rewarding if you pick a final pairing you care about, but you'll feel like you're slogging through all the unnecessary discussion posts that could just be in-person discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Finneran can, admittedly, be a lot to handle in the morning, but she's a passionate and caring professor who does her best to keep her class interested and engaged. She is incredibly knowledgeable and the feedback she gives on essays + her Tools for Writing Well module are invaluable. She is a bit out of touch, but overall she's a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: avoid her at all ur costs...

Erin is narcissistic and a good pickup artist. It's fun to see the way she downgrades you, but tbh, she's over 50 and still earns 5 figures as a lecturer...
For those ppl being demeaned but highly rated her, do y'all enjoy being masochists??
She is a joke....
This class is intense (lots of reading and writing) but so much fun. Grading isn't super hard as long as you're clearly making an effort and reading. Finneran is entertaining and kooky.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Will grade you based on whether she agrees with your argument, not how well you argue it. She only supports her interpretation and will reject yours. Any question she asks is just her trying to find a segway to talk about whatever she wants to talk about. Often condescending and wants you to be confused so she can explain it to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Faux humility and humble bragging; not recommended overall

Most tedious class I've ever had:(( It's ok if you just need a decent A, but u spent 3 hrs a week sitting in dull class and discussing outdated&wearisome topics- from ppl's face obviously u can see how they are waiting for class to end; she's incapable of teaching argumentation so the only thing I learned is arguing self to drop from her class AEAP

100% take this class with Finneran, it's her baby and she's super passionate about the subject. A good amount of writing (~500 words weekly) but it wasn't graded harshly, and felt necessary to process the big topics and complex theory. All writing was submitted via public Canvas discussion, so you also get to learn from other students' work too.

Dr. Finneran is an amazing professor. The class was challenging, but she held reasonable expectations and truly cared about the progress of each student. Her teaching was interesting and engaging. This class truly changed the way that I look at writing, and I would highly recommend.

I loved Erin Finneran. She was so helpful and intelligent, yet humble. She was relatable yet respected and super intelligent. She read our essays with genuine interest and care, and she took her students' lives very seriously. I felt safe and supported, yet pushed and challenged at the same time. I really feel grateful for having had her.

I love Dr. Finneran. She is an amazing academic and writer herself, you can tell she REALLY knows what she's talking about in this field of study, so her teaching is naturally incredibly helpful and rewarding. She cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I learned a lot and ended up satisfied with my progress as a writer.

I have immense respect for Professor Finneran. I've had her for two classes (Art of Poetry and currently, Modern Texts) and she always brings energy and wit regardless of the class size and time of day. Her lectures are incredible and never fail to shape my worldview to any degree. She is also flexible and understanding of individual circumstance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Finneran is one of my favorite professors I have had a WashU. She has pushed me to become a more thoughtful writer and is really passionate about what she teaches! She is also very forgiving when it comes to providing extensions on papers if you explain your situation. She cares about her students and always wants to help!

Finneran's humble bragging will remind you of her academic accomplishments. Her grading is inconsistent, and you'll receive higher grades as the semester goes on so she thinks you've improved as a writer. You'll waste time on tedious rewrites. You won't learn to be a better writer; you'll only learn to write how she wants you to, style be damned.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Finneran is one of my favorite professors at WashU. My writing skills are not strong, but I was still able to get an A on almost every assignment. She is understanding of different backgrounds and gives freedom on each assignment to write about something familiar to you. I would take a writing class again, only if my prof was Dr. Finneran!

Solid but not great teacher. Inconsistent grading on essays, gave me an A on the essay I did an hour before class after giving me a B on every essay before that. Class discussion is ok, but she really wants you to participate. Feedback is very helpful, especially in office hours.

Finneran has SO MUCH ENERGY. At 9 am it can be a bit overbearing, but she genuinely is passionate about Irish literature and she really wants you to feel the same way. Her grading is not too harsh and if you come to her with a specific reason for why you need more time or whatever she'll be happy to grant it. In general, no complaints!

Finneran knows what she is doing. Her class is hardly ever boring and she can be  entertaining in a goofy way. Has much knowledge of the subjects she teaches. But she also has this obsession with little details and perfectionism that makes the classes quite complicated. She does feel compelled to complicate matters sometimes.

Finneran's amazing! She has a wonderful spirit. She infused our class with passion and inspired each of us to do our best in life and in school. She helped create a community. And we all became huge fans of Irish literature, whether we had been or not before the class. Love EMF!
Insane amount of work compared to other college writing classes. Farrell is nice and caring but the workload made me wish I chose another class.

Citizen scientist is not an "easy A." You'll do good if you read the material, don't wait until last minute, and take his feedback seriously. Dr. Farrell is very intelligent and great for a good academic conversation. A lot of Chicago citations but he provides lots of thought-out feedback. Very fair even if you have different viewpoints.

Professor Farrell is a very nice person, and he genuinely wants to see you succeed. He is happy to meet with you outside of class. His grading can be very vague and ambiguous, which makes it hard to tell what you need to improve on the next time around. He is very picky about formatting. Be prepared to spend a lot more time than you expect.

Office hours weren't helpful, grading criteria is vague, discussions were boring, and there was no direction to them what so ever, maybe questions over the reading or things to think about would help. Grading for English in general is weird, what makes him entitled to give out grades. I ran my essay through diffrent professor said it was great.

Dr. Farrell is a kind and passionate professor who is deeply invested in his students' learning. Though he may seem intimidating at first, his discussion-based classes reveal his approachable and engaging style. The course is challenging but fair, with clear expectations and a thoughtful AI policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nathaniel Farrell for CWP Citizen Scientist was pretty good. He is overall a good and caring guy, and is ultimately happy to work with you and wants you to succeed. His essays, directions, and class style can be ambiguous and hard to understand exactly what he wants, but if you ask him, he is happy to clarify things or even meet outside class.

His class discussions are super engaging and so much fun, but you have to put in the work ahead of time (often medium-long readings) and during the class period (active participation). The essays work best if you check in with him (after class or office hours) a couple of times to get revisions. Also, he hands out 1-week extensions for free!
Very bad rubric and prompt is never clear. Skips me during office hours, letting other students who arrived after get help first. Also hurried me along one time to get to another student.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's lenient and a fair grader. Gives good feedback, and if you incorporate it well your grade will improve lots. You'll get out what you put into the class- probably the one of the most linear effort-to-reward classes there are.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had. His grading is unclear and subjective. He favors certain students, checking up w/ them after class. A classmate and I made similar mistakes on essays, but I was graded much more harshly. His office hours are unhelpful and vague. Lots of readings and a few papers, but appropriate for a 3-credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the worst prof ive ever had

As someone majoring in English...one of the worst professors I've ever had. He is vague and unclear with grading and carries a narcissistic, demeaning attitude towards students simply trying to improve their writing. I would advise you to take any other college writing class besides this one, even if it is work heavy.

Dr Farrell was a pretty great college writing teacher. He's a fairly lenient grader, classes are active and engaging, and his feedback and expectations are clear. I was surprised to see all the 1 star ratings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Farrell is very passionate and engages in class discussions. He gives vague instructions and has extremely high expectations that are poorly communicated. He is extremely nitpicky and sometimes straight-up condescending. If you want a chill College Writing, steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The instructions for assignments are vague and confusing, but if you ask him he will clarify. He is very nice and understanding. Pop quizzes on readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really sweet guy. Tough grader on essays but accessible for feedback. Pop quizzes on readings

Nathaniel is a very polarizing professor. The class focuses heavily on the readings, which there are a lot of, and not as much on writing. He often wants your papers to have a specific argument and it is very difficult to go against his view for paper. Some times class discussions great sometimes they are terrible. Only take this class if you care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: WILL COLD CALL YOU. Theres a lot of reading and it will hurt your brain. Tough grader but will help you with your essay if you seek out help. Took The Scholar and Social Change and got an A. Class is discussion based and grade is only a few things. VERY LENIENT WITH DEADLINES
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Farrell is fantastic. Just get prepared for the class discussion and work hard on the revision.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Nathaniel was the best introduction I could've had to WashU. He has a genuine interest in course topics, making class discussions insightful and engaging. Through Nathaniel's thoughtful feedback and guidance, my writing skills significantly improved. Nathaniel is very understanding and it is clear he only has the students' best interest in mind.

Professor Farrell is an excellent teacher. He is caring, understanding, and is genuinely passionate about the course material. If you contribute meaningfully to class discussions and take the time to write solid essays you will get strong marks.

I could not recommend a more dedicated and thoughtful professor! After having Dr. Farrell for 2 semesters, I have walked away with an incredible improvement in my ability to write and think critically. He has a great way of pulling unique ideas and genuine intellectual curiosity out of all his students. He's also very understanding with due dates.

Professor Farrell was very accommodating with personal issues and extensions and gave good feedback on the essays. He clearly cares about his students and is passionate about the class's topics. He puts a lot of thought into the material and grading. However, it's a hard class that requires reading that may be boring if you're not intersted.

Good person, cares about students, passionate about course. By no means an easy class; you need to do 15-40 pg readings before almost every class and be prepared to discuss (or take a pop quiz) on them. Three essays that need (!) to be high-quality. Course certainly improved my writing, he gives really thoughtful/insightful comments on drafts.
Farrell made citizen scientist really interesting and thought provoking. Although this will not be a walk in the park, I think my writing skills improved greatly, don't shy away from Farrell!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nathaniel is a quirky and kind guy. He is incredibly knowledgeable about literally everything and is good at leading discussions, although he can be a bit pretentious about his own interpretations of readings. The class isn't very structured, but when it comes to developing paper writing skills he gives thoughtful and helpful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Nathaniel is a great professor. He is caring and cordial when it comes to his relationships with students, and meeting with him for help outside of class is greatly useful. That said, CWP112 is a lot of work, so stay on top of it.

I didn't rate him a 5 because I found his lectures and instructions somewhat convoluted sometimes, but this was minor.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The course requires time set aside for some content-heavy but very interesting readings, but it isn't much work if you just participate and do the readings. Farrell is very understanding overall, cares about your growth as a writer, gives good feedback, and clearly states what he expects in drafts and revisions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor was nice, go to his office hours, very helpful. There's a lot of tough articles we had to read, so set time aside for them. A lot of short essays and long essays throughout the semester. Overall, I learned a lot from this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Farrell gets hate because CW is a required class&no one wants to take it, but the hate is kinda undeserved. He's not the easiest grader, but if you put effort into your essays you'll do well. Participation in class matters, so make sure to do the readings. Overall, content was genuinely interesting; you can tell he tries&cares! Very understanding!

The class is a decent amount of reading, but the readings are normally interesting and are applied in class discussions. Grading was fair - the average on most papers was around 90%. Farrell was understanding of extenuating circumstances and was available outside of class regularly.

A lot of students complain about Farrel, but if you get to know him, he's actually a very caring professor. You have to talk during office hour to get an A. Very interesting lectures and engaging reading materials, which separates him from the mediocre writing professors.

You can't just skate by and expect and A, but you probably won't get a C or D either. Grade is very based off of essays. If you at least skim the readings most of the time, try to participate in the class (usually very interesting), and put effort into your final essay drafts (only 3 essays), you should do very well. Very nice/smart prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: so picky. and if you don't agree with him you basically fail. he assigns so much work for no reason. like this aint prelaw u aint a real prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Gives great feedback on essays and gives you a lot of freedom on the research essay.

Has a very one-dimensional view towards any of the assigned readings. Although there is no right or wrong interpretation of a text, be prepared to get shut down in class discussions. He is also very unclear and vague in essay instructions and the feedback given during office hours is also useless and vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The WORST teacher I've had in college/high school. He's super pretentious in an earthy, "I'm saving the environment and I'm a poet" way and is such a hard grader that it destroys your confidence in your writing, not helps it. I say this as an honors English major who cares deeply for the environment. Please do yourself a favor and which out!

professor for college writing 1. he is a very opinionated adjunct professor who has his certain way of looking at the text--either you agree, or you do poorly on his essays.  also, very strong favoritism towards people who participate in class (giving some people rewrites and not others)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Forough makes it clear from the beginning that this class will be difficult, but she does an amazing job preparing her students for exams. Through solving problems in class, homework that reflects the content, and even practice exams... the class content is easy to follow.

Im ngl Im writing this right after I just had the test. It genuinely had me praying for guidance from above. I thought I was prepared with my cheat sheet but the test was nothing like the practice test. She does give fun attendance quizzes tho.
Great professor explains concepts clearly and makes the class engaging

Her grading scale is honestly very fair and equitable to all students (different weight for each exam). She does have a monotonous tone while lecturing (a fact she admits), but you can watch her lectures at 1.5x speed after class. Her exams are pretty fair, and as long as you do the homework and practice exams, this class is not too hard.

Everyone says DAT220 is easy, but it wasn't intuitive to me at all. Lectures are boring, but she cares a lot about student success + wellbeing. Has attendance quizzes every class (attached with a fun fact). Assignments are easy and exams are similar to practice exams.

She is a great professor, but I do not think the class is very helpful for improving technical skill. If you want to learn coding, just go to a random CS course. You will learn several model for basic analytics, and you will deal with excel for a long time in this course. They are easy, but grading is kind of strict.
Forough is dope. She loves her students (despite her monotony lol) and makes the content easy to understand. Also has the best attendance system in Olin.

Provides helpful lecture note packets, but a large portion of grading is not on demonstrating an understanding of the actual material, but instead writing it in the way that she wants/shows in lecture. Otherwise a good prof.
Such an easy class. Prof is a bit monotone but I found her very nice and funny. She is super understanding as well.

Very nice and very helpful. The entire course is organized extremely well, which makes learning content and keeping up with things much easier. Content seems hard at first but is presented in an easily digestible way. Exams are fair and you are allowed cheat sheets. Genuinely seemed to care about her students in and out of the classroom.
Amazing professor. Most organized professor, teaches important concepts that would help outside class too. Highly reccomend.

One of my favorite classes taken at washu. Lectures can sometimes get a bit boring, but if you follow along with her notes, it makes the problems on homeworks and exams way more doable. In class, she tells you exactly what she is looking for in grading, and she cares about learning more than grades. The material we learned was very practical.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really like how this class was set up. The expectations were all set and the grading was super cut and clean. I love how she does the problems in class. We learned coding this sem with anaconda. That was super fun. Overall do well on the homework and exams. There are a lot of TA office hours, which was nice. She is the best!

Forough is one of my favorite professors I have had so far at WashU! This is not a hard class. Exams are weighted so that your worst score is only worth about 17% of your grade. Yes, the problem sets can be a bit tricky but if you take advantage of office hours you will be fine. The class was very interesting, we learned Excel Solver and SQL.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's clearly a nice person, knowledgeable, and grading was very fair, but she's a boring lecturer.

Does not post annotated lecture slides which makes doing the problem sets very difficult as you have to go back and rewatch hour and a half long lecture videos. Problem sets are also a large percentage of grade which makes it frustrating when it's hard to find the notes from class. Also goes very quickly in class which makes her hard to follow.
She is very nice and clearly cares about the subject material. However, not engaging during class: speaks very softly, doesn't repeat herself, and asks questions in the form of statements.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really liked Prof. Ahangar. I was prepared to dislike her because I hate statistics and usually don't do well, but I enjoyed this class. If you pay attention and do the homework, you'll be good. I half-paid attention in class and did well w/ homework and did average. She has a dry sense of humor & you can tell that she cares about her students (:

I really liked her class because I could tell how knowledgeable she is. This was her first semester and she adapted to students' complaints when they did poorly on homework and exams simply because they didn't pay attention in class. Her practice exams were similar to the real exam, all based on the homework assignments we had.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Funny guy and somewhat engaging class- some lecture days were boring and he can be kind of a tough grader, but you just put in a bit of honest effort for the essays with some office hour visits and and an A is very achievable. Have an open mind to the class, participate a little bit and its alright. Nice guy too, wrote a letter of rec for me after

Jason does a great job inspiring thought-provoking conversations. Grading criteria was always very clear, so just follow the rubrics and pay attention in class when he goes over essay expectations. He's also super funny.
Makes me want to quit my philosophy minor.

Professor Gardner is clearly very knowledgeable about phil and does a decent job teaching the course. It's just very monotonous if you aren't super passionate about philosophy. He's not a mean grader-- just fair, and even though he doesn't take attendance, it will factor into your participation grade. He's very honest--all around nice guy.

Dr Gardner was a decent professor. He always was able to answer questions people asked, which made the class more engaging. The structure of his class is strange: no electronics and no notes whatsoever. Just an hour and a half of straight philosophy. Maybe if you enjoy philosophy, you'd find his teaching style fun, but wasn't for me personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Homework is all completion and takes like 2 minutes if you do the readings (I did not). Attendance isn't mandatory, but there is a participation point thing, so if you miss classes, you better speak a lot. Cool professor that had great, in-depth responses to basically every philosophical thing you threw at him.

I really enjoyed this class. Maybe I just got lucky because all my classmates were very active, but Jason was able to speak on everything at length, the syllabus fit together perfectly, and the essays were challenging but made me learn significantly.

Do people at WashU just hate thinking? I took this class at SLU, and Jason knows the texts front to back, has a great dry wit, actually cares about your ideas, and is extremely reasonable about everything (e.g., grading, lectures, paper topics). Could not ask for a better philosophy professor.

Gardner is emotionless--quite weird. Did not make any connections with students. Honestly try and participate in the beginning so he remembers you. Was not helpful during office hours--meet with the TA, so much nicer and graded everything. Did not make much of an effort to create an inclusive environment to encourage people to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is decent (at best). Do not waste your time. Not even a professor he's a lecturer so at the very least there is no need for him to shame students or treat them so poorly.

Poorly taught class, everything is graded by the TA. Student Beware, you will not earn above a B in his classes. Make sure you put this class on pass/fail early on because professors and TAs will give out high grades during the beginning of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jason Gardner, this professor is one that is very 'big' on mental health. He doesnt gaf.
wouldn't take him again. dont waste your time. class is pretty easy but if you need an extension he will ignore your email. does not care about mental health.
Classes were hit and miss. Some days were interesting and thought-provoking, while others were incredibly dull. Overall a decent professor

Jason was kind as a professor. He offered extensions as long as the privelege isn't abused. The class itself is relatively boring. If you participate during class, your grade should be fine. Expect homework based on the readings after each class. Not the most engaging class and essay assignments were more difficult than expected. Only 3/semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The readings are engaging, but the actual lectures are not because we spend up to 30 minutes on one topic at a time. Since there is a no-technology policy, it is excruciating to sit there for that long and listen as he repeats what everyone said back to them. Tough grader on essays, almost no personality.

I absolutely loved this class. The readings were so interesting and I found the essay topics thought provoking. However, Professor Gardner is a tough grader. Overall, has been my most interesting class at WashU
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is not personable at all. If something in your life unexpectedly happens or something else, he does not care. Probably the worst professor I have ever encountered. Even if something happens out of your control, he will make it known that he does not care.

class was very interesting. imo he treats women like they are dumb when they talk in class. its like he will repeat your comment and then mansplain it back, doesnt do this with men tho. topics in the course were very thought provoking.

Be prepared to speak up a lot in class, but every class is mostly just going through the readings from that week and having students ask questions about it or challenge certain ideas. There is homework due every class but it's nothing too time-consuming, just short summaries of the readings and questions you had about them. Interesting class!

Prof. Gardner was super understanding, gave extensions as long as you didn't abuse the privilege, and was very accessible outside of class for questions and advice on papers. He was clear in class, gave students space to ask any questions and offer opinions, and clearly went over grading protocols. I would definitely take his class again!

I took Phil 120F with Jason. I'm not sure why his rating is only 3/5. The pros most certainly outweigh the cons. He is a great, engaging lecturer who makes sure students enjoy class time through dialogical, classroom discussion. These discussions include several deep, interesting thought experiments! He is, however, a little tough on essay-grading.
Attendance is not mandatory. He will say it is. Would not take again, Prof. Gardner is not understanding about mental health. Don't waste your time.

BME was such an interesting class! You'll cover a wide variety of topics and it can feel a little bit like whiplash at times. Classes are heavily discussion-based so make sure you do the readings prior to class otherwise you will be totally lost. Prof. Gardner is very open to hearing all opinions and offers counter opinions only when needed.

Professor Gardner's class, Problems in Philosophy, is relatively standard with clear criteria of what is expected. Complete the homework (less than an hour each week) and participate in class (ask questions!) and you'll do well.

Class was a little too heavy on discussion, but did pull a lot of concepts from a lot of different writers which was nice. Met with him a bunch outside of class; good explanations, dry humor, great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Hard grader on essays (even if you go in for office hours). Take the midterms instead of doing the essay options.

One of those professors who you just have to tell them what they want to hear. Appreciated that they did bring writings from different authors into the discussion, however. The class was horribly structured though, student discussion is important but we wasted altogether too much time on it. I'd rather hear the expert talk most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took biochem with Dr. Patti a few years ago. He is a great lecturer, but I felt more than slightly deceived when I realized in graduate school that all of his lecture material and figures are adapted verbatim from a different biochem textbook (Lehninger) without attribution
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just finished my 2nd yr of med school. I can't emphasize enough how influential Prof Patti's class has been. The guy has a truly amazing mind. Learning how he organizes metabolism is worth taking his class alone, plus he gives the best lectures. Keep your notes. You won't find the material in any textbook, at least not in such a logical format.

If you want to experience the hell of biochemistry, just come and take Gary's class. He is the most awful lecturer I have ever seen. He is good at being a hypocrite smiling to everyone but also degrading everyone in front of other professors. 

As known the star of Chemistry Department, Gary even does not give a sht to other faculties.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Patti gives good lectures but clearly doesn't like interacting with students, he's never available. He also doesn't provide a clear rubric for grading, and undergrad and grad students in the class receive wildly different grades for the same work. After reading a few of his papers it seems like he just dumbs down stuff he wrote the book on.

Can't say enough about Dr. Patti- I love this man. Best professor at WashU. His lectures are engaging and clear. His tests and quizzes are hard but fair. He demands you learn the material and not just memorize it. He cares deeply about the subject and his students, and is happy to help students outside of class. Don't miss out on taking his class!
Taking this class was the best decision I made in college.

Best class and best prof I had at wu, by a lot. Made me realize that most classes at wu are just pure memorization. Take this class if you really want to learn science. I actually took biochm 2 for credit twice. Once w/ Patti and once w/ someone else. They let you because they know how diff Patti does it. Not even close-Patti is the absolte best.

Had heard great things about this class. It's more than lived up to the reputation. Single most influential class I have taken. Makes a lot of stuff you learn in undergrad click for the first time. All science majors should definitely take it.
First time I've ever not wanted a semester to end.

If you're premed, definitely take this class, because it makes metabolism in med school SO much easier. Dr Patti integrates biochem with basic pathology (diabetes, hypercholesterolemia, etc) in a way that makes you really THINK, and completely changed the way I approached science. Go to office hours with q's- he's a delight to talk to and be around

Everyone told me to take this class because "Pattie is so amazing"...I don't see it.  He is rather rude, and he does not like interacting with students.  The grading on the weekly quizes is arbitrary.  He gets irritated when students ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Truly an amazing class and an incredible professor. Having just finished biochem in med school, at some point I only used his old notes for metabolism instead of books or notes from med school. The way he teaches it is honestly brilliant and makes it very intuitive. Hard work, but by far the most rewarding class I took at WU!!

This was probably my second favorite class, behind Chem 111.  Patti is wicked smart, and he is a serious researcher.  He tries very hard to bring the material, which is pretty much his research, down to a level we can understand.  I like the material, I just wish he cared more about all of the students, not just the star students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Patti has had the single most significant impact on shaping my life. I'd be following a very different path had I not taken his class.
I'm now in my first year of medical school. So far, this class has been the most helpful in preparing me out of those I took in undergrad.

Dont take Krezel. He's boring and you won't  learn anything. If you only need 1 semester of biochem, take Patti.  He will waive the first semester pre-req.  I dropped Krezel and still did well with patti.

Do everything you can to take biochem with Patti. He only teaches every other year, but he is definitely the best by far. It's tough, but you'll truly learn and he lowers the cutoffs in the end so everyone does pretty well. Awesome class--best science class at WashU.
Interesting material presented in a dynamic and compelling way. My favorite class in my college career. Smart, clear, organized, and helpful professor. A must take class.

Taught by one of the best professors at WashU. Even though I did not do particularly well in the class i can honestly say this is one of those life changing classes. Makes you see the world in a totally different light. Amazing teacher, amazing class.

Patti is awesome.  Professors like him are why I'll miss WU when I graduate.  He truly cares about students.  He was willing to meet with me personally and talk about anything.  Then he followed up with me several times to make sure I was doing OK.  Changed my perspective of science and my career direction.  Best class at WU.
Hardest class Ive taken. Its tough but you really learn. Didn't like the guy honestly but he can teach.
Wish Patti taught both semesters of biochem.  I would have probably changed my major to biochem.
Hands down, most enjoyable class I've taken at washu.
I'll make it simple. The best science course I have ever taken and I am not a pre-med student. I'm actually considering switching my career path because of Dr. Patti.

Patti is the absolute best of the Biochemistry teachers.  He only teaches every other year, so plan ahead.  He really knows his stuff - impressive mind.  His background in medicine and chemistry puts a great perspective on the biology.  He has great TAs also.
I didn't appreciate science until I took his course.

Class requires a lot of effort but is taught at a high level. Definitely worth it. I am consistently rocking the Biological section on practice MCATs. I give much credit to this class for my scores--a lot is familiar from class.  Prof Patti is awesome. Great teacher and, without question, most well dressed and attractive prof I've had at WU.

Incredible class. Lectures are early but prof's excitement kept me engaged. Class was well organized and lectures entertaining, but exams are extremely difficult and early (boo!!). Great for premeds. Dr Patti's application examples are fascinating and relevant to practical things like fat, exercise, vitamins--types of examples you never forget.

If you are premed, I highly recommend this class.  I expect this to be one of the most useful classes I took as an undergrad.  It is hard, but you could not ask for a better professor.  He emailed me personally several times in the semester to follow up on questions I asked.  You will learn a lot!

Best class I have taken at Wash U.  Dr. Patti's lectures are amazing.  He is full of energy and the most enthusiastic instructor I have had here.  Did not expect much going in, but his class changed my opinion of biochem and what I want to do in science/medicine.  Pretty challenging, but rewarding.  Great class!!

Excellent lecturer, friendly, willing to help students. Exams are difficult. It may take some time and effort getting used to his test questions. Quizzes are reasonable as long as you study the material. I strongly recommend this class. For pre-med students, this course prepares you very well for the biological sciences section of the MCAT.

Prof Patti is a great lecturer and this class WILL DEF prepare you for medical school.  Great class overall.  Exams are hard, but fair and you can do well if you study hard and talk to him.  Office hours are really helpful to help with logic.  Good to take with Cell Bio, which is all memorization but Patti's class sort of explains it all.

Class discussions are designed to discuss only what she would like to, and she asks vague questions, looking for a specific answer. She's definitely better in a small group, and her assignments are pretty fun. Definitely have to suck up to her and put in a lot of effort to receive a decent grade. Her grading is also strange and confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Gao-Miles is a terrible teacher. By far the most reading intensive class, and I was taking three Literature courses that semester. She expects detailed notes and perfect recollection of readings, and she will create quizzes that test only your ability to memorize. Assignments are also boring and almost impossible in the time she gives.

This was the most frustrating class. She assigned so much reading but classes were an exact regurgitation of the reading. If anyone strayed from restating the reading, she shut them down. She graded very few things and was not clear. Grades weren't put in until the end of the semester: I thought I was doing ok, then surprised with a lower grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 1) You will never get full points on an assignment in this class, there will always be 0.5ish points taken off for not following the vague instructions 2) she does not allow for her class to be taken pass/fail 3) her classes have intriguing content and are supposed to be very discussion-based, but she will end up talking for the majority of it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Probably better off avoiding; as other reviews have said, vague instructions but specific grader

Avoid: 1.Vague instructions you get docked for 2.grades assignments on letter grade meaning you usually get 93 on basic assignments 3.Talks during discussion herself and asks leading questions looking for specific answers 4. Expresses disappointment in us OFTEN 5.insane amount of reading on some classes, especially for a first year seminar.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Gao-Miles is not understanding with predicaments that come to her students, such as a book being backordered. She also gives extremely vague instructions for her assignments and then grades off of a rubric she made up in her head without telling us. Also expects hours of reading and note-taking before class and calls it all "easy".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Gao-Miles can be a very sweet professor if you attend her classes and kiss her butt, but if you're a mediocre or quiet student, don't expect too much from her. Participation and attendance are mandatory. She gives vague details on her assignments and then takes off points for the criteria not mentioned.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Guy is a very kind professor. Lectures are hilarious and genuinely make my day, although sometimes he can be a little difficult to follow. He tries his best to make his class not stressful for students e.g. untimed exams, plenty of TA office hours to get help on homework, etc. Exams are weighted heavily but very doable.
Guy is one of the best professors and men I know. He's everything I want to be in life and more.
He's great!

Guy is genuinely the best. He was amazing in class and OH, explained things clearly and in an amusing way, and his class was a great time. HW is challenging, but it is expected that you will go to OH so there are a bunch of options. Plus, he grades his exams very conceptually so if you know what to do and he can see that you will get full marks.
We love guy!!
Genin = Goated Chad Engineer

Genin made the lectures extremely entertaining! Sometimes it was a bit hard to follow what was going on in the in-class lectures. In general though, the content was fairly straightforward and there was lots of partial credit given for assignments/exams.

Professor Genin is the best professor at WashU. He is how I imagined college professors to be: energetic, enthusiastic about the material and a stress-free classroom. He is clearly a super smart guy who knows a ton about the field. 100% recommend anyone to take him even if you aren't really into the topic he is teaching.
A chad of a professor, emphasizes learning over grades so it's a stress-free experience. Overall 10/10
Love this professor, literally stood on a table to demonstrate what he was talking about and to get the students engaged.

Guy is one of the best professors at WashU- an engaging and entertaining lecturer, very patient and helpful at explaining concepts, and cares so much about his students. He takes the time to get to know everyone and encourages us to collaborate and form community. If you put in the work, you will do well. Wish every professor was like him.

Genin is without a doubt the best professor I've had. He has an obvious passion for the subject and it shows in his teaching. In a class of 60+ people, he made an effort to know each of our names and get to know us personally. 12/10 would take another class with him.

Incredible professor and a great person overall. He is extremely knowledgable in so many areas within all Engineering fields and will do everything he can to help you succeed, both in his class and in general.
He is extremely intelligent and knows what he is teaching.  He is fair and keeps the class fun and interesting!
By far my favorite professor ever! He is extremely accessible and willing to help. He also has a great sense of humor and keeps the class fun!

Made things interesting and fun.  Knew the material very well.  Extremely available to and concerned for students.  Anybody who offers to have office hours on Saturday night is indeed in a class of their own.

Genin is a brilliant man. He is great to talk to in person, and very helpful. His lectures aren't very clear though. The course needs a new book, Genin didn't teach the same way as the one we used, so we couldn't use the book for help, and the problems he taught in class and tested on were different than the ones assigned out of the book.
Amazing proffesor and person.  Need help with anything, just ask him.  Very easy to talk to.  Everyone needs to experiance his teaching.
Amazingly good professor. Adjust your schedule to take him, it is well worth it. Makes otherwise dry material come to life. Also is concerned about students, not only about the course itself
Great person and an even better professor
He's an awesome professor and is really approachable and helpful.
Great professor! Very funny and easy to get along with. Teaches very well! The test questions are hilarious.
The best engineering professor I've had in 3 1/2 years.
funny teacher
He is almost always in his office willing to help out with anything.  He is incredibly dedicated to his students.
very funny, somewhat paranoid, but very interested in subject matter and easy to understand and approach for questions
Very entertaining, helpful, concerned for students, makes his classes interesting
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
A really funny teacher who cares alot about his studnet and the subject. He would even let the classes to rest if he sense the class is not absorbing the materials
He explains concepts well and gave out prizes for winning kahoots. I like him.
Very rude and not helpful. Always makes students aware he is disappointed in them and a very hard grader.

Hugh Wu himself is a really nice guy. He really gives Asian dad energy: kinda stiff/awkward but wants you to succeed. First few weeks are meant to intimidate; after that, he never cold calls and material is way easier. Super responsive to feedback, easy to reach outside of class. Lectures are boring but not his fault the material is meh. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Asian dad vibes. Lectures are a bit boring but he posts recordings + slides after class. Go to class b/c TAs track participation. Curved exams, manageable if you study. TAs are helpful for hw. After midsemester evals he adjusted his teaching style and let us drop an extra hw assignment. Overall very responsive to feedback and wants you to succeed.
My favorite class for the semester because of Wu, who clearly cares a lot about students' learning and wellbeing. A great teacher and an even better person!
Such an amazing professor! I really enjoyed the classes. MGT is a course that helps you grasp the fundamental principles of the business world.
AMAZING PROFESSOR EVER! I really enjoyed the classes. MGT is a course that help you grasp the very foudamental principles of business.

The first few weeks were definitely heavy, but things got better later on and felt more manageable. Some topics were a bit boring, but he did what he could to make them more interactive and fun. On a personal level, he is really caring and understanding, listens to feedback, and is very approachable if you ever need anything outside of class.

A lot of the reviews here are biased. Wu's class isn't very engaging, but it means you'll have an easier time in class overall. His class has a smaller size, and since the MGT final selects 2 students from each professor's class, there's a higher chance of being chosen for the final compared to Oren's class.

The lectures are very fast paced and often times new materials are not explained well or expanded upon. Subsection is pointless and the ta's are very unorganized. The exams are very difficult and are graded very harshly. Little instruction is ever given on assignments, and ta's always offer conflicting information.

Met with him several times to receive feedback and deferred to the TA's every time, who were extremely unhelpful. He is also really bad at answering questions on the material. Basically said on the first day if you haven't taken micro then you are at a severe disadvantage - Why not restructure the course then? Not like we ever used the micro stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is very nice and approachable. The TAs are also helpful and always available to answer questions. The first test is on the tougher side, but the curve helps balance things out. Overall, it's a solid class, especially if you stay on top of the material and take advantage of the resources offered.

He is very lecture heavy but not engaging at all. He keeps a monotonous tone throughout and when you have him as you 8:30AM professor, it is a battle not to fall asleep. Tests were fair, the curve helped too. Even when others tell you that the exams get easier, keep studying to beat the curve and get a good grade.

This class is very poorly designed. The lectures are dry, Hugh just reads off slides and his explanations to questions are insufficient and difficult to understand. Aside from this, the course does not teach anything meaningful, it is just meant to be difficult for students. Grading criteria is heavily dependent on which TA you get.
Loved this course! Everything is quite  straightforward and Prof. Wu is very fair. The class is well-organized and topics are interesting and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor was fine for a class that isn't great. Lectures aren't overly interesting but attendance is required. First test is HARD (avg was a 59%) but after that it gets better. Be prepared to read + study a lot, as well as put a lot of work into the case competition.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You definitely will need to do the work for this class, but as long as you do the work and go to office hours with TAs, you should be fine. Sometimes, he is a bit hard to understand, and occasionally, if you ask questions, the answers are slightly convoluted. Wu teaches concepts as interesting as he can and does want every student to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Wu teaches alright, he uses examples during class to connect the material, and if you closely listen to him and clearly understand what he is saying, you will most likely be fine. If you don't understand anything that he said, talk to TAs, he isn't good at answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Class is very poorly designed. You won't actually learn anything too meaningful or useful, but the class makes you work extremely hard if you want a decent grade. Case Comp teammates can make or break the whole semester. Hugh is a dry lecturer, not helpful when you ask him questions. I'd say about 5% of the TA's actually know the content well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wu is a pretty dry lecturer overall, and tests are hard (but curved to the point where it doesn't matter). MGT100 is a poorly designed class in general (case comp is a ton of work that feels rather meaningless), and TA subsection is useless. Be ready to do lots of work. Wu also takes the class a bit too seriously, but it's not a dealbreaker.

MGT100 is an incredibly informative class, and Dr. Wu is a great professor for it. However, it is also incredibly difficult, especially if you have no prior microeconomics experience or get a bad roll on case competition teammates. Wu is dry but the content is (IMO) very interesting. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is a nice person and he is very knowledgeable about the content. The course has a heavy workload, but the materials are useful and very applicable to the real world. Learned quite a lot through lectures and the case competition.

Not the greatest lecturer. Explained concepts decently but answered people's questions poorly. Tests are hard but class is curved so it's fine. Definitely meant to scare first year b schoolers/BUCS. Eh professor/class overall.

Very standard MGT 100 class. I could understand the lectures clearly (lectures were sometimes very monotone and boring) with the help of some TAs. Professor Wu is soft-spoken, kind, and helpful if you approach him. I recommend reading the course pack (it's ok if you don't) and taking advantage of his office hours (no one goes, so why not).
Case Comp is very time-consuming, and lectures were often difficult to understand. Hard to determine your final grade until it is given since everything is curved at the end.

The goal of MGT100 is to honestly frighten students a bit. At first, it will feel like Hugh is the driest and least caring professor. By the end of the class, he will probably start to lighten up (not too much though), and you'll understand that he cares, but not in the conventional ways you've known before. My advice: study, study, study.

I will concede that Hugh's lectures can be pretty dry given his monotone voice, but he is a very knowledgable person and makes things easy to understand. About the course, MGT 100 is graded heavily by case comp, and 3 exams. The case comp is pretty easy, but the exams are a little more annoying. They are poorly worded, but the curve is generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be prepared to work hard. 3 exams through out semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The grading on the case comp is harsh. Exams are not that hard if you fully understand all the concepts in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is nice and clearly wants his students to learn. That said, his lectures can be quite dry, and he is not great at giving constructive feedback. All grading is done by TA's, so your only interactions with him will be during lectures. My biggest critique is that MGT 100 exams are poorly written and hard to understand.

I disagree with all past reviews. Jason was constantly sexist. Not intentionally, but it was uncomfortable. He doesn't do his own job and is proud. I'm concerned this man is such a big deal in the research he does. He thinks AI is the best and uses it to make his exams and slides. Exams are TRICKY--must memorize exactly what is on the AI slides.

JASON IS AWESOME!! A very engaging, funny professor who makes the content so interesting and comes to class with the perfect level of energy and optimism. One of the only classes I've been actually excited to go to in the morning. Exams are not the easiest, but are very fair and not worth much of your grade. Absolutely take this class!!

Highly recommend this class! You'll learn interesting topics from a professor who is genuinely passionate about what he does. He's truly interested in each individual student, and his humor makes lectures entertaining and fun. Sometimes test questions were confusing even though I studied, but they make up only 30% of the grade so I still got an A.

Interesting and low workload. Caring professor that wants you to do well. 2 exams (15% each, study 3-5 hours max). Take some notes in class or just study off the slides and you'll do fine. 1 creative assignment (10%, takes 4-5 hours). 1 eight page final paper, but with relaxed guidelines. Maybe 20 hours outside of class the whole semester.

BY FAR my favorite professor and class so far at WashU. His lectures are fascinating and clear. He is very caring and understanding with his students and creates a vibe in the class that is so positive and supportive. Class is easy to do well in if you study a bit. 10/10. I genuinely enjoyed attending class. Take him, and you'll thank me later.

My queen. If you can take any intro physics professor, it should be Hynes. She explains concepts in a way that's accessible to beginners (other professors… not so much). She's so kind and wants her students to succeed.

If I could recommend any physics professor, it would be Dr. Hynes! She teaches physics in a way that's accessible to beginners (other professors in the department… not so much). She's very detailed in her explanations & cares about helping students outside of class. The class itself is pretty difficult, but she makes it more manageable.
She is extremely engaging in class. Her lectures are awesome and she really helps you understand physics. The class might be hard but she is definitely the best.

Her lectures were so clear and engaging. I previously hated physics but because of her I began to enjoy the subject. Super approachable and easy to ask questions to, overall incredible professor and incredible person
Big lecture room, hard to follow along at times. Sometimes she would rush through things then get flustered and make mistakes along the way.

This is for Physics 191 and 192. Professor Hynes is an amazing lecturer, explains concepts clearly and welcomes all questions. Her teaching style is perfect for students who like taking thorough notes. She's also incredibly kind and supportive, which makes a big difference. Concept-wise, physics is challenging, but manageable and not impossible.

Professor Hynes was an amazing professor! she takes the time to explain the concepts very clearly, and is always available after class to answer any questions you have. She is very energetic while teaching, and brings cool demos to class!

I didn't have a strong physics background before taking this class, but Professor Hynes helped me greatly develop my confidence in physics. She shows a great enthusiasm for the subject, which enhances the lectures. She gives great examples during class. She is very accessible for questions after class as well.
Hynes is an amazing professor. Her lectures were very clear and she does a great job of explaining difficult content. Definitely take Hynes if you can for physics.

hynes is an amazing professor that is passionate and prepared. she cares about her students. id recommend going to office hours, they're right after class and the homework is hard, and there's a lot of it. would recommend
