Professor Hynes is a deeply caring and sweet professor who often stayed 30 mins extra every office hour. Her handwriting is super neat and color coded! Lectures were easy to follow but sometimes slow paced. Exams were similar to past exams and lots of extra credit is given! Pro tips: do the weekly quizzes in office hours.
Clear lectures, Sending lots of love to physics department bc of the generous grading and clear instructions

I've never liked physics that much but Hynes brings lots of fun energy to class making it surprisingly enjoyable. She is an engaging lecturer and takes time to answer questions and make things as clear as possible. She is very accessible outside of class and very accommodating. She cares a lot about students and is one of the better profs I've had.

Love Dr. Hynes! She really made physics dynamic and interesting, even to a physics skeptic. She clearly has a lot of passion for teaching and it shows in the lectures -- always prepared and welcomes questions. Her in-class demonstrations were fun and memorable. Overall 10/10
Professor Hynes is very caring, clear, and prepared. She engages with the class and does her best to make sure everyone understands each concept. Would highly recommend taking her class.

Professor Hynes is great at what she does. She plans her lectures well and does everything in her ability to cover as much examples as possible. However, there are times where she is unable to complete some examples (though she does post solutions), and this is due to many different reasons that include students bombarding her with questions.

Dr. Hynes regularly makes mistakes when solving problems in lecture. Poor time management in lecture and often is scrambling and rushing to finish problems at the end of class. Take other profs if you can. However, she is a very nice person and is very open to answering questions.
Queen. Her lectures are very straight forward and she walks you through how to solve each problem.

Hynes is one of the best professors I have ever had, if not the absolute best. Cares so much about her students and puts so much effort into her lectures. Genuinely wants you to learn and will do whatever she can to help you. Also has amazing outfits.

Hynes is no-questions-asked one of the best professors at WashU. Take her. Her lectures are amazing and she's a genuinely kind person who is helpful during office hours. Lectures walk you through problems and show you exactly how to solve them. She makes sure everybody understands.

Dr. Hynes is incredibly clear in her lectures and takes extra time to ensure that everyone in the room understands. Even if you don't have a good physics or math background, she will be with you every step of the way to be sure you succeed. Also, attend the exam review sessions. There is always an example question in there that helps on the exams.

Hynes is a very nice person but tends to teach about 1 lecture behind everyone else. This means you don't know the material in time for the weekly quizzes. I would probably go for Medieros, everyone seems to like him, but definitely the second-best physics prof and she always teaches the 10 am section which is well-timed and fills up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally the sweetest professor ever. Physics is a difficult subject by nature, but she explains it in a way which is both understandable and interesting. Sometimes I feel as if she goes a bit too slow for my preference, but other than that she is an excellent professor!

Easily the best intro phys professor. I actually had a different teacher but ended up just watching all of her lecture recordings. My ability to do the homework skyrocketed after I made that decision.

extremely kind and answers questions well. could go more in depth into explanations but its an intro class i guess. this is more of a critique of the classroom itself but 90% of people there are premeds and are doing something else on their computer, so dont expect too interactive of lectures

Easily one of the best professors at WashU. Lectures are very clear, and her notes are extremely thorough/well-written. Hynes really wants her students to succeed, and she makes the most challenging concepts seem really intuitive. She and the Physics Dept. did a great job in transitioning the class online amidst COVID-19 pandemic. 10/10 recommend!

Hynes was always super energetic and very enthusiastic about the material she was teaching. She was definitely very knowledgeable, and made complex math concepts in physics like line and surface integrals seem simple. Even in a large lecture hall with 100+ people, she fostered an interactive class environment that made it feel smaller.

Physics wasn't my strong suit anyway, but she was incredible. I had Israel first semester and she restored my faith in the science. She was patient, energetic, kind, and always prepared for class. Her lectures were helpful and applicable to homework. Incredible teacher, clearly cares
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hynes has deserved a chili for a while. I came to fix it.

Worst intro class at washu. Do not take physics unless you absolutely have to. The textbook they use in this class is by far the worst one I have ever seen (if you dont believe me search up the reviews for it). The professors were probably paid off by the publishing company to force us to use these textbooks.
Dr. Hynes is a good instructor, but the class really requires a lot of outside work in order to be successful. High school physics would be very beneficial even though this is an introductory course.

She is very clear in her lectures and she is very timely. She seems very interested in our progress and she always wants to help us do better if we seem to be struggling. She is always there for her students. I think other lecturers have a darkened tone while her lectures are upbeat and more enthusiastic.

Professor Hynes is dedicated and sincerely interested in providing the best possible environment for learning and enjoying physics.  Beyond that, she is always responsive and understanding, even taking the time to grade my homework herself (usually done by TAs) when my varsity sport forced me to miss class on the day it was due.  Simply the best!
HE IS SO GOOD
Literally changed my life. If you see this and don't take this class you're only hurting yourself. Won't shut up about this class and this professor ever. I love him. So. Much.
Really good lectures. Really nice.

Prof Hindle has been one of my favorites at WashU. He gives great lectures but is most importantly fantastic at facilitating discussion in class. He's a detailed grader who give valuable feedback and all around a kind person. Cannot recommend taking a course with him enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I am not a history guy but I become interested in minor in history after his class. Amazing great lecture, and Amazing detailed feedback for each homework--he is literally writing an essay to review my essay. Only three essays as all grading writing assignment for the whole semester, no other tests.
Passionate about the subject, wants you to succeed.
The GOAT, my failings were my own. One of my favorite people.
Really bad professor. Not sure why bio hasn't fired her yet.

Disclaimer that I dislike bio, but the class was genuinely the worst lecture experience I've had. She is just not good at lecturing and that's a problem when that's 100% of the class. Learned more material cramming the final then cumulatively through her lectures
Her lectures are so boring and she makes things way more confusing.

It's genuinely incredible how a teacher assigned to a class designed off recycled AP high school content can somehow unteach that content and make it incomprehensible. DO NOT take her class under any circumstances or you will pay with your GPA. If I could fire her I would.

Don't get me wrong: the content in Bio 2960 is very similar to AP Bio, which is one of the only reasons why many students are able to excel in this course. However, even with prior knowledge of biology, Hafer makes the course extremely incomprehensible. Her voice is so monotone that many students nap during class, and she only reads off the slides.

she doesn't seem passionate about teaching and her lectures are very boring with her just reading off the slides. there's also a lot of material thrown at you if you don't have a background in biology. thankfully lab, activities, and quizzes are a buffer for your grade

I think that she needs to reflect on why she became a professor. There is very little effort put into her lectures and they are monotonous and boring. The fact that less than a third of her students actually show up says all that needs to be said.

Dr. Hafer is a great person, not a great teacher. She mostly is just here for research, so the lectures are kind of just a side thing for her. Honestly, just skip lecture and do it on your own and you'll end up not wasting your time.
Most hilarious lecture I've ever attend. Reading a ppt every time makes a primary student can take over her job.
My Apple accessibility reader can read slides better than she does

Genuinely in shock at her inability to convey material in a digestible and effective manner; pasted a paragraph on a slide and read off of it; doesn't seem to comprehend that students can read too; no logical progression of ideas, and general disregard of basic pedagogy. At the end of every lecture, I reflect and realize I learned nothing.
Professor Hafer has a very unique style of speaking which makes the listener appreciate her silence. Her class was great for my health in that I greatly improved my sleeping habits as a result.
0/10 professor. The ratings speak for themselves.

Absolutely worst professor. Cannot answer basic questions.

Never answered a single question properly, openly states "I don't know" with no formative response or follow-up. Told the entire class that success means "getting an A." Most students do not learn in these lectures. 

Do not recommend.
Unfair exam. Students are taking the same exam with different time sections

Teaching style consists of reading off the slides, unenthusiastically. Half the time I'm struggling to grasp what is even being discussed. I'm genuinely confused where the logical progression is in ideas and the foundation of knowledge for this. Talks about some ideas as if it is common sense: it's not.
Ratings speak louder than words.

she is genuinely only bearable on 2x speed. otherwise, it is not worth going to lectures when she just reads the slides. like i can do that on my own time much faster. exams are doable but you honestly need to study every single slide bc everything is up for grabs. exam averages r in 70s-low 80s.

I love love loved Dr. Hafer. She was always willing to help us out and she also has a great sense of humor! Phage Hunters was my favorite class freshman year. The class was a good experience as someone who has never done research, but it's definitely important to stay on top of everything, especially second semester!!
Horrible lecturer. Can not explain a concept to save her life. Completely disrespectful during class too. Might be the worst thing I've come across as a student.

I enjoy biology, and I was able to succeed in it, but Prof. Hafer's teaching style was NOT good. She read right off the slides, which isn't a problem by itself, but her voice is so monotone and she seems very unenthusiastic about teaching. I learnt 5x better when a different professor taught a lecture, even with the same read-off-the-slides style.
Easy to do well cause its pure memorization of vocab and diagrams. Awful lecturer. I don't think I've ever met a professor who consistently answers questions without answers.

Awful lecturer - nearly impossible to take notes from her class as she rambles through large amounts of content rather quickly by reading off of slides and no additional explinations. Kinda ridiculous that shes teaching and intro bio course at a school full of premeds. if you didn't take bio in high school, this class is gonna suck a lot
Professor is extremely harsh and will pick on people in class. Lecture is very boring and not taught well. Avoid at all costs

Had her for phage hunters. Class is difficult but doable. Hafer's lectures aren't great but very important so pay attention to them and take notes. There aren't many lectures in phage hunters so the few lectures there are heavily affect quiz scores.
Unclear. It was okay.

So frustrating. Refuses to answer questions about content, during or after lecture. Grading on exams is disorganized, takes forever, and takes off silly points. Impossible to get above a 95 on an exam. Luckily exams are worth very little. I love bio but this made me hate it. I wonder how many kids she turns away from bio.
had not taken ap bio and this class was incredibly difficult. test grading criteria is super specific to the point where they are actively trying to find points to take off your grade.

Even during help sessions, she acts irritated at students for asking questions & not understanding content, when all she does in lecture is read off the slides. The material wasn't that bad, but tests & quizzes can be difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hafer reads off of the slides and does not add much regarding expertise. Though she will stop and ask questions, she can rarely answer them, which is disappointing. If you have taken AP Bio before, it may be okay that she does not teach the material, but for first-time Bio learners, the lack of actual explanation and guidance makes it tough.

She's nice and funny but just reads off the slides. The material can be learned without attending her lectures. We rush through content and don't spend as much time applying it. She says the tests emphasize conceptual understanding, but they were fairly basic and mostly memorization, which was a loss educationally. Exams aren't weighted that much.

In my experience, she was nowhere near as bad as she was made out to be. You have to give her and Kunkel grace for reading off slides when there is so much information to cover that there is no way to lecture without them. Overall she is ok - not amazing but not terrible. The midterms only make up 25% of your grade which is extremely fair.
she reads her slides
It's clear that Hafer has a passion for her students, but her lectures are sometimes boring and I find it easier if I just studied in my dorm instead of going to lectures.
Not going to lie, I didn't go to lecture because it was such a waste of time. She read off the slides the whole time. Loved biology until I had to take it with her here.

Hafer is way better than all of these haters say she is. She explains what is on the slides very clearly, which has been extremely helpful because I haven't taken bio in a while. She just teaches you what you need to know. (I cannot say any of these things about Kunkel).

She gets a bad rep but is just not great in a big lecture setting, if you talk to her or take another class with her you will really like her. Class was fairly easy and we got note sheets for exams. It was just boring.
reads of the slides in slow motion and proceeds to explain absolutely nothing. Baffles me how she is still employed. dont take this class unless you are sleep deprived and want an hour nap per day
Reads off her PowerPoint
Could be a more organized lecturer and Bio 2970 is hard, but honestly easier than 2960 - I liked the flipped classroom style.
Does not seem to love what she teaches... and that is a MAJOR problem. Can't spread inspiration without seemingly caring about the subject...

It's hard to enjoy learning biology when the prof seems to had learning, teaching, and students in general. Hafer constantly brought a bad attitude to class and was very dismissive and rude when asked questions.

This class was horrible. Lectures were very boring and she just read off the lecture slides. Very unhelpful and therefore the exams were much more difficult than I expected. Extremely specific and little partial credit.

Hafer doesn't really seem to like students, but she isn't all that bad 1 on 1. She does teach off of slides, but there are so many things in biology that need to be visualized that I found it a fine way of teaching. If you can focus on the material, it can be an enjoyable class.

It sucks to say that BIO 2960, a core Pre-Med class at WashU has been probably the worst class I have taken in my life.  She sounds like she doesn't know what she's talking about in lectures and refuses/dodges people's questions.  She is also extremely rude and has no passion for teaching.  Exams are poorly worded and contain niche questions.
Kathy was not a good lecturer, she is pretty monotone and it got kind of boring. She didn't seem happy when anyone asked questions and always brushed them off. Not very invested in students.
She seems unapproachable in lecture, but she is nice outside of lecture. She does not do a great job of teaching in lecture.

I have heard people like her when they have her in bio lab but does not excuse her being bad at teaching. You can't just read the slides and expect that to make sense to students who have not taken AP Bio. Do not take this class unless you have enough drive to self teach or need it as a requirement.

Sometimes (a lot of the time), reads off of the slides and struggles to explain the material. Cannot explain disputed content well, and the ambiguity of test and quiz questions warrants contesting the 'correct' answers. Attendance should not be necessary and most of the content could be found on public websites. The textbook is virtually worthless.

HAFER is hilariously bad. She yells at students for her own mistakes. Only teaches the class because no one else wants to take her place for fear that they will also have their reputation tainted. She is not accessible outside of class and her feedback is that you should've known better. Class is so disorganized I learned more in high school.

Phage Hunters was overall a good experience. Basically everyone gets an A, and I found the content interesting. Hafer, however, is blatantly rude to students and did not treat the AI with respect. Her lectures were easy to follow, but I couldn't stand how she treats others.

Kathy Hafer cares so little about this class and about the students in it. Expect monotony, reading of slides, and extremely difficult to understand rambles. I barely made it through this class. Kunkel is better, but not by a lot. Hafer is the worst lecturer I have had at WashU.

Kathy Hafer is not only one of the worst professors, but one of the worst of people. She doesn't care for students or her fellow faculty in the slightest and it shows. She yells at students, denies to answer pertinent questions, and is absurdly arrogant. The class is required for many so push through it, and don't let Hafer define WashU professors.

Very poor instructor. Simply reads off the (very content heavy) slides and does nothing more. Extremely unenthusiastic, making lectures boring and useless. She also disregards student questions and is very rude towards them, creating an overall hostile and unwelcoming environment. The class itself isn't too hard, but prepare to teach yourself.
lectures are very fast-paced; impossible to take any decent notes; weekly quizzes do not represent the level of difficulty of the midterm and final exams

The 2960 profs never write anything on the board, and instead read slides (many of which are just blocks of text) at a conversational pace. I genuinely think it's impossible to take decent notes in real time for their lectures. They also used the exams being online/open-note as an excuse to make the questions extremely subjective and ambiguous.
She spends more time explaining how she won't explain things instead of explaining things

She is very unapproachable when asking questions. She clearly shows no passion for biology, teaching, or even students so I am not sure why she is a professor. If you ask a question, you will most certainly receive a demeaning response. In class, students can often be seen doing other work. The other professor, Dr. Kunkel, is noticeably better.

The way this course is taught is absolutely awful. lecturers may be nice people but they do not know how to teach at all. they read off slides everyday and expect us to soak up a bunch of details and information like we're einstein or something. also it hurts more because my highschool didnt have a strong biology program so im struggling
terrible. couldn't care less about teaching. shows up and reads the slides. her voice is annoying.

Frankly, I am horrified that Prof. Hafer is still allowed to teach bio 2960. Success is dependent on previous knowledge and the slides provided for lecture. Hafer read off of the slides, did not allow us to ask her questions before or after class, and was disrespectful towards students. I have never experienced a more terribly taught class.

Im shocked she is a professor considering she literally hates her students and has zero patience, organization, or clarity. Doesn't explain what we need to know for quizzes or exams. She told us in lecture we "didn't need to know" some information then put questions directly related to that material on a quiz that week.
Does not have the knowledge to answer student questions, and sometimes refused to answer them. The class is run very poorly and is very disorganized.
you would be better off watching crash course videos than attending her lectures. Rude and unhelpful 0/10, rounding down.
She's hurt the souls of every students she has taught

Very unprofessional and not very helpful at all. This is an intro class and she acts like every question is a dumb one. I understand it's a large class but I still wish she would be nicer and more willing to help students. I am a transfer student retaking intro to bio AND I took AP bio, but if I hadn't I would definitely really struggle
Not nice
Be ready to study a lot on your own. She reads off the slides and you have to figure out where to go from there.

Nonexistent is the only one day that you guys are going on and what is happening in your room lol and I hope youre having fun and enjoying yourself and your life together too bro love and merry thanksgiving to heaven bless your lord bless.

DO NOT TAKE PHAGE!!! I am warning you guys this class was so bad. They advertise this as a fun awesome class where you get to do research but that is absolutely not the case. She is boring, has no energy, and puts the entire class to sleep. I drink 2 cups of coffee and somehow still fall asleep in her class.

Absolutely useless professor. I have no idea how she was assigned to be in charge of intro bio. Refused to answer students questions, and often ridiculed students for asking questions when it was clear that she just did not know the answer herself. Should be fired

It's apparent that Kath Hafer hates people and hates her job. All she does is read from a powerpoint slide that is written at a level of bio not understandable for people who haven't taken ap bio. If you're like me and didn't take ap bio, you will have to teach yourself everything.

Dr. Hafer seems to be a very sassy person, but in reality, she cares about students. I know students in my class complained a lot about the lectures and exams. However, I couldn't believe others could lecture better than her. I've also taken her lab session. She's a fantastic teacher!
Worst teacher I have ever had period. If 0 was a rating option I would give it.

For a school that is ranked number 10 for their biology program, I have no idea how Professor Hafer landed a job. It's pretty obvious she enjoys being there less than her students by the way she treats her colleagues and TAs. I think that she would be better off working at a public high school. Also, she overuses the adjective squishy. Not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible person and professor. She hates her students and her colleagues, can't lecture without reading off the slides, and can't answer basic questions. Not accessible either in or out of class. When she has a bad day, she takes it out on her students. The tests and quizzes are not terrible but the grading is ridiculously unfair.

For a professor that says she's dedicated to teaching, she sure seems to hate her students and TAs. Seems to genuinely dislike her students, and yells at people for asking questions during class. Also seemed to have problems with the TAs and yelled at one on a Zoom call five minutes before class started. Not very accessible outside of class either.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You're literally graded on random chance. Example of a question that would be on a test in this class: "List some colors that start with the letter 'S.'" The students answer: "Sandy brown Sangria Sapphire Scarlet Seashell Sepia Sky Blue Slate grey Smalt Spring bud Spring green" The grading: 0 pts. Did not include steel blue.

Avoid at all costs. She only read off of her slides, word for word. She has a very condescending tone, and beware of asking for help because she will attack you for asking basic questions. I've asked many questions and the only answer she gives is "because that's the way it is." Your best bet is crash course instead of lectures.
Very unhelpful, does not know answers to some relatively basic question, is very not engaging lecturer

Hafer does not care about her students at all and seems to go out of her way to make class harder. She is extremely rude and condescending when asked questions (and rarely even gives an answer), and she does not act like she wants to be giving a lecture at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hafer's lecturing isn't great, so just show up for the iClicker extra credit if you want it. She's not very personable; a friend of mine emailed her about a mistake on MT2 and she responded with a passive aggressive refusal. Class is memorization heavy, but not challenging otherwise. Do the practice tests and problem sets  likely get an A.

Not the nicest person, but thats not what matters. Shes straightforward, and I value that in a professor. The tests arent meant to trick you, theres just a lot of information to memorize, and shes pretty upfront with what you need to know.

I LOVED Dr. Hafer. I would always feel welcomed during office hours, and get a kick out of her interesting stories. The class was not easy, and I had to work for my grade. Even though I didnt earn the grade I wanted, I at least learned something from my experience. And thats all that matters. Overall, a very solid choice.

Professor Hafer's lectures aren't too revolutionary, mostly reading off slides, and she is not the friendliest professor out there. However, the class offers 2.3% extra credit which means you can have a B- test average (which is the usual test avg) and still earn an A- thanks to how course assignments are weighted. Memorization heavy.
Awful teacher. It seems like she doesn't even understand half of the things she is teaching about. Reads off slides and is very condescending. Do not recommend.

Personally, I liked Professor Hafer. Dr. Hafer seems to tire as the day progresses. In the morning, she really cares about you. In the afternoon... That's when the horror (see other comments) happens. Grades rely mainly on memorization-heavy tests. No tricks. Just do all old tests and understand the tiniest details on slides, and easy A.

condescending. dont ask questions unless you want her to call you out in front of the class. not friendly. talks to herself when lecturing more than the class so often you have no idea what is going on. material is easy but she expects you to memorize very specific pieces of information

Biology is not a hard class compared to General Chemistry. However, the professor is moody and very condescending. Depending on her mood that day, the lecture will be very different. I also don't think she tends to understand her own material that well. She always replies to questions with, "Well, that's not my area of expertise".
Literally just reads the powerpoint slides (which don't contain that much information). You're better off not coming to lecture and just reading the textbook
Avoid. Horrible at lectures.
do not recommend. at all.

A lot of the comments sum up this incredible professor in a nutshell, by which I mean that she is a nutshell. She picks and chooses biology topics to teach, which causes the class to not have a broader theme. The grading policy on tests is arbitrary, so you are better off dumping all the info that you know for each question. I preferred AP Bio.

Intro Bio is even worse than before now that she is the main lecturer. As a person she's unhelpful and curt with students. Her exams are horrendus. I studied exactly the same way and felt the same for exam 2 and 3 and I got a 95 and 65 respectively. Semantics on the exams screwed me out of so many points and the regrade policy ignores it. AVOID

She's quite rude to students in lecture, and even more so outside of classroom. You get the sense that she does not want to interact with students at all. My friends and I joke that she should be sent to Fontbonne since she's just that awful.

I really, really, do not like Dr. Hafer.  She is somewhat condescending to her students and once yelled at me when I went to her office to ask a question.  I would avoid her and bio2960 if possible.  She is a better lecturer for 2960 than the other professors, although that doesn't say too much, as they are all quite bad.

She is extremely close minded and opinionated about everything.  If you ask questions at a help session she will rip you to shreds (this happened and I cried after, not exaggerating and I am not a crier).  She made 2960 a living hell.  Grading is completely unclear and memorizing every stupid detail is the only way to do well.

Prof. Hafer doesn't seem to care about students; I know she manages the grading for two intro Bio courses (Bio 2960& 2970) and therefore has a lot of administrative duties, but her attitude is very much "this is what happens, I don't really care about lack of transparency." She is also a horribly unclear lecturer (she sometimes subs for main profs)

Terrible teacher, incredibly rude and unmannered outside of class, really not worth your time to talk to her. She's the organizer of bio 2960 and 2970, which makes sense because these classes are very disorganized. Doesn't know the material outside of her narrow brain-- thankfully she doesn't teach much of this class.
Decent lecturer, though certainly well below what should be expected from a professor of such a large class at a highly ranked university.  Is often quite rude when asked questions outside of class.

I loved Dr. Hafer! She was so helpful, and I wish she could teach the entire course of bio! The other professors are ok, but with Dr. Hafer, I completely understand, and I learn a lot more. Take her lab section, or take Biol 191 (Freshman class), because I did both and I loved it and got As in both. Dr. Hafer is probably one of my fav professors.
Reminds me of Dolores Umbridge from Harry Potter: kind of scary and wears pink. Cold and sarcastic in a way that can be condescending. I would not go to her for help first.

She's a better lecturer than Majors, but she seemed kind of uninterested and also a bit snippy toward students who tried to ask her questions. I didn't have her for lab but I guess she would have been a good teacher for lab since that's her section.
Can be strict at times.  Seems to be easily annoyed.
A bit of a humorless person, but very competent as a lab instructor.  The labs and their grading are very easy - if only the entire course were so simple!

I had the worst Orgo 1 experience and Heemstra changed my life this semester. He is accessible in office hours and clearly cares about his students. Orgo is hard but Heemstra really explains and gives you time to think and discuss with others during lecture. You can tell how experienced he is and that he really is passionate about teaching.
Nice and knowledgeable teacher, but the learning objectives were not clear. I guess I left with some understanding of orgo, but what I really learned was how to review problems for exams.

Although orgo is a very challenging class, prof Heemstra made it very organized and interesting. He is a very nice person, and he really tries to remember your name. He is also very knowledgeable about this field. I am very glad that I can take my two-semester orgo with him. It is a great class.
The class was fine, but I found I ended up memorizing problems and the LA worksheets. If you do that, the exams are straight forward. I must say I am not sure how much I actually learned.

He's the best professor you can get for organic chemistry. Obviously, it's a hard course but he's the man you want to learn it from. He's very charismatic and his lectures just make sense, especially compared to the professor I had for Orgo 1.

I appreciated that Prof. Heemstra drew out the mechanisms and tied concepts back into FMO theory. Exam questions were difficult & really creative, but I thought they were pretty manageable and generally like the LA worksheets. Personally, I found the content more intuitive than in Chem 111A.

Material and exams were fine. Study old exams. Dr. Heemstra's lectures were fine, but I never felt comfortable with him. I guess he is better than Chen, but isn't there anyone better for orgo? My RA said to take Moeller…but I don't think he teaches orgo any more.

Dr. Heemstra is better than Dr. Chen, but overall I found the course just a lot of memorizing. It was not hard, but not good. The bonus is the course was Tues/Thurs so I got it out of the way before Friday.

Prof Heemstra has figured out a way to teach orgo in a way that feels appropriately paced. He methodically goes over each new concept, and from that point on, expects you to practice it on your own. The material is not easy, and he likes to challenge students on exams, but he is a great prof.

I absolutely love Dr. Heemstra. He truly cares about his students and their well-being outside of his class. The class itself was also great. It is tough material but he teaches it so well, and it is so rewarding when you take a tough exam and get a good grade on it. His class was one of my favorites even though I don't particularly like orgo.
Lucky to have him as my prof. Had 261/262 with Heemstra and am so grateful to have had him. Would be lucky to have another professor like Heemstra.
Goated. I feel privileged to have been taught by Heemstra. Couldn't have asked for a better orgo experience.

Kind, smart and enthusiastic. Helps you understand why certain chemistry is favorable with orbitals, thermodynamics, rate, and sterics. Research questions on test can be daunting, but you will be good if you can identify the reacting portions of molecules. Such a nice qualitative continuation of gen chem; I have learned so much. 261/262

Great professor who made ochem a positive experience! Strongly recommend working through all workshop packets, which will help in your understanding of concepts and certainly improve your exam performance. Prof Heemstra often makes himself available outside of class, which is also quite helpful!
A very enthusiastic professor who is incredibly accessible outside of class. If you thoroughly complete and understand the packets, his exams are very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Heemstra is an excellent professor who cares about teaching. He is always there to provide extra support to students during office hours, and his annotating slides with us during class helps a lot in the learning process. The class does go in depth about concepts, so it is important not to fall behind, but overall, would recommend!!

Heemstra made Orgo so much easier than what had been said. His lectures were very clear and engaging. The assigned homework and optional problem sets were very close to what was on exams and he would sometimes pull problems from those with a slight change. Put in the work and do everything he asks and you will do well.

Heemstra is fine. The bonus is the class is not hard, and he gives you everything you need. The downside is you end up just getting ready for the tests instead of learning the material. I am sure I will spend a lot of time next year learning orgo for the MCAT.

By far the best orgo 1 teacher. Gave great lectures that were enjoyable, easy to follow, and supplemented by humor. Very accessible outside of class. Very lenient with grading and partial credit and always gives extra time on the exams, which many think are easier than the other profs exams.

Prof. Heemstra is one of the best professors I've ever had & he genuinely cares about students. Strikes a delicate balance between challenging you, while being understanding/reasonable. He draws everything on his slides, so it's easy to follow his lecturing. Nothing but good things to say!

All of the test content was thoroughly taught through his powerpoint making studying for the test extremely easy. He seriously cares for the student's success and even give extra time at the end for exams!
Absolutely amazing teacher! Explains concepts very well, make sure to go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Goated.

Like most students, I was pretty nervous about orgo. However, I thought Heemstra was good at explaining and I really appreciated his clear lecture slides and recorded videos. He is very clearly passionate about what he teaches and took a creative approach to his exams, which some may have disliked but I found it made the class more exciting.

Ehh...I was hoping for better, but I guess it could have been worse. He seemed a bit rushed to plow through material and did not spend much time going into details that would help create intuition. It is king of a shame that the quality of professor in Chemistry has gone down every semester since 111.

Heemstra was pretty standard. This class is very lecture heavy but he does do his best to explain everything. He's pretty accessible. Didn't really go above and beyond or anything, but also not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He presented clear lectures, and was accessible outside class. Exams will contain real world examples.

BIG TIP: Download the textbook and textbook answer key on Libgen or Z-Library. Use these to do the assigned textbook readings before each class, and the assigned textbook problems after every lecture. This will make studying for exams a breeze.

My course is online. I think the professor was using generative AI for most/all of her assignment instructions & course materials. While materials were informative, task instructions were extremely hard to follow & sometimes irrelevant to the task, causing misunderstandings. Class mostly based on poorly designed group project. Poor communication.

Iva is a sweet, caring professor. She makes the material approachable as Italian grammar can be quite convoluted, and lectures are small enough that you'll have plenty of time to practice and get questions answered. She brings her dog in sometimes!!!

This class was really challenging for me, but I was able to pull through. There are a lot of resources available, and Iva is a great professor. If you're confused about something, ask!! I do wish that some of the resources on Canvas about new tenses etc. were a bit more clear. Sometimes I got confused because it was all in Italian.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: the best teaching i've had in college so far, she made italian my favorite class and cares so much about her students. love her!

Iva is a great professor who truly cares about her students. She checked up on all of us every lecture and genuinely cared about our well being. Most of my class were art school kids and when things got tough for them, she would have relaxed classes and even brought in her dog once. Do the online homework and participate-learning takes practice

Iva is a wonderful professor who truly cares about her students. She checked up on all of us every lecture and genuinely cared about our well being. Most of my class were art school kids and when things got tough for them, she would have relaxed classes and even brought in her dog once. Do the online homework and participate-learning takes practice
did not enjoy the class. did not learn much Italian either. would definitely not recommend this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She's not a good profesor at all. Doesn't teach, class is boring and doesn't care about students. Would never recommend her class.  Find another profesor or don't take Italian.

I LOVE IVA. I cannot say enough good things about her. Iva cares about her students and will really appreciate and notice if you participate in class. She makes classes fun by playing current music or videos and even invites classes over to her house for dinner! Not a hard garder. TAKE ANY CLASS YOU CAN WITH HER.

Probably the nicest professor one can have! Class is very relaxing and feels more like a conversation than a lecture, but at the same time you also learn a decent amount of Italian. Also extremely lenient on grading, probably will end up with an A or A+.
She's super cute and loving like an adorable italian mom. The class is very easy, you just have to go to it. Not much homework. If you took spanish it is a breeze.
She's a wonderful person and teacher. I highly recommend taking a class with her before you graduate!

I absolutely loved her. Not only was she a great teacher, but she was fun and funny at the same time. She is so sweet and always up for a good laugh. She created a class with a great atmosphere and we all became friends. I recommend her a million times over!

I'm probably biased because I naturally love Italian language and culture, but I really did enjoy this class. She's very nice and helpful in explaining things and answering questions. In fact, all my Italian professors at this university have been really good on the whole-the Romance Languages Department should be commended for its hiring procedure
I have not met a single person who does not love Iva.  She is amazing.  Take her classes if it is at all possible.
By far my favorite teacher at Wash U
Iva is pretty damn hot, but she also teaches really, really well. Makes the class fun, makes learning the language very easy, and makes great Italian food as well. One of the best at WU.
Great teaching method, although I would rather have a real Italian person (she is from eastern Europe)
Iva is Hot and is way too sexy for Work...
Iva is terrific! Her teaching style is terrific, and she really cares about her class. It was really fun being in her class, I would reccomend her to anyone!
I <3 Iva!! What a wonderful, sweet professor! She truly enjoys teaching and it shows.
Iva is great--very concerned with the development of every individual student in her classes.  A lot of fun to talk to also--she even had a bunch of us over for dinner at the end of the semester.
Very enthusiastic, wonderful person. Concerned for students, interesting classes, great personality, makes language fun and easy to learn

She is very enthusiastic and encourages participation. She is also very organized, and does not take days off like some teachers I know. You can tell she loves her job, and she takes personal interest in students.
She's awesome.  Really funny and sweet.  My favorite prof this semester.
Mi favorito!

Great guy. Very caring about students, has a sense of humor too. Lectures can be a little unstructured which makes it hard if you're not following along but if you put in some effort, you'll get a lot out of it. At the same time, he's a pretty easy grader so if you don't you'll probably be fine too.
Infante is the best professor I have taken at WashU. He is one of the nicest guys ever and grades very nicely as well. I'm pretty sure everyone in his class ends up with an A.

Very kind and concerned teacher - he cares about you a lot and makes great strides to look out for the class, including extending deadlines quite often. I am naturally pretty good at writing but it seemed like pretty much everyone was getting an A for each essay. You can participate and write well in this class without reading each book in detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Infante is the best professor I have ever interacted with. He is understanding, the work load is very manageable, and he is a genuinely kind (and unbelievably smart) person. If you can take a class with him you have to, he encourages the exploration of literature in a way that you wont find elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Infante is such a nice and genuinely caring person. Despite the fact that I never understood a single reading and could probably, at the end of the semester, not tell you what this class is about I would take the course again in a heartbeat. It is rare you find a professor as nice and class discussion was always fun even when it was confusing!
Great teacher and nice person. Readings can be a bit existential and hard to understand, but grading is not too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Wonderful man! His World Lit class made me think about stuff I have never pondered before. His class is very discussion-based, and I learned so much through this style of learning. I would love to take another class with him-- very enthusiastic, easy class, amazing professor!! Cares about his students a lot. Take World Lit with him if you can!!!

Prof. Infante is super enthusiastic, kind, and reasonable. World Lit challenged my thinking but was never too stressful, and he both gave great lectures and made sure the discussions went somewhere. You can tell that he loves the subject matter, and he is really willing to help with papers. If you put in effort, your worldview will expand a lot!

Professor Infante is great! World Lit is a really interesting class and he clearly is very passionate about it. He chose some really great texts and always gave insightful lectures. He is very laid back and approachable, enthusiastic about what he teaches, and is a pretty easy grader. Overall it is a very casual atmosphere and highly enjoyable.

He's a G. First day of class he played the Pixies, I've never met anybody with a more impressive name than Ignacio Infante, his accent is infinitely dope,  he's just a funny and laid back guy. And he definitely knows his shtuff. Essays aren't too bad, I liked the books but you didn't have to read carefully at all if you pay attention in class
Prof. Infante is a wonderful professor, very engaging and fun to listen to.  He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed.  Awesome teacher!
World Lit was an amazing class!!! Ignacio is the best. Take every class you can with him!
World Literature with Professor Infante was a great introductory class. The works he picked for us to read and view were, for the most part, very interesting.

Prof Infante is both an adorable person and a fabulous professor.  He listens to his students and makes time to meet at least once during the semester with each student in the class. He make required material interesting and understandable. I furthered my Spanish significantly in the 2 semesters in his classes. SPAN 307 & 334.
We love nacho!!

Very political professor but I think that is to be expected. He is a great professor to take if you have never been exposed to another world view besides your own (you will learn a lot!). take any class with him and it will feel like a great experience and worthwhile!

Readings will seem like a lot at first, but skimming should get you by fine. Discussion boards are the bulk of your grade so definitely write about them like you care and you should get at least an A-. He is so funny and kind, and the people who have a problem with him usually disagree on his political views. Final project is low-stakes and fun!

I took LatAm165D a few semesters ago and have taken a class with him almost every semester since, including The Binational Condition and Survey of MC. Assignment criteria is very clear, and his lectures make you want to pay attention rather than it being a chore. You'll know pretty immediately if you want to keep taking the class.

Nacho is a rly good lecturer. Obviously very knowledgable and passionate about what he teaches, and funny, too. The final project was probably my favorite kind of final ever--low pressure and fun. A large part of your grade is from weekly prep boards. I did many late, but the extra credit made up for a lot.

Nacho is a great professor—probably my favorite this semester. The class involves a lot of reading every week, but if you are interested, the readings are fun. The class is graded only with weekly prep boards and a final project, which is very chill. Nacho is very accessible outside of class and sometimes makes some hilarious jokes in lectures.
Super kind and funny. Extremely easy to get an A. Maybe 1.5 hours of homework per week. I fell asleep during every lecture since there were no exams. You won't get an A+. Accessible outside of class

I wasn't a huge fan of this class, but don't let that dissuade you if you're truly interested in Latin American Studies. There was a LOT of reading and the lectures weren't my favorite, but the professor is very knowledgable on the subject. Super nice guy who truly wants you to learn. No exams and final project was very fun.

Incredibly intelligent professor and you can absolutely tell when you listen to his lectures. Lots of reading and it's important to have a general idea of all content to get good scores on the weekly discussion boards and quizzes, but content is pretty interesting. Final project requires barely any class content, but really cool.

Either you love Nacho or you hate him. I found his lectures to be very informational and entertaining. There is a LOT of reading in this class, but the weekly assignments are simple and pretty open-ended in your favor. Nacho has a lot of passion for these topics, and it almost makes you care that much more about the class too. Overall a great guy!

Nacho is by far one of the most inspirational and knowledgeable people I have ever met. Though he is unafraid to express his own opinions or assign lengthy readings, he is receptive to feedback and respects the diversity of perspectives of his students. Making the commitment to engage with the materials will result in an unforgettable experience.
there are a lot of reading but it's nothing you can't skim through
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: this class made me hate college. when i tell you this class will literally take away your sanity and any chance at having a social life, i mean it. one assignment consists of multiple 45+ pages of readings, videos, a prep board, and a quiz all in one. please save yourself the trouble and find another class to take :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: IMO Nacho is impressive with extensive knowledge and does a great job of recounting L.A. history factually. My only complaint is he spoke the entire class and people zoned out. Easy to get an A if you do assignments + lots of extra credit opportunities. I read a life-changing book for this course and received wonderfully kind comments on my paper.

Nacho teaches opinion as fact and says some really inflammatory things. You have to agree with him in your discussion posts and papers in order to do well. He assigns more reading than I have ever had and most of it is redundant. He is interesting and has a lot of knowledge, but is hard to follow in lectures and mumbles a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nacho was, overall, a very good professor to learn about Latin American affairs with. The course is reading intensive, with a multiple-choice quiz and a 200-word prep board due at the beginning of each week--lots of extra credit is offered if you do happen to miss something though. Attendance is mandatory, so be prepared for the commitment.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Participation matters--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I hate this class. Unless you hate America and are ignorant of politics you will also hate this class. Every lecture comes from a strong socialist bias, and the amount of reading is insane. It is a very one-sided class and other opinions are not acceptable. Sure, he can be a funny guy, but I walk out of class with anger every time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend avoiding Nacho. His lectures are long and not easy to follow. He does not allow computers in class and is constantly berating students who don't study what he considers worthwhile fields. He assigns 20 page papers and is not at all helpful if you go to office hours. If you want a good grade, be ready to suck up to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Nacho is one of the best professors I have had at WashU.  He is one of the top people in his field, but still cares so much about his undergraduate students.  I have asked him for recommendations, gone to office hours, and overall could not recommend him or his classes more!

One of the most influential professors of my college experience. You'll do a lot of reading but he makes lectures incredibly interesting. Definitely take this class! It changed how I see the world. Also Nacho is fantastic and will write rec letters for you if you need it.

one of the best classes that i had at wash-u. although he's a hard core leftist, he has strong reasons for that and it is very worth learning such perspective. frequent quizes, A LOT of reading, need to cite all the books used in class to write a mini 8 page paper but his class is sooo inspiring.
Amazing Teacher! LOVED IT

I can't believe only 2 people have rated Nacho. He's an AMAZING professor and if you have the chance to take him... do! He's extremely smart and thought provoking and he really cares about getting to know all the students personally, even in a class of 120 people.
This is my favorite class. I've had a few health problems so far this semester and "Nacho" has been very flexible and understanding. He's a great guy, and his class always wakes me up in the morning.
This professor is awesome! He assigns A LOT of reading, but other than that his classes are always really interesting, he knows his stuff, and he's funny. I would definitely recommend this class.
This guy knows his stuff, truly. One of the best presenters of information out there, and you do not want to miss his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor may seem intimidating at first, but is highly knowledgable and can make seminars very intriguing. My experience was only slightly diminished by the TAs unclear grading criteria. The professors are not the ones who grade the papers, so it is very important to speak to the TAs.
None of the papers are graded by the professors themselves. They are helpful, but they are also quite intimidating. Quite heavy reading load, and will occasionally cold call on students.

Professor Inazu is incredibly intelligent and a talented lecturer. He provokes lots of interesting thought and interacts extremely well with students. All essays were graded by TAs but he clearly puts thought into the prompts and sets you up for success. Made me much more interested in law, and I highly recommend taking a class with him.

Inazu is primarily a law professor, and his level of knowledge shines through in his lectures. There are no slides or recordings for this class, so attendance is important. The few papers you have for the class are graded by TAs, but pay close attention in class because valuable insight is given. Excellent lecturer, made me interested in law.

Families and Social Inequality was a great class. The grading was clear, the open-note midterm and final exams were fair, and class activities were engaging. Readings were a good mix of journal articles and news articles. Professor Ishizuka is a kind and understanding prof. Great intro sociology class to take.
This was a pretty easy class. There weren't a lot of assignments, the midterm and final were open note, and he's really nice. Very supportive and available to help.

He's genuinely a really nice guy. He's sweet and funny, making lectures not that bad. Very big on readings, having minimum 30 pages of reading each class, but you talk about the readings in class and do group activities. You can honestly do fine if you don't show up sometimes, just beware of pop-quizzes, but he's very lenient on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty good teacher. There are a lot of readings for homework and his lectures essentially go over the readings, so sometimes they felt redundant. Nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: The professor is super nice and tries very hard, but the class is not very exciting. Lectures are just going over what we read, so I didn't see the point of going to lectures. Readings are heavy in this class, so I would not recommend if you can't read 20+ pages per class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class I took was a mix of lecturing and group activities. There is a lot of reading, and doing the reading on time makes the essays and tests a lot easier. Prof. Ishizuka is a really kind teacher who always has time to help, and clearly explains his rubric/requirements for writing assignments. I highly recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Annoying that the professor said she was going to curve substantially only for her not to curve.

Professor is very unprepared and mostly reads off slides. Multiple classes started 20+ minutes late due to repeated “technical issues.” She repeatedly stated a generous curve and told us to “take it easy” during the final (bc of curve), and gave a false, overinflated estimate with no details. The curve ended up being extremely small. Do not take.

The course is straight from CMU. There's no point in going to class if you find the link to the recorded CMU lectures online, which have better lecture quality. Also claimed she was going to curve the course the entire semester, only to not do so in the end.

Angelina Lee offers good explanations for the difficult concepts in this class. She struggles, however, with providing clear answers to clarifying questions and with questions about specific details. If you get the explanation the first time she's great, but otherwise it might be a struggle.

She reads off lecture slides from CMU, and doesn't actually explain any content further than the bullet points on the slides. She also goes way too fast through the lectures. She is also incredibly difficult to contact outside of class. She is bad at responding to emails and piazza posts, and when she does, her responses are not helpful.
Use CMU's slides and read them but actually teach nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super hard lab. The last two was insanely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She doesn't care about undergrads at all and is so focused on her own research. Her lecture videos were so boring, and she basically read the slides. Her exam was T/F on super minor points. Really? It's just lazy to give a T/F exam in college. I went to her OH and she was incredibly unhelpful. I regret taking this course with her.

This professor sucks. The lecture is straight from CMU and she just reads off the slides and sometimes stares at them cause she constantly doesn't know what she was talking about. She's extremely unreasonable with accommodations.
The pace and the structure of the course is perfect for a junior year CSE student. Slides are clear and the prof is always accessible outside of class.
Lectures are hard but really helpful. Materials are really good (because it's from CMU). Be prepared to challenge yourself in labs and exams.

Class was insanely hard. She's not great at teaching, she mostly just reads off the slides, which frequently have mistakes in them. 5 lab homeworks, the first 2 aren't bad but the others are pretty hard. Midterm and final were brutal. I don't recommend this class, but if you need it then take it with someone else if you can.
Iver Bernstein once said, "Great historians provoke." He certainly is a great historian by his own qualification. He provokes often.
Super nice guy. I learned a lot. Take this class!

The lectures were quite boring and went by very slowly. The discussion sections were interesting, though. He assigns an enormous amount of reading which was hard to get through. But he is an easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Iver is a brilliant individual, however, his lectures drag on for what seems like hours. Boring lectures, although he does deliver them with much enthusiasm. I do wish that I had dropped the course when I had time to, would've saved me lots of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bernstein is an exceptional professor. He is very empathetic and genuinely cares about individual students. The class is reading heavy, and he eventually had to reduce them towards the end of class. It is also tough to navigate the course on Canvas as he doesn't utilize it adequately. He is a fair grader, and I usually enjoy his lectures.

Bernstein is the best professor or teacher I have ever had, and I went to the best private high school in my state.  I go to his office hours with paper topics and history project proposals and he's able to ground my thinking and point me in the right direction while making it clear that he values my ideas. He is kind, thoughtful, and brilliant.

Professor Bernstein is one of my favorite professors at WashU. . I have never gotten such helpful and in-depth feedback on my writing. He really wants his students to succeed and he was super easy to go to if you had questions about your writing. A lot of reading, but I would highly recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Bernstein is a knowledgeable and flexible professor. He is super intelligent and loves to discuss deep historical questions with his students. He can sometimes lecture for too long, but I think he was generally informative and well-spoken. His class involves hard work on two big essays, but it is totally manageable.
It's no secret that Professor Berstein knows his stuff, but his material may come off as rather condescending.

Assigns a LOT of reading.  No exams, but 2 essays.  Grading depends on whether you have Bernstein or a TA for discussion section.  I hear he is a difficult grader. Main lecture usually starts out interesting then gets boring because he goes off on tangents that aren't very helpful for our papers. I hear he is clearer in discussion section, though.

I found him to be an awesome professor.  He was very clear, and I made sure to attend class and take notes which really helped in the papers.  No tests, just two long papers and a presentation.  A LOT of reading.  Not an easy grader, but it's very easy to learn in his class.

I did not enjoy him as a professor - his lectures were disorganized and he rambled a lot and I don't think the examples he chose were relatable to the material. I also found him SO intimidating, but that could have been just me.
Makes history fun and interesting. Cares about students.

Undoubtedly knowledgable, but it's true that he is a *bit* proud. This may or may not be justified. It can't be denied that he's a very good teacher of history. Likes to assign a lot of reading and starts class late, but many would say it's wroth it. It wouldn't kill you to get used to hearing someone speak eloquently, even if it can be overdone.

He is outrageously eloquent and one can not help but be intrigued by his lectures.  However, his eloquence can on occasion be too flowery for someone who enjoys the facts of history.  I am a Civil War buff, but I didn't like his Civil War course because he focused too much on the surrounding social aspects and not enough on the war itself.

Although his lecture style is not for everyone (he can be a little unorganized and aloof), Bernstein is one of Wash U's best professors. He is very helpful, interesting, and he is one of my most influential profs.

To all those people who rated him as boring: you were probably too dumb to understand what he was saying. This man speaks as if he is reading from a brilliant textbook or novel.  He is eloquent, thoughtful and deep, bringing subject matter that was dull in high school (US history) into a whole different light. Do the reading and listen up.

By far the worst professor I've ever had. He grades extremely easy, but having to sit through his lectures is not worth it. He is repetitive and extremely boring. If you had to choose between taking one of his courses, or being hit by a shuttle bus- choose the shuttle bus!!!
great class, very nice guy as well, really cares about his students
If you don't like lectures, do not take this class. If you do, you will enjoy it a lot.  Bernstein ties in really interesting material using many different mediums.  I liked it.

I didn't pay attention once in the lectures cause I was too busy trying to keep myself awake yet I still managed to get a good grade.  Hes a really easy teacher but so boring that its just not worth it.

Iver was really boring to listen to during lectures and I had a hard time staying awake.  I think he knows what he's talking about, but it was hard to tell because I was trying not to fall asleep.  He's a pretty easy grader though.

Professor Bernstein is an extremely brilliant, insightful, and captivating teacher who really goes out of his way for his students.  He gives a lot to his students, but he expects the same in return.  However, if you don't enjoy reading/discussion...this is not the class for you.
Great Professor. He may be a bit hard for non-history majors. The lectures were very enjoyable. Ta-Kevin Butterfield was also great. Really enjoyed the class, but it did take a lot of work.
dont bother going to class. lectures are all over the place and difficult to follow. man is smart but doesnt convey himself well. ta kevin butterfield was great. too bad he couldnt teach the class.
He's good, but sometimes longwinded and circuitous.
Great for hitory majors, otherwise, choose a more general history class.
Iver is an arrogant**** who only cares about himself. His lectures start a half hour late, which is annoying because you get there on time and just sit...lectures are dec but the guy is a giant ****.
Professor Bernstein is by far one of the best professors that I have had at Wash U in the past two and half years.  I Highly recommend this extremely smart and interesting prof.

Lectures are painfully boring and class discussions are not much better. Knows what he's talking about, just doesn't present the information in a way that is condusive to staying awake. Definitely avoid
Bernstein is a great lecturer and extraordinarily knowledgeable, but he is a pretty tough grader that looks for very specific things in your papers.
Good lecturer.  Discussions in class are weak, but overall the class is beneficial.
No Comments
Great guy, great lecturer, passionate about history

Changed class rubric, 3 tests instead of 2, but were replaced by graded cold call days in class over group cases. Was very condescending/rude if you didn't know the correct answer on those days. Fast-paced lectures. Confusing to know what he would ask on tests due to the change from 3 to 2. Tests are copies of previous years. Personable guy though.

Lectures were fast-paced but all slides are posted with lots of practice examples. Exams are nearly identical to past exams. 35% of grade attributed to group cases that take ~4 hours to really understand. No homework or quizzes, so it's up to you to prepare for exams. Mandatory attendance. Super funny guy. Textbook not required but helps.

Jared Jennings is my dawg. His practice exams are so similar to the actual exams that if you fail it's genuinely on you. These ratings are absolutely not fair, just do your best in lecture and pay attention and he'll be your best friend.

Dr. Jennings is very knowledgeable when it comes to accounting, and he makes accounting concepts that are typically more advanced seem clear. However, he does not grade homework and puts almost all of grading based on exams, so if you mess up just once it's difficult to get back up again. Would take another class if content was not so fast-paced.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are not an accounting major, I would not recommend Jennings. Accounting is tough for some and Jennings goes quite fast. His class is graded by only quizzes, exams, and participation. He is accessible outside of class, but he is one of the harder accounting professors. Seek help if you need, and get ready to drill the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT take accounting with Jennings. I left every lecture feeling confused; he provides little to no support for students to understand the concepts.

I think he's a good accounting professor. You need to put the work in to get an A. I got a C- on the first midterm, but then clutched up on the last 2 and was able to get an A-. He's a funny guy, expects a lot for an intro acct class (like memorizing statement of cash flows). Not hard conceptually though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While some like Jennings, his lectures were always super fast-paced to the point where you have to dedicate a lot of time outside of class when studying. He gives the last 10 or so years of exams for practice, but I struggled to find an "accounting mindset" as a non-olin student, and it was super discouraging when he would not offer any advice.

The exams are similar to the practice tests, no homework, he's caring, and his test questions were straightforward. Yes, he goes to fast in lectures, we don't need to memorize ratios, and you'll have to put work in to get an A. And? Yeah, exactly. If this is your biggest gripe with an accounting prof, then you don't know how good we have it.

No homework which made it hard to learn. So much memorization so would've rather taken this with a diff prof who allowed cheat sheets. He's a nice guy who is good at keeping lectures engaging, but he expects way too much of his students and their ability to memorize the whole course (especially as someone who wants nothing to do with accounting)

Jennings teaches material at a pace which is often pretty unachievable to keep up with without spending hours outside of the classroom. Though he seems friendly at a surface level he is not very approachable - in fact he is slightly condescending when asking for help/questions.

ACCT 2620 is not an easy class. If things click, that's great, but if they don't, it's hard. Jennings goes fast during lectures, so you'll walk out confused. However, there is no homework - just do like 5-6 of the practice test exams he gives you the week or two before the exam comes and you'll be good. Highly recommend office hours too.

In spite of the large amount of material to memorize in Accounting, this class is not bad. Jennings gives the past ten exams to study and ends up basically copying and pasting one of the tests for the actual test. I really liked Jennings as a professor, as he would constantly tell jokes and stories to make the class more engaging. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He will teach you accounting. Read the textbook sections he tells you to, pay some attention in class, and study well (he gives 10 years of past exams and picks one randomly to reuse for each exam w different numbers), and you will do well in the class. Tells funny stories sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jennings made accounting interesting. As long as you do the past tests (which we have the last 10 years of) and participate in class, you will be fine. One thing to look out for is that 75% of your grade is based on exams, and there is no homework. Overall interesting lecturer and a very doable course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jennings is a nice guy, and the material is straight forward, but he's bad at explaining things and bad at lecturing.

Professor Jennings made his Intro to Financial Accounting class as engaging and interesting as possible for an accounting course. He did his best to make confusing concepts easy to understand in lectures by using plenty of examples. Tests and quizzes can be difficult but he provides plenty of practice exams as resources to prepare.

People tend to dislike 2610 and for fair enough reasons. It's a lot of memorization and learning via trial and error (almost like learning a language). That said, Jennings's lectures are very engaging, and his decks are thoughtful and informative. Biggest gripe is that he doesn't let students leave during class (even to use the bathroom).
Professor was nice; just make sure to show up to class and participate. His tests are super hard and you need to do practice exams from previous years to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jennings was a great professor. Lecture slides on Canvas. I needed to read the textbook to understand everything. Exams were fair and he posts a ton of practice exams that were very similar to the actual exams. Jennings was available in office hours, and he always wanted to help. He really cares about students. My favorite professors at WashU.

Overall a solid professor. He went too fast through the lectures in class and I often had to find what he flew through in class within the textbook later. Midterm Exams were fair but the final covered wayyyy too much material for one person to memorize.
I still can't understand why students are not allowed to use laptops in class. The material is boring and not related to the exam. U need to do practice the previous exams if want to get an A.

Don't listen to the reviews from last year (20-21). Jennings is great, great guy and has some interesting and funny stories in class. Exams are fair, only a bit difficult due to the breadth of material covered. Helpful in office hours. 3610 is obviously more difficult than 2610 but highly recommend even if you're not an accounting major.

Jennings is an amazing professor!!!! He has bro energy and is very chill. I also truly appreciated how patience and enthusiasm when he answered questions, both inside and outside of class! His grade breakdown is tough, but he gives you the exam questions in advance so it's very fair. He made a boring subject interesting and understandable. :)

I'm TIRED of all the Jennings slander. I was scared going into this semester after reading all of the negative reviews, but he was actually a great professor. He goes through plenty of examples in class, doesn't test on random details (all tested material was covered in class), made his exams extremely fair, and was overall a really cool guy.
The Material is extremely boring and most of people around me are regretful to take this course. The tests and quizzes are difficult too.
To be honest, he is not a good professor. Teaching is very awful with very crazy tests.

Professor Jennings definitely teaches difficult material. Your grade is entirely composed of tests/quizzes which definitely raises the stakes a little. My biggest issues with this class were that he tested specific things that he glossed over during class and the test questions were much more difficult than in-class examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Low quality class... stupid tests and quizzes. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: For 3610, his class lectures were pretty clear (with a few exceptions) and there were plenty of examples to study from for the tests/quizzes. His class is test-heavy, as is with any accounting class so that's within the norm. I don't love the material, but he made accounting at least somewhat interesting and he's a really nice and understanding guy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 75% of this class is exams, means there is no room for mistake for such an entry level class. Lectures are horrible and exams are like nightmares. Better take with other Professor.
Pretty awful teacher. He would often add material to the test and quizzes that he didn't effectively cover in class.

Stopped going to live class after he began cold calling us to answer questions we've never gone over before. He will say the material is easy during class which makes me feel stupid/scared to ask questions in fear of not understanding concepts that are "easy". Was thinking majoring in accounting but now I would literally rather do anything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures mainly on NEVER TESTED material and does NOT focus on REAL WORLD. Lecture reflect NOTHING of the tests. Condescending and unhelpful in office hours; doesn't understand the students' feeling, always over-confident about his ability in explanation. Test questions are difficult (especially after drop and Pass/fail period). Not ethical.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dont know how he got some fine reviews before. But his ACCT 2610 class/exams/quizzes is terrible, absolutely terrible. This is not my personal opinion, this is a VERY common feeling in his entire class. He is not even a OK teacher in any aspect.

Took accounting before I transferred to WashU (got an A) but they wouldnt accept it for credit so I had to take accounting again.
