Im eternally grateful for my previous knowledge which helped me pass his extremely hard tests. Got screwed on the final though, cant imagine what it was like for students who had this as their first accounting course
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jennings is a good instructor, teaches fine. Exams are impossible to complete and graded harshly. His final is very, very hard, he is a true innovator on the next generation of hard classes in US colleges. Some WashU classes maybe hard, but Jennings is at the next level.

He keeps you enrolled by giving easy quiz before the last day to drop. This semester, when WashU extend the P/F grade option change deadline to 12/14, he made every quiz before the deadline much easier, and then give an EXTREMELY HARD final on 12/18(when you are persuaded to keep this class as letter grade). His teaching is a joke, so do his tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tested on things not taught in class nor mentioned in the textbook. He made exams and quizzes harder this semester in comparison to past ones. Some of the terms and concepts I encountered for the first time on the exams. I printed out the past 8 years worth of exams/quizzes to study each time and still would not be able to perform well on tests.

He was a super nice guy and really cared about us understanding the material and the logic behind it. Lectures have a lot of examples/practice problems that are very helpful. The class itself is pretty difficult and would be regardless of professor, but I really think that he was effective in teaching us the subject.

He expects you to read the chapter thoroughly and understand the material before the lecture on that chapter. During class he basically reads you through the chapter very fast so don't expect to learn during class if you didn't read the textbook beforehand. The tests are much harder than the slides but he curves up in the end. Very nice guy tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor with clear lectures. Some professors assume you know things so tend to skip over steps but that is not the case with Jennings. He makes sure to leave time for questions and his office hours really help! He is funny and makes the class interesting. I was questioning whether accounting was still for me but now I am sure it is.

Awesome professor for financial accounting. Very clear lectures. Goes pretty quickly and will let you out of class when he finishes his lecture, but will always answer any questions you have. Helpful in office hours, too. Exams are very fair, but comprehensive and there's a lot to remember for them. Overall great, down-to-earth guy.

Professor Jennings was really awesome to have as a professor. I had heard bad things about some of the other accounting professors which worried me as a marketing major. Professor Jennings is definitely the professor to get! He lays everything out as straightforwardly as possible and his powerpoint slides are exceptional. He's also a super nice guy

As a non-accounting major I was pretty worried about taking 2610 after hearing such bad reviews of the class from others. However, I was lucky enough to have Professor Jennings as a teacher. If you're going to suffer through financial accounting, suffer through with him. His powerpoints are fantastic and he's really there to help you.
Joe is the best professor I've ever had.
Joe is an awesome person. Definitely take his class again. Always caring and inspirational. He is so helpful if you are struggling with your future major, especially if you are a Bio-person.

Jez is one of my favorite professors at WashU! He is extremely genuine and it is clear that he is invested in the personal and academic success of his students. He has so many great stories and experiences to share - take a class with him if you can!

Such a nice guy who is super passionate about the topic. Took him for a first year ampersand program about biotech. Presentations went really in depth on topics we were not tested on and was great for someone interested in biology without having to worry about memorizing all of it. Case studies were graded easily as well.

Joe is incredibly genuine and a great person, as well as a great professor. I am lucky to be in a two-year program with him, and he has already been a great help to me outside of class as well. Despite being incredibly accomplished and high ranking in the university, he truly treats you like a fellow scholar, even during instruction.

Really nice guy. Very enthusiastic about biochemistry. His slides are great (you don't really have to ever touch the textbook.) He's readily available to talk to outside of class, about biochem or just a chat. My favorite bio department professor.
Real nice guy! Wants everyone to understand everything even though it is diffult sometimes. Easy to get to know and want to get to know. One of my favorite professors of all time.
Content is not that hard, just read and fully understand the slides for the exam and you should be good. Talks a lot about materials irrelevant to the course.

I took Intro to International Business with Dr. James. I think these ratings are a bit harsh, while she may get off topic often, she is one of the most thoughtful and caring professors I've had at WashU. Not quite sure how she is in MGT380, but it's clear she's very knowledgable about business and a fantastic person.
If you want to hear her life story, take her class. She will talk about anything but the content of the course and then grade you on the content she did not lecture on. Overall unpleasant experience.
dont take this class

This is the most work I have ever had to do in an Olin class. There are many class exercises (that aren't really done in class) and case assignments. However, I learned so much from this course, and Professor James is an amazing teacher. She cares a lot about her students and will help you succeed in her class if you put in the effort.

This class was so awful - the prof just rambles about irrelevant information about her personal life for half of the class time. If you ask her a question she will do anything but answer it, and she is the strictest grader I have ever experienced. Do NOT take her class if you do not have to, any other professor would be better than her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: James was the most subjective person I have ever met, and though she is smart, she shouldn't be a professor. She talks down to her students, and her office hours are practically pointless. She will speak over you at any given moment, not letting you voice any concerns or questions you might have if they disagree with her perspectives or logic.AVOID
Got an A but not worth it. Take a different class. So much busy work. She is also challenging to listen to because course is so hard to follow.

Has tons of experience and knowledge in finance, strategy, etc. but often rambled about personal stories that didn't seem necessary. I learned a lot through the case studies, but there were A LOT. It was much more work than expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: I have never had a more incompetent teacher. She spent most of class rambling about unrelated topics - I know more about her life story than I do about any class material - and assigns a TON of work. She can't explain anything clearly and will out student's private conversations and grades to the class without asking permission.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The best of the best. She cares about her students a lot and their progress with the subject. She also has a very well-rounded and thoughtful perspective on life in general. Would highly recommend.

Jain Ji is an amazing professor who is super committed to helping students learn Hindi, in whatever capacity works for them. She is not only extremely knowledgable about Hindi, but also very accommodating and caring towards her students' lives. This ended up being my favorite class of the semester and I would highly recommend!

Jain Ji is the goat. Very rarely will you have a professor who is understanding of your schedule and personal life to the extent that Jain Ji is. The class is pretty easy if you have even a basic background of the language. If you don't it's a bit of a grind at the start but if you put in the effort you'll do just fine.

Professor Jain Ji is incredibly sweet and caring to her students. intro Hindi 111 is relatively easy for most students with some background knowledge, for students like me who had no background in hindi it is alot of work. She gives a ton of homework every day though if you actually do it (and not google translate) it can be genuinely helpful

Jain ji is the kindest professor I have ever had. She strives to make her course content understandable. Her workload is easy to fulfill, so don't be daunted by the high credit count. My only complaint is that she sometimes has moments where she loses her train of thought or makes mistakes during her lectures, but she always promptly corrects them.

Cell Bio is definitely one of the more challenging higher level Bio course because it relies heavily on memorization, but the structure is fair and the professor is passionate. The lectures are generally strong, though some concepts could be clarified more during class. Overall, I had a great experience learning the subject.
:( after that final

Taking this class is like a part-time job. Requires at least 15-20 hrs per week to survive. Mid teacher who likes the content and is friendly. However the quizzes and tests were made a lot harder from practice exams. The course was also made harder with a weird quiz system where you basically have to guess or hedge your bets. Poorly designed imo.

The professor is passionate about the subject. Midsemester changes to course structure and esoteric or unreasonably specific questions that make up a significant portion of quizzes and exams make this difficult course even harder.

Cell biology is a very difficult course, but Professor Wang is passionate about the subject which makes it more interesting and enjoyable. I only recommend taking this course if you are genuinely interested in the subject and are ready to study for hours each week. The tests are very difficult and studying is extremely necessary, but it is worth it

Very different from Calc 1 with Johnson. Exams are quite challenging with no curve ever, and one question wrong can deduct you a whole letter on the exam. Besides exams, the workload is light, but you have to study a lot to get a good grade in the class. You can drop a midterm for the final though.

Genuinely kind and caring prof! I struggled a lot with calc 2, and he ended rounding me up at the end. Can be confusing in lectures sometimes--I often found that there was a clearer or simpler explanation for a lot of the concepts, but he's great about providing resources (recorded lectures!) and highlighting where you can get extra help.
He is very understanding person. All of his exams were mid 70 range and final was 60 range for his class--no curve. Yikes.
His lectures are really helpful if you actually go to them. The exams aren't always super similar to the practice exams but if you study you'll do fine.

run. genuinely run. the class average was less than a 70 for every exam and he never even curved it. be prepared to study for a week and still get a 60. calc 2 doesnt need to be that hard but he makes it like that.

Prof. Johnson is so sweet and really cares about his students' success. The study guides are almost exactly like the exams and there's a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Subsections were not very helpful for me but you have to go to get credit. Overall very considerate prof with a well-organized class.

Silas Johnson is a nice guy, but his grading is extremely tough. Exams are weighted very heavily, and the averages are usually in the mid-60s, yet there is no curve at all. Lectures are fine but don't always prepare you well for the exams. I recommend avoiding his section unless you're prepared for a tough grading scheme.

Professor Johnson is very approachable and kind, but his standards for a “good proof” are extremely vague. Exams are graded very strictly, with many points deducted for minor mistakes. Lectures, homework, and exams feel poorly aligned, and his expectations on exams often differ from what is emphasized in class or homework.

Lectures were engaging, but the reason why this class was horrible for me was the grading. Homework and exams were graded harshly, and tests were made almost impossible to finish with no partial credit. Hours of studying became futile, and class exam averages were in the 60s. I am really discouraged and changed my math major because of this class.

Silas Johnson is a enthusiastic and kind lecturer who seems wholly unsuited to teach a higher level math class. The grades for HW were overly critical and for a class that is proof-based he spends little time on writing proofs in class especially towards the end of the semester. If you are considering him for a lower level class I would recommend.

I didn't learn much from his lectures, so I studied the textbook and that's when the concepts began clicking. I also wasn't used the how much small mistakes would impact my grade. Each point was 5% of the test grade (50 minutes each, 20 points total). He focused the lectures on a lot of the theory and proofs but not the topics in the homework.

He's a good guy, and that's probably the most important thing. But he's also very weird. And not the most entertaining lecturer. And he records lectures and doesn't care about attendance so very low motivation to go/pay attention. However, clearly passionate about the subject and gives VERY fair tests. Wouldn't take him again but easy A if you try.

Strong and thoughtful explanations. Lectures more theoretical than anticipated, which was nice. Short exams w/MCs allow for many opportunities to lose pts, but MCs, along w/the computations and explanation problems, weren't that hard. Material builds on itself, so a strong foundation with early content makes it easy to understand new content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Johnson constantly stressed the importance of understanding, yet the structure of the course didn't support that. Exams were rushed and heavily weighted, homework felt disconnected from lectures, and office hours were overcrowded and unhelpful. The course felt more punishing than instructive, which was disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I never showed up to lecture but Johnson posts recordings and a ton of other resources on Canvas. The material seems like it's being taught very fast but the exams always end up being reasonable -- also you get a mini cheat-sheet which is crucial since this class covers a lot of arbitrary-seeming rules and theorems.

He is excited about what he teaches, which is nice, but his grading policy is extremely harsh. The in-class exams are rushed, and all the midterms are given in 50 minutes. These exams determine more than 60% of your grade, which makes the course dreadful. His lectures are fast-paced, and I don't have time to digest the information he throws at us.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor and clearly knows/ is excited about the math he teaches. Only qualm that I had with this course was the in-class exams. The questions had significant weight since there were so few. It was stressful to prepare and stressful to take. Tests are also 75% of grade, so 150 minutes of midterms count for 50% of the course (final is 2hrs).

Professor Johnson is a great lecturer and super approachable. The class was very interesting, and it is clear he is passionate about what he does. The class was extremely difficult (especially the problem sets!!), but Professor Johnson was always helpful during office hours.

Johnson has a big heart for what he does, both as a mathematician and as a lecturer. He is so genuinely interested in the course material and deeply cares about being a good professor and taking questions seriously. I highly recommend. Especially for this class, there's a lot of online resources out there, but Silas will get you excited to learn.

He teaches SOOOOO FAST, like both he and Green teach at the same time, we already finished chapter 5 and they were just started chapter 4. Is also hard to catch up during class. The point takes so much portion on each question, the total of each exam is only 20, so basically if you messed up one writing question you are screwed. But hw are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Johnson is one of the better calc professors at WashU, which says little because the math department here is severely lacking. Very test heavy class, but his lectures were pretty good, overall understood the material. Online Fridays every week are a bonus.

This class is very test heavy in general, but that is not specific to Johnson. Johnson is a nice guy but you can tell that he is pretty odd. At the beginning of the year, I found myself pitying him more than anything else. I feel like the most helpful part of this class is his Friday video lectures. Might as well not go to the classes.
Super friendly in class and takes the time to explain topics in depth.
He goes a lot into the "why" something works. If you don't like that you might not enjoy him as a professor, but he is such a good. I really liked taking Calc with him.
he's pretty good
One of the best math professors at WashU hands down. Super intelligent and passionate about his work and always available in office hours for help. Try to take calc with him if you can.

Johnson was engaging during lectures, compellingly teaching interesting material. The content it self was difficult, as reflected in the proof-based homework. This course is not for the faint of heart, but Johnson is always willing to lend a helpful hand if asked. Johnson is a good professor, but only take 4351 if you truly love math.

I really like professor Johnson. He cares so much about the material and his students. The first exam might've been a bit too hard but the final was very fair and we had 2 take-home exams. Psets could get a bit lengthy, but the exams were always easier than the Psets. Would recommend if you love math!

Lectures are boring and go a bit too slowly. He organizes the class very easily so that all the hardest questions will be seen in class or on WebWork (homework), and the exams are honestly far easier than all of those. If you can do the practice exams, you should be able to do rather well on the actual exams.

Professor Johnson was a great professor to take number theory with. He is very knowledgeable about the subject, and he did a good job explaining the material during lectures. I felt the exams were fair, and we were given two take-home exams to help de-weight the in-person exams. He also offered lots of extra credit opportunities on PSets and exams.

Johnson is the best professor I have had in the Math department. His lectures are great and he cares about the material. He also cares about his students and goes out of his way to help students. Highly recommend taking this course with him.

Awful. The lectures are boring (not that most people go), the teaching style is mundane, and the exam will try to trick you. Dr. Johnson also makes no effort to assist struggling students. Try taking this class in a fall with another professor if you can.
He was great.
Bro didn't release exam statistics because of how horribly it went. The only thing that can save me now is Jesus.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even so much as thinking about this class genuinely makes me want to cry

I want to like this class so bad because Prof Johnson is nice, the content is interesting, and people in the class seem helpful. It is just way too difficult and feels like a full time job with overtime. So I have come to despise it which definitely makes me feel a little sad as a math major.

I can't take this anymore. I am spending so much time on this class yet doing the worst in it. I feel like I've lost my sense of pride in my work and all sense of feeling about how I perform. Someone said the class feels inaccessible and I've never agreed more. I wish i had advice to not take this class before i jumped in head first.

What went from being my favorite class at the beginning of the semester is now my most dreaded, scary, difficult, impossible class. He's not understanding of our time or responsibilities outside of this class and expects us to spend hours on HW while giving us the most impossible exams. Steer clear of this class if you want to keep your sanity.

Came to rate my professor cuz I thought I was the only one feeling terrible about this number theory class. But looks like theres a ton of others that feel this way as well. I guess it speaks for itself, just don't take MATH4351 with Silas Johnson.

This class is so disappointing. As a math major, I was so excited about Number theory and cryptography. but this class has been more annoying than fun and has destroyed my self esteem. Prof. Johnson is a good lecturer but makes the class so inaccessible almost. The problem sets take at least 10 hours and the exam was graded SO harshly.
I genuinely do not think it is possible to get an A in this class. The HW assignments are graded so harshly, and the exam averages are incredibly low.
Too hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Johnson is a good lecturer and a terrible grader. He wanted us to learn how to write rigorous proofs so he took off major points on the weekly problem sets for the most trivial errors. Not to mention the problem sets probably took around 5 hours on average to complete. I wanted to like him, but this class was more annoying than fun.

10/10 professor- easily the best for Calc 1. Tests aren't too hard- definitely use the Study hub section that he posts on canvas to study because he puts a lot of extra practice there. Textbook can be found for free online and is only used for optional extra practice. Homework is much harder than exams, but you'll get that with every math prof.
Excellent prof, teaches really well but includes a lot of extra information that would not be tested.

Professor Johnson is a nice guy. Lectures are helpful but not mandatory (he may get off track during lectures by trying to prove theorems but it's okay). Tests weren't too hard. There were also many opportunities given to receive extra credit. If you pay attention and study a bit, then you'll be fine. Textbook isn't really necessary.
Johnson is really good at explaining things and the test  are straight forward.

Really great lecturer, you can tell Johnson is extremely passionate about Math. Only complaint would be that many of the assigned homeworks contained unnecessarily hard problems that even the TAs could not figure out without an integral calculator.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's the best

Professor Johnson is clearly passionate about math and provides clear guidelines of how to succeed in the class. Overall, lectures go by relatively quickly and exams are straightforward for both calc I & II. I would just watch out if you haven't taken precalc recently.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor overall! Very friendly and highly recommend going to his office hours and getting to know him. Passionate about the subject and always encourages his students to explore math beyond calculus. He is also very helpful and understandable.
I had Johnson for Calc 1 and 2, and I am very pleased with my experience. Sometimes rambles during the lectures, but otherwise is quite funny and a very solid professor. I would highly recommend him.

Prof Johnson is incredibly friendly and warm and you can tell he's passionate about the subject he teaches. The class is pretty straightforward; as long as you understand the problems he does in class, the exams will be a breeze.

I enjoyed having Silas Johnson for calc II. His lectures were often very engaging, but I will admit that he does seem to explore the more theoretical side of the concepts as opposed to what we apply in exams. He's a great, kind professor who made calculus somewhat interesting.

He's not a bad person, and one-on-one he's incredibly helpful, but BEWARE the in class lectures-- you'll have to teach yourself. He's the type to already have expectations for the answer in his lectures so it makes it harder to follow along- if you can wait for Schafer, DO IT. My grade is due to my TA and the Organic Chemistry Tutor, not him.

Great professor and person - cares about students' success and available for office hours, questions, etc. Most homework is Webworks which are unnecessarily hard/grueling (but possible(. In-person lectures Monday and Wednesday, Friday lecture is a 45-60 min video but sometimes takes up to 2hrs to get through if you're doing all the examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, Dr. Johnson is a great professor and I would strongly recommend him if you have to take Calc (either 1 or 2). Concerning the material, this course starts off manageable but picks up in difficulty fairly quick. However, Dr. Johnson is a great lecturer and cares about students and their success. Lastly, this course is very exam heavy.

Silas is a great professor; ask questions and go to class! He has a good pace but things escalate in difficulty pretty quickly so you have to both be on top of the new topics and keep in mind the old ones. Go to his office hours and do PLTL to help too though to get a variety of explanations even if he is pretty good.

Enthusiastic about math, but must put lots of time into calc outside of just understanding lectures. Well-organized Canvas page. Webwork was stressful & above exam-level difficulty. Master practice exams, bc final grade is based on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy and consistently accessible outside of class. I did not find his lectures helpful though. He spent a lot of time talking about hypothetical problems or working out problems that were WAY more difficult than what we were actually expected to learn. Homework was very difficult too. Master the practice tests and you will do fine.

Prof Johnson is clearly passionate about math and teaching. He cares about his students and wants them to succeed.  His enthusiasm made me appreciate calc more. The practice exams were very similar to the actual exams.

Johnson cares a lot about math and making sure student feedback is received. But, he spends too much time in lectures talking about things that aren't on the exams and that are useless. Sometimes classes drag on and he would ask us to participate in the most random questions. Exams are only 18 questions, so be careful on that.

Wasn't really a fan of Silas's lecture style/lectures in general hence the 3-star rating, but you can tell he cares about his students and really loves math. He is accessible during office hours and the class itself will vary in difficulty depending on your background with Calculus, so try to stay on top of your work.

Silas Johnson is a phenomenal professor. Although I haven't completed my first semester here at WashU, I highly doubt my opinion of Dr. Johnson will change in the next month or so. In general, he's a great professor who cares about his students and teaches well, and the course itself, Math 131, is made rather easy through him.

SILAS IS AWESOME! Not only did he manage to make Calc 2 easy, but I also have a log of his funniest quotes every lecture cause he's just so iconic! Here's two of them: "You should make sure it's real algebraic magic and not weird algebraic bs." "If you saw this integral on the street, would you be able to attack it?" - Silas Johnson 2022.

Attendance isn't required for main MATH132 lectures (I never went), but be sure to keep up to date with Zoom recording/slide decks. If you do, no textbook is required. The only frustrating part of this class is the required subsection; they're often at 9 in the morning and no one wants to be there. Other than that, pretty standard calc 2 class.

Dr. Johnson was my Calc I & II professor; he has been the best and clearest instructor I have had at WashU. I enjoyed how enthusiastic and concise his lectures were--his energy made each class worth looking forward to. He explains difficult topics comprehensively and creates a thorough understanding of content. He is very gentle and approachable!

Johnson's 132 is one of my favorite classes I have taken at WashU thanks to Prof Johnson. He is clearly passionate about teaching and his students. He does a great job of getting all of the topics across to students and is very accessible and willing to help anyone. He also was very accommodating when I had Covid.

Super interesting and helpful math teacher! Glad I took him for Calc I because he really helps you with any problems you have during office hours. Tests are also very similar to practice exams, so no surprise on exam day :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: make sure to go to your subsection meetings... it surprisingly affects your grade more than you might think

You can tell he's passionate about what he does, and he seems to genuinely care about it. If you stay present during his lectures and follow his lines of reasoning, you will do well. His tests are very fair, which I always appreciate. There will be almost NO random stuff on the tests that you've never seen before, so just know the stuff from class!
Super sweet and a great lecturer. Professor Johnson is always accessible after class for help on concepts and Webwork problems. He obviously is passionate about teaching and is great at it.
I love Dr. Johnson! I had him for calc 1 and 2 and he was extremely helpful in both. You can tell he loves his job and his subject. Go to office hours for webwork help!

The best math professor I have ever had in my entire academic career. Professor Johnson is excellent at teaching difficult concepts in Calculus. He understands that the material can be difficult and is sure to explain everything he teaches in the most approachable manner. He is also an incredibly nice person; its easy to ask him questions.
Explained math concepts very well. Goes into depth about the proofs for theories and math problems.

Prof. Silas is one of the best math teachers I've had. He gives very detailed explanations of the material we're learning and he's very accessible outside of class. If you're ever struggling make sure to go to his office hours! He's really cool and an overall good teacher. Calculus is hard in general, but he tries his best to explain it well!

Prof Johnson is super nice and adapted the class extremely well to the pandemic. You can tell he actually cares about his students and really loves teaching. He is very receptive to emails and is helpful in office hours. The class is pretty homework heavy and was a lot of work but you get the grade you work for. Would definitely recommend.

He's always ready to help you and he makes his lectures easy to understand. It's also super easy to ask questions and get clarification on the more difficult parts. Even when the class moved online halfway through the semester, he made it as easy as possible to succeed.

Professor Johnson is really great. He's approachable and truly wants to help his students succeed. The practice tests are very useful. The tests are manageable and the class is pretty easy-going. I really enjoyed the class!

I had Prof. Johnson for both Calculus I and II. He is truly an amazing professor and always available to help. His exams are short, and if you miss a couple questions, you could be dropped a letter grade. However, he gives you plenty of chances and opportunities to succeed in the course and roots for everyone to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Johnson is amazing. He's the absolute perfect prof for the calc 1 calc 2 sequence because he teaches the most important fundamentals of calculus that will help you later on in math. The grade has an easy grading policy and easy exams although they are worth a lot of your grade. Take calc 1 in fall and 2 in spring so you can have Johnson :)

Dr. Johnson is a hit or miss for many students. While I attended almost every lecture, many of my friends chose to skip and did well in the class. His lectures can be very boring but he truly loves what he is doing. Exams are super easy if you know the content on the practice exam beforehand.

After the first month I can count on my hand the amount of time I went to lecture. Johnson is a good guy but I didn't get any benefit from lectures that do not reflect the hw(quite a bit of it), subsection(also unhelpful), or exams. The information is in the slides(somewhat) and textbook but I self-taught through the class with the help of pltl.

He made so many mistakes on webwork (and in ppts). For example, the very first webwork had a question that took me 96 attempts to get the right answer and turned out to be him entering the wrong number. Every time he made a mistake, I had to waste more than half an hour on the wrong problem doubting myself and asking friends who are better in Math.

Professor Johnson is a gem. Although the weekly homework was hard, he was very accessible at office hours and would help you through work without just giving you the answer. The midterms were take home, but you could work with him in office hours. The final was 40% of your grade but wasn't super hard and modeled directly off of the practice exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: hes a very fair professor and really good in my opinion. Do your work and do all the problems and you will get an A almost guranteed

he's definitely better than the other professors for matrix. he always provided a review guide of exactly what topics are on the midterm, as well as a practice test, which I know the other professor does not give. take him if you HAVE to take matrix, at least not Chi. class lectures were hard but the hard stuff was never on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Prof. Kerr is very nice, the lecture note for this class is super detailed and done in legible LaTex (note that this doesn't seem to be the case in other classes).
The lecture doesn't skip every step of the proof, so its really hard to catch up.
Honestly, the grading is very generous, and if you work hard, you'll get the grade you deserve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Clearly passionate about the course content and about helping students learn and engage with difficult math. Was very flexible, and granted numerous extensions. Gave detailed exam prep and exams were fair, and graded very reasonably. Great professor!

Very fast lectures. I found it more valuable to just go over the lecture notes myself, although they were hard to read at times. Homework length ramped up after add/drop, and by the end of the semester I was spending 12+ hours per set. The homeworks are generally indicative of the exams, and the exams were fair. You do as well as you think you did.

Really kind person but bad teacher. He is passionate about math himself, but shouldn't have put these in lecture and homework. I guess he wants students to see more math but it actually confused and discouraged us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Kerr is a good guy. Don't take him unless you truly want to challenge yourself. He will mix many other hard things, such as Algebra, Geometry, Differential Geometry, etc, making this course super difficult. The homework problems are very challenging, but the exams are fair. The grading is not too tough. Office hours are somehow very helpful.

kerr is an amazing professor and one of the reasons i considered and became a math major. class is very fast paced and covers a lot of topics. however, you can tell kerr cares a lot about his students and the material. homework makes up most of the grade and is graded leniently. exams are fair and practice exams cover all the necessary material.

classes are very lecture heavy and can feel like a drag, but kerr himself is wonderful. work load is a lot, but grading is easy and homework makes up most of your grade. this class is what led me to become a math major. adore him

I absolutely loved the Honors Math sequence! Kerr is an amazing professor and just a nice person. He's really understanding about our workload and is always happy to give an extension or explain the material again. His lectures are goated. They can go fast, but once you get used to it, you realize how cool they are. It's hard, but very rewarding

Kerr is absolutely awesome. The start of the semester is a tough adjustment as he lectures really fast, but you get used to it. He's just a great guy, explains everything really well, is happy to answer questions about and beyond the material, and is understanding about the workload. Homework is very fun. If you like math, you will like his class.
He gives great lectures, but the course is simply too hard.
Very fast but rewarding. He always showed us his cat after the zoom meeting.
this man is amazing... i hope to be as smart as him when i grow up. great class! especially for math majors.
Matt teaches excellent course and gives good grades at the same time.
Best professor !!

It truly pains me to see people in classes like 132 and 309 complain about Matt, he wants to teach math, not teach you how to use math so you can get your prereqs out of the way. If you merely want to get math prereqs out of the way, take someone else. If you want someone to open the door to advanced mathematics and teach math, take his class.

It is a great injustice that Matt Kerr is not rated a 5. When he lectures, it is clear how passionate he is about the subject material . If you take a course with Matt Kerr, if you put in as much effort into the class as he does teaching it, you'll be sure to learn many useful things, don't be afraid to ask questions.

Lectures are fast-paced, but Prof Kerr's energy made them incredibly interesting. While it takes effort to keep up with lectures and homework can be extremely difficult, he is always willing to help outside of class. He is one of the easiest people to talk to and he truly wants every student to do well. My favorite professor!

Professor Kerr is amazing! He really cares about his students and really wants them to succeed. It was a difficult class but he did everything he could to give me the opportunity to get an A- or higher, even though I struggled a bit. He has a very fast teaching style, which is definitely difficult at first but not something you cannot get used to!

Super passionate about the material and gets excited while teaching. Lecture material is very advanced and theoretical, while homework and tests focus more on applications, which is a nice balance and makes the course easier. You really learn a lot.
He gives good lectures and well-organized notes. The exams are way easier than what he taught in his lectures. Also very nice person and definitely accessible after class.

You can clearly tell the dude is very smart and knows exactly what he's talking about, but does not realize at all most people are students learning this stuff for the first time. His lectures are too difficult because he skips steps, goes way too fast, and uses huge terminology/jargon. Reading the textbook is a must if you want to understand.

It's much easier to complain about how hard Kerr is than appreciate how great of a learning experience his class is. If you want to learn math and are willing to put in the time to learn it, the class is an incredible learning experience. His lectures are outstanding. Don't be afraid; many get irritated by the fact that his lectures are difficult.

Please do not take a class with Kerr. It was one of the worst decisions I mae this semester. Going to lecture actually confused me more than skipping it because Kerr goes way too fast, does not know how to explain anything, and provides terribly hard and complicated examples. I completely taught myself all the material outside of class. SKIP!!!!

He is infuriating during class. You can tell he is trying his best, but his examples and explanations are confusing a difficult to follow. The webworks are too long and too difficult, to the point where it makes more sense to just plug the problem into Wolfram Alpha than to waste any more time trying to solve them. The tests are also very hard
Matt Kerr is super hot.  And smart.  Beware: he will actually try to teach you real math.

Kerr is by far the smartest human being I have ever and probably will ever come into contact with. He's brilliant to a fault; he seems to underestimate the difficulty of the material and darts from one concept to another with remarkable and oftentimes frustrating speed. You will learn a lot if you put in the time and effort.

Kerr is a huge nerd--it's great. He's full of dad jokes; if you love math, you'll love Kerr. As a lecturer though, he can be confusing. Read the textbook before class! Makes lectures way easier to follow since he goes so quickly. His explanations aren't the easiest to follow. Definitely a lot of outside learning. Tests are fair but challenging.
Tests and homework are extremely difficult, lectures are very fast and examples usually arent well-explained

Kerr is a smart guy but goes VERY fast in lectures and self-study is a must in this course. I had to drop the class because I got completely lost with his lectures and failed a test, and have heard of many upperclassmen withdrawing from Kerr's class only to do much better the following semester.
Most of your grade will be exams and quizzes. The lectures can be a bit boring but you'll get through. The content sometimes appears simple but the tests sure weren't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very nice and clears up info. Exams are very difficult, PLTL(extra practice course on weekend) practice exams are the best resourc. Lectures is just an introduction to the material; you need to practice outside of class. The professor for this course doesn't really matter; there are good resources to answer questions. I also like her demos.

It can be tough to understand, but she knows her stuff. I would say pleasant, but no nonsense. Exams can be tricky. Carefully read q's and anticipate there is a trick involved. No doubt she is the best option for 1601/1602 - I would avoid Hamdi.

Not sure why people are rating Dr. Luo so low. The class is hard, tell me about it. But she is so nice and truly wants you to pass her class. Chemistry is hard, but she tries very hard to make you learn as much as you can.

1601 proved more challenging than I had anticipated; however, I appreciated how Dr. Luo reinforced chemistry concepts I had previously encountered yet felt distant from. Her lectures are content-rich. The exams are a time crunch, even though I consider myself a strong test-taker. I switched to 1702, but I would've took 1602 with Luo.
Chem1600 can be a very challenging class, however, Luo makes it much better. The content is challenging and the tests aren't very straightforward, so study hard.
She was hard to understand in lectures, but if you put in the effort you should be able to get a good grade. Make sure to use previous quizzes to prepare for exams/final.

Dr. Luo was an amazing teacher. She really cares about her students and wants you to succeed. She offers a lot of help when you are confused. The homework and quizzes for this class weren't too bad, but be prepared for pretty tough exams!
Very interesting class, with many resources provided, but beware: tests in this class are different beasts.

Professor Luo is a great professor, and I enjoy her lecture style where she hand writes notes. The lectures are very fast paced, but if you do all of the problem sets (both graded and non-graded) and go to PLTL sessions, it's not so bad. You have to know exactly what you're doing going into an exam because you really are rushed, like everyone says.
Does not engage with students much outside of the classroom.

The material is challenging and fast-paced. Her lectures are solid, especially if you like taking notes. The professor-student relationship is more formal. The exams are no joke, extremely difficult and very time-pressured. I highly recommend taking PLTL it makes a HUGE difference in understanding and keeping up.

exams are extremely difficult and thorough, designed to be a time crunch. while this class is a beast, it changed my entire approach to learning for the better, and it helped me become a much stronger stem person. i'm taking orgo at a different university this summer and the depth and difficulty of 105/106 has prepared me really well.

Something is wrong w 105/6. After 2 semesters I am not sure I learned anything except how to take tests. I am not sure if it was J Luo's teaching or the organization of the course, but it was very frustrating.

I high Aed 105 but 106 was a beast. I was in between A- and B+ range. Exams were insanely difficult. Take chem 105 and then 112 if possible bc their exams and class curve is much easier. Dr luo was a joy to work with, tho, and she wants all her students to succeed. the way 106 is built tho is impossible and this was her first time teaching it
I liked professor Luo. She gave clear lectures and didn't go too quickly.
chem is rly hard :( but luo genuinely wants u to succeed and is always accessible after class or at office hours or even for personal meetings. lots of resources to succeed

If you are going to take 105 - take it with Dr. Luo. She covers all the material, and actually knows what she tis talking about. She offers help if you ask for it, and will have one on one meetings to discuss where you are struggling in the class. The tests are HARD, but if you're pre-med there is no getting around it.

Lou knows her stuff and is very oriented and detail oriented (maybe too much so). Questions on exams are often marked wrong if you do not exactly use her words, even if you got the question right. I don't know, but she seems to resent that she is teaching us. No excitement and she does not connect.

Dr. Luo is an amazing professor. She is very caring and her lectures are clear. She is very approachable if you are struggling in a topic as well. The exams are very difficult and have a major time crunch. It is very important to use available resources in this class. Overall, I learned a lot during her class and am taking her for Chem 106 as well!

Dr Luo covers all the content efficiently, but I think the class could be a lot more engaging if she demonstrated some passion for her subject. She tries to give allegories, to help students understand the content, and half of them are good. overall she is a boring but efficient lecturer.

Dr. Luo is an amazing person and professor. The first few weeks of school I sobbed in her office thinking I couldn't handle college-level chemistry and she was so kind and understanding. Definitely schedule a meeting with her if you are feeling overwhelmed she is so nice!!! I had never taken any sort of chem in high school and managed to do fine!

Dr. Luo is a great lecturer who knows how to effectively teach the material in a crystal clear way! While the course is not easy and the exams are difficult with a huge time crunch, the professor team provides ample resources outside of class for help. Your success in the course requires taking advantage of as many of these resources as necessary

Luo is hands down the best chem 105 lecturer. It's very to understand her and she teaches the topics really well. Her note-taking style is amazing. However, 105/106 (also 111/112) is a very hard class and the exams are tough. She's still the goat tho.

She was extremely unhelpful, rude, and disrespectful. If you do end up taking this class I recommend not even showing up to lectures and just watching the recording because she goes way too fast in lecture. If you want to go to ask questions don't because she won't answer them and will just tell you to rewatch lectures and read the textbook.

Intro chem is lowkey a premed weedout since exams are such a time rush, but had no complaints for Luo. Lectures are pretty notes-intense (lots of copying/writing/drawing), but they're always recorded/posted, attendance optional. She explains things pretty well and seems to genuinely care about making sure people actually understand what's going on.

Dr. Luo is so sweet. Lectures were super clear, and she always wrote down the little side notes, so you weren't scrambling to scribble down random tangents. I have never felt more calm in a class. Straightforward quizzes/exams. Love her!! Also, she never complains about how most students/staff mispronounce her name :'D (pls learn how to say it)

Dr. Luo was definitely caring, but a bit boring. She was expecting and ended up on maternity leave, so that could be part of the lack of energy. I was hoping for new material, but it ended up being just like highschool, albeit with a few trick questions on exams. So, not a bad course, but not a great course.

Luo is an absolute gem and you should definitely take her for 105/106 if possible. She is so sweet and cares about her students, but also is a girl boss and so smart. She teaches very clearly and makes it easy to take notes and do well on assessments. The class is hard, but she makes it enjoyable.

Professor Luo explains concepts in a way that makes sense to mos. Her demonstrations are always informative and, at the end of the demonstration, she asks for feedback. Although, the lectures are content dense, she always somehow manages to make the class laugh. Attendance is not recorded but, personally, I feel like being in lecture is the best.

Dr. Luo is the best professor I have had at WashU. She is extremely organized, and her lectures are easy to follow. I struggled with chemistry in high school, but Dr. Luo explains everything in a way that is easy to understand.

Dr. Luo is a fabulous professor and you should definitely take her class if you are planning on taking chem 105 at WashU. The tests are definitely challenging but as long as you go to lectures and stay on top of work and studying, it isn't hard to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Luo is the best prof to take for 105. She is fine, but the course is hs chemistry, at best. Just memorize hw problems and ez A. Don't take 105 if you are doing a science major.
Great Professor, easy class, dedicate an hour / week and you will be fine.

I LOVE Professor Luo. I had a limited chemistry background and was very nervous for this course. But, Luo is an incredible teacher and made the content very understandable. Chem 105 as a whole has great, accessible resources that you should definitely take advantage of (PLTL!!!) This class definitely requires work, but it's far from impossible

Dr. Luo isn't just a professor--she's a teacher. She's an incredible lecturer who cares about her students. Topics are always well-explained, and she's very accessible outside of class if you need help. She's encouraging, and emphasizes improvement over perfection. Dr. Luo is passionate about both chemistry and teaching. Take a class with her!

Chem 105 has definitely been the course that has taken up most of my time this semester. That being said, Prof. Luo is a wonderful instructor, and you can tell that she truly cares about her students the subject she teaches. Definitely dedicate lots of time to studying for exams, and take PLTL, and you will ace this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Everything pretty much everyone else has said here!
took 106 first and then 105. Luo makes these concepts as easy as a breeze. Tests are nothing compared to 106. Enjoy chem 105 while you can before getting into 106

Luo is definitely one of the best lecturers in the chem department. The class is hard but that's not her fault, there's just a lot of content. The scale for the class makes it easier to get a good grade but you will definitely still have to study.

Luo is super kind and incredibly talented. She even manages to make chemistry interesting! One note: don't waste your money on the textbook, you won't need it, all the necessary study materials are provided by the course. Class can be hard, but resources are always available.

She is incredibly organized compared to the other 105 professors. Stay CLEAR of Bakupog. He is all over the place and hard to understand. She is very accessible and makes an effort to get to know students. Utilize all the resources you can and you will do well. Ask questions early as well. her accent takes an adjustment but it ends up being fine.

Dr. Luo is a gem of the chemistry department. She is genuinely such a great person and will answer any question you have, both clearly and thoroughly. She is very knowledgeable and skilled in chemistry and is compassionate and understanding. She is the reason I somewhat enjoy chemistry now. Thank you Dr Luo!!

Luo is an excellent lecture and explains concepts thoroughly. Gen chem is quite difficult, but if you just put in the effort to read through your notes and engage with all the material and ask your questions, you'll be just fine. You can always reach out to her during office hours, in class, or even through email, and she'll explain it clearly.

I think Professor Luo was a great teacher. She truly cared about her students and wanted to see them succeed. Her lectures were well paced and it was easy to take notes and keep up. Her tests were hard, but if you studied your notes, understood the content, and went to PLTL, you could do well on them. Overall, 10/10 for Luo!!! Such a sweetheart :)

Luo has definitely found her calling in teaching Chemistry. She is able to explain stuff clearly and easily, and makes an effort to know students by their names. In 106, she is not a lecturer, but she will help more than Mabbs. Do not depend on Luo to teach everything to you; use her as an aid for understanding concepts. 106 is a rigorous class.

The sweetest. Even though it was a large lecture hall, she made an effort to know the students. I wasn't expecting her to ever even know my name, but sure enough, she did. Goes over lecture clearly. Take PLTL to gain a deeper understanding of the concepts though, as this will help with quizzes and exams.

Although I chose the pass/failed option and did not go to class regularly, I'd like to say she is amazing and inspirational. Go to her office hours and she will definitely share a lot with you! The class is difficult so you need to try hard.

Chem 105/106 was the hardest class I've taken at WashU and Prof Luo's teaching did little to remedy that. Definitely go to office hours but also join PLTL and make sure you have a solid grasp on the material because the example problems she goes over are not nearly as difficult as the exam questions. Chem 106 is nightmare fuel compared to 105.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you're confused by any concepts, you can always count on Dr. Luo to explain things very clearly. She's very helpful during office hours and she truly cares about her students. She's able to explain difficult concepts very easily, and I always come out of her help sessions with a broader understanding of the material.

She seems pleasant, but she can be rude in help sessions. Makes you feel stupid. It is also frustrating to ask a question, and she just repeats herself without answering the question. I would hope a professor could explain topics without looking at a key or her notes. Just memorize the problem sets, and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Shes a nice person, but the lectures she gave often were not representative of what was on exams (class examples were too easy). She is accessible but sometimes when she explains things it actually made me more confused. Nice  easy
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thought I was the sh!t the first day of class. It seemed so easy to begin with then got hard FAST. The first exam grade really humbled me, then I got As on the next midterms but missed the A by a handful of points due to the final. Dr. Luo offers a welcoming atmosphere to learn chemistry, but dont mistake welcoming for easy.

Such a great prof honestly. Material and tests are definitely hard but she explains topics really well in lecture. She really knows her stuff and is more than happy to help. Schaefer is one of the most wonderful teachers I've ever had. He is always happy to help and gives a lot of opportunities for help outside of lectures. If you have the choice, take any one of his classes!
