While the transition to college math wasn't super easy, I really enjoyed taking calc 2 with Schaefer.

Professor Schaefer is a great teacher. He really understands the material and presents it in a pretty easy way to understand. The homework makes up for a fair portion of the grade so the grades aren't solely based on exams. Overall, great class and he is very inclusive and cares about his students.
Genuinely a great math professor who cares about the success of his students. Easy to follow along with and is always willing to answer questions
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I found this class difficult but Professor Schaefer's lectures were great. Lots of examples to refer back to.

I know people that watch all of Schaefer's lectures on top of going to their Calc II professor's class because he is so great at teaching. On top of that he is just a great guy. He also cares a lot about his students and is VERY receptive to feedback. He goes above and beyond to make the class enjoyable. Couldn't recommend more, 10/10!

An amazing person and professor. Although Calc II is by no means an easy class lectures are well planned, well-paced, run smoothly and prepare you for the homework and quizzes. Professor Schaefer seems to get the perfect balance of time for questions, lecture, and the time seems to really fly by. It is clear that he cares and wants you to succeed.
Best math professor I've had so far.

I love this man. He taught this course hybrid during covid, allowing students to come in. He really made a difference, easily the best course I took the semester. Very good lecturer, I can tell he really cares. If his ratings are low it is because the class is hard, not because he is a bad teacher - he is far from that.

Despite his poor handwriting, I thought Prof. Schaefer explained concepts pretty well, or at least well enough for me to understand them for the quizzes. Quizzes every week can be annoying but ensures you are cumulatively understanding the information. He is very accessible and willing to help, and the workload overall is pretty standard.

I also had him for 233. He is a completely reasonable and intelligent professor, and I thought he did a perfect job explaining concepts and performing examples via online lectures. His explanations of calculus concepts were the clearest I've seen any professor give. Quizzes are not easy, but 100% manageable, and I had option to drop lowest 2 or 3

The hate for Schaefer isn't warranted especially if you take his classes in person. You can really tell that he cares about his students and makes an effort to answer any and all questions in class (and gives comprehensive and thorough answers on Piazza). Very good, likable guy. Exams aren't too bad but sometimes are a bit conceptual. Good lectures
Really nice guy. Good lectures, bad handwriting

I took him remotely, so take this as you will. I am not a big math person, but his lectures were interesting and thorough to make me understand concepts I had not previously. The hw is not too bad, but the quizzes/tests will be difficult, so make sure you attend your discussion sections, as often the quizzes will be based more on those than the hw.

It's a lot of work. I don't know if COVID played a major role in my opinion on this class but I think Prof Schaefer could've done a better job of finishing examples in lectures, providing HW that at least resembled what we were being quizzed on, providing any practice quizzes, & giving reasonable length quizzes. Some of the quizzes averaged  55%.

This is a hard teacher. I personally liked him. Many people did not. He taught the concepts okay but I think he cared about the students. The quizzes are HARD. However, read the syllabus and you will see that the class grading scale gives leniency. You really need to do textbook problems, pay very good attention in class, and work super hard

Professor Shaefer is a really great guy. Although this class was definitely the hardest class I took this semester, I think he did a good job teaching considering the pandemic. The best part about Professor Shaefer is the amount of genuine care he has for his students. He is incredibly accessible by email and writes really kind & lengthy responses

Professor Schaefer is an amazing prof! I don't always enjoy math, but his lectures were consistently interesting and informative. There was usually some stuff that I didn't get on the first pass - I think he could've gone a little slower - but I was always able to get help in office hours. Quizzes and the Midterm were hard but fair. Study lots!

I feel like it's tough to give an accurate rating for prof shaefer. On the one hand, he's super nice and gives very in-depth help if you're looking for it. On the other hand, his lectures aren't great (I imagine that pre-covid lectures would have been better). and his quizzes are really hard.

Prof Shaefer is a nice guy but not a great teacher. He acts like we are supposed to know the material before we've even learned it. The pace of the course is way too fast and he does not prepare you for the homework, assignments, and quizzes.

Somewhat dry lectures but he presents the content very well and he is very articulate about everything he teaches. He returns things late and feedback is somewhat suspect (feels AI) but is overall a good professor for a pretty easy grade,

The topic of this class is very interesting and important, though Professor Krummenacher is a bit of a dry lecturer and it can be difficult to stay focused because of that. The class was not difficult, though.
Such a dry lecturer. Boring class and unnecessary critical when grading. Still, it's an easy class and he's a nice guy.
Somehow made some very interesting content incredibly boring and milquetoast. Unfortunate use of humor makes lectures legitimately hard to sit through. Class was pretty easy though...
Incredibly boring class and a complete waste of time. Very dry lecturer. Weirdly harsh grader for never giving any guidance. I did not enjoy the class and definitely did not recommend it.

Nice guy and good lecturer. Dry at times. Grading standards seem to be applied inconsistently and are often unclear. Grading of assignments also takes extremely long despite there being only about ~50 students with 2 professors and 2 TAs, even with mainly group projects. Mandatory attendance and voluntarily speaking in lecture is a must to do well.

As someone who isn't very familiar with Environmental Science topics, Professor Krummenacher was a great introduction! Although lectures felt dry at times, he is seriously a caring guy. I had a lot of circumstances in which I had to be absent during the semester (illness, family issues), and he was very understanding of that.

Took Environmental Racism with Scott, which he co-taught with Angela Hobson. Straightforward class, very accessible. Learned more about STL from slides and guest speakers. Final assignment was a group project but my randomly assigned people were great to work with. Caring, had pizza/oranges party last class. Awesome option for STEM credit class!

He's so sweet. Class is super interesting and it's easy to do well. Homework for every class is just reading, but I never did them, and it was fine There are a couple quizzes and a final essay, but he prepares you well throughout the semester to do good on the essay. He's engaging and puts up slides that are easy to take notes on. Would recommend

Professor Krummenacher is truly outstanding. He gives great lectures, is understanding, and genuinely cares about individual students. He is also very understanding if you speak to him about a missed deadline. I would 100% recommend this professor. He has exceeded every one of my expectations for a teacher.

I have really enjoyed class with Prof Krummenacher. The textbook for Sustainable Cities is actually excellent and this class has been a really positive experience for me. Lectures can be a bit dry, but this guy loves a dad joke. Homework and quizzes can be time-consuming, but aren't too difficult. Great class!

Prof Krummenacher is caring and obviously passionate about what he teaches. The class is pretty easy, and all of the assignments are based around building up to the final paper. The only con is that he is a very slow grader and often does not grade quizzes/assignments by the time he says he will, which is frustrating.

Dr. Scott is very clear about grading, expectations, and homework. Class was organized well. He is also a kind person and very understanding 

This class has a few online quizzes (open note) that were easy if you'd been in class. There is a finally essay, but the class builds up to it all semester with smaller assignments that become incorporated

Although he cracked jokes during class and did his best to keep it interesting, class lectures were at times dry if you didn't LOVE the content that day. Had attendance problems to the point where they created a sign-in sheet in the middle of the semester. Great speakers though and easy grading and quizzes.

Sure, he can be dry, but he's so caring and fun at the same time. Take a class with him! You'll get a good grade if you try, and super interesting topic. Such a sweetheart. He combines group stuff with individual work. Will be taking his classes next year.

Definitely felt like I was challenged in my views during class in a good way that broadened my horizons and adjusted the way I think about things. Scott breaks down concepts well in class and is great at answering questions and responding to criticisms and requests about the course - he always tries to make it as good of an experience as possible.

just lots of lecturing. some quizzes that were really hard. honestly did learn some interesting things but not worth a semester of my time. he did round up my grade like an extra point at the end which was nice

This course taught me so much about the environment & urban landscapes! Yes Scott is a bit dry but I enjoyed the readings and class and it was super organized. The final paper was stressful but he structured it well & I am so grateful I learned how to organize research. Scott wants students to do well and appreciates in-class participation.

Prof. Krummenacher is a good lecturer if a bit dry.  He can go on some tangents or not get the point, but he is pretty good about answering questions and giving relevant feedback for assignments. Overall, the class taught me a lot but it could have been a bit more interesting.

His lectures aren't particularly inspiring as he isn't quite Bernie Sanders when it comes to charisma. But Scott is a kind, humble man who is genuinely interested in his content and wants students to learn and succeed.

Scotty K is probably the best professor ever. He has a dry (but great) sense of humor and loves the material he teachers. He makes an effort to get to know you, even in a big class, and his lectures are great. His passionate hate for cars and urban sprawl are hot. Definitely take this class!

Pretty good class, great professor. Nice, approachable, funny (in a dry way). He is passionate about the subject and tries to make even the more dull material interesting, and he usually succeeds. The textbook is very dense and boring, but lectures were engaging. Probably won't study environmental policy further, but still glad I took his class.
He is the most average professor in the history of professors. He is fair and boring. His humor is so dry it makes me thirsty.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class can be dense sometimes, but if you like the material it isnt a problem. Exams are pretty straightforward, and if you know your stuff you'll do well. Highly recommend his office hours; if you're confused about anything he's super nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Krummenacher is a very kind person and he really cares about his students. I found many of his lectures to be boring, but I care about the subject matter so it wasn't too bad. There was barely any homework and the exams are very reasonable if you go to class and read the text book.

Professor Krummenacher was awesome. His lectures are so straightforward and tests are relatively easy multiple choice. He's not trying to trick you. Unfortunately this class is at 8:30 am so everyone is half asleep, but it's still not too bad. Could be more exciting and engaging, but still the material is interesting and feels very relevant.

Globalization, Urbanization, and the Environment was a big disappointment. The material is mostly surface-level and descriptive, with little analysis or explanation or policy discussion. Yet somehow the tests are frustratingly difficult due to tricky wording or nuanced details which don't test your comprehension at any real depth. I would avoid.
Matthew Kummer = GOAT

I think a lot of the reviews here are unfair. I took two semesters of lab with Dr. Kummer and had a great experience. He was always willing to answer questions, cared about how students were doing, and genuinely wanted people to succeed. You could tell he put a lot of effort into helping students. I thoroughly enjoyed both semesters.

Professor Kummer is incredibly nice, understanding, and supportive of his students. It is obvious that he cares very deeply. Unfortunately, the class is just incredibly difficult... but he tries his best to have a positive attitude towards it. Took all student feedback into consideration when shifting from 1751 to 1752. Humble and respectful guy.

While the exams were difficult, Kummer has been the most accommodating professor I've had so far. I found his end of year speech endearing and I believe he truly takes students feedback into account to improve his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of improvement from Chem 1751. 1751 was not bad, but 1st exam was bad since the practice exam was easier, after I figured out the strategy for later exams. He gives 10 points for writing notebook and 5 for problem set. Reports can be challenging, but help is available. Funny lectures cool shirts, interesting guy outside of chem
Pretty good!

Dr. K has improved a lot as a lecturer. First 1751 midterm was unreasonable and the reason for all the 1 star reviews. Excessive writing for 2 credits. However, he has improved a lot at teaching and took feedback into account second semester. Great guy, course should be better for future students.

Kummer is clearly passionate about chem lab & supporting students. There's strong support through office hours & help sessions: use them to succeed. Exams were better than first semester; understand why the experiment is set up that way, report calculations, common Sloppy mistakes, & how the core ideas can be extended to novel exam scenarios!

Dr. Kummer is clearly passionate about chemistry and cares about the students in his class. His new curriculum has understandably caused some changes in the student experience, but he takes feedback under advisement and is responsive to criticism.

Sweetest professor and responds so quickly to any concerns, absolutely amazing and very interested in topics. Above this the class has gotten a lot more comprehensive since the first semester. Overall though would not recommend class , like some else said for 2 credits you get so much extra workload and stress. Professor is nice, but hardest lab.
Nice guy and good lecturer. The class wasn't great first semester, but he improved a lot of things pretty quickly.
Kummer got nicer as the year went on but overall just a really rough class that is very difficult and time-consuming. Very stressful and should be worth more than 2 credits. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great guy, cares about his students and is positive. Class could have been structured better but will improve with time probably.
Cares a lot about students. First time teaching so not everything was the most clear. Things will probably turn out better as years go on. Handwriting was really time consuming ,though.
This was a very hard class, but Dr. K definitely cares about his students. If you go to mentor hours and put the time in it is possible to succeed

Professor Kummer is very clearly passionate about teaching the material and lectures are bearable due to his enthusiasm. However, there is an incredible amount of work that must be done for this course, both in preparation for labs and exams. I have spent upwards of 4+ hours filling out my notebook for one pre-lab.

Nice guy but his class sucks. Way too much work and way too hard for a 2 credit course. I don't think the poor design of the class is Dr. Kummer's fault though, and he genuinely is very kind and approachable outside of class. Overall, good prof that cares about his students, but unfortunately, his class is just one that you gotta suffer through.

If I were to give an award for the most improved professor at WashU, I would give it to Dr. K. The class isn't perfect, but his ratings from last semester don't reflect his current standing. No practice exams and the autograder is finicky, but I'm sure he'll make adjustments next semester.

Dr. K is so caring and is overall such a wonderful human being. He teaches a very difficult pre-med course, so it's going to be difficult. If you just do the work and apply yourself, you'll be find. He really is passionate about Chemistry, so I respect his enthusiasm and work.

Copying the procedure in notebooks takes 3+ hours, but it's for safety and accidents actually decreased. No practice material for the midterm and the average was a 60%, final was better. Lotta outside support/office hours. Boring work, hard for ppl with little chem background, but he's very enthusiastic and overhated. 1752 autograder unfair tho.

Dr. Kummer is seriously amazing. He originally got a lot of hate because people got a wake up call to the demanding nature of college courses. Without a doubt the most enthusiastic and caring professor I've met. Truly wants whats best for his students. Course expectations are extremely clear, lectures are to the point, lots of resources for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. K is a phenomenal lecturer and is one of the most caring and kind profs I've met. He is alw ready to help (he will respond to you with the utmost detail if you email him!). However, the course itself is incredibly difficult in terms of workload and does not match the credit hours. This is an issue that needs to be dealt with by the department.

The class is really hard but builds up your science skills. It makes sense he has low ratings because freshman aren't used to the workload. It is kind of a jump into the deep end introduction. Please give him the benefit of the doubt, he's passionate about the topic its just a really hard class.
The class is naturally a difficult course and I think no other person could have managed it better than Kummer. You can tell that he is very passionate about chemistry, and he is very eloquent.

A kind and funny man... this is a problem with the whole chem department having no mercy for their students. There is a misunderstanding in what the goals of the class should be. This class is a 2 credit course but is incredibly demanding and it is set up horribly. If he/chem d wants this performance the credits must match.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a good guy. To succeed in this class, you have to make sure you are reading the lab manuels and not falling behind (which I have yet to do).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice guy but nah bro
as of march 5 he has a 2/5 lets see the damage from this midterm

Difficulty does not match the credits. Kummer is a good person, and a good lecturer, however the setup of the course is just unfair. This and chem lecture combined account for 60% of my course workload. In 2nd semester Kummer introduced an extremely buggy auto grader that is prone to errors. I don't know why this change was made but it is not fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kummer is one of the nicest professors you will ever have; however, he makes the course extremely difficult. It is evident that he's passionate about chemistry, but his lectures and exams can be really hard to follow/prepare for. You'll hear a lot of bad things about him, but mostly because people didn't get an easy A.
Course is a little hard especially if you've never done AP Chem but still doable and Dr. K is very caring
Such a nice guy, some of the tests are very hard. But a genuine guy that cares for his students.
Great Guy. Genuine, just teaches a hard subject. Probably the best guy to do it.

This is a tough class, and there are quite a few aspects of gen chem lab that are not fun. The reports are tedious, the homework and tests are challenging, and sometimes it can feel overwhelming. I don't believe there is much that Prof K can do about those things. He works hard on the material, and he cares about us.
I am thankful to have him as a teacher. He is kind, understanding, and professional.

This class demonstrates that WashU has, by far, one of the hardest chem tracks out of universities I've looked into. Best of luck to all of the pre-meds who will be taking his class. Any commentary about WashU chem lab being EASY is OUTDATED, but Kummer is otherwise lowkey a GOAT with how he handled the shut-down emergency situation (look it up)!
Lots of work, but he is super nice and understanding!
His class is hard but he's really nice!!!

Though many people hate on him because the class is difficult, he is actually very kind and understanding. Multiple times I have submitted things to the wrong places, and he has been very understanding in getting it sorted. Additionally, unlike other professors, he is very accommodating.
The goat :)
W professor - my goat

There appears to be little consideration for student workload balance or modern instructional practices. The rigidity of the teaching philosophy does not align with current educational approaches that emphasize clarity, accessibility, and student development.
I like his hawaiian shirts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Pick a god and pray.

First weeks were diffucult, have to write labnote books but don't copy exact b/c it takes to long. Lectures are not useful, lots of content to cover in little time. Reports aren't bad lots of help avaiable, study reports for exam. Since it is new instructor there was no accuarte practice exam which caused people to think exams were going to be easy
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: him cannot teach. Him expect you to learn by yourself and write hours worth of words. overall, it upset me.
Dr. Kummer is a great professor and is the goat

Chem1751 is an extremely challenging class. Dr. Kummer is fairly unclear in his expectations and there is SO much work outside of class required to succeed in class.
I would only take the class if you took AP chem in highschool beforehand.

Kummer isn't a bad teacher, but one lecture/week isn't enough to cover the material. Labs mattered little compared to exams, and review materials were SCARCE. He's passionate ab chem and easy to talk to but copying down pages from a book is ridiculous. Use AP Chem credit to test out.

Very sporadic lectures. Not great at organizing. Confused by his own material and with only one lecture per week, unable to teach the majority of the content. In this class, you are on your own. Go to office hours and go to mentor sessions for your own sake, please.

I feel bad for the man because I think he really is a nice guy, but the class he made sucks. The workload is not equivalent to the credits you earn. The actual labs are okay, but there is so much material to learn for the midterm and final, especially if you are in 1701, there is little overlap, so you are essentially taking two chem classes.

Professor Kummer is enthusiastic and truly cares about chemistry and teaching us the content. The exams are fair if you pay attention and understand concepts instead of memorizing a bunch of content, and the labs are pretty well designed. However,  he expects you to hand copy the entire experiment  procedure which is tedious and a waste of time.

Class is nowhere near as hard as people claim it to be if you properly read the manual and ask when you have questions. Basically half of the content is from AP chem and he does explain it in lecture (which I suspect people don't listen to). This class suffers from a lack of time though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I got good grades all because of  online videos. I had very few chem knowledge and this is the HARDEST class this semester. He teaches literally NOTHING in his lectures and there is NO real practice problems. Don't take if you can.

Professor Kummer relies too much on the lab manual when presenting the content in the class, leading to confusion as he does not cover a lot in lecture. Outside of the material, he is a very kind person, but going to mentor help sessions is a must if you want to succeed in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Kummer really expects you to think like a scientist, think critically, and to really question every aspect of the content. Requires A LOT of time (more than gen chem for me) to understand, I swear every sentence in that manual was important, GO TO AUTRY'S HOURS FOR CLARIFICATION!! learned a lot, but i think class could be handled better next year

Considering that this is a 2 credit hour course the amount of work is high. I ended up spending 4-6 hours on each lab manual. I ended up doing better in Chem 1601 then this class, which simply shouldn't be the case.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Kummer was definitely enthusiastic and seemed like a genuinely nice person. For a two-credit course, Chem 1751 was pretty difficult and time-consuming, but I did really appreciate the curve at the end. Overall, just make sure to go to the TA/Lab Supervisor/Mr. Autry's Office Hours and use the resources you have!

I had zero chem knowledge coming into this course. If you're like me, take 1601 along with chem lab since there's a lot of overlap. That being said, you will need to self-study a lot to get a good conceptual understanding. It's completely doable however. Key is to aim for perfect scores on all experiments to give padding for exams.

Kummer is generally alright, his rating is because of students bombing the midterm due to lacking practice materials, which I would expect to improve as he teaches more. The procedure copying for hw is tedious, but other than that even without practice materials I think the exam difficulty is a bit overblown tbh as long as you review your reports

Listen, if you cheap out of this class - get reports from other students, don't read the manual or pay attention in lecture - you'll obviously struggle on exams... you didn't do the work! 

I do agree the content is much for students who have never taken chem, but Kummer is a caring and intelligent professor. Work hard and you'll be ok.

Kummer is clearly passionate about chem lab and supporting students. There's strong support through office hours and help sessions: use them to succeed. That said, for a 2-credit course, the workload and stress felt excessive. Exams were tricky; my A likely reflects prior chem background, which feels unfair to others.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Kummer cares about students, which was evident in the curve for the exam score. However, too much is expected of students for a 2 credit course, and lectures do not prepare you enough for the exams. You will have to self study most of the material. Also, grading of prescans is very strict.

Dr. Kummer is very kind and nice, but the curriculum wasn't organized/taught amazingly. The lectures didn't teach a whole lot (so a majority of the course is self-studying). There are good mentor sessions/office hours that can help walk through concepts (or get answers to lab reports :)). Lots of learning crammed into one semester!

First midterm was difficult, only did decent because of previous chem knowledge. Final was fair and reflective of the class. There is a 75 point drop provision which is nice if you score more poorly on one exam. Expect to self study lots, lecture is not super informative of content and covers more about the current weeks lab.

Yes the exam average might not be ideal, but they curved it. Also this class has all types of students as it's a large intro prereq class, so the mean might be skewed. Just put in the work, go to office hours/help sessions for the lab, don't procrastinate and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No prepatory work, and honestly unrealistic asf.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Experiments were easy but exams were near impassable as the average for the final was a 67.87%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: just read the book gang

I found that the grading guidelines were not very clear and copying the notebook was very tedious, but I appreciated that there were so many help sessions/office hours. The lectures themselves were fine, it helped understand the experiment better but people were always loud during them. Also the lecture hall was always full.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was a free course. The labs were stupendously easy and the midterms even more so. People just complain because they just chatGPT all their lab and problem set results and never bother to study. Simply paying attention is lecture is good enough for a A+ in this course. Kummer himself is an amazing and very knowledgeable lecturer and prof.

I think that Dr. Kummer is probably a really great person. But this class was designed poorly. I spent hours every week writing my lab notebook which consisted of purely copying procedure steps out of our textbook. It was a huge waste of my time and felt disrespectful to my learning. I wish he would change the design so that we could learn more.
WashU find new professors, please... This is ridiculous.
dont do it :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His first year teaching this class and it should be his last. 2-credit course but consumes most of my time. Midterm+final were really hard with NO real practice or preparation to help you. Lectures completely useless and don't help. He talks vague and can't really teach. If you want a good grade, you have to waste more time going to office hours.

The instructor conducts the course as though it were a full‑time class, despite meeting only once per week. Assignments are graded with little to no allowance for partial credit. The pre‑notebook requirement consists largely of repetitive copying and pasting, offering minimal educational value. I would not recommend this course.

First half of the semester hated the class; writing the notebooks was so much work, and the midterm was unexpected. The second half of the semester did better. Read the manual and actually understood the report, spent less time on the notebooks, and focused on the manual, did so much better.

reviews.comment: literally horrible, unorganized, ridiculously hard and ridiculous amount of work for a 2 credit course.

reviews.comment: This class isnt real. No past exams, nothing is taught during the lecture, harder than chem itself. 10/10 not recommended
final is in less than 7 hours WHAT DO I DO GUYS. LITERALLY COOKED. DEEP FRIED. BD BURGER PATTY LEVEL COOKED

Prof Kummer doesn't know what the word teaching means. Bro has a PhD but for the wrong course prob a mix up when getting hired. pls don't take if at all possible. business is always a good major to end with.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Taking Professor Kummer's class was damaging beyond academics. The cutthroat environment he created made learning feel secondary to fear and competition. I felt isolated, constantly anxious, and mentally drained. By the end, my confidence and mental health were significantly harmed, and I would not recommend this course to anyone. Strongly avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is horrible and doesnt teach.

This has really been the worst class I have ever taken. I am cooked for this final exam, because of the fact that there is nothing to study. Before this year, chem lab was regarded as a pretty easy class, but of course this is the year when a 2 credit lab is harder than the actual chemistry class. Washu has to do something, because this terrible.

I'm trying to study for the final exam right now, but the only materials I have is a manual that is required to memorize almost word for word in order to understand what is going on, and past lectures where the teacher assumes everybody knows what he is talking about, never explaining any examples. Something needs to change.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Never take this course. Made me switch majors. No matter how much work you put in its not enough. You were always expected to participate even if sick. Lectures are genuinely so useless to go to. Only goes over what you will do in the lab, which you already spend hours a week on copying down your lab manual.
Don't take this course. Makes you copy the lab manual before every lab. The midterm was outrageously hard and nothing like the sparse "study materials" provided. I'm changing majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Made me leave my major

This course truly made my first semester at WashU miserable. I think decisions need to be made about alternative professors for teaching this course next semester, because the general consensus is that this situation is failing severely. Super nice professor, very focused on students and helping us learn. Exams were similar to homeworks, and we had extra credit on some
SDS 3030 is a class with hard content, the class moves very fast but Prof. Moncada is very good at explaining each concept. If you go to lectures you should be fine.

to be fair, it was her first time teaching calc 3 and she made mistakes occasionally but she is such a sweet lady you can't even be mad at her for it. she walks around the room and helps you on problems and i think she's much better one on one than in lecture.
Sweet person but bad teacher. Love her in person but dont want her to be my prof for classes.
You basically have to teach yourself the entire course

I took Statistics for Data Science I with her. She is a good professor and cares for her students a lot. However, she makes mistakes on her slides almost every lecture, and her explanations are not the best for statistical concepts. Her exams are pretty long for an in-class exam as most of us did not have time to double check the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, very kind and willing to discuss and help with any issues before/after class.
super sweet prof but couldn't explain class material to us properly and made a lot of mathmatical mistakes when explaining problems which confused the students even more
made lots of mistakes during lectures

Really kind lady but her lectures aren't the greatest. I think she knows the material but kinda struggles to do it properly during examples and wastes class time correcting mistakes. I learned most of the content by myself either via the lecture notes or youtube even though I attended almost every lecture

Sometimes she will spend too much time doing basic computations rather than explaining Calc III material in depth, but she is helpful. A lot of criticism that I hear is about the structure of the class (not stuff in her control). Not understanding everything as it is taught in class doesn't make her a bad teacher -- it makes it a hard class.

Moncada was a very sweet professor and was constantly talking to students and giving advice or extra explanations. I think that she kept up a decent pace in the content unlike what many others students think. Sometimes the time we devoted to certain concepts felt a little strange, not enough time for difficult subjects. Still a great professor
Easy class but not the best teacher.

She was nice, but not a great professor at all. She would be behind as much as a full lecture at times compared to Thornton and was just very disorganized. If I took this class again, I would 100% recommend taking it with Thornton, as I learnt so much more and finally understood the content after going to his lecture times.
Moncada the goat she changed my B+ to an A-. She is also a lowk chiller

Great professor, super kind and caring. It's clear she wants all her students to succeed. Slides were very accurate and helpful to the test material. No final & extra credit at the end!! Would strongly recommend taking this course w/ her if looking for a good foundational stats class

She is a very sweet and caring woman who is obviously very knowledgable on content. She also fought for our tests to have a more realistic difficulty with the rest of the calc team. She moves slow in lecture and gets hung up on answering one student's question that should be for office hours. Not bad if you have her but there are better options.

her first time teaching calc 3. great person so sweet and funny and caring. but the class was based off of thornton's textbook. hard for me to understand how she teaches. i like her ipad tho. i ended up going to thorntons after a few weeks bc i could actually understand what thornton was teaching (also he writes the exams)

(Stats 3030) Moncada is super sweet and very accessible. Although, I didn't feel like I always had enough time on exams they did reflect what we did in class. However, a lot of it was computations that you need to know from calc 3. It is not an easy class, but it's interesting. If you stay on top of the work and go to office hours you will be fine.

She made Calc 3 enjoyable, well at least a little bit. Super helpful and accesible! Yes she may struggle in lecture with explaining subjects and technology issues but she shows empathy (far more than Thornton). I may have learned more by going to Thornton lectures but I wouldnt have enjoyed the class without Mrs. Moncada. Hard class but fun!
Very caring, took time to answer questions. PLTL, discussion, and HWs much more difficult than tests.
Kind and energetic. Content is pretty interesting. Exam problems are very computational and easier than HWs but harder computations than that of the calc classes.
I am shocked by how low these ratings are. I love her! She is so personable and made walking through the icy mornings to go to stats lecture bearable. Class is easy and she makes lectures fun

Lots of people say bad things about her, I don't think they're warranted at all. She's never significantly behind and always catches up. It's usually because she wants to answer all the students' questions, which is beneficial in its own way as well. She's a super sweet and enthusiastic teacher that genuinely cares about your understanding.

Super sweet person. However, the lectures are difficult to follow. The explanations and analogies don't work well when conveying material. Frequently falls behind other classes, although this is partly due to thorough answers to students' questions. Be prepared to self-study a decent amount of material.

Lizda is a caring, sweet human being. Unfortunately, it is very difficult to attain an A by attending her lectures alone. She cannot teach the content properly. I failed my second exam because of how confusing her lecture is. I do not recommend. I switched to Thornton halfway and am doing significantly better. I do not recommend this professor.

Super sweet, but comes to lecture unprepared, constantly corrects herself or is corrected by students, gets super frustrated when her iPad doesn't work, and falls behind and has to rush because she takes too much time answering questions that might be best saved for office hours. Sometimes it's better for me to skip lecture and teach myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the sweetest people but shows up to lectures unprepared. Students correct her often. Doesn't know how to use her iPad. Spends too long answering questions that should be asked in office hours and lectures feel slow. If math/calc comes easy to you take another prof, but will go out of her way to help students that are behind
Not really sure why she's teaching calc 3, she barely knows it herself.
Lectures are slower than the other professors, ended up spending more time on my own to get the same results.
Really nice as a person but lectures were not great. We always fell behind the other sections. Had to teach myself most of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's not bad
Slow lecturer, falls behind on content, thick accent.
I only showed up to 3 classes at the end of the semester for extra points on the final. The lecture slides she posts on canvas are pretty good.

Lectures are very average. She posts all her notes so no need to go to lecture. She is very helpful in OH for hw and other questions. Though, her exams are a bit tough. Knowing the concepts helped, but I lost too many points making small mistakes. Class content is anything too crazy. If you took AP stats you'll be extra chilling.

She is a great professor, but be aware of this class is not same with 3200--the content is more probability-based and exams are a little more difficult. Her exams are sometimes difficult, and the average is not high if she does not give you extra credit. Please prepare well for the final. 
Exams worth 75% of the total score.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Moncada-Morales is a sweet person, but content is challenging, and she can put unexpected curveballs on exams. Super accessible outside of class though, so take I wouldn't say take with caution, but know you're in for a lot of work.

Do not take this class unless you absolutely have to for a data science major. Moncada is a very nice lady but she just reads off equations and formulas in class and her exams (which are 50-minute, in class that each make up 25% of your grade) are brutal. I lost my 4.0 in ugly fashion with this class.
Great teacher and lectures posted online, pretty straightforward and easy material. She's also super accessible outside of class and tries her best to help students.

SUCH an amazing professor!! She genuinely cares about students, is super approachable, and accessible outside of class. The content can be tough, but totally manageable if you go to lecture. Also, if you study, the exams are very fair and reflect what she teaches. If you put in the effort, you'll have a great experience. Highly recommend!!

Do not take class with Professor Morales. Her tests are ridiculous, and she is very unhelpful. She consistently has errors in the homework solutions and even left off part of a test question and only realized in the last 10 minutes of the test. She didn't even give us points back on the question. Very harsh.

Lizda is a queen and I love her. She is the funniest professor I've had. All of the exams are straightforward and she will not try to trick you at all. If you just show up to class and study for a day or two you will be fine. If you see her as an option for a class, PICK HER!!

Professor Morales is so kind and truly cares about her students. She is accessible to all students outside of class and during exams for any questions. She made Stats very understandable although there were some challenging concepts towards the end of the course. Would 100% recommend taking with her.
great professor! clear lectures, straightforward exams, and was accessible outside of class

Morales is very caring and considerate teacher. For her first time teaching, she did a very good job of teaching intro stats. Class was very manageable and there was a final project rather than exam which is always a plus. Highly recommend.
Professor Moncada is a great instructor and a really caring teacher. She is ready to help students succeed and did a great job for her first semester teaching.

This is her first time teaching, and she is fantastic! Lectures are clear and well-organized. Attendance at subsection is the only requirement, but you can drop 3. Exams are straightforward and fair. She is very accessible and enthusiastic about helping students in office hours. Textbook homework is weighted strongly in this class. NO FINAL EXAM!!!

5331/2 are Phd Qual, so I suspect he treated 5331 with a rather strict, German-style. After some feedbacks, he has adjusted his grading policy and most people got A level. For math, he provided enough discrete examples and wrote note this time. If you check Kerr's note, you will find Carl's is more friendly. Overall, 5332 is a good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As previous comments mentioned, this class has around 16 students, only 3 of whom were in A range. He didn't curve anyone. He didn't care about his students at all.

Imagine a course where ambiguity is the curriculum: stakes high, and you're guilty until proven otherwise. You learn resilience and self-study because lecture rarely yields clarity. Exams read like another class; grading is strict and partial credit is metaphysical. If you already know the material, you'll do fine. By definition, this is Carl Lian.

Carl did this thing where he tried to write on the board as fast as he possibly could and also never stop for questions. He told me that "you aren't meant to be able to solve all of the homework problems" and that "In Germany they just take one exam per year but if you fail its ok because university is free." We unfortunately don't live in Germany.

As the previous comment mentioned, if you haven't taken this course before, earning an A is nearly impossible. Even some students in the top 25% of the class would not have received an A-, much less an A. The grading criteria are unclear, and the workload is heavy even compared to other graduate courses.

He's the worst professor in this department. He used other professor's notes but didn't follow the order and even notations. It's impossible for you to get an A in his course if you've not been familiar with the subject before.
I've been studying here for over three years. Based on my experience, I'd suggest avoiding him. He's been the worst professor I've dealt with in our math department.

Ok first of all, I have never EVER  had such a b1c7 professor. Not only did she display the worst favoritism that I have ever seen but I genuinely pray that one day she will be n3glected in a nursing home.

One of my favorite teachers my first semester of college. She cared for every student, and fostered a close-knit class environment. As somebody who has never done 3d art before, the class was very challenging, but she supported me well along the way. She was also hilarious and knowledgeable. I definitely recommend taking 3d with Ms. Stouffer!

I loved my semester with Lindsey - just respect her and she will respect you. I found her advice clear and well-rounded. Truly one of the best teachers I have had in arch thus far. She comes from a unique background of design and doesn't have an ego. She's down to earth, caring and honestly just cool. I loved my semester with her.

Lindsey is unorganized with vague grading criteria. Very fluent w/3D shop materials, but not understanding to students unfamiliar w/3D concepts & construction. Only feedback we got was the final grade during winter break. Compared to other 3D profs, Lindsey had more unique prompts but the unclear grading expectations make it not worth taking w/her.

In my experience, Lindsey is a caring professor who is generally overworked. This class is hard and not everyone makes it through but being taught by her inspired me so much. She had such unique ideas to suggest when I was stuck and easily worked with me if something came up. While not perfect she always listened and adjusted to our needs!

This was a great 3D design class! Lindsay is a great teacher! She's super understanding and helpful. As for all 3D classes, Studio time is super heavy and you need to be ready to make the time to come in to work on projects outside of class. Ask thoughtful questions, show up to class, and she'll love you!

Lindsey is incredibly caring. I had my first encounter with severe anxiety as a freshman and she met with me outside of class to help me get through it. If not for her, my first semester would probably have been completely shot. Admittedly, her expectations and instructions are not very clear, and she sometimes gives contradictory feedback.

She's a tough grader. Also, she is not really caring - she's so result-oriented that she doesn't care or pity students who pull all nighters. My friend told me she napped for 10 min DURING THE BREAK because she was tired, and Lindsey deducted points bc of that for her midterm, and warn her to be always awake EVEN DURING THE BREAK
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: required participation

I took her freshman studio class, and loved her! she's never gives direct answers to your questions, but only because she wants you to figure things out for yourself. She's a pretty tough grader sometimes, but if you put a lot of effort in, you'll get good results. She's pretty disorganized, but that means that you can often bend the rules with her

Interesting woman, lots of lumber. If you don't love lumber you will love it after this class, or just love complaining about it. She's legit. And makes you do reading that has nothing to do with class. And the last project she gave us was a big piece of nonsense. Better with the technical side of 3d.

Interesting class. I had never been interested in 3D art before her class. Lindsey is fun, but can be frustrating for students who want everything to be logically explainable. Assigns research projects that have little to do with class. Projects can be limiting, but at the same time intellectually stimulating. REALLY intense on the woodworking.

This professor is disorganized, uninformative and unfit to teach.  Her assignments are terrible and allow for as little creative freedom as possible (one assignment was to make a wooden box).  She is arrogant and is to be avoided at all costs.

Her laugh is either really annoying or just hideous. Her projects are hard to understand at first, but she likes when you ask questions and figure stuff out. She doesn't give anything higher than a B at midterm so don't worry if midterm grade isn't great, you can easily get an A if you put in the extra work.  She likes good craft and perfection.
horrible!  this professor is biased and unfit to hold the position.  puts on air of intelligence... too bad it's fake.  avoid at all costs!!
Loves to talk, easy though

Such a great guy. Lectures a ton and can be slightly boring but I thought the high majority was really cool. He is a genuinely nice guy who clearly cares a ton. I had no musical background and still liked. took some time for some assignments but you'll def get an A if you try.

Lenihan is a genius in his field. Some of the material will be difficult if you don't have a music theory background; if you do you'll be fine. Some classes Lenihan just talks about music in general rather than music theory; I've learned a lot just from coming and listening. Take a class with Lenihan if you appreciate music - you will enjoy it.
Amazing professor, one of my favorites at washu by far. Really cares about growth and learning. He is a jazz wizard

This is an unbelievable class. It's basically just him talking about his experience in the music industry and it's very light work load; all you have to do is compose a few short melodies. He doesn't really believe in grades, so if you don't get the grade you want he's happy to talk about it and change it.  Totally recommend.

One of my favorite teachers of all time. If you have any questions he's very accessible. His exams and final were take home. He LIVES for music and knows so very much about it. I would have coffee with him just to hear all that he knows. He performs often, too. Take a class of his if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: He is just great. I dont need to explain myself beyond that.

Prof. Lenihan is a God among men. He will forgive your 3-week late assignments as long as you show interest in music. I highly recommend him as a theory teacher, conveys concepts clearly and knows EVERYTHING ABOUT MUSIC. Some of his classes will never mention theory at all...classical, jazz, pop music, he knows everything. Highly recommended

An absolute musical genius. If you have the opportunity to take a course with Lenihan, do not pass it up. If you show up and do the work you will get an A. And I promise you, that A will be well-deserved. Just by being in Lenihan's presence you will learn more than you could imagine.

Amazing teacher! Absolute music genius! Very helpful outside of class and hands down the greatest guitarist I have ever had the great fortune of meeting.  If you have any interest in music (jazz, classical or otherwise), take a class or private lessons with him!
Best professor I've ever had.  I learned more in this class than any class I've ever taken.  He integrates the Western canon with the subject at hand to give an enormous view of the world of music.
Inspirational, precise, and...well...cuddly.

Simply, Lenihan is a the greatest musical mind at Wash U.  As a teacher, he can get sidetracked talking about politics or whatnot, but it's worth taking a class with him just to witness this incredible human being in action.  He should start his own religion.
This class was awesome and I learned a lot. It helps you look at music in a different way. Prof. Lenihan is an awesome teacher and everyone should take a class with him.
Kindest and most caring WashU professor of all time! His comments on essays or short assignments are often longer than the assignment alone. Gives amazing insights!

Professor Monahan is amazing! Lucky to have him for Bearsprints for Success. He gives a lot of comments that shows he cares about students on thought papers despite being graded on completion. In class, he is also very energetic and funny, which makes discussions not boring. Highly recommended to have classes with him!

Amazing professor. Made class exciting to come to. He truly cares about each student's success and is readily available outside of class to discuss anything. He writes very meaningful comments on each student's paper, and I can honestly say I've become a better writer because of him. Not an easy class tho; papers are hard and very mentally engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Cool guy, fun class

Dr. Monahan is the BEST College Writing professor. Period. As someone who's never been proud of my own writing before, I can confidently say that he truly elevates and polishes your writing abilities. He is a very dedicated professor, and I mean it when I say that his feedback is often longer than my essays. Office hours is super helpful as well.

Professor Monahan is amazing! I was lucky enough to get him for college writing, and I feel like I hit the jackpot. He gives amazing feedback on all papers, and it is obvious that he cares about each individual student and their success. Highly recommend taking a class of his; you're guaranteed to learn something valuable.
Good boy. I like him. Chill and challenging and chooses interesting material. Always.

Too bad I could only pick three tags, because this professor is one of a kind. Take his class, it'll only be the best decision you have ever made. He is helpful, he wants you to become a better writer. He makes that happen through his engaging personality and fun discussions. No, not a lecture, but class discussions. Success in an enjoyable fashion

Have taken every one of his courses.  You will never go wrong with him as your professor.  His eyes have a humorous glint. You will think you've got it all worked out and then bam he'll slip in a new topic that makes you go hmmm.
Super chill, funny guy who has his quirks but gives marvelous feedback. Take his class. You won't regret it.

Awesome professor. He gives huge amounts of really good feedback on all papers, and grades them in a very reasonable manner. He was very helpful both in and out of class whenever I had questions about any of the essays. Very enjoyable class discussions too--he's a funny guy. 10/10, you want him for College Writing

I've never been a good writer and I came into writing 1 thinking I was going to hate it. Prof. Monahan (not Mono) made this class enjoyable and changed the way I view writing. His self-deprecating humor in class and extensive comments on papers are awesome. I'm definitely going to try to take more of his classes.

I'm writing this two years after I took Writing 1 from him and he is still my favorite professor here by far. He left incredibly helpful comments on your paper. He'd just cover it in comments. Also one of the funniest people I've ever met. As long as you're not "too cool" to participate, you'll love his course.

Actually my favorite professor at WashU. Am most definitely a better writer because of him and absolutely loved taking his class. He made class so fun and engaging, our discussions were great and he was always extremely willing to help. If you want an A in the class, you just need to reach out for his help and he will give it.

Monahan is a really great guy. He's funny, engaging, and is among the most helpful of professors I have ever seen. He gives extremely (and I mean, extremely) in depth comments on essays that help very much when revising, and he's always willing to spend extra time to give more feedback on papers. Definitely among the best Wash U writing proffessors
Amazing professor.  Well worth the time, money, and effort.  The world can be opened up in a new light within just a few classes.  Once you take one of his classes you will be hooked.

Dr. Monahan is the best. He gives pages of helpful comments on papers, has a great sense of humor, cares about his students, and I'm pretty sure he's the Second Coming of Christ. Plus, he used to be in a band called the Piss Shivers. Too cool.

I was dreading Writing 1. But, from the first day of class he walked in and actually made it interesting and entertaining. I always did well in writing in high school and didn't think I needed that much improvement. I was very wrong and he improved my writing so very much. Gave extensive and helpful comments and was available to meet for extra help
So smart, really funny, and gives more feedback/comments on papers than any other teacher I've ever had. Subtly cool, incredibly devoted.

Exposition - Great class the way he teaches.  Discussions are thought-provoking and usually humorous.  He's simultaneously a bit stiff (we never got to have class outside) and rather easy-going, with a great sarcastic sense of humor.  Papers are returned covered in comments - responses, criticisms, tips, etc.

The class I had with Monahan was a really good one- the readings and discussions in class were so fun they seemed almost frivolous, but all summed up were really educational. Monahan will paint your papers red! He is very in depth with his comments which was really helpful. I ended up learning a lot in what I though would be a boring class!

The first day of class, he walked in quietly wearing his sweater with tie tucked in, and I was skeptical. But this guy was amazing... best sense of humor, itneresting, helpful. Though merely a grad student, he's better than most professors I've had.

Really great professor. Had him for writing 1 and learned a lot from his class. A very good sense of humor and conscientious at the same time. Talkative while maintaining his inner depth. He is also the most helpful professor I have ever had. I  added him to here because we really need professors like him. WU should begin a serious eval on profs.

DC is an easy A, but a boring class with guest lectures every class. Easy group projects every other week. Everything is graded on completion. Robert is two-faced, acts like he's your best friend when talking, but he won't care at all about you outside of class. Got falsely reported for not participating in a project, almost failed me because of it

Class description is the biggest catfish as the structure is weeks of guest lectures (extremely boring) with one elementary level group project for the "lab". Very easy A (graded on completion/a simple criteria for module reflections). Presents a cool, funny persona but lacks sincerity and is pretty uptight. Some classmates were huge fans though.
Professor Morgan has great class materials but the crew pratice would require students to spend 11am to 10pm during weekend. Also sometime he's quite pushy and makes the conversation a bit toxic
So mean, you must be attend every class even being late is not allowed. Also, you need waste a lot of time to be a servant without any payment after class.
I wasn't a big fan of the structure of the Designing Creativity class. There are many guest lecturers and reflections on various topics. I went in expecting a more skills based class.

Very kind and engaging professor. Important lessons and messages, but the guest lecturers could be boring. Projects were fun, but what you get from the class depends on how much you invest. I was tired after my morning lectures and didn't have the energy to be engaged listening to a stranger's life story.

Rob is great! He memorizes every student's name and talks before class. The class starts a little boring, but about half way through the lectures became really eye opening and made me engage more with the class. It definitely is a get-out-of-it-what-you-put-into-it class and the group members can vary drastically in terms of enthusiasm and care.
It was a really easy and amazing class for the first years. if you can take it you should.

Good lecturer and held the attention throughout the class. However, he is unclear in the syllabus about the time commitments of the class, also some assignments are much less than others so there is kind of a gamble aspect. I liked rob he is a little passive aggressive/ sarcastic at times and that has helped true with everyone I've talked with.
Morgan is one of the sweetest human I have ever met. He is caring and helpful either inside or outside of the class.

Designing Creativity was easily one of my favorite classes first semester. Light work, homework, and expectations, it's an easy A, sure, but you get what you want out of this class. Helped me discover that creativity is an actual passion of mine. Rob is a firm lecturer but an understanding professor as long as you try.

Rob seems like a caring guy, didn't interact with him much because of the nature of the class. Designing Creativity was essentially a free 3 units and A+. Questions could be done ahead of time. Guest lectures could get stale and group labs were extremely open ended (to the point it felt like busy work), but again the class was like zero effort.

Rob is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had. This class is mainly made up of attending class for guest speakers. The homework is to submit one question for every guest speaker which is very reasonable. The crew aspect is definitely a time commitment outside of class, but he takes 20 minutes off of every class to give us back our time.

Rob is really nice and this class is the easiest A as long as you show up to class (attendance is taken everyday). It was cool to have a class about creativity. Most classes are guest speakers (like TED Talks). I got a little bored but I'm hesitant to complain (again, super chill time). I don't know that I gained so much, but I'd recommend it.

Rob pours a lot of passion in teaching Designing Creativity. There was a unit on failure that stuck out. Rob spent a lecture describing the necessity of failure in success and gave us examples of his own failed projects, and even got the Provost to speak on his own failures too. Lots of inspirational speakers in this class, fun and easy projects.

Robert Morgan is one of the most self-righteous profs I have ever seen, his class is a humongous waste of time (one of the assignments took 70+ hrs of inflexible time in just two weeks). He is also one of the least understanding profs with absolutely no sympathy for mental health. He also gets away with curving down. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: MJ is approachable and cares about connecting with students. However, her lectures tend to move quickly and can be difficult to follow. While she incorporates interactive activities to keep the class engaged, they are not really helpful.

I LOVED MJ RABIER! She is an incredible person, and I personally loved her teaching style even though it could be rushed at times. She is incredibly sweet and will be more than willing to meet with you on weekends, and will extend due dates if asked (on a reasonable basis). Genuinely was one of the most patient and caring professors I've had.

She is a really nice prof. and seems to care about her students. There are very few things that you are graded on in this class so just be prepped for that. The lectures were sometimes rushed, which she did acknowledge however. Knowledgable on the topic of accounting. Her style of teaching is not for me,I don't like feeling forced to participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Did not like her teaching style, and you're graded mostly by the tests, which are exponentially harder than she prepares you for. Beware
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rabier has incorporated a lot of feedback into her course and I really enjoyed taking it (SP2026). She has dropped down to two exams, cut out some content, and made it a lot more engaging for students. She's one of those professors where all you have to do is ask! She's super open to scheduling office hours on the weekend and extra help.

She's a great person, fun to talk to, funny, and genuinely cares about her students. She's flexible and open to suggestions and feedback with her teaching style, too. She does lecture insanely fast, though, and your grade is essentially made up entirely of exam performance. Overall, I think she is great and definitely over-hated.
During our lessons, the exercises she solved were straightforward. However, the exams were unexpectedly harder than she had prepared us for.
Awful

Great with emails. But I don't like her teaching style, need to spend other time to watch pre-class lectures and spend lots of time just doing practice problems which is not the way I prefer to learn. Will not take her class again
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her teaching method sucks with the style of having students watch lectures before class and doing practice problems in class. The content on her exam is not straightforward to the stuff you do in class. They are significantly harder.

MJ really cares about students and wants to be there for us personally. Really nice woman. However, I don't like the "flipped" classroom style with asynchronous lecture recordings and then the class is working on practice problems. Homework is optional, only grades are exams. Exams are straightforward. Good professor, bad class.

I adored Professor Messbarger! I was in her Italian Museums course and she brought this amazing enthusiastic energy into class every day. You can tell she's extremely passionate about the subject and it actually made me add an art history major. She is also very kind and truly cares about the students. Take her class if you have the chance
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Messbarger is one of the kindest professors at WashU! She cares about every student personally, not just academically. She always starts class with checking on every person and is very passionate about what she teaches. Someone said she randomly would use Italian but she's literally married to an Italian... so they clearly weren't listening.
Class is very religious-heavy (does not match course description).

for art of med, the TA you have makes or breaks the class. art of medicine was a little boring and random but messbarger made the history part interesting. not a lot of effort required, but read before discussion, participate, and study before exams and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's okay but lectures kinda boring

Genuinely is one of the gems of the WashU languages department. Even for just an intro level Italian class, she puts a lot of care into the lectures and is extremely interactive with the class. Not just talking at us, but engaging with us. As for homework, VHL is as helpful as you make it; reading the textbook coincides with doing the homework.
Professor Messbarger is the BEST! She is so kind and accommodating to her students. Her lectures and assigned readings are very engaging. Minimal assignments, but participation is important.

Messbarger is very passionate about historical analysis, art history, & Italian culture, which composes much of Art of Med. She's very email-responsive & caring outside of class too. However, the Art of Med experience can become stressful if you get a biased TA. If interested in medical humanities, you should definitely get to know Messbarger!

Prof. Messbarger is a great professor. She really cares about her students and is always willing to give extensions/work with you outside of class, understands freshman year is hard, etc. Always answers emails. Her grading criteria and assignment directions can be unclear, so you'll need to ask for clarifications or settle with a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof messbarger is a stereotypical humanities teacher. Says nothing but says a lot. Lots of weird hand gestures. Art of medicine class was really an art history class. Talks a lot about Italy for no reason. Easy a though if you really want to suffer through losing lectures that have no point to them.

I took a class with her years ago and decided to take another class with her. She is incredibly powerful and knowledgable. She really strives to make you a better writer. On a first paper, I did not do well and she really wanted to help me improve. You must work hard to earn a grade so that you leave the class with lifelong skills. Love her!

Italian use is very frequent in class so the lectures are sometimes confusing. The lecture slides are not aesthetically appealing, but do contain enough information for review. Memorization-heavy. Also, the lectures are sometimes arbitrary on historical facts and analysis, and do not invite much argument from students.

I took The Art of Medicine with Professor Messbarger, and it is easily my favorite class for far. professor Messbarger is extremely passionate, and can make almost everything interesting.  She is an amazing person outside of class, and very easy to talk to. Get to know her!

The Art of Medicine is one of the best classes I have taken at WashU. Professor Messbarger is so passionate about teaching this class and she takes an interest in each individual student. The class brings a new perspective to the medical field that was so interesting to explore. 100% recommend.

Dr. Messbarger is absolutely one of the best professors I have had at WashU. Her Italian Women Writer's class was amazing. I was extremely hesitant to take it, but she was inspiring and knowledgable. The readings, though sometimes boring, came to life in our discussions.

I'm in a freshman seminar about Italian museums, and you can certainly tell this is her area of expertise. She keeps lectures relatively interesting though the readings are terrible. I have to agree that she's very conceited. She had us read her own book, and I don't think I've ever seen someone so excited to talk about themselves.

I ADORED Professor Messbarger. Passionate, funny, down to earth, caring, and generally awesome. I could come to class after a bad day and leave class in a great mood. Her energy is infectious!! She made the course so interesting and the final project was actually fun. You must take a class with her if you get the chance. It'll change your life.

Had Messbarger waaaay back in '97.  I already loved the Romance Lanaguages and she helped me get my start in Italian.  I'm now married to an Italian and spend at least a month per year there.  I'm also fluent. Thanks for the great foundation Dr. M!!
Passionate about Italian and her students.  Also a cool fashionista.

an excellent professor in all categories.  everyone please ignore comments about her being arrogant.  rather i would say she has an air of authority about her, but she is definitely very accommodating to other people's interpretations and points of view.

Mrs. Messbarger was one of the best professors I've ever had.  She was very easy-going but she expected a lot from her students.  Her classes were always fun and the discussions were lively.  I wish I had taken more classes with her.

I found this professor to be extremely conceited and I am not the only one. Of course, the fact that she studies the anatomy of the **** as her research doesn't help much (No I am no kidding or insulting, that's what she does, people told me). I wouldn't reccommend taking her class. Better to spend  summer in Italy.
I liked Prof. Messbarger.  She was very enthusiastic and she spoke very clearly.
Boring and conceited. Many people think she's arrogant and I agree

I find instead that she's a snobby ****. She's thinks she's this great prof. but she's a mediocre prof in a mediocre department. Course was easy, espe.lly if you had ita in high school. Great way to get an A but the woman is really unbearable. Lots of people don't like her and think she's arrogant.
I loved Prof. Messbarger.  She is really fun, interesting, not uptight, and teaches very effectively.  She really cares for her students, and she has a lot of fun teaching.

She is condescending in office hours. Not a good lecturer for a big class so she relies on group discussion although she says it's for our learning. Her TAs are power hungry so grading is a little harsh especially for an intro class. The content is interesting but don't expect her teaching to make you interested.

Dr Moinester was a great professor: super passionate, engaging, and accepting. Although the lectures were great, the best parts of the course were the guest lecturers she brought in and the documentaries we watched. The readings could be long, but you don't need to thoroughly understand them to do well in the course.

Truly a great professor, she is super kind and passionate about the subject (Punishment and Inequality) and it shows. She's an engaging lecturer. The readings can be a lot but we usally break them down in class. The course is perfectly structured, exams are written and with some preperation and a notecard I'd say you'd be set for a decent score.

Professor Moinester's lectures were engaging and her passion for the subject was clearly conveyed. She takes student feedback seriously and always makes herself available for further help outside of class. Guest speakers, documentaries, small group discussions, and lectures were all fascinating. Punishment and Inequality is a must-take class.

Dr. Moinester is truly a wonderful professor. She is so knowledgeable about the course material, and her class structure of combining lectures with active learning discussions really sets students up to succeed. She is also very accessible outside of class and is always willing to help. It was a privilege getting to learn from her!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Moinester is the type of professor who you kinda just watch in awe as she lectures. It is so cool to be taught by an expert in the material - when it comes to Mass Incarceration, she probably knows as much as anyone in the world.

Her class was fascinating and organized; the readings built off of each other and concepts were cemented in class.
Simply wonderful. Highly recommend taking a class with her.
I wish Prof Moinester taught more classes because I would take another class of hers in a heartbeat. Truly loved this class and the material.

Prof. Moinester is really amazing and Punishment and Inequality was the reason I declared my sociology major. She is so smart but still approachable and so caring. I took the class online during COVID and she still made the course engaging and I got so much out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Not a great prof and quite frankly person

How are you teaching about hardware and software when you are unable to explain or use either? Doesn't even make it up with people skills -- she's rude and dismissive to students and corrections. Poor lecturer and doesn't even try to see the perspective of her students -- goes on and on, no one understands, and she sits there confused as to why.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I resent y'all for banishing her to UMBC - it shocks me to hear that she has taught before because she seems completely unable to use Blackboard as a software. 160 pages a week (she decided to include a second textbook unprovided by CMI, extra $53), improperly configured assignments, passive aggressive, and refuses to admit fault. Boo.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is definitely very self-learned as she doesn't have a regular "lecture." However, if you do the Zybooks, pay attention to the labs, and try hard on the homeworks, you will learn in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is very easy from a grading perspective (zero tests), but Professor Singh is just disappointing.
