She's extremely passive aggressive and even a bit rude toward students who ask for help -- always ask the TA instead. Also, she never really teaches -- there's a weekly "discussion section" on the non-lab day, but that felt more like a quiz.

all the labs are tedious and very long. No one is able to finish that on time. there are quizzes on labs after each one of them. Many things irrelevant of the lab content. No one can get a good score and these quizzes make up a huge part in final grade (NO CURVE OR ROUNDING). 

AVOID YOU MUST

Prof. Singh seems to have a lot of enthusiasm for teaching and seems to take interest in her classes. However, her explanation are very unclear and hard to follow. The assignments are boring and tedious. TAs for this class carry.
After taking her class you realize how good the other teachers are.

She is not necessarily a mean professor but this is one of the worst courses I have taken in my time at Washu. You are graded on very few assignments/exams, the slides are really bad, and the grading is odd. Our first exam had a high grade of 85/95 which i think is absurd for the difficulty of the content. The optional textbook is your friend.
Pretending to be a professor

She has a significant lack of depth in understanding the subject matter. The lectures are extremely poor, and she is oblivious to this fact at all; she seems to blame the low average grades on students not focusing on her useless lectures. The grading also lacks transparency and is tough. Just don't take her class whatsoever.

She is a terrible terrible terrible lecturer. The content and exams should not be difficult at all, but everyone does horribly due to the fact that she cannot teach. She gets visibly frustrated when students do not participate, but it is because nobody understands what she is saying. Don't bother asking questions, she will give you non-answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take her course! She seems disrespect her students. After receiving a very bad mean and median scores in the mid term exam, She seems thought it was only because all students do not work hard and did no curving at all. She knows nothing about her terrible lecture slide and quality of her lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: hard to negotiate
Don't take her class; I have never seen any professor who disrespects her students like she does, and she knows nothing about what she is teaching.
She don't know what she's talking about

Terrible professor. Just so bad. That being said, if you are diligent, grading curve is easy to succeed with and can be an easy class to get an A in. Some office hours will be required to get through some of the more tricky homeworks.

Her lectures are so convoluted that most of the time it seems as if she doesn't even know what she's teaching. I agree with the other rating here that says she probably could not complete her own course. I survived this class basically 100% on textbook readings and office hours.

Incredibly boring lectures and difficult homework. Does not explain concepts well. Read the zybook readings carefully if you want to know about the conceptual stuff. I scrolled down a few pages of my psych notes (cuz I have a psych exam right after) during the time she gave us to do the worksheet and she interrogated me like I was a thief.
i'm like 80% sure she couldn't complete the course herself

Lectures were mediocre (mostly reading off the slides), and very disconnected from the Lab and Homework assignments, which make up the bulk of your grade. Python is required for this course, and having basic knowledge beforehand will make a massive difference. Luckily there are a lot of TAs to help with poorly-worded and confusing homework.

Singh seems like an overall nice person but her lectures are terrible. She took over the class recently so she just uses the old professor's slides and hardly knows what she's talking about. Her head TA does almost all of the work on piazza to help students. A lot of times questions are vague so it's easy to lose points on homework assignments.
She might not be the best explaner but she actually cares for the students to learn the material. She is one of the chillest profs and lenient grader.

She yelled at me once for after asking clarifying question about her lecture. Don't even get me started about lectures either. She simply reads off slides that she barely knows herself. None of the material in this course is her own and is from a previous professor. The only way to get through this class is by spamming office hours.

What she did was basically reading out powerpoint from a previous professor and translate it in a much more confusing way. After taking cse217 I decided I will never do anything related to data science again in my entire life.

Do not take. Material is so poorly taught by Singh you are forced to rely on OH. I think a past professor created 217 and Singh simply took it over and knows nothing about the material. Studios must be finished b/c there is a quiz that day on them. Can't miss studio more than once. WS, coding assignment, and studio quiz all due throughout the week.

Everything she said in class was so confusing and there were videos from a better teacher but she stopped uploading the videos few weeks ago. I was sick and cannot go to the lecture last week but there was no videos uploaded

Don't take her cse217. Grading is ambiguous. Lectures recording are heirloom from others. Labs are self-learning what lectures don't cover. Discussion sessions are lectures, but with barely any nutrition. Grading is also chaos. She don't know grading rubrics and make random promises and graders are harsh and students lose points. Avoid this.
Excellent course, but it is really tough. The exams really make you think. Ultimately, grading is very fair and reflects how much you learn.

Very challenging class, but you do learn a lot. There is anxiety about grades, w some classmates insisting they will curve. K...grades just came out. Grade lines are legit (I got an A by 1 pt), so they do just add up your points. This is nice & fair. Overall, great semester, but you work hard.
Great teacher and human. I was first hesitant to approach him, but he is so great. I really like how he cleared up the kinetics material for me.
Such a unique teacher. He is funny and effective. Just so engaging you can't help but learn during his lectures. That said, his evening help sessions are even better. Hope to have him again.
I really like his teaching style. Mostly chalk w some ppt for pictures and plots. He genuinely cares that we are learning. HS were great for discussing topics.

Awesome and funny professor and person! He's not the kind of professor that acts like he's above everyone else, he's very approachable and can joke around! He's not the best at explaining things, but you can watch Daschbach's lecture videos sometimes, or go to her office hours to supplement Loomis's lectures. Also, the exams are way too hard.

Don't let anyone fool you, this is a challenging class. Yet, the grading is extremely generous. Loomis is engaging & funny. He makes some "typos", but he owns up on them. His help sessions are key. This was his and Prof. D's first time w this course, but I am sure it'll be even better in the future. Quoting Loomis "great shtuff".
Had Loomis last year for Quantum, and it was so challenging. I am now in grad school, and I am just realizing how much I learned in his class. He makes you work, but you learn so much. just so good.

Prof. Loomis is the best at WashU. He knows how to present material and assign problems to ensure we learn what the material means and what it can be used for. You start thinking wth, but after you digest it a bit, things fall into place. I am so thankful I could take Prof. Loomis 2x.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loomis gets it. He is hard, but very fair. You will have to work, but you will learn a ton. Just one of the best at WashU. I will miss him.

Hands down the GOAT. His courses are challenging and 401 is no exception but he is great. He works very hard to ensure we learn the material. At first I wished there was less HW, but doing it and being graded on it made us learn the material. The exams were tough but fair if you did the HW. Grading was very reasonable with no curve.

CHEM401 or also known as MATH401 or Physics401. This is a hard class so review and ask questions. He cares a lot and does whatever he can to do to answer your questions and he will challenge you, but you will learn a lot. He can really teach for sure, but you have to put in the effort or the class will consume you.
What a journey. 1st 2 weeks I was wtf. Then, the math started making sense. The last 1/2 of the semester the quantum started making sense. Stick with it and trust Loomis. Such a rewarding class.

Incredibly challenging class, incredible professor. By far the most difficult class I've ever taken. You'll have to work hard, but Prof. Loomis works equally hard to help you succeed. Passion for the course material is apparent in every lecture and humor makes learning the content tolerable. I'll never forget Pleft spectra.

THE BEST CLASS I have ever taken. hard material but i had so many lightbulb moments. i do wish i would have taken 401 my sophomore year as it explains gen chem material and organic would have made so much more sense. brush up on calc and don't be afraid to ask questions if you miss something.

First day he joked "this course should be called math 401" and then started lecturing... he was right. He's incredibly supportive tho, good at explaining tough concepts from different angles till you get it. professor=understanding, material=very hard. Lectures available on zoom, receptive to course feedback.

Loomis is a goof ball. This is the most difficult class I've taken, but if you put your nose to the grindstone you can do well. Through all the anxiety he'll still make you laugh. He's very fair when it comes to grading, though his exam are tough. I love the guy.

What sets him apart: he will sacrifice everything to make sure that you succeed
I dunno, I love this guy. Tough, but he works harder than anyone to help us. I would run through a wall for this guy. I wish I could take another class from him.
Loomis is def a goat, but I wish he would not push us so hard. We as seniors don't want to work that hard. Less hw and problems with less math would help.
Some don't like Loomis because he's tough. They're nuts. He is the best prof at WashU. He works crazy hard to make sure everyone learns. I love him and this course.

401 is really hard. A ton of calc. Don't let that scare you. In the end, there are only a few different types of integrals needed. Loomis has bent over backwards to help us. Just a good, but hard course.
Absolutely the toughest class I have taken a WU. I am so happy that Loomis taught it though. He's always willing to help us, and he can tell he cares about us.

Loomis is an incredible and dedicated educator. He has not taught 401 for a while, and it seems as though the math prereqs changed over that time. So, he spent a ton of time modifying the content and meeting with us to make sure we could learn the material. This course is very hard, but you end up learning so much. Work together on problem sets.

One of the best professors at WashU! Loomis is hilarious, passionate, and genuinely cares about helping students succeed. The lectures are engaging, and using unstuckstudy along with the textbook makes the material click. Tough but worthwhile class.

Quantum Nanostructures IS NOT EASY. The topics are super difficult and require a good understanding of quantum physics. Homeworks were ridiculously hard, and the exams impossible. That being said, amazing lecturer, very engaging. Going to office hours saved my life. Very accessible via email. Can't miss class or else you're behind. 100% take class!

The GOAT!!
I took 111A w/ Loomis 2 years ago, and I am still realizing how much I learned from him and that class. He just knows how to teach and connect with students.
sir you saved my grade,love ur classes, still hot in 2024

You do not realize how good Loombach is until you take other courses. The team is incredible and passionate. They just know how to teach. They have remained my biggest mentors at WU. I will miss them.

I have now had Prof. Loomis for 3 classes. It does not matter what he teaches, he is the GOAT. Prof. Loomis strives to make sure every single student in the class walks out understanding the material. He is hard, but we students end up loving the material.
He inspired my whole approach to learning in undergrad... This person is one of the best professors you'll ever get to know in your career.

Great instructor, great mentor, and great human. 111 prepared me for my academic career at Wash U, without Loomis and 111, I am sure I would not have made it through. He has given me so much invaluable career advice since my first year, and he always pitched it straight and respectful.

Loomis just knows how to teach. I did not know what to expect with a grad course, but I learned so much. He brought together many aspects from Gen Chem, Inorg, and Phys Chem and tied them together to show us properties of semiconductor nanomaterials. I am so glad I opted to take this course as an elective.

I took Loomis 3 yrs ago as a freshman. I liked him then, but I am realizing now that he is the best at WU. Yes, he prepared us well for science, but he also taught us how to think, how to ask questions, how to understand problems, and how to study. I hope to be a smaller, female version of him down the road.

I once approached Dr. Loomis at his office to inquire about a question relating to semantics: "If hydrolysis is the breaking of a bond, shouldn't analysis be the breakage of the anus?" Let's just say, he answered via nucleophilic backside attack. WOULD DEFINITELY RETAKE!! SO KNOWLEDGEABLE! BEST PROFESSOR AT WASHU. HE IS A MUST-TAKE!!!!

Loomis has genuinely been one of the most devoted and caring professors I've ever known. He would often stay at his student help sessions until midnight to ensure that each student gets the most complete understanding of the material. His lectures are never boring as he is a hilarious person whose passion for chemistry is infectious. He's the best!

111 is a very very challenging course, but the fact that I received basically the first B of my life and still love the man says a lot. He was incredible in so many ways and truly cared not only about the subject but about the students. In a lecture hall of 250 kids, he knew my name and many other students' names. He is amazing!
Funniest and most caring professor. He pushes each student to do better in an encouraging way and does his best to set you up to succeed.
The LEGEND. He will challenge you and help you. There is no better teacher.

Context: I took a lot of hs Chem, and was going to skip 111/112. 
Loomis and 111 are incredible. I had so many ahah moments where my hs material became clear. It was a bunch of work, but so rewarding. Loomis did not just teach to me though. He worked hard to help all of us. Incredible semester.

Professor Loomis is one of the best professors I have ever had. Chem 111 is really tough, but he is very passionate about the subject and makes chemistry super fun to learn. Highly recommend this class if you want to learn a lot with incredible professors.
Just theee best. be ready to work, but he will help you.

Loomis + Daschbach = Best class ever!! They will push you, but you will learn. D is great w/ notes and details. L is great w/ explaining concepts and real life connections. If they ever teach together again, you must take this class.

Definitely the best professor in WashU I've seen so far. Passionate. Funny. Cares about the students. I can't believe he is leaving but I can only wish him the best. He's an amazing professor and you should always take his class no matter what it is, he will make it worthwhile!

Just an incredible teacher and an awesome course. Loomis changed my mindset and expectations for myself, WU, and learning. I almost placed out, but my RA convinced me to take 111 - thrilled I listened. So much more of Chemistry makes sense now.

Loomis (& Daschbach) are incredible. It was a tough course, but I learned so, so much, not just about Chemistry, but also about learning and adjusting how I think. I will always cherish this semester.
HE IS VERY FUNNY .Both him and Daschbach are awesome. read other reviews for detail. would 10/10 recommend if you plan to go premed over the 105-106 sequence

OK, Loomis is hilarious and an excellent lecturer. He is also a genuine person, who really cares about his students. I just watched a StudLife video of Loomis and Daschbach reading their RMP reviews...they are such a great team. They feed off of each other in class and in the video. Take their course and you will learn how to think.

Loomis is Awesome!

Loomis is Really BIG!

Loomis is Hott!

I took Loomis' 111A course three years ago. I am still realizing how much he taught us. The class prepares you for science and medicine. It teaches you how to think, and gets you away from memorizing. All students interested in STEM or Medicine should start with Loomis.

Loomis is a fantastic lecturer and very funny. Very willing to help students -- attend his office hours! Daschbach and Loomis did a great job organizing this class. Genchem is difficult, but manageable if you put in the work. Go to office hours, they were the most helpful resource outside of lecture.
Prof. Loomis is hilarious! Amazing prof, great lecturer.
Loomis is awesome.
Loomis and 111 are iconic and I was not disappointed. What a great, but extremely challenging course. All STEM students should be required to take 111.
Great course and an even greater professor. You will work so hard, but you will learn so much. This is why I came to WU.

Not gonna lie, your journey of becoming a great doctor or working in the medical field starts with this man, Professor Loomis. Amazing lectures, great explanation to very possible questions, extremely hilarious, and have tremendous care for his students, especially the front row and the 7th students who failed and retook the class just to see him.

What a fabulous course!!! Team 111 is the real deal. Do not listen to four-year advisors. Take this class if you want to learn Chemistry and learn how to learn. This course changed my mindset. Loomis and Daschbach are equally good and complementary.
Loomis is great, but tough. He works way hard. Shoot, I had a lecture given by Gru. Who does that, especially on parents day? So funny.

Loomis is just so good. Gen Chem, nah. It shattered my expectations. The story of the electron was great, and we took a tour of quantum, molecular orbital theory, and ended with molecular interactions. This made high school chem so clear. Definitely go to his office hours, they are a must. I have to give a shout to Daschbach too. GO TEAM 111!!

Hands down best professor I have ever had in my life. He genuinely cares so much about chemistry and making sure every student understands. He is willing to stay in office hours as long as needed to ensure everyone's questions are answered. They want you to succeed, you just have to use all the resources and go to class. Definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's loud and jokes around a lot. Gives great feedback, knows his stuff and explains everything well
Chem111A is a very hard class but you can get whatever grade you want if you work for it. It is doable but not free. Loomis is a great lecturer and person.

Loomis was super helpful during office hours. He always took the time to make sure everyone understood concepts and answered all questions. He is good at explaining all the sides of a concept. Also, since we didn't have lectures in person, he dressed up for Halloween on the zoom call <3 Definitely can't want to take another class with him!

Professor Loomis is an amazing professor. He always makes his lectures engaging, funny, and genuinely cares about his students. He is always accessible and makes sure every student succeeds. He made a difficult topic so interesting and I really hope I can take a class of his again.
Absolute legend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is very difficult, especially over Zoom. He is an amazingly caring professor, and he makes the material exciting and relevant by talking about his own research. It was confusing how content was divvied up between lecture, recitation, and CCVs, and I wish there were more problem sets to practice with. Loomis hosts great office hours.
Great prof and course - the best course at Wash U this past Pandemic semester.

A ton of work, but if you do it, the material is not that hard, and you will do fine in the exams. Loomis is able to make sense of it all, and he pushed us to learn. I gained a lot is skills that will help me throughout my career. Great prof and course.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Loomis is an incredible teacher who cares about students. He has a clear passion for Chemistry and his research. "General" chemistry does not mean "Simple" Chemistry. This is a tough class. You will need to work nearly as hard as Loomis to get a good grade. Use Loomis as your main resource as he is great at breaking down & explaining topics.

Loomis is a great teacher and a better human being. He has ruined my college career because I will now be comparing all of my professors to him, and they won't have a chance. He worked so hard to make sure the entire class understands even the toughest of concepts. What a great semester. I will miss him.

I love Professor Loomis so much. I have taken one class with him and feel like we have a real bond because he cares about his students and makes himself available for everyone. His lectures are hilarious and extremely informative and the exams are difficult but based on the work - make sure you do the practice problems!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers/professors I've ever had, you'll be lucky to have him as a prof. He made a very confusing and notoriously difficult subject enjoyable. He has genuine passion for teaching and is the most knowledgeable prof that I have ever had in the subject they teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Loomis is great. The highlight of the semester. I was afraid a virtual semester was going to be a waste. Not true. I learned so much, and I had fun. Mon pm help sessions were insightful and so beneficial. Get him to talk about research and he really shows his excitement. It takes a ton of work, but you won't mind.
Great Professor! Professor Loomis is super knowledgable, friendly, and approachable. Professor Loomis made a hard class enjoyable.

Just finished the best class I probably will ever take. Loomis (and Daschbach) made 111 a great learning experience, even with Covid and Zoom. I just wish we could have done the course in person. Incredible dedication to teaching and the students.

Loombach is fantastic. Seriously, the Loomis/Daschbach team has far exceeded my expectations. This is my favorite, but hardest class, even though it is through Zoom. They provide so much support and help. Loomis runs marathon help sessions that do not end til everyone gets their questions answered. What a great semester.

Loomis is awesome. He works so hard to help us. Really hard class. He is co-teaching with Daschbach, and that is great. Ying and Yang. Hard, but interesting exams. Realistic score expectations though.

Loomis was great. Course should be called Story of the Electron, but it is cool. Very challenging exams, but it is not difficult to earn an A. He works really hard to make sure everyone gets their questions answered. He is an impressive force and the best at Wash U. He does cool research too.

A huge curve (should be smaller) makes this class easier than it should've been. Other than the first test, I thought that the difficulty was exaggerated (I had no prior chem experience). Put in the work before the test and you'll be fine. Dr. Loomis is also hilarious and the best STEM professor at WashU. Very approachable and gave us free monster!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So good. He tells you how hard it will be, but he works crazy hard to make sure we do well. Plan ahead for exams or they will rock you. Incredible class.

Simply an incredible course and Professor. My advisor told me to take Chem 105, because you need AP Chem for Chem 111. Nonsense. Loomis made the hardest material crystal clear. He works very hard to make sure we all got the material. Just a great semester. I will take any course he offers.

I am a graduating senior, and I realize more and more how great Loomis was. I had him first for Gen Chem, and he and the course were fantastic. I was fortunate to have him as my major advisor, and he has gone above and beyond my expectations. He is an incredible educator, an excellent mentor, and he truly cares about the well being of all students.

Loomis is the funniest teacher/professor I have ever had. He really engages a classroom of 250+ students. He knows the information extremely well, although sometimes his lectures were a bit unorganized. He loves getting to know his students. Although the class is challenging, Loomis is there to support his students.

I love, luv, luvv Loomis. He is incredible. It is amazing how much he cares about ALL of the students. This really comes out in his help sessions, where he seems to take it personally to make sure everyone gets the material. The course is super hard, but with no curve and all of the help he and the other instructors offer, it is doable.

Best ever. I thought I would hate it, but his Story of the Electron makes so much sense, and is kinda cool. The guy knows how to teach. He gives these amazing evening help sessions on the 40, and stayed until 3:30 am one time helping us. His class is tough, but so, so good.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Loomis is fantastic; he uses humor in his teaching style so if you learn that way, he is a great professor. He really cares about the students and has help sessions on the 40 until 10 at night. Easily my favorite teacher thus far
Professor Loomiss lectures are generally extremely clear, and he adds a lot of humor in to keep students engaged. I thought this class was fairly easy, especially if you keep up the current topic.

Taking his class right now and want to write this before I get my grade. Loomis is incredible. He really cares and works really hard to make sure we understand the material. Loomis offers help sessions on the South 40 at night so we can just pop in. These are incredible. Passionate about Chemistry and students.

He was an amazing professor. I had him last semester and is still by far my favorite teacher at wash u. chem 111 is really freaking hard but he was hilarious and made the class enjoyable. if you go to his help sessions, he will see that you care and will do his best to help you to do well

Loomis is fantastic.  He takes it personally that everyone learns the material, and he works very hard to make sure all questions are answered. I am a junior, and I have not met a more dedicated educator. I want to take more classes with him. Don't be afraid of 111, just take Loomis.

Chem111 has some great professors, but Loomis is the best.  He really gets into it, and he absolutely wants everyone to learn Chemistry, or should I say the baby quantum mechanics behind chemistry.  Great guy and great class.

Just finished the most amazing semester with Loomis.  I have decided I want to be a professor, and I hope that I can be just a fraction of him.  He is really smart, caring, and funny.  He works really hard to make sure everyone gets the material.  He seems to take it personally if he can't convey something.  Simply incredible.

I thought I hated Chemistry and that I never could ever understand it. Thank you Dr. Loomis, for showing me how wrong I was. A funny professor, I loved going to class (dont switch lectures because you dont think he will be serious). He really cares, makes everyone participate, and I learned so much from him
Loomis is the best professor ever. He is super entertaining and makes Chemistry more fun to learn. The material is very difficult but Loomis always stays to answer every single question.

Loomis is great.  Best professor at WU.  The material comes fast, but he can explain things extremely well.  He really rocks in help sessions, where there is more time and he can go through multiple ways to explain concepts.

Loomis is so good at teaching.  He can explain things so many different ways, even the most complicated topics.  I will take any class he offers.  Yes, all of Chem 111 is rushed, because they need to cover a bunch of material, but it is the best class.

Loomis is an awesome person.  He's a hilarious guy, and he knows how to relate to students.  However, his lectures definitely got progressively worse throughout the semester.  I don't really know what happened, but basically everything after the second exam he managed to make pretty unclear even though the concepts were easier.

Teaches the underlying physics/chemistry behind what we knew from h.s.  The concepts are tough, but he knows how to convey the material.  He has a lot of energy, is really funny, and is able to keep our attention. Best class I have taken at WU.
Loomis is incredible.  He is soooo smart, but he is the first normal-guy professor I have ever met.  You can ask him anything, and he will be able to answer it so you understand.

Great lectures, and able to answer any question.  Some say he should write more on the board, but I think that would ruin his lectures and their flow.  Go to his lectures, and then get the notes from Daschbach's lectures.  He cares about all of the students, and he does not curve , which is awesome.
Great professor for the first 3 exams, but for the post-exam 3 material I'd recommend going to Daschbach's lectures as it gets a bit confusing. Great teacher and super friendly :)

Great Professor!  His lectures and help sessions are hands down the best.  He can explain anything.  He clearly cares that all students get the material, and he wants everyone to do well.  I will definitely take any course he offers.

Loomis is sooo amazing.  He tries to connect with each and every student, he even learned all of our names.  He will stay for hours after help sessions to make sure we get all of our questions answered and until we really get the material.  I was blown away, he even emailed me to congratulate me for a good semester.  He is someone to look up to.

Loomis is the man.  I actually looked forward to his lectures sometimes.  Not only does he know the material very well and teach it well, but he makes lecture super entertaining.  One of the funniest people I've ever met.
Great.  Best professor and best course ever.
Loomis is the real deal. So smart, a great communicator, funny yet serious about education. I love everything about him and his class. Yes, he tries to learn every student's name.

Loomis is AWESOME!!  Really smart and a great communicator.  Tests are challenging, but doable.  You will definitely learn all of that orbital stuff the glossed over in h.s.  Absolutely take Loomis for Gen Chem.

Loomis is awesome.  He does not write down as much as some of the other professors, but he explains things so that you can understand them and you will not need to write everything down.  Go to his helps sessions.  He will answer anything about the material, and you get a really good idea of how the material fits into the rest of science.

Loomis is an incredibly talented lecturer. He keeps the class entertaining while still covering the material. His biggest fault is that he gets so passionate about some of the material that he slips in Chem 401 material which can confuse some people. Overall I think he is a wonderful teacher who really cares about his students.

Loomis is fantastic.  He explains everything extremely well.  He also make sure we are all on board as he goes through even the most challenging material.  If something still is not clear, go to his help sessions - he is great, and he will stay until you get it.

The best course I have taken at Wash. U.  Based on Chem 111, I thought this would be good, but it was even better.  He does not use a text book, but he complements his lectures with literature handouts.  I now have a good understanding of electronic properties of semiconductors and see how size can alter these properties.  Take this course.
Loomis is GREAT.  He made Gen Chem exciting, fun, and challenging.
Best teacher I've ever had

Loomis is Absolutely Great!!  He definitely combines entertainment with a lot of materials...taught at an extremely high level.  He is extremely committed, and works extremely hard to make sure students get the material.  Definitely the best of the 111 teachers.

An incredibly insightful lecturer and teacher.  Loomis fills in all of the gaps we may have had from high school, and then opens us up to the cool world of quantum mechanics.  He is amazing.  I have not met a professor who is so passionate about teaching, and who cares so much about all of the students.

Amazing Professor. Lectures engaging and extremely thorough.  Occasionally goes off on tangents and slightly out of order.  But, if you take a few minutes a week to draw connections, easily one of my 5 favorite instructors of all time.

Loomis is not your average professor, he is incredible.  He does not fit into any stereo type.  Somehow, he is very funny, engaging, and a "normal person".  At the same time, he works extremely hard to get the most out of the students.  Just a great semester.
Loomis was great, even at 9am. He was very organized, very entertaining, very helpful, and very caring. I can't wait to take another class from him.

Loomis is the Best!  This is not a repeat of h.s. chemistry.  It is much, much more.  Loomis brought in quantum to show us how electrons behave, and how electrons dictate chemistry.  It seems like a bunch of junk, but it is really cool.  The tests really push you, but they are not normalized, which is great.
Great!!!  He is seriously the perfect professor.  He's entertaining, smart, passionate, caring, and seriously demanding.  Take his class, even if it is the 9 am section.

Great professor in a tough class.  Loomis goes the extra 9 yards to make sure students, who work hard, understand the material.  He regularly stays past 8 pm for his 3:30 help sessions.  This is important since some of us feel intimidated by the harder questions that sometimes come up at the beginning.  He is great, and really funny.

Loomis is awesome.  He is really funny, and a great person.  Try to get to know him.  He definitely pushes students to learn, not memorize, and while his exams are very challenging, he grades accordingly.  The Quantum stuff is really cool.

Loomis is hilarious, he keeps everything interesting. The class itself is very difficult but if you just make it through it you'll be fine. Loomis is tough but he makes the material interesting and is just a great teacher. Glad to have met him
Loomis is great. He is full of energy and can explain anything 5 different ways. He is also tough, but he does that for our benefit. What a great semester.

Loomis makes 111 great.  He is extremely clear, and is able to teach to everyone.  He is funny, and always knows when to use humor to break up dry material.  He is a great person with whom you can consult about academic, scientific, and career issues.  There is no better at Wash. U.

Great professor and a great course.  It's amazing to learn about the true origins of the atomic and molecular wave functions.  111 has a bad reputation of being a weed-out course...couldn't be further from the truth.  Loomis does aim for low means, but broad distributions.  He does not normalize, but his means are a mid B.

Loomis is the best.  Yes, he's entertaining, but he uses that to keep our focus on the material, which is no cake walk.  He is able to explain everything 4 or 5 different ways so that everyone has a chance to learn.  Take his class.

Loomis was awesome. He would stay for hours and hours after help sessions until all of us felt comfortable with the material.  What dedication and care about the students. He even e-mailed me today telling me how I did, and he gave me a ton of confidence for next semester and in my career (even though I am premed).  Thnx Loomis.

He lived up to and surpassed my expectations.  He is very interesting, and I appreciate how he is able to convey even the toughest concepts in an understandable manner.  He is great.  I hope I can take him again.
No doubt the best at Wash U. Try to get to know him. He is a great person too, well rounded, funny, smart, and very caring.
Loomis just won the "Best Professor" award at Wash U, yet he is one of the toughest professors there is.  There is no need to say anything else.

GREAT CLASS!  GREAT GUY!  He is able to teach us the actual origin of the atomic wave functions and their consequences on chemistry.  Absolutely fantastic.  By not curving, he was able to bring together the entire class, which helped all of us learn the material.  I agree...go to class.
I Put in the wrong rating last time, Sorry Loomis~
Honestly, go to Class if you have Loomis.
He is so awesome - more than willing to help whatever the need is. He makes it his goal to know all 300 kids in his lecture class and he pretty much succeeds. BEST LECTURES EVER + EVEN BETTER PERSON

Yes he is funny, but he is crystal clear.  It is really cool to learn about the real properties of electronic orbitals.  I am not sure I understand quantum yet, but I want to learn more.  Loomis is absolutely great and interesting.  He is especially awesome in help sessions.

Decent. His explanations are quite, good and hes an engaging lecturer. He's also a brilliant guy who has a lot of passion for chem. Sadly, the class has a terrible propensity to laugh at everything he says, filling his entire lecture with people laughing at his sometimes funny commentary. Frey is better - energetic but not trying to be a comedian.

I was told I had to take Chem with Loomis, and I have not been disappointed.  He is great.  Funny, smart, and a great teacher.  He is the most personable professor I have ever met.  He is trying to memorize all of our names, and he has even offered to have lunch with all of the students.  He is a must.
he is awesome
lOOMIS IS THE BEST.  SERIOUSLY, HE IS THE ENTIRE PACKAGE.  GREAT AND ENTERTAINING LECTURER.  CARING.  SMART.  EAST TO COMMUNICATE WITH.  HE KNOWS HOW TO GET THE MOST OUT OF HIS STUDENTS.
Professor Loomis is a fantastic teacher! Clarifies difficult concepts. Tests are challenging, but satisfying if you do well. Overall very interesting class

Overal best teacher at Washu. Material was novel to everybody regardless of whether you had taken ap chem or not. Very difficult class but he was an amazing teacher who was able to dumb down the material then build it back up quite well. Always available for help, cared deeply for  the students dand gave out difficult, but reasonable exams

Professor Loomis is the best teacher I have ever had.  He is brilliant and I learned an incredible amount during my first semester at Wash U.  Sure, he's hard, but college isn't supposed to be easy.  He is also willing to help and talk to you about the course.  If you get the chance, take his class.

I never imagined that a professor would care so much about how the students do and how much they learn, but Loomis does.  He is incredibly smart, and a genuine person.  I agree with the previous, he is also the funniest ever.  Take Loomis for Chem 111, if at all possible.

Loomis is HILARIOUS. His class feels more like a comedy show than chemistry, but I still learned so much. He knows what he is talking about and loves to interact with students and answer questions. Bottom line - his class was awesome. I don't even like chem that much and I liked it.

Fantastic.  He can scare you at first, but he just tries to get everyone involved and in tune with what he's talking about.  It was really cool to see this phys chem perspective of chemistry.  I'm looking forward to taking him again.  Pay attention to him and you will do fine.

Great lecturer!  He is even better in help sessions.  He seems to carefully think about our questions and then is able to explain the material in multiple ways until we can see what he is talking about.  Just amazing.  I'm not sure his exams need to be that tough, but he adjusts the grades.  Take him.

Loomis is awesome. He is way smart, yet he knows how to communicate even the hardest material. He cares about the entire class, and he wants everyone to learn the material. Warning, get ready to work, because this is not your average Chem course. Loomis has changed my mindset about how to learn. I can already tell it will help me in all classes.

Loomis was great.  Perfect tempo and mix of background material with new concepts and just enough application.  By the way, he definitely expects you to learn the material, and on exams you have to use the material to solve problems that you have never seen before.  He will definitely push you.
Fantastic guy, knows exactly what he's doing and how to cater to students without making the class too hard or too easy.  Really fun class that i enjoyed going to throughout the semester.

Loomis is awesome.  Smart, caring, and funny.  He forces you to think in a new way.  You can't just memorize you have to learn and understand.  This was probably the first time in my life that I have had to do that.  It's great.  Take Loomis if you can.

Loomis is the best!! I was dreading this class at the beginning of the semester, and it was definitely hard, but Loomis made it a class that I actually enjoyed! He's funny, but he's serious about helping everyone understand.

Dr. Loomis is a riot.  He is a really good lecturer, but he is the best in help sessions.  He seems to be willing and able to explain things different ways so that everyone can understand the material, which is tough.  You can tell that he really wants everyone to learn about Chemistry, but he also realizes that it is not for everyone.

Loomis is full of energy, character, insight, intelligence, and compassion.  Seriously, he does a fantastic job.  Somehow, he is making Gen. Chem. very interesting, even though I have had 3 yrs in high school.  I hope I can have him for Quantum.  Take this course.  You will work hard, but it is worth it.

Great man and great professor.  Truly dedicated to teaching and helping his students understand the material. He makes chemistry both enjoyable and rewarding. Highly recommend you attend his lectures.
Pchem I is an incredibly dificult class - do the HWs, if you do it right they will help you. Office Hours are a must. the only way to do well is to work hard.

Math 401...maybe, but it is a good mix of quantum physics w/ chemistry.  I like how he brought in new aspects of quantum.  I wish he would use a different book.  HWs are a bear, but do them or you won't have a chance.  While he is hard, in the end he is a very fair grader.  Don't be afraid to go to office hrs...he can definitely explain things.

It is only halfway through the semester, but he is good.  A bit hard, but a good mix of math with physics and now chemistry.  I wish I had him for Chem 111...that would have been a blast.  Rock on Loomis.
Lectures are just an opportunity for him to "perform" as he copies handwritten notes onto the blackboard.  Good comedian, poor professor.

A really difficult, but excellent course.  Loomis is great.  To learn from someone like him is why I came to Wash. U.  I can't imagine a better Quantum course.  I wish that I could have him in other courses.

He is HARD!  Somehow he knows when we're lost and he spends the time to get us up to speed.  A mean of 50 on exams is daunting, but he knows that if you get a 50 you know more than 50% of the material.  I have had great profs here, but he is the best.  He has convinced me to go to grad school for Phys. Chem.  Take this class, be prepared to work.

Excellent mix of math with Quantum and actual experimental details.  Gives you great intuition for spectroscopy experiments.  A must for anyone interested in advanced chemistry.  You don't have to be a grad student to take it and do well.

Just a great class and a fabulous professor.  He really cares if people understand the material and we follow the importance of the material.  You must take Gen Chem with him.  Frey was my assigned Prof., but you will get much more out of class with Loomis.  I look forward to having him again.

Loomis is excellent.  He knows his stuff and he can teach anyone.  He keeps you entertained, but does not distract you.  He is really, big...get over it and go to his office hours, it is really helpful.  Because of him, I have switched from Biochem to Chem.  I hope I can have him for my advisor.

You don't have to have taken AP chem.  Some stuff just requires you to be able to solve problems.  Be sure to go to class and not tune out when you're there.  Read the book and look at the examples when you read.  Be prepared for questions you've never seen before on the exams, this guy is famous for making hard exams.

A nice guy and pretty entertaining, but he assumed that everyone had taken AP Chem.  he obviously knows his stuff, but since he knows it so well that is obvious in his teaching, which sometimes got overly complicated

I did well in the class cause I had taken AP Chem before.  I thought he did a good job of going over the basics first and then taking more time on the hard stuff. Best if you go to class rather than watch the lectures, but watching them is better than nothing. One of the better chem teacher to have.
He has trouble explaining it as if we dont already know what he is talking about. The class assumes you've taking AP chem
He makes chemistry class really fun.
Really cool but it's a hard class.

Didn't have Loomis as my lecture prof. but went to his help session every week. Makes it very clear that he expects alot from students but also is sincere and concerned for them. Takes the time to answer questions as thoroughly as he can. Writes really hard tests questions though.

Chem was a difficult course but Loomis always made himself available after class and help sessions for any questions that could not be answered.  He also offers questions that are similar to those which appear on the tests.

Loomis does a great job of keeping the class awake and he made class bareable. He gets a little disorganized & confused sometimes, but it's not as dry as Frey's lectures. He has a human side and actually cares about students, something the chem department isn't known for.
Professor Loomis is hott

Loomis was a funny and entertaining teacher. However, his lectures were unorganized and unclear. So much so that I would often watch Frey's lectures to ensure that I was caught up on the class material.

Gives a good combination of material with humor to keep us in tune.  He really knows this PChem stuff and can relate it on any level.  Wow!!  Everyone needs to hold on tight because he goes way fast.  At the same time he stays aware if students are not up with him.  He rocks!
Good teacher, HARD class
Comical...definitely will keep you awake!
Loomis was very entertaining.
Loomis is awesome. I had Frey and left her class and just went to Loomis' lectures because he kept me awake.
Made the material interesting and fun to learn.
Professor Loomis makes this class very fun and interesting.  He is a great teacher.
Everyone needs to take this class and it's ment to weed students out.  With that in mind, the class isn't so bad.  Loomis makes class interesting, but it's still really hard.
I found Professor Loomis to be very helpful and concerned about his students.
interesting and funny lectures---though sometimes unprepared for class making his notes hard to follow
prof. loomis is really funny. the subject matter is really hard, but he usually makes it interesting. dont let your cell phone ring becuase he will answer it.
made things unclear to me, presented his notes in a jumbled fashion. inappropriate in class
made the class really interesting and fun
He made me stop hating Chemistry.  'nuff said.
Made chemistry worth while!
No Comments
Entertaining, personable, very smart. You won't fall asleep even if you hate Chem. Just visit him if you have questions. He wants students to do well but enjoys challenging them.
He is a very funny and entertaining guy, which makes his lectures more interesting. The subject matter is very hard, and he moves kind of fast, but I always enjoyed going to his lectures.

He makes the class very interesting, very funny, some people goes to his class for entertainment...also flicks people off.  On the other side, he actually covers all the material you need to know for the exam.  His class gets higher average than Frey's.
Nussinov came through for me!! The course was hard but she was there to help to give extensions to explain. Be prepared to work and you will be just fine.

One of the most caring professors I ever had. She is genuinely there to get you through the material if you want to learn. The material was not difficult but it's a lot. I like her circuits class more than 2190.

There was lots of work, but it was mostly done in groups. Professor Nussinov was flexible with deadlines, and the exams were fine if you attended class. The antenna case study was great, and it ended with a fun poster session. I would take her class again.
So detailed focused and oriented. Not much to learn but spent a enourmous amount of time doing unnecessary tasks.

Circuits was a challenging course and was loaded with a lot of coursework. Outside of that, it was very doable, and Nussinov was always there to help out, whether that was in the lab, ICE, or homework. If you put in work into the class, you'll be fine. Through her, I had a very thorough understanding of circuits. Also, exams were fair. Love her.
exam was nothing like the practice exam

Lectures are long, boring, and not really coherent. Way too much work outside class with lots of research, case studies, biweekly time-consuming assignments, homework, and exams. Instructor is nice but doesn't really seem to care about workload feedback. This class is one of the least enjoyable I've taken so far.

Not great lectures. Too much work and research considering it's a math class. Case studies could be interesting if the workload (within the case studies and outside assignments) weren't so much. Kind professor.
Her passion for the subject was contagious! Even though her course was difficult, I could tell she wanted her students to succeed.
Lectures were not worth going to; she reads off slides that have many mistakes. Workload was way too heavy for this course and not enough time was given for exams.

Tsitsi is an amazing prof with good lectures, passion, and a caring attitude. That said, she assigns an insane amount of work to the point it becomes busywork. The labs do not need to be so much work and graded so harshly on small formatting errors. Also I did not feel they contributed much at all to my understanding. Exams are ok but a lot for 1hr

Overall shes very nice and understanding. There is just way more busy work than ideal in her classes. She is also a very strict grader and generally does not make things easy even when they could be. Most weeks there was an extra thing to do that pushed the workload over comfortable.

Professor Nussinov is a good professor, but it's clear in 2190 that she needs more resources. The lectures are definitely dense with material, and it is unlike any math class I've taken. I think more revisions are needed to this class so that the learning outcomes are clearer.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Nussinov is very kind and clearly cares about her students, but the lecture quality is mediocre. Mistakes and typos are frequently found in slides and posted notes, and oftentimes points are taken off for very random and trivial reasons. Thankfully there's a generous grading cutoff, and she's definitely willing to help during office hours

Solid professor, really cares about her students' learning and well-being. The material itself isn't too bad and she provides great notes, but there's a lot of busywork. Exams and lab sessions could allow more time, but you get a cheat sheet for exams that can get you some points back. Get ready to put in a lot of time to write lab reports.

Some people say that she is a bad professor but she is actually great. Yes the material is hard but she makes sure that everyone in class follows along and makes sure that you are very prepared for the exams and labs. Amazing homework help and will guide you through the same problem 100 times if needed. Also always in a great mood. GOAT
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
There was no time to actually learn the material with the amount of lab work and hw. Too much busy work to actually understand what I was doing.

That being said, because there was so much going into the grade other than tests so it was pretty easy to get an A, but if you want to actually learn circuits, it takes a lot of discipline and time.
Prof Nussinov is an amazing and caring lecturer! You learn a lot about circuits in this class. Once you understand the material and practice problems, everything becomes natural

Professor Nussinov herself is very kind and helpful. Her notes are very well-organized and the course content itself is pretty straightforward. For the class itself, there is A LOT of busy work. The homework + in-class exercises + labs take up so much time. The lectures were sometimes a bit boring/confusing.

Great provided class notes. She cares a lot about individual students but her course is extremely tough. Exams are low stakes but difficult and there's a heap of homework. You'll get by if you're interested in the field but otherwise prepare to have no free time.
She's just a lot...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: So much busy work, but everyone gets an A. Take ESE 230 if you want to have no free time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Extremely nice professor and very helpful if you find her after class. The lectures are excellent and slow-pace. Lots of potential extra credit. However, this class has a lot of homework and a small (usually) exercise after each class. The A level is 85%. Her grading is very generous; in case your work meet all requirements, you will receive >90%.

Dr. Nussinov is one of the best professors I have had at Wash U. She is incredible and really cares about her students. Her grading scale is amazing and she makes sure everyone understands the materials.

Circuits was my favorite class this semester. It is a LOT of work, but if you manage your time well and go to office hours and recitation, you will be fine. Dr. Nussinov is really helpful and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Nussinov genuinely cares about students. She was always available to help and very accommodating. She lectures well and provides good notes.

This class is simply a lot of work, especially taken online. Fortunately, Nussinov is super accommodating and accessible outside of class. Her lectures and explanations are clear, but I would still go to office hours (upwards to like once a week). Overall, she's super kind and really cares for her students.

Apart from labs that were difficult online, this was my favorite class. Professor Nussinov was very accommodating. Organized lectures and class material and super responsive by email or Zoom. thank you for a good semester.

Dr Nussinov cares about her students! She is available to help when the class material gets overwhelming. Her online class this semester is one of the best classes I have taken. I feel this class would be way better in person.

Professor Nussinov provides lecture notes which are clear and concise, and her lectures are decent as well. Quizzes and homework were manageable; not overly difficult, but still got you thinking. The one issue I had with the class was the insane amount of time it took to receive feedback on lab reports.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is alright in terms of content, and Nussinov definitely tried to make it a more pleasant experience during Covid by dropping the weight of quizzes and making them easier as things went on. However, labs tended to get graded late and the class uses Pearson MasteringEngineering for some of the homeworks, which is extremely frustrating.

Nice person but horrible teacher. She was unorganized and made a lot of mistakes in class and even in her homework/exam problems. It once took me three days to convince her that her solution to a simple step function problem was wrong. Ridiculous. She also failed to communicate actively with the class.
i love her lectures!
Professor nussinov is a great teacher who cares about her students. She is even more helpful one-on-one. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS and I repeat GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Nussinov is an outstanding professor. She takes her students opinions very seriously and is very clear in lecture. However, because this is a large class, it is hard to hear her if you do not sit near the front. She bases her exams on "easier" versions of the online homeworks. Very fair professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: If she taught any other classes, I would take them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She does not have many redeeming qualities. Her lectures are spotty and badly done, there is a lot of busywork, the labs are downcurved, and are a literal mess. The only upside is that she's nicer in office hours, so when you take 230, make sure to go to office hours. It is worthwhile to note that she is not helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Overall, Nussinov is very caring. She works through plenty of examples in-lecture, and is super accessible during office hours. Lab reports are a time-sink, however. Expect to put in several hours in each report. Sometimes makes mistakes in lecture, but is a lot better in a smaller group/1-on-1 setting than she is in a lecture setting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took this class last fall and got an A+. Dr. Nussinov had a lot of group activities that were very helpful. The work-load was heavy - this is a 4-unit course. She was very helpful and friendly every time I went to see her. Circuits was my best grade of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Nussinov is a very good teacher but the class was too large with close to 200 students. I think this class would have more positive opinions if this was a smaller lecture class of 40 students. It would make a difficult subject more accessible and understandable. A very caring professor - go to office hours if you can.

I learned a lot in this class. Participation is mandatory though you can skip class twice without consequences. She has an accent - but its not too bad. The exams are hard if you miss class. Office hours are super-helpful. It was a big class - Dr. Nussinov handled it well. Solid teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Circuits was by far one of my worst classes, and Nussinov was a big part of that. She's really nice, and pretty helpful one-on-one, but she can't lecture well at all. Makes mistakes all the time, and isn't always super clear on what's expected on exams. To be fair, she is new to teaching, and will get better. For now, I would not recommend.

Lectures don't align closely with exam content. Students who come in without prior stats knowledge will find it difficult to keep up, as the course relies heavily on independent learning. Be prepared to do a lot of self-teaching.

Nice man willing to help students in office hours. However, took a long time to grade exams & homework assignments. Tests are short, which means small mistakes have a large effect on grades. The content (various tests of statistical significance in experiment, basically no math) is not too hard, but don't go into the class thinking it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I struggle with math, but I couldn't have asked for a better professor. Really wants students to succeed in the class, but will also challenge you.

Prof Nestojko is just a great human being; he's funny and he explains stats really well. Lectures are a little boring but he tries his best to make the content engaging. There isn't too much work and the tests are straightforward and fair if you study.

The one thing about this course that drove me INSANE was the number of redundant, repetitive minor assignments. They were poorly scheduled and, in my opinion, unnecessary. So if you hate classes where the work seems never-ending, do NOT take this course with Nestojko if you can help it. Otherwise, he tries his best to be engaging and helpful.

I think the content of the course is interesting. John tries to be engaging while teaching, and that is a nice thing about his class. Exams take a majority of your grade which forces you to memorize rather than learn. I would avoid at all costs if you are trying prioritize your GPA.

Course is very organized and straightforward. Lectures are a bit slow but they're recorded (so you can just watch them at 2x speed later). Dr. Nestojko is pretty chill (dad vibes) but can be passive aggressive when irritated... dude is only human tho, just try to show up for lecture and be present.

His class is a little bit slow, which is perfect for statistics beginners but might be a bit boring if you have statistics background already. Not a lot of homework, and they are quick to finish too. The exams are pretty straightforward and similar to the examples he goes through in class.

Dr. Nestojko was so fun in class and always available for questions. I had issues during the semester, but he was always willing to assist me in whatever way he could. I will say that the exams do impact your grade quite a bit. I did struggle in the class but not because of Dr. Nestojko and I would definitely take one of his classes again.

I took Psych300 and Psych301 with Nestojko (in different semesters). Psych300 will be a cakewalk for most people, especially if you have prior stats experience. Psych301 is a ton of work especially in the second half of the semester, but Nestojko does a great job of supporting students and teaching them the content in an engaging way.

His lessons are engaging and understandable. In his larger lecture based classes, he tries to maintain engagement, but he is better at facilitating that in a smaller class setting. He won't try to trick you or make the material too hard to learn, which other professors will do at Wash U. He's very social, which took some time for me to get used to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Nestojko gave me weird vibes. Sometimes he was extremely nice and caring, other times he came off as insanely passive-aggressive. The class itself was pretty easy, even if you have no stats background. Very lecture-heavy and can get boring. Lots of mini-HW assignments throughout the week, but they help prepare you for exams.

Easy lectures, 2x speed voice, & sweet BUT don't get him "mildy irritated". Records lectures, attendance is counted randomly with polls. So... not many people showed up to class recently and he got upset about it. He moved an assignment originally due in the weekend to the same day and did not upload the recorded lecture on purpose because of this.

Lectures can be a little dry but that has more to do with the content and less to do with the professor (you can only make psych stats so interesting). Nestojko does a wonderful job at explaining concepts clearly in a manner that is very easy to understand. Would recommend for anyone looking for an easy statistics or NSM credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Nestojko is an amazing professor. He is very organized and friendly and is great at explaining concepts. There are lots of homework and group projects, so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Nestojko is a chill dude and his lectures are pretty interesting. Fair grader and his study guides make it pretty clear what he expects you to know for the exam. Took all three of the classes he taught at WashU and would recommend any of them. (P.S. since I know you read these, this review is actually me).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at WashU; he is engaging, funny, caring, and an excellent teacher. There is a nice balance of lectures, reading, and assignments in Psych300

This man is an angel. He is the most caring and amazing professor on this campus. He is an amazing lecturer and really cares about his students so much. His experimental psych class is hard (not his fault) but he is great.

Dr. Nestojko has probably been my favorite professor at WashU so far. He is a dynamic, funny, caring lecturer who can make a class as dull as stats a good time. Not only this, but Dr. Nestojko makes his expectations clear at the beginning and is always willing to be a resource to help you succeed.

I'm a psych student, not particularly interested in stats. As such, I didn't find the class very interesting, but it's probably the most ideal stats class offered. Nestojko is super nice and has great dad jokes, and the workload isn't crazy. Your grade is mostly based on 4 tests, so you need to study, but you can bring 2 pages of notes to exams.

Although this class seems to be a lot (you have to write two nearly 18-page papers throughout the semester), he gives plenty of feedback to help you do well. I attended office hours nearly every week during the times that we had to write the papers and I did very well. He does a great job of helping if you go to him to ask for it.

I took stats and experimental during a really difficult time in my life, and I really struggled w/ the material. Dr. Nestojko was so patient w/ me & always made sure that I understood the material. He made dry, boring material as interesting as possible, and he's a firm but understanding professor. Be prepared for dad jokes! Love him!
Such an incredible professor! Learned so much in this class and was excited to take another class from him. Highly recommend!

While he definitely was caring with this pandemic with deadlines for exams, this class was full of busy work. Tests arent too bad, but sometimes the wording of some questions isnt so great. This class was just very ok, not extremely remarkable.

Genuinely cares about his students & is SUPER understanding. Exams are easy, they're exactly like the study guides. There's a lot of HW, but doing them helps on exams. HW is not super difficult as long as u watch lecture. I really appreciate him considering the mental health of his students & allowing extensions on assignments. God tier professor!!

I never leave reviews for my professors, but Nestojko really stoked my ire. The amount of busy workquizzes, Jasp assignments, etcis absurd. Not only that, but Nestojko is awful at explaining these concepts. Sure, the exams are easy, but it really feels like this professor never respected his students and their time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Best thing about Dr Nestojko? Hes accessible. I emailed him in a panic at 2am the night before a paper was due. He responded in 10 minutes. Kind, funny, and a great lecturer. I recommend him for both psych stats and experimental psych. One of the best professors at WashU.
Simply the best. Don't settle for less.

a cheery, positive demeanor can carry a sometimes-dull subject like psych stats very high-- nestojko does just that. a great instructor, and honest with students. during this whole quarantine thang, he constantly reassured his students that he'll do anything possible to make the learning experience easier on his students. warning:has many dad jokes

I have never written a review for a professor on this platform, but Dr Nestojko's is one of the best professors at Wash U. He is extremely accessible outside of class and cares deeply about his student's success. It's not a show up and get an A type of class (you need to study and do well on exams), but it is very reasonable if u try.

Ive taken two classes with Nestojko and both were great. Experimental is a potentially difficult class and he made it easy and entertaining. He is a funny and engaging lecturer and the test and quiz material comes almost all from the slides. I recommend taking any class you can with him
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome prof -- super prepared, knows what he's talking about, funny, and tests are very reasonable. Only downside is that there are 5 exams, which is a lot, but online assignments/homework can boost your grade. Not the most interesting class, but he definitely does his best to try to make it not painfully dry.
Professor Nestojko is a great professor! He cares about each student as an individual, gives great feedback, and is pretty chill.

Explain things clearly and patiently! Very concerned about his students both in class and outside of classroom. I was the only international student in his summer class, and he asked me if I felt left out and cooperated well with project group members. He also made sure that students who did not go lecture know what happened and can catch up
A great instructor! Very open and involved, by far my favorite professor.
It was ok. As long as u pass the exams you will do fine.

The first half was easy but the second half is full of difficult functions, and each class you get 15-20 more concepts you need to implement, which goes too fast to digest. I really wish you can teach, instead of relying on these self-taught videos. Teachers are supposed to teach, as the word itself suggests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course has definitely improved, and the materials are much more manageable than described in the previous comments.

Shocked to read the negative reviews. The course has been extremely reasonable, and the notes/resources provided are more than sufficient. You don't even need to watch the online lectures if you just read the notes. Prof. Chehrazi has been helpful and efficient. Exams are open note. You're only way to fail is over-relying on AI.

Interesting class for sure. His TAs were very useless, and he announced two got fired mid-semester for not showing up to office hours. He got a grad student TA who was great.
Class is.. easy but then you have 15mins to finish an assignment that should be a lot longer. Expect to lose points there, but not much else.

Only goals in class are to prove how smart he is and to find small things to take points off for. Will give you a 0 on the lab if you forget to include your student ID. Gives 15 minutes to do an in-class lab that he claims is exactly like the practice questions he assigns but makes the required output slightly different to confuse people.

He's a pretty intense guy. Python is really not that hard but the timed 20 min "labs", which are more like pop quizzes make python 50x harder than it actually is. He's also not the most helpful when asking for guidance in the labs. Make sure to prepare before class and stay alert in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Hands down one of the worst professors I have ever had. He could care less about the students; teaches essentially nothing the entire class, and is about as unclear as you can be about the grading system.

Professor Reynolds is a fantastic history professor, and her knowledge and passion for the topics is very clearly on display. Super interesting to talk to about the subject matter, and easy to approach about any questions. Reading workload is quite heavy, but not all of it is essential for succeeding in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I love her so much she's genuinely my icon, and I have gone to her about projects in other classes because I knew she could guide me and help me out. The class is a LOT of reading but you can get away without doing all of it. I highly recommend this class!

Dr. Reynolds is a top-rate professor at WashU. Her enthusiasm for the material is evident every time she teaches. She does not give many essays and is a fair grader. She uses participation with the material in return, which is enjoyable. She is one of the sweetest professors I've ever had; I couldn't imagine leaving WashU without taking her class!
I took Late Ottoman Middle East. Professor Reynolds is one of the best profs at WashU. Really knowledgeable and really understanding of student schedules. Take a class with her if you can!

Very good teacher, very good lecturer, really knows her stuff. However, extremely partial.  Took 20th Century Middle East and it was completely from the Arab, anti-Zionist, perspective.    I'm a liberal but this class made made me sympathetic of the Israeli cause.

Class had a ton of reading, much of which I found uninteresting. Nonetheless, she is a first-rate professor who really tries to explain things thoroughly. She is very understanding of any problems students may be having. Would recommend her as a professor -- perhaps not this class though.
Great lecturer, knows her stuff!  Highly recommended for students in any major concentration.

Prof. Reynolds really knows the topic well and she always hands out outlines of the lectures with key terms on them.  She is also very good at getting people to participate in discussions.  My only complaints are that the class covers a LOT of material, which made it a very fast-paced and thus somewhat difficult class.

Neumann was actually a very caring and accomodating professor. The class contents were very useful and relevant in terms of data science, so make sure to pay attention because these concepts are what you are going to be interviewed on during internship apps. One thing I dislike is that the grading scheme is not clear, so you can lose points easily.

Grading is too tough, and barely gives out full credit for homework. She's a nice person, though, and very willing to teach. However, she deducts too many points for unnecessary writing mistakes, and the quiz setup does not really make sense (too many problems in a short time period).

shes super scary and intimidating if shes the one doing your demos and not a TA- good luck! but shes really smart just not the most approachable. its very possible to get an A in 217 if u spend a while on the hws/projects so dont be scared but grading is tough

This class was just annoying. You have to come into class for annoying and pointless lectures that are basically replaced by the Zybooks you do before class. There is often not enough time given for labs as well. As long as you start the homework and projects early, you should get an A in this class.
Not recommended. Don't get yourself in trouble.
Attending classes but not giving participation points, with multiple communications that were ineffective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is by far the worst course I've ever taken at WashU. Absolute horrendous structure and group work makes the class much harder to learn. Homework is not clear on grading and asks a vague question with no outline of what is expected. I don't understand how being super strict with no expectation outlined is fair and helpful to learning.

Absolutely love Neumann. She's really passionate about data science and teaches pretty well. The class can get kind of confusing with proofs and complex math but the assignments you can do with partners and the test is more conceptual than math heavy. She's super sweet and helpful (but can go on tangents sometimes)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class has no tests and everything can be done in a group or with TA help so nothing is too bad. As long as you start the hw early, you should be fine. Neumann doesn't really teach the actually coding parts that well since the class is about data science (not learning python) but it's not super hard to grasp. Easy class to get an A in

Best 217 professor in my opinion. No exams, just weekly homework, in-class assignments, and zyBooks. In-class stuff is usually boring, but not too hard, you just follow the instructions. You don't get enough practice with any of the libraries used to get super comfortable with them. You just have to look at your old code to complete assignments.

Marion is super nice, passionate about data science, and really helpful one-on-one. 217 was at times disorganized with some unclear grading criteria, but generally I learned a lot of practical skills from her. Home works are weighted heavily, but going to OH pretty much guarantees a 100 on them. I liked Marion and her class!

Prof. Neumann is very caring and approachable to the class, and is very helpful, but the problem is that she needs some time to review the materials to understand herself. She sometimes makes mistakes or fails to answer students' questions during lectures. HW, implementation projects and exam is a bit hard, but group projects were pretty easy.

There was no exams but A LOT of homework and worksheets to be done alone. But they are not that hard so u'll easily get A if u work on it. This class was literally watching a bunch of recorded lectures, do hw and worksheets and labs(in a group). She doesn't rly answer clearly to piazza questions; this class felt like self-taught.

Not the biggest fan of Neumann. Her lectures are kind of hard to follow, and it's hard to see how they apply to the HWs.
