She doesn't give grading rubrics beforehand, but then she grades assignments using extremely specific criteria. Certainly a caring person, but the structure of her class gave me anxiety and makes me not want to take her again.
Not a good teacher. Since she has bad english, her exam questions ended up being incomprehensible. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Clearly knows a lot about the field, but certainly grades like it. Lectures were relatively clear but lack of posted notes is annoying. Not an easy A but certainly doable - you just need to stay on top of the (admittedly long) homework.

This is a really good class, there are assignments every week but they're not too hard. You learn a lot of real world skills and Professor Neumann puts in a lot of effort to make sure they are up to date, removing things from the course once they become obsolete industry wise. The slides and homework are good
I think the class is not too hard so Prof. Neumann can have more time to play words game with students instead of improving her teaching skills.

Neumann doesn't talk about things in a concise manner. In a lab section, she planned to talk about the slide for 15 mins, and eventually dragged on for almost an hour, leaving us with only 20 minutes to finish the lab quiz. This happens quite often. She also takes points off for minor format things that do not relate to the course itself. AVOID.
She's very disorganized. Slides are disorganized. HW instructions have bugs.

Very nice professor and very fair in her assessments. Her primary focus is that you leave her class having learned a lot and excited to learn more by continuing your studies. She cares a lot about the student experience and the value a class will bring to you

She's very disorganized. Slides are disorganized. HW instructions have bugs. Have a tough "midterm" at the end of semester tested on everything. Tough final project. Almost every HW per week takes a full day. It's not her material really challenge you intellectually, it's her disorganization really frustrates you and kill your time.

Neumann is my advisor and I've taken one class with her(cloud computing). I don't really understand all of these bad reviews, I had a great time in her class, homework was reasonable and so were tests. She taught the material well, and only tested on the material she covered in class.

As others have stated, Neumann means well, but is not a good lecturer. Many times she has copied a formula on the board and pauses to try to understand what she just wrote down because she doesn't even know it. You're better off just reading the book than attending lecture. Was told this class would be easy - it isn't. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Neumann is very nice and wants to be a good professor, but simply isn't. She is extremely scatterbrained which makes lectures very confusing, and she does not explain the material well. The class material is also bad, and she had the ability to change it but chooses not to. The homeworks are also brutal. I wouldn't recommend her or this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Questions in homeworks and exams are hard to understand. Lectures are far not enough to finish homeworks. Disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 1. She gives really horrible lectures. She needs to learn math. It's clear that she herself doesn't completely understand the topic. She often gets herself lost in the middle of deductions. 2. CS department should consider inviting some math professors to teach this subject. They are much more consistent, precise, and clear.
Her lectures were disorganized. She didn't even know what she was talking about.

I suggest her to watch Andrew ng's videos before teaching this course. Mostly I really don't understand what she is talking, it seems that she just copy all the notes onto the blackboard without explanation, I'm sad I took this course and I spent so much time on that then I realize I should watch Andrew's videos from the very beginning.
Class is really disorganized, theory and proofs everywhere, I used Andrew Ng's youtube videos to learn this class instead. Avoid her at all costs.

Ledesma-Ortiz makes you work but is also so kind and accommodating to students' needs (she once moved an exam because it was scheduled on my birthday). The small class sizes means everyone participates which can be scary. Her Spanish accent is beautiful to listen to, and she sometimes goes on fun tangents about her family and Argentinian culture.

Professor Ledesma Ortiz is one of my favorite professors at WashU. I find her class to be quite fun while being a great atmosphere to improve your conversational Spanish skills as well as your comprehension of many different cultures. The first unit is fairly difficult but outside of that her class is a must-take if you're interested in Spanish!
I took Ledesma Ortiz for Span 302 and I loved her. Great class and she was super clear about instructions and we always had nice discussions.

The first unit of the semester for this course in particular is really difficult, however other than that Profe is an excellent teacher of Spanish. She's a native speaker, super willing to help, funny, and she explains things in a way that just makes sense to me. I would definitely recommend Profe Ortiz to anyone on the fence about taking Spanish
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Definitely need to go to class to do well, as participation really matters in Spanish classes. She's a great teacher tough, I don't think many people got below an 85% (as long as you try, you will do well).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: To be honest, I was super scared of her the first couple lectures (I actually almost dropped the class, but I stuck with it). Over time I began to realize that she is a super sweet lady. Yes, she cold-calls sometimes during discussion so you need to pay attention, but my Spanish genuinely improved so so much, and she is so understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really caring and sweet lady, and always work with you to make sure you fully understand the concepts. You definitely have to keep up with the work, but it's not difficult to succeed in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: I missed a lot of class in Spanish 201, but she was great about helping me work around it. Everything you need to know is on the syllabus she gives. Great teacher in class too. She speaks clearly which is great for a language class and her tests are pretty easy.

Great person but she grades pretty hard and expects a lot out of her students. She's very good about being available though and her office hours are very helpful in my opinion. She isn't the course coordinator, and thus she often blames administrative fallacies (mistakes on practice tests/actual tests etc) on the coordinator.
She's a wonderful woman but her class is unnecessarily difficult.

Oren is great. Good lecturer, funny, and nice. Participation is a key part of your grade. Tests were hard and seemed confusing to study for, but the Olin curve helped. Your Case Competition group is key to this class. People have mixed feelings about this class due to their teammates in this. TAs are helpful. Good intro class for Olin.
Amazing lecturer, always engaging with the class and giving opportunities to participate. Was a great introduction to the Olin Business School as a Freshman. Could be a tough grader though.
Very nice person, but a quite challenging class.

Oren is the sweetest and super kind but he does move quickly through topics and exams are often confusing. He does care a lot about his students and made sure we had a good time. Grades are heavily inflated based on case comp performance.

Reshef's lectures were quite hard to understand at times, especially the math. He breaks things down to their "intuition," but the concepts are confusing and difficult to grasp. Slides are jumbled with tons of numbers and he doesn't explain the relationship between them well. Participation heavy.
Funny prof. Required Course. Love Oren.

Though the class was difficult, Oren himself made it more enjoyable. He had a good sense of humor, engaging lectures, and tried to care about students. I don't think he's condescending or intimidating, but you'll have to be ready to participate in discussions and be wrong/challenged. But, his exams are tricky and rely heavily on lectures/reading.

Teacher was great and made the class more interesting. The class in itself is difficult because the exam questions tend to be worded to give you a hard time. However, the exam scores are curved so if you do above average, participate in class and do well on case comp you should manage a good score in this class.

Oren was a great professor! His lectures kept me interested and wanting to learn more throughout the semester. From what I know, his class is more difficult than other MGT 1000 profs. Grading is slightly weird: he keeps grades hidden until the end of the semester when he weights your grade relative to peers. Overall, a great and personable guy.
"If you do well above the curve you will do well", no shit. Not a good class or taught well with terrible review under this one.

I took this class in spring 2025 and it was my favorite at WashU. This class is hard, but not nearly as hard as people make it sound. If you get well above the curve on 2/3 exams and have a strong showing on the case competition and participate in class, you will do great. I learned so much in this class and loved Reshef's humor and knowledge!
Bad, not good.
Just bad. Stay away from dude.
Makes the class hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Class is fine, but Oren is very condescending.

He is honestly an extremely handsome guy that is great to be taught by. He teaches great and any of the bad comments are lying. He teachers amazingly and everything is so easy. I honestly didn't even have to study at all just breezed through the course. Almost everyone gets an A, you don't even really have to study just try to show up sometimes.

The course content itself is the easiest, but this class is by far the most confusing one. No matter how hard you work for it, don't expect to receive a good grade for the extremely simple material. On top of that, you won't know your grades until the semester ends. Overall, this class is simply a scam.
just dont take this class with him.
The course is expansive. The mindtap we only use 3 times cost around 130 and a textbook cost 120. The textbook is just the course reading, dk why need to buy it.
Grading is mostly done by TAs. Especially for case analysis, you can easily tell how subjective and unfair the grading is.

This course is the weirdest course I've ever taken at this school. The material itself is easy, but the exam questions are very confusing and overly subjective. The questions and answers don't make sense oftentimes.

Oren is an amazing and very engaging lecturer. Participation matters in this class and the people who regularly participated tended to do better. At times, Oren can be inaccessible outside of class, however he genuinely seems like a caring, very smart guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Oren is a great and engaging lecturer and is respected within class. While he joked around, his condescending and "knows better" attitude made class tense. The content was fine, but because scarce practice (esp. math based questions) and abstract exams, learning was difficult. Worse, the grade scale and cumulative grades were never given.

Oren has good lectures where he explains the material thoroughly and gives good examples. Tests were hard because the material was presented in a different way than it was taught in class, so students can work toward developing "intuition", but there's always a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are super engaging and fun! However, he is kind of condescending (a lot of people describe him that way) when he calls on people in class and gives you basically no validation at all when you answer questions. The tests are kind of hard, but the curve is good and if you do well on the case competition your grade will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Oren is very smart, and very good at lecturing, but condescending. If you're not a favorite, it's much harder to succeed in the class. Tests are designed for failure and he acts like they are very easy, which can be frustrating. While presenting for case comp, he was laughing at us, not paying attention, and asking questions we'd already answered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Oren was okay. He came off as condescending, and I didn't find him to be a compelling professor. The class is not fun: The content isn't complex, but the tests are seemingly crafted to discourage students. That said, be prepared to encounter oddly-worded questions. Worth noting: I was "on track to receive an A-" all semester but received a B.

Oren was great. MGT 100 puts a lot of content and a case comp all into 3 exams and a presentation. He made class as fun as it reasonably could be, and pretty much made sure everyone participated. doing so was a bit scary as you'd get called out, but it forced me to actually prep a bit for class. First exam is HARD, after that it isn't too much work
Super engaging and fun class. Tough tests but the curve helps out with that

Reshef is good at lecturing and responding to student questions. He is not afraid to call a comment stupid and tries to sneak some comedy into class. The class is fairly easy, but the grading system is unclear, which can cause unnecessary stress. The exam questions don't match up with practice questions, but the grading is generous.

MGT 100 was my hardest class this sem, but also my favorite. Reshef is super intimidating at first, but I would recommend going to office hours because you can get to know him and find out that he cares a lot about the subject and the students. Tests are kind of worded poorly but the curve is life saving. Enjoy this class, embrace the challenge!

Although Professor Oren shows much care and passion for his class, he came off as very condescending to me especially if you don't have the right answers. Also, the class is very test heavy so three exams in the class are worth a lot in terms of your grade. Make sure to come prepared and do the readings! Also participate as much as you can.

Oren is a great guy with a great personality. It's clear how intelligent he is and he is a good lecturer. You definitely have to put in the work in this class but it's rewarding. Take a class with him if you get a chance!

MGT 100 is a very mundane and useless class, but Oren makes the best of what he has. He's a hilarious personality, explains concepts very well, and gives very helpful feedback for the case comp. He's a bit intimidating at first, but don't be afraid to ask questions because he's very helpful.

I really liked Oren. He is very intimidating at first, but the class is really not that difficult even though they do try to scare you at first. If you put in effort your guaranteed a B+. Also don't use the online reading. I didn't read once and did fine.
Good lectures - easy to understand the content. The course is difficult but TA and professor help will go a long way. Oren means well and is a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Reshef can be a bit rough around the edges but is a really great guy once you get to know him. He's incredibly intelligent and a great lecturer. He genuinely cares about his students and takes students' feedback seriously. Highly recommend taking classes with him.

The course was relaxed and reasonable. There were no surprises with grading or in-class activities. The assigned readings were enjoyable and thoughtful, and the assignments pushed students to become better writers.
Super cool professor who is very passionate about what he teaches. Grading can be tough and sometimes the material can be much more complex than you're prepared for, but overall pretty good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: chill guy & easy class; can be argumentative. i agree w/ a lot of his views and was still nervous in class discussions. also, note that on the syllabus he reserves the right to mark a grade up or down when the grade does not match his assessment. i didn't attend office hours, so probably do that to avoid being marked down. improved my writing tho

I loved my time with professor O'Bryan; he was a great teacher and cared about his students. His lectures were always interesting and I absolutely loved attending class. He was extremely easy to talk to, and was extremely knowledgeable about writing. In taking this class, I know my writing got better - STRONG RECOMMEND

I started the class liking O'Bryan because he is funny, but throughout the semester things changed. He lost his patience and had a really short fuse during discussions. My class was small and cooperative, so there was no reason to get angry with us. He was also overly assertive with his political views. Not helpful for my Legal Studies minor.

Did not even grade our essays in time for the final or other essays, so feedback was useless. He was also overly critical without real reference to the rubric, which always included way more difficult content than what he would actually describe in class. One of the most difficult and time consuming classes I've taken at WashU

Pretty funny and easy to talk to. But a few things he did ticked me off: He often talked way too much, to the point where he was just dominating the conversation rather than letting us speak. He was also very disorganized. He also made a lot of assumptions about students, so I didn't often feel comfortable sharing my true views in the classroom.
Honestly, the coolest professor at Wash U. Hands down. His lectures are always dynamic and interesting. He's super down-to-earth and really cares about students.
One of my favorite professors at Wash U so far, very fair and eager to help
Pretty good Writing 1
Can be disrespectful at times Doesn't highlight class expectations thoroughly
Professor Olson teaches like Jim from The Office.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Olson is a highly underrated professor in the department imo. His use of humor (mostly unnoticed) complements his lectures well, and I found his class to be well organized and easy to follow. Attendance isn't required, but going to class makes a huge difference in grades. I met w/Olson a few times and he was incredibly willing to talk/help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Olson is one of the best professors at WashU. While he assigns a decent amount of reading, he cares a lot about his students and is super accessible outside of class and is always willing to explain things if you are confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: We were graded on only three exams and one paper for the entire course, making grades very important. Only one essay question is asked on each of the three exams, and there is a laughably minimal amount of feedback given after each. The professor is funny and seems like a caring guy, but he is not a great professor.

Nice guy, class was boring at times (polisci isn't my area) but he made it interesting with small tidbits. Other review is tripping because I checked the quiz average (a 95) and the final essay average (a 92), with even higher medians. Doesn't mean the class was easy per se but I think the expectations were clear and he was also willing to help.

Dr. Olson is a believer in in-class essays and then offers very little feedback and grades harshly. Class was boring and assessments did not fit the material. He did not care about the individual success of students.
Good professor and the class is incredibly easy. Pretty boring class, but the time could honestly be used like a study hall
took intro to gis with olson. super nice guy, just show up to class since attendance is madatory and you'll get a good grade
Everything is a completion grade, all assignments and essays. Attendance is mandatory and he makes the polleverywhere due during end of class. Just complete work and easy A
Very easy grader bc everything is for completion! Such a breath of fresh air in comparison to other classes at washu!
Super easy class, barely any hw. Hes pretty funny sometimes too

He is super chill and this is a very easy class. If you are interested in the content, there are many opportunites to learn more and the class talks about many different topics. If you want an easy humanities class, this is it.
Professor Olson is always looking out for students and wants everyone to do well. He's anti ChatGPT, so just try to do the best in your assignments, and you will get an A.
Class was pretty easy. Just do your assignments and you'll get a 100 on them as long as you showed effort. Just attend class too and you'll get an A easily
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Olsen said some crazy things, but overall his lectures are pretty dry. The class is easy and essays are graded on following the rubric (completion). I really enjoyed the many guest lectures we had. Take this class if you want an easy A and low-workload.

dude's chill asf. he's incredibly knowledgeable & just wants to know you are trying. easy grader, light workload, just show up and you'll get an A. can't praise him enough not even tryna glaze him like that but shiii here i am. bald suits him.

Professor Olson is the best professor at WashU. He knows his stuff very well and is super approachable. He does a really good job in getting to know his students and cares for our learning. Grading is very simple and he will let give you an A if you show effort and engagement.
so unbelievably easy and kind. take an upper level class with him you will get a gpa boost. he legit says he doesn't care about grades and pretty much everyone gets an A

Kyle is one of the best profs I've had at WashU. He genuinely cares about his students and isn't a trad prof who is super formal. He wears hilarious track suits and his classes are very easy to succeed if you just do what he says. I HIGHLY recommend him. You will boost your GPA

I took the class as an engineering humanities and it was very easy with low expectations. All graded on participation/completion. I also learned a lot through guest lectures, which were fun and taught interesting content such as tattooed women in ancient Egypt. Dr. Olson is clearly knowledgeable and wants students to learn without causing stress.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Olson was awesome, very caring and knowledgeable guy. Lots of extra credit opportunities and the assignments were extremely easy. Take this to knock off a HUM req and to boost your GPA
A true expert and a really nice guy. Class is incredibly easy and chill, but lectures were interesting! Great guy all around.

lowkey goated and overqualified for his job. Is very knowledgeable, likes to adapt the course to what people are interested in and get feedback from students. Course was a little unstructured but I got the sense it was because the class is brand new and he was testing things out. If you do the work you should have no concerns about your grade

I took Anthro 3261 and the class was amazing! I would 100% recommend taking this class or taking any class by Kyle Olson. He is very laid back and approachable if you need help. Overall the most interesting 300 level course I have taken.

Olson does a great job with World Archeology. It is one of the best classes to take for your HUM. Pretty much everyone got an A. Attendance at guest lectures is required but you can watch on zoom or in person or check the recording after the fact to find the answer to the attendance question. Definitely take this class, very little workload.

He is fun outside of class. However, the way he taught this class made me regret being a chem major. He punishes you heavily for making mistakes. There is little room for practice and growth beyond the homework and staring at the math on posted lecture notes that he never taught in class. Exams were never also representative of lecture content.

Worst professor I have ever had at WashU. Lectures are disorganized and the order did not make sense. He spent little time and made many mistakes on important topics and took lots of time on random details. Exams are insane and he gives little if any partial credit for anything. I would rather drop out than have to take another one of his classes.

Professor Okuno is a nice guy and can be quite funny but that's about it. Lectures are highly math-focused, barely conceptual, and completely different from the lecture notes posted. He also gets confused during lectures even though he has lecture notes in his hand. Exams were crazy different, it's pointless to try and study, better luck guessing.

Very funny and nice guy, but this class was so frustrating. Problem sets, practice exams, and review sessions did not reflect what was covered on the exam. The concepts he spent the most time on and the ones we practiced the most were the ones that didn't show up on the exams.

It is not clear that Dr. Okuno understood the material he was trying to present. So, instead he lectured on mathematics he did understand. Then he tested on the quantum, which he did not understand and he could not explain to us, even after the exam. I would love to know where he got those exam questions from, cause he did not create them.

I do not get him or the class. He presented one thing and tested on another. I understand teachers want us to think, but he tested us on unrelated material. Where in the world would we have learned how to do any of those problems.

Dr. Okuno is a really funny and great person outside of class. However, he has the talent of making a difficult class even harder. His handwriting is completely illegible, and his published notes often don't follow the lectures well. The exams were extremely difficult and the practice exams/problem sets given were not even slightly comparable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were often very confusing, and sometimes he didn't know what was going on. I understood more if I didn't go to the lecture and just read the lecture notes independetly. What was covered on the exams was not very reflective of the problem sets and problems that were discussed in class. The average for the 2nd exam was 38 :(

Okuno is the worst. He spent the first 3rd of the semester going over math concepts, but then said he changed his mind, and we won't use all of it. The 2nd 3rd we started doing 111 material, but somehow he made no sense. I had to get help from my undergrad TA, who for sure knows more than Okuno. The 2nd midterm was impossible and confusing.
how boring can someone make a lecture. seems chill. exams were okay. so many assignments. the assignments never stop. really sticks to his rules.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Orr's lectures are a great time, in general. Many laughs are exchanged, and if you pay attention and genuinely attempt to learn you'll be fine. Exam being cancelled was almost 2 days notice. The poll to cancel, make take home, or keep the exam was sent 3 days before the exam.

James Orr is not a great lecturer. He would often make bad explanations and then ask "is this making any sense" when no one would really reply he'd just continue. He struggles to do practice problems on the board. Despite these facts, if you ask him one-on-one a question he seems to really know what he's talking about and is relatively clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What do you mean the exam is cancelled... Literally sent out the message just 10 hours before the final

Took multiple courses with prof Orr. While I can tell he tried, the teaching quality is really below average. Gave non-answers to students' questions on 361 in lectures. Only saw him 2 times in 132 - he didn't teach 132 at all but threw lots of pre-recorded lecture videos from the last decade.

361 is a notoriously difficult class but Professor Orr does a great job teaching it and is always willing to help. Most lectures are really boring and hard to follow in nature but sometimes Orr is able to make them at least somewhat interesting. Labs are extremely hard and time consuming so utilize TA office hours. Responsive on Piazza.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Solid lectures, and really good class. Labs are genuinely interesting and super fun. Easily the most rewarding CS class I've ever taken

I think Orr could be an amazing Professor. He is super good at explaining things one on one and definitely knows his stuff, but his lectures are not good.

For the exam I had to basically just read the whole textbook to learn the content (after attending most of the lectures).

This class is also super challenging but the content is interesting.

Proff Or is a very good professor, but 361 is just very hard class. The exams are CRAZY and labs definitely extremely time consuming and hard. Labs in terms of difficulty: 

Lab 1 (Data Lab) < Lab 3 (Buffer Lab) < Lab 2 (Bomb Lab) <<<<<<< Lab 5 (Malloc Lab) < Lab 4 (Cache Lab)

Very hard class with a pretty average professor. I like this slides and he seems pretty keen on explaining and helping students. Beware that this class is really hard and though he is a good professor, he cannot save you from the hard assignments. No complaints
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy just did not teach and the assignment and studio instructions can be really vague and confusing at times. Expect to do every assignment in office hours because the TAs are life savers. Its not hard to get an A though, just get the work in and ask for help.

Orr's a nice guy and very willing to help, but be ready to spend countless hours self-studying this course. The lectures were not very helpful, and the labs were super time consuming and this class was pretty poorly organized. It felt like you were learning nothing in lecture and then expected to know everything when it came to exams/labs

CSE 361 is a difficult class, but Orr does a decent job of delivering the content. Grades are harsh, as there are few opportunities for partial credit on assignments. Exams are difficult, but not unreasonable if you study. Orr was kind and often moved back deadlines. Cares about students, it's just a difficult course that should've been broken up.
This class was very tough, but Orr's clear lectures make it manageable. Professor Orr set up lots of office hour opportunities and provided clear guidance for the assignments.

Bro is the actual GOAT. Like I would show up to class every day, huge smile on my face, ready to see him. If you think a professor can't make your day, think again pal! James Orr saved my life. Without him, there would be no meaning, no purpose, and no happiness in my life. He lifted the veil from my eyes and showed me the way of the compiler

Orr is a really nice guy (based on a few interactions), he was always willing to give help when needed and was nice with his explanations. Besides that 132 was a pretty terribly organized class (in my opinion). Sure I got an A, but I didn't really feel like I learned a lot from it. I wish they did live lectures instead but I cant complain too much.
Have never taken a class that is more poorly organized than CSE 132. Everyone got an A in the end but basically learned nothing.

Professor Orr does a decent job running the class along with TAs but it's hard to properly rate him when the class itself is lecture-less. Assignments are time-consuming, so it would be best to find a partner and work together. Almost everything is self-taught through videos and studios. Be ready to invest time in office hours for assignments.

If there was an 'N/A' rating for professor quality, then that would apply here. He never professed; the whole class is self-taught, which, for someone with little to not background in computer science, is absolutely horrible. Not a good class at all. The content has potential but is ailed by a horribly organized class and harrowing assignments.

Assignments are time consuming, but exams are manageable especially due to their low weight in the final grade. Lots of extra credit opportunities and the prof is responsive to questions/regrades. Best thing you can do is find a friend in the class or a friend who has already taken it
He is not the best at explaining things, but his recitation videos are helpful. Start the assignments early and that will help you a lot.

I only interacted with Orr once or twice during 132. When I watched his recitations, he was actually really great at explaining concepts in a clear way. The issue is he designs his class to have as little interaction with students possible. 132 is self-taught or taught by TAs. The grading is easy though - go to office hours and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Professor Orr is absolutely over-hated. His teaching style is not particularly exciting but he presents the material in a coherent way and he fully answers questions during lecture or in office hours.

The main problems with 361, cheating and low lecture attendance, are not Orr's fault and cause many students to perform poorly.

There is no doubt that this class is difficult, but Orr's lectures are clear and informative. The tests are similar to practice exams and the weekly participation quizzes. Orr also curved the midterm exam (which professors in the past have not done). The labs can be difficult ant time consuming, but they come with an automatic 2 day extension.

Barely teaches. You could learn more by just going online and learning about GDB and C. All the stuff is CMU 213 anyway. Lectures are lifeless. Monotone. TAs basically don't care about the course. You can get good grades on the first three assignments, but you WILL bomb the test and you WILL bomb the next two labs. Don't take if you care about GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think Orr gets a lot of flack for teaching classes that are broken to begin with. 361 is hard, but Orr teaches it fine. He gave us more extra credit + curved exams than past profs. He does want students to succeed, and is always willing to explain anything ppl are confused by on piazza or after class. Overall, nice guy and fine lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Orr has very little interaction with the class. All the videos (which are okay) are from a different professor. Orr's young and so he's easy to talk and communicate with if you reach out to him. If you want help I'm sure he'll provide it. He replies decently to piazza post. Allowed a cheat sheet on exams. Watch prep vids, read tb, and you'll be goo

I am not sure if it was the structure of the class or Orr himself, but 132 at washu is terrible. Very little real world application, all the material is on the online text, and the test are difficult since most of the test is material you never cover. Do not take this class if you do not have to. I think I saw Orr maybe twice the whole year
Better self-learn than going to lectrures. He's like a PowerPoint Reader.

He is eager to answer questions and cares about his students, but his lectures can be confusing and hard to follow. He makes mistakes while working through examples, and seemingly confuses himself trying to correct them. Pretty middle of the road as far as math profs go. Take Schaefer if you can!

I can't speak to Dr. Ouyang's higher-level math classes, but at least for Calc II I found him to be an engaging and great teacher. There were a few times that I couldn't follow him in class, but the course resources ensured that I understood the concepts eventually. That said, I'm excited that I'm taking Schaefer next semester for Calc III.
Dr. Ouyang is a very kind professor who is always willing to answer questions, including during lecture. Decent amount of work each week, but nothing unmanageable.
PROF CHUCKY GOAT-YANG! Ignore the haters, he prepares you well for the final if you pay attention.
He had great jokes and made sure to answer questions thoroughly. He was also great about highlighting material we needed to know on exams, and telling us what mistakes to steer clear of.

I was a bit nervous at the beginning of the semester, but Professor Ouyang exceeded my expectations! He's not perfect—he sometimes makes mistakes or says things too quietly—but he's good about giving clarifications when you ask questions. He's goofy and iconic, and I enjoyed his lectures.
I had Ouyang last spring for real analysis and I loved him. He is very good at explaining things and cares about his students. The class is hard but he makes sure you walk away with a good grade.

I feel like this professor gets a bad reputation despite not really deserving it. I think he did a wonderful job teaching calculus 2 and I hope that he continues to teach the subject. I believe that students shouldn't be too alarmed as the professor is doing much better teaching this subject.

Dr. Ouyang was a great professor for Calc II. His lectures were very clear and really helped me understand the material well (which is important because there's a lot of material). Dr. Ouyang made sure students knew what prior knowledge they needed to understand new material, and discussed common mistakes and how to avoid them. Would recommend!

He's a great calc II professor! Lectures can contain lots of content, so if you want to pass the class do your best to attend them regularly rather than watching recorded lectures. cracks a few jokes every once in a blue moon too :)

Professor Ouyang gets a bad rep, and it's easy to see why. If you don't understand the previously covered topics, you won't understand his lectures. He is a good professor who cares about his students in his own way. Only complaint is that he can be condescending if you ask a "bad question," and he tends to show too many examples of "don't do this"
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I feel like Ouyang does really deserve all the hate he gets from his rating. It might be from more difficult classes, but at least for Calc 2 he's really not that bad. The only bad thing I see in him is that he tends to explain unnecessary "wrong ways" to do things and also gets stuck for a few minutes when he makes a mistake or is trying to think.
Exam was not as hard as I expected. But he is a really bad lecturer. Do not take his class!

(4111 - Analysis) Ouyang was somehow more difficult than his reputation.

At first, I thought he genuinely did not care that our problem sets felt punitive rather than constructive, but I realized after the first exam that he just completely doesn't understand the level that his students are at.

*this rating is for math 4111 intro to analysis but that wasnt selectable. He isn't a bad lecturer, but he sets an incredibly high standard. Yes, this is a famously hard course, but the questions on his exams are very difficult and in high quantities for the given time frames. I never had time to check my work, I couldve spent 4hrs on his 2hr final

I'm actually taking the Math 4111 Introduction to Analysis with him. He clearly explained all the concepts and theorems with very interesting examples.The lectures are great. You can easily catch up without feeling bored. The homework are average difficulty with plenty of time to do. The exams are super easy with lot of extra credit. Easy A class.

This professor grades everything, including exam extremely strict and would deduce points for minor issues. He cannot explain contents clearly and attending lecture and understanding all assigned material is not sufficient for optimal grade.
Made the class unnecessarily difficult and wasn't very supportive

If you have the opportunity to take matrix algebra with another professor, do it. It's is not a hard subject, but he's a terrible teacher that makes the concepts seem unnecessarily hard. He's very condescending and talks down on students. Also, he doesn't keep his canvas updated so you don't know how you're doing in class until it's too late.

Perhaps the WORST teacher I've EVER had. Assumed students were already familiar with the course material and seemed offended when anyone asked for clarification during class. Exam problems were unlike any encountered before. Homeworks were rarely graded before the exams and no practice material was given. DO NOT TAKE.

This dude expected us to be experts at Matrix Algebra and would put questions we've never seen before on exams. I definitely learned a lot in this class, but my grade doesn't reflect it at all because of the difficulty of his tests. He doesn't give practice exams and doesn't grade homework before the exams. This was my lowest grade in a class ever.
I would not wish taking his class for credit on my worst enemy

In Ouyang's class, it was extremely frustrating that he didn't provide practice exams for midterms or the final, especially since they make up 75% of our grade. In addition, the exams had questions that were extremely different from the ones in our textbook. Taking Ouyang's class was very discouraging, I would not recommend 309 with him to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ouyang has been the most disappointing instructor I've encountered. He does not use Canvas, provides no practice exams or study guides, and ignores homework and any Piazza questions. This lack of effort and disregard for student success creates a frustrating and unproductive learning environment. Shame.

This guy is a complete joke. He needs to learn how to take criticism as a way to improve as a teacher instead of a personal attack on his character. Clearly his ego is too big to understand that his students could have benefited from more practice material leading up to exams. I ended up doing fine in the class, but as a professor he was just rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unbelievable. Tried to ask a clarifying question in lecture once, and he proceeded to essentially berate me to the class for not knowing something. The final exam was 9 questions and 2 of them felt related to anything we've done in class. Genuinely out to get you as a student and is flat out rude

DON'T TAKE! Lectures were confusing and always felt like he was rushing to get through material. Very exam heavy yet he refused to provide practice exams/study guides and the questions on exams were nothing like homework or in-class problems. He's arrogant and would rather blame poor performance on his students than reconsider his teaching methods.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ouyang explains matrix the way someone might explain nuclear physics to a rock - assuming it already knows everything and just forgot for a moment. His teaching style is like trying to read a book written in invisible ink while it's being hurled at your face. Questions on exam make sense only if you exist in a universe where 2 + 2 equals pain.

Charles Ouyang is by far the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. He does not care about his students one little bit and is outright disrespectful. On top of that, he is a horrible grader and refuses to give any sort of reasonable partial credit. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.

Although the content in Matrix itself is not extremely difficult to grasp, Professor Ouyang does an extremely poor job at preparing and assessing students fairly in this class. When met with constructive criticism from an alarming majority of students, he instead placed the blame on us for being "unprepared" rather than changing his methods.

I think Prof. Ouyang is a good lecturer. The way he explains the concepts seems very clear to me. That being said he doesn't want to be running the class. He seems like he thinks he going against the students and provides little resources before exams. I think he would be better of in a smaller class with students who are math majors

Math 309: Imagine you've never had a brownie. Lectures are like a brownie recipe---lists of theorems and definitions. Tests ask you: How does the brownie taste? But you never even baked the brownie. Matrix is highly geometric and Ouyang's lectures failed to connect theorems/definitions to their geometric meanings, making it difficult to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is half the reason I'm transferring out. He's all over the place and doesn't have the written homework graded before exams, but still expects students to be able to know how to do the work correctly. The lack of feedback combined with his poor lecturing ability makes this class exponentially more difficult than it should be.

Do not take 309 with Ouyang. The exams are weighted so much. There are no practice exams or feedback on homework before exams. He does not know how to teach or engage with students. When students try to give feedback on his teaching, he gets defensive and just blames the students for not knowing the material and implies it is our fault.

Ouyang's 309 class is very test heavy. His tests are made up of 5 questions, each question worth 20% of the entire grade, yet make some questions unreasonably hard. He provides no practice exams and asks students to study test based on homework and textbook questions. However, the graders for the homework couldn't provide useful feedback on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am speechless. I took Linear Algebra with him, where he showcased his inability to integrate material and answer questions. He loves to hear himself talk, not teach. In Matrix Algebra onNov, 12 2024, Dr. Ouyang ranted for over a half hour about the students' inabilities to "do math", stressing his lectures/lecture style was not the problem. AVOID

Prof. Ouyang had no practice tests for any exams in a class where 65% of your grade is an exam. He said to study with homework Qs but included questions that aren't like HW. There are no drops on exams and no late submissions on homework. The exams are 4-5 questions long but weigh so heavily on your grade. I don't recommend this teacher for matrix.

Tough grader for the first half of the semester. Then found out nobody was getting an A. The second and third exams were easier and the final grades were fair.

Lectures were easy to follow, and he would repeat/clarify ideas if asked.
Professor Ouyang organized his lectures very nicely.

He certainly has room for improvement as a newly hired AP, and he is quite strict about the completeness of proofs, but this class was really not that bad. He offered a lot of EC to make up for the low midterm avgs and never tested on the hardest concepts. I only got ~70 on the first midterm but really improved over the semester and got an A+.
Worst professor I have had at WashU. He gives absolutely no partial credit and he rarely answers questions on Piazza. His announcements are rude and his grading is horrendous. Avoid him at all costs.
I believe this class can be fully remote.

She genuinely wants to make her lectures engaging, but she doesn't seem to know how. She filled the course with numerous guest lectures, teaching only a small portion herself — even the TA had to deliver one of the guest lectures. The homework assignments feel meaningless and disconnected. Many of the lecture topics are at a high-school level.

She sounds like a kind person, but the class lacks engineering principles on the medical device that we're supposed to design and the physiology. Pure concept cram. Her class is homework heavy, with 3 homework sets due in the same week with no heads up for a grad level class. A bunch of guest lecture that leads to nowhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. O'Brien is a nice professor, but O'Brien only delivers high school level stats and that is half of the course. The rest of the course is pure biology without any engineering principles, which violates the core of the course. There are no quantitative materials about the reproductive system, nor biotech that utilizes quantitative approaches.

She is a joke. Literally knows nothing about probability/statistics, which is half the content she teaches. Studied very hard for her final exam and she dumbed it down so much that all of my studying was unnecessary. Also, her content really isn't taught from an engineering perspective; it's just a bunch of biology information with no point.

A really nice lady and a good teacher however in my year was very over zealous with the amount of work assigned. Too many questions on hw and exams. Lab reports have very little guidance. However, it was her first year teaching and she seems really exciting and willing to get better. Over not that terrible either.

She's everything they say but worse. I'm surprised no one is talking about her ridiculous lab reports that provides no information on how to do them. She even gives out advice sheets that still doesn't even work. I find the most ridiculous part to be that the student's final presentations were tested, meaning we were doing the teaching for her.

Professor O'Brien has organized lectures, but the lecture contents are intensive. There are also too many questions in each homework, making me overwhelmed. I hope the homework can be less intensive but can guide students to a deeper understanding of the course materials.

Dr. O'Brien is nice passionate about her material, and puts a lot of effort. But there is just way too much stuff to memorize and review. I have had mental breakdowns due to the overwhelming amount of workload and material that I have to review for. I hope she'll understand there's too much content and will change, because she seems really nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her classes weren't hard, but were extremely tedious. She overcompensates her first semester of teaching this course by stuffing Stats and Physiology together, to which she did poorly in explaining either. Her lectures are tedious and uninteresting. She has unrealistic expectations of workload and seems to forget students are taking other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I did feel like I leaned a lot with the professor overall. Sometimes they go off track and use real world inappropriate examples but it is part of life. He tells a lot of his real world stories that help you understand what position you might be in, in the future. He does call on you unexpected so be prepared. The last test is straightforward.

I took ACCT 4640 (Audit). He changed the course from prior years, assigning more detailed and time-consuming homework. The work wasn't hard, just a big time commitment. Very old-school: no laptops, nametags, and frequent cold-calling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Got into a heated argument with a student that left the class very uncomfortable. He had a hard time reading the room, wanting us to talk about dicey political topics in an accounting class? Focused so much on "real world stuff," but I'm walking away from this class with distain for cost accounting. Wish this class wasn't required. It was painful.

The least inspirational core BSBA class imo. I understand that cost management is important, but this content was way further in depth than what a non-accountant needs to know. Homework and quizzes are based on the textbook, but he only cares about ~30% of that info, so it's a waste of time. Very boring, often incoherent lectures. Take Jennings.
get ready to teach yourself everything because he sure doesn't. class is just examples.

I took this virtually over the summer, and had a great time. Prof. Palmer was helpful and available for questions. The written questions were basically a P-set with a week to finish. The short answers were on a live, timed, in class session. Also not too bad, a lot easier than the mid-semester class.

Palmer's class was a really good experience in my opinion. Not too difficult and overall reasonable exams. The one thing to note is that the take-homes can take a long time, but they are not too hard to succeed on. If you pay attention in class and ask questions, you will get a good grade in the class.

Lectures were kind of boring and the take-home assignments were all pretty hard, but Palmer was open to answering questions and I thought the TAs were nice. If you read the textbook and understand quiz questions, you'll likely do well in the course.

Solid professor with lots of accounting experience. Grading is fair, and if you are willing to put the work in, you can get at least an A- in my opinion. Exams aren't difficult but again, you need to study and take enough time to complete the take-home portion. He is understanding a nice guy to talk to also, I think other reviews are too harsh.

Great professor and great guy. Lectures are slightly monotone but this is accounting, what do you expect? Always accessible out of class and responds to emails. Clearly wants his students to succeed. Tests are easier than the review that he gives. Grading depends on the TA you get. Projects are tough and one TA may give you an A while the other a B
Honestly just a really nice guy and fair grader. Accounting is inherently a mundane subject but his classes are definitely more interesting than I expected. Great Professor!
Great Teacher, super caring but the course material is boring and requires a good amount of reading. If you are ready to put in the effort you should be able to get an A

I honestly learned more by looking at the slides from the textbook then from his lecture. The grading system is weird and makes it hard to tell where you are in the class. Also, assignments are graded very harshly so be careful for flow through errors. He is a fine teacher but I am not a big fan of the way the class is tought.

The course is heavily reliant on the textbook, and his teaching is okay, but a little too problem-focused in my opinion. He also gives two-part test. One part is a written take-home test you work on with a group, while the other part is a multiple-choice in-class test. Both are not too difficult, but again, heavily textbook-reliant.
Nice guy but not a good professor. Lack of clarity leads to self-teaching through textbook

Accounting with prof. Palmer has been a good experience overall. Class is definitely a lot more rigorous than other sections, but it is very manageable. He is charismatic and passionate about the subject, and although he often goes on tangents, I always felt that I had a handle on the material, even when I did not do the lengthy textbook readings.

He uses the textbook to teach and spends class trying to pick complicated problems because he expects you to have a basic foundation for accounting already. In reality, he is supposed to break down the information to a practical level so students can learn from him.
I personally really liked Prof Palmer, if you do the chapter readings before class and make an effort the class if definitely doable!

Supposed to be an introductory Accounting class but waste of the hardest class I have taken at WashU. He is a terrible lecturer and he makes everything so boring and hard to understand. Also gives an insane amount of hard quizzes and take home test and finals. The amount of stress this class caused me is beyond measurable. Don't take !!!
Enjoyed the class. He liked to give advice in real world accounting which I enjoyed. Learned most of the real content in the homeworks online. Only a few paid attention in class.

Palmer's lectures don't help me learn. Last class, he passed out a packet of problems and didn't even go over a single one, but instead lectured about accounting-related stories and was unclear about the points he was making. Class is mandatory and his grading criteria seem clear on paper, but there have been many regrade requests, etc so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Palmer doesn't teach during his lectures. Rather, he either does unnecessary practice problems or tells stories about his life. Because of this, students are forced to self-teach from the textbook. Homework takes multiple hours per week, there are bi-weekly quizzes, and exams are incredibly long. Take another professor for this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awesome professor!

The sweetest professor with a clear love for what she teaches. Essays are graded fairly and with positive feedback as well as criticism. Incredibly understanding about circumstances outside of class, and I genuinely enjoyed coming to class each day. Highly recommend both her as a professor and her early texts and contexts class.

I cannot recommend Dr. Pawl enough. She is one of the best professors I've had at WashU - extremely knowledgeable, very accessible outside of class, and it is clear she cares about all of her individual students. Our class discussions were always very interesting and I genuinely looked forward to going to her class each week. Take a class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at WashU. She is so caring, funny, and kind - I genuinely looked forward to class. Generally has high expectations on papers, but as long as you meet with her and discuss your thesis and ideas, you should do well.
The absolute greatest professor I've had in the English department. Jane Austen is a fantastic class alone, but I would absolutely recommend taking any class you can with Dr. Pawl!

Absolutely love Dr. Pawl. She is the sweetest prof I've had at WashU, she genuinely cares and is incredibly knowledgeable about the material, and I cannot wait to take more classes with her in the future!

She is one of the best professors I have had at WashU and I would recommend her class to anyone. She is clearly very passionate about her work and her students and takes time to get to know each student individually. I was scared about taking a writing intensive, but she was very helpful and made it easy for me to excel. I couldn't say one negative

Not only is the class easy and interesting, Dr. Pawl is the kindest woman I have ever met. She genuinely cares so much about her students. Definitely recommend going to office hours to get clear advice on how to proceed and get a good grade, but also to get to know her. Truly an amazing professor, everyone at WashU should take her class!

Dr. Pawl was amazing! The reading assignments are manageable and class is entirely discussion-based, but she moves through topics very well and makes English Literature really enjoyable, even if you aren't necessarily interested in all of the texts. Her feedback on papers is extremely thorough. Even if you're not an English major, take her class

austen class ! was really incredible. she has so much excitement and interest for the subject and for students' opinions and she is, for the jane austen class at least, so So knowledgeable not just about the novels and the author but also about the time period and the literary/social/etc context in which the novels were written... 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor. Super interesting and responsive to students. Loved her Jane Austen class. She makes college reading fun. The class is definitely a ton of work, but I highly recommend it. Also, she's a fair grader.

She reacts both positively and negatively to papers, which is a welcome change.  She is understanding and approachable.  She makes the class challenging without making it excruciating.  She leads the class in thought-provoking discussions and keeps class lively and engaging.
hot hot hot hot hot Jane Austen hot hot hot
Fun class - makes boring parts of writing interesting. Her comments on papers are very thoughtful, but her grading is a little tough.

One of my favorite classes ever, very engaging and fun.  Discussions were great, the whole class was really involved.  Comments on papers were very helpful, thoughtful, and thorough.  At the end of each class and the end of the semester, I've wished it could go on longer.

Fabulous class, professor knows what she's doing when it comes to teaching a class where 90% of the students have read at least two of the books on the reading list.  Kept us going and led some absolutely fantastic class discussions.
No Comments
makes writing fun again
I find Amy Pawl appealing, but her appeal's a little appalling.
Very friendly and interesting.  She was approachable and was always willing to help with paper topics and continue class discussions.
I love Stephanie Pippen. She is so nice and one of the best professors ever and she really cares about her students and I recommend everyone take her class cause she's so cute.
Best professor at WashU.
This is probably the best writing intensive class to take at WashU

If you are looking for a writing intensive that isn't very difficult but is also really fun and interesting take writing the natural world with Pippin. She is super helpful while you are working on your essay and you can go to her for help all the time. There is also a small amount of reading for each class and only 3 papers the entire class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE PIPPIN! She is hilarious and makes class enjoyable. This was (very unexpectedly) one of my favorite classes at Wash U. If you have to take exposition, take it with Pippin! It's a very easy class, and she usually lets you out early. I highly recommend this class
A great professor who is able to make Writing 1 a fun class. Expectations for assignments were sometimes unclear, but that was more the fault of the course structure/prompts than of her.

She makes class very entertaining! She's a great teacher who tries to keep things interesting, but is a bit too caught up in the vagueness of the texbook and unclear about what she wants.  Not really her fault though - the assignments are vague to start off with.
Ms. Pippin runs a very pleasant class - interesting discussions and funny stories.  She encourages experimenting with your writing, and doesn't seem particularly tough on the grading.

i had a great experience in her class. cares very much about the student. she is very understanding and laid back. her class has a very relaxed atmosphere. she seemed a bit strange at first but i learned to love her goofy attitude which became incredibly addicting. easy grader. very nice person overall.

I love Stephanie.  One of the nicest professors I have encountered.  Very understanding and cares for students.  Not a difficult grader and not overwhelming with assignments.  She understands that her class is not the only one a student is currently taking.  Very willing to meet one on one and I strongly suggest it as she is great to get to know.

She makes the ecomp curriculum so much less nauseating. She's very lenient on the assignments in terms of when you turn them in and what you need to do on them compared to other ecomp classes. She is also very nice and concerned about the well-being of her students outside of class. If you're having a bad day, she'll notice and ask about it.

I hate the class, but this is by no means Stephanie's fault.  She makes a horrible class slightly more bearable, and she's fun.  She seems a lot more qualifed than a lot of the other ecomp teachers I've heard about.
Very nice and supportive of writers just beginning to find their voice.  Approachable with a great sense of humor.

Real nice and helpful.  She always tried to look out for us, often understanding the stupidity of many of the ecomp assignments and changing them accordingly.  Her ecomp class is 10x better and more interesting than most others for sure.

Super chill!!  Class was overall easy, but I think it had potential to be more interesting given the subject matter. Exams were mostly just memorization, and many people did not attend class. He offered EC assignments and was a very generous grader. I'd recommend taking if you are interested in forensic anthro or want a light class.

Prang did a great job of keeping the class interesting and engaging, as well as explaining complicated information in a really easy-to-understand way. A bit difficult to access outside of class. There was a lot of material to learn, but the tests were mostly on big-picture/most important material.
Great professor! He makes his grading very clear so you are aware what is expected of you. Yes, the class is a lot but he makes it fun and doesn't look at you stupid if you ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you love Professor David Strait, you'll definitely love this guy! Lots of memorization, but if you give yourself a few days to study you'll pass. Had 2 exams and 2 short papers, but honestly the workload is very manageable. He's also very understanding of mental health issues which I appreciated.

Dr. EA is very kind and passionate, but her communication with the TAs was poor, which made the class more difficult than it needed to be. Whenever I asked a question to a TA, they never had a clue as to what was going on. She did go through some difficult personal experiences this semester, so I would hope the future would be better.

Intro to public health is a lecture-heavy course, and there's a moderate amount of readings to do. Dr. Quinn is a nice and caring professor, but is a bit disorganized with lectures and assignments at times. Nonetheless, this class was a great intro class, and she had many fun stories to tell.

If you like her class depends A LOT on the attitude you go in with. She annoyed me early on b/c she is all over the place but I grew to love her chaos and view it as pure passion and love for her work. She has such fun anecdotes and cares so much! She's also very understanding of personal circumstances and is willing to be flexible. ABSOLUTE QUEEN!

Prof Quinn is so passionate about public health. The public health 1000 class is lecture heavy but prof quinn tells such interesting stories and anecdotes that really explain the importance of public health. I would take her class again and wish all my public health teachers were as passionate as her. Smart, respected, bad-a

She's very knowledgeable and passionate about material. The courseload I think was very reasonable: 3 exams, 2 papers, 1 project. My 1 complaint is that the exams were kinda hard to study for (some were easy, others hard), some included random details/stats. But there are usually some freebies (helps boost your grade).

EA Quinn is definitely quirky. Her lectures are all over the place and can be a little dull at times. Outside of class she is a little more helpful. I would say the exams for Foundations in Public Health are not great and I unfortunately did not learn anything from the lectures, making studying a nightmare. I would not recommend this class.

Am expecting to receive an A once class is done. Dr. Quinn is very knowledgeable and incredibly enthusiastic about the subjects of this course. There is no busy work in this class; only three exams, 1 two-part paper and another final paper. Exams are fair. Very chill and flexible overall; am really enjoying this class a lot! Highly recommend!

Cntd: Her video also made fun of students using disability services, and she tried to compare herself to another professors stating that its sexist she isn't recognized as much as him. She will just have a lecture, never finish the material she is supposed to cover in class, and then say oops my bad.
This was so easy. Do the 10 half page papers early on in the semester then you can relax. Basically include your notes from the guests and maybe a couple sentences on what interested you.
She's definitely quirky and some of the exam questions are confusing but the class is interesting and she gives you a lot of opportunities to get points. Take lots of notes on everything she says!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I have taken 3 courses with Dr. Quinn-Human Growth and Development, Obesity and Nutrition, and Darwin and Doctors. She is great and really cares about her students. Plus, she takes the time to relate course material to current events (she's always up to date on current research), and takes ample amounts of time to answer any questions.

Quinn had good intentions, but she was quite unclear and hard to follow in class. Lots of information that was overwhelming at times, but super interesting! Get ready for the time of your life: placentas, high fructose corn syrup, germs (you can never have too many), and TB...
Some of his test questions didn't really reflect understanding and emphasized rote memorization. Other than that, he showed good command of the material and was a decent lecturer
His recorded lectures were very confusing. He was extremely monotone but I could tell that he was trying his best. Overall, he isn't the greatest, but the class is easy enough to do well in.

You can tell it's his first time teaching the course. Maybe he's just nervous but he has a poor command of the classroom. The pre-class lecture videos aren't really helpful and are pretty bleak. However, he's super sweet as a person and very passionate about evolution.
Very nice and caring. She ensures you learn without imposing loads of homework on you. Her grading is generous, but it is not a blow off class. If you try you will succeed. Nicest professor I've had.

Qin laoshi was super nice, understanding, flexible. She really focused on in-class participation, making class chill and fun to be at. There were 2-3 quizzes/test a week that were cumulative of vocabulary but weren't too bad + generous grading for lvl1. Class requires a lot of work/prep if no prior experience. Would take her lvl2 class if I could!

Qin Lash is the best teacher, and everyone will say so! She is making sure you are participating, and I cannot wait to take her course next semester, She also loves to join us in our awesome laughing sessions, and it's fun! You will learn the most Chinese you will ever learn in this course, and I highly recommend it to anyone excited about Chinese
Qin Laoshi is a fantastic professor at WashU. If you put in the effort, you will get an A, but outside of that, she really cares about the students and genuinely wants you to succeed.

Qin Laoshi is amazing!! So nice and caring. Class is rigorous, but if you do what you're asked, you'll come away with a great knowledge of Chinese. Very reasonable expectations and wants to help you succeed, but there's homework EVERY night. Classtime is very engaging and participative.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Qin laoshi is amazing!! Absolutely love this class. The class is rigorous, there is quite a bit of homework (something due every day), and you have to participate all the time. However, this has all only helped me learn so much Chinese. Definitely take this class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Another great class from the Chinese department. Qin laoshi is funny, entertaining, understanding, and engaging. I definitely continued to expand on my Chinese after taking Chinese 1. There is even more vocabulary than in Chinese I, but if you took Chinese I at WashU then you know what to expect. I sometimes felt the class moved too fast, however.
English is not professor Chang's native language, but he did great job to handle with the English teaching. He was a very nice person to help students on any questions.

He is a wonderful and knowledgeable teacher. He always concerns about our grade and encouraged us to study hard and get a better grade. In his teaching, he often used examples from western cultures to explain the Asian art issues.

He is a wonderful and knowledgeable teacher. He is very nice to give us 4 exams and drops the lowest one. He always concerns about our grade and encouraged us to study hard and get a better grade. In his teaching, he often used examples from western cultures to explain the Asian art issues.
very organized class, and wonderful professor.
Each class was very organized and I believe that I have learned a lot about the Asian history, culture and art, this is one of the best professor that I have had at the university.
Professor Qing, is not a great professor!
Their is nothing positive to say! About Professor Qing!
Dottie is the goat. I love her. Take her class

Intro Macro: If you show up and pay attention you will get an easy A and learn a fair amount. If you don't show up or don't pay attention you will get an easy A and not learn much of anything. Most chose the latter.
super nice teacher and easy class!
Dottie's class is really interesting. She makes office hours very accessible. If you have a willingness to learn, you can get a lot out of this class.
Cannot believe I skip all lectures but still get an A+......Attend this class with friends bc there are great amount of group works.
Very passionate about what she does!!! If I had to take any Econ class, I would 100% take it with her
Professor Petersen makes macro engaging and accessible. With multiple extra credit options, the class is manageable. Utilize Unstuck ai and the textbook to supplement her straightforward lectures.

Great professor. Is always in a good mood and leads the discussions well. All materials were available on Canvas. Attendance did not matter whatsoever, the amount of extra credit she gives means you can skip all lectures and still earn a high A. Exams are all take home quizzes and are open book/notes. Very quick to respond to emails too.
If you want to get an easy A, take class with her!!!!

She is the best! So nice and so understanding. Very reasonable assignments and quizzes + group quizzes weren't too bad. She gave us tons of time to do the final project and split it up into manageable deliverables. Only complaint would be that the canvas was hard to navigate. Usually finding the homework was harder than actually doing it.
good
Really caring really nice. Just take her
She was very on top of things and had lecture recordings and slides all posted on canvas, which was very nice. She also was very funny and laid back during lectures.
Econ isn't my thing, but the class was super easy and professor petersen was really funny and definitely cared about her students.

Would highly recommend macro with Dottie, especially coming from someone that hasn't taken an econ class before. There are multiple opportunities for extra credit, and as long as you follow the general place of the class, its pretty easy. She is also super funny and makes lectures enjoyable.
If ur taking macro take it with dottie, shes the best. she made lectures v engaging and is very accessible outside the classroom too.
Make sure to have a good group for team quizzes and final project. Super easy class otherwise, would highly recommend even if you're not the most interested in economics.

I can't say I learned much from her lectures. Her resources posted on canvas were very helpful. She gives plenty of extra credit and is super nice. Just not a super interesting topic but does her best to keep the class engaged. A very easy class and I recommend anyone take because if you put in minimal effort you can get an A.

Skip the lectures, she says "no one gets an A without reading the textbook" but thats BS. Just learn from her slides and by googling stuff. The quizzes in 1021 carry your grade so dont throw that. You need a good group for the team quizzes and project. She gives loads of extra credit

Dottie is very passionate about economics and caring about her students. The individual quizzes are open note and untimed and the homework is graded on completion(and you don't even have to do all of it). As long as you end up with a good team for quizzes and the final project, you will do well in this class.

Very kind and caring professor. Lectures can be dry though and she tends to go on tangents about things that are pretty self-explanatory. Weekly homework assignments graded on completion. Individual and team quizzes all online. No final, just a big project/presentation on investing in other countries. Lots of opportunities for extra credit.
dottie is the GOAT. nice grading, fun lectures. you also learn alot. totally reccomend
Dottie is an incredible professor. This is my go-to class when recommending econ to non-econ people. Take it, you'll like it.

Can be very wordy in her lectures, but her excitement makes them manageable. She's lovable, while boring at times. Very short HW assignments that are only graded for completion. Don't need textbook. All you need are the slides from class which she posts. Find a good group of 4 for team quizzes. Final project is a non-issue if work is split up.

Very easy class and worth taking. Likable professor. EVERY assignment in this class is online and very do-able. You only need 60% of poll's answered for full attendance. The lecture's are OK but nothing spectacular. The final project isn't that bad even if only a few of the group of 8 are responsible.

A very kind professor who cares about her students despite teaching in a large lecture hall setting. Content can become tricky at times but if you try you'll generally receive a good grade. Lectures can seem long but you can tell that Dottie is passionate about what she does.
