Make sure you do take the time to study because the quizzes and exams can be tricky! All in all, a perfect french class.

Phenomenal professor who cares about his students. Always very patient, flexible on assignments, and genuinely wants you to succeed in his class. Course was almost too easy but I still felt like I learned (or at least solidly reviewed) a lot of material. Highly recommend taking his classes if you can!

Probably one of Washu U's best language teachers.  He was nice, helpful, and flexible almost to a fault.  The coursework was generally easy, but the class still covered a huge amount of ground in one semester.  Magnifique!
Jouane is the reason I am still taking French classes. I was going to quit but his teaching was so great that now I can speak the language and love it

HE'S SO HOT. I'VE NEVER HAD A CRUSH ON A GREY-HAIRED MAN BEFORE. HE MAKES ME WANT TO EAT BAGUETS UNDER L'ARC DE TRIOMPHE ALL DAY. But really, I did learn a lot in his class. He's very approachable and friendly and learning how to speak french from a native french speaker is a great experience.

In general, I think a good professor is an honest one who cares about their students, helps them learn, and grow throughout the semester. Based on that criterion, VS excels. While grading can feel tough early on, the assignments are weighted towards the back half of the semester, so the ones that count are the ones you do the best on!
I took her course a few years ago and I still have nightmares about it. Tough grader and many passive aggressive comments. You will have to put in much more work than other college writing courses.

This class taught me the importance about checking RMP. I ignored the warnings on here about professor Slachman and that was a grave mistake. Although the themes of the class are somewhat interesting, professor slachman is a harsh grader and you will be forced to put in much more work than necessary for a mandatory, entry level writing class w her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I'm sure she has a deliberate teaching philosophy but being steered toward a topic based on my race rather than what I proposed was sure educational. And nothing motivates like reading a “model essay” aloud to the entire class and declaring it so impressive it earned a B+. She brings in her dog for the finals week though.

Ending up in her class taught me the importance of checking RMP. Unclear rubrics and a harsh grader. If you want a decent grade get ready to put in 120% effort. This course singlehandedly took more time than all my other courses combined. Sometimes gives good feedback and definitely teaches you how to endure a difficult course and Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Thought I was done with this class for good, but last night I had a nightmare that I was somehow still stuck in it this semester. I woke up in a cold sweat and thought I'd been dragged back for a second round of her harsh grading. Not sure if my writing is improving, but these nightmares are definitely getting more solid—and well-structured.

Although I initially did not love Prof. Slachman, I got used to the flow and learned a lot about writing. The class was pretty fast-paced, but in the end, it all made the final paper less stressful as she gave lots of time for the research assignment. Classes were sometimes awkward, but above all, I learned a lot.

I would not recommend this professor to anyone. Assignments had no rubrics or guidelines, Professor Slachman's feedback was unclear, and her comments in class often made me feel disrespected and uncomfortable. Use the writing center it will make a big difference if you want to boost your grade. Switch out before it's too late.
you are cooked

Well well well. After a semester with Professor Slachman I can say that my writing improved. I found her feedback to be helpful but oftentimes it felt as if I had to reach out to her outside of class to know what she wanted from an assignment. NO RUBRICS UNCLEAR EXAMPLES. Overall it's possible to succeed but it requires work and won't be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: After 4 months of passive aggressive comments on my essays, 3 mental breakdowns, insanely harsh grading, and the inability to use the bathroom during class, my suffering is finally over. Please for the love of God switch out of this class by any means possible.

Slachman's grading criteria are as clear as a foggy day in London. Honestly, if confusion were a class, she'd be the valedictorian! Claiming to be an "expert" in academic writing after a ten-year hiatus is like calling yourself a chef because you once microwaved a burrito.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The only cwp professor that one should try to avoid at any cost. And for the sake of God, we know that you have forged good comments about yourself, Dr. Slachman.

Professor Slachman is a harsh lecturer who, from her high horse, spews out endless but useless advice and examples. Her attempts at humor often feel more like attacks, leaving us uncomfortable and drained. Her academic explanations are ineffective, and I frequently feel on the verge of a mental breakdown in her class.
This class will improve your writing but there's a good chance it'll come at the cost of your GPA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Would not be surprised if professor Slachman wrote the previous rating for herself. I can speak from a full semester that her class is brutal. It's capped at 12 students as all CWP classes are, but we ended the year with 6 total. She likes to call out students and interrupt the flow of her lectures for trivial reasons like someone looking tired.

Of all the classes I have ever taken, Dr. Slachman's by far caused the greatest increase in the quality of my writing. She isn't a tough grader; she just actually cares about teaching you how to write. Talk to her. She's very friendly and willing to help. Because of her, professors consistently tell me I'm one of the best writers they've taught.

Do not take a class with Slachman. She has a condescending tone with students and constantly puts them down during class both individually and as a whole. She is the most brutal CW teacher while other classes are an easy A. She provides no constructive feedback and is an incredibly harsh grader. Her canvas page is unorganized and she is a bully.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Slachman reifies the "Nightmare" aspect of the Dreams and Nightmares class. This professor structured each lesson with a contrived goal in mind, and remained disorganized throughout the semester. The course is meant to be understandable by all, yet she sets unrealistic expectations for her students and shames students who do not meet her standards.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Definitely my hardest class first semester, but looking back, it was exactly what I needed to whip me into shape for college. Bring your papers to her outside of class and visit the Writing Center frequently before you turn them in for a grade. This class is what you make of it - I'm proud of the writing I did in here - but be prepared to work.
She doesn't let her students drink, eat, use technology, or even smile! STG
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: It's funny this woman only ever teaches one class. I feel she should stop at this point. Her grading is definitely tough but it all boils down to if your writing is specific enough for her. Doesn't like giving As, and makes students very stressed which is ridiculous for a freshman course. Her course evals don't lie. They're all the same every year.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Slachman was by far the worst professor I have had. She is overly critical and not in any way constructive when she gives work back. She creates an overly intimidating working environment where the student's voices are not heard, and it is either her way or the highway. Single handedly ruined my freshman year GPA. DONT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I've had bad teachers before but she is the worst of the worst. First off, no matter how good an essay is, she will still find a way to tear it apart and make you fail. She does not want her students to succeed and she overloads them with work and makes them feel like their voices aren't important. I would NEVER recommend this course to anyone.

I got a decent grade, but it was pure luck. You have to be EXCEPTIONALLY specific with how connect ideas and argue how they're "important to culture." She's sweet, but as someone else said, she can be very rude and condescending. Flexible-ish with deadlines, unreasonable grader. If you're stuck in the class, you'll survive, but try to get out.

I would not recommend this class whatsoever. This professor incredibly intimidating and she makes no effort to make you feel like your voice holds any worth in her class. If you want to have your freshman college writing course be what endangers your GPA, sign right up. If you're reading this hopefully you still have time to drop or switch profs.

Basically, Slachman was actually the bane of my existence throughout my freshman year. This class is supposed to be an introduction to writing and should be very easy since every freshman has to take it. However, Slachman will make your freshman year a living nightmare. She grades harshly and has no remorse for any regrades. You will not get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not an experience I'd want to go through again. She spends a large portion of each lecture individually calling out students and usually picking on them for something minor. Her instructions and feedback are usually vague and ineffective, and she gets upset when a student does not understand what she wants out of them for an assignment. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If I'm really, really trying to be devil's advocate, it seems like she cares about improving your writing skills. However, this class has been one of my worst experiences for multiple reasons. She's an impossible grader, condescending, calls you out in class, extremely vague w/ instructions, and drains the life out of you. Run for the hills.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She means well but can come across as rude and condescending. She likes people who participate and are engaged in her class- make sure to complete all readings and assignments because she will call on you during discussions. She's a tough grader on essays and does not explain the assignments or her expectations very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Professor Slachman last semester and I wasn't sure about her at first but I couldn't switch out (tried) and I actually ended up loving her class. It was hard but like in a good way. I learned a lot and she really helped me with my writing. The theme was interesting and I didn't mind the reading. Spoiler alert: Frankenstein isn't the monster.

She is hands down the toughest grader for College Writing. Her feedback is more critical than constructive and she will outright make fun of students if she doesn't like their answers. Take the class with anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I wish never to meet her again. Give pretty low grades for almost all the papers
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Chill and sneaky hilarious. Gave us all the questions for the midterm and final beforehand and recorded and posted every single lecture. Nice guy. Not the best lecturer.

This class has no exams and just a final project which makes it conducive to learning, which is awesome. However, the content is extremely difficult and hard to understand. Additionally, the homework sets will take around 10-15 hours to complete.
Such boring, unhelpful lectures. Lectures didn't relate to homework. Nothing seemed to connect. Nice guy. Grade is all homework and final project, no final exam.

Perhaps it's the pace of the course, perhaps it's the lack of test review material, perhaps he may be better teaching upper-level math, but I genuinely found no benefit in having Wickerhauser as a professor, and certainly many problems. Complete self-study of a class, and I still feel like I learned nothing. Avoid this professor, please.

Content was not fundamentally too difficult, but lectures were inconsistent in clarity and very proof-based which made prep for exams and doing any problem-solving very difficult. Pretty much everyone had to study off the textbook-which is also not great. That being said exams were mostly fair, but the lack of practice materials was prevalent.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Some days he explains the concepts well and everything makes sense, whereas other days he gets lost in his lecture notes and nothing makes sense. Reading the textbook is the way to go for his class. Exams aren't too bad, but trying to learn the content is rough
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid Wickerhauser for DiffEq. He's smart but struggles to teach clearly—lectures are proof-heavy with incomplete examples, leading most to stop attending. Exams (80% of your grade) reuse worksheet problems, are graded harshly, and lack past examples. Recitations help; lectures and office hours don't. Be ready to self-study, ask people who took it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: too genius for differential equations . Only for 400 level or graduate level classes .

Made this class as hard as it possibly can be. For an engineering major just trying to progress in math he wanted to teach it like we're math majors while a good portion of us are not. If you want to get a decent grade and actually understand what you are doing take this class in the fall or with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a great professor.  The class itself of 217 is really interesting with a clear division between the conceptual side of things and the problem-solving side of things. Wickerhauser focuses far too much on the conceptual side, however, gets lost in his own explanations. If you plan to take the class, self-studying is the only way to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You might enter into four stages of doubt. First, you might doubt whether lecture is helpful cuz you don't know how to do homework. Then, you might not quite understand the textbook. Next, you might go back to lecture and find out understanding does not help you memorize. Finally, you don't know what you are studying cuz you go back to memorizing.

Lectures are interesting and inspirational because he aims to explain things thoroughly. However, examples are often given at the last five minutes or not at all. If you happen to be as dumb as me, with his lectures understood, you might have no idea how to do the Webwork or worksheet. You have to read text book and search for past exams.

You might think you registered for a differential equations class, but you're actually learning applied real analysis. Most exam questions are proofs and way too difficult if you're not an actual math prodigy. As someone who has taken advanced real analysis classes, I can say he's too smart to be teaching differential equations.

Wickerhauser tried his best, but his exams were simply too hard. I am glad he made me work harder because I learned more I guess. I believe he is a nice guy, but maybe just too smart for differential equations. Definitely a step up from calc 3 last semester. No practice tests and not very accessible as well. Math help room could only help so much.

Study-hards need to bend over to get an A  in. I attended all lectures and tried to interpret what he said. I took down notes in different colors, trying to capture the important formulas/concepts. That's how I got above 90 first three exams. But in final I see no respect for the study hards. Smart people wins, dumb people like me are eliminated.

If you ever thinking about taking diff q under his name. I hereby sincerely warn you. RUN. RUN AS FAST AS YOU CAN, run as you are in a 40 yard dash in the NFL scouting combine. 
Grade base on the tests. No previous test given + questions changes from last year. Messy hand-writing, impossible to learn from class. Basically TA teach everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very large disconnect between what is taught in class and what is covered in homework/exams. This is further amplified by no access to practice exams or review sessions of any kind
He's evil i can't do it with him
Let me put it simply: Avoid Professor Wickerhauser.

Class is just proofs with all exercises ‘being left as an exercise' for the class. Occasionally gets confused by what he writes on the board. Textbook is helpful, find upperclassmen who can give you their old exams (often similar to the real test).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor I have had, Lectures have 200 seats and are attended by 30 students. Doesn't ever clearly identify what we are covering or what is on the exam, if he does identify what is on the exam it is usually incomplete list
will get mad if you mispronounce homogeneous it is hOmo-gE-nEous. Tests are not horrible, but going over the recitation worksheets is very helpful.

His lectures are hard to follow and he rarely gives any examples during class making the homework much harder and more time consuming. There are no extra practice problems given to help with test studying. If you go to office hours, he is pretty responsive and helpful, but asking questions during lecture is hit or miss.

I took Dr. Wickerhauser for Biostats and it was one of the best classes I've taken at WashU. He gives clear explanations and if you don't want to show up there's a zoom/zoom recording. Homework isn't that bad, it's just weekly. Take-home exams and a final project that you can work on with a partner.

The other reviews are spot on: he gets lost in his own lecture notes, sometimes leaves problems unsolved on the board, and massively underprepares you for the exams. That said, if you: 1) can self-study, and 2) can do the Webwork by yourself, the class is not that bad at all.

Prof. Wickerhauser's lectures are full of challenges but very enjoyable. His way of teaching without slides let us focus on mathematics itself. Also, Prof. WIckerhauser is super helpful after class to answer students' questions.

No lecture slides, bad handwriting. Often gets lost and checks his notes, then leaves it as an investigation for us to figure out. Provides good past exams and there is great overlap, which is a plus. Hope you are able to self teach from textbooks!

Lecture is great if you genuinely are interested in math, but it never applies to the exams. I had to stop going because he would stop during lecture just to look at the textbook, and it felt like I had to guess to even know what I was supposed to learn. Disorganized, the homework changes the day before, and there are not enough problems.

Professor Wickerhauser is not for everybody. He teaches with a very high level of understanding, and his lectures are very proof-based. That said, he actually makes the material interesting from a math perspective. His teaching is complex, but it makes sense. I would only recommend taking his course if you have an actual interest in mathematics.

Great professor! He is willing to help out students struggling from the work (I really do recommend the students to go to his office hour. He explains it so well and kindly). He is considerate. The class itself was also interesting. The workload was average, and the difficulty was also average. Well-structured and organized class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Wickerhauser is great. He definitely emphasizes proofs in his lectures, but I really appreciate that, especially in an upper division class. The quizzes aren't very hard, and the exams are challenging but fair. I will definitely take more classes with him. He's great.
Professor Wickerhauser is a great teacher. Teaches mainly through proofs or supplementing readings. Difficult but fulfilling homework.

Evidently his 100-level classes are taught at an inappropriate level, but he was great (and very reasonable) in 322 as well as some guest lectures he did in 400 levels I took.  He taught some of the more complex ideas behind the actual statistical applications, but tested mainly on applications and strictly what what was covered in class

Professor Wickerhauser is a very smart man who is not very good at explaining basic concepts in calculus. His lectures are entirely proof-based and his exams did not look like anything we saw in class or in the homework. The lectures were not helpful, and they did not translate into the homework problems. Only way to succeed is to teach yourself.

Wickerhauser teaches in a very proof style that takes some time getting used to and the test means are very low (expect 50's). However, all the below reviews were prior to his curve adjustment. Originally the cut off for A- was a solid 90. However, he ended up adjusting it so that a 75 would give you an A-. Most people ended up pretty satisfied.

I don't want to be misleading so let me say this straight off the bat: I would rather amputate one of my big toes with a butter knife, then sew it back on using a crude, un-sanitized, rusty sewing needle, all without any form of anesthetic, as opposed to taking this class ever again.

Prof. Wickerhauser is an incredibly smart man who is too smart to teach introduction classes such as Calculus II. He cannot dumb himself down enough to communicate to students without a strong background in math, mostly taking this course as a prerequisite. The tests were impossible  and left little room for error. No calculator or formula sheet.
prbly a better professor for higher level math, but for calc 2 he makes everything overcomplicated. the means on the exams are VERY low, the questions are hard, and he barely even adjusts the curve

Hasn't done a great job for calc 2. Lectures are meant as a supplement. Expect to learn all the material on your own.  However his lectures are usually interesting enough if not interactive or relevant. Its refreshing to see a professor who treats students as capable and doesn't dumb it down. He'd be great for upper level courses. But calc 2? Nah.
Not at all recommended for calc 2.
I dropped this course and lots of other people did too. most don't even go to lecture anymore, its that bad
save your gpa, DO NOT take calc 2 with this guy

his tests are unreasonable and he barely curves. his lectures are longwinded, irrelevant, and unhelpful yet he still expects you to know the material and things beyond what's actually taught. not considerate of the students at all, nor does he reply to emails. worse than all the other premed classes i've taken. awful professor.
dont do it. horrible,at least for calc 2
Avoid at all costs.

went to class a handful of times. Sounds great with higher level math, but was absolutely horrible for Calc 2. the material isn't horrible,  he just dost teach in a coherent way. Most people stopped going pretty soon after the class started.

Prof. Wickerhauser clearly knows the material and explains difficult topics well. In his Biostats (322) class, he would often delve deep into the statistical reasoning behind analyses. The material he covered in lecture sometimes exceeded the level of the class, but he did not put these complex problems on tests--he's a reasonable and great prof!
Brilliant mathematician, and extremely interested, nice, and helpful professor.

Very elaborate lectures.  Derivates theorems that aren't really relevant to homework/tests.  Tests were much more difficult than homework and offered no explanation for this.  Nice guy, brilliant mathmetician, i'm sure, but a mediocre prof.
Avoid. She is too busy being nitpicky to actually teach you

I was a solid Spanish speaker before I came to her class but began to struggle with grammar. I would attend her office hours for extra help, and instead of actually helping me learn the Spanish language, she went on and on about how she couldn't give me detailed feedback because of the "integrity of the assignment" everyone else cheated on. AVOID!!

Gets on your nerves very quickly. She nitpicks every sentence you say for grammatical errors but almost in a judging kind of way. She takes forever to grade and her discussion questions are always weirdly worded. Again really easy, but her nitpicking makes me never want to take another class from her.

Braxs is a fine and fair professor, but not an especially engaging one. I imagine in a lower level spanish she would be a solid teacher of grammar and technique, but in an upper level class based on discussions and content, her contributions feel underwhelming. Almost all the classtime is spent in small groups discussing, not with her teaching.

The class is really easy and you just have to show up basically. The syllabus is clear about what you have to do. Sometime she kind of goes off of the syllabus but its not that big of a deal. The only problem was that she graded everything like 2 weeks after the semester was done which was a bit annoying but oh well.

I loved Braxs. She grades very fairly, she's organized, she's super engaging and she's got a great sense of humor. She also makes her expectations/what you need to know on exams very clear. Just make sure you participate!

Absolutely great Spanish professor -- extremely kind, always available during office hours, and good and explaining information. The class is definitely more difficult than I thought it would be and is fast paced, but if you study you can do well. Does take a bit to get back tests/compositions and such, but not ridiculously long.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was my first Spanish professor at WashU and she set the bar really high. The class wasn't incredible difficult but it also wasn't a joke. She made the class enjoyable and helped to increase understanding. Only downside is that she takes awhile to grade essays/test/etc...
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is a very difficult essay grader. Accordingly, she does not really teach class material very well in class which made the exams super hard since they are nit picky. Also she is very late to class all the time and not really helpful when trying to discuss graded material.

Professor always comes late to class. Never shows up on time and comes unprepared. She comes 10 minutes late to almost every single class or will sometimes come so late that she just cancels class. She even comes late to classes on exam days. Very unprepared, not an ideal teacher.

Ok, so she's a very easy teacher. Her grading is lenient, and she never checks for homework. BUT, she absolutely sucks at teachingdoesn't teach. Also, she sometimes will blatantly treat a student badly if she doesn't like them (speaking from personal experience). So, easy teacher, but can be moody.
An awesome professor in terms of helpfulness and availability
great professor!

Professora Braxs is very friendly and laid back. this goes both ways. it is the week before finals and I have not been shown my grades on anything-even after multiple emails asking her for them. she is a hard but fair grader but very unclear. dont take her if you arent fully confident in spanish
She's a very good professor.  She is available to help and while the grading procedures were unclear, they were pretty fair.  Definitely a good choice.
Great teacher. Very approcheable and willing to help if you are willing to put the effort
very enthusiastic. makes class interesting and fun. get material across
very good at making difficult readings clear.  workload not too intense, and has great personality, so always makes class fun and enjoyable.  not an easy grader, although probably a fair one.

Professor Vittert tends to get off-topic during class, but I found her lectures very interesting, and she gives many real-world statistical examples. Her class is not very difficult; just make sure to participate and raise your hand when you can. That brings many students' grades down.

Great lectures but tests were pretty unrelated to the material she covered in class, so you had to learn from Pearson or outside. Also had some weird Olin grade distribution requirements (no more than 30ish% of the class getting As) that she tried to impose then walked back on.
didn't really teach, but easy material
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not learn much because the lectures were not useful. Studying for the exams often required finding resources/content not from class

honestly, she doesn't really prepare you at all for future stats classes. she doesn't teach much actual material, flexing her accomplishments in class and making her students listen to her own podcasts for homework. and she is super unclear about grading and doesn't respond to emails.
easy class, horrible prof
you can have a 99 the whole semester and still end with an A-, doesn't respond to any emails
Very unfair grader. Showed up to every class and participated a lot + had a 99% overall and still ended with an A-. Doesn't respond to emails about grades, either.
Literally just arbitrarily picks your grade at the end of the sem. Class is super easy but bad prof.
Super unclear grading

You can have above a 95 the entire semester and get an A- because of how unclear your participation is graded. Lightest class you will ever take but you will likely still not end with an A because you won't even know you will get an A- until you literally see it on your Webstac.
Good, interesting lectures, but the grading is very unclear.

Participation matters a ton, and you could have a 99% in Canvas and attend every single class but you would still end up with an A- if you don't talk enough. You also don't know what participation grade you have until the final grade is posted.

Prof Vittert almost always has a case study to go along with her lecture which is cool but doesn't always teach you exactly what you need for the tests. This year was her first year giving said tests, and I don't even think she made them. Overall, interesting teacher and accessible outside of class if you need help.

Amazing lecturer with super interesting case studies. That being said, the exams are quite bs. Be prepared to do a lot of preparing outside of class for them. The project and homework are easy though, and she is a very easy grader, offering extra credit to make up for low average exam scores.

Vittert is very personable and an accomplished professor, but most people I know learned little to nothing in DAT 120. Most tests were online and so was homework (you got multiple tries). That being said, I heard that the course is more difficult now, so hopefully you get more out of it so you aren't cooked in DAT 121.

The in-class case studies are her just mostly flexing her accomplishments (deservedly so), and she has a great sense of humor. You won't learn anything ground breaking, but it is a solid intro class. There is a group project element which can eat up time out of class. Attendance is tracked and graded, so stay on top of that.

Vittert is an engaging lecturer and as someone whose attention drifts easily, I really appreciated that. She is very sweet and funny, but I felt a lot of the time what she lectures did not translate well to homework and quizzes. I would just beware of that, as there will be things that you have to teach yourself throughout the course.

1. You can't learn a lot from this class, but you could learn from Prof. Vittert how to think deeply about a fact by using stats knowledge (e.g., is it misleading).
2. She didn't teach technical stats knowledge. You should learn literally almost all by yourself. She didn't teach the knowledge that is tested on quizzes.
3. grading is not systematic.

Professor Vittert is a charismatic and inspiring figure, and her lectures are incredibly engaging - she really drills into your head the importance of data. I agree, however, that she doesn't teach much of the actual course content, which leaves you ill-prepared for DAT 121. Those without prior stats knowledge will struggle a bit with the quizzes.

I agree with a lot of the reviews here- Vittert's lectures ar interesting and she uses a lot of case studies that make the class feel applicable to real life. However, she doesn't teach much. Bus students are required to take 2 more stat classes after this, and no one I've talked to feels prepared because of her lack of teaching actual statistics.

One of my favorite professors at WashU. Prof Vittert's lectures were very interesting and engaging. She was helpful and understating with the final group project. She made me more interested in stats, and she always gave real world examples that helped me understand the material better.

Professor Liberty is literally one of the best professors I have had at WashU. She was really supportive when my group had issues choosing our project topic. She is so understanding and honestly cares about her students' success. My advice is try to participate in class and take your group projects seriously!!

Highly, highly, highly recommend. Incredibly personable, very nice, and excellent at not just explaining material but also making sure you understand why said material matters. Not sure if she's doing Dat120 again but whatever class she ends up teaching take it.

Professor Vittert's lectures were very interesting. I learned something new every class. She will occasionally lecture about required statistics topics but most of the time she emphasized the importance of statistical analysis through case studies. DAT120 is an easy class with a few quizzes and a large group project.

The lectures and case studies were so cool and I really enjoyed this course with her. A lot of her work is really interesting and after taking this class, I've become much more interested in dat. highly recommend dat 120 with vittert

A compelling and intriguing professor. Her lectures are interesting, but when investigating lecture content, it is lacking a lot of the actual statistical concepts or principles that often come with a stats class. I didn't take stats in high school, so I needed this aspect more than others. Overall a great professor, but I didn't learn too much.

DAT 20 is such a stupid class since all you learn are the very basics of statistics that 99% of WashU students already learned in high school. However, Vittert makes up for how mundane this course is with her very entertaining lectures, which mostly cover engaging case studies. Quizzes are online, final project is easy, take this class w Vittert.
Very easy and interesting class. The case studies we do in class are cool. Don't feel like I learned much about stats though...
Awesome teacher and really cool. Do case studies every class which are really interesting, and quiz material was incredibly easy if you took stat in high school.

Incredibly easy class as long as you do the work. Liberty is a super cool person, goes through interesting case studies in class. Most of grade determined by weekly homework assignments and semester-long (group) data project. Beware if you want to actually learn statistics, this might not be the most rigorous/challenging/rewarding class for you.

Professor Vittert is a very funny gal; she makes going to class worth your time. The content itself is not difficult and she does a great job using case studies to apply the concepts in an understandable way. She's the most chill professor I've had so far at WashU! DAT120 will be as easy as you make it for yourself, go to class, and do the work.

Professor Liberty was very understanding and cool. At the end of the class during there's a big event at Olin where the board of trustees and chancellor would be at, she invites students from DAT120 to talk to them as student ambassadors. Her lecture style was very interesting, but there is rarely notes, so a lot of self studying.

This professor is the best professor I have ever had. She not only teaches the material to understand statistics, but she also teaches why you should care about data and how it can be misused. There were barely any quizzes, however I still learned more than I have in a lot of my other classes. She is always available to students as well.

Professor Vittert is an incredible teacher. She makes you really care about your learning, and the class overall is not very difficult. While it may be easy to get an A, you will learn so much about data science and see the impact of your studies in the world.

Pretty straight forward about what will be on exams, VERY easy grader if you show work. She is looking to give as much partial credit as possible. Shes looking to make stats accessible to everyone and will meet you where you are with math as long as you seek out help. Office hours are extremely helpful.

honestly not a 5/5 math teacher generally, but a 5/5 math teacher for washu. super impressive statistician - has amazing credential and a real gem for the school. can be a little hard to follow sometimes but overall solid teacher and super charismatic/funny lecturer

Literally the greatest teacher I have ever had. I am required to take this course and thought I was going to hate it, but it has been so so good. It isn't easy, but she is actually the best teacher ever.
Overall not great. Didn't know a person could be so disorganized. At times she seemed a little petty.
Great professor highly highly recommend, very nice and funny, cross cultural dispute resolution is a interesting class
Professor Del Valle is a wonderful human being. I really believe he's using his position to do good things in this world and is looking to help students in their careers and lives.
highly recommend

Highly recommend Professor Juan De Valle! I had him for my negotiations class, and he always finds a way to make things fun and exciting! When I started my negotiations class, I thought I knew everything about negotiations, but boy was I wrong! I truly learned a lot from him.

Chel is an incredible professor who truly cares about her students. If you speak with her in class and attend it will enhance your experience. While attendance is not required, I highly recommend because you will learn so much from her! I have thoroughly enjoyed this class and will be taking more with her.

Most passionate professor ever!!! She truly cares about all her students in the GCP program, and although the contents of the course did not interest me at all, she made the experience super low stress and discussion based class. Only like 3 main assignments for the whole semester, and she graded super leniently.
Amazing teacher, open minded, understanding and extremely nice.

This professor is absolutely amazing. The class would not have been as interesting or revolutionary without her. She is truly exceptional, and I love everything she does. I'm not just saying this—please take this course if you want to see for yourself. She deserves every single star she has received.

Chel is a fantastic professor who has fundamentally influenced my worldview. She is so caring, and wants to make sure we learn and understand rather than check off boxes for assignments. I highly recommend taking a class with Chel if possible. life changing!
Amazing person and course (GCP)! Her activities, although a bit out there, truly give so much value to the course. One of my favorite classes and best experiences.

What an amazing, lovely, and powerful woman.While her teaching methods may seem uncomfortable and unorthodox at first, I found that some of her exercises and lectures allowed me to connect with the world in a way that I can only grateful for! Easy and creative projects. Lots of discussion! Super fun and enlightening. Love you, Chel! #gcp4ever

prof spees is one of the most caring, funny, and approachable professors ever, n probably one of the best profs in the chemistry department. the class itself is rough and there is an endless amount of work. 3 reports w revisions, weekly notebooks..time SINKS but you learn a lot.., 5 hour labs. but i grew a lot as a scientist, so it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My GOAT, very inspirational
one of my favorite professors at WashU. takes so much care of his students and their learning. would take every class with him if i could
Great guy!
best help sessions- entertaining and you will learn.  Dr. Spees is the man
GREAT RECITATION LEADER....this guy was hilarious
He's super cool and gives great book recs. Great guy to riff with before class
This Professor is also my advisor and is one of the most passionate, concise, and wonderful. He is dedicated to his students and a wonderful scholar

Billy really cares and wants everyone to succeed. He isn't a tough grader and doesn't assign a ton of work, but you have to participate in class to do well. He's also a fan of group/partner work. I learned a lot about Latin America and enjoyed our discussions, but this class was on zoom during COVID which definitely made it less engaging.

Acree is a great guy who genuinely desires to get to know his students. He will do a check-in during class to make sure the students are not too stressed. His literature and film selections are interesting, and usually not super difficult to understand. Class discussions are thought-provoking. Acree is also an easy grader!

Billy is one of the best teachers I have ever had.  Not only does he completely know his stuff, he really makes an effort make us engage the material in a variety of different ways, making the learning experience fun and new throughout the class.  If you have the opportunity to take a class from him, I highly recommend it.
I absolutely love Billy! He is so charismatic and really loves to teach his topic. The class was engaging and I learned a ton! I absolutely loved it!

Professor Acree is a great professor. He is always prepared, engaging, and available for help. Great facilitator of class discussions. He knows his stuff. Be sure to do the readings and participate and you should do fine.

I don't get get why his rating is this high. Tough exams, where he purposely gives less practice so that everything students see on his exams is brand new, and harsh in grading them. Lectures are abysmal...stares at the wall and never looks at his students. Took him two months to answer an email about a disability issue I had, which he disregarded.

I was nervous going into ECON4001 because of its reputation as a difficult class, but while it was hard, I was pleasantly surprised by Weinstein's engaging and humorous lectures. The tests were graded harshly, with very little partial credit given. His unit on game theory was awesome and genuinely my favorite part of my econ major so far.

I really enjoyed this course. Although lectures might get a bit boring sometimes, I think Weinstein explains the concepts fairly well. The homework is slightly challenging, but exams are relatively easy as they are almost identical to past papers.
Decent professor, but gives writes very time consuming homework that is graded strictly. Also, exam 2 is ridiculous.

He's a pretty good professor, but his lectures are a bit boring. If you're going to take intermediate micro, take calc 3 first. In my class all of my friends who took calc 3 including me had a pretty easy time. The vast majority of the kids scoring 50s, 60s, 70s, could not handle the math well enough. Exams are exactly like practice tests.
He's a great professor and throws in a couple of jokes here and there, cares for the students and is a chill guy to talk with in person outside of class.

Do NOT take this class if you don't have to. He's a terrible lecturer, and his lectures don't really line up with the homework or the exams. Lecture slides are very word-heavy, but the exams/HW are math-heavy. Exam 2 is very hard so he says he'll curve it, but then curves overall grade so the curve barely changes anything (didn't affect my grade)
he is very organized in class, and I really like his teaching style. He also carefully asks if everyone understands when explaining concepts. totally amazing professor.

He is funny in an awkward way, tries to crack jokes throughout lectures. Attending the lecture and doing the weekly homework really helps with understanding the theoretical concepts and prepare for the exam. He gives enough materials and support to succeed, and exams are curved.

Pros: Very straightforward with concepts, tells you all the formulas/methods you need to know. Curves so 50% of the class gets A- or above.

Cons: Super boring, monotone. Doesn't explain concepts well or at all. The second test out of 3 was very unfair/difficult given what we learned. Tests are worth 70% of grade. Homework is pretty difficult.
Straightforward professor who gives you all the info you need to know, but requires strong grasp of key concepts in order to succeed
Kinda awkward but in an extremely sweet way. Cares about students and the workload/exams are fair. Not an easy A tho; you'll definitely have to work for it.

Weinstein is a good teacher and uses real world examples to get his point across. I can tell he had a few difficulties showing us his mathematical steps over zoom, but overall I never felt he failed to teach us the material. He is also a nice person and happy to answer questions. If you know the homework, you will do alright on tests.

Class content is challenging but not impossible to follow, the problem is (maybe now since all classes are online) none of what is presented in pre-recorded lectures ever matches up the content of homework. Despite him always saying to reach out for help or questions and seeming like a genuinely nice guy, I never got any emails back when I wrote.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely an awkward guy, but he gives clear and straightforward lectures and tries to keep things humorous.

He is a great professor. His explanation of the materials are thorough and dense. He makes sure that everyone understands the course material by going through homework problems. Exams and the amount of homework are fair. If you go to lectures and do the homework problems, getting an A is super easy. Amazing professor.

Weinstein gives very boring lectures. You could just read his PowerPoint slides. His TA's grade all of his exams, and he does not care if they take off many points for little errors. If you mess up anything on an exam, expect a lot of points off.

he is a fantastic human being, very funny and passionate about Econ. he makes dad jokes. I would recommend his class, he makes it easy enough to succeed (even though I did not do well, which was my fault!!!!) -- just do the homework, pay attention in lecture and you can get an A

Content can be a little theoretical while in class, but the homework always clears it up. Weinstein also does a great job going over homework afterward in class and being available during office hours to help you through it. Wouldn't say too much of it, 1 hour a week. Exams are very fair and often match the practice exams- definitely do them!

The class material is dense. There are weekly assignment which can take many hours. The lectures are well taught and the tests are fair. He is a fun person and very accessible outside of classroom. If you study hard you can pretty much get an A, but definitely not an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: LOTS OF HOMEWORK

Professor Weinstein is a hidden gem of the econ department. The class I had with him was well taught and fairly graded. I learned a lot of material without ever feeling too stressed. Attending class does help your grade, but I actually really enjoyed attending class, he makes econ fun and exciting.

Great Prof. if you get a chance to take a class with him. Grading is fair, and expectations are clear. Lectures are great. Just be sure to do the practice exams: they're practically identical to the real ones. Overall, great class, couldn't ask for much more.

Jonathan Weinstein is not only a great professor:  He's a great man.  But in all seriousness he's the sweetest, nerdiest guy who wants his students to succeed.  Exams are all easy; mostly identical to the homework and past exams.  Definitely take a class with him.

Class I was the most likely to fall asleep in. Very boring and only gets a little bit better when you get to game theory. Tests are pretty straightforward if you take the time to learn the concepts though. Extremely nice teacher.

Keeps class as engaging as possible. Like a lot of Econ lectures, the material can be a bit dull, but he makes up for it. Homework is often challenging, but he makes up for it by counting it as a large chunk of the grade. Exams are reasonable, with the occasional curve ball thrown in. A bit awkward in one-on-one interactions, but a very nice guy.
Clear lecturer. Makes topics interesting. Slides are very useful. Old exams and problem sets are very useful. Review sessions before exams are also very useful.
Extremely clear lectures, no need to read the book. Posts all slides online. Exams aren't that tough if you go to class, problems almost exclusively come from in class examples or homeworks.
Very clear in lecture and very useful slides. Exams are not easy by any means, but if you know your stuff they are manageable, and the class gets curved. Overall pretty good

Professor Waters is a very funny and passionate person, and I can tell she really enjoys the topics we discussed in class (Technology and Selfhood). While she didn't have clear rubrics, I think that trying, staying in contact with her, and letting your voice show in your writing can help you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Waters is a bit of harsh grader; rubrics are quite long yet somehow fail to explain what is needed for an essay. She did give assignments leading up to essays that were very helpful in writing the essays. The readings were interesting but our class discussions were not. I have nothing against her, but probably wouldn't take her again.

shes really cool to talk with, very helpful 1-on-1. personally love her 5/5, but i understand how her teaching style isnt everyones favorite. i do think im a better writer now. worked my a$s off & it paid off, but ideally an intro writing class would be less difficult. i cannot stress enough that to get a good grade you should be putting in the hrs

She is a very harsh grader but lacks any good feedback or criticism, and anything she does give isn't legible. She is a bit rude and unprofessional if she doesn't like what you wrote, as she grades based on her own opinion and no specific rubric. Very lecture-heavy. She talks for most of the hour about what she thinks. DO NOT take writing on aging
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very kind and understanding woman. Sh's down to earth with realistic expectations and gives generous extensions if you reach out and communicate. She assigns a fair amount of reading per class which you generally should do. She doesn't give out easy 100s but she is also not a harsh grader and does her best to keep you in the high B to A range.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is kind and extremely lenient about late work/ extensions, often times not penalizing for unexplained late work. Unfortunately, she is an extremely picky and frustrating grader, someone who doesn't believe any decent paper deserves more than an A-. The same goes for participation. The work is not hard, but her poor grading goes unexplained.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Caring professor overall. My only criticism is her grading - she leaves very helpful notes on assignments, but her rubrics are very subjective. She believes there's "no such thing as perfect", which is fine, most people can still get high grades, but don't expect 100%s. That aside, I appreciate the depth and nuance she brings to the topic of aging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I think calling Aileen Waters a professor or even a teacher is rude to other professors. Aileen Waters is a grader, she will not teach you anything in the class, moreover expect that you already know it. She comes off as arrogant, and thinks that nobody is better with grammar rules than her. Overall, harsh grader, not that pleasant of a person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice professor! Approachable and always accessible during office hours. Gives useful feedback on assignments. Not a harsh grader, the lowest grade for me is an A- (I'm not good at writing at all). Readings are kind of long but manageable. There are some small assignments but they are preparatory for essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor who genuinely cares about her students and offers lots of valuable feedback. Tough grader, so go to office hours if you are struggling, she will guide you in the right direction. Also, the class is a lot of work and a lot of writing, so be prepared to put in the work. Participate in class, keep up with the work and you'll be fine.
Go to her Office hours. She is extremely helpful.

Prof Waters was a great writing professor. I am someone with very little interest in writing, but she made this class one of my favorites this semester. There is a good amount of reading before each class. She is very available for feedback on assignments and goes out of her way to help students. Text and traditions is a very interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think most people don't want to take college writing, but as a professor she is pretty good. She gives you good advice on what to do; the only thing that is a deterrent is that she is not an easy grader. I have not yet gotten an A on my assignments and her essays are required to be 4-5 pages, with the last one being 10. Also lots of busywork.
Professor Waters is kind, understanding, and overall a good teacher. She is a harsh grader, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really loved her in college writing. Definitely heavy on the essays. She really cares about her students though and will always give an extension if you need one. Would definitely take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Classic English teacher. Assigns lots of reading without realizing how much work she's actually giving, comes off as a bit snarky at times, will probably never give you a full A, and relatively disorganized. However, she gives good feedback on papers and promotes a good environment for in-class discussions. As far as CWP profs go, she's alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: really fun class! fast-paced at times but she really cared for us

Absolutely goated professor for Chinese for Heritage Speakers 1. Very understanding and dedicated to her work. Cares not for the grade but for actually understanding. Be expected to participate frequently in class and volunteer. Pretty lenient grader for everything, homework and assessments.
Fun class.

TRUST THE REVIEWS!! She is every single person who takes her class' favorite professor. You learn an insane amount of Chinese in one semester, all while loving it. It's five days a week, which means you learn so much but she still makes it fun. Super easy grader, although there are two quizzes and a test every week.
Just take a class and you'll see!
BEST TEACHER EVER

Absolutely amazing. She is definitely one of the most kind, caring, and understanding professors I have met at this school, and I would 100% recommend taking her classes. The assignments sometimes take a while to do, but she is very lenient with her grading and gives good feedback.
Love Love love this professor. She is so nice and caring. This class has a lot of readings regarding to Chinese poems. A lot of writing and reading but class discussions were super interesting.
Wang is a darling lady, the absolute sweetest! She goes at a reasonable pace with her lectures and is flexible if you need to make up assignments.
Dr Wang is so nice. She's so caring and understanding with the deadlines. Make sure to participate. I took Heritage Chinese 106 and it went well! I learned a lot from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Wang Laoshi is one of my favorite professors I've had so far at WashU. She is so sweet and lively. I look forward to class every day because of her positive attitude and her willingness to help you with pronunciation. She's very accessible and welcoming during office hours and will chat with you to help you practice speaking Chinese.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Wang Laoshi is one of the most caring and kind professors I've encountered at WashU! Her class is interesting and I hope I can take another class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Wang laoshi is the most amazing teacher I have ever had. If I could pick someone to be my godmother, it would be her. She's so hilarious, friendly, and really cares about how you're doing in class. Chinese takes a lot of work, but I scheduled my 2nd-semester schedule around Wang's class. So receptive and kind, you should definitely take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I have taken. If you are considering taking a lang., take this class. I have learned so much Chinese in one semester. There is a little adjustment at the beginning to the teaching style (speaking the whole class) but u get used to it. A lot of hw, but manageable. Wang laoshi is so caring, entertaining, and a fantastic prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a caring professor. The Chinese program at washu is also very highly rated and it's because of people like Wang laoshi.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Wang is one of the best professors at Washu. The amount of Chinese you learn in a semester is crazy and that's a testament to how good she is as a teacher. You have to go to class everyday or else you won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I love Wang Laoshi. Best teacher I have had at Wash U. I am so sad she isn't teaching 2nd year chinese. I scheduled my second semester schedule around making sure her class fit into my schedule, she's fabulous and so friendly.

Wang Laoshi is the best! Not only will you learn a ton of chinese but she is also the sweetest professor. she will go out of her way to help you! she makes class very enjoyable and her examples are so funny!
Wang 老师 is wonderful, like the rest of the Chinese department I've encountered at WashU.

OK so if you over the fact that Chinese is basically the hardest class offered at Wash U, this class was awesome! Wang laoshi is really nice and accommodating!! Wang laoshi has more energy than any other teacher I've ever had, and she is really dedicated to teaching.
Extremely good professor. Always excited and prepared to teach class.
A lot of work. Nice and caring Prof. Tries hard.
Extremely lovable.  Not very strict.  You'll learn a lot if you want to.
Wang Wei is extremely caring and always willing to help. She also puts you in a good mood because she's funny and energetic.
No Comments
I LOVE WANGLAOSHI! she's so cute, and makes the class environment very relaxed :)

This class is so much fun, and you really learn a ton.  Wang Laoshi is quite the amazing professor.  She is arguably the best I've had at Wash. U.  She is very funny and keeps the classroom atmosphere relaxed.  She also makes sure you understand the material and helps you when you don't.
I love professor tang! Sweet and fun class
He is the best prof in the department!!!!

Dr. Tang constantly encouraged us to discuss the material with each other, which is somewhat uncommon in math. His classroom always felt welcoming and safe. The homework assignments were shockingly easy and the exams were also not very challenging, but I don't think that's inappropriate for a first class in abstract algebra.

Professor Tang is a very personable guy who is clearly knowledgable about the subject area. The class feels like a community, and he encourages this. The content material for the midterm was unclear to some, but that wasn't a huge deal. Would recommend.
Professor Tang is the goat
One of the best professors in the math department. Tang is a brilliant mathematician and truly cares about his students. Made me love algebraic topology.
Great Professor
Very kind guy and one of my favorite professors at WashU. Also very helpful and supportive towards his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honors Math is graded very lightly but the material is so confusing. The professor is nice, but only lectures, most of which are very similar. He doesn't wait to see if people are understanding, he just keeps plowing through proofs. To top it off, the homework, quizzes, and tests are graded so lightly that you don't know what you don't know.
Professor Tang is a very clear and patient lecturer. He is helpful outside the classroom and truly cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Tang is a generous grader and an eminent, talented mathematician

Professor Tang is a super talented teacher. He's amazing at what he taught and able to answer almost all of your questions. If you want to dig deeper into mathematics, he is definitely a great person to visit.
Truly cared about us. Lectures were sometimes tricky to follow, but was always willing to explain and was enjoyable to listen to.
Great teacher.

Professor Tang is clearly concerned for his students and shows up to class enthusiastic about teaching.  Some people thought he had high expectations but he did outline them clearly.  Highly recommended for students interested in math (or physics) and not taking the class based on requirements alone.

Tang was a decent teacher. As far as foreign profs go, he was pretty easy to understand, and he emphasized the important concepts pretty well. He made his expectations for the exams clear, and gave helpful practice tests.
One thing he said in the first lecture was really true: "the textbook is very important." Indeed it is, cuz that's how you are going to learn in his class, by reading the book yourself.

He was a great professor that made me love math. His examples were great and very clear; you would never think that differential equations is difficult once you learn from him. His homework assignments were basically the exams so if you can do them, you should get an A in the class. Plus, he has a generous curve (most people get A's).

Although Prof. Tang is hard to understand, I think he did his best. The good thing about him is that he repeated many times the important things he wants you to know, the things that he said that will appear on the test. I would say going to his class is important because it is useful to take notes because some of the problems on the tests are from
Some of his lectures weren't very interesting, but you could tell he was trying. Some of the material is difficult, but you could tell he tried his best. Occassionally even made a joke or two!
inarticulate, unhelpful, but entertaining.  Probably the only people who got anything out of this class were mathy people before they took it

attributes justifications and conclusions to being "magical" or "beautiful". difficult to understand, but even more difficult to follow once you are able to understand. going to class was merely time away from reading your textbook where you would ultimately learn all of the material. however, listening to him attempt to teach was very entertaining
BEST PERSON EVER

took Chinese 306. Liang is exceptionately patient, kind, and passionate about teaching a holistic understanding of Chinese culture & Mandarin. She is also considerate of student mental health/extentuating circumstances. TA was also effective w/feedback & responsiveness.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Liang Laoshi, like the other professors in the Chinese department, is amazing. She is patient, kind, and a thorough listener, always nodding her head when you speak. She is a bit older but seems to have lost none of her passion for teaching, as every day she came to class steadily prepared and engaged with us all.

Liang Lao Shi is a fun teacher who enjoys class discussion. She follows the curriculum as standard by the department. Grading is standard and not hard to get an A if you put in the effort. She is always willing to help and approachable outside of class. It's very clear she much prefers tangentially related class discussion.
She's really nice and a great prof all around.

Liang Laoshi is a fantastic teacher and a really genuine and good person. I took her class freshman year and she continued to go out of her way to say hello to me (she always remembered my name, background, interests) even when I was a senior!! She is engaging, has a great sense of humor and is really inspirational. Take her class!

Excellent lecturer. She is patient with students of all language standards, and has a great wealth of knowledge in Chinese literature, history and geography. Was one of the top students in Beijing when she was a college student there decades ago.
Sometimes hard to understand her, and can't say the lectures are very engaging, but she is funny and cares! Always let us out early too!
her lectures can be hard to follow and her writing on the board is incredibly messy, but those are my only complaints. Sometimes she didn't take the whole class time for better or worse

If you have any degree of social anxiety I would not recommend Dr Wang. She cold calls on students and bullies them when they don't have the answers and is just generally rude to students. She is also a sub-par lecturer, so to adequately understand the content I am forced to watch the other lecturers recorded videos. Would not recommend.

Does not take any time to explain concepts or problems. Does not speak great english which can sometimes make it extremely confusing what she is talking about/saying. Often gets confused by the problems or her own explanations which makes it very confusing for students. Overall a horrible professor for such an important/large intro level class.

The professor is super hard to understand. I was in her class for 2 weeks and luckily was able to switch. Do not take 192 with her unless you already have a physics E&M background; will be very tough to learn in her class.

Prof Wang isn't great at teaching 192. She clearly knows her stuff but struggles to convey info to students combined with her being hard to understand. She goes through examples fast and consistently ends class early instead of taking the time to explain each example thoroughly like other profs do. I've resorted to watching Hynes' lectures.

Professor Xi cold calls students and insists upon getting an answer from them even when they're uncomfortable. Her explanations can be very complicated making the lecture material difficult to understand - I've had to rely on just textbook material. While she clearly cares for her students, overcomplications make the content much harder.
Xi was a great professor and it was obvious that she cared about her students. She did a great time teaching the class for the first time!
Great prof. First time teaching and did a great job.
Prof Xi was overall a great lecturer, although her English is not quite perfect. However she was very friendly and helpful if you had a question about the material.

The material is presented very poorly in class. In general, the material taught is not reflective of what Pan expects students to know. The material that he does teach is explained poorly, leaving students more confused than anything else. The tests are poorly written and are often ambiguous, leading to massive grading errors.
He is extremely difficult to follow, the only learning I did while taking the class was from reading the book.  Avoid him if you can!
Worst class I have ever taken in my entire life. I had to teach myself all of the material. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. However, he did curve the daylights out of the class.
Probably the most confusing and inconsistent Profesor I've ever had. If you absolutely must take 217 the semester Pan is teaching, check out Paul's Online Math Notes. It'll help
Actually not that bad. He gave me A+ in the end and basically everyone got higher than B+
The worst. He made a lot of typos throughout the semester and basically he just read the textbook during lectures. Not helpful at all.

Professor Pan is arguably the worst professor I've ever had.  He blindly reads from the textbook without explaining, isn't perceptive to students' lack of understanding, cannot answer questions, and speaks very poor English.  He aslo makes typos on tests.  Along with 34 of the class, I stopped going to his lectures to teach myself from the book.
It's his first year teaching and he seems like a good guy, but he's honestly terrible right now.  I barely went to class and just read from the textbook, whether in class or at home.

All he did in lectures was go through the examples in the textbook. Additionally, he refused to go in depth with his explanations during lectures. His tests have had typos before. Try to avoid him at all costs. But, in all fairness, it's his first year teaching, so he just might need some experience under his belt before becoming a good teacher.

By far the worst professor I have ever encountered. Please just don't take any of his classes or you'll regret it. The lectures consist of him reading examples out of the book and skipping steps (he won't clarify if you ask a question). The exams are difficult and filled with mistakes. I honestly don't think he even cares about teaching at all.

Literally the worst ever. Lectures are not helpful and tests are poorly written and difficult. Easily the worst teacher I've ever had. Whatever class you are considering taking with him, just wait and take it later

421 was the only option for the rating, but I took Intro Astrophysics I with Yajie. One of my most chill and lovely physics classes in my life. Absolutely amazing content and explanation. The HW problems can be a bit challenging but go to office hours does help a lot.

yajie is literally amazing--one of the best profs at washu, for sure! the concepts are difficult, but she does a great job simplifying them and makes sure that your grade reflects your hard work. she's super understanding and will not let one bad test define your overall grade! she's very accessible outside of class too
Yajie was a slayful professor. She explained difficult concepts very thoroughly. I learned a lot in this class. Will be taking Physics 422 with her next semester for sure!
Good teaching skills and case-based approach to learning used by Prof. Yaron. He teaches really well and makes topics easier for students to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exams are difficult and focused on understanding over memorization. Overall tough course but he makes it pretty easy to digest and understand

first year teaching undergrad and you can tell. lectures aren't very clear as he goes too fast. participation matters. i was lost the whole time i'm not gonna lie. wish i took the class with a different professor. had office hours once a week.... so that didn't help either
VERY lecture heavy. Strick with attendence. Can tell he takes his classes very seriously. Sometimes he goes thru stuff too fast and cannot articulate because of accent. Good person but too strict

Does a great job at introducing you to Arabic, and the homework is pretty manageable. Homework is very important, and tests are pretty easy. Heavily prioritizes attendance and participation, and he tries to make learning fun and engaging.

Such an amazing professor!! can be slightly disorganized and go on rants but very knowledgable person and really wants to get to know his students. if given the opportunity to go on the ampersand trip, go! One of the best experiences and so incredibly fun to learn more about him and his family

Dr. Tarbouni is a wonderful professor, he is gives invaluable insight to the topics in the course and makes the content very accessible and interesting. He's also a great speaker with a good sense of humor and engaging anecdotes. You can tell he really cares about his students and goes out of his way to make sure everyone succeeds.

Dr. Tarbouni is a great and very knowledgeable professor! Though he may go off on tangents often, and might be slightly passive aggressive at times, he makes class enjoyable and interesting, and he is extremely qualified. He gets to know his students well too. I 100% recommend taking at least one class with him!
Awesome professor! By far one of my favorite professors this semester. I would highly recommend taking a class from him. Very caring and willing to help!

Dr. Tarbouni is one of my favorite professors at WashU. He is invested in his students as well as the content within this class. He can be a bit scattered at times, but overall, he's a fun guy who you can learn so much from.

Dr. T is without a doubt the best professor I have ever had. After taking his first year program, I wanted to take Arabic even though I can't speak it at all just to take another class with him. He goes on tangents often, but they are all related to the subject. Spending time with him is also worthwhile, he cares about his students so much!

Do not worry about your grade because he grades easily. Just do the work and there are so many opportunities to learn a lot from Tarbouni(he has done so much!), the readings and other students. He is a bit unorganized which can be frustrated but remember that the class is really what you make of it and you will get out what you put into the class.

Super chill class and while his grading criteria are not exactly clear he is pretty lenient with grading. Attendance matters and is a part of the grade. Fun in general and responds to emails pretty quickly (within an hour even, sometimes).

really chill class, just showed up and did the readings and got an A. learned a TON too. Tarbouni cares so much about the subject and his students, and spending time with him is WORTH IT. he wants to get to know all of his students and help all of them out, its amazing. also likely the most interesting person i've ever met.

tarbouni is an amazing professor- he is so funny and knowledgeable and made material very digestible. assignments and tests were easy. he made arabic very approachable for new people and enjoyable for people with experience. attendance is MANDATORY. my attendance was bad this semester for personal reasons and my grade definitely reflected that

Easy class. It's five days a week and there's a lot of homework at the beginning, but after you learn the alphabet, there's not too much. Most things are graded for completion. He wants to give his students A's, so as long as you do most of the things, he'll give you an A. He talks a lot and goes on tangents so it's a low effort class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Tarbouni really cares about the topic of the class. It is mostly discussion based between the students over the readings. He can be a little all over the place and the class is as well. The end of there year project was really easy and there is little to no homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very easy language class and super understanding guy
Really funny and nice guy. Just show up to class and chat with him and you'll get an A. Wish I could take way more Arabic classes with him.
Pretty easy class, just show up and talk in class and you'll be fine. The tests are just like the practice tests.
Very knowledgeable about the history of the Arabic language. Very encouraging and responsive to learners. One of the best.

Material becomes harder 2nd semester but he does NOT step up to teach it, he falls back and became increasingly lazy and confusing.  Lectures not content based - he speaks about what he wants and sometimes reviews the vocab but expects you to understand and teach yourself grammar on your own. Confusingunclear grader. Insecurecan be patronizing.

It's a beginning language course, so the material is challenging.  Prof is flexible with homework and assIgnments.  He is good at explaining the material, but sometimes has unrealistic expectations. He frequently goes on interesting and humorous tangents.  Grading is holistic and mysterious, but he's pretty fair.

Tarbouni is a super great professor! He jokes around a lot and makes things fun, especially second semester. I learned so much in his class. Also he's not that much of a stickler on homework; just be sure you have it all done before the test and you'll be fine. 5/5 would take his class again.

This man is truly an amazing professor. He is very smart, has a great sense of humor, and is quite intellectual. While the class is demanding, he is fairly laid back guy.
