Even though learning Arabic might be intimidating, he guides you through it step by step, making it totally manageable as long as you put in the time.

TAKE THIS COURSE! Tarbouni is absolutely fantastic. He is incredibly fair, and very funny. I signed up for this class on a whim, and am so glad I did. The course is so much fun. Materials are explained clearly. Even though the class is work and is difficult, it is manageable, and so so so worth it.
Very good at explaining grammar and linguistics, clearly cares about students, makes many funny jokes in class, make sure to do the homework.
He was a great teacher and really wanted his students to do well. He prepared his students well for each test and never tried to trick us. Excited to take him again
Great class!
Great professor!!! Genuinely cares about students doing well, do the homework though and you'll have an introduction to more than just the Arabic language,but the culture of the Arab world too.
No Comments
Good teacher, helpful.  Not always on topic, but interesting.  Good with linguistical help
Really nice guy, and knows alot about lingustics. Sometimes gets off track, but is a good teacher overall.

Professor Yasuda got me back into what learning a language feels like. Naturally, this comes with a lot of work and time spent in-class thinking and speaking, but I found this to be very worth it. She understands that none of us are perfect, and generally grades on the easier side. Also very accessible through email and office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is challenging, but Sensei Yasuda is very energetic and eager to help. She is always willing to help outside of class I really enjoyed being in her class.

I could not disagree more with the first couple of reviews. Yasuda sensei is a wonderful instructor and genuinely wants her students to learn Japanese. Cold calling and getting things wrong is all part of the learning process, and if you're looking for an easy way out of that, then you probably aren't ready to take a language course in general...
Well scheduled class, attractive lecture, and warm-hearted care make her one of the best professor in language classes.

Really well-organized course with a smooth and enjoyable learning experience. Every assignment, activity, and project is thoughtfully planned to help you improve. My language skills have grown so much over the past semester. I'm going to Japan this summer and feel ready to speak a lot of Japanese thanks to this class!
I really like her Japanese class.
I love her japanese class!

Yasuda sensei is a nice teacher. She is very energetic in class which would definitely keep you awake and focused. She is passionate and really want to help you actively learn and be skillful in Japanese. The grading of the class is lenient and fair. Good class overall, kept me motivated and enthusiastic about learning Japanese. とてもやさしいせんせいです。

I took 101 and I am in 102 now. Amazing professor- She is extremely engaging, wants to know your life, and yes cold calling. But that's how you learn a language. Even if you get stuff wrong on homework's she gives full points. There is a LOT of work but it is worth it.After the first class we can all speak japanese well.

Agree with the other comments. She makes you embarrassed in front of the whole class if you cannot answer her question on the first try. Not a difficult class but wouldn't take a Japanese course again.

Easy A as long as you do everything asked. She's not a bad person but not supportive as all, communicating with her can be very stressful. Prepare for every class, otherwise it will be quit embarassing when you can't answer the question right and she asks you multiple times, no one can help you out.

Easy A class, but be ready for lot of awkward q and a session. She will made you to answer a question so many time until is smooth enough for her by pretending didnt hear it well. Your grade is really depends on her mood of the day.

This class is not a lot of work and tests are similar to practice exams and homework, but he does not really teach. Additionally, he curves down which hurts people's grades. Overall, a low-effort class where a high grade is achievable.

The amount of effort he puts in to the course is utterly disrespectful and unacceptable. It is obvious he is not interested in teaching, and the department should step in to evaluate his course. He is doing a disservice to many students interested in pursuing other economics courses, and it is a selfish way of approaching teaching.

Professor is objectively bad (poor lectures, not accessible, minimal study resources). That being said, if you want a free A then take his course. Exams are nearly identical to practice exams and 4 easy homework assignments throughout the entire semester.

He barely shows up in office hour (I once waited for one hour in front of his office and still failed to see him), and not accessible out of class. You should learn the content by yourself--which is easy. His tests are easy, and the grading is not tough. Sry but I cannot keep my attention focused during his lectures.
Great professor and easy exam. Dont hesitate to take his 4011 class! just spend two days before taking the exam you could get a A+. He's also a nice guy

This professor is quite terrible. While exams are not that hard, his lectures are very fast-paced and he is almost impossible to reach outside of class. You can tell that he does not really care how you do in his class and he does not give much effort in any regard. Do not take his class.
Awesome class with few and easy tests and homework(only 1 HW before the first test). No outside of class effort needed, just go to his class you will understand everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Goto office hours and ask for example questions for each chapter. You will see similar questions on exams. The main problem with Prof Yenmez was that you don't know what kind of questions you will face. But if you know this, it's relatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice dude, but he barely gave anything to prepare for exams. There are 4 homework assignments in total, with 1-2 questions per homework, and he only gave out 1 practice exam because so many people begged. Exams are easy and short if you understand what's going on, but lectures are very confusing and he rarely checks his email.

Taught a dumbed down version of intermediate micro but the course feels just as hard or harder b/c his lectures are bad. Decided to teach us matching and auction theory instead of game theory for some reason. Class starts off easy but quickly ramps up in difficulty after the first exam. Feeling very unprepared for future upper level econ courses.

Nice and seems well-intentioned, however, this was the most poorly run course I've taken. Exam questions are easy if you understand the material but lectures are confusing and boring and he doesn't give nearly enough practice hw/questions. I left the class feeling like I didn't learn anything, but rather learned what to do to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: really great professor, probably one of the best I've had at WashU. class was tough but manageable if you put the work in and went to office hours/recitation. TAs were also really helpful and were always very reachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: honestly seems like a well-intentioned professor... but can't teach at all. gives zero guidance before exams and homework is quite different from lecture material. unclear explanations in class. no idea what to expect from any of this guy's material
Easy A, but you'll learn nothing.

professor chen is definitely a smart guy and a go-to researcher in AI at WashU. He has deep knowledge in his own field, and his lectures and researches touch on a lot of applications in other areas too. The course itself is very group-project heavy, and the grading is pretty lenient. I'd recommend it.

Chen is probably the top AI researcher at WU; his lectures are very good, deep, concise, and insightful. Just hope he can give a few more lectures than class presentations. The homeworks are fun and practical

Although Chen is a decent lecturer, his class design is awful. You'd learn more about the topic in the first three weeks of the electrical engineering undergrad course. Chen lectured around 6 times and the rest were peer presentations (he doesn't even attend these himself) with no in-depth content. Insanely easy A but don't expect to learn.

This class is ridiculously easy compared to any 500-level class, especially a Theory class. His lectures are very clear, but it only lasts for a month, and the rest are presentations and a group project, which are all graded uniformly.

He is very knowledgeable about the topic, right to the point. dunno about others, but this course has the right difficulty for me who just want to know more about optimization but don't like too much math. the course presentations by peers are awesome as they cover some current applications in machine learning, which I am eager to learn about
Prof Chen is going to offer about 10 lectures and skip the rest of the semester. So you basically just going to listen to peer's lectures, which has various quality.

Chen is an expert in optimization. What I liked most is the organization of the course: a mixture of classical stuff and modern applications. He would condense a 400 page textbook in to a series of insightful slides and pick out the key concepts for us. Oh, you don't need to be a math genius to pass this course.

You'll learn the core material of nonlinear optimization pretty solidly, as that's the part Dr. Chen covers himself. The modern stuff is, unfortunately, left to students (who are all assigned to groups, each group giving one lecture on modern techniques). Some of the student lectures were excellent, but others left quite a bit to be desired.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Get the core knowledge of nonlinear optimization from a series of insightful lectures, notes, and examples. No deep theories or hard maths, suitable for those who want to apply optimization in their research or practical problems.
Do the Labs, Studios and Extensions on time. Listen to the lectures, you will be ready for the exams.

He is now my favorite professor - lighthearted and well-meaning.  He clearly has a very deep knowledge about and beyond this subject. He can always find a way to cleverly explain difficult concept through drawings and metaphors. Also he has a good sense of humor and told quite  a few good jokes in this class.

Very good teacher, although sometimes not very clear and too quick. He is certainly a truly smart guy with deep knowledge of CS. His class is most suited for those who are keen to learn and self-motivated.
A good and fun teacher. He introduces Java by showing a lot of cool stuff such as drawing graphics and playing music. I'm now obsessed with it
He's a very boring lecturer.  Luckily, you only need to look at the slides he sends out.  Unfortunately, there are quizes during lecture, so you have to attend.
He is good enough as a professor. The occasional showing of his sense of humor always cracks me up.
Handsome young prof with living coding and magic tricks!
Good professor. Thanks for a great semester. I am now seriously considering to get a minor in computer science, a thought that seemed crazy before the class.

He made the grading clear at the beginning. I had a great semester and learned a lot. The CSE131 is not as easy as one would except for a introductory course. Overall a good professor, accessible and fun. The live coding he did during class is very helpful.

Chen is a terrible teacher.  He teaches this intro-level class as though the students have been doing computer science their whole lives.  His accent is difficult to understand and his teachings are nearly irrelevant to the quizes.  This is a consensus among most of the students in his class.
Very smart, but not a great teacher. You will have to go to the TAs a lot. Recommend using outside reading to supplement the instruction if you want to learn this material.
Not very good at explaining concepts, seems unwilling to provide assistance outside of class other than TAs. Sometimes hard to understand through his thick asian accent.
He is a very smart guy. Lectures are helpful -- explain difficult concepts almost effortlessly
Lovely dude, pretty easy class if you don't underestimate it. Make sure to go to class because he started springing attendance quizzes that were worth so much randomly halfway through the semester.

This course was fairly reading heavy but the tests were open note, and there's a semester long project. My test avg was 85 but I still got an A. Bowersox is chill and easygoing so I reccomend. Attendance is randomly taken on days, but he made us well aware for those who pay attention, and grade changes helped inflate grades at end of sem.

The class is ok but is quite misleading. For instance, 7% of the grade is attendance quizzes (not stated in the syllabus), and they randomly scaled in points (the first was .05%, but the last was 2% of the total grade). Ultimately, unannounced/late grading adjustments (i.e. subtracting 10 pts from an assignment) unexpectedly changed my final grade.

He's passionate about what he teaches and is knowledgeable but the class is simply too disorganized. We started off with no syllabus, grading criteria changed throughout the semester, and exams ended up weighing less than random quizzes that weren't about the material. While he is a good professor I wouldn't recommend taking his class.
Had Bowersox for Intro to Environmental Policy. Chillest guy ever.

Just an awesome dude. Funny, engaging, and energetic to be around. While he often overprepared for lectures (we never got through all the slides), we still were able to learn a lot. Lots of reading, but not checked per say; definitely important for the tests though. Group project sucked a bit, but everything else was fantastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Actually chillest prof of all time
Definitely makes mistakes on his own quizzes, but will be flexible about fixing them. Generally very chill, not too much hw, loosely graded writing assignments, funny lecturer. Easy class.

Bowersox is a really good professor, very knowledgeable. He helped to connect me with upperclassmen and settle into WashU. This class is super easy, TAs and Bowersox are all easy to communicate with. You're only graded on attendance, tests, a end of semester group project and singular essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Poli Sci 3760 GUE with Bowersox and he is a great and relax professor. All of the lectures were super interesting and he's a really knowledge person. The assignments were low pressure and his grading was pretty easy. Highly recommend taking any class with him!
Love Professor Bowersox and would highly recommend taking his class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Zach is a phenomenal professor, incredibly knowledgeable, and very friendly. I came into the class interested in the topic and feel like I've left with a deeper understanding of the difficulties within the legal, political, and research contexts of human trafficking. If you want a chill prof where you'll learn a lot, definitely take this class.

Prof. Bowersox is easily one of the best professor at WashU. He has such a full understanding of the material which is crucial to how I interacted with the content. He is super accommodating and if you communicate your needs (i.e. for an extension) he will gladly help. This is a professor who you can learn from in every single interaction!

Zach is a really chill professor, has a great sense of humor, and very knowledgable. Can ask good discussion questions and runs great office hours, I could always get help if needed. My one caveat with the course (Human Rights) was how broad it was, if you want a more theory based class or more in depth as opposed to survey, not the right class.

Prof. Zhang clearly tries his best to teach but the overall course policies need to be restructured. Grading criteria are unclear, midterm exam worth 30% has very little opportunity for partial credit, and instructions for the final project are very vague and easy to lose points.
You learn a lot of things in the class, but the exam ends up being based on whatever topic he decides to focus on. There is no clear rubric at all, and the grading expectations feel very unclear.

Numerical calculation matters the most. I'm pretty sure he'll give full credits even without any step by step solution as long as you get the "correct final answer". He doesn't give credits for understanding i.e. set up equations the correct way but make calculation mistake? -30 points.

Punitive grader and very unforgiving of any mistakes. Small mistakes can cost 20–30 points and late policies are heavily penalised. Because assignments with penalties can't be dropped, missing even one can significantly impact your final grade.

The midterm carries a very heavy weight but contains very few questions, meaning that making a mistake on a single problem can destroy your final grade. The final project's grading is based completely on the professor's personal preferences rather than any clear or transparent criteria. Expect attendance right before/after breaks or final class.
I wish the professor can read the comments about him and make some changes. I respect his passion in the subject, but the class has been a disaster to take. Consider carefully before enrolling.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgable about the topics however, he extremely unorganized and does not stick with the syllabus. It is very difficult to keep up with the quizzes and the quizzes are weighted heavily.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: As others have said, the slides are amazing. If you put in the time to review the slides and re-solve the example problems before tests, you'll be fine. Beware that he's a stickler about notation--it is very easy to lose points (they add up) over a missed carat or non-standard variable name. Don't miss the attendance quizzes and you'll be fine.

very unclear and harsh grader, will take points off for many things & is condescending irl. both midterm averages were 70 (worth 30% total) and he doesn't curve. doesnt provide opportunities to increase your grade. boring lecturer (just use the slides, which are kinda confusing but better than lecture). just avoid this class....diffeq was easier!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the WORST Professor at Wash U. Take 328, never take this guys class. He is not understanding, lectures are very slow and has made the semester for me so much worse.

Not as bad as people say. May be a little condescending, office hours are questionable at times. Always tries to show up excited, genuinely interested in the material. Lectures get a bit boring towards the end of the semester, also review the material outside of class. HW's are on the easier side, exams are tough. Good luck!
Awful professor. Run!!!!!

I hate this man. Never take a class with him. I went to office hours once to ask him a question and he laughed at me and said my question was common knowledge. Everything he says is on the slides so it's not like you even need to go to class except for the pop attendance quizzes. Only one midterm and the average was 70 (and he doesn't curve).
Cannot articulate crucial conceptual points across and is the worst teacher at WashU. he claims to follow his syllabus yet refused to drop my lowest homework which he clearly stated in the syllabus
DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

The previous exam and quiz were both okay, but the final project score for the group was very unclear and heavily compressed. Our group completed the task according to the description provided, but still deducted a lot of points in the end, and he didn't have a chance to argue with you. Don't come to his class!!!

Professor Zhang clearly tries his best and always teaches with a smile on his face, but lectures are very monotonous and it's very easy to get completely lost. On the bright side, his slides are very helpful and he's fairly responsive on Piazza. The course content itself is very theoretical and proof-heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I recommend taking CSE 417 rather than Zhang's ESE 417. Zhang gives droll, useless lectures. He gives frequent in-class quizzes that are graded strictly, he does not tolerate notation that does not match his own. Additionally, he times attendance checks just before breaks to ensure students can't go home early. He is an unkind, unhelpful teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only one thing: run away from this professor!
Terrible lecturer and an extremely harsh grader. Will take 10 points off your quiz for a single notation.
Terrible lecturer who does a horrible job at explaining concepts. Extremely harsh grader who will take points off based on grading criteria that were never specified.
I can tell he really tried at the beginning, and it turned out that the first few lectures were great. Then he ended up literally reading off the slides.

He just reads off slides. Is a tough grader, and really feels like he puts no effort into teaching at all. I have never been more bored in a class then his stats class and I learned absolutely nothing I feel like.

So many unanswered Piazza posts. He put in some effort and tried to explain the concepts but just ended up reading from the slides. Open book/notes for quizzes and exams and you can get most answers from following the slides examples.
Dr Zhang is a strict grader and all of his quizzes don't have any reference to what is taught in his class. His lectures can get boring because he reads off of the lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Seldom answer students questions on piazza Tough grader on quiz
He simply doesn't care about his students. He rarely answers Piazza questions and assignment instructions are vague. TAs also aren't helpful. Programming sessions are useless.

Seldom answer the students' questions on piazza. Give the marks according on his mood and distribution line. A  liitle bit of stubborn on his teaching level. In summary, do not choose him except no choices.
Dude is a terrible teacher.

He is a decent lecturer, but it sometimes can be hard to understand what he is saying. His slides are amazing and are sometimes better at teaching than him. Assignments are graded very generously and all exams are open notes. I left this class learning a lot, but I recommend starting the homework earlier because they take time.

Prof. Zhang needs to work on two things. 
1) Fixing his lecture slides so that they are readable and let alone understandable. You spend most of your time in class trying to decipher the information on slides rather than learning any ideas and connecting them. 
2) Figuring out more relevant ways to test us on machine learning concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures left much to be desired as he read off slides, and if the projector died, he wouldn't fix it. Little to no examples were provided during the lectures, making the quizzes and homework challenging. There were sparse guidelines for the final project but a lot of expectations for style, content, etc.
Overall, a good professor. Concepts are illustrated clearly in the lecture slides.

Simply reads off of the slides. Gives very vague answers to piazza posts. Once class was over, he sent a random email at 9 am in the morning stating that you need to send in a proof that you completed course evaluations now as he is entering the grades, rather than giving students more time to send the proof. I saw the email only 2 hours late.

I regret taking this class. He just doesn't know how to teach this. Running late on course content, pop quiz worth 30% of grade, exam before HW answer and right after class), the average for the final was around 75, but he does not do anything about it. I recommend taking 3200 or section 02.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Jinsong Zhang is not only a bad teacher but is also incredibly not nice. His lecture notes are incredibly opaque, and his notation is often awful and inconsistent. It would be ok if he was willing to be more helpful out of class, but instead he is rude and unhelpful. I spent most of my time learning from other sources online. What a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The midterm was really bad... half of the material in the test was covered during the prior class, leaving us minimal time to do the homework for practice, prepare the cheat sheet, and review all the material. Only four multiple-part question on the test. If one does not know how to do the first part, one is screwed for the question...

Great professor. His powerpoint lectures are well organized and he breaks down machine learning topics in a clear and understandable way. There is not an overwhelming amount of homework, and the TA support was very helpful. The grading was fair. The coding sessions are useless, though.
1. Does not permit the use of laptops in class. Totally a technophobe :( 2. Doesn't provide cheat sheet in exams. Wants you to make your own :( 3. Good Person tho. Lets you turn in hw late :)

Idk how he is in Prob Stats, but Signals and Systems with Zhang is... bad. When I told an upperclassman engineering student who was teaching this class, he reacted with surprise and a small amount of horror. - restrictive tech policy (no laptops for notes) - disorganized lecture - textbook is more comprehensive than lecture - not easy to talk to

My goodness, I'm going to be honest here. Calling this class probstats is a lie. He teaches everything (including statistics) using probability, meaning that you leave the class slightly more useless than when you started. Also, don't expect to rely on any intuition that you might have gained in a high school stats class. Very, very theoretical.

Though he has minor accent, his class is very well prepared and organized, and he tries to make student engeged. The homework and small tests are a lot, but they do focus on lecture materials and you'll be fine if you listen to the lecture carefully. I will recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pretty average professor, provides decent lectures but is pretty soft spoken. The PowerPoint slides are pretty succinct. Homework is pretty long and graded harshly. The exams were reasonable but not easy. Just keep up with the work and dont slack off. He likes quizzes.

Zhang is a good professor overall. His slides are organized and you can find everything from the slides. He gives lots of proofswhich is also part of the tests and exams. Slides is the success to this class! Homework problems are long, but they really ensure you to understand the material. You can do well if you really spend time on it.

Zhang knows his stuff pretty well, and his lecture PowerPoint slides are not bad. He synthesizes the textbook pretty well and is usually available for office hours. The homework grader is pretty picky, so do the homework carefully over the weekend. Keep up and study, lots of quizzes! You can get an A if you really work for it.

Zhang is a very organized professor, and if you are able to understand his slides and examples you will be ok with the class. He does assign long weekly homework assignments, but doing these really ensures you understand and are learning the material. Cares for students and will make an effort to help you if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The worst prof I had in college. Lectures are extremely hard to understand- his English is terrible which makes it hard for him to explain stuff clearly. Slides are just a copy of definitions/examples from textbook. He takes attendance so a lot of students just show up and sit in the last row. Tough grader, doesn't give curve. 8 exams in total.
Lectures are very organized and clear, although can be boring at times. Prof. Zhang does give a lot of homework and has a lot of tests throughout the semester to make sure you are keeping up.

Excellent person who really cares for his students.  Lectures can be very long and boring, but his in-class examples are important to pay attention to since they are very similar to the homework problems and tests.

Zhang makes the lecture so boring it is a pain to sit through the class. Worst part is he can't really explain things well and this is very bad for a math class with a lot of understanding involved. The weekly homework can be very challenging to do. He also gave an exceptionally hard final to separate the grades among students.

The class material itself is boring and he makes it way worse by not able to explain things well. The homework is very tedious and can be really long. Tests are easy enough if you understand the material well, which a lot of people find hard with him teaching.

The kind of person that would talk about politics and war at Thanksgiving dinner and thinks he is the funniest person in the world. No rubric for his assignments. Slides won't be online. Would leave a tiny writing space on quizzes and expect you to write a novel there.
The grading rubric is so unclear. Feedback given and grade itself are unclear and unfair as well.

Class is not as "free" as some people suggest -- still easy, but he made it slightly harder due to feedback. Attendance is now mandatory (sign-in sheet) and later quizzes required notes from prev lectures. Content is genuinely super interesting (lwk wish I paid attention earlier instead of playing Tetris) and would totally take his other courses.

He's really funny and his lectures are actually pretty interesting if you pay attention. There are also a lot of extra credit opportunities. The writing assignments aren't too bad but it's sometimes not super clear what he's looking for. The hardest part of the class was waking up at 8:30 but I would definitely take it again :)

The instruction is so unclear.He often fail to follow any consistent criteria.Even when criteria are provided,no one seems to care about grading fairly. People who skip most classes receive the same participation grade as who attend EVERY SINGLE class.People who complete their work beautifully often receive worse grades than those who do it roughly
Don Not like his class.
I Do not think that his grading is fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: His class is fun to take! I had zero knowledge about this topic, and he encouraged me "You are born to learn this." All assignments can be done by Internet (namely ChatGPT), even if he found out, he will only talk to you without any penalty or redo for the assignment. Overall, it is a great pleasure to take his class!!!

Professor Ma is amazing. There are so many extra credit opportunities and he responds to emails super fast. Pay attention to class and do well on quizzes and attend the subsection to ensure good grades.

Amazing lecturer, I'm so happy I took him for Chinese Civilization. This class goes through a deep history from ancient civilization all the way up to today. Interesting discussion sections once a week. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Keep up with the material (don't procrastinate) and you'll do good on the quizzes. I hope to take Prof Ma again
Professor Ma is one of the nicest people I have met at WashU. Try to get as many extra credits as you can. The lecture is enjoyable to listen to and the material is easy to learn.

Dr. Ma is a great guy and a very well-respected scholar in his field. He lectures for a while with pretty generic slides but has interesting things to say. One day per week is a discussion section on the readings. Each week there is a short-answer essay quiz based off the readings. Also has outside of class events you have to attend. Cool class

Awesome professor. Like another comment said, my only qualm was that his lecture slides didn't have much on them so note-taking was just scribbling down passing phrases. Very interesting class though, and he's a super funny person.

Professor Ma is such a kind man! Expert on US-China relations and Chinese history in general. He also oversees the undergraduate Chinese major. Super nice guy. Chinese Civ class had a lot of readings, but the grading was easy (drop 3 lowest weekly quizzes, participation, and attend 3 outside events). No final. Lots of extra credit opportunities too
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Ma is both hilarious and incredibly knowledgeable. Class is always pretty engaging and the homework was doable, although sometimes reading-heavy. The only problem was he did not have good lecture notes, he just talks the entire time. Otherwise a great professor.

Knowledgeable about Chinese studies. Perhaps one of the most engaging professors I've met at WashU. Cold-calls students in class, but in a way that's not intimidating. Expectations for assignments could be clearer, though. In general, the class's topic (U.S.-China relations) is pretty important.
The scale of grading is weird

The problem with Professor Ma was that he was, to a degree, unclear about the expectations of his class. His lectures tended to ramble, and it was never obvious what he expected us to know from the texts or derive from his presentations in class. The guest lecturer who taught about half the course was even more disorganized. I learned very little.

Very funny and sarcastic teacher. Likes to lecture a lot but other than that the class is a lot of fun. Very insightful about modern China since he experienced it himself. I?wouldn't say the class is easy it has a decent amount of workload. But professor Ma is a very fair grader. You will do fine as long as you do all the work.
He is a great professor. He lectures A LOT but if you can deal with that then take his class. IT's very fun.

Great teacher! Has a bit of an accent but is always willing to help his students excel. He's a great lecturer and knows what he's talking about. Understands that we have other commitments and is willing to make deadlines work for us. Very sarcastic and funny.
Professor MP is one of the most amazing professors WashU has to offer. He really does care, and that makes it very difficult to NOT want to do well in his classes. Lock in, he's a great dude.

Professor MP has to be one of the best at WashU. He has relevant readings that are actually interesting, he cares about his students and class discussions leave you filling fulfilled. This course just had just a couple papers. As long as you did your best and actually cared about the class, you succeeded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS. Professor MP is amazing and very caring about his students. This class does have a lot of readings but it is very manageable and if you need any extensions for writing an essay all you have to do is ask. This class is very heavy on communication and participation!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super interesting class. The class is discussion based and he does a great job posing interesting questions and conveying big ideas. The workload isn't bad, you read 3 medium books, 4 essays (2-4 pages), and a few texts and movies. Really friendly nice teacher who has super interesting ideas. Anyone can do well.

Black Masculinities is one of the best classes I've taken at WashU. MP is engaging and makes the class fun and interesting. Workload is manageable. There are 3 essays, one presentation, and a final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: In the Cultural History of Hip Hop class, he and Fenderson would bring in their own personal items so as to transport students back in time so as to trace Hip Hop's history. Incredibly charismatic and caring, MP is one of the best.

I took the Hip-Hop ampersand which isn't a "real" class, but MP made it feel like one while still having a lot of fun. You can tell he cares so much for each of his students. The class was pretty discussion-based, but MP always made discussion prompts interesting and approachable. Take a class from him if you get the chance!!

MP is literally one of the best professors at WashU. No matter what course you take with him, he makes the content very engaging and you get excited to come to class. He is so supportive and is great to go to for office hours to chat about the course or anything else you may want to speak about. 10/10 recommend for AMCS and AFAS courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awesome, engaging, cool professor. Why aren't more teachers like this?

Took Black Feminist Theory (SOC 3003) with Professor Luna, and I had a good time. She can be a bit blunt, which may be why she doesn't have great reviews on here, and her lecturing can be long. However, you learn a lot, and she answers questions well. She gives out plenty of reminders for assignments, so you always know what's going on.

Frankly, I'm shocked Luna has such poor ratings. I found her kind, genuine, passionate, incredibly knowledgeable, fair, accommodating, and interesting. She is a true expert in her domain which makes learning Black Feminist Theory from her amazing. I was a bit skeptical at first, but she quickly won me over - I think she's a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: all of the other reviews are right that sometimes she comes off as passive or uninterested. but i truly believe that it just takes a second to warm up to her and when she gets used to you; she is very kind and helpful. just make sure to show up to class and participate and youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wouldn't take this class again if I had the option to. Isn't clear about participation being graded and lectures are boring and aren't engaging. Doesn't list any of the assignment guidelines online and is often hard to understand what exactly she is grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Luna is very knowledgable about her field of sociology, but she has no idea how to teach. She was probably one of the worst teachers I've ever had. Her lectures consist of mumbling and off-topic information. When we do have discussions, they are boring and unhelpful. Classes only have like 4 grading criteria with no rubrics. Please do not take!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She is unapproachable and condescending when it comes to questions. The class is very interesting, and it is unfortunate that her personality tainted my experience in the class. She gave me an extension for an assignment due to illness and revoked it because my submitting a discussion post showed that I was no longer sick.

Beware. Lectures are bumbling/incoherent and only summarize the assigned readings. Conflicting explanations of instructions. Easy grading but wouldn't suffer though the class again. No class discussion(only happened once, when we asked specifically). Students do not feel comfortable asking questions, and she rarely provides a useful answer.

The worst class I have taken at WashU. Luna has tons of requirements of expectations she does not make clear, she communicates in a condescending fashion, and she only has like 5 things making up your grade but with no rubrics for anything. She interrupts students and claims to be a discussion based class but rarely allows for discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very poor instruction
If you study very hard you could maybe do ok. Just self study until you can take higher levels.
Bro just doesn't teach and just yaps off slides to push a political agenda, absolute sh*thole of a time in her class. DO NO TAKE. IF YOU NEED TO TAKE SPANISH, PLEASE SWAP.

Worst experience with a professor ever. This was basic Spanish, and I've done Spanish for ~2 years. Doesn't teach, just glosses over slides, only decent activity was when she was being watched. Textbook is also $250. She's not even a teacher, teaches only how it aligns to her ideas, and "it's this way but idk why it is." DROP/SWAP IMMEDIATELY.

Extremely subjective grader. Feedback on the group project was very contridictory and when addressed in the final report said it wasn't substantial enough. There is not clear grading guideline for the case write ups and sometimes I'd be taken off points for not going into enough detail when there is a limit on how long the write ups should be.

Minyuan is one of my favorite professors at WashU. The class is mainly focused on interesting lecture discussions. There are some assignments, but they are essentially graded on completion. Make sure to read the readings because she will cold call

One of my favorite professors at WashU. She truly cares about building relationships with her students and our learning. There aren't any exams or quizzes in her class - only readings, case memos, and a final project.

Professor Zhao constructed one of the most interesting courses I have taken at WashU. This class felt more like a higher-level discussion session than work since she is so engaging with the students- always interested in what we had to say! She does cold call, so be sure to read before class, but will always help you out if needed!
Professor Zhao was a fantastic professor. I learned so much even though there weren't even tests. Professor encourages participation and will twist your mind in a good way.

Minyuan is such an excellent professor! While she does like to cold call, class is really an engaging discussion. She ensures that all student's views are challenged. I honestly learned more from her class than any other Olin class I've taken. While lectures are very intellectually stimulating, the grading and homework is pretty minimal/easy. 10/10

Minyuan was an incredible professor! Her corporate and global strategy course was very engaging as she uses a mix of both lecturing and case studies to illustrate what we are learning in class. She cares about her students and is always available for clarifying questions or even just to chat! Arguably one of the best professors at WashU

Minyuan is one of the best professors I've had at WashU. She cares so much about her students and wants to see each one succeed. She leads discussions well and infuses humor into the topics. Participation really matters so make sure to read the cases and come to class prepared to talk about them in depth. Overall a wonderful person and prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Zach was awesome! Totally a goofy guy but hes hard to dislike, cares about his students and is clearly very smart and passionate about the topics. Lectures are pretty clear and if you pay attention and study the tests arent harder than they need to be.

short king, pretty goofy, but u can tell is smart as sh!t. why he kind of fine?? lectures pretty good, nice hair, test were challenging, but that comes with the nature of the class. study and you'll be fine. knows what he's talking about so he acc answers questions u have. do feel like he sm0ked a bIunt b4 class sometimes tho, take that how u will.
Great professor. Cares about his students and makes the classes adequately hard for the level of knowledge previously required.
Really cool guy and he clearly cares about his students. Lectures are interesting and he is clearly passionate. Tests are somewhat difficult, but manageable.

Professor Reagh is a very kind professor and seems like he truly cares about all his students. I really enjoyed his lectures, and he also seemed to have much better grad student TA lectures than most of my other classes. He is a very fair professor and the grading is also very forgiving.

Zach seems to be a great person; However, as a professor I felt his lectures were a bit disorganized, unlike other biopsychological classes. Some of the quiz and test questions I felt were trick answers but he also makes sure to throw in some easy questions as well. Overall I would say his grading criteria for papers is fairly clear.

Enjoyed and found him to be a good teacher overall. Personally was not the biggest fan of his humor and sometimes I wish language used to describe the science was more formal. Some test and quiz questions were ambiguous. I found Dr. Reagh to be a nice and caring professor, and I think many people vibe with him, I just did not particularly.

I really like Reagh as a professor: he was really funny and down-to-earth. However, this class is one of the more challenging psych classes in my opinion. There is a lot of material and the tests can get very specific. Regardless, if you have to take it, I would take it with Reagh.

Entertaining lectures and funny guy. Test questions are very particular and specific -- you can know the study guide by heart and do badly on the tests. Exam and testing security is horrendous so you get put in an awful situation where you either cheat like 1/3 of the class is doing, or take the L and get a poor score on the test.

Zach is awesome. His lectures are fantastic and provide everything we need for tests. He outlines all the content concisely and reiterates specific topics. The tests can be challenging, but it's cause the content is difficult. I wish he would incorporate the quizzes after each lesson, like a lecture review quiz, so we could encode content better.

Zach is super friendly and material covered in lecture is interesting. The exams are harder than they need to be because the multiple-choice answer choices are convoluted and written with confusing syntax. Unfortunate because I understand the material well but pick the wrong answers due to misunderstanding sentence meaning.

Zach is so open and engaging with his students in and out of the classroom. He is very accommodating and understanding of unforeseen circumstances. Clearly, he wants his students to do well. Cog Neuro is a basic psych class... lecture-heavy with tests/quizzes, but with him, it is very interesting and fun. Best psych class I've taken at WashU!
This was a very great class, but the lectures were very fast. However, he is a very great professor, and he leads an amazing course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures can cover lots of material. Expect to spend significant amount of time reviewing notes. But his exams and grading policy are very lenient.
He leads a great class, but it is very lecture-heavy, and taking notes during lectures can sometimes be stressful. Overall, he makes the class very interesting and enjoyable.
Zach is one of the best professors I have had at WashU. He displays care for both the content he presents and his students. Every lecture, I walked away having learned something interesting.

Prof. Reagh is an interesting lecturer, and is very accessible if you have any questions after class. Grades mainly based on four exams (drop lowest one), and online quizzes (drop lowest 1/3). Exams are mostly multiple choice with around 4 short answers, average is high. Overall fun class! Would recommend.

I would not argue the fact that this man is technically qualified to be a professor. That being said, how he ended up choosing this profession is beyond me. It's a sad joke that people pay thousands of dollars for this course to receive nothing in return from this professor. It's frustrating that the quality of proffs. is this horrendous at WashU.

Prof Zhang had the toughest quizzes and final exam I have ever taken. Although he was very knowledgable about the topics covered, the language barrier along with unorganized writing on the board sometimes made it tough to follow along. He did not give much guidance when it came to how to study for the quizzes/exam. He had some funny moments I guess

Prof Zhang's lectures communicate material adequately but are very tedious. Practice problems done in class accurately represent homework and exams. However, he puts little effort into the class. All problems and lecture material are straight from the textbook, and he does not communicate with students outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Fuzhong is not a honorable person. He does not respect your time. In his world, he is a tenured professor and he earns a pre-set salary anyway. So he would assume you are the same. He does not care whether you achieve anything beyond drifting and passing the time. He has a dark character. If you do not satisfy him in his way, he would sabotage.

The lectures are long by being a 4 credit class, but he is fantastic at teaching. His notes and lectures are well organized and easy to understand, and he makes it very clear what concepts are necessary both through the lectures and the homework. I was never shocked by an exam. Never miss a lecture, that's at least how to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Throughout the entirety of this course I was very impressed with how clearly Professor Zhang was able to communicate his ideas. We did a ton of practice problems in class which were very helpful on the homework assignments.

Decent teacher. Has an accent which makes lectures hard to understand, but provides good resources to help study for his exams and his slides are very helpful. Also, the lab is run fairly well and he is willing to help you if you have a question/something isnt working. Tests are easy. Overall, decent professor, not amazing but not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor with so much practical knowledge. His labs are great place to explore and connect what you just learnt in his lectures.
He was an okay professor, his lectures were really unorganized and didn't teach you much. Most of the work is easy and the exams aren't hard if you do the HW's but he isn't that good of a professor

Love his teaching style. He connects theory with real-life engineering examples, and making complex topics easier to grasp. The labs are where everything comes together where you will find lots of teamwork and fun.
A great professor. He is interactive, humble, and genuinely invested in helping you succeed. His labs are always fun and engaging. Also expect an exciting but challenging group project.

He is truly one of the best professors in the department. Humble, kind, and always respectful. He communicates expectations clearly for both the lectures and the labs, and his classes are genuinely enjoyable. Even without course assistants, he was always active and present during the labs, offering help and guidance.
Thank you, Professor Manzoor.
The class isn't hard if you do a little bit of practice. The lectures are fine. Exams are simple. Labs are easy (ask professor questions).

He's fine. Not the best or the worst, but he kinda has no clue what's going on. Wouldn't choose him over another professor but wouldn't mind taking again. Very few assignments and they're not written super well. The lab is run very well though.

He's honestly a good professor, but needs a little more experience in order to effectively teach students in a way that instills understanding. I find him funny, but a lot of people don't get his humor. He's very helpful and knows what he's talking about. You just have to show enthusiasm to receive enthusiasm from him. Overall, great professor!
The class itself was pretty easy and straightforward. The professor tried to make the class engaging by including real-world scenarios and telling jokes.

Lectures have almost no structure, and the order of content throughout the semester doesn't make sense. Grading is unclear and varies every lab, TAs don't provide much help. Overall just very very unorganized. As a person, though, he's really funny and seems to really want students to enjoy the class; unfortunately nobody paid attention in lecture.

I always found him very enthusiastic and full of energy during classes and lab sessions. It's rare to have a prof who is actively engaged during the entire lab period. Whenever I raised my hand, he was there to help. One area for improvement could be providing clearer rubrics for the lab reports, which would enhance clarity and confidence.

I really liked his teaching style. He was very well prepared with very interactive lecture slides. His project part was fun but also very challenging. The lab part of the course is a great fun with easy lab activities.

Hard to understand, his labs are very easy but graded with an invisible rubric. His project is also graded with no rubric but instead whatever he feels like. Impossibly unreadable handwriting on chalk board. One of the worst professors I have had during my time here so far. 1/10 would not reccomend.

i'm not sure what's happened since I took her class compared to the other ratings, but she was a really tough grader. Classes were fun and she is awesome, but the assignments were challenging and she pushes YOU to figure out the how to make your work even better.

Laura is normally a really nice professor. Sometimes she's a little crazy, but very undemanding. I think she could push her students harder. You can get away with not very much work. At the end of every crit, even if the work isn't great she'll say, "But overall, VERY good work." :) I like her though. FUN projects!
fun class, she had really fun projects and was a pretty easy grader.  she let you know if she didn't like what you were doing, but loved stuff the majority of the time

Good overall - really cares about students. Can be a little crazy at times, but knows her stuff. I liked her 2D class because it was intense on nonobjective work, but some students didn't like the class for this reason. Work takes a long time; stickler for even paint surfaces on value scales. Picky where it counts, but pretty freeform overall.

This is definitely not an “easy A” course. The workload is heavier than expected. Also, some of the earlier 5-star reviews do not seem very representative of the average student experience. They read more like they were written by his previous PhD students rather than by typical students taking the class.

Jha clearly didn't spend enough time preparing for this course. He was frequently late for class. He never provided answers to homework assignments or exams. Every class felt rushed and disorganized. There was also never any meaningful feedback on the programming projects. I had to teach myself mostly. The content of this course was not practical.
This course is very boring. The professor's slides are of poor quality. Many important details are missing from the slides. We never received any feedback or answer keys for the tests and exams.

Though the homework takes some time, Jha tries hard to make sure no student is lost and can get good grades by giving lots of extra credits (Most people got A and A+). The most useful and inspiring class I've taken so far!
Definitely one of the easiest for BME electives. <4 hrs per week spent on this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jha is really good at teaching and knows what he's talking about. Exams/HWs/Projects were fairly ok. Easy A :)
One of my fav course at washu! class content is extremely interesting and let me see the world differently and critically. Would say one of the course that you should definitely take here.

There are lots of fun illusions and we learned the neural mechanism behind them. The content could def turned into a fun podcast. Prof.Abrams used lots of illustrations and demos during class which make things really engaging, and he had a good sense of humor. If you want to learn more about fun things in the world you should definitely take this!

His lectures are long and boring but you're forced to pay attention or else you'll fail the exams. No, the textbook doesn't help and neither does his review session. The exams are hard and long and 90% of your grade. Do not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good but difficult
Tests are worth almost 90% of the grade, insanely difficult and meticulous. Lectures are boring as hell. Really regret taking this class. Avoid this prof if you can

Definitely my favorite professor of all times! Prof. Abrams has a great sense of humor, and explains difficult concepts (such as neural networks) extremely well. The class is super engaging as there are countless demonstrations, many of which are interactive. The exams are graded on z-distribution, so 1) go to class & 2) read the book!
He is really confusing in lecture and his tests are very difficult. He doesn't seem very organized

Tough class overall. Should never miss a class and always take notes. The lectures are the most important. The exams are pretty tricky even though he said it's not at the beginning of the semester.Take the optional final (the questions are all from the last 3 midterms so it really boost ur grade)
Really good professor with great sense of humor. Exams can be tricky though. Lecture material is much more important than textbook stuff so try not to miss any classes.
hilarious! smart! and tamale!
Fantastic Prof! Tough, but fair grader.

Take his class pass fail and switch to credit if you end up doing well.  The demos are really interesting and Abrams has a great sense of humor. But even if you have memorized all the material for the exam, it is unusually hard to get an A.
Great class. Not the easiest but I would recommend Prof. Abrams above most of the other psychology professors. Lectures are very straightforward and concepts are well explained
Professor Abrams is great. Definitely take this class! He's a really nice guy and a good teacher too.
I love Abrams. The class is pretty hard in my opinion, but his enthusiasm makes for the topic makes the class pretty interesting. I'd take it again, but maybe pass/fail.
Professor Abrams is a really cool guy. Very interesting subject matter and the demos were super cool. You have to work hard to get a good grade but I'd definitely recommend this class.
Incredibly dull topic. Tests designed to make students do poorly. Don't take this class if you can avoid it.

Terribly boring and completely uninterested in students.  His statements and teachings are often refuted in class and he seems painfully unknowledgable.  He will make you hate Psychology.  The class could be made compelling by a better qualified individual.  bottom line: I strongly DO NOT recommend taking any classes taught by Professor Abrams.
Good teacher, relatively tough subject, easy tests
unclear and uninteresting
abrams doesn't care about his students at all or make any attempt to get to know them. his tests are full of trick questions. he thinks he is much funnier than he actually is.
well organized class, great review sessions, helpful when asked questions, and pretty funny.
No Comments

Tricky tests, hard info. Very tough class. Interesting demostrations, but when there aren't demonstrations you need a pillow. Grades on a pretty good curve. I would not take the class if I had it to do over.
Really interesting classroom demonstrations.  Very sciencey.  Tests are tricky because there is a lot of detailed info to learn.
Very dry sense of humor. Some really great demonstrations of different illusions.

This guy is the man. He is monotone and dry which makes him hillarious because he looks like a combination of Jerry Seinfeld and Ray Ramano. The class is straightforward--read the book and go to lectures and you will do well. Some class examples are pretty trippy.
Tried to make class time interesting with lots of experiements, tests were pretty easy if you studied his notes really well.
Very interesting class, though the concepts were difficult.
No Comments
prof abrams is the coolest
Arrogant, rude and boring - holy tenure! Where did this guy come from?
the class was interesting and he made it fun with his dry sense of humor and a whole array of optical and auditory illusions.

Great Prof!! Funny as hell if you have a dry sense of humor. I know his classes don't appeal to everyone since most psych majors don't care about cognitive psych but he teaches it well and tries to make it interesting for everyone by using lots of demostrations.
before the first test, he said "it's not like i'm intentionally trying to trick you-," but as the semester went on this statement seemed farther and farther from the truth
some material was pretty interesting, but after a while material and teaching got somewhat dry. material wasnt that difficult but tests were tricky and curve was pretty tough
Experimental isnt fun with any prof.  But abrams reminded me of a less witty seinfeld, amusing in pointing out striking absurdities.  class was entertaining.

only take sensation and perception if you like being bored to tears and have ever wanted to follow through with the "so painful i wanted to drill a hole through my skull with a pencil" threat.

He is so cold!  When phones went off he would just stare at the person, and when the TA's phone went off he made fun of him.  If you talk too loud he will just stop talking and stand there.  Material easy and interesting, but graded against class makes it HARD, 5 out of 70 A, 15 A-

Incredible professor. So clear and patient in the way she explains things, very easy to keep up with. I was dreading this class a bit because I have never been a math/stats person, but she had me convinced I would be a math major had I had her as a teacher in the past!!!
Great person

reviews.comment: EXTREMELY accessible and helpful

reviews.comment: Chiller prof
Love Jager down. So organized and made stats enjoyable. It has piqued my interest in future stats courses

This class is a moderately difficult class, but interesting and useful. The final project was really interesting. I like Jager a lot and she is really nice, but I don't love the way she formats her notes (even though it works great for most people). You should definitely take this class and Jager is great!

Gonna go against the grain here. I liked her and she gave very intuitive lectures but her tests were really difficult. Docked off points for minute errors (or just miscommunications) and I would often get into regrade wars with a TA. I also thought even though she was good at explaining, she was not at all entertaining. Had little motivation to go.
Favorite teacher in the stats department!
Nice teacher. 3200 is hard ans hard to get A, but she is really nice and helpful
Jager is a great professor that really cares about her students. Her lectures are great - if you show up, pay attention, and do the homework, you will have every opportunity to succeed in this class.

Jager is the best professor I've had at WashU. Her well-structured, follow-along notes make complex material easy to understand. She presents challenging topics in a clear, conceptual way that's easy to follow. Be thorough with the class notes—understanding them will set you up for success in exams and other statistics-based courses.
helpful when I asked questions, good lectures, usually prepares you well for the exam but I wish there were more review questions.

JAGER IS THE BEST! Her lectures reminded me of high school with easy to fallow notes. She was very accessible outside of class and would send out reminders for every important date. Content can be hard but I found exams generally easy except the last midterm which was needlessly difficult. If you have taken AP Stats class won't be too bad.

Best professor at WashU by far! Post lecture notes weekly so its super easy to catch up if you've missed a few lectures. Her lectures go at the perfect pace, HW and exams are pretty fair, textbook integrates seamlessly with lecture. Host office hours weekly, super helpful and patient.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are hard to take notes on unless you have an ipad. Nevertheless, Jager clearly cares about her students and makes tests manageable. Lots of homework that is graded on correctness though.

She's super kind and she's always happy to help. There is a lot of homework and her lectures cover lots of content really fast, but she teaches it very well given the short amount of time. Despite all that homework, it's a pretty easy class.
Super kind, breaks down the concepts really well. Pretty easy A in my opinion, just keep up with the homework and the tests'll be fine.
Icon. Learned more from her two classes than from the rest of the math department put together - wish the school had more professors like her!
Lectures are optional any easy to catch up on.

Dr. Jager possesses every quality you would want in a professor. Her lectures are clear and concise, her expectations for the class/assignments are laid out clearly, her exams and grading policies are more than reasonable, and she's an overall kind and caring person.

Jager is an absolute GEM. I had never taken stats before so was a little nervous for this course. She is gives exceptional lectures and is one of the best professors at explaining information in a digestible way. Even though I am not a stats major, I would 100% take another course just to have her as a professor again.
She's the GOAT in stats.

Best professor on campus. Def take her 2200 before taking 3200. The lectures are explained detailed and easy to understand, the hw are helpful. The final project is so easy can literally finish it in 1 hour.
The best teacher ever, and nothing to complain about. Just follow and listen to her class, and she will make your life easier. I wish she could teach more of my stats classes.

Definitely the best STEM professor I have had here at WashU so far. Though it is hard to point out a single highlight, she does just about everything you should expect from a great professor. Her lectures are perfectly clear, the exams are fair, and she is very helpful. I had a great experience and would strongly recommend taking a class of hers.

Dr. Jager is the standard. Crystal clear lectures with guided notes. Exams were overall straightforward. The final is a group project that should be relatively easy to complete and do well on. Respects the students and never talks down to them.
Just amazing idk what else to say. First math class I've enjoyed in a really long time and it ended up probably being my favorite class of the semester. I love you Abigail Jager

You can clearly tell she really knows her material and loves teaching. My biggest criticisms are sometimes it feels like we would learn a very theoretical concept and then go straight into challenging applications of that theory. Also, I wish we had more practice problems or some sort of a study guide for the exams.

Tests are 70% of the grade but are much easier than in class problems, and similar or easier than HW problems. Content slowly goes from a 2/10 to 8/10 in difficulty, but she is always eager to explain things and help. Weekly problem sets that take 1-7 hours. 60 minutes of required videos per week. I would take this class again if she is teaching
One of the best lecturers in the math department. Explains concepts extremely clearly and cares about the success of her students. Would highly recommend.
Amazing professor! I really liked that professor Jager included examples after to teaches a concept. Really helps to fully understand new ideas. If you need a math course this is the one!

Had a great experience w/ 1011! Easy enough class, especially for non-STEM majors. Office hours were incredibly helpful and she was very understanding. She records every lecture, so you're only required to go for in-class activities. I would recommend the class to everyone.

Professor Jager is the BEST math professor i've ever had! Maybe even best professor ever. She cares a lot about her students and their wellbeing. If you are confused with anything in the class, just go to her office hours she will make sure you understand all the material before you leave. I also love how organized her class is!! She's amazing!

Jager has been one of the best professors I've had at WashU. She delivers clear lectures, and always posts review for the exam. I personally liked her teaching style of having fill-in notes. It is a sort of grindy class with 3 midterms, daily hw and quizzes, and a final project, but you can definitely succeed in this class.

Prof. Jager is the best math professor I encounter at WashU. She gives good lectures and is very accessible outside of class. The workload for this class is very manageable. Exams are also not difficult. Definitely deserves a 5 star.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jager is pretty much all you could want from an introductory stats teacher. She explains concepts clearly. In-person lecture attendance is optional, and you'll do great with a combo of recorded lectures on Zoom and reading the textbook. An easy class but definitely not a blow off class.

Professor Jager teaches a great class. 3211 is a lot of material by nature and it can get overwhelming. She was very helpful and accessible after class, during office hours, etc for any questions. Exams were allowed a cheat sheet of formulas. Definitely would take it again, one of the coolest stats professors in the department!
Very easy basic stats class. Starts from the basics so everyone can follow. So streamlined and clear, you always know what the expectation is.

(I took 3211 not 3200)
Jager was super helpful, grades were mostly based on exams but if you kept up with the notes and homework you'll be fine.

Dr. Jager's lecture is amazing!! She is definitely a gem at WashU. Try to go as many in-person classes as you can (although I barely went and thus got an A-). It is not easy to earn an A in MAT 3200 and you have to do some extra questions if you want to earn an A.

Absolutely a gem, you can tell she cares about you and you doing well in the class. She will take time to help you even outside her office hours. She is very helpful and answers any questions you may have about the material.

Dr. Jager is enthusiastic about teaching statistics and is a genuine person. Her caring demeanor makes going to lecture worth it. She answers questions with a smile and makes sure you walk away with a solid understanding of the answer. 2200 has some work outside of lectures but as long as you're willing to put in effort, it's very easy to get an A.

Jager has only 5 star reviews on RMP and rightfully so. On the first day, she shares an online link to the textbook so everyone can access it for free. All of her lectures are clear on every topic and she is very accessible inside and outside of the classroom. 2200 is a very easy class for anyone that is mathminded or not and I recommend it highly!
She's super sweet, incredibly easy to understand, very clear in her explanations. Maybe the best STEM teacher I've ever had.

I had already taken Stats so the class was not difficult, but my AP score was a 4 so it wasn't accepted. Overall she has been one of my favorites so far (I'm a Fr.), lots of enthusiasm, reminds me some one you wish was your mom. She is open outside of class and responds to emails well. First exam is mean median and mode so not much studying needed.

I love Professor Jager! She is one of the kindest people I've met and is great at explaining concepts. The notes are given to you ahead of class so you can print them out and fill in the blanks. This made it so easy to learn the material. She always uses super clear examples and there are no trick questions on any of the exams.

Loved her! Super smart and inspiring. Her lectures were so clear and straightforward and they were posted on canvas every day in case you couldn't make it to class. Tons of points in the gradebook, so you can still make a good grade even if you mess up an exam. Super nice woman overall and very helpful to everyone!

Professor Jager is amazing! She is super nice, cares about her students, is always available to answer questions and help, and teaches with real examples and explanations rather than abstract mathematical theory. She wants all her students to succeed.

Professor Jager is such a great professor. She is so nice, super caring, and explains the material so well. She explains things so thoroughly (sometimes too thoroughly!) and makes the material easy to understand.

Prof. Jager is great! She makes clear, helpful, and interesting lecture videos. After taking Math 3200, I really want to change my major to statistics or math. A lot of that has to do with Professor Jager and Noroozi. Thank you!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the nicest professors I've ever had, Prof. Jager cares more about her students understanding concepts than any other professor. She uses real-life examples that make understanding the concepts feel useful. The three exams were very easy and the homework is easy as well, just learn the information. Very easy intro class overall.

Everything you would want in a math teacher, in my opinion. Extremely clear lectures that make note taking a breeze. Teaches concepts in a consistent manner, so you can see the similarities between different units. Also teaches in a way where you can easily apply concepts to homework and exam problems. Very kind and accessible outside of class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Abby has the most amazingly structured classes I have ever taken! The fill in lecture notes are really thorough (but get right to the point) and easy to follow. Expectations are clear in this class, she sets you up to learn the material well which makes for no surprises. And she's incredibly friendly and accessible! This class made stats enjoyable.
She's amazing and so so nice. She is super responsive to emails and one of my favorite professors at Washu. She really cares and wants to see her students succeed!

I took the morality and markets course. Prof Van Engen is a great dynamic professor that keeps lectures engaging, however this class was unnecessarily difficult. Two essays amounted for 60% of the total grade, and the high on one of those essays was a 95... Do not make the mistake of taking this class for an easy elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took Morality and Markets and had a really great experience. Make sure to participate because they track it obsessively, and will screw you over in the end if you don't participate when the semester ends. Readings are intriguing, and the comic duo with the other professor is fun. There is more work than you'd initially expect for such a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I enjoyed having Professor Van Engen in Morality and Markets. He's a really funny and caring guy, and what he expects from you is clear. One mistake I made was not participating enough in the course, so make sure to do that if you decide to take it. Overall, the concept of the class is very interesting (business and morality), so do consider it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Morality and Markets and Professor Van Engen. He is so interesting, funny, and has great insights. This class is the best. Participate because they do track that. Do your reading because it will make the class more interesting and the books are good. This class and professor are great!!!

Had Prof. Van Engen for Morality and Markets. He's not bad at all. Encourages participation and is willing to meet outside of class. The class grades you not only on your essays, but also on your in-class participation, so raise your had and talk. Limited to no feedback on assignments by TAs, which is frustrating at times. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Van Engen is just such a nice guy and such a good professor. He took a subject I frankly didn't have much interest in and made it fascinating because you could tell he was so passionate. He's so kind and really wants all of his students to succeed. Not an easy grader per se, but not too tough either.
Van Engen is one of the best English professors I've ever had. He is so passionate about teaching, and has so much knowledge. I would highly recommend taking any class with him.
She knows her matetial and links everything we learn to real life experience.

Love her classes. She cares about us.
I learnt a lot from her.

reviews.comment: She knows how to teach. I advise other professors to learn from her.

Horrible professor, she explains nothing never answers questions in class or clarifies how grading works, never returns grades on assignments and the final was on material we were never even taught. Worst professor I've had at WashU

Professor Abraham is a good professor. He is rather lecture-heavy but his tests and papers are doable. I ended with an A in the class and I never felt as though I was working super hard to get it. If there is one thing to note about him, it is that he PRIORITIZES ATTENDANCE. Don't skip class. If you are taking a religion class, take him.

Professor Abraham just recently transferred to GMU and I took his Religion 100 class this semester. Overall, he's a good professor but his lectures can get boring. There is a quiz due every other class day but you can take them up to 10 times and they're based off of the readings.  He always encourages us to go to his office hours (cause he's new.)
