reviews.comment: Very interesting lectures and super helpful. Great professor and really understands the material. Keeps everyone engaged and interested
Tough grader, Boring lectures, Always takes the same side.

The best professor I've had at Wash U, I can't recommend him enough. Genuinely interested in student opinions, makes complex material fun and easy to understand. Highly available and helpful outside of class. If you're considering taking a class with him, do it.
Abraham was a pretty funny guy. Class was a little dry at times, but the quizes/tests/papers are all ridiculously easy.

Easily the best professor I've had at Wash U. An all around great guy, he makes discussions fun and engaging. If you're considering taking a class with him, do it. You'll be glad you did. (And ask him about his feelings on Marvel v. DC :))

FANTASTIC professor!  Engaging lectures, interested in student views, even if they contradict his own, and stimulates great class discussion.  Do the readings and come prepared, but it's absolutely worth it for the best class I've had at WashU.  Also really cares about his students and is more than willing to help if you need it.  Great guy!
He was very helpful
He was great. Very approcable.

An eminent authority in his field; his feedback on my work was critical but right on the mark, and made my rethink many positions I was previously certain of. Without doubt a real scholarly asset to the university, and to his area of work.
Lectures are extremely dull and pointless, he is not available for help outside of class. Do not take this course!

Lectures were excruciatingly boring and completely unnecesary because all he does is read an outline (no depth) that he has made from the reading. He's not really a nice person; he doesn't respond to my emails and you can't talk to him in person becaues his english is bad.

Good professor who is very down to earth with the students. Had some very entertaining lectures, especially when diving into the conceptual connections to real life on the subject matter. Other lectures that were focused on solving mathematical problems could be boring and tedious.

Professor Ahn is incredible. Hilarious, engaging, and clearly understands economics. Lectures at a very quick pace and you often have to look back at notes to understand the material, but he provides a running list of notes for reference (no slides or lecture recordings). Practice exams and problem sets are nearly identical to exams.
Tests were hard but he had a good curve, lectures were boring but he knew the subject well

Firstly, I want to acknowledge that Professor Ahn is an amazing person. He is very funny and cares about his students. However, his lectures are difficult to follow, and he doesn't always fully address questions when asked.
exams are curved but were pretty difficult, good lecturer but moves quick
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's funny and has a few entertaining stories but his lectures felt rushed and were unclear. The majority of us were confused, and the only reason why I did ok on exams was because I studied A LOT for each exam. His handwritten slides were hard to understand in and out of class, but I heard other micro professors had slides in the same format.
funny guy but cannot teach. most lectures were entertaining but didn't learn much relevant material unless studied outside of class.

Professor Ahn is a really funny guy and cracks a ton of jokes during class. His lectures are heavy with content but if you put in a bit of effort, do the homeworks, and make sure to relearn concepts you don't know, you will do well in his class. Homeworks help a lot and his tests are very fair in my opinion.
Great guy and good teacher. He cares!
Bad lecturer. Most of your grade is exams but good curves.

Ahn is a funny guy and personable, cracks lots of jokes about gambling and poker. However, when it comes to teaching, there's room to improve. Sometimes very unclear about the material, and there are typos on almost ever single assignment/exam which is frustrating. The material itself isn't hard, but I went to office hours every Wednesday!

Horrible lecturer even though the class is lecture-based. He also makes typos on every HW and test, even the final! Very carless, both about his work and about the students. He does occasionally go on interesting tangents but those don't make up for how badly he teaches. Exams are most of your grade btw, so be ready for that. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ahn is a funny guy, as he would constantly share his passion for gambling, but he isn't really good at lecturing. He seemed to make topics harder than it should've been and sped through lectures. He also changed the format of the tests to include more MCs than FRQs which made the tests more difficult than previous years.

Speeds through lectures, definitely knows his stuff but does NOT know how to teach. Practice tests before midterms were a breeze compared to the real thing. Doesn't care about the students. He loves to tell us that "grades don't matter" but also makes it hard to do well in his class. You really have to teach yourself bc lectures are SO unclear
One of the best professor's I've ever had, solely due to his lectures. They are so entertaining and awesome. Class isn't too much work and the tests are straight forward.

Interesting guy, talks about random things in lectures. Practice exams and answer keys FILLED with errors that really inhibit learning. Not a horrible class if you do all the practice, but plan on reaching out to TA's a lot to get clarification on incorrect solutions.
lectures are usually pretty interesting.

Professor, he's a caring dude, but the lectures he makes is not good. For his tests, do the previous practice test to ensure your success. Also go to office hours for the problem sets, it may or may not be helpful. During class he does make interesting points not related to the lectures.

Lectures are okay but he can ramble and the class loses focus/understanding. Material can be manageable but he makes exams a bit tougher and will admit this. He doesn't seem to care too much about the students and their success (e.g. canceling OH exam weeks). Overall, a fair class made harder than needed.
Good lecturer

Professor Ahn is an absolutely outstanding person and teacher. He is not only extremely intelligent/knowledgeable on the subject, but he is also accomodating and understanding for students who are struggling outside of class. He gives extensions as needed and knows that we are trying our best. He is definitely a top WashU professor.

Professor Ahn is a really amazing person. He truly cares about his students succeeding and was very accommodating when it came to helping students outside of class. He helped to make the difficult content as accessible as possible.

Professor Ahn is a friendly and approachable professor. He truly cares about his students. He understood that being in a once-in-a-century pandemic with little to no breaks could take a toll on students' mental health. Thus, he adjusted accordingly by being extremely accessible outside of class and giving students ample opportunities to succeed.

David is a fantastic person. Very funny and approachable. His lecture notes are usually really helpful. His practice tests are pretty accurate to the exam. Sometimes lectures are a little hard to follow. Really cares for his students. Highly recommend taking a class with David.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: She gives very lengthy and useful assignment feedback, is not an especially difficult grader, gives relatively little work, and is a kind person. But she gives rambling and boring lectures, assigns largely uninteresting readings, and gives assignments that feel worthless and don't contribute directly to your writing ability.
Professor Adams is so helpful and understanding. She is always willing to give extensions if needed. She is also a pretty easy grader and provides thoughtful feedback on your writing.

Although a bit disorganized, Professor Adams provides insightful feedback on essays in the form of voice memos, which I found peculiar. Also loved the heavier emphasis on nightmares in D&N. I don't think it's possible to get anything but an A in this class if you turn everything in and at least try a little bit. Also she's funny in an unhinged way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I genuinely had fun in this class. Prof Adams is such a nice and funny person and her method of teaching is very interesting. She may be disorganized at times, but I feel that makes the class even more exciting because it opens up new discussions that I would never have done prior. Super approachable teacher and always emails back quickly.

She tweaky af but she low-key chill. She talks to herself and mumbles but it's chill cause it doesn't usually pertain to you. She grades things a little late. she shows up to class late A LOT. lots of reading but you can usually just BS and get away with it. Any way it's a good class. As long as you show demonstrated effort, you will get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a fun professor who does not grade harshly, strongly recommend her class

Prof. Adams is very caring and gives excellent feedback on papers. Workload is manageable, but lectures can be dull. As others have said, she's disorganized. She's canceled class last-minute multiple times and takes a long time to grade papers.

Also, for D&N, she chooses a lot of horror media for assignments, so watch out if that's not your thing.
Rachel was amazing! She's a bit disorganized, but keeps class fun and engaging. She gives useful essay tips and is a nice grader. Definitely participate in class, that is really important!

Classes are unorganized. Takes her months to give feedback. She never submits grades so you never know what grade you have currently in the class Grading is tough and very unclear. Hard to learn from her.
Classes are extremely unorganized, and she never sends feedback timely. Grading is tough and very unclear. You can barely learn anything from her.
Professor Adams was great! I had her over the summer for FSAP. She is very helpful when you need it and class was very laidback. Would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really great professor. Knows how to keep things light, fun, and engaging. The Dreams and Nightmares theme is really cool to explore because you get to analyze interesting topics like the supernatural. The film analysis section is very interesting because it's something different than just analyzing text. Fun way to get the CWP credit.

Easy way to get your CWP credit. The short creative writing assignments at the beginning of the semester were fun and engaging while the longer essays had genuinely interesting topics (ex. metaphorically analyzing a movie) and were graded fairly. Minimal reading.

Professor Adler is an incredibly nice guy and a very compassionate, flexible instructor, which gives his class a more relaxed vibe that makes it a lot easier to actually learn. He throws out candy to his morning classes, doesn't give too much work, and actually teaches and helps students 1 on 1. GOAT professor
Prof. Adler is so nice, cares about his students, and teaches material in a compelling manner!
Adcock is a professor to be avoided. I cried about her class many times as she made me feel incredibly stupid no matter how hard I worked.

Very intelligent, but would be much better suited as a researcher than a professor. She is very abrasive in person and aggressive over email, no matter how nice you are to her. She shoots down any topic that explore impact of religion on SA, something I found blatantly offensive at times. I would not recommend taking her classes to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I LOVE Professor Adcock! She's really nice and helpful. The class isn't easy, but she will stand by you and help you along the way. Tough on papers, but will help. Fair on tests. She will only test on what's been discussed in class. LOVELOVELOVExmillion

She is very passionate about teaching and making sure students understand what she teaches. She grades harshly on papers but its not that bad. You have to go to class and take notes in order to do the papers. The midterm and final are ok but it require a little studying.
Very open to suggestions but very clear when lecturing on topics of great complexity
No Comments
Just take good notes and you'll be set.  You don't really need to read every week, but it helps.  Base your papers off class notes.
very enthusiastic...go to class, take good notes, and you have an A
Easy teacher. Nice person. Gives good notes in class. Tests are quite easy.

He assigns a lot of work and it's challenging and mostly massive scale with charcoal. You end up creating a lot of ugly work, but it's fun, and he's helpful and fun. I loved my TA (Meghan). He seems to lighten up towards the end of the semester, so it's fun and I learned a lot.

all the critique of jamie is warranted- he assigns a LOT of work, and definitely likes to hear himself talk. that being said, i liked him as a professor, and learned a lot in his class. assignments were interesting, though fast-paced. has some great technical feedback, but don't be afraid to push back against things that compromise what you want.
Tons of outside work, but you'll learn a lot, and he's a very genuine person

Jamie assigns a lot of work but wants you to succeed. He is very understanding of people having different interests within the art world. Though some of his assignments are annoying and maybe not what students are interested in, he makes it up by having the final project be very open ended, allowing students to be creative.

Jamie's assignments were ridiculously hard. His assignments were bizarre and forced us to create work that reflected poor taste. I hated his class- it made me question my artistic ability and interest in art in general.

Remarkably pompous, unrealistic workloads and expectations, never TAUGHT us anything, wasted time constantly in crits by talking about himself, and didn't bother to learn everyone's names (there were what? fourteen of us?).  In general, I hated every moment of being Jamie's student (if you could even call me that considering he taught me nothing.)
By far the best core drawing teacher. Encouraging grader and very nice man overall. Yes, workload is high, but completely worth it.
jamie's class is hard but i liked him. he's so enthusiastic and loves art and all the sketchbook assignments pay off. if you don't want to put effort into core drawing don't take his class.
Wonderful teacher- he seems very demanding, but in the end it pays off.

Adams is overrated in my opinion.  Slightly pompous.  A bit too interested in chatting and wasting time.  Advice is sometimes a bit vague and not practical.  Nice guy, but irritated me.  Wouldn't take another class of his.

Jaime has decent advice in crits, however he delays a lot of class time talking about himself. Its hard to get past his ego and at times he can come across as **** (though I don't think this is his intent) I didn't learn as much as I had hoped and I thought the final project was ridiculous.
Demands a lot of you; be prepared to work very hard outside of class. At times has a skewed view of how much a student can actually do.
Tough professor, but very helpful.  You'll improve a lot.  Lots of outside assignments (much more homework than other drawing classes).
No Comments
No Comments

Jamie is an amazing teacher. I made incredible improvements during the semester. He assigns a LOT of work, though and holds very high standards. Compared to the rest of the drawing teachers, it seems his students make the most progress.
Nice guy who gives good feedback. Absurd amount of work outside class, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is undeniably good at what he does, having shown some of his work in class.  However, His teaching methods are god-awful. I dropped that class after 4 weeks. In a drawing principles class, he had us recreating old paintings and sculpting stuff.  The workload he assigns is huge. The way he taught it always felt like I was doing  something wrong

Makes me hate drawing & want to switch out of art school( & i love art). So much work, that you actually dont even improve,cause you try to just finish the assignments. Spend all my time on his homework & it doesnt even pay off in terms of good grades. Cant focus on work for other classes. Good feedback if asked. Switch out while you can.

His drawing class is the hardest class I have taken. The workload borders on unreasonable, and I spent many nights up past 3AM to finish homework. Assigns work as if his class is the only one you take. He gives feedback if you ask for it and can be helpful. Picky in how he wants everything done. Two midterms and two finals. Picks pricey supplies.

Since this class was taken for an elective course, the skill levels varied a lot, making it difficult to grade subjectively; but if effort is put in then an A is basically guaranteed. Prof Cox is really great at what he does (painting, go look him up), so he'll be able to give you great feedback on your paintings without being too critical.

He can be helpful when he isn't playing favorites. Tends to ignore students who aren't sucking up to him.  Has quite an ego.  I do think he knows what he is talking about, but he doesn't meet the requirements of a graduate studio professor because he doesn't take an interest in each student's project equally in moving forward through semesters.
extremely thoughtful. passionate and knows what the hell he´s talking about. hes a baller!
Wasn't really helpful. Has a bit of an ego.

Prof Neiman is an exceptional professor who built an extremely interesting collection of readings & lectures. This has been one of my favorite and most educational classes at WashU. Last 2/3 of the class all reading-based discussion - easy to get by w/o readings but they're worth doing and interesting! Most of your grade is attendance/participation

Neiman is extremely passive-aggressive and lacks empathy for personal struggles and traumatic life events. Stg he thinks his class should be your highest priority and that any opinions countering his are invalid (I lost points on 2 assignments bc he disagreed with my opinions). I highly recommend that you avoid 3105 and Neiman at ALL costs!

The class structure is based on rotating tasks: one week you present on Thursday, next week you present on Tuesday, next week you review a film, and the week after that you get a break. Also a final project at the end (he lets you do creative things with it). Course content was interesting, certainly worth the work. Kind professor that cares.
I enjoyed Professor Austin's class. It was a good introduction into work-shopping and he is very kind. We read some interesting pieces as well.
He's a nice person, doesnt give feedback on writing, easy class!
Super nice and laid back guy.  Definitely made writing feel approachable regardless of your previous ability.

Professor Austin is a caring teacher, but we received no feedback on our work for the class. It was nice to earn good grades for putting in the effort, but I was hoping for more substantial feedback on my work. We also didn't really discuss readings and often jumped around randomly doing things that weren't in the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Austin is really supportive and cares about his students. College writing is not easy, and I earned a pretty low grade at the beginning of this semester. However, Prof. Austin is always there to help you. I just attend the office hour to talk about my essay, and then I did well in the end. Just take college writing with this professor.

Ron is the best. i hadn't had a good writing teacher until i had him for college writing. he offered to help me outside of class and reached out to me multiple times asking how each paper was going. he really cares about his students and he's also not very strict with deadlines. overall, a chill guy with interesting things to say about each reading

Ron is a really nice guy, definitely strange though. there's no way to describe it, he's just... different. he gives a lot of feedback during work time that doesnt necessarily have to do with the question you asked. it's a pretty chill class though and doesn't involve a lot of outside work. the projects are fun and he's funny+entertaining
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Decent teacher, both fun and frustrating. Here's the thing: he's crazy. Funny at times, and his laugh is great! However, art as a whole is such a subjective thing, and his interpretation of your art may be less than ideal. He's very scatter-brained and shifts due dates sometimes without warning. He assigns random side projects then forgets.

ron is a fun guy; rly interesting to hear him talk about clay. he's a v opinionated guy, and always ready w intriguing fun facts that you're never quite sure how to respond to. you have to put in Work outside of class, esp if you've never worked w clay before. ask him for help and he'll be helpful; otherwise, he'll mostly leave you to work in peace
nice professor and kinda odd but assignments are random

Ron is pretty scatterbrained and often disorganized. He's the kind of professor who would be super encouraging while you were working on a project but then criticize you during critique, making you wonder why he didnt say anything to you while you were working on things. lovable guy but definitely didnt learn much about 3d design

Ron can seem somewhat scatterbrained and (hate-to-say-it-but) illogical sometimes, but if you *ask* for help, he's incredibly helpful, and he usually surprises me with some wonderful insight during studio visits.  He's also very open to negotiating how things are going within the major and that flexibility is very nice.
Really funny and very involved in his student's progress and development as artists.
Classes with him are a lot of fun, and he's very available for help outside of class.
really fun, and a genius artist. very available for any help outside of class.
brilliant and hilarious.
Wonderful artist and very caring mentor.
Avoid him
This professor is one of my favorite professors at WashU

same as other review.The reason why he has gotten such good reviews is because people know him as a celebrity from a surface-level conversations with him
He would pretend to be warm-hearted but a little hypocritical and he was often mean to others when we communicate deeply
This guys a certified chiller, my dawg fr
easy teacher cse 107 is free

This class is unfailable. He teaches reasonable well, and sparks interesting conversations about data science and CS at large. Clearly very passionate about his subject especially when a guest is there.

Cytron is one of the best professors in WashU's CS department. He gives major dad vibes and is a very nice and chill person. His lectures can get confusing sometimes but attendance isn't mandatory and he offers a lot of extra credit to make up for that. His slides are also very comprehensive. This class is easy A if you do the work.
Ver fun and engaging prof (and nice lectures). Class itself was pass/fail and attendance base, but no homework

I also took him for 131. I'm not sure where people got a sense of rudeness from him. He offered 101 as an easy, extra in-person seminar option when most classes were online (COVID). He offers incredible perspective and intelligence. He will hold a discussion about anything you want to talk about. Also has the typical wit/humor of a CS guy

Good at explaining concepts and answering questions, but he was pretty rude and condescending. Although the workload is heavy and constant, 131 isn't too difficult to do well in as long as you pay attention and there are so many chances for extra credit so take them. I ended up TAing for this class in the spring after taking it in the fall.

Cytron was good at answering questions and giving feedback, but he does say things that can come off as rude. He teaches Java concepts really well and offers chances for extra credit (going to come in handy if you bomb a test). I think taking his class does pay off and if you're interested in comp sci you should give it a try!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Good teacher but not a nice guy
Gives good feedback and does help during sessions but is kinda rude.
-great class but professor was extremely condescending towards students -would not take cytron again but should definitely take cs
He is really mean...

A lot of what's needed to be said has been said. He's a good lecturer, will answer questions promptly, and responds to advice (people this semester complained the lecture speed was too fast, so he slowed it down).

Flipped classroom. At first the videos were very helpful/informative. By lesson 7 everything went downhill, the videos stopped teaching the material well & by week 9 all hope was lost for learning. THERE WAS SO MUCH HOMEWORK. Towards the end it was completely overwhelmng. Learned a lot of java. Need good time mgt. Exams were fine. Easy to get an A

I really regret taking this class, I thought Cytron was good before taking this class because he was pretty good for 131 and 247. But he just doesn't know how to teach this class, and very messy syllabus, the average for the final was around 60, but he does not do anything about it...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Mundane lectures and does not stick to the syllabus at all. Accessible to meet outside of class but looks down on you if you don't know the material. Not good at answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Cytron was one of the rudest professors I have ever met. He was incredibly disrespectful to both students and other faculty members. I witnessed him many times yell at students during office hours for not understanding the materials and I have also seen him be rude to his fellow faculty. No adult should behave the way he does.

The reason why he has gotten such good reviews is because people know him as a celebrity from the videos or have had very, surface-level conversations with him!Ron Cytron is maybe the most horrible human being I know; frequently yells at people for not understanding, talks down to students and adults, and makes life hell for people he dislikes! NO

He is really good at explaining CS concepts to beginners. He made somewhat complicated things simple and he is so far the best CS professor I have met in WashU(I have not taken many CS classes). Midterms are fair and doable, the course itself as an introduction to CS is an easy GPA booster as long as you complete all labs and studio on time.

Professor Cytron is great! He's very nice and you can tell he wants you to learn. Had him for both 131 and 247. 131 has his online lectures, along with weekly labs and studio with classmates. 247 was hard - labs and exams were very difficult. But Cytron as a professor is awesome.

Cytron is a celebrity at Washu, for good reason! He takes massive pride in CSE131 as it exposes CS to students for the first time and he does what he can to make it enjoyable/less intimidating. This course has a TON of support, w/ an army of TAs who will help. Tests are never too difficult as he gives you everything you need to do well.

This class is a lot of work if you have no programming experience, but putting in the effort will get you an A. Labs can be hard but exams are fair and a sheet of paper is allowed. Cytron is an awesome guy and the lecture videos sort of make you feel like he's a celebrity, but he makes himself super accessible to students.
Amazing professor. Makes comp science so approachable and hands on and is always willing to help. He will learn your name and make you feel like you exist despite the 600+ students that take 131.
131 is a great course. A good amount of work, but not too hard. Even in such a big class, Cytron is approachable and extremely helpful.

First off, Cytron is the gem of the CSE dept., bar-none. However, he wasn't fully on his A-game for 431 - it's a difficult course, and his lectures can be a bit monotone and meandering, although if you can stay focused they're very solid. Learning curves for labs are absolutely brutal. Still a solid class, plus he wrote the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Cytron's a really nice guy but he doesn't make the class that interesting. Lectures can be pretty boring and he drowns you in slides, and the labs are just "fill in the function" so they don't really help. The difficulty is pretty tame though compared to other engineering courses though, and he's always looking at ways to improve the course.
Great professor who actually cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Honestly I don't know why people give Cytron so much high score. He is simply an interesting person, that's all. His teaching is useless, and his grading policy is highly unreasonable.
Excellent professor - knowledgeable, cares about his students, and passionate about computer science. I switched my schedule so I could take 247 while he was teaching it.

Greatest professor/teacher I have ever worked with. Prof. Cytron got to know me on a personal level in a class of 600 kids. In addition, he has an amazing ability to explain complex concepts in simple, everyday terms. I wouldn't have continued on my computer science education had I not had him. His exams are also incredibly fair.
Wants you to succeed and learn and love comp sci. Truly a saint

Cytron is respected by many. Really helpful and clear, and obviously wants you to like comp sci. The class can be time consuming, but it's really easy to get an A if you put in the time and seek help (TAs were my saviors). Extensions can be stressful if you don't start early enough. Exams were easy. You come out with a basic sense of Java.
Great professor, always available to help his students. Clear online lectures, really teaches you comp sci. DO NOT BUY TEXTBOOK! It's easy to get an A if you do all the required work.

He completely ruined CSE241 and turned the class into a crap-like CSE247. Really learned nothing in this class. The class is called Algorithms and Data Structures while before the first midterm we were taught none algorithms and one data structure. Spending ages teaching the prerequisites to this class. Gonna skip to CSE541 next semester.

An excellent introduction to computer science. Having begun the course with no programming experience whatsoever, I am amazed by how much I was able to learn over the semester, thanks to his teaching style.
Cytron is the man.
Professor Cytron was my favorite professor all year. Even though he had so many students in his class, he took the time to get to know each individual. If you get Cytron, you are lucky.
Professor Cytron made computer science really fun, and found a relatively easy way to teach a pretty hard topic.  He is an 5 star teacher.

Great professor!  Much more clear than Chen; very helpful and really cares about students, very accessible.  Cognizant of student's needs regarding scheduling and approaches to learning. Highly recommend taking his class!!
Cytron is the man. Made the material accessible even when I had no idea how to code before coming in. Take this class if you want to learn java thoroughly and, more importantly, marketably.

Cytron is the man hands down. I had no prior coding experience and he made the material accessible and understandable. If you have any interest at all in learing Java (useful life skill people), take this class!

Writing this as an alum. I took teachers like Dr. Cytron for granted, but looking back I owe them a huge debt of gratitude. Dr. Cytron did a great job at instilling core CS knowledge in his students and was a model of professionalism.
One of my favorite teachers at WashU. If you work hard and your code does what it's supposed to do without looking atrocious, you will get an A. You'll learn the course material mostly from the labs.

Awesome teacher, arguably the best one from the CS department, and definitely amongst the top of all engineering professors. Very helpful towards students, and makes sure you understand the problem and theory well.

The material was kind of boring, but the professor is great.  Was always available for help whether by office hours, email, after class, etc.  Homework wasn't too hard.  Some exams were difficult but were curved generouly (average for each exam was just below a 90).
My favorite professor at WashU. I'm writing this as an alum, but he's worth it
Fantastic, very helpful
Awesome teacher, one of the best in the department.  He really cares about teaching students.  Office hours are super helpful if you're falling behind.

Fun teacher. Although the course is labeled as for beginners like me, it really isn't. His discussions in lectures are abstract and difficult to relate to actual code writing. However, many TAs can help.

Cytron is an awesome guy and is extremely accessible.  I agree this class is hard for beginners, but go to his office hours and he is very helpful.  Lectures are a bit tedious and it's hard to anticipate what quizzes are on, but he allows retakes so it doesn't matter.  He also allows (encourages) you to turn in assignments late.
An extremely good professor who makes every attempt to help beginners understand the material.
Awesome guy but this course really isn't for beginners as it is labeled.
Great Teacher! Cytron was incredibly nice and helpful and his grading system is the best. Very easy to succeed if you put in the work. I highly recommend taking his class.

Very little code writing/reading done in lecture, extremely hard to follow if you've never seen programming before, majority of discussions are abstract.  He said that the course assumed we know nothing to begin with but it really didn't seem that way at all.  Syntax isnt taught, making the Intro to Computing class even harder on beginners.

GREAT professor...fair grading, interesting lectures, tests were take home but challenging.  encourages you to learn -- he is always helpful.  take any class he has, he is one of the best cs professors here.

An amazingly brilliant man. One of the best in the CSE department.  He made Software Engineering Workshop interesting and touched on a variety of relevant, useful topics.  Take him if you have the chance.
My favorite professor. I've taken him for many classes, and he is always amazing.
Cytron is a great teacher, and this is one of the most important classes you can take as a CSE major here at WashU.  Highly recommended.
One of the best in the whole department.
One of the best teachers had at Wash U.
No Comments
Puts a ton of preperation into his courses. One of the few teacher who actually got me interesting in the subject. Awesome.
No Comments
Great professor.  Lectures boring at times, but such is life with computer science.  Great guy.  Highly recommend.

Professor Cytron is extremely nice and is willing to answer ANY question, no matter how inane, and will never make you feel stupid or embarrass you for asking. A fair grader, and he comes highly recommended.

I loved Ron's class.  I had no experience with 3D design before, but he made the process of transferring 2D thoughts into 3D designs easy by giving really good advice.  He encourages independent thinking and is very understanding of the different methods in which people approach projects.  He's amazing, one my favorite professors I've had at Wash U

Ron is one of my favorite teachers here at Washu.  If 3D is new to you, he eases you through the process smoothly, challenges you, yet cuts you some slack when you really need it.  A great guy and one of the nicest teachers here.
Ron is a total teddy bear-nice and compassionate, but he still challenges you to make great work. Taking his class was fun and interesting.
My favorite person ever! Ron Leax can say something to you in passing that changes the entire was you look at art. I feel honored to have experience learning from Ron.
Has interesting things to say but often gets off topic. Is supportive for students.

Ron is an asset to Wash U's art program.  More willing to support and council his students than anyone I've ever encountered.  This man has more knowledge of ANY other teacher I've encountered- art, science, english, etc.  And to top it off, he splits his time between his students and his work perfectly.

I took both Calc I and II with Friewald and the grading was super favorable - I'm not great at math, but got A's both semesters with a moderate of work (nothing compared to Gen Chem!). I agree that lectures could get boring, but cut him some slack- what do you expect from math? He's obviously passionate about calc and is eager to help his students.

I had Prof. Freiwald for both Calc 131 and 132.  His lectures were boring and it often seemed like he was just talking to himself.  The webwork was 10x more difficult than what was taught in class.  The exams were tough, but he allowed notecards.  He dropped a fair amount of quizzes.  Go to class for clicker points.
Simply put, he cannot teach math to others. Going to lecture actually makes things more confusing. Would not recommend to my worst enemy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His exams were very T/F heavy and he weighted the final very heavily. Also, his exams were super theoretical and exams were tricky. Not clear during lecture and unable to explain things in multiple ways.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors from of all WashU. I have had my fair shares of professor taught courses but Freiwald tops the bunch as the worst. Can't teach, tough exams. You'll need not only the book but Advil to not suffer a stroke as result of this class. Not to mention, who teaches integrals a week before the final and then comprises 50% final...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: :( a combination of torture and deathly boredom.

I cannot speak for other math courses Freiwald has taught as I have only taken Calc I with him. That said, he is by far the worst math teacher I have ever had--and I have had some really bad ones. The only reason I knew what I was doing was because of high school math knowledge. His lectures are so confusing to follow and he is WAY TOO THEORETICAL!
Had to watch youtube videos which gave me my grade. Worst professor till date. All you suck ups are ranking him well.

He is one of the worst professors I've had at WashU. WAYYY too theoretical. He was so interested in every little detail that he missed the main point. The exams are true false trick questions. Take this class with anyone else.  Several of homework each week, not counting the suggested problems.

As someone who considers themselves pretty good at math, this was a hard class. Lectures are somewhat all over the place, exams are T/F and multiple choice on theory rather than application. HW and webwork are easy, but exams are 70% of the grade. He does write nice notes for every lecture, but I wouldn't take Matrix with him unless you have to.
One of the worst classes I've taken. Lectures are not helpful. Read the textbook. Webwork and homeworks are easy, and then he wrecks you with multiple choice and true false tests. Really poorly done.
Too theoretical. Interested in every minute detail but never helps you get the overarching principals. One of the worst at this school.
He is extremely helpful. In fact, he is the best Math professor  I met in Wash U!
Best prof in Washu. take it if you can learn 309 with him. Most interesting prof i have ever met. Exams are easy and he is a generous grader. Always helpful at office hours.
Best math teacher/ teacher I have ever had! His class taught me so much not only about topology but the mathematical/ scientific way of thinking.

Professor Freiwald is to this date the best professor I have had in the Math department and possibly all of Wash U. He is extremely helpful and his lectures are interesting. I would definitely take Math 309 with him.
Great class. Great professor. He really cares about his students and helps you if necessary. Although attendance is mediocre, definitely go to class, since he explains things extremely well in class.
I took Calc 1 in high school, and I still couldn't understand anything he said. He didn't explain anything clearly; I went entirely off what I learned in high school.

Make sure to keep up with suggested readings and practice problems, or you may get lost in lectures (especially if you haven't taken calc before.)  It's fairly easy if you take the initiative to utilize help resources and ask questions outside of class. DON'T FALL BEHIND.

Wow, this guy is incredibly organized. He follows the syllabus perfectly and his lectures are fluid and informative. The material isn't easy, but he clarifies the difficult topics well. Never mention formulas like the chain rule until you actually get to them in the lecture...he'll know that you've taken calculus already (which everyone has done)

Best math professor I've ever had. Never seen someone so organized before. Exams are not easy, but very similar to homework problems. So if you start studying early for the exams, you can get perfect scores. Take any math class with him!

an absolutely terrific class. lectures are interesting and very clear, and ronnie frei is always willing to go over something someone missed. homework was sometimes time consuming but always reasonable and exams were straightforward. recommend this class for anyone with an interest in math, major or not. one of--if not the--best profs in the dept.
Fantastic teacher. Incredibly clear and extremely helpful. Best professor I've had here so far.
awesome class. he is incredibly clear. i'm taking another class by him this semester. best math teacher i've had in washu so far
best class ever
I hate this man.....sigh...why did he have to ruin math for me forever...ugh...if you can avoid taking his class DO!
Alright Prof if you've already had Calc in high school; otherwise, difficult to understand

I took Calculus I in high school and still had a hard time understanding the material that was being taught in lecture.  Eventually, I stopped going to class because it was pointless and a serious waste of my time.
Very hard, understands the topic but not how to teach it.
Prof. Freiwald made the class extremely challenging.  I learned new things in Calc that I had not in high school.  He did an OK job.

He is definitely a very smart man who loves math and wants his students to understand it as much as he does. However, he must think we're a lot smarter than we are because the work is very hard and his lectures are dense.
The pace of the class was way too fast, not enough time was spent to ensure that all students understood the material.

I went into the class thinking I had a pretty good understanding of calc.  I soon learned that i was wrong as every assignment and test was a challenge.  Class didn't teach anything and the textbook provided minimal teaching.  Basically, you're on your own.
he was a good professor if you already had background on the material---but for new people, he would be probably be horrible---he did seem to genuinely care about the students learning though
his class is totally pointless and he never really answer any of the questions in class. going to class is a total waste of time.
Nothing was really gained from the actual time spent in class.  All material had to be learned on your own.  The only reason I went to class was to listen to his jokes.
he sounds like John Lithgow from Third Rock from the Sun and he is having an affair with his multi-colored chalk.

Professor Freiwald was awful. He seems to be incapable of teaching or helping students understand any of the material. He was also not very helpful when students needed help or had questions. His exams were significantly harder than the material taught in class.
Class was so boring I couldn't make myself go.  The final was really hard but the class was curved a lot in the end.

Freiwald is a nice guy who thinks that calculus 1 students are a lot smarter and more interested in math than they really are. Hence, a lot of class time is devoted to doing complicated proofs of various theorems that have no practical application on an exam or homework. He makes time for students.

going to class is pretty pointless because he just does proofs the wole time that really arent that helpful. webwork is ridiculously hard and on the mult. choice parts of the tests there is like 10 answers, which sucks. hes REALLY boring.

His classes are pointless- he just reteaches what the book taught. The webwork is on stuff you haven't learn and its unneccessarily hard. The questions on the tests are harder than the practice ones. Quizzes range in difficulty.
This guy really knows his stuff and tries really hard to explain things out.  Can get boring w. proofs and stuff but if you like math, he's good.

Shalev is a great guy - willing to help and pretty funny. However, it was sometimes hard to understand what he meant and he made it somewhat intimidating to ask questions. If you read the book and go to class it's not hard at all.

Prof Shalev makes accounting interesting and enjoyable --after all, it's not rocket science, as he puts it. He tries very hard to make sure students comprehend the material and takes our evaluation/suggestions seriously. Come to class prepared, or you'll be lost. Overall, highly recommended. Prof Shalev is talented and has a great sense of humor :)

This class=living hell. it is so boring in class it will seem as though you do not need to read. READ you must READ class is pretty useless but he counts your attendance and participation for 7 points. I suggest reading thoroughly and studying for quizzes. have a friend sign you into class
run away as fast as you can

I'm so surprised he has bad ratings on here! I took his thermo class and really liked it. The structure of the class worked well for me. I like reading before class, hearing the lecture, then working on problems in class (not graded). He is also very willing to answer questions during class. He made thermo easy to digest.

Agonafer keeps his lectures pretty straight forward and most of the time he will lecture half of class and spend the rest of class letting us work problems and asking him or the TAs for assistance which is really helpful. Group project was kind of intense but I guess this is a graduate level course. He is a professor who is always open to helping.

Shows up to class incredibly unprepared & stumbles through his lectures regularly. Not sure if he looks at the PPT before he starts lecturing to even see whats on the slides. Doesnt explain concepts clearly and struggles to answer questions. Dunno why attendance is required when his lectures leave you more confused. Entirely self-taught class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A pretty disappointing professor. Class lectures are hit-or-miss; derivations and examples are plucked right out of the textbook and not always presented clearly. Obsessed with a required research project that he is very strict about. Frequent (but short) homework assignments. The midterm was hard, but average was still in the B range. TA's are ok.

Awful lecturer. Does not review slides before classes, lectures are the first time he's seen this material since he taught it last year. Changed the criteria for our group projects 3 times so far, and not for the better. Pop quizzes whenever he feels like it, terrible at answering questions and explaining concepts clearly. Self-taught class

He breezes through his Powerpoint slides and examples, which are sometimes more confusing than as presented in the textbook. Very obsessed with a required research project. The homework was short and fairly difficult, but graded easily. Not the best prep for the two pretty hard exams though. Lots of pop quizzes. TA's are pretty good/available.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It's not his fault that the subject matter is relatively difficult. He does his best in class to summarize the best important theorems, but the best prep for tests is to read through the textbook examples on your own.

This professor is amazing!! 10/10. He always made sure to provide extra help and go the extra mile to make sure the class understood. Participation was also very important! It also helped a lot especially because his class was based on zoom. My spanish definitely improved and it was such an easy, motivating class!
Good guy, but is a stickler for attendance. Also class participation counts more than exams.
Very nice, stickler for attendance; wants you to do well- appreciates it when you come to office hours and when you ask questions that help not only you but the entire group
Really nice, smart, and helpful. Really wants his students to do well and enjoy Spanish

Probably one of the easiest spanish teachers. Very willing to help and nice. I'd say that his teaching abilities might not be amazing, but still strong.  If you want to for sure do well at, perhaps, the cost of learning a lot, take this class.  BTW the class is COMPLETELY grammar-based. don't worry about material (at least with this teacher)
really great guy, super nice. Kind of hard to meet with him one on one. Easy to understand, makes material interesting.
Extremely talented professor.  I wish I could take more classes by him.  Thanks.
Best part of the class when I took it was the TA.  Gus is HOT
Worst teacher in the college
Worst teacher in the department. Period.
No Comments

Lectures were a bit dry, very reading heavy. Dr. Aksoy is super super knowledgeable though, you can tell she's passionate about her research. Make sure to ask questions/participate in class to make the most of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting material but lectures generally dry. A lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Aksoy's class is lecture-based and some classes can feel boring, however many topics are interesting so overall I found the class worthwhile. Her class was not super easy, but also not excessively hard. Aksoy is a bit disorganized but she is certainly an expert on political violence and terrorism, and I learned a lot from her.

Aksoy is a smart professor, but she's a dry lecturer. Not very accessible outside of class and a harsh grader. She means well, but she comes off as disrespectful and uncaring in both her grading and her office hours. Course material and topics on Political Violence are pretty interesting though. Forget asking about extra credit or any sort of help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Ethnic Violence with Aksoy; I felt she was a generous grader and a kind professor. She did a pretty good job of teaching in lectures and although I was not completely wow'd by the course, I definitely learned a lot of helpful ways to understand conflict. Lots of reading, midterms not bad, papers super easy, lectures are average.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed Political Violence and learned a lot about current events. Great way to get a broad overview of important conflicts occurring in the world today/in recent history. Midterms were average difficulty for poli sci; they just required very close attention to the readings. One short final paper. All in all not too difficult.

She has a lot of knowledge about the subject but she isn't very understanding of non-native speakers who can't speak with the same fluency as a native speaker. Participation is graded extremely harshly (if you don't talk constantly you wont get a good grade). Must put in hours of work on presentations to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is really passive-aggressive, and she has an accent in Spanish which makes it hard to understand her. I think in general Washu should not have non-native-speaking people teaching Spanish classes. She is a tough grader and expects you to participate every single second of class and calls you out even though you might have nothing to say.

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR! She's the harshest grader I've ever encountered and relies on students to lead discussions rather than actually teaching. It really seems like she DOES NOT care AT ALL about her students and just wants them to suffer. She expects students to read RIDICULOUS amounts. Wish I could have rated her a 0.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tsuchiya is a nice professor and its clear that she knows everything there is to know about her subject. However, her accent is far from native making her hard to understand at times, and she constantly interrupts you while you speak. Relatively tough essay grader. Expects students to know as much about the literature as she does. Overall, not bad.

She is incredibly smart and knows almost everything there is to know about Spanish literature.  That being said, she doesn't understand that her undergraduate students don't know as much as she does, especially about the history of literary movements in Spain.  Her expectations are too high for a 300 level elective.

Not hard.  Never did the reading and got an A-.  Really boring classes and her accent is far from native.  Be prepared for a lot of stuff about women and gender.  The class should be renamed "el papel de la mujer en la sociedad".  On the upside, she's a nice lady.  Ironically prefers guys to girls even though she's a women's studies prof.
unpleasant, not interesting, nit-picky
No Comments
one of the most irritating prof. i've had so far...says 'mm hmmm' every 2 seconds and interrupts you while you talk.  horrible spanish accent...why can't wash u find native speakers to teach?
Fine - not incredibly exciting or incredibly boring.  I'd recommend her.
No Comments
don't ever take her class ... they should have gotten rid of her long ago, but I think she has TENURE ...

While Professor Grice was a very nice person, it is obvious she wants her students to have certain perspectives. It was hard for me to express my real opinions, as I thought it may affect my grade if I wrote or said something that was different than what she wants to hear. Class is fairly easy tho, take at your own discretion.

A great and passionate professor! Professor Warren-Grice cares deeply about every student and the well-being of the classroom and offers great support/flexibility in the classroom/course. I would say participation is important but the discussions are not stressful and facilitation is very much student-based so it is very easy to chime in!
I personally really enjoyed class with Professor Warren-Grice, I found her to be approachable and understanding, and foster an inclusive classroom experience.

Worst professor I had in college. The class was easy, but bias in her opinions was ludicrous. Went out of her way to be hostile toward opposing opinions. She was even negative toward certain religions. The class is all busy work, and fully inefficient. She has big-time favorites. If you are not, then you get scolded in front of your classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Taught this class more like a seminar, did not teach the law so much as she taught her own opinion. Did not welcome other viewpoints, even if they were not necessarily conflicting. Had very strange, unsubstantiated takes on the law that she taught as gospel. Inflexible with students and assignments were unhelpful. AVOID AT ALL COSTS

She is very well versed in her field and her class is a great place to have debate. The subject matter is interesting and she does a good job about covering many aspects. She was always interesting and approachable.
Good professor. Very organized. Very sharp and is respected in her field.
Relatively easy.  Class went pretty quickly and was somewhat interesting.  I have no interest in family law as a practice area, but it was overall worth taking.

Jami Ake is the best professor I've had in all of college. Her classes are intellectually stimulating and deep. The content is complex but she is there to help you understand and make connections. Her assignments are clear and she is open to letting you follow your interests. She cares deeply about her students and I would take every class she has.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I learned so much from her class. Her lectures are so insightful on the text we read but she can carry them out with the nicest mix of humor. Her comments on your essays are great but her gradings are not harsh. She likes to chat with you and know about you beyond the classroom. Dr. Ake is my favorite professor and she makes my semester worthwhile

Jami Ake is amazing! Not only was this class so fascinating and well designed, but the discussions being led by the students made it so special. I learned so much from my colleagues and Dr. Ake made the classroom a welcoming space. TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!!

Really great professor for literature. She cares a lot about her students and leads really great discussions. She's really funny and lighthearted and engages the class really well even when it comes to dense texts. She's not a tough or easy grader and provides really helpful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, clearly passionate and so intelligent. Once showed up to class with a black eye and STILL led an amazing discussion. Bit of a tough grader on essays, but her feedback is super helpful and clear. Participation graded on quality, readings can be heavy, but manageable. Love Prof Ake!

Great professor. I took classical to renaissance literature. One of my favorite classes (I studied engineering). The texts chosen were interesting and the paper topics made us think about the stories differently. She asks probing questions to facilitate class discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jami is one of the best professors at WashU. She is hilarious, caring, and gives great feedback on everything. Participation is important but the class is discussion based, though its very casual. If you don't read you won't get much from the class. Jami is phenomenal and the highlight of my semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Jami is my favorite professor at this school. She is clear in her grading, her lectures are easy to follow and take notes on, and she is always open to student feedback or questions. Gender Violence can be intense and she does a fab job breaking it down and using humor to lightened intense situations. Take this class- changed my life.

Loved this class! Lots of reading, but tons of opportunities for extra credit. The pop reading quizzes are easy if you did the reading. Super interesting topics and conversations, and Ake is truly a fair grader if you put in the effort. Wonderful woman overall and wonderful class! Take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a really great professor that a lot of people respect, and a wonderful teacher. Her advice and commentary on my essays really helped for other classes, and she was very clear about her grading. The class is a lot of reading, but it's divided into completely doable proportions. I really recommend the class, and I love Professor Ake.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I want to be Jami Ake when I grow up. She is a wonderful human being and an amazing professor. If you have the opportunity to take one of her classes, do it. Gender Violence definitely changed my life. Jami's lectures are engaging and relevant, plus she is hilarious, upbeat, and cares so deeply about every single student.

Jami is so amazing! She made me laugh every class period with her sarcasm and her witty sense of humor. She is a great teacher, grades fairly and cares about all her students. Definitely worth all the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Ake is the best professor I have had at WUSTL so far. She is fair and cares deeply. She gets to know all of her students on a personal level. She encourages students to disagree with her and promotes amazing discussions.

I've now taken two classes with Jami, and she really didn't disappoint.  She is by far the coolest person I know, and serves not only as a role model, but also as a true mentor to those who seek her out.  She's a phenomenal lecturer and overall professor and I always look forward to class or just chatting with her!

Jami awake might be the coolest person to ever walk the planet. She's an amazing instructor, underrated lay a genius, and is so passionate not only about what she does, but also about her students and making sure they succeed. Her advice and encouragement is how I discovered my passion and became a WGSS major. She's incredible.

I was told by older students that I had to take a class with her before I graduated -- and it did not disappoint. She makes you think critically about any other class you've taken/ things you think you know and is great at facilitating discussion. She genuinely cares about her students and it shows.

I truly love her. This is the only class I take that I look forward to. Jami, never ever stop teaching because you are one of the most inspirational people I have ever had the chance to learn from. If you have a chance to take a class with her, do it!!

Jami is actually one of the coolest people I've ever met.  She's hilarious, super down to earth, and always there to support her students.  She's actually a genius, and I'm simply amazed by all she does.
Favorite teacher this semester. She is inspirational and funny. Take a class with her!

Ake was the best professor I have had yet at WashU. She made Shakespeare so incredibly fun (which honestly is hard).  She encourages your opinions and discussion, but led most lectures. Always down to laugh, always happy, really helpful and understanding. Wants all her students to succeed which is amazing

Professor Ake is an incredible professor! I've never been interested in english, but I found myself fully interested and focused in all of our discussions! I would take a class just to have her as my professor again.

Jami Ake is basically my idol. She's a funny lecturer, extremely helpful, and generally personable and wonderful. Some people find that she's a tough grader, but I never thought her grading was anything but reasonable. Anyone and everyone should take Violence Against Women if they can-- you'll look forward to going to class.

Best professor I have had yet. I would highly recommend that anyone take Violence against Women with her. Very flexible about attendance, grading, and deadlines as long as you are putting in an effort.

A nice balance between lecture and discussion, I learned a lot, and the weekly quizzes weren't that bad. She's one of the few people who is simultaneously brilliant and good at teaching classes, and she actually cares about her students beyond the classroom. If you get the chance to take a class with her, DO!
Dear Jami Ake: I will hang desperately from your every word. Never ever, never stop teaching.

If you can get into one of her classes, take it! She is probably the smartest woman you will ever meet in your life, and she's hilarious. I still stop by her office just to talk. She's extremely knowledgeable about course material and college life in general.
Very articulate, provokes intriguing discussions. High expectations for papers; simply send her a draft beforehand. Great teacher!
No Comments
I absolutely LOVE this teacher. I am going out of my way next semester to take another class by her. TAKE HER CLASS!!
No Comments
Absolutely amazing!

Literature is not one of my main interests, but Professor Ake managed to make the class very engaging.  She is both humorous and very knowledgable.  A tough grader of writing, but her criticisms are always fair and helpful.  Recommended.
I loved this class, and Professor Ake was wonderful!  If you attend Wash U and have any thoughts at all about taking a Women's Studies class, TAKE AKE!
Really nice lady, difficult class, but worth the work. You learn a lot!!!

Hands-down the nicest professor I've ever had, goes out of her way to help students with classes, life, anything. Also the most challenging grades on essays, but quizzes are easier and very frequent. Take a class with her before you leave WashU.
Quizes weekly at least.  Women studies prof who takes notice of the sexual side of Shakespeare.  Tough on papers.
lots of work covering a lot of dense material in a short amount of time, but she's a good professor.
definitely willing to help by doing one on one counseling about papers, etc.
So accessible, fair, truly cares about her students, and challenging!
Friendliest, most approachable professor I know.
extremely dedicated to and passionate about what she teaches
Fantastic professor.  One of the best I've ever had,  kept my interest throughout even with a topic I've found can get a bit dry.  Definitely recommending her to my friends.
Absolutely one of the best professors at WU. Dynamic, challenging, hilarious, extremely intelligent, perfect to talk to about anything and everything
Good class, but quisses are annoying

Incredibly dynamic.  Knows her material like the back of her hand.  ALWAYS makes her classes interesting and funny.  You can just drop in on her to say hello or have a 45 minute convo about life - she's fabulous.  Definitely take a class with her before you graduate.
Dean Ake rocks!  Her classes are hard but sooo good!
Hilarious and manages to fill her lectures on renaissance lit with SEX
Fantasic!! Best teacher ever!
Intelligent, funny, and kind!
No Comments
Funny as hell, and knows her Shakespeare.
Good prof- some of the students lost her on the hearsay exceptions, but that's a problem with the legal concept rather than the teaching. Very helpful with questions and requests for clarification.
A great teacher!
great prof

It would have been nice if you could have strung a coherent sentence together and focused on the class subject. Thanks for cancelling classes to suit your personal schedule. Teach something that will be on the bar exam.
Great professor who expects her students to keep up.
consider yourself lucky if you get assigned to aiken your first year.

Manic waving hands distract from lecture. Disorganized course rambled, skipped over torts she didn't like (ie, not dealing with women). Randomly gave extra work, ie: day before Thanksgiving, to highlight the plight of women in our cases. She never noticed that most students were never prepared and just distracted with questions about womens rights

I enjoyed her classes, and we had good discussions in class. Readings and content are very interesting and rewarding. She's a pretty lenient grader. Cares about timeliness and improvement. She's very left-wing and will share her opinions in class, but encourages discourse. Most of the assignments are done in class, and the workload is light.

Dr. Allen was okay. I particularly didn't enjoy the class at first, but once we got to do our research project on whatever we wanted, I enjoyed talking to her and writing a lot more. Dr. Allen really tries to make sure everyone gets a good grade, but can be a little picky at times. She also does and will curse in class.
Would take again if I could.

Super lefty...she likes to be pushed on her ideas but will spout some pretty left-wing stuff. You read some long articles but only have to get the main idea. I had fun because i like to debate and she respected that. Other ppl didn't get their participation points bec they just didn't say anything.

This was a great class! Looking back, it has been one of my favorites at WashU so far. The content is really interesting and the grading is fair (not difficult to do well if you put in effort and incorporate feedback on essays). While there are many small writing assignments, they help your grade/are not difficult/help you prepare for discussions.

A lot of reading and writing, but all the reading was enriching and fascinating. I loved hearing her thoughts on the reading and discussing the homework in class. She can be a relatively tough grader for essays.

Really straightforward expectations. Decent for college writing and work is awful for the first half (had three 500-word assignments w readings some weeks) but the effort required drops after that. All assignments except for papers are participation graded, and can redo papers if you get a bad grade. Overall easy A for mid-work and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of my most frustrating professors of all time. Extremely left wing so if you have any differing opinions get ready to sell your soul for the next semester. SO MUCH BUSY WORK but not too many papers. If you kiss up to her and do the work, you're pretty much guaranteed to do well. Seems like a nice woman but I'm so glad this class is over.

This class was literally so easy- yea we got busy work but it could literally be done in 30 min and you didn't have to put much effort in + you could submit at any time for points. She also let us revise final papers which is not the norm in most CWP Classes. She was also a pretty easy grader and it was easy to get a solid A

Coming in 2nd semester, I didnt think much of CW & skimmed over leftover options to choose this. I quickly came to discover that the workload of this class is abhorrent. A paper worth of writing every class. Currently 3rd semester as a double in major in McKelvey and this might be the highest workload I've had from an individual class. 

Just don't
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Allen is a great College Writing professor! She does expect you to read a fair bit and put a decent effort into the weekly assignments, but this makes students more effective writers. She is lenient with attendance, too, which is nice. As long as you participate and make an effort to enjoy the readings, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: CW P&P is heavy in workload, so be prepared for three 500 word assignments a week in addition to the standard essays in the CW curriculum. The professor is heavily left-leaning politically (even by WashU standards) and does not leave a lot of room for opposing viewpoints. Otherwise, she allows unlimited regrades making the class manageable.

Straightforward with what she wants in a paper. Lots of work, but almost always participation for discussion posts. Going to class will help with writing paper in discussions. Not a very good writer and I learned a lot about writing and my struggle did not show up in my grade. Will read over your paper and give you feedback before submitting.

More difficult for me to take her College Writing class coming from a school where I didn't do much writing. Very organized professor and readily gives feedback. Helped me become a better paper writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Having Dr. Allen for CWP was a solid experience. I enjoyed our discussions in class, but many times it seemed that you must agree with her ideas to get good grades. That being said, work was abysmal and grading was easy. I spent minimal effort on each assignment and finished with stellar grades.

Professor Allen was amazing for college writing. There were assignments due every class but she was very clear with the directions and what she wanted. Same goes for papers just listen to what she has to say during workshop, you will definitely get an A. Also, if you participate she will like you. I ended with a 96% and loved her.
Fairly easy grader and lax with deadlines, but the workload is heavy and participating in discussions is pretty much required for a decent grade

Dr Allen is an interesting person and teaches in a very personal way. She feels passionate about random vocabulary use and ranted about using the word "utilize" is stupid. besides that I loved the readings we did and learned a lot from our discussions. She is a little tunnel-visioned and only wants her way which is hard for essay writing.
In class discussion felt difficult at times as she would argue most ideas shared by students, however, her writing advice was genuinely helpful and helped me grow as a writer.

To sum up the other reviews, she has a very liberal point of view, if you don't like that then you probably won't like her. She is pretty blunt and won't always agree with you. I thought she was amazing. Discussions had so much depth and she really helps us succeed in all our essays. LOVED her and this class, and was actually excited to show up!!

A great professor for College Writing Program! The lectures and individual meetings are inspirational. You can easily get a good grade if you participate in class and do a few required reading and writing. To succeed in essays, simply listen carefully to her advice on individual meetings and follow them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Extremely condescending. Makes a terrible enviorment for people to participate in class. Literally disagrees with everything you say. Super smart woman, uses her talents to look down upon her students. Probably wont like you if you are white or straight. Class is a ton of busy work and a lot of reading. Overall not impossible but a hard CWP.

Allen is fairly biased and can be argumentative, but is willing to see your side of the story if you can back it up. I thought her grading critiques were ridiculous and nit-picky at times, but won't ever outright fail you on an assignment. Lots of reading and discussion posts. Has a dry sense of humor that either hits or misses. Decent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Allen is pretty unapologetically biased. It comes out in everything she teaches. If you want a good grade, you should write/say what she believes. She sighs and gets upset if she doesn't like what you said and she gave the international students a hard time with their grammar and writing styles. She's extremely critical and blunt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Solemn and intellectually stimulating. Prepare to have your opinions challenged. Going into college, I was nervous for college writing, but I definitely finished as a stronger, more sophisticated writer after her class. Readings for every class were a few pages, only 2 papers + final, so not much out of class work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The course is heavily based on readings, discussions, and papers. The readings include a wide range of topics, closely related to contemporary issues. Dr. Allen gives really detailed and inspirational feedback on papers and really widened my understanding of many topics. Very nice professor and person.

I had Dr. Allen for CWP: Place & Perspective. The class was always discussing the readings. Readings are generally short, interesting, and about a wide variety of topics. Assignments are very fair and build on each other. Lots of opportunities for feedback/growth. Dr. Allen is anti- everything, so be prepared to have your beliefs challenged.

Dr. Allen gives much criticism to your papers and ideas yet not in a rather harshly. Make sure you do the readings. Once you learn how she likes essays written and write to her style you will do fine in class.

What an AMAZING professor. I'm writing this message a whole year after having her, and I can't begin to thank her enough for how much easier her class has made my college experience . She worked with me so much to develop my skills, and is a great person!

The readings for class were interesting and her expectations for papers were well outlined. Discussions in class were very engaging but she often pushed her personal beliefs, which was a turn off.  Very approachable and cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Fair grader, gives good feedback. Seemed like the students who did the best in her class wrote exactly what she wanted them to write. In-class discussions are interesting, but she tends to push her own personal views and is generally not responsive to dissenting opinions. Pretty funny woman, though.
Great professor, pushes her students to be better and expects a lot from them. Lectures are fun but mandatory.

Dr. Allen is very intelligent but NOT open to dissenting opinions. She has a very liberal point of view and if you say anything slightly conservative she is quick to jump on you and make you feel like a morally bad person. It's a bummer because she's very smart and funny but comes across as condescending.
Very cold, disinterested professor.  Hard to have discussions with, and I felt like she just absolutely did not want to teach our class at all. Didn't learn anything from this class.

The class itself is fine, but she is usually grumpybitter and we tend rehash the same discussions over and over again.  She isn't really open to dissenting opinions and treats you like you're stupid if you don't understand something.  Brilliant woman, but personally just didn't click with her.

Dr. Allen is among the most hilarious, delightfully quirky instructors I've had. She's SO intelligent and did an excellent job engaging everyone in the class. My writing has improved a great deal thanks to her. Dr. Allen is the best!
Odd personality, but if you can see through that she really helped me with my writing.
