Lectures were a bit all over the place. He's nerdy and awkward but in the best way. Such a nice guy. No attendance, but he made an effort to get to know those of us who came. Went to his office hours multiple times, and he was always eager and excited to help
Great guy.

He is the cutest little man alive. Obsessed with pokemon and math. He is super nice and answers every question you may have. I suggest to take the lectures seriously and pay attention cause section didn't do anything...
Dr. Chang is. a very nice person, however, I do not find him to be a particularly great teacher. It can be very hard to folllow what he is doing in class and often it only makes sense to him.

Prof. Chang is SO NICE!! He truly makes math enjoyable and really wants you to succeed. He is one of the most patient teachers I have had. I recommend going to lectures/office hours just to hang out with him.
Favorite person in the world. Never seen someone who so obviously loves their job. Deeply patient and thoughtful in his interaction with students.

I love him so much! He's super cheerful and into his lessons and you can tell he loves what he does. He's super open to meeting with students outside of class and is great at explaining the problems in class. Tests are awful but that's not his fault he doesn't make them, the TA's do :\

Chang was such a nice guy with a beautiful love for math. As someone who is decent at math, Chang's passion for what he teaches made it more interesting. He was a little awkward in lecture but still tried his best to be funny and engaging, which means the most to be. Overall great at explaining problems and deserves a promotion!

Alan is genuinely one of the nicest and sweetest people I've ever met. He prepares thoroughly for lectures, is very accessible outside of class, and writes fair exams. It is so rare to find a professor who is both passionate about their subject and students, but Alan really does it all. I highly recommend taking his classes.

Alan is incredibly nice. Both his love of math and smile are infectious. His lectures are very well-prepared, and they certainly helped me intuit analysis. As is to be expected, 4111 takes time and persistence, but Alan is an excellent prof to take it with.

Very unpredictable teaching style and grading criteria. This man has never thought about the student experience in his class. He grades very harshly, and tends to be very uncommunicative about how grading works and what to expect from the homework. If you take this class, get comfortable not knowing exactly where you stand in regards to grades.
Nice and accommodating, boring class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Alex Bradley does not provide rubrics for this course, and he provides minimal feedback during office hours.

I think that Alex's teaching style has changed in recent history, which is why his reviews on here are great. He assigns long, lab report readings every single week which are graded by AI, homeworks are hard and students are rarely prepared for them, and exam criteria is unclear, making it hard to succeed. I didn't enjoy this class or his teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Alex really gets to know his students. In Special Topics, we had a great small class and he worked with everyone to allow us to build skills. Just enough lectures to provide background but mostly hands-on. Very collaborative and caring.

I had Alex for Geology Bootcamp. I loved every second of that class, mostly because of him and Phil (the other professor). The two of them were like a comedy duo, constantly cracking jokes with one another. You can tell that they're super passionate about geology and love teaching it. They're also very personable and overall fun guys.
Alex is the bomb
Lectures were great and always super clear, exams sometimes difficult but the grading policies were very generous and fair, learned a lot and really great class overall
Great professor. Took topology with him, and it was a difficult, but rewarding class. Recommended for anyone who loves math. Beware, the exams will kick your ass

Daemi is a really caring professor who will go out of his way to help his students. He makes sure you understand whatever question you come to him with, is very accessible outside of class, office hours were good and optional problem session was helpful. His teaching made multiple choice/conceptual questions on exams very easy to handle.

His style of lecturing was writing out many examples, and elaborating on concepts/definitions along the way, on the blackboard, which I personally found helpful for success in this class. He takes questions, stays after class to help, is helpful during OH, and even hosted weekly problem sessions despite the asynchronous model. Good pick for 132
He tries his best and is kind to students, but his lectures could be more helpful. He explains calc 2 like he's speaking to another mathematician

Daemi is one of the most underrated math profs at WashU. I took his calc3 this semester and it was great. Lectures were amazing with helpful examples and he was always patient to take questions. He shows care for his students and genuinely wants you to succeed. I enjoyed our class and the math. Would take again!

Matrix with Professor Daemi was doable. Some tips would be to go to office hours if the Crowdmark is hard and make sure to take diligent notes of the definitions he gives. Also, the practice exams help prepare you for the midterms and finals.

Unclear and hard to follow in the lectures (for me). But, homework is very relevant to tests so if you spend the time each week to skim the textbook, skip through a few khan academy videos, and/or go to academic mentoring so that you can do the homework well, you should do well on tests. Nice guy, just inexperienced and not the best lecturer.

Too much homework. I found him to be unhelpful and a bit rude outside of class. Talked to the board too much. Each lecture was individually good and well-explained, but they didn't always line up with subsequent lectures very well. This made some topics more confusing than they had to be, since it was unclear whether we had seen a topic before.

Teaches by filling boards with a textbook style of progression with definitions, examples, and proofs. Can be a little fast sometimes, but I enjoy this style of teaching through discovery and building up concepts.

Guy clearly knows how to do the math but just has no real ability to teach it. He just stands at the front of the class and does work on the board without much explanation. Better off teaching yourself with the textbook.

Daemi literally just writes and speaks in very low and confusing tones -- it's hard to understand during lectures. Although Daemi is very intelligent, you won't learn much from going to lectures. The homework is ok but hard due to the lack of knowledge students have.

Daemi seems to be talking to the board instead of the students 90% of the time, and he shows no capability as a professor to teach the students. He writes too much, rushes over concepts, and just simply doesn't explain that much. With that being said, he is a very nice person and will explain concepts to you if you ask him with follow up questions.

He was one of three professors during Calc 1, but I only met him during office hours. He helped me a lot when it came to math problems I was struggling on and really took time to get to each of the students' questions! He's really caring and always wished us luck on quizzes or whatever else was going on at the end of office hours. I respect him

He is genuinely a kind teacher that explains concepts so well. It is a very easy to understand course with very interesting material. The tests were always fair, you get exactly what you give. He may not be the most animated professor which may set you off the first few weeks, but stick with him, he is good at what he teaches.

Wonderful professor! psych dynamics of empathy was one of the most interesting classes i've ever taken. Midterms are extremely straightforward (94% average), and he didn't assign homework. I've recommended him and this class to everyone I know

Empathy was a great class. Entertaining lectures that featured lots of video clips and ended very early often. Lambert is a great professor and gives fair exams that are easy if you study. You should take this course.
Stanley Tucci is really stepping up his game and going out of his comfort zone masquerading as a WashU Professor

Cool dude!
Love his striped scarves!

The class content is interesting, and Dr. Lambert is nice and helpful. I missed a class and he agreed to schedule a meeting with me outside of his office hours to answer my questions about the missing lecture. The class pace was perfect---not too fast or too slow. Reading the textbook and paying good attention to his lectures are important.

Awful experience in this class. This is not the easy, pscyh class that people make it out to be. Lambert drones on during lectures and reads of slides that have a single photo on them without any words making it impossible to learn material if you miss class. Grade is based off MC exams which purposely trick you in answer choices. DO NOT TAKE THIS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you cannot take multiple choice exams or thrive off a test-based course. I know that goes for most of the psych classes, but take it with another professor if you need this credit. The exams are tricks and contain information you will have never learned about.  Trust me, take it off your RW1. It will save your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class! The material was interesting, and lectures were clear, engaging, and not too dense. Dr. Lambert has a fun sense of humor and was happy to answer questions in and out of class. Attending class and reading the textbook are necessary to do well on the midterms, but they're not otherwise difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You can very easily get a B if you just show up to class (not even take notes) & study the textbook for a single afternoon before the exam. An A will be a little harder but still pretty easy. The entire grade is out of 150 points, 4 50-point MC exams one of which you can drop. Talks a little slow sometimes but overall 7/10 for lecture entertainment

I really wanted to like this class and professor, but was very disappointed. The content was interesting at first, but became very repetitive as the semester progressed. I could tell that he was passionate, but lectures were still dry. The exams were absolutely ridiculous and asked the most niche details from lectures. 30% interesting, 70% boring

Prof. Lambert is one of the few professors I have had at WashU that I genuinely did not like. His lecture style was dry and not engaging, and the tests included a ton of material that was only in the textbook, never covered in class. He was inaccessible outside of class and not interested in individual students. Would not recommend.

Grade was mostly based on multiple choice exams which were so poorly written. Typos, incorrectly coded, tricky wording. 10% of the exam had to be regraded. Unprofessional and frustrating. A member of the teaching team told me Its not about what you know in defense of trickily worded questions. More about reading his mind than material retention
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lambert is very knowledgeable and makes this relatively new course interesting. However, as the semester went on, the tests became trickier and trickier, some questions just felt like pure trick questions. Even knowing the material related to those questions well won't guarantee getting the right answers.

Professor Lambert seemed fairly passionate about what he was teaching and allowed for as much classroom engagement as possible given it was an online course. The course itself would get a bit dry at times but I hear it's much better in-person. He seemed a bit aloof at times, but I usually managed to find something interesting in every lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was the first year this course was offered and Prof Lambert was the best person to teach it. You could tell he was passionate about the subject, though it wasn't always clear where the course was going. His lectures are funny and interesting. His tests are very fair, so as long as you go to class, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really interesting course! Prof Lambert is very knowledgeable and helps students engage with the material. There are clicker questions once in a while so you have to come to class or you could miss points but class is super interesting so it's worth it to come! Tests are very fair and are formatted like all other Psych lecture exams (50 MC q's)

As a marketing major, I found this class extremely useful and interesting! Prof. Lamberts lectures were always clear (though sometimes a little boring). Simply going to class and keeping up with the textbook sets you up for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The lecture is very bad. Can't really extract things useful. But you still have to go to the class anyways, because for each exam there will be a number of questions that are details covered in the class. Exams are heavily focused on the text books, which is totally different thing from the lecture.
Dr. Lambert's Social Psych class was great! His lectures always kept my attention and his tests were not too difficult if you show up to lecture and read the book.

As long as you read the book and go to class you can't possibly do worse than a B+ in social psych.  He makes it very clear what you need to know from lecture and the rest is covered by the books bolded terms.  Some of his lectures are really interesting, some not so much, but overall good prof

Lectures are helpful, clear. Can be kind of boring (esp. after having Sommers). Tests are mostly fair; he put a question on the test that came from a section of the book that he explicitly told us we didn't have to read... otherwise the test was pretty standard. Definitely have to go to lecture and read the book.

Lambert is a good professor and he is available to explain material to students in office hours. He gives good lectures and is clearly an expert in his field. However, he does not respond to emails and he can be aloof and forgetful. He will say not to read certain pages because they won't be tested on, but then the exam will have questions on that.
Lambert is a great lecturer. I'm almost always surprised when class ends because it feels like an hour hasn't passed.
Liked him a lot! His lectures are very interesting and he moves at a good pace. I would take another class with him. His section on social psychology was extremely well done and interesting.

Class was fairly interesting until you realize that social psychology is kind of intuitive. Even though the material seems easy, he manages to make the tests extremely tricky. Make sure to try to find someone's backfiles or beg for a practice exam because the first test blindsides you. Once you get a hang of taking his exams, it is OK but tough.
He cares about his students, and makes the material interesting.

Great lecturer topped with interesting material. A lot of the lecture is from the textbook, but he linked it w a lot of relevant and topical info. If you read the book and attend the lectures, you should be good. Not sure how different his teaching style is in larger lectures, but liked him a lot and would definitely recommend the class.

Despite the interesting subject matter, he made class kind of boring. However, the textbook isn't bad reading, and if you read the book and go to class you should do well on the tests. It's all multiple choice, but he tests things that he emphasized in class, except for sometimes random stuff he'll ask just to see if you went.

Liked social psych when I came in, but he somewhat killed it. Lot of his lecture was important for the test but also laced with self-depreciation. It made for a somewhat awkward class, but it was rather dry watching him read his slides... Still, not impossible and not horrible
Literally just reads his slides out loud, can be very boring. Least favorite psych class so far. Dry.
took social psych with Lambert! Liked him a lot! the class was interesting but make sure you go even though its a big lecture hall. you need those notes for sure! i would recommend it!
Lambert was a great professor--made me want to major in psych.
Good, somewhat funny lecturer.  Occasionally rushes the lecture and sometimes feels distant, but overall a good prof for a big intro course.
He's a good guy...go to class. The test questions come from lecture like 95% of the time

The course material was very interesting, and the textbook was easy to understand.  He basically teaches from the book, but there are some things he says in class that are not in the book.  It's a good class to take.
Tends to get bogged down on topics in lecture, but overwhelmingly in depth in his class

If you've taken AP Psych, don't be fooled like I was. Make sure you go to every class and TAKE NOTES, because those are what the tests are based on. The test questions are all multiple choice, but often have ambiguous answers and can be confusing unless you've memorized his notes to the letter.
Lectures not always interesting since he sends slides ahead of time. Very easy tests. Decently interesting.
pretty funny guy. exam was not too hard. reading the book didn't really help all that much. very complete lectures.
His own interest and excitment about the subject makes his lectures interesting.  He obviously puts a great deal of effort into his preparation and it should be appreciated.
very interesting, you WANT to listen to him when he speaks. was very helpful because he provided the notes for the classes and was more specific with the exam material.
His lectures were clearer and easier to follow than the other lecturers for the class, and he gives you a good idea of what's going to be on the exam.
boring lecture style, but he actually really knows a lot and does really interesting work

Kinda quirky but funny. Really nice guy with a true interest in psychology. Tests are extremely fair and pretty easy if you go to lectures and read the book. Great class even thought it's a giant lecture.

Lambert is interesting and funny, and Social Psych is a great class. I highly recommend it. If you want to get an A, it really helps to do all of the readings (I found the book pretty enjoyable anyway).
He was cool. He's a nice, down-to-earth guy. Really honest about his own struggles and seems to relate well to students.
Good guy. Interesting class. Tests were pretty fair. With minimal effort, should get a B pretty easily.

although kind of boring, Lambert is a fairly good teacher and the subject material is interesting.  Tests are a tricky  - but its easy to do fairly well in the class. Lambert seems willing to help and cares about students

Lambert is sometimes interesting in class. He is not very confident in his slides and you can tell by the way he answers logical questions that conflict with his slides. On a grading note, his tests are of a mediocre difficulty with a couple questions that are pretty ambiguous. Easy B+ with extracre
Interesting course material, not very difficult, approachable, knows what he's talking about

I liked him the most of the three. He went at a good pace, lectures were clear, and his test fairly covered the material covered in lecture. Not the most dynamic or exciting teacher, but its obvious he still cares about the material. Still a good professor.
Lambert was pretty good.  He wasn't super clear in some of his lectures, but that's about it.
Lambert was my favorite out of the 3 professors. His lectures were interesting and clear and he has a very endearing style of teaching.

His lectures were constantly interrupted by his research. I appreciate the attempt to introduce advanced topics in an introductory class, but his research just wasn't very interesting (and it's validity could be questioned). He tried and seemed nice, but his exam was not well written at all.
Not very clear but a nice guy
The worst of the 3, he doesnt teach well at all, but a nice guy i guess.
Not Bad
No Comments
I honestly don't know what his deal is.  He's the pushover of the psych department and he seems to be proud of it.  The word "tool" comes to mind when talking about Lambert.  Lambert, ha!
No Comments
No Comments
Super long readings and not a very engaging lecturer, but she is caring and accommodating towards students. She grades generously, so if you can get through long readings, you'll get a good grade.
I love her! Super nice, easy content, clear lectures, fun discussions. She assigns a lot of reading, but just graded on reflection journals. Easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She is extremely nice and assigns a ton of reading. I would highly recommend her and her courses to any WashU student.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor was very caring and nice. Be prepare to read 50 pages text before each class because this class is very discussion heavy. I learned a lot about the culture and different perspectives through this course. Very interesting points of views were discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very caring and inspiring. Topics are highly relevant and she is dedicated to involving everyone in conversation. Extremely validating, which encourages students to participate. Didn't love the readings she chose, and she assigned a ton of reading for homework. However, she integrates it well in class. Extremely personable, take a class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a wonderful professor, I'm so glad I had her. Strongly would recommend taking any class she offers, she makes every student feel respected and teaches you a lot without making her class ridiculously stressful. You should definitely read and participate but if you have an off day it's nbd. Can't say enough good things about her.
Truly the nicest professor ever and makes you so comfortable discussing difficult topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I enjoyed her class. You get to know everyone because of all the group work.
Great class. I'll use these skills for sure
great class
I wanted this class to last for two semesters
She's a great professor. Highly recommend!
She's flexible with students and understanding, If you pay attention and put forth some effort, you'll get an A in her class.
Helpful lectures if you're paying attention. I've learned a lot in this class, and I highly recommend her

More than 50% of my grade is in the air right now because she has not graded our major assignments, she is pretty tough with grading and usually it is not reflective of the rubric. I would have taken this with a different professor if I didn't need to graduate early.
Great class. I gained some skills that boosted my confidence when it comes to writing and also giving presentations.

I liked going to this class most of the time because she changed things up and it was usually something different. She also gave really good feedback and let students revise their work for a higher grade.

I like that she always tried to get everyone involved in the class discussions, and I learned a lot about technical communication that's already been helpful. Her class went by pretty fast because her lectures were interesting and we worked in small groups a lot. She's a cool person too.

Very nice person and very caring about her students. As a teacher, she was ok. Didn't really learn that much or felt engaged. The class itself is not entertaining so that's not her fault. Outdated and unhelpful resumes and cover letters during the career unit. Don't procrastinate on the final report, or it'll be a pain to finish during finals week.

Professor Bialek is a really nice professor, she's really helpful outside of class. She assigns a fair amount of reading. Her class is way more philosophy based than I thought it would be, which makes the lectures sometimes a bit hard to follow and sometimes a bit too theoretical imo. Overall, the topics were interesting and I learned a lot.

i love bialek!!! i've taken good life and love and reason with her (good life is very philosophical, but those lectures were amazing. legitimately) i am not a reader but she is so very good at breaking down the reading to make sense and integrate it with other materials and ideas. she is so understanding and flexible about extensions. 1000/10

"The good life between religion and politics" is a lot more philosophical than the course description sounds (especially for the first half of the semester). Because of that, it wasn't my favorite class but great professor and not too much work

Professor Bialek does an amazing job discussing very interesting topics. She is very understanding of extenuating circumstances and is such a good person. The readings she chooses are genuinely interesting, and I have nothing but good things to say about her!

Professor Bialek is caring and thoughtful. She is an engaging lecturer and is friendly to the students. Her major assignments take time but she is more than happy to help you and you get chances to improve your grade.

Professor Bialek is insightful, helpful, and super nice and accommodating. I highly recommend taking "The Good Life Between Religion and Politics" with her at some point. She ensures you have multiple chances to get a good grade, and the course content is super interesting and relevant to how we live our lives.

She's amazing and hands-down the best professor I've ever had- and perhaps the most knowledgeable, as well. It is a little intimidating to speak up in class because of it but she is very validating and respects all ideas, even if they're nowhere near as informed or complex as her own. Would absolutely recommend for Thinking about Religion!

Great professor -- very passionate about the subject and incredibly knowledgeable. A conversation with Prof. Bialek will show you how little you actually know about the readings for her class. Very accessible, and gives great, thorough feedback on essays. Would highly recommend Thinking About Religion as an introductory RS course.

Probably one of the worst professors I have taken. Grades extremely biased and contradictory. Lectures are extremely boring as he goes on tangents and confuses himself. Seems like a smart man, but cannot articulate what he is trying to say. I would not take this course again, and I do not recommend.
Very sweet and knowledgable. Unfortunately, not a great professor. Lectures are monotonous and as I am writing this (over 3 months into the semester), a single grade has been put in the grade book.
Success is dependent entirely on understanding of readings, but the professor clearly has a good heart
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I understand why people *don't* like Dr. Larson but he is very insightful. The feedback he gives on essays is more comprehensive than many of my writing professors. He also allows revisions, which leaves room for improvement. My main critiques would be that his grading turnaround time is long and the syllabus is a bit confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't get a single grade back until the end of the semester. Received final grades WEEKS into the NEXT semester. Extremely unfair and biased grading. Lectures consisted of him going on random tangents. The readings were barely explained. Absolutely NEVER take a class with him. It felt like a complete waste of time and I Iearned basically nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took in Spring 2022. Cares a lot about the topics but at times is tangential in lecture and the content can be very repetitive in general. Grades not returned until end of semester with no specific feedback offered. Really nice tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This dudes voice will put you to sleep in 4 minutes. Do not go to lecture.

Larson can be a bit dry at first, but if you're really willing to engage with him on the theory you'll find that he's really a sweet, kind man who is really interested in what he teaches. You really have to make the effort! His tests aren't hard; he gives you all the materials you need to do well both on the test and in lecture--but they ARE long.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had him for molecular evolution. The concepts were poorly taught and Dr. Larson seems to have a tough time articulating what he means. The importance of concepts compared to one another was completely unclear. The course was only made more confusing when he told us to disregard parts of our reading in exchange for his contrary ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: awful worst prof in bio dept.

His lectures are incredibly boring and he repeats the same thing over and over with different words. He often starts sentences and doesn't finish them. I stopped going to class because I couldn't pay attention during his lectures. He's the easier professor, but I enjoyed Duncan's section more because it was  interesting.

Larson's part of 2970 is the reason I got an A, just memorize how to answer his questions and you'll be fine. Stats should really be a prereq for this class, I had no idea what poisson distributions or statistical parameters were when I was in the class and it made the content very difficult to understand, I was just going through the motions.
Larson is an extremely slow lecturer but cares about his class. 100000x better than Duncan, which isn't saying much.

Larson is a pretty boring lecturer, not going to lie. However, he definitely has good intentions; he patiently answers questions in lecture. The material for this second half of the course was a lot of calculation and understanding parameters, which I thought was confusing and not clarified in lectures a lot of the time.
It seems like he's trying to teach well, but the class is extremely boring and usually poorly motivated. I came out understanding very little of why we were doing the calculations we were doing.

Professor Larson is a nice guy but his lectures are very boring and drawn out since he speaks very slowly. Just watch the videos online at 2x speed. Pretty easy exams compared to Duncan's half but averages are way higher so you have to do even better to beat the mean.

Overall a good teacher who is very knowledgeable in evolutionary biology. The material definitely gets a little dry, but it's not too bad. His material is also way easier than Duncan's, so it's a nice change of pace when he starts teaching. Do the problem sets, old exams, and memorize terms and you'll do fine.
Textbook use was low, but overall as long as you do the practice problems and practice exams, you should be able to do well on the tests.

Cares about his students. (He sent the whole class an email because some girl left behind a hairbrush--haha.) But his lectures are VERY boring. He tends to be slow and wordy. It is amusing when he gets so excited about biology. Learn the definitions and do the old exams. 3rd exam mean is high, which makes it hard to do well (z-score wise).

The material is not the most interesting (sometimes boring), but Larson really cares about the class/subject and is a really nice guy!  His exams are very easy, and I definitely learned a lot in this class.

His lectures notes were a bit disorganized as one has to jump from notes on the board to notes on the powerpoint to notes that he states but that are not written down anywhere.  If you pay close attention during lecture, however, you can grasp the concepts.  The exams are extremely easy and he reuses questions.
Great Professor. Very reasonable teacher. Tests come straight from the notes. Great class.
SO BORING

Although he has a monotone, he is one hundred times than whoever teaches the first part of the course. He is very clear about what he is saying and tries to incorporate philosophy, geology and history into biology, which is very educational.

He taught the second part of the course, which is significantly easier than the first part. Not the most interesting material in the world, but he tries. He's also pretty boring, but he does have his moments. He cares about the subject and his students.

Nice guy, but a medicore teacher.  While sometimes interesting, his lectures often suffered from a monotone delivery and abstruse terminology and definitions.  His exam questions were much easier than those of Duncan.
Sooo boring!!!
Not a good teacher.  Class is extremely boring with powerpoint slides.
Really nice guy. Very quiet, and laidback lecture style, but I thought he was pretty clear. Learned a lot.

cool guy. VERY SMART. frighteningly so...hence him coming across slightly bizarre. fair grader and he gives the potion to rewrite papers. all in all I learned a lot and was constantly scratching my head tryig to understand the concepts...great experience.

disorganized, boring, dull, math all over the place, no social content which you'd think he'd have since he's atlking about darwinism and we all know what consequences that had (i.e. social darwinism). Extremely unhelpful in office hours, detached, uninterested and seems like teaching is a nuisance
No Comments

One of the most godawful profs at WU. If you can avoid, him do so! Boring in class, tough grader, doesn't relate to students; he belongs to that class of scientists who think of teaching as a nuisance and hence treat you like $*it when you talk to them. Hard to take notes in his class, no org.
very helpful.  lectures can be boring.  quirky guy, and very nice.  Macroev required a lot of reading but tests are organized taking that into consideration
Boring, knowledgeable
boring as hell
absolutely best professor at washu, super engaging, really cares for his students, fun classes. hard exams but they're open note, he just wants you to really think. 100000% would recommend
GOAT professor
Amazing teacher. Lectures are easy to understand.

This has been one of my favorite classes at WashU so far! I took it over the summer and found all of the content really interesting. Tony is very kind & understanding; he is great at explaining all of the details in the class and tying everything into the bigger picture.

I took this class over the summer, and by far, Tony was my favorite professor. He is extremely invested in his students' progress in the class and his students as individuals. I could only be so fortunate to have him as my pre-med advisor. Biology of cancer is difficult, however, utilizing all of the resources provided ensures a good outcome.
Goat
Dean Smith teaches very challenging material. But, he is kind, caring, and always wants the very best for his students.

10/10 would recommend taking any class offered by Prof Smith, he really cares about his students and wants everyone to get the content +succeed. Really sweet guy and clearly cares about his field a lot.
He's such a great guy. Bio of cancer is definitely very difficult but he is very committed to making sure you get the outcome you want.

reviews.comment: definitely a class that is easy to pass. she is very quirky and does often go off into tangents about topics. I found the subjects interesting, but usually the classes felt long and boring. The readings are also very long.
Literally the sweetest funniest woman ever
Highly rated for a reason. PMP is a fun course everyone should take.

I absolutely love Baril, she's such as sweetheart and is always ready to help her students. I also really enjoyed her class, i literally recommend it to everyone. Please take this class its so interesting.

One of the sweetest and most approachable professors. Incredibly organized, passionate, and always willing to help. Lead interesting lectures. Mapping assignments can be tedious, but overall not too much work. I had a health emergency during finals and Baril was the most understanding of all my professors. Definitely cares about her students!

Amazing professor. Class topics are quite interesting, and she encourages everyone to contribute. You can miss up to 3 classes, miss more and lose 15% of your total grade. Attendance is strict; nevertheless, she always learns the students names and is willing to meet outside of class. Email responses are somewhat slow. No exams or quizzes.

Baril is a great teacher and the readings and learning checks are very rewarding as they often come up in other classes. The grading scale makes it easier for students to get a good grade. The final project is all up to you and besides the beginning module, the class is very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Present Moral Problems serves as a great Intro to Philosophy course! Prof. Baril sparked discussions in every class and lectures were always lively! A mix of take-home exams and projects spread throughout the semester; take notes and attend office hours for help and you'll be fine! Prof. Baril was always enthusiastic and made class enjoyable!

Professor Baril is a great professor, and even though my class was a bit quieter, she never failed to make every topic really interesting to discuss. Initially, I wasn't excited to take PMP, but it was my favorite class so far at WashU!
She is the best!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Baril is by far one of the best professors iv had here at WashU. Her lectures are engaging because she is always enthusiastic and encourages conversation. Her expectations are made clear from the beginning and she isn't harsh in grading. As long as you keep up with the readings, her courses are fairly easy.

A very kind person and instructs Present Moral Problems in an engaging, approachable way. A bit of an adjustment at the beginning to such a discussion-based class but the topics are very interesting. Only tricky thing is the writing assignments, which take quite a bit of time from experience, but put in the work and you'll succeed.

Professor Baril is an incredibly kind and caring professor. She stumbles a lot while giving lectures but you can tell she's passionate and is really trying her best. I dropped the class because I didn't feel like the class discussions adequately prepared me for writing the papers. I would have switched it to an audit if the deadline hadn't passed.

Professor Baril is extremely caring and kind, it is evident she cares about her students. Her class is discussion based, which can sometimes be awkward if students aren't willing to participate. Nevertheless, the workload is very light, and she is an easy grader. Overall, an easy class that will force you to think!

Prof. Baril is really nice and I enjoyed Present Moral Problems. It was a pretty easy class, and Baril is a very generous grader. Sometimes the lectures were kind of boring and there were long, dense readings occasionally, but mostly we just spent class debating different topics and the homework was typically light.
I struggled in the beginning, but Dr. Baril gave really good feedback that helped me for the rest of the semester. She's very helpful and makes herself accessible outside of class all the time.

Dr. Baril is probably the most caring professor I've worked with in my entire undergraduate career, always willing to go the extra mile and even beyond that for her students. She designs her class so that it's almost impossible to do poorly if you show up every day, and the daily quizzes are easy points and will motivate you to go to class.
never give enough pratice questions
She is a good teacher!

reviews.comment: Ok, she expects that you know why more than you are required and straight up doesn't teach the material she tests you on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. The course is curved after the final so it is possible to do well, but it is not worth struggling to teach yourself every bit of material in the class, as you will not be able to follow any of the lectures unless you are already an economist.

Every point I made in class, she seemed to shoot down, and she was kind of mean about it, which I found very discouraging, as it was a discussion course. I was excited to take the class and found it interesting, but her approach felt passive-aggressive and not open-minded.

Professor Cislo is the best professor I've had at WashU. She gives amazing lectures that are very engaging. Grading is very fair. You get out of it what you put in. WGGS 100B with Cislo is a 100% must take.
I absolutely loved intro to WGSS with Dr. Cislo. They are very passionate, knowledgable, and patient. They seem to genuinely care about students. There are many opportunities to get your grade up!

I've taken a couple of classes with Professor Cislo and enjoyed both. She cultivates a welcoming atmosphere and is clearly passionate about what she teaches. The courses were both discussion-based which keeps you engaged. Professor Cislo's grading criteria are very clear so you're set up for success as long as you do the readings and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment:
Cislo was really good at helping me understand the material and apply it to other readings. Very homework heavy but still very interesting to learn about. In-class was more discussion (about the readings) based than lecture based, especially as the semester went by. 
There were a lot of ways to raise your grade and tests were pretty easy
Dr. Cislo facilitates great discussion!

Amy is a truly caring and down-to-earth professor. One of the best Intro WGSS professors you can have. However, they do assign quite a lot of readings, so be prepared to dedicate 1-3 hours on each assignment. But, every reading makes you think. Very discussion-based, but definitely a class every WashU student should take, regardless of major.

Her class is easy, and she's a chill grader, so if that's what you're looking for, go ahead. But, I don't think I gained anything from her class. She's rather close-minded, and for her, a lot of things she considers to be black and white, and not at all grey (doesn't consider context). Very condescending toward people she doesn't agree with.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This is an incredibly easy class, especially if you take it as an upperclassman. Amy is wonderful and I learned a TON! This class really helped me to identify as even more of a feminist and stand up for myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Would take again

reviews.comment: Cislo is so amazing and understanding.  She really is there for all of her students and wants you to succeed.  The class is really discussion based and she perfectly splits putting her own opinion and letting you and the class form your own.  Also, she does a good job of bringing everything together and explaining new terms and connections clearly.

If you have the chance to take a class with Cislo, DO IT. She is fantastic. She doesn't dominate the lectures, yet she provides her opinions and makes them extremely interesting to listen to. She is hilarious and does a good job covering the material and making it interesting. Would love to take another class with her.

Amber Jones is the sweetest most caring extravagant person. I cannot rave enough about how lovely taking her class was. She made Fridays enjoyable somehow and brought us snacks for the early morning. I would recommend her over and over again because she is super understanding. I made some of the best friends in this class as well and I'll miss it.

You have to be engaged in class, lots of activities, talking, reading, presentations, etc. But she is super nice, is understanding if you need to leave (but do not abuse it), and is very, very, very passionate about what she is teaching.

Dr. Jones is amazing and understanding, by far my favorite professor. She cares about student success, gives a buffer time in the beginning of class, has short breaks throughout class, and listens to what students need. Class involves a short lecture, discussions, and a tiny group project.  assignments are reasonable and not harshly graded.
She is understanding and caring, and she is very meticulous about your playing that she may seem intimidating. But, she is overall a great person and a hard worker who wants the best for you.
She is very understanding and caring, and at the same time, she is meticulous about your playing. She is a great person and a hard worker who wants the best for you.

She moves very quickly, WAY too much work for a 2 credit class.  She also seems angry a lot of the time...maybe because her students don't practice enough. You really need to practice and learn the material - she gives pop piano quizzes and long written mid terms and finals

As others said before, she moves VERY quickly. She plays absolutely beautifully herself, but expects the students to be able to keep up. I had to practice a TON outside of class in order to barely get the assignments down, and then we'd be on to the next topic. If you are looking to learn piano just for fun, I wouldn't suggest her.
She will move fast, so keep up. Practice an hour before if you are very good at another instrument. If not, couple times over at least two days before the next class.
No Comments

She is an amazing piano player, but she moves very, very quickly.  She expects a lot of outside practice out of her students, and she assigns a lot of work for each class.  If you've never taken piano before, I would suggest taking private lessons in concurrence with this course.

The class for me was rather easy. The test is toned down for people who know nothing about philosophy. I got 100% for two of my exams. I do not know why others complain about her grading. But her lecture is indeed quite boring. Passing the microphone to hapless students is a futile exercise. Some students spoke with wisdom hollower than a vacuum.

Her reading assignments are all over the place and it is hard to grasp the essence of the text especially when the texts are hard to read themselves. Lacking organization. Grading seems arbitrary no matter how hard you try. Self-absorbed, and I was interrupted for several times when I was talking because she has to correct me based on her thoughts
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't understand Gais' higher rating. Demotivating and self-absorbed lecturer. Dont *learn* anything in class + the homework is just reading/annotations which is deceptively easy. Tests have quote IDs and she has illogical grading. Interesting material that she ruins with her narcissistic lecture style. Steer clear for lecture classes.

I did well in her class, but Dr. Gais is not cut out for teaching large lectures like 106. She treated it like a discussion section—lectures just consisting of passing a microphone around and hearing hypotheticals + Q&A (essentially pointless). Every class she'd use cuss words to try and seem cool, but it was cringey. I didn't learn anything useful

As a political THEORY class she actually covered only LITTLE theory and ideologies; all the readings are leftists, so what about the second half on the political spectrum? What about Burke? What about Hobbes, Locke and F.A. Hayek? Those who give her a high rating has exact the same terrible taste as hers. Shame for you guys

WTF is the meaning of reading ANTIGONE?? LOOK IN MY EYES AND TELL ME,  is that political theory? Same for Lorde and King, those are great social activists but they should not appear in the INTRO to THEORY class. UNPROFESSIONAL CLASS!

Gais isn't the usual prof for poli theory, but she did amazing. Readings were enjoyable and manageable and while lectures aren't mandatory, they're super helpful. People who gave low ratings likely don't know how to take proper notes and expect to just copy and paste from slides. Exams were a breeze as long as you attended lectures or just read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I know Gais will not be teaching Intro to Political Theory next year, so I can't account for how she is in smaller classes, but this was not very good. The lectures were not very informative, and the second exam was oddly different than the first and third.

A large lecture with exams is not the best for political theory but she did a fantastic job! She exposed us to a many authors across time, race, etc. and expanded my view of what political theory looks like. She makes lectures seminar-like, with lots of question time and analysis. Just read the texts, listen well, and you will do well.

I feel she is not qualified to teach large lecture classes. She ran our 200-student lecture class as if it were a 10-person discussion section. Also, get ready for the most ambiguous test questions. The whole class failed the second midterm (70 average) and refused to take any blame for the poorly written questions and instead blamed us entirely.

reviews.comment:
NONSENSE that she get such a high rating score.

(1) TERRIBLE teaching style: letting students read quotes during the lecture & waste time 
(2) BAD reading list choice, don't expect to learn what you want 
(3) use AWKWARD multiple choices that you cant understand why this is the answer. 
(4) A MEAN score of 74 for EXAM 2

DONT COME, RUN !
Take this class; don't be afraid to share your thoughts on the readings.
Show up to class; do the readings. Really good class overall.

Dr. Gais is, without question, the best professor I have had over the course of my college career (I am a senior). When you engage in the class, you will learn so much, be exposed to new and different ideas, and be challenged. You have to put in the work and be on top of things, and if you are, you will succeed without a doubt.

TAKE THIS CLASS! Learned so much and felt like a much better student coming out of it. You have to go to class and participate consistently to get a good participation grade, but you'll feel smarter after doing it. Prof is super great and so intelligent. You get what you put into this class for sure. The students control the experience. No screens.
Show up to class. You have to participate frequently its discussion based. Gais is awesome. No screens.

Absolutely no criteria for grading, very subjective. She grades things based on her own opinion of them and doesn't tell students how she is going to grade projects until after students turn it in. Be prepared to participate, participation is heavily weighted, though she does prefer to call on male students. Nice professor, but doesn't grade well.

Extremely interesting material and class discussions. King and willing to work with students. Very manageable workload. However, she strongly favors people and voices that agree with her own as well as non-outspoken individuals, and this is reflected in the grade you get.

Class is exceptionally easy, but the only grade with actual stakes is participation, and there is no actual indication of your participation until you get the final grade back. Stay on her good side or else you'll be in trouble with no discernible warning.
Fantastic teacher, with really in-depth knowledge on a lot of issues and very interaction/discussion-focused classroom environment.

Really chill professor, sometimes maybe a little too chill. Facilitates really insightful class discussions, however, depending on who your classmates are and how interested you are in the subject matter, you might find her classes to be a waste of time or one of the best classes you have ever taken.
All around amazing. All her classes are super low stress and enjoyable if you love political theory. Would highly recommend.

reviews.comment: I didn't feel like I learned anything and it was boring
Very kind and understanding professor. Her class is a treat compared to my other more lecture-based classes. Reading and homeworks are all very manageable.

Dr. Gais teaches the most chill Poli Sci class at WashU. No tests/quizzes, just weekly annotations and brief written reflections. The class itself also entails lots of intellectual discussions about exigent issues in politics today. Would highly recommend taking her class if you are a Political Science major.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is one of the easiest courses I have taken thus far. There are readings, discussions, and weekly reflections. No exams.

Professor Gais is definitely my favorite professor. The class is discussion-based and super engaging. She is not a harsh grader, and she doesn't give a lot of pressure on the students. Will recommend it to everyone.

Amy is a fantastic professor. She makes sure her students get the most out of her class but never makes us feel stressed. Her Text and Tradition classes are mostly discussion based, which is great if you're more of a collaborative learner. She really makes you think before you speak, and she makes you think better, if that makes sense. 10/10.
Dr. Gais is an amazing professor. You'll be excited to show up to class. Would 100% recommend taking a class with her at some point. You won't regret it

Professor Gais isthe best professor I have had here at WashU. I took modern political thought with her and got so much for the class. Highly recommend. Taking another one of her classes next semester.
One of the most kind and caring professors at WashU. Dr. Gais genuinely wants you to succeed and become a better writer and thinker, and she will help you out as much as possible along the way.

reviews.comment: Super awesome, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. HC changed my life! I took GAIA and it quite literally changed my way of thinking about the world. Please take a class with her if you can! She doesn't assign too much homework and the essays aren't too long. My final paper, which was crafting my gender analysis practice, was one of the coolest papers I've ever written.

I loved Dr. HC in the GCP class.  She is an incredibly strong woman, and clearly very passionate about Ireland and gender studies. Amy expects a lot as she should, but is available to help and clarify if needed.  I highly recommend getting to know Dr. HC if you have the opportunity.

Gender/IR/Irish History are clearly Dr. HC's passions and she is a phenomenal instructor, even though I had no experience in any field. Readings were often tough and class structure varied widely, but this was outlined in the syllabus and was to be expected. Dr. HC was always willing to explain concepts more and justify grades. HIGHLY recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. HC cares so much about both her students and gender studies. Her passion always shines through. I loved the course content and her, although the reading was way too much and the class was often a bit unorganized. Felt like a little community. Definitely have to put the effort in, but I learned a lot. She is available and talking to her helps.

I had Heath-Carpentier for Gender Analysis in IAS, which taught me so much. Heath-Carpentier is caring and open-minded, but I felt she was disorganized. Her lectures were hard to follow and she graded harshly without clear feedback. Thankfully there were opportunities to gain back points so I was able to receive an A. I recommend the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Amy HC is a lot of work and very theory focused but when you show up to class she explains things. Best prof I have had thus far. Cannot recommend enough. Also insanely good career advice!

Pond is a fantastic human being. The only flaw she has is how deeply she understands the content, where it can be hard to track what she is saying. Likewise, Game Theory for Political Scientists is very heavy on the notation, which can also be confusing.

Do take her courses!

Amy is a really caring professor who genuinely wants all of her students to succeed. The lectures can be a little bit wordy or unclear at times, but she is accessible during office hours and there is only one exam early in the semester. The final project is relatively simple and the rest of the graded material is generally straight forward.

Lectures dragged out quite a bit. Attendance was mandatory and would give pop quizzes occasionally on really unnecessarily long readings. Despite all these negatives, however, Dr. Pond was extremely caring, a very fair grader, and always willing to help outside of class.

Dr. Pond's lectures were informative in the subject, but definitely a little drab. Grading for exams/essay/presentations was very forgiving. Attendance was mandatory and frequently checked. The course pace was slow yet grew disorganized towards the end due to not keeping on pace with the content. Textbook not really needed to succeed.

Really supportive and kind professor. If you're ever having trouble Pond is always extremely accessible and willing to help, just make sure to reach out to her. Only complaint is that lectures would sometimes drag too long.

Doesn't rly know material too well. Convinced she is a spy larping as a CS professor, would be the only backstory that makes sense. Entire course is ripped off of Berkeley's Intro to AI (with Berkeley watermarks in assignments). Class is interesting/easy though.

i feel like everyone is so dramatic. the lectures can be boring and exams can be hard, but she gives extensions, grades very nicely, and gives so much extra credit. if you just do the homework's and actually do the projects you will do just fine in this class.

Took 412A and 3050 with Athena Tabakhi. She mainly reads slides without an in-depth explanation. 412A reused Berkeley materials that were better taught. 3050 was lab/project-based, but labs lacked any sort of guidance, and one project wasn't even graded by her; it was graded by peers, which I don't even know if that's allowed. Would not recommend.
She once spent the whole class doing nothing but reading out the output from ChatGPT for her lecture... that's how this course was taught, as least that's what happened in 2023.
I really liked this professor W
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I advise future students to avoid this course. The course provides pseudo-code, so most projects share the same logic, and submissions are compared to previous ones. As the code base grows, the chance of unintentionally repeating past code increases. The instructor is arbitrary, offering only two options: deducting points or a hearing.
I'm convinced she's either a low-level NPC or part of a social experiment.
Pretending to be a professor.

Went to 1st 2 lectures, found out a lot of what she said was blatantly wrong, and then never went again. She would sometimes walk around studio, but never actually offered to help anyone. The one time someone in my studio group asked her for help, she said she couldn't help because she herself didn't create the assignment. Was not good :(

Tabakhi seemed to know concepts well but didn't take the time to explain them. You will learn and understand most of the concepts in this class by doing homework as the lectures are pretty useless in explaining things. You are also not taught a single Python package or line of code in this class so good luck coding the projects all by yourself.

I first took CSE247 with Tabakhi and strongly disliked her as a professor. However, I feel as though she does better teaching higher level material in 412. I've enjoyed her lectures more and feel like she knows the content better than in 247. Overall, pleasantly surprised with the course after a poor experience in 247 with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Tabakhi seemed to lack professional knowledge and was unable to answer student's questions accurately. In fact, she doesn't seem to understand student's struggle every time. The pace of the class is sometimes too slow and she still doesn't do a good job explaining the important concept. She heavily relies on her slide.

I would just say don't go to her lectures. Even if you can't go to another professors lectures you're better off going to google than her. Her lectures often get needlessly complicated, she simply wrong a lot, and usually just reads off the slides.
Exams are difficult but curved. Homework can be long but only 3 throughout the semester, and she is very flexible in giving extensions.

I never left one of her lectures feeling less confused than when I had walked in. If you have her as a lecturer, I highly recommend either just going to another professor's lecture or relying on the textbook.
Lectures are difficult to understand, kinda just steamrolls through the slides. How often you go to office hours and talk to the TAs in this class will likely be the deciding factor for your grade.

Tabakhi is a terrible professor. Attendance dropped to probably 1/4-1/3 by the fourth lecture. I stopped going completely after that and did just fine in the class. Explanations are convoluted and difficult to understand. When asked to help with a problem on a test, she said that "she couldn't help with problems she didn't write" and got defensive.

She is a little misunderstood. I came into the course very concerned she also has a reputation for making very difficult exams. However, throughout the course, my perspective seriously changed. She gave me extra points for my first exam. I would recommend to participate in class so she recognizes you and she will return the favor. Know math.

She ripped the whole class content from stanford but with much less depth yet she still is incapable of explaining any of the concepts well in class. She does pollevs worth like 5% of your whole grade to make you come to class but you wont see a single person paying attention because she cant teach.
Terrible. Lectures are really confusing, and she never hosted office hours. She missed 25% of the lectures of the semester due to various reasons. Jealous of those who enrolled in another section.

Exam are 30% total of grade, but you can achieve 100% on everything else. If you attempt to study for the exams, you will probably have to use the textbook and online resources from UC Berkeley (the class is entirely copied from ucb cs 188). Her lectures will familiarize you with the content. 3 projects, 7 HWs, attendance only 4%. Not super helpful

For 247, get Cole if you can. Tabakhi's lectures are really confusing and she's not very accessible outside of the class. She sometimes reads through the slides and does not explain the contents at all. However, if you get her like me, it's okay. The grading is pretty easy and I learned the most by reading Cole's slides!

The fact that Professor Tabakhi has a PhD in CS is honestly astounding. There is no point in going to lectures because she cannot explain the material. I find it hard to believe she didn't sustain a serious head injury since being hired. I went to her for help just once, and she said she couldn't answer CS questions she didn't write. Disgraceful.

She cares about the students learning the material well and tries to make the lectures engaging. The course is modeled after Berkeley's so there's plenty of online support. The projects are fun though the exams are hard. As long as you pay attention and do the work, you should have a good time. I really enjoyed the class!

Athena is a really bad lecturer. She talks too quietly to hear in the back. Even if you can hear her, she still explains concepts so poorly. BUT, if you get her for 247, you are not screwed! Don't even bother going to her lectures -- Go to Sievers' lectures or watch his recorded lectures. Luckily, there are other ways to learn besides her content.

She's okay. The class is literally a copy of berkeley's so I would recommend if you dont like her lectures to look up the berkeley ones and do the exercises. The exercises are pretty much practice exams for the midterm and final so def pay attention when she goes over those.

even though she copies the materials from CS188 she can't teach.
She can only use tough exam to proof her existence. What a shame!

lecture is hard to follow and has little correlation with projects. You will have to learn python all by yourself in order to do the projects, which are super long.
Midterm was pretty difficult, and there is like zero practice for the exam except few exercise she mentioned in class. And it count 20% of the grade.
Absolutely terrible professor. Class content does not relate to projects. You are left learning/relearning much on your own. Would recommend taking the course with another professor.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Entire course content taken from Berkeley's AI course and it seemed even she was confused by it. She made multiple mistakes during class and was often corrected by students. Half of the course grade is also very hard exams. A class avg of 80 on midterm was deemed too high so no extra credit opportunities.

247 is a huge class, so I don't blame Professor Tabakhi for seeming distant. That said, sometimes the lack of energy does detract from the quality of lectures. She sometimes blazes through important stuff and proceeds to linger on more trivial material. Also doesn't do much other than reiterate pre-lecture content. Not bad, just rather boring.

Seems like a very genuine very fair and caring professor. Lectures are a bit boring but he sprinkles in some humor which helps. If the lectures were not 80 minutes but 50 minutes it would be much better as they can drag on a little towards the end. Exams are very fair and do not ask anything unexpected. Overall great experience taking his class.

The tests are really straightforward and if you go to all the lectures and study a little before the test, you'll be able to do well! Lectures aren't always super interesting and a lot of it is memorization though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice guy! Not the best lecturer but is receptive to feedback and simplifies the concepts so that they're easier to understand. Most of the class is rote memorization and based on what he says so take pretty thorough notes. Pretty easy class, but the whole thing is based on exams so if you're not a good test taker, you're gonna have to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Looks, dresses, and talks like Kevin Spacey. Decent lecturer with good humor. Advice to Andy: Reduce exams from 5 to 4. Use Canvas announcements instead of Canvas DMs. Make lecture material more accessible (recorded lectures and/or study guides with detailed guide of what you would like us to know). Fix microphone issues so students can hear you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: typical language class here at washu so the load is pretty heavy. carey is a good person and wants us to succeed in learning Spanish; however, she does speak in a way that is lowk sounds like she is babying us. it is hard to ask for extensions or special requests and doesn't really prepare us well for the exams.

She does not give as in deep exam preparation as the other teachers in this course, such as exam practice sheets, which other teachers do give. I ended the class with an 89% because I accidentally turned in a blank file for notes we had to turn in and I didn't notice until a few weeks later and she is very strict with grades, so she didn't care.

The homework is essential, but Carey's expectations are always very clear. If you get your work done and care about the content, this should be a solid class for you. Tests always felt harder than the rest of the work, but are a moderate part of the grade. If you genuinely want to learn Spanish, this will teach you.

The sweetest woman alive. There's a lot of work for this class, and it moves quickly, so it can be challenging to fully grasp concepts, but Carey is an angel: so kind and helpful. She cold calls, but it makes meeting the participation requirements easy. If you like Spanish and want to improve, take this class.

Professor Carey is a great teacher and person. She cares a lot about her students and wants them to succeed. Workload isn't bad at all as long as you stay on top of it, especially supersite. She's not the easiest grader when it comes to tests but she's definitely reasonable. One of the best Spanish teachers here, she deserves a much better rep!

Professor Carey is very fun and caring in a cool aunt way. But when it comes to classwork and homework, she don't play. There is VHL Supersite work that is always assigned in the class, but you're able to work ahead and it's not hardly difficult to get done as long as you're caught up in the class. Do your best everyday and the class will be good.

Carey is a good professor, she cares a lot about her students and she's very nice but she is a very tough grader. There are a lot of assignments in this class and although she gives clear explanations, it is hard to do well in this class.

She printed out textbook pages so buying looseleaf not necessary, but do need access to VHL. Grades very harshly but eases up at the end of the semester. Takes off a lot of participation points for being late to class. Some busy work. Hard to do well. Nice person. Takes long to respond to emails. Understanding if you talk to her in office hours.

She was very passive aggressive and made me dread going to class. She will get mad if you aren't giving her your undivided attention and leave rude comments to you on canvas and decrease your grade. Take the class pass fail, it'll save your GPA and reduce your stress.

extremely caring and allowed me exceptions and extensions because of mental health reasons. just had to communicate with her about those issues before the date of the assessment or assignment deadline. if you go to class and show you're trying she'll like you

Professor Carey is a nice woman for the most part. However, she is by no means my favorite professor. She WILL NOT give 2nd chances. Miss an assignment due to mental health issues? Too bad, no make-ups. She'll expect you to email back the day of, but won't do the same herself. Would not recommend.
Absolute terrible professor. Would never recommend

I absolutely enjoyed this class. Professor Carey was nothing like I expected. I did hear some negative things about her but this goes to show you that you dont always go by what people say. She was highly engaged with the class. Topics were wonderful. Assignments were meaningful. Kudos to you if you choose this one.

Profa. Carey is very passionate about Spanish and teaching young people. She is very engaged every class period. This class is only taught in Spanish (which can be intimidating at first) but it really allows you to solidify your understanding at a faster rate. I recommend taking Profa. Carey if you are interested in Spanish and ready to work!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I love her. Yes, the work is hard and there is always homework but that is simply the curriculum, she's just amazing at teaching it. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Profesora Carey genuinely cares about how her students perform in class. She assigns a ton of homework, but you learn a lot as a result.

Profesora Carey is an amazing professor who encourages students to go outside of their comfort zones with the language. She is a tough grader, but is always willing to meet students and is very understanding. The course is fast-paced, but so are all the sections of Spanish so it's not her fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a nice person but is out of touch with how to effectively teach this class. The material moves quickly and she doesn't go in depth on some topics that really matter on exams. Exams are not formatted uniformly and sometimes have surprises on them. There's never material learned in class, it's always just review of what was learned at home.

Dr. Carey has high expectations for her students and keeps them accountable. Essentially, she treats them like the adults that they are. So while the material in introductory Spanish classes is difficult, she is incredibly organized, thorough, and always available to help outside of class. She's also really funny. But yes, prepare to work hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors at WUSTL. Extremely harsh for no good reason. Seems like she doesnt really care about students. Would not recommend.

Dr. Carey is well organized and very clear with her expectations. If you are not an extremely self-disciplined person DO NOT take her class. She doesn't give second chances and expects everyone to act like an adult. All the HW & dues make you feel like you are chased by a bear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Carey was so amazing. I felt like we created a real friendship. She is lovely. I learned a lot from her and she explains clearly.
Assigns a lot of work and very harsh. Not good at explaining concepts. Do not take her class.

She has a high rating from old scores. One of Worst professors I had at Wash U. She is not a native speaker, so her methods of teaching are very rote and do not reflect a natural language speaking/learning environment.  Grades harshly, quizzes and tests were often covered in red.

Very difficult professor. Assigns a lot of work and multiple assignments per day. She is great at explaining things and makes the topics interesting. However, she is extremely strict and by the book. SHE WILL KILL YOUR GPA. Definitely helps you learn Spanish, but in a world that values grades, it's simply not worth taking her class. Stay away!

Carey is an amazing professor! By far my favorite Spanish professor at WashU! You have to go to class and do all homework! If you show that you are dedicated to learning the material and participate in class, she will not only ensure that you have all the tools necessary to understand the material, but to succeed in the class.
Very horrible teacher.She does not teach well.
Excellent instructor, I highly recommend Amanda's classes. She is fair and an effective teacher.

Amanda Carey is such a great Spanish professor.  She is pretty hilarious and makes learning the language fun.  Taking this class with her will greatly improve your writing abilities and you should have a strong grammar foundation afterward.  Also, she's nice, approachable, and caring--I highly recommend her!
One word--GPA killer.   JUST STAY AWAY.

Don't let her sweet smile and good looks get you--this woman will kill your GPA. Yes, she's an effective teacher, but she's also a VERY VERY hard grader--the hardest in the Spanish Department. STAY AWAY.

Don't take Carey for 307. Although she teaches well, she's unfair and docks points 4 dumb reasons. 4 example, she docked 20 pts from my friend's 2-page essay just cuz it was 4 lines under. She also subtracts points 4 other trifles, such as having English bosquejos, excess heading, default margins, and other nonsense. She has one of the highest drop

Sra Carey is an organized teacher who clearly explains new material. She's also very helpful during office hours. My only complaint is that she's very stern. Do not expect her to adjust the syllabus, give extra time during exams, or accept late work. She's tough, and she won't bend the rules under any cir****stances. Besides that, she's good.

Sra Carey is awesome.  She makes sure you understand the material and speaks very clearly.  She makes class fun, has a good sense of humor and understands where the students are coming from.  I suggest trying to get into one of her sections if you're taking any of the classes she teaches.

Whoever complains about Carey is ridiculous. She's incredibly amiable and actually cares about her students. She gives you advance warning (she gives you the sheet she's going to collect with a due date written on top -- that's the only thing she ever collects) and is pretty fair when it comes to the grading. She rocks!

Sra. Carey is an unbelievable teacher. yes, she does collect hw but only a few times and she tells you in advance when she is going to. she is so easy to understand, she is funny, and she relates to students easily. take 307 with Sra. Carey.
Sra. Carey is extremely helpful and cares much about her subject.  She is a great teacher and wants each of her students to do well.

i LOVE sra carey. She's made me love Spanish again. She's ALWAYS available to help you out and is so much fun. i look forward to this class. She isn't hard on the homework like the other person said, the only time she takes up homework is when she gives a blue sheet, so you KNOW she'll take it up. Take this class with Sra Carey!

She is one of the few teachers that collects homework and she's real tough grader on particpation, which is worth so much in the class. She actually grades the homework every day while other teachers don't even collect it.

Probably the nicest, most organized, and easiest to understand spanish teacher I have ever had.  If only all spanish teachers could be like her the world (of learning spanish) would be a much better place.
Sra. Carey is very nice and extremely organized. her accent is very easy to understand. definately one of my fav professors.
Excellent teacher.  Very Organized, concerned with her students, helpful, cheerful, excited to teach.  Highly Recommended!
Very nice and always willing to set up apptments with students for office hours if you have trouble with anything.
Great teacher, lots of fun!
Nice comments, Luz
Wonderful professor. Accent easy to understand. Fair grading, even when a certain third group member decides to do nothing and a third of your project is missing.
Least humane Professor I have ever seen
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things
