reviews.comment: If you don't answer at least 2 questions a class, you will fail. Let's guess if there are 50 students in the class, each question takes 2 minutes to answer, if all students participate, he doesn't need to lecture at all! What an easy way to teach! He gives the worst exam and expect you to know everything, even things he never taught before.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Enjoyed going to classes. The assignments are tough mainly because they're usually based on real life data, making things not clear; the professor asks students to make assumptions and move on if stuck. But if you do go through all these, you will learn a lot. Go to classes and ask questions. It is where the professor actually gives you information

Extremely knowledge/intelligent. Puts a lot of work into preparing lectures and the class in general. The weekly problem sets are hard and will probably take a long time. Learned so much finance it's ridiculous. Teaches interesting and useful topics like Monte Carlo Simulation. Can't say enough praise.

Professor Manela isn't easy, but he's very upfront with his expectations. Very approachable for help. Surprisingly funny at times. Not an easy class, but doable. Come prepared and he'll get you where you need to go.
She teaches this class very well. It would be boring with a lot of other professors, but she engages you the whole lecture. Lots of energy!

Would highly recommend taking Prof. Hardin for OB 360. She is a great professor who is highly energetic and makes class enjoyable and applicable to real life. The one problem I had with her was that the grading was not always clear despite giving a rubric. The comments she gave and the rubric did not always line up with the project/paper.
Prof Hardin was great! The lectures were well planned and group assignment were actually enjoyable. One of the most valuable classes Ive taken in undergrad. I recommend her for OB 360 to everyone.

Prof Hardin gives amazing lectures and is one of the best professors at WashU! She keeps students engaged with lots of interactive and fun activities and has restructured the OB course to make content super beneficial and relevant for college students. She is very relatable and funny and always on top of email and there to support students as well!
Demanding but if your hard work will pay off! You exit the class with your mind blown! Make sure you work REALLY hard.
took his "Music in the Holocaust": fascinating class, very demanding but thought provoking. extremely knowledgeable prof.
Took his 'Jewish Identities in Western Music'; a very knowledgeable Prof who sets high standards. Topics were fascinating and relevant far beyond the class.
excellent course (even if very demanding).
Awsome!
Very difficult, not understanding, expectations were way too high for an undergraduate student with little background
Intro to Israel Studies course taught through history, music, and literature.
Finally, ?Intro to Israel Studies? with no political science (thank G-d).

Genuinely the best. Could not recommend enough. She's not only a good teacher that actually provides useful feedback and help, but is the kindest person ever. If you need more time on a project, she will absolutely give it to you to ensure that you produce work that you love and are proud of.

An amazing professor, mentor, and person. Her feedback is never too critical but is VERY constructive and will open your mind to processes you would've never thought of. You can tell that, on top of her knowledge of the material, she cares for all her students and will take time out of her day to help and understand every student as an individual.

Prof. Hubbell is the best teacher I met at Sam Fox, she is very kind, helpful and professional. She always help us when needed and give effective and useful feedback of our work. The 2D class covers the fundamental principles of design and all the projects are very creative and fun. The workload is manageable. Highly recommend taking her class.

Dr. A is dedicated to helping you learn. That does not mean giving you a good grade or saying things the nicest way possible....but you will learn and your work will improve. Her courses are time tested.

Dr. A is brilliant and super funny. She actually cares about us learning basic research methods. I feel like those who don't like her are frustrated with the group work, which is mandatory for Brown, also are maybe being ageist. She's the bomb. She takes teaching very seriously, is avail if you need anything, wants you to learn and be excited.

Nitpicky. Entire class is based on group work except for two exams. Unfair grader (gives those who didn't do any of the group work higher grades than they deserve). Speaks to students as though they are unintelligent. Outdated.

I took this during the 3 week summer term, which was very intense. She really knows her topic, with 30 years experience. She returned papers within a day, with detailed, helpful feedback. She was reliable and cared about our learning. The format was mostly powerpoint lectures, which meant it was content-driven without creative delivery.

This class had the potential to be interesting; it wasn't. The three hour block was wasted with power point presentations and semi-irrelevant debates. Pedagogically, the instructor does many of the things we as educators are told NOT to do. Irrelevant worksheets abound while actual teaching and engagement with the class are missing.

This class was okay, although there were hugely long powerpoints that were extremely boring.  You'd think a 3 hr class would be more discussion based, but it wasn't, really.  Take home exams were not horrible, though, if you used the book.

Augustin is nice.  But... 3-hr long classes: so boring, in-class time is usually wasted except with maybe speakers.  TOO MANY ASSIGNMENTS but she changes the syllabus every year.  Unsettling mix of low-effort (in-class) and high-effort (assignments).  Required for educ. major.
Great class
Great class, super knowledgeable professor!

Microbes and the Environment is not exam-heavy at all, so if you struggle with exam-taking too, this class is perfect for you. You can also really tell how passionate the professor is when she teaches.

This class was the best biology class I've ever taken. Though this is a serious class, she makes jokes in class, which I appreciate . Additionally, the weekly tutorial sections were challenging yet beneficial in that they allowed me to develop scientific literacy skills. Because of this and guest lectures, the material never felt foreign to me.

I loved Microbio with Dr. Bose! She is incredibly kind & a great resource for all her students, plus is fair & offers extra credit. The exams were very similar to the lecture material, which were current & covered relevant topics in the field. Tutorials were challenging sometimes but interesting and rewarding. One of my favorite classes by far!

Dr. Bose is truly one of the best professors I have had at WashU. She made Microbio so interesting and fun to learn. She's one of the most accommodating professors I've ever had and is always willing to help and answer questions if you reach out. As a Bio major, I have taken many advanced bio courses at WashU, and I am so happy I took this one!

Dr. Bose does a great job explaining very difficult concepts. You have to attend lectures and spend a lot of time reading through and memorizing them. The exams are solely based on the lecture material and include some bonus points as well! She is also very helpful if you need assistance outside of class. If you put in the work you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I already posted, but I had more that I wanted to add. Dr. Bose is the first professor that has mentioned being predental to me, and honestly, that really meant a lot to me. She cares about the wide array of things that her students are passionate about. I love STEM jokes, and Dr. Bose definitely slipped some into her lectures making them enjoyable

Dr Bose made this material exciting and made me want to come home and tell my family what I learned in class. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She gives plenty of extra credit and is always available to answer questions. Yes, the material can be difficult but if a student puts forth the effort you can do well.

Dr. Bose is a committed and caring professor. She is very passionate about what she teaches and makes lectures useful and engaging. While there is a high volume of material, there are resources available to succeed. She holds many office hours and is approachable and willing to accommodate you so you can get any help you need. Great class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course went online like other WUSTL classes last spring. Bose did a great job with the transition and I got an A+. The open book, take home exam really helped me with the course content and absorbing it.

Its a 4 credit class so you should expect it to be more work than a 3 credit class. Some intro concepts are talked about which in my opinion was very helpful. Dr. Bose is clearly very smart and thinks microbes are cool. Friday tutorials are often hard. Tests are very long, but its possible to do well. Material can be a little disorganized.

Great class for refreshing old concepts and also great for chem majors for MCAT prep. Just don't slide with classroom work, quizzes and discussionsand you will easily get an A. She gives a half a grade up. So you will get an A+. More than half the class got an A or A+ as their final grade.

Class is curved down to a B- so only about 5 people gets an A-, 10 people gets an A, and nobody gets an A+. Tests are a rehashing of the slides, which you have to memorize completely. Professor is clearly interested in the subject but is also very mean. This class is not required unless you're on the microbiology track, so dont take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Didn't enjoy taking the class. The other commenters must be referring to a different class because the material in 349 is completely unrelated to the MCAT. Frankly, I forgot everything I learned from microbio after taking the class because it was pure useless memorization. Don't make the same mistake as I did by taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great class. Very well organized. If you attend class, do all the quizzes and tutorials, you will get an A. She also gives a ton of extra credit.

Dr. Bose runs a very organized course. The course really helped me learn new concepts for medical microbiology. It is a difficult course but most people did very well if they attended class. You don't really need the textbook unless you have forgotten freshman biology concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hard to do well but whatever its washu so my grades are already bad.

Shes okay I guess... lectures are not recorded and they are very dense. She takes attendance and threatens to report you to your advisor if you skip class (lol). For the tests if you lose more than 10 points on a 250 point exam, youre not getting an A. Id advise taking a different class unless you really like bacteria.
Class has a stupid grading system. Only 10 people will get an A and everyone else gets their GPA destroyed. Don't take!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She worked with me the whole semester even though I took it only for credit. Great teacher! Don't worry about the lectures being dense. It just means you don't have to write as much during class but rather just listen to her. She has fun stories!
Really passionate instructor. Difficult class. She is always available to meet outside of class. Tests are tough.

Lectures were very dry and dense, but the material was interesting so it evened out. The tests weren't always written super well but they were fairly straightforward on the whole. Dr. Bose really does care about the students though and is very willing to meet outside of class and check in, and she is also super passionate about the material.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Arch is one of the most intelligent people I've ever met. She truly cares about the subject matter and her students success. She took student feedback into account and changed the course accordingly. Every day I was smiling the whole class both due to her evident passion and hilarious quips
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor. Willing to change aspects of the class based on student feedback. Clearly very caring, very very passionate about her work. I really liked her.

This professor is not professional. She forces the class the write only during class time and on Lockdown Browser. It is hard to feel like she is a caring and empathetic teacher when she automatically treats students with distrust under the guise of "AI and cheating." Hard to improve my writing when teacher is not friendly.

I was excited to take a class with her after reading the positive reviews here. However, from the first time I met her in class, she came across as abrasive and snappy, even though we had never interacted before. I thought maybe she was having an off day, but she remained consistently cold/rude to me, compared to how she treated other students...

Professor Arch is clearly very smart, and extremely knowledgeable in her subject area. However, I sometimes struggled to follow her lines of reasoning in lecture; we seemed to jump from one idea very quickly to another. The class was interesting, but overall lacked a sense of coherence and clarity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class online during COVID in SP2021 semester. The class was pretty easy and we did lots of sentence diagramming. What I mostly remember though is how I was going through a really hard time at that point in my life, and Jennifer was incredibly supportive. And I still think of it 3 years later, which is why I am now writing this review.

Dr. Arch is by far my favorite professor at WashU. I have now taken as many classes with her as I can and each time I find myself engaged and excited to be there. She is one of the most intelligent people I have ever met and she cares so much about her students. Reading can be intense, but worth it for sure for the in class discussions

Professor Arch is a phenomenal instructor. Not only is she incredibly knowledgeable, she is also enthusiastic about the material. She wants you to learn it, not necessarily get everything 100% correct, so that being said her grading is very fair. If grammar and sentence structure excites you in any way, take this wonderful class.

Prof. Arch is fabulous! The Sentence in English is a joy to take; if the idea of lots of drawing and learning terms like "adverbial objective" tickles your fancy, enroll! The quizzes are graded fairly. The class is a bit reading heavy in the first half of the semester, but calms down as you get into the self-analysis projects. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!

Professor Arch is a phenomenal instructor. She is extremely knowledgeable and her enthusiasm for the material she teaches is evident and contagious. It is clear that she cares about all of her students. I've had her for two courses and would take all of her courses if I could. Highly recommend!

I took this class off a whim and it ended up being the class I learned the most from. Prof Arch is very passionate about sentence structure. There are quizzes every week to make sure you are digesting the content. You always get feedback on your quizzes and papers so it is clear what grade you should receive at the end of the semester.

Prof. Arch is the best professor I have encountered at WashU. She is kind, caring, and intelligent. She gives wonderful, passionate lectures and is always willing to hear students' thoughts on course material. She is an exceptional teacher and is readily available outside of class. It is evident that Prof. Arch cares about her students' well-being.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Arch is the best writing professor I have ever had, and the only negative thing I can possibly say about her is that thanks to her, it'll really suck whenever I have to take a writing class with another professor. I don't think any other class could have changed how I view writing in such a positive way. Try sentence diagramming! Do it!

Arch is awesome; I wasn't sure what to expect from the class (if I would even learn anything) but she made sentence diagramming meaningful and interesting. The class is pretty easy, too. Deep down she is a nerd, and it's great. She's good at leading discussions and bringing up interesting questions. She values students' opinions. Great professor!

This class and professor had been recommended to me, and they did not disappoint. Professor Arch is easily one of the most knowledgeable and interesting professors I've had at WashU. Her lectures fly by, because the material is just so interesting. The assignments are hard, but they are definitely worth it because it ties the whole class together.

I had almost no interest in the history of the English language before taking this class, but Professor Arch made the subject truly fascinating.  She really knows how to facilitate class discussions, and no matter what the subject matter, is always well informed.  She is very friendly and helpful during office hours.  World Class.

She's absolutely amazing. Definitely a tough class and she runs a tight ship, but her grading is easily the fairest I have ever encountered in college. If you get a B, you will know every single reason she gave it to you. Will also answer every single question you have at office hours, no matter how dumb it sounds. Truly cares about teaching
One of the best classes I've had at Wash U, First E Lit class too so don't be scared off by the 400 level part.

Professor Arch is, hands down, the best professor I've had at WashU, either as good as or better than Professor Loomis (who is also awesome). She facilitates amazing classroom discussions, picks interesting topics, and knows her stuff. She's quirky and interesting, and she truly cares about her students. I highly *highly* recommend her classes.

Professor Arch is very clear in her lectures and comments on papers. She cares a lot about her students and the material. She was very helpful in meetings and requires that you meet with her before papers to discuss your ideas.
Interesting choices of articles in her course reader. Sometimes overly political, but this works well for Argumentation.

Dr. Arch is a marvelous professor; she truly knows the material, especially Chaucer.  In my experience, she is very interested, helpful, and kind.  Also, she is amazing at facilitating class discussion.

Jennifer Arch is the closest I've come in the English department to actual class discussion.  She is an amazing facilitator of dialogue, and more ideas were thrown around in just one of her classes than in all of my others combined. Oh, and she's kind of hot.

honestly, i was not looking forward to taking this class because it sounded like it was the most boring thing ever. but she makes it so fun! i actually ENJOY going to an english class, which is pretty much unheard of. she is seriously an awesome, incredibly cool professor and i would for SURE take another class with her.
Kind, humorous and knowledgeable. Love him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took 3 courses with him in 2 semesters. A knowledgeable professor and a nice person.
Very kind, approachable, and knowledgable in his niche! Be prepared to study a lot for exams and work hard on your papers for that A.

Dr. Aravecchia is so passionate and knowledgeable, and he clearly loves teaching. I've never learned more from a single course in my life! He gives great feedback while not being overly harsh, and is very engaging in class. If you ever get a chance to take his course, DO IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very caring for students. The lecture materials are interesting and although there are a lot to memorize, gradings are not tough at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Aravecchia is my favorite professor in the art history department. Highly recommend his classes! If you put in the work, the classes are not difficult.
prof aravecchia is super enthusiastic! there's a lot of material to cover in his classes, but it's all interesting and he's a really engaging lecturer
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Aravecchia is awesome. He is very knowledgeable in both Archaeology and Classics, especially in Egyptian matters. His Reception of Egypt in the Greco-Roman Antiquity class is quite interdisciplinary. The discussion on his class is quite active and inspiring, and he pushes students to think about readings.
Prof. Aravecchia is very friendly and fun. Hes also passionate about teaching!

Have really enjoyed taking his class. Super passionate about Egyptian art and throws a lot of information at you, but you really only need to memorize a few things to do well on exams. Will grade so that his students succeed

I had Arthur twice for classes at Maryville University and both his classes were well structured. I learned a lot about different Adobe programs and digital art as well as how to think outside the box to come up with a unique design. He is friendly and open to all different kinds of art, which makes his class more personable. Highly recommend!

Very knowledgable about adobe programs, gives good feedback during critiques. Hes also pretty young so he is very approachable (and cute lol). I learned a lot during this class and would definitely recommend that everyone take it, esp with arthur if you have the chance, even if you are not in the art school.

Santoro's class was a great experience! I came in with some knowledge of Photoshop, InDesign, and Illustrator, but his lessons helped me learn new techniques and improve my skills. He explains things clearly, gives creative projects, and is approachable if you have questions. Definitely recommend his class!
Having just graduated I'm posting reviews for the best classes I took here. Ray's was one of the 2 best. His enthusiasm for science is totally contagious. The Mars stuff is way cool. Thanks!!

Ray is an awesome guy. His lectures are interesting, and he loves to tell personal stories during them, which are usually pretty funny. Always willing to chat outside of class. He also works on NASA's Mars Rover expedition, which is super cool, and he shares a lot about it in class. Content was a bit bland at times, but Ray made the class worth it.
Amazing opportunity to be taught by the guy who is the Principle Investigator on NASAs Mars Rover mission!  He's down to earth, no ego even though he's a giant.

If you're a Pathfinder, you're going to love Ray. Not always the clearest professor but he keeps his lectures interesting. Just learn to treat everything he says as the gospel truth because he's basically a god. Do the extra readings if you're so inclined, but they're definitely not required.
The greatest professor ever.  Caring, interesting, funny and a great guy outside of class.
An awesome professor and adviser who cares about his students.
Knows his stuff. Willing to explain things to you. Take advantage.
He did not use a book, and I had a terrible time trying to learn from his fast, cryptic lectures!!!
An awesome advisor, very easy to talk to and very likeable and helpful.
The absolute BEST advisor at Wash U
There to guide you and offer advice but doesn't micromanage. Terrific teacher and advisor.
A hottie genius---unique
No Comments
No Comments

I learned more in Nakissa's Muslim societies class than in any other class in my life. His classes are all lecture but he will take tremendous time to answer questions people have during class and is quite accessible outside of class. Take his class!

Professor Nakissa is a must-take WashU professor. His lectures are fantastic, he's passionate about the material he teaches, and his perspective is both fascinating and unique.  Up and coming star, so take a class with him while he's still here!

Beginning of the course was kind of dry, but he's really passionate about the topic, talks a lot. Gets more interesting as the semester goes on, for sure.  Quizzes based completely on reading, would highly suggest keeping up, but he grades incredibly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Amazing guy. Might seem tough on the outside, but he's such a softie and a great professor. As long as you come to class on time, put in a lot of effort, and show that you care about this class, you should do well. Make sure that you participate in critiques and never feel intimidated to ask him questions! He truly wants to help you succeed.

Arny is one of the best professors in Sam Fox. Hes extremely helpful, knowledgeable, and hilarious. That being said, be prepared to work. His class is very challenging and he expects a lot from his students. He constantly encourages them to push their abilities. In the end though, it is entirely worth it just to have a class with him.
Hes literally my favorite prof in sam fox. Hes got a really dry sense of humor and genuinely cares about how you do in his class. But DO the work and actually show up
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Flexible with projects and open to students individual ideas. Grades based on physical labor/not very accommodating to everyone's working methodologies. Feedback given is generalized and often unhelpful, though he is knowledgable and will provide resources according to individual students interests.

Arny was so amazing. He was incredibly relaxed with students while expecting hard work. What was most impressive about his class is the amount of freedom he gives his students. I don't think he ever shot down an idea, rather, he worked with the student to make it possible. Arny was funny and friendly and not afraid to be friends with his students.

Arny is an incredible teacher (in both 3d desing and material systems), but you have to be willing to work hard in his class. If you put fourth the effort, regardless of your major, you will get a great deal out of his classes.

amazing professor, if you work hard he will respect you and reward you by being all the more helpful. he gave me an appreciation for working with space that i never thought i would have. he gives very interesting and challenging assignments, but the work really pays off. AND he's got a very good/dry sense of humor which makes class enjoyable.

Tough on the outside, warmer on the inside than you would guess. Prove yourself to him and he's got your back for life. Sometimes tries to pass off obvious things as profound, but generally very helpful.

For 3D Arny is tough in the beginning but very helpful. If you work for him, he'll work for you. Great guy and really cares about students. For Material Systems, he really lets students do what they want withing certain limits. Very helpful and makes class fun! Take his sections if you can!!
No Comments
A tough class. Very talented professor, very creative, very helpful. Tough love. Grades very very hard at the beginning of the semester, eases up as semester continues.

This class was set up such that the difficulty ramped up considerably for the third exam. I personally had a difficult time digesting course content and felt like I did well in the course because of my background in Mathematics, not from my improved understanding of Economics. Professor was incredibly kind, just not the right learning style for me.

Agree with below. The professor is nice, but everything else is terrible. I've learned nothing from lectures, and there isn't any resources available for you to study on your own, except for a few unhelpful slides. The questions that show up on quizzes and problem sets are always different than what we are expected to learn in class.

I honestly dont understand how people do well in this class. Lectures start out interesting and you blink and all of a sudden if its just pure "math"? It's a very theoritical class but at the same time it has a lot of mathematical calculations. The textbook doesnt help at all with quizzes or hw's. The entire class is based on 2 hws and 2 quizzes.
Hard to understand but knows his stuff
Entirely composed of lectures where you talk about the world's problems. Interesting topics arise and he provides a unique point of view on a lot of these issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think his lecture was fine. The only problem for me was that his grading standard was not very clear, which annoyed me a lot at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Said on the second day of class that if you did perfectly on the exams and never attended class, you'd get an A-. Take this class only if you want a GPA boost--otherwise, stay away.

Costas Azariadis is yet another example of why free trade is a great policy. He's probably Greece's best export in the past century. The man's brilliant, but easy to talk to. Those questions people spend entire semesters with in Polisci? Costas can give you an answer in five minutes. Meaning of life? Five minutes more. I'm jealous of his grandkids.

I think the commenters here do not give Azariadis the credit he deserves. Azariadis is a really nice professor and hints at the ways you can get an A in the class. What I heard from a lot of people is that other professor teaching this class give boring lectures and ask very difficult questions in the tests.

Total baller! If you do what he asks (show up to class and review section) you will do well.  If not you won't do as well.  Lectures were for most part very interesting and on current topics.  Good guest lectures.  Tests are easy but graded extremely hard.
total waste of a student's time. absolutely horrible lectures..

I learned a lot in Rebeca's class and really enjoyed the readings, discussions, and writing assignments. She communicates the material clearly and keeps the class engaging. I saw a noticeable improvement in my Spanish skills by the end of the course and would definitely recommend taking her class.

I enjoyed class with Prof. Fromm Ayoroa. The media we consumed for class was generally interesting and she seemed excited to teach it. She's generally very sweet and accommodating, but I do feel like I learned more with other Spanish teachers.

The class has a decent workload (as is typical of Spanish at WashU), but nothing too difficult. Prof. Fromm Ayoroa is a wonderful instructor; she fosters a caring, collaborative classroom environment and clearly communicates deadlines and grading criteria. She speaks at a good pace: not too rapid-fire, but still improves students' listening skills.

Prof. Ayoroa is very gentle, understanding, and overall fantastic professor. She gives great feedback on papers, doesn't cold-call, and prompts students to think critically. Her class environment is super low-pressure but not boring at all. If you can, take her section of any Spanish class you need to take. Her spanish is easy to understand too!
Fromm Ayoroa is a really fun teacher. She always keeps the energy up and is pretty fun to have teaching lectures. She's chill and the vocab sections were always pretty easy.

Prof Fromm Ayoroa is literally so nice. She is very understanding and I always felt I could talk to her if I needed an extension or something. The class is very chill and an A is attainable. I also felt I actually learned in her class. I would highly recommend.

Genuinely I have nothing bad to say about her. She radiates very bubbly, friendly energy and is always looking to chat with students or encourage them to speak. She does not freely correct grammar as some other professors do, which I think is great because she wants us to mostly get our point across without nitpicking every little thing.

She is so sweet and understanding. Class is sometimes not super entertaining and she does assign a lot of readings and movies to watch and discuss but tbh you do not really have to do that in order to do well in the class. We have papers every few weeks and she gives a 24-hour grace period and gives decent grades most of the time!
Amazing professor that genuinely cares about her students. She's very clear about what she expects from you and as long as you apply yourself and put a genuine effort in her class, you'll do well.

Fromm is the best Spanish teacher I've ever had. She explains everything very clearly, and makes it super easy to ask questions and speak up in class. The hour always passes really quickly, and sometimes I'll even be sad at the end because I was having a good time! The class was challenging, but I'd take it again with her without a doubt.

fromm is my favorite person ever. I want her to adopt me. She was so helpful in my learning of spanish and she was so patient, kind, and understanding. my fav spanish prof ever and Im thinking of taking an extra spanish class just to learn from her again

Fromm is the most amazing Spanish prof in the business. You'll have the choice between which section you want if you're signing up for 307 or 308, so make sure to get yourself a section with Fromm. She's super caring and expresses a general interest in her students which feels great. Sometimes she will bring in cookies for the class.

Some of the material might have been challenging, but she always explained things well and was willing to answer any questions. Class was upbeat, and the hour usually flew by. She was easy to understand and gave us fun exercises in class. For Spanish 307, Fromm Ayoroa is a great choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super great professor. Easy to understand and quizzes are super easy. Tests are harder, but she's clear about what will be on them and gives good review materials. Compositions always have rewrites.

Loved her class and found it easy to do well. Hardest part is all of the grammar but if you practice a lot the exams aren't bad. Papers are easy to do well on and always have regrades and reading quizzes are super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had Fromm for 307 and 308. Her 308 class is much easier than 307, yet still very interesting. She is very understanding and all of her essays have rewrites so it is not hard to do well. She is also very clear about what will be on the exams. Cannot recommend her more!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Fromm Ayoroa is super nice and genuinely wants you to learn the material she is teaching. However, this class in not an easy A and there are a lot of assignments (tests, papers, quizzes, etc.). If you are someone who is willing to show up to every class and seek out help when you need it than Prof Fromm Ayoroa is a good choice!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good professor - explained things clearly and was very approachable. 308 was pretty easy overall.

Rebeca is a good professor. She is super awkward in class (which is sometimes pretty boring) and can be unclear at times, but usually she is easy to learn from. She isn't too tough of a grader, either; her department gives her ridiculous guidelines that you can tell she doesn't like to follow. Recommended over most in the department.

307D is a hard class...she's a hard grader, but she's so nice and approachable that it makes it alright. she's fairly laid back and is easy to understand (no thick accent)...tests are reasonable if you study...sometimes quizzes and homework can be a little dumb...but definitely not a bad class to take
Fourth year at WashU. He is by far the best lecturer I have had in my WashU career. Engaging and personable with a good sense of humor. Made me excited to go to class
Great guy, understands his students well. Is very young so connects well with current events

Nice guy, does a lot of discussion of current events as they relate to the class material, which was helpful for learning/putting the class in context. He's good at explaining concepts, too. Homework isn't terribly difficult, exams are definitely on the hard side.
Great

Unprepared in an emergency, doesn't explain expectations at all, then grades unfairly based on unknown and uncommunicated guidelines, doesn't make the class interesting, lots of reading. She does give clear feedback, however, and I think I'm a better writer after this class. You just have to work hard and go to office hours(!!). Supportive in OHs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Benjamin's writing identity course was good overall. Your writing skills will really improve, and she gives good guidance and feedback, but you have to put in lots of work for the class, readings, and projects. If you're looking for an easy CWP class, this is not it, but if you're looking to improve your writing skills, then take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Just take college writing next semester. This is NOT worth it.

Dr. Benjamin's Citizen Scientist class was pretty interesting! She clearly has a lot of experience teaching writing/college writing, but she's new to citizen scientist. Some readings were a bit difficult, and there were times when many assignments were due around the same time. However, Dr. Benjamin is very accessible outside of class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Benjamin's CWP is definitely on the harder side. There is a LOT of reading, more than other CWP classes, most of it isn't necessary or helpful. It is a small class and you get a letter grade off for absences and tardy's. She is a HARSH grader with little help on how to improve your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: one of the most difficult professors I've taken. the class is participation and completion, especially since its a small class. you only get one unexcused absence then points off your final grade. She doesn't use modules on canvas and everything is posted in a weekly announcement. dont recommend. more workload than other CWP sections. harsh grader!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Benjamin has been one of the most supportive professors I've come across here at WashU. She provides such deep insight and is always willing to meet with students after class, regardless of topic. She has been a pillar of advice for me, an advocate, and makes me feel seen on this campus. Show effort, provide input in class and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class pushed you to stretch your ability to think and produce in a way that revitalizes creative thinking. However there was a substantial amount of reading and writing compared to other college writing classes. Additionally her grading and feedback was not always consistent. However Professor Benjamin is very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I recommend taking her for college writing. The class is not a heavy work load-until it is time to do the research essay. She also cares a lot about her students and will work with them outside of class. Compared to others students professors, Dr. Benjamin was one of the best as long as you put in effort for the assignments we had.

Prof Benjamin is nice and helpful! She's clear with expectations. Class is usually engaging/interesting (depends on students though bc it's a small class). Her teaching style is very easy to follow. The work outside of class isn't much until we get to the research paper. If you need help with your paper, meet with her and she will definitely help!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: i love her so much but there are a lot of writing assignments. She truly cares!

Professor Benjamin is one of the most caring and enthusiastic professors at WashU. Both in and out of the classroom, she displays her passion for writing and literature. This love for her subject shines through in her teaching. Easily one of the best professors I have ever had.

Professor Benjamin is empathetic with her students and understands stress. She grades mostly on your effort. I got an A in this class, and here is my biggest advice right off the bat: go to her office hours when possible, do the readings for class, and talk in class when relevant. She is a great person and definitely a little quirky!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Benjamin's writing identity class definitely had a much heavier workload than other writing identity sections. The instructions for the papers and assignments were sometimes vague, but she's very accessible during office hours. Definitely go to office hours and prepare to discuss the assigned reading if you want to make an A
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: assigns her papers the day it's due, she says take the L, bruh
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I do not consider myself a fan of writing but Professor Benjamin made Writing Identity a class I looked forward to every day. Her approach to teaching is generative and thoughtful. She chooses texts which anyone would enjoy and learn from. Benjamin will make you work hard, but she will improve your writing. She's also a caring, fun person.
Really sweet professor. She facilitates a lot of discussions so if you don't participate, she will notice. Definitely recommend Writing identity over the regular writing course.
Take it!

Would not take again, definitely not worth the immense amount of reading she assigns. Her class Writing Identity was unpleasant. Save yourself the trouble and don't take it. The only pleasant thing I could add about her is that she tries to engage us by trying to be funny her sense of humor isn't the best though:/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Benjamin is a must-have instructor for all freshman. I opted to take writing identity rather than the conventional Writing 1 class and it was amazing. Although I started off the year with pretty bad grades, the professor helps you work through your struggles and overall, you become a better writer and person. I can't give enough credit :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Eccentric but in a good way. Entertaining and puts a creative spin on boring required material. She'll love you if you laugh at her jokes! Hard grader but tailors her standards to each student and is REALLY helpful in office hours, very available by email/in person. I had low expectations for the course but she taught me so much.

Ms. Benjamin is an excellent teacher in that she engages the class and encourages her students to learn through participation.  She has this amazing ability to teach her students an exorbitent amount without them even knowing what hit them.  She encourages learning by seeing things in a different light. She does make you work for your grade.

Beth is my favorite professor I have ever had! Not only is she hilarious and engaging, but she thouroughly explains the topics and makes sure each student is understanding the material. In her class, I have never felt like just another student. WGSS has been one of my favorite courses, all because of her!
Horrendous professor. Never really objective in grading

She grades very harshly and is so against grade inflation that she seems to have made it her personal mission to not let anyone get an A in class. On individual assignment, the highest grade she gives is a 95 (and that is a rare occurrence), even if you did everything perfectly. I would NOT recommend anyone taking her class if they don't have to
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Horrible as a learning experience.

Beth is what professors should strive to be like. She cares about her students in a way that is so genuine. She is both kind and honest, and she manages to facilitate a classroom of laughter and good vibes despite the wide range of students you get in a gen ed course (WI). You will look forward to going to class each day. Also attendance is strict.
She is an amazing teacher and really cares about her students! The class can be tough and she is a harsh grader, but I think it is worth it to learn from her!
Beth is a great prof. I recommend her to anyone and everyone. Our class both learned and laughed a lot.

Beth is one of my favorite professors I've had during my time at WashU. She's super nice and amazing at facilitating class discussions that feel impactful, and she gives amazing feedback on writing assignments. If you haven't taken a class with her yet then you should get on it ASAP, you will not regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Beth is by far the best professor I have had in my time at WashU. She is tastefully hilarious and does an excellent job of including everyone in our class discussions. She is kind and thoughtful and gives excellent feedback. If I could take this class again, I would! If you're on the fence, don't be! She will make your time as WashU SO much better!

Beth is absolutely amazing. This class has to be one of my favorites at WashU, and that's largely due to Beth. She genuinely cares so much about each and every student, and goes out of her way to make personal connections with everyone. Her teaching style is wonderful and she is hilarious. She truly wants all her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is hands-down, my favorite class I've taken! Beth is one of the kindest professors I've had and really cares about her students as learners and as individuals. My skills as a writer have improved so drastically in her class and taking this course has reignited a love of reading for me. If you do anything in college, take a class with Beth!

I can honestly say this has been one of my favorite courses at WASHU, and it's all thanks to Beth. She is endlessly caring, accommodating, hilarious, and a genuine joy to be around. I will be genuinely heartbroken to not have her as a professor next semester, and I recommend taking any course with her you can! One of my all-time favorite professors

She is the absolute sweetest! Participating, reading, and writing papers is a big part of the class and it can be challenging, but I think it is so worth it. She is an amazing teacher and really cares about her students' success!

Beth is an outstanding professor. I took her class with no background in the subject, but her clarity, energy, and student-focused approach quickly made it one of the best courses I've taken. Beyond being a kind and thoughtful person, she's also one of the most compelling and entertaining lecturers at WashU.

One of the best profs as Washu. She's extremely smart, funny, and makes every class captivating. Definitely take her if you can. She's deeply committed to her students and fosters a learning environment that's welcoming and inclusive.

Beth is easily the best teacher I've had at WashU. Her classes are extremely engaging, and she is brilliant and laugh-out-loud funny. If you have the chance to take a class with Beth, it would be a huge mistake not to. She cares deeply about her students and goes out of her way to foster an inclusive classroom and respectful dialogue.
Beth is a great teacher! I have taken 2 classes with her and have really enjoyed them! I suggest everyone take a class with beth!

Extremely passive aggressive, different races and religions were not treated kindly. The class would have been great if she wasn't such a bully. Seemed really nice at first, turned out to be a awful. I withdrew from her course and retook it with another professor and it's been phenomenal.

Dr. Windle is an amazing professor! She genuinely cares about her students and has a gift for explaining difficult concepts with clarity. Attendance is important but it comes from a practical rather than rigid perspective. If you're an English major definitely try to take Lit Theory with Windle

Beth is truly a great professor. I took her Argumentation class having zero experience in similar courses, but her incredible teaching skills and attention to students quickly made the class one of my favorites. Aside from being a great human being, Beth is probably the best lecturer on this campus. She is witty, engaging, and very well spoken.

Beth is by far the best professor I've had at WashU. Not only is she brilliant, but she is able to articulate class concepts masterfully, even when the material is complex. I always left class feeling confident about our readings. Beth is everything a student looks for in a teacher - inspiring, challenging, engaging, accessible, and hilarious!

I can't recommend taking a class with Beth enough! She brings a lot of positive energy to the class. She expects a lot from her students, but has the teaching skills to guide you there. Takes a genuine interest in the lives of her students too!

I've been queer for a long time but I what I found special about Beth's classes is that she provided me and my classmates a lot of space to bounce our experiences off of each other's and those of the authors we read, She knows how to cultivate a strong and productive class culture and knows how to give insightful commentary on essays and discussion
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you are not a gay man or trans person you will probably enjoy Beth. She has okay lectures, but makes highly generalized claims about groups of people you talk about in class. Her descriptions of papers are not often descriptive enough, so get ready to ask for more info. For a positive, she does have a lot of different class materials to study.

Beth is a fantastic professor! She is thoughtful of her students and always open to discussing your journey in the class and how you can best succeed. Participation is important due to in-class discussions, so spend time on the readings. Office hours are incredibly helpful and an excellent resource for the few papers that the course has.

Beth is a wonderful person, but her class won't be great for people who already know the subject unless the other people in the class are at the same level. She also doesn't provide trigger warnings for any of the content in the class despite there being several sessions that revolved around discussions of sexual assault and slurs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Beth is one of the most caring, accessible, encouraging, and passionate professors I've ever taken a class with. She encourages open discussion and makes sure that every student has the space to voice their thoughts. I highly recommend taking her Lit Theory course, or any of her classes on queer literature.

Beth Windle is literally the most kind and encouraging professor I have ever met. She reads everything through the lens of feminism and queer theory, but as long as you have good evidence for your readings of a texts and aren't being bigoted, she'll see your perspective, too. Don't be alarmed if she says something "mean;" she's just teasing you.

If you do not interpret something the same as Beth or try to disagree with her to any extent, she will act as though you are dumb, and make passive-aggressive comments towards/about you. The class is okay, but I wouldn't recommend it. Beth is easily the worst professor I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Beth is the best!! I took College Writing with her and she quickly became one of my favorite professors. Since then, I've taken many other of her classes. While there is lots of reading and writing, the content is very enjoyable and she gives great feedback. But most of all, Beth is incredibly caring and has your best interests in mind.

I had Beth for Writing Identity in my freshman year, and I learned a lot from that class - from reading papers/books and extracting useful information to interpreting different documents then analysing them, the class was challenging, but really interesting. Beth always had lots of energy and also lots of passion for what she was teaching.

Beth is an amazing professor and human being! Her college writing class changed my approach to writing. Her class is challenging but she's very caring and will make sure you understand the assignments. Fair grader and leaves constructive feedback before final draft. Would definitely take another class with her!

Beth was one of my favorite professors my first year. College Writing: Identity is very difficult and writing-heavy, but prepares you well for writing in future classes regardless of how tied you are to Identity as a subject. Office hours were incredibly helpful, but be sure to request them early. Attendance is mandatory for every class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: she made me cry 3 times in a freshman writing class. if you didn't have her exact opinions and weren't that one kid who always contributed and talked a lot in class discussions, she won't think that you're competent enough in her class. i usually loved english and writing classes, and she has made me avoid the department here.

Amazing!!! One of the most enjoyable courses I've taken at WashU. The discussions were great and I looked forward to them every week. Classes were very reading-heavy, especially for an intro class, but it's pretty doable if you don't do it all the night before. Classes are mainly discussion-based so attendance is super important. HIGHLY recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Beth is honestly the best English/writing teacher I have ever had. She was super encouraging and really boosted my confidence in essay writing. I learned so much in her class and her passion for the material made the class even more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Beth checks off all the boxes in being organized, compassionate, a great personality, and memorable. Discussions are like friendly conversations, accepting of all ideas and with spontaneous and fun connections! Outside of class, the advice I have received from Beth regarding writing and life in general has also been invaluable and rare.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Windle is an incredibly subjective and difficult essay grader. We read many poems and philosophical pieces, but Beth would mark you down or call you out in class for misinterpreting a reading. I often left Beths class feeling stupid and discouraged because multiple times she told me I was missing the point in front of my classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Windle is so compassionate that she'd listen to my anxieties outside the classroom; her classes are no less educational than her personality is inspiring, as I learned how to write college research papers. Lastly, why would my other classmate wait till the day before the deadline to visit her office and why wouldn't they follow her feedback?

Go to office hours and she'll give you feedback. Follow that feedback (EXACTLY) and you'll get a good grade. Don't go or don't follow the feedback, and you'll get a bad grade. She will also rewrite your thesis for you the day before the paper is due and expect you to change everything. Don't take her class if you want to learn to actually write.

"A real gem" is a spot-on description of Professor Windle. Not only is she fun and hilarious, she cares about each student individually. I suffered some health issues during the semester, and Professor Windle was incredibly accommodating while making sure that I never lapsed in my learning. Beyond being a great person, she always made class fun.

Professor Windle did a fantastic job of respecting every student and making all students feel welcome and comfortable in class. She exposed us to a wide variety of topics that expended our knowledge and led to intriguing discussions. I was so pleased with my experience that I am taking another class and with her next semester. Highly recommend
Makes class enjoyable

Had a great experience with Dr. Windle! She made all of our classes really fun and made a boring topic (writing and argumentation) really interesting by letting us argue about real topics, including school specific policy changes as our final. She was really inclusive and inquisitive, making things relevant to us as students and you f adults.

I had some of the most interesting discussions in my life in Beth's class. I've never had her for English, but Beth is incredible at teaching WGSS. She's really good at challenging your thinking in provactive ways but is also open to discussing ideas she disagrees with. She grades writing assignments pretty tough, but the midterm is super easy.

Kinda hard to know what she expects of you, but she is very willing to meet with you and discuss your assignments before u submit them. Her class is so boring cus she just talks a lot and slowly so I always got sidetracked but if you are communicative you'll do well

For my grade I've done a lot of work
Using every resource I had
Completely rewriting my essays sometimes
Knowing that she won't be satisfied with the quality of the work despite all the effort.
Yawning in the class will get you C-
Obedience will get you A+
Understanding how she grade would obliterate your sanity.

Dr. Berson teaches in a very unique fashion that is not conducive to everyone's learning style, but it was a breath of fresh air from every high school writing class that I've taken. She uses a lot of crazy metaphors in class, and you will be constantly entertained by her care for students, random activities, and constant struggle with technology.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ruth gives little helpful feedback, reading material doesn't have anything to do with the theme of the course, she uses weird metaphors to teach writing styles, she doesn't know how to use canvas, and she doesn't post grades. Oh, and even though she "doesn't believe in grades," you'll get a B at the end of the semester.

She has an ok average grade as a professor based on very old reviews. She is old and a very bad prof. Do not take! Also, there is literally a review about how she talked too much to be effective on Sep 19, 2001! 8 days after 9/11. Like wow. 9/11 just happened and someone was like I need to get on the internet and complain about Ruth Berson.

Berson's College Writing was my least favorite class ever. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. We had no grades tab in canvas and she refused to give back grades on any assignment so we just didn't know our grades until the end of the semester and had no chance to change. Class time was spent with irrelevant tangents and bs busy work. Toes out constantly. Run! :)

Mediocre to poor professor. Too much of the class focuses not on writing but on unimportant subjects. Her grading is also vague and comments are not the most helpful. Her teaching was very passive. We didn't use the textbook or books once, yet we were required to buy them. The expectations for the papers were unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Berson was a great professor, and I really enjoyed her class. It was a lot of fun, and we discussed many controversial subjects. Her grading can be weird because she never gave me anything above a 93. However, she offers extra credit, which can boost your grade up to an A.

I loved the class. It was so interesting, and the readings were awesome. There's very little lecturing, which keeps things from ever getting boring. Berson is eccentric, but not horribly so. She may seem intimidating at first, but really she's nice and very knowledgable. And who the hell cares if she doesn't shave? That's none of your business.

Mediocre to poor as a teacher.  All of the readings were clearly copies of what SHE read in Women's Studies as an undergrad (they had her original notes in them! Ugh!)  I was not engaged in the course at all.  As a side point, she does not shave her legs or armpits, and lets it show.

She picked good readings but wasnt passionate about anything, and tried to to make wierd points or off the wall analogies. Not everything you want but easy if your not really interested in womens studies

Pretty easy grader, and it's difficult to pinpoint anything wrong with her teaching, as she is clear and usually pretty helpful. She can be pretty abrasive and close minded at times, though. Probably not the best introduction women's studies.

I took this class in spring 2005, and maybe she improved  since the other evaluations, but I loved her!  I will admit that she is not the best at teaching, but the readings, discussions, and ideas are amazing!  On top of that, the readings are short and there's only one test.  Great Class!!!

She was great at picking out interesting readings, and the subjects were well organized, but she was pretty passive as a teacher and not very thought provoking. When she lectured she just sort of sat there reading off paper quickly.  Class dicussions were okay.
I thought she was very interesting, lots of class discussion, always helpful.
No Comments
Not my favorite class.
I felt like some of the expectations for assignments were unclear.  Class discussion was lacking -- when it occured it was interesting and I enjoyed it.

If you want an objective rating of Berson, please do not let the other bad ratings of her influence you.  She may be somewhat eccentric, but is that what we are really looking for in a good teacher?  She is extremely helpful, always ready to chat about papers, class, etc.
Waste of my time class...just weird all around, and I'm NOT talking about the subject material!
like u cant teach
Wears crazy clothes, easy grader
No Comments
I love your class
No Comments
Talks way too much to be very effective in a discussion class.

It was a pleasure to be in Dr. Schaal's class. She is a highly regarded researcher in her field, and you can tell that she really wants you to learn. In the Plant, People, and Environment class, she enriches the experience through plant tasting and field trips. Though the exam format may not be the best.

overall very kind and accessible, you can tell she cares a lot. open ended exams were extremely long (around 15 long response questions for an hour 20 class) and impossible to get full points on. if you work really hard, attend lectures, study a lot using the study guide, getting an a is doable. overall way too hard for an "intro" class

Such an amazing and accomplished person! The class is very surface-level and accessible to anyone, no matter their scientific background. Exams relate directly to lectures, so if you take notes and review the study guide you'll do great!

Love Schaal! She's extremely sweet and really cares about EnviBio. Tests are all open-ended questions but she provides study guides and exam reviews. Brings in guest lecturers as well, and is ultimately a really interesting class, would recommend!

Schaal is the best, so so kind and extremely helpful. She worked with Obama! Lectures aren't recorded and the slides provided can be vague, so attendance is pretty necessary. Tests aren't difficult and study guides are given, but they can be kind of long. Overall, a relatively easy course with a delightful woman- would highly recommend.
Baojun Jiang more like Baojun goat
Nice professor and amazing lecture. Lenient grader.

Super nice professor! His materials are definitely harder for a marketing class. Homework and tests are math-heavy rather than concepts. Got a lot of interesting knowledge from this class. The game simulator was fun. If you like math, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor explained the concepts very clearly with many examples. Very useful examples and slides. I like it that the course was not too mathematical as I had expected.

Extremely nice guy. Covers the basics of pricing in a very clear, easy-to-follow way. Did a decent job of making lectures interesting, and grading procedures were pretty generous. Exams were take-home.

This class is not for people who learn by doing. The lectures are informative, but there is very little in-class practice for the actual problems on the exam, and instead come from homework problems and practice exams that you self-teach yourself. Slides often don't cover all the info if you miss a class. Not a social class whatsoever, just lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class, pretty easy if you pay any attention to the lecture which not many people do... TAs grade very generously. Only complaint is a lot of the answer keys do just say "see class notes" which doesnt always help. Accessible in office hours, very willing to help. Generally, interesting class topics too

Class is fine but often focuses on examples and scenarios that will not be relevant on exams. Notes for studying for exams are terrible. For a cumulative final, half the "solutions" were literally "see class notes," meaning you are expected to dig through three months of material to find explanations or definitions.

The professor is extremely helpful, both in class and after class. Teaching is great, though with thick Italian accent and pace is slow. Grading is not clear enough. Class notes are enough for preparing for exams and ecommended textbook is not very helpful.Overall, it is a great course.
Thick italian accent makes it hard to understand at time but she teaches very well.
She's a solid teacher, sometimes hard to understand. Grading system is a bit weird. but game theory is interesting
Just not a good experience. I was hoping the small group setting would help me, but in the end, it was not productive. If I could do it again, I would do the regular track and take PLTL.

Dr.Bakupog was AMAZING! Coming from a small town, adjusting to chemistry was difficult. I was enrolled in regular 1601 chemistry during the fall and I rarely received help even after using every resource available. After switching to Dr.Bakupog, I received enough support to be on the same level as my peers to be confident in my chemistry work.

I regret taking this small-group class w Bakupog. His lack of teaching and explanation skills go past any language issues. I realized he does not like to have indepth discussions because it is not clear he understands the material. I really feel like I am not ready for orgo and I will likely study 1701/1702 material over the summer.

Very kind and passionate person. Unfortunately, his pre-recorded lecture videos are hilariously bad. Way too fast, hard to follow along, and unclear. He also can't answer questions for the life of him. The concept of low enrollment is great, and I enjoy the active learning and class format, but as long as Bakupog is the instructor, don't take LE.
Great teacher! One of the best I have encountered at WashU. Really cares about the students. I miss being in his classes.

If you don't understand something he'll help you until you do. Lecture is typically watching a video before class and then doing a worksheet in class. He also held countless review sessions to help study for both the final and the midterms.

I'm currently in the 1601 LE (changed course names) with Bakupog and honestly he's made chem easily digestible. I'm able to keep up with my peers in Dr Lou's lecture as well. Only thing I will say is be prepared for a lot of practice work honestly, but it does pay off. This year there is also a TA who is great at explaining things, overall 9/10!

Bakupog was incredible. His treatment of his class convinced me to become a chemistry major. He goes above and beyond to make sure you feel comfortable, but you must be ready to reach out to schedule extra help. If you are insecure in your chemistry capabilities, take the low enrollment section of his class.

Chemistry is a difficult topic, but Bakupog does a great job of providing resources to fully grasp the material. Most assignments are online/at-your-own-pace and give you a safety net for exams. Exams are very straightforward. Bakupog has a very caring personality with a motto that "no one gets left behind".

combo of videos and elementary discussions were not beneficial. if we asked a question and he couldn't answer he would say do not worry it won't be on the exam. why can't he just answer the questions. I get it some might be not relevant but give us the respect of an answer.

So, I was told to take his section as he would help me get up to speed. That did not happen. He went very slowly, and I am now less prepared than my roommates who took the big 105 and definitely my friends who took 111. If you are looking for a single, easy semester of chem then you can take this, but you will not get a good grade.
Just not very good. He follows a script, but struggles to explain things when asked. He clearly wants to be liked, but it is clear he doesn't know how to teach.

Bakupog is all around a good teacher; motivational, shows he cares, open to questions. He wants you to learn and knows the class is not necessarily easy so wants students to keep with the pace of the class. He is great at explaining concepts and has a good pace!

On day 1, he gave a speech which is one of the best speeches I have ever heard. It was simply amazing. Keep an eye on the cumulative points you need to get an A and stop putting too much pressure on yourself to get perfect scores on every exam. I got an A and I just did enough on the exams. Work hard on homework and review questions. Cool guy!

I had Bakupog for CHEM 106 recitation and he was pretty poor at explaining literally anything. He would go in circles and never really get to the point. He's nice and cares about students, but it's impossible to learn anything from him. He made so many mistakes when he led problems even when going straight off his notes.

Bakupog is great and made the class fun! Large lectures are not the place to be expecting a lot of explanations. You need to utilize recitations and the other supplementary programs. Large lectures just cover the basics because it is so much material to cover for the semester. Looking forward to Chem 106. Very welcoming and accommodating guy!

Bakupog is a really caring person but he does not effectively teach the material. I stopped attending his lectures about halfway through the lectures and watched Dr Lou's recordings from the morning section. It was so much clearer and my grade went up. Doesn't really know how to answer questions and is a bit confused sometimes
Terrible, just terrible. He reads and writes on the board straight from his note. It is unclear he understands what he is saying. You have to learn on your own.

Bakupog is a "cool cat". Love him! For a large lecture, he is always trying to cover all the material needed for quizzes/exams. Sometimes, he will tell us that he needs to go at the speed of light and which means there will not be much explanations. However, when he slows down, he explains the material very well and in a hilarious way. Humble guy!
I really wanted to like Bakupog as there is not much diversity in STEM, but he is terrible. He has a rough time communicating and he cannot explain concepts. Luo is much better.

Bakupog is truly a sweetheart. He makes chemistry, a sometimes really boring subject, extremely fun. He is the best of the best. He made CHEM105 really easy to understand and would always ensure student comprehension. I love him!

All the PLTL leaders missed you. Please come back and teach PAM again. We missed the community we used to have when all the leaders would leave PAM together after the large class discussion. There was togetherness and we were always ready to lead our students. Now, we leave PAM with confusing answers. Please come back and save the PLTL program.

I agree with this latest review. I have no idea who is entering positive reviews, but it cannot be someone who is trying to learn. Dr. Bakupog is mild mannered, yes, but disrespectful, and he can only read his notes. He cannot answer questions or explain things. Do Not Take. I should have taken 111, even though it is harder, it is better.

I do not know why my previous review of Bakupog was removed, but he is terrible. The first day of class he made inappropriate comments relating his course to Christianity. He also suggested we could die during the class. Since then, it is not clear he understands the material. A new professor (Heemstra) came in for the next session...much better.

I am in Chem 105 now and I love how humble this guy is. He is always the first to say that he is not perfect, but he tries very hard to make things great. His attitude makes me know that I achieve success without being perfect. He is respectful of students! He is very encouraging. I hear chem 106 is hard but I am ready to dive in because of him.

Chem 106 is a different animal. It is very quantitative, and you must work fast on quizzes/exams. I really loved Dr. Bakupog's style. He is supper helpful and willing to go over concepts. He is friendly and made an effort to know everyone's name. This was a POGIL class, and he checked in with each group before the large class discussion.

The Prof. was able to provide a welcoming and collaborative environment in which he stressed the importance of working as a community. This paved the way for much inclusivity. He is super cool and I like his funny jokes, which makes the class safe. He really cares a lot about student success. Great guy with positive attitude. Gave helpful advice.

Dr. Bakupog is the absolute best! This man is a living legend. I cannot say enough kind words about him. He was an absolutely amazing recitation leader. His explanations were always very clear and helpful. Always so happy to teach chemistry. He made such an effort to connect with all of us personally. Knew my name by the second week. Will miss him!
Lectures are a bit all over the place at times but he is a kind guy who cares about his students and wants you to succeed. Will miss him as the 105 lecturer

He really cares for everyone that reaches out to him and always lets you know what the expectations are. Out of the entire chemistry department, he is BY FAR, the most helpful professor and highly recommend going to his help sessions.
He does his best to help and his help sessions are spent reviewing for that weeks quiz or exam. I am grateful for his review sessions and that can be seen in my exam grades.

He seriously wants to see students succeed - go to his office hours and you'll see it for yourself. Although he spends a while on each question, he's generally very helpful in preparing students for the exams. He's very kind and approachable - he'll go out his way to help you in any way he can (email, separate meeting, etc). Great guy
If you go to his help sessions before a test he will help you so much. He is also kind and you can tell he really wants students to succeed.

He is one of the top best college writing professors at WashU. I was in his Writing Identity course which taught me to explore deeper in the meanings of readings. Course was not task heavy and rather very chill. If you ever needed an extension, he would be very understanding. He is very open and creates a welcoming environment. 10/10 def recommend!

Professor Bassett was nice and chill. He tried his best to engage students in discussions and teach them the deeper meaning behind stories, using a mix of articles, books, art, and writing formats. His assignments were simple, and he gave good feedback. He was a great intro to college. Would definitely recommend taking his class.

Colin is the best! A good amount of weekly assignments outside of class, but very manageable and pretty enjoyable topics. He's understanding and nonjudgmental. He led great discussions and encouraged creative and analytical thinking. Was always happy to meet outside of class to discuss writing, reading, or life. Best college writing professor.

incredible professor and chill class. you'll get a A easily as long as you show effort. they are very understanding, kind, and passionate educator! you are very lucky if you get him for college writing.

Didn't get tons of helpful feedback, didn't really learn much about writing. But I don't think that's through any fault of his own; the class is just built to be chill, hit or miss depending on who takes it. I don't enjoy being vulnerable, so prompts could be eh. Colin is a really nice guy, too nice honestly considering how much class I skipped.

definitely one of the best college writing professors at WashU. Super understanding and grading policy is super lenient. Class time is rather boring unless students participate, but overall would definitely recommend.

Nice guy, grades lightly. Kind of boring, but not a bad experience. Only reason wouldn't take again is because other students take opportunity to be really vulnerable about their identity, and if you aren't really vulnerable, might be hard for you to share and participate in discussion
Probably the easier college writing class: Writing Identity. Lowest grades on essays were like a 90 and was extremely helpful and nice.

If you show up and show a genuine desire to improve you will probably do well.
