I had a lot of other heavy classes and this was a nice lighter thing to have, especially compared to things I've hear about other college writing classes. The professor is also extremely kind and understanding about any extenuating circumstances!

Colin Bassett chillest college writing professor out there. Super lax deadlines for everything. He's really approachable and cares about his students. I feel like I didn't learn a lot from this course but he does provide really good feedback on essays. I know so many people who hated college writing and I didn't!

Colin is super approachable and an easy grader! I'm an engineering student with a heavy courseload, and I still managed to get 100s on 2 papers. A lot of assignment deadlines are super flexible, and he's super kind and easy to talk to if you're struggling. HIGHLY recommend

Pretty easy to get an A if you turn in your work. Colin is very accommodating and understanding. I needed to meet with him urgently when I was working on my research paper, and he made himself available for a meeting immediately. He gives very good feedback which has improved my writing, and he's very knowledgeable in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super sweet guy and very approachable for help. The topic was rather boring but he did a good job incorporating lots of different activities that didn't have to do with writing. Also gave lots of room for revision and feedback and was just super caring and understanding. Assignments were very open-ended and flexible.

Good guy, forgiving with deadlines. Still, he seemed not to care about teaching. Showed up late, scrolled on his phone, let the class chat for the first 20 mins of a 50 min class. A tough mix because he wastes class but expects good writing on essays. Very nice, though; I wonder if this was just an off semester for him.

One of the best teachers I have ever had. I was a strong writer going into this class, but Colin Bassett provided great feedback on every one of my submissions. He was a really nice, kind, and approachable guy too. I miss his class terribly.

Such a great guy and a great professor. He genuinely cares about his students and gives good, detailed feedback so you know exactly what to work on. He is a really relaxed guy, approachable, and understanding. Asynchronous format reduced the workload and he taught CWP really well and did not make it boring. 100% would take his class again.
Nicest guy I've ever met and made me not hate writing classes. Really clear and good feedback on what he expects and how he thinks you can improve. Loved Writing Identity.

It's always a dance, - trying to find good TA's for larger lecture classes. Colin's way of speech and conducting the classroom is strange at first, but grows on you. He cares - and that is what matters the most from a teacher. Highly, highly recommend for Writing Identity. Made the University Writing requirement actually one of my favorite classes.
Colin is so nice! If you are struggling with papers and go to his office hours, he is always willing to help and your grade will improve. Highly recommend him for Writing Identity!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Prof Basset was an amazing Writing 1 teacher. He was a fair but hard grader so you have to work for a good grade. However, he was very easy to approach and cared for his student's. I really enjoyed the class.

He has high standards, but gives the best feedback I've ever gotten on any essay before. Really helped me as a writer, and is always prompt and open to student opinions during discussion. Classes are always interesting, and you end up learning significantly just from reading his comments on your papers. Truly, someone with great insight who cares.

LOVED THIS CLASS!!! He was so helpful and encouraging. I feel like it's definitely doable to get a good grade, but it hard to get a great grade. He makes class so fun and interesting, and he's really funny.

Colin is a really, REALLY nice guy, but an immensely hard grader. Do not expect an A in this class. Getting B's or C's on essays is very common. His grading is very arbitrary, and though he's very insightful, I hated how hard I would work just to receive another fat B. Try to get another Writing I teacher if you want this class to be a GPA booster

He is amazing. He is really interested in all of the students and provides deep and helpful feedback. My fiction improved immensely through the semester, largely in part to his excellent advice. It doesn't hurt that he's gorgeous either :)
Not a fan, condescending
Homework takes forever and is often irrelevant to exams. He comes off condescending in lectures and when speaking to him. Avoid at all costs.

If you go to lectures and understand the material on the slides, you will do great on the tests. On the exams, I didn't encounter any trick questions or material that was not taught in the class. The only thing was the homework was very long.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ReadingComprehension2610

Not sure where the other reviews come from, Barrios is genuinely a great professor, hosted many review sessions before exams and gave great lectures. The homeworks are long but they really help you understand the material well and find gaps of knowledge. Exams are fair, but 2610 is a rigorous class so be ready to work for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: The homework is ridiculously long and frequently not related to test content. He is very unaccommodating and aims for a grade distribution lower than any other Olin professor. He's just generally the worst.

John is one of my favorite professors at WashU. He genuinely cares about everyone in his class. You must make an effort to get to know him outside of class. Attend review sessions and office hours! He wants you to succeed!!

Barrios is a good professor who cares about his students. Accessible outside of class and he really wants you to understand the material. However, the class is not easy, and studying is a must. The bad reviews are from his previous curriculum, but he adjusted it. Definitely recommend.

This man teaches with an ego. He previously taught at UChicago's masters program and it seems to have gotten to his head. He clearly cares more about his research than his students. The weekly assignments take 5 hours minimum because he formats them at the expense of your mental health. Avoid this man at all costs, take 2610 with another professor.

Worst professor I have had at WashU. There is weekly homework and Quizzes, which each takes at LEAST 3 hours. The final 35% of your grade, and it's the only test. His lectures are super unhelpful, as all he does is speak conceptually, rather than showing students how to do actual problems. Would never take a class with this man again.

If there's anything I've learned in this class it's that input = output. Professor Barrios didn't put much effort into the class yet expected us to make it our main priority. The syllabus quite literally being the least accurate sheet of paper I've encountered in my lifetime didn't help either. He's a kind guy but needs more perspective imo.

He got mad and angrily asked us why we wouldn't answer questions and how the same people were raising their hands. Also, the syllabus said that the final exam was online but decided to change it to in person halfway in the semester apparently. There were no emails or announcements on Canvas til 2 days prior. Only communications in person.

By far my least favorite class that I have taken in all of my academic career. His lectures were impossible to follow. Slides were so busy and explained very poorly. Quiz questions were nothing like what we learned in class. Homework and quizzes took upwards of 10-15 hours a week and were so inconsistent. Avoid this class at all costs.

As a business undergrad I was forced to take this class. I selected barrios because it fit in my schedule better, worst decision of my life. I have never spent more time on a class for absolutely nothing. His online homework platform grades inconsistently and everything comes down to the final exam worth 35%! No help in class either. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never felt so lost in any course in college. I tried following along with the textbook, but it doesn't help. The difficulty of the class is unnecessarily hard because Barrios fails to help his students understand the content. He's always asking if we have questions, but when we ask, the answers are not helpful. I don't recommend this course.

Have you ever dreaded class so much that you saw skipping a lecture as "taking a mental health day"? That was this class for many. Barrios' humor consisted of self-deprecating jokes and putting down students. Homework alone took 10-15 hours, grading was inconsistent, and quizzes were sometimes proctored. This class needs nothing but improvement.

There are many short assignments for this course (heavy volume) but they are easy. Additionally, Dr. Barton is very caring and understanding of extenuating circumstances. I recommend taking Bio in the News with her.

Lecture explanations were often unclear and poorly articulated, making the material hard to follow. She frequently struggled to answer student questions on ungraded problem sets and did not consistently demonstrate strong command of the material during lectures or discussions.

Dr. Barton's lectures were clear and she explained concepts really well. Some of the questions on activities, quizzes, and exams were worded in confusing ways, but she was always receptive to student feedback. I thought the course was pretty fair overall.
Honestly, I liked her. She responded well to feedback and at least seemed more lively than Queller. There were so many typing and grading errors, though.

People here seem to be misreading Dr. Barton. Sure, she made mistakes, but she is human. Go to her office hours, chat with her, and you'll see why. She is so caring for you as a student and as a human and is always willing to clarify concepts as needed, or simply chat about life! She is amazing, personable, and relatable- Love!!

Ignore all the haters, I don't know why she gets such a bad reputation. She cares for all of her students and will give any help you need, as long as you ask. She is very accommodating of anything that may arise in your life and helps you through it.

She's super nice and knows the content. Beware though that she talks SO SLOW. The pre-lecture videos were all the same length as Chalkers but his are all content while she spent 1/3 of the time talking and 2/3 thinking. No joke videos on 2x speed sound like normal speed talking. Other than that she's chill and I would take a class with her again!

Bio in the News is so chill. She's also so chill. The content is really simple but she still makes it engaging. Definitely take this if you need Natural Science and Math credit! Super nice and really cares about students. A couple of in-class group activities, but you can make them up easily if you miss class. Def take this class.

I like Barton a lot, but I don't think that she's a great professor. Doesn't seem to have a full grasp of the material she is teaching, and we often didn't get through the in class activities when she was leading them. One of her lecture videos straight up has wrong information in it (how to calculate lod scores video, she does it wrong lmao)

Nice and understands the difficulties with being a students and juggling schoolwork and other commitments. She is a bit informal with students and sometimes has a bit of an attitude. She is helpful during office hours for her own content but isn't super knowledgable about the content from other professors in the course (taught by multiple people)
She is really nice
wait i couldnt do this for biology in the news but i love her she is the best and a chiller

Barton takes the fact that students talk in her class personally and decides to not explain things for that reason. I don't think that is a great way to get authority in a class but she is okay at explaining. She also is not a fan of people asking questions after class.

Horrible professor. Lecture videos never have any actual examples and she never explains when to use equations. Her quizzes are very hard and in-class activities are confusing. She is also a bit passive aggressive during lecture and doesn't explain concepts well. She oversimplifies concepts in videos but gives very hard questions on quizzes/exams.
Class is not bad, but professor has a bit of an attitude and made many mistakes.

She throws out ten different equations during a short video but never actually explains when to use them or their significance, you just have to guess right. Also, she talks so much but says nothing in her lecture like I genuinely learn more from just reading the slide than hearing her talk. I don't bother even attending class.

Super condescending and her teaching is still on par with the review from 2019. She will not continue lecture until someone answers her questions in a large lecture hall, and threatens to cold call if no one volunteers. She also gets many basic biological concepts wrong constantly. Do not recommend but you most likely have no choice.

Barton and Chalker both teach bio 2970 and are both awful teachers. Barton doesn't know anything either seems like she just learns the slides the day beforehand and tries to explain it. Always pauses during her lecture videos because she doesn't know what shes saying. I don't know how they're the bio professors at WASHU LOL.

The teaching staff did a good job at transitioning to online. The quizzes were a bit rushed every time, but the exams could easily be finished on-time. Could have explained concepts more thoroughly, but office hours remedied any confusion from the lectures. One of the better professors at WashU. Other classes can be much, much worse.
The whole classes are made up of bunch of equations and she doesn't explain the logic behind the equations. She just goes ahead and plop in the numbers for the entire lecture.
She has a very roundabout way of explaining things - overall she's not too bad during the online semester but I can imagine it could be worse in person.

Barton comes off as very condescending, teaches concepts VERY poorly (she gets basic biology concepts wrong frequently), and treats lectures like they're 10 person classes, often asking questions to the whole class and not continuing until someone volunteers to answer, even going so far as threatening to take off points if no one answers.

This class was a mess. Barton started off lecturing well (compared to Chalker, at least) but by the end, she was messing up whole biology problems in lecture, wasting tons of time. Would answer all questions in lecture, wasting more time. Not nearly enough practice problems. Problems sets were awful. Textbook didn't help. Exams were a grab bag.

The class is so easy that it is difficult to stay awake. The textbook can be safely ignored, as can most of the notes. I learned nothing over the course of this class. Nonetheless, Bhattacharya was completely unhelpful and arbitrary in grading. Worse, he sometimes exploded with anger at the class and the students. Avoid him at all costs.

Unable to explain anything in an understandable manner and the way he grades things is incomprehensible. The class itself is relatively easy but he uses this to lull you into a false sense of confidence. The average for the final exam was 30/100 compared to 90's for everything else.

Don't take MEC 290 with Bhattacharya.  Brutally easy class. Felt like I was in 8th grade, but then he'll give you (and the entire class) a B on his imaginary grading scale.  I was informed that the class AV was a B+ (I received better than class AV on all but one assignment and had extra credit and received a B).  Dumbest professor I've ever met.

He clearly has been doing this for a long time and knows what he is talking about. It can be a very fun class and just go with it. He can be fun but almost always stays pretty serious. Take the class decently seriously (do the small bit of reading). He's a good professor.

Dr. Whitaker's class is a fun way to get into acting. He was always eager to teach each class, and cared about the progress of each individual student. I do not agree with some of his acting techniques- he teaches acting with a director's mindset- not a performers. However, if this doesn't matter to you, 100% take his class! He is wonderful.

Fundamentals of acting is definitely a good break between lectures as the class is fun and entertaining, and there is basically no out of class work besides the final- final is acting in a 8-10 min play w a partner + a 1-2 min monologue. If you are good at memorization this should be easy. Whitaker is fine, the class is easy so it's chill

Great professor, and really enjoyable course -- especially if you enjoy public speaking. Lots of hands on work in class, but pretty minimal amount of work outside of class (except for writing 3 major speeches throughout the semester). Bill creates a really fun learning environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I've taken at WashU. Bill is an amazing professor who makes each class fun to attend. He expects a lot from his students and you need to do work outside of class, but he's a reasonable grader. Definitely take Bill's classes if possible!
great class for those that already have some public speaking experience because he fine tunes your ability, but as an introductory class he expects a lot.

Simply put, Bill's great. He has a way of guiding you and helping you think about your work in many different ways without micromanaging it. He's a big fan of the actor's impulse and puts a lot of trust in his students to work together in order to produce the best work possible. He asks a lot, but if you're willing to do the work, you'll be fine.
Bill is my favorite. Seriously, he's the man.

Bill is a great director, but not a particularly great directing professor - he has a hard time codifiying what he wants from you and how he's responding to your piece, his comments are often along the lines of "I don't know what it is about that music that is making me go 'hmmmm,' you know?"  He grades easily and does not read your dir. notebook.
Wonderful caring man. I looked forward to his class.
Absolutely fantastic.  Working with him is the highlight of my day.
No Comments

The warm ups and exercizes were fun, but it's not the safest environment for growing as an actor.  His comments on scenework were often vague, along the lines of "it's not working for me."  Good if you're a spontaneous actor.  Was always very available to help outside of class.

He's good at explaining things and obviously really cares about what he's teaching. He cares so much, apparently, that he screamed at and berated students in front of the class more than once for not coming on time or not having memorized. Take the class, but watch yourself.
Great guy, lots of fun
No Comments
Bill is fabulous.  His does not sugar coat but is never too harsh.  He is fun and interesting, and a pure joy to be around.
No Comments
Very good at what he does.  His energy is unbelievable, especially for an 8:30 class.  If you get the chance, take a class with him.
No Comments

I loved Gothic Lit with professor McKelvy. Class format is just like a book club, and therefore participation is very important. The grade distribution is a bit brutal as the final is worth 50% of the grade, but he gives very clear criteria of his expectations. I'd definitely recommend focusing on your prose and formatting as much as content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's clearly passionate about the material and is good at guiding class discussions. He's not very good with technology and doesn't use Canvas well at all. Grading criteria are strict, as you will be marked down for minor formatting mistakes. Overall, a good and engaging teacher who gave helpful feedback and assigned interesting readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives the most boring lectures you have ever heard. Be prepared. He will chastise you for looking at the time or getting up to use the bathroom. He will call on you blindly and is a very hard grader. Avoid if you can.

Took his first-year seminar on detective fiction and thought it was really interesting. He's very knowledgeable about a lot and takes time to connect the reading to bigger themes while still exploring what's actually in the text.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall, he is bland. In discussion, Professor McKelvy will repeat your points as if they are his own. He does not make the content exciting or applicable but is a decent guy. He also refuses to use technology and doesn't submit grades on Canvas. I wouldn't recommend taking the course with him.

To be honest, I have no idea why this man hated me so much. I really feel like I deserved an A in this class, but it felt like he did everything in his power to prevent me from getting one. When he graded my papers he would drop me a letter grade for misspelling one or two words. When presenting, I always felt like he was trying to prove me wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: a nice guy, gave rly kind feedback on one of my papers that was V validating. i didn't Love his lectures tho and tho he's ofc rly intelligent and good at what he does, his personal style wasn't Captivating for me.

Professor McKelvy is brilliant and is so well educated in what he is teaching. He is able to lead discussion very well, using every student's comments in a positive way. He is very kind and helpful - in class and with essays.

A solid professor. Will neither be your favorite of the year, nor your least favorite. Dry sense of humor, and appropriately knowledgeable as a professor. Worth taking, and certainly not worth avoiding. Has an incredibly knack for picking up whatever nuggets of truth his students suggest in discussion, no matter how asinine or off-topic. Is kind.
McKelvy is a true intellectual, not at all ideological, generally a charming gentleman.  His comments on my essays were highly instructive.

I highly enjoyed Professor McKelvy's class. He is very intelligent and reading discussion always made me so excited to come to class because of the insightful things he had to say about the Bronte sisters. I loved this class and I will definitely take another class from McKelvy--he is wonderful.

i loved his class.  we read a good variety of poetry, and he put things very eloquently.  promoted good discussions, and the workload wasn't bad at all.  could tell he was genuinely interested in his material.  def take a class with him.

He's a nice guy and very good at engaging the class.  Lectures are discussion-based, so make sure you have something to say about the readings.  He's really wordy and sometimes it's hard to decipher what he's getting at, but under all that I think there is a sense of humor and true concern for his students.
no, no. nono, no nonono.
GREAT professor.  in my opinion, mckelvy is one of the most intelligent professors in the english department.  DEFINITELY take any class with him.  really nice person as well.

I don't know why McKelvy's getting such mediocre reviews. He's a sweet man who genuinely cares about his students. Not a hard grader. His comments are useful. His teaching style is comprehensible and intreaguing. Classes were discussion based, but he added his input where necessary to great affect. I would highly recommend him to any who asked.

Do you like literature for its sterile, esoteric, and uninteresting qualities? You may very well love Bill McKelvy. He doesn't get you excited about what you're reading; he prefers to read passages a hundred times trying to, say, deconstruct the color red, or some obscure Latin quotation. Values ten cents words and pretentiousness over heart.
Nice guy but very wordy and boring.  Asks questions that seem to last for 5 minutes.  Very difficult to stay awake in his class.
No Comments
Very articulate but at times obtuse and minimally helpful. Tough grader, and poor at lecturing on subjects outside of Victorian literature.
Stingy with A's.

A strong, intelligent professor.  Focus in Victorian Literature and is markedly better in the teaching of mid-to-late-19th-century stuff than stuff outside of that period.  Advanced classes are generally better than non-advanced, survey-type courses.
Very articulate.

Overall not too difficult of a class and really interesting in general. As a professor Siever was clearly passionate and cared about his students. Lecture attendance was not mandatory though studios are. Homework difficulty was variable but generally nothing too surprising or out there from what was taught.

Very energetic dude who is passionate about his job. I thought it was kinda hard to keep up with the large variety of subjects covered in 260. I also think the policy of "you fail unless you get above a 70 average on exams" is pretty insane. If i got above a 64 on exam 2, I would finish with an A- but below 57 I would fail the course.
the toughest grader in washu. give you zero even when you make the smallest mistake

Professor Siever brings a really energetic vibe to the classroom and 260 is very interesting and doable if you put in the time. Homework can be pretty time consuming but it gets better. Lots of reading for pre-lecture prep but they really help in understanding what's presented in lecture. Responsive on Piazza. Free candies during studio every week!

Professor Siever did not do the best job teaching CSE 247 in Fall 2021, but he has gotten a lot better. His lectures were funny and he explained the content in a way that was to-the-point.

The class was a bit too slow, but it made me very interested in learning more about the uses of FPGAs and how more complex computer architecture is designed.

Infinite improvement over WDR for 260. It was his first semester teaching it, so the pacing could be improved. Some of the early homework assignments were tedious but that got better over time. Overall pretty fun class. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but I'd recommend going. Labs on Thursdays were mandatory and always felt a bit rushed.

Siever is a good professor, he gives good feedback when you need it and is accessible both inside and out of class. He takes pride in his lectures but does tend to go fast sometimes. Make sure to read the textbook before coming to class or you might not understand the material. Tests are reasonable but make sure to study all the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was very clear but would sometimes speed through topics, but I still learned a lot.
He was very clear and a great lecturer!

bill rules, i would take any class he teaches (even 365 which is hard as hell). he tries his best to make it enjoyable when the material gets really hard towards the end of the semester, but he's just a solid dude who obviously cares a lot about students and teaching cs :)

Siever was super helpful but my section was taught by Mtabakhi (who was very bad). His videos saved me when it came time for exams. Class itself is annoying and can be difficult but the extra credit helps a lot (5% on top of the final grade).

247 is just kind of a stupid class the way its run, so like I can't hate on Siever too much. His lectures can be confusing sometimes (often), but  just make sure you do the extra credit and try your hardest. Its just a class where you can try your hardest and do bad on the tests etc. but thats how it is. Know when to give up its okay.

Amazing guy! His lectures are good and I personally enjoyed and found the unfinished portion of lectures or supporting videos he posts on canvas to be very helpful. His grading criteria is great and fair, it doesn't put a lot of pressure on doing well on exams to get a good grade in the class.

Siever is a great professor to take for 247. He is good at explaining the concepts, and he makes use of technology often to show examples. One thing is that he sometimes cuts the lecture short and posts videos on canvas instead, which I don't really understand. Overall a good professor.

Very structured class ;don't necessary need to attend lectures to succeed but Siever's charm won me over. A very wholesome professor that explained data structures very visually and descriptively. One complaint is that he does not go over the mathy portions of the class too well, i.e. the master method.
Siever seems like a really nice dude and is a very solid lecturer. Enjoyed 247 and learned a lot!
if something come up, don't expect him to care
He gave lots of opportunities in the course structure to get help. Super good at communicating with a large class and staying up to date with all Canvas instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Siever is great at explaining concepts and is very available to contact outside of class through Piazza or office hours. Exams aren't too bad given that you have a general understanding of the topics, and the labs (homework) can be tricky but help is often available from either Prof. Siever or TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This should not be a 200-level class. As a senior, it was the most work I've done for any computer science course.

Siever's a pretty chill dude. Had him for 247 online so I didn't interact with him in person at all, but he did a good job explaining confusing concepts in lecture. He's also accessible on Piazza. He also lays out clear grading expectations and you'll always know where you stand in the class. Hoping to take a class with him irl in the future.
I dont understand why people rate him so highly while the credit is mainly for the design of the course. He is a jerk who didnt care about what students were thinking

I took CSE 131 with him in Fall 2019 and TA'd for him in Spring 2020. He was both helpful and personable when I took the course and tried his best to help students understand the material. He was also helpful during test review sessions and explained confusing problems and topics well. Definitely take a class that he is teaching.

131 was the first computer science course I have ever taken, but the assignments in this class, as well as the resources made available, definitely made it doable. I didn't interact with Professor Siever much, due to the sheer size of the course, but when I did he was very helpful. He takes student feedback very seriously when planning!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I had Siever for CSE131, so I didn't interact with him a ton. However, I found he gave helpful feedback and was very friendly towards students. I would definitely take more classes with him. And CSE131 in general is a fantastic class that I would highly recommend.

131 is a very self taught class, there isn't much professor involvement. However, whenever help was needed, Siever was incredibly helpful. He really knows what he is talking about, he is very passionate, and very approachable. He makes you want to take more computer science classes. I strongly recommend!

Bill is great, a top professor at WashU. He is really smart and cares about his students. He is also passionate about the material he teaches and passes that on to the students. I'd recommend any class he teaches.
Bill is a great teacher, an awesome guy, and enjoys the subjects he's teaching, passing this enthusiasm on.

Not a ground-breaking professor but she explained the material really well and made complex and dense readings easier to understand. Lectures and discussions were always super thought-provoking. My main qualm was that she clearly had favorites in the class and graded accordingly. If you want to be one of her favorites, go to office hours a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Fantastic lecturer, very funny. She *is* heavy on reading though, and you can't get away with skipping it.

Despite using this site quite a bit, this is the first time I've actually gone out of my way to write a review of a professor. In short, Professor Bivar is just gleaming with wit, awareness, and intelligence. She is the type of professor that makes an hour and a half feel like it was nearly 10 min. All in all, one of the best at WashU. Must take!

Lectures were entertaining, but the required reading was unreasonable. She assigns literally hundreds of pages of reading per week and gives pop quizzes on them and expects you to know specific details. Not worth it unless you're able to prioritize it above your other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Bivar gave us a test with a bonus question, then decided later to count the bonus question as an actual graded question on the exam. This brought everyone's grades down on a midterm worth 25% of the final grade. Any reasonable person understands that a student will answer a question labeled "bonus" differently than a normal question.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof Bivar is great. She's obviously very smart and her lectures are clear and organized. She's funny and engaging with the class. She expects you to read a lot, so be warned if that's not your strong suit, but overall I learned a lot and the class was a great experience.

I like her multimedia approach to lectures but she rarely shows a genuine understanding of the course material or explains the most profound parts. A stickler by the rules. If you miss more than one class, you will lose half a letter grade. No exceptions given. That is a pretty irritating combination.

The readings she selected are perfect for the class, and the lectures clarified the readings in an engaging, non-biased way. Not particularly easy or hard, but I enjoyed the class because the material is very interesting. She was always available for help outside of class and for help on the final papers. I think she's a great professor.

The books she chose for the class are premium and classics of political economy. Not the best lecturer though, but tries her best to engage students' interest. If you work really hard, it is possible to get an A in her course. But definitely not easy A. Overall, not the most knowledgeable or eloquent prof, but an okay one.
Uncompromising, unforgiving and overall an inept lecturer with deficient knowledge of her field(only seems to know modern French history well) One of my worst educational experiences at Wash U.

Chem 358 is a super fun class, so if you're interested in organic synthesis, take it. The class is essentially run by the TAs, but Dr. Birman is a core resource when working on your project. As long as your science is good and you do your best, you'll be just fine grade-wise. (Also, don't worry if you don't finish your project...most people don't.)

This is a difficult advanced lab class that is meant as a preparation for graduate level work. Don't take just to satisfy advanced lab or writing intensive requirement especially if you are a premed. Overall Birman is a genius who can struggle sometimes to simplify things down to an undergraduate level, as English is not his first language.

The lab was so disorganized. At the beginning of the semester, you would have no idea what you were doing in lab until you got to the class that day, and then you'd receive barely any instruction and were expected to perform the lab perfectly. By the second half of the semester, Dr. Birman would disappear from the class after five minutes.
A must take class for every WashU student! This class will make your college life complete:D LOL

Vlad Birman is an awful teacher. His lectures are hard to follow and his exams are even harder. Study the textbook like it is your bible, make sure you look at his lectures to see if there is stuff not included in the textbook, but besides that only use the textbook. Grading is pretty lax though, very generous curve

Vlad is the worst professor I've ever had at WashU. His grading is inconsistent, his tests are absurdly difficult and downright unfair. I got a 36 out of 100 on a test once and that was an A. Avoid taking a class with him at all costs

Birman himself has a good sense of humor. He sometimes makes leaps in lecture that are difficult to follow but make sense after further explanation. To succeed in the class, make sure you really have all the material in the textbook down. Once you do, work on as many practice problems as possible. The final grade is curved pretty generously.

He clearly wants (and attempts) to help students but falls short. Lectures follow the Wade text closely so it's best to go through the book too. The only way to do well however is with practice tests and problem sets because lectures alone will NOT prepare you for his exam questions. His lack of partial credit makes the class very hard.

As a chemistry major I had passion and interest in orgo until Birman. His lecture ranks the worst I have ever had. He once posted practice problem answer keys on the day of the exam, literally less than 6 hours before the actual exam started. The forth exam had an average of 27 out of 100. Think twice if you want to take his class.

It may seem like 262 is more memorization, but there is actually application written in the test. Problem solving through piecing together syntheses is one example. It's best to read and take notes on the textbook, and use the lecture notes as a supplement with extra syntheses. Was not too bad, if you are willing to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Birman seems to have good intentions, and is kind. However, he could improve his organization, clarity, and insight into what organic chemistry is like for a student. Practice work was given very sporadically, which really hurts a student's chance to practice the confusing class material on their own.

Prof. Birman seems to be a smart guy who loves chemistry, but he is unable to give a lecture in a way that can be understood by students. He's also actively rude. Do absolutely everything you can to avoid taking his class!
i managed to pull an A off in this class, but dont let anyone tell you differently, this guy is hard as hell.

He might know chemistry, but he cannot teach.  Who is he talking to?  Not the students.  (I bet he has friends in his head that he is talking to.)  Just memorize everything he says in class, and then pray.  You might pass.

The only B I have received in my entire life. He spends the entire class staring at the blackboard. And if anyone asks him a question, he seems incapable of understanding/answering it. Horrible class. I don't understand how anyone can rate him as a good teacher. Brilliant chemist. Exams basically all synthesis.

This is crazy...Birman is terrible.  He is telling us to just memorize and you will do well.  Last year we were taught to learn and apply material and that is all gone.  Organic has to be better than this.

The difficulty of this class should not undermine his competence as a teacher; Granted the time commitment is very significant, but he is a very considerate person who will go to lengths to make sure you understand the concepts

He is terrible.  I am not sure why, it is not just his poor speaking ability, but he just cannot convey a coherent message.  I don't think it is nerves, because he is the same way in office hours.  He means well, but he should not be teaching.
bad. please avoid.

A hard class to teach but definitely loves his students. His notes are exquisite, he doesnt even need to bring a piece of paper to the lecture it's all in his head. Just pay attention and go to his office hours. He is VERY NICE. Just tell him you want to do well and he wil lnot let you go wrong.  Goodluck in the class and be positive.

Great teacher, everyone says he is hard, but all chem classes are hard and require studying lots.  Good guy, and very easy to speak to him, and nice to speak to him.  exam questions come straight from his notes, especially the hardest ones, after practicing the book, read over and over his notes.  if you go to office hours he will give you problems

Birman is a liar and a horrible teacher. He does not follow his grading criteria on the syllabus so good luck getting a decent grade. Also, he tells students that certain subjects WON’T be on the test, but he lies and tests us on those subjects anyway. I can safely say that Birman is by far the worst teacher I ever had.

He started off rough, but come on, it was his first time teaching. Sure the tests were hard, but if you did ALL the work and went to a couple help sessions, they weren't that bad. His teaching and organization was actually pretty good after the initial bumps. If you really learn it in his class, mcat orgo will be a walk in the park.

Previous comment is so off. Person probably got an A in his class.  Birnam is bad and has no real interest or experience when it comes to teaching. Avoid Birnam....He is the worst professor in the chemistry dpartment!
He's not that bad people!

What a joke-Birnam is a genius. I got straight As in all my previous chemistry classes until I took his Orgo class, then I got Cs on all of my exams.  I worked very hard at studying for his lame exams and still I did poorly. He may be a genius to some, but in my mind he is by far the worst professor at Wash U.
Simply the worst professor in the chemistry department

Don’t let some of these positive remarks fool you. Maybe Birman improved as the semester progressed or maybe his students just became better at teaching themselves. His review sessions were only helpful because he gave rejected exam questions. Don’t ask simple questions during a review session because he will ridicule you in front of the class.

Simply a Genius. He knows so much chemistry it will send chills down you spine. His exams are damn hard, but all the material is covered in the class and he even gives very good practice at his office hours. This class is not for the weak hearted, or the lazy.  Be ready to work and ready to learn and you wil be pleased.
Prof Birnam should stick to research.  He is  a horrible professor, and should not be allowed to teach. I use to like chemistry until I took his class! I no longer want to major in chemistry!!!!!
Prof. Birman has greatly improved as the semester has progressed.  He is extremely helpful in office hours and in his review sessions.
He got off to a rough start, but he's really turned into a pretty good teacher. Way more organized and clear at the end of the class.

Not just a bad teacher, but terrible at running the class in general.  He has no concept of how to help stundents learn or in any way inform them about what they need to know.  On top of that he does unacceptable things like put material on an exam form a lecture he did on the exam day.

Last semester I go an A this semester I am barely getting a C.  Go figure?  Birnam sucks!  You can't understand what he is saying . Half the stuff on his exams he never talks about during class. This is his first time teaching this class and I hope it is his last!!! Don't take any classes with Birnam! Worst teacher at Wash U.
Just bad.

vlad sucks!! his exams are impossiblly hard, so hard that even if you know your stuff you don't have the chance to show it. i studied so hard, memorized the rxns, understood the concepts, and still did horribly. you have to be a chem genius to do well. the exam means were 50's, ridiculous.

I am sorry for this guy.  He acts like he tries, but it's just so hard to feel sympathatic towards him after the first exam.  True enough its his first time teaching such a big class, but you would be expecting some improvements along the way...  But he's just as horrible as he ever was.
No Comments

He sucks.. his teaching is okay but sometimes hard to understand and if you ask any question in class he'll start shouting at you. He has no hard and fast rules about grading. he'll deduct your points whenever he wants to. Do not ever take his class.
Worst Class Ever! Avoid the Troll.
Gave a lot of feedback about the final paper, very knowledgeable in his subject area. He even wrote the textbook!
The best!

This was my second class with Professor Harmening and my first online class. He is one of the best professors at WU. I learned so much about criminology. Be warned though, he teaches nothing that is not real life. Some of the material is troubling, but as long as you know that going into it. His course was very easy to follow.
Just had Crisis Intervention with Prof Harmening. Amazing! We talked a lot about Ferguson as it was happening. I came out with a new perspective for sure. One of the best classes I've ever had.

Professor Harmening is very knowledgeable in the forensic psychology area.  What makes the class better than most is that he has years of experience that he brought into the classroom.  He had very interesting cases to compare to the material discussed in class.  The class was interesting and never a dull moment.  It was a memorable class.

The single best class and instructor I have had at University College! Prof Bill teaches nothing he hasn't done himself in real life. I never once got bored in his class, and he is very engaging for the students. He never read from his slides or even his notes, and he actually wrote the textbook we used! The best of the best!
Professor Bleeke is really nice. He knows a lot and he is really patient. His office hour really helps. Like him a lot.

This class was very challenging for me (like a definite struggle) but Bleeke made me hate it so much less. Truly a great, caring, heart-warming and hard-working professor that has brought so much value to the chemistry department. Chill guy 1000/10

The class is set up very well. If you are coming from 111A you'll be just fine, but the lectures are a step down from Daschbach/Mabbs. He took the time to show every derivation for each equation which was helpful for conceptual understanding (but was never explicitly graded).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Bleeke always explains concepts very clearly and coherently. Unlike other professors, he makes it very clear where a number he wrote down is coming from. His evident passion is also infectious and has helped me to become increasingly interested in chemistry throughout the semester. Hats off to a great professor and decades-long career!

He is a good lecturer who knows the material well and is likable. He often dives in deeper than necessary into proving equations the class doesn't actually test us on. Overall, the main thing is that he makes the exams extremely difficult with a heavy time crunch, so I'd definitely suggest doing a lot of practice before exams.

Professor Bleeke is the most down-to-earth professor I've had this freshman year. He makes Chemistry enjoyable to learn and his enthusiasm for science is contagious. Whenever we encounter new learning, my friends and I enjoy referencing Professor Bleeke's "equation of the day" catchphrase.

He seems like a very passionate guy who cares about his students, but his lectures are so boring and monotone. I fell asleep almost every day in class. However, his lectures are easy to follow and he is accessible to students outside of class. He does a good job of communicating all the necessary material when able to engage students.
I like Bleeke as a person; he is very nice and caring. However, his lectures do get confusing oftentimes.

Prof Bleeke is awesome! He's very nice and approachable. He makes the material easy to understand, and the exams are not too challenging, although you need to really understand the material. Absolutely recommend to any chem majors who need an elective.

Bleeke is a pretty chill professor and teaches inorganic chemistry at a good pace. My tips for the class is rewatch the lectures if needed and do the homework and ask questions, and you'll be fine for the class. Averages were pretty high for this course. Bleeke understands what is out of reach for the course and makes very fair exams.

Dr. Bleeke is a specialist in inorganic chemistry. He's the best fit to teach this inorganic chemistry class. The class was well-organized given that it's Dr. Bleeke's first teaching this class, which is amazing. As long as you are keeping up with the reading assignments, attending all lectures, and clarifying all problem sets, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The greatest teacher I've ever had.

Bleeke's "equation of the day" was always awesome and a great way of getting everyone excited. Lectures could feel monotonous sometimes, but all the information is really important for tests and quizzes. Bleeke genuinely cares about the material and you can tell he finds it interesting and is trying to make it fun. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Equations of the day were always the highlights of my day. Lecture could sometimes become a bit dull (lots of scribbling numbers and equations) but for the most part, he seemed like he genuinely cared for his students and wanted us to learn and enjoy learning the material. He put a lot of effort into polleverywhere questions for us to practice.
Nice person, very knowledgeable, but be ready to completely fall asleep by how painfully monotone and boring he is as a lecturer
Nicest professor at WashU

We love Bleeke!!!!!!! He is genuinely a good lecturer and it doesn't hurt that he is one of the sweetest people ever. Consistent with every other professor in the GenChem department, a great professor.
I didn't love chemistry, but I loved him. Funny, engaging, clearly passionate about what he does. A bit dry every so often, but overall, pretty much all you could ask for in a professor.

Professor Bleeke was a great teacher! For me, his explanations of the material are very clear. The material, compared to General Chemistry 111 may be easier if you have previously taken AP Chemistry. Even if you haven't, the class supports students in every way possible (POGIL, PLTL, etc).

Bleeke is the real gem of the Chemistry department. Take 112A with him, you won't regret it. Sure the class can be boring at times and it's not always the most interesting material, but with equation of the day and his usual sense of humor, Bleeke got me through it!! 10/10 recommend.

Chem 112 is basically AP Chem with a little more depth in all of the topics. You can easily tell that Bleeke loves chemistry and teaching, although he can be a little bland at times. His equation of the day is always amusing. You definitely have to study for exams, but there is A LOT of practice material posted on blackboard/backfiles.

Bleeke is a great professor! His lectures are very straightforward, and he keeps the class engaged with his sense of humor and his equation of the day. As long as you put in the work, doing well in the class is achievable.
Professor Bleeke does a great job teaching some tough material, though he can be very bland at times. Equation of the day was by far the best part of his class.  Overall the exams were fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Bleeke is great. Every lecture was very clear and well-organized. Kept students engaged with his famous equation of the day.
Really amazing  professor that uses logic that is easily understood to explain challenging concepts.  Make sure to take notes on the things said verbally not just the things written on the board.

Tests were a lot harder than first semester General Chemistry. Equations of the day were a waste of valuable lecture time. Tried to explain concepts to students but class was kinda bleak. Most students fell asleep or stopped going to class.  Book is utilized a lot more and make sure to take good notes (more than just copying from the board).

Professor Bleeke explains things perfectly clearly, organizes his lectures well and helps anyone that asks for it. He is a great professor - more than what most people can ask for in any class. People just gripe because he isn't the most animated guy around, but if you actually pay attention, he's engaging and interesting.

Bleeke is the man! I don't know where these boring comments are coming from but he kept the class alive with his cute humor and "equation of the days". Not too tough of a class, just do the problem sets and you'll be fine.

Nice guy, but really, really boring.  I stopped going to class and used the video.  You can just fast forward and look at what he writes on the board.  Also, read the text.  Find old exams, because he never asks anything new.

Prof Bleeke is the sweetest!  Although the class is not as interesting as 111, he does such a great job explaining the topic.  One great thing is that Bleeke is completely straightforward.  He goes through everything that you need to know as opposed to 111.  Bleeke is a wonderful teacher!

This was a really boring semester, and I don't think that I learned anything new.  WU should consider letting us skip 112, but you should definitely take 111.  I know the material is not as interesting as what Loomis teaches in 111, but this was tough to pay attention to and Bleeke made it even more boring.  In the end, I was very disappointed.

Bleeke's straight-forward.  He is very sweet but his style is a bit dry. If you pay attention in class, you can do the problem sets which is basically the test.  If you can't get in the afternoon section, not terrible to watch streamed lectures...

Organometallic Chemistry is an interesting course, and Prof. Bleeke teaches it well. He explains the material very thoroughly, so as long as you pay close attention in class the exams aren't too bad. Recommended.

After 111, this class was a snoozer.  He teaches directly from the book.  Nothing else.  He also repeats his previous material for almost 15 mins at the start of lecture.  His exams are way too easy, and should not be graded on a curve.  If you miss 8 points you can drop from an A- to a B.  Yikes.  He also seems v. bored with the material.

Much easier class than 111. He's not the most exciting lecturer (he's like the guy w/ the dinosaur show in Mrs. Doubtfire), but he knows his stuff. He's kind of endearing with his lame jokes and sweatervests.

I seriously don't know where all these "boring" comments come from.  He stays on topic during the lecture and doesn't run all over the place with random tangents, that's all.  Explains everything very clearly, and there's nothing on the tests that he hasn't taught you how to handle, unlike the 111 profs.
He is a very boring lecturer, but he does tell some amusing (however bad) puns.  He's too nice to hate, but too boring to love as a teacher.
he's nice and everthing but unbelievably boring...i have the hardest time concentrating in this class, puts me to sleep!
Good prof. Very clear, tests aren't too bad.
Talk about unbelievable.  You go from Loomis/Frey, who are hard but excellent, to Bleeke, who is too easy and boring.  I was going to be a chem major after first semester, but now I am not sure.
He's really nice, a little boring.  Lectures are good, you don't even have to read the book.
Professor Bleeke is a good teacher but is very boring at 9am.  His monotone voice tends to put me to sleep.  Although I hear that he adds random jokes in his 12pm class.
Very Nice Professor, has some trouble captivating the attention of students.  Nonetheless, a very helpful Prof and he never stops trying...
He's great. Always willing to help, just stop by his office.
BORING!
Bleeke is the man...Very nice guy, class well taught and not too difficult. Highly recommedned prof.
No Comments

Very interesting class; prof Blanc is actually interested in hearing students' thoughts and fosters a good culture of discussion. the combination of history and literature is really well done. he is encouraging about students' work and offers a lot of extensions if you ask.

OMG. Not enough good things to say about him. I'm not an English kid in the slightest and I got through his class without reading a single book. Classes are never boring, and he is genuinely so caring. I cannot imagine him giving anyone a bad grade. (VERY) light assignments and the final paper is only 5 pages. Plus midterm assignment was fun + easy

Prof. Blanc's utopianism class was very intellectually engaging. I learned much about the world, not just about the novels we read but also their place in the context of the university an city around me. Some texts were hard to understand and you're expected to read them, but Prof. Blanc created a warm classroom where students could ask questions.

By far my favorite class this semester! I took a first-year seminar from him called Utopianism in American Literature. Professor Blanc is great at facilitating class discussions and summarizing ideas/concepts. The directions for essays were straightforward, and the feedback that he gave was very helpful. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Blanc lead dynamic classroom discussions where everyone participated and was heard. Assigned readings were interesting and followed the (well-made) course syllabus. Essay feedback was constructive and actionable, and his grading system is transparent and fair. I highly recommend taking a class with him, regardless of your writing background.

I loved college writing with Dr. Bloomquist! She is always full of energy and enthusiasm, and you can tell that she cares about her students. Very approachable. The readings are also very well-chosen--honestly enjoyable and very insightful of STL.
Also, she is very accommodating with extensions as long as you communicate with her!

Dr. Bloomquist truly cares for her students, but she is a tough grader, making it challenging to earn an A despite strong effort. Her class involves a significant amount of busy work, much of which feels unhelpful. As a pre-health student, I often spent as much time on this course as I did on chemistry and calculus, which was really frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Bloomquist is a very nice person, and she genuinely does want to help you in class. However, grading was often harsh and inconsistent. Other college writing professors are much more lax, which will get frustrating. Essay prompts were confusing. It could've been just me, but sometimes she talked to us like we were children.

She is nice and very enthusiastic about writing. Despite that, she gives a lot of unnecessary work and grades harshly. I heard that she often caps people at a 90 and slowly raises grades over time, but personally I felt like some of my better essays were severely undergraded. She also can be a bit condescending at times. Not an easy A class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bloomquist is a great professor that really cares about your improvement as a writer and will be open to helping you if you seek help. Sometimes the grading seemed inconsistent, but she was always open to talking about past work.

I quite like Bloomquist, both as a professor and as a person. A couple of caveats:
1. Class is quite homework heavy
2. Grading can be frustratingly inconsistent/marks can seem arbitrary (i personally felt some of my better works were underscored and my poorer ones were overscored)
3. Sometimes exercises/assignments can seem elementary/unnecessary

Bloomquist is probably one of the most enthusiastic and caring professors at WashU. If you want help, she will provide it. She requires you meet with her for 15 minutes, 3 times, and it's really helpful. My only problem with the class is some of the small homework assignments and activities in class seem like a waste of time. Amazing professor.

Dr. Bloomquist is an incredibly nice person who is always willing to help, and puts a lot of time and effort into giving students feedback. However, she was disappointing for a college level writing class. Zoom could have been a barrier, but the way she spoke to us felt like I was back in middle school. I think my writing got worse.
Put in effort and you can do well
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely go to office hours, will definitely help you prepare for midterms. Final exam was tough
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: tests were unpredictable and overall class structure was poor

He's actually pretty good and very underrated. Gives fast but good lectures, and gives good practice problems. Two of the midterms has 93ish medians, and the final is alright. Just do all practice problems and it'll be an easy class.

Prof Thornton is a funny guy, but his class is anything but fun. After buying his own required textbook, the class moved very quickly. If you study A LOT, the midterms are fine; however, the final was significantly harder than any of the midterms. There is very little partial credit on exams (mostly MC). He is accessible for limited office hours.

He is a pretty standard lecturer who clearly knows what he is talking about, at least for my class he made the book that you use. He makes jokes that are kind of funny but sometimes fall flat, but at least he tries. I was in a large class and if you asked him to explain something he would take the time to do it right, which I appreciate.

I like his lecture style, as it is mostly comprised of doing problems which suits how I learn, and he taught most material alright. Tests weren't too hard in my opinion, just use the past tests he gives (which I appreciated) to study which I found more helpful than his review sheets. Lectures weren't mandatory but I would highly recommend them

For Calc. III
Blake Thornton is alright. He says weird stuff sometimes but he's not a bad lecturer. I actually had Moncada (do not recommend) and switched to Thornton and learned much much better. He uses the classic chalkboard and spends adequate time with problems. Alright guy, good professor.
show up to lecture and you'll be fine! i didn't and still got an a-

This class was very difficult (especially the final) and was graded on three midterms and the final. Dr. Thornton was an excellent teacher, and I would not have done as well in this class without his willingness to meet with students and explain things, so I would recommend doing that and listening to the advice he gives.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: if u can wait to take this class in the spring with schaefer...do it. thornton wants to make the test harder every year-practice exams are nothing like the actual test. and exams are weighed A LOT. the final was incredibly difficult. he added conceptual stuff that we've never tested over. if u miss one MCQ its like 4 points already. avg on final=76
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Decent professor, but will tank your GPA. Just take Schaefer instead

Very knowledgeable professor who truly cares for Calculus. Solid lectures but speaks rather fast for my learning. Grading criteria isnt clear enough in my opinion and the exam difficulty is often extreme. Good person but very blunt in attitude. If you want to do well then give 100% effort and attend office hours (super useful). Best of luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Thornton is one of the best teachers I've ever had. His teaching is clear in class, and he is very enthusiastic during office hours. All the exams are of appropriate difficulty, and each includes an extensive review sheet covering everything you need to know.

Thornton is a great guy, and his lectures demonstrate how clearly passionate about math he is. He is always willing to help during class, after class, or at office hours. Can be a bit blunt at times, but it never impacts how great of a teacher he is. He also regularly acknowledges that Calc 3 (my class) is challenging, which is refreshing to hear.

I don't understand why there are negative reviews of Thornton. He has been exceedingly accommodating and fair in Calc 3 and genuinely seems to care. Class is structured out of a workbook with plenty of practice problems and we are always prepared for exams. Calc 3 is an easy class as long as you show up and put minimal practice in outside of class.

I'm not sure where some of these reviews stem from, but Professor Thornton was one of the best professors I had at WashU. Yes, he is a little blunt and tough, but he's there to help and cares about your success. Always super friendly during office hours while also being extremely helpful. Calc III made MUCH more sense to me thanks to him.

Calc III felt very fair under Professor Thornton. You get out what you put into it. To prepare for the exams, study previous tests found on the WashU exam archive online, and understand that homework can be quite heavy sometimes. Everything is based on the workbook, but he posted it on Canvas (save $). He can be quite harsh in office hours, though.

Tests were not hard if you paid attention in class and did practice problems which there were a lot of. Not the most friendly but good at explaining the concepts needed for exams and did lots of examples in class. Workbook is not totally necessary, but definitely helpful to have. Class was mostly about application not full understanding.
Prof. Thornton was a enthusiastic lecturer and explained concepts well. He teaches primarily out of a workbook that isn't necessary to get

This was the worst intro to college I've experienced. His lectures were rushed and unhelpful, with no recorded content. The workbook was full of errors, and if you didn't practice from it, you were lost. I had to teach myself everything. This class made me question my passion for a subject I love. Avoid if possible and take it with Schafer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thornton was really enthusiastic during lectures, and while he can go a bit fast, its needed to cover all of the content. I definitely would've fallen asleep in any other calc 3 class.
Had him for calc3,overall not a hard class but pretty rude guy. Would recommend taking it with a better prof- schaefer usually teaches spring who is a lot better.
honestly not bad. lecture is pretty useful bc you fill in solutions in the workbook which is helpful. tests aren't very hard besides the final

It's a hard class and it's centered around the curriculum he made, so do the workbook problems to study. Not great 1-on-1 and okay in class. My guide for this class is to do the workbook problems they are super helpful.

Take this class with another professor if possible, but you won't be utterly screwed if you take this class with Thornton. He's a pretty laid back guy, but all of the studying came from hours and hours of self studying. His lectures didn't help a lot that I just stopped going after a month. The final exam was also a mess with tons of mistakes.

Poor lecturer not very approachable. He was condescending and rude on several occasions. The final exam had several mistakes and was designed very poorly. Claimed that the professors went over each problem to see if it was reasonable (don't see how that's possible given the numerous mistakes that were on the final). Disappointing class.

Not helpful in lecture. Speeds through things and expects you to know it. The final was nearly impossible this semester (the average doesn't show it but it was) and was full of difficult computations (MUCH different than the review sheet). Wouldn't recommend

Bad Lectures but not mandatory. His Lectures seemed always to be unable to explain the concepts clearly. 
Homework is important, try to figure out how to solve the questions on his textbook( also written by him). Webwork is far too difficult compared with his textbook but still counts.
Approachable after the class but not very friendly.

Awful professor. Not the worst lecturer, but clearly incompetent. Gave a final exam which was far too difficult and full of mistakes. Also apparently been weird with students in the past and sometimes gave a hostile vibe in class. Probably shouldn't be teaching, but that goes for most Calc III professors other than Schaefer.
Workbook is extremely helpful. I didn't go to many of the lectures but the ones I did go to were informative and pretty easy to understand.

Blake is a nice guy but an ok professor. His lectures are fine, but he uses the workbook as an excuse to skip over conceptual and deep explanations. You will teach yourself a lot in this class. He's not a professor to avoid, but there are certainly better. Take Calc 3 with Schaefer if possible.

BUY THE WORKBOOK. Lectures follow it exactly (general theory/conceptual stuff + all practice problems). He explained concepts pretty well, seemed patient enough when asked questions. 

Exams are quite straightforward and easier than webwork. 

Honestly Thornton wasn't bad, although have heard/read some not so nice things about how he treats people.
Great professor. Tests were reasonable & lectures were usually good. Any gaps in understanding could be taken care of by going to his office hours or asking after class.

I know that my review doesn't make him or calc 3 seem all that great but he really was a fine professor and the course no more difficult than it should have been. While I do not like all of the grading policies I think that for the most part it was fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thornton is an effective professor who explains things pretty well and makes lectures fun. Doesn't have a deeply caring vibe but you'll get everything you need from him, and he is helpful. Effective teacher, fun class, mid guy.

I do not think Thornton teaches well. He makes fun of you when you ask questions for no reason. He seems to get mad when you correct him. He also makes concepts way more difficult than they are. I honestly would use online videos because they explain better sometimes.

Prof. Thorton was a very enjoyable professor, and his course was probably my favorite academic course this past semester. While the class is often conceptually challenging, attending office hours regularly (especially from the start) will help you not fall behind. 

This class can be a lot of fun if you're willing to put in time outside of class.
Not a nice guy but exams and grading was not too bad.

Thornton's lectures were to-the-point, which I personally like but can be difficult with certain topics. He always went over key problems in class that were on tests, which I appreciated. He also always made sure to scan the room for questions and was fairly accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do workbook problems, don't sweat the difficulty of webwork (it's not reflective of exams), and go to lecture. If you need help, ask your friends or find another resource that isn't the professor. He sometimes isn't the most pleasant person to ask questions esp if you're a woman, so just something to keep in mind.

Thornton's Calc 3 has been mixed. He tries to listen but fails to explain some concepts. The lectures go through his workbook, a book of problems, that you will have to buy. I think it is the best format for covering so much content and it has good practice problems but the book has so many mistakes. Exams are tough and worth 75% of final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thornton is not a good lecturer by any means. They made the exams much harder this sem. The reviews were not very helpful for the exams, especially for the final. Exams are worded in ways that practice problems or past exams can't really prepare you for and he can be super condescending on piazza. Just take calc 3 another semester if possible

If you're passionate about learning math, then Thornton is a great professor. He's a hilarious lecturer and explains concepts really well with helpful visuals. However, he tends to make a lot of algebraic mistakes when he's solving problems in class, so make sure you pay attention well enough during lectures so that you can catch his errors.

Thornton is a really nice guy and seems to want you to succeed. However, his lectures are often unclear and his office hours were not helpful; he gives advice such as "yes, this is hard" (no elaboration). But he does make himself available and if you need to take his class it will not be too painful, just amusing and a little frustrating at times.

Thornton is okay. As materials get harder his lecture becomes worse. Just because students did well during the first exam, he purposely makes exams much harder to keep exam averages down. Homework is useless since non appears on exams. He brags about textbooks he wrote, which have tons of typos. His review sheet and exams are also full of typos.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy SUCKS. His teaching is terrible and his tests are cruelly made difficult for NO REASON. Imagine telling students, ON AN EXAM, that the problem (worth 14 points), is going to be nearly IMPOSSIBLE to solve if you don't get the first part right. Yeah he just sucks I don't know what else to say.

Had his class for Calc 3 and it is clear that his teaching quality has dipped in the past years. If you look at previous years he had a high rating and a good reputation among the WashU math department but sadly he has since gotten comically worse. Class is not impossible however he makes many mistakes, is arrogant, and an overall not nice guy.
Heavy work
Make the exam too hard

Professor is very nice and helpful. Attend office hours if you need help with Multi Variable calc, he'll make sure you understand it by the time you exit his classroom. I also had a amazing TA during my studies. If you can choose your TA, choose Josh Covey. He's more understanding and will take the time with you to figure out math problems.

Not a big fan. Lectures were NOT good and as the content got more difficult, he got worse at teaching it. I should've studied more for the tests, but I kinda gave up because the lectures were so awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Calc 3 my first semester of freshman year. I was terrified entering a tough university and taking a known to be a difficult class. I breezed through the first 2/3, but the last third was very difficult. Professor Thornton, however, hosted office hours almost every day and was extremely helpful. He made Calc 3 great! lots of resources, too!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Weekly HW due (usually more than one problem set) that can be unnecessarily hard (way harder than exam questions). Quality of the lecture videos sucks, so going to class is your best bet. Difficulty increases as the semester goes on. Tough material isn't explained as much as it probably should be in lecture, so be prepared to do extra on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: An OK lecturer. However, he uses the tough content as an excuse to teach worse. As the content got worse, so did the quality of lectures. WebWork is a HUGE pain however, and recitation is completely useless. Exams don't try to trick you, but ONE mcq is worth 5 points, so there's really no room for error. Do a bunch of practice and you'll be alright
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not even in his class (I have another professor) but I show up to his lectures because he is a very helpful teacher.
Honestly really straightforward expectations. Go to class, practice, show up for the exam and you will do fine. Use all the resources available to you WashU gives plenty.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Thornton is AMAZING!!!! A little fast-paced, but is great at explaining tough concepts. The exams are pretty easy if you study the practice exams.

Thornton sent an email out to students that did poorly on the first exam and in his email he implied that students who did poorly did not put enough effort into this test and even suggested they should switch out of his class. I understand trying to provide options for his students but the way he conveyed it was insensitive and rude :/

I enjoyed having Professor Thornton for remote Calc 3. His lecture videos were clear. He was very responsive to Piazza, even during break. He genuinely cares about your learning and will make sure you understand the material or make it easier to access (e.g. making a YouTube playlist). I did the WebWork but never used the workbook or textbook.

As the concepts became harder to understand and more complex throughout the semester, so did the lectures. I went to his office hours once to ask for help and he told me that I should know how to do it. Webwork was horrible and usually more difficult than the exams and the exams were pretty fair.

People don't always say the nicest things about Thornton but I actually started to attend his lecture rather than my professor's because I thought he was much clearer. He gives you time in class to work through examples, makes himself available outside of class, and in my opinion explains topics clearly. Textbook & workbook also give much practice.

Bad lecturer, and he gets progressively worse as the semester goes on. He's a strange guy, and will sometimes be condescending to students. Webwork is horrific, the exams are not always very fair, overall it was a poorly taught and organized class and I learned more online than in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: class was very unorganized, only examples with no explanation. Left me very confused all the time. After the first exam, I went to the other section of lecture and my grades improved a lot. also low key sexist. not a fan.
He is boring and a bad teacher
There is nothing you can do about it anyway, you have to take the class and it's given by him.

Thornton cares about his students. He tries to make jokes and to engage the classroom. His worksheets/guided notes that he provides every class are excellent.
