His lecturing is mediocre: throughout the year he got progressively worse at conveying and explaining the calculus. USE THE TEXTBOOK if you need extra help/extra problems.

Thornton is hilarious, but don't expect to learn much. He's a better teacher than Yasha but only marginally. He often skips things and tells students to just figure it out on their own. A lot of times he writes down a bunch of stuff on the board and then turns around and asks if you understand it even though he didn't explain it at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: this class was awful. I ended up dropping after the 3rd exam because it was so difficult. test averages were very high because prof. Bickel's students would do so much better, so there wasn't really a curve. and thorton is just weird. just dont take calc with thornton

Professor Thornton is very knowledgeable but his style of teaching does not reflect this. He frequently skips out on explaining steps, saying that we can figure it out for ourselves. He also likes to focus on what he finds interesting rather than what we will actually be tested on. Tests were typically much more difficult than practice.

Webwork isn't bad. Graded on clicker participation so go to lecture if you end up in Thornton's class. He is often condescending and even refuses do to examples after the class has requested it. Was generally unhelpful and was a poor lecturer, and doesn't seem enthusiastic at all. Would not recommend him to anyone, because he made this class hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Blake's obviously super smart, but he doesn't know how to explain the math in his head to people not on his level. Take Bickel if you can (she's more of a "teacher" personality), but Thornton will definitely keep you entertained and you will learn some. The weekly struggle through webwork is great for making friends. Also, his sandals are A+

he's very intelligent but in a way that makes him hard to learn new concepts from.  he laughs at students when they ask questions because they sound so simple to him. also will go through entire problems just to explain that he accidentally did the entire problem wrong.
He's funny

Professor Thornton was a great teacher.  he would make sure everyone understood the concepts he taught and went slowly, also giving us worksheets to follow along and do our own problems while he taught the material. The tests aren't horrible, and he is much more approachable than other math teachers.

While Thornton graded on a huge curve and actually teaches unlike many calc teachers at Wash U, he favors students who have taken calculus in high school. For those who have not, it is much more difficult to actually learn new material from him and you must seek extra help well in advance.
he's all over the place and often hard to follow in lecture. doesn't explain things very well and is almost rude when asking for help. I'm sure he's a very smart man but he was a subpar calc 1 prof.
Good calc teacher. Clear explanation.

Good teacher, but expects students to be involved during lecture.  If something is unclear, make sure you let him know it, or else he'll assume everyone understands and will breeze right through the material. Does care a lot about students, though, and often will devote entire classes to review.
great teacher, makes great class handouts everyday for the whole class where you can do practice problems and where he summarizes the day's topics.

Horrible Teacher. Incoherent. Unorganized. Taught fast, without explaining. The problem was that everyone had already had the class before, so no one ever called him out on his poor teaching. The only real benefit of his class was the generous curve. I've had better teachers in high school.

Very intelligent and funny (corny).  Really goes over the material well.  Is very approachable with questions and makes plenty of time and resources available for those who need help.  He can go over things fast, but is willing to explain things if you speak up.  Overall a great professor.

He has annoying speech patterns and moves very quickly in class. He refers to the entire class as "you" and often asks "do you understand?" no one who is confused ever raises their hand. He caters to the small number of top achievers in his style of teaching and leaves little room for anyone in between or struggling.
Prof was very helpful and trys very hard. Very nice guy and great class overall. TA's were very helpful as well. Just make sure you go to class.
He does go fast but is really nice and will always go back and explain. I found him very helpful during office hours. I also was very well prepared to do the homework and take the tests.

Professor Thornton was irritating, fast-moving, and unhelpful in all aspects of his class.  He zoomed through material making those who had even taken calc in high school need to double back to catch full topics they'd missed in his lecture.  He also has a very rude and narcissitic office manner.  Take it with somebody else if you can.

Unlike a lot of professors here, Thorton will take the time to go back and re-explain something if the class doesn't understand.  I won't say that you never have to study, but going to class makes it a lot easier and you don't have to try to teach yourself calculus.
this class is SO EASY. Just make sure you go and you'll NEVER HAVE TO STUDY. Seriously

Blankenship is probably the worst professor in the bio department. This course taught me nothing. It restated everything i learned in the intro bio courses with a far more ridiculous grading system. You would lose points if your answers were right but didnt match up with what the professor had in his key. Absolutely ridiculous.

It was difficult simply because the TA's knocked off as many points as they possibly could. The material wasn't difficult to understand but the TA's were very picky. The professor was extremely nice and wanted to help but was often very busy.

Grading policies aren't transparent in the slightest.  You just kind of get a grade in the end, and hope that you are far enough above the median to get in the A range.  Decent lecturer, just make sure to memorize every detail on every slide.  Sounds like a pain, but you'll get an A if you do it.

Unfortunately, this class is taught much more as a biology course (massive amounts of route memorization,) as opposed to a conceptual course. That being said, if memorization is a strength, this class shouldn't be too difficult. Note: 2/3 of the class get some type of A or B, so grading is fairly lenient.

Teacher does not understand math, and can not teach biochemistry. Needs to learn what normalization means, and needs to learn what is relevant and irrelevant. The guy wastes some much time taking about how cool a picture is and barely talks about the important topics. Anybody could have done a better job than him.
Worst professor ever. Avoid her at all cost. She makes my college life 10 times worse. Very condescending. Not willing to help. Wish the school fire her immediately.

I agree that she is condescending and makes whoever that talks to her during office hours extremely uncomfortable. One time I asked her a question in the office and after I finished talking, she said "you tell me" and started playing with her pens as if I weren't there. I wish the school could fire her seriously. Avoid her at all cost.

She doesn't know what she is talking about in class, seriously. You get nothing out of her class unless you read the textbook and teach yourself. I agree with an earlier post that she is condescending, and it makes anyone who goes to her office hours very uncomfortable. In general she is very mean to the students. Avoid her AT ALL COST, no kidding.
I agree with all the comments of the previous poster.

Provides almost no assistance out of class; makes no effort to reach out to students.  When classmates had serious issues, she stopped allowing office appointments and stuck to her insufficient office hours, during which huge lines of panicked students choked the hallway to her office.  She is condescending when help is needed (often).

He is a nice guy and loves what he does, but the class is unfair. People get graded for participation, and a lot of the time, he calls out on people "randomly," but it happens to be the same people. In addition, you don't see your test after it's graded. It's confusing, you feel like you build a relationship and focus in class, but end up with a B.

On the first day of class, Jon makes it clear that class will be difficult. However, it's clear that he cares about what he teaches. I usually don't speak up or reach out to professors, but Jon truly is one of one. He strongly encourages everyone to participate, email him, and give him feedback. Difficult class, great semester!
Do you wanna bad grade, curve? - sign up. Don't ask me why.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I usually don't write these, but Jon deserves an exception. By far the best professor I have had here at WashU. Jon genuinely cares about students and is always willing to go the extra mile to be a fun and approachable professor. While some aspects of the course may be challenging, I really think they helped me get the most out of it.

OB3150 has genuinely been one of my favorite classes ever taken. This is the only class that I've not only actually paid attention to, but also honestly enjoyed. Jon makes lectures extremely engaging, and the class feels like a community. Jon is a really great guy who truly cares about all his students and I loved having him as my professor :)

I get why Jon gets negative reviews, but it's mostly from students who want to sit in class and work on other things without engaging. Jon doesn't allow that. He cold calls and uses a unique, interactive style to show how concepts play out in real life. Reading quizzes exist but are only 2% total. Try it and decide yourself.
This prof is extremely tough. Feels like his main task is to run over and that's it….
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor is super fast in teaching  it's really bad. Tough grader. Quizzes every class. Super hilarious. Insincere. Smile and think bad about you.

Geniunely one of the most unfair classes that I've taken at WashU. He tries to be too fair to the point that it becomes unfair for everyone and reinvent classes. There's a reason why most classes are taught the way that they are...

Jon is the best professor, his lectures are very interesting, and he is so engaging. Sure, this class is not perfect, but nothing is. I'm a pretty cynical guy, and he won me over. 

Life is about more than grades. Take Jon's class!

He has very strong first impressions, good at selling & marketing himself with the course;  but please don't fall for it. The reading quizzes every morning of class are definitely not "easy" unlike the syllabus. Grading gets difficult/random throughout the semester. I HIGHLY recommend to NOT take OB3150 (used to be 360) with him. It's not worth it.

Constant "Turn and talks" (3-5x per class), paticipation points, and reading quizzes every day make the class become about performative learning. He has a lot of energy. I leave class feeling like I've done a lot of reading but not learned much of anything.
So tough grader. Sometimes super unfair to your circumstances.

My favorite professor at WashU. He's very energetic and fair. He continuously encourages you to go to Office Hours and reach out for help! The class concepts are very interesting and really changed the way I look at life.

Jon Bogard is an excellent communicator and can explain things in a great way. His lectures were highly energetic and engaging and he knows how to command the attention in the room. Studying for the exams is recommended because he is a do things by the book kind of person and his lectures build off the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Jon is the most passionate Olin professor at WashU by far. He has a ton of energy and is passionate about what he does. The first day of class, when I walked in, he high-fived every single student and knew everyone's names already. This class is interesting and fun, and is not super demanding. Jon constantly asks students how class can be improved.

I was super skeptical on the first day of class because we (literally) started off by clapping and stomping. As Jon will tell you off the bat, the level of energy/participation in this class might not be for everyone (which is intentional). However, I am so grateful I decided to stay because Jon is genuinely the most incredible lecturer at Olin.

Bogard is a great professor! Super engaging lectures and genuinely loves his job. However, he gives out reading quizzes every morning and you have to be on time. Only 4.5 mins per quiz. Also cases are reallllly annoying to write but overall would take again and enjoyed going to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jon Bogard is the best professor I've ever had. He truly cares about teaching and making an impact in his students' lives. Although at times the energy and excitement are a bit much for 10 am, it shows his passion and dedication to teaching. I can't recommend taking this class with him highly enough, he will make an impact in your life.
Lots of content, was an interesting way to start the day, however sometimes it was too much at 10 am on a monday
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Jon is one of my favorite professors at WashU. He was always willing to help, and he genuinely cared about his students. The class content was also interesting, and I learned a lot from his lectures. There are 2 exams in the class that were somewhat easy if you took the time to understand all class concepts. Participation also really matters.

Jon is great at lecturing and makes the class overall awesome. One thing I didn't like was that there were a few seconds of participation and then back to classwork. His inconsistent participation requirements make the lectures a little confusing. Take this class if you are extroverted.

He is easily the most caring professor at WashU. Wants you to succeed and is there to help you. So enthusiastic and lectures were really interesting. I hope to take another class with him before I graduate. Truly one of the best out there

One of the most engaging and fun classes I have taken at WashU. A decent amount of work and reading. I took the class at 8:30AM and it is one of the few classes where I am not clock watching the whole time. Class is fun, prof is super nice (brought popcorn and candy for us), and even listens to his student's feedback.

one of the most engaging and energetic classes. While this may be welcomed by students looking for an energy boost in the morning hours, it was a bit overwhelming for me. He makes cold calls in the middle of class to ask surprise questions. I prefer a quieter, more organized class, so Jon's class didn't work well for me.
Great professor
I really dont like this professor

This professor was my favorite since coming to WashU. Very kind and caring, and will give an extension for anything as long as you submit a request early enough. Engaging conversations. Not hard to get an A in the class.
Was great, great prof, enjoyed the class, work hard and you shall receive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: please don't take this class...

reviews.comment: this professor is HORRIBLE
avoid at all costs.
stay as far away from this professor as you can.
Do not take this class
Horrible. Do not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I dont know who is rating this professor so highly but y'all be on something.
horrible..

Her grading is fair, no easy A's here, but that's true for most CWP courses. In fact, I think this one is easier than many other CWPs (at least easier than other technology topics). It simply work hard, and you'll earn a good grade. Tip: Revise assignments exactly as what she advises, then you'll earn a pretty strong score.

Pretty strict grader, so don't expect any easy a's. However, they are very understanding and accessible and wants you to succeed. Solid professor for college writing in comparison to many other professors, and if you work hard it is easy to bump up your grade.

This class isn't my first choice when selecting my cwp, but my experience so far has been fine. There's a good extension policy, the professor is usually understanding, grading can be tough because she rarely gives very high marks to buffer your grade but it isn't unreasonable, I was also cooking on a few occasions which made me feel accomplished
they are super nice and are very clear about what they expect. doesn't give out free A's but is definitely not a harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very caring and accessible professor. She is very flexible with extensions and due dates and wants her students to succeed. Solid College Writing Professor, but is a strict grader.
bad professor
bad. just no.
just don't take this class.
Just have nothing good to say about this person. Don't take her? Their? Don't even know what its pronouns are but. Avoid the class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Decent amount of writing, but not much different than the other college writing courses. Easy grader and very chill teacher overall!

Professor Boese is kind, passionate about this class, and super flexible regarding accessibility outside of class. She genuinely wants kids to succeed. To me, she has always seemed like a fair grader, but I also put in work. Use your office hours with her to discuss your papers as you work on them because she gives great feedback.
Super nice and definitely willing to help but her grading is tough.
Really liked having Blank for Calc II! He'll often go on tangents, but he's so funny. He once showed my class the comb he uses when he cuts his hair.

Very bad teacher. Rambles on about subjects not related to stats(such as cereal from the 1970s) Assigns coding homework that no other professors teaching 2200 assign. Very funny and nice guy if you go to his office hours but not very good at actually teaching the subject. Tests are not too hard if you make a good cheat sheet and use calculator

Not a good communicator whatsoever. In lecture and his lecture notes, you have a hard time figuring out what he's trying to say, and he goes off topic frequently. When he explains something you end up more confused than you were before.

I took AP Statistics in high school so i was lucky enough to fare well in this class with no help from Blank. He makes no sense when he lectures. His own notes are over complicated. The third test will hurt and if you have not done well on other tests you will not get a good grade. DO NOT take this class with him.

Clarification: textbook  his own 'class notes' textbook PDF's  Also, First President U  WashU.   Though he seems like a nice guy, his teaching style makes the class appear deceptively easy. Lectures, though not crystal clear, often made sense to some degree. But exams didn't reflect the lectures terribly well. He went on tangents in class often
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Confusing and not very clear in lecture; often makes mistakes on exams. Avoid.

Brian Blank is a mess.  His lectures are all over the place, he didn't use a textbook, and his exams were unfocused and unrelated to class.  His grading can be lenient at times, but taking a class with Blank is the ultimate toss-up.  Funny and sweet guy, but overall don't recommend.

He's an all right professor overall. Unlike some math professors, he is a very approachable guy and responds to emails pretty quickly. His lectures get confusing, but he types his HW/practice exam solutions very thoroughly, which is where the bulk of my learning took place.

Professor Blank, while not the best at teaching, is by far the funniest professor I've had at WashU.  His exams are pretty easy so long as you put a bit of effort into the class (read his online textbook!).  He does make quite a few errors on his exams, however, which is frustrating.

Blank gets really off track, is extremely unclear, and is terrible at answering questions. I got an A in the class by reading, rereading and rereading his online textbook. Do every possible problem and try to write everything from his online lecture notes down on your note card. Don't worry about not having a textbook, use his online one.
Skip class, watch khan academy instead. Lecture notes are confusing. Lectures themselves are filled with unnecessary discussion of cereal boxes and 1970s references.
Blank gets a bad rap, but he's actually a pretty good teacher if you pay attention. He  rambles sometimes, but most of the times what he is saying is actually kind of interesting.

Lectures mainly on obscure material and does NOT focus on core concepts/problems. HW + Weekly Quizzes reflect NOTHING of the tests. Condescending and unhelpful in office hours; doesn't understand when students don't 'get' it. Emails are incomprehensible; test questions often have errors he insists students should've 'noticed and spent less time on'

Took his Calc II class this semester and it was much more difficult than it should have been. In lectures, Blank spends too much time on unessential background information and flies through the limited examples he does in class. His Webwork was much harder than any exam or quiz question and was basically useless to learn from. Not a great experienc

Blank isn't the best lecturer and often gets sidetracked during lectures and talks about irrelevant information. He does plenty of example problems but doesn't thoroughly explain concepts. You can get by without going to class. Do suggested exercises and old exams to study. If you can, avoid Blank for Calc 2.

Blank gives several example problems in his lectures, but does a poor job of explaining the steps. He also can get a little sidetracked when he rants on about the history of math. He's not the worst lecturer, but definitely not the best.

Generally a pretty nice guy, but his lectures are very vague and confusing. Makes a lot of mistakes, including on the exams. He doesn't assign a textbook but I would definitely recommend using one for the course, simply because his lectures/notes are not always very helpful. Expect lots of random tangents, too

Blank is a very good lecturer. He puts all relevant theory on the board in very clear handwriting. Also does good examples in class. Notes you take will be very helpful for homework. The class is hard but this is not his fault. If you take good notes, do practice problems, and SEE HIM FOR HELP IF YOU NEED IT (or email him), you will do fine.

Horrible. Ignores the textbook, teaches using his own personal longhand way of doing problems. quizzes+HW are long and count very little. tests are tricky, confusing, and test your 'reading through nonsense to find a question' ability rather then your knowledge of the material. Adds unnecessarily difficult integrals to complicate problems. Avoid.

Avoid at all costs barring a natural talent in statistics. Your interest in this very captivating subject and its powerful predictive powers will be in tatters by the second midterm exam. A textbook is not assigned - instead a horribly written PDF handbook that is about as clear as mud is given instead. If you must take this course, buy a textbook.

The class started off great and the first two tests were pretty easy. Then one day he said "I expect the averages to drop two 1325 and 1425 for exam 3 and final". Ever since that day he was not helpful at all. Not to mention he always has mistakes on his tests that can really put you in a time crunch because he tells you with 10min left. avoid

He's the master of making simple things look way more complicated than they are. This applies to both the class material, and the tests. He said he didn't like the textbook that other prof's who taught the same class used , and wrote one himself throughout the year. Worst book ever. One of the easiest classes at WashU made extremely confusing.

Blank wastes class time and then rushes to fit the class material in during the last 15 minutes. Honestly, just don't take it if you don't have to. The class isn't worth it unless it's required for your major.
Professor Blank is funny, but...I didn't learn much from his class. He ususally told jokes until running out of time and then wrote what should have been emphasized very quickly.

Awful lecturing. Going to class helps marginally. His textbook was a mess too, which makes sense given it was written by him. I managed to do decently in the course by doing every practice test he had. I would stay away from him unless you have a natural grasp for the subject. He does have funny tangents though.
Don't get his humor; Experimental Questions During REAL EXAMS!!!

He wrote the book so if you didn't understand his lecture, the book wasn't too much help. Calc III with him is basically his version of Calc III, it's more about learning how to answer his style of question than learning the material. He posts all his old exams and he recycles a lot of questions so do the practice exams and you'll be fine.
Dear old Brian thought it was reasonable to put "experimental" questions on the test, which he in no way prepared us for and then weighted those questions extra heavy. That is truly unacceptable.
Great professor, very funny in class. Tests are not terribly hard, and suggested problems from the textbook are helpful.

If you can take Calc II with a different professor, do it. He wrote the textbook himself, which should be a good thing, but since he can't explain it in class, it's not surprising that the textbook makes no sense either. He's really hard to follow in class, and his tests are pretty difficult and all multiple choice.

I don't get the bad comments, either. Calculus is a hard class to teach, but he is clear and organized in my class. And he might just be the funnies math professor I ever had. I woke up everyday looking forward to his class, even though he posted all lecture notes.

I don't really understand the comments below. He is absolutely clear regarding what he is teaching. Also, his lecture note is exceptional (his handwriting is really good). Absolutely brilliant yet nice at the same time (which is bit uncommon in a academic setting). Very flexible. Take any course with him if you can.
Made us all buy his horrible, worthless textbook. Did well in this course only because of Paul's online math notes and Khan Academy, no thanks to him.

Don't know why he got so many complaints. This guy is nice. Okay he's a bit geeky, but that's definitely not a problem. The course material is arranged reasonably and the expectations for exams are easy to follow. He's also helpful, replies emails promptly and stays a long time after class talking to students who have questions. And exams are fine.

He is a likable and quirky man, and very knowledgeable when it comes to his field, but he absolutely cannot teach. Very hard to follow and teaches from his book that he wrote, which is likewise as confusing. To make matters worse, his exams are also quite difficult. Get a different professor.

Blank is an interesting guy who likes to go off on tangents about funny things that happened to him and about the history of mathematics. As a student who isn't always comfortable with math, I found him hard to follow in lecture. He does a lot of examples, but I find them overly complicated, and they sometimes obscure the key points of the material

Having personally read RateMyProfessors before enrolling in this course, I can tell you that I do not think Prof. Blank is nearly as bad as these ratings would make you think.  He has a pretty good sense of humor (even if his jokes are pretty corny) and if you go every day and do the work, you'll do fine.  Textbook not necessary if you go to class.

I highly recommend taking Blank if possible.  Granted, I was in a very small section, but my class loved his humor and eccentricities.  If you go to office hours, he will do his very best to help you understand the material.  The grading scheme is very lenient, so getting an A should not be difficult with minor studying.
GET. OUT. NOW. You'll immediately regret taking this class with Blank.
Very funny. Sometimes his lectures are difficult to follow, but it always becomes relatively clear by the end.

blank uses a text he wrote if you want to pass dont read it. Attendance not required but it will be more work for you if you dont go. if the whole class is confused blank will ignore it and push forward.  If you dont get something buy the calc to for dummies book or go to justmathtutoring.com this class is annoying but not hard to pass

I expected more of this class.  It started off fairly reasonable, but as the semester went on, we all got lost- but Blank kept pushing on.  One plus is that you don't need to know much to do well on the tests.  Grading system was... interesting.
This guy is a horrible teacher... Lectures are horrible and his tests are unfair...
I learned about Maple and cave men drawings in Calc II. The book makes everything more complicated than it is. Easy class, terrible professor. I never went and got an A.

If you like jokes about chalk and useless anecdotes about the bleak social life of a helplessly quirky math professor, brian blank is your man.  If, on the other hand, you go to class to learn, even just a little bit, you should steer well clear of anything this professor is responsible for.  Nice guy, TERRIBLE professor.

I'm just glad I took Calculus BC in high school or I would have had no idea what was going on. He is a terrible teacher, but funny sometimes. Avoid taking this class. Go on to Calc 3 or stay at Calc 1 if he is teaching 2. He's smart, but a bad teacher. He does basically no examples and crams the lecture into the last ten minutes of class.
The class was all about Maple, Falcons, and Hawks attacking squirrels or at least what made sense. Everything else didn't.

Interesting guy.  The material presented was usually clear.  He is awkwardly funny and that makes it worthwhile to attend class. LOVES maple. Wrote the textbook. Overall a good guy, I wish he taught Calc 3.
Brian Blank is so fantastic. He is silly to listen to and goes on many random tangents. Sure, his tests are difficult, but they won't keep you from doing well in the class.

I used to love math, he made me hate it.  He can not teach.  He may be brilliant, but does a horrible job at communicating concepts to the students.  Worst class I have ever taken.  Apparently most of the Math dept isn't good either.

Prof Blank's lectures were rather funny and interesting.  He is a very socially awkward man, but has immense knowledge of the material he covers. Going to class is not always needed, but his lectures do help somewhat if you pay close attention and are able to not get distracted by his odd and very random stories.
Don't go to class.  Learn how to do every problem on the practice exams and you will get an A.

He was able to explain concepts decently, but his tests were impossible. They were in Maple and we couldn't use any type of calculator yet often answers were decimals or ridiculously hard to figure out. Additionally you could never see how similar problems were worked since all he had to do was type solve into Maple. He's occasionally entertaining.
Not bad. Class is optional and those who do show up usual fall asleep. Spends most days discussing how much he hates yellow chalk.
maple!

He is very boring and his lectures are impossible to sit through without falling asleep. He is not very funny, like most people say, but he is awkward. For instance, he'll make some bizarre comment that goes way off on a tangent and then just stand there with a strange look on his face for a few seconds. Then, everyone will start laughing.

He has a habit of making absurd and funny statements, which makes lecture tolerable. However, this does not help his abysmal teaching skills. He rushes through example problems without making his reasons for doing what he is doing clear, making it very easy to get lost or confused. Take the practice exams he posts--they help.
Really enjoy his humor, and he's absolutely brilliant.
Prof. Blank is a very funny guy, and keeps lectures entertaining but I didn't learn a thing all year.  This class is easy so it makes it worth it.
I love Blank! He is so nerdy but i find him really funny he keeps it entertaining for me. He really knows what he's talking about too hes a good teacher
avoid this class at all costs.  he is hardly a teacher, I only learned from the book and practice exams.  I never went to class and got an A tho bc the scale's so high
Blank is so funny in a really nerdy way. He's a good teacher, i actually find lecutres helpful.
we are so entertained by this man that we have created a notebook dedicated to his bizarre class comments. PS he wrote the textbook.

There were never more than 15 kids present in class, even on test days out of the 60 in the class. He loves maple more than his stories about loving maple, which believe me take up 65% of class time. If you even get enough energy to go to class, you will be asleep within the first 10 minutes of class. Not recommended.

I stopped going to class.  The T.A. was more helpful because Blank doesn't teach because he's too ADD to teach a full class properly.  Not to mention that he's horribly non-motivational and not helpful at all.  He said he was too lazy to grade written tests, so they're multiple choice, which I think is ridiculous.
i hate maple so damn much  why can't he just show solutions and post in pdf so we can actually use what is posted on the web
Very easy class, but very odd teacher
Awesome funny guy. Really nice to talk to also, approachable. I love his stories, soooo funny!! Best math teacher i have ever had. Class is easy too.
horribly unhelpful

SLU student took 132 over summer.  I don't understand the bashing.  He is one of the best math teachers I have had and made Calc II easier.  He does tell lots of weird stories that are sometimes boring; he seems to know TONS of random information..
In my view, he teaches really well.  Just do the recommended problems and the class is easy.

I don't know why he gets bashed so much.  He does talk about a lot of unrelated stuff but I'm not much of a math person so I find that more interesting than most of the actual course material.  It's easy too; his grading scale is a joke.
No Comments
No Comments

I took this course in the summer to avoid 15 weeks of going to class on Friday.  It sucked.  On the bright side, there was no homework and everything was straight from the book so you could get away with really poor attendance if you were so inclined.
Makes no goddamn sense half the time, and tells a lot of boring stories.  Seems like an okay guy, but not much of a teacher.

Try his course in summer. He has interesting stories/tangents. I realize hardcore math/science majors might not like that, esp. 'cause he doesn't like to teach to the mult. choice-oriented curriculum, but mult. choice math sucks ass anyway. He's not bad.
Took a really easy topic and made it much too difficult.  Presented everything theoretically and without examples.
Not very clear at all, talks about a lot of off-topic things
No Comments
It's a tough subject that he makes much more difficult than it needs to be
No Comments
really tough teacher.  pretty lazy and teaches too much with Maple

This is one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. He is so passionate and excited about this class and these topics it makes the class so much better. I really recommend this class if you like neuroscience or discussion of disorders. I did very well on the exams for just studying for like 3 days before each exam.

LOVED HIM. Dr. Bogdan's lectures were really clear and he would always tell us what we will be tested on and what is just extra info. He also organizes in-class review sessions to go over the key points that he'll test us on. He is really friendly and super passionate!

I hear Professor Bogdan is quite a great guy when you get to know him. Unfortunately, Abnormal Psych was asynchronous this semester due to Covid so I didn't get to experience this class to its fullest potential. I could still feel his passion towards the subject and he truly cares for his students. Definitely recommend taking if offered in person!
Love this class and professor! His tests are straightforward but lectures may be a bit heavy on content for some. Study your lecture notes and you'll do just fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very confusing lectures and little help outside class. Difficult as an online class.

Reviews here were misleading for me. You can tell he's passionate about teaching and the material is interesting but lectures are an extreme overload of information and it's extremely confusing to figure out what is on the test and what isn't. If you take for abnormal psych, get ready to work hard and take very thorough notes to pass.

He's a really nice guy and is always available to work with students outside of class. GET HELP IF YOU NEED IT! This is generally a very hard class for the non- pre med psych majors. He really wants to make lectures interesting and engaging, but he's a very confusing lecturer because there is so much info and he speaks very fast and jumps around
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The class content isnt difficult but it is very anatomy heavy so get used to that. Bogdan is an amazing professor in the sense that he is always willing to answer questions and entertain some ideas during class. But sometimes he is hard to follow because he speaks like hes at a Nobel prize conference. His exams r literally straightforward. 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The material of the class was difficult, but he was really enthusiastic about it. I felt like he really wanted us to succeed and be interested in the material. He's also very intelligent. I would love to take a class with him again.

Professor Bogdan is one of my favorite professors at WashU. If you're going to take Abnormal Psych, definitely wait until he's teaching it. Extremely helpful and gives clear and entertaining lectures. The tests are easy if you attend class; you can tell he wants everyone to do well. For every test, he hands out little bags of candy to each student!

I took this class as a freshman and found the content of the class very interesting- Bogdan does a great job of making the material understandable. The tests themselves were hard for me, but I partially attribute this to be a first year student who didn't have the best study habits. Would definitely recommend Abnormal with Bogdan!

Ryan Bogdan is an amazing professor. He's very passionate about the material, and extremely approachable. His examplesdata in class all come from up-to-the-minute research being done in the BRAIN lab (which he heads), and his enthusiasm is contagious. Make sure to attend class and take notes on what he says- his lecture slides are outlines only.

You HAVE to take Abnormal with Bogdan. I always felt excited about going to his lectures. For every exam, he gave us all (hundreds of us) candy with notes about its significance (studies, cultural anecdotes, etc) and overall is an excellent educator.

so the class isn't mandatory but you'll seriously want to go. he's adorable on stage and tries to be super hip with music before class everyday. he really knows his stuff, is great at answering questions, and he's SO helpful outside of class (especially if you have any interest in research/ grad school). definitely take abnormal with him!

He's seriously the best, can't wait to take of his classes. Class is interesting, tests are fair, he's incredibly clear and answers questions in class really well. He genuinely cares about his students. He attaches gum/candy to all of his exams!! Don't pass up the chance to take one of his classes!

By any means necessary DO NOT take ANY class with him!!! He is the most unprofessional professor Ive ever had, does not grade, has no material prepared for class, and the class is so excruciatingly boring. He has unreasonable expectations for the class and does not provide proper help for the material. RUN NOW WHILE YOU HAVE THE CHANCE!!!

Do not recommend taking his class if you are a freshman. He is a very tough grader on writing in my opinion. His seminars are a little boring and he talks a lot during class. But ask for help if you need it and  pretty reasonable with extension requests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fun class but lectures almost always got sidetracked and he was largely unprepared. Unclear feedback on essays and took points off for not knowing niche details that only he as an expert would know. Still, he seems like a pretty nice guy. Definitely do not take if you only need LCD credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is the laziest professor I've ever had. He does not prepare for his lectures whatsoever because there are no lectures. Every class is a Q/A session. He is without a doubt an expert in his field but has no interest in teaching. His grading is far too harsh and then has the audacity to send us an email telling us he is disappointed in our effort
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Bornstein seems to know everything there is to know about medieval Christianity, and answers any questions knowledgeably and with humor. A warm and intelligent teacher.

Interesting professor, but the worst at grading that I have ever had. Didn't get any grades the entire semester. Only knew how I was doing when final grade was posted. Unresponsive to emails and expectations were not clearly set. Disappointed.

This class was extraordinarily disappointing. The lectures were disorganized and often not related to the reading material. His feedback on essays was useless at best. I had very high expectations going into the class that were most certainly not met.
Very unorganized. Seems to be more of a literature style teacher than a professor of history. Terrible lecturer, mumbles  a lot and doesn't really make a point

Professer Brantmeier is really knowledgeable and passionate about the field. She adjusts the class to the students' interests and covers a wide range of material. At times lectures can feel a little disorganized, and it'd not always clear what to take away from the lecture. But overall I would recommend her courses.

I loved Global Health and Language, and would definitely recommend it to anyone that is Pre-Med or just looking to learn more about healthcare. Professor Brantmeier is super engaging and always comes to class prepared as well as making herself very available outside of class time. She truly cares about her students and wants to learn about them.

I took this Linguistics and Language Learning course in 2021. Prof. Brantmeier often connects the course readings to experiences outside the USA and details how much she learned from communities abroad. She emphasized the need to address ongoing structural issues. Amazing course!

Dr. Brantmeier approached this course with care and respect for the communities we studied, encouraging us to engage critically rather than passively consume information. She challenged us to think beyond surface-level narratives, fostering meaningful discussions that felt relevant and thought-provoking. A truly eye-opening class!

I took this course in 2022, one of the most enriching classes I've had. Dr. Brantmeier balances accessibility and rigor while presenting diverse perspectives through readings, guest speakers, and site visits. Though class time wasn't enough to cover every layer, we had access to all key insights.I would take Prof Brantmeier again in a heartbeat!

Dr. Brantmeier is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. She is approachable, supportive, and goes above and beyond to help students understand the material. Her lectures are engaging, and she encourages discussion. Always willing to provide extra help and feedback. She's an outstanding mentor and instructor. Highly recommend!

Honestly, the class is a huge disappointment. She is passionate about the topic, but stretches a small, shallow amount of content over the course of the semester. Discussion is lacking, I was frequently bored. Major white-savior energy. She did take us to IISTL and had a few guest speakers which were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Brantmeier's teaching is difficult to speak on because she provides little substance in the first place. There was consistent lack of work or difficulty, which I appreciated during busy times of the semester, but it quickly made the class feel frustratingly empty. Fascinating course topics were presented in repetitive and one-dimensional ways.

Brantmeier's people on the move course is easy to succeed in. That being said she lacks in a lot of areas as a professor where policies are very unclear and do not make sense. She can be hypocritical at times.

All in all, the grading is very easy and she will help when you need it but the class is likely not worth your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a nice professor! She's very passionate about what she teaches which makes her class fun. The course is reading heavy but you can get away with not reading as long as you participate during discussions in class. She genuinely cares about her students and is very understanding.

The class content is SO interesting. I have recommened this class to everyone I know. Not a harsh grader, but she does expect you to do the work and give your opinions even if the topics are harder. Dr. Brantmeier takes an interest in her students and tries to help everyone find opportunities outside of class. TAKE A CLASS WITH HER.

While the class itself wasn't super interesting, Professor Brantmeier is a real gem. She's clearly unbelievably knowledgeable and cares a lot about her students. She tells the most amazing stories about her life too.

Profa. Brantmeier is absolutely wonderful! I was really nervous about taking a spanish lit class after being away from spanish for a year. But she's incredibly friendly and helpful and makes you feel comfortable in class.  Because of having her for 308 I decided to double major in Spanish, which i had not planned on. I definitely recommend her.

Community Building is one of the most influential and meaningful classes I've ever taken, if ethics classes actually focused on the development of the individual this is it. There is only one project and the material can be emotionally rough but it is worth it in the amount of experiences and lessons you learn. Take this course, it means more.

Community Building was the most important class I have ever taken or ever will take. Bob will give you opportunities to learn things you wouldn't otherwise learn, meet people you wouldn't meet, learn and grow in ways you never would've expected. 10/10, everyone should take this class.

Prof. Hansman is one of the most inspirational people I have met. Taking his Adv. Freehand Dwg course changed the direction of my life and helped me connect with myself. He is a true artist - he shared his work and life journey, and he brought clarity to what a creative life can be. His own life and work with St. Louis communities is awe inspiring.
crazy guy but you'll find he actually cares a lot and is a good guy. but dont be fooled, you'll have to work your ass off

Oh god, his teaching style consisted of insulting his students, assuming all of us were rich and selfish, and he put himself on his condescending highhorse. What did I gain? The knowledge that such a "good" human being could hate everyone else.
You definitely have to "drink the cool-aide" to really get into Bob's class. It's a bit removed from reality but what you will learn will certainly change your perspective.
Bob is awesome. He's tough, but he's the kind of teacher that tears you down so that you can build yourself up again, better. One of the best professors I ever met.
Take his class if you want your GPA to drop.

All aroud a good guy, but is completely crazy. Very difficult grader. If you're not an unbelievble artist there is no way you can get an A. Way too high of expectations for an intro level class. You have to have very tough skin to be able to tolerate his "constructive" criticism.
Very lovable guy but extremely difficult grader (does not inflate grades),  likes to go nuts with the classes, wants total participation.
Complete out of his mind when it comes to teaching about true inner city problems. I hope that one day he sees what the rest of us do and finds ways to make the real world better.
Bob truly pushed me to new limits...take any class with Prof. Hansman to grow as a person
One of the most engaging and interesting classes you can take.  Lots of work, but you have to do the things he is teaching to learn it effectively.  Great teacher who cares about students.
Bob is just an amazing person and teacher. Truly cares, and you can learn so much about color from him. One of the best!

We had to do a lot of big, boring drawings.  If you actually do all the work when he says to, you will be drawing every second of your life.  Once you get behind in the class theres no coming back until you pull the all nighters right before they're all due.

Bob is amazing! Hewlett is the best class I have ever taken. If you want to understand social implications of architecture, and grow as a human being, take it. Studio is also amazing, especially if you like to draw ALOT.

Hewlett Program one of the best classes, and one of the most enlightening experiences, of my life. No joke. A very honest and sincere person. Great in studio, but Hewlett comes very very highly recommended to any arch student. Bob is the man.
Incredible professor and human being.
bob is the man.  Hewlett [121] is the best class ever.
Bob is awesome. Take all his classes
bob is god
One of the best professors at the school. His class is fun and he is so flexible with assignments.

My favorite teacher, maybe ever. Such a genuine, nice guy and clearly cares about his students. Shares his passion for math and his other hobbies, and the whole class is very conducive to learning. The choose-your-own-adventure format is hard to understand at first but it works really well. 

Taking 3180 and 3190 with him was amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is amazing. I took his EnCalc class online during the summer and I think he is an amazing teacher over all. He made sure to ask if anyone had questions anytime the subject was confusing. He keeps it real and honest. When something is difficult he make sure that you fully understand it. He's a great guy and he loves rollercoasters!

Mr. B was very funny and always started class with a fun topic of discussion. He really remembers what it was like to be an engineering student and is very flexible with due dates for assignments and attendance, which is reflected in his standards-based grading model. This model allows for a bit of backloading and correcting up incorrect work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mr. B was a great teacher who taught by connecting the topics of EnMath A to real-world engineering scenarios, which I liked. I also really enjoyed the standards-based grading of the class, which was intimidating at first but ended up helping me succeed. Also, very accessible outside of class with 6 office hour sessions a week.

Mr. B is the goat. Always funny and makes lectures engaging. Grading is super fair, HW is based on completion, and there are no exams (quizzes and final project only). You can get up to half of the points you lost on quizzes back; he genuinely wants students to succeed. He also hosted a "bake-off" at the end of the semester which was super fun.

Mr B is probably one of the best professors at WashU. He made Enmath B (ESE 319) very interesting, and he'll do everything he can to make sure you understand the topics. His grading and expectations are very reasonable/attainable, and he genuinely wants you to succeed

Brennan is an all-around great teacher. Brennan's lectures were engaging, interesting, and useful. He's very funny, makes the lectures entertaining, and I genuinely looked forward to attending his class every week. Assessments and grading were very reasonable and fair as there were lots of opportunities to gain back points. 11/10 would take again.

The way Mr. Brennan has this class set up is awesome! You have the ability to learn a lot and be challenged, without it stressing you out like other classes! The environment of this class is really great. Also, Mr. Brennan is very clear on expectations and very accessible outside of class. He's a professor that actually cares about his students!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is really great and offer slow pace lectures. Homework are graded solely based on completeness not correctness. The course content is really difficult but tests are not heavy math. Sometimes, you need two letter papers to complete a question so make sure you have enough time to do all works. 2% bonus if most people complete survey.
Mr.Brennan is one of the top teachers at Washu.His lectures are clear and engaging. He got me to show up to every class for his humor alone. He's also great for reaching out to and asking for advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuine interest in the topics was evident, & that made lectures exciting. His engineering background meant that he had a strong understanding of applications & understood his audience (eng majors, not math majors). Kind, understanding, & enthusiastic; enforced expectations in a respectful way & made an effort to get to know every student.

Awesome professor! Very organized and clear on expectations, reasonable grading, and reasonable difficulty work. You will learn a lot but the class structure makes it not stressful. Plus he's just a caring, nice professor generally.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm no English Major, let me preface, but I will say I really enjoyed Prof Brown. He's exceptionally articulate and the humanities world really piques my interest. I enjoyed his feedback on my essay ideas, and I liked the amount of work for the class. The work is appropriate, and it feels like reading is the main focus.

Very fun seminar class where you can explore different works(though texts kinda depressing). Professor Brown offers incredibly useful suggestions for essays, cares about you an lot, and actually gives really high grades so long as you follow the instructions.
Professor Brown is awesome!! This was by far my favorite class of the semester. He leaves in-depth comments on essays, and it's clear he cares a lot about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took postcolonial lit with professor brown and loved it. He is super sweet, funny, smart, and makes his class fairly stress free while remaining engaging. It was really nice after a week of long lectures to go to his class and get to enjoy discussions with peers. The topic got a tad repetitive after a while but I still enjoyed the readings a lot!

Definitely my favorite professor I've had so far at WashU. Clearly has a strong passion for the material and is always willing to help if you need it. Recognizes that students have different strengths and weaknesses. Great to talk to during office hours and is very understanding. Spends a lot of time thinking of which books to read and it shows.

I really loved having Prof. Brown this semester! I have no background at all with Caribbean Lit and I found the course very informative and challenging in a good way. I will say he is a stickler for paper copies, so be sure to have one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: An absolutely fantastic professor. He's funny, encourages great discussion, and gives the best feedback out of any professor I've had at WashU. I've already taken 2 courses with him, and I will take more if given the opportunity
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Definitely fosters good discussion in class, and the workload always felt very manageable.
A great teacher! Sometimes he only agrees with his own opinion, but he is super open to other opinions still. As long as you are invested he is a great grader & teacher.

Great professor. Less structured than other english professors (who aren't a structured group themselves) but he understands his subject matter and cares about his students. Students who benefit from strict lectures and teacher-led discussion might find his class, in which students lead the discussion more than the professor, challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Literally no lectures.  We read these amazing Caribbean literature works with no context. I feel like a missed out on so much in this course because he never gave us any history about the Caribbean islands or cultural points of reference. However, participation wasn't mandatory and the books are amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor, really helps students improve their writing.

Unproductive class discussions. The class dynamic was fun, but he did not come up with questions that furthered any discussion. Participation is important. Really specific essay formatting and structure, but after the first essay he explains what he is looking for, and if you follow his structure exactly, then your grade will improve.

Professor Brown was a pretty good teacher. Caribbean Literature is definitely foreign for some, so he was really good about giving background information and making things clear. He sprung a pop quiz on the class during the craziest week of midterms season because he wasn't sure if we were paying attention, and he was sadly right. Overall, great.

The nature of 347 is suffering and loads of work. You will feel like you never have a break, and honestly will crash out. However, exams are not that bad. Questions asked are quite reasonable. Buhler does a respectable job at trying to teach difficult course topics. Only curves exams. Overall, good luck. It's going to suck no matter what.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'd like to commend him for an organized semester. Our Exam 3 was on the last day of classes, and we weren't made aware of this until 2 months prior, but he clearly put effort into trying to accommodate. The lectures are... OK, but I stopped attending early on. You'll learn most everything from the TAs.

347 is notoriously hard, but Buhler makes it as approachable as one can. And for a tough topic, I actually think he did a very nice job making lectures (fairly) approachable and demonstrative. I think a lot of poor ratings are just because the class is inherently hard which isn't his fault. Definitely take 347 with Buhler over any other proff.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cool guy. He lectured well and made the class really interesting. Miss the man
347 is the worst
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This semester's Prof. Buhler is perfect in 541T and last semester on 347. During COVID, he is very accommodating and caring, holds very interactive class sessions, gives very nice feedbacks, and gives very interesting lecture videos. His only con was poor handwriting, which gets avoided from this semester. You learn a lot from him, a thinker.
Grading scale seems really inconsistent and he is not at all accommodating of students issues; class is super hard and the only support is super crowded TA hours.
Lectures very clear and helpful. Exams challenging but interesting.

Honestly just feels like he doesn't care about students and receives a lot more joy from getting to take points away from students than seeing them succeed. Terrible lecturer, decent slides, understood nothing from him talking, most things from the slides when he didn't use 500 slides to make a simple point.
Great Professor for Algorithms, in both teaching and research. Received lots of help from Piazza and lectures.

This class might be one of the worst I've taken at WashU. They are getting rid of this class and replacing it with a 500 level class which we have been told is supposed to be the same difficulty. About 50% of students dropped this class. The midterm was a failing average.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: You really need to be on top of your game throughout to really ace this class. To rephrase, it is a matter of time, as to when you start feeling lost. Easier material  tough exams and homework Tough material  pretty straightforward (but still tough) Extra credit is up to 4 points on 100 where you need to correct around 25 solutions/point

I have had the opportunity to take two classes with Dr. Buhler.  He has high expectations and often teaches classes that would be demanding despite those, but if you put in the effort you will leave the class impressed with what you managed to learn in a semester.  If you're expecting to coast through 584 or 541, I must urge caution.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Buhler is a basic professor who is out to prove a point. If you really want to learn the concepts, take an online Algorithms course, or just read CLRS by yourself.  You'll learn more and get your money's worth. 541T is not worth the tuition cost or time. If you do take it, be sure to cheat on HW. Everyone else does.
The best teacher ever, you can learn so much from his course, he can always explain difficult things in simple words,  and he is hilarious and passionate. Love his class.

If you think logically and have a good math/proof based background, Dr. Buhler's explanations will make a lot of sense. Otherwise, you may have trouble understanding him. However, he is helpful if you have questions, and is willing to listen to student feedback.

Buhler will work you to death but in the end you realize that you learned more from him than everything else you did with your undergraduate career. Almost everything that makes me a strong computer scientist I learned from this guy. And his stories are great.

If you can tolerate a jolly man giving 1.5 hour long proofs on the chalkboard, this is the class for you.  The course material is interesting, but I would recommend bringing a crossword puzzle to class.

As a rising star in computational biology algorithms, Jeremy simply oozes intellegence. Naturally, many problems deemed reasonable by him are often more challenging to the average student.   Bright and upbeat in class, resourceful out of class, and always ready to discuss theory, Jeremy is indeed a gem of CSE.
Prof. Buhler is one of the smartest guys you will ever meet.  His classes are hard but he will teach you what you ened to know.

Buhler is a good teacher, which can be said for so few CS profs.  He also runs a very organized class.  That's a plus as well, since so few profs know how to do that either.  All around, a very good professor.  Have no fear taking Buhler, his classes are solid.  So what if he's a nerd?
A jolly nerdy fellow. He's a little strange, but does a great job teaching the topic. Assignments, labs and lectures are very organized. Very pleased with the course.

Took a subject I was expecting to hate and made it quite interesting. He's a huge dork, but I loved his teaching style. He does go off on tangents, as someone said, but they usually relate to the topic in some way that shows its practical use.

He likes to rant and go off on tangents.  Homeworks are rough, tests are like long homeworks.  I find him annoying, but at the same time he's like a hamster at the front of the class; I can't take him seriously.
Absolutely fantastic at explaning things.  His lectures are incredibly well organized and easy to follow.  Assignments are tough, but well explained.

Prof Hyde really tries to get to know his students individually and foster connections. It's hard to get a hold of him outside of class and his office hour window is very short. The quizzes can be a little difficult, but a lot of the class is memorizable/based on the study guide. He speaks very quietly so make sure to sit near the front.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hyde is incredible! He's incredibly excited about linguistics and always seems so happy to share his knowledge with the class. His dry humor makes class engaging and fun; I was always excited to come to class and learn.
professor Hyde's the goat

Hyde has been one of my favorite professors ever! He's hilarious, caring, and got me more excited about Linguistics than I could've imagined. He does speak very softly, so you'll need to pay close attention to what he says in class, but otherwise a very easy and interesting course!

He's probably staring down awful grad placement rates and decided the solution was to crank the course difficulty to absurd levels. Still warm outside class, but in the room he mumbles through lectures, nitpicks assignments to absurdity, gives no credit if you don't have the exact thing he wants, nukes our grades, and calls it rigor. Brilliant.

Professor Hyde thinks he is all dry and witty, but his lectures are painfully awkward. He talks like he's amusing himself instead of teaching anyone. Sitting through this class is a waste of time and energy.

His lectures are interesting and he's a really funny person himself. The class is pretty easy and you just need to show up to lectures and understand the study guides to do well. I will say that you have to take quizzes in person and the other prof gave take-home quizzes.

Dr. Hyde was so funny, and he has a cool bird he brought to class. The class was super easy; you're only graded on the quizzes, so make sure you do the study guides as the questions are taken from there. Overall, Dr. Hyde is such a nice professor.

I love this man. His dry humor is so funny and he cares about making personal connections with his students. I do not like Linguistics, not because it is difficult but because it just isn't my thing. My favorite part of my experience in this class was Brett Hyde, I would love to take another class with them.

Honestly not a difficult class if you're willing to put in the work. The tests are a combination of the study guide (verbatim) and in-class material. Lectures weren't recorded, so going to class will save you on more than a few of the test sections. Hyde was a really cool, fun professor. He'll tell you exactly what to study for the tests.

Overall great professor. I took this class to fulfill a requirement outside of my major and it was pretty much what I expected. I didn't find the material interesting, but it wasn't boring either. Sometimes, it'd be hard to stay awake during his lectures though. Study guides were easy and I didn't have to spend much time studying for the quizzes.

Dr. Hyde truly cares about helping his students learn the material. The material itself is interesting, and he delivers it in a way that makes it easier to understand. Quizzes were reasonable, although it would've been nice to have more guided practice before them. Otherwise, he was an amazing professor, and the class was great. Highly recommend.

I took this class pass/fail. It was a pretty easy pass. No final just quizzes every other week. If paid enough attention in class, you really didn't have to study for longer than like 30 minutes before.
I love Prof Hyde!!! At first, I thought he was a meanie but then I realized he just has a dry sense of humor! He is hilarious!

Super dry sense of humor, I enjoyed it but it's not for everyone. He'll def like you more if you ask good questions and are interested in the material. Not a hard intro class, the structure is v chill and he's a good teacher.

Speaks kind of monotonous/deadpan and has a dry sense of humor, so some people might not like his lectures, but I find him hilarious. Quizzes and HW are easy if you listen to his lectures and read the book, and if you show that you're confused in class, he'll go over problems in different ways to make sure you understand.
Super easy class: 2 attempts for quizzes, unlimited attempts for study guides, can change answers for discussions after seeing others' answers if you didn't like your answers
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing class - made me decide to minor in linguistics. Just show up to lecture, and you'll do well. Plus, you'll want to show up.
Boring lectures and disorganized style. Avoid.

This was easily the closest thing to a joke class I've ever taken in college. However, Hyde truly is an interesting and nice guy, and is without a doubt THE single funniest professor I've had or will ever have. Super sarcastic/deadpan/jokingly mean. Class is pure fun, really - both the material and the overall experience.

He is really hard to meet with outside of class, but you won't receive a good grade in upper level courses unless you do. Not a very dynamic lecturer. Focuses unnecessarily on his own work and interests, does not provide a good background in material. He does care about students, but this translates to having to meet with him more outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: AMAZING
Amazing professor, would take any class he taught

Hyde was a really great professor. Witty, interesting, and knows his stuff. He was able to take what I would have assumed to be a really dry topic and liven it up. As he says, linguistics is like sunshine. In his class, it kind of is.

Hyde is such a legit dude, really funny dry sense of humor and he cares about his students. This class did tend to drag a bit, however, because there is not a ton of active participation like in his intro class. No exams which is nice, but these are replaced with difficult (but not impossible) weekly assignments. Overall, a good class!

AWESOME class! Such a funny teacher. He made me laugh on a daily basis. He is a fair grader and the class is interesting without having too much reading or being very difficult, which I appreciated. Highly recommend this professor and class to everyone.

He's an entertaining, down to earth kind of guy, and likes to involve his students, whether by having students complete problems at the chalkboard or joking around. Prof. Hyde has a rule that if your cell goes off in class, you have to buy donuts for everyone. This semester, his phone went off, and he bought the class donuts!
He's a really cool, nice guy.  He teaches the class slowly and clearly.  The exams are all extremely fair, and only one of the four exams is at all difficult.
He is really good at keeping interest levels high, while also being there for any questions.

Hyde is great! He has a delightfully dry sense of humor. He tells you EXACTLY what will be on the exams. He DOES care about your success and will help you if you need it. He is quite clear, and this material just isn't very difficult! He DOES give back exams, but doesn't let you keep them and give them to your frat or sorority. Sensible policy IMO.
I can see why he has a following! He cares about his students and teaches well. I highly recommend taking a class with him before you graduate.

Boring, awkward lectures. Difficult grading scheme for such an intro class. Unhelpful outside of class (in class too?). Never gives exam back. Very poor interaction/communication with students. Almost zero concerns for students.

Completely agree with previous post. Grading system is messed up. Test is really out of like 200 points when he claims it's only 100, but you are not allowed to argue with it. I found out that he just became difficult this past semester because he realized people were taking his class for an easy A. NOT ANYMORE!

Look, the class just isn't easy, he is really boring and he grades weird. He doesn't grade with percentages, he takes off 2 points for each thing you get wrong, making tests out of 100 points, even though theyre like 130. It's insane
easy.  and yeah, he makes some funny comments, but mostly i thought class was boring.
One of the most interesting and funniest professors I've had at WU, but I don't see what makes this class an easy A.  It was far more difficult then I expected.

Quite possibly the funniest teacher I've ever had.  He makes linguistics class a comedy session.  Sample quotation: "Linguistics is like sunshine on green fields.  It is the most glorious of all intellectual pursuits".

Hyde is like a depressive-type stand-up comedian. Class is always a riot with him, and the material is not hard so you don't mind him wasting class time to heckle visitors and tell hilarious personal stories.  If you're looking for an easy class to fill a req. or get some credits, take Hyde.
Class does not challenge you at all. Need all of 3 brain cells to get A.
He's no powederpuff
Great guy, lots of fun. Really interested in finding students excited about linguistics. Candid, honest, and funny as hell. One of the best professors all around I've ever had.
i love professor hyde!  he's so awesome!

professor hyde is great, one of my favorite teachers at wash u. he makes an effort to stay on friendly terms with students even after class is over. but if you're looking to be challenged, his intro to linguistics class is sort of a joke. i wish he would have demanded a bit more from us.
Amazing prof! He is the funniest, wittiest teacher and you need to take a class with him. (just don't wear flip flops!) If he picks on you, he loves you. And his children are adorable!!

Dr. Hyde takes on various personalities, prefering to teach as he was taught.  Obviously in command of the material, any possible questions are entertained, allowing for a deep understanding of the material.
Engaging, has good sense of humor, not that much work
Great teacher, classes are very fun
great prof.  keeps things interesting.  flirtatious.  fun.  picks on some students, but does it in a nice way.  if you hate being called on in class, this is not the one for you
One of the best professors at WashU.  Amazing interaction with the students on an individual level which makes you feel really comfortable in a class of 50.  Take this class!
One of the most intelligent and considerate professors I've had.
His lectures are kind of dry but he is hilarious and interacts really well with students. curves grades very nicely.
No Comments
Brett Hyde cares more about his students than most people I've ever known.  The true intellectual enthusiast.  TAKE HIS CLASS!!!
Linguistics is cool!  My favorite prof at Wash U.

This guy is always talking about things that aren't on his slides. We rarely cover the topics in the lecture notes. If you don't already understand finance, you are screwed. His Canvas is very disorganized, and half of the study materials you aren't allowed access to.

If you don't know every finance term by your third class, then you're in for a treat! Seems too old to be teaching and is very aggressive when people have concerns or don't know what the frick hes talking about. Absolute chud.

I thought Buddy was an okay professor at first, but as you progress into the class, you lean absolutely nothing! The exams are open AI so don't even bother trying to actually retain the information, there's no point. He also says some very racist comments that are completely unnecessary. If you want to learn anything, do not take his class.
You just have to show up for attended. he allows you to use AI on exams which is very nice. No assisgnments in his class either.

Guidelines say that I cannot write about Buddy showing favoritism, but he clearly has some. This guy transfered to the University of Utah, and is by far racially biased and unorganized. During the first lecture Buddy said, "my last time teaching, my lecture hall had a sea of Asians. It's nice to see some normal people for once." I have more to say.

Frankly, this course has been an utter waste of time. We learned absolutely nothing from the professor, who only briefly read off his own PowerPoint slides in the very first session—without any form of interaction or engagement. For the rest of the course, we were essentially abandoned and forced to present everything ourselves.
Don't teach anything. Ask GPT!

I appreciate the effort from Mr Soubra and the genuine effort he gives for students.

Thank you!

Great professor, he cares about the student actually learning the content as opposed to just memorising.

Highly recommend
if you want increase your presentation skills, choose professor Buddy.
Good professor who offers more opportunities outside the classroom.
gooooooood

I had his CFAR for credit in my last semester. It's absolutely an awful experience. He assigned tons of work but none of those work are meaningful. You need to spend at least 4 hours per week for his assignment but learn nothing from this class.
Conveys class material very thoroughly. Lectures entertaining, always open to questions, and gives great feedback. Very kind and wants his students to succeed.

Professor Burton's care for his students is obvious from the very first day of class. While he does assign a heavy homework load, it serves a purpose and as long as you do it consistently you'll be fine. His classroom is very inviting and he is always open to providing extra support/help. Overall, his course was one of my favorites this term!
