reviews.comment: I had Professor Burton for two semesters and he's great! Although we had a lot of VHL homework and quizzes, the class was fun because of his engaging lectures. He always understood when we struggled a bit and encouraged us to participate even if we weren't confident.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: very invested in building an intellectual community in class. I found him to be pretty funny as well. very accessible professor, would take again 10/10

reviews.comment: I took his first year seminar on the Laws and Courts of Ancient Athens. Professor Bubelis is extremely passionate, knows a ton, and is very caring. reviews.comment: He is the sweetest person ever!!! SO caring and understanding, overall an amazing prof. His lectures are so interesting and he genuinely cares about teaching. reviews.comment: Took History during Alexander the Great. Very kind professor. Very passionate about the topic. The map quizzes are really difficult. A LOT of difficult reading because of the translations and the not super exciting content. Take if you're a history buff. If looking for an engineering elective (as I chose to), pick an easier class.

Buckley is a pretty awesome professor, he really knows his stuff. The class itself is a bit tricky for a 300-level course. If you can bear with the math, you'll learn about some pretty interesting and relevant topics. Overall the course was graded fairly. Buckley also did a good job of keeping the class engaged by making jokes.

Truly an amazing dude - funny, brilliant, and really creates a community within the classroom the really makes you wanna learn. Unfortunately, he makes it a point to include very challenging math in assignment (grad level stuff). HW becomes incredibly hard very quickly, and tests are consistently tough, including the final.
The homework and exams aren't really related to astrophysics, it's mostly just math and quantum. Good class if that's what you're looking for, but don't take it if you want to learn about space.

cool guy, interesting stuff- most of the time, very hard homework

Super hard class. Not a very interesting class or lecturer. The tests are super hard. Pay attention to things she says in class that are not written on slides because she will put them in the test as well. I did not enjoy it; she seemed kind of nice, though.

reviews.comment: Just don't take the class. Was not helpful and exam was way to difficult for and Intro class.

She brought in a guest speaker for one of our classes, and the speaker she picked had a very thick accent, and most of the class couldn't understand her. I had to then go to office hours to receive help on re-learning that lecture.
Goofy ahh professor. Worst exam in intro psych.

I found her to be tough to work with. She puts a lot of questions on quizzes and exams that do not come from slides or lectures. I felt like I was constantly trying to teach myself the class notes rather than feeling it had been taught to me.

I found her to be very passive-aggressive. At times I had trouble with technical issues or couldn't submit an assignment due to valid reasons she would not accommodate. Her methods of teaching are hard to follow, especially as a student with learning disabilities.
Very clear and engaging as a lecturer. 10/10!

reviews.comment: The lectures were okay but more engaging than the first professor. Take this class in the fall if you plan on taking it.
Bugg was alright all things considered. She was slightly boring at times, but overall a pretty decent professor. Quizzes were tough, though. I thought she explained concepts well.

Honestly not the best at teaching but still I thought it was interesting. Since the class is split into three parts, you kind of have to get through it but I mean she is nice and approachable just not as engaging.
Lectures and explanations were always really clear, and quizzes reflected what was covered in lecture.  Overall, Dr. Bugg was very fair and I understood what she was trying to say in lecture.
The quizzes consisted of trick questions that do not corroborate with the lectures or slides.

For the most part a good professor. Interested in the subject, gives lectures a clear structure, and answers the Piazza well. However, lectures can be a little boring at times, and she explains things in a slightly confusing way. Her quizzes were unclear and the hardest out of the three instructors', but if you do well on the others you'll be fine
AVOID

She is a sweet lady, but a wolf in sheeps clothing. The course is structured like a third grade classroom in terms of STRICT rules, but you are expected to perform at the level of a grad student. AVOID THIS CLASS TO SAVE YOUR GPA. thank me later.

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, awesome guy. Lectures are amazing and insightful, if a tad unorganized. Raise your hand, talk to the guy, know the readings coming in and it will be a great and pretty easy class. I will say very frequent pop quizzes about very specific parts of the reading (ie summaries dont work) but the readings are usually great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, one of the best I've ever had. His passion and curiosity is contagious and his lectures were the highlight of my week

Dr. Craver is passionate about discussing with students. He understands you and will point you to the materials for further inquiry. Moreover, Dr. Craver gives very detailed remarks on papers,  from concept structures to phrasing and clarity. Writing makes thoughts organized. The skills I learned from this course are beneficial in the long term.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Great Professor! You could tell he was really passionate about the class content. The course material wasn't the easiest to grasp, but he did a good job of hitting the key points. Encouraged discussions and was easy to reach outside of class. He was also flexible and responsive to feedback from the class.

Carl Craver is extremely enthusiastic and knowledgeable in his field, and is a great person. You can tell he genuinely cares for his students. He does go on tangents sometimes, but his lectures helped me understand many advanced topics. Very effective in the high-level seminar I took, but may be difficult for students newer to the field.

Craver's Philosophy of Science class is a really worthwhile experience if you're interested in philosophy or science.  It's not explicitly stated, but you should probably take some sort of philosophy or logic class as a background. There's also a fair amount of reading outside of the textbooks.

I also was in Philosophy of Science class.  Yeah, the amount of work's not too bad, but he's not the easiest grader either.  His lectures are very fast-paced but he often goes off on tangents that are so confusing.  He also wasn't very accommodating and wasn't so nice outside of class.  Definitely a helpful class and I learned a lot though too bad.

Carl Craver is hands down the most engaging lecturer I've ever had! I don't know about his PNP 201 class, but his Philosophy of Science class was one of the highlights of my academic career. Two in-class essay exams and two out of class papers. If you have any interest in science or just want to be a better thinker, TAKE THIS CLASS!

I do not recommend him at all. While he means well, he is too pretentious and smug to actually know if you're getting it. He is all over the place, disorganized in every way and is not especially all that smart to act how he does. I would consider waiting and taking any class he teaches with someone else.
No Comments

Class was interesting, but the material was difficult. Craver is very smart and gives interesting lectures, but sometimes he goes on long unrelated tangents which are hard to follow if you aren't well verse in the topic. A bit disorganized.
I'm sure he's a great person, but Craver isn't the best professor. He often is disorganized in and out of class, to the detriment of his students.

Dr. Craver is an incredibly interesting and likeable professor.  His lectures are intriguing and he often encourages class discussion.  The class material is difficult to engage in since it is mostly independent,however Dr. Craver is approachable for help.
An easy going professor who really teaches you how to think. Professor Craver may be a little disorganized, but a great, helpful person to get to know

craver is an incredibly funny, laid-back guy; great to have as a friend, but he does not belong in the classroom.  our tests contained material we never could have guessed would have been on there, and he was extremely disorganized and wasted precious class time--i don't recommend him.

Dr. Craver is creative, good at inspiring students, good at both lecturing and listening, incredibly helpful, funny, frighteningly intelligent, and an amazing professor.  Teaches a very hard class, but is a fair grader.

Dr. Jenkins is the BEST. She is super funny, cares about all her students, and is very enthusiastic and engaging. The class is never boring and the class atmosphere is very friendly and chill. Love her!

Professor Jenkins is awesome. She is like a hoot. I have had two classes with her, and every interaction with her is very encouraging. She is very passionate about her students becoming better German speakers. If you get the chance, take a class with her.
She is the BEST! German class is incredibly engaging, and I have learned a great deal without spending excessive time studying.

Professor Jenkins is one of the most amazing professors I have ever had, she is extremely caring, extremely funny, and will further your interest in German. The class is not too hard, as long as you put in the time on all the homework and classwork. I would love to take another class with her, she makes going to class something to look forward to.

Professor Jenkins is truly the best. She is hilarious and engaging, and always reads the mood of the class very well. I only recently started learning German but she has made helped to improve my skills tremendously, while also allowing space for me to make mistakes and learn from them.
She's a very light grader. You'll get an A if you show up, but the content is very challenging. She tries to push you beyond where your German currently is and does a pretty good job at it.

I ADORE carol jenkins with my whole heart. she is definitely one of my favorite professors at washu. the class has a bunch of homework but she is really understanding with extensions and turning in work late. the class is really entertaining and fun and we chat a lot

Professor Jenkins is really fun and really good at teaching german. There was a lot of homework but I think that they are switching up how homework is done in the german department. Overall great experience and would take her courses again

One of the best professors I've had at WashU. I looked forward to her class everyday and loved her enthusiasm and kindness toward students. She genuinely wanted you to learn and improve on your skills. Definitely take her class!!

Prof. Jenkins made German my favorite course taken this semester. She made classes very interesting, encouraged a ton of participation, and has a very fun personality. I really loved learning the content. I wish I could continue taking German with her!

BEST GERMAN PROFESSOR I'VE EVER MET. Personality great and knows everything there is to know about German. All you need to do is review the work that has been covered and you'll do fine. One person in the class never studied and he was the only one that struggled. Participation is main part of the class. I plan on minoring in German with her.

reviews.comment: She has a fantastic sense of humor, which makes her classes very entertaining.
2 classes (1998, 2000), both excellent. She's a fantastic teacher, I'm glad she's still at it!
Sooo cool, really nice, great feedback, very positive.  Who knew ecomp would be fun?
Fun class and she is very nice.
SHe is awesome. If you dont have her for Ecomp, switch into her class. She is easily side tracked ;)

For once I had an English teacher who cared about what I wrote and how well I did in her class.  She has a quirky sense of humor that kept me laughing all semster.  She grades well and gives great feedback.  She made EComp fun, period.
She was a wonderful e comp teacher. She took a very boring sylabus and still made the class entertaining. She was very laid back too.
She definitley puts in a lot of effort and makes the class as enjoyable as possible.
I guess she belongs to the German dept but she taught my Ecomp class.  She was very entertaining, and a fair grader.

5/5 prof, 3/5 class. Lovely interesting dude with lot of passion and great lectures. However assignments sucked and were graded by TAs with no clear grading criteria so you just have to get lucky there. Mine would dock points for bs reasons like not knowing what a word meant. If you love the technical aspect of film, go for it, maybe not for casual

I loved this class! The professor so whimsical and genuinely hilarious. He's easy to reach outside of lecture. Grades are based on essays and quizzes, with a lot of advance notice and study resources. Don't be scared of the 7-10pm lab. It's a movie night with a ton of great films and I looked forward to it every week.

Very eccentric, but also very funny. So many things he says are so out of pocket. Really informative though, and his passion for film is palpable. Really great way to force yourself to watch a litany of great films, and to deepen your understanding for why they're great. Don't take this thinking it'll be super easy though, like I did!Difficultgrade

Professor Burnett is the best! His passion for film can be felt through his lectures. The class does take some work, but it's not overwhelming. He communicates important quiz dates and paper due dates well. If you like movies or looking for a 3 credit course that doesn't require too much work, definitely take.

He is probably the best lecturer I have ever had. He is really inspirational and it is so easy to be stay motivated and involved. You are graded by a TA, but they are all really easy to contact out of class and are really driven to help you get the grade you want. Professor Burnett really cares about the subject and is so willing to just chat.

There is a reason why this man has such good ratings. He is so full of whimsy and passion for what he does, it comes across during every lecture. He is also super accessible outside of class, he extends office hours leading up to every big assignment. Def take a class with him if you're considering it even a little!
Best lecturer at washu hands down. Essay grading is harsh but not bad if you go to office hours.
Best professor yet. Incredible lectures. Great office hours. Take the class.
Phenomenal lectures, truly a one-of-a-kind lecturer. Burnett is so passionate about film and sharing with us this passion.
Best lecturer at WashU no doubt. The other reviews say it all. Numbers don't lie.

reviews.comment: So inspiring and an amazing, caring lecturer. One of the best profs I've had at washU.

All the other reviews sum up his amazing lectures so I just want to say don't take this class thinking it'll be an easy A. The concepts are relatively simple but you will need to really understand them and apply them to your papers (the course is only graded on papers and a midterm). If you're interested in film, I'd definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dude's lectures are unbelievably engaging. Felt like I was going to a show every time.

Absolutely the best professor ever. His passion and excitement radiate off his dynamic lectures and I never wanted to miss a class. Also genuinely cared about students and would move due dates if lots of people were busy. Also gave very very clear instructions and lots of help. I've never seen a professor enjoy teaching so much.

THE BEST. As a first year, I don't know what I expected, but this was the best class of my first semester in college. Colin was so nice and the workload was super light. I definitely recommend taking Intro to Film if you want an amazing professor!

I loved this class. Please take it regardless of whether you think you're interested in film. One thing I will say is that it is a lot of work and the style of assignment will be very new to most people. But the harshness of the grading depends on your TA which kinda sucks. I had a tough one, but still ended with an A+ in the class so it's chill.
Enthusiastic, loves talking to students outside of class, gives great feedback, engaging lectures...in every way an amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Burnett is that dude. Life-changing course, has forever changed the way I look at films for the better. He is an amazing lecturer. It's a fun game to count how many times he says "not at all," or "titillating" during lectures. Great selection of movies throughout the semester. TAKE INTRO TO FILM!!!

Can't overstate what an amazing lecturer he is. Funny, full of energy and passion, cares about students. Kids who aren't enrolled in the class come to sit in and listen. Your TA really determines the difficulty of the grading, but they seem to be mostly fair. Straightforward expectations. Take this class!! It's amazing and he is a fantastic prof.

Really a very high-quality teacher - approachable, good-spirited, and one of the best lecturers in Arts and Sciences. I'll echo the other review on here that said his lectures are like "performance," because they really are easy to pay attention to and absorb. The class itself can be a little boring as the writing assignments are repetitve.

Probably my favorite professor at Washu. Definitely the best lectures I have ever sat through. I felt like he was giving a performance every time. I really enjoyed watching films I would have never been exposed to outside of this class. There is a learning curve to writing essays in this class, but overall Highly recommend just because of Burnett.
best professor I ever had in WashU. definitely take his class before graduate!

This guy is the best in the game. I always looked forward to going to his riveting lectures every week. He is truly an inspirational guy and taught me so much about film. The best lecturer at Wash U hands down, with a doubt. His class should be a required course.

A lot of paper which were challenging but the lectures were amazing and everything was explained so well and tied to real film examples. He's just hilariously quirky and fun to watch lecture and listen to. I always looked forward to class.

I really loved taking a class with Prof. Burnett! He's really enthusiastic about the class and seems to really truly care about his students. Even though the class is pretty hard and the instructors can be hard graders, I think it's worth giving it a shot, especially if you're willing to put the work in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: It was C's first time to teach visual effects last week and I am so honored to be one of the first students to hear his talk on the new section! He was decked out, delivering a spectacular talk on the effect behind how a fairy moved and on how filmmakers transfer meanings behind visual decorations (especially in Pan's Labyrinth). Highly recommend;)

One of the best professors I have encountered! He is SUPERB. Going to his office hours is a pleasure and you will learn a lot. His wisdom lies beyond his knowledge and profession. You will walk inside his office with "?"s and leave with "!"s. Plus, ask about his fav cartoon character and you will get a very unique and insightful answer Trust me ;)

I would write an essay talking about how inspiring and influential Dr. Burnett is but the word count does not permit me to do so. Listening to his class is a pure spiritual enjoyment. Sometimes I feel I am not listening enough and hope his class can last for 90 mins or longer! He is both professional and kind, engaging us every second! I LOVE film!

I took his James Bond seminar and 325 three years later, even though I'm not a film major. His lectures fantastic, and he leaves really detailed commentary on assignments and meet with you for as long as necessary to provide amazing feedback. The classes were fun, but also improved my skills as as a student. Plus, he is so kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Saying this guy is awesome is an understatement. Best class I've taken in my ENTIRE LIFE. I was taking the class pass/fail and still showed up office hours every week just to talk movies with Dr. Burnett. A truly amazing teacher and person. If you are a Wash U student you should be required to take his intro to film class!

Professor Burnett is one of the best professors I've had so far. Not only does he deliver his lectures in a fashion that engages the students, but he is also very knowledgeable about his field. In addition, he is very happy to assist students with their papers to get the best grades they can get.

Colin was so friendly and wonderful in class. I don't think there was ever a class where he didn't make me laugh. He really seemed to want to get to know his students and he was absolutely the sweetest man who has ever taught at WashU. Definitely would take again. It's no accident he has a perfect 5.

Best teacher ever. He really brings his lectures to life. Also, a very kind man. I had a traumatic experience where I accidentally slept through my midterm, and he still let me take the test, no questions asked.
I'm studying engineering and this was my favorite class for the semester. Dr. Burnett is extremely passionate about film and it has now it has rubbed off on me. Cannot recommend this guy enough.
He's great! Wonderful class, he really cares about the subject and gives great feedback if you go to office hours. An easy, worthwhile class
Hilarious guy. My favorite teacher at WashU. Going to class is a joy. The class has a lot of papers and the TAs grade tough. Highly recommend that you take any class that he offers.
Really great
Burnett is the man. Take Intro to Film and watch good movies!

Literally the best professor I've had.  Extremely passionate about the material and clearly loves to teach teach it.  I legitimately looked forward to this class every day.  Plus his chuckle is adorable.
super enthusiastic every single class. really cares about his students, and just a really nice person in general
Proferror is very nice. Gives students good feedback, but is very serious about plagiarism. Checked the work by plagramme  plagiarism checker.

THE CUDDLIEST MAN ALIVE! His lectures are so organized, his knowledge of film so on point, and his stories of life in Canada so hilarious. A brilliant, engaging, and kind soul who radiates a love of teaching and is always there for students outside of class. One of the best professors I've had at WashU.

I'm obsessed with this incredible quebecois. He's passionate, quirky, clear, and knowledgeable- I wasn't even sure about taking a film class before this! His tests are somewhat challenging, in that he is detail oriented, but they're not tricky to prepare for. I always love going to his classes, and I get bored easily in quasi-lecture.

Colin is literally the best professor I've had through both college and high school. He is so passionate about film and it really shows. I have taken three classes with him and he's actually the reason I became a film major in the first place. Take a class with him before you graduate!
Fun, engaging, and a great teacher. Not necessarily an easy class, but he makes the expectations very clear and makes a cool subject fascinating.
Energetic, funny, goofy, genuine, knowledgeable, and interesting-- he's got it all.
Fantastic professor!

Incredible teacher. Will be taking more classes with him partially because they interest me, partially because I know his enthusiasm and teaching ability will help make them interesting. Incredibly nice, genuine, and passionate about the subject.

I have had both Intro to Film and Global Art Cinema with Colin, the lowest and highest level clases he teaches, and loved both. He provides exceptional information that is always clear and he is willing to give you as much out of class help as you need. Always posts lectures online/provides screening prompts and chooses great films for screenings.

Burnett was a really engaging and easy to understand professor. Really nice guy too. He just was sort of unclear as to what he expected on his papers which threw me off. Easy tests and interesting lectures.
helpful!

You might have some issues with her TAs and in terms of their grading and feedback but Prof. Wayne definitely knows her stuff and has good lectures that don't just read off the powerpoint (for the most part). A LOT of supplemental readings that are focused heavy on theory, just get the general feel, no need to read the whole thing. Read textbook
TA was frustrating in terms of feedback/grading, but I had no issues with Prof. Wayne. Felt like a very good introduction to the polisci major, and class was fascinating.

reviews.comment: Carly Wayne for intro to International politics was good overall. Learned a decent amount and grading was only based on a few things. Great professor was a little bit less involved later in the semester but that was because she was having a baby.

Maru's tough-love approach in this course can be uncomfortable, but it's worth it. The class demands significant time and effort, so stay proactive—attend office hours and communicate with the professor, classmates, and TAs. This professor gets off on humiliating his students. He has never once finished a lecture because he always gets stuck on the most boring tangents. This was 100% my favorite class this semester. It was a very light lift and Paul is extremely knowledge and passionate about the subject, which is obvious if you see his twitter page. If you want an easy and extremely interesting class, this is the one for you.

Great guy, would 100% take again. His love for the Solar System and the science behind it really shines through in his lectures. Tests are easy. Great personality when it comes to his lectures, and while they may be long they are very entertaining.
Prof. Byrne's 60k Twitter followers speak to the quality of his space humor. Easy, interesting class; would recommend for CS majors looking to fulfill the science requirement.

Great professor! Makes the classes super engaging and easily accessible through Canvas. Took The Solar System with Professor Byrne and really enjoyed it. It is heavily exam based, but as long as you pay attention to lectures and take notes in class, youll be fine.
I would 100% recommend taking a class with Dr. Byrne. He is very passionate about the information he teaches and incredibly interesting as a person.  His classes are relaxed and low-stakes, take one!

Very good at breaking info down into bite-sized pieces. Also likes to give lots of one-on-one feedback.

Andrew is a good teacher if you like freedom.  He doesn't give much direction and unless you've impressed him with your writing, he's very lenient.  For those he prefers, he grades on a much more difficult scale!!

(Grad student lecturer) Andrew is uptight in the beginning of class but he loosens up twds the end. Not the greatest, not the worst. Learned a lot from the course and she was super kind. Much better than the second-half of the course taught by the other professor (Linda).
Overall,  very clear lectures and expectations. Good at explaining difficult concepts. Would definitely recommend.
Very well-organized and did a great job explaining everything clearly. Offered many office hours and constantly sent out reminders/emails; truly cares about her students.
Kind, really well-organized, pushy but in a good way. The exams were very hard but curved. I start appreciate her even more after experiencing how the other professor messed up everything.

On the verge of falling down a building, I type these words to warn. Do not take the class of Prof. Cai, for it shall cast you down one cliff after another with no rope to grasp nor light to follow. My family ruined, my lover gone astray due to the grade I have received.
Unfairly hard exams, which do not test student actual knowledge about the course. Learning will not help because the questions are way harder than the examples discussed in the coursework.

Very good Professor who trully cares about her students! Do study hard and you will learn a lot from her course. However, the course content is very hard so I would recommend fixing it and don't put everything in a semester.  However, a very great prof and highly recommended!

One of the most kind, compassionate people I have ever met. She creates a space for people to feel accepted in a topic that can feel daunting and overwhelming. Glad to have had the privilege of knowing her and would recommend anyone to take her classes.
Beautiful soul, wonderful person.
Dawg
jian cai was a very kind professor and cares about her students so much!!!

Lecture and homework can be overwhelming, tests are definitely hard: the final exam was a 3-hour open-note exam and the average was still low as 65. However, she did curve it in the end. Problem sets are absolutely heinous and longer than every other professor who teaches mec. Gives quizzes but doesn't mention that or their weight in the syallbus. I would opt for Gray.

wow. what an awful experience. mandatory cold calling. she randomly picks a few names every class to pick on. some names get called on more than others. super hard to understand lectures. review sessions unhelpful. office hours unhelpful. open note exams (hardly helps) doesn't know how to lecture without a prepared packet with all the answers.

AVOID. Makes class unnecessarily challanging, misleads students as to what will be on the exam, and makes her section way harder then the other teachers. Has to curve exams so much because students are so unprepared and generally perform so poorly... the average on her exams is usually around a 50%.

Decent teacher, easy class. I'm not a big fan of writing, but I actually enjoyed her class, and I learned a lot, especially presentation-wise. I liked that we got to choose the topic for our final paper.
Professor Ciurria is incredibly kind and you can tell how much they enjoy teaching. I enjoyed this class and would highly recommended it to anyone interested in bioethics!

I always left class with a new or valuable takeaway, and Professor Ciurria was always patient and helpful in explaining the course materials.  Very few Professors care as much as she does about the content, and I felt like her approach was relaxed, but highly informative.  Make an effort in the discussions--it really is worth it.
A very flexible professor who values students' learning by offering different lecture styles and encouraging class discussions. A very pleasant and supportive professor!
She is a lovely professor that truly cares about the subject material and is willing to go the extra mile for her students!

One of the best professors I've had at WashU. She is clearly passionate about the material and is a versatile teacher. She appeals to many different learning styles and uses modern technology well. She is an asset to any department.

She is so awesome. She is super knowledgeable about all the topics covered in class and has great takes, especially on prison heath care and incarceration as a whole. I thought it was super illuminating to be in an environment that facilitates learning rather than a desperate need for a good great. Take her if you can!

Professor Ciurria is a great and caring professor. She makes her classes thought provoking while not making them necessarily difficult. I suggest taking a class with her! (Although she no longer is teaching at WashU)
she is soooooo easy

she is insanely easy. everyone should take her. half of class is attendance. everything else is graded for completion essentially. she answers her own questions so u dont have to do any reading. all you do is show up. avoid dimarco like the plague and take her
Really interesting class, and as long as you participate, you will do well. Highly recommend this professor and this class.

One thing to note is you have to consistently do well--there's no room for a bad grade bc it won't get averaged out--but it's not hard to do well on everything as long as you do the readings and pay attention!

reviews.comment: Great and funny teacher! Pretty easy class, but the material can be hard to understand, so pay attention to lectures if you don't understand. Class is pretty much just a lecture, but then you have discussion at the end, which I think adds a lot to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very sweet guy who's kind and caring. Nice grader and very easy to get an A. Lectures were a bit boring and one-sided but he gives time for group discussion at the end. Not life-changing but definitely a good class. Don't go on computer and not participate during lecture, he won't say anything but will tank your participation grade at the end.
Fun and interesting lecturer with good discussions.

Took this class Spring 2025, and it was great! Colacchia is super caring and gives interesting lectures. Meet with him for OH and he will help you do well on papers. Take your time and put effort into reading responses so you get a few 3/2's and it will go a very long way later in the semester!

Great intro philosophy professor. If you do the readings (~40 pages/week) and write the reflections (>300 words, >500 for extra credit) you'll get at least a 100% on every homework. And if you're a good writer and willing to put in a bit of effort, you'll get an A on the essays.

Professor Colacchia's great at running a discussion-based class and goes over assigned readings and presents philosophical concepts very succinctly. Many readings are very long and confusing because of their archaic language but Colacchia breaks them down really nicely. Very helpful feedback on essays which is great for revision.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you want a introductory philosophy course, take it with him. Very manageable and most of your grade is based on homework, which are reflections on the weekly readings. There are no tests -- only reflections and essays. Half of the class is discussion based within your small group. Very chill, grading is reasonable, and he gives extensions.

Colacchia was an amazing professor who cared about his students and was incredibly passionate about his work. I've never had a professor who was genuinely passionate about the material they taught as Colacchia. He also has a ton of extra credit opportunities encouraging you to go above and beyond. He gave very good explanations of the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: For Problems in Philsophy, he definitely cared a lot about the material and made it engaging. Reading reflections before every class (~300 words) and half of the class divided into seminar style conversation which kept it interesting. Essays were pretty easy and he offers great feedback and advice if you follow it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very articulate; he knows the concepts well. Helpful in planning for final essays, fair grader, gives a lot of extra credit opportunities, good slideshow presentations.

Great prof for intro philosophy. A good survey of topics, with reasonable but sometimes cumbersome readings. He changed the overall course requirements by giving us more options for the essays after having to grade the first (of an intended 3) but this is because he gave very thorough feedback. Recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Learnt a lot about philosophy which is honestly a chill change of pace (as a stem major) and the class structure sets you up for an A as long as you put in the work for the essays (ask him for feedback and act on it). Bit of a tweak sometimes but overall good dude and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Colacchia was a really chill dude. There are two weekly readings that vary in length and complexity, and you also have to write a short summary of them. Overall he seems to care about his students and has good lectures in class. He is a little unorganized and can leave you waiting half the semester for grades though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professor's I've encountered at this school. I was always excited to attend her class and the readings were incredibly insightful and transformative. The essay's and projects allow a lot of flexibility and creativity. Lecture heavy but in my opinion they are all very engaging and she always encourages you to share your thoughts.

Once, I emailed the Chair asking whether Dr. Chen's lit course would be offered in the Spring. The professor added Dr. Chen to the email, and Dr. Chen replied yes, signing off with her first name, Letty. I then replied, thanking Letty for the response. She yelled at me for using her first name, saying she was "Professor Chen" to me. Cruel professor

Her lectures are interesting. The readings that we did were interesting; I just wished the class was more structured because it seemed like the materials were all over the place. I enjoyed the TA lectures; they offered great perspectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Applies also to grad classes.

Pros: not much group work
Cons: lack of lecture and discussion prep, hostile to different critical opinions (grades lower without explanation). Unhelpful feedback to assignments ("interesting"). Will try to gaslight/threaten you if you attempt to privately express concerns about the class or class-adjacent issues.

Because of her background, she unnecessarily focuses on too much political ideology part rather than analyzing novels and stories themselves. Sometimes very biased with extreme points of view. Need to purchase expensive textbooks. Avoid if you really want to know anything about Chinese literature instead of being brainwashed by anti-China opinions.

There is a lot of reading for this class, but it is really interesting and helped me learn a lot. The lectures provide the historical situation of the readings, then a lot of class is spent discussing. Prof. Chen has a really cool background and brings that to class. I learned so much from this course and enjoyed taking it.

Class is pretty straightforward - usually you discuss the readings assigned. Definitely have to buy the assigned books. She lectures occasionally to give historical background of readings. Prof. Chen cares a lot about the class content and wants to share her knowledge, but class can be boring. Great TAs. 3 papers are basically the whole grade.
I don't know where you people are getting that she is easy, but she is not. We have one week to write a 20+ page midterm. No joke. I'd avoid if I were you.

Interesting class but professor is extremely biased. Discussion is usually guided toward her view, shoots down students' comments sometimes, gives a one-sided view of complex history. Be careful with her essay assignments, because she will grade you on much she agrees with your interpretation.
unclear on assginments but casual to talk to

Grading's not hard.  But extreme unclear and vague about projects.  Grade is extremely subjective, because 60% is 2 group presentations and 40% on participation and attendance.  There's no hardly any work besides reading.

Awesome lady. Very flexible and understanding.Super nice and friendly. Easy class - read novels, articles, and watch movies - but learned a lot of interesting stuff. Only 2 graded group presentations. Definitely highly recommend.
Everyone participates and debates heatedly in her class... She's the BOMB!

Professor Jiayi Chen is amazing! The course covers so many interesting materials, and I learned a lot. She gives great feedback and offers a lot of freedom for the final project. Highly recommend for anyone interested in EALC!
EASY A class as long as you attend the class and read all the require materials. Very reachable outside the classroom.
Gem of a professor, shows genuine interest in the material (which frankly I did not have in the early days of the class), not too tough of a grader but will push you to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the best Professors in WashU who has a great passion in teaching and Chinese. She gives great lectures and inspires her students to think proactively! Highly recommended. 1000/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes I have ever taken at WashU. A great introduction to early and imperial Chinese literature. We go through many different dynasties and themes. The classroom discussions always go into smaller groups, which was always very fun. The papers were also fun to write. Professor Chen was a very enthusiastic lecturer. I recommend.

Prof Christenson is a great lecturer, and I enjoyed attending his classes. He cold-calls in class by going down his attendance roster randomly, so make sure that you show up to class having done the readings. The exams are pretty straightforward and based on the textbook. The lecture is a reiteration of the chapter, but usually entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love Dino, great professor. Gets too much hate, all you have to do is read and show up to class and you will do very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice and caring, funny dude

This class was overall fine. His lectures were usually interesting, and grading was generous. That said, his socratic cold-calling makes lecture attendance almost required, although technically it is not. He also bans all single-use plastics and styrofoam in his 200-person lecture, which is something. Subsection is a complete waste of time.

As long as you read the textbooks you'll be fine. tests weren't very hard as long as you have a basic understanding of American politics. lectures can be hit or miss but you have to attend because he uses cold calls students from the attendance list. but dont stress he doesnt expect you to get the answer right it's just a way to take attendance.

dino is cool but his lectures are pointless and hard to take notes,his exams are heavily based on the textbook(which is long as HELL) pretty hard to study for exam. weekly quizzes are completion grades BUT DO THEM! go to subsection and lecture for participation bc those points rlly matter. he coldcalls so do read before class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not a great professor, he has boring lectures but makes it mandatory to go because of his socratic method (you never know when he will call on you). If you have some basic knowledge of the US government, you can do fairly fine but still would not recommend (he is hot but that doesn't make up for his bad teaching)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a good professor, the class is very test heavy but they are pretty easy as long as you read the textbook, it's purely over the textbook. He uses the roster to randomly call on people for attendance but the overall class isn't bad at all. His lectures are kind of fast so its hard to take notes, but just read the textbook!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a really nice professor if you go to his office hours, super caring. Tests are hard, with lots of details and complicated questions. Interesting lectures. Readings can sometimes be tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dino is a chiller. He gives clear, concise lectures that cover pretty much all of the class content. Go to class, scan the textbook, and you'll be fine.

I love polisci and was excited for this course, but the lectures just aren't cohesive and make it impossible to take notes. He's super nice and funny, but just spouting random sentences with weird slides. I had to read the entire textbook for tests because he gives you nothing in lecture and no practice quizes or another quizes at all.
Super nice guy and good at teaching and leading discussion. Huuuuge chiller and just an awesome guy all around.

Professor Christenson is a nice person, but not a great lecturer. You can skip lecture completely, as long as you read the textbook you'll be fine. Tests have a strict time limit but they're all multiple choice, so as long as you have a general sense of the content his class is a pretty easy A, just don't expect to actually learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, if you go to lecture he obviously cares about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He does really care about his students, but his lectures can get boring at times. The exams are heavily based on the textbook, so if you read the textbook you should do fine in his class.

He's a great guy, really wants students to do well in class. His lectures mostly cover base material so I heavily recommend reading the assigned chapters in textbook. Just read and study for the exams and you'll do just fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly not a super hard class, his lectures just suck. He pretty much reads off the slides and doesn't really say anything insightful or interesting. He's probably the worst professor in the poli sci department at Washu. The class is basically, a repeat of AP Gov. Try to take this class with Reeves if possible.
Not bad if you complete all the assignments and participate in small section. Reading the textbook and taking detailed notes are a must! He is generally a nice professor.

Christenson is one of the worst teachers I've ever had. Coming into college, I was interested in a political science major...I am now mostly turned away from this career as I had such a displeasurable experience in his class. His lectures are difficult to pay attention to and his tests cover lots of material not discussed in class. Just bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Can't stress this enough - MAKE SURE TO TURN IN ALL OF THE WEEKLY ASSIGNMENTS AND ATTEND EVERYTHING. They are for completion and worth 40% of your grade. If you do these you only need a 88% test average for an A which isn't bad because the tests are fine. Prof is decent and will help outside of class. Not my favorite class but not a bad one either

He was a pretty average professor. He is knowledgeable and passionate about politics but his lectures can be boring. You don't really need his lectures as the tests are based on the reading but Professor Christenson seems like a nice guy who would be willing to help outside of class. He is new to WashU + this class so he may improve with experience

He's a TERRIBLE professor. You can go/not go to lecture and get the same grade. Tests are automatically graded when you submit (and worth 60% of your final grade), so he doesn't look at them at all. You have zero time per question, AND he has TYPOS and some WRONG answers to the automatically graded test questions. Honestly disappointed with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of work, 94+ is an A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is definitely not a free class, but it's so so interesting. She discusses pretty complex material in a way that makes it super digestible, and the exams aren't really that difficult if you are an alright writer. You honestly don't even have to do the readings as long as you go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even though the topics in lecture are very dense and usually abstract, Hayward will come up with a simple everyday example of it in lecture to make it easier to understand which is helpful. Readings are hard, but you honestly don't even need to do them if you go to lecture. Going to lecture is way more important for the tests.

I would not recommend taking this as an intro course. The class is graded largely on three tests over the course of the semester. The grading scale is awful especially for an intro course. She is not very receptive to students asking for help. The readings are long and don't actually prepare you for the test. Choose another intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tests are a lot of memorization, which is nice when you have good TAs like we did. TAs and Hayward hold a lot of office hours, so use them if you're struggling! I got more out of the TA labs than the lecture ngl, but that's because I don't like how she sets up her slides. Def still go to lecture though. If you study, you'll be totally fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really did not like Prof Hayward, she doesn't understand that this is an intro class, she was expecting too much from students. Grading scale was also ridiculous considering the difficulty of the class. The readings are ridiculously long and complex, and she brags about the difficulty of her class. If you want an intro class, stay away from this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hayward is an incredible lecturer. The reading can often become annoying and a little too long, but if you get the basics, and the lectures will be on the test. The tests are mainly memorization of the readings. She is a really nice person and obviously cares about the topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although attendance is not mandatory GO TO LECTURE.  The readings are incredible dense (although interesting) but the lectures are directly representative of the content on the exams.  I also recommend going to subsection.  Hayward is a great professor and as long as you put in effort, the class is doable and rewarding.

Great professor! Go to lectures, everything will make so much more sense. There are reading quizzes before each lecture, but they are super helpful when studying for the exams. Other than that, you are graded on 3 midterms (mcq/short response: 1-2 sentences) and recitation participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hayward is an excellent professor. While the assigned readings are very long (and can probably be skimmed), doing them will lead to a greater understanding of tricky concepts and thus greater success on the exams. Her lectures are very to-the-point, and she has an entertaining way of delivering them. Attending lecture is a must. Great class.

Hayward is a great lecturer. She makes all the lectures engaging and humorous. The grading of the class is extremely unforgiving for an intro class. Homework is half credit for being a few hours late and no credit for being after class. Exams are too short and one mistake is 5% of your grade. They're phrased for you to pick the only wrong answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are tough but amazing lecturer. Super interesting topics.

Definitely would recommend her Political Theory class. Easy A if you attend lectures and take notes. A lot of reading, but she sums them all up very well in class. Plus the subject material is interesting if interested in political science.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: FANTASTIC. Clear lecturer who makes complex political theory more understandable. Definitely take her into to political theory class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took Power, Justice, and the City with Hayward - not all the material was interesting but there were some lectures/readings that were actually really eye opening. Would recommend if you're looking for a fairly interesting course with a cool field trip at the end

Her class is not an easy A by a long shot. However, she is a very good lecturer and attending class works wonders for understanding the material she discusses (which is very dense). There is a lot of reading in the course too, but as long as you get a general idea from it and pay attention during lecture, you should be fine.

Distills and explains readings so clearly that actually reading the material becomes unnecessary.  Generally well prepared for class; unhelpful lectures here and there but overall good preparation for exams and essays.

Is a fairly clear lecturer. Is accessible outside of class to discuss material with. Seems nice enough. Lectures and her examples do a fair job of summarizing and clarifying readings, but can ultimately be too vague; if you want the most accurate understanding of readings to do best on tests, do the readings, etc.
Great Prof, her class is really tough. Great class to take if you like theory, stay away if you're just fulfilling requirements. She's nice, helpful, and pretty damn cool.

Power, Justice, and the City.  It was writing intensive and since this professor is new to WU, her idea of writing intensive was spending just as much time rewriting each of the 5 papers, and all of them were worth the same! Very long, boring reading. Half the class pretended to understand.  Check out ratings from Ohio State University.

Great at lecturing and explains things well. His exams can be difficult but he wants you to succeed in the class and learn. If you do bad on first 2 exams, the final will replace BOTH exams. 1 group project but he splits work up into small assignments. He has a good grading system and I thought I was cooked after the 1st exam but he was helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Clayton is incredible! I never thought finance could be made interesting, but he cuts through the monotony well and explains not only the economic theory behind finance but also its very behavioral implications. Fascinating (finance) content led by a very kind, engaging lecturer.
Gives good lectures and is very nice. Answers questions very well and really cares about students understanding topics and doing well on the class/exams.

Highly recommend Clayton! He is a really sweet professor and teaches material well. Projects aren't too bad when divided between 3-4 people. Lowkey slacked on the first exam so don't do that. Managed to still get an A from the second one. Lectures can be a bit boring, but that's just the material. Exam schedule is flexible too!
Easily the best Olin professor, he's super clear about expectations, and actually wants you to know the material and succeed.

One of the best professors I've had so far. The lectures were very clear (also recorded), notes were helpful, group projects felt actually relevant and had very clear guidelines that made them easy to do well on, and the exams were not too bad. Great guy and I hope I can take another class with him in the future.

Clayton is probably the best professor I've had in Olin. He cares so much about his students and will try to help with anything he can. His lectures can get a bit boring (considering it's a finance class) but he's such a nice guy. He gives lots of handicaps for tests and projects and will try his best to accommodate if something happens.

One of the best professors I've had at WashU. Extremely caring and kind to his students (and thus not a power-trippy, cold-calling prof like some I've had). Provides ample prep material leading up to exams, and the projects he assigns build real-world skills yet are made easy to follow and complete. Absolutely amazing professor.

Grant is one of the best professors I have ever had! He is a great teacher, and he cares so much about the students performance and will help above and beyond. Truly a perfect professor. Take Fin 340 with him!
easy grader idk what these comments are talking about. So boring though. If you memorize the specific works you can easily get an 100%

Incredibly boring lectures & assignments with ZERO structure. I feel that random works were just constantly thrown at us for no apparent reason. Her class memorization format & overall lack of structure just wasn't very conducive to actual learning and appreciation. Take it for credit, but don't lose faith in art history-IMAAD is much better!
boring class, tough grader
no comments, won't take it anymore
Boring class. Have to memorize a lot of stuff. Grades depend on AI evaluation, and they are harsh and unfair. Even perfect work can barely get an A. Attendance is recorded randomly. Worst class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Swan is a kind person, and this class is a good starting point for one to develop skills of visual analysis and an art historical lens. However, there was a very uneven emphasis on different eras of art, and toward the end (High Renaissance and Baroque--nothing after the mid-1600s was explored) lectures felt shallow and rushed.

Very boring lecture. All ended up drawing or sleeping during the lecture. Yaps in the beginning of the lecture about something random or previous lessons for about 30 minutes. DESPISES any AI and even Grammarly (still got good grades though after using them). A lot of extra memorizations. Overall pretty nice person, but not as a prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very memorization-heavy class. You will need to learn 30-40 works by heart with dates, materials and historical significance for exams. Strict no tech policy. The professor does random attendance quizzes. I loved the TAs though! Dr. Swan is an awesome and very knowledgable person, but the class itself can drag on and isn't an easy A.

Overall, Professor Swan is genuinely a lovely person and is obviously extremely passionate about Art History; however, whenever it comes to choosing individual sections, I highly recommend not picking hers. She takes off a heavy and unnecessary amount of points for slight, minor mistakes, and the course would be better if it were a smaller lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course is required for architecture, and I can say it wastes my time. The readings assigned for every class are useless, lecture is so boring you WILL fall asleep. There's barely any guidance on essays and assignments (they're graded harshly). She does random attendance checks and the class overall feels like a joke. Nice person, bad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Im not an art student and tok this just for fun to balance a course load. I didn't expect how much memorization and random dates I would need to know for tests. It was interesting to interprete the art of course, but i hated the discussion and all the useful assignements. If your not studying archetitecture or not interested, not worth the time.

There was an immense amount of readings "required" before each lecture, which got in the way of many of my other more important classes. As far as lectures go, as someone with attention difficulties, I could barely pay attention in her class. You genuinely have to sit in the front and do this for the love of the game. Way too much memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Course may be interesting for some, but for the most part boring. Immense amount of required readings before every lecture. The midterms require you to spend lots of time for a course that ISN'T even required for any major. All in all this course isn't necessarily hard, but too time consuming in comparison to core classes which makes it frustrating

Heavy workload, need to remember every detail of artworks in order to perform well in midterms, which would ruin your life if you have multiple midterms together. Another big portion of the grade is based on essays, but she never talks about how to write a good one and help is limited. Attendance quiz pops up. Each lecture has reading material.

Lectures were quite boring, but made more interesting when she would go on a tangent about how much she hates ChatGPT and Grammarly. The subject matter is interesting enough, but not overly so. Phones are also strongly prohibited. Overall, not too difficult, but not too interesting.

Professor Swan is super passionate, and although somewhat disorganized not hard to understand. I found her lectures really fun, and she puts effort into trying to make the course accessible for students who might be taking it for a degree requirement. some effort is required in taking notes and paying attention but it's not a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Swan was very passionate about art history, however, it seemed as though her assignments were mere busy work rather than anything substantial. She claimed that we were not allowed to use grammarly because she wants writing to be "hard" for us when it was just an art history class. She also had random attendance checks bc ppl skipped.

prof. swan's lectures made me really sleepy. she does have a sense of humor and interesting content but she has lots of tangents. once she spent forty mins in lecture going on a tangent about grammarly and how it's prohibited. seems to care about her students. decent prof but would be better with a smaller group rather than a 200 person lecture.

one of the most boring class lectures that I have attended. Dreaded coming to class because it just felt like a complete waste of time. doesn't record lectures and slides on canvas are not helpful at all for reviewing. was not a good class, made me lose interest in art history. Has a strict no electronics policy unless you have accommodations
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She cares a lot about her students and does her best to make every lecture engaging + funny. There's a textbook but all of the info needed comes from her lectures. She's very passionate about what she teaches and really emphasizes the importance of what we're learning.

Dr. Swan is great. Although the pacing of the class was a little confusing, she is extremely knowledgeable and seems to genuinely care about you as a person, not just as a student. Class was also relatively easy with the only major writing assignment being the final. If you get the chance to take a class with her, you absolutely should!!

100% take this class if you have the chance. I had never taken an art history before, but Professor Swan is so caring and approachable that it quickly became one of my favorite classes. Doesn't believe in exam-based learning so all of our assessments were writing assignments. Don't miss out on taking a class with her if you have the chance.
It was the most boring, worst class ever. Felt like I did not learn anything, and depending on your section leader, grading is extremely harsh.

Western Art history is SO chill (and easy) w professor swan. the subsection leaders (grad students) grade everything, but swans lectures are genuinely interesting. I'm no fan of reading random facts off slides but she just has a good aura and is funny at times. workload is so light that I thought I read the assignments wrong. 100% recommend. Easy A

Swan is incredibly knowledgeable about her field, and her lectures are always interesting. She puts in a ton of effort into making the class engaging and fun for her students, and I have found none of the assignments to be horribly difficult. My only criticism would be occasional tangents in lectures, but the engaging curriculum makes up for it

Very interesting class and activities, but lots of content that wasn't always related to what we were learning. Professor Swan restructured the course after the midterm, and I found that helped a LOT. Lectures still occasionally rambled on and it was sometimes unclear what we really needed to know. Swan is incredibly knowledgeable about her field.
Self important with no industry experience at all. Full of himself, and a classic know it all.
A 4-star review? Sounds like he wrote it for himself.
“A self-important, and boring person—about the only thing you can learn from them is how to waste time.

This class truly feels like paying tuition for assignments. Class content equals assignment instructions: a one-page PPT to create your own, with no guidance on communication. Grading is rigidly focused on word count, page count, and formatting, while the actual content is worthless. A dog chained up on the street could replace this teacher.
Saw some of these reviews and thought no way he could actually be that bad until I got my first graded assignment back and saw I had 20% of my grade taken off for writing 98 words instead 100

I'd leave a 0 rating if I could. Somehow I think I came out of this class more confused and less prepared than I went in which is certainly a feat. I'd leave every class astonished that this guy is a real professor. His class feels like a fever dream.

Clive is most likely the most pompous professor I have ever had. Whether it was praising the AI-created image he made or a picture of Forest Park he took, he used weird metaphors to highlight his own importance over teaching the class valuable real-world skills. I genuinely hope WashU goes in a different direction regarding his tenure.
Such a shame this is a required class. Waste of time.

Muir is one of the worst professors I've ever had. He's condescending to students, his grading is extremely contradictory, and all of his assignments make no sense. He often kept us past the class time limit. He doesn't care about the substance of work at all, just that you follow his arbitrary guidelines. Everything in this class is meaningless.
A meaningless class, a useless teacher, a meaningless group assignment.

450A - internship

Very disappointing that professor don't understand half of the students enrolling in the course are in very intense finance internships and competing for a return offer. So many homework that it's hard to balance with the already heavy workload. He also said that he failed 50% student...very unhelpful and unbalanced

It was an interesting class, and more like a literature/communication class compared to other business classes.  The professor is very artistic/poetic and helped us develop a more artistic way to deliver narratives to others.

This professor's Business Communication course is disappointing, focusing excessively on writing format rather than content. Assignments must be exactly 300 words, with strict grading on format leading to 20%-30% deductions. Feedback on the actual substance is lacking, replaced by critiques on format, word count, and the number of paragraphs.
DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!!! HE IS SO BORING! HE CHANGE HIS MIND QUICKLY AND HE EVEN EXPECTED You to write something exactly 300 words! RUNNNNN!

he's chill, very kind and accessible outside of class. exams were a little rough compared to previous years but still doable, and the content + case studies have cool applications. had the tendency to tune out during his lectures to work on other EE classes..but lecture slides were great to review! good luck fellow ESE's!
Very reasonable homework and exams. I love his course. He's a really nice person and always does a lot for his students.

Easy grader, exam was too easy but as a student I like that. Light homework, enough example in lecture notes. The entire course was about some main theorems, if you don't want to go through the proof you can spend 3 hours on each homework(only 5 in whole semester) and skip all lectures, or you can follow Clark on class.

Super easy grading. The case studies were essentially a guaranteed 95+ as long as you did all of the work, and the homework was also very straightforward. Two exams, both were pretty light. Lecture was pretty boring so I stopped going and would just watch the recordings or read the slides for confusing topics.

Lectures are somewhat monotonous, but Professor Clark is great at answering questions in a small setting. Go to office hours if you're confused and he's really nice and helpful. Projects/case studies could use some more guidance and be prepared to self-teach all the coding part. I'd recommend watching 3Blue1Brown's linear algebra videos first.
Dr Sommers is an extremely kind professor who will go out of her way to help you succeed in her class. She makes standards very clear. She also has a strong passion for the subject and texts we read.

Dr. Sommers was absolutely amazing. Drama Queens is centered around interesting content and Sommers balances her role in daily class discussions well. She is super available and helpful regarding assignments, and it's very clear what you need to do to get a good grade. Would 100% take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (**I took Drama 1104 Shakespeare- it won't let me enter it) Dr. Sommers is wonderful! She cares a lot about her students and getting personal with them. She was by far my favorite professor this semester. She's always down to yap about Shakespeare with me, which I absolutely loved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Really ridiculously kind, cheerful, friendly, enthusiastic. Wont let me put it in but I took L13 exposition with her. Her exposition class was mind-numbingly boring in terms of content but I really enjoyed her energy and attitude. Easy workload and really wants to work with you.

Dr. Sommers is an amazing professor. I have taken two classes with her and loved them both - she always finds a way to make dense material fun and engaging and she is super approachable. Definitely take a class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Sommers is incredibly passionate about what she teaches and goes above and beyond to care for her students. She has fantastic ratings from all her university positions for a reason. Her feedback and grading are clear, and discussions feel lighthearted and enjoyable. I'd take another class with her in a heartbeat!

The words I have for this woman are invariably good! Dr. Sommers is an amazing professor who really does care about her students. Her classes are so interesting and disscussion is mandatory, but as long as you have done the readings you'll be fine. Assignments are relatively easy as well! For reference I had her for an Ampersand program.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Sommers is such a lovely person who is so passionate about literature! Her Shakespeare class was super enjoyable and she brought kindness and humor to class discussions. She genuinely cares about her students and will meet with you to discuss essays. If you are going to take a Shakespeare class, take it with Sommers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super sweet, lovely person. Her lectures were not the most engaging I have ever had, but she also didn't grade too harshly and was pretty accommodating whenever I needed something. Passionate about her subject!

Dr. Sommers' class was amazing! Her grading on papers and things is on the tougher side, but definitely fair. Like most literature classes, her class was entirely discussion based. She was super engaging and made class very interesting and enjoyable. Some readings were a little on the long side, but most everything else was very manageable.

For CWP 1501: Ampersand Ireland

Dr. Clark was an amazing professor! The class is discussion-based, so it's important that you do the readings. The classes are always very engaging, and Dr. Clark clearly cares about the ideas/perspective of every student. I learned a lot and really enjoyed myself.
Wonderful professor and person!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Protect this man at all costs. He is such a wonderful professor and person. If you need to take Argumentation, make sure it is with him. The class is a very low commitment, just a few workshops and essays during the semester, which he grades generously as long as you put effort into it.
Loved Modern Lit with Dr. Clark, he is great at facilitating discussion and cares about his students.
He's the goat he makes me wanna take the rest of his classes

This professor was the best college writing professor ever! The way he engages with the class and encourages participation both in class and on writing assignments! Definitively learned a lot about Irish culture and writing! Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor. He clearly has an investment in each student and is a great teacher.
Absolute dog. One of the nicest professors I've had at WashU. Hydrology is very hard but she makes it worth.

This is one of those classes that completely changes how you see the world. Homeworks are applications of topics covered in the lectures. Dr. Masteller is really enthusiastic about the topics and makes lectures interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The assignments are not indicative of the lectures. I thought that the lectures would help me understand the assignments, but even attending the TA's office hours did not help enough. An extremely tough grader as well and is sometimes not explicit about what is wanted for assignments and exams. I would not take this class unless necessary.

Dr. Clouser's class is discussion based and she encourage the students to lead the discussion, which improve our speaking skill and confidence. The readings she assigned are very inspiring. Her grading is pretty clear and easy as long as you complete what she told you to do. The deadlines for many assignments are also really flexible.
Best intro class I have ever had, although the information dragged sometimes Rebecca always made it enjoyable and welcoming

Rebecca is such a great professor!! She has a great sense of humor and makes class really entertaining. It was a very small class so we all got to know each other very well and had a lot of fun together. Highly recommend taking this class as a freshman, it's so easy and interesting. Will definitely be taking a class from her in the future.

Rebecca was such a nice teacher to have, it kind of gave the feel of a high school class. You got to know the people in your class really well and it was not stressful. Lots of group projects and graded usually on completion. 100% recommend as a first year course, eases you into the havoc of college

Intro to Human Geography with Dr. Clouser was a lot of fun, some sections of the lectures/textbook are more boring than others but human geography really is her life's work/passion and it shows. Not necessary to read the digital textbook because she'll do a lecture overview of each reading in class, easy grader for projects and writing.
Class and lectures were very boring and confusing. Take it if you want an easy A

Professor Cowsik has achieved a lot in his time as a scholar and honestly has better things to be doing than teaching an intro physics course. The class is all graded off homework and two easy to complete projects. He's a chill and caring guy who will extend deadlines if you just ask.

Professor Cowsik was super intelligent and basically an Einstein of his field; it made me sad that most people in the class were not interested by astronomy at all but he really tried to make it as good as it could be. Soft speaker so try to sit more up front; A very kind, sweet, brilliant guy. 
8.5/10

Man is too smart to be teaching an intro solar systems class. People stopped showing up to lecture which I felt bad about, but he's still a great guy. Easy class, he made it as interesting as he could. Sometimes it showed that he was smarter than everyone in the room which made it hard to explain some basic topics.

Professor Cowsik is a truly accomplished genius (look up his Wikipedia) that you can learn a lot from and is chill. His notes are difficult to read, and you always don't know what is going on in the class. All tests are take home, which are slight extensions of the weekly homework sets. You have to fumble hard to not get an A in the class.

Professor Cowsik is very passionate about his subject, but speaks softly and is difficult to hear even with a mic and small classroom. His handwritten notes are difficult to read as well. Graded on homework only, once per week. Midterm and Final are the same as HW but a little longer, all take-home. Easy class with a bit of Physics background.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nobody went to the lectures, and the TA gave the homework assignments. The midterms and the final are taken home, so that makes it easier. Great professor, super understanding

Orgo lab is really not supposed to be a lecture class. It is graded sometimes harshly but Dr. de la Cruz really does want her students to be successful. She gives opportunities for extra credit and generally orgo lab is 100x better than gen chem lab like seriously very chill as long as you do the prep work.

labs graded fairly easily. quizzes are SO hard. you have to memorize the procedure almost to do well. labs themselves are easy and orgo lab is way more chill than gen chem. de la cruz is ok and decently helpful but is cryptic for the problem sets that are UNDROPPABLE

The lectures help you answer the problem sets. Labs are often graded leniently, although the quizzes are unreasonably hard (often received 1 or 2 out of 5). Seems caring towards students, although I have never interacted with her one-on-one. I do wish more guidance was provided in lab and clearer rubrics were given. Due dates were consistent.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things
