reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. Like actually so bad

Cruz is a sweet & humorous person, but she is a horrible orgo lab prof. She jokes about us struggling in orgo and never gives direct answers to simple questions during recitation. I hate to hate her since she's so warm in person, but I can barely understand her cryptic hints during recitation-- & it's not even bc of her accent. She's just confusing
L teacher
Horrible teacher.
Simply incompetent. The most unorganized class I have taken at WashU.
Very kind and caring instructor

Dr. de la Cruz really cares about her students and goes out of her way to be accessible to students. That being said, she is not clear with her grading criteria and is not very organized which was frustrating. The best way to get through the class is to regularly go to office hours to clear up anything that's confusing.

This professor has not been clear all semester and is really condescending. Also her English is horrible. I have attempted to explain to her my situation with regard to the practice sets and she doesn't even know her own assignment schedule--claiming the problem set was due way after it actually was. Big waste of time.
One of the best professors I had at WashU! Always happy to help and genuinely interested in what he's teaching!
Best professor ever. No exams. Weekly Assignments. 3 Skips

The class was well-taught. Compared to some of the other CSE coursework I've taken, I learned more in this class with the hands-on assignments. Some of them can be time-consuming, but there are lots of office hours / Cosgrove is always there to help.
Simply my favorite. A must take professor

I like this class because your grade depends on how much work you put in and it's a guranteed A. Cosgrove is super passionate during lecture and always come in with a great attitude. I do think there are way too many assignments. People say this class is easy, but I wouldn't say it's easy unless they're using AI on every Assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: CS Dpt Goat should be a 5.0. Class goes over fairly challenging topics for a 200 level, but no exams make it easy to get a good grade. Incredible lectures, Prof cosgrove cares more than any prof I've had about his students. 131 is still based off his projects and assignments, as no other prof has been able to make better ones. take his class.

This class is taught through video lectures of a random UW professor. Cosgrove's lectures add nothing & often devolve into unstructured rambling. The only thing he does add is more homework, claiming this approach reflects his “high expectations” of WashU students, yet there's little evidence of the same standards for his own work. Waste of time.

The assignments are very easy and you actually learn a lot of applicable skills. His lecture are very free-style and conversational, sometimes feels like he doesn't really follow a topic. But overall great professor.
Engaging lectures and really cared about his students learning and succeeding. We love Prof. Cosgrove!

Best professor in the CS department that I've had so far. Gives great mini-lectures at the start of each class and does everything he can to make the course as engaging as possible. Dennis is a very caring and fun person. Lots of assignments, but they're all relatively easy and build up to a deeper understanding of parallel programming. We stan.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had and makes all of his "lectures" as enjoyable as possible with jokes. The assignments aren't bad and if you get stuck there are plenty of TA's outside of class everyday who are all superb themselves. There isn't a single reason you shouldn't take his class

Prof. Cosgrove is genuinely the best CS professor this school has to offer. This class is actually perfect. Prof. Cosgrove is caring and genuine, the TAs know what they are doing, the assignments build on one another very well and are relatively easy if you keep up with the class. I hope that when I declare my CS major I get this man as my advisor.
Breaks concepts down in a way that is easy to grasp, his use of metaphors is unmatched

Prof Cosgrove is one of those professors who makes WashU what it is. Your grade is based on the completion of a number of coding tasks (all of which have the unit tests provided). He cares about you as a student and human. Don't be deterred if the first 2 weeks are hard, it gets better. JUST TAKE A CLASS FROM THIS AMAZING MAN ALREADY!!

One of the few CS professors here that you can tell truly cares about the stuff he teaches. Genuinely enthusiastic about the course. Had actual discussions and took feedback from students. 

231S is also the best CS course. Easy yet informative. Take it if you can.

Professor Cosgrove really cares about his students and you can tell he is passionate about teaching as well as constantly improving his course material. Labs and studios are relatively easy and instructions are well-documented. He is also very accessible and is willing to spend lots of time even outside of class time.
Terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Treats teaching like he's teaching computers. Does not have any regard for student welfare or quality of life in his class, and his system is fundamentally flawed.

One of the most enthusiastic and engaging professors I've had for CS at WashU. This class is really interesting and Cosgrove is so dedicated to his students -- he's even willing to hop on Zoom to help provide advice on assignments in the evening. Overall, such a nice, understanding, and helpful professor. Would love to take more classes with him.

This professor is an actual gem within the CS department- smart and caring. He's never afraid to break down the material in an understandable way, or try to put it in a way for you to understand. His class was very difficult when I took it because it was a very new course, but I learned a lot and I found it 100% worth it. Get ready to work.

Cosgrove is a great professor and a great person - he genuinely cares about the success of the students and, for example, will actively modify course structures to accommodate the needs of the students. But he's also a bit awkward, and can struggle when it comes to handling individual student disciple/extra-academic issues.

really cares about students understanding the material and will go over it with you as many times as it takes for you to get it. Very nice and caring and respectful. Easy class overall and you learned about as much as you put into this class. The class was being taught for the first time so understandably there were many flaws
He really goes out of his way to help students and obviously puts in tons of work to build the programs needed for the class. The best CS professor I've had at WashU.

Professor Cosgrove obviously cares a lot about the course he teaches and the students in it. He often goes out of his way to help students so that the course would be accessible to everyone. CSE231 is a new class as of fall 2016, so there are some polishing to do further on, but I would say he is the best professor I have had so far.
Unorganized, and wants you to know information she didn't teach

I think that Professor Crain absolutely knows her stuff, has some great examples of how the law works, and brings a practical eye to what she teaches, but at the same time, her classes feel like a sort of soupy mess and the casebook that she assigns is bewilderingly disorganized. Very mixed feelings.
Professor Crain is terrific. Her Labor Law class was incredible.

Professor Crain is BY FAR the best professor I have had in the Law School.  There is an immense value in going to class, where she doesn't just walk through the facts and holding of a case (unlike so many other classes).  She is an extremely prominent professor in Labor / Employment Law, and it was a real honor to honestly learn labor law from her.

Craig is the best professor I've had here at WashU. I had him for Bio4525, and you can tell that he's someone who truly cares about his students and is passionate about the course material. He's a very engaging lecturer and fosters a collaborative teaching environment. We sat in groups of ~6 to figure out problems and give each other feedback.

Dr. Smith's BIO 4525 Structural Bioinformatics of Proteins Writing Intensive was a great class and he was a great professor! All of the content and expectations were very clear and he walked us through the process of writing our papers. He is not only super helpful with class but a great mentor overall!

I took Bio4525 with Dr. Smith. He teaches this class with so much enthusiasm which made the class exciting and engaging. He took the time to get to know each one of us on a personal level and fostered a really friendly community within the classroom. 
This class taught me to write scientifically and gave me skills I will use in my research career.

Craig is AMAZING! I took his Protein Informatics advanced lab and can not recommend it enough. He is the most caring professor and went above and beyond in the course. All of the work you do is during class time.

Prof Smith is really funny and walks through each lab clearly so everyone understands. However, I think his lab AI does all the grading for the lab reports, so I found that the grading was weird/random. I would get points off for calculations where my friends would not get points off even when they used the same equations and got the same numbers.

I was generally interested to learn biology, but Craig Smith made enjoying learning it so difficult. I was often one of the last people to finish, and he would make you feel dumb for this. His lab lectures were very poorly executed and not well explainedwhich is typical for freshman weed-out classes at WashU. Disparaging, intimidating, and awful.

Dr. Smith might pause sometimes in class, but he's funny and you can tell he cares about his students learning the material. I took his UCollege Biochem class and you needed to study for his tests, but if you did, you would do fine.
Really confusing lectures that often contain mistakes and are very hard to understand. I don't understand the course material at all.
Great professor! Great class!
Dr. Smith is a great professor. He really cares about his students. He's funny and good at explaining things. He makes biology make sense.

His lectures are extremely dry, and he has an speech impediment (slurring, a slight stutter) that makes him hard to understand. Though I'm sure he's a nice guy,  I absolutely would not recommend taking a class with him.

Dr. Smith is hands down my favorite professor ever at WUSTL! He plays awesome music in lab, he's super helpful and caring, and he's an amazing teacher. One of the nicest people I've ever met. Jokes around with students and makes the lab section something to look forward to weekly! I can't recommend his subsection enough!

Cruz is exceptional at teaching biochem especially in 3 hour chunks. He is so sweet, kind, bubbly and passionate about biochem. It is a lot of content, but Cruz is able to teach it very well. You just need to memorize literally everything and you will ace all the exams.
Professor Cruz is very funny, kind, and fair.
He's a funny guy, does his job well, sets clear expectations.

Prof Cruz is such a silly and fun prof. Lectures are long, but he does his best to give breaks and add in his repertoire of dad jokes. Genuinely cares about students' success and clearly enjoys teaching biochem.

He cares about individuals but not really about learning tbh. He expects you to know a lot of material coming in and doesn't have any resources to facilitate learning outside of lectures. As long as you can memorize about 150 slides of material per exam and know most of the content before taking the class, you should do well.
Awesome professor with very clear expectations and fair tests. Enjoyed this course very much.
Made bio lab enjoyable and feel like a breeze! Really good at explaining concepts and answering questions in a way that makes sense to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Cruz is engaging, has funny examples for biochemical mechanisms and makes UCollege Biochem interesting. The class is a LOT of work because it's memorization heavy, but the tests are very similar year to year. Tests also have extra credit, so it's easy to do well. No "-" grades either. Also a great lab professor for 2960, made lab fun

Dr. Cruz is a very knowledgeable and kind professor. Lectures are long but the material is presented in a very clear manner. Biochemistry is not an easy subject, but Dr. Cruz does a great job of breaking down the topics so it does seem more manageable. The material is also very helpful if you are planning to take the MCAT.

All memorization. Lectures were boring, so I'd just memorize everything before the exam. Extremely dense (only had 2 exams, so the tests were quite stressful) but this class is not trying to trick you like the rest of the science classes do. No higher-order thinking involved, but the most I've ever studied for a class. Lots of work, but not tricky.

Biochemistry is a difficult subject  Lectures can be confusing but he is more than willing to clarify. His exams are pretty long and difficult but if the concepts are well understood before hand it is less challenging.

Dr. Cruz is a nice guy. However, his teaching abilities are subpar. All he does is go over 50+ slides without really explaining the material. Tests are difficult to impossible unless you are a wiz at memorizing information.

This is one of the worst professors I have ever had. His lectures are terrible, very confusing, and not well organized. He doesn't post the slides until 45 min before class and doesn't really "teach". He just talks the whole time even if students are complete lost. He is super hard to get ahold of, even taking a week to respond to email.
Helpful and friendly.  Good course (Biochemistry).
He sucks at lecturing hardcore... yea he was awesome in bio lab, but he cannot teach.
He explains the lab very well and helps a lot in the lab part. He's a very energetic person and plays Hawaiian music in class. The labs are easy but he makes the labs even easier.
Really laid-back and tries to make learning the material enjoyable.  Very willing to help out and answer questions.  I hated Chem. Lab... but loved going to Bio lab.
Not helpful, not friendly, and not clear when explaining things. Completely dismisses you if you have a question about the lab write-up.
No Comments
Dr. Cruz is a great lab instructor.

Craig Anderson is a very understanding professor and will never overwhelm you with an unreasonable workload. There were a couple "pop" quizzes throughout the course on reading material, but they are usually only 2-3 questions and multiple choice - a grade booster. I would recommend his marketing class,  and the midterm/final tests were not harsh.

Overall nice professor, I've had a solid experience in his MKT 370 class. Pop quizzes on assigned readings are VERY frequent (almost every other lecture, but easy if you read, just annoying). Homework assignments are mostly just 1-page papers on cases, which are graded fairly. Easy class, but the content is honestly kinda bland.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really great and kind professor; you can tell he's open to feedback and making sure students learn and understand. Lectures are a tossup between being really engaging and interesting or boring depending on the day, but he gives plenty of time and feedback for any assignments so if you regularly attend class, you'll do fine.
nice guy. expert. easy going but has appropriate expectations.

He's obviously a very smart guy, and offers a lot of humorous/interesting anecdotes from his life. The biggest problem is more with the class itself and the material. In short, he's a good professor (though a pretty hard grader especially on papers) but the class itself could be improved.

Crisp is not a bad teacher at all. He tries to keep things interesting, tries to tell jokes.  The problem is that the curriculum for Comparative Politics is terrible, as is the textbook.  When dealing with such vague and useless material, no one can teach well.  He's really not "mean" nor "boring".

Although it is clear that he himself knows the material very well, is probably a good researcher and seems like a nice enough guy, he was never meant to be a teacher. His biggest flaw is that what he lectures is a different topic to what is on the powerpoint (which is also overly convoluted), so it's impossible to write anything down. Confusing!

Honestly, he wasn't the greatest teacher ever, but if you do the readings ( approx 20-30 pages due per class) and study the slides after class, it's a very easy A. I missed a lot of classes, but since most classes were focused on the reading, I didn't have too much trouble.

Do not take a class with Crisp.  The workload in comparative politics was more work than I have done in any poly sci class and I am a senior, poly sci major.  Not only is it work intensive, but the work is not interesting.  Heavy reading too.  Lectures are boring and discussion sections pointless.  Crisp is really really really bad.
Very interesting if you're a polisci major. Lets lectures be dominated by student questions. Though he comes across as a huge jerk, he is very approachable outside of class.
No Comments

Basically the biggest jerk alive.  He wouldn't give me an extension on a Monday test after I had just gotten mono that weekend even with the shs head physicians note.  Besides being an ass his lectures were boring as well that the course materials.  Dont take this class

This class was terrible.  He assigns way too much reading and one of the course books was not available thru the bookstore until half way thru the semester.  He always made a power point presentation but never put it up long enough for people to actually write down what it said.  Very bad professor.

Very heavy reading for an intro class. Crisp is interesting enough and intelligent. But he isn't the best teacher in the world. If you're just taking a political science class for fun, avoid this one. If you're majoring in it, then go for it. The content is useful for future courses. Plus Crisp has a good Polsci mind and is respected in the field.
awful

Doesn't teach very well, and gives very vague explanations.  Is practically worthless if you meet with him for help.  Creates tons of slides, skips through most of them, and keeps the worthless ones up for too long.

Worst Wash U class I have taken so far. Course description very misleading. This class is all about rational choice b.s. A lot of work for an intro class. Crisp obviously had no interest in teaching and had TA's do everything. Only cares about his research. Thank god the TA's graded.
No Comments
No Comments
Lots of group projects and presentations, but she's a very generous grader. Overall great!

This class was honestly super chill, which I appreciated. We also got a lot of practice with listening and speaking, which I hadn't had a lot of practice with before. Just put in effort on the assessments (papers and projects), and you will be totally fine. Dr. Cunill is the sweetest!
Professor Cunill is very kind and her classes are discussion-based. I enjoyed taking Spanish with her and would do it again!

I haven't had a single Spanish professor that I haven't liked and that remained true after taking Professor Cunill's class (302). She does a great job facilitating conversation and shows that she cares about her students. My conversation skills greatly improved thanks to her and this class so I would strongly recommend taking a class of hers.

[Rating for SPAN 302] Such small class size (10 people) that class discussions are very chill. Discussion topics/questions are interesting. Readings/videos are interesting too. She doesn't really correct grammar, which is something I wished she did more often. Nice class overall.

Cunill has been my favorite Spanish dept faculty. She is easy to understand, super flexible, and gives great feedback in order to help you improve. She knows some of what 303 assigns is busy work and doesn't really care if you don't do it. She can be a bit monotone but I love her

Profe Cunill came up with really interesting topics and facilitated a variety of lecture, group discussion, and media content. There was a significant amount of group projects, homework, and quizzes, but it was definitely manageable. She covered a variety of social sciences, from law to psych to public health. Overall, a solid choice!

Prof. Cunill was one of the better Spanish professors I have had. She was easy to understand when speaking. Participation was encouraged and she was considerate enough so that I felt encouraged and free to participate rather than pressured to. The grading system was not 100% clear, but grades were not strenuous anyway.

Prof Cunill is wonderful! She is so sweet and cares a lot about her students. 355 was extremely well organized and her expectations are very clear. If you do the work, you will do well. Could not recommend this class more highly!

This was my second class with Cunill, and she didn't fail to impress. If you participate in class you'll do just fine in this class. The papers seemed to be mostly graded according to grammar (but this was her first year teaching 341 coming from only teaching 308 which is more grammar-y). Also the discussions in class were often quite interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her lectures are so chill they're almost conversational. Although essays are done independently, she gives a lot of good ideas for theses so as long as you listen and take notes when she discusses the readings, you could practically create a paper out of what you've already been told. Good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She's a great teacher, so easy to understand, and an easy grader. She really just wants you to succeed and be interested in what you're learning about. The class is really interactive and honestly just fun.
Loved the class, inspired me to study in Madrid this summer. Easy but good professor, gives great feedback and incredibly relaxed and helpful about any issues. Absolutely take Prof Cunill if you can.

Cuillé is a very kind person who, given the relatively small seating capacity of his courses, cares about the individual performance and health of his students. I found this course to be easier than my AP French class in high school, but this course can still be intellectually stimulating if you try to participate. Exams are curved generously.

Easy grader - let us do corrections on papers, quizzes, and exams. Very friendly and accessible prof. Class ranged from very boring to mildly interesting. Gave a decent amount of reading and grammar exercises, but you could get away with not doing most of it. Overall nice professor, class was an easy A.

Professor Cuille is great. His syllabus and instructions for assignments are very clear. He also includes short presentation activites in pairs in addition to his discussions. He also has some funny moments where he speaks French randomly and makes some lighthearted jokes.
favorite professor at washu. you can literally revise your essays to get higher grades. he really cares for the mental health of students and wants every student to succeed.

As a Comp Lit Class expect to do some reading. He was very knowledgeable about the texts, very keen eye. As a seminar class, he guided the discussion quite a bit, having us focus on certain aspects of text, compared to more free form discussion that I've had in previous classes. An enjoyable, stimulating class.

What a perfect way to end my undergraduate career! Cuille was hilarious and charming. Knew a lot about French culture (actually being from France probably helped) and it was a pretty chill atmosphere. Also learned a lot.

Dr CuillÃ© stands out as one of the best professors i have had in my time at Wash U. From professors I have had in PNP, IHP, and the pre-med requirements, he is one of the best. He teaches a great literary modernites course. Wash U would be hard pressed to find a better professor to lead such an in-depth and intellectual course.

Wonderful professor! One of my absolute favorite classes of my undergraduate career. He is personable, flexible, extremely knowledgeable, and one learns much in his class. Wish I could take more classes with him - the passion and learning in the classroom is wonderful.
I've taken both French and literature classes with this professor and I must say that he teaches both fields very well. His lectures and engaging and in depth. He is also very accesible and helpful,
Excellent instructor. He cares about his students and tailors class time based upon their interests. I am not a Humanities major but I started taking literature classes because of his class.

Course on Literature & War Extremely knowledgeable professor who has a passion for the subject matter that is contagious.  He also very mirthful and makes class time go by quickly, using a multimedia approach.
Great teacher!! My passion for French has grown considerably because of him. So helpful, and very nice. Grades easy.
great prof. not very clear but very entertaining, so the class goes by very quickly. grades easy, always willing to help. a lot easier to understand when he speaks French rather than English

T and T class on emergence of modern identity.  Very interesting class.  Prof. does have trouble at times expressing his ideas but don't let it fool you is very smart and well versed.  Grading is fair to easy.  Great guy solid prof

I take my words back. Prof Cuille indeed has trouble conveying his ideas because of his broken English. Though extremely amiable and approachable, Prof Cuille has a poorly organized course plan and  sometimes comes to class poorly prepared.

Took a humanities course Prof. Cuille should not have been teaching--he was unclear and poorly versed in the subject matter much of the time.  He also had unrealistic expectations for students--kept adding to the workload at the last minute, for example mandatory "makeup class" during finals?!  Redeeming factor: a VERY easy A.

Freshman Seminar on the Ideology of Speed. Very interesting class with relevant topics at first, but began to lose focus once we got out of the defined topic of futurism. Very multimedia. I liked this class even though most didn't. He gave us a book to read that turned out to be ****graphic; he hadn't read it before assigning it. Interesting.

Took a humanity class with him and have to say he is fantastic. Although he struggles a bit with his English because he is from France, he presents the difficult material with thoughtful clarity and complete patience. He is knowledgable in many areas like philosophy, history and western literature. He is a fair grader and your hard work will pay of
good class, good teacher

Prof seemed nice, but he doesn't grade your papers/projects. Your grade depends on how nit-picky your TA is. Long lectures with interesting topics, but the small group discussions with the TAs can feel dragged out at times. Lots of reading, but it's interesting stuff. None of it really matters though if you have a harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I learned a lot in this class, but not from the professor. He assigned some extremely interesting readings, but he never explained what we were supposed to take away from them or organized the lectures well. We were always discussing the readings a few lectures after we actually did them, which was confusing. Also, the grading criteria was unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: David is an amazing lecturer and a leading scholar in sociology. It is so cool being taught by an expert like him. Soc2020 was so interesting and we grappled with some difficult concepts, but his lectures clarified all concepts. He facilitates tons of class discussion and genuinely cares about his students. I cannot recommend him enough.

David is so caring about students and is always willing to meet. He is a genius, a top scholar in the field. However, the class is very theoretical and lacks a clear structure. His lectures are hard to follow and often boring. Lots of difficult readings. It was definitely a challenging course, but the grading was pretty kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Really great professor but very theoretical and hard to follow sometimes. Asking questions and demonstrating engagement are key. A lot of reading and you have to do it or you will be confused in class and the papers will be hard to write. Very doable papers although vague grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took Order and Change in Society as my first intro to Sociology course and Dr. Cunningham did a great job with it. He's enthusiastic about sociology and teaching and it really shows in class. His "lectures" are more in the style of a facilitated discussion and he encourages participation. If you do the reading and show up, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: difficult and mean！

Professor Cuny is knowledgeable, but extremely rude and condescending. His class revolves around either you agreeing or disagreeing with his opinion, and much of your grade is determined by group projects and non-constructive feedback. Overly stressful class with very little actually learned, would definitely, definitely NOT recommend.
Mean af and always mumbling with no ppl could understand what he is talking about in the whole course.

Do you know what "Shi" is? If you don't know, take his class. I never saw a rude and sarcastic professor like him before. He is just like trying to imitate the style of classes from Ivy school, but he is a poor and unskilled imitator. He has a high-level educational history, HOWEVER, THAT DOES NOT MEAN HE ALSO HAVE A HIGH-LEVEL TEACHING SKILL.
if 528 is not a requirements course nobody gonna enroll

Pros: 
-seems like a nice enough professor, a bit sarcastic but that didn't bother me.

Cons: 
-course grade depends on some participation points and the final
-cold calls
-video lectures do not help at all with the timed final
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to experience a class where the final exam determines your grade for the entire semester, then this class would be a good experience.

His way or the highway, even if they both are valid. You will be ridiculed in front of the class and learn nothing from it. He is very smart, but this class doesn't teach you anything beyond just using historical information to predict the future. You are not taught to analyze businesses beyond what is common knowledge. Grading depends on mood.
Awful personality
Not a nice guy.
Oh, someone (may not Cuny himself) reported my previous comment and made it invisible. Enjoy your class with him lmao.
He is very strict and any small mistake will be scolded if he finds it. I believe I would have given him a 1 if I hadn't seen my letter grade.
I personally thinks very highly of professor Cuny. He is very analytical when viewing investments and very "pleasantly unagreeable" in nature. Much recommended if you want to learn real stuff.
Professor Cuny is the best professor I have ever met in Olin.
We will never take this course again.

The grading criteria is blurry, you would not know how he gives the participation mark, and it is huge in the total mark. Your GPA can be screwed in some way you do not understand. Professor Cuny is good at spotting calculation mistakes and is quite knowledgeable. However, he is harsh and would not let anyone challenge his authority in class.
Had a hard time understanding his lecture. Cool clothing style though.
very strict on details for industry investment presentation. Good knowledge on modeling and industry insight.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great professor- doesn't care about the petty things and makes it easy to pass but challenging to high pass. Keeps the focus on the learning.

Very poor professor especially for an MBA program with students with work experience.  He's incapable of asking clear and concise questions.  During exams there is often a line of 5-7 students at the front of class waiting to ask him questions.  He seems more focused on asking riddles that teaching students how to model and solve finance problems.
Good teacher. Good guy.
Great professor and an incredibly knowledgeable guy educated at both cal tech and stanford. The material is challenging, but the class has a hefty curve.

I took Fin 340 and FIN 441 with him but I never understood his notes/class. I had to borrow notes from other professor's section to study for the exams.He is a great guy though and very knowledgeable of the subject he is teaching

Cuny is easy, clear, and hilarious in class. However, I feel like the class was almost too easy. I feel like I could have learned a lot more from an intro corp. finance course, and I know some of the other professors who teach this course do a bit more. Also, love the hawaiian shirts and orange soda.

Charles is one of the greatest professors at Olin.  He's incredibly supportive and generous, and he really cares about students' personal, professional development.  If you are interested in finance, his understanding of the material is mind-blowing.   If you're not, he can still make the material engaging for you.
Hard and challenging material, but not hard to get an A. No textbook. Wears cool clothes.
Cuny is a fantastic professor.  He is extremely helpful outside of class, and covers all important material in great detail.  He is the best finance professor I have had so far.
No Comments
Mind-numblingly boring - not recommended for those who get little sleep to begin with. But the curve is generous.

I actually ended up really liking this class.  I learned a lot and it really came together in the end.  The cases can be a lot of work, so make sure to start them early.  When you finish them and realize you're right, it's seriously satisfying, though.  Also, he has a generous curve at the end and is helpful when contacted through email.

cynthia is very sweet, but do get ready to read. the class's discussion flow is heavily based on who is in your class so pls read and talk it makes all the difference. to study for exams LOOK AT HER SLIDES AND TAKE NOTES, she makes the reading digestible( you could bs some) most of the key questions she ask on exams she mentions in class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is such a kind professor. She creates such a welcoming space for students. The class is mostly discussion-based and there is a lot of reading each week, but it's an easy A if you do all the reading (at least before the exams).

HORRIBLE PROFESSOR RUN AWAY! She doesn't like opinions that aren't in alignment with hers, be ready to be judged and your grades will reflect it. Instead of spending time on vivid discussions that are related to WGSS, she will tear your opinion apart.
Lots of reading and fun discussions in class. Very chill and very accomodating as long as you communicate.

Prof. Barounis was very receptive to some health issues that I had this semester, so big points to her on that. Otherwise, her lectures were entertaining and spawned good discussions. Readings could vary, but I would say they are mostly pretty short.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is seminar based and is very dependent on the quality of the contributions made by your peers. I was lucky to has a class of many smart and caring peers, who moved the discussion along well. Understandably, the professor only gives minimal political and social commentary in seminars, but implicitly does so when picking our readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class revolves around the readings that you do, which there is way too much of. Often times we only cover half of the readings that we do. Discussion is largely based on the quality of your peers. The professor's political leniencies are also very obvious (natural for WGSS). Rare closed-book intro WGSS professor, so make sure to read up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Barounis is a wonderful person and instructor. She was incredibly forgiving with extensions so don't be afraid to ask her for them. This course has a lot of tough material but she was always able to break it down for students and get us to actually talk about it.

Dr. Barounis is a really amazing person and professor. I've taken two classes with her, Intro and Bodies out of Bounds: Feminist and Queer Disability Studies (favorite class I've taken. It's a must). She's incredibly understanding about extenuating circumstances when it comes to extensions and she really cares about her students

This class is fantastic! Quite a bit of reading, but stay mostly on top of it and you should have no issues. Prof Barounis generally reviews the main points of the readings very well, so you can get away with skimming sometimes. She is such a wonderful professor - very caring and considerate, and she definitely knows her stuff! Exams are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: very good class. be prepared for a LOT of reading. also for exams u need to memorize all of the authors and match them with the readings which is not the best method if you dont remember which excerpt was from which, but dont say I did not warn u. pretty understanding professor tho and accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I like her intro class! It is reading-heavy but her lecture is very helpful in understanding those readings. She is also very understanding of deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I really liked her intro class.  It is very methodical. You will get out what you put in.

She is very bad at facilitating conversations. Classes were unstructured and it was hard to learn the main idea of each reading. We always got distracted on side topics or stupid line of argument. That said, it is an amazing class! If you can't take it with another professor, take it anyways. The class is good if you have smart classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She made it very hard; dogmatic and tough. Other sections had open book exams whereas we had to remember ALL the readings for short response questions, plus an impromptu essay for the final. Class discussion were not facilitated well, basically everyone talked about their own opinions about the reading. I thought it would be so interesting, sad.

Ma is very kind and CSE514 ended up very easy. I found her lectures incredibly boring though. The content itself is actually pretty interesting and not too hard - I just think she presents it in the wrong way. Ultimately, I think this class could benefit from a different teaching style other than lecture-based but still would recommend.
Best professor I've had in this university. Lectures are clear and fun. Uses Kahoot for lecturing so it could be more interactive. Truly cares about students.

Easiest upper-level class ever. You will get out as much as you put in. Cynthia is an angel and really puts a lot of effort into producing good materials for her class. The most annoying thing was when Cynthia would start lecturing and I couldn't hear her because other students in the lecture hall were blatantly talking loudly with no consideration

She taught me data mining in the spring of 2024 and has instilled a deep passion for ML modeling since then. Although I didn't get an A, the seed she has instilled helped me decide into pursuing and furthering my studies in ML application. Now leading a ML team, I still come to her during her office hours to talk and discuss. SHE IS AWESOME :D
Explains stuff super well. Cares about the subject

Professor Ma has been one of my favorite CSE professors at WashU due to the Kahoot lecture style ensuring that everyone understands the content before proceeding. The course has a lot of callbacks/preparation for CSE417T, so it will be easier if you have taken/good to prepare for that class. Feedback on written assignments is somewhat slow.

Amazing! The entire CS department should take notes on how to teach a class. Well-planned and engaging lectures. Clearly defined assignment requirements. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit. Fair exams that mirror actual activities from class and homework. I just can't do it justice with words. Take this class. Thank you, Professor Ma!

Prof Ma did an awesome job with Data Mining. She was super kind, explained the content well, and gave lots of opportunities for extra credit throughout the semester. She also incorporated Kahoot into lectures, which was fun and increased student engagement. Other CS profs at WashU should take notes from her on how to teach a class properly.

The HW and Exams that she designed contained frequent errors and ill-defined parameters.  Resultantly,I frequently had to seek clarification via email.  Her response was often VERY delayed.  For example,a parameter wen needed in a HW was temperature dependent.  It took her 4 days to respond. Such carelessness and and non-responsiveness was typical.

Lectures were very helpful. Her notes are very organized. She talks pretty fast, but to some extend that gives the class more energy(which I appreciate since thermo is a pretty boring topic). Learned a lot of Matlab from this class too, didn't anticipate it. The class is by no means easy, and it requires a lot of work. But it was very rewarding.
Dr. Lo is really enthusiastic about teaching and her concern for students learning shines through.

I agree with the previous comment. The class is boring and it's hard, but Lo is always willing to help. You can tell she's passionate about the material and tries really hard to get us excited about it too.
Class is unbelievably boring but she really does try to make things interesting.  She's ALWAYS available to answer questions and tries to be fair with her grading.

All you have to do is show up to class pretty much and you'll get an A. If you miss more than two classes, you can do extra credit up to three times to make it back. His classes are always interesting and will do like meditation or stretching days if students are feeling stressed. Easy A class, would recommend.

intro to contemp dance-very easy A. david very passionate. u lowk just dance and do weird stuff for like half of class. the other half he talks. he talks a lot. i was tired every class. but fun and no homework no final.

I loved this course with Professor Marchant so much! If you have any interest in dance, take this course. The professor is so encouraging and makes everyone feel comfortable at the skill level they are at. He promotes an environment where you can learn about modern dance history and explore your body's dance style without judgment.

He's a really cool guy, and makes the class super accessible to non-dancers.  Definitely go in with an open mind, some of the things he says and has you do are a little bit out there, but if you let go of your inhibitions, you get a lot out of the class.  Attendance is mandatory, otherwise, a very easy A, would definitely recommend.

As long as you come to class and appear engaged, this class is an easy A. Marchant is a fantastic person and always interesting. The class may seem a little weird at first but I absolutely loved hearing him explain his perspectives on dance and life. I am not a dancer at all, but I never felt self-conscious.
David is a wonderful dancer and human being. His class is all about exploration and grades you on your personal effort (meaning most students get high marks). I highly recommend this class!

If you really invest yourself in the class and the dance performances on campus, you'll definitely grow to appreciate and understand his unique worldview. A fantastic dancer and a helpful, wonderful teacher. I never once felt self-conscious - he sees beauty and potential in every dancer. Did not play favorites, at least not in our class.

awesome. really laid back.. just show him you are trying and that you care about what he has so say for at least the length of the class. expects nothing more than any one else.. an easy A. (definitely does not play favorites in class)
No Comments
David always seemed open to letting us explore and play in whichever way we seemed fit.  I loved this class and would take it again in a heartbeat.

Rude and forgetful. Told him I had sprained ankle (happened during semester) and he kept telling me to do things he knew I couldn't do b/c of my ankle. I had te remind him about 15 times. Also he totally plays favorites with students.
No Comments
No Comments
No final, just a midterm. He's very passionate about the content which makes it a little less boring!!

He's an engaging speaker and clearly has a lot of energy. The intro class was a great way to just enjoy learning about American History, but you should actually like history. There are lots of long readings and there isn't a review for the test. While it was just him lecturing to you, he made it more enjoyable. He does read off notes a lot.

I had already taken APUSH, so the material in this class wasn't new to me. However, Professor W.S did an awesome job at presenting American history in a new, interesting way. This class is only graded on a few things, but none of those things were particularly hard. Some of the readings felt unnecessary, but I enjoyed W.S and taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cool course, good professor, and not very much assignments. There's a lot of reading to do for discussion sections and the midterm is a big part of your grade, but the lectures can be interesting if you're interested in US history. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory, but the historical IDs aren't posted anywhere other than on the board in class.

Midterm exam carries a lot of weight. Attendance is pretty much required until then because the content of the exam comes from the IDs given in class. Exam isn't too hard. Although the class is easy, the lectures are boring beyond belief. He reads from a script for the entire class, and almost nobody pays attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved my studio with Derek. He let me have my design freedom while integrating his experience and led me to better my project. I would absolutely take his studio again as my work from that semester is my favorite project
He's intense, solid all around.
Knows a lot about water and stuff other than buildings.
Challenging, rigorous, lots of work but learned a lot.
A great Chair and leader of the MLA program with strong interdisciplinary approaches in his architecture studios.
Experience professor, knows a lot about architecture, landscape, urban and water

Although he is present and has fairly good comments towards our work; his ego and personality gets in the way of his teaching. The feedback often got personal as he would comment on our personal lives or call out people during discussions. If he could keep conversations purely constructive and give more respect, he would receive more credit.

Used to be chair of the department, isn't anymore thankfully. Outside of school a lot of people don't want to work with him so be careful throwing his name around. He can be temperamental. He is part of the generation that thinks suffering is necessary in an architecture and he sometimes puts the suffering part before the education part.
Derek is a wonderful professor and provides amazing feedback during desk crits.
Compliment his Corten steel rectangle house and you'll get an A. Just play along with his ego and you will do fine.

Derek takes everything really personally. Classes tiptoe around his moods. He won't ever admit to not knowing something and will blame you instead. Will storm out of class to cool off at. 

He isn't necessarily all bad. He knows a lot about rivers and landscape architecture. Just don't rely on him to be a reasonable, stable, or supportive person.

Challening, yet very rewarding professer. He won't hold your hand, and has a reputation of being difficult and moody, but that's unfounded and typically comes from students who aren't pulling their own weight. He will give you a lot of rope, sometimes seemingly vague, but in the long run will reward with dividends in the open-ended field of design.

Reasonably knowledgeable about landscape and watershed but is incredibly moody and makes everything very personal, particularly against international students struggling to understand instructions when he makes fun of them. Changes his mind often, pretends he doesn't. Desk Crits are pretty unproductive with his temper.
Unless you want to know about New Orleans, not that helpful of a teacher.  He can go off the handle and has personality swings.  When he's being Professor'ish, he's good.
No Comments

Genuinely every lecture is at least partially focused on sex, particularly the female body. I get that it's an element of 20th century American cinema but there's no reason for us to be analyzing this many naked women. Everything is about sex. Made me uncomfortable.

No syllabus given, no rubrics given, no grades posted until the end of the semester - he's a mess, please avoid his classes if you can. Also, watch the adam neally on his work on the Katy Perry lawsuit - it's hillarious
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only homework is discussion posts and the occasional essay. The lectures are really interesting and important to go to especially for the midterm and final. class is really chill just be sure to pay attention during lecture especially the first half of the semester.
hot

Had to work really hard just to get a C. This professor will assign unnecessary amounts of home, and is nit picky about answers. You can answer the same thing a different way and hell take of points for it. He is very strict, and though he seems serious about his work, he is more obsessed with policing students for their mistakes.
Don't let the class description fool you - it's not an easy A by any means. You'll have to work semi-hard even if you want a B.
Great Professor, energetic, passionate about the material, and fair.

Pros: Energetic. Knowledgeable. Interesting topic (pop music).  Cons: Takes attendance. Much more work than bargained for (2 quizzes, 3 papers, daily listening journal, midterm, final).  Study = good grade but a lot of grunt work

Is unable to support students with coding. Makes students feel less than for asking valid questions. This was a hard review to write since she is well respected. It's important to admit when you don't know how to code and not make your students feel bad about asking questions about it! I'm glad I left Washington University in St Louis
Not very well organized, but fairly engaging as a lecturer. Not terribly helpful answering questions one-on-one.

Very interesting & engaging lecturer. This is one of my favorite psych classes I have taken. I thought her grading system was very fair and she gave a lot of opportunities to raise your grade (there were short assignments & quizzes in addition to exams).

Surprisingly unorganized, makes a lot of grading mistakes, gives weekly quizzes that ask absurdly specific questions, and is extremely inflexible. That said, she's a good lecturer and knows her stuff - you learn a lot. I'd suggest taking this class with another professor or you'll get very frustrated.

Weekly quizzes that are ridiculously hard! Constantly makes mistakes grading...even on tests! Takes forever to get grades back to you. Bottom line, incredibly unorganized...TAKE WITH ANOTHER TEACHER!!!
Tests were rather tricky and rather nit picky.  Grading on the final paper was not explained nor was it consistant with the other papers.

Lectures were clear but mostly consisted of reading aloud the DSM stuff from the textbook.  Very unapproachable outside class- I tried twice and she seemed annoyed.  The exam questions definitely tried to trick you.  The movie paper grading was very unclear and sketchy.

She was very clear in offering explinations and examples in class of all the material.  However, the grading of the last writing assignment was a bit weird.  People did end up with lower grades than expected.
nice braid.
It was a good class. Very straightfoward. Homework was easy as hell, one paper that was graded hard but not to bad to write, four exams and you can drop one.

She just read off of the slides everyday. Tests were pretty easy, but the movie writing assn. was graded really weird and she was unclear about it, so everyone got low grades and it does affect your overall grade.
The lectures were often boring, but the material is interesting and presented clearly.
Tends to be difficult when it comes to pickiness of test questions. May seek to trick students.
keeps the lectures interesting.  she is enthusiastic enough to keep me awake.  fun personality, but there is one paper in the class and it is graded very wierd and unfairly.
easy to understand and tests are easy
This professor has the stupidest grading system I've ever seen...I missed ONE question on one paper and got a D.  Excellent lecturer, horrible grader.  Take from Kurtz if worried about GPA.
Not helpful

She's so clear and concise. She doesn't test on stupid stastics you'll never remember and she doesn't teach the boring stuff no one cares about. The subject is interesting, the teacher is engaging, the tests are easy.
i was so excited to take the class, only to find a professor reading off her slides the entire time. boring and completely unhelpful.
Meh...it's an easy A if you like Abnormal Psych
SOOOOO BORING She just reads off the slides.  I fell asleep in her class every day and so did half the class.
i found her teaching to be really boring...only lectures and slides.  abnormal psychology is such a cool subject but she made it incredibly dry.
Down to earth, sense of humor, very focused, recommend highly
one of the better psych. professors at WashU; easy to follow and very straightforward with the material; leading researcher in schizophrenia;
she is not clear at all and not helpful. she is also vindictive. take abnormal from kurtz!
Excellent professor. Only teachees things that have empirical backing.
I learned a lot in her class.
She's great - very clear and very nice!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Barbour interests me more as a person than as a lecturer. But his assignments are very straightforward. QP is honestly one of the best classes at WashU, but I don't think it's overly difficult (esp Barbour's section of QPI). Only reason I got an A- and not an A was because I fumbled Silva's exam.
QP is the hardest class you will ever take.   Barbour is the most educated and well poised professor you'll ever have.
Unique lecturing style - always on the lookout to help students, although he will NOT spoonfeed you answers. Arguably the best professor in the BME department.
great professor take advantage of his office hours
No Comments

Dr. Killen is an amazing professor and person, but only take his class if you are ok reading 150-200 pages per class, including history textbooks. Only take if you are very interested in the subject. Do not take if you only want the trip to Ireland since it will probably be canceled again.

Dean Killen is a very good professor, though his class has A LOT of reading (so be prepared for that). He very clearly cares about his students and all the ideas that they bring to the table. I definitely feel like I've learned a ton from this class (Irish Lit)!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Killen.  He is so kind and cares so much about his students.  However, he assigns a LOT of reading so be prepared to keep up with it and have things to say.  He is a wonderful person, and I am grateful to have him as my advisor and teacher freshman year.

This man is amazing and has guided me through so much of my time at WashU. His classes are SO MUCH reading though, but mostly because he doesn't realize how much he is assigning. You don't need to read it all. As long as you have enough of an understanding, you will be able to write essays and interact just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Killen is a wonderful teacher and an extremely caring man. Very passionate about Irish literature and always willing to meet outside of class. Highly recommend!

Dean Killen is my advisor and my professor. He's very passionate about Ireland and its culture, and he's very helpful when it comes to providing advice as well. I really enjoy going to his class everyday!
She is a great teacher. Be sure to keep up with the homework and don't be afraid of office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Ditto puts a lot of effort into her lectures and is very available to help. There is a lot of extra credit/exam revision credit available so even if you struggle you can do well. Be sure to stay on top of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Ditto was accessible outside of class and was flexible with students. Homework was completion-based and exams had corrections, which made it easy to do well. However, the course was tedious and it was hard to pay attention as the teaching style was not interactive. Homeworks were time consuming and didn't always align with exams or lessons.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Diallo is amazing. Super chill, easy class, not a lot of hw, test was easy. I had a lot of fun in his discussion sections, very inspiring, cares a lot about students' voices.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Diallo was a pleasure to take class with. His grading is lenient and easy, and he appreciates when you go beyond in the reading responses. Readings can be a bit much on top of other classes at times, but it is manageable if you set aside a day or two to really sit down and do it. Overall, I would take this course again and again. Exam was easy!

Professor Diallo is very passionate about the subjects he teaches, he is very kind, and he cares for his students. But, he assigns a LOT of reading in this class. While they were interesting, the load was overwhelmingly large some weeks. He is also very unclear about guidelines for big projects such as papers and exams. Thankfully he grades easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: African Immigration was one of my favorite college classes. Prof Diallo chose excellent readings, guest lecturers, and shared so much about his own immigration experience. This class is not hard and prioritizes learning about what immigration from Africa entails. I took away and reflected a lot from this course and couldn't recommend it more!
Professor Diallo is amazing. He is very clear with his projects and homework and the actual work itself is not too bad, with 1-2 hours of reading per week. His grading is also easy and lenient.

Prof. Diallo is a fun instructor and so passionate about the topic he teaches. The class is easy with 1-3 hours outside of class commitment for reading response. He's also very understanding and cares about his students. Will definitely take all other courses he teaches

Professor Diallo is very knowledgeable on the topic of African history and the youth in Africa. This class is fairly easy and interesting. Do not stress about the reading response, final project, or the country presentations they were very low maintenance and did not take much of your time. He's an amazing professor and you learn a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Diallo is clearly very passionate, but it sometimes felt like the class was taught at a high school level. We only read one text a week and then were graded on writing a one-page regurgitation of the information. Discussions were fine but I didn't feel like I learned that much. Liked the map test and student presentations

Dr. Montaño is very understanding. As long as you read and genuinely participate, she will be cool with you. She cares of the things she teaches and is very flexible in her deadlines. She is the most open-to-feedback professor I know. If you care of the subject she teaches, take it but if you are looking for an "easy-a" class, she isn't for you.
She was very excited to pick on students specifically freshmen. Too many readings and if you didn't read it, even if you contributed to discussion, she would use you as a target.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dropped her class with 2 others. Very heavy on reading & if you don't know the material throughly she will notice it and judge you. She doesn't try to hide dislike of a student and it makes the learning environment hostile. Montano is passive aggressive, tries to make others feel embarrassed, and very disorganized. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Unbearable, unpredictable, and insufferably boring. Montano has been the worst professor I've had at WashU so far. Do NOT take this class. She is incredibly disorganized, passive-aggressive, and unclear on her expectations. She expects everyone to agree with her and does not explain what she looks for on assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are disorganized and her gradings are unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The reason I chose this class was because it was interesting and seemed fun. Oh man how much I regretted this class. Be prepared to read and how she thinks. If you don't see it how she sees it, she tends to degrade your thinking. A lot of repetitive reading and how boring her lectures are. She also tends to go on long tangents and not grade at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Boring class with no intellectual stimulation whatsoever. The readings are repetitive and pleonastic, the seminar days are more like quizzes, and she's rude to students. I found her to be extremely judgemental. Do not, do not, do not take a class with her.
Extremely disorganized, changes dates often and does not update the syllabus. Lectures as if she is reading right off of a piece of paper which is very boring.
Professor Montano is disorganized. It is often very unclear what the homework assignment is, and she often uses last minute emails to change our schedule.

EMPHASIS on Get Ready To Read. Not as bad as the other reviews say. She is not the best teacher, but her research is very interesting. Do the readings, GET READY TO PARTICIPATE IN CLASS, and you'll do fine. I took the class because "Angels, Prostitutes and Chicas Modernas: Women in Latin American History" was an interesting-sounding name.

Montano is inaccessible outside of class. She does not provide clear instructions and provides no feedback. Grades are determined by participation and very few large assignments (which you do not get feedback on, even the midterm). There is a lot of reading required and she gets very specific and angry if you do not remember/reply correctly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Awful. Provides unclear directions (if any) and odd assignments. Randomly calls on students in class and gets outwardly angry and yells if they do not give an answer she likes. Only provided feedback on one essay this semester and assigned grades with no feedback for the rest of the sem. Inaccessible outside of class and never responds to emails.

She calls on people randomly and asks difficult questions about the readings (and gets annoyed if you don't know the answer). You have to read and take thorough notes on all the readings. Also, sometimes her instructions and lectures are unclear
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Absurd amount of reading. 3 textbooks with supplemental articles. Expected us to remember reading assignments from3 weeks ago and gave pop quizzes when we didn't. Participation can make or break your grade. Gave opportunity to rewrite midterm and gave good feedback to improve paper and better write the final, both were out of class.
One of the worst classes I've ever taken. She gave so much homework it was literally impossible to keep up and didn't present the material in an engaging way.
Terrible guy, you don't know how bad a prof can be until you see him!  The worst teacher I have ever had!!!!
Extremely Easy but class isn't worth going to
I don't really understand him, but he brings pizza and drinks to class
try to take it with someone else. he's not bad, just very very boring
No Comments

Don't bother buying the textbook.  His slides are clear and ALL of the test material draws verbatem from his slides.  With minimal effort: easy B.  With some effort, easy A.  Cares about his students and his heart is truly in the right place.  Try to take w/ Johanek but if not, he's fine & easy.
really boring in class.  not much work. but take it with a different teacher if possible
I love Donsub Rim

Surprised that I ended up with an A in the class because of how much I struggled through it.  Going to class is not representative of the content on the exams and honestly just confused me more.  Supplement class with Khan academy for sure.  Super super nice guy though.

Rim is a nice person and an average lecturer. He answers questions thoroughly but sometimes spends too much time doing so, to the point that he leaves out or glosses over critical concepts which end up appearing on the exams. He altered the homework multiple times because there were mistakes or he had forgotten to cover the material.

I do not understand why Prof Rim has been rated so badly. In my opinion, he is a great professor and it is easy to earn a good score in his class. His notes is clear and he tries his best to help students.

Attend lectures, do the homework and you should do well. Lectures follow the textbook so you can get away with skipping lectures, but I wouldn't recommend it because he talks about homework and we got off track from the syllabus schedule. Don't be too stressed if your grade is lower than expected because he curves tests at the end of the year.

Dr. Rim is great! I went to his office hour a couple of times and he is super helpful. After he knows I never went to his class, he did not blame me or complain about it and suggested I read the textbook.

Beginning of the semester was a little rough, lectures could've maybe been planned/organized better. There wasn't too much feedback on work, grading was a little slow. With that said, Rim does care about his students and wants them to be successful. Overall content wasn't too bad, sometimes tests were tricky but partial credit was provided.

Rim is uniquely humorous and caring. Though he usually teaches graduate students, he did adjust his way of teaching throughout the semester, and inspired students to seek knowledge instead of merely achieving good grades.

Restating what someone else said but lectures were definitely super theoretical and often confusing, and he had the habit of going over a lot of proofy stuff and explaining things in an unnecessarily convoluted way. My advice is to learn primarily from the textbook and go to lecture/OH for to review what you read.
His lectures were not helpful AT ALL. A lot of what he explains is super theoretical and is like you are reading a more confusing version of the textbook.

We never got our midterm projects (from March) OR our final project back. We never even got to see what score we got on them. I'm pretty sure she never graded them and then just gave everybody an A in the class because the deadline for submitting grades was approaching fast. If I wanted to learn with no feedback I would go to YouTube. 0/10

The homework in this class is weekly with tons of math and programming that take 6-10 hours to complete. This class is tedious and hard, but it does an amazing job of teaching you useful and practical math and computer science methods to solve real-world data science problems. Biggest issue is the lack of feedback -- I got no comments on anything.

Professor Ding is awesome! Her class is hard, don't get me wrong, but she gives you the best tools to succeed that she can. Exams are only 30% of her class and she allows a one-sided cheat sheet and gives you a study guide. It is a difficult class and you have to put in the work, but Professor Ding gives great lectures and grades with kindness.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A lot of students really struggle in her classes. Never truly felt like I understood the homework, and never felt prepared for the exams but somehow managed to pull through with a fine grade.

Professor Ding does have a slight accent, but it is not too bad to the point that you can't understand her. Her notes are pretty helpful and if you keep up with her lectures, the exams aren't that bad. She gives out a lot of extra points (gave an extra 5 points back on most exams this semester) which was very helpful.

we conducted a small class attendance survey... students who attended classes at least once last week performed better in exams than those who did not attend the class by 6% in Exam 2 and became statistically significant
Jimin

FYI 5% is a single multiple choice question... She is disappointed by our low exam averages but can't figure out why...
She is very enthusiastic but too hard to understand. I need to listen to her lecture recording twice to understand what she is saying.
Toughest thing I've ever done. Will eat a lot of hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very rough class. Probably the worst professor I've had at WashU. The homeworks ask for ridiculously advanced R knowledge that she doesn't teach in course, and her lectures are extremely hard to follow. Avoid if you can.

Professor Ding is a VERY nice and funny person and she is accessible in her office hours, but those are unfortunately the only good things I can say about her course. The lectures are confusing and hard to follow, and the homeworks are very difficult. Also the computer problems she gives using R are far more advanced than they should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Accent makes her extremely difficult to understand. Test questions are poorly worded, and tests are only out of 15 points, so if you get just a few points off your grade tanks. Worst class I've taken at WashU.

Ding is a sweet person, but an overall mediocre lecturer, failing to explain already tough concepts. Students who work hard can usually attain an A (she gives great extra credit opportunities).  Her exams can be tough and her homeworks are time consuming, but she is definitely fair overall.  Sadly, she yet remains the best 3200 prof. at WashU.
Ding Is The Best Math Professor At WashU.  She Is So Nice And Accessible And Funny During Class.  I Love Her.

So she's hard to understand at first, and uses a lot of power points to teach (can be annoying), but overall is a decent professor. Attendance will give you 3% at the end, and she also offers extra credit, so if you give some effort and A is definitely attainable. Her tests resemble a lot of her old exams, so just look at those.
Great professor. She is very engaging during lectures. Test are easy if you do the homework. Easy A class since she gives a lot of extra credits.

I came into this class really wanting to like statistics. This did not happen. Ding is a very sweet, smart woman. However, her English is subpar and she isn't engaging. Her grading criteria for homework is arbitrary and not clear, and her tests are out of  only 15 points, with 9 of those points being multiple choice that are poorly worded.

I went in knowing quite a lot of  stats and still did not do well. She does not present the material clearly (in part due to her accent). Her exams are largely controlled by a small amount of poorly worded multiple choice; in short, if you get a few wrong your grade suffers A LOT. The exams are not a good indicator if you know the material.
She is hard too understand
Awful. Just plain awful. I went into this class loving statistics and now I'm unsure if I even want to continue with a math major.

She writes everything important on the board, and is usually clear with examples. She seems to genuinely care whether the students are following her, and does her best to answer questions in class and office hours. Has reasonable expectations overall.
Class is somewhat boring, attendence rate is about 60%. However, class notes are wonderful and helpful, and the professor is nice.

She does not make the difficult subject matter enjoyable or easy to understand. Her accent is very strong and she does not explain things well. She usually just repeats what is in the textbook and does not help get you prepared for exams or SAS homeworks. Try to set up a study group for this class.

Ding is a very sweet woman who tries very hard to be a good teacher... she really, really does. Sadly, however, she is still without question the single worst teacher I have yet to encounter in my academic career. She basically copies the book VERBATIM onto the chalkboard and then proceeds to read it super fast and explain NOTHING.

The exams are easy, but the grading for the homework assignments was somewhat arbitrary and poorly explained. This wouldn't be a big problem if the homework wasn't a substantial portion of one's grade, but it is.
Useless lectures. She literally reads from slides from time to time. Refuses to help outside class.

Ok professor. Subject can get very boring and tedious. She teaches pretty much straight from the book, but it is worth it to go to class because she does a much better job of explaining material than the book does. Tests are difficult but it's the calculations that make it difficult- not so much the content. Fair grader.

Decent professor, considering how mind-numbingly boring the topic can be. Assignments are fair, though they often take much longer than you would expect. Exams are really tough - found it hard to anticipate what would be asked.

Professor Ding is really great at being available for office hours.  Her lecture style is clear and efficient.  The exams are brutal though.  BRUTAL.  Weekly homeworks: not so bad, as long as you don't try to do it all on Sunday night every time.

Prof Dowell is a nice and pretty funny guy. However, his classes are boring and you learn more from the Supersite homework than you do from him. He assigns meaningless homework, but his tests are pretty straight forward. However, he gives arbitrary grades for compositions. He's ok but his class isn't the best for actually learning Spanish.

Take Portuguese with Prof. Dowell if you want an easy A. If you actually want to learn Portuguese, I'd look for another professor. Great guy, very caring, teaches through humor. Isn't actually fluent in Portuguese though. His slides are in Spanish 80% of the time, and you will occasionally be docked points for writing in Portuguese. Fun class.

I can't deny that some say señor Dowell does not teach very well, but his courses are always relaxing and with plenty of activities (although the activities don't really help that much). He is also an easy-grader and gives good scores.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Dowell makes learning Portuguese very fun and approachable. As someone who has never learned another language before (I'm a native Spanish speaker), I was pretty nervous at first but the encouragement and practices Dowell gave me increased my confidence, performance and fun in Portuguese. Just do the assignments and participate!

For Spanish 302, Dowell is super chill and easygoing. You will definitely have to participate a lot in this class and he does cold call quite a bit, but the material is pretty easy and surface-level. He's a super easy grader as well––he gives pretty much everyone an A.

Professor Dowell is highly accessible outside of class, actively encouraging students to attend office hours. However, the class is extremely fast-paced, as noted in the syllabus. Expect to participate a lot and dedicate 1+ hour daily to Spanish studies outside of class; otherwise, you risk falling behind and struggle with quizzes and exams.

Content was easily digestible, but my experience in the course last year was ruined entirely by him. He is incredibly stuck-up, and lets his ego get in the way of his teaching. And he's just an overly-negative person. I would have loved this class if it was taught by a different professor, honestly.

He's a nice guy, but as a teacher he isn't good. He doesn't put much effort or care into the class. There is a lot of homework. Also this class is designed to learn grammar outside of the classroom through an online textbook. It is hard because he doesn't explain the grammar or concepts in class. You need to participate in class everyday.

SPAN 101** 
I recommend not having Professor Dowell. Dowell does not lecture or teach within the class period, only showing PowerPoints based on review. Spanish is not a difficult subject but Profe Dowell DOES NOT TEACH, which creates difficulty in the comprehension and understanding of the course and language.

After two classes with Prof. Dowell, I can confirm he is very easygoing and makes classes enjoyable. He does cold call students a lot, and doesn't give the best feedback on papers, but he is a great teacher and engages with students very well. He doesn't give too much homework either. I highly recommend him for Spanish and Portuguese students!
