I had Dowell for Spanish 102 but that wasn't an option. The class is a lot of work but that's not really his fault, it's just languages at WashU. He's a nice guy as long as you put the work in and do the assignments.

*Note I had Dowell for SPAN202 but that was not an option to select*

Profe Dowell is very caring towards all students and even helped give back a few extra points on some assignments at the end of the semester to help bump my grade up a point.

However, SPAN202 is incredibly grammar intensive with a lot of busy work and was not a great class.

Professor Dowell is an inconsistent grader, with not much lecturing ability. He is a quick email responder, and makes everything we need accessible online, but he is not very organized and I feel like I didn't learn as much as I should have in the class.

(Took 101 but was not an option) Haven’t taken any other language classes yet, but honestly the worst professor I have had so far at Wash U. Inconsistent homework vs lecture topics, and clearly does not care about the class.

Very kind man, and an easy grader. He doesn't have the strongest accent, but he's really passionate about Brazil and makes an effort to continuously learn about the culture and language. He also really enjoys class discussions and fun activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Super nice guy! Show up and participate and you will have no issues.

Professor Dowell really is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students so much and will do anything to make sure you are happy and successful. Class was really enjoyable and I actually felt like I gained a lot of speaking skills. Easily the most caring and nicest professor I've had.
DJ Flowe is the GOAT. You will not regret taking one of his classes, probably the best History professor at WashU
One of the best professors at WashU. Cares really deeply for his students and it is a pleasure to be in the class.

Not only is Prof. Flowe a very kind, forgiving person, but the content he presents is consistently fascinating, the readings are interesting and often pretty short, and the workload is manageable. If the workload becomes unmanageable, Flowe is flexible. His kindness shines through and makes his class environment so comfortable.

DJ Flowe is the goat. Really interesting class, though I wish people engaged more because often times people just wouldn't do the readings and wouldn't speak in class so few people ended up talking. The more you engage the better. Flowe is super sweet and funny, and I really enjoyed his lectures.

This class was exciting and Professor Flowe was great. We took field trips etc. to learn about archival work. The class was really easy, only graded on a few participatory team work projects, and professor flowe is super supportive. Tbh I wish it was harder because I wanted to get a bit more from the topic, but nice to have a easy class.

Professor Flowe's class was very interesting and yet the workload was very chill.  I wish we would've gone a little more in depth with some concepts but nonetheless very enjoyable and a great professor!

I love Professor Flowe. He is such a caring and interesting professor. The course topic was super interesting and provides a lot of real life examples. Professor Flowe creates a relaxed environment and Im always excited to show up for this class. If you're considering this class, you should take it.

One of the best professors & courses I've had! I took "The Politics of Black Criminality and Popular Protest". Given it was remote, Flowe kept me engaged and excited about the material. It was student driven, but he often interjected with insightful comments that added to the content. I'm also pretty sure he gave everyone an A on every assignment.
Heavy reading and moderate writing.

Professor Flowe is amazing and definitely my favorite at WashU. I loved taking his class this semester and I hope to take more classes with him in the future. He is an incredible lecturer and a caring person. He is funny and makes jokes in class to keep the energy up. He is very understanding when students are sick or need to miss class.

DJ Flowe is one of my favorite professors. He is passionate about what he teaches and it really comes across in his lectures. The class is very easy, but we did talk about some pretty heavy topics regarding race/gender. Be prepared to have uncomfortable conversations (definitely a good thing in college). Flowe is very chill about grades/deadlines.
great lectures, deep topics, really cool dude, not very difficult but so worthwhile.
The teaching style was not so engaging (but it was accounting), but the instructor really cared about students.
His practice exams are like the bible for the course
Goat T3 Olin Professors OAT
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: explain concepts clearly, good slides.
Great professor overall, engaging lectures, covers alot of material. Exams are almost same format as past exams and he makes it clear what to study. 3 exams total and some hw assignments.

I honestly loved this professor. He did his best to ensure you understood the material throughout the lecture.  he talks a bit fast and goes through the material pretty quickly if you do not stop him but that was one of the things I loved about the professor. His exams were also pretty straightforward, no trick questions with difficult wording.

Good lecturer. He was able to incorporate interesting, real-life examples into his slide shows. He posts many practice exams, which are so useful for studying. He made a class about financial statements about as interesting as it could possibly be, to be fair.

Chris's class was the first in which I've had proper structure and deadlines for a music course, and it was great. The homeworks are always due on Sundays, and yes they're a lot of work if you procrastinate, but it works like a list of tasks that can easily be spread across the week. He gives great feedback on your music and is a wonderful person!

Took 1320 with Chris. If you want to take a class to really learn more about your own creative process, take a class with Chris. He is incredibly inspiring and will always show you what to do and how to do it when helping make music. Chris is able to explain material in a methodical and efficient approach fr students. Chris is amazing!

I took 1313 and plan on taking another class with him in the spring. Absolutely my favorite class I've taken! I was genuinely looking forward to class days. We just get to learn about music and spend time making it, and his passion for the subject really shows. Quizzes are easy enough, and his feedback is incredible.

If your goal is to hone your creative mind this course is for you. Class sizes are small (10-12). He always graded based on the vision of the artist. His genre was a lot different from mine but that never stopped him from helping me improve in the ways I wanted!

Best professor I've had at WashU ESE. She cares about teaching and about her students. She is an excellent communicator a fun professor overall. I have the utmost respect for Dr. Wang and appreciate her commitment to her students.

Her lectures are great. She tries her best to help you if you get stuck with a wonky circuit. The material is not too tough to understand but the report takes a decent amount of time to complete( around 4 hours for prelab and lab).
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is so amazing!

Taken FL2020. Professor Wang really goes the extra mile to help students understand the interesting concepts behind EMag for EEs and is a very accommodating person in general. She also makes the class quite manageable; weekly / biweekly homework sets only have one or two medium difficulty problems, quizzes are fairly easy, and tests were take-home.

Amount of readings is very reasonable. Material is important if and only if it is mentioned in class. He often won't tell you what the "correct answer" is. That's the point: there often isn't one. There are different ways to interpret the facts and the law, and that's what you need to know.

Very sweet prof. Don't be afraid to ask him questions.

Fair grader
Very engaged lecturer
Accessible outside of class
Knowledgeable
Gem of a human being and an excellent professor

Prof. Drobak is lovely and I enjoyed his class, but his instruction is incredibly unclear. His answers to questions often conflict. You don't know what to take from the cases. Compared to other prop classes, I felt unlucky w/ Drobak.  Frustrating to dedicate time to figuring out what the law might be vs. understanding + applying what the law is.
closed book exam

Easy A, provided you "put in" the work. 2-3 hours per week of studying, case briefing and review. Read, read and read! Professor Drobak is a phenomenal professor. He provides an excellent teaching platform for legal jargon in civil procedure. Incredibly tough course content but he has a way of making it enlightening and easy to absorb.

The material by itself is confusing, and he teaches in a very open ended way. You ask questions, he smiles encouragingly. Can be frustrating. Use an outside source to make sure you have tackled all the concepts that will appear on the final- which is closed notes btw. Nice guy, shouldn't teach 1L courses. Has office hours, but isn't helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Truly phenomenal professor. Class won't be easy, but you'll learn the material in an interesting and engaging manner.

Had John for fed jur and property rights.  Great lecturer, but a lot of the heavy lifting on organizing the material is up to you outside of class.  That's how it's supposed to work in college, but having to earn a grade is synonymous with "bad teacher" on this site.  Drobak will bring out all sides of an issue and let you decide for yourself.
I had him for antitrust, civ pro, & property rights.  I loved his teaching!  He's really tough but you learn so much.  My favorite professor, highly recommended.
The material was pretty boring at times but he was a nice guy--helpful, concerned, always available to talk, etc.
I enjoyed his class very much.  Very friendly, and very comprehensive in his teaching.

One of Wulaw's best TEACHERS. More concerned with sharing his knowlege than PROFESSING it. Perhaps the sweetest Prof, he's no pushover. He'll point out your lack of preparation in the middle of class with a sincere smile. He'll bar you from the final for excess absences. If he's teaching anything in which you're remotely interested, take the class!

I only took CSE131 because it was required for my major. I don't have anything bad to say about Dr. Shook, but I don't have anything great to say, either. Very milquetoast. Exams can be pretty tough but the review materials prepare you well. Wouldn't go out of my way to take again but wouldn't change sections to avoid him either.

This class was actually so easy. You only have to show up five times for the in class assignments which are fairly easy, especially if you do go to class. There's like no outside homework if you go to class everyday. If your group is good for the group project, the class is such a free A. If you're group isn't good you are still able to get an A.
He was pretty clear but its a tough course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a very average professor in all regards but the class is very easy, so it wouldn't really matter who the professor is. He definitely cares about the class though which is good.
Lectures are alright but don't cover everything

This class was quite the difficult feat. His lectures were honestly fine but the way the course is set up truly made it a battle. Lecture is only once per week, meaning the content is completely self-taught. Labs were stressful and made little sense. Lack of exam resources made preparing difficult. Do not recommend for first time comp sci students.
Ok lectures but his attitude and behavior towards students are bad.
I found it extremely difficult to enjoy the class or talk to him considering his attitude and behavior towards students. Little help for tests. It is not the worst thing if you get him but not good.

While very easy, this class was a nightmare. Lectures, which are unhelpful and boring, are basically required as they give a quiz at the end of each one. The class is so large that you will interact almost entirely with TAs. Studios were not helpful. Uses an online textbook. If you have never coded before, beware - this class will not teach you.
He had great analogies, and was easy to understand in lectures. I liked his enthusiasm for the subject. Although the class is pretty much self-taught, he clarifies material really well.

Shook is a nice man from far away but deeply unpleasant when you need one on one help. His lectures are decently clear but very slow paced and boring. Studios are helpful though, just pray you got stuck with a ta that doesn't treat you like a child.

Shook lectures pretty well, but it can be boring. Exams are not bad if you put the work in, however, writing out large chunks of code can be brutal. Not the end of the world if you get him, but not the highlight of my week. Also, people might call him snappy, but only when you're twenty minutes late; he's not rude if you're a decent student.

Attendance isn't mandatory but you have to be there for the quizzes. I had no prior cs experience and I found it challenging at first. I spent 90% of my exam studying making the cheat sheet and I didn't really understand the material. Doing the exam prep questions and having that on the cheat sheet is all that you need to do well on the exams.

I personally struggled with this class, since I don't have any previous background with CS and Java. Based on the fact that we are taking quizzes every class at the end of the session, a lot of times I just found myself reviewing for the quizzes during the class. The time I do listen to the class, I found the explanation to be a bit confusing.

I personally don't like the design of the course, especially the fact that there are quizzes every class and you never know what's going to be on the quiz( concepts, what will be printed, or short written code). I found myself studying for the quiz than actually focusing on the lecture for a lot of times.

Not terribly hard if you put the work in, but lectures are boring (maybe me just not liking CS), and he is snappy with students. Not the end of the world if you have to take his classes, but not the highlight of my week.
Prof Shook's class is pretty easy, but he's so unresonably condescending, disrespectful, and uncooperative to students seeking assistance. I almost had to file an accomodations grievance with dr.

I had no particular issues with Professor Shook, and considering I knew absolutely nothing about Java before this class, I found his lectures resourceful and clear. Grading is very lenient, making this course easy, but the material itself can be frustrating for beginners. The test reviews he provided in lectures were most useful for exam studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: While his class wasn't hard, it doesn't mean he's good professor at all- I think people who rated him high don't realize that. Shook is not a good professor and is SO disrespectful to students. I had horrible interactions and witness him yell at students multiple times. I do not understand why he is allowed to teach if he hates the responsibility.
lectures were helpful and he went through example problems in all the lectures. His style of teaching made the content easy to grasp and the tests were easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: It isn't a difficult class at all, but I question the way it is organized. Lectures are entirely unnecessary and a waste of time. Assignments seem good in theory, but the way they are set up and the instructions are very confusing, making them take more time than they should. Studios aren't really helpful and the tests are easy if you study.
Lecture was very monotonous and largely not helpful. While the class was pretty easy to figure out by yourself, everyone would have benefitted from more useful lectures.

Professor Shook's class was engaging, and the lectures were helpful, though not absolutely necessary to succeed. Even without prior computer science experience, I was able to follow along and earn an A. The material was manageable, and the class was a good introduction to the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Shook isn't a bad professor at all. I stopped going to lectures after the first few weeks and did just fine. Studios in labs are required, but lectures aren't necessary. Everything you need to know is online. Shook seems interested in what he's teaching, but he does seem strict with some things, such as detailing what's going to be on a future test
he's not very understanding and won't help you if you need it
Absolutely no need to go to lecture whatsoever. Easy to get an A in the class. Exams aren't weighted that heavily. Studios are graded on being there.
Fine professor. There's really no need to go to class and almost all learning is done in the labs and on HW.

I didn't go to his lectures because I didn't find them helpful, but that isn't necessarily a bad reflection on him. He was a nice guy but had a condescending tone of voice (whether intentional or not). He was really helpful when I had an issue with late credits and gave me more.
Shook definitely doesn't suffer fools gladly. I learned through doing the assignments and going to TA office hours, lectures are very skippable

Pretty easy class, you have to work to get a score as low as mine. 90% of the learning is done on your own outside of class, I high-key just didn't feel like doing the learning. Turn in the assignments and it's impossible to not get an A. If you want to learn and not just farm GPA, I suggest learning Java on your own time and skipping 131.
Boring, kind of rude, but class is easy. Also his name is Gary supposedly

Never coded before in my life, so it was pretty hard to manage at first esp since it's so focused on independent practice. I would say still go to lectures because the tests tend to mirror the exercises a bit, but also def go to office hours. Tests were fine as long as you have a basic understanding of the material.

Great professor. Lectures are clear with interesting examples (attendance is not mandatory and recordings are available). Much self-learning in the course but materials are abundant for understanding and practice (if you do all the exercises and assignments, then you will have no problem with the tests). 2% extra credit. You can drop the final!

I had no coding experience whatsoever, and the class was okay. I think the best thing is to try your best. Go to TA office hours, helps so much -- I went all the time for assignments. The actual professor is not involved, but the TAs are great. Wish the class did rounding though and extra credit for late coupons too.

I came into this class with zero coding experience, so it felt like a big jump, especially since Shook only goes over the exercises in the module and not the actual concepts themselves. My main recommendations are to go over the recitation recordings for studying said concepts and to go to TA office hours. Tests were fine, nothing too unexpected.
he did me dirty rahhhhhhhh

I just took the class in fall 2024, and I think Prof. Shook is not as bad as the rating. He teaches everything in the module, maybe a bit slow paced, but he always answers any questions in lecture and does a revision session before each exam. It could be a bit hard for people with zero coding experience, especially the last few modules.

He was really kind to me when I talked him during office hours actually a really nice guy but the class is hard and he doesn't teach well. The professor before him was so well and I use that canvas page because it has slides and videos and other resources. Dough is not a good teacher dont take this class if youre not ready to teach yourself

I have no coding experience and I have been doing pretty well in the class. The class is set up in a way that is mostly asynchronous so he does not teach you very much, but seems like a pretty nice guy. Everything is pretty chill except the exams are a little hard, but you get a cheat sheet!

This was my first intro class to computer science. In the first lecture, Professor Shook claimed you hadn't needed to know a line of code prior to this class. Complete lie. For someone who has never coded, this class is a complete nightmare. I was planning to major in computer science, but this class alone turned me away. Horribly designed class.

He doesn't teach at all. His TAs try to help with assignments but sometimes even they struggle to explain it, so assignments and studios take a lot of time to finish. Test is straightforward. Nobody comes to his lecture.

Shook didn't teach much at all. The lectures are a waste of time if you read the textbook, which is also terrible. I taught myself CS last semester, and it's embarrassing that WashU or Doug Shook might think they had anything to do with it.

He was condescending and unfair to students, especially with his course policies which were very strict (no makeup exams for almost any reason). Also, many students felt uncomfortable around him. His TAs basically led the class and were amazing in answering all of the questions that he failed to teach us. Easy to do well with office hours.

Professor Shook is not a good lecturer. The TAs basically teach the course for him.  He also is not understanding or flexible at all, and will not accommodate personal situations in the classroom.  Tests and assignments are mostly easy for this course though.

Prof Shook don't even teach the class, he never showed up and there's no communication whatsoever. However, his TAs are amazing. The class was easy for me so I never had to ask questions, but if the content is new for you it might be hard.

The class itself is well designed in my opinion but Professor Shook doesn't really help much with it. Rather, the TAs are the ones who are helpful. I will say though that it is somewhat difficult to rank Professor Shook since you will interact with TAs far more than you will with him, but my few interactions with him were fine.

Shook doesn't really play a big role in his class. CS TA's will carry you and you have to appreciate them. My only interactions with him were through lectures where he was repeatedly passive aggressive towards students. I'll give him the benefit of the doubt since TA's have a high opinion of him. Reach out to him and I'm sure he'd be down to help.
Shook was quite condescending and didn't really take well to questions. The TAs pretty much run 131 and the exams are pretty easy so you'll be fine, though.

Prof Shook was nice enough, and the lectures were helpful when he did code writing problems. As others have stated the assignments are very difficult, but the tests are much easier. I didn't really enjoy the class, but it was easy enough to get an A.

He manages to turn even the simplest of classes into a scripture-reciting session. His class is an unparalleled cure for insomnia. It's a rare talent to amass such a collection of poor reviews for teaching what should be the easiest of all CS courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally found it boring, but probably because I do not like CS, as it turns out. Assignments can be tough, but tests are easier and are pretty fair. Shook has days where he is super passionate and some days where he is kind of hard to follow and less passionate. He hates it if you ask about tests, but overall he is just fine.

Professor Shook was actually better than I expected. I found that doing the modules before going to lecture/while in lecture and going to his lectures was the most helpful for me. If you follow along during class and do not get distracted, you will notice the content isn't difficult. If you need help, you can go to TAs office hours.

Doug Shook's CSE 131 is a class run by TAs. The lectures are helpful to some people but most will just skip them. I highly recommend doing the code and not using chat gpt because you will fall behind otherwise. Pretty boring teacher honestly but atleast grading is clear and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Shook is not the best prof to take your first computer science class as it might make you question your major. He's also rude and judgmental when answering students answer in lecture. I also want to take the time to thank the amazing TA that helped me for hw and pass this class but Prof. Shook...
This class definitely NOT meant for those who had no coding experience before. The homework assignments are hard and take very long time to complete.

I don't have much Java coding experience, but I thought the class was pretty easy and straightforward and you have a lot of time to think through your answers on tests. Shook doesn't go over anything useful in lectures though so just do the module readings and talk to TAs. He also is super stingy about talking about the test format/content

This class isn't made for those who've never taken a computer science course. It goes very quickly and there is little help to learn everything. The assignments are difficult and Shook's lectures are very poor. Often when you ask basic questions, he claims we should already know them and does not answer. This class is entirely run by TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Shook was extremely bad at teaching, I would not recommend attending the lectures at all for this course. I was already vaguely familiar with the content of the course and I found that when I went to lectures, I left more confused than when I started. He also is just kinda rude. At the end of the day class was extremely easy, but bad prof

I'd only take him again because the class is required. If you take this class, skip lectures he is incredibly condescending and won't go over anything useful. The weekly studios are required and a good place to learn and demo your work at with a TA you know well. Overall not a hard course, just do the assignments honestly and you will be fine.
Doug is so funny and the class is so fun!

He does not teach. Lectures are useless. He also is very condescending when students ask questions that he deems as "irrelevant", when they're just common questions students ask in order to understand. If you have no prior coding knowledge, don't even think about taking this course bc you have to teach yourself. There's nothing intro about it.

So incredibly condescending. He lectures now yeah, but its uninformative and he hates "stupid questions" (aka questions he deems under his expertise). DO NOT ASK ABOUT THE FORMAT OF THE EXAMS. Good luck soldier.

Very reasonable guy, always understands if something's going on as long as you communicate. That being said, he's not the greatest at teaching -- I came into the class with prior knowledge but even then felt like he didn't explain concepts very clearly. Lectures felt dry/useless, I ended up going to only half of them and self-studying the rest.
This class is basically run by TAs. GO TAs!

You will probably see him once the entire semester; but as a class, 131 is very relaxed and they set it up so there are lots of opportunities to improve your grade even if the content doesn't come to you easily. Very self-taught class, but plenty of opportunities to meet with TAs if you need help.

My rating is for Doug, but the following is for the course:
Overall, CSE131 is a great class. I enjoy having the ability to learn on my own, so how Doug didn't exactly teach didn't bother me. Also, if you can, refrain from relying solely on office hours (unless needed). This can be a rewarding class if you struggle on your own for a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Getting a good grade is easy in the sense that if you do all the assignments correctly, you'll prob get a good grade. The tests are much simpler than the assignments. I hated the nonexistent teaching, which made it extremely difficult as someone w/o any CS experience. Had to spend literal hours outside of class teaching myself and in office hrs.

This class was very much student-led. I don't think I've ever talked to him once because he's never in class. The TAs are more the professor than he is. It's a teach-it-yourself type of thing because he is useless. So many people drop this class. You will only pass this class if you have friends

The class itself is almost completely self-taught and I barely interacted with the professor at all. He was helpful during test prep periods but not any other time during the class. Do not take class if not planning on going into Comp Sci!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Solid guy for 131. In my opinion, the exams were very easy but the projects were fairly time consuming and going to TA hours helps a lot.

Saw the professor about three times during the semester, he held helpful review sessions before each exam. Ngl in order to get a good grade, you're most likely gonna have to be at office hours a lot. I was there more than I was in class. Assignments are the hardest part of the class, do all of those and the exams and you should get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Definitely not a beginner friendly course. You can get by through office hours and receiving help from TAs, but if you really want to learn how to code your best bet is to look elsewhere. Professor was helpful once every exam cycle by providing review sessions, but besides that he is not really present.
Shook is fine but this is a TA taught class. Definitely a grind with no CS background.
Only saw prof 3 times over the semester for review (was good at helping us review but that's it). Class was ran by TAs with minimal help by prof.

No lectures and no teaching which makes the course more confusing and difficult than necessary for a beginner. TAs basically answer all your questions during class and do all the "teaching" so take advantage of office hours early. Don't let it steer you from CSE because it's hard to fail. Basically a DIY become a coder in 12 weeks bootcamp
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly he wasn't the best professor but because he doesn't actually teach the course (you do textbook readings, then do studios/assignments with TAs) it doesn't really matter. He was always great to meet with after exams though!
If you take this class, you will rarely see the professors as the class is TA-led. He is a good teacher when you see him, but it is just very rare that he will show up.
I honestly have not seen him at all. There is NO lecture, basically a self-taught class. If you have no coding background YOU WILL SUFFER.

Professor Shook doesn't provide any lectures throughout the semester, the TAs carry the class, all you have is a pre-studio, then a studio, then an assignment that is significantly more difficult and unrelated to the studio. The class says that you need no prior comp sci knowledge and that a lie, the class should be called intermediate comp sci.

Get ready for any concerns to be dismissed by him. In his mind, the class has been taught so many times that there's no way that someone is struggling. He doesn't understand that one size doesn't fit all, and he claims to want to help students while simultaneously acting defensive and dismissive when someone dares to question the course layout.
not choice the professor, never teach, only outside lean everything and not friendly for new learner

I have Shook for both 237 and 435 (which was 530s). While he introduced a lot of useful concepts in 237, 435 is just a terrible class IMO. You learn more from CMU database lectures on youtube. The B+ tree assignment is unnecessarily difficult and is not worthwhile. Guidelines for projects can be a lot more comprehensive and detailed.

Hi so basically he doesn't give any lectures and you kind of see him once in a while or during in-office hours. However, if you make the effort to reach out to him and have questions he is very receptive and willing to help. He's more like a resource than a professor. He's also a very nice guy outside of class.
Bruh this mans was mad funny. Literally saw him twice so he is really not involved with the class. Shout out to the TAs they carry this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Class is almost completely self-taught. Assignments can take a while if you have never coded before. Many of the students in the class have coding experience and make the class look easy. Exams get progressively harder throughout semester, but if you study for a few days before the exam and go to the required weekly studios, you'll get an A.
Doesn't actively teach the course so you won't see him apart from Thursday labs where he walks around and answers some questions but very accessible during office hours and genuinely kind professor.

Shook for 131 is hard to rate as the class is mainly self-taught with lots of help from TA's. 131 is set up with very clear and consistent expectations and is generally a pretty simple introduction to coding. You do not need any previous experience coding to take this class. Shook seemed helpful but I hardly interacted with him.
This class is so fun!!! Literally just do all the assignements, and extensions and you will be fine. As long as you put in the work and start stuff early you should get a high A!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This course is just an online self-teaching one. If you have no CS background, you will still be fine. Shook cares his students so much and keeps a flexible policy towards the class schedule. This is an easy A course that would not make you stressful. Just take this course as a freshman in CS!
He is the best professor I have ever had class with ! He made my semester, really understanding and helping each student..
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The teacher (Doug Shook) does NOT teach, and your grade depends on how chill your TA is. If you don't have a background in compsci, you should RUN because every assignment, you have to do on your own. It is like a puzzle but you don't know what the pieces are. Even if you pass, this class will drain you of any interest you ever had in compsci. HATE

Shook doesnt teach his own class and has his TAs who are absolutely clueless teach his class for him. Nobody in the class does the work themselves, everyone you ask will say they got it from someone else so if you put in the time to learn it youre put at a disadvantage. Youll learn a lot from this class and do well but its not because of Shook.

The class is fairly easy in my opinion. But if you have zero experience coding then you will probably need to go to TA hours often which are pretty busy. The class is basically self taught and you barely see Shook (maybe only during studios). The class is basically led by TAs and you only need to attend class on studio days

This semester he gives unlimited extensions to all homework to the last day of class, which is good in a COVID season. However, the homework's tests are not well structured and some hw like B+ tree is very hard. It is not hard to get an A though but you may not learn a lot of database as you expect. A mediocre class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Really good course. Learn a lot. The project is not very difficult.

had for 131 as well, clearly cares about the education of his students. is incredibly helpful in office hours (go to them!!!), but can occasionally come off as harsh/sassy due to... concise wording. can tell if you put in the effort before asking a question. was a good teacher in 237S because he really likes the material. respects effort the most.

If you're at wash u looking on this webstite because you're scared to take 131 because you have no comp sci experience, don't be scared. The class is basically all self taught, so it really doesn't matter how great or horrible the proffessors are. Shook was helpful during office hours though, and I really recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Does not teach the course, unhelpful

Shook is a pretty average professor. His lecture videos get the core concepts for studio/lab across. He can be sassy in answering questions, but when he's not he's often pretty helpful. The homework projects can be pretty big time-sinks, and grading is often done by T.A.s. Exams grading is also precise.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Supposedly he's helpful during office hours, but he is really sassy whenever he responds to a question. Basically leaves most of the learning up to you with the course website, doesn't really teach.

Shook was possibly one of the worst professors I have had at WUSTL.  During an exam, he stood in front of the classroom and said, "If you have any questions, go ahead and raise your hand, but I probably won't answer them." Whenever I have asked a question or clarification, he has audibly scoffed at me like I am a waste of his time.
Shook is the man. An expert at what he teaches, not afraid to share his vast knowledge, and do it in a fantastic way. He teaches material very approachably, and is a nice guy all around.

He's a pretty great lecturer and made the subject really enjoyable. Exams are open notes so it's not hard to get a good grade. He is also incredibly helpful outside of class and responds to Piazza posts SUPER fast.

I took this as a summer course, hence, group assignments were an integral part of the grading.  Its a nice course where you get to learn about a lot of new concepts. There is aslo an exposure to several tools to analyze codes. As long as you work sincerely and meet the deadlines, its a very good course to score well.

Basically a required course for me (there were two other worse options for me), but Shook seems to be incredibly passionate about the material (understandable, considering he has a Comp. Eng. degree). I'm not at all interested in compilers, but I can say Shook is incredibly skilled at teaching. I wish he taught some courses I'm interested in.

You can tell that Prof. Shook really cares about his students and wants to make sure they learn the material. He's extremely accessible outside of class and has the fastest Piazza response time I've ever seen.

Professor Shook is an unbelievably strong lecturer and is very reasonable with grading on quizzes, exams, and labs. You should absolutely take 431 if he is teaching it. As long as you go to class and pay attention, not only will you do well in the class, but you will enjoy the material. Could not recommend this more.
I really learnt a lot from him but he can be pretty mean at times when he gets overwhelmed with questions. Lectures are quite helpful though.

The snarkiest, most unhelpful teacher I've ever had. He never gives a straight answer when people ask questions and then posts mean comments on Piazza about being disappointed with our exam grades. This class is supposedly for beginners but anyone who didn't have a background in programming was totally clueless. 1010 would not recommend.

Professor Shook was consistently available to help and was always able to explain a problem clearly. Every time I went to him for help, I left knowing more about computer science. He did an exceptionally good job of explaining problems in such a way that you could arrive at the conclusion at your own pace. I hope I take a class taught by him again.

This was my first computer science class, and I thought Professor Shook did a good job of teaching java to a beginner, and his lectures were engaging. The material does get more challenging towards the end, so if you can, keep up with your extensions, and do a couple for each unit to get enough practice with the material.

I do not recommend him at all.  I learned virtually everything on my own by looking on the internet.  I actually came into this class very interested in computer science, but this class killed all of the interest that I had.  For me, this was not a good introduction to computer science.

Do prep work before taking this class.  Lots of kids have already taken comp sci and they move through pretty smoothly, but talk to anyone who hasn't already taken any programming courses, and you'll find that everyone is confused and struggling.  Not good for a so called intro class.

He is the worst professor. He thinks he is the man but really its the TAs that help you with the class. And do not copy labs because he will send out an stupid email saying that he is going to find you and report you. But in fact if you copy the lab and understand it then you will be fine for exams
Good

He is an engaging lecturer. Very, very accessible outside of class and on Piazza. His powerpoint slides can be sparse, which makes it difficult to review material after class if you don't take good notes. Once you get your head wrapped around the abstract concepts in the class, the homeworks and labs aren't too hard.

Shook is surprisingly passionate about compilers. He answers questions on piazza  and grades really fast, which is remarkable considering there are no TAs. He expects people to do the readings/work, but I managed to get by only using the textbook sparingly. He is a hard, but its the type of difficulty where you can figure it out with time.

Doug Shook is by far the worst instructor I've ever had. You won't learn anything from him-he clearly doesn't know the material. He reads off another professor's ppt slides and never explains anything in detail. He even got the easiest question wrong on his own final! I am embarrassed for the WUSTL computer science department for letting him teach.
Good professor! Interesting! Recommend

Great lecturer. I rate Reeves highly as a prof, but I didn't like POL101. Conceptually not rigorous, but tests can be hard due to memorization of readings. The 1 test I read textbook was easy, but I didn't for rest and scored average. I bet his upper levels are great, but I don't recommend 101 if you have other hard classes and don't want to read.

The lectures are unrelated and pointless, I had to read and take notes on every assigned textbook chapter before each exam, sometimes getting up to 200 pages. The TA study guides are hit or miss, so I couldn't rely on them. The exam questions are badly worded and super specific, it felt like no matter how well prepared I was I would still get Bs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i stopped attending class after exam 1 and i never read the textbook, i just used the grad TA's study guide and I got an A- . Your grade is mostly based on the 4 exams throughout the semester but is heavily boosted just for attending subsection. lectures are fun and interactive but don't contribute much to what you need to know for the exams.

Good lecturer but very disorganized. Most of the learning comes from the textbook rather than lecture. The majority of the points come from the four multiple-choice exams. Unfortunately, review material was posted way too close to the exam dates, and exams took more than two weeks to be graded. Very nice professor though and easy to work with.
Very nice guy. He is super considerate and kind.
Great lecture and very easy, essentially just graded by test scores.
Very easy course. Interesting lectures.
Great great great Intro to American Politics professor. Relatively low quantity of graded materials/grading opportunities throughout the course, so it's pretty light.

Professor Reeves is truly a talented lecturer. If I could take a class with him every semester I would. I had some family emergencies and he was extremely helpful with making sure I was ready for the make up materials, but more importantly that I was ok as a person. If you're considering taking this class, do it!!!

Professor Reeves is amazing. Best professor I've had. His lectures are very informational but still fun. I learned a lot in this class and would take it again if I could. He's a funny guy and seems to care about his students even in a big class.

Informative lectures with opportunities for discussion in class; Prof. Reeves is open-minded and really helpful in office hours. The 4 Exams that make up a majority of your grade have some surprising questions under-discussed in class lectures, but these are the exception.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Multiple-choice tests actually proved a bit difficult at times. Lectures often felt long and tough to endure

I literally studied the review cards sent out by the TAs for an hour the night before every test. I went to lectures and subsections but did other homework during them and managed to get an A- in the class. Extremely easy (reading the course text would definitely help)

Good lectures but they do get boring and some questions on the exams do come from the lecture. Exams aren't terribly hard but are sometimes worded weirdly with some unexpected content. Textbook is needed but can be found online. Not as easy of a class as some of these ratings will tell you
He is great! Go to his office hours!

Reeves is a great professor. For such a large class in a lecture hall, he does a good job of engaging students, although most of what he says is straight from the textbook so not important to attend every class. Tests are written by the graduate students - beware of weirdly worded questions. Otherwise, highly recommend as it is a very easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Reeves is a great lecturer and the expectations for this class were established very early on. Lectures M-W, occasional assignments due Friday, exams, and one subsection within the week. If you don't know much about American Politics/US History, you will need to read the textbook and study. Otherwise very nice intro course!

Friendly guy but not the most engaging lecturer. Homework is easy and lectures are pretty pointless. Exam content is easy (taken pretty much directly from the textbook), but questions are worded really weirdly, making the actual tests more difficult.
Gives awesome and engaging lectures. Homework is very manageable. Would highly recommend
I took this class during COVID and it was the easiest class ever. Tests were 50 multiple choice (there were 4). Just showing up to the class literally makes up 50% of your grade

Reeves made American Politics on Zoom enjoyable. Like any intro class, it was mostly lectures and MC exams, so not always the most engaging. You have to read the textbook and supplemental readings closely because the exam questions can be tricky. Overall, a good class, but probably not worth taking if you took APUSH or something like it.

Best professor I've had this semester. Very entertaining lectures (at least compared to other professors) and great use of technology. Easy grader and easy tests made for a great intro class. Highly recommend.
Reeves is a nice guy, and the class was well put together. It's an easy A as long as you pay attention and know the vocabulary in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Am Pol was pretty easy. Reeves wasn't super involved, just a few weekly lectures. Still, he teaches well and is a really nice guy if you ever had any issues or need help. His tests are straight from textbook and notes and easy to pass.
Reeves is a great professor and the class is extremely easy.

I had Reeves for Intro to American Politics. He was an engaging lecturer, despite the size of the class. He also ties current events into the class and keeps the material relevant. The tests are all multiple choice, which is nice. However, I didn't find him to be very accessible outside of class. Would definitely recommend taking a class with him.

Not AS easy of an A as a lot of people say; you definitely have to read the textbook (which is pretty boring) and pay attention in class to do well on exams. Awesome professor and class was super interesting, but you have to actually try to get a good grade.

Easiest class I have taken at WashU. Honestly easier than my high school gov class. I would use lecture time to do other hw bc the class was so easy and I wasn't learning anything in lecture. Reeves was fine, an obvious liberal from Maryland. He was sometimes funny. Still not an easy A for some ppl, bc exams were basically the whole grade, no drop.

I disagree with the others comments on here. It's not a super easy A, and I believe the average on tests was around an 86-88. On top of that, the cutoff for an A in the class is an 94 not a 93. Basically getting a good grade comes down to reading the textbook weeks in advance, and taking thorough notes. Reeves was a great professor overall though.
Really easy A if you go to class
lecture heavy but good use of current events. four exams based on lectures and book.

Highly knowledgeable professor. Lectures do not address textbook material in high detail; a student must read the text individually, as lectures decidedly emphasize application of material to the current administration. Because lecture takeaways are also assessed on exams, attendance is critical in addition to thoroughly reading the text.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor! Take a class with him if you can. I've taken several and each one is better than the last.
Really great professor. His lectures are entertaining which makes the class interesting. I would highly recommend taking one of his classes.

Probably the best professor I've had at WashU. Pop quizzes can be annoying, but overall he's amazing. He makes the topics interesting and genuinely cares about students. If you keep up, it's fairly easy to do well.
Great lecturer, takes pretty simple information and makes it interesting. If you pay attention in class and take notes and skim the reading, you get an A

Professor Reeves is one of the best professors I've had at washu so far.  His lectures are engaging, funny, and always cover current events in the world.  Reading the book is a must for this course, but it isn't too bad. Overall, a great class taught by a great guy.

Loved him! Outgoing, funny and tries really hard to make class fun. Lectures were not dense but more a complement to the reading.  Definitely need the book.  Readings are long but if you don't get behind they should be no problem.  Exams can be a little tricky but overall not bad.  Would take again 100%!
Lectures are very general (you need to read), but clear and class is easy.

He's a good lecturer, but the lecture is not really essential to doing well in the class.  You definitely need the textbook (which is one of the most boring textbooks I have ever read).  No papers, the tests are all multiple choice, and the only homework is reading.
Three multiple choice exams.  Lectures are pretty interesting (as lectures go).
Good class as intros go.
It's an introductory lecture course, which can by dry at time.  But overall Reeves makes it interesting with engaging lectures, videos, and humor.  The exams are also very straight forwards.
Very boring. That's about it-- just a very boring class where you don't learn much.

I wasn't familiar with the material before, and I found the pace of the course to be just right.  The exams are multiple choice and are very straightforward.  There is a review sheet, extra office hours, and all of the slides are posted.  Plus Reeves is a clear lecturer and tries to liven up the lectures with videos and current events.
Painfully slow lecture-- very uninspiring, and the class was not about American Politics so much as it was about American government. He made 50 minutes seem like 2 hours.
Overall, a great professor. Prof. Tuch teaches high quality classes that are well structured and executed. He's responsive to emails after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Teaches corporations class like a securities special topics course in derivative shareholder suits. Prepare to spend a lot of time on that and agency. Sends out supplements with relevant info to be read before class, which is helpful. Exam is schedule, and open notes, but is too many questions crammed into the 3 hour timeframe allotted.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Makes Sec. Reg. super easy and understandable.  Uses power points and practice problems from case book in class.

He's a very nice person especially if you attend office hours which I found really helpful to walk through specific problems much slower. The practice exams closely reflect the actual exams and there was a generous curve applied. My only critique is that sometimes in class he would go very fast and wouldn't record lectures.

Very boring lectures that I did not learn much from. Doesn't record lectures, practice tests vary from the real test.  He's friendly and will answer questions on Piazza/in person but overall I don't think the teaching style helped me succeed in the course. Even with PLTL I struggled.
Super boring, awkward, and slow. Take a different professor
Would recommend him. He is good at explaining the topics during class and he is always eager to answer your questions. The math department does a good job with Calc 2.

Professor Green may not be for everyone, but I personally enjoyed his often unintentional deadpan style of humor/teaching. Green and the other calculus II professors never left a question unanswered on Piazza and demonstrated a clear willingness to help their students understand the essence of the course. Do many practice problems for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Butler cares about the subject and his students. He includes many activities that help you review during class, so if you engage in the group projects you should be prepared for the exams. Sometimes on the group projects, it seemed like points were taken off randomly, but it's never that many. Really, he's a nice guy and understands everyone's busy
I loved this class! Andy Butler is a really great teacher. His lectures and teaching style are extremely clear, and he is very accommodating and easy to meet with.

Andy was really fun to take. His Myths and Mysteries of Memory course was more difficult than I anticipated, but still very interesting and fun in general. He is amazing if you reach out, and will work with you as much as possible. The exams were graded fairly tough, but after the first exam it was much easier.

I really liked Dr. Butler and the Myths and Mysteries course. He was really kind and engaging. He really cares about the content of the course. There were quite a few group projects and tests. I didn't expect to take such challenging tests in the course, but it wasn't too bad.

Andy is great. I took his Educational Psychology class. The lectures were really engaging, the structure of the class is the best I have had. He incorporates feedback, tracks student learning, has group and individual work, and is accessible outside of class. He also remembers everyone's faces and names (there were 50 students). 100% take again.
The professor was good at lecturing but he was so bad at communicating his ideas with us. He did not participate in any activities we did in class.

Professor Stone is a great professor who cares about his students and offers useful help outside class. A capstone of his class is a lengthy research paper, though I found it to be an amazing and beneficial experience. There are few grades, but if you are interested in the material and pay attention in class you will do fine on the midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Stone is very accessible to students and genuinely cares about their learning. While his class is lecture-heavy, the content is really interesting. Professor Stone tries to facilitate discussion whenever possible on less lecture-heavy days. You have to put in the work but will learn a lot and grades ultimately reflect that effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Judicial Politics with Prof. Stone was great. He's super organized so you know exactly what to expect from the course and grading and the class is really interesting.

Prof. Stone is fresh out of grad school and full of energy, and passionate about what he's teaching. It is very clear how much he cares for student well-being and the thought he puts into comments and feedback on tests and papers is astounding for how fast he turns them around. Puts on great lectures and is pretty darn funny on the occasion too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Duncan-Shippy was an amazing lecturer and teacher. She really cares about her students and the course content. What more can you ask from a professor? Homework was not difficult and class participation was always fun. Would 101% recommend this class to anyone, even someone with no interest in education. Very laid back vibe in class.

I'm taking Dr. Duncan-Shippy again this semester, but she truthfully is such an intelligent, kind and beautiful soul. All the conversations with her have been so insightful and she's such a force of nature. She's a little bit of all of the women that I look up to in life, she brings them all together to create someone so intricate and loving.

Dr DS is by far one of the best professors I have had at WashU. She made a 3-hour class one that I wish didn't end! Discussions were guided but not controlled by Dr DS, and she was extremely helpful both in and outside of class. The class is reading-heavy but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor! Her lectures were interesting and she created a relax environment for learning. You can tell she loves being a teacher and she genuinely cares about every student. She does take attendance and participation matters, but overall she's a very relax grader. Assignments were short papers and the final is a group project.
Dr DS is a great professor and very caring! I loved learning about education systems and took a lot from the class.

I took several of his classes and have had fantastic experiences. He's extremely knowledgeable and great at explaining concepts. He shares his vast professional experiences, providing students with a deeper understanding of concepts/applications. Most importantly, he goes out of his way to help students with course material and career aspirations.

Professor Dutta is the best instructor I have met at Olin. He not only helped me develop a strong grasp of finance theory but also challenged me to apply these theories in his valuation projects. After taking his class, I feel much more prepared for my professional career.

Great instructor. Helps students learn theoretical concepts and relationships. Leverages industry experience to show real world applications and examples. Wants students to do well and understand (loves and rewards participation). Patient. Great mentor for me on my path towards graduate school. Textbook is a supplement, not required part for grade.

Nothing but respect. Hands down the best professor I've met at Olin. Truly cares about students and wants to succeed. His lecture does not usually follow textbooks, but rather has a lot of insights on how to apply financial skillsets in business settings that makes hour long lectures a breeze.

NYU MS / Wharton MBA, worked in banking, former Senior Economist at Fed Boston, etc.
taught at Princeton, JHU, and WashU while concurrently working on multi-million/billion dollar deals
Need I say more?
If you have an interest in finance and haven't taken a class with Professor Dutta, I strongly recommend it.

Professor Dutta is awesome! Truly cares about his students academically, professionally, and personally. I have taken 3 finance courses with Professor Dutta almost solely because of the professor. Incredible teacher, wealth of experience, and an inspiring individual. I personally believe every finance student should take a class with ProfessorDutta

Teaches from actual experience.
Pro tip: Class participation can/will save your grade.
Amazing professor, would recommend all finance students to take his course.

Hands down the best finance professor I've ever had. Professor Dutta is the best. 
1. Unlike most professors, Professor Dutta teaches from actual experience in industry
2. Doesn't like to give bad grades. Go meet with him and show effort.
3. Effort, interest, participation > intellect, knowledge. Show that you care, you will get a good grade.
tons of industry experience and genuinely cares about student development in class and beyond

Fantastic professor! He has tremendous industry experience and a strong theoretical background, so his lectures are very informative. He takes time to explain concepts thoroughly and goes through examples where needed. He also relates what we learn in class to his real-world experience. He's very approachable and helpful outside of class as well.
Great Professor! Very emphatetic and an ocean of knowledge.

The professor is very knowledgeable and knows his subject really well. He speaks not only from a technical perspective, but also from a practical viewpoint which makes the course unique and informative.

Prof Dutta brings excellent insights from his industry experience and shares real-world practices in Valuation. I would highly recommend his classes if you are into strengthening the conceptual and technical aspects of finance.

- Random extra credit in class and let the students he likes answer it first, this also applies to the participation credit  
-  Very unorganized lectures, may be lost during the lecture with technical difficulties or confusion
-  Office hour will get randomly cancelled or removed

Nice person, but will not recommend due to teaching quality

Professor Dutta is exceptionally knowledgeable about all the subjects he teaches. He has real world experience and often references anecdotes from his time working in the industry. He is approachable during office hours and is great at answering questions and working through solutions. 10/10 Professor, would recommend anyone take a class with him.
Prof Dutta is the Lebron James of Finance Professors! Absolutely could not recommend him more - my favorite ever professor at washu, very fair with his grades and really values class participation.
Incredibly experienced professor, who teaches you so many things about the industry. He is a very fair professor and wants see you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor knows a lot and really enjoys what he teaches about. He sometimes goes on tangents and could be more clear, but he will take the time to answer questions if needed and make sure the class understands everything. If you didn't do well in FIN 441, much of what was covered there will be reviewed in the first couple weeks in this class.

Overall, he is a great professor that combines lecture with his personal experience from the years he worked at IBD and restructuring. The lectures are full of anecdotes and pact with knowledge at the same time. The class puts emphasis on both group case studies and weekly open-book, open-classmate quizzes.

No guidance was provided on HW, and questions were set up to trick you.  Avoid this professor at all costs.  Basically, you're teaching yourself throughout the semester which makes things very stressful.

Lectures are exact copies of the textbook with the same examples and no further explanation.  Homework is often solved wrong, and when correct, solutions are hard to follow.  Cases are open-ended but graded with a rubric looking for very specific things, making it easy to lose random points.  Overall a good guy, but easier to just teach yourself.

DO NOT TAKE HUMAN GENETICS. Duncan does not show up to his OH bc he simply FORGETS about it. He has not responded to most of my emails and does not have clear grading criteria. Average is a 60 for the class although tests have curves. The TAs are not helpful and the graders takes FOREVER to grade. Also he missed the last day to submit final grades

Biol324 had a ton of guest lectures, but Duncan was pretty good about taking the information that they gave us and translating it into an exam that wasn't impossible. All slides get posted online so going to class isn't required. He seemed a little scatter-brained at times but is a good professor overall
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Especially after taking Bio 2960 at WashU, having Duncan as a bio professor was so refreshing. He was MUCH clearer than any of the other bio professors I had and he wrote on the board rather than relying on powerpoint slides, which made taking notes much easier. Tests are straightforward, easy to know what to expect.
This class was ridiculous but he made it much better.

Awesome dude, he is really into the whole drosophila thing. He may not care too much about you as an individual but he clearly loves what he is teaching and tries really hard to communicate the information thoroughly and clearly. Exams are hard but what do you expect from an premed intro class at at washu?
lectures are scattered, doesn't explain key concepts, struggled to find help, tests are ridiculous, worst class i've taken at WUSTL.
Made introductory bio way too hard.

Duncan is kind of all over the place with notes; it can be very unclear what he is talking about in class at times, even if you've done the reading in the textbook. The textbook isn't very helpful most of the time; it doesn't go nearly as in depth as class. I went through this class by basically teaching myself and going to TA hours a lot.
He's fantastic! Though, at times, not the most exciting lecturer, he teaches interesting material and is great at answering questions. I definitely recommend taking his class!

As unhelpful as a professor gets. I took the class this Summer, I emailed him to set up a meeting time because I didn't understand the material, and he responded with a class-wide email to direct all questions to the TA (who was fabulous, but she couldn't help me as much as he could have.)I highly dislike Dr. Duncan, Larson is better in every way.

Duncan can be dry and his notes sort of scattered. That being said, if you really understand his notes and the problem sets, the exams are doable, though there is always that hard question no one gets. He's not the most riveting, but once I took the time to actually understand his lectures by going over the notes, I found his exams much easier.

Duncan makes the pretty dry material seem slightly interesting. But watch out; he writes frustratingly difficult exams and just doing problem sets won't save you. Another weed-out similar to 2960 and many premeds will cry.

Restored my interest in Bio. It was a pleasure to go to lecture every day. He is a lot tougher than Larson, which is why some reviewers say they like Larson better, but he was way more interesting. Tests were conceptual. Don't bother memorizing old exams because he'll write new curveballs. Make sure to UNDERSTAND the problem sets.

Very interesting lecturer. Sometimes dry and slow but cares a lot for the class. Lectures go through basics and problems go through mediums. Tests are where you have to really think using what you already learned and worked on. Don't read the book unless you don't understand basic concepts... Work the problem sets over 2x w/o looking at answers.
Even though the class wasn't easy, Duncan taught the material very well
Very dry lecturer. Runs through material without really explaining. Writes difficult tests that try to trip you up.

He sounds exactly like Milton from Office Space.  That being said, at first I found him to be a pretty boring prof.  However, as the class progressed his lectures got more interesting.  He really cared about the class, and helped students understand the issues of genetics that affect all of us.

Very good at explaining topics- I think some students overlook that due to the difficulty of genetics itself.  Is surprisingly funny at random times.  Exams are difficult, but you don't need to read the book unless you don't understand lectures.
Very interesting material, tests are difficult.
Very****ty lectures. Repulsive voice.
Utterly incomprehensible. Dunno why he is still teaching.
He taught the first half of the course quite well and his exams are manageable. Only the materials covered in class will be covered in the exam so studying the notes is enough for the exams.

A good professor. He made genetics much more interesting than I thought it would be. Exam questions are difficult, but generally based on problem sets and similar to previous exams. Understand the problem sets and you should do well.

Pretty dull lectures, but he does cover the material on the exams.  However, the problem sets were very important to learning what he wanted to teach.  I didn't get enough understanding out of lecture to actually do the problem sets.
A very solid professor: lectures are always well-planned and clearly presented.  Sometimes a dull lecturer, but his sense of humor occasionally shows itself.  His exams are tough, but not unfair.
Good professor, seemed that he liked being there teaching, taught the subject well and made it remotely interesting
Duncan is the man! He told us to not give up when attempting to have children, even after a miscarriage. And he passed out at his wife's amniocentesis!
Cares a lot for his students and makes class interesting.  He is a great professor.
listen to him say echinus cut on streamin video. I liked him alot better than templeton.
Ba-DuncaDunk Slam-Duncan
Dr. Duncan is a very good lecturer, and I learned genetics very well. Now in medical school, I'm finding what he taught me very useful.
No Comments

Duncan and I are cool even though I think he infected me with his evil demon cough (don't sit too close). He makes some interesting comments and asides.  To do well all you need are class notes and problem sets. Duncan r0x0rz.
monotone voice
Bad problem sets, quizzes unfair.
I liked him.
Way to make biology ten times more complicated than it actually is - read the book, do the problem sets, read the lecture notes, but don't go to lecture.

Duncan was disorganized and made me fall asleep.  Maybe some of that is because the material itself is boring, but the guy isn't particularly energizing either.  Don't expect the homework and lectures to prepare you very well for the exams.  Templeton's half is better.
I liked this class, and I thought Duncan was funny - definitely don't ever read the textbook, just do the problem sets and you'll be good to go
Little that Duncan says makes sense, I had to learn from the book and the labs. The worst prof Ive had yet.
horrible experience. this person is very full of himself and does a poor job of teaching. his homework assignments had nothing to do with what was discussed in class and the exams were the same
Pretty boring, not good at explaining the material. Usually I'd read the book in these cases, but the textbook for this class is absolutely horrible.
exams were difficult, means were very low--granted it's a "weed-out" course.  however, i've done the homeworks and reading, attended every (painfully boring) lecture.  boo.
very ineffective and boring professor
Pretty hard tests, but he has the best lectures that I've ever had at WashU.
Most redeeming quality is that he deemed textbook to be unnecessary.  Low class-wide test scores were something he blamed on the students, rather than his teaching.  Very self-centered.

Really enjoyed Music Cognition. Beware to all who sign up, this is a music class, but that is not a bad thing. As a psychology major, I really enjoyed it. The professor was really flexible about late work. :)

Music Cognition was ridiculously easy. You had to participate and submit 3 short papers. He definitely cares and is clearly nice and passionate, but the class can be dull. However, it applies as a philosophy req for PNP and is a solid and very easy class. Helps if you are interested in music.

Duane tries his best to capture the interest of the class but the content of the course (mainly academic papers) and his disposition (nice, tries to be funny, not exactly commanding) leave a lot to be desired. He's truly happy to help out whoever needs it and answer questions but doesn't really get the chance when half the class is asleep.

Tries to make class engaging but is sometimes difficult to keep understanding and interest if you're not into technical parts of music. Beginning of Music Cognition class is super great, but gets less and less interesting. Duane does lots of in class examples and exercises though so it's pretty interactive
Professor Duncan is passionate about teaching and mentorship. He cares about his students, is incredibly knowledgeable, and will be a lifelong mentor if you get to know him.
Professor Duncan is one of the best professors I have had at this school. he really cares about his students and if you try and participate the class is easy.

Prof Duncan is actually the best. He is super knowledgable about the politics of education and he really wants everyone in his class to be interested in the subject as well. He is super relaxed about deadlines, and pretty much everything for that matter, and he understands that your not just a student but also a human being. 10/10 recommend.

Professor Duncan is absolutely incredible. He changed my life and the passion he has for what he teaches is contagious. His classroom is a forum in which he encourages ALL to speak their mind and he literally tells you what you need to do to get an "A+++" in the class. Use your TA if you have specific questions- he works very closely with them.

Professor Duncan can be very engaging when students show high levels of interest in the material. He brings an abundance of energy to the classroom and prompts meaningful discussions. The classes I have taken with him were among my favorites at Washington University.

Literally the worst professor I have ever experienced. We had class once a week at 4. He cancelled two for no reason and just didn't show up to one of them. He was super lazy, never responded to emails and turned our grades in 2 months late. I set up a meeting with him to discuss a paper and he didn't show TWICE! I would avoid his classes.

I took his Intro to AFAS class. Prof. Duncan is a cool guy, who truly cares about his students. But he often seems a disorganized and takes forever to grade and hand back exams and papers. His class isn't easy, but he does offer a lot of extra credit. Very funny and down to earth. Overall, great class.
Amazing instructor.  Expect to put in work however the rewards are great.

A fantastic professor who truly cares about his students.  The wonderful thing about his class is that the material is predicated upon the discussions we have in class.  In this way he tailors the immensely broad topic of African-American studies to the needs and interests of his class.  This makes the class extremely relevant and entertaining.
Speaks his opinions and rarely on facts. Doesen't take any interest  in his students and never knew my name by the end of the semester. Boring and ignorant.

Extremely biased and only pays attention to certain groups of people in class. A lot of reading. Says a lot of things that later classes have disputed and proved wrong. Couldn't stand this class, so dropped it and will take somewhere else. Turned what could be a good class to pure torture.

I took his Ebonics class, and it was immensely enlightening. He really changed my worldview, and increased my critical thinking levels ten-fold. Take a class with him and increase your intellectual analysis. Just remember to participate and write REALLY well.
The most fun you'll have while learning

Easily the best prof I've ever had. I took two classes with Garrett and felt constantly engaged and constantly amazed by the amount of thought that was expected of me and that he stimulated in me. A truly amazing individual!!!
Professor Duncan is an amazing man.  He will push you to the limit and challenge you with his work, but it is all worth it.  Take a class with Duncan and you are promised a fulfilled education.
absolutely brilliant.  do your part and you'll learn a lot.  he expects a lot but it's worth it

great prof, great course. don't ****him off... Lectures need to be more structued. He does have structure but then all lectures stray, which half of the time is cool and the other half is less interesting. Papers graded fairly. don't be late
No Comments
No Comments

This is an absolutely amazing man! You MUST take a class with him. They are engaging and informative. He'll require work from you, but he'll give you back just as much if not more than you put in. Exams are usually take homes.
She was super helpful throughout the class and was clearly excited about what she was teaching.
Professor Duchek is simply amazing and gives incredible lectures. I always look forward to coming to her class because of the high energy she has and her genuine love for developmental psychology.

Professor Duchek is a great professor. Her unit of Psych 100B was really interesting and fun. She is super smart, but also a really nice and caring person. No need to read the textbook if you go to class and take notes. The exam wasn't too bad, but it was harder than the other Psych 100B professors' exams.

The examples she gave in class - often anecdotes and videos - are funny and representative of concepts. Lectures clear and engaging. Most exam-relevant info are in her lectures so don't skip classes. Makes clear what material is important and what is not, very helpful sample questions provided! Humorous in class and warm in office hours.

LOVE her and her lectures are so interesting. You HAVE to go to class because her lecture slides are pretty bare, so take notes on what she says in lecture.
