Tests are kind of tricky, but once you get the hang of it they aren't too bad. If you can take a class with Duchek, DO IT. She cares so much about her students and is such a funny, warm person.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Duchek is great! She is genuinely nice person who wants her students to understand the concepts she is teaching. However a lot of people go into dev psych thinking they won't have to work and quickly find out this class involves a fair amount of studying. If you are willing to do the work, I 10/10 recommend Duchek!
Amazing professor! Would definitely recommend taking one of her classes soon if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Duchek is sweet and a great professor. Had her for 321 & Intro. She definitely cares about her students. Tests are heavily based on lecture, so showing up to class is worth it. If there is something on the test that was not covered in lecture, she will be specific about it. Tests are pretty hard and require lots of memorization & studying to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I can't speak highly enough of her... a truly phenomenal professor. Easily one of WashU's best.
I wish I could take every psychology class with Professor Duchek, she is a real gem. Best psychology class I have ever had at WashU! I can't rave about her enough.

Prof. Duchek is a fantastic professor! She is engaging and takes care to try and learn as many names as possible in 200-300 person classes. She's incredibly kind and her lectures are fun too! She even brought in multiple times (for developmental psych) some colleague's children for us to play cognitive games with in front of the class!

This woman is incredible! She makes expectations clear, so studying for her tests is very straightforward. She presents the material in a super engaging way so that you remember her anecdotes and thus the material. She is a wonderful educator, if you get the chance to take her class, do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Duchek is by far the best professor I have ever had. Her class was my favorite throughout my college experience thus far and if I could take it again I would. She is a great lecturer and her tests are extremely straight forward. If you pay attention (which isn't hard in her class) you will be just fine! Love love love Jan Duchek

Clear lectures and expectations. Lectures are emphasized over reading the textbook (you only have to read some parts of the book), i.e. definitely have to go to lecture. The easiest prof out of Sommers and Lambert. She's also a nice person!

I can't rave about Professor Duchek enough! She really is fantastic. If you have the chance, take any class with her. She explains things so clearly. She really is there for you and wants to make sure you understand the material. She is a dynamic lecturer who makes boring lectures interesting by adding personal stories to narrate her lectures.
Really engaging lectures, very clear in what she expects, connects with students easily. Very nice outside of class. The type of person who will get you hooked on Psychology.

Prof. Duchek is engaging, exciting, and well prepared during every single class.  She keeps the material relevant and interesting and makes a point to get to know students' names.  All the exam questions are from lecture and when they're not she tells you exactly where to look in the textbook.

Duchek is my favorite professor I've had at WashU so far. She is incredibly sweet, an engaging lecturer, and a fair test writer. Her tests are very straight forward and always from the class notes. If there is going to be a question on the test that was not discussed in class, she'll tell you the exact paragraph to read in the textbook.
Made the psych fun and interesting, and presented information very clearly. The tests are extremely hard, but it's worth it to have her and take this class
Funny and passionate professor. Class goes by pretty fast with lots of video clips and she sometimes brings in babies. Warning...tests are hard.

Duchek is really funny and gives you a lot of life lessons throughout class. Her lectures are very clear and she often has great clips to add to it. The hours went by so fast, the class was thrilling. Take Dev Psych it's the best. Exams are hard though, but worth it.

Her lectures are fast-paced but very clear and informative. If you have all the lecture notes, you will be able to get good marks on the exam but there are some questions on her exams which test random facts from the textbook! I learnt a lot in this class and Professor Duchek is very kind and approachable.
Duchek is one of the sweetest and helpful professors at Wash U. She genuinely cares about her students. However, her exams are really hard.
Great teacher and person! She made a mandatory psychology course interesting and is helpful in any way she can be. Her slight humor makes class fun. Textbook is not needed.
Funny, engaging.  Sometimes lectures drift into interesting, but inconsequential discussions.  Great intro course.
Great to learn from her, tied off course very well

Duchek is an amazing woman and a fabulous teacher.  She keeps the entire class engaged and is hilarious.  She makes the already interesting material even better and makes you want to come to class.  The tests are a little bit hard but totally worth it!
Best dressed
The best of the 3 teachers. Entertaining. Knowledgeable. I liked her a lot.

I liked the class. Thought the lectures were very helpful and entertaining. Duchek very knowledgeable in area and could answer questions easily which was nice. Only complaint is that the tests were kind of ambigious and a little too nit-picky with the two of the above, none of the above, etc. Overall though, a good learning experience.

Great teacher.  Going to her class was the higlight of my day.  She is very funny and makes the class very interesting.  If you study the material the tests aren't too bad.  I can't recommend her highly enough.

I was actually excited to go to this class every day.  She is a great teacher--very approachable.  And I didn't think her tests were that bad at all.  Since it's developmental psych, she brings in babies before each test, which is great!

She was an alright teacher, my least favorite of the three though. Her lectures, though pretty well done, strayed very far away from the course material and had some irrelevant personal stories mixed in. I just hated her tests. By the far the hardest. She tested mostly on little details and facts.
Duchek was the hardest of the three, but she was my favorite.  Her lectures were great, and she made things entertaining.
Tests unnecessarily tricky, but enjoyed her lectures most.  Good, clear teacher in lecture.

I thought she was the best of the professor rotation for the class, but her exam too did not reflect what I had learned. I did really like that she was the expert on the section she taught, though, and look forward to more classes with her.
Professor Duchek is awesome! Take every class she offers
Looked forward to her lectures!
So helpful and so nice. She's the best.
good, clear teacher.
My favorite of the 3 teachers.  Very interesting and really knows her stuff.  Funny and makes the class enjoyable.
very interesting lectures
i didn't like her...she had an annoying voice and told irrelevent stories...plus i didn't learn much from her
Great class, wonderful teacher!
great teacher, explains everything clearly and is interesting.

The best prof. that I have ever had! I have had intro, developmental, and experimental psych with her. She made all 3 very interesting. She really cares for her students and is always willing to help. You have to take one of her classes sometime at Wash U.
My favorite of the three 100B teachers.  She made class fun.  She makes me want to take developemental or abnormal psych.
No Comments
Agree with the first comment, really involved and engaging with the class.  GREAT prof and fun to have.  Take ANYthing with her!

One of the best teachers I've ever had. Interesting, knowledgeable, cares about students, funny, well organized. TAKE ANYTHING WITH HER THAT YOU POSSIBLY CAN (ex: intro to psych, experimental psych, developmental psych)

The most kind and knowledgeable professor! I am fortunate that I took a class with him. I wish I had taken more of his classes earlier. Attendance is not compulsory, but please make sure you are familiar with all the homework. He is very responsive if you have any questions.

SEX/UAL PRE/DATOR 
CHECK THE NEWS 
DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!

Has behaved inappropriately towards female students historically (see several news articles available online for more information) and is under investigation for SA. Do not attend his class, protest his presence and stand with survivors.
He has been accused of SAing over 7 girls - stay away!!! He was put on leave and now is back.

Prof. Dybvig is a legend in financial academia and practice. His knowledge base is vast and he is up-to-the-minute in his currency on any topic in securities valuation, portfolio theory, and corporate finance.  He is a treasure to WUSTL and an invaluable resource for any student with the foresight to utilize his knowledge.  Seize the opportunity!

An... interesting? guy. I can't say he's a good teacher, though. His lecture style is EXTREMELY dull, but he definitely knows his stuff. Problem was nobody took the class seriously, & so I learned nothing.  If you're looking to learn a lot,  find a different class, or be prepared to go very out of your way to engage him in (or out of) class.

I took Feminist Research Methodologies and it was probably my least favorite class in the entire WGSS department at Wash U. Prof. Dzubak is no doubt very smart and knows what she's talking about, but she is not very accommodating whatsoever and has due dates at weird times on the weekend. Only take this class if you need to!

reviews.comment: This class is the intro-to-your-thesis class, and I actually enjoyed it because I was able to develop my project. But, if you're not too passionate about your topic, you probably shouldn't take this class; she wants people to put in the effort as if you're going to write a thesis, so if you won't, it's a lot harder to care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: No Comments
No Comments
Earleywine can teach well but was incredibly hard to get a hold of during office hours.

The most fabulous writing teacher in the universe.  This writer truly understands the art of teaching fiction writing . . . and there is no better instructor in any MFA program in the U.S.  If you want to write, Robert Earleywine is your man.

great professor in class- gave great readings and great feedback- not very willing to help outside of the classroom though- said he'd happily write recommendations for me, but then dragged his feet and acted like I was asking for his kidney
Very, very helpful. Class is engaging. Very funny in class. Can be intimidating at first, but you quickly learn he's got a big heart. A lot of fun!

Definitely knows his stuff, but sometimes hard to understand. He really has a passion for what he is teaching. Only complaint is that he really doesn't seem to care about students on a personal level, more interested in career.
Very, very average- probably not at his best in a large lecture class.
Brilliant, engaging, very student-centered.

definitely a very smart guy with very high expectations.  often aloof, and wont hesitate to tear you to bits if he thinks your argument deserves it.  once had a grading conflict with him and he was *very* unsympathetic, even confrontational.
No Comments
Had him back in the mid '80s. Still think he was one of my best profs. He was on my master's thesis committee. My only complaint, he was pretty aloof. Maybe that was shyness.
No Comments
Lazy, lazy, lazy

very nice guy, understanding of conflicts with due dates, incredibly tough grader - don't be fooled b/c it's children's lit. sparks intelligent thought by tearing arguments to shreds. know what you're talking about and eliminate holes before speaking.

Interesting professor. Gives constructive feedback and encourages student. Sometimes gives readings out and make people take notes for homework. The drawing homework he gives out is generally time consuming.

Very difficult if you are not an art major or good at art. I did every assignment but got a B as I was clearly the worst in the class. Still quite an understanding and helpful guy, but do not expect an A just for doing the assignments.
Took for Portfolio Plus. Early is a fair grader and caring to students of different art levels.
Had him during the Portfolio Plus summer program as our drawing professor and was incredibly helpful and respectful.

Professor Early has a very logical and formal approach to teaching drawing which may not be the most engaging format for some students. However, I found his class to be very helpful in building upon my abilities as an artist and designer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I mean, who doesn't like John? He's the most approachable professor in Sam Fox in my opinion. I always enjoyed my time in his class.

One of my fav professors - take his class if your schedule permits! I met over three people who have taken his classes in the past, and once they heard I'm taking John's class they all congratulated me. Always answer every email outside class. Organized. Fun projects with a sense of accomplishment. Helpful and considerate. Absolutely fair grader.

I had 2D design with John and he really pushed us to think about design concepts. His projects force you to think critically and he emphasizes process. His 3 projects each took about 1-2 months to complete, though we were all pressed for time during the week of the deadline. Good about replying to emails. Pretty ok feedback. Fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I think John is famous for being nice. He gives good feedbacks even after class, and he's always accessible if you email him with any questions. He is caring and fair towards every student. His projects are interesting and inspiring. It's a pleasure to take his classes; I've already signed up for another drawing class that he'll teach next year.

He's very clear on what he wants to see from the projects he gives out- but even if you stick with what you want, as in not take his advice, he still respects you and your work. He's very enthusiastic about teaching and has a chill personality.

I really like John's class because he gave us a lot of freedom during the creative process but guided us in the right direction. He gave us a lot of time for each project which made it easier to make a complete piece in the end. would recommend

He thinks art can be taught through only logic and the whole time in his class it felt like math. Step A, Step B, and so forth. I just really did not like his teaching style. Many other professors I had were on the contrary. It was just him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: John's very into creative process, his feedback is good if you're willing to talk to him as you work (not the night before). Sometimes John can change his mind on you which is confusing, so be willing to change your ideas as well. Be ready to talk about your work. You really get out of the class what you put into it. Overall John's great. #lovejohn

The projects we did were extremely limiting and elementary. They actually  made me like art even less because they took a lot of work and were a huge chore with little to no personal voice/exploration. His grading criteria is extremely questionable and not consistent. Vague feedback. Likes concepts that are very elementary and overdone. Hated it

John always helped me pick out little mistakes and suggest changes that helped make my pieces much better. He is very supportive of students of all skill levels, and can help make even a beginner student an amazing artist.

John is eager to help students make their projects more successful, but often his advice is rather vague and unwelcome at first. But once you start thinking about it and applying it to your project, all becomes clear and you find yourself with an amazing end product.

Would highly recommend him as a teacher! I loved his 2D design class, and I learned a lot from him. If you ask questions and use the in-class work days he gives you to check in with him you won't have a problem. Missing critiques will kill your grades. The assignments can take awhile, but overall the workload is reasonable. Expect to work hard.

John is a pretty good professor but can be ambiguous with his instructions, which can be tough because he can be very particular about what he expects in a project. If you are clearly putting a lot of effort in and ask lots of questions, you will do well. Projects can be complex but he gives a very reasonable amount of time to complete them.

I love John!!He is amazing! Though sometimes he is ambiguous( well he kindda likes subtle things and is too nice to say bad things) which confuses people, he is a great instructor who is there for you! And the class was really interesting!

I had John for 2-D design, and he was a really relatable, easy to interact with professor.  He is really engaged with his students and can be helpful in developing ideas and working through your process.  It can be a little hard to understand how to succeedget an A on a project, and his lectures on design concepts can be a little simplistic.

John tells you what you don't want to hear, which can be hard but usually results in a better final work. He doesn't really take into consideration how much time you've devoted to a piece, and will try to steer you in another direction if he doesn't like where you're going. Sometimes it can get frustrating but you definitely learn a lot from it.

Hardcore, real world experience.  Walked us through his own very public background and what he learned, then brought in speakers to do the same.  Amazed that his "Iron Laws" kept coming up - both in class and outside.  I started the class like one of my friend - wanting to drop and then stuck with it and learned so much.  My friend missed out.

"PW" acted as more of a coach than a traditional Professor.  He clearly turned his class into a 'working lab' for professional success using the topic of Entrepreneurship.  I credit my job interview success with his class - far more practical than any others I have taken.

Prof.  Weinhaus is a mix of academic insight (his "Iron Laws"), real world experience, and total one-on-one attention to our individual performances.  He gave extra credit  just w/in our grasp, intended to lead us toward further improvement.  He constantly told us that he drove us so hard so that he knew he could rely on us "in the real world."

A very sweet man. Sure, he covers twelve semesters' worth of material in a single class. Sure, his tests are so ridiculous that 40/100 curves to a B. And sure, you'll be pulling all-nighters on a weekly basis in order to get any homework points at all. But he wants to help you, and he wants you to succeed-- so go to office hours and it'll be okay.

In this 1st-course on matrix algebra, Prof. Wilson refused to give any concrete examples or even draw an actual matrix with actual numbers. He came into every lecture without any notes and just recited proofs from his head. He spent much of office hours complaining about how close-minded students who don?t understand him are-not very helpful IMO.
Might not be the most exciting lecturer, but extremely helpful prof who really cares about his students.

Possibly the worst teacher I've ever had. Class notes are worthless, impossible to follow, and tests are an extremely poor representation of what we learned. No outside help available and lectures are a drag. Required class but I would put it off to avoid having him teach it.

Apparently, anyone can teach at a prestigious university today. Over complicates material which should not be too difficult.  No one will score well on his scale.  Lectures are useless; spends time bashing text (which he chose) or lulling us to sleep. Tests in no way resemble the assigned homework (or chapters which they're suppose to be over.)
Nice, but tends to drone on in lectures.

ewww, I dont know who said that he is the best teacher at Wash U, but that is ridiculous.  Unless you're quick at math, he's incredibly hard to follow...  Larry Lin, the TA, on the other hand, is Hot, helpful, and fun.  Overall, not the best class, but it's required, whatcha gonna do?

Difficult professor who does not empathize with students. Rather, he stubbornly sticks to his conviction on teaching abstract concepts that kids taking B-School Calc 2 do not need. Larry, the TA, is the reason the course is livable. Without him, this course would be an utter disaster.

The class is tough no matter who teaches it, but his office hours are extremely helpful.  You will cry if you miss them.  A lot.  And then your grade will suffer for it.  But with office hours, everything is better, and understandable.
Prof. Wilson is the best math professor at Wash U
good teacher, very, very helpful to students who seek help
good guy who will listen and help if you approach him
One of the best.
His inability/unwillingnesss (which, I'm not sure) to teach calculus concepts outside of the book makes you want to cry.  Nice fella, though.  Office hours VERY helpful.
A bit confusing and confrontational when questioned.  Moves at an average pace all the time, not slowing down when students need help, not speeding up when they do not.
Wonderful teacher
Boring and Confusing

as long as you know what is on the slides, you should be fine on the exam. does show videos and gives examples, but sometimes what she said felt very memorized and less like she was teaching in the moment.
Her music at the beginning of class is best part. She comes across as kind and helpful in class, but in office hours she seems annoyed and cold.

Willroth was a good professor, I just didn't like how she wrote her tests. She didn't provide many practice questions unlike Bergstrom, which made it difficult to properly prepare for the tests. On top of that, the test questions were worded differently so it was harder to succeed compared to her practice exams. She's cool though.

Dr. Willroth was a great lecturer! I found her lectures to be engaging (especially with the Think Pair Shares), and she clearly outlined what would be tested on exams. The slides didn't contain everything mentioned in class, so you had to take notes.
She's a good professor, just not very enthusiastic. If you can take the goat Brian Bergstrom, take Berg. Anyways a great class, very doable exams, interesting slides.

Willroth always gave a very intellectual vibe! Her lectures were very clear, informative, empirical, and well-prepared. That said, compared to Bergstrom, her exam was a little more tricky, yet still manageable. Overall, though, she is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not have good slides.

Professor Willroth makes it clear on what will be tested through her learning goals on slides. You don't need to read the textbook. She provides practice quizzes and resources to aid learning. You can skip her classes and just look at slides she posts  and you will still do fine.
Super nice and played music in the beginning of class. Test was reasonable and there was nothing super surprising on it. Class could be super easy if you just stay on top of your notes and work.
Very solid. No complaints-- she gave review questions and was very clear about what would be on the exam. Engaging lectures too.

She was fine, but my least favorite of the three intro psych professors. Her lectures were very similar to the textbook so if you read it you don't feel like you need to come to class. I like how she plays music at the start of each class, she goes at a good pace and is happy to answer any questions.
Very organized and clear about what to expect on quizzes. Would definitely take a class with her again

Very clear with what content will be on the quiz (has learning goals and practice quiz questions after each lesson). Ultimately cares about the success of her students and very open to feedback (especially during the mid-semester evaluations). Lectures are kinda dry.

Pretty easy. Out of the three intro psych professors for the fall course, she had arguably the easiest quizzes. She also took student feedback into account and incorporated more quiz practice in class. Always was clear about what would be on the quiz. Lectures were boring sometimes.

Very clear with what will we will be tested on. Good lecturer but sometimes hard to pay attention. Ultimately easy class and quizzes are mostly based on the lectures so you don't really need to read the textbook.
Prof Willroth was a good lecturer.  Her quizzes where clearly written and easy to understand.  She played music at the beginning of class which was fun.

Professor Emily Willroth was awesome, and her lectures were amazing, and my only critique is her slides for her lectures were a little text-heavy but theyre posted every week so you can review them, so its not hard to do good in the course

Dr. Willroth is a decent lecturer. She has good pacing and presents the material in a clear and digestible way. She is also pretty good at writing quizzes--the questions felt fair and were not too confusingly worded. She played music at the beginning of class, which was nice. Overall, the atmosphere was comfortable whenever she was lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wroblewski is a reliable professor with clear expectations and grading criteria. Although lectures can be a little dry sometimes, she is approachable, flexible, and considerate of her students. She also provides really thorough study guides for exams which is super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ANTHRO 3876 Darwin and Doctors: Evolutionary Medicine and Health: Best professor/class ever (& Science GPA)! You learn medicine from evolutionary anatomy/purpose & function of body parts & how we got them, sex/pregnancy, cancer, genetics, physiology, sleep, addiction, stress/depression, nutrition/diet, microbio, global health! Straightforward exams
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wroblewski was an amazing professor! She was kind and accessible to me outside of class and with my disability accommodations. Her lectures were not mandatory and they were interesting. She puts all material on Canvas including lecture videos. We only had exams and they were open note and available for a full 24 hours. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice person, not my favorite lecturer. Readings done outside of class, and she walks through problems in class. Then we work as a group for quizzes, and the problems were hard. Lectures weren't super exciting and engaging. Required class so you'll have to take it, just beware of the amount of outside the class learning you'll have to do.

Professor Boyd was one of my favorite professors at WashU. Her fluid dynamics course was amazing. A TA once rushed through the grading process of one of my tests and gave me well below what I deserved. I showed professor Boyd my work and she was extremely caring and raised my grade. Overall awesome professor.

Ok teacher. Tests aren't too hard but the in class reading quizzes are hard. She assigns reading for homework so she barely teaches in class and just has us do questions which is okay practice. The readings can range from 20-60 pages of heavy textbook content and the reading guide is useless. Part of ur grade is also determined by your group
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Boyd is one of the best professors I have ever had. She provides amazing lecture materials and reading guides. Class time was spent solving problems in groups which was useful when identifying what I needed help with. Dr. Boyd is so helpful and her expectations are reasonable, so if you put forth an honest effort, you can do well. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Boyd is amazing. She is good at explaining tricky concepts and very receptive to individual questions. She provides very thorough course materials, including reading guides and practice problems. The homework assignments are pretty reasonable as well. 10/10 would recommend.

She is mainly reasonable and wants to help you. She is a nice lady. But she is the worst professor, she records her lectures by reading off of her notes and really skips many concepts and steps. Her AI pretty much teaches 90% of material. She will drop you an hour long lectures that you need to take notes on on the same day that it is due.
She's an absolute gem of a professor, definitely among the top three I've had at WashU

Emily Guignon is the best French teacher I've ever had.  She has an incredible flair for making texts, vocab, and even verbs memorable, but you have to do the work of studying yourself. People on this page complaining about this and that clearly put nothing into her class.   What made you think she or anyone else would spoon-feed you Gerber?

Guignon's teaching style is confused and disorganized. I agree that she jumps from topic to topic, and an hour class seems to drag on for forever. Tests and quizzes aren't too hard though, but the work becomes tedious, and she is not very helpful. From what I here, it's also really hard to meet with her outside of class.
I stared at the clock the whole time. Such a boring class, in my opinion. Other people seemed to like her a little better than I did, though. (I accidentally posted this under 307, but I took 201.)
I stared at the clock the whole time. Such a boring class, in my opinion. (Other people seemed to like her a little better than I did, though.)

Guignon is continuously aggravatingly disorganized and tends to jumps from one subject to another while diverging on various unrelated tangents every 5 minutes. She knows her stuff very well though and is usually exceedingly helpful if you ask questions, especially if you stay after or go to her hours.
Mme Guignon is super disorganized and we rarely stuck to the syllabus, but otherwise she's very nice and sweet.

This teacher was the most disorganized one I have had in four years at Wash U.  She never had a class plan, which made us fall behind often, but then she would try to catch up to the syllabus, meanwhile leaving entire acts of plays and entire poems undiscussed after they were assigned readings.  It was REALLY frustrating. Not recommended.
awesome

Love her! She's exciting during class and makes it fun and enjoyable. Very relaxing and conversational. Her quizzes are a little tough sometimes, but there are so many, it's easy to get a decent grade. I'm excited to take 201 with her.

Guignon, while a very nice person, is the most disorganized prof. I've had so far at Wash U. She forgets to bring quizzes on scheduled quiz days (so she makes them up on the spot) and she has been known to misplace papers and tests. Her tests are very difficult, particularly the final.

She is super approachable and really helpful. Class sometimes got a little boring, but I think that was more the nature of the class than her. I really enjoyed having her and look forward to having her again.
Hard tests.
She has a bad reputation but I enjoyed her class as well as getting to know her.  She invited all of her 307 students over for dinner at the end of the semester which was nice.

she is seriously SO sweet. a little disorganized, maybe, but the sweetest woman ever. she's just so nice! i feel like no professors here are like that. and she's a great teacher. it's not one of those classes where you stare at the clock the whole time. you won't regret taking her classes.

He seems like a kind man, but is very scatterbrained and not good to teaching the material. I had to do a lot of studying and teaching myself the material outside of class to do well and thankfully my calculus from high school gave me a solid foundation. His is the last math class I ever took.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is the reason I had to stop taking math classes at WashU. I graduated over 10 years ago, and still remember how awful this man was as a professor. His terrible instruction for both Calc 2 and Intro to Stats left me unprepared to take more advanced courses, so I moved on to other areas of study. If you actually care about learning, AVOID!!!

Spitznagel is your typical tenured professor. He's obviously very interested in the material, but mumbles & is difficult to understand in lecture(I ended up going to 2 lectures max the entire semester). Tests are each work 25% of your final grade, so as long as you self-study from the textbook & know the material, you should be able to get an A

Very nice guy and good at working-statistics. However, he is a terrible professor. He is absent minded in class, tells random stories, and does not teach the material. If you want an A, you better go to all the help sessions and read the book every night to learn the material for yourself, especially since he tests over things not covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Do not take any course with him. I do not think he knows the course materials well and he does not care for his job and respect his students at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Run for your life.
Hard to understand, mumbles words, unfair test questions, avoid at all costs.

tests arent hard. all questions from textbook with the same number so if u solve all questions on textbook you will get an A  i got an A on his 3200 class, but self-taught from the first chapter to the last. I personally think he is not a good lecturer, but his class is OK to get an good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This guy is extremely soft-spoken, doesn't have productive lectures, goes off on thousands of tangents, and has no structure for the class. I personally think the material isn't extremely hard,  but his teaching style hasn't allowed me to learn anything (even though I took a stats class in high school that was very similar). AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was my biggest regret. Stopped going after the first month. I just read 4 chapters on the night before the exam. So yea --- don't take his class unless you hate yourself.
Don't take his classes. Please don't do that to yourself.  He's a nice person, but that sadly does not translate to being able to teach coherently
Can't hear him
He is a great lecturer!
AVOID ALL CLASSES TAUGHT BY HIM

Not a clear lecturer. Mostly goes over homework problems. Doesn't do a good job teaching how to use SAS. Goes on tangents easily, some classes you learn more about the history of the statisticians than the math itself.  Class content and old exams are not good predictors of exam content.

Hands down the worst class I've ever taken at WashU.. The lectures were completely useless as Spitznagel consistently went on tangents. Not to mention, he literally changed the material that would appear on the final 3 days before. Definitely avoid taking any courses taught by him.

Wait a semester and take the class with another professor. Doesn't cover much material in lectures. He just mumbles to himself in lecture and is hard to understand. Also doesn't respond much to emails, so it is hard to get help outside of class. This semester, he also changed the material covered on the last exam 3 days before the actual exam...

He barely explains anything in class except for maybe going through how to do a few of the homework problems.  Other than that he makes no effort to have a lesson for the class and so none of the material from the chapter is explained.  He spends most of the time on SAS (which he doesn't even teach well) and hardly any time on the actual material.

Do not take a class with him. You cannot understand anything he says, and when you can actually understand his words, all he talks about all random tangents. There is not curve and the class is abysmal.
Easy class to do well in if you do all the homework.

Worst professor ever.  0 concepts or syntactical patterns taught in class.  The best thing he does is book problems, but he doesn't explain any of the underlying reasons.   Free documentation for SAS is awful because the  license is so expensive that  everyone uses R , so it's impossible to teach yourself even with the book.

Yes he does have quite an arsenal of amusing vignettes at his disposal, but no, he does not know how to teach statistics. The problem is that there is far to much material in the book, and he tries to cover all of it, and so only ends up explaining a small fraction in class.

This man is the stereotypical embodiment of a tenured professor. He has no incentive to teach well, and it shows. Readings cover far too much material to address in class, not that he tries to anyway. Additionally, the homework assignments all use statistical software (SAS, STATA) but he make no attempt to teach the language of these programs.

A brilliant Renaissance man, & one of the smartest people I have ever known. Absolute tops in his field. I believe he uses the afore-mentioned cartoon references & questions in an attempt to make his points both clear & memorable. Thoughtful, kind, hard-working, & generous with his time.

Huge fan of his. Some may complain that his lectures are boring - but you really have to listen. He has so many anecdotes and stories and jokes and will drop knowledge on you like no other. He's helpful in office hours and the exam questions come from hw. He loves stats and it shows. Sometimes, I can't help but wish that he was my second father...
Taking this class destroyed all interest in Statistics for me for fear that I become as useless and boring as the professor. Do not recommend.

He is a HORRIBLE teacher. I went to class maybe 3 times and I'm getting an A though, because it's completely self taught. Just read the textbook and do the problems. The test questions come straight from the homework.

Extremely easy. The questions were all taken from previous exams and HW problems. He was quite fair. Not necessary to go to class. Just read the book. The textbook we used was fantastic. I went to three lectures and will end up with an A. He's kind of eccentric and not so politically correct, but I don't have a problem with him.

I've heard 3200 is real awful, but 2200 is manageable as long as you DO THE HOMEWORK before the tests. You can try to follow him in lecture because he does occasionally say useful things, but for the most part, he is completely unclear. Just learn from the textbook, do the homework, and you should be fine on the tests.

MISERABLE.  I learned absolutely nothing.  I've been in the class for half a semester and know less about stats than when I started it.  The homework has nothing to do with the class and the tests have nothing to do with lectures or homework.  Save yourself, and pass this one up.

Extremely difficult tests but a very large curve at the end of class. No use in going to class except to get code for computer programs. Lectures are useless and very confusing. Don't expect to learn anything in them.

Does NOT teach well.  Especially in the 3200 class where you are learning programming languages simultaneously.  He will go through examples of code without explaining the how or why of each statistical process.  I suggest taking with another teacher.  He is fair with grading at the end however. It's all on-your-own bookwork if you want to do well.

The worst teacher in every way possible. seriously. you'd think that all the comments made about him couldn't all be completely true. wrong. tests are impossible, class is useless, average final grade is low 70s, and he refuses to curve. STAY AWAY.

Read the book before you go to his class! I actually wanted to drop this class in the first week, but it got better and better once you got used to his way of teaching. Yes, he does skim over the material, but since he is a real statistician, those he touches upon are actually really useful.

Spitznagel is a pretty funny guy, but sometimes he goes on tangents that don't relate to the material. He's not all that helpful in class because he seems to just skim over the material quickly. However, he is answers questions in office hours.  Tests are on the hard side and he doesn't curve, which is very annoying when the final average is a 73%.

Professor Spitznagel is actually a really funny guy, if you understand his sense of humor. He was extremely helpful in office hours and he really does care about his students. He sits on the bench in the math building and will answer any questions you have, even "What is the meaning of life"? I liked him as a teacher.

Be warned:  This is both a stats class and a computer programming class. The only reason to come to class is to get the programming code for the homeworks.  But the exams have nothing to do with that.  He doesn't really teach anything for the exam.  He assigns too many recommended problems and then puts those on the exam.  If you can't finish...
Ed is the worst teacher I have EVER encountered. I learned nothing at all except to hate math. His tests were absurd-- he asked questions about comic strips in the textbook! Unbelievably bad.
aweful.

People give him so much**** that he doesn't deserve.  He makes class much more entertaining than most math classes w his random facts/weird sense of humor, and if you do all your homework and come to class, the tests really aren't too bad.
This man is amazing. Although he may not be the most engaging lecturer, he makes funny random comments that make the class worth going to. He's a good stats teacher, and I'm glad I took the class.

I think he actually teaches with his eyes closed, although it's hard to discover this because his lectures are so unbearable to be at and he actually teaches u nothing, although in his tests he asks u random facts of random jokes he makes in class- he sucks

Not sure where all the negative comments are coming from, he was fantastic for stats. I expected to hate the class, but came out loving it. He works ridiculous hours, so he's easy to find in his office, even at midnight. Having taken stats classes at other universities, I can confidently say he's much better than average.
absolute bullsh*t. his teaching must be the worst in all of WashU.
horrible teacher
probably the worst professor ever- not only was he horrible at teaching, but he was it was impossible to contact him outside of class...do not take any class with him
HORRIBLE I will never again take a class of his. I don't care if he INVENTED stat, he would still suck at teaching it.

He is a very nice guy and is much more helpful if you go in for help.  His teaching is not very clear but you have the second chance on tests which helps you to understand the math and boosts your grade.  Work with your friends!!!

Spitznagel is truly a dedicated teacher who ahs some very innovative methods.  That being said, his style of teaching this course was not a good match AT ALL to the textbook used. Unfortunately a lot of people do not appreciate Spitznagel's dedication.  He is supposedly good for stats though.
blah
too many tangents
Easy class, ****ed strange man

Spitznagel enjoys himself immensely in class, but this should not be mistaken for interest in his students. Be aware that the only funny part of lectures is that he actually thinks he's teaching. It's impossible to teach yourself with the outlines and TAs have trouble with the hw too, so good luck!
Horrible teacher, horrible lectures, weird topics, don't take his class
I found it very difficult to learn from Prof. Spitznagel.
Don't go to class.

It's unfortunate he was teaching calculus because it is clear that stats, not calc, is his expertise. He truly cares about his students and wants them to do well in the class but he is unable to teach calculus well and to keep his students interested in the subject.

I didn't learn anything from Spitznagel, and I went to lecture every day hoping that he would teach for once. He never did. He's a bad lecturer, but he genuinely believes he's teaching calc in an innovative way, and he cares about his students doing well.
He should stick with teaching Stats, not calculus.
terrible teacher, awful class. hated every minute of it

Grade wise, it's a easy class.  You'll have to TRY to fail.  However, the grade doesn't compensate for the ridiculousness of the class.  Every Friday lecturer is incomprehensible, and even the TAs admit it.  However, Spitznagel does appear to care very much about the class, but he doesn't teach.

I stopped going to class after day 3.  Some of the later homework was ridiculously difficult, but as long as you tracked down a TA to show you, the class was pretty simple.  Grading system worked in favor of the students but was really impractical.

very interested in the practical applications of math... this is hard for someone who is just taking the class because they have to, but he tries hard to get you the best grade possible... i like the way his tests are set up and the lab and recitation help your grade
This guy doesn't teach a single thing all semester except for random facts about newton and euler.  His tests are ridiculously easy, don't expect to have to think in a new way.  waste of time
horrible class-doesn't teach but goes off on useless tangents.
Class was an easy A, but what's the point of having students 'write' the exams?

The guy is a terrible lecturer.  Random tangents.  Same thing as the review before, except we are a few weeks from the final and only about 30 percent of the kids show up for lectures.  Thats how bad he is.  BUT the class is easy, so if you take him don't show up and just do the work.

Goes on random tangents in the middle of lecture, so that any information conveyed is disjointed and unuseful.  Only a few weeks from the final, and the first exams are still not fully graded.  Information necessary to HW not conveyed during lectures.
Likes to go on tangents, but a good teacher, and very willing to help out.

Yes he is crazy, yes he talks about a lot of stuff that really doesn't have to do with the MATH per se, but he makes class entertaining and sets up the class so that you CAN SUCCEED-- test system is great.  Worthwhile prof for Calc II

Rambles a lot during lectures, almost no real information is conveyed. His exams are impossibly difficult, not representative of the homework, and no partial credit is given the first time around. Last exam, avg score was 47%!

Kafalenos is certainly a demanding professor, but it's refreshing to have someone who expects you to push yourself. She genuinely cares about her students, and though she has high expectations, she is willing to work with you to help you meet them.

Rather incomprehensible--she has the voice of Miss Fowl from Jimmy Neutron. Kafalenos is clearly very interested in the field of comparative lit, and her excitement shines through in the classroom. She's taught this class for a while, and I wouldn't be surprised if she rigidly formed her analytic opinion of each work examined ages ago. Inflexible.

Difficult class; it is boring because she basically lectures about literary theory the whole time and has a set lesson plan and there's no room for discussion or participation. Her essays are hard and really specific but she just wants you to repeat what she says in class. Nice woman, but often unclear. This class is a requirement for the major.

Honestly, I think that Professor Kafalenos gets an unfair rating here.  Yes she is demanding but it is really refreshing to have a teacher who actually expects us to engage with the material.  She sometimes can be hard to understand but she really knows what she is talking about and does not let unsupported comments stand without explanation.
Most incomprehensible professor I've ever had. It is a mandatory class for the major, but it's miserable. She hates life and wants everyone to be unhappy with her.
painful. necessary for comp lit/comp art majors and doable, but painful. tough grader.

Too old and outdated to teach. Trying to pretend she is talking about important philosophical ideas which easily wins the applause of the bunch of con artists sitting in the class. When will she retire so i can major in Comp Lit again?

She is incredibly smart and really a leader in her field. She may speak kind of funny and look kinda weird, but she knows what shes talking about and she is very nice and helpful. Class was pretty intense though.
She's an old ****
She is nice but very unclear.
No Comments
Considerate, but demanding-- Expect most Wash U students to take big  A s...
Lots of work
Intense teaching style, with the use of cases and practical negotiations.
Prof Elfenbein leads discussions well and is an engaging speaker. It's apparent that she's passionate about the topics she teaches and wants her students to grow as leaders.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hillary leads a class on a topic that is meant to take people out of their comfort zone. This class forced me (a passive by nature) to come to better learn when to confront and challenge situations in order to achieve more favorable win:win scenarios.

Hillary is a very engaging and informative professor. She does a great job of mixing lecture materials with practice in the classroom. You can tell she cares about her students and is a very genuine individual.

Dr. Elfenbein was an amazing professor. I had her for two classes, and I could not have been more impressed. Fantastic lecturer, great sense of humor and an earnest passion to teach. All she expects is that you be there and be engaged.  Anyone who would ever say a cross-word about her is really commenting on their own character .

This week-long Negotiations course was one of the most intense courses I took during my MBA program; however, it was well worth the effort. Hillary does a great job of breaking down the negotiations process and teaching you how to understand the various factors at play. This should be a required course- many business and professional applications.

This course has provided invaluable training for my current management role. Hillary is able to present best-practices for leadership and leadership development that are evidence-based and firmly grounded in organizational behavior research while also teaching the real-life, practical application of such information.
She always showed interesting video clips to support class material, and clearly had a passion for religious studies. Her explanations were easy to understand.
Kravchenko starts out slow, but warms up throughout the semester. Very participation heavy, and many opportunities to discuss. Office hours are helpful and she cares about students.
Very interesting course and many avenues for great discussions
Great and wants studnets to do well.

Not too hard, but easy to lose points fast. Can only miss 7 points total to keep an A. If you want a professor who prays on your downfall, take this class. Never send an email; her response will make you feel terrible about yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I adore Dr. Kravchenko. She's truly one of the most caring professors at WashU, and her class is so interesting. I struggled with a lot of health and personal problems this semester, and she was so understanding and allowed me to complete the work on a timeline that worked for me. Additionally, the course is fascinating and thought provoking,
Not a hard class but I was very unengaged with the material, classmates, and her. Lacked communication and seemed like she did not want to be there most of the time. Interesting content though.

One of the best humanities courses I've taken. You're not forced to participate vocally, which is great for people who hate speaking in discussions (like I do). You can get participation credit by just filling out worksheets she gives out. She very clearly outlines what she wants you to know, pretty interesting class too.

One of my favorite teachers I've ever had! She cares a lot about her students and their understanding. She gives a good amount of reading, but for tests, she gives you everything you need to know and there are no surprises.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The class was okay, though more reading heavy than I expected. The exams can be challenging at first, but once you know what to expect, they're not that bad.

I love Prof. English, even though she challenges us. The exams are not very easy, but once you get used to her style, you can get it. She presents her lectures very well (structured). However, her class is kinda speedy and she wants to cover as many things as possible in her lectures. It's reading-heavy. She is strict but responsible. Go to her OH!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance not mandatory but it's hard to keep up if you miss a lecture because she doesn't post the complete lecture slides online, and then asks about extremely specific details from the lectures on exams. Assigned textbook readings are extremely long.
Her courses are very well structured and organized, but the wording of her exams can be confusing. 30% of exam questions draw from the textbook.

The professor is not accommodating with missing lectures, if you do it is nearly impossible to get the material. Lectures are not recorded and if you miss you are expected to go to office hours just to learn. Tests ask about the most irrelevant details that test your memory more than your understanding of the material. Wish hadn't taken this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class specifically because I'd had such a good experience with Dr. English in a previous class, and my expectations were fully met. She's really engaging and understanding, and having had a weak base in experimental psych she was super helpful in meeting with me to go over questions I had. The final was worth 60% of our final grade tho.

Prof English is an amazing lecturer - she's very engaging and provides fun examples to help students understand the material. To do well in psych of personality, you need to go to lecture and read the textbook because the exams draw from both. You have to work hard to do well but it's interesting and relevant material and I highly recommend it!

Dr. English is for sure one of my favorite professors at Wash U. She adapted the class a lot to help us out with things we noted on our midterm feedback form (namely she included more test prep). She also has some of the most organized lectures, and even though they're an hour and a half I never felt bored in them.

This class is mandatory for psychology majors, so I wasn't expecting it to be fun or interesting. Professor English really tried to make it fun, but the material was really dull. She also went through the material really fast and didn't always explain everything we needed to know for exams.

didn't know what to expect because this was her first year at washu, but she was great! her powerpoints are really clear and great for studying. she definitely tested a lot of material from the textbook (that wasnt discussed in class) but it was awesome how she included lots of videos, activities, and questionnaires in class.
Extremely supportive and great all around professor. Class discussions were always extremely informative and intellectually stimulating. One of the best professors I've had!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Eng is knowledgeable, understanding, encourages creativity, creates great discussion environments and supports students every step of the way, truly caring for their academic and personal growth. His classes are not just intellectually stimulating but also captivating and relevant. You won't regret taking any class with him!

Dr. Eng is one of kindest professors I've had at WashU! Classes are usually short reflections, lectures based on readings, and occasionally short media reviews -- like most humanities classes. He is incredibly supportive of students and their work. Very conscientious grader and understanding if you need to take time off!

Professor Eng is phenomenal. He genuinely cares for every student and is interested in their insights. Participation is a quarter of your grade, but he is understanding if circumstances impact your participation. He provides positive, constructive feedback on papers and allows opportunities for revision. A slay all around. Eternally glad I had him.

Seriously my favorite class that I took the semester that I took this class. Professor Eng is really understanding when it comes to outside circumstances and is flexible on deadlines if you give a good reason. He really encourages a fun discussion space and helps you to understand the gravity of the issues that you discuss.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a super nice guy, gets to know students personally and is available outside of class. Class starts off easy and then picks up, with the last unit being pretty difficult, so start strong at the beginning and you should do well. I wouldn't take this class if you have 0 familiarity w stats but if you know some of the basics you should be good.

I was really disappointed in this class, I had read previous reviews hoping to find a caring professor, but I am still looking. Ted was not helpful with questions on Piazza, even kind of rude at points. You basically have to teach yourself in QPM. Not a great lecturer, left much to be desired. If given a second chance, I would avoid this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ted is the GOAT. Whoever mentions that he is not caring is lying. I took this during a very difficult time in my life and he was there the entire way making sure I was on top of things and got my assignments in. QPM is a bit tough, but Ted's a great professor to help you weather through it.

He might give the facade that he cares a lot about his students, but you would be mistaken. Not a great lecturer and would never actually answer questions. Lots of material on tests and problem sets, you're expected to know, were not discussed in class or in the book. Try to avoid this class, instead, take Data science for politics if possible.

Ted's kind of a legend. Legit the nicest dude around, he's always there to support his students and cares about everyone. He definitely makes you work for it though; QPM is not an easy class, and you've gotta do a lot of learning if you want to succeed. Take CSE 131 or a stats class before QPM if you want to have an easier time. Ted's the GOAT tho.

I just finished the final and because were in Covid it took me 25-30 hours and Im not kidding. DO NOT TAKE THIS IN A PANDEMIC. Thats a mistake you dont make twice. I came in to this zoom class not being able to code and Im leaving the same way. To be perfectly honest because everythings online, if you wanna learn, you gotta teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: An extremely accessible professor who is always open for questions and discussion, especially via Piazza. He responds to Piazza posts + emails quickly. Knows his stuff and a kind soul; he wants students to succeed, does what he can to help. Lectures sometimes drag but material is important to internalize. Lab sections essential for learning coding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures too fast for me to even keep up and there are no recordings. A bit disorganized and this was probably only this class but students would always talk over her in a know-it-all way and she wouldn't do much about it. Sort of specific, but I couldn't really pay attention in class after that. Super interesting material, but poor delivery imo.

Lectures were very, very fast and sometimes hard to follow, but she's generally good at explaining concepts. Things took a while to be graded and it was unclear what we would be tested on, which seemed unnecessary. Often didn't reply to emails, but was accessible during office hours and was also happy to help with the project. Generally good.

Prof Van Engen delivered good lectures and explained the concepts clearly. There are no recorded lectures, so you have to go to class. There is a lot of content covered relatively quickly, but she gives you all of the tools to succeed.

Chill, engaging teacher. Multiple times changed things from syllabus to accommodate class. Lectures get long but you don't need to pay attention(it's interesting stuff tho so you should), just review the slides. Textbook reading not needed, but practice problems for tests are in there. Quizzes every couple weeks but they're easy. No HW. W class.

Van Engen is a great professor! Lectures were engaging and entertaining. Lots of participation from the class share their language experiences. Involves a lot of taking notes, but it's interesting and easy to take notes. Great introductory class to be exposed to different linguistic areas! Lots of quizzes and exams but generally straightforward.

She was a bit tough, but I learned A LOT in phonetics. She is really knowledgable in the field and as a Linguistics major I am glad to have taken this class. She is pretty disorganized, and took very long to grade everything, and it wasn't super clear what was going to be on exams, which was a bit annoying. The course was fast paced, but manageable

Van Engen is not only super knowledgable about linguistics but super sweet and passionate about the field as well! Intro to Linguistics was lecture heavy, but she made the lectures entertaining with jokes and videos of her kids. If you are interested in the field, I'd highly recommend taking a class with Van Engen! It was my favorite class!

Professor Van Engen is great! She's really funny and overall an amazing teacher for the subject. She explains everything very clearly and makes linguistics a fun and interesting topic to learn. Tests contain a significant amount of material so you definitely have to study, but they're reasonable so if you study you can definitely do well.

I took Dr. Van Engen's intro class purely out of interest and as an elective, and it ended up being so interesting and enjoyable. The first lecture seemed intimidating and difficult, but stick it out and it's quickly great. Her lectures are funny and engaging, and she's also a genuinely kind and cool person. Would definitely recommend her class!

Professor Van Engen is very enthusiastic about linguistics and very knowledgeable. She makes a complex topic simple and easy to understand. Incorporates a lot of fun videos and pictures to try to make the lectures more engaging. Would definitely suggest taking her class!
Really articulate professor invested in her subject. I enjoyed class. She does have a bit of a monotone though.

She is awesome! like a genuinely cool person. Very clear and interesting. She kept people engaged and encouraged participation and always seemed willing to help. I think if you liked the material and studied it was not a hard class

Professor Van Engen was funny and engaging, but the tests asked for very specific details about the material, especially things she never really made clear. It seemed like she just wanted to trip us up rather than actually teach us.

Professor Gabel is very nice and friendly, ready to help if you need it. We had a lot of readings but you don't necessarily need to do them all in full. Tests were a bit tricky because we had to memorize 50+ paintings and it wasn't always clear what she was looking for as answers. But her class was really interesting and I definitely recommend.
Amazing and very kind professor. Really knows her stuff!

(Pleasure and Pain: European Fashion as Art History)
Might be my favorite class I've ever taken. Gabel's lectures are super interesting and engaging, and she is the nicest person, I totally recommend. You definitely have to put in some hours of studying for the exams, but they are very doable if you do, and you'll know what to expect.
Gabel is really caring and an excellent lecturer. However, her grading criteria are sometimes unclear. Still, it's worth taking, as it's a super interesting course.

The least engaging and prepared professor I've ever had. The previous post is accurate when describing the improvisational feel to lectures, I never felt like Kurtz was fully prepared and her lectures were rarely enjoyable. If you want to learn about the music beyond a basic, basic survey of jazz history, avoid this course.
At times culturally insensitive

If you're interested in learning about music, avoid Dr. Kurtz. Her lectures are improvised, and she does no preparation prior to class. This class has absolutely 0 structure and you will learn nothing about music. The class is an easy A, which is the only pro. I'd learn more about music from a Kidzbop CD than a Kurtz lecture on jazz music.
I love this professor.
Very Clear and very nice a person!
She is a very great lecturer. They are very clear and easy to follow. She also extremely approachable.

Estle is amazing. I took this over the summer just so I could take it with her. She gives out study sheets that tell you exactly what will be on the tests, gives very clear instructions for the papers, and is always there to help students. She stayed after class with me for an hour just because I wanted to get ahead on my work.

Estle is my favorite professor ever. This class could have been insanely boring, but she made it interesting (still can't figure out how). She is sweet, fun, and gives study guides that tell you exactly what will be on the test. Read, pay attention in lecture, and do a normal amount of studying and this class is wonderful.
A lot of material covered in 8 weeks but she is a fair grader and the weekly quizzes are open book. Nice teacher, friendly and responsive to students, must get the text.

super sweet; explains the material clearly; very willing to help outside of class.  lectures can get a little boring at times but that's because she repeats material until she believes everyone understands.

She's very good at explaining things, has a lot of patience, kindness, and particality. One of the best teachers I've had my whole wash u career. Took Psych Stats and Experimental Psych with her and U-College Behavioral Analysis all in the same semester.
best. professor. EVER. seriously, take every class you can with her.

She cares for her students so much, it is evident that she actually wants you to learn the concepts and succeed in her class. She does a better job explaining statistics than the math dept and is always available for office hours if you need help. One of the best teachers I have ever had a WUSTL by a long shot.
Amazing! So helpful and nice. Almost seems like she should be teaching kindergarten instead of college which is both good and bad.
She also teaches at Columbia College and is a really good teacher.  She is easy to understand, responds to discussions, gives feedback, and is very nice.  I recommend her.
Extremely nice, discussions are thought provoking; I enjoyed the class a lot!
I loved this class! Any freshman thinking about taking it def should.
Great Professor, very accessible during office hours. Super caring and chill in and out of class. Great experience during this class!

Quite possibly the GOAT. I signed up for this class on a whim but it was really interesting. Dr. Fournier is supremely kind, very understanding, and does a great job lecturing. He sparked my interest in a new topic and I would go out of my way to take him again if possible.
love this class such a good prof!!

Herzog is a very nice person and tells a lot of dad jokes. He tried to learn everyone's names in a 100+ student class. The course materials are HARD and some of his lectures aren't the clearest, but exams are open-book so just make a very comprehensive cheat sheet and you should be fine. Everything else is pretty much free points. Overall recommend

My personal favorite professor from my favorite course. He expects a LOT from students but is generous with grading and in your first conversation with him he will impress with his knowledge, sharp mind and passion for his subject and for teaching. WashU needs more professors like Dr. Herzog.

One of the hands down best professors at Washington University. Some other Neuroscience classes are downright terrible (ahem, Principles of the Nervous System) but Dr. Herzog, and his partner in crime Dr. Carlson, run a phenomenal NeuroPhysiology Lab. He is enthusiastic about teaching, cares about your understanding, etc - a wonderful mentor.

Is very biased in grading such that if you happen to be a teacher's pet, you will "do very well". On contrary, you could put all the efforts in the world into this class and not have the grade reflect the work and efforts put forth.

Took Biological Clocks from Dr. H Spring 2011. He is a fantastic teacher - I've heard his neurophysiology lab is great too. His course material is challenging, but he explains it all very well and makes the classes worth attending and enjoyable.
No Comments

Fun class and great professor. Languages are always hard but she is very patient. Like any intro language, in class participation is crucial and theres a fair amount of outside homework/studying. Prof. Conti is friendly and a fair grader. Not hard to understand even when speaking only in Italian.
Nice professor, great class!  FORZA MILAN!!!!

Dr. Conti is one of my favorite professors I've had at WashU. I took the three-course language sequence with her and absolutely loved it. She became a source of comfort and stability in my life, sort of like a favorite high school teacher. Very kind and laughs and smiles a lot. If you're at all interested in Italian, I highly recommend her courses!

I took her Italian Food Italian Culture class. Was a lot of history and culture. Some parts of the class were pretty heavy in work. She likes you to log on every day and participate in the discussion board. Other than that the class was fun and I would take it again.

Conti was an amazing professor. As you get more advanced in Italian it's essential to be as much in Italian - listening, speaking, reading, and writing - in class as possible. Conti was great at pretty much always speaking in Italian and providing feedback politely in class and on assignments when we slipped up. She's so caring and quite funny.
She is kind and helpful. You will need to put in plenty of time outside of class but if you use the textbook to study you will do fine. Tests/quizzes are very reasonable.

I was hoping that the class would be fun since it was a Italian Food course. I felt like everything I responded to regarding the discussions werent good enough. I understand the Professor is looking for certain things but I don't think I deserved a D. This brought my GPA down tremendously. I have been on the Deans List several times. Never a D.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Conti is so sweet and truly wants all of her students to succeed. Definitely a learning curve having to communicate 100% in a foreign language, but she ensures that everyone understands what is going on. As long as you stay on top of the homework assignments, the class itself is very manageable.

Professor Conti is very clear and extremely helpful. She is open to scheduling outside office hours and offers information about italian groups and activities on campus that add to learning a new language.

This is for Problems in Philosophy. His lectures were very interesting and covered a broad variety of topics (so if one week doesn't interest you just wait until the next). Attend lectures as much as you can! Though I would say that having good discussion and posing good questions is more important for your participation grade.
Professor Brown's class was interesting and he is a very humorous lecturer. The class is largely discussion and participation is mandatory, so you must do the reading.

Eric is a great guy and is an engaging lecturer. I found he was accessible to meet with outside of class. He makes plenty of jookes in class and encourages questions from the class, sometimes the class is just about the questions being asked and not whatever he planned. I think above all this guy loves philosophy and loves talking about it.

This is for Present Moral Problems. If you wish to take it P/F, take it with someone else. Lots of reading and stringent criteria for essays.

This class should discuss motivation and modern education in general because as far as I can tell, it gets everything wrong. 

Oh, and he swears (unnecessarily) a lot in class.

Prof Brown was actually a really good professor/lecturer and had really interesting conversations in class. He welcomed dissenting opinions but oftentimes challenged them. The only reason I went with a 4 was because it was difficult to get over his liberal bias in the class. Made some trump jokes but a solid philosophy professor nonetheless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor.

Just lectures. That's it. He has no other purpose. If you meet with him, he just doesn't help. There is absolutely no structure in the class. No in class discussions. There are no essay prompts so if he doesn't like your topic you're kinda f'ed. Also outside of class he just isn't a nice guy. I don't get why people like him.

Firstly, he is very knowledgeable; he's like the human version of an ancient philosophy encyclopedia; however, he lectures far too much and there is almost no space for discussion. If you have an argument, he will quickly shoot it down. Essays are difficult cause in class he doesn't really tolerate counter arguments to Plato.
Knowledgeable and inspirational.

Amazing professor. Absolutely loved his teaching style but he does not grade the papers, his TA does, and she is actually the worst. Unfair grader, comments don't make sense, hard to contact, etc.  Would be my favorite class if she was not a part of it.

Incredible professor.  I enjoyed his class the most, by far, my first semester.  Reading the works and listening to his explanations and often-hilarious examples in class were eye-opening and actually life-changing.  I would take another class again with him in a heartbeat.  Also not that much work involved - 3 short essays and 5 easy quizzes.

basically, i am in love with this man.  amazingly clear and knowledgable, and I wind up in hysterics just about every class.  very down to earth and excited about teaching.  i wish he was teaching a more advanced course next semester!!

Professor Brown is an exceptionally clear thinker and a great teacher.  He always seems to conjure up hilarious, memorable, and helpful illustrations.  Opinionated, but in a good way; he'll take a well-reasoned stance and defend it.  He is a true product of a good liberal arts education.  My favorite prof at WashU; highly recommended.

In a word, fantastic!  Brown is exceedingly clear, uses great explanatory examples, and brings his passion to each lecture.  Knows his stuff inside and out.  Structures his class so as to acquaint you with primary material while simultaneously strengthening your basic philosophical skills.  And he's hilarious.  Take this class if you can!
Run, don't walk, to take a class with Professor Brown.
Spontaneous and incredibly knowledgeable. Brown is AWESOME!!!!!!
Awesome professor. Best I've ever had. Engaging discussions, helpful assignments and a phenomenal understanding of the subject and ability to teach it

I had Dr. Brown for an intro class, but was disappointed to find that I would be unable to take a more advanced class in the following semester.  Extremely helpful, using varied examples tailored to fit the situation or discusstion at hand.
This guy is Socrates reincarnated or at least as close as you'll get.  Eric rocks.
Enthusiastic, makes course interesting with a unifying theme.  Smart as a whip, but not arrogant about it (he will debate with you in class, though)
Makes class interesting

Wonderfully sweet man, and made intro to philosophy fun and easier to understand than i thought it would be.  most of his jokes are lame, but he's having so much fun teaching that you laugh right along with him anyways.  a good time.
He is a great individual. Very insightful

Waste of time. Demba likes to toot his own horn. Lots of eye rolls from students when Demba lectured, aka read from text book. Took class in 2014, but went to a seminar this winter and learned five times as much as Demba tried to teach.

Isn't engaging, doesn't give straight answers. Teaches but isn't in to teaching. Reads from slides and ends class. Doesn't work problems for clarity. Lots of students stop showing up to class because they'd gain more spending that time reading.

The only reason I ended up with such a good grade: 1) got a lot of tutoring, 2) Demba offered an extra credit project 3) He threw out the in-class final grade because everyone failed. I took nothing away from the class except relief.

He teaches a variety of Econ Classes.  All tests are take home and open book.  sounds easy but they are meticulous.  Very fare instructor who understands if you need to miss a class.  I've had at least 4 of his courses!!

Great STEM class for a non-STEM person. Loved learning about the solar system, cool projects that felt like puzzles, but are a bit challenging so try to find good group members. Quizzes make up most of the grade, they are generally not too hard if you can reference the textbook and if you listen in class. Super nice and accessible prof.

This class is very interesting. It's only composed of bi-monthly quizzes, group projects and homework. If you're worried abt your grade bc of the quizzes, DO THE EXTRA CREDIT!! overall this was a great class and you can get an A just by paying attention at lectures (he's very engaging).

Very interesting class and nice guy. He really tries to make the lectures interesting and engaging.
