The quiz questions can sometimes be really hard and worth a ton of points, so be careful with the quizzes. Everything else is easy points if you do the work (homework and group projects) He's very funny and smart and the topics are interesting!

Professor Errando is amazing! I had him for Fall 2020 and he worked really hard to make the class interesting. His lectures are engaging and interesting, the non-reading homeworks were really easy, and there were some cool group project(s). If you just read the weekly readings from the textbooks then it's an easy A.

If you are not a STEM person and looking for an NSM distribution credit, take 125A! Errando is very nice, his class is easy, and he keeps the material engaging. Group work is common (but not hard) and you need to participate in class. Quizzes were easy on Zoom (open note) but may be harder in person.
If you have the chance, take physics with Dr. Errando. He gives amazing explanations and every single lecture is well structured. You will learn a lot and be very well prepared for the exams.

Best science professor I have had at WUSTL hands down. Manel is an extremely engaging professor that makes hour long lectures fly by and make you wonder where the time went. His lectures are exceptionally clear and thorough. Students could score an A in the introductory physics sequence by simply attending and reviewing his lectures carefully
The subject matter was really interesting and the homework was relatively easy, but the quizzes were hard and each question counted for quite a lot. So if you missed a few, you were in trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very good at explaining concepts and ideas in physics, while also keeping the class engaged with occasional humor. The class is still tough though, but that's with any of the 197 professors. Asking questions in class was always easy to do. I recomend taking intro physics with him.

Really great guy. He's friendly and easy to approach. If you feel that your test was graded unevenly by the TAs, submit a regrade! He's very reasonable when it comes to giving back (deserved) points. Lectures are clear, make sure to go to his review sessions before the exam!

If you know the book, you'll get the grade. The dude's a genius for sure, but he prefers to go really in-depth into one topic rather than cover the chapter evenly. That being said, class is enjoyable enough, he takes questions and has the dry humor if you listen for it.

Errando is very approachable, very good at anticipating what students might be confused on. He genuinely cares about each student's success and my friends in the class and I never once felt scared to ask him a question after class. He is very clear and a fantastic lecturer who keeps your attention through the lecture.
Very interesting course material covered at a relatively easy level. Exams are easy, beware the grading on the homeworks. He is very funny, I highly enjoyed the class.

He can explain quantum physics to a five year old and, perhaps even more impressively, to ME. He uses the simplest, hands on examples to depict quite complicated theories and equations, and he is is so funny (both with the things he says, and the way he uses his entire body to teach) that scary numbers become friendly adventures. Take his class!

I've learned so much in this class, but it moves SUPER fast. Be prepared to spend hours a night on homework, because he'll ask you to translate what you wrote, and if you didn't, he'll take note.  He is an amazing professor but overly sarcastic and definitely stays true to the "proud" Israeli stereotype. Tests are always on the material from class

Giore is very caring for his students. My only complaint is that the book heavily relies on Jewish cultural references and geographical contexts without much introduction. Take this class during your first three semesters when you have the time to put into it.

Giore is by far the best professor I have had at WashU.  He cares SO much about his students, and is truly a wonderful teacher.  His textbook (which he wrote himself) is phenomenal, and the online component is incredible.  I learned so much in this class and truly enjoyed every moment of it.
He rocks. One of the best professors I've had. His book is also awesome. You will learn a ton in his class. Definitely take it.
Giore lights the fire of my each and every day. He's simply the man.
I love Giore!

Giore was definitely a highlight of my Wash U experience.  Goes to great lengths to help his students and make learning interesting.  Just be sure to do your homework, turn it in on time, not miss class without a good excuse, and be prepared to participate - you'll learn to love it, promise!
Such a good professor, very engaging, makes you want to be in class...and you definitely won't fall asleep!
Really good prof, cares a great deal about his students and their progress. And when he says attendance is mandatory, he means it. Go to class and do your homework and you will be fine.
He can be a realy meany. DO YOUR HOMEWORK!!
Great professor.
No Comments
Giore was very helpful.  I came from a background of NO Hebrew, and ended the year being able to read, write, and converse decently.  He has a strong sarcastic sense of humor.
No Comments
No Comments
So easy

He's a great lecturer but somehow manages to be boring.  I can't explain it.  I just brought sudoku to class every day.  It helped me deal with the boredom while still being able to focus on the lecture.

Great professor. Even though I slowly learned over the course of the semester that philosophy isn't a subject I particularly enjoy, the class discussions were always very interesting. The workload for the course was quite manageable (something that any science major will appreciate).
Very enthusiastic about class. Tells great stories and, even if subject isn't interesting, he finds a way to entertain you.

great guy and great lecturer. subject is pretty boring, but the workload is light. my only complaint was that every piece of work we did was read/graded by the TAs and none of it was read by j. claude himself.
One of the best professors I've had at Wash. U. He's a really nice guy, an interesting lecturer, a very fair grader, and makes very complex concepts easy to understand. Go to his office hours!!

a descent professor. Sometimes a bit unclear but the subject he teaches is fascinating. You don't have to be genuinely interested in philosophy to take his class. Very easy grading very lax about attendance and super nice.

Nothing terribly wrong with this professor. A fair grader, sometimes a little bit unclear about his teaching but overall very lucid explanation of difficult concepts. Take his class if you have patience and are seriously interested in philosophy. He is very lax about the paper deadline and also does not care too much about attendence.
Cute, but unprepared and too repetative. He does not seem to have an agenda, and class drags.
Really interested in his subjects, helpful, friendly, but you must like the topic already to be interested in his lectures.
actually going to class was pointless... and the ta's graded everything based on their own opinions. overall, skip this one and take bioeth if you're looking for a good phil class.
Really liked his subject. But, like all philosophy teachers, there were many times that he sounded like a pompous ass.
he made me interested in the environment...i recommend him and this class to all
No Comments
Super guy, great teacher.
A southern gentleman.  Genuinely concerned for students, encourages shy students to become vocal.  Much more of a "guide" through the readings than a lecturer on a topic.
Great professor. She's really nice and if you participate she will love you

In addition to being a well respected scholar, she is also a concerned and interesting teacher. She gives a lot of papers, but she reads them all very carefully and gives good feedback. Great teacher!
Her lectures are somewhat unorganized, and discussion sections are a complete waste of time.  Nonetheless, she is interesting, a fair grader, and a nice lady.
Great teacher!  Great class!
EVA RUSSO FOR PRESIDENT 2016. Seriously, take German with her even if you didn't think you wanted to learn German. She's patient, fun, goofy, and a fantastic teacher.
Hands down the best professor I've ever had. Amazing human being too. I would stay for a German major if she teaches every class.

Excllnt teacher & deprtmnt. Sad Im a senior! Extremly dynamic w an unbelievable amnt of energy. Shes excllnt at motivating participatn & at keeping it animated & interestng. Little use of paradigms w emph on immersion--Effective! Little slow if u've taken langs be4. Tests often w a fair amnt of drills. Practically BEGS u 2 meet w her for office hrs
Professor Russo is the best professor I have ever had, she is an excellent and professional educator, and she really cares about her students.
Not easy. Class fast paced. You learn a lot. Best Introductory professor of the German Department.
Professor Russo is an excellent teacher. Classes are extremely interesting. She makes German seem like a breeze. Daily work is required, but enjoyable. Highly recommended!

Possibly the best teacher I have ever had in my entire life.  She makes class fun and is so helpful and fair with homework assignments.  She goes out of her way to offer review sessions.  She spent almost three hours of her own evening time reviewing with us for the final exam.  I can't imagine anyone doing a better job.

Absolutely outstanding!  Works WITH students to increase their own personal skills and never compares students to each other.  She cares more about your attempt to learn German than your accuracy on individual homework assignments.  I hated German when I got to Wash U.  Because of her, it is now my major.
AMAZING TEACHER!!! truly cares about students. Helps people inside of class and out. Very fair grader, wants you to succeed! I have had her for 4 semesters of german and she is the best
Great teacher, very engaging and fun.

SOOO incredibly nice and helpful, will let you turn in work late, very understanding, most of all she just wants you to have fun and learn the material.  AWESOME teacher. late twenties/early thirties. the whole german department at washu rocks.

One of my favorite teacher's I've ever had. Is a clear, concise lecturer that uses practical examples from the real world to reinforce the material. Cares about his students and has a great sense of sarcastic humor.

Nice guy, a ok teacher, however if you have the option of Sterling or him take Sterling. She is a better lecturer and doesnt let a select few ppl dominate the class. BEWARE: Hernandez makes u think u are doing better than u actually are by curving the class mid-semeste rand then changing the scale after the final to curve so the class avg is lower

Being a young professor he is very friendly and close to students. He understands the challenge we faced just coming into college so he really tried to help us. He can be a little confusing from time to time, especially when it comes to economics stuff. But in general he is an excellent professor in business.

He really cares about his students and does a good job of explaining things most of the time. He was very reasonable. Tests can be hard, but he takes a lot of liberty when it comes to moving up final grades a few points.
Decent professor. Nice guy.
Terrific guy!
With a spirit that will not die...
oh the humanity!
No Comments
One of the best business professors I've had at WashU. Lectures are engaging with midpoint breaks, test are straightforward, and he's pretty funny. Highly recommend!
Grades are often very delayed with no clear guidelines which set a lot of students back at the very end of the course.
Amazing professor, probably the best professor in the bschool I've had at Olin so far. He is a really kind and understanding guy. Just make sure to go to class and do the homework

Gonzalez is an easy going professor, and he was always willing to help students. I was genuinely interested in the class, and I'm glad I took MKT370 with him. The exams are easy if you know the basic class concepts.

Professor is very nice. He's accessible during his office hours, and his tests are relatively easy if you pay attention to his class. Lectures can be boring, but it's comprehensive. You can always access his slides a few hours before your class period.
You'd think a professor who has spent their career studying social interactions would know how to a) be nice & b) engage their class but...here we are
WIll push you but super interesting course!
I really enjoyed Foley's class I truly learned so much

Discussion-centered + the most insightful  soapbox rants. Never taken so much from a class (or professor). Foley creates the kind of environment that forces you to grapple with things we take for granted. Dare I say best class I've taken at WashU? Absolutely. They are always available and actually care about their students.

I had an amazing time in Dr. Foley's* class. They are an amazing professor who's extremely engaging with her humor and relatability. She's up to date with Tik tok references which made their lectures extra enjoyable. Their expertise really comes through and they'll push you to think about complicated topics in very interesting and critical ways.

Don't take a class with this professor if you aren't a grad student. 

They are inaccessible and unforgiving. I've never written a review on here before even though I've had some bad professors, but I can't not warn other students about Folley. 
Made my friend cry.
Excellent professor. You can tell they care about their students' learning experiences. Readings were lengthy and sometimes dense but usually interesting. Would recommend.
Good GPA-booster. Maybe don't take if you're super serious about Spanish?
David is the GOAT! If you have the option to take his class, jump on it!!!
Fun class. Agree it's a bit easy or less oratorically intense than I expected

Definitely the best Spanish class I have taken at WashU, and Profe Cortes Ferrandez made all the difference. He is engaging, assigns reasonable amounts of homework, and gives great feedback on all the final project drafts. He really sets you up for success in the class.

I love him! Super kind, chill, and funny. Passionate about what he teaches and makes classes diverse in activities and engaging. Standard structure of WashU Spanish course with presentations and final paper-- unique in practicas, which are like open open-note test at the end of units. He gives very good feedback and makes a good class environment.

Prof. Cortes-Ferrandez took a difficult class (1020 is one of the most demanding in the Spanish program) and made it such a fun experience. While the workload is intense and you should be prepared to spend time studying, he gives a lot of credit for trying and really tries to help his students succeed as much as possible. Absolutely recommend.
Awesome professor who cares very much about each student and makes learning fun! I would definitely recommend taking Spanish 102 with him.

Fun class and he's light on grading. Feels more like a high school class. Since assignments are light, he cares more if it looks like you're paying attention rather than testing if you actually are, so take notes with a notebook.

Dr. Cortés Ferrandez is one of the best profs in the Spanish department and is funny, articulate, and the class is pretty chill. Definitely do start the final essay early though it is not something that lends itself to last minute grinding.

I love Profe. Cortes Ferrandez, but this class isn't one to take if you want to truly challenge yourself and improve your Spanish. Great for Spanish second majors / minors, though. We speak English a lot in class and rules around this are very loose.
Incredibly interesting class—especially if you're interested in language and Spanish. Advice: start your final paper ASAP. Writing it last minute is not fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. You can tell that he truly wants his students to succeed. Willing to help everyone gets a's in class by offering to make up assignments. Super nice and makes class fun.

He is by far my favorite professor. Throughout the semester, we learned so much about different topics, and although we moved on to different topics each week, it did not seem overwhelming. He makes the class very engaging, which is super nice because it is not your typical lecture class. He is super understanding as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Cortes Ferrandez has been my favorite Spanish professor at WashU so far! His assignments require you to think about the topics presented in class, but are designed in a way that does not cause as much stress as other classes. He is a fair grader and really cares about the students.

One of the kindest souls at WashU. Tests were from the HW and the final literally had a 94% median. The tradeoff resulting from this class being super easy is that it may not be proper prep for future proof-based math courses. Other than that, you can 100% tell this guy knows what he's talking about and i still learned hella from this class

Undoubtedly the kindest and warmest professor; accessible in office hours; exams are easy. Lectures from textbook can be a little dry. I think he assumed students' knowledge of certain topics, which made some explanations a little tricky. As a result, I had to solidify my understanding independently.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. He'd often give you the pool of problems he would pull from for the exam. Easy A, but his lectures were so engaging I ended up learning a ton. Absolute amazing professor take a class with him any chance you get

So so sweet and super nice guy. Super easy to reach and made a lot of person accommodations. Not the most engaging lectures, but at least for the class I took you did not need to go at all. Tests are super easy and based only off homework. Easy A and cool dude but if you need a prof to learn from in class probably take someone else
Renato is bursting with passion and excitement for math, which makes him a very fun professor to learn from and study with.
Dr. Feres is definitely the best!!!
He is a very inspirational person. Definitely take classes with Feres as many as you can.
Dr. Feres is a very kind person.

Professor Feres is the best and the most caring professor I met at WashU. He has made a valuable contribution to the Freiwald Scholar program and to the department. His enthusiasm for teaching mathematics serves as an inspiration for students to acquire knowledge. Professor Feres is super accessible outside of class and a real expert in math.
Homeworks weigh a lot than usual

Feres is one of the friendliest guys on this campus. He can be a dry lecturer at times, but he teaches straight out of the textbook, so attendance isn't mandatory.  His grading is incredibly easy: tests are entirely based on the homework and most (75%+) of the class ended up in the A range.  Take him if you can!
Maybe the nicest professors I've ever had.
So likable, brilliant, easy, interesting and awesome. Best math professor ever! Take any class you can with Renato.
A very nice teacher with great teaching style.
He is a fantastic instructor, who clearly enjoys what he is teaching, which makes his lectures very interesting to watch.  He made Calc 3 seem like a breeze, and is excellent at answering questions

He's very cute.  That's what he has going for him more than anything.  He's a very boring lecturer.  About 70% of students are present at any given lecture.  His exams are all questions from the book work, so that makes the class pretty straight forward.
RF: a terrific teacher, an extraordinarily kind man, and a truly brilliant individual. Exams are very manageable if you do the assigned problems.
Renato is a true champion. He wears cool flannels, is a boss, and his class is pretty easy
Cares a lot about his students, very nice man and will dedicate himself to making sure you understand the topics. Tests are extremely easy and it's quite fun to attend his lectures.
Really nice professor.Very concerned about his students.

Prof Feres is great. His lectures feel a lot like he's just having a conversation with you, unlike teachers with which you feel a strong disconnect. Speaks slowly which is good, though not very loud. In class he leans more towards the theory stuff (harder) but tests only on what's in the book (easier).  If you do your homework you're set.
A very nice guy, but goes very slow.  Not that he's slow intelligence-wise, just isn't good at lecturing fast.

He was very helpful and was concerned for his students. Wanted to make sure we understood the material, and was very good at answering questions thouroughly. Nicest professor I've ever had. Tests were easy, and the final was a take-home. Feres is a great guy.

feres was a great guy and he could always spend a long time helping me when i needed it (and boy did i need help)...but i only needed help because his lectures were so hard to understand and the textbook explained things just as badly.
one of the nicest professors I've ever met.  He met with me and helped me for hours and I was even in his class.
great professor. Nice materials, very supportive

I thought I took current macro issues not stories from my 70 year old professor. He prioritizes his tangents from 2008 rather than actually explaining the macro behind 2008 and assuming students have perfect background knowledge on it. He really should consider retiring after this school year because he's not the fun prof I was told he'd be

He is a prime example of why college professors should have teaching certificates to teach. He is unclear, disorganized, and vindictive. No one with a position of power should be allowed to wield it unqualified. This is furthered in his TA who is taught to grade with an iron fist, albeit less so. Overall only take 448 if you LOVE, not like, macro

He takes things too personally and holds a grudge against students all semester and this is reflected in his grading. Conversely, if he likes you that is also reflected in your grades. Get on his good side, go to class AND participate a lot, go to office hours even if you don't have questions, and relearn your writing style to match his liking

Teaching and grading style is akin to that of a toddler showing you their favorite toy but constantly correcting you when you called it Mr Bubbles not Mr Bubdles. He's 100% informed but after 40 years has become entitled to thinking his no slides, no script, just wing it lecture style still works. Also people have unique writing styles, embrace it?
Only take this class if you are fluent in ADHD eco-babble because this man absolutely cannot string together a coherent sentence. He's very smart and friendly but please don't be my prof
Excellent professor. Fair grading, likes to ramble in his lectures but overall makes them engaging and fun. Feels like he genuinely enjoys his job and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Fazzari has an exceptional research background, which reflects in class lectures on the Keynesian model, the Intrinsic Keynesian model, and MMT. I wished we would have covered Friedman/Monetarism (perhaps a compare and contrast assignment with Keynes would have been cool).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Fazzari looks at economics beyond simply growth and efficiency, incorporating an important macro perspective. He cares about his students and gives great feedback on essays without being a harsh grader. This class is relatively easy, but does have a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Fazzari is a good person and an interesting lecturer. Loves to field questions, will not throw unnecessary curve balls.

Fazzari is engaging, helpful, and genuinely cares about his students and wants to see them learn. Economic writing is a difficult subject, but he brings it down to earth with a good sense of humor, engaging lectures, and extremely thorough evaluation of all your writing assignments. You will always know how you can improve after he grades.

The class is uniquely a writing intensive class in the econ dept which I found to be extremely helpful. Fazzari's a great professor and I found his lectures are extremely engaging and current, and his 'intrinsic' Keynesian perspective is unique and compelling. Although the class is mostly lecture-driven, he also encourages questions from students.

Fazzari can ramble and get flustered (and often does), but he's a brilliant economist and, more importantly, cares that you understand the subject matter. You get out what you put into Intro Macro, but Fazzari's great if you engage with him and are remotely interested in the subject

His 104 class really comes off as a current economics class, which would be fine if any of the intro students knew anything about economics. So he ends up balancing intro topics with modern economic issues, which makes the lectures incoherent for intro students. Take it with Bandy; it'll give you the solid foundation you need in economics.
One of the best professors I've had at WashU. Take his Current Macro or any class with him. You will not regret it. So helpful and friendly outside of class and always entertaining during lectures.

I can't speak for his intro class, but he's great for an upper level.  While he does have his biases, he will completely acknowledge them and still gives more than a fare perspective of other viewpoints. He encourages discussion and, even though he might favor his beliefs as I mentioned, he will not discredit a good point.  Overall, great teacher.
Great Class, Great teacher, take it from Faz, you'll have a great time and learn a ton!

Good class, but the guy is just a cocky person. He has no reason and will not discuss things with people who think different. I guess he still thinks that Macro is king, but Micro is what changes the world.

A decent teacher, but spends way too much of his time on demand-side policy for an introductory class. He rarely makes an attempt to appear balanced in his presentation of the material, and while he did spend a week out of the semester covering supply-side macro, no one would dare call this a survey course on economic theory. Be forewarned.
He's funny and knows his stuff, but damn this was not an easy class.

Fazzari is an amazing professor. His enthusiasm motivates you to care about Macro as much as he does and makes the subject interesting. He's straight-forward, clear and extremely knowledgable. I love his "textbook" and enjoy attending his class. I feel confident with what I've learned from him. Take this class!
Best professor ever!!
Best professor I've ever had
He teaches extremely well. Understood everything he was saying, and learned a lot about macro.
No need to go to class consistantly, he puts his lecture notes online and they are EXACTLY the same as his lectures (same jokes and all)
Nice to have professor who knows what he is talking about
One of the worst profs ever...Most incoherent eco-babble. Ignore the smileys---fair warning.

Don't take him. He's very statist, biased and just rambles about the same one topic all class. He taught economic princples which have been refuted and discredited as though they were true. Sitting through his class literally hurt my ears.

Fazzari is pretty good at making some otherwise boring material more interesting.  I'm not really interested in economics, but Intro to Macro is also great for those interested in making more informed decisions in the political sphere as well.
He is very clear and engaging; also, very receptive to helping students.
one of the best teachers i have ever had...very knowledgable, very enthusiastic...really makes you like economics
The FAZZ rocks
Awesome
His great teaching made me swicth to Econ. major
He used no textbook, and he didn't need one.  I would recommend the Fazz to anyone.
gets 'in the zone' when he's lecturing -- so into his work that it makes us excited about it too
No Comments
No Comments
lecutre notes online!
No Comments
No Comments
Fendy is really that guy! His classes are very engaging and he prioritizes student success. Could not go wrong with any class you take with him cause you'll end up taking another the next semester!

Professor Fenderson is a gem, in the jewels that make up the AFAS department. In the Cultural History of Hip Hop class, he and Manditch-Prottas were incredibly engaging and interactive with all students, and genuinely care about you and your learning.
Fendy cares so much for his students, and I was always excited to go to class. He's super approachable if you have any issues, though I'm doubtful you'll have any under his teaching.
Professor Fenderson is very caring and fairly lenient. I recommend every to take a class with him. He's chillll!

I LOVE PROFESSOR FENDERSON!!! He has been my absolute favorite professor. He is thoughtful and actually cares about his students well being. He is lenient with deadlines and is understanding when things have come up and students cannot complete assignments. If you are debating taking a course with him, do it!!

Professor Fenderson genuinely cares about his students and how they're doing in and outside of the classroom. He leads discussions in a very engaging manner that makes you look forward to the readings and time spent in class. I couldn't recommend his class on the Civil Rights Movement anymore.
Fendy is great!

He's a boss. He's a young guy who just got his phD and really gets it. One of the rising stars in the growing AFAS field. Loved the design of the course where much of the work really exposed you first-hand to some of the true issues that African-Americans continue to face in this country. Would take another class with him in a second.

Don't take a class with Dr. Ferrer unless you feel comfortable teaching yourself the content.  He frequently came to office hours without looking at the homework he assigned, so when you ask questions he says he doesn't know because he hasn't looked at it yet.

Ferrer's lecture were messy and it honestly  didn't seem like he came prepared for lectures, as he would bounce around topics and do problems incorrectly which made lectures very confusing. I took Physics 192, the next Physics course, with another professor that also teaches 191 and she was vastly superior to Ferrer. Nice person, bad prof.

He does a good job of making the lecture engaging and interactive (which is pretty hard with physics) but he usually runs out of time or does the problem wrong so it can get confusing. It is a tough class but if you take advantage of the resources like PLTL you can do good.
Ferrer thinks that everyone in his class understands physics already, and he goes over his examples very quickly. You will have to do a lot of self-teaching in this class, so be prepared.

He's got to be the worst prof I've had at WashU. I don't think he realizes that he's teaching to students with little to no physics knowledge along with the ones who've taken physics before. He's so bad at explaining things, so I had to watch the other lecturers' lectures to feel like I stood a chance when it came time to take the exams.
This guy is an absolute genius. Great physics professor

Ferrer is a really funny teacher w good jokes and makes class go by so fast. Does a lot of proofs but will do examples if you ask him to. Neat accent. Does a lot of in class demonstrations and makes them really fun. Will call on random people but doesn't destroy you if you are wrong like some professors. Overall entertaining and informative class

Ferrer is funny and he is willing to explain concepts thoroughly if you have questions. Beware. If you sit in the back, he's more likely to call on you if you don't raise your hand. The class itself is a bit of work due to daily and weekly homework assignments.
Great lecturer. Doesn't much budge on grading however.
He is quiet unclear about his lectures, he is pretty bad that take away your attendance score easily, he even makes the Mid Term 1 the hardest ever happened in WUSTL history!!!!

Professor Ferrer is the man.  Always makes class fun, keeps lectures interesting with numerous 2-minute problems.  Has a very good demeanor when discussing in class about the mentioned problems.  Although the problem sets are tedious and the textbook is way overused, this is not his fault.  It is how the course is designed.  As a teacher, he rocks!

Material can be very difficult but Ferrer is clear and intelligible in his math.  Problem sets are extremely time intensive and involve an understanding that goes way beyond lecture.  Exam difficulty varied from absolutely impossible to pretty easy so you really have to be prepped for anything.

Had him for mechanics spring 2011. He would cover material in class only after he had assigned and collected homework on it, so class was pretty useless. I ended up reading the textbook cover-to-cover, and the class was still hard. Exam questions came completely out of left field.

He's got a cool Spanish accent.  His lectures focus on proofs rather than example problems, which is a problem, because his problem sets have extremely difficult problems that the textbook can't help with.  An easy problem set is one that can be done without any outside help.  Exams range from impossible to manageable.

as someone who's slow on the draw when it comes to rote memorization in languages, even I found Wulaoshi's class to be incredibly productive. he really, *really* cares about his students and said that if he could, he would teach heritage Chinese forever. loves teaching, and that love shines through. easy A or A- as long as you *try*-- he can tell.
Wu Laoshi is like a sweet grandpa. love him. The only thing is he throws a lot of shade at Taiwan :(
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a great professor, really patient. He's not super demanding and really wants to see students do well. I wasn't super challenged by this class, but still was able to learn a lot. He doesn't incorporate a lot of review, unit by unit, so that's mainly up to you to do.
Wu Laoshi is very clear, funny, and helpful. I always looked forward to attending his classes!
I love Wu Laoshi!!!  He is a great great man.
Don't need to prepare for tests as long as you pay attention in class. Fun class.
very easy to follow. You don't really need to prepare for each class.
The class is really easy.  The first couple of days is really stressful because there's so much vocab in one day.  But the tests are so easy that I don't even study for it.
Beginning Chinese for Heritage Speakers.  Nice teacher, eager to help out, pretty easy going and will give you hints on quizzes :)
One of the worst
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Zach is awesome

Dr. Feinstein lectures rather poorly, and tends to gloss over conceptual material. Exams are take-home, so you end up simply replicating methods step by step from lecture and homework, rather than actually ever learning the "why" behind the methods. I don't feel I got much out of taking the course, but it was required for my major.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Lopez is a super nice individual and seems accommodating (regrades and such). There were two tests at 30 and 35% of the grade respectively, so if you messed up one you were done for. Very long lectures and sometimes it is hard to tell what he will test since all the slides are fair game, but he goes off on his own example tangents.

Most of the learning in Figueroa-Lopez's course takes place in lectures, he places a heavy emphasis on his presentations, often including obscure information to be tested later on exams. This makes it difficult to distinguish important material. He does teach this information well, giving simple explanations that convey the material well.

Lectures are hard to follow. Unclear learning targets -- hard to tell what are the most important concepts versus stuff that is just "extra". The homework vs. lectures vs. practice exams vs. actual exams aren't very similar, making it hard to anticipate what will be on exams. Hardest class I've taken at WashU, harder than SDS.4211 and CSE.417T.

He goes over stuff from the previous class at the beginning which is nice, but isn't the most clear about what you do and don't need to know. The class is more of a Math for the sake of it and not 'learn this for the exam/life' which is difficult. It is a lot of content but he is definitely the best option for 439. Make sure you go to class.
Do your part, and you'll do just fine!

His teaching is ok, but he's not a good professor. He promised to do an independent study with me, but he ghosted me during semester. He wanted me to withdraw when ddl passed. I got a "No Grade" on transcript. He also offered to write recommendations for my master application, which he didn't do. Why would you offer something if you don't do it?

I learned a lot in class. It was definitely tough but that had more to do with the material than anything. He cares about his students and is super accessible outside of class. His notes were helpful too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Figueroa is a good professor and definitely cares about his students. He's accessible outside of course, and creates notes that make the material easier to understand. It's important to keep up with the material, and go to office hours and to make sure you understand the material to do well. I loved his class and learned a lot!

Unclear lecture notes with many typos; un-curved exams made of random stuff from nowhere in the textbook or homework that questions you the necessity of studying for his exams. As a student who previously made As to all other math classes, I chose to stop letting him add more probability to my transcript. Please avoid him at all cost.

It's really hard to do well in a class where the professor sends out almost daily emails with mistakes in whatever he tried to teach. Every exam this semester had at least one error, sometimes problems that couldn't be done with the given information, not to mention it's hard to learn from someone whose first language isn't English. Avoid.

Tom Fields is the man. Probably in the top 3 professors I have ever had. He makes dry, complex topics easy to understand and engaging. I think other professors at Olin should use him as a gold standard on how to teach classes - he clearly puts tremendous thought into the curriculum. I cannot imagine anybody disliking him.
Really good class. Would definitely take again
Great class
Professor Fields is awesome...but can we have some cases that aren't from the 1980s?

Did everything he could to offset these issues: short time to cover the material, 100% online (due to COVID-19). Was always available to meet 1-on-1 or group. Funny, warm, and wicked smart! Nothing intimidating about him. Can't say the same for the content... The exams were really tough, but grading was fair.
Makes Financial accouting so much easy and fun to study
One of the best professors. Extremely helpful, very approachable, genuinely cares about student's learning.
Best instructor. Very clear, funny, flexible attendance, and open book in exams. I can't tell if I love accounting or its just his effect!
Loved his World Lit class and almost all the books we've read! The pacing is ok, but you have to read quite a bit. The group discussions were most fun. He's super nice and cares about his students.

He is a nice professor, WorldLit is an interesting class. However, he isn't the best at leading discussion. Because he's so nice, he lets obnoxious, arrogant students go on and on and lecture the class when I would much rather hear what he has to say instead. He is a light grader, just show up. Pray you don't have any know-it-alls in your section.

Pretty standard compared to other German teachers at WashU. The online tests were a bonus, and none of the assignments were graded very harshly. He is quite nice, so do not worry about having him as a professor at all.

Lectures were so boring, we would discuss the same prompt for three weeks at a time. The readings are an average of 160 pages a week. Andre does not have office hours and is not open to students with perspectives different from him. His TA was much easier to engage with. Some books we read were GREAT, some were STUFFY and violent to women.

I took his World Literature course and enjoyed it a lot. You'll read a lot, but its totally worth it. He's great at moderating in-class discussions and not a tough grader. Also, he keeps the lectures short. The weekly posts on the discussion board were a bit much sometimes. But if you like to read and show up, you'll get an A. Great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fischer does a great job guiding class thought and discussion while allowing people to go off on whatever tangents they want. The only reason this isnt 5/5 is because the reading will eat up a significant amount of time, you need to be able to skim and scan with minimal annotations/notes to stay on pace in the class (world literature).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took World Lit with him, class itself was easy but the reading was VERY excessive for a 200 level and he was not receptive to students saying it was too much. Lectures are very dry and don't contribute much to the reading. He didn't always respond to his email, I found the TA much easier to reach and to engage with. He's a nice guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Fischer is a fantastic professor. If you like to read, but would rather have in-depth discussions as opposed to lengthy tests and papers, Professor Fischer is your guy. Readings are long, but interesting and Fischer leads great discussions on a wide array of topics. Very knowledgeable, but values the opinions of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great lecturer and Earth History is my favorite class I've taken at Washu. It is very lecture heavy. Problem sets are often and pretty much require asking the TA or him clarifying questions to get a good grade on. They are challenging and concepts are not always covered a lot in class. Otherwise, he runs an amazing class. Super interesting!
This guy is crazy smart and knows what he is doing.
Great lecturer. Expects a comprehensive understanding of course material.
Fantastic professor. Course material was interesting and clearly explained. Always available for help if you need it.

If you have any interest in writing creative nonfiction, take a class—any class—with Kathleen. She is a wealth of knowledge who genuinely wants each of her students to grow as writers. She has a huge heart and, though she never tries to force her intelligence on you, a huge brain. I doubt there is a person alive who regrets taking a class with her.
Kathleen is the sweetest professor. So kind and thoughtful and my writing improved in the course.

Kathleen is just wonderful. She cares about her students so much and will push you to grow as a writer. She's so down to earth and provides intelligent, incisive feedback. We need more of the compassion and quiet erudition she exudes, both in college professors and in people in general. Love her, so thankful I got to take a class with her.

Please do yourself a favor and take a class with Kathleen.  She is a wonderful writer and person, she cares deeply for each and every one of her students, and she will give you amazingly helpful feedback on your writing.  Her class was the only thing keeping me sane this semester.
Professor Marshall really cares about students learning and would constantly review labs to make sure everyone is on board.

Dr. Marshall is one of my favorite professors at WashU! She is so kind and caring. She genuinely cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. She is very approachable and always happy to explain things you may be confused about. Zooarch is a fun hands on class and as long as you pay attention and do the work you are sure to succeed!

Dr. Marshall is pretty adorable. Her lectures are also very interesting and follow a clear flow. She covers a wide breadth of material but it is all covered surprisingly in-depth. Very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about her area of study, makes sure that students get the best, most recent information. Tests format makes testing less stressful
I had Dr. Marshall for African Archaeology. The class was awesome and she's just adorable

10 ago, Dr. Fields was the first college professor I'd ever had. I was a first generation college student from nowhere special, nervous and out of my depth. In retrospect, he was the worst professor of the 50-60 I've had between college and grad school. Thanks for nothing, Doc! Hope you're reading this review and getting pissy like the first time.

Don't ask him questions during class, but if you ask him after class or during office hours, he is more than willing to help you. Also his hand writing is a little messy, so get used to it but don't comment on it.

The moment I laid eyes on Harvey was the moment I said I do...I do not want to be in this class. Why you may ask? Is because he wrote in piglatin, despite his 6-pack and sexy ass and dark chocolate complexion. He also taught me to learn how to learn...

He's...well, he's Dr. Fields. He's got a lively personality, and he has a lot of ideals regarding how students need to learn to think. I personally like the pace he sets in lectures. All of that said, I think the ideals he tries to uphold are as hopeful and encouraging as they can be ridiculous.

Dr. Fields is a great teacher.You have to adjust to his personality, but he is very intelligent and will challeng you to THINK. He will help sharpen your learning skills, knowledge and when you are done with a session with him,you will feel capable of teaching anybody,&for sure of what you do and don't know.He does genuinely care about ALL students

I suspect that Dr. Fields is an adequate professor. We are ultimately responsible for our education so take the aforementioned comments with a grain of salt. He has a job. This is more than can be said about WashU students who will graduate soon. The majority of whom can't wipe their asses without parental support from their mommies and daddies.
Not bad, but he did go to Morehouse. What can you expect?
In his eyes, if you're taking this class, he's automatically better than you...at life.
This professor made me cry because he said I was wrong in asking something, but as it turned out, I was right. He is extremely arrogant.
He'll make you feel worth less than the cost of the textbook.

Lectures are interesting, but he talks way too quickly and just writes things on board without teaching them. If you try to ask him a question he will make you feel like crap. He's not a bad teacher, but he's arrogant. If you can handle his arrogance, you might be okay in this course.
Not even Alvin and the Chipmunks talk as quickly as he does...

This is a great class but not for everyone. If you're interested in issues of race, gender, power and privilege-and particularly if you've felt your personal and political values are very different than most of your fellow students-then TAKE THIS CLASS. It is unlike anything you will take in law school. Flagg is brilliant. She's also a hard grader.
Who wants to take this class?Please avoid it at all cost.

Confusing. Less about knowing the material and more about following her exact (literally) mental process. "I don't try to grade based on what a student knows about the subject."  If you have something she's looking for, but it's not where she has it in her outline? No credit. Class is ridiculously slow. Also, confusing outline requirements.

Loved her class, completely useful, and unlike any other law school class.  I would not take it if you're conservative though, because the class is bias, though you shouldn't go to law school at all if you're conservative.
no actual teaching, just whining- told students that her grades are totally random- takes off points by mistake, acknowledges that, but then refuses to restore grade- AVOID AT ALL COSTS!
**** teacher but it was okay because she only went after men. Refused to stick to the state class guidelines and tried to change regular class into a seminar thus violating ABA rules.

Easy A. The assignments are pretty long, but they are graded very leniently. He is very smart and knowledgeable in his subject area, and conversations with him are truly intellectual. There is a final paper and presentation that requires a considerable amount of effort, though. Low stress, learned a lot, and again, easy A.

One of the easiest professors at WashU. The class is lecture heavy and sometimes they can be boring, but grading only consists of ten reading assignments and the final paper. He is very knowledge, easy grader, and gets excited when people participate in class. He is easy to reach outside of class and provides help for the final paper.

Great professor! Cares about his students and the course is a great introduction into the academic field of political science. He's an expert in poli sci, and familiar with professors around the US and they're exciting work in politics. If you're interested in representation and political mechanisms, couldn't recommend more!
by far best teacher have had at this school. hws were thought provoking and interesting

Explained material clearly. Tests were incredibly easy and problem sets were hard. You'll walk away with an A and a solid understanding of basic game theory. Beware though, slow pace at the beginning of the class picks up dramatically by the last month or so.
Fox is passionate, very approachable, and wants his students to succeed.
He is a decent professor, but it is hard to follow up from the 111 professors. The class is difficult, but if you spend enough time outside of class, it is doable.

Fournier was fine. A little on the boring side, and he seemed a bit uncomfortable in help sessions. He struggled with answering questions. Be ready for a letdown after 111A. (Still take 111A/112A over 105/106, unless you are doing taking science courses.)

What I come away with from 112 is that Fournier got the job done He wasn't especially charismatic about it and sometimes he needed to go into greater detail, but with work outside of class you can get everything down. I didn't find his office hours to be great because he'd just answer questions curtly and not explain the why or the how of the topic

His lectures while some find a little boring are well structured and presented for the most part very clearly. The exams are difficult but not impossible and the grading is pretty fair. This course is challenging but doable and worthwhile
nice guy, lectures easy to follow and make note taking effortless. class was easier than 111 but still much more difficult than ap chem imo. but if you do the non graded you will be fine

Dr. Fournier is an amazing professor. He explains concepts in a straightforward manner, although this is his first time teaching Chem112A. He can derive each formula by starting from the basic principles so that you can thoroughly understand the origin and meaning of each formula rather than just memorizing it. Exams are fair, and it's easy A.

Chem 401 is tough because it mixes abstract concepts with a ton of math and physics. I just wished Prof. Fournier could give us some explanation into what the math and quantum mean. He might be too smart to teach this class to undergraduates. Nice guy, but I would not want to take a course with him again.

Professor Fournier is nice, and I want to like him, but it was a frustrating semester. He really does not explain things well. If you struggle understanding the meaning of mathematical equations and constructs, you will struggle in 401. He is not able to give intuition into the math and the consequences of it.
Really great lecturer and kind person. Quantum mechanics is a difficult topic but Fournier makes it digestible and highly enjoyable.

Fournier is fantastic and enthusiastic. P chem 1 is unbelievably difficult and the homework sets are insane. However, he is always happy to meet with you and discuss even the simplest concepts as many times as you need so that you can understand them. Go to office hours! Hardest class I've ever taken with one of the best professors I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Understand it is Quantum Chem, there will be math. Kinda fun to learn the math for the content presented in Chem 111. Fournier is very organized caring. His lectures are a bit fast, but he reviews content at the beginning of every lecture. You have to do the homework (it is also graded) because some of the content is presented through questions.

I genuinely enjoyed attending every lecture -- he is never stale and he GENUINELY cares about you! Beware: HW Sets are very challenging and long, Exams are not easy by any stretch of the imagination, and the class made me do more math than some actual math courses. Will you learn a lot though? Yes. It's a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hard class but great professor who explains things very well, and if not, he is very accessible outside class. He loves using excel for homework a bit too much though... It is math heavy, but everything you need to know should be covered in lecture (I've only taken Calc 3).

This is a tough class, especially if you haven't seen the mathematics in a while (or ever). Joe does a good job lecturing and is pretty much always available to help you get through the homework sets which are typically very tough
Good guy. I remember him from TV - Opie from Mayberry. The course involved a ton of math, maybe a bit too much. He worked hard to get the material across. Overall, an ok semester.

Super nice guy, very approachable, accessible, and willing to help. His lectures are super well organized, well paced, and I genuinely enjoyed going to every class. He is able explain concepts in a conceptual and mathematical ways both very well. Content is hard but not so bad if you stay on top of it. Office hours were always super helpful.

Awesome professor - super available outside of class and really willing to help. Very organized and homeworks are super relevant to class. However exams are very difficult so be prepared to have to really know whats going on

Religion and Science. Hands down, best professor I've ever had. He's absolutely nuts, but in the best way possible. Has a ridiculous amount of knowledge on pretty much everything. Super-educated guy, yet really approachable. Sure, his lectures will go off topic, but it still remains the most interesting and engaging class I've taken

Crazy, in the best way possible. Incredibly intelligent, expert/wellknown in his field. Must take a class from him if possible. Not the most well organized class, but everything he mention whether directly relevant or not, is important for any person to know. So much to learn from him. Class not hard, workload very small, optional fieldtrips rock.

Classes have no focus, direction, or cohesiveness. Massive amounts of reading are meant to substitute for the absolute waste of class time. Makes you memorize and define whatever comes into his mind with no connecting theme. Left every class wishing I could have 90 minutes of my life back, an utter and complete waste.

I had Flinn for Primal Religions of the Americas.  Its hard to understand, the class isn't normal, you can't really take notes because its so random, but you learn a lot and get to think about things you never thought about before (like why did the Northwest stories always have sexual aspects).  The main assignment was making and painting a mask.

The person who posted a comment below is a complete hater to the max. This man is incredibly intelligent and gifted in all domains of academia. It's apparent that this whinny person below did'nt get his A (cry me a river). You will leave this class as a better person (unless you're the loser that posted the comment under this one!)

Senile and decrepit. Assigns too much reading, and uninteresting stuff at that. Grades by opinion and never responds to e-mail. He told us at 10 pm the night before our huge dictionary assignment was due, when it was already too late, that, oh yeah, we could have done it as a group. Never had to deal with such incompetence from a professor before.

sacred shrines and holy places: crazy prof, interesting, shows a ton of slides though and many movies. has a lot of information but biased and brings politics into the classroom constantly. should have him once in re stu before graduating. not a lot of work, but grading is weird and not explained. only get the hitech text, he doesn't use anything e

Professor Flinn was one of the most interesting and insightful professors I have ever had. He can be tough to understand at times, but usually he is very funny. He is definitely not afraid to hold anything back in class.
Took 2 classes with Flinn. If you don't care about your grade and want to learn alot, he is the best prof. at Washington University. Great guy!
Very interesting, but sometimes unclear
Flinn is hilarious, has a great personality and wants his students to do well.  The unfortunate truth is that he just can't teach, so don't take the class if you're anal about grades.

disregard the 11/28 comment. a few people in the class complain about grades instead of accepting that they didn't do as well as others. i disliked Flinn at first, but he grew on me. He's unorganized and incoherant (I learned more from the TAs in review sessions than I did from Flinn all semester) but the class makes you think and Flinn's fun.

Flinn's a very interesting and insightful professor.  I think his class is a good experience.  I disagree with the other comments from 11/28.  I think this person is a little deranged, as you can probably tell from what they wrote.

NEVER EVER TAKE THIS CLASS.  for that matter, never never take a flinn class.  there is no standard of grading, no organization, no actual learning happening.  and by the way, the dictionary (separate from the final paper) is going to be AT LEAST 50 PAGES for this class.  thats about as long as a thesis!  this man is clearly deranged
Incredibly interesting, but also incredibly disorganized. If you like structure, don't take this class. If it doesn't bother you that the syllabus is only for show, don't miss it.

Hokay, remarkably entertaining professor, but his classes desparately need organization.  He fumbles sometimes with clarity, but as long as you don't believe anything he says, you'll fair very well in his class.  He has some great tangents.  Very interesting man.
Flinn is awesome

very interesting character. i enjoyed the class.  he does go off on random tangents, but what he says is still interesting. didn't like how 45% of grade was determined by 2 projects due the finals week, 2 days apart from another.

Awesome guy and professor. Killer stories.  Ask him to tell the one about the corpse.  You'll expand your knowledge and your opinions a great deal through his class. Definitely take any of his classes if you get the chance.
i'm a fan.

Awesome prof... like some people said, hilarious but distracted. Someone you have to experience to understand, but not for everyone because of the way he is. The amount of work isn't too bad, but can be a handful if you wait until the end of the semester to do.
Flinn's awesome, ask him about the corpse story.
Flinn only picks on people that he knows can take it.  Scatterbrained, yes, but always considerate of those who might not be able to handle his eccentric personality.  Best prof. at WashU.

Hilarious.  Knowledgeable in practically everything.  Great stories.  If you take him for a summer class, he always invites the class to his house for cheesecake - truly representing what kind of guy he is.  Amazing field trips!
Interesting guy.  Can be disorganized, but makes you think *really* hard.  Very insightful.
i agree with the last comment...he was always picking on people, and could never stay on the subject we were supposed to talk about.
could not follow any of his lectures because of how many tangents he took each class. he picked on people for their beliefs, which is not cool for a religion teacher.
Flinn's awesome.  He is VERY KNOWLEDGEABLE about virtually everything.  He is the kind of professor all academics should strive to be.
Excellent professor, the tangents and stories are wonderful, and if you take several classes of his, you really do soak up a lot of history of Christianity.
Very fun and interesting professor.
ya definately crazy, and his tangents can just go on and on. Expectations of the class and of assignements are very unclear and fieldtrips to local holy places are random. Very frustrating sometimes
Super guy, good teacher...Tells lots of great stories, and gets you involved in the class.

One of the best professors at WashU, take Math 310W/3015 with him. So nice, explains everything very well, genuinely loves math and his students. Always willing to help out outside class and even after the class is over.
Me might be the smartest professor I have ever had. If you have the chance to take 310 with him do it because he was great. Knows the material well and makes the class fun. Would recommend.

This man is a gift to the world. If you can, take Math 310 with writing with him. He explains everything super well, he is always very obviously engaged in the content, and he is always willing to help in office hours. He also has the cutest dog that hangs out in office hours!!!

Prof. Frankel is such a great math professor! He explains complex concepts in an easy way and is always happy to help students in OH. He really wants each student to understand the material and do well in his class. HIGHLY RECOMMEND taking 310 with him!!!

Frankel was a good professor, at the back half of the semester it got a lot easier and I stopped having to put a lot of effort in, take that as you will. He definitely cared about students and it was clear how welll he understood the content. Overall good professor. (but was not very good at responding to emails)

This guy is an absolute gem. Easily the best professor I have had and will ever have at WashU in any department. It is very clear that all he cares about is his students actually learning something and becoming more interested in the topic. Made it very doable to succeed in the course and learn a lot/be more interested. TAKE HIM FOR ANY CLASS.

Great professor who is super supportive and engaging. Class material could be very random but provides some insight to higher math. Also prof Frankel explains concept very clear and it's easy to understand. Sometimes the course pace could be a bit fast, but he is willing to answer questions after class or during office hours. PLEASE TAKE HIS 310.

Prof Frankel is the best math professor I've ever taken. As a CS student, so math doesn't come as second nature. Still, I've felt like my math acumen has at least doubled through this course. The course surveys vast branches of math that may be tough, but Professor Frankel explains in such a clear and concise manner that everything seems intuitive.

Honestly, the best professor that I've had in college so far. Super genuine and cares about his students' success. Will sometimes skew the topic that we're covering to talk about super interesting that relates to the real world. 1000% recommend taking his class.

Wants students to learn and have fun, and his lectures succeeded in doing this. Explained concepts well and encouraged students to ask questions. He also held office hours where he happily answered questions. However, material covered felt slightly disorganized. I do wish the class was more rigorous, esp. regarding proofs. Felt it to be too easy
vanriper was very passionate in teaching and cared for each student! however, grading was harsh at times

She's a nice enough person and is knowledgeable about her subject but is a super tough grader and gives horrible feedback. She is a very picky grader and even if you fulfill every part of her rubric, she will still find something not to like. She seems to think she is very charitable, which only makes the experience more frustrating.

Felt like a high school class. Didn't go into depth on like anything. Not the college education I'm paying for lol. Much better advisor than teacher lol. Kinda wack grading. Stickler about being late.

the sweetest professor ever! Her class was extremely easy, as most classes are group activities  where you are expected to engage. We did have to read a chapter each week, but as long as you skim through it and write a few notes, you'll be fine. The midterm and final were open book which made the class very low stress. I love how passionate she is!
VanRiper did a great job teaching engaging content in fresh ways, combining in-class activities, guest speakers, and group projects into a mix that really helped me retain the content.

Eccentric, but also extremely caring and invested in this class. She liked to interact with students and was happy to answer any questions. However, the class was frustratingly disorganized -- we never knew when assignments/tests/presentations were and what the expectations for them were. Also struggled with technology. Still worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: While the course itself was not challenging, she led lectures like a high school classroom. Lots of time-wasting learning exercises that didn't impart any knowledge. Additionally, I didn't feel that she treated me like a real person, often speaking in a condescending tone.
Very good professor. She cares about her students and is incredible flexible on extensions. She's also very kind

Charlotte is one of the most caring instructors at WashU. She is so invested in her students as learners and as people. She always strives to validate the ideas of each student and encourages participation in a way that is welcoming and not pressuring.

Cares a lot about her students, gives good feedback, and is very accessible outside of class. Lectures can sometimes get dull and you might feel like you're back in high school. Very kind and wants everyone to succeed. The reading schedule can get heavy but is mostly manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor that genuinely cares about her students. Very accommodating and wants you to succeed. Material was interesting and was taught remarkably. Highly recommend Professor Fressilli for any course she is teaching.

Charlotte creates such a welcoming atmosphere for students and is genuinely so passionate about what she teaches. She's really good at engaging students and generating interesting discussions. Grading is very fair and you're set up for success if you complete the assignments.

By far the best professor Ive had at WashU. Genuinely cares about the mental health and wellbeing of her students and goes the extra mile to make sure we are doing well. In addition, extremely helpful when answering emails/office hours and will help guide you no matter how lost you feel in writing. Definitely the most helpful prof and kindest heart

this is a 10 person class and he asks questions so he can answer them himself. Lovett doesn't accept any answers other than his own singular "correct" opinion. i've been in this class for three months and he hasn't let me finish a sentence without interrupting me.

This professor refuses to acknowledge that anyone other than himself could be in possession of a correct answer. He does not allow for differentiation in analysis nor does he pose questions grounded in the texts. He is incredibly boring to listen to and discourages students to make connections to other works or approach w previous knowledge.
Unhelpful grading schemes
No comment

Felt like Plato listening to Socrates. Whenever I have a question about politics, I consistently ask myself "what would Lovett say about this."

Hard to get above an A- but always left his lectures feeling inspired and wanting to learn more. Definitely one of the top 3 professors if not #1 at WashU.
Very lecture heavy but his lectures are great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are a little boring but interesting topic and the professor is very knowledgeable.

These reviews do not really capture my experience in his class. Honestly, I have never been more frustrated with any professor. Generally unhelpful when explaining literally anything. If you do not already have extensive knowledge of the topics, DO NOT take his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you are unfamiliar with philosophy, you probably will not learn much from this class. Generally unhelpful with feedback but will grade harshly.

Theories of social justice was a fascinating class. There is a lot of reading, but if you like pol. theory they are all interesting, just takes a while to get through. Lovett is a fantastic lecturer and explains all of the ideas in an approachable manner. Rarely left a lecture with a question. Knows his material well and engages questions well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Social Justice is a great class for polisci majors. I thought the material was very interesting, but it's a large-ish lecture so there is limited opportunity for discussion/participation. You don't need to buy the books or do any reading if you go to class every day!! Take his Global Justice seminar if you prefer discussion. Moderately hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lovett is a nice guy and clearly very knowledgeable, but he drones on for the entire class period day after day with no semblance of participation whatsoever, usually continuing on past when class is over without noticing. He relays what's in the reading to the letter and repeats himself endlessly. One of the most boring classes i've ever taken.

Great professor. Brilliant, engaging, challenging. You get into some pretty hefty political philosophy and he makes it, if not easy, at least navigable. Has high expectations and won't give a good grade unless you've earned it.

Theories of Justice: a really interesting course and I learned a lot. Lovett is a great instructor and very clear in explaining difficult concepts. Exams are straight forward and easy, term paper requires work.
Interesting lecturer with extensive knowledge and preparation. Difficult to get to meet with outside of class, doesnt seem to like meeting with students much. Tough and sometimes unclear grader.

Lovett is BRILLIANT. Amazing just to sit in a class and listen to him for three hours a week. The class (Early Political Thought) wasn't particularly hard gradewise, but I'm sure if you do the reading (unfortunately I didn't) you'll get a lot more out of it.

Really smart guy. Seemed meek in the beginning but he knew the material backwards and forwards and made it really interesting. Would recommend him to anyone, as long as they are willing to work for their grade.

Extremely knowledgeable - this guy knows his stuff. If you want someone you can ask almost any question about this is the guy you want. Takes some work to get above a 90 on papers, but the lectures are interesting and I learned so much.

I felt that he really cared about helping his students improve. He had fairly high expectations for a class full of freshmen, but he was very available to help students improve their papers and graded on improvement. I feel that I got a lot out of his class.

Lectures are interesting+interesting material, yet Lovett is quite the difficult grader and he is not clear his on grading procedures either...just a whole bunch of numbers in a margin leaving the student confused. I would haved asked him about it, but he is very shy and not that approachable outside class.
He is very attractive
An incredible amount of reading, and the readings tend to be wordy and confusing.  Lectures are interesting though.
No Comments

Frachetti does cool fieldwork so it's nice to learn from a professor who has some interesting research under his belt. This course is super theoretical and sometimes feels a bit meandering - wouldn't recommend taking if you're type A and prefer an organized canvas page. Very big picture course - took very few notes. Also, tons of group projects.

A couple of one-page papers, one take-home midterm, a final paper, and one group project presentation. The lectures were interesting, but I sometimes lost track of what he was saying. Great professor overall who exhibits passion and care. Be prepared to go outside a lot (we analyzed the landscape of east end campus/Brookings as well as forest park)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Frachetti is an amazing teacher. He truly cares about what he teaches, and he does not fail to engage with his students. His inspiration comes from his unique experiences, which you cannot find from anyone else. His class is not difficult at all, but I only suggest taking it with an open mind, and a desire to truly understand the nuances.

Course material was interesting and Prof. Frachetti is a really engaging lecturer. That being said he is almost never around to answer questions or get help from. When you finally get a chance to meet with him he acts like he is too important to answer your questions. It's a shame, the class could be so cool.

Very intellectual man. I love listening to his lectures, and the readings are usually interesting. He will notice if you aren't there even though he doesn't take attendance. The exam is very difficult, but the final is pretty chill. Highly recommend this class if you want a light workload but inspirational class in your schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Really engaging lecturer, but his tests are not on the material presented in class (or in the assigned readings for that matter) and he is terrible to try to get help from. He is unavailable 99% of the time and the 1% of time he will talk to you, he acts like he has better places to be. Wish I would have known, wouldn't have taken this class.
Fun class but exams are relatively hard. Exams are a bit long and should answer faster. Recommend to take it pass/fail.
Great class and great professor. He took a very relevant and interesting topic and made it fun.

Awesome dude- passionate about what he's teaching, which is essential in this class due to its novel subject matter (first time Landscape Studies have been taught here). Has a zest for teaching and is committed to each student's comprehension and success. IS AN ASSET TO THE WASH U COMMUNITY
He is the best professor I ve ever met. He speaks fluent in my language - russin, really smart. I like him......
He is sooo hilarious! And hot. Oh, and a good teacher too.
Very laid-back and funny, tells great stories about his experiences as an anthropologist. Very real.
Amazing professor. Always gives high grade and detailed handwriting feedback. Great sense of responsibility that cares everyone. Really like his teaching style!
Really cares about his students.  Quirky, funny guy.

Professor Frankel is a phenomenal professor! One of the best professors I've ever had. Every week I looked forward to his Business Analysis and Financial Statements class. He truly cares about what you get out of the subject matter and engages you in class discussions very well. I highly recommend him. His knowledge of the subject is outstanding.
No Comments

Excellent lecturer. Rather clear on elucidating the objective of the European Union and is a great strategic thinker in his own right. I was glad to have taken his EU class and shared affinity for his Europhile stance, which is admirable in this day and age.

I really enjoyed this class but found the material to be incredibly difficult to understand. If you don't already know about the EU, be prepared to spend a lot of time figuring out the differences between a ton of similar organizations and nitty gritty policies.
Great professor, class has a good mix of activities and assessment types

Discusses course concepts in relation to real-world events in lectures, which make them engaging. Lectures are sometimes not as focused, though. There are a lot of readings, but that's just the nature of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Either Prof Gabel has done some serious soul-searching over the last few years, or these reviews are way off-base. Politics of the EU is a lot of reading but it's not overwhelming, especially if you keep up throughout the semester. Lectures are super engaging and grading standards are reasonable.

workload was truly insane(~1000pages vs. ~500 for my other classes);lectures are interesting but sometimes hard to follow as he tries to be oratorical;occasionally arrogant;exams-very hard;you've got to be very precise in your answers;yes there were reviews for the exams but still too much reading-this class must be your 1st priority!!!

Politics of the EU. Great class. Yes there's a LOT of reading especially in the beginning, but come on you are in college now (and in the top rated school in the country). Professor is knowledgeable, lectures are interesting. Majority of the grade (70%): midterm and final, professor is very clear about what will be on the exam in the review session

Gabel is on his game when it comes to the EU, but expectations are very high in regard to absorbing 1000's of pages of material for exams.  Hmmm what will he ask on his exams, overarching questions---NOT, in fact, he asks detailed info on less important things that you wouldn't think would be on an exam.  wording on his exams are difficult

Pretty arrogant.  Each test covered ~1000 pages of reading and was the majority of the test.  Gabel talks down to his students.  It isn't "daring" them to challenge him.  He responded to about 50% of my emails and blamed me for something that was his fault.  I'm not taking any more polysci classes bc of this experience.
Dr. Gabel is incredibly smart and dares you to challenge him - he loves it.  You have to be on your game if you do.
His grading isn't clear but the work is very easy. He his a great person and very genuine. I enjoyed his class.
