I really like Prof Ward as a person, but was really disappointed with his class. Expectations are incredibly unclear as to grading, what he wants out of assignments (essays don't have prompts), and class structure is very unorganized. He seems to not know what he wants to do with the course and improvises class time.

Does not have clear grading criteria. Lacks clear instructions, engagement skills, and structure when it comes to lecture and often rambles. Not very great at giving critical and productive feedback in a manner that doesn't delegitimize work. Has a syllabus but jumps around A LOT and this makes it hard to figure out what material should be prepared
homeworks are annoying. good teacher, but the class is more difficult than people make it out to be. ta's can grade quite harshly

Prof Garnett was clear with was expected and gave out a decent amount of extra credit. Completely manageable class if you put effort in. My biggest complaint about Prof Garnett is his attitude. He was consistently sassy and rude to students during the entire semester. Just stay up to date with the zybooks, ignore his attitude, and you'll be fine

While professor Garnett might be kind of boring on the surface, he's passionate about what he teaches and is funny in lecture. That being said, the class is easy if you do the online Zybooks textbook and don't chat/copy the homework. You also get 0.5 extra on your total exam scores for each lecture you attend over the course of the semester.

Don't trust low reviews! This was my favorite class of the semester and the lectures were super beneficial.  Brian is very passionate about math and said some of the funniest one-liners! His personality is super quirky but very kind. Gives extra credit for coming to class. Downside, homework took a long time and I found the 2nd exam to be tough.
Hes so boring and a robot don't take a class with him he has an ego and comes off mean especially if you don't understand something. Very test heavy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy and great professor. He can be a bit awkward, but he knows the material down pat. He has a bit of a no-nonsense attitude, which you may like or you may dislike. Exams are fair. If you go to class and don't cheat on the homework, you will do well. Attendance not required. Homework is not hard but takes 5 hours per week on average.

Honestly my favorite class at Washu so far - but not because of Garnett. His lectures were pretty boring so I stopped showing up (only go if you need extra credit), but the material in the class itself is really interesting from both math and cs perspectives. Homeworks are free and exams are straight forward if you actually do the zybooks exercises

Prof. Garnett is probably is the worst prof. He doesn't show any sympathy and is anxious when teaching, he talks like a robot, and he doesn't look around to see if students has questions during lecture. ZyBooks doesn't contain all the details we expected to know as he mentioned this during lecture, even though attending lectures is optional.
Never went to class, learned everything from the zybooks and was able to get an A. If you can do the homework you'll do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: hes lowkey kinda mean but a pretty good prof. go to lecture bc he goes over stuff that isn't in the zybook but is on hw and the tests and you can get extra credit.
Brian is the best. No slander will be tolerated.

Super awkward guy but really sweet and good at teaching. Lectures can get kind of boring but they aren't required to go. If you do the Zybooks reading and practice problems, you'll do find in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kind of an awkward guy but seems to genuinely care. Also active on WashU Reddit which is kind of funny. Exams are like the Zybooks and if you put in the effort you will definitely get an A.
Easy class, his lectures were boring but at least useful

Clearly the better Garnett. Good at teaching logic and discrete math. If you read the textbook and go to class you will do well. Exams are fair and assignments are graded forgivingly. Great class, highly recommend

I don't particularly understand where the negative reviews come from. CSE 240 was a well-taught class and I learned a lot. Lectures were helpful but not mandatory, and the textbook made things quite clear. Exams are fair and as long as you do the homework you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring/redundant since the professor just writes/talks through what's covered in the textbook, except the few times there are long examples not found in the book; those will usually be on the test. However, it's still a very straightforward class and the prof is very responsive/helpful on Piazza. Not super enjoyable, but does the job.

To be honest, no disrespect but I didn't go to almost all of the lectures because the Zybooks covered all of the content and everything from the class can be learned in the Zybooks. There is a lot of hw from the Zybooks. However, while the lectures can be boring he seems to be a helpful and caring guy, at least from the few lectures I went to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Garnett is one of the first professors at WashU that I felt really cared. He actually responds on Piazza all the time and clearly cares about getting to know his students and having them succeed. It also is an interesting course and both his lectures and the textbook help solidify the concepts so you feel well-prepared for the exams.

Some people say his lecture was boring, which might be true, but I found it ok. If you attend classes and be present, you will get decent grade. I attended to all the classes and did not study much outside of class.

At the end of the day the exams look fairly similar to the homework and the content is mangeable. His lectures are boring/not helpful and his notes are very messy, but by closely reading the textbook you are 100% set for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The worst lecturer I've ever had. Answers in with attitude, barely looks up, and not rly accessible outside of lecture. Lectures suck but he gives random quizzes that add points to exam grades. Exams are on homework stuff but you won't get your homework graded before the exam. Take it with a friend and live & breathe Zybooks to survive this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Scrabble champion. Looks straight out of the 80s. Walking CS prof stereotype. I concur with the review below this one wholeheartedly.

His teaching style (partially prewritten iPad notes) is sometimes hard to follow, unorganized, and can be too fast. Got lost easily due to these reasons. He isn't that good at answering or taking questions (awkward, doesn't look up often & can be sassy). The exams are fair/similar to homework problems. Would recommend utilizing the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is fairly easy and his lectures are pretty good, but you certainly do not have to go to lectures to do well in this class. His exams are very much like homework problems.

Let's be real: you are not going to go to lecture. Zybooks will be your lecture, your professor, and your god. You will put in just enough effort, get a good grade, and move on. This is the main attitude for 240. Garnett is a nice guy and is a good enough teacher, but low energy. The weekly homework is often a slump, but good for learning.

prof Garnett's lectures were boring at times, but he goes at a slow enough pace for you to get all of the notes down. He gives easy, low-stakes quizzes during class for extra credit. Exams are okay if you study, and the hw he assigns prepares you well. Overall a decent professor for 240.

Been said already. Lectures a bit boring and unorganized, his notes aren't super readable at all times. However, exams are EXTREMELY fair, homework policy adds an extra 100/0 to your HW grade. Lectures give minor extra credit from "quizzes" but not super worth it. Can pay minor attention and still get all the concepts.
Best lecturer on campus. 100% better than roman. Smartest chess player ever, and 240 is good class ok ok
Easy class, good prof, smart guy too!

Read/take notes on textbook, and use piazza for homework problems. He's responsive on piazza. He can be funny sometimes but otherwise lecture not necessary at all. The lecture tends to be a mediocre, unorganized recap of the textbook reading. Exams are usually fair and not excessively hard. Spent 4-6 hours a week outside class.

Garnett is overall a solid professor. He isn't particularly amazing, but his lectures got the point across, and his tests matched the problems we practiced. The lectures are a little boring, but you can get by without paying much attention to them. His style can be more challenging for difficult topics, which can problematic.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easy self-taught class, uncaring professor, fair exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
This was the hardest class I've taken in my life - Garnett did not much it much easier. His lectures are dense and very proof-heavy, although he is good one-on-one. Much of the learning is self-taught or from the TAs.

However, his class is very fair. The exams are a direct reflection of the homeworks. Study the textbook and you'll ace the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's overall a decent professor. It's important to attend lectures or at least watch the recordings. Lectures go by pretty fast but the ZyBooks really help you understand the concepts more and provides good examples. Exams can be a bit difficult but doing a lot of practice will really help. TA office hours & asking him for help is also recommended!
So hard. Angstrom  towards students not good teacher and hard grader

Lectures were faster, meant for people with CS knowledge (which I have none of), were pretty boring, but still were helpful in fleshing out the concepts, so make sure to watch lecture. There were extra credit pop quizzes, so bonus there. Exams weren't bad, they were reflected by the homework. Prof Garnett wasn't amazing, but he also wasn't bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Garnett is a nice guy, a little quiet and awkward but he is good at explaining the topics in class. 240 is also not so difficult conceptually. Make sure you have enough time for hw because they can be pretty long. Also be in lecture to get better understanding and take the quizzes for extra credit.
Garnett is a fine professor. Goes a little fast during lecture, but is ready and willing to answer questions and provide help outside of lectures. Not the worst and not the best

Bad teacher overall. We have exams before we get our homework solutions returned to us. Is incredibly unspecific about what we will be tested on. A direct quote: "The test will include questions and problems that you will be prepared to answer after doing the reading and homework." Then proceeds to test us on things that were not on the homework.

Dr. Garnett is a good prof. These bad reviews are straight-up wrong. Brian is super nice, helpful, willing to meet with students, and makes a fair class. It's hard to not be fair when the entire class is on logic and discrete mathematics - the most objective subject in the entire world. Brian and the TAs are here to help and the class is not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The course overall was fairly difficult, but I found the textbook readings and exercises far more helpful than Prof. Garnett's lectures. I finished the class with an A and watched maybe 3 lectures at the most. Lectures are very proof-oriented even when we aren't doing proofs (in HW or exams). A necessary but difficult class, and Garnett is okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Surprised by the bad reviews. I found Garnett to be a pretty straightforward prof with clear expectations and fair grading criteria. Yea his lectures aren't the most interesting in the world, but he does a good job at breaking down confusing concepts and explaining them clearly. He was also very organized, especially when we turned to ZoomU.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The midterm was super poorly handled; everyone scored probably at least 10% lower than what they deserved due to awful rubric points and misleading questions. Course policies were needlessly stringent: many students had issues accessing data needed to finish assignments and yet TAs and Professor were entirely unwilling to offer any extensions

Honestly, I'm not sure why the reviews are so bad. Garnett is a decent grader, this class is all proofs, so a lot of the time if you request a regrade you can argue your point. He is accessible outside of class and he knows his stuff. He is kind of awkward, but overall not bad. He isn't like AMAZING, but I would take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: literally the worst. hes so rude. people are afraid to ask questions to him on piazza because of his sassy responses. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!
extremely harsh grader, also has little to no respect for students. Infamous professor at WashU

He seems to prefer to complain about doing his job than to actually do it. After a particularly poorly-worded test, he complained on piazza about how many regrade requests there were and told us we were entitled. Maybe its just a problem with your test?
Heres the best tip when dealing w brian: dont stare directly into his eyes. they are completely black and he will analyze u and take your soul.

Brian Garnett is one of the most incompetent teachers I have met. He is disrespectful to students on Piazza, makes jokes that are objectively wack, and can't explain much at all. Overall super unhelpful professor who made an easy class hard. Smh
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Childs has an amazing sense of humor that captivates his students. Seriously cannot recommend him or his classes enough!

A very useful class which was also very manageable. The course was designed to be very straightforward and to teach research methods that might be harder to understand in a different setting. You get good materials to study. The instructor is helpful. Class is very interesting. This is perhaps one of the best classes I have taken at WashU.
Childs is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are super interesting and he very clearly cares about the content and students.

Professor Childs is a really fun lecturer. I learned a lot in Cultural Anthro. I hear next year is his last year teaching the class, so I definitely recommend trying to take it with him if you can. He's super smart and interesting, but has a great sense of humor and makes class really fun. Even if you aren't an Anthro major, take this class.

Of two Cultural Anthro professors, Childs is the most entertaining. He does a great job bringing in different types of media and has lots of funny anecdotes. All the test questions come right from the lectures, but that is an insane amount of material. You don't have to do the readings, but show up to class!!!

These were lectures that made the material fun and we used the textbook, but a reduced price version because he disagrees with how books are marketed. You must go to class and do the readings or you will fail; they're interesting! He makes jokes and answers questions in office hours. Come prepared with questions. People generally love him. STUDY!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pop & Society: pretty easy and straightforward class. He makes lectures interesting and engaging. As long as you pay attention in class and review your notes, the exams are a piece of cake. He supplements his lecture powerpoint with videos, images, animations, etc. and posts the notes online so you're not frantically writing during class.

He is a great guy with a passion for anthropology. All of his examples in class have to do with his research, which makes his class really interesting because he's so interested. Do the readings, go to lecture when you can, and it's a fairly easy class. He is approachable and a great guy which makes class that much better

One of my favorite classes that I've taken at WashU. An amazing professor, who makes his lectures interesting and engaging. Grades are composed solely of 3 exams. He posts all the notes online as well as previous exams so studying the material is not difficult.

Took this class on a whim as a freshman to fulfill a social science cluster and it convinced me to major in Anthropology! Professor Childs is great lecturer and researcher and explains the material very well. The class also provides a good introduction to various fields of anthropology. I highly recommend taking this class!

Awesome lecturer that presents fun material. Like others have said, going to class is totally worth it just to hear Childs lecture. Class is certainly easy as long as you study the notes he posts at least 3 days prior to the exams. I don't think doing the readings is necessary as long as you go to class and study the notes thoroughly.

Best class I've taken here. Fairly easy, really interesting- the way I'd like every class to be. Childs is a phenomenal lecturer and makes class entertaining. Was easily my favorite class every day and the one I learned the most in. Can't say enough good things about him.

His class is one of the most interesting that I have taken at Wash U. A very good lecturer who uses a lot of helpful examples to illustrate concepts. Quite a bit of reading material, but if you look through all of the readings and attend the lectures, you'll do well in the class.
easiest class at wustl.

can't give this class a high enough review. Childs is a great lecturer who focuses on mostly interesting stuff. On top of that, the class is incredibly easy and lecture notes and old tests are available online so attendance is not necessary at all; i still went pretty often just because i like Childs though. Tests are incredibly easy

An interesting class and an inspirational professor. Someone wrote before that he will make you laugh and cry in one class--I read that before taking the class and it's completely true (in fact it happened more than once). If you're at all interested in Tibet, you should take this class!

Childs makes every effort to make sure students succeed in his course. If you go to class, pay attention, and take notes there is NO reason not to do well. Childs is passionate about his stuff-- knows it well and teaches it in an easy, understandable manner. All in all, great class to take if you are looking for a laid-back atmosphere. Recommended!
Loved this class! It was a pretty big lecture (like 300 people) but he makes the class seem a lot more intimate through his teaching style. I definitely recommend this class!
Very interesting class! Highly recommend taking cultural anthro with Prof. Childs. Videos are fantastic!
excellent teacher, has a great sense of humour uses youtube and real world examples, best class taken freshman year, he is easy to a point.
Simply amazing. Lectures are interesting. Class information is seemlesly integrated with his research of Tibetan society. My favriote professor so far.
class is really easy. but he can't really teach... makes jokes that don't make sense. he seems to be teaching from memorization than actual knowledge. just shows where all that tuition $ is going!
Childs is the shiz-nizzle...

BEST CLASS AT WASHU!! Childs is an AWESOME teacher. He makes class so interesting - found myself laughing and crying during class. HIGHLY RECOMMEND! Also, Childs has the most intricate powerpoints that you can access online. Grades based on only 3 exams, most heavily on just one. Follow the study guide. Class starts on the hour so don't be late!

I only took this class because other classes I wanted to take were full and it ended up being my favorite class of the semester.  Childs is a great teacher, very knowledgeable, organized, and obviously passionate about the subject.  Highly recommended class and teacher!

This guy is awesome, mainly because he let us watch Monty Python as part of the class. He's uber funny and even though the class is 3 hours long, it usually doesn't feel like it. Especially recommended if you like Tibet.

Childs is a great professor and an awesome guy. He put together really interesting readings for the class which I still talk about and remember today. His presentations were entertaining and helpful and he has a lot of knowledge to share. Highly recommended.
No Comments
prof childs is so kind and willing to help his students! lectures were fun providing the class read the material and participated- he loves his own jokes too...a nice and interesting professor
Fun guy with creative assignments. Lots of reading, but doable. Interesting guy - did a lot of fieldwork in India and Nepal. My entire class wants to go to Nepal now for spring break.
He is so nice...I wish I could take him for all my chemistry classes!

He is now teaching at UTD. I read this comment and I just wonder who did really give this man a job at UTD to create the same horrible experiences for students at UTD!! he is one of the WORST professors I have ever seen. No sympathy or respect towards students.
He shouldn't be in academia!!!
He is terrible and unapproachable.  He does not care about the students at all.  The whole semester was all about him entertaining himself.  Worst ever.
Horrible! Never again.

Thank God the semester is over.  Gelb is terrible and does not care at all about the students.  It is clear that he was counting the days until he leaves.  I hope he will not be teaching wherever he is going.  Gelb:  get rid of the notepad!

If you expect to learn any practical chemistry, you will be sorely disappointed. He knows his stuff, but even after 40 hours of listening to him, you probably wont. His test questions are seemingly meant to trick students and you'll have seen nothing like them in class. Truly horrible.

Pompous, bad teacher. Knows his stuff, but doesn't care about students. His lectures are boring and he spends the whole time deriving equations as opposed to actually teaching us anything useful for the exams.

He's not the most engaging professor but he is very passionate about his subject. As others have said, he's very interested in theory that no one else cares about which is pretty annoying. Going to class is a waste of time as he never adds anything of importance that isn't in the notes in lecture.(just copy someone's notes)
Gelb is horrific.  He does not care at all about if we are learning anything.  I am not sure he is talking to during lecture, but it is not the students.  Get rid of the notepad and derivations.
Awful. Derives formulas the entire class period. no interaction with the class whatesoever
Spends a ridiculous amount of time on theory rather than giving examples.

WEIRD.  He is off the charts weird.  I don't like just copying his notes as he writes them, but at least we know exactly what we have to know.  His tests are straight forward, and a bit too easy.  With so many students, I would rather harder exams to spread out scores, but also to better push us.  I'm not sure all the derivations are needed.
Quirky guy. Class merely consisted of us copying what he wrote on lecture slides onto our own copy. Tests were fairly straight forward (more than first semester).
Overall Gelb's lectures are well-organized and easy to follow but I found that he spent way too much time on derivations of equations rather than applications. His hair is awesome though.

the man you want for gen chem II. lectures are extremely well organized and clear. he makes it interesting as well. great hair, great sense of humor. exams are challenging but doable (not like 111 exams). quizzes pretty straightforward if you do the hw. the hw problems he makes up are real hard, but generally you get by with the text problems.
he tries to teach but tends to go off tangent of what we are supposed to be learning about. he seems pompous, but i think it might just be the hair.

This is an excellent professor. His lecture slides were very organized and his derivation of equations in class really helped me to connect and understand many chemical principles. His tests can be a little bit tricky initially, but by the end of the semester you'll be able to pick them out. Overall excellent professor!
He knows his stuff, and his exams are not impossible.. Not too many curve balls.
Lev Gelb is WONDERFUL. He's organized and clear. It's extremely evident that he really knows his stuff. Plus he's endlessly entertaining.
Far better than Buhro, whom I had first semester, Gelb was clear and prepared for class, though his expectations for the exams were often unclear.

Haha, oh Gelb, I really do miss your hair flips during class -- C'mon guys, let's show a little love and vote him "hot." The side part with long side-swept bangs, very shiny, very well-conditioned. Anyway, I had him the first year he taught at WU, so it's been awhile. But he was okay: not too hard, not too confusing, but very entertaining.

Am retaking the class from another professor and realizing just how terrible Gelb really was. The topics are not hard, but what the hell did he teach? Did he even teach? Do not take his class....total waste of time.

I am going to be a chemistry major and I am now realizing that I learned nothing from Gelb even though I earned an A.  I have no clue who he was talking to during class, but it was not the students.  I am planning on sitting in on Chem 112 this semester to try and learn something.
Gelb was SOOOOO much better than Regina F. I really enjoyed how he acted like he knew everything; I mean, he DID know everything, so that's fair. He rocks my socks...twice a weekend.
Unless you enjoy watching an arrogant man flip his obnoxiously long hair out of his face while he proves random formulas, don't take this class, or at least not from him
Not as bad as everyone says... better lecturer than Fry. His arrogance is actually pretty amusing.

You might as well learn chem from the book because all he does in lecture is work through proofs that have little or no relevance to what you will be asked to do on a test. If you have him, get help. Get help from Cornerstone before you fail the 1st test.

Scatterbrained, goofy (awkwardly so), and gives extremely tricky tests. Like another said, only gives proofs during class w/ a lot fo mistakes. Assumes we know all, so teaches us next to nothing. PASS ON GELB IF YOU WANT TO LEARN CHEM!
No Comments
Terrible teacher and insanely annoying
i dont know for sure if hes still here, but very unclear, didnt explain things clearly, only did proofs in class, made lots of mistakes.... DO NOT TAKE CHEM WITH LeV GELB!!!
The most inspiring professor in my first semester at WashU. His knowledge and experience are beyond the scope of this freshman course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Early Political Thought is one of the best classes I have taken at Wash U. Professor Pepe has been teaching for decades and he knows everything under the sun. He is passionate about what he teaches and loves talking to students outside of class. He even gave me several books. He's a little old school but I loved that. Would take again if I could!!!

Highly recommended. Not merely an enthusiastic professor, Pepe commands an encyclopedic knowledge of history pop culture. These anecdotes and a robust Brooklyn accent have given me fond memories of Latin class.

Professor Pepe is an approachable, very nice man. He is not young, but he is more vital than profs half his age. As a teacher, you can tell he has developed an effective style that suits him well. Plus, he really knows his stuff. What's not to like? I'd take him again.

A wonderful professor.  He can ramble sometimes and seems a bit out of it, but he is just as on top of the material as ever, and he has an eagle eye for talking during class.  Going to office hours is extremely helpful and he's a very nice person.

By far my favorite teacher I've had at WashU. Doesn't stick to schedule or topics always but learned something about everything. Knows his stuff and always willing to help out his students. He isn't an easy teacher, but he wants to give his students good grades, so make an effort and e-mail him/go to office hours if you need help getting an A.

Great teacher.  Unique style, but you get used to it and grow to like it.  So far my favorite teacher at WashU (only had 2 semesters though).  Just make sure your writing is concise and  to the point and you'll be fine for Pepe.  Less is more.
decent guy but can be anal about  attendance.
nice guy, loves Latin. a little rough around the edges and not great if you've never taken Latin before, but he honestly cares and will make time to help you.
Simply a great prof. Gives a lot of his time to students. Pepe rocks.

His quizzes are super hard but the test was easy and he works really hard to give everyone an A.  Don't sweat the bad grade because he'll  probably "forget" about a quiz or two and help you out a little.
Pretty hard classes, interesting person, fair grader

Very intelligent and learned person. He wants you to work very, very hard but in the end it all pays off when you realize that you have learned a lot. Quizzes on daily basis keep you "fresh" and very "informed"

Pepe is a quick-witted prof who will not take any flighty BS. rambling--not really. He pulls out interesting parts of the readings (which are good to read--why are you in school if you aren't reading?) i learned a ton in this class, and pepe is well prepared for class and on the ball.

Rambles WAY too much, calls on people if they don't raise their hands (and doesn't call on you if you do raise your hand).  Didn't read a single book, managed an okay grade... hated going to class on a daily basis.
Unclear, rambles a lot. I didn't like him
very smart, relatively easy if you keep up. no finals, no tests, just a very short weekly paper.

Too smart for his own good. His points don't come across clearly. Also, this isn't a class you can take and not do the reading for unfortunately...he calls on ppl randomly, gives quizes, and assigns weekly papers. It a lot of work for relatively minimal reward.
nice guy. willing to help.

Rambles a lot in class and is very organzied but he makes the material intesting. He makes the quizes hard and never told us how our grade was determend but in the end it worked out. Always there to help if asked and tries to accommodate the student.
Calls people out for BS. Everything this man says is genius.

very unorganized, items that do not appear in lecture or reading are on the quiz. doesnt let class know how the final grade will be figured, interrupts students while they're asking questions. not a good professor, although he knows his roman history
Doesn't have a clear lesson plan, generally just rambles on about random things.  Quizzes cover material that is not always discussed in clas..
No Comments

I was excited to take this class because of the proposed topic and was left extremely disappointed—many of my peers agreed. Dr. Gilbert spent daily discussion preaching about her political beliefs and made speaking in class feel very unsafe. There are so many amazing classes in the edu department, so if you can, avoid taking a class with this prof.

Dr. Gilbert makes speaking during class a frightening experience if you say anything that slightly differs from her opinion. She preaches to the class about tangents and her opinions the whole class. The class truly felt like a waste of time despite the content's potential. I was miserable in every class and later found that many students agreed.
Dr. Gilbert is an amazing professor. If you're considering the class, even with no previous background in philosophy, I would take it! You'll learn a lot and enjoy learning along the way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: You have to come to class because you do group assignments every day, but you learn so much and have so much fun it doesn't feel like a chore. I always looked forward to coming to class and learning with everyone. Prof is amazing and is so caring even outside of an academic setting. Participate as much as you can because you'll learn lots, def take

Lots of review was created 10 years before. Professor Gill do not teach C++ now(or some semesters?). He teach graduate level course Rust. Graduate students probably not care about ratemyprofessor points. However he gave good lab instructions that is renewing. Rust is definitely a hard language to learn but conveys high level system safe ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It looks like most of Professor Gill's ratings are for 131. I didn't have him for 131, but I thought he was one of the best professors I've had for 332. It was a heavily lab based course and the book covered everything you needed, but he always offered good insights and extra material. Also he's really nice, and very helpful in the lab setting.

He is very helpful if you talk to him in personemail and really appreciates when you show interest even if you don't show up to class. His instructions are extremely unclear and his lectures can be pretty boring. The studios can take a lot of time, so it is best to just save them for the end of the semester and speed through them.

He's not the best at explaining new concepts. His class is a lot easier if you come in with some experience with OOP. But his labs & studios, which are comprehensive and walk you through all the concepts, are very helpful, and the exams are fair.

Gill is awesome. It's true that he knows the material very well and speaks abstractly, but you can interrupt with questions and he'll answer. Only my friend and I did this in class, even though he encouraged it. Maybe that's why some people have trouble, so be sure to ask if you're lost. He's a very happy and helpful guy, and fun to talk to in lab.

Gill is impossible to understand. When he lectures, 90% of his words are jargon that only experienced programmers get. The studios are helpful but get hard fast and are intimidating since you can't learn from the professor at all. The labs are ok.

The studios are helpful as far as learning the material goes, but they get hard fast and going to class doesn't help because of how confusing Gill's lectures are. 90% of what comes out of his mouth is jargon that only experienced programmers understand. I try to pay attention but I have no idea what he's saying.

Studios can be boring - but are helpful if you take them seriously. As a lecturer he isn't great at making the material super exciting(especially when he starts talking about the STL) but you can tell he has a passion for it. I recommend doing some supplemental reading for the class (free tutorials). Exams aren't hard if you have a good note card.
Really knows what he's talking about with C++.  He always came to class prepared.  The labs were kind of fun, and exams weren't hard at all if you showed up to class.  I think he's a great professor.

He gets a lot of criticism, but if he's teaching a small class like this one, and you're fairly good at computer science, you will like him. His tests are much more reasonable than Ken Goldman's are, that's for sure. Labs aren't THAT bad.

We did the same lab 5 times in a row, just using different syntax each time. Horribly, horribly boring, and his lab descriptions are very unclear. Lectures are not worthwhile, since he just reads straight from his PowerPoint slides, which he posts on the web anyway.
Holy crap, is he ever bad.  I had an enormous amount of trouble, as he couldn't explain anything worth a darn.  BAD PROFESSOR
he is a horrible teacher
The lab instructions did not make sense. Class was not worth the time. He did not know the java syntax, but mystically we were supposed to know it.

I stopped going to class after the midterm. It didn't matter. I didn't learn anything in class anyway. There was no textbook for the class, which was ridiculous, since Gill didn't teach anything in class either. SO glad the semester is over!
He's very large and very jolly, but that certainly doesn't make him a better instructor.  I have to read some parts of his labs 12 times before I can comprehend them.  His TA's don't even like him.
I havent been to this class in months. There is no point in going, because I a third grader could teach me better than he could.

Considering that people who knew how to program prior to taking this class have trouble with it, it's amazing that someone like myself (no prior Comp Sci instruction) manages to pass with his awful and unclear teaching style.  His assignments/tests/quizes vary greatly in differently for no reason.

Scatterbrained teaching style while repeatedly covering the same material. Still manages to lose inexperienced programmers with poor explanations. Posts new information on labs the day they're due.  Labs are simply exercises in debugging since they require no original thinking or problem solving.
Worst professor ever.

Kareena is one of the best professors I had at WashU. Other reviews say she never gave feedback, but she always gave great feedback to me and my class. Course expectations lined up with university requirements and she was still flexible. Her passion for the subject is obvious and she was always considerate + realistic with students about grades

Professor Gianani was always very constructive and gave applicable criticism while respecting our individual styles. I grew a passion for nonfiction, which I never thought I would like. The workload was challenging, but manageable. The course was very organized and easy to follow. I was encouraged to speak up in discussions, but never pressured to.

Professor did not give us grades till the end of the semester, and I did not get back feedback on ALL my writing. Grading scale is extremely arbitrary. Work load was ridiculous, had to write two whole page letters for every single class and annotate 20 pages. Often forced students to read private writing activities in front of class
Do not take this class. Her feedback was so unhelpful and we didn't get any letter grades until the end of the semester. She often called students out in class and made people feel uncomfortable.

Professor Gildner's lectures were very organized. This class is mostly centered around big concepts and events throughout the history of global health. Grading is very exam-heavy, and how well you do on the exam is mostly on how well you memorize the slides' info; that being said it is pretty easy to do so; would recommend this class

Dr. Gildner was very nice and her lectures were clear, so I still gave her 4. However, I personally found the course content very boring and repetitive at times. Some units were more interesting but others were very stale. If you know the powerpoints it should be relatively easy to get an A.

Great lecturer and nice person overall, but class was kind of common-sense based (expect when learning about the diseases). Tests were all memorization and pretty easy (the final short answers were the same as the practice test) but grading can be a bit harsh

This class is relatively unnecessary and boring. We cover SOOO many topics at a surface-level explanation. Most of it is common sense. It is very content, memorization, and PowerPoint-heavy. She gives you LITERALLY 30 seconds to answer the Poll Everywhere for participation and gets angry if you do not pay close attention to this INTRO class.

Dr.Gildner is an okay lecturer. If you do not need to take global health, I would not. It's a very surface level class and you can get back by doing minimal work/memorization. Dr.Gilder is very nervous and it impacts her delivery of the material both in its validity and passion.

Introduction to Global Health is very lecture-heavy, and attendance is required. However, Dr. Gildner tries to make her lectures interesting with videos and graphs. Tests are easy as they are rote memorization and the SciComm project replaces a second midterm. In general, she is super caring and wants her students to succeed.

Class is largely "death-by-powerpoint," with exams being based on pure memorization. However, they are incredibly easy and can be reviewed through simple flashcards. Her lectures can be a bit boring, but Gildner is a very polite professor who will answer your questions clearly and is approachable. Very manageable class.
Super nice, lectures can be boring at times
She is really great! Easy-going, understanding, and great lectures. She values participation but doesn't demand it and that can make all the difference.

She is really an amazing Professor. She is very relatable. I highly respect her as a Professor. I enjoy her ability to teach but also drive the classroom conversation. I took four classes with her and each class was different and adjusted to her students as well.
Better than the other lecturers and way better than the actual professors at wash u.  She gives real world outlook and challenges your opinion in a constructive way.
Giammar is a great professor that truly cares about his students. EECE 101 is a hard class but Giammar wants to help you succeed if you put in the effort. I would definitely take his classes again.
Dan does a great job of roping you in for ChemE then it gets rough but it's not Dan's fault. Dan's class has been my favorite during my time here.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Love Giammar. Super caring, passionate, and made lectures interesting. A little bit hard to get help with outside of class (office hours were very sparce and for the most part didn't work with my schedule) but was always willing to help. Very inspirational and inspired me to be an engineer!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dan Giammar is a true gem. He cares about his students and is always happily available for questions/comments/concerns/feedback. Engineering classes are difficult but he has made this class enjoyable as well. Would recommend this class for anyone interested in water systems but also just interested in public health engineering! Very applicable
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really tough grader on extensive problem sets, but is always willing to help out. Lectures were informative and interesting and I feel better prepared to work in water treatment after taking this class.

Giammar was a really great professor this semester in tough class. For the past several years he has taught this course together with Dr. Jay Turner and Giammar is often considered to be the "easier" professor. I found his lectures to be very clear and his tests had a MUCH higher average than those of Dr. Turner.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Giammar is a fantastic lecturer. His tests are difficult, but partial credit helps you make up points. Loves discussing the curriculum in office hours. Overall a great guy and teacher!

Daniel is the most inspirational and caring professor that I have experienced. He is very helpful and cares about his students and whether or not they are learning the material. He is passionate about the work he does and is always enthusiastic.

Its hard for an intro course but it gives you a great feel for what being a chemical engineering major means. if youre in a PST and do the readings, getting an A is possible. Giammar is awesome, really cares about what he is teaching. Lectures can get a little dry but he's nothing if not very organized and methodical.
sucked
Lacked enthusiasm in teaching

I found it very difficult to follow explanations from the instructor. I was able to get by during the first two units based on knowledge I had gained from my AP Physics class in high school. Unclear explanations and mistakes in problems by Professor Gibbons left the class reserved and nervous about answering questions. The book was not helpful.

I sympathize with Professor Gibbons, but he is a little too old to teach. He is really not clear, sometimes he can't even understand our questions. The course is easy enough so it wasn't a total disaster. But for anyone without prior physics knowledge I suggest you find another section for 197 ASAP, because u will be stuck with him for 198 as well.
Good teacher, friendly and available. Class is both easy and interesting. Does not take attendance. I don't see why everyone finds his class so boring, I had fun.

Solar System Astronomy: worst class ever with him. it is a 100 person class but only 15 people show up (im sadly one of them) because he's so boring. Also, it is supposed to be an easy math course but it turns into intermediate physics quite quickly. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS
very helpful in the lab
physics 117 is just plain hard, and many non-physics people take it. don't let those ratings change your opinion   he's a great teacher, knows a ton about electronics, and he smells funny
No Comments
Worst.  Professor.  Ever.
He tries really hard to explain things but isn't the best at it.
No Comments
He couldn't explain anything if his life depended on it.

Classes were mostly online synchronous lectures. They were very paced very well, and Prof Zanarone would spend as much time as requested on any given topic. Material was usually easy to get a grasp on thanks to examples. Sometimes lectures could get boring, but overall Professor was very nice and engaging. Grades were a bit of a stress, but not bad
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not to be mean, but I think he was the worst professor I've ever had. Part of this could be a language barrier, but in general I didn't find that material was presented clearly and questions were not well answered. He was not very available outside of class. Everything left to TA's who were also very unreliable. Exam averages were constantly low.

Lectures don't teach you anything. If anything, they make the material more confusing. He's Italian, so English is not his first language, so I don't blame him too much. He left everything related to grades up to the TAs, which was a disaster because the TAs were not particularly good at their jobs. Overall a really nice and caring guy though!
She's amazing at helping you learn from your mistakes. Although the quizzes are quite challenging, I think she is an amazing professor who involves everyone in her lecture.
Marcus-sensei holds her students to a high standard; however, her feedback is excellent and gives one an idea of what needs to improve. The Wash U Japanese Program is excellent.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She demands a lot to students and is really harsh on the grades. I am just holding on to this class for my culture credits and I would never want to face her again after this class.
She seems intimidating af at first, but she's actually the bomb dot com???? I'm love her?????
an awful experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Provided handout/online schedule with what she would expect from her student each day. As long as you prepare what you are asked for she will give solid A (its not alot either). Some people can find her attitude assertive or demanding respect, but that is more like her trying to recreate what japanese class would be like, not being strict or mean

While this style of language learning does take a week or two to get used to, it is engaging and very useful when you become more comfortable with it. Marcus has an intimidating presence at times, but she does take into account effort, not just results, sotell her if you are struggling and ask for advice. The homework load is not bad at all either.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I'm going to have to agree with the previous reviewMarcus-sensei can come across as strict and scary, but really, she's a great person! Her grades are fair; you don't have to ask and answer questions promptly and perfectly to get a five for the daily ACT classes, as long as you show that you know what you're doing.

I'll admit initially that she comes off as an intimidating person, but she's an intelligent, at times humorous, teacher. You don't have to do perfectly to get a five in ACT class, just as long as you can correct your mistakes.

I will never take her class again. I guess she thinks she is the most important person in the world so that she deserves GREAT respects from all her students. Never question her. She has a condescending attitude towards everybody in the class and plays favouritism.
A very good course.

She is one of the best teachers I've ever had.  She is very demanding, but if you let her, she can be a great advocate and truly cares about her students.  I don't know where everyone got her rudeness or favorites-playing from, but I wasn't her favorite and still loved the class.  I did well the first year, but did worse in subsequent semesters.
Rude and plays favorites. Makes you feel like an idiot if you get the tiniest thing wrong. The other Japanese teachers are great though
Her gradings are extremely unfair. It is hard to earn good grades in her class. EXCELLENT performance without mistakes usually gives you only a 4.5/5 which is a 90 in the class.
Insecure and patronizing. The worst educational experience of my life and I got an A. Plays favorites

DONT EVER TAKE A CLASS WITH HER. She is the worst teacher I have ever had. She is condescending and plays favorites. She must be insecure about something because she has a god complex. The other Japanese teachers are ok. Knowing what I know now I would never take a class with her again!
This is the worst teachers I have ever had. She was also the most mean spirited people I have know. I did fairly well in her Japanese class. Avoid her like the plague!
Doesn't have the humor of the other Japanese teacher (Aridome), but genuinely trys to help. Occasionally livens up the room by discussing stories of her major Japanese errors
very demanding and will jump to assumptions. Takes multiple times to state your questions since she jumps to what she assums your question is. she wont help you succeed if she doesnt like you
biased and snappy
favoritism, intentionally try to eliminate students

Literally only takes his own opinion as valid, if you genuinely care about learning a balanced approach to the material teach yourself -- he honestly doesn't seem to care about teaching his students at all and his lectures are convoluted at best

He is definitely a difficult professor but he really makes you think and learn. While he might be blunt, he always has his students best interest  in mind and is very willing to talk about how to improve. Further, he REALLY knows his stuff so be prepared to be told you are wrong or misinterpreted- don't worry it will make you better in the long run

He will only accept his own opinion as the right answer but doesn't explain anything clearly enough so you never know what his opinion is well enough to spout it back at him. Plus, he's arrogant enough to believe that he's open minded but always right at the same time. Don't take this class. I wish I'd headed the negative reviews. Semester wasted.

Interesting professor with an unconventional teaching style. Doesn't really believe in spoon feeding, so if you want to succeed, do the reading, think about it, then go to class. Fairly difficult so if you're not good at this stuff and/or lazy, you probably won't like this professor.

Though Gibson may be an intelligent political scientist, he has little idea how to teach students. His grades for papers seem arbitrarily assigned, and his exams have nothing to do with the material he teaches, which is without any clear organization. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS I DON'T KNOW WHY HE IS STILL TEACHING! SO ARROGANT!

Gibson is a highly qualified political scientist, but he's more interested in research than students. He assigns too much reading, but you can get by reading the intros and conclusions. Class discussions can be interesting, but his opinions dominate. If you flatter him enough he sometimes allows himself to be corrected. Give him what he wants.

Political Tolerance in World Politics. This teacher is THE WORST PROFESSOR. HORRIBLE, RUDE, ARROGANT. I beg all students never to take a class with him in hopes that the zero interest level will get him fired. WORST TEACHER EVER, never take a class with him, EVER EVER. Too much reading, too much writing, ridiculous expectations. THE GUY IS SO MEAN
absolutely beyond me why he is teaching. he clearly has no use for it, or for his students.

There was some interesting material, but I don't think I learned anything. He was also the author of almost everything we read, so it was hard to form different opinions regarding the stuff. Gibson is also very unclear. DO NOT TAKE.
Very BORING, class not worth any time, you learn basically nothing, he gets an F in my gradebook!

While his dapper style is...interesting to look at, he is not interesting to listen to...unless you want to hear about what he has written and what conferences he is attending...you will only be "accountable" for what gibson thinks is "legitimate"
What a jerk.  So full of himself, completely unapproachable.  His arrogance gets in the way of actually teaching the material.

Interesting class. Professor very full of himself. Not really into creativity. To do well in class learn to think like him. Stroke his ego, that seems to help also. Take his paper's really seriously, he sure does.
Very interesting professor
Class was sorta confusing, seems to always be fishing for a specific answer. Class discussions don't seem to really go anywhere. Overall though, an interesting professor.
Interesting in a people-watching sense. Very odd man. He's snobby and full of himself.
Taught more his opinions than any fact, and did not seem to even know what he was talking about a lot of the time
Full of himself
He knows the value of a good education.

Glenn is extremely unclear and grades arbitrarily. He has no rubric or syllabus outlining any of his assignments in this class, leaving students confused and unsure of how to properly complete assignments. He grades randomly with no feedback and is not approachable. I was extremely excited to take this class but Glenn squandered my excitement.

glenn is the best professor i had in college, and it wasn't close. it wouldn't be a stretch to say he's changed my life by helping me build perspective. 

he's a cool dude. he's not easy, but if you put the time and work in, he cares enough to go more than the extra mile. he genuinely cares about his students. i cannot recommend too highly.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. 
His classes teach you no information, that is when he has a lecture. He only has 8 lectures during the semester, so that students can "teach" with their 7 group presentations. 

Your actual grades mean nothing. He grades based on how well you performed in relation to the other students, not how well you performed.
Booooooooo

Unfortunately I regret taking this class, even though I had a good grade at the end. Professor MacDonald is dry and text bookish.  Didn't find this professor compelling in terms of really encouraging any learning.  Almost felt like I was having the concepts read to me rather than really having an expert provide key insights to connect the dots.

His class has easily been the hardest of my three years at WashU... and I took it as a freshman B-School student. He just makes things a lot more advanced than they need to be and ends up forgetting to build a foundation of basic concepts. Definitely super calculus intensive.

I took Micro with Glenn my freshman year and disliked it a lot. However, this class seemed so interesting so I chose to take it, and I was not let down. There are a lot of guest lecturers; Glenn knows so many cool people. He really likes participation and having a conversation in class, which led to very interesting discussions.

One of the worst professors at Olin. Totally agree with the other comments about him being an elitist and ruining my semester. He's overly theoretical and doesn't prepare for real world examples. Has a real big ego.

Glenn is a really good professor who really strives to give the students the best learning experience. So many incredible and inspiring guests speakers. If you want to go into the entertainment industry, this is a MUST TAKE. Glenn also sends internship and job opportunities in the entertainment industry to the class on a regular basis.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Glenn tries to be nice but this class is HARD. The class has no clear grading structure. Your grade is calculated based on how you do in relation to other students. The problem sets are convoluted and the exams are nothing like the problem sets. The class is extremely challenging but if you are someone who likes a challenge, go for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The homework/exams are incredibly complicated and are very applied when compared to the easy examples and content covered in class. Ex: in-class 1+12 on HW find the circumference of the earth. It was an interesting class, but I wished that the grading criteria was more clear and that the lectures included test like examples. Cool dude though
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Glenn is a nice guy and very smart, but his lectures are entirely basic theory with absolutely zero application (no practice problems). Therefore, his problem sets and tests are significantly harder than anything taught in class. This gets frustrating as the semester goes along. It's an intro class but is taught like a high level econ course.

This class was awful. Don't get me wrong, Glenn is extremely intelligent, but that leads to an elitist class that is extremely hard. I went into this class with an open mind, but came out depressed and not confident in myself. Please try and get a different professor for this class; it ruined my semester at WashU and made me super anxious/stressed.

Professor MacDonald is not the guy to give an easy A, but he's really passionate about what he's teaching and he's always available for the students. He is willing to sit with a student and discuss higher-level issues with them. He uses real world examples in his curriculum and I think the hard work needed in this class was totally worth it.
Tough but very rewarding

This class is difficult. Although Macdonald tells good stories, he just doesn't seem to care enough / take the time to go through example problems in class thoroughly. He comes off seeming apathetic and self-centered. Most of the real work of teaching students how to solve the problems is done by the TAs. Going to the help sessions is a must.

RIA was my favorite class I've taken in the Econ & Strat program. Mostly graded on group projects which give you the opportunity to present to real clients. You'll spend the whole semester with your group, so pick a good one. Class attendance only mandatory when you're scheduled to present or when he gives a quiz.
Nice professor with interesting life stories, but not so good at teaching. TAs do the job. Tests are POORLY and randomly graded and you'll never get solutions back.

This class is taught at such a high level and while you may think you're failing all semester, the curve is enormous.  Class lectures are very theoretical and the problem sets are all application, so it's essential that you go to the TA help sessions.  You learn a lot in the end, but it's a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is hard, the material is covered at an extremely high level, problem sets are a lot of work, but it was one of the most rewarding classes I have ever taken. Glenn is one of the smartest people I have ever encountered and his experiences are priceless.

Throughout the semester you think you're going to fail, and then he curves your grade a ton at the very end and most people get As and Bs.  He's a nice guy and interested in his students, but the tests are -very- difficult.  Go to the TA study sessions!

Glenn is a great professor and great person. Super cool guy! Also one of the nicest guys I have met. He is always willing to help students. Very knowledgable both in economics and in other areas. Although the course is difficult he curves it so that most people end up in the A or B range. He teaches the material very well

Professor MacDonald is a good professor who always has interesting stories to share with the class. As for the class itself, if you are good at math, the class will make you think but you will understand the material and succeed. Profssor MacDonald likes teaching with math and I think it makes the class more interesting.
Amazing professor.  One of the hardest classes you'll take but completely worth it.

He's really cool and 'hip' and makes class fairly interesting, but his exams and assignments are very difficult. To do well, make sure that you go to help sessions with the TAs. Also, although he says that it is optional, buy the textbook he recommends. Practice problems in the textbook are pretty helpful.

Was in a rock band, always in jeans and t-shirts, and loves to talk. I fell in love w/ econ b/c of Glenn. He answers any question thoroughly and patiently - even obvious or stupid ones. He requires a lot of critical thinking in his homework. And yes, his exams are hard - but you'll get better if you start going to his office hours.

not as great as everyone makes him out to be. he definitely does not teach the material well, the ta's do all the teaching. his tests and homeworks are ridiculously difficult. take this class with someone else if you have the option

A very intelligent professor. Probably one of the best in the business school. He lets his tenure get in the way sometimes and makes it seem as though you dumb for asking a certain question. The class is definitely difficult, but the curve at the end is a big one.
Absolutely useless professor.  Does not teach material but leaves it up to the TA sessions.  Home works and tests are impossible and poorly graded.
Great professor. Clearly loves to teach and loves his subject, is knowledgeable and smart, best stories ever (do ask him about non-economics things).
..........i like him

Glenn is a really good teacher.  Makes it easy to understand the material in class.  But the tests and problem sets are certainly not easy, though there is a curve, still not an easy class.  He's a great guy though and definitely worth taking as he is the best of all the MECO profs out there.

Glenn is a great professor. He makes class very entertaining, and really cares about his students. He wants to help his students very much, so come to his office hours. The exams are hard, but are curved very nicely. Ask him about what he did before being a professor, he's got lots of great stories
Glenn MacDonald is the man.  Take his classes, pay attention, listen to him, learn, and ask him about his background (he told us he had more fun than all of us put together when he was a kid).

Glenn is awesome because he's down to earth and relates to the students. Yeah, his class was a bit confusing, but find me a micro class that isn't. If you've taken AP Micro, this class should be a breeze, and if you haven't, then go find someone who has. Attend all the classes and review sessions (free hw answers) and you'll be fine.

Material not too difficult but you are expected to know it backwards, inside out, up side down, at mach 3, all at the same time. Tests not too terrible, but be sure to look at the practice exams. The homeworks can definitely claim you if you don't watch what you are doing. TAs are sometimes unfair with the grading of HWs. Good teacher!

Material can be hard to understand, 1st exam is TOUGH, and you have to explain EVERYTHING and all details on homework. Exams = open notes, but use time wisely. He's quite fun and has good real world examples & plays music in class. He's obviously very intelligent but may be hard to understand if you don't think in "business-like" terms

the class is hard and the averages are low, but its curved to a B+.  go to the help sessions with the TAs and you'll get 100% on every homework.  glenn is the most willing to help outside of class professor ive ever met.
Bloody hard...If you have to take it, definitely avoid taking it with MacDonald...take it with another professor and it will be a bliss...you will be in hell if take him...
awesome guy, would do anything for a student, makes it fun and interesting and really applies it for you

MacDonald was pretty good. I didn't really like the class that much. It was too theoretical, and just thought that MacDonald was making the material harder than it had to be. His tests, though doable, were ambigious in lots of places. The TA's were horrible though. Most inconsistent grading ever.

GREAT teacher. Definitely the best teacher I've had in the b-school. Knows his stuff, explains it well and clearly, and very approachable. Very nice guy. Homeworks and tests can be challenging but straight foward.

If you enjoy both math and economics, this is the class for you.  His lecture slides are very comprehensive.  The homework is never lengthy and always straightforward.  The exams are very doable, too.

MacDonald is one of the best profs at Wash U.  You can definitely tell that he really cares about what he's teaching, the subject and the students (and it's not all about the MBA's).  He's extraordinarily nice and will spend hours just chatting with you.  Hard class, but definitely worth it.
VERY VERY HELPFUL
By far my best professor, EVER.  Fun, nice, friendly and really cares about his students.  If you bomb the first 2 tests don't worry.  He RARELY gives below a B.
Great philosophy on teaching, really pushes you to understand.  Much more theory than just mindless application.  Highly recommended.
Smart guy who has a lot of great real world consulting examples to help the theories you learn become clear.  A must for future consultants or for top management.

Having just graduated I'm posting reviews of the best courses I took here. This was definitely one, even though it was covid year and all remote. I learned more, and talked about it more, than any other course. Lectures were fascinating and powerpoints helpful. Readings were a bit heavy worth it (with a few exceptions). Loved his book. Thanks!

This is one of the worst classes. Glenn makes us remember specific details from his long lectures to be tested on. He strays away from helping us actually understand bigger concepts. If you're not on top of your work, you will never get a good grade in this class. He didn't foster any sort of live interaction with himself and the students.

The lectures were all remote and recorded and they were mostly really good. Some were pretty opinionated but he backed the opinions up. He covered some remarkable and surprising material. The grading was not too hard.

Super interesting class, but it is very important to stay on top of the course work since it does get a little overwhelming at points. Very knowledgable professor with a serious passion for what he studies and teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class covers some interesting/ problematic points in history but the lvl of detail that we have to memorize is absurdly unnecessary. Exams test us on whether we are able to spit back specific facts mentioned in lengthy readings/ lectures rather than assessing how well we understand concepts. I do not feel like I'm gaining anything from this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you're the kind of person who's really into corn this is the class/prof for you. There's a LOT of reading and you WILL be tested on it, so doing that and attending lectures are basically the only requirements. But don't get scared of the fact that's it's basically an agriculture class, you'll learn some interesting/scary things about the world.

Interesting content, but not well-delivered-- not a very understanding or flexible professor. Actually ended up curving down one of our tests when the average was a 91 (which I thought was unfair, especially considering the test was open-book and we had access to all the material).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Stone is incredibly disorganized. His slides are confusing and his lectures are really hard to follow, and he doesn't do a good job of connecting all of the material together. The class is interesting in some ways but the lectures do drag on frequently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The exams may cover personal opinions of his and it isn't clear what is important or not in lecture. Often the readings are emphasized over everything else. He has his own website with factoids you must know verbatim, no extra credit, not very friendly, cusses every other sentence (it's distracting), and digresses into story time more than teaches.

This is a very interesting class and with engaging lectures. I think I truly learned a lot from this class but I was turned off by Stone's attitude. He was quite arrogant and showed little concern for his students. Be prepared to do a lot of readings because you need to know them for the tests! But the class wasn't too hard and is worth taking.

Professor Stone is not the most likable nor approachable professor, but he is very clear in teaching the material and makes the tests simple and based on lectures.  Very interesting class, for majors and non-majors in anthro.

Glen Stone's food seminar was one of the best educational experiences I had at Wash U, even if the reading load was a bit excessive.  But the books were great, the discussions were engaging, and I still think about the seminar regularly.  He is a real teacher, and also went out of his way to help me after I graduated.

I took Brave New Crops with him, and the class was somewhat interesting; some lectures seemed to drag on. Stone can be kind of ignorant of students and not the most friendly or approachable. The quizzes/test are not very hard if you study.
the worst professor i have had at washu in a non-science course.  really acts as if he could care less about any of his students.

Professor Stone is one of the best professors I've had here at WashU.  I would highly recommend to those WUSTL students remotely interested in agriculture and our current industrial agricultural system.
Unusual class but fascinating.  Stone's lectures are brilliant. I'm taking another class of his next year and looking forward to it

The topic is very interesting, and he is an engaging and dynamic lecturer. The tests aren't hard, but you won't know what you got until the end because he waits to curve the tests. Also, he isn't helpful in office hours.

Had very little interest in anthropology, not to mention any real knowledge of genetically modified crops and organizations of societies, but Professor Stone really turned me on to such topics and I took a second class from him. Just a great professor, and love when he introduced his own research and field experiences into class.
Loved this class.

Culture & Environment is one of the best courses here.  Stone gives a perspective on environmental issues that was different from what I had always heard, but always clear and well supported and interesting.  Plus now I know how many pigs Ireland exported in 1846, which I had wondered about.

The class is very interesting and it is not hard to sit through but this class had so much reading, it is almost impossible to fit it in with your other work. Stone is also a bit arrogant in class, however you do learn a lot.
His ego keeps him from being a good professor. Please get over yourself.
Great course.  I'm sorry it's over.  Thanks a bunch, G Stone
The final was way hard and the class was too big.  But I would definitely recommend it.  It's a very interesting course and he gives excellent lectures.  It's a course that will stay with you.
One of the best courses I took in the last 4 years.  The whole thing was brilliant.

The class could have been interesting if the professor had been more interested in teaching and less so in proving his own intelligence.  He really does know what he is talking about, but he would be more effective in conveying it if he was a little less arrogant.
a really interesting class; i would definitely recommend it

It's a great class.  Lectures are outstanding -- Stone is interesting & organized and knows exactly what he's talking about, and can be very funny.  You end up re-thinking some important issues -- like what overpopulation really means.  He encourages discussion even tho it's a big class. Most of the readings were good but a few were tedious.  Do NO

My favorite class all year.  Why? 1) innovative class on important topic.  You learn about how the world works, not just about GMOs.  2) unusually good lectures, thought-provoking & entertaining (altho not as funny as Culture & Env -- why is that?), discussion encouraged  3) GDS was a good guy and very encouraging to me.  Don't miss this class.

This class is informative and not difficult.  You can easily get an A as long as you keep up with the readings.  As much as it focuses on the issue of GM crops, it also analyzes the rhetoric of opponents and proponents.  There is something about Dr. Stone's personality that rubs me the wrong way, but he runs a good class.

awesome course.  lectures were extrelemy interesting, usually entertaining too.  stone was brilliant.  plus i got to have dinner with a very interesting guest speaker.  this website only lets you rank on "easy, helpful and clear", but this one gets top marks in "interesting" and "important"
One of the best courses I took in my 4 years here.  Wish I could take another course with him.

This class was A LOT of WORK - he can sometimes be witty but overall he is cocky and gives a lot or work. Overall this class was BORING - unless you have an interest in agriculture, farming, environment alteration and GMOS. I dont  recommend it.

africa was a pretty good class. stone tends to teach his opinion...he'll point out how you can't stereotype africa and then he'll make a generalization. that said, he's good at lecturing in front of a big room. but don't bother talking to him after class. he acts like you're bothering him, even if you're asking a question about that day's lecture.
A lot of work but really REALLY interesting.  One of the best courses I've had at Wash U, one of the best professors for sure.

Stone is a fun guy, comes off a little arrogant, but he's hilarious. I would recommend culture and environment over brave new crops not only because i found the material more interesting but also because it was a little better organized. BNC was a great class though
I totally looked forward to this class.  Awesome lectures.  I learned a lot.  What did he do that was "arrogant"?

GREAT lectures, fascinating + funny.  Most interesting class I've had at wash U.  He was totally helpful -- encouraged questions, stayed after class to talk, did review sessions, was great to talk to in office hours, even set up dinners with students!
a pretty self-righteous guy, but a good class.
Real good, has a viewpoint but backs it up with facts and presents the other side as well. Entertaining lecturer.

Taking several classes from him makes me realize how formulatic he is in his teaching method and thats helpful in studying. He teaches his viewpoint but lays out the facts and I usually agree with him, so it's ok.

You can't hate on stone.  Sure he talks about himself, but at least his stories are interesting.  Classes are great and very informative.  Makes good JOkes too.  Tests are cake so long as you read and go to class.  Go to the TA if you need help, cause he is always busy or at least pretending to be.

My favorite professor! He's so funny! Yeah, he's kinda arrogant, but in a really great way. His class is probably the most interesting I've taken, and totally easy. I definitely recommend him. I'm taking another of his classes next semester just because I enjoyed this one so much

Stone is very inconsiderate when it comes to asking for his help outside the classroom. He doesn't genuinely care about his students. He is also the most POMPOUS, ARROGANT professors I've ever had. He constantly praises himself during his lecture. If you want a jackass for a teacher, take him.

This guy is one of the most pompous self-indulgent professors i've ever had.  he knows his stuff and the class is highly topical and very interesting, but the constant plugs (giving his own articles as reading and other articles that mention his name) are incredible gross.  easy though.
HILARIOUS!

Prof Stone is a great lecturer.  He is funny, highly intelligent and has the ability to explain/teach really boring material in a way that makes it seem interesting.  His tests are great and easy to take.  I highly recommend this professor.

Gleaves is one of the best professors I've ever had at WashU. The fundamentals of materials science can be a dry topic, but Gleaves livens up the class with anecdotes of his experiences in industry, in Vietnam, and in academia. We covered a lot of material, and yet everything made sense. AFAIK, most of the class got an A on the final exam.

Well.. He taught us the most important and essential concept of Materials. This course is a very unique course. But you need to know fundamentals of chemical engineering or to read the textbook before the class. Easy A, if you do your assignments.
Greatest professor I've had in college.

He did not care about teaching at all.  He just wrote equations on the board all day without explaining anything.  Always held us late.  Couldn't remember what topics he had even covered so far -- gave us homework on things we'd never talked about at all.  So disorganized.  The only good thing was his stories.
No Comments
No Comments
