MTC-Modern Technological Challenges, it was too long for the class box.  I love Prof. Gleaves, he is one of the most interesting and engaging teachers I've had.  I look forward to taking more of his classes.
No Comments
Prof Godigbe cares about his students and was helpful during office hours. The exams are not extremely difficult if you take the time to study.

I personally disagree with the past couple comments. Tests were very straightforward and fair, got 100s. Dr. Godigbe's lecturing was very clear and helped me to learn a lot, and this was my first business class ever so I was a complete novice. Would highly recommend, Dr. Godigbe legitimately cares about his student's success and is very helpful.

Godigbe does a good job at answering questions but can run through the concepts pretty fast during lecture. Very test heavy (based on lecture) and the grading criteria isn't super clear (but he tries his best to make sure you end up with the highest grade possible). Honestly, he's not a super bad professor but the class itself is terrible.

Bright is online-savvy but fuzzy grading criteria. Lectures are hard to understand unless you do a ton of learning and mastering concepts outside class. Exams really matter -- I had an A before the final exam caused me to earn a C average. Additionally, he schedules multiple students at once for online appointments, which I find disrespectful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Godigbe was a pretty good professor. The class as a whole was confusing at times because we would be super ahead of the syllabus but tested on content from a while back. The midterms were not too hard and the final was pretty easy. He cares about his students and wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely reasonable teacher, almost similar to a high school history teacher. Very straightforward lectures and as long as you know what's going on in class and have a good idea of the readings (which are sometimes long but not insanely long), you'll do well. Very nice guy and very chill class.

Professor Gochberg is awesome. Sure, it's not an easy class, but I learned the most in it out of any class I've ever taken. This class gave me a huge interest in environmental policy and now I may major in it. The readings can be long, but I learned a ton about life from them. Use office hours, he wants to help you! He's a sweetheart tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Gochberg was one of the most unreasonable graders I have ever experienced. He gives no practice and he takes off points for not including information that he did not ask for. I am a premed student and took this class to see if polysci was a better fit for me. After having professor gochberg, I will not be pursuing any political science.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable in his field, very clear and understandable in his lectures, and approachable outside of class. Don't take this class if you're looking for easy credits, the readings can be long and the exams are difficult but fair. If you don't do the readings, the best you can get is a B/B+ (what I did). Concepts are very similar to econ.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Does a pre-recorded lecture for each day, then the class period is for reviewing the reading and discussing it. Gochberg facilitates great discussion and has great insights into the material. Knowledgeable in his field. Most of the readings are interesting if you're a political person, though some can get long. Grade mostly based on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures were definitely discussion heavy, and some of the readings were pretty difficult. Grading wise can be a little bit tough, but not unreasonable. Professor Gochberg is definitely accessible and willing to help if needed, and engages with the class well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: By far the worst/hardest class I've ever taken at WashU in the course of 3 years here. Lectures are boring, short, & are hard to understand. Only 2 exams (papers), a handful of discussion posts, & the hardest grading I've ever had. Be prepared to work your ass off & fail. Feedback on the papers is not beneficial, no scoring guide given. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very good class. Lots of real world examples.
Great instructor

A fantastic professor who teaches the material extremely well. His class is really just a lecture for an hour and a half, and although it is sometimes boring. Other than that, He's very easy to talk to and has very organized powerpoints that are very helpful when studying for exams. He's a great guy and great professor, definitely recommend him.

I had Professor Griffith for both Religion and American Society and the Abuse Crisis in Modern Christianity. I cannot recommend her enough - she gives a fair amount of reading and wants people to participate in class but lectures are super interesting and she's so sweet, super understanding, and just wants everyone to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Griffith was caring and really wanted everyone to participate and engage. It was a heavy subject but she made a really wonderful class experience and most of the class was facilitated discussion. I'm sorry she's going on sabbatical in 2024.

Dr. Griffith is an amazing professor and I have really enjoyed taking her class. She is super supportive of her students and very responsive to emails, and wants to help you succeed. She does assign a lot of reading each week and expects participation in class disscusion, so be prepared to get called on and know what you're talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Religions of St. Louis was one of my favorite classes I've taken at WashU  it's an amazing opportunity to learn so much more about the city and its religious mosaic. Dr. Griffith assigns a lot of reading and a lot of papers, she is an excellent scholar, teacher, and overall human. I learned so much and was constantly so inspired by her.
3 hour class that meets once a week, and for each class you need to read a book (think 200-500 pages each week). Class usually ended within two hours, but it was a rough time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: WashU needs better econometrics professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Reads off the slides the entire semester. You are better off taking Econometrics with another professor. Save yourself.
TAs teach better than her, lectures are all over the place, take econometrics with any professor other than her.
For 413. Her TAs teach better than her. Johnson just rambles and reads off slides. She is nice, but she doesn't care. Course concepts and exams are not difficult.

Can second what others said. Probably the nicest person in the department but lectures are physically impossible to follow. Copies the textbook 1:1 to the slides, rendering them useless in class. Problem sets are easy and she gives tons of extra credit opportunities tho. It's hard to figure out what content is actually relevant for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: ECON 352 is a wonderful survey-based course and you can learn a lot. However, the professor's exam is almost out of the lessons. Most of the exam questions are not prepared and you should find these through the lecture PPT yourself, some of them are subtle and sharp. The professor does not have a clear lecture thought, the key points are scattered.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worst prof ever
If you are present for class and pay attention, she will point out important slides to study for the midterm and final. She is willing to help outside of class when and if you need it.

She really doesn't teach you anything. The idea of the course was so cool and interesting, but she copies the textbook word for word into a powerpoint and then reads directly off the slide. It was hard to stay awake. 70% of your overall grade was exams, and her lecture style does not prepare you for the exams at all. Overall not a good professor.
The class was genuinely interesting and it should also be an easy A if you follow the instructions. Professor was also willing to give clarifications at any point.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Smart and puts a lot of effort into helping students. If you come there to learn, you'll enjoy it. Class isn't particularly hard, but in case you just want to pass, there might be easier choices.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst class I have ever taken. Lectures are dull and slides are boring. The last 3 classes the professor has sat down and read from the slides (that I believe come with the textbook) and didn't move a single time. Not worth your money. It's a shame WashU allowed this teacher to teach. She is clearly smart and very nice, but not a good teacher.

Every lecture consists of her sitting at the front of the classroom and reading directly from the powerpoint slides. She erratically skips slides just to make her lecture fit the class period. She is VERY nice but does not prepare for lecture at all. I learned more in high school economics.

Kasey is really sweet and we love to have the most random class discussions about ANYTHING. She leaves tons of feedback on your work and is really lenient about what you can write about. There are a lot of essays but it's a great choice for college writing. Be prepared to read and discuss mostly about gender/political issues. Great class!

If you're more introverted and don't really talk during class, then you might find yourself disadvantaged here. Participation really matters because the in-class discussions make up the bulk of class. They're also the reason why class is so much fun! She's also super easy to get in touch with outside of class and gives really constructive feedback.

Every class was a treat. While we often got derailed from the reading we were originally analyzing, the discussions were always engaging and insightful; I always felt like I learned something walking out of class. Also, she is such a wonderful person to talk to, so much so that I'm proud to say I've found a mentor in her. Take her if you can!
Professor Grady is an engaging lecturer and fair grader. Though some of the readings were a bit boring, she does a good job of breaking them down in class and relating the topics to our lives.

If you don't like letter grades and do better with percentages, then she isn't for you. However, she is so easy to talk to in a small setting, she gives great feedback and grades on time, and she gives smaller assignments to help ease into larger papers. Would 100% recommend. Really like her a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I took this semester, she made the class. The in class discussions don't require lots of preparation but allow deep discussions. She runs a fun class that gave decent feedback on the few essays we did have. Fun in class discussions that are guided and improved by her input.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing college writing professor. This class is not necessarily an easy A (does grade on performance), but if you put in the effort, you will do fine. Gives great feedback on essays and I genuinely enjoyed going to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Grady is a really charismatic professor. I did find it frustrating that she never gave "number" grades and gave a lot of A-/As which is a huge range. If you aren't too bothered by what grade you get, she's great. But if you do care, it definitely feels like she gives As based on vibes which can be really annoying.

One of the kindest individuals you will ever meet and best professor at Washu thus far. She makes class time interesting by choosing readings and topics that are heavily based in pop culture/social justice and has authentic discussions in class. Definitely not an "easy A" english class where you can cram a paper in a night but one worth taking.

AMAZING teaching style reaches a broad range of students. Great feedback on papers and carefully chosen readings are worth the read. You'd be lucky to get her 'Power and Commodity'. Engaging with students and works hard to create conducive discussions. She is extremely understanding and makes her students feel valued. 10000/10

If you want to be the only person saying "I liked college writing," take Professor Grady's class. Her readings are relevant, interesting, and not very long. Class discussion is thought provoking, but not ridiculously academic. She is very understanding, accessible outside of class, and always ready to support you. Long live Professor Grady!

Prof. Grady's is by far the best and my favorite prof. at WashU so far. Her lectures and assignments are fun and educational. Her classroom is like a family and she is always willing to help her students on assignments. There was ever a boring day in her class, like when I dressed up as a cow. I find myself missing being in her class all the time.

If you're taking college writing, you better hope you get a subsection with professor Grady. She is universally adored by her students and always takes time to get to know them. Her class discussions are interesting and the readings are not too bad, especially if you're interested in the subsection topic (power & commodity culture).
She is an amazing professor, but overall college writing is an ok class. She helped make it more interesting.

Professor Grady is an amazing person. She is hilarious and tries to get to know her students on a personal level. She is a bit of a tough grader, but gives good feedback on papers. I always looked forward to her class
Great professor and course.
An incredible professor who actually makes class very fun. I would take a class with her again because of her nurturing she is with her classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kasey Grady is the BEST professor at WashU. I genuinely looked forward to going to class and doing the readings. RUN, don't walk to take a class with her.

Professor Grady is truly a delight to have as a professor. You can tell she really cares about her students and assigns readings that are actually interesting and fun to read. At the end of the semester she takes feedback on which readings the students liked the best and the least to take into account the interests of her students.

It's hard to leave an impression on students in a mandatory college writing class but Grady definitely does. She is beyond kind and one of the nicest people I've come across. She has helped me so much with the typical freshman struggles, especially as a Deneb student. She made me and others feel very cared for and seen. Hands down best prof.

She is extremely fun and entertaining. The readings can be a bit much sometimes, but if you at least skim them you'll be alright. She gives good feedback, is available for office hours, and clearly explains what she's looking for. If you put in effort, you'll be ok. She's also very understanding. Class is engaging and funny. Wonderful professor.

Professor Grady is very personable and tries to make everyone feel welcome in class (she set up a GroupMe this semester so people could stay in touch with her and each other). She gives detailed, helpful feedback on your papers outlining the things she liked and how to improve on others. In-class discussions were engaging and funny. Star Wars fan

Professor Grady will always go above and beyond to make her students feel welcomed in her class. In her class discussions, she actively welcomes all perspectives. Professor Grady cares more about her students than any other professor I have had.

Prof. Grady is amazing. As others have said, the largely discussion-based class can go off the rails, but I learned how to craft arguments better, and she has a knack for relating to her students. She cares deeply for her students and gives super thorough feedback. I know you can't choose your College Writing prof., but just hope you get her!

While most of my friends said they didn't learn much in College Writing, I feel like my writing improved from Grady's class. She was helpful in office hours, energetic in class, and gave great feedback on papers, which made a mandatory writing class more enjoyable.

Very cool/young/relatable prof, but grades tough. Even a small mistake/critique can bump you to a B+/A-. We don't learn THAT much about how to actually craft an argument in class; we really just talk about controversial topics/articles. Seriously an incredible human being; you have to work for your grade, but definitely learned a lot in this class.

The class is very much discussion-based, which means it can get disorganized rather easily. I did not learn much writing skills in this class, but surely had many inspirational talks. Definitely talk to Prof. Grady outside class! She's very caring and can really provide personal advice about writing.
I'm so lucky to have Grady as my college writing professor!! Highly recommend her classes.

Kasey Grady is not only a hilarious, relatable, and great teacher, she also truly cares for her students. She helps with various aspect of a student's life even above and beyond class. She is a truly kind teacher and all her students have nothing but good to say. Her comments on your essays make any revision easy so if use the help you'll be ok.

Grady is an excellent professor. I could easily tell how much she cared about her students' success and that she was actively interested in teaching us writing skills. She takes feedback seriously and is very reasonable with respect to extensions, grading, and homework. The class challenged me to become a better writer without being overbearing.
Grady is amazing. Her grading system is unpredictable but she is hilarious and makes class interesting. Make sure you go to class and participate.
Love her!!!!! My favorite professor. She is so funny and really cares about you. She is also just a really great person and is such a good role model with her positive attitudes and everything.

Kasey Grady is an absolutely amazing professor! Definitely my favorite one I have had in college. She gives amazing feedback and is really funny. She doesn't grade too hard but she isn't too easy either. She definitely gives great comments. She also gives extensions in you need them.
Provides an infinite amount of 1-on-1 meetings if needed. Has a strict rubric, but wants her students to succeed and improve in their writing skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gregory is kind and nice, and genuinely wants her students to succeed. She is also approachable outside of class and you basically can ask for an infinite amount of 1 on 1 meetings with her as long as you want to. She provides useful feedbacks and clear instructions for what she's asking for.

"Professor Gregory is extremely kind and is willing to give extensions if you are feeling stressed or can't submit your best work. The grading is a bit strict, but if you put in a bit of work everyday instead of cramming you'll do well in the course. Overall very fun class and very informative, with good feedback."

Professor Gregory is extremely kind and is willing to give extensions if you are feeling stressed or can't submit your best work. The grading is a bit strict, but if you put in a bit of work everyday instead of cramming you'll do well in the course. Overall very fun class and very informative, with good feedback.

She assigns way too much homework. She also says she "understands" how busy her students are but then expects them to be able to keep up with all the homework and essays that she assigns. Her essays are very specific and ask for a lot, but she doesn't give students enough time to write something that meets her expectations.

Professor Gregory is amazing! She is very understanding and always accessible outside class. She genuinely wants her students to succeed and gives fair feedback and grades. Go to lecture and try your best and you will be alright!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really like how he taugh the lesson. His reponses to students' questions can show the huge amount of knowledge he has.

Classes were almost all lecture in an un-engaging, awkward atmosphere. Slow paced. Many people called this their "daydream class." Many readings were interesting but very dense. A lot of your grade is based on two papers.

This is an easy class to get a good grade on with minimum effort. However, I recommend doing the readings (or just skim them as some can be pretty long) to be engaged during the lecture. He makes really good points and answers questions creatively. The "essays" all follow the same structure so with practice it will be easy to get good grades.

Dr. Gulledge is very knowledgeable, and the course material was great! Class was centered around readings. No exams - just an essay every week-ish, sometimes graded P/F. Lectures could be slow-paced/hard to pay attention to, at times.
Best professor. I am a huge Gulledge stan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is super quirky and goofy. Although the course is reading-heavy, you can honestly get away with not reading articles for lectures, although not so much for essays. He also disagrees with most of the readings, so it makes for a more interesting class. His grading isn't too difficult and the end-of-course debate is pretty enjoyable.
Waitman was the BEST prof I've had. Enough said.

Prof. Waitman was monumental to my first semester experience. She is so caring and recognizes students' other academic commitments. Her discussions in class always had meaningful insights to take away. I highly recommend Prof. Waitman to future college writing students.
I'm in her class right now and she is great. I would pay extra to take this class.

SPEND THE TIME NEEDED DURING REGISTRATION TO GET PROF. WAITMAN. She is a kind grader who is very flexible with deadlines (she calls the extension period her "Grace" period). She truly cares for ur well-being, wants to hear ur writerly voice and opinions, and is not afraid to get off-topic in class. 100% recommend. TAKE HER CLASS. SRSLY... worth it.
Such a sweet-hearted person! Class is so chill and Prof Waitman is very understanding and helpful! Take her class if possible!!
i would do anything for her, if you have to take college writing she is the only professor that makes it an actual enjoyable class
Take her class.

I spent 45 minutes during registration just trying to get this college writing class with Professor Waitman, and I can tell you that it was worth every second. She is very thoughtful, gives a lot of feedback on your work before it is actually graded, and also brings her dog to class which is fun.
Best teacher in this school I wish I could take her for more classes. Best college writing professor. 100% take her class. Best professor in this school

Prof. Waitman is SO caring of her students and she makes the classroom environment extremely welcoming. Words can't describe how much respect and love I have for her. She is a professor that truly truly cares about her students, and I really appreciated that. also her dog is so adorable!
Sweet and caring. So so kind. Allows for self-direction in writing assignments. Emphasizes voice and personality in writing. Manageable workload.

Prof. Waitman is the BEST college writing professor on campus. 100% this is your sign to take her (@first-years). She basically grades on completion, but doesn't actually assign much work, and the work she does give have huge grace periods after the due date. She is such a wonderful, caring person, and you need to take her.

Professor Grace is a nice and caring professor. She is respectful and understands how you take other courses and consider this when assigning assignments or readings.  Additional time on an assignment, she calls it the "grace" period which is a lifesaver. She also brings in her dogs at times and she is playful and makes the classroom more lively!

She is the BEST college writing professor WashU has, and not just because class is super easy. She's also very understanding and works with you to make sure you get your work done. The more you participate, the more she works with you so go to class! Literally the easiest professor I've had.

Arguably the "easiest" professor in the college writing department. Very laid-backed discussion-based teaching style. She canceled class a couple of times which was great. We also visited Kemper Art Museum twice during class which was fun. You are guaranteed an A if you show up and attempt to put in the smallest ounce of effort.
Became a lot more difficult this past semester than the current reviews say. Would not recommend.

Waitman is an easy professor, but that's because she doesn't really teach. Basically, she sits with her dog, stutters, and gives everyone an "A." I took her class and received an "A," but in later writing classes and on other writing assignments received low grades and was not prepared for other classes.

If you can get into Grace's college writing class, do it. Drop another conflicting class if you must. College writing is such a drag as a mandatory class, but Grace is the best possible option. Most assignments are graded on completion and I had way less work than all my friends in other sections. She's so chill and brings her awesome dog to class.

I just want to say that Grace Waitman makes her class TOO easy and that is not fair to other students with other professors. Grade inflation is insane in this class. That said, she should change her grading to make it more difficult so that it reaches a balance with other professors or else CWP is really an unfair game.

Best college writing professor ever. Almost everything is graded on completion and we have up to a week or more long grace periods so no hard deadlines. Gives great feedback on rough drafts for the final drafts. No surprises/tricks, everything is clear. No necessary readings and no graded in class writing assignments. Asynchronous Fridays.
Professor Waitman was my favorite professor. She is extremely nice and gives great feedback on writing. She is also flexible with most deadlines. I highly recommend taking her class.
Freshmen: take College Writing with her. Best option out there.

Professor Waitman was the bomb. She was pretty easy with grading but still gave solid feedback and class discussions were generally insightful. She really cares about her students. She brought her dog to class daily!

One of the best college writings profs you could have here at WashU. Cares about students and understands different skill levels; most homework is graded in a fair way and includes helpful comments. Would recommend!

Definitely the best College Writing Professor at WashU. Incredibly understanding and caring towards her students. Class discussions are always fun, especially when Grace brings her dog in! Having Grace as a teacher made the class much more enjoyable and inspiring. Super fair grader and very flexible deadlines. Take her class!!!!!

Professor Waitman is one of the kindest profs I've ever had. She genuinely is interested in your life and wellbeing. The course has a lot of writing, but she is very flexible with due dates and understands different skill levels. Not a hard grader. Very nice and brings dog to class sometimes.
I really like Prof Guinness. Quizzes every other week can be a lot, but it breaks up the content into small pieces. I found the content really interesting and a good mix of theory and application.
Material is clear and logical; notes are posted; quizzes mimic the exercise. Learn and you'll be fine. Deduction is gone over so you will gain solid foundation for linear stats model.

He is a kind man, however he does not explain the calculations in depth. He writes the notes on the board and that's it. You have to teach yourself the concepts to be successful in this class. Quizzes are every two weeks despite not applying the concepts in other applications.

Quizzes every other monday! INSANE. He doesn't take the time to go over things and usually brushes over important calculations that will be on quizzes.I think he is kind but the structure of the class is ridiculous and beyond stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rosas is extremely intelligent and an amazing lecturer. Never studied more than a day before the exam and got an A. Just make sure to do the readings and show up to most classes and subsection and you'll be good. Class grades are curved.

One of my fav profs at WashU. Readings can be a bit difficult to understand sometimes, & pop quizzes are specific on certain details of the readings. If you read closely, you should have no problems. Exams are also quite difficult, so make sure you study. His classes aren't easy A's, but what you gain from his classes is invaluable.

Rosas was great, really strong and coherent lectures, which helps for an intro class. Made material accessible but also engaging and interesting in a large classroom setting. Definitely my favorite of the poli sci intro classes at WashU, I'd recommend if you're looking for an accessible poli sci course about a wide range of various political topics

I liked Rosas a lot. He's very well spoken and gives great lectures with a lot of detail. He's super knowledgeable and loves talking to students outside of class and getting to know them. Felt like I had a good relationship with him, even though it was a big lecture class. He's a pretty bad exam writer TBH, but he curves a lot so it's all good.

I learned a LOT from Rosas. He has a depth of knowledge and teaches with nuance and detail. The tradeoff is that he is a harsh grader. Students will not get an A unless they study well for his tests and pay close attention to readings and lectures. Overall, I think taking his class is definitely valuable, but be ready to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The material isn't too difficult to understand, but it's definitely important that you keep up with the reading and study your notes well in advance of each exam. Test questions were mostly focused on small details from lectures/the book, so good memorization is key. You definitely need to attend class because he gives frequent pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Doesn't technically take attendance but gives very frequent pop quizzes, and missing those quizzes can kill your grade. Definitely important to keep up with the reading for the sake of the quizzes and exams. The material is very simple to understand if you do the reading, but it can be kinda time-consuming to keep up with it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: For his first time teaching comparative politics, he did a fine job. Lectures were pretty bland and restated what the textbook said for the most part. He explained confusing topics well. The pop quizzes were annoying and hurt a lot of peoples' grades. The exams were straightforward. Basically if you read the textbook and take notes, you'll be fine

Readings are tough but Rosas is flexible and lets us know what he's looking for with each assignment he gives us. He's a great practitioner of empirical-style polisci. You walk away from each lecture feeling smarter about this style of academia and in understanding politics. Very, very helpful in giving feedback & direction with your research.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Excellent, passionate, and insightful. He asks challenging questions which makes discussion engaging and has a nuanced, economic lens of examining Latin American politics. inspired my interest in the region's politics! Lots of homework and reading, but not too difficult to stay on track if you take good notes and pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class was artificially rigorous in the sense that material was not hard but assignments were time consuming because of verbal trick question type approach and because they were uploaded to give 5 days to complete them and not 7 in majority of classes. Also, evaluation stressed homework more than exams for some reason. I hope it is same for everyone

Interesting material and a very smart guy, but his lectures were not very engaging.  There was tons of information and it was difficult to process everything in class at a pace that could keep up with the lecture.  Also, really tough exams.  Rosas clearly has a very firm and detailed grasp of the material, but was not great at transmitting it.

Rosas singlehandedly turned me off of Political Science... go to class and you'll be bombarded by 90 minutes of solid information without any time to breathe.  Tests were ridiculously inconsistent, and class was murderously hard to sit through. He is a great guy though!
He speaks to quickly and can't be understood. His tests ask unfair questions and his review guides are useless.

When he speaks quickly, he can be a little difficult to understand.  You must do the readings to do well on the pop quizzes.  I thought the grading was fine, only because i got a 100s on both exams though :-).
He makes you work for your grade but you learn a ton of really interesting stuff.  Definitely recommend his Latin American Politics course.  He has a cute accent and all the girls think he is hot!!
He is from Mexico, so a little hard to understand.  He is an incredible guy and a thorough scholar, however.

To his credit, it is a difficult class to teach...so many countries.  He made it clear that the concepts were more important than the details, but it's still kind of difficult to prepare for the exams because you don't know what to study.  Really nice and helpful, but lectures droned on and on...
great professor, very smart, but class was too big and grading is a little weird.

Guillermo is soooo nice (and some would say hot). His grading scale is weird and he's not the best lecturer. Kind of disorganized. I guess just take it if you like good looking, nice, 30 something Mexican guys

Professor Guofu's course is very interesting. The content is a bit difficult if you don't have a basic understanding. It is more about application rather than mathematical reasoning, so it is acceptable. There are code examples shared, which is very interesting.

Dear two posters below me - I think your comments say more about you than the professor. PS. Guofu is hilarious, has comprehensive notes, is very helpful outside of class, and is one of the top finance professors (research and teaching) at WashU. He will NOT be fired.
terrible professor  i went to half the classes and got nothing out of them and wondered to myself why i ever went in the first place
The prof. can't speak English! FIRE him please!!!

Tough class covering some tough material.  The guy has an accent but is one of the MOST enthusiastic profs I've ever met.  He loves the subject and tries REALLY hard to make classes entertaining (by making dumb jokes, burning books) and is SOO helpful outside of class. Shows real care for students.

His accent's Chinese, not Korean... but yes, is difficult to understand, but he's very willing to help and answer any questions. His notes are comprehensive, so you learn much more in this class than just what's required by the course curriculum.
Can anybody understand what he says? This is US, not Korea.
Really hard to understand. Really hard material. Not a good combination. He was really nice though, and very enthusiastic.
Really enthusiastic, really into what he does which is awesome! He also has great lecture notes. But the material is hard..and he's somewhat hard to understand
Accent sometimes very difficult to understand, but his lecture notes are excellent.  I took this class a year ago, and still refer back to the notes when I need to know something about options.

Liz is the best drawing professor one could hope for... after a second semester of drawing with a different professor, I realized just how much she pushed me in Drawing I and how much I was challenged to do better in her class. She is incredible  in how much she cares... she even continued to give me feedback on my pieces for later classes. :)

I've said this to my friends but Liz is a skittle. She may seem tough on the outside but once you get to center, the very core, she is extremely sweet. Liz's class is definitely requires a lot of hard work and dedication, but very enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Liz is such a knowledgable & devoted professor. Her class is challenging but the projects are interesting & enjoyable. Whatever previous drawing experience you've had, you will definitely learn & improve from her class as long as you put in the effort. She may seem harsh at first but she truly cares about each of her students & is very approachable

Liz is amazing! She truly cares for her students and wants to see them succeed. She introduced us to a variety of mediums & techniques, gave us interesting projects & challenges every student to give their best. If you're prepared to work hard & put in time Liz is worth it. Your drawing skills will improve tremendously-- would 100% recommend Liz!

She's great in every way. In the beginning of the semester, one student stated, "I lived in constant fear." That was true. The homework was a grind and in class work was intense under her careful watch. But, the stress was worth it to develop a great relationship with this professor. She really helped me become a better artist, not just at drawing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While this class is one of the most challenging classes I have this semester, I enjoy it a lot. Liz encourages us to be creative and cares for all students. I am impressed by how many different techniques we've tried and learned in just 3 months. The process of practicing might be tough and time-consuming, but you won't regret it.

Liz makes an introductory drawing course beneficial to students of all levels and makes sure to challenge each and every one of her students. There's definitely a lot of time that needs to be invested in the class and in homework, but I am amazed at how much I have grown in my drawing ability in just one semester. 100% would  recommend to everyone

The class is incredibly difficult and there are some days that I want to give up. But Liz is incredible and always ready to help. She challenges students to dare for greatness. If you want to be grow as an artist and person, Liz will lead you. Liz cares for her students immensely and is proud of us when we succeed. How can we not giver her our all?

Caring guy who wants students to understand and execute the essence of anthropology. I have massive respect to Bret's research on Bolivia especially. One of the few teachers here who defend critical thinking and truthful curriculums that expose imperialist brainwashing. I wish WashU would bring back his Global Dream class!

Extraordinarily boring for what should be an interesting topic. Offensive levels of humor that are inappropriate for a professional setting. Overall not a kind man, shows little empathy for his students and blames his own shortcomings on them to the point of ridicule. Has too much of an ego for his own good.
Thought provoking and very insightful! Great class for anyone with genuine interest in learning.

Gustafson doesn't do much for this class because it's guest lectures, but I would highly recommend. As someone who had no experience in anthropology, it was super interesting to learn about the work of all the anthro professors at WashU, including Gustafson.

Professor Gustafson has been the best instructor that I came across at WashU. His class is engaging and open to diverse voices. If you truly want to be in a university level class this is it! Take a class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: a great professor and person.

Prof Gustafson was genuinely one of my favorite professors at WashU- not only does he care about his students, but he takes their concerns seriously and listens well! He simply doesn't tolerate ignorant/uninformed perspectives in his class. As a jewish student, I can confidently say he made me feel safe and welcome in his class :) would take again

It's rare to see a professor who puts his theory/teachings into practice. An inspirational and supportive professor, who will put himself at the front lines to support and stand up for underrepresented students. Uses his tenure for good! 

Y'all are smart kids...use your reading comprehension to read through the misconstrued dominant narratives.

Bret Gustafson has been one of the most enlightening professors in my entire ArtSci education at WashU. He truly cares about increasing awareness about overlooked peoples in Latin America, the US and elsewhere. I have encountered very few like him on campus and I am so grateful for his instruction!
Questionable humor.  Some was offensive but afraid to speak up.  Interesting material.  Could be better, wish I took the other section.  My friends like it much better
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gustafson's class is perhaps the most important course you'll take at this university. He is a professor who is truly passionate about his students and his service to humankind. I'm incredibly thankful to have learned from him.
Gustafson has a great deadpan. Proseminar is pretty straightforward but he organized it well and made expectations clear.

Definitely take this class. Material is important and something you likely won't encounter many other places at WashU. Bret's humor is wry and witty. Exams are pretty straightforward; ours were all online and you could take them with other people.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gustafson guest lectured in my energy and environment course. He was noticeably bitter, almost angry as he taught. In fact, one of his anecdotes he ripped on his neighbor who drove an Escalade (gas guzzler). During the Q&A, I was really intimidated to ask any question that might challenge what he had talked about during his lecture.

Bret Gustafson is one of the few professors at WashU who genuinely cares about what he teaches and whom he teaches. GEAD was a pleasure to take and was perhaps the most important class I've taken thus far.

Gustafson organizes and introduces new lecturers for each class. He's kind, funny, and easygoing. Grades are based on a couple of midterm papers where you reflect on and respond to lecture material. This is a great survey/intro class for those wanting to learn about the different subfields of anthropology.

Still in the process of taking this class! Bret is definitely one of the best professors I have had the pleasure of having, everyone should definitely take this class. Cannot recommend him or his class ENOUGH

I took Global Energy and the American Dream with him. This class was so impactful and mind-blowing. Guy is kinda whack but in the best way. You will get honesty and learn a lot and question how WashU allows this class which kind of exposes WashU along with America and the world. Awesome class, awesome teacher. I think about what I learned often.

Professor Gustafson is tremendous. Everyone should take this class. It is truly eye-opening. He is one of the few rays of hope at a university full of an administration and departments who take orders from the fossil fuel industry.

Gustafson is passionate about his subject. Global Energy & the American Dream is SUCH an important class to take if you care about this world at all. And DO the readings. The books are life-changing, especially Carbon Democracy and This Changes Everything. Also he's a hottie and has a slight Southern-ish accent that will melt your heart.

GUSTAFSON IS ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS AT WASHU. IF YOU CAN TAKE HIS CLASS, TAKE IT. ANY CLASS. but global energy and the american dream is so so important and wonderful and he's incredibly committed to his students; his lectures are personal, provoking, and i wish i could take this class twice. I was not bored for a single second. Also i love him

Definitely one of the best professors at Wash U! He is very engaging and makes topics interesting and relevant. He is always there to help students and is a very nice guy in general. Although his classes can be somewhat reading intensive, they're definitely worth the effort.

Intolerably slow lectures, very monotone, not always clear on how essay grades are assigned.  Not a mean fellow, just a boring one.  Homework material did not correspond with out of class expectations.  Bad experience overall.

Great professor, extremely helpful. He made anthropology a much more interesting course than I thought it would be. Most of the class involves just going over the reading material and discussion your view points
AWESOME!
While the class was somewhat interesting, he was very uninvolved, and unwilling to give guidance.
Interesting Class with little work and good lectures.  Sometimes slow but worthwhile.
Kinda a boring class sometimes. But overall interesting, straightforward grading procedures. Not too much work.
Very hot, but kind of a tool.  His lectures sometimes are boring, he is very monotone.  His tests are challenging. But nonetheless, the overall class is not that bad.
the class is interesting, and you only have to read a few books and go to class, and also he is the hottest professor!
Good teacher, some of the books are hard to read and understand to the level he expects you to understand them. Not easy but not horrible either.

i love this class.  he never lectures for the whole 1.5 hour time (and then apologizes when he keeps us over an hour)...too bad though b/c this class is one of the most interesting I have taken at this school. not easy, but really interesting

Bapi was a complete disaster. Didn't explain the final project to us until the last week of class, then disappeared completely during finals week and never responded to emails, even though we had the project AND a final. Probably one of the worst professors I've had at wash u.

Class was very easy if you had prior programming experience. Gupta taught pertty well, and had a fun personality. He answered questions well. He overslept through class on 4 or so occasions, which was amusing.  Class not mandatory, but a lot of people stopped coming and he locked his (online) code out of annoyance. So it's probably better to come.
No Comments
Class was a good concept, but he was unprepared for most lectures, and much of our time was subsequently wasted literally doing nothing but surfing the net.
This guy is the MAN.  Very clear explanations, very accessable outside of class, very willing to help.  In terms of personality, probably the coolest teacher I've had here.

She is a very easy marker and decent lecturer given that French 307 is grammar-oriented and not a hard course to teach. However, there is a great distance between her and students. She is enthusiastic without a doubt, but she does not seem to show a genuine interest in students' affairs. I easily see her as a teacher but not as a friend.
BEST PROFESSEUR EVAAAASZ!

Mlle Maucher is the best French professor I have ever had! She genuinely cares for her students. She will challenge you, but is so willing to help you outside of class.  I learned a lot very quickly and enjoyed every minute of it. She does a very good job of making class fun by incorporating different types of media.

She was nice but very scatterbrained and unorganized. This resulted in the attendance of the class being drastically lower later in the semester than earlier in the semester. She did not remember whole lectures she taught and would go back and reteach the same slides—until the TA or a student stopped her.

Only midterms and final project are counted for grade, so there is no redemption opportunity. The test is very specific and memory-based; but Professor Hale uses anecdote in her lecture, so it is very difficult to know what to study for. She is a nice professor, but overall, I would not recommend taking this class for credits.

Sandra Hale is very nice and she definitely knows her material. The only problem is the way she conducts it. She strays off lectures by telling long personal life stories, the study guides are very "misguided" for the tests, and there are only 4 grades in the entire class so you have to make sure you ace the 2 midterms to have a good grade.

Hale is nice and well intentioned. However, she constantly has tech issues, spends half of class on tangents, and tests are totally unpredictable. She would frequently end up adding 10 points to everyone's grades due to questions that were incomprehensible. I wouldn't recommend this class unless required. (I took it as an elective)

Hale is a nice person, but I really struggled in her class because of her inability to use technology and her unclear study guides. I found myself having to put in significantly more effort to study because of her shortcomings which is why I ultimately withdrew from the course. Again, nice person, but easily the worst prof I have had so far.
I loved Professor Hale!! I feel as if she's super genuine and accesible outside of class. Interesting lectures with her mini-anecdotes as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While I think Hale is a really kind person, she's not a good teacher. She uses her life story to teach and goes on long tangents. With no attendance required, there's no motivation to hear her talk about herself more confidently than class content. She doesn't always post lectures. Also, if you don't do well on the 1st exam you're nearly screwed.

Hale is super nice as a person. That being said, she is not the most put-together professor. She often goes on tangents and tells irrelevant stories. Not to say that it wasn't entertaining at points. Though this does make it harder to focus in lecture. That's why I ended up watching lectures online at 2x speed. Interesting class material though.

Sandra is very interesting to listen to, you will learn literally every corner of her brain. You will know her family, her childhood, but all of this makes it very difficult to actually understand the information you need to know. I would love to have her as a friend however a teacher she makes it a tad difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice professor who tells very interesting stories. She is very clearly passionate, knowledgeable, and an experienced (published!) researcher in Developmental Psychology. The lectures are entertaining and the exams are fairly easy. This class is fun and I would recommend it to everyone!
She talks about her own story a lot during classtime so it may be distracting, but overall the tests were not so difficult and you can get good grade if you review lectures

Personally, I love Dr. Hale as a professor. I think she's super sweet, her lectures are funny, and our conversations have always been super interesting. But, her class structure does make it difficult to do well. It's hard to tell what is going to be important and what is a tangent. But, once you get used to her style, it gets much easier.

Dr. Hale is clearly a knowledgeable researcher. She's also very kind and tells great stories. That being said, class was pretty disorganized. The textbook material was incorporated into lectures seemingly on a whim & the slides were hard to read. Preparing for exams (on which almost your entire grade is based) was consequently an absolute gamble.

Great professor and researcher, less great lecturer. Although she is greatly respected and I enjoyed her class a lot, she goes on a lot of tangents. Her grading was not hard and based almost entirely on midterms, with one major essay for our final.

A kind, warm-hearted, and talkative grandma-like professor. But too old to teach. Incessantly got stuck on technical issues. Gave random off-topic interesting anecdotes but have no use on the exam. WashU should make sure professors are technology savvy to a certain extent.
awful lecturer

Professor Hale is a very nice person but she always seems to be unprepared when giving lectures. I took this class online and asynchronously and she would also post the video lectures a few days late. It also seems like she doesn't use her own slides because she spends a good amount of time trying to figure out what is going on in the slides.

1) professor clearly communicates her expectations for students, including when they should refer to the textbook, what types of essay questions to be prepared to answer on exams, etc. 2) professor will accommodate your needs (empathetic)! 3) AMAZING powerpointsthey are organized, illustrated, and highlight key points 4) TIP: attend Q&As!

definitely the most difficult class I've taken at wash u. not an easy a, but definitely the most I have learned by FAR in a psych course. she is adorable and obviously very passionate about teaching. the averages on our tests were low B's - high C's, but you CAN do well if you go to class, pay attention, and do a bit of memorizing. def recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the sweetest professors I have had and definitely an expert in Dev Psych. That said, lectures are very fast paced (even hard to keep up with notes if typing on the computer) and you have to memorize a boatload of psych studies for the tests (# of participants, type of study, etc) which is time consuming. If you study a lot, you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is definitely a very nice person, and she is definitely passionate about what she is teaching, but she wasn't the best at conveying the information to everyone. She does tell a lot of good stories though that pertain to what we are learning, which kept class entertaining. Tests were very hard and a little unpredictable.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Hale is a lovely, lovely woman. Her impressions of little kids are so cute. Her big flaw is that she speeds through her slides and one can't copy down all of the information in time and the complete slides aren't online. At times, she puts up graphs with no labels and no explanation. Her tests are hard, but she is always helpful.

Experimental Psych with Hale was honesty the worst class I have taken so far.  She doesn't use PowerPoints with her lectures, and just speaks in a very haphazard way for the two hours of class.  She seems to care about her students, but is impossible to follow and can't explain concepts in a succinct or clear manner.

She is an incredible sweet woman and clearly is passionate about psychology. Absolutely wants her students to do well. The problem is, although she knows her stuff, she is not so great at communicating information to people who don't have the same experience she does. Sweet, smart woman, not the best teacher, but she really cares
The tests are more challenging than you might expect, but Prof. Hale is always available for questions and outside help. Papers for this class are a bit challenging as well.

The only thing that got me through the class was the TA. Hale's tests were hard but she curved so it turned out OK. Still, it was a frustrating class because she didn't communicate clearly what she wanted out of the papers and project.
Prof Hale is really understanding and fair.  She cares more about her students doing well than designing tricky tests to limit the number of people who get As.

It is really difficult to follow her sometimes. I think she is very smart, but she has a hard time communicating ideas to her students. Also-all about Cognitive psychology..if you aren't interested in that field, take someone else.

She really limits what you can do for your final project.  It's a good thing I had a very helpful and nice TA because no one knew what she wanted us to do or anything she tried to explain in that class.
No Comments
No Comments

It is difficult to explain how dialed in this class is. So much of it -- the exams, the daily problems, the participation system -- has been carefully crafted and well thought out. This class is hard, but it is so much easier to do it all when everything feels so intentional. fr though... do the daily problems when they are assigned

She' a nice person but her classes are exam heavy and graded by a few things; it gets even worse with a twist of her OCD. What you learned is not reflective of your grade. She teaches in the engineering dept but I found her teachings are not helpful for my other engineering class. It's more like a principle based math class

Absolutely PHENOMENAL. EnMath B has the potential to be a really difficult course, but under Hastings, it's incredibly manageable. Go to lecture, inform her of any absences, go to her office hours for help-Hastings' EnMath B is incredibly fair, and will return to you EXACTLY what you put into it. It's not easy, but she makes it approachable.

Dr. Hasting is a kind person, and she seems to genuinely care about her students. But this class is way too hard. The homework is okay, and it's easy to get help on, but then the test is insane. This class is a prerequisite for a lot of other engineering classes, but I didn't find that it actually gave me any knowledge I would need.

Good professor. Very difficult exams. Homeworks, if you follow along with your notes (she does fill in the blank notes), are easy. Requires everyone to ask a question or answer a question once during class during the semester. Super helpful office hours. My biggest regret is not following the notes during class, they were very helpful.

EnMath A is much harder than EnMath B with Hasting. This woman clearly has terrible OCD and is very unmerciful in grading. I lost SO many points on exams for having the correct answer, but either not simplified, factored, or expanded enough for her taste. I did all of her practice problems and still not get an A. A lot of my friends are getting Cs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Hasting for EnMath A and EnMath B and she is probably the best professor I've ever had. Her lectures are so organized and intentional, and she truly has thought out every aspect of her class. Her exams are crazy hard, but you really learn the material in her classes. She's iconic tbh

Dr. Hasting is the best math professor I have ever met. Class notes are helpful and clearly explained each concept. The class materials are excellent foundations for higher level class. I have applied math techniques from ESE318 and 319 into physical chemistry. Do her daily practice, review notes before exams, and then you will survive.

The best professor I've had at WashU. A lot of people complain about her exams being too challenging. They are challenging only because she is making sure you understand the concept and not just know how to solve an equation. Her lectures are super organized and she gives clear feedback on work. Major Tip: Do her daily assignments.

Hasting is definitely a good teacher, but I felt that the class was unnecessarily difficult. My friends who took EnMath A with the other professor had easier homework assignments and easier exams. Also I do not like how her policies for students with disabilities made it more difficult to receive accommodations in the class.

Dr. Hasting is a truly amazing teacher. While exams and homework can be difficult, she is amazing at communicating topics so that you truly understand them. Exams are 81% of the grade, so make sure you study, but she offers plenty of practice materials, including 2 practice exams per exam. Will be taking her classes again in the future.

Like everyone else said, notes are great, teacher cares about your learning, but the tests are probably the hardest that I've ever had in my engineering coursework. Also a lot of the math isn't even applicable to engineering problems.

Dr. Hasting is a wild mix of one of the hardest professors I've had and one of my favorites. Her class was hard. I got a horrible grade. Her tests do NOT reflect your knowledge level. But she is a great lecturer, very available outside of class, and wants you to succeed. She just doesn't really understand how much time students have for her class.
Great teacher but insanely hard, I unfortunately had to withdraw from the class after the third test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Hasting's classes are very organized and well prepared. She is nice and cares about her students. She is very accessible outside of class through email. Exam questions can involve small details, but they for sure appear somewhere in the notes. If you think her exams are tricky, you probably didn't understand the materials well or study enough

She is a great person, but a terrible lecturer. If you purely love math you would like her course, but if you like to have real life understanding about your material, she has no idea what she is teaching about.

Her lectures are absolutely amazing; I've never had a professor as organized with her notes as Dr. Hasting. Her notes are so clear and if you have trouble with anything she is very accessible outside of class and helpful in her office hours. I took ESE 318 with her and went back to take ESE 319 with her because of how much I enjoyed her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I've ever had. I took ESE318&319 with her. Overall amazing! Great lectures, organized and tied to real-world applications. Eager to help her students learn. Super accessible; couldn't make off. hours so I made appointments with her and she was very accessible. DO THE DAILY PROBLEMS. Although recommended, they are necessary!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor! She is SO organized and precise. She cares so much for her students. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS SHE WILL ANSWER ANY QUESTIONS. I figured this out way too late. Her exams are also out of 30 points which means missing just a few things can bring your grade down significantly. Stay on top of the material and you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Amazingly clear lecturer. If you just come to class, you'll walk away with a great understanding of EnMath A. However, her tests are quite tricky and she seems to test enough on small details that it feels like your grade isn't based on your overall understanding of the material. If it's on the test, it was in your notes though.

One of the best teachers I had in 4 years at WUSTL. Knows the material, knows how to teach, and knows her students. Lectures very organized and "tie together" well. Super accessible for office hours/help. Tests can be tricky but fair. I would take class with her again over a better grade with another prof just based on how much I learned
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: There is no doubt that she truly cares about her students; by the end of the semester she had memorized everyone's names. She works to make sure that you understand the material. She's always willing to take questions and while many found her tests difficult, they are not impossible. Honestly one of the best math teachers at wustl.

If you take Hasting you will probably learn a lot of material, but her tests are IMPOSSIBLE. You have to know every minute detail in order to do well. Take Hoven for the A, its better for your gpa in the long run.

Her tests are very tricky and not easy to do well. She is a very professional teacher and treat her work very seriously. Good teacher, hard to do well. I won't take her again for 319 because GPA is more important to me

Her notes are  all you need to do well in the class. As long as you read the notes thoroughly the day before the test and look over the two practice tests she gives you, you'll do pretty well on the test. You can also go to her office hours and check homework answers with her, which can be pretty helpful.
Tests are not representative of your ability to solve problems. True False, multiple choice and short answer that were made to trick you.
She's insanely overrated... En Math is pretty useless, you just review the past 2 years of math.
take it with hoven. she isn't worth wrecking your gpa over

Professor Hasting truly cares about her students and values their experience at WashU.  Her tests are difficult, but she wants her students understand the material.  I had her last semester, and she made my semester.  I would be willing to take a class with her and get a B over getting an A with another professor, merely because of her teaching.

Take Hoven if you can. Some claim she is clear but if you put her lecture next to his, they are of equal merit. She chooses to test specifically on trick question multiple choice and true false for math. Very little application. Hoven's tests are written to test if you know the material. Her HW is easier, but her class is a joke. Take Hoven.

Professor Hasting is absolutely amazing. Her lectures are incredibly clear and never confusing. This doesn't mean that the tests are easy though! She really makes you study hard for the tests (hw is easy). You will have an incredibly strong foundation in engineering math if you take this course, even if her tests are more difficult. It's worth it!

Great class. Copy ABSOLUTELY EVERYTHING on the board because you'll need them later for tests which don't seem too hard at first but will destroy you if you're unprepared. The lectures are amazing! It's hard to fall asleep in class because she keeps it very engaged.

Hands down best math professor I've ever had. Great teacher, and homeworks are easy. You really have to know your stuff to do well on exams, and even then you aren't guaranteed an A. But she is fair, and you will learn a ton. Take her class if you're willing to go to class and study hard for exams.
best professor at washu. not easy but 100% worth it. always take enmath with hasting!

Professor Hasting is absolutely amazing. She is the best math teacher I have ever had. Her lectures are incredibly clear and organized. She is so helpful and even learns everyone's name in the whole lecture hall. The exams are very difficult because they are mostly multiple choice and true/false, which just do not fit in math courses. Just amazing!

I didn't appreciate the trick questions in the exams. The math was pretty easy, but it's also easy to make mistakes in exams. You can only get two MCs wrong on average to get an A, which I think is ridiculous. Exams eventually boiled down to how good a cheat sheet you make because it's all about getting the trick questions right.
Hasting's engineering mathematics is one of my favorite class in this semester. Her notes are wonderful and helpful to the exams, though the exams are tricky.

Easily one of the best math professors I've had. Very clear, approachable, and reasonable. The tests never seem that difficult, but you usually do worse than you think you did because they are tricky.

Professor Hasting is with no doubt my favorite professor ever.  She is extremely thorough and organized, and she will cover in depth anything she'll test you on.  Additionally, she continues to impress me with how much interest she takes in each student.  If I were to ever teach, I would strive to be just like her.
Difficult class, but the most helpful and wonderful math professor you'll find at WashU.

The worse class ever! she is so suck at grading. she has sign sit for tests. all tests are multiple choice and true/false.all the tim just write and write pages of class note and memorize them for test and she knows how to trick you. learned nothing of the ENHGINEERING math because she was a math major and spent all calss on driving the formulas.
Professor Hasting is very helpful and does a great job of making the material easy to understand.

You can not judge students' potential just through multiple choice and T/F questions. I did not think the class was that diffucult compared to other class I am taking, however, its diffult to get good grades..and no any partial credits... frustrating.I won't recommend taking this class with her.
Great teacher. However worst exam format ever. You cannot test mathematical knowledge with multiple choice questions. Come on we're not in middle school anymore!
One of the worst engineering experiences for me! She doesn't care what you think. She just cares how much you like her

You must do the daily assignments to have a chance at doing well in this class.  The tests do not let you show how much you know; rather it is carefully crafted to be as confusing and nit-picky as possible.  That said, she is the best math teacher I've ever had.  It is a note-intensive class, but she makes it worth it. Great teacher, harder class.
Her tests are ridiculous!  You go in there thinking you knew everything and then get a C.  Also, the true/false are not math related more if you read her notes and the book.
Tests are impossible
very good math professor

This class is tough, the test are almost entirely true/false multiple choice, so you will have little chance to show your capabilities.  It may be nearly impossible to get an A, a B is do-able.  Take this class with someone else if at all possible.
hard class!

Problems with her class: 1. the practice tests. she does not hand out any practice tests prior to the exam, instead she wants her students to visit her during office hours. you cannot check your answers.2. homework problems. homework problems really have no essential value whatsoever in preparing for the exams.

Hastings is definitely worth changing your schedule to take. Her notes are amazing, and they are all you need for the class. However, if you miss even a day of class, you could fall quickly behind. Collected hw is easy and follows lectures. For tests, make sure you know everything on her notes, and you should get at least an easy B.

Hasting's days of teaching diff Eq is over. This whole semester I felt like she was way overrated. I hear this is her first time teaching Matrix Algebra, so I might give her a benefit of the doubt. But nonetheless, the course was not what I expected. She seems to really stretch things in the book. There wasn't much of what we learned on the exam.

Take anything you can with Dr. Hasting. Her notes are incredibly organized, and she keeps the class engaged as she teaches. Really tries to get to know all her students, even in a larger class. Makes difficult material more comprehensible.
Dr. Hasting is a goddess among us mere mortals. She is too fantastic for words. If EVER there be a choice to take any of her classes, do it.
Good teacher.  But its still an intense class
Very good lecturer, who writes everything on the board and will make sure students understand the material.  Scantron tests screwed me for this class though.

Dr.Hasting rocks. Period. Her lectures are crystal-clear, unbelievingly organized, 100% flawless, and are enough for students to excel in class. She is always willing to give helpful extra-help outside of class. Her assignments are interesting and well-declared. Her exams are reasonable. It is sad she is leaving math department.
Like most others, I have nothing bad to say about her.  I still found the class pretty difficult, but I think that's mostly the material/my laziness rather than an inability to teach on her part.
she is incredibly well organized, exams are extremely straightforward

An amazing math professor.  Extremely organized, and lectures are always clear and demonstrate pertinent examples.  Her exams are of medium difficulty, but she always makes it known ahead of time what her expectations are.

Professor Hastings is a very good teacher.  She gives the best notes, and does really good examples.   The homework is really easy, especially the MATLAB assignments that she gives you hint sheets for.  She is always willing to answer questions outside of class.

Very well organized professor. Nice, helpful, and concerned with the success of students. Great communication. Even though there is no other teacher for Differential Equations, you will be glad to have Prof. Hasting. Maybe that's why there is no other professors for the course.
Professor Hasting is probably one of the best math teachers at Wash U; however, her grading scale makes it a little difficult to excell in the class.
Awesome.  Greatest college professor ever!!!!
A pretty easy class with excellent teaching and organization. GO TO CLASS and you'll do fine. But get cocky and you'll end up paying for it
Best math teacher I've ever had.  Ever.
the only teacher worth taking this class from though she really emphasizes attendance
Hastings makes learning Diff Eq if not easy, at least manageable.  Very organized with handouts and reviews, she writes everything she says on the board.  Good at answering questions.
No Comments

Hasting is an AWESOME teacher. Lectures are very well organized and clear. Tests are fair and predictable. She is very available with office hours and likes to chat too. She WANTS you to learn and like the course.
Good teacher, but hard class.

Very organized lectures, lots of helpful handouts. She's a Maple fan, but WU uses Matlab for Diff Eq, so she doesn't do anything difficult with Matlab and gives examples with the homework that are almost exactly what you have to type in. Fair exams.
She's very sweet and leads class in an engaging way. Course content was diverse and interesting, and assignments were creative.
She is very passionate about her lectures. Her grading rubric is very clear. Amazing professor.
Very sweet, lots of group discussion.
Professor Haklin is the most lovely and wonderful human being both inside and outside the classroom. I was only ever to take one class with her and I truly wish I could have taken more.

I'm not a French major or minor, so I was not super invested in this course. That being said, the prof made it quite engaging and is incredibly nice and caring. I would highly recommend this course if you're looking for an easy French LCD.

Chem is challenging, but her lectures were very clear and helpful. Concepts were explained in a way that was easy to follow and without assuming prior knowledge, which was really helpful for anyone who hadn't taken chem in high school.

Gen chem wasn't my favorite course but the teacher was a really solid lecturer. Course grading is based on the idea of "continuous improvement" which I was not a fan of but otherwise a difficult but fair course

Dr. Hamdi is such a nice and caring person! I always looked forward to her lectures every day because they were engaging as well as moved at a good pace. She answered questions so well and made it very easy to get help outside of lectures. Tip: take the PLTL and go to all of them. I thought I wouldn't need them, but I got my A because of it!

Prof Hamdi is incredibly underrated as a lecturer in regards to her actual teaching skills. In my opinion she was WAY better than Luo and helped me understand the material pretty well. However, the exams are BRUTAL in this class so get ready to be humbled. If you take this class, make sure to take PLTL with it, it was only thing that sorta saved me
Tests were unfair.

Although I'd say the lectures were engaging enough, I would say that the content taught appeared very simple in comparison to the quiz and exams given. The way the concepts were taught were some times also very confusing and I often needed to seek clarifications. If you take this class PLTL packets are the closest thing to the exam exercises.

i am not sure i learned anything. i switched from 111 to 106, and that was my first mistake. the 111/112 courses are much better taught and organized. hamdi was not good at answering questions or explaining concepts. exam questions had tricks in them instead of challenging us with material. i would avoid hamdi and any course she teaches.

honestly as hard as this class it, i enjoyed the material. she's a very engaging lecturer and makes tough concepts decently easy to understand. homework is fine but the exams in this class...harrowing experience. be ready to walk out of those midterms feeling like a shell of your former self.
overall a pretty solid lecturer. people hate because the exams are really difficult, but you just have to put in the work outside of class and go to office hours.
Hard but fair class. The workload is heavy, but Dr. Hamdi provides enough support if you stay on top of things.
Dr. Hamdi explains things well, but the tests are difficult. She is approachable outside of class and gives useful feedback if you ask for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class moves fast and can be overwhelming, but Dr. Hamdi is fair and clear in her expectations. Exams are hard but reflect the lectures well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough class but manageable if you put in the effort. Dr. Hamdi is helpful and responds to questions, but you need to be proactive in seeking help
Dr. Hamdi is a solid professor who explains the material well. The class is challenging, but she provides good resources. Be ready for a heavy workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class
