reviews.comment: Hard class, but Dr. Hamdi makes it manageable. She explains difficult topics in a way that makes sense and is always available for extra help. Highly recommend taking her if you're serious about learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hamdi is passionate about chemistry and it shows in her teaching. She challenges students but also offers plenty of support. Stay on top of the material, and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had! The material is challenging, but Dr. Hamdi is always willing to help. She provides detailed feedback and genuinely wants her students to succeed.
Super kind and knowledgeable professor. She explains concepts well and ensures students understand the material. Attending office hours is a must—she is very helpful and patient.

Dr. Hamdi makes a difficult subject manageable with clear explanations and a structured approach. She responds to emails quickly and is very supportive. Be prepared to work hard, but you'll learn a lot.

Dr. Hamdi is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students. Her lectures are well-organized, and she is always available to answer questions. The class is tough, but she provides plenty of resources to help students succeed.

I don't understand why Dr. Hamdi gets so much hate. Yes the class is hard it is intro to general chemistry. But she cares for her students so much and always answers my emails promptly. I feel like the class is super organized and Dr. Hamdi is a big part of why. You have to take this class for pre med and while its hard Dr. Hamdi cares.

Dr Hamdi is a very kind and honest lecturer. You can tell she enjoys what she is teaching and it shows. She puts so much effort into being accessible to students when we as students are available. Chem 105 is a hard class. There is a ton of concepts that get covered at a very fast rate. Make sure you are following along and getting help.

Dr Hamdi is really accessible for students to get help outside of class. And is very open to giving you lots of feedback to improve your score. Chem 106 is a class is very hard, but the professors are very accommodating and work to your student schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Hamdi will help you succeed if you put in the w
Her lectures aren't for everyone but I liked them. The class is very hard.

I do not understand why she is a teacher. Hamdi avoids questions and seems to get upset if we ask any. She is a bit insulting insisting we should know more than we do. I took 105 because I dont know the material. I switched to 112 to avoid her this semester.

Dr. Hamdi is a wonderful person who clearly cares about her students and chemistry. However, her quizzes and tests are downright horrendous. This is the hardest class I've ever taken, costing me hours of sleep and stress. GO TO OFFICE HOURS with her and Mrs. Mabbs. In those sessions, they're extremely helpful and will make the quizzes feel easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Harsh grader and creates incredibly difficult tests.
Strong and rigorous lecturer. Always willing to answer questions. Explores the material in depth with you during help sessions. Very sweet and kind.
Awful. No reason to go to lecture. Go to other profs for help. Just read the book and learn it on your own. Get old exams as most questions are reused (minor changes).

Dr. Hamdi was such a great help during office hours. I went to her office hours every work to do my homework and lecture review questions. Overall this class is very work heavy but Dr. Hamdi does an amazing job taking the time to explain the work and work with us. She is honest but a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hamdi was a horrible professor point blank period. She discouraged students struggling in the class to drop their pre-med aspirations and refused to announce exam averages.

Terrible professor. Asked her students for feedback on her teaching and the next day, she told the whole class that she read the feedback and didn't care about what her students had to say. Terrible attitude and would constantly be corrected by another professor. TAKE 112 EVEN IF YOU TOOK 105 BEFOREHAND!!!

Mediocre to acceptable teaching, but her condescending and unsupportive nature overpowers any instinct to enjoy this class. Incoming students, beware: she holds grudges across semesters, and will be annoyed if you- god forbid- ask multiple questions across help sessions. Memorize relationships instead of just formulas. Use 112 practice exams.
Professor makes tests that are impossible to finish in the allotted time. On top of the length, they are noticeably more difficult when compared to the coursework from previous years.

Just a frustrating year in chem. The exams and interactions with Hamdi were abhorrent to most of us. The only students who did not mind her and the class were those who took AP and knew the material or upper level students who should be on our class.

I only took a single semester of chem in hs, and I did not think the material was hard. The exams and quizzes were out of left field though and oft not related to what we were taught. Very frustrating year.
Hamdi seemed nice but she is not a good teacher. She really cannot write quizzes or exams. My PLTL leader said our practice exams were written by Prof Luo last year. Those seemed reasonable.

As someone who didn't take AP Chem, this class was really difficult for me. I didn't really have a problem with Hamdi, I thought she was pretty good. However, her tests were really hard (mainly because of time). Intro chem became my full time job lol
Hamdi is terrible. She cannot teach and she really does not know how to write exams. Such a frustrating semester and start to my career. She made my decision to major in Bio instead of Chem EZ.
idk why everyone saying shes bad, they prolly didn't study or studied bad. Final was ez af. Class was easy A. Literally need 83.5% or higher to get A lol. Preschool work
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the practice exam represents nothing for the real exam but are actually exams from the past years, don't know the point of making exams really extra difficult and setting the A line unapproachable

Prof. Hamdi is a pretty decent lecturer, althought there are moments when she drops the ball on that. The tests and quizzes are extremely difficult and nearly impossible to aquedately prepare for. If Hamdi is not in charge of writing exams and quizzes I feel she would be a great professor, unfortunately, that is not the case.

Dr. Hamdi is a good lecturer, but the exams are so difficult it feels unfair. The practice exams are not representative of the actual exams, and even with tons of studying and practice, my friends and I keep scoring in the 40s-50s range which has been very frustrating.

honestly, I think her lectures are fine, just don't ask too many questions because she will get flustered and angry with you. her exams' problem difficulty is far higher than practice material, which begs the question on how she expects students to generally perform well. she isn't even redeemed by her personality as can get rude one on one.

Prof. Hamdidity justifies her practice exams by saying that they tell us the layout of the exam, and nothing else. She once announced to the 9AM section that the practice exams were not of the same difficulty as the actual exam--as in it is easier. She says we are too used to high school where practice exams are 'mirror copies'.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hamdidity should not give exams that she cannot pass. Seriously. If you go and ask her to explain things on the answer key, she cannot. She seems to resent the students who seek help. How dare us interfere with her "busy" schedule in hopes of learning the material. Do not take this class no matter what your advisor says to do.
Terrible experience. Lectures are unclear and confusing. Exams are not a good representative of what the practice material is. Impossible to do well.

Do not take this class with her. No matter how hard you try in this class, the exams will never reflect what you studied. Her lectures are so fast and I never once walked out understanding what just happened. She even openly admitted that the "practice exams" are NOT a representation of what the actual exam is. Overall, terrible experience.

Terrible lecturer. Exams were impossible to finish or do well on. Usual average on exams were clearly detrimentally low and she refused to release averages. Practice exams/quizzes were far from representative of the difficulty of the content, as she always found a way to pick at information that was mentioned once in lecture.

Exams are impossible. You can do all the practices that they give, i.e., quizzes (versions A-C), non-graded homework, practice exams, etc., and still score a 40% on the exam.
One time, before class started, Ms. Mabbs commented on how hard a problem was on an upcoming exam and, Professor Hamdidty said, "it's supposed to be hard. it doesn't matter".

Never take this course with this professor. I would not recommend Hamdidty at all. She took over the Chem 105-106 course for 2023-24 and it has been impossible to perform well. Based on rumors and a survey, exam averages have been between 40-50 %. As reference, a 75-80% is usually the 'A' range for the class.

Dr. Hamdi is caring, dedicated, and wants students to learn and succeed. She makes herself incredibly available outside of class and is extremely kind and helpful during office hours. The class is built for you to do well if you put in effort, although it does require LOTS of effort.

One of the worst lecturers at WashU. Will write something on the board and immediately cover it with another board. I thought she was a nice person until the last week, when I asked her a question about my final and she was incredibly rude and condescending.
HS Chem all over again. Prof Hamdi is just ok. Nothing special. I admit I never went to help sessions. Do go to PLTL. I am worried about being ready for orgo though.

Dr. Hamdi seems nice in person, but she is not a good teacher, she often seemed confused with the answers to problems she assigned, and she was dishonest about her grade lines. Overall, it was a rough semester.

Hamdi is extremely caring, kind, and passionate. This class was hard if you did not take AP Chem but Hamdi hosts office hours twice a week and they are EXTREMELY helpful. Exams and quizzes are difficult and like other reviews said, it might be confusing in lecture but she does a GREAT job explaining if you go to office hours to ask questions
This is an easy class, but grades are arbitrary. Even though it is a bit harder, I strongly recommend taking 111/112. It is taught better, and it will better prepare you for orgo and MCAT.

Not a good teacher or course. Hamdi told me I was doing fine, and I would earn a B if I continued w how I was doing. I did, but nope. She gave me a C+. Do not believe her, she does curve. I feel so misled.

Just not an engaging or inspirational instructor. It seems like she does not care if we learn or accomplish anything. The course content was on the easy side, and it was easy to get an A even if you did not learn anything.

Hamdi is very passionate about what she teaches and her lectures. However, it feels like her teaching doesn't prepare me for exams and the weekly quizzes. She sometimes struggles to explain things or drones off when the entire class is lost. The main issue is the department itself seeks a lot more out of students than what Hamdi teaches.

Dr. Hamdi was nice & the course seemed organized. The material was not difficult, but Hamdi struggled to explain things. Tests were all over the place, some problems were right from hw, many did not make sense, and others even Hamdi could not explain. If you have to take 105, take Dr. Luo. She is serious, but at least she knows the material.

Mixed bag. Grading structure makes it a hard class. Extremely smart dude, doesn't make you memorize small things but instead focuses on concepts. Teaching style makes the material fascinating, but definitely stress-inducing with cold-calling, swearing, and of course the daily quizzes. If you're interested in neuroscience, highly recommend.

Very engaging and enthusiastic lecturer, and mini quiz setup and discussions were effective for distributing the learning. That said, he prioritized anti-cheating over learning. Would not post lecture notes, so if you had to miss class then you didn't have access to course material. Also, about half of the quiz questions were simply memorization.
Single-handedly destroyed years of social anxiety therapy by aggressively cold calling and shaming those who try to speak out against it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
My qualms:
- strict attendance policy for the Friday discussion sections, even if you have a university-sponsored event-- they don't make exceptions.
-  Passionate but rambles & drawings and explanations of topics are not very clear.
- Your grade is 70-% daily quizzes (out of 5) just getting one wrong already puts you at an 80% which is hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was easier for me than for most. Focus on big concepts, not small details. It even helped me reconnect with my passion for research- mainly due to the class structure, not Keith. He can feel narcissistic and cold-calls often, which makes things tense, but don't let that discourage you; the course itself is genuinely solid.

Keith is an arrogant, egocentric, narcissistic person. Keith publicly humiliates students, lies, and tries to hard to be cool. He talks more about how great a professor he is than actually teaching. Fun fact, he also cheated on his pregnant wife with Dr. Lambo and is now married to her. He doesn't wear shoes or socks in class, which is disgusting.
This dude wild fr.

Frustrating when you do the readings and the quizzes are on details from the beginning of the semester. Class is great if you have prior knowledge/can cram. Too much of class spent making fun of students/cursing/trying to be funny that it is hindering a person's learning at that point. I don't understand the positive ratings on here, honestly.

Keith is a great professor. He is really passionate about lecture material which makes the course super engaging. PNS is one of the best classes I've taken at Washu, and it has made me more excited about Neuroscience.

Keith was an awesome lecturer. His humor makes the class much more enjoyable and the content makes you want to pursue a career in Neuroscience. All information is given to you through lecture and pre-lecture readings, and the Friday subsections really help you learn to read scientific papers.

Very approachable, engaging, gives interesting lectures. People complain about having a quiz every class, but I would much rather study some material constantly than be stressed about a huge exam. Feel like I learned more in this course than any other course at WashU (concepts are applicable to real life) and he gives EC to boost your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Makes me question my motivation for school, interest in neuroscience, and passion for science in general. Is constantly discouraging and arguing with students and always brings an arrogant attitude to class. Would never take this class again.

Genuinely one of the worst profs I've ever had. He is extremely disorganized and condescending. Frequently calls the entire class "mega introverts, nerds, etc". Cold calls then insults/makes fun of students with social anxiety. Overall, a very unwelcoming and discouraging class that makes you want to quit school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your entire grade will be based off of your ability to comprehend textbooks and scientific papers with no help. He gives terrible and unorganized lectures and expects his students to be experts on material he didn't teach them. Get ready to be cold called during lecture, and participate in discussions. Avoid this class at all costs if you are able.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mans is always in a pissy mood and dislikes students in general. Your grade in the class depends solely on your performance on micro-quizzes every single class in person, and ACCURATE participation in discussion sections (inaccurate explanation= -50%). Condescending attitude during lecture, extremely paranoid about cheating.

reviews.comment: ^^what everyone else said

For a professor to dislike students as much as he does, it makes one wonder why he became the professor. He actively discouraged premed students and often used dismissive language when speaking to students.
This guy wakes up every day and thinks to himself how can I ruin a premeds life in the easiest way possible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I have never posted anything to this site because I have never felt a need to talk about a professor this strongly. However, he is the absolute worst professor/teacher/educator that I have had in my entire life. Hes discriminatory and sets students up for failure. He has both tried to expel innocent people in the class for no reason (probably beca
Hard to succeed in a class when the prof wants you to fail and will do anything in his power to ensure you fail. Makes me sad that the school hires and respects people like this
Doesn't like pre meds and accused over 40 students for academic integrity violations. Throws you into assignments with no warning but TA's are helpful. Beware taking this class.

Has a personal vendetta against pre-med students and will say so in class. Aggressively on the lookout for AI violations. Class is hard enough on its own, but it feels like the prof is actively rooting against you.

Prof Henke is really nice. He assigns A LOT of reading. He is available to help but is a bit of a harsh grader and looks very closely at individual sentences. He also doesn't always answer your questions in discussions. Overall, he's a great human being and I learned a lot his class but it was a lot of work.

reviews.comment: Had Prof. Henke for Comp Lit 2107. Very accessible for feedback, lectures were discussion-heavy. Grading gets tougher as the semester progresses.

reviews.comment: I had Professor Henke for Literature and Democracy and it was definitely a very reading-intensive course. Going to office hours helps a lot as he is very patient and gives you a lot of detailed feedback on essays. I highly recommend the course if you like the small seminar vibe rather than having class in a huge lecture hall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Henke was great! I had him for Literature and Democracy; he was incredibly engaging and very kind to his students. It was a lot of reading -- around 9 or 10 books -- but it was mostly manageable. You write around 4 papers throughout the semester and then a larger final. If you go to class ready to engage he will love you.

Be expected to read 4-6 hours outside of class. Prof. assigns around 9 books to buy, and wants you to have the physical copies. Tocqueville, Whitman, and Shakespear focused. The last units that touch on women and Black people's role in democracy got cropped short. Very nit-picky with papers, expand on what he says during class you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Literature and Democracy was deff my favorite class to sit through. So interesting and he is a very good lecturer. However, only take this class if you want to read about 4 hours between each class. The readings are good but there is a TON OF READING. He is a tough grader. But it is manageable.

Henke is okay: I would take him again if I had to. I had him for Literature and Democracy. The main problem I had was communication was varied in speed when it mattered. His critiques on papers are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Henke is by far one of the best and most caring professors I've had at WashU. Don't skip out on the opportunity to take a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Henke is an extremely knowledgeable professor, and he is adept at interpreting the nuances of literature. He also is very accessible and is always happy to chat after class or whenever honestly. Hes not a tough grader and he is always receptive to debate and commentary.
One of the worst teachers in the PAD. Take your Theater Culture classes with a different professor.

Class code not listed, took Addiction Lit. Class is the same every day, mini-presentation into long discussion. Wonderful arbiter, felt like harkness-style learning where we learned from each other, not just them. Some of the most interesting texts I've read for a course. Also incredibly compassionate!

Great professor! They're one of the most passionate and kind people I've ever met. If you aren't used to their grading style, it might seem like harsh grading. It makes sense, I promise! Go meet with them! They give great feedback that makes you understand your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had! Their feedback is incredibly detailed and actually helps you improve as a writer. They care about their students and are always willing to meet during office hours to discuss your work. The class is challenging but fair, and they push you to think critically and explore your ideas.
Extremely nice and passionate. Grades fairly. Participation in class discussions is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Incredibly kind and understanding professor. Amazing in office hours and overall very accessible. The content itself was amazing, though sometimes class discussions were repetitive and a bit dry. Overall, the readings were compelling enough that I was fine with a boring class here and there.

Professor Henderson made college writing surprisingly fun! The readings were fascinating and always sparked great discussions. They're super generous with their time in office hours and we're always able to meet outside of them. Highly recommend!

Professor Henderson is great! Their passion for the subject is clear, and they genuinely care about their students' success. The class can be challenging, but if you put in the effort, you'll learn a lot. They're approachable, fair, and always willing to help if you have questions.

The highlight of Prof. Henderson's course was the content, which was extremely interesting and gave me things to think about long after the course ended. They are also very nice and extremely understanding. However, they are a relatively harsh grader, and class was extremely formulaic which became irritating as the semester went on.
Boring class that they make too difficult. Much harder than other college writing professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Henderson is very kind, caring, and respectful. They care about the students' feedback, foster open discussions, and guide the discussions to make sure important themes are addressed. They pay great attention and encourage the students' interpretations. Literature of Addiction was my favorite class of the semester.

Henderson was not the most engaging professor. Discussions were awkward and did not foster an environment for inclusivity and support. I tried to engage with setting up meetings one-on-one to get additional help, but still felt no connection or much guidance. Grading was always tough--never knew why tho. There are easier CWP's with nicer prof's.

I like how most of the in class and homework assignments are pass/fail, but the essays that are actually graded for credit are graded hard. They have a high standard for essay and its hard to get an A on a paper. Participation and attendance matter, do not miss any classes it will affect your grade. Honestly, try to pick an easy CWP professor.

I would consider myself a good writer. I am typically an A-paper student and have always received high scores in other English/writing classes. However, in Professor Wren's class, I consistently received low B's on my papers. They have a very big list of criteria, and it is pretty unattainable. I would avoid their class if you want a good grade.
Very difficult. Not given nearly enough feedback on the last two (of three) papers. Do not take.

Took literature of addiction which was an impressive course to take on as a teacher. Discussions were sometimes boring and awkward and I wish they had spent more time organizing/structuring the class day.  They are very smart and good at handling tough subjects, we didn't shy away from anything in this class from race to gender to sexuality.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: They assign so much hard reading in few days. Only few people barely get A's even though its a mandatory class. At the beginning of the year they said if you participate once every class your good for the participation grade but they still subjectively gave us a score at the end of the year.

Heather is a hilarious wonderful amazing professor. Just cares SO much about her students. Class is always a little chaotic and all over the place but in the best possible way. Modern Humor Writing was such a joy to have in my schedule and I recommend it to people all the time. If you can take any class with Heather, do it.
Heather is a great professor and really cares about her students. The class was engaging and I feel like I learned a lot about writing through her great feedback.
Heather is awesome. Such a fun, intentional professor. Loved this class and learned a lot!

If you can only take one class at WashU, TAKE MODERN HUMOR WRITING. Heather is incredibly funny and caring and the class is an easy A as long as you do all the work on time. Every single class I felt like I was learning something fun and I was constantly laughing. This class made me feel less stressed every time I was there which is so rare.

Heather was fantastic, probably one of the nicest professors I've ever had. Her class is very engaging and she teaches very well. You WILL improve your writing ability in her class. There are weekly reading/writing assignments, but nothing overly long and they're generally interesting. She's also really personable and funny!

Heather is wonderful and the classes are a joy to attend. She's an incredibly engaged, thoughtful and funny professor who genuinely cares about her students. We were assigned either 1 short essay or a reading/response assignment a week, which weren't too bad for me even as an engineer. I'd take Humor Writing again in an instant.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Heather as a teacher, because she actually gave me comments on my stories that helped improve not just the piece but my writing in general. Is a very genuine person who is also concerned for students outside the classroom. Always willing to meet and discuss things with you. Bonus: she's also really funny!
Wants you to succeed. Lots of writing, but it's a writing class so what do you expect? The assignments are engaging and the workshops are a great experience. I recommend this class to everyone.

Heather is very helpful in her feedback and gives interesting readings, but gives a TON of writing assignments.  I knew this was a writing class, but did not anticipate how much of a time commitment this class would be.  She usually assigns an essay a week.  Only take if you're willing to write a LOT.

Hirsch is extremely passionate about his course material. However, he can be condescending in class if a student doesn't answer correctly or doesn't properly nuance their answer. There is also a lot of reading that he expects a strong understanding of, and the essays come fast and furious and can have confusing or overly theoretical prompts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Would not recommend taking his classes. He would yell at us in class for things that were plainly his own fault and he shows little empathy for students. Stopped a class halfway to ask a student if they had worn their outfit just for him. Very self absorbed overall.

Participation is very important. You will be put on the spot, and a generic or slightly off-track answer will be pushed back on and challenged. Expect to hear "not quite, anybody else?," and don't take it personally. Hirsch is actually very compassionate, meet with him outside of class and don't mistake his passion about the material for antipathy.

I haven't had the worst experience with Prof Hirsch, but I won't take another class with him. He is knowledgeable, but he doesn't communicate clearly and will frequently contradict his own slides or assigned readings. However, he has offered an extension to our class, and his grading has been fair for me so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't take Hirsch's class if you care about your grade or want to actually enjoy the classes you're taking. He assigns an ungodly amount of reading and expects you to remember every single bit of it. He asks you to participate in class but if you say anything that isn't exactly what he was thinking, he gets snarky. Please don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't normally use this site out of principle but I saw that Prof. Hirsch has a really low score and wanted to try to change that. Hirsch is one of the most knowledgeable, wonderful professors that I have had and I would strongly recommend his courses to anyone interested.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had so far. Doesn't give any extensions, doesn't seem to want to see you succeed, truly unhelpful and a really unnecessarily tough grader for some reason. Just a really awful experience overall:/

prof hirsch rly doesnt seem to respect students' thoughts or their time. you can pass if you do the work, that's not the hard part; his lectures are entirely without any argument/thesis, he's really badly organized, and he has no clear grading criteria. 0/10 i would have learned more by just buying some books and reading them on my own time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Hirsch certainly knows a lot about the subject but assumes immediate understanding of complex historical events from students. Papers were graded very harshly and arbitrarily. Readings also took me nearly 4 hours before each class to read completely. However, the 3 assigned books, rather than usual readings, were incredible and worthwhile.

He is a very knowledgeable professor in his field, but his lectures are very boring. He grades papers unnecessarily harsh, and it is almost impossible to get an A in his upper level courses. It is one of those classes where there is a ton of reading and he actually expects you to do it all. Good guy, but pretty arrogant and not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hirsch is a tough grader, but an excellent teacher. He really cares about the topic, gives good feedback on essays, and is a great guy to talk to outside of class. Don't be upset if you don't get an A in his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Material is difficult, but he tries to make it digestible and simplier. Homework problem sets were a bit tricky, but exams were on the easier end and very fair.

such a solid professor who really cares about his students. homework is hard and the lectures are dense but that's just how the class is unfortunately. he does his best to explain it in a way we can all understand and is extremely accessible outside of class. lots of extra credit opportunities to offset a bad exam grade! love hickman

Econometrics is a daunting and difficult subject, but Hickman is the perfect guy to teach it. He tries to make every class fun, and explains intuition behind everything in simple terms. Homework is tough but exams are very similar to homework/quizzes. Came away from the class actually interested in what i learned, thanks in large part to Hickman.

I love this course. Prof. Hickman is so incredibly gifted at teaching. He makes very intimidating econometrics theory digestible and interesting! However, the take home assignments can be quite lengthy but extra credit is common, and tests are largely based off the readings quizzes. 

Just use the force and all will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The content in this course metaphorically parallels being thrown into the deep end of a pool, but the grading is very fair. Stay on top of the readings and homework and you'll be fine. Although the lectures can be heavy, Krawczynski's passion for astrophysics motivated me to learn more every day. The trip is fun too if you like Physics research.
Professor Krawczynski does a great job explaining really advanced content in easy and understandable ways. He cares about all his students and helps us succeed

Professor is very smart and clearly very passionate about the subject but his style was very frustrating. Final grades felt arbitrary considering participation was 25% of the grade and in a 20 person first year seminar, he only knew maybe 3 student's names at the end of the semester. He also didn't give the final grade breakdown until I asked.
unclear grading criteria

Literally love prof Krawczynski. He's hilariously passionate about physics and an incredibly smart guy. Everything he says is very advanced so it's alright if you don't understand everything but it also makes the content extremely interesting. He explains crazy stuff so sometimes he gets lost in thought while he's talking lol. W professor.

Literally the sweetest and most passionate guy to ever walk this earth, but way too smart to be teaching intro levels. I didn't understand a single thing he said. Super easy class (no exams), but I wouldn't take him as freshman; hold off and when you're an upperclassmen or grad student, I have a feeling he's amazing.

Awful. Lectures were terrible and entirely not engaging, nor did they make sense half the time. He would blatantly ignore students questions or give non answers. Syllabus was unclear, grading criteria were inconsistent and completely unclear as well. Was blatantly rude to students and unwilling to work with them. Take anything else.

Krawczynski is nice, comes up with fun and interesting topics, and enjoys speaking to students. Homework can be tedious but is easy and in-class quizzes were always a breeze. He and the TAs are also always available to help. If you need an NSM credit and are not a math/science person, this class will work out well for you!
A bit boring but easy

I love this man. He is so sweet and cares so so much about what he teaches and is so knowledgeable. He genuinely just wants his students to learn and succeed and gives you every opportunity to do so. He does have mini quizzes you have to answer in class but they are very easy, so you have to show up to get the points. One of my favorite professors.
Easiest class I've taken at WashU and also super interesting. Henric makes it easy for you to succeed in class, while also learning a lot of cool things.
Professor Krawczynski is an awesome lecturer. He's engaging, hilarious, and inspirational. He makes an already interesting subject even more fascinating.

At WashU, you're always supposed to choose classes by the professors, and that was exactly why I enjoyed this class so much. Professor Krawczynski has such enthusiasm for the class that it becomes interesting even if you don't have a background in astronomy or physics.  The assignments and quizzes are also easy!

Professor Krawczynski is such a cute professor who really cares about the material he's teaching as well as the students he's teaching them to. He always tries to find ways to interact with the students, and his lectures are awesome--so is his accent.
I didn't think the class was all that great. I found his accent to be really annoying, and the material was very boring. I just took this class for the NSM cluster, and I'm glad it's over.

Great professor.  He really likes to teach and you can tell that he cares about whether or not you're getting the material.  He also doesn't keep the class going the whole time unless there's enough material to fill the whole time, so it lets out early a lot.
this was the most fun class i took all semester, not to mention its fairly easy and he is the most adorable man alive.
fun teacher.  do the reading and its an A

This class is really easy but requires a decent amount of work.  You have to go to every class because you have homework due each day and you get participation exercise points which count 10% of your grade.  Tests are pretty easy and come exclusively from lecture material.  Learned some really cool stuff as well.

he is the most adorable man in the entire world... he lets you take a piece of 11/8" paper, fill it front and back, and take it to exams.  he blushes a lot and is a very cute, lanky german man.  TAKE HIS CLASSES!
this class is very interesting and prof krawczynski is great to have.  he makes it fun and you can tell he enjoys teaching!
Good guy
No Comments
very interesting and fun class

Very funny professor who isn't above answering people's questions during class (and let me tell you this one guy in our class would drive most professors insane).  He makes class interesting and easy.
Very funny, very clear, great class, great prof.
although has a thick german accent is funny and wants the students to succeed
great course for non-science people!
Great guy. Really nice and has genuine interest in everyone learning. His german accent is thick at times, but i highly recomend his class to anyone

Funny German dude.  His accent is hilarious and understandeable all at the same time.  He's lighthearted and very understand to those who have never had any kind of education in the sciences.  He's good at getting people interested.  Get him if you can.
he explains everything thoroughly and it's very easy to get a good grade. his demonstrations are interesting and his accent is really funny too ;)
No Comments
Very interesting class and easy to understand material.  Professor Krawczynski is enthusiastic and cares a lot about making sure his students understand the material.  Bonus: German accent.

I am a senior and social gerontology was by far my favorite class ever. Lectures were organized in a way that facilitated discussion while moving through the content. Pat made it easy to participate. He sprinkled humor and personal anecdotes into lectures that made them feel more interesting and built rapport with students. Would HIGHLY recommend.
Dr. Hill is an amazing professor. His lectures are very engaging and he has a great sense of humor!

Prof Hill is a great guy! He is very knowledgeable on the subject and you can tell he has a lot of passion for psychology while he is teaching. Be warn, he is a tough grader but it just makes you want to try harder.

I was excited to take Personality Psych but Hill sucked the joy out of it. He doesnt know how to teach and is lucky that Google exists otherwise no one would be crossing a 5 in his exams. His slides seem like they have been made by a toddler who just learnt how to screenshot on their parents' laptop as they are just graphs with 0 explanations

Explains little in class, often reading verbatim off slides, consistently ended lecture 15-20 minutes early, and communicated nothing. Test and problem set phrasing was unclear and misleading.
Requires a ridiculous amount of self-teaching and studying to succeed.

Unless the profs teaching BIO482 change, avoid this class if your major permits.
Lectures for 30-40/50 minutes and tells us to figure out the rest. Better off reading the textbook.

Biochemistry should be an interesting topic covering many materials essential for students' future careers. However, Jackrel and Pakrasi made this interesting class a terrible mess. The lectures are poorly organized. Unclear criteria grade problem sets. Exams contain topics not discussed during the lectures. Pretty annoying.
Prof. Pakrasi was a very interesting professor who knows his subject well.  The class is a lot of memorization with means around 80.

Pakrasi was definitely the most interesting bio professor I've had so far. The lectures were interesting and the material made sense. He assigned a reasonable amount of reading. I certainly wouldn't mind having him again.

the tests are ridiculous.  its as if they can't come up with enough things to ask, so instead there are really dumb questions that are completely irrelevant to biology.  pakrasi is very clear, lectures directly from the textbook, and HATES when cellphones go off.

he's an awesome teacher. the person who called him a liar is a complete idiot. he/she probably got a bad grade and decided to take it out on Pakrasi cuz Pak's the man. doesn't put up with **** and is the first bio teacher to make it interesting.

Didn't we already have half of this stuff in 2960? The lab is a big waste of time too (but all the intro bio labs are).  They should focus the entire semester on physiology, or else find something else to take up the first half of the course, like cell bio.  Of the three intro courses, this was the least interesting in terms of material.
He didn't write very much on the board and I didn't like the fact that the slides he showed weren't available to print out and we had to search for them in the book.
Incredibly condescending and unapproachable.  Horrible classroom manner.  Made me hate the class.
He explains things clearly.  Shuts down people who ask too many questions!! Interesting
Just another WashU science teacher who is a liar.  Why this man teaches, I don't know.  I remember nothing that he taught.

I don't really know why he was teaching the lower-level courses, because he obviously didn't care about them.  Poor blackboard etiquette, poor explanations.  Said material would not be on final; it was.

Prof. Mukai is very nice and accessible if you have any questions, but his lecture is quite boring and basically copying notes. He has a lot of notes and he teaches really fast. I would say this is the hardest class I have taken in college. Even if it says only Math 4111 is required, you should take topology and linear algebra before.

Really surprised to see people give Mukai such great ratings. His lectures are not clear at all and if you're new to differential equations you will need help to understand his textbook. If you don't know Matlab you also have your work cut out for you. Get a tutor and you might be able to work your way through this class
Great teacher! Knows his stuff, and he is a nice guy.
One of the best professors you will ever have! Extremely clear and knowledgable in his field and his text book is amazing!
Keep up with work!

Don't let anyone else teach you Signal and Systems. Mukai is the only one who knows how to do it well. It'll feel like you're not learning anything in this class at first, but by the time the final comes around, everything starts making sense. Daily quizzes so you have to show up to class, but sadly most people leave after this 3 min quiz.
Dr. Mukai is one of the best teachers at Wash U!!!
Dr.Hores is an extremely nice and caring professor. This class is super straightforward and is graded more on completion than on super complex assignments.

Hands down the easiest course I took this semester. Notably, though, Sommerhauser seemed to be having a difficult semester and was quite disorganized—at one point, she even said, “what even is a syllabus anyways?” That said, her exceedingly lenient grading made up for it, and I would definitely take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's truly a fantastic professor. Always helps students in times of need and connects with them outside of the classroom.

Prof. Sommerhauser/Hores is a very kind and knowledgeable person. She seemed a little disorganized and stressed this semester, so it took her a long time to post things or respond to emails. Class was easy for a 4 level and had no exams. It was almost entirely led by student presentations/projects which is kind of weird and not great for learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Hores always brings a lot of silly and fun energy to class. Although occasionally disorganized, she keeps you regularly updated and is clear about expectations. Truly a very caring and engaging professor who is passionate about her class and creates a great classroom environment!

It felt like she didn't know what she was doing sometimes. It was her first time teaching this class. She is obsessed with primates because they're her specialty. Studying all the names, dates, and concepts you need to know is the toughest part; it's quite a bit of material. I learned that I don't fare as well with boring lectures and MCQ tests.
Very funny and personable, just pay attention to lectures and you'll do fine.
Incredibly boring. Reads off the slides. Takes forever to speak. Always says "you know". Avoid classes with her at all costs

Her love for primatology is somewhat permeating. Her love for the material kinda makes you want to learn about them yourself. If you treat the class as one large connected story tracing the evolution of humans, it'll be easier.

I really liked this class and Dr. Hores. The content was interesting and I think Hores did a great job showing her passion for it. There is a lot of memorization though, and the slides can be very disorganized, with ideas sort of mismatched together.

While Rose is a great professor there is little motivating you to attend lectures. Lectures are heavily slides based and the slides are posted. There are only 3 MC exams the entire semester . Tons of memorization (species names, dates etc.) some MC questions can be extremely specific. If memorization isn't your jam prepare for a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded on three exams. Exams are relatively easy, just need to memorize. There is a textbook, but you aren't required to read it. Posts lecture notes so that you can review them after class. Knows and cares about what she's teaching, lecture can get a little dull sometimes though. Gave everyone a 100% on the exam once due to a grading error.

I really enjoyed taking Evolution of the Human Diet with Dr. Hores. She is a great lecturer and seems to be really passionate about what she is teaching. The class seemed a little bit disorganized at times but if deadlines were changed it was always clear so I really did not mind it that much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very dry lecture style -- Hirst tends to drone on and I noticed most students weren't paying attention during the lectures. Over the course of the semester less and less students came to class. Nice guy, though, and pretty accessible outside of class. Posts all the presentations online.
Great in upper-level classes when you have a basic idea of the subject. He has high expectations, but he is available outside of class and genuinely cares about his students.
Super smart dude. Lectures are advanced but interesting. Gives great feedback and really wants to help students. Not an  easy class though.
Really smart, lectures are really interesting. Pay attention. Go see him after class, willing to help with anything. Very invested in students' success.
A very knowledge professor who does not teach the thing you could easily find online or in the textbooks. But also demanding.

Tremendous professor- didn't have him for a big lecture class, which seems to have made a big difference. Very engaging, very intelligent. Expects you to have not only read the texts but to have thought about them and come up with some analysis. LOTS of reading, but worth it.
Great professor. Extremely knowledgeable and willing to help. Recommend Western Civ. Seems to know EVERYTHING.
My favorite professor ever. I will take class with him as many times as possible because D. Hirst is the man!
Very good professor. Lectures can be difficult to comprehend sometimes, but very smart and knows everything about his subject. Very willing to help
Very interesting and helpful. Dry lecture style, but lectures are very informative and contain all the answers for the essay exams.

Very Boring teacher. Do not take West Civ 1 with him. Rambles on stage and does not explain his outlines or the readings. Its basically pointless to go to class because no one knows what he is saying.
Probably the most boring professor I have ever had. Just stands and talks, not interesting at all. Does not prepare you for the exams or papers at all. Do not take his class if you do not have to.
Professor Hist is the man. His daughter Lilly is smokin.  The class sucks, but Jenny Westrick was a great Ta.
such a history professor. really easy but also extremely boring. do not go to class, only subsection. and you will do very well
Loved the class.  A little dull at times, but I learned a lot from him.
A little boring sometimes but very enthusiastic and extremely willing to help students
mind numbingly boring
Delightfully enthusiastic
so boring...
