No Comments
No Comments

- Reads directly off of slides and shows little understanding of the material. 
- Many homework topics are not discussed in the lecture. I had to teach myself many concepts to do the homework.
- Shows no empathy or flexibility for students.
She is not educated on the topics, reads directly off of slides, content is boring and she gets very moody. Not a joy to be around, overall an easy class but man I hated every second

No explanation on every term we learn. Boring lecture with a reading machine. Full of words in her lecture note, but she wants us to make a "research speech" with less than 10 words in each PowerPoint.

This professor is a joke. She taught class by reading her ppt. No explanation. She just read it. 
The test in this course has no relationship with your hw and class questions. Prepared for the test by reviewing HW and in-class question is useless.

Housni is a great professor who is super caring and adaptive. We all came into the class with different levels of knowledge and experience in Arabic, and he fully altered the class to cater to our needs. In-class activities are super helpful and useful for everyday Arabic speaking. Overall, amazing guy who made Arabic enjoyable to learn.
Definitely a reasonable and invested Arabic teacher. The effort you put in the class is reflective of what you get out of it.

Bennis is a very good professor. He uses a flipped classroom model which I think is the right way to approach a language like arabic. He gives great feedback. Some might say that he is very difficult but I think that just comes with the fact that arabic is a hard language. But, he does his best to make it as easy as possible.

I like Housni, he cares about each student in his class. I enjoyed him as a teacher in 107 and 108, but there were some things I wish were different. Sometimes he wasn't super clear when grading. He could have made the class more engaging, sometimes we spent the whole class quizzing each other on vocab. Importantly, we didn't finish the textbook.

Housni is a kind, genuinely passionate professor who cares about students and their success. This class is full of beginners, people willing to learn, and it created one of the best learning experiences I've had yet. If you have even a slight interest in Arabic, pursue it (with Housni if you can he's the best of the best). It's not hard, I promise!

Professor Bennis is an amazing teacher. Arabic is a really difficult language, and to learn online especially. However, he did a wonderful job with both managing the virtual format and keeping the class engaged and enthusiastic. He knows the Al Kitaab series really well. A fair but challenging grader, he is always clear about what can be improved.
Not a great teacher, and expects a lot of students. Tests are very hard, and very repetitive class with just memorizing vocab and grammar over and over again. Wouldn't take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Bennis is an excellent teacher, providing a solid foundational understanding of Arabic. Students' skills will grow a lot in the course because of the extensive conversational practice each day in class, relevant homework exercises, and journal assignments.
No idea how to teach, really harsh and thinks people should know the vocab within an hour. Very condescending and expects a lot even with his terrible teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed taking arabic with him! A really funny guy and is actually very helpful if you reach out.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: expects too much of his students. nice guy outside of the classroom, but isn't very helpful in general. if you plan on taking arabic with him, good luck. his tests are hard and he mostly speaks arabic in class so it is very hard to keep up. lots of homework and tests but it is useful in the end. nice guy, mediocre class.

Very helpful. Wants students to succeed. Class is laid back and a lot of fun. Tests are tough, and for most of the semester you will not know what your overall grade looks like, but he builds in an invisible curve at the end of the semester. Put in the effort and you will do well.

This year has been a monster in Arabic, especially given that we covered 18 chapters this year (not 12 like previous years). It is definitely a big commitment, and the exams leave many students hurting, but there is likely an invisible curve at the end of the semester. Is very available for help .
Great understanding of the language. Could be a bit more clear at times. Plus his class is pretty laid-back and fun
I liked him a lot, but a lot of people thought he was condescending. I'm learning a lot and can't wait to class with him next semester
He's amazing. He makes learning the language so much fun, no joke. plus he's kind of funny, in a wierd way.

He's a great teacher but a bit condescending if you ask stupid questions. Not as laid back as tarbouni but a lot more organized. You will definitely work harder in his class versus tarbouni's but you will probably learn the language better.
He doesn't explain things well and doesn't stick to the syllabus or return graded work promptly and is really busy.
He's a great guy.  If you have the option, take arabic with him!
great teacher!
This is the first semester i've had Housni.  He's more easy-going that Hanaa, but i like the way they both teach.
He's AMAZING!!!!!Take him, not Hannah Kilany!
Awesome teacher, but Arabic is not easy.

He forced us to prepare three different 5-minute presentations for three cases before the guest lecture day. And the requirement was announced just one day before. Each case has at least seven questions and requirements, including design tables and plans. During his class, he often got stuck on his logic. That is ridiculous.

AVOID HIM AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE!!!!!This is the worst professor I have ever met! He always stucked during the class because he does not know what is he talking about. Also he put too much work load to the student. Even for a guest speaker lecture, he will post out three case studies for preparation and require us to write answers as a homework.
He does not know what he is doing. Excessively controlling, if he want to do so, maybe do it in some early education programs not graduate degree.
He almost reads off the slides with a heavy accent. Not a very intelligent guy but is unusually condescending.
No more pro like this plz. Learned nothing of design

Dr. Yin has a lot of technical knowledge but his design knowledge is nearly zero. I learned nothing in his studio course and he also taught nothing. If he will continuously teach studio, especially comprehensive studio, in the future, WUSTL will never turn back the top rank which it occupied many years ago.
If this Pro does not leave, Washington University will never turn over.

Very kind and forgiving, only 3 essays all semester which was nice, but you don't get feedback on any of them until the end which makes writing the second 2 a little more difficult. Readings were pretty long and necessary for discussion, but interesting enough. Hou is pretty disorganized but it makes the class more chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Hou is kind and clearly cares a lot about the field and her students. However, I think she's a little overworked, between all the classes she teaches and being a mother of three little kids. As a result classes were often cancelled or sometimes we were just shown a video we could have watched at home.

Professor Hou as a person is very kind, understanding and passionate about the field of sociology and social justice. However, her lecturing style mostly consists of her rambling; her explanations are very unclear at times. The book helps explain a lot of concepts. She also tends to cancel class abruptly and takes a long time to grade assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One day I just crossed out half the notes because she decided it wasn't worth telling us in advance the material wouldn't be tested in any way whatsoever. Wastes class time with random activities and then gives you an exam that you can cookie cutter prewrite so it becomes a typing speed contest.
Good flow

She's always available to help you, tries to make an uninteresting subject interesting (CivPro will always suck, she cant change that). Great teacher, cool person, really accessible. You are lucky to have her.

An extremely kind person. Makes you feel like you're in kindergarten but it's kind of nice. It's easy to get a pretty good grade in her class--the exam is pure regurgitation--but it's hard to get a really good grade, probably because she keeps everyone close to the mean so she doesn't have to give too many really bad grades. Also, she's a cutie.
No Comments
Not sure what's with the dislikes on the last two. Had him for the same class. Chill guy, not too much work

I had Ian for a first year seminar, linguistic approaches to comparative mythology, and he was an excellent professor. Super knowledgeable, funny, and passionate. Homework was consistent but not too much and always relevant. I feel like I learned a lot.

Great person with a dry sense of humor. Homework/grading is pretty easy which lets you just enjoy the class. Lectures are interesting; he's clearly a very knowledgeable linguist and you're always learning new things to think about. Fantastic guy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Computational Linguistics is an awesome class. The material was very difficult at times, but the grading was really lenient, which allowed me to actually learn a lot more, rather than overly focusing on grades. This was a field I didn't know much about and am now really into. Highly recommend.

His lectures are interesting, and doing the reading is important to stay on top of everything. He gives quizzes about every two weeks, and they test understanding and ability to apply information (only a little memorization). The prof. is great, and the class is fascinating. I would highly recommend taking the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You have to go to class and pay attention. You have to do the reading. The night before a quiz you should do the practice exercises. That's the whole class structure. I absolutely loved it. Fascinating subject and Ian was a great professor. Moves pretty quickly, but I learned a ton. Highly recommend. Doesn't require a ton of time outside of class.

Dr. Hollenbaugh was an amazing professor. The tests required work but tested understanding, not memorization and the class was informal in a good way (though it would have been nice to have some more partner work). Make sure to do all the readings and practice questions as early as you can though as the class covers a LOT and moves quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Make sure you do the readings and recommended exercises fo reach chapter before quizzes. If you do these consistently, should be fine. Good prof, interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice, talkative, and welcoming. You will learn a lot and she enjoys teaching content outside of the textbook. The only issue I have is her grading can be very critical of little things, but you will earn a good grade if you try. Overall very good teacher and she wants you to learn. Only 2-3 hours of homework per week. Great professor.
She's the best!!!! I love her energy so much.

Chen Laoshi is a great professor. She cares about her students and genuinely wants them to learn as much Chinese as possible. She changed the pace of our course after she found that we were struggling so that we could focus on learning instead of just getting through lessons. She's a tough grader, but her grading is fair. Great energy in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Chen Laoshi is an amazing professor, I would definitely take her class again. I really enjoy her classes, and although the material is sometimes hard, it is always rewarding
Ta shi yi ge hen hao de lao shi. shi fen piao liang! Wo ai Chen lao shi!!

I took heritage Chinese and she was so funny. The class was pretty intense esp because you only meet three times a week instead of the usual 5 for language classes. Preparing for tingxie quizzes and doing the homework definitely took a long time but class itself was a good time
she's amazing!

Chen Laoshi is great.  She is so funny and loves to laugh.  She makes the class a lot of fun.  She is very picky with character strokes, and is probably the harder of Chinese teachers.  But, she makes class fun and is a great teacher - you will learn a ton and enjoy class.  Highly recommend.
She's AMAZING! She's utterly hilarious and is super helpful when you ask for it.  She may be the hardest grader but as long as you pay attention and do your work you'll be fine- mei you wenti!!
Fun and nice, but definitely the hardest of the Chinese Teachers

absolutely love diaz as a person. super chill and genuinely seems caring. however, the class is an absolute joke. definitely the easiest class i have taken in my life, to the point where it felt like a waste of time. the class was so superficial that i feel like i didnt really learn anything. beware if you are actually interested in diffeq

Professor Diaz is one of the best professors in WashU math department. He gives clear lectures and cares his students. The practice exams are helpful as they are just mirrors of the real exams, so an A is super easy in his class. I feel this course (differential equations) is really helpful for my career development as it's useful in engineering.
Loved professor Diaz

From what I've heard about other Differential Equations teachers, Diaz is definitely the way to go. You can ace all the exams except the final (the final was very difficult). However, since the final counts for 30% of your grade and is MC with 5pt questions, you NEED to work hard for it and be perfect. Practice exams tell you what you need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty chill. Content is hard, but he will tell you exactly what you need to know. The practice tests will be exactly the same as the real test, but with the numbers changed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Humberto's DiffEq class is an ideal class. He tells you exactly what you need to know, and makes hard concepts easy. Do the practice exams. Humberto Diaz is a professional mathematics teacher; not only will you learn Differential Equations, you will feel better about your math skills. Very accessible. TAKE HIM FOR DIFF EQ!!!!!

Diaz is a clear lecturer, teaches concepts well and outlines what you need to know. He devotes lectures before midterms to test review. Extremely easy tests; If you knew how to do the practice test, you were set as the real deal is essentially a carbon copy. Crowdmark homeworks were challenging and sometimes unrelated to lecture topics, however.
Gives clear lectures. There could be fewer homework problems, though.

A lot discussion in class, participation does matter. She's very generous and willing to help, as long as u have a good excuse, it's possible to extend your deadline a little bit. The only thing is that she might not grade the assignments very on time, most of them are graded at the end of the semester.

Great professor overall. As long as you participate in class discussions and put some decent thought and effort into your papers, you'll be just fine. She offers help outside of class and is lenient with deadlines. Very understanding and offers solid feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
HONESTLY THE WORST PROFESSOR EVER EVER TRUST ME DO NOT NOT TAKE HER COURSE 
- TAKES 4EVER TO GRADE PAPERS AND NEVER RESPONDS TO EMAILS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I got B's and C's on some assignments, but she always reached out to me first to offer help. She did this with every student, which is super caring of her. She's very passionate abt the topics we read, and she's rlly leninent w/ deadlines. She only took 2-3 weeks to hand stuff back, similarly to other Eng profs. Super sweet and you'll get an A.
JUST RUNNNNNNNNN AS FAST AS YOU COULD

After turning in an essay, prepare to wait months to receive feedback. I genuinely believe she does not read my essays, as she always states I do not use any quotes when I purposely ensure to use a quote in every paragraph. She is a very nice person, but I do not recommend her as a professor.
AVOID HER AVOID HER AVOID HER

While Dr. Hu is not the best at grading she is one of the most caring professors ever. She did not make the class the huge deal that some of the other college writing professors did. She was very open to letting us make writing identity our own based on our identities. She is also very understanding of heavy work loads and will extend deadlines.

the worst professor at this institution. AVOID her at all costs and you won't regret it. she is so unqualified.she doesn't even grade anything and gives you a random grade (she likely rolls a 6-sided letter dice down the stairs) with absolutely no feedback. if there is feedback, it doesn't make sense. I wouldn't wish one semester of her for anyone

Dr. Hu is such a nice person that it almost hurts to leave her a bad review. She is extremely slow at grading; you are guaranteed to receive feedback on writing well after that feedback is useful. Additionally, I didn't receive a single comment (not one) on the 9 page research paper that served as the final paper for the class when she graded it.

Nice prof but so unprepared. Doesn't respond to emails. Never grades on time; crams grading (prob doesn't even read what u wrote). Extremely harsh grader- will take points off for random reasons. Expects a lot from her students while not attempting to help them. Trust me, do not take this class - it will ruin your gpa + confidence as a writer
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Hu is an amazing professor who really cares about her students. She makes everyone feel welcomed and greatly improved my writing. She often extends deadlines and makes expectations clear. I went in knowing I was not the best writer, however she built my confidence and made college writing a good experience even when  I dreaded taking the class.

Rita is kind to her students and flexible with extending paper deadlines. But, if you don't write the way she wants or argue something she agrees with, she will grade you down. She also rarely gives full credit for assignments. If you don't already know how to write, don't take her class because I think it's harder than real English major courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not a very harsh grader in my opinion. Class is pretty boring--half the class is usually spent talking about deadlines, the other half either talking about a reading no one did or a lesson she borrowed from someone else. Boring is worth it for a (relatively) easy A though. Sometimes deadlines are a little short, but she's flexible with them.

She is a great professor who is good at inspiring students when they are hesitated about their essays, and always willing to answer our questions after class, though sometimes giving scores and feedback a bit late.

Professor Hu is very kind and cares about her students. She will give an extension if needed and I always enjoyed the class discussions. My one criticism would be that she didn't grade or provide feedback to a major essays till after we finished the class.

Professor Hu is literally the worst professor ever. She is ALWAYS unprepared. she does not give clear instructions and on top of that reuses essay prompts from pasts essays and so nothing makes sense. she sets insensible due dates. overall horrible experience, do not take any course with her.

Quite literally the worst professor I've ever had. Blatantly unprofessional and unqualified, yet she works in the law school? Showed up to class 5-12 minutes late everyday, always unprepared. Only offered 2 office hour morning sessions during other classtimes. Didn't provide any useful or clear feedback, "???"s were common. Constantly made excuses.

This professor, Rita Hu, is genuinely HORRENDOUS. I wouldn't wish taking this professor upon my worst enemy. The essay instructions are incredibly vague which allows her to take off points for absolute bogus reasons when grading. Avoid this unqualified professor at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very harsh on content of paper, extremely liberal in viewpoint and grades clearly based on that. the identity part of the course only means she talks about race and gender almost exclusively, and almost never mentions religion or age or any other part of a persons identity.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I thought WashU's stupid college writing program was meant to help you *become* a good writer. Guess not in this class, though. She basically gives hardly intelligible, vague, and complex assignments, doesn't explain or teach us anything, and then gives everyone a B. You are expected to be a perfect writer on day 1. Avoid her at all costs, please.

She is an extremely hard grader, you will never receive 100 on any assignment. She is extremely condescending when giving feedback and honestly does not help much. Her office hours fill up fast so getting help outside of the class is tough. This class lowered my confidence in writing and I would not take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She gives us these meta and difficult prompts but does not explain or help in any regard, and then on top of that grades really harshly. The class discussions are her talking for an hour and her being super unclear about what a good thesis is. Dont take her college writing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her grading is harsh even though she never explains the prompt clearly. Never really teaches how to write but expects us to be writing experts at an entry, basic mandatory college writing class. The average is low, and without a curve, this will be one of the harshest, toughest college writing classes on the entire CWP roster. DO NOT TAKE HER.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is exhaustive. Definitely one of the most difficult college writing classes. Skip her if you have her for CWP because I am drowning in constant essays (smth that other classes don't do) long readings. It's really difficult pushing out long essays weekly without much feedback and clear directions. Interesting reads but no time to enjoy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm only halfway through the semester with this horrible professor but I want to scream everytime I'm in class. She sets us up to fail--never explains the assignments clearly and then complains that all of us are terrible writers and gives all Bs. Literally makes us hate on other students' assignments, which is extremely awkward. Don't take her!!!

Huo is a mixed bag. His lectures were confusing and straight out of the book. I would strongly recommend reading the textbook before coming to lecture so you won't be as confused. His tests were very difficult (and tedious as far as the algebra went) and the average was about 70, but he curved to an 85, so it wasn't that hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He doesn't teach well. Straight from the textbook. Difficult to follow and understand. Unclear grading criteria. More than once, he switched a policy midway through the semester making things harder for students (changing test format and removing allowed materials).
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very hard exams that focus a lot on conceptual content (so you have to really actually understand the material - not just plug and chug) and lectures derived directly from the book (so class attendance is at maybe a 40% at best). HOWEVER, seems like an extremely nice guy who wants everyone to do well and so far VERY generous with the curve.

Do NOT take matrix with Huo. You're better off waiting to take it w/ Shapiro. Our "practice exams" are Shapiro's old exams but then Huo makes his tests more difficult/conceptual & no notecards. I keep acing the practice exams and failing the real exams, which makes me think I'd be acing matrix with Shapiro instead of being in the C+/B- range w Huo.

Not a great professor. Accent can be hard to understand at time. His lectures are way too abstract/theoretical and delve into proofs more than we need to pass the exams. Does not do enough example problems. I learned infinitely more from WebWork, Crowdmark, and other online tools than I did from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The lectures are just so boring. Its hard to pay attention to so you often find yourself just skipping class because you wont get anything out of it

He's perfectly competent but lectures are dense & a bit boring. I felt confident in my math skills going into Exam 1 but did poorly because the test focused a lot on concepts/rules. Engineering students tend to prefer doing actual math/problem-solving questions rather than just memorizing "rules" and ideas. I'd recommend taking with another prof.

While Professor Huo was at times not the best lecturer, he really cares about his students and was always extremely helpful in office hours. He was always ready and willing to clear things up outside of class and was great 1-on-1. The HW was manageable and the tests were written in such a way that I always felt prepared. 10/10 would recommend.

I think he really cared about teaching and took it very seriously, and this showed. I enjoyed the class, and thought he took it at a nice pace. He carefully explained everything and followed the textbook enough so that you could read it over later to get an idea of something you missed. HW was also very fair and manageable.

I took Repps in 2008 as one of my first courses toward my post-Associates Bachelor's degree. It is now 2017 and I STILL think about how horrible of a human being he was toward me in a class a decade ago. I complained then, and WashU did nothing. I graduated from WashU, but warn any student there - BAD (non-doctorate) prof, he should be fired.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: IA 5622 with Professor Hudson was an engaging and informative dialogue style course on the Arab Spring and Arab Winter. What I invested in learning about the region has been instrumental in developing my foreign relations outreach and policy formation.

Attendance is crucial. If your one of those who like to skip every other class or go as you please then you will fail his course. It's discussion based which means YOU NEED TO BE THERE! Quizzes are simplistic and papers are general and simplistic as well. He's leans towards the liberal side of things but does offer opposing argument.
Very serious about not being late to class. Very easy class with weekly quizzes as long as you show up and do the required papers and debates you can get an A.

I wish I'd read these reviews before enrolling in any of Hudson's classes. I would have known what to expect from him. Yes, there are some know-nothing students who appreciate the fact that he teaches absolutely nothing, but this outrageously unfair to the rest of us who pay good money to "learn" something from the IA program. Do avoid this creep.

I took Repps class against the advise of all the negative reports on this site & I'm so glad I did!! It turns out, lots of students enjoy his classes & go back to take more of his classes (including myself). His style of teaching is discussion-based rather than lectures. I found him to be quite helpful both in & outside of the course work...

How is that this ignoramus continues giving classes at Wash U? He is the most bias,mean and biggest bully I've ever met.  Why is that nobody complaint with the school about him, is beyond comprenhension. His knowledge and experience about the subjects he teaches is abismal. He just gives a bad reputation to an otherwise outstanding University.

He's a nice guy. If he likes you, the class will be fun, but he is almost hurtful if he doesn't. Too strict on attendance and doesn't trust students. He can give opportunities to those he does like. Not a good addition to WashU. I wouldn't take him, just on the off chance he doesn't like you.

This was the absolute worst class I ever took at WashU.  I thought I would learn something about NGOs. What I got instead was a series of unstructured and discussions that were so disorganized, we barely referenced any of the numerous and expensive books he made us buy. You can find better ways to waste your money than this, so avoid it if you can!

For a guy who doesn't seem to know much about teaching, but still offers courses on topics he has no qualifications for, Repps has quite a racket going at UCollege. If you play along & pretend he's an awesome teacher you'll get an A; if you challenge his limited knowledge, your grade will suffer. Also, the "textbooks" this ignoramus uses are a joke

Avoid this professor at all cost. He likes to discriminate and is abusive. He grades very unfairly. He will not take into consideration other course work you have done. He should not be teaching. Does not prepare his classes. A disgrace for Wash U

This course was Israeli-Arab Conflict. This course was mediocre. He teaches history and not really current affairs or international relations. He is not updated I doubt I will take another course with him. He likes to bully smart students. I think he has a complex of inferiority. The quality of the course is really bad
I wouldn't take another course at all with him if you what I mean
Shouldn't be teaching. Almost never prepared. Very easily discriminated against women and anyone with a conflicting opinion.

Good professor, all the readings I did actually improved my understanding of the class. Made sure we basically knew what to expect from the exams. Attendance is graded together with homework submissions (completion grade) out of I think 20% of the grade.

Professor Kang is amazing. He is so approachable and is super accessible outside of class. He truly cares about his students and tries to get to know them one-on-one. Lots of readings, but they're easy, no pop quizzes. Essays are take home. Is super understanding, and offers tons of extra credit and ways to makeup attendance. Totally recommend!

Easy MCQs and some essay Qs
Just go to class and you'll do fine.

Really outstanding lecturer & professor. Made the class super engaging and interesting. Kang cares about his students and I really learned a lot. There is a decent amount of reading + weekly homework but definitely manageable. There were 3 midterms, not exactly sure what the formatting is because it changed throughout the semester.

I took Drawing1 with Dennis last semester. He was pretty chill and the atmosphere was relaxed. The class focuses a lot on figure drawing and he really likes to see improvement (that is mainly what your grade is based upon). I wouldn't say that Dennis is an easy grader, but he's pretty fair. However, I must admit that I don't feel I learned a ton.

I actually had Dennis for both drawing 1 and 2. He is a super chill person and gives really nice feedback both academically and just random stuff. Although the class does get a little boring with the amount of figure drawing we did, the way he approaches figure drawing really helped and definitely made me a lot more comfortable with it.

Dennis is fairly straight forward in his drawing 1 class. A lot of figure drawing, can get fairly repetitive. It's hard to tell whether or not you are doing well in his class as he does not give you any grades. He doesn't assign too much outside work, mostly projects for the weekends that are usually still lifes. Overall, a pretty neutral class.
I loved Dennis! He was always very understanding and helpful. Critiques were always insightful.

Dennis is a very nice person! However the class is a bit boring as we did figures for WHOLE semester!!! But you can always have fun by yourselves like do some creative things with figure drawing you are doing, explore more.

DRAWING: Dennis focuses a ton on figure drawing (every other day with a model). He prefers to give little to no feedback during class, so if you're confident in your drawing abilities it's a relaxing atmosphere that's more about personal exploration, but if you're new to drawing you'll probably struggle to improve. He's empathetic and easy-going.
Great teacher. Very involved in helping students grow in their own strengths. Class is always fun and interesting. Had figure drawing one class per week for nearly the entire semester.
Great! My drawing ability improved significantly with Hyland. However, it helps if you have previous drawing experience. Most inexperienced students will get a get a B-.

The best teacher I have ever had. His class was definitely challenging but I learned so much from him. He is  incredibly supportive and you can tell that he wants his students to do well. He was very understanding when I did not turn in an assignment on time and did not give me a hard time about it at all. This guy is AMAZING.

Prof Macmullen has amazing passion and insight with what he teaches, however, quizzes (daily) and tests are very complicated and based on very complex philosophical readings. Seemed more suitable towards political science. Intense grading system. Class section is awesome; you learn a lot and have TA's who are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: MacMullen is a great lecturer, but has transformed a political philosophy class, which he has clearly taught at a different institution, into a weak way of evaluating the ethics and values of public policy (PUBPOL302). Class is bizarrely weighed on your ability to break down complex philosophy BEFORE you attend lectures. Little to grapple with.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Macmullen has a gift for simplifying complicated & dense political theory and poses questions in class that are interesting and fun to grapple with. Thoroughly enjoyed his lectures. The readings can be long/difficult, but he is ready to help as long as you ask. The quizzes are manageable if you do the readings carefully. Loved this class.

His approach is bizarre in that there are no papers or discussion sections--only daily quizzes. Political theory is meant to be engaged with, grappled with, questioned, etc. I saw some strong political minds do poorly because they couldn't recite facts easily, only provide keen insights--yet insights had zero value (no participation score).

Professor MacMullen is an exceptional lecturer. He is clear and funny, and actively seeks student interaction. The readings are rather dense and can take a while to understand, but are crucial to passing the class due to the daily quizzes that make up most of the semester grade.

Intro to Pol. Theory was my favorite class this semester. The texts assigned were dense, complicated, and heavily philosophical, yet absorbing and intellectually satisfying. Macmullen does a fantastic job explaining abstract concepts through practical and often hilarious examples. Would recommend for those seeking a challenging and rewarding class.

I took Intro to Poly Theory on a whim, and it turned out to be my favorite class this semester. Readings are certainly difficult, but his lectures are extremely thought provoking. MacMullen himself is very clear and extremely intelligent, with a very incisive way of examining common suppositions.

Ian MacMullen is an amazing lecturer--he takes complicated concepts and makes them accessable to an intro class. He also has dinner in bd once a week with students for casual discussion and is positively enthused to talk to them outside of class. That said, you will have to read and work hard for your grade. It is much tougher than most intros.

I'm Majoring PoliSci but really disliked this class.  His lectures are extremely boring and self-centered and seems to have gotten lazy.  It is very difficult to gauge how well you understand the readings before the quizzes and can think you know it amazingly and do horribly on the quiz.  Is interesting material but wouldn't recommend taking it.

Professor MacMullen was definitely cool at first, but upon realizing that this class was legitimately a philosophy-type class graded entirely through answers from vague daily quizzes and multiple-choice only exams, he becomes significantly less awesome. He is a decent lecturer, but he teaches from a single slide and doesn't post anything online.

I took his intro class to see if I liked poli sci, and his class convinced me that it's what I want to do. The readings are super challenging and somewhat time consuming, but I've gotten so much out of them. He's an enthusiastic lecturer and a great teacher.

So far, my favorite professor at Wash U no question.  Makes really dense material very understandable. Not sure 106 should be an intro class but take it anyway. Taking his history of political thought class next semester for sure.

I looooove him!One of my favorite professors at WashU. Very intelligent and nice (with a British accent). The class is very difficult, especially the readings assigned. But if you spend time on it, you will love it.
Best professor I've had.  Lectures are interesting (if you've done the reading),  attendance isn't mandatory, but makes the class considerably more cohesive.  Take all his classes.

Polical theory: Brilliant, interesting, and motivating professor who absolutely knows what he is talking about.  Broke down very dense and inaccessible texts to make them not only clear but also thought provoking. Great class, awesome teacher.
Complex theory is made accessible by fantastic professor.

He's a great lecturer: he takes very complex political theory and makes it understandable. Go to his office hours for the papers, he'll help you alot. This class is more philosophy than political theory but it was fun anyway.

Dean MacMullen is very British AND has a lisp.  Makes long lectures about Hobbes and Rousseau much easier to listen to.  He is a really good professor.  Very methodical, very clear, makes tough material very easy to understand.  You can learn a lot from him.

Dr. Ifri is a fantastic human being. His class is interesting, but it is very important to 1.) read the readings and 2.) pay attention (his french is rather quick and sometimes he mumbles). Tests were short essay questions, so it is important to know your stuff. Overall, cool class, though.

He's a really nice guy, unfortunately I think he's stuck in that "I've been teaching this same thing for 30+ years" phase and is so very boring. He needs to incorporate technology and get his students excited...or at least interested, in what he's saying.
Knows a lot, interesting classes yet a bit all over...I enjoyed his classes though.
Il un homme veritablement généreux et honnête, j'ai beacoup aimé ses classes...prenez un cours avec lui, vous allez certainement apprendre quelques choses et s'amuser
A very passionate teacher who has a vast knowledge about France in general. I really enjoyed the class and his teaching style, though he does tend to speak rather quickly in French.
Prof. Ifri is a genuinely nice guy.  His enthusiasm for the subject matter is evident, but it is easy to get by without keeping up with the reading.

Nothing to get too excited about by this professor.  He's OK, just OK. Definitely NOT the greatest.  It's hard to explain, so talk to someone who's taken him before. Beware, he has a fetish for Proust!

Sheren is a lovely professor, and I found her engaging (unlike other reviews?). For a 200 level art history class, it is a tad rigorous (2 papers, 4 graded readings, hw, midterm w/ 100+ works, required attendance). It was also weird that you had to use readings in the exam. Besides that, lectures are interesting, and she is nice to talk to in OH.

She is so so funny and makes lectures super interesting and fun. Even though participation/attendance wasn't mandatory, I never wanted to miss a class because I often felt inspired by the art she would teach and the art movements she would delve into. Super good at making connections between things and explaining art in funny/meaningful ways.

Such a person may appear disinterested or indifferent towards their responsibilities as an art history professor, and may prioritize their own sense of humor over providing meaningful critique and guidance. This behavior may lead to a lack of respect from students and undermine the credibility of the academic institution. (This is art)

Professor Sheren's Latinx Art class held many many pros than it did cons. While you read a lot, and participation is required, it all adds up beneficially in the end. You have one project/paper all semester, and you do it bit by bit which makes it easier. Profesor Sheren is also just a delight to talk and discuss with. Her passion shows.

She is probably one of my favorite people, let alone professors, at WashU! To be honest, contemporary art is not really my thing, but I still enjoyed class with her immensely. She's also adapted very well to an online format! She was always easy to reach despite being remote and the assignments were really creative and fun. Would highly recommend!

Very caring and supportive. She gives a lot to read and requires you a good command of the readings. But she is very approachable and always willing to help. Her feedback is very detailed and constructive.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One of the Professors I respect the most at WashU. Learned so much in her seminar, and looking back she really taught IMAAD differently/more critically than many profs would. Lots of work and participation is required, grades fairly. Super helpful and accommodating professor and extremely knowledgable!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: My favorite art history prof at WashU. She makes you work to get good grades, but at the same time will work with you if you need accommodations/extensions. Lots of assigned reading that you can get away without doing, although it'll be harder to participate. I learned so much in Ila's class and recommend her if you're serious about art history.
It is a good lecture to fall asleep except the chairs are uncomfortable.
Hate her lectures. She really thinks herself hilarious but actually cold and awkward. She speaks too fast and not to the point and never fails to make you fall asleep.

She's not really a stand-out professor. Her lectures are interesting and she's engaging but she gets annoyed really easily. She has her TA's take phones from students and she's always berating the class to be quiet. Granted, it's not too difficult and you don't really need to read for class. The other teacher (Klein) is more boring but more tame
You will love his introduction to physics. He is the best you can hope for, for an entryway to a more in depth knowledge of the universe.

This was your average intro science lecture course. Dr. Israel would spend all of class going over examples (it was an inverted classroom). Sometimes I wished he would spend a smidge more time explaining concepts but it was fine. He would mess up not infrequently during examples which was frustrating but students caught them mostly.

Dr. Israel was one of the better 197 professors this semester. He worked through a lot of examples and clicker problems throughout the class and I always felt well prepared for the tests. He seemed to be excited about the material and made sure to supply us with plenty of fun in-class demonstrations to keep us interested.

Coming from 117 with Solin, this class will be one of your favorites. All semester you'll be conditioned to expect something bad (again... Solin), but it won't come. Sweet guy. If you ask a question, he'll always be willing to help you. Listen to what he says: use hw problems to prepare for tests. He prepares the tests from the hw. ISRAEL ROCKS!
Really good teacher who keeps class interesting and interactive. He's a nice guy and wants you to succeed.

He is one of the best professors I have had in wash u. He knows what he is talking about and he always maintains a positive environment in class with his jokes and demonstrations. The class is actually fun except the material you learn. But he should get more control of his own class. He lacks charisma but its okay.
fun course, interesting and well-taught
nice guy but not a great teacher.  i learned very little and struggled on hw assignments and tests
No Comments
No Comments

If you don't want to take one of the hardest and worst classes at WashU, then taking orgo during the summer is the way to go. Although it's fast-paced, it's much easier to understand. I mean, would you rather get a 60 on exams during the fall or spring, or a 90 during the summer?

This is the most difficult class you will probably take at WashU. It is worth it, but you will literally need to study every waking moment. Focus on nailing lecture exams as lab grades weigh less. Prof. style is not for everyone and you should attend lecture every day. Getting an A isn't impossible, but it is not a walk in the part. Good luck
I loved Dr. Iha's teaching style for the orgo summer sessions. It was very clear & concise, they answered all of my questions, and the order that we learned things in made sense and was very helpful.

It's an enjoyable experience to take organic chemistry with Dr. Iha in a summer session. Dr. Iha explains the concept very well in video lectures, and there are lots of extra credit opportunities. The only problem is that Dr. Iha is sometimes disorganized, but generally, I would recommend this professor.

Dr. Iha was the worst lecturer I've ever had. The course itself was very easy. Dr. Iha really tried their best to make this course harder. There was not a solid source of information. Online "lecture" videos were just those you can find on Youtube. I did great in both finals and get good grades; I enjoy organic but not Dr. Iha. Dr. K was great tho.

I tried to take Chem 261 over the fall semester and failed baaad. Was nervous to retake over the summer, but now I wish I'd just done this from the get-go! Prof. Iha is an amazing prof., they're kind and pretty funny (although very millennial) and in-person lecture is all about practice so even if you're behind on lecture you still learn so much!

The professor made you feel like a bad student for asking question on the material. I took the second semester of organic chemistry (Chem 262) this spring with a different professor and despite teaching a class 8x larger than this class, I found him much more helpful and in touch with the students.

A class that should be taken in person and not online. Students felt unanswered and unattended to, and the class was mostly self taught. Very little margin for understanding students. students should not be made to feel like they arent trying hard enough if they dont understand material that they had to teach themselves from prerecorded lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Iha is great at explaining things and really cares about her students. Sometimes she can be sarcastic and that might be intimidating, but she doesn't do it to attack you personally it's just her personality (and she's pretty funny). I highly encourage spending time at her office hours any chance you get. It'll be lots of work but worth it!

Outside of the classroom, she's one of the most interesting individuals to know, incredibly artistic and funny. Inside the classroom, I wish she would have been more professional. Her lectures are clear and organized, but her plethora of foul language and scare tactics took away from her performance as an instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is a hard class and if you are not willing to work hard DO NOT SIGN UP. A third of the class usually drops midsemester in 261 and 262 is half the size of 261. Dr. Iha is the best lecturer I have ever had. I got an A 261 and A+ 262, so its possible to do well but I worked 9am-midnight every day so be prepared. Amazing Prof. Hard Class.

This was an extremely difficult class, but I came away from it loving organic chemistry. Dr. Iha was great about connecting the concepts were learning to biology and biochemistry, and learning organic chemistry concepts (in significant depth) has enriched those topics for me as well. I highly recommend this instructor.
Took her class during the summer. She gives out extra credits in every exams. Her lectures are organized and fun to attend. Still, this is probably the hardest thing I have ever done in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took orgo during the summer, had no life for 2 months. But 2 years later, when I took the dental school test, I studied for orgo for 1 night, and got a 99% on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Despite Dr. Iha's excellent knowledge of the topic, her conduct in class is unprofessional. Complaints about salary and sarcastic, condescending answers to students' questions have no place in a classroom, no matter how knowledgeable the professor is. My advice: don't let the Wash U brand fool you, and take this course elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Terrible . You go to lectures to copy what's on the board. No time to think or listen to what she says. Taking pictures of the notes is not allowed so if you miss something too bad. At least 1/3 of the class considered dropping towards the withdrawal deadline. Oh, and she'd gleefully tell you how much you'd suffer.

There is no course evaluations for this course so she wont take your input. Also she does not give out test mean scores and gives zero partial credits during exams. I heard that the course has gotten harsher than last year. Would NOT recommend taking this.

Dr. Iha, besides being the clearest, most organized science teacher at this school, really cares about her students. She works tirelessly to make sure she is available to give quality and personalized advice. Lectures were easy to follow and the problem sets prepare you for fair exams. Highly recommend orgo over summer bc of her. She's awesome

Obviously difficult for learning so much in a short period of time, but Iha makes it more manageable by being a great lecturer and fair tester. She makes the class engaging and as entertaining as summer orgo could possibly be. We used the textbook A LOT.
The class is brutal during the summer, but she does as good a  job teaching as anyone could.

way too much material to cover in 5 weeks no matter who teaches it it is brutal.  She cares about the students and tries her best.  Average grades can range from 90 out of 100 to 13 out of 25.  If you take the summer orgo class be prepared to have no life and no time for anything else until its done. It's like having finals week every week!
Friendly helpful fun energetic.

Smart, organized, and has this rare ability to articulate the most arcane topics in a clear and interesting way. He's tough and very strict on maintaining a fair playing field. Bottom line, attend his lectures and you wont regret it.
Great lecturer. Clear in explaining concepts. It's sad that he left the school. Will no longer be available to take his courses again.
A smart and great presenter! Challenging but very enjoyable experience.
Best professor I've had at WashU
One of the best professors.
Doesn't live up to the hype.
Best prof in the Bschool. Smart, interesting and caring. Tough but great course.
Great professor! You can get an A if you put in some effort! He is awesome!
Clear, helpful and funny. Transforms complex concepts to clear and interesting stories.
Seems to care about his students, but he often seems rushed and distracted.
I heard this class was hard, but it really wasn't as hard as I thought.

Great Professor! He's always willing to help his students. I agree with other comments, this is a challenging class but you will learn so much beyond just an intro class. Put in some efforts and you can get an A. I got one.
Great professor, really wants his students to learn, but it's a very tough class. If you must take FIN 340, I would definitely take it with him.

Great professor! very engaging with his students, and always willing to help. BUT, the course is very difficult, especially for an intro to finance class.  You need to put a lot of work into his class, all exams are very difficult too. Nonetheless, I think he's an awesome professor! Pretty good looking too ;)
Very willing to help his students. His class is very challenging but you learn a lot, and a lot more than students in the other 340 classes.
super interesting class minus political correctness!!

Class consists of writing seven 3-5 page memos and taking two exams which are basically memorizing information; it's a pretty easy class.  Sened occasionally gives too much detail, mumbles, or talks exclusively to his TA, but he has so much firsthand experience and knowledge on the subject that if you have any interest, you should take it.

No idea what he's talking about much of the time, but he's very easy and nice to students. Lectures get sidetracked by tangents or absurdly technical details, but he's brilliant and entertaining and willing to help.

Sened has the rare combination of Academic expertise and first hand experience in Israeli politics. The material can be bit dense, but he compensates for it with leniency in grading. Overall, I really enjoyed the course and would highly recommend it.

Gives intricate and hard to understand lectures sometimes, but likes when people come in to ask questions to clarify.  You just have to be pushy about making sure you understand what he's saying.  Very devoted to mentorship of students!
Boring teacher, but will give you a B+ just for showing up, and the final is just the homework reprinted.

I took Rashkova and Zhiyu Zeng for SCOT356. Very lecture-heavy with a couple of group cases and homeworks. The midterm with Rashkova was very fair, but the final with Zeng was pretty rough (but curved generously). Both professors are knowledgeable in their material, but lectures can be very hard to pay attention to at times due to heavy accents.
Class content somewhat difficult but she is very supportive.

Professor Rashkova is one of the kindest and helpful professors in WashU's business school. Yes, SCOT458 is inherently difficult, but Professor Rashkova does her best to make sure students understand what she is teaching in-class. I needed extra help sometimes and she was always ready to assist! Very intelligent and interesting person to talk to :)
good prof

Goes through content in class as if we already know it, doesn't teach us the equations properly and how to apply it, homework is way harder than class content, exams take hours. Professor Rashkova is a nice person, but not a great teacher/professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: nicest professor in the world

Professor Lapuka is a super nice guy that genuinely wants to get to know his students. The class is basically lectures with several group projects throughout the semester to apply the material. He does cold call students, but it's to ask for opinions, not to try to trip you up. If you show up and do the work, you'll do well in the class.

Best professor I've EVER had! Genuinely cares about students learning and enjoying the learning experience. Learns everyone's name and cold calls, but in the kindest, least intimidating way (he makes the class like a conversation and calls on people to ask for opinions). Graded on two exams and pass/fail group projects. Take his class it's amazing!

Prof. Lapuka takes the time to learn every student's name... but beware of cold calling. All of his lectures are interactive but can be repetitive. He takes forever to add things to the grade book and there are only 3 exams that count for the majority of your grade. If you pay attention in class, you will do very well. Overall he's a good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Darko is a great teacher and is down to earth. Makes the class enjoyable and is late only because he works at Boeing. Never kept us overtime tho. Lots of HW that are only worth 15% of your grade BUT doing them will make the tests seem too easy. Take my word. My 1st test was a solid B with some HW done. 2nd test was much better after doing all HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Ivanovich shows up late and can keep class late. He likes to drop F bombs and talk about sports and money, maybe because he hopes the bros will think he's cool. Tests are taken from the examples he writes on the board, so take notes, but don't bother to ask questions. He won't answer them, keeps to his notes, and will just call you stupid.

Darko is a gem for the Joint Program. He is very direct and won't sugarcoat anything. His lectures are good, and he is also really funny. He's the perfect person to teach the first circuits class for EE.
He was cool
Very easy professor to get an A on. He mumbles a bit but is very funny and entertaining and is a great teacher.

Nice guy but he mumbles and it is nearly impossible to understand what he says. There is no set schedule for the class so planning ahead is near impossible. Going to class is useless. A very frustrating experience.
He is nice except the fact that he covers material too fest.
He is very nice except the fact that he sometimes covers the material too fest
Such a bro, just do his homeworks and prepare for the tests 2 days in advance you'll be fine.
Nice guy, but mumbles to such an extent that I really can't hear a thing he says in class. Self study, fewer than 20 people go to his lectures because they are terrible.
Awesome professor. He's really nice. Super laid back. And you don't have to go to class. And his tests are easy.
His tests are ridiculously easy and only take about 20 minutes to do!!! This is not a time intensive class as long as you do the webwork every week! If you don't have to take 131 take 127!!!!

Izenberg is quite simply one of the most brilliant people you will ever meet. He knows everything about everything. On top of this, he is incredibly helpful and willing to help outside of class, explains topics with crystalline simplicity, and conducts a fair and organized class. Highly recommended
Such a wonderful professor. I would recommend any of his classes in a heartbeat.

The best teacher I have ever had.  I took two of his classes, each one changes your perspective on some aspect of life.  You must pay very close attention in lecture otherwise you will be lost.  If you stay with it, the results are transformational.  If America knew what he taught, we would live in a very different world. Inspiring delivery.
The best professor I had at Washu, by far. he is as good as it gets. izenberg prepares for lectures and delivers them with a passion that found in one out of every million professors

I agree that he is brilliant, but he seemed to make the subject incredibly boring. Maybe I am just not smart enough to comprehend one of his classes, but the readings and discussions were often incredibly boring. We had about a book to read each week, and by the end everyone had given up on finishing the reading. Really great guy. Boring class.
Take any course he teaches. He is jaw-droppingly brilliant, and a phenomenal, phenomenal teacher. His courses will change the way you think.
He's the best professor that i've had at Wash U.  I never did the readings but I should have because I would've done better in the class and they were interesting.

By far my best prof ever.  Have taken several of his classes, but still get so much out of every one I take.  No hyperbole when I say his classes are life changing.  Presents materials in historical context, but with striking current relevance.  Cares about students.  Fantastic insights.  If you take only one class at WashU, it should be his!

I would argue that Izenberg is the best teacher at WashU. He is absolutely brilliant, and his classes fly by if you are at all interested in learning.  He is really funny, caring, considerate and thoughtful, he makes students feel comfortable. Take his classes! You won't regret it!
Good Professor, very intelligent and articulate. Better in small seminars than large lectures.
He's a really nice guy, the assigned readings are very challenging but class discussions make the reading worth it.  However, the grading was tough to the point of being unfair.

He bores me. He knows his****, but that doesn't matter, most academics do. He doesn't engage with the class enough. I always fell asleep because he never moved from his podium. I feel like if he really cared about his material or the engagement of the class, he'd not always read off his notes.

Fascinating professor.  Great sense of humor.  You will learn a great deal.  Class is fun and interesting - not a burden.  You'll stay awake even if the material bores you.  Appropriate time to do assignments.  Professor is very helpful with any questions.
Great lecturer, teaches some of the most interesting courses at Wash U. Totally agree with above posting!
Wonderful!  Very knowledgable and clear.  Class has changed my life.  Incorporates history, literature, politics, and art to give a whole new understanding of our world.

Ridiculed students for asking questions. Was so disrespectful to students, a student confronted him after the midterm and they began to argue. The greatest barrier to learning in this class is the professor.

Chetkar is a caring guy and absolutely means well. Unfortunately, he is just inexperienced. Lectures were confusing and he often struggled to explain concepts clearly. Basically taught myself the course from old professor's lecture notes. I am sympathetic towards him, as I'm sure being a first-time lecturer is very difficult.

Great guy but unfortunately terrible professor. Explanations are very convoluted and unclear.  If you want to actually learn statistics this class will make that very hard for you. Exams are easy but again you will come out having learned nothing. He really tries but he just needs much more experience and guidance when it comes to teaching.

A humble guy w strong Indian accent. Really not good at teaching, struggling explaining concepts or giving examples. Download the notes from other profs can help you keeping up w his slides. However, really really nice on grading. Overall an easy A class, but kinda need a bit self learning.

Completely unhelpful. his lectures are him just reading out of a textbook as if he is also reading it for the first time but he's prettending to be a toddler that doesn't know what math is. Outside of class it is almost as if he will go to any length to not help students. 

avoid at all costs.
I loveeeeeee Jeff
Jeff is amazing. He is very caring and loves what he does. He is very knolwedgable about his work and is always willing to help

I love Jeff, he's a great human and truly cares about his students. He creates a supportive and engaging environment where you can actually learn and understand the basics of machines. It's a great class.
I found this class hard but I love this professor.
I love Jeff.

Amazing professor! I am TAing for his class next semester because there is no other way to be in that class again! I love his easygoing attitude. He says what he needs to say and will pop into our groups throughout class to just check in, crack a unhumorous joke, yap about class, etc. Overall great professor, fun class, and always there for you!
10/10 dentists recommend taking Jeff's class.
Take this class!!! Not very indicative of engineering but, coming from a non-engineer, it was still super fun.
Jeff is awesome

My absolute favorite professor I have had so far at WashU. Jeff makes your day so much better just by attending his class. The intro to mechanical engineering is exactly what it should be as it gauges your interest to the subject and allows you to get a better understanding of mechanical engineering as a whole.
Amazing professor, 100000000/10. He has made a grand influence on my life. I own a pumpkin with his face.

A really great and caring professor. MEMS 101 is inherently incredibly easy, and the role of the professor wasn't super intensive. Took during covid, but in person. Hands on class and very threadbare intro into relevant engineering tools/software. Jeff is friendly, big Naruto fan. I just wish this class went deeper into stuff like Arduino.
Awesome Prof!
Jeff is a gem in the mechanical engineering department. I loved MEMS 101 and MEMS 202 with him. He is hilarious and loves engaging with his students.

Great guy, very respected, and very accessible outside of class. The only negative is that the class is very reliant on textbooks or online lectures rather than in-class instruction. However, it's easy to do well and he makes the class a lot of fun. He is very appreciated by students.
Jeffrey has a great personality that makes it a pleasure to come to class. Class was not difficult in any respect but still facilitated learning about some cool stuff.
Chillest professor I've ever had. If you ever have the option to take a class with him, know that it will be an easy A.
Professor Krampf's classroom is a really chill environment that is stress free with low expectations. Intro Mechanical has hardly any work outside of class and is focused on in class projects.

we stan jeff. 10/10
but fr, he is chill, and you'll learn while having fun. would recommend taking a class with him, great guy.
Mr. Krampf is an amazing work of art. His classes are enjoyable. He inspires me.
Jeff is great 11/10
If you want to build your character... Become a boss of linear algebra... take this class, otherwise you will digress
HE IS THE GOAT!
Easiest class . He let us drop 2 exams and they only one that counted was an easy 100

Sanchez is an amazing lecturer and is super passionate about math. His lectures are engaging and helpful, and he publishes notes for all students to use. However, Sanchez's exams are EXTREMELY hard. This class is difficult.
Amazing professor but hood tests are really hard. You have to really work for a good great but soo worth it

Sanchez is an incredible lecturer, very organized, prepared, high-energy. One of my favorite classes, and I don't say that about every math course. Tests are hard but the practice exams are incredibly relevant and worthwhile. Going to office hours regularly throughout the semester was the best decision I made in terms of understanding the content.

His lectures are fantastic if you separate them from the exams he gives. For the other 4 courses I am currently taking (a mix of 2-level and 3-level courses), I have midterm exam averages of around 95. But my midterm average for this course is around 70, though I spent more time studying this course than all other 4 combined.

Sanchez is one of the funniest teachers I've had. He makes the course material super engaging. The class is not super easy and sometimes it can be hard to understand things conceptually. But he curves the tests and allows you to replace an exam with the final. He is also super caring and genuinely wants you to succeed.
Great!

Really engaging and fun professor. He makes the topics interesting. The tests are hard but he curved the class and let us replace the lowest test with the final at the end so that the grades ended up being reasonable. I like his style a lot and I learned a ton. He made me enjoy a relatively hard math class, and for that I am very grateful.
the greatest math lecturer at washu but his test are so hard

Super funny and enthusiastic professor; made the subject interesting. This was going to be my last math class but he made me want to take higher level math. Tests are very difficult; you'll have to work hard to get a good grade. He's very receptive to feedback and requests for help though and made FL2023 semester much easier/provided more resources
He made it a lot easier for fall 2023, solid guy with reasonable exams now. Would definitely suggest, Im on track for an A+.

Prof. Sanchez is a great lecturer and does a fantastic job of imparting the important lessons of matrix algebra. He is funny in class and truly seems to care about his students. If you want to learn matrix algebra, take his class. If you care more about your grade, don't. His tests are challenging and more conceptual than most math classes.
The most intelligent professor I have had at WashU, hands down. Great professor if you are a math major or truly interested in the subject. He will push you to really know the stuff!!!

Professor Sanchez is actually a really good lecturer; it's just that his tests are really hard. Generally, tests in total are worth more than half of your grade and what makes them hard is that many of the questions are theoretical rather than computational. Still, I feel I am learning a lot and homework takes about 3 hours a week, so not too bad.

I honestly think he is misunderstood. He LOVES to mess with people in class and taken lightheartedly, it makes the class really enjoyable. He is super sarcastic and cares if you show up to class. He does seem to care a lot about the students but also about earning a good grade rather than being handed it. Just go to class and apply yourself!!
professor Sanchez is a nice person. he cares about his students and he is super enthusiastic about math. Sometimes he thinks his students are as enthusiastic as he is, but sadly they are not.

Lectures are good and he's a funny guy, the exams are just a lot more difficult than what he covers in lecture. Teaches to the one person that spends 40hrs a week studying. Exams much more conceptual. Helpful during office hours though.

Professor Sanchez is a great person and is very clearly super enthusiastic about what he is teaching, and also cares a lot about the students and their learning experience. However, the exams are incredibly difficult and are worth most of the grade of the course. I would recommend taking it with a different professor if grades are a high priority.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are incredibly difficult and very theoretical. His explanations often left me more confused than before; I learned more from the Math Help Room and from classmates. Beware of typos on the tests, don't hesitate to bring something up! Only take this class if you're a math major, if not, I highly recommend taking it with someone else.
Professor is nice and he interacts well with his students. However, his lecture is mostly reading the textbook with lecture notes he made based on the textbook and exams are really difficult.

Sanchez is a great lecturer and explains concepts very well. He gets to know his students well and doesn't give a lot of work. However, his tests are EXTREMELY hard and are NOT good measures of how well you know the material. There are only two midterms and one final, so these tests are weighed heavily. Don't expect the best grade in this class.

reviews.comment: I liked her a lot, I think she's very passionate and cares a lot about her students. Her exams are difficult and averages are low, but if you study enough they're doable.

Long, monotonous lectures with exams covering minutia. Grades are slow and she takes off even on the "gimme points". On exam 2 I asked a clarifying question and was told if the questions were not written vaguely students would do well in the class. Studying not super helpful and the questions are written to confuse us, not reward good study habits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She makes the class significantly harder than it has to be and is it is clear that she is very inexperienced in teaching. The tests are constantly trying to trick you rather than evaluate concepts. She reads off of a script and constantly stumbles over her words, which makes exams much harder. Papers due at same time as exams.

Dr. Sun is insanely unreasonable. This course was actually ridiculous. I got an A by the grace of god. And because I put SO MUCH time into it. The tests are wildly detailed, and for the amount of content that you have to MEMORIZE, this class is SO not worth it. Such a shame, because with a better teacher, this class would be super interesting.

Dr. Sun is a good lecturer but the tests are not doable. She will pull a question from the tiniest thing on any one of her slides, with each exam covering roughly 360 slides. Half the class switched to pass fail and many in the class spoke with Dr. Sun about her exams being impossible and she was not receptive to feedback. Do not take this class.

I switched the class to pass/fail after the first exam, hoping to switch back later, but the 2nd exam grade didn't come in time. Her lectures are boring, and exams cover every detail from slides and long readings. The tests are tough, requiring a week of prep at the very least. Other assignments are time-consuming but don't help much with grades.

Is awful to listen to during lectures, drones on for an hour and a half about things not related to the course, or the course title. She grades impossibly and her feedback on exams and assignments is next to worthless.

Exams are VERY hard. She gave us a study guide of concepts that I turned into 88 flashcards. I used active recall and testing for least 12 hours to prepare for the exam, excluding interruptions. Questions were worded confusingly, covered small details, and concepts were left out of the study guide. I should've listened to the ratings…

idk if its bc shes from new zealand but her tests r different.
if u cant remember every little thing from the slides u need to drop the class
Very boring teacher and class.

Tests averages are low, but they are not hard. People probably don't study but if you do it is easy to score high. Some of the other stuff is graded a little harshly. She just reads off notes the whole time. Not helpful and didn't answer my questions during office hours. Class is quite boring, most people don't show up. Would not recommend.

Dr. Sun has no empathy for her students, especially those in DR. Her lectures are straight-forward, but memorize every detail to do well on the exams - all 4 of them, plus the final. Multiple choice are do-able but looked for very specific answers to open-ended questions. Papers are also due around the time of each exam. Not helpful office hours.

reviews.comment: Confident in her teaching. Direct, no-nonsense professor that values her time and yours. Caring and amicable.
Engaging, kind, and caring teacher. Chinese 3 has 4 sections a week and I wish I had more because it is so much fun. I've learned so much in such a short time.

Wang Laoshi is a great instructor. I agree: she is quite standoffish when you first meet her but that will fade. Do not be fooled tho, the workload (hw, readings, quizzes, tests, & presentations) is A LOT. U need to live & breathe Chinese constantly -- Wang Laoshi makes that doable. She truly wants to see u improve and u def will. GL y'all!

This class was significantly more work than prior Chinese classes at WashU. So much reading and vocab! That being said, Wang Laoshi really cares and wants to know if you're feeling overwhelmed with the work so she can adjust the course and help. Don't be afraid to ask questions or say if you're struggling.
