reviews.comment: She's the best!
Wang LaoShi is the best! That's all.

If you have taken a class in the Chinese department at WashU, you know what you're in for. There is a lot of work, but every Professor I have taken is an amazing instructor, including Wang Laoshi. The lessons in this course a little bit longer with more vocabulary, but you will learn a lot. Study the textbook thoroughly, and you will do fine.

Had Liang Laoshi before and the Chinese dept seems on top of their game. Wang Laoshi was awesome. Class was a lot of work but very rewarding. 4 people in my class so my Chinese improved a lot due to good class structure and Wang's office hours. Recitations also helpful. Make some Chinese native friends and go to the Chinese dept events for fluency!

I just finished Chinese 360 with wang laoshi. Not gonna lie, at the beginning, it was super hard for me(compared to ap Chinese) and I considered dropping but if you review every day, you can be very successful in the class. 

She's super helpful in office hours and encouraged me to keep going, and I've seen so much improvement so thx  wang laoshi!

Wang Laoshi is a great professor. She can be a little standoffish when you first meet her but she warms up and is very kind. She is very accessible and always gives good feedback. Participation is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wang is an incredible teacher. She's super kind, patient, understanding, welcoming, and accessible. Canvas page could be a little better organized, but she follows the semester plan and syllabus exactly so you know what to expect. Attendance and participation are super important, but if you do the work it's not hard to do well.

Really, really appreciate Wang Laoshi. Grew on me a ton as the semester went on. She is very professional but overtime opened up more and clearly really cares about her students. She is very patient and a great teacher, and was pretty lenient on the students who were obviously less invested in the class. Also not that hard to get an A if u show up.
wang laoshi is literally the sweetest

<3 <3 I had Wang Laoshi for my first chinese class at WashU and was not disappointed. She is super caring, personable, and since the classes are small, all of her students a have gotten really close with her. The class difficulty is fitting for the level, and if you are ready to take a 300 level chinese class, she is the teacher to have for sure.

Wow wow wow, what an amazing laoshi! She is so kind and really wants you to know the content. As long as you put in effort and show it, you will get a good grade. She is very forgiving and makes it clear that learning is the only goal. Take any class with her and you won't be disappointed!

reviews.comment: She doesnt require too many assignments done because its mostly studying and showing what you know. Shes great at clarifying and slowing down when youre confused.

She's lowk a little bonkers but as long as you're honest and up front with her she'll be chill on missing assignments/late work. Participate in class and she'll love you forever. She will also fully sit on her desk while lecturing so be ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor! She is very honest and cares about her students' success. Very accessible during office hours. Definitely take advantage of it.

I loved Food Culture and Power. While she is a tough grader, if you take the time to go into office hours you basically get an A– she will define exactly how she wants you to change your paper. It is such an awesome class if you are interested in the topic, but not an easy anthro course, definately and extension of prior anthro of food knowledge.

If you aren't interested in the topic, this is not your blow off class. If you are interested in getting into the readings and having tough conversations the class is incredibly enjoyable.  Readings are long, expectations are high but gives very good feedback and is accessible out of class.She consistently goes above and beyond for students
Loved her class! Definitely passionate about the material and makes you care about it too. I loved the sources we read from and I feel like I learned a lot! Dry humor and sarcasm, very funny!
Overall just a solid professor without much more to be said. If you aren't interested in the class material the course will be terrible but your gpa will thank you.
HORRIBLE. avoid at all costs.

By far the worst professor I have ever had at WashU. She is just genuinely rude and has clear favourites. She is a subjective grader and makes up false plagiarism reports. Do not take her unless you want your GPA to suffer.
WORST PROFESSOR AT THIS SCHOOL. She is SOOO biased. DO NOT TAKE. She is an incredibly hard grader and will explicitly say she doesn't like people based off your "vibes"
Great prof that will grade you fairly especially if you get on her good side. Can go on tangents during class

Jill richardson loves the game in a way few can conceptualize. she loves assigning long readings but is passionate about the subject and every class is a socratic seminar. would take again but get ready to work hard!

reviews.comment: All of her classes are ones where you can do hw during class lol. This particular class she gave quizzes and all the answers were always all A, but that coulda been her TA's fault. She's brilliant. VERY political but genuinely bipartisan (left leaning but bipartisan in class). She's casual and witty. VERY helpful outside class. Writing assignments.

Writing assignments are graded very easily. If you're looking to boost your GPA, this is a good choice. Her content is really interesting, but the presentation requires focus.

She's underrated! She's very passionate and helpful (in office hours). Most people are just not interested in her class, but it was pretty easy to get a good grade if you tried (which most people didn't). Her voice is monotonous & she has a disability so she can't have slides on the screen, but she posts them and gives very comprehensive lectures.
likes to abuse her power and make students feel bad in any way possible
run. literally no reason to take her ever

The lectures are unhelpful and lack value. The take-home tests are graded inconsistently and scrutinized excessively. She spends the entire lecture reading from notes. Attendance is overly enforced, and false accusations of cheating create unnecessary stress for students, especially during finals.

Useless lectures that add 0 value. Take home tests are arbitrarily graded with a microscope. She just reads notes for the entire time. Took attendance too seriously and falsely accused people of cheating, causing needless stress for students during finals season. If you read this and take this class, it's on you.
The class is not as bad as most people say. However, grading is quite arbitrary.

Richardson is a horrible professor. Her Culture and Environment course is structured extremely badly, with the majority of the grade based on arbitrarily-graded tests. i'm gonna lie, she's an amazing prof
seriously though is as bad as the reviews say and takes attendance way to serious for a 150+ person class. Also what are her grading criteria? it seems like she rolls a D20 with an int bonus of 5 like??

This class isn't as bad as the reviews suggest, but one thing I agree with the most is the grading criteria. It feels impossible to predict how well you're going to do on the tests. She is very nice and I don't see why there's slander here on her character. I just hoped she was either more lenient with test grading or more clear on the rubric.
This class is the definition of GOOFY! Don't be fooled for it being easy since everything is take home. My grades varied

Dr. Richardson was one of the worst (if not THE worst) professors I have had at WashU. reviews.comment: Do you have a family emergency that you need to leave class for? Be prepared for an academic integrity violation and trial. She fetishizes expelling students and getting marks on their transcript because she's oh so important and her class should be your #1 priority too.

Jill Richardson, a professor known for imposing personal ideals, often grades students based on how closely their responses align with his predetermined "correct" answers. She taught us when she had covid and then taught AGAIN. Her exams are unreasonably hard in terms of grading and you can receive points in arbitrary intervals like 20.2/25 or 22.3/25. The graders kinda look at your writing and decide its a 8.8 with no reasoning to take away 0.2 points

this woman is one of the worse teachers at washu. she's condescending, thinks she's so disabled from her non-existent migraines, says she doesn't like students based off their "vibes", and requires everything on paper. i have never avided a prof more in my life. avoid this woman at all costs. god FORBID you're not a democrat ur destined to fail

reviews.comment: Food, power, and culture was easily my favorite class of the semester. It's kind of amazing how Richardson can talk for so long without slides or full outlines about various topics. She does say some out of pocket things though, and is very clear about her political stance (not in a forceful or necessarily bad way), but conservatives take heed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Richardson clearly cares about her students and is passionate about her work. However, the lectures could get monotonous, and there were readings due before every class. The class isn't too hard, and the grading is mostly based on writing papers.

Professor Richardson is thoughtful and caring. The class was interesting and rigorous without being too overwhelming with work. She's accessible to meet with outside of class if you have essay questions. 100% would recommend.

So Professor Richardson is rather new to teaching but she's trying really hard to adapt and improve. She really cares about her students and she is really accessible. She's also pretty resourceful so reach out if you need any. In short, one of the most thoughtful professors at washu but do not expect really organized lectures.

Professor Richardson is clearly a brilliant academic, but she is not a good lecturer at all. She cares about her students, but her lectures are so incredibly boring that it's actually difficult to stay awake. The course content is also not that engaging due to the types of readings she chooses to assign. Overall, not worth your time.

Lectures are a little monotonous and boring. Her comments about student work can come off as abrasive. That being said, she seems to be trying to improve and adapt the class as best she can with student feedback. Her Canvas page is also very organized and it's easy to understand the course structure.
He doesn't know how to lecture at all and you have to learn everything yourself.

He is very test heavy. Additionally, he does post his lecture recordings. If you really want to understand the math/logic behind what he does, you must revisit the lectures/recordings at least twice. Doing this was how I studied for his transport exam and it went very well. His exam is based purely on mathematical logic.

Shao is very intelligent, but has very poor lecturing ability. For some reason, all of his classes are VERY test heavy, which makes it very stressful. Only reason I did well in the class was because the exams for biomechanics are very straightforward, but that is mostly because of Dr. Setton's influence. If Shao had his way they would be impossible
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gives 0 care for students and show no passion in teaching. Learned it all by myself and didn't even get an A. Ruined my perfect gpa.

An incredibly smart professor that seems to struggle disseminating his knowledge to students. His lectures come off as very scattered and unorganized, but every once in a while he hits the right spot and clearly communicates a point, but most of your understanding will come from youtube, chegg, and studying.
Class is hard. Lecture is so dense. So many derivations and not enough practice problems.
Shao's lectures are very hard to follow, and he has a pretty negative attitude about teaching in general. I learned the majority of the content on youtube in 1/3 the time.

Beware that he will curve down he grades based on where the classes large drops in grades are When people were confused by their grades he was so unbelievably rude hes also horrible at teaching and i did not learn a thing he also took off over 20 points on a test question that i got right cause i didnt show my work enough for him
I have told people to go elsewhere for BME undergrad than WashU because of this professor. Unfair, and is rude to students. I haven't learned much in this course.

So Professor Shao is pretty interesting. I had him for both BME 240 (biomechanics) as well as 367 (Transport) and I will say he was 10000% better at teaching transport. He clearly knows the material a lot better and is just more efficient at communicating information to a smaller class. 240 is a pretty challenging class, 367 is much easier.

Terrible professor. Thinks he knows everything and doesn't give students the benefit of the doubt or time for explanation. Hard to understand, examples are meaningless, and grading scheme is non-sense. I hear if you speak with him in Chinese he'll give you a better grade. He's also my advisor and he couldn't care less about my existence and choices
Terrible professor who thinks he's God. Btw he doesn't even know his course material well, but god forbid you ask him to double check his work.

Incoherent, and does not help students at all. If you do not understand something, he will simply tell you he explained this in class and ask why you didn't pay attention. Also difficult to understand.

Dr Lu is an amazing professor! He really cares, and Management is an interesting class with lots of projects, activities, and even Kahoots in class rather than just sitting and listening. The case comp is fun too.
Best professor, bad TA
Professor Lu was amazing. He always made sure content was understandable and interesting. The TAs were also great.

Professor Lu is a great professor with interesting lectures. However, the class falls apart with the TAs, who are not knowledgeable and give poor advice, and the grading, which is unclear. Your grade appears out of a black box, if it is even returned. Your case comp group will include freeriders, and the entire thing is judged on vibes, not merit.

For a class so heavily praised, it was an absolute disaster. Lu is an excellent lecturer and deserves a 5. Unfortunately, his condescending, unhelpful, and misleading TAs tank the class. Grading, handled by the TAs, is completely arbitrary and isn't released until December. The case competition is flooded with free riders and judged subjectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lu is a good professor on his own, but the TA's destroy the class. They have an often incorrect knowledge of the subject and fail to prove themselves useful for the most simple tasks. This leads to points being deducted arbitrarily and adds an unnecessary degree of difficulty to the class. Case Competition is an unrealistic charade of foolishness.

Good: great professor, helpful TAs, resubmission chances, exams were only 13% of grade, personally my fav class of the semester 

Bad: don't know grades for anything until end of semester, huge case comp project - assigned groups so ur screwed if it's a bad gorup

Professor Lu was a fantastic management professor. He was receptive to his students' schedules and lectures were very straightforward and useful. My only complaint from his class was the $150 textbook that was only really used for one unit. If you do the readings and have good group members for Case Competition, you will do great in Lu's class.

Dr. Lu is a kind individual and easily accessible outside class hours. Although the reading can be intensive occasionally, the Kahoots fill in the gaps, so you aren't entirely lost in class. The only downside is that we have a $150 textbook we barely use, and we cannot view our grade until the end of the semester.
Good professor, currently taking his cources, exam1 a bit difficult, teaching perfect.

Dr. Lu is a kind man and a great professor, especially given that it was his first-semester teaching. Though you will invest a lot of time outside of class doing readings and group work, he is more than willing to help you and will always greet you with a smile when you approach him. He's understanding and approachable and I'm thankful I had him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lu is building up a well-deserved cult following in his first year. Such a nice guy, great personality, and cares about his students understanding concepts. Genuinely, this guy rocks. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, do it.

Incredible Professor. His lectures are very engaging and very direct. He is a clear lecturer with no unnecessary fluff or rambling. He seems to genuinely care about student success and learning, and provides clear feedback.
Dr. Lu is an amazing professor and overall such a nice person. He made content easy to understand and genuinely cares about his students success. Definitely recommend taking this class with him!!

Dr. Lu is an amazing professor. He is very knowledgable and really loves what he is teaching. He is invested in his students and makes class enjoyable. If you pay attention in class, the tests closely match the material you cover. He also prioritizes making sure students understand the material instead of just memorizing it.

Dr. Lu was hands down such an amazing professor! He genuinely cares about his students' success and is super funny. He always answers any questions efficiently and I loved the case studies that we got to work on in class!

Dr. Lu is an amazing professor!!! He is so funny and actually cares if we learn the content. He's also super accessible and always responds to emails. I wish I could take this class again just so I could have him as my professor again.

Dr. Lu is very engaging in class and explains topics super well. I was nervous about MGT 100 because of everything I had heard, but it was not as bad as others made it seem. Lu is always open to questions and is accessible outside of class as well. I had a great time in this class and would definitely take a class with him again!
Nice guy and really cares about his students
He is a great professor!

Dr. Lu is the best professor I've had so far. He really cares about you doing well in his class, he removes unnecessary readings from tests, and if you have concerns or want to talk to him 1 on 1 he always makes time for his students. On top of that, he understands all the concepts he teaches and answers all questions really well.

Professor Lu is one of the most kind and caring teachers I have had. His homework does include long readings that take up a decent amount of time if you are a slow reader like me, but they are very useful. Prof Lu is a little shy at first but over time he opens up and class becomes a lot more fun later on. Would highly recommend him.

Best MGT 100 prof for sure. Cares about the content he teaches and is willing to take feedback from students about the course. Exams are fairly light if you attend lecture and participate, and the class is graded on a curve anyways. Also, does Kahoot review the class readings with prizes for winners?

Best MGT100 Professor. Dude took half the readings off the first test. It's way easier than Dr. K and also more interesting and relevant. Super caring and understanding. He's a little shy at first, but once he gets to know the class, he's pretty funny. He provides many relevant cases and is accessible outside of class. 10/10 would recommend.

Professor Lu is knowledgeable and always answers questions on class topics. He's flexible with deadlines and even remove some assignments. TAs handle non-lecture tasks like office hours and grading. The class isn't difficult if you stay on top of readings, focus on understanding rather than memorizing, and participate actively (hard but its 17%).

Dr Morris is a wonderful teacher and explains concepts very clearly. He always tries to get to know his students, and during office hours, he is super helpful. This class was hard, but he made it a lot easier with his teaching ability.

Spent more time on discussion questions rather than teaching. A lot of the complex topics are missed as we are discussing elementary physics questions rather than learning material beyond it. Just watch Dr. Hynes or something.

Honestly I thought he was funny and his lectures were pretty engaging. But the examples we did were pretty simple and sometimes I felt less prepared than the other sections. But he is overall a great teacher. He gave us a really helpful shortcut equation for the second exam which the other sections didn't get.

I loved Jonny. He is a genuinely chill professor and a fun and entertaining lecturer. He is extremely willing to help if you ask for it with homework or exam regrades. His lectures are also generally engaging but definitely were supplemented by rewatching the content videos and other lecturers to be fair. Would take his class again.

Prof Morris is a great guy, and made class super engaging. My only issue is that he would often not cover all the material that would be on the test. Rather, he would spend class on super easy examples or on demonstrations. I feel this made us less prepared than other sections. However he went above and beyond to help students outside of class!

Jonathan was a good lecturer who kept lectures entertaining with jokes and cool demonstrations. My only gripe with him is that he often interrupts students while they're asking questions and answers what he thinks they're going to ask without letting them finish. Also, test points were often taken off for unclear reasons.

Professor Morris is an ok lecturer, but he doesn't always include the necessary content which other teachers of the course do, which left me feeling a bit unprepared for quizzes and assessments when compared to others. I had to watch other professor's lectures in order to learn all the content. He learns the names of students and does want to help
a great professor
Homework is so difficult and it is useless.

I think he must be much busier than before. Which means he always seems unprepared for the class. Also, he is reluctant to give credits to the students who struggle. I got A Level in another math class much harder than optimization, so I believe this is not my problem finding this course is really hard to learn. Good luck guys, things are changed.

Professor Li often repeats himself on difficult-to-understand topics which was very helpful. He cares about his students and really wants them to succeed. The final exam schedule was made last minute, which was a bit stressful.

Professor Li was great at explaining things and was usually very organized in class, making sure to cover all of the necessary background information before diving right into the more rigorous optimization content. The material was interesting, the workload was manageable, and there was even opportunities to make up for missed points.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Li really knows his material and is very mathematical. You will struggle but learn to appreciate optimization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Singer is one of my favorite professors at WashU! I have taken several courses with her and she always shows her interest in the subject with her students in an inspirational way. Highly recommend her courses!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Singer is talented at facilitating interesting conversations and brings in fun and quirky elements (like strange baked goods she has concocted) to liven up the class. It is evident that she is passionate about the readings and topics we discuss.
Gave constant homework/class assignments on weekends. Very lecture heavy that were tedious and repetitive. Would not recommend compared to other French courses I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: For a French course (I took Contagions FREN 322), Singer's class was abnormally difficult. I'd be rich now if I saved money every time she'd assign a length assignment over the weekend (or really at any given point at time). However, Prof. Singer is a very kind and funny person, so I found this course to be like tough love, if anything.

Julie is such a sweet professor. I've thoroughly enjoyed class with her this semester. The topics she teaches on are very interesting, I find her to be very engaging, and she really cares about her students. Strongly recommend taking her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, I really enjoyed Dr. Singer's class. She is very adamant about participation, but she is also rather enthusiastic! Homework was given every night, but not always taken up. There was only a midterm and final in terms of tests, but there were 6 papers over the course of the semester. Our grades were  cushioned, no reason to perform poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She gives a lot of interesting lectures, but I didn't feel like I really learned a whole lot in the course. More culture focus, but the course is advertised as writing-oriented... We did six essays, but they were more like peripheral assignments than core figures in the learning process of the course. Overall, good teacher teaching the wrong stuff
Prof. Singer is very enthusiastic and seems to really care about her students. I've definitely improved my French in her class.
She's great best French prof at this school take as many classes as you can with her
The best French professor I've had so far. Endearing, understanding, helpful, clear, and extremely likeable. You'll learn a lot and never feel overwhelmed.
Excellent teacher.

Julie is really sweet and cute. She likes her job but she has those days and understands if you do too. Her powerpoints are kindof tedious and she teaches material after we've already been assigned and completed homework on the subject but she's not too unrealistic and actually respects her students

Takes a bit for him to warm up, but he is so inspiring and fascinating + funny! He really rewards hard work, and turnaround times assigned for each project were very reasonable in my opinion, as long as you are pretty locked in during class time. Just a genuinely super cool guy. The way the class sorta opens up/ramps up is great.

Juan Chavez's class made 3D less intimidating and genuinely fun, even though I was more used to 2D. He's caring, accessible outside of class, and always willing to help. The assignments were super cool—like designing shoes or a beekeeper suit—and kept things interesting. Definitely recommend taking his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My favorite professor of the semester! He obviously cares about his students and made the studio a safe place to learn and grow. This class was challenging as someone who didn't know much about 3D, but I learned so much and ended up really enjoying it.

Professor Chavez has incredible ideas for projects that really expanded my technical and conceptual 3D ability, and artistic ability in general. He is really kind but also still pushes us to be the best we can be. I had done very little 3D work in the past, and 100% want to continuing pursuing 3D because I loved this class so much.

If I could take this class again, I would in heartbeat! Juan Chavez has been the best professor Ive had at Washu so far! If you are looking for a class that can be an introduction into sculpture, this class is amazing, if you are looking for someone to push you and help develop your craft, this class is amazing! I highly recommend this class!!!
She is very kind, and wants her students to truly do well.
She gave great in-class feedback, with specific advice on how to improve pronunciation. Her tests were always fair, and she tailored her lectures to whatever the small class needed help with.

The sweetest professor I've had. She's so kind to all of her students and is always encouraging us during class. She'll work with you on pronunciation until you get it right and understand - she'll never give up on you! She's funny too and I genuinely looked forward to this class every day :)

I love Lu Laoshi! Class sessions are super engaging and you'll always leave feeling like you learned something new. Workload looks like much more on paper than it really is. I had zero prior experience with Chinese before taking Chinese at WashU, but Lu Laoshi made it ten times less intimidating. Going to miss this class so much

She's an amazing professor, the way she teaches Chinese is very efficient, and she's so sweet. I enjoyed the class a lot because she made it enjoyable. Chinese isn't easy but it was fun and light with her as a professor. I truly wish she could be my Chinese level 2 professor.
She is an amazing caring teacher. However there is a lot of homework in the class. Definitely would take the class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lu Laoshi is an absolutely amazing professor. She makes learning Chinese so fun in a low-stress environment. She leads our class extremely well, balancing friendliness with a desire to learn. She's been my favorite teacher this semester and is a large reason why I'm continuing Chinese.

Lu Laoshi is the best! So sweet and understanding. Learning a language can be hard, but she's really lenient with grading and it's very easy to get extra help if you need it. Of course, beginning Chinese is a 5-unit course, so there is a lot of work, but it honestly it is super manageable, and I treat it like a break from my other classes!
This class is great.
This professor is awesome. Easy class, was nervous at first but would recommend. I think underclassmen could take it.
Easiest A of my life!
So easy! Easiest 500 level class even easier than undergrad courses I took!

He sometimes is a really mean person and would not be happy to help you understand some basic math concept, probably he think it's too easy and waste his time. However, a lot of extra credits which makes me can skip final project(18% of total). Expected to spend a lot of time on homework like a 6 credit class. Teaching is not bad.
The amount of homework if you're not familiar with Mathematica is unreasonable, Ofttenly taking 20-40 hours for biweekly Homeworks
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tao is among the most awesome professors I've had at WashU. His lectures are very interactive, engaging, and crystal clear. The only catch is that the homeworks and exams can be tough. Still, if you find yourself in a position where you can take a class with Tao, you should definitely sign up.

Professor Ju is one of the best professors I've had ever.  He knows what he's talking about, and tries to make things interesting, fun, and worthwhile.  He is also a genuinely nice guy that cares for the students he teaches.  His classes involve a lot of work though.
Great professor

I took Existentialist Thought (HIST 3904) with Judaken, and I found that his intelligence can overshadow useful guidance for the struggles students face in analyzing heavy philosophical literature. His harshly graded essays can have ambiguous (or non-existent) grading criteria, and the pace at which material is presented is sometimes ruthless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: wouldnte let me say the class but i took existentialism with him. such an amazing class, one of my favorite.not an easy A at all though, only take this if you are excited about the topic and are willing to think deeply about it - readings can be long and dense but he work thru it in class, not many essays but they impact grade heavily-
Incredibly biased, canvas was so unorganized and he would blame you for not knowing what was needed to be done, long readings that you could not finish in the time limit

I enjoyed Dr. J and would take another class with him. That being said, my classmates and I felt that his grading was somewhat arbitrary. Participating in class does not entitle you to a good participation grade (it's unclear what does). However, his lectures are excellent! He is accessible, cares, and will reward you/notice if you work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. J is incredibly knowledgeable but this class was the hardest I've taken at WashU. So many assignments, very difficult grader. Participation is insane, discussion posts (with direct quotes) every class plus participating in discussions doesn't guarantee you a 100 for the day, only 2 absences allowed. Learned a lot but class gave me gray hair.
Great Ideas that Changed the World is the best class I have ever taken. Dr. J is the best professor I've ever had. Could not say more

Dr. J is an outstanding professor. I have truly enjoyed taking his class this semester, and it has further deepened my love for History. He gives terrific lectures and is super empathetic. He also provides many opportunities for extra credit. I would 100% encourage any student at WashU interested in History and Religious Studies to take his class.
Professor Meyer inspired me to get a Classics Minor after his class, when previously I'd been very leary of all humanities, especially the classics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Would recommend!

lectures are interesting and no electronics were allowed (the class was too distracted). grading is fairly lenient but not a very clear rubric provided. readings aren't required if you take notes in class (a must), except to find evidence for papers. extra credit is offered.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The Roman Republic had a clear structure and clear expectations. Pretty reading-heavy, and did have in-person quizzes - attendance is graded but going to lecture is necessary anyways since the slides typically don't have much information. Overall achievable, straightforward, and interesting if you like the history
Easy class and very nice lady
McClannahan is great, 234 had 2 quizzes a week(5 questions, completed at home) and the only other grade came from a paper/presentation(4pg). Really interesting and not hard to get a good grade in.

A great course which is accessible for students no only in the STEM field. She makes sure the course is truly an intro course and allows students to choose where they want to focus their learning. There isn't too much work (only an essay and presentation and quizzes after each class). Definitely worth taking. Lots of guest lecturers and field trips
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I learned so much from Brendan from every lecture! He actually cares about students absorbing the fundamental ideas about AI. He is knowledgeable, kind and easy-going.

I am really sad to see many students here didn't appreciate all these at all... alas, if you only want an easy course, maybe just do data mining...

Juba is not a good fit for 347, a challenging, required course which many CS students come in ready to hate. The disgruntled genius MIT grad that all professors aspire to be, his standoffish nature can put people off. If you come in interested in the stuff he talks about (theoretical CS) you'll learn a ton, but otherwise the material can be a grind

I really appreciate Prof. Juba. He is a great educator. Even though I got the first A- and this ruined my plan to graduate with a 4.0 GPA. Every course at WashU should have strict grading to avoid GPA inflation. Many CS undergrads at WashU has a 3.9+ perfect GPA, this is so ridiculous. A decent CS school should give minimum A's for academic rigor
Very good at forming questions for a class, very bad at lecturing, very bad at scheduling and planning content for a class, abhorrent at managing a class and communicating with students

Unequivocally the worst professor I have ever had during my time at Washu. He contributed absolutely nothing to the class other than ridiculous exams and a condescending attitude towards students. I believe, without a doubt and in all seriousness, that he should not be allowed to teach this course again. Clearly doesn't care to be a proper teacher.

The professor gives an insane amount of homework and expects students to complete within a short period of time (eg. 3 different homeworks within one week). In addition, we are not given initial homework feedback until 3-4 hours before final submission is due. Professor is unresponsive, unavailable, and gives passive aggressive Piazza responses.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor - does not know how to teach. Does not seem to want to teach. He has 0 empathy for students, does not respond to collective student feedback, and responds rudely to questions. HWs are due before lecture videos are out. The class is almost entirely taught by TAs who don't even understand all the recitation and HW solutions.

Juba on Piazza in response to a student complaining about 3 homeworks due over 9 days, partially during Thanksgiving break, with lacking office hours, plus an exam (the next day at the time):
"I hate to put it this way, but problems like on HW 9 are on tomorrow's midterm. If you need office hours to solve them, you are going to have a bad time."

Would give him a 0 if I could. The absolute worst professor I have ever had at WashU. He is the rudest, most condescending professor when you ask questions, doesn't create a welcoming learning environment, and is never willing to compromise for the sake of students. Avoid taking 347 with him at all costs!

He is unresponsive and expects homework to be done before he releases the lectures for that homework. There are no resources for students struggling in the class except for TA hours, but TAs said they do not know what is happening. It's sad to have such a bad teaching system for this class since it is a required class to graduate with a CS degree.
Seems unwilling to work / compromise with students, and unfit as a professor.

Condescending professor who can't run a classroom or explain concepts clearly.
Examples from the first day:
Having students verbally explain complicated solutions across the classroom (incomprehensible).
Condescending towards students who made an incorrect guess.
Condescending towards a student who asked for clarification on a poorly written proof.

He explains things in a very detailed and clear manner. The logic of the proof is coherent. Really enjoy his class of Theory of Computation (CSE547). Though I am a programming guy, I still can follow all of the maths and logic. His exam, though, is undoubtedly difficult, but if you enjoy solving challenging puzzles, his course is the right choice.

Juba doesn't teach with students in mind. Teaches for the sake of teaching  he clearly doesn't want to be there. He has a very stand offish attitude when you have a question about something you don't understand which undoubtedly results in asking less questions (not that his answers are ever helpful). Highly recommend you take this class elsewhere
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: CSE 347 is a required course to get a degree in computer science. But you do not need to necessarilt takeit at WashU. I highly recommend taking this course at another university. I have friends who took it at Rutgers University and transferred the credit back to WashU. Your time in college is precious. Do not waste it by taking this course at WashU
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not only is Professor Juba a terrible teacher, hes also not a nice person. He is belittling and condescending. Professor Juba is available outside of class, but youre better off trying to figure it out yourself or getting a tutor. I will never take a class with him again. Exams and HWs are graded so arbitrarily it feels like and English class.

Don't recommend taking this course with Juba. I heard the other professor like Buhler taught the class a little better. Lectures are bland and unhelpful. Ended up just trying to teach myself the material through the use of the textbook, online lectures from other universities, and youtube tutorials.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I usually give professors who teach difficult classes the benefit of the doubt but Juba is the exception. With the coronavirus pandemic all other professors have drastically changed the course syllabus and have been very accommodating. Juba has not. He changed nothing about the course except that it's online and says that it is "out of his hands".
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: God, where do I even start. Worst class I've EVER taken. The content of this course is hard to begin with but it becomes even harder because of the terrible professor. He may be a smart individual but that doesn't automatically make someone a good professor. And he is NOT a good professor. Not accommodating, lectures unhelpful, among other things.

This professor is the absolute worse. He takes no care of his students when asking for smallest of accommodations especially in regards to the Corona epidemic. By far the most confusing lectures. He writes a mile a minute and expects students to grasp extensive concepts through 1 practice problem. HW and exam problems are graded subjectively...
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Juba is famous for his confusing lectures. But if you know him more, you will realize he is actually very nice and friendly. Be prepared to read outside the classroom.
She was very rude and condescending to other students.

Worst WashU teacher I've had. Did not give me my legal disability accommodations and told me when I asked her about it after that I have "no right to complain about my accommodations." She told me no one else failed the exam, it wasn't difficult, and pressured me to drop the class.

Amazing professor. Class is extremely hard. You need to memorize just about everything said in the lectures for the tests so be sure to take good notes. While difficult, it's extremely interesting and rewarding and will definitely teach you how to learn things. McDermott is titanic in the field of memory - you couldn't find someone more qualified.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Vaughan is a very understanding and kind professor.

Although ESE205 doesn't involve much lecturing, Professor Vaughan is always there for his students. He is always happy to help and is willing to work side by side with TAs. He would even dedicate extra office hours on weekends, especially toward the end of the semester when everyone's working overtime to finish their final projects.

Ken is new to teaching ESE205 and things were a bit rocky from a management perspective, but unlike other professors he completely recognizes any issues. Ken cares a lot about students and is never "out to get" anybody. Expect lots of extensions for labs when needed. Ken is the perfect type of professor for a lab style class like ESE205.

Professor Vaughan is a fantastic teacher and very kind person. Despite significant issues I had unrelated to course content, he was incredibly understanding and made sure accommodations were made to salvage my learning. I am extremely thankful for his support and highly recommend taking a class with him whenever possible.
Cannot speak highly enough about how much I love this dude, you are able to speak freely and advocate for your ideas no matter how unpopular. Such a chiller. Also shoutout to him, he went to my HS.

This man is my favorite professor at WashU. Professor Keeline's teaching style is unique and entertaining, and he has a unique ability to make content very interesting. He learned everyone's names, and he is very caring and understanding. Show up to class and speak up, and you'll do great; he will blow your mind; he's awesome.

Keeline is one of the kindest, most interesting humans to ever walk the face of the earth. The class was discussion-based and very lightly centered on readings, but a lot of the conversations we had made me totally rethink everything I'd previously believed to be true in the best way possible. Prepare to have your mind-blown!
Very personable, understanding professor! He's friendly and does his best to make class engaging and interesting for students. Basically impossible not to get an A.
Professor Keeline has the rare ability to make any content interesting. Highly recommend

Keeline is incredibly understanding, accepting, and funny. He always makes students feel comfortable speaking up in class, and encourages creativity by giving us the freedom to do projects/speeches on any topic of our choosing. Always gives positive feedback too! As long as you show up and speak up, you'll get an A.
Such a nice and respectable professor. Encourages open communication and is very understanding. Participate in class and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Canvas is overwhelming but its a point system so if you do what you're asked you will get a good grade

Such a chill but quirky guy. He really values student success. I thought the workload was very manageable and a lot of times fun. He's lenient on deadlines, and is okay with negotiating some of the work. The classroom was a very safe space and literally I would recommend him like a million times over.

Mr. King is great! If you put in the work and follow his guidelines for writing assignments (which he goes over in depth), this course should be an easy A. Very enjoyable classroom environment and low-stress if you manage your time well, although Mr. King is generally lenient on deadlines.

Mr. King runs this class much differently compared to other professors, so it depends on what you like. If you do the work, follow the guidelines on canvas, and listen to his feedback, you will end up with an A. The workload is not too bad.
Mr. King is an elite professor. He has a ton of interesting stories, brings in knowledgeable guests, and helps all of his students become better speakers and writers.

Mr. King is a great and understanding teacher. He believes late is better than never, and Canvas might feel overwhelming at first, just ask—he's super talkative and willing to help. Make sure to 100% follow all the instructions for essays, even the "drafts". He gives harsh comments, but just ask, he will explain and re-grade if you make changes.

Basically a walking eccentric professor stereotype—you either love him or hate him. Canvas can seem overwhelming, but the workload is a lot less in reality. Definitely reminds me more of a seminar-style course! Essays have a strict rubric, but Mr. King also incorporates a lot of interesting assignments beyond the basic college writing criteria.

The assignments for this class are very helpful and practical, one of them helped me get a research opportunity. He gives harsh feedback on essays but there are a lot of participation points throughout the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor King was very caring and pretty funny. His feedback is tough but almost always right. He implements a rewrite policy that boosts your grade while allowing your writing to improve based of his feedback. Also, a third of the class was participation so it was very easy to do well given you put moderate work outside of class.

Mr. King's not great if you're not already interested in writing, and I never would have taken the class if it wasn't required. He has a very clear idea about how he thinks essays should be written and gives very harsh feedback (way too harsh for freshmen in a required class) if the rough drafts aren't exactly what he imagined. He is funny though.

Chris King is chill. You can guarantee about half of the points by completing the assignments, and he's quite flexible with deadlines. Essays are long and annoying at times, but the workload is mostly manageable. He gives harsh comments, but the scoring criteria are pretty clear and grading isn't horrendous (I survived as an international student).

this man is a joke. He comes in here and gives you these expectations that he is not able to deliver on. His grading scale is bogus. It is out of 100 points, so if you lose a point on an assignment, it could mean a whole letter grade. His guest speakers are fine, but during this time he literally falls asleep. class=joke. just dont expect to learn.
very enjoyable class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class has three essays, while the remaining assignments are super simple (will take 15-30 minutes to complete). Critiques are harsh, but will help you get a good score if you follow through. Instructions are straightforward. Classes are enjoyable since he's funny. He's also easily approachable after class. Overall, if you need an A, Mr.King got you

This class is a massive waste of time; for half of the semester, King just brings in guest speakers to talk about their careers, rather than actually teaching us writing techniques, which made going to class seem useless. King also gives really harsh oral critiques, so it can be demoralizing to listen to his feedback since it's always negative.
he is so nice and so easygoing. not hard at all to do well. deff take.
Super interesting guy, friendly, and funny. Harsh critique but if you work to address comments it will translate to a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. King is a good teacher for students who are already pretty good at writing and are able to take criticism. Regarding feedback, he doesn't hold back and tries to make the grading criteria as objective as possible. He is pretty eccentric, which turned off some of my classmates. Overall, I say he's a good teacher but it depends on personality.

Did not teach students how to write. So you were stuck if you didn't have prior experience. He even said he didn't like the analysis paper so simply didn't teach students how to do it. When asking for extra feedback, he didn't respond back. Didn't learn anything from this class, don't recommend.

Mr. King is the best. He has a very unique personality, and it's great. He puts in a lot of effort to make the class great. He grades pretty hard, but luckily there is a rough draft for you to get feedback first. 10/10 recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Wellman has a unique ability to create a learning environment without stigma. This ability allowed us to interrogate our own beliefs on topics around which most of us grew up in echo chambers.
One word: Legend. Take the class

He is soooo engaging and makes learning fun. However, personally, I felt as if this class I had to utilize memorization over actually learning about philosophy. You have to memorize like 8 different chapters for  both the midterm and then the final, and it was just super stressful. If you do not have time to dedicate hours to this class, don't take
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite possibly the greatest professor I've had but also the midterm and the final were the two most study-intensive tests I've ever taken. Worth it but be prepared to dedicate an entire week to studying for the two tests. The class itself is perfect and so entertaining. It was at 8:30 and I was genuinely excited for it.

Kit is the best prof I've had at WashU, he is so so funny & made an 8:30am thoroughly entertaining. He is caring, charismatic, and Cool... his wacky thought experiments and random references are the GOATs. Critical assessment is vital to the course so come to class ready to tear apart the essays (and take notes early!). Cannot recommend Kit enough.

The best prof at WashU. He makes sure that our understanding of the books is strong, and he is very open to questions during office hours/email. He is pretty clear about what he wants from the essay, and will also provide comments on a draft if its sent early enough. Will def be taking a class of his again!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I mean this guy is super cool and fun, but the grading is just too tough! I get the only B in my entire four years for this program! Guy does not tell your final exam so be ready to get amazed by your low af grade!

Kit is easily the best professor I've had at WashU. He is funny, intelligent, and really inspiring. The way he breaks down the readings and guides the discussions makes the class incredibly entertaining and beneficial. There is a LOT of writing and reading but Kit absolutely makes it worth your while. Dude is the GOAT
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Absolutely incredible professor. Every class was a joy to attend (even at 8:30) just to hear Kit's dynamic and oftentimes hilarious lectures. Classes are structured interactively and everyone works together to figure out the arguments behind papers. Lots of mandatory reading and tests require a lot of memorization, but it's worth it just for Kit.

Kit Wellman is the best professor WashU has ever seen. This class is hard because the exams are memorization based, and there are only 2 exams. That said, I have never learned so much about ethics in my life, nor thought so deeply about issues outside of a class. TAKE IT

This class changed how I think. Kit has discussion-based lectures, so there's a lot of room to participate and help yourself understand the material. He is very passionate about what he teaches, and he inspired me to love the material and be passionate about life. Do the daily summaries and read the essays and you'll learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
I'd take Kit 100x again: amazing philosopher, lecturer, and human being. Class was at 8:30 and I never thought about skipping it. Explains well bc he knows content is hard. Actually cared and remembered little things about us. Butyour grade is only based on 4 things and the TA graded mad hard. Reading-heavy. Learn early what 
a critical analysis is

Wellman is incredible. I was scared to take a philosophy class but no regrets. Class is summarizing readings and students volunteering to share/ask clarifying questions. He's enthusiastic, passionate, thoughtful, and makes philosophy approachable for anyone. He truly cares about his students and is invested in their success. Class is entertaining.

One of the best professors I've ever had at Washu. SO FUNNY. Totally made the 8:30am classes worth it. Make sure to do the daily write ups and you will easily get an A. Its such a fun class and Professor Wellman is amazing!!!

I took Present Moral Problems with Kit and he is just a great professor. He's incredibly engaging, funny, and you can tell he cares a great deal about his students. Students, beware that your grade only consists of 4 assignments worth 25% each, so it's hard to redeem a bad grade. But I would highly highly recommend taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wellman is great, gave me a positive introduction to philosophy. I'm not a philosophy major, took the class for ArtSci distribution requirements, but am glad I took it. You got to do the reading and go to class, though. It will likely be very difficult to do well without going to class. Discussions in class are very straight-forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I would absolutely consider Kit one of the best instructors I have ever had. I took his class at 8:30 a.m. and I loved it so much that I never opted to stay in bed. Kit is widely accomplished and makes his material funny and engaging. Be sure to do your reading and take notes during his class, though, or the exams will be nearly impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Be ready to read the text, it will be basically impossible to follow along if you don't. Also attendance isn't mandatory per say but good luck doing well on exams if you don't show up. But he makes lectures fun and informative and this class challenged and changed my world views. Would definitely take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kit is great in class. Lectures (more discussion-based) are super interesting and fun. This is a great class. However, he doesn't grade papers and his TA may be tough. He also isn't too accessible outside of class, but you can easily meet with the TA. Overall, you should definitely take this class: you will learn a lot and be interested throughout.

Kit was my Philosophy Teaching Assistant at the University of Arizona.  Kit provided the most positive learning experience in my four years in college.  Kit's lectures and office hours were positive and memorable.
Amazing teacher. Kit keeps his class relaxed but remains engaging due to his humor and passion.
Really great professor. Will hopefully take again!

Seriously the best class I have ever taken at WashU. Kit has a fantastic sense of humor and really tries to be relatable to his students. One day, he told us, "Most of you won't take away anything of value from this class. But some of you, the ones that care, will take away the skill to think critically and participate." Very admirable. Love him.
Great Guy..Keeps things interesting and up to date. I would take a class with him every chance I could possibly get because of the his ability to hold my attention.

One word I can use to describe Prof Wellman would be superficial. He talks about worldly matters in class most of the time while ignoring the profound nature of philosophy. He might be fit, handsome and funny, but that is not the qualities I look at in a professor. For all the superficial folks, he is your man and idol. He is here to entertain you.
He's hot and funny.  And a good professor.
He is not only handsome and fit but also a fantastic person and a knowledgeable proffessor.  I've never been so comfortable with a teacher that knows so much about all the mucky mucks.

While funny one of the laziest profs ever.  Obviously does not read text or even really look at it before class (admitted as much), does not hold office hours except by appointment, and basically has TA do everything.  Also at times seems to have trouble with opposing view points.
Kit's a great guy. Very helpful, and a very funny man. Made an 8:30 AM class a pleasure to wake up for.
very interesting, WONDERFUL man and teacher. helps to go to class
Made sure class was fun and interesting. Very nice and funny guy.
hilarious! great prof
He's cool.

Kit truly cares about his students and goes to great lengths to make himself accessible. Though one is inspired to attend class more often in an attempt to counteract the difficulty, attendance is largely optional and typically not an advantage.

Dr. Kidder was awesome! He was a super engaging lecturer and was also available outside of class to meet whenever I was confused. I liked this class a lot and would highly recommend. The quizzes and tests were not terribly difficult, but some weeks we had a lot of homework (though you don't always have to read everything to succeed in the class).
I like him
Such a great guy. Really accommodating and wanted to help us do well. Thought he was super interesting to talk to and wish I went to more office hours after the fact.

Professor Kidder himself is a great and caring person. The class has lectures and group assignments. All of the assignments were graded by TA's who were strict. I got points taken off for minuscule things that seemed excessive at times. Interesting class, but beware of the TA's and put in more effort than you think on the assignments.

I personally found the Earth's Future lectures quite difficult to get through because they were very long and not the most engaging at times. The Canvas page could be very disorganized, with assignments posted late, links in confusing places, etc. Kidder himself is very, very kind and understanding though. A great person, just didn't like the class

The class and Professor Kidder weren't too bad. The lecturing can get a bit dull at times, but there aren't many assignments. The concepts can be interesting to consider, but once again, it is boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredibly nice person and interesting lecturer. Earth's Future is a very easy class; if you participate in section and give effort on projects then you will do well.

I heavily disliked this class, but Dr. Kidder is a nice professor and gives great lectures. You can tell he has a passion for teaching and climate change, and this energy translates well in class. We had group assignments every week, and projects were graded very harshly. Wouldn't recommend the class, would recommend the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Would highly recommend Earth's Future: Causes and Consequences of Global Climate Change to any incoming first year. Both Prof Kidder and the other prof Brent Williams are super caring (i.e. cancelling class when its nice out for mental health) and you will learn a lot about climate change (which is super important!) Considering changing my major

TR is an amazing professor to have. I had him for Earth's Future and it's probably one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. The information is really interesting and the group projects in class will help keep you engaged.

TR is amazing. I took Earth's Future which has mostly guest lecturers, but TR was the most caring, funny, and smart professor. I would absolutely take another class with him. It wasn't hard, but I learned a lot, and he was great. Super nice and always willing to chat: he really wants to get to know his students, even in a bigger class.
Great professor.  Knows his stuff.  Show up do the reading and you will do great.  Likes to open up for discussion.  Made the class enjoyable.
Cool dude.

This professor means well but only take the class if you're not interested in science. He tries to teach some stuff he doesn't know enough about, like chemical cycling (he wrote CO2 with a small O and the 2 like it was a power). grading is wack too, goes from hard to easy over course of the semester for everyone, no matter what the quality of work.
Tough class (warning: unofficial "writing intensive" class...) but he's really helpful. take it if you don't mind challeges. you will get rewarded for your hard work.

Excellent professor. I had her for civ pro, her lectures were very clear, engaging and encouraged thoughtful discussion. Provides a lot of in class-practice throughout the semester. Readings aren't too heavy, but staying on top of them and consistently practicing is key to doing well on the final.
I simply don't get the hype. She is a very nice professor and very knowledgeable, but she's not very clear and her teaching could certainly use some improvement.

Took for Employ Discrim. Not sure if the subject was easy or if Professor Kim is such an incredible professor it felt easy. Honestly one of the best professors I've taken. Would go out of my way to take another of her courses. Material was explained so clearly and I feel I actually learned the subject 100%. Also super caring & LGBTQ friendly.

Impossible to say enough good things about Professor Kim. She's super clear and to-the-point in laying out the law, and also manages to weave in policy discussions and students' opinions on the law. She's friendly, funny, and extremely smart. If only all law professors could be so lucid.

Professor Kim is definitely one of the best lecturers in the law school. She knows the material cold and is an absolute genius in the field of employment law. She does not play hide the ball like some of the older professors, and will always make it a point to give you the black letter law while easing into the more abstract doctrinal concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I really liked Kim. She taught things I use all the time in my jobs and internships (that people who had other teachers don't always seem to be familiar with). She is nice, fair and straightforward. no laptops are allowed which is always annoying to me but i do get it i guess since its a big class and she tries to facilitate conversation.

Pauline Kim is brilliant and literally no one dislikes her.  It's spooky how many people I've talked to who will volunteer the exact phrase "I want to BE Pauline Kim."  I had her during 1L, and I'm not necessarily interested in employment law, but I'm going to take it, of course.

Professor Kim is a wonderful instructor.  She calls on students regularly but never puts them down.  She worked as a attorney for California migrant workers for many years, and aside from being brillant, brings a unique perspective and insight to the subject matter.  Plus, she encourages you to stop by her office ANY TIME!
A good professor. Shes professional, organized, and well-informed.

I wish I could go to the lectures without having to do all the work! Seriously, Kiousis acts like we have no other classes so be prepared for some insane amounts of work and difficult exams. Switching to McKelvey may be easier than taking this class! But it is really informative and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. K is absolutely incapable of listening to opinions that remotely differ from her own. She completely limits the range of debate in class, even though it is a discussion-heavy course. She will interrupt and belittle you if you attempt to have a real opinion in class.
Kiousis cares so much! Taken her for two classes, will always take her again. Love her.

Such a nice woman. It's hard in the times we live in to measure participation in class at such a high degree, but I get it. Wish her and TAs did more investigation into groups and who was actually doing work. Overall, 10/10 great lecturer, keeps it interesting, brings in cool people. GOAT woman.

Great professor love her teaching style.


Bie shang. Kuai Pao.

Very prepared presenter, takes current events and ties them to class material. This class may not contain difficult concepts, but is very useful to career development and understanding the world through economic theory. The career development portion of the class is incredibly useful to each student individually.

Her lectures were pretty good, she was personable and tried to relate content to students and stuff happening outside of the classroom. The TAs grade everything and they are usually the ones you talk to so besides lectures you don't really interact with her in the class besides that.

Do not take this class if youre looking for an easy elective. This class is not it. You will work on 4 really annoying quizzes that take minute details from class lecture. The case comp was especially annoying requiring lots of work outside of class especially since the TAs and professors kept saying how our ideas were not "creative enough".
MGT100 has been my favorite class so far because of Dr. K
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a great professor, inspiring lectures, caring about students, reasonable amount of work in and out of classroom. Could confuse what is going on in the beginning, but the TAs that she has are great help in addition to Dr.K. Explains a lot, but asks a lot on exams also, so listen carefully for everything that have been told on the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. K is an amazing person and professor. Her lectures are super engaging and her class feels more like a community than a lecture. However, if you hate reading (like me) tests are super difficult and ultra specific to the long readings she assigns. If you participate during lectures, you'll do fine in the class (there's a big curve)

I really like Dr. K as she's a passionate prof with great teaching skills. The lectures she was teaching were actually fun as they are very informative and engaging. There are readings for this class but not required and lectures are posted. Overall, it's an easy class (except for case competition) and would definitely take another class with her.
exams are heavy reading tested, never gets through slides but great lecturer and engaging. lack of organization and you won't know your grade all semester.

I hated this class. Readings were long and excessive and exams asked pointless questions about very specific details from the reading (pointless in that they weren't testing your understanding of the concepts, just your ability to memorize every word from hundreds of pages of readings). Felt like a very unfair class to me.

Fantastic class! Dr. K brings energy and passion to every lecture and to the iconic case competition. She truly cares about students and their success. MGT100 with Dr. K is legendary and one of my most memorable experiences at WashU. Highly recommend!

The readings are excessive, esoteric, useless, and unfocused. A vast amount of topics are covered, none are specified and Kiousis makes it HARDER rather that easier to understand content covered. Expect to never speak to Kiousis directly, as she will always defer questions to TAs instead and be offended when there is any opposition to her opinions.

In the nicest way possible, Dr. K thinks she's smarter than she actually is. I've found her very unwilling to answer any questions and will just immediately refer you to a TA bookslave. If you actually want the professor to help you, you can wait in the 50-person line of brown nosers that never fails to spawn after every... single... lecture. Sigh

Dr. K is probably the best professor you could have for MGT100. She injects a passion not just for business, but also for teaching itself, into each and every one of her lectures. In turn, this energy made every class interesting and engaging. While MGT100 itself is a tough class, Dr. K and the TAs did a great job of providing help when needed.

This was a great class! Dr. Kiousisis very engaging and cares a lot about students. I loved her lectures and learning about different jobs. I put a lot into the class a s for a lot put of it. A must take for non-business majors!

MGT200A is definitely an easy A but I don't really think I learned anything. There is really no homework and you don't need to pay attention in class. I guess you will take out of this class what ever you put into it but you can definitely put in little effort and get an A.

Dr. K is arguably one of the best professors at this school. She is so caring and an incredible lecturer. This course is not easy, but she appreciates and respects those who put in the work and participate. I HIGHLY recommend taking her for MGT 100.

So caring, passionate, inspirational and knowledgable. She had engaging lectures, incredible organization, and great slideshows. Semi-heavy readings, but not unmanageable. Definitely takes a lot of out of class work but it's worth it and tests are curved. I would recommend everyone take a class by Dr. Kiousis

Genuinely one of the kindest, most compassionate professors I've had here. Was told to take the class with her by a friend and it was the best decision I ever made! She seems to actually care about fostering good relationships with students and her class was a breath of fresh air. Love her!!
She was the best professor I have ever had. She cares about her student and really wants us to success in life.
Kiosks is iconic. Lots of homework but she's the best.
Dr. K is a great teacher! She is inspirational and gives great lectures. The case competition in her class is a great experience and the TAs are great!
The test is so hard and the way she gives question is not reasonable at all. There's a free rider in my group, but no follow up was given after reporting the issue.
Great lecturer, but class itself is tedious and can be a lot of work. Overall, was a fun class and very interesting

This is a great class! Dr. Kiousis is an amazing lecturer and the class made me realize I want to major in business. Make sure you go to class and subsection. My subsection TAs were great and helped my group for our case competition project. Get to know them!

The professor is good. But the grading criteria is so vague. Participation matters. If you participate in class, you will get a good grade. It is kinda unfair for students who is shy and don't like to answer questions. Even if they try hard and do well in class, they may not get a good overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Kiousis is the best professor I have had at WashU! She is an amazing lecturer and kept me interested even when I had a lot going on. I looked forward to going to her class for every session. Also, the case competition was a great experience! A must take at WashU!!!!!
Good lecturer, but most of the homework assignments in this class seem like busy work. The grading criteria is excessively vague, making it difficult to understand how our work is being evaluated.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. K is a fantastic lecturer! One of the most organized and engaging professors I have had at WashU. She uses a lot of real-world examples which makes her lectures feel more applicable and she encourages people to participate despite it being a somewhat large class. Attendance is a must and prepare for a lot of quizzes, but overall great class.
Great class. Dr. Kiousis cares about student.  The cases are really interesting!

Dr. Kiousis was a great professor.  Our case competition on Disney (not Tesla like the other review said, that was a different professor) and it was really fun!  I learned so much!  I wish other professors cared about students as much as she does.  She inspired me to study business.

If I could give her a 2.5 I would, because she's just alright. Way too much outside work. Class was disorganized and run by TAs. Lectures could be learned by just reviewing the slides. Tests were structured around specific material and were so obfuscating! She is, however, a nice person. I wish she had more office hours and accessible outside class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Really good lecturer and fun to talk to outside of class

Class is really well organized, uses a lot of practical real-world examples, and she makes the material accessible.  If you put in the work, you'll do well in the class.  She definitely cares about students learning the material and wants us to succeed.  Great class overall.

MGT200A. Dr. Kiousis is the best, most inspirational teacher at WashU. Her passion for her job is palpable. She prepares well for lectures with engaging graphics (and sometimes music!). Cares deeply about student feedback and loves to hear opinions in class. Take this course if you're curious to test the waters in business and gain life skills.
Great professor that cares about students.
Fantastic class. Great professor.

Dr. Kiousis is always willing to help her students and typically gives really exciting lectures. Definitely make sure to do all of the required reading, and reach out to course assistants for help and you should be all good! This was genuinely one of my favorite courses at WashU.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Great class and great professor! Make sure you talk to Dr. K after class or at office hours. Shes really interesting and is very helpful. Must take at Olin!

This was the most valuable I class I have taken at WashU. Dr. Kiousis is a fantastic lecturer and cares about students. The cases were really interesting and everything I learned I used in my internship this summer. I felt like it really gave me an edge over the other interns. Would take another class from Dr. Kiousis any day!
Great class!
I loved this class! Dr. K is a great lecturer and the cases are really interesting!
A must-have professor in the business school! Dr. K gives amazing lectures and she is an incredibly powerful speaker.
Dr. K really cares about her students. She spent a lot of time with my group and offered a lot of feedback on our group project. She's really great! I will definitely take another class with her.

This is the class in which I've had to do the most busy work, which says a lot since I'm pre-med. A typical week consists of 1+ group projects or homework assignments and about 100+ pages of reading(we had 200 pages due 2 days after an exam). I've heard this is the weed-out of the business school and it is spot on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved this class! Dr K cares a lot about her students and teaches you about really interesting companies. Inspirational teacher who will take time to talk to you about career interests and job prospects. Go to her office hours if you can!

I learned a lot from this class and Professor Kiousis. You study real companies all semester and do a final project on a company you get to choose. It was one of the most valuable classes Ive taken at Olin.

MGT380 is the worst class I've taken at WashU. Uninteresting material, little to no actual discussion, zero expectations or explanations of what assignments are going to look like, very boring lectures. Could not tell you what my grade will be at any given point in the class. Avoid if you can.
Dr. Kiousis was an inspirational teacher. I loved her class! She went beyond all my other professors this spring to make her class engaging online. A must take!
