Prof. Kiousis is a NECESSARY professor to have in a WashU business education. She teaches hard work and dedication, but it pays off in the end. The exams are long and difficult, but the homework and case competition balance it out. Participation is key, as she will raise your grade if she believed you spoke up in class.

Dr. K is a decent professor. The lectures are usually interesting and are based on the millions of pages of readings. Lots of homework outside of class--group projects, papers, econ practice questions, etc. She isn't very accessible behind her army of TAs, but the TAs are great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: seems intimidating, but is actually one of the most brilliant and caring professors you will ever have. the class is work but Kiousis offers countless resources to make your life easier. absolutely loved her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Literally one of the best professors at the school. She'll change your perspective about the business world.
Easily approachable and cares about student well being.
Great class if you want to go into consulting. I really like the professor!

If you dont do the million readings she assigns, you wont get a good grade since you wont be able to participate in class (you are graded on participation) and the readings make up most the test. overall, she is a very caring and passionate proffessor. i have learnt so much in the class - stuff that doesnt only pertain to buisness.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Taken several classes with Kiousis but they've all been similar quality. Pretty wishy washy non specific content, and she tends to get off topic and ramble. I never took anything away from any of her classes, but I had to take them because they fit into my schedule.

The reading are not logically coherent with her lecture. The workload is absurdly large, and there are a bunch of weird readings just for simple intro to econ. She is a cocky person who loves to stunt the experience she had and being proud of the unreasonable workload. Got no choice but take MGT100 in Bschool. Won't have any class with her.
Great class. Learned a ton. Nice professor.

Do not take business strategy with Professor Kiousis. Great woman, but the class is entirely unstructured, expectations for assignments are never clearly articulated, and the amount of reading she assigns is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good class. Kinda tough. Fair teacher. Participation is important. Must show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a very interesting professor who makes class pretty interesting. She REALLY values participation and talking to outside of class for whatever reason will make you stick out in her mind (in a good way). If you're engaged throughout the course, she's willing to negotiate grades. She also really cares about her students what she's teaching.

Dr. Kiousis is truly an inspirational woman and has been my favorite professor at WashU! She's created an incredible environment in Management 100 that engages students from all different backgrounds by constantly incorporating real world content. If you don't take Management 100 with Kiousis, you've missed out on part of your WashU education...

Kiousis is great! She truly cares about her students, which can make a huge difference. I had some life challenges during the semester and she worked with me to make sure I was able to turn in all of the assignments. She is an incredible prof and you'll learn a ton. DEFINITELY take.

I absolutely loved this class and the professor!  The lectures are engaging and kept my interest all semester.  I recommend this class to anyone interested in business whether you want to major in business or not!! Great class!

I absolutely loved this class and Professor Kiousis! She is a great lecturer and very nice person.  If you keep up on the reading and study for the exams, you will do well in the class.  You will love the case competition. One of the best experiences of my life!  It was because of this class that I am now a business major.

Professor Kiosis is one of the best teachers I ever had! She is super knowledgeable and passionate about teaching. She has a very energetic style. If you do the cases and follow the lectures and participate you will do well AND learn a lot!

Professor Kiousis is one of my favorite teachers! She is always available to meet in her office and is extremely helpful. The cases are interesting, and she does a good job integrating them into the lectures. The class is straightforward: if you study the material, you will do well.

Loved this class! I learned a ton about real companies.  You need to read for class and study for the quizzes.  The final project was a lot of work but well worth it.  It is a big part of the grade.  ...  The professor was super nice and helpful!

Fantastic class and professor! The professor really cares about her students and has very interesting lectures.   Participation matters so try to talk in class.  The exams were fair but tough.  Loved the case competition.  It was a lot of work but fun! Would love to take another class from this professor!!
Great class. Professor cared about students and wants them to learn.  Prepare for class and ask questions. Class participation is graded and helped me show how much I knew.

On the case comp she gave all one person in our group a score much higher than the rest of us, and that person didn't have a lead role.  Reached out to her SIX TIMES to understand our grading with her and every time she said she was busy and would try to get on it in a couple weeks.  Never got an explanation for our grade. It turned my A into a B.

Take it with another professor if you can. Not really open for discussion; she doesn't take disagreements very well. You don't learn much from this class, other than learning about what companies did in cases. The classes are mere recaps of the cases and not much room or creativity/discussion.
Very caring professor, but disorganized. Class is almost completely case based and involves a lot of participation. Case presentations are fun and competitive. Great class.

Marshall is one of the kindest, most generous professors at WashU. He is so passionate and supportive and makes his classes such a joyful and enriching environment. Flexible about deadlines if you communicate ahead of time--just really wants everyone to succeed. Can't recommend enough.

Marshall offers a lot of guidance on writing and specific points where you can improve your story. He offers feedback and gives areas on where stakes can be added and where it can be expanded. Overall, Marshall really cares about his students, and his writing exercises and comments have made me a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Got great feedback on my work. Read a lot of interesting pieces. Was readily available to help me think through my pieces outside of class. Frequently interrupted the women in the class, but let the men ramble on without interruption. Kind of a red flag. But a nice guy otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've never received so much feedback on my writing ever by a long shot. He'll write 6 pages single spaced feedback on your workshop piece. If you want to really improve as a writer, take this class with him. If you are passionate about writing, want to take risks, and explore new things, this is definitely the class and the professor for you!

A really nice guy, clearly cares about helping you improve your writing. Participation-heavy and a lot of work for a 200-level class, but overall worth taking with him if you want someone to push you to be a better writer. I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The professor is very nice in person but gives really tough grades. Participation heavy and he keeps track all the time! A lot of readings and writings. If you want an easier pass, his classes aren't the best choices.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Not really sure what people are on about here...the IMAAD course & lectures are incredibly well structured, a VERY welcome change after taking IWAH the semester prior. I found his lectures honestly interesting and enjoyable for the most part. A significantly better class compared to it's sister class in IWAH in my opinion.

I found Klein's lectures to be very engaging and even funny at some points. His class was incredibly well structured, and I really appreciated the easy access to information on Canvas. I feel the criticism he receives is unfair, as if you actually pay attention to the readings and go into the lecture with an open mind, it can be very entertaining.

He had such interesting and engaging lectures. I loved his structure, using "keys" to guide each "chapter" modern art. He offered spunk while balancing the dense load that art history is. He is very passionate and will connect you with further options outside of the classroom too. Your grade can be dependent on your subsection leader however.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Although I'm not sure if he would be as good for a smaller class, I found Prof. Klein to be great for IMAAD. His lectures are consistently very interesting, and he very clearly outlines the contexts of how the artwork in question should be understood. However, I didn't feel like he cared to know us as people, but that could be due to class size.

Professor Klein is knowledgeable about Dada and Surrealism, but he doesn't allow room for differing opinions. During class discussion, he is passive aggressive if he doesn't agree with your idea. He cuts female students off while they're speaking and is pretty overtly misogynistic in his lectures. His lectures are also really boring and monotone.

I cannot begin to explain my hatred for this man.  He is a terrible teacher. He doesn't explain things well and the only I learned from this class is that it's okay to never go to lecture but read the recommended articles and still get a 98 on the midterm. Just proof that you don't need to listen to his BS to pass the class.

A lot of students don't like Klein because of his personality, and the fact that he spends much of his time setting up the context in which the artwork was created, but I found his technique both engaging and thorough.  Not for students looking for quick sound bytes of information that they can easily regurgitate in an exam.

I've taken 2 courses with Prof Klein and I've enjoyed both. The previous comments are unfair, though his style requires some getting used to. He tries very hard to phrase things in the most precise way possible, which might initially seem verbose but they were helpful for my own writing. Knowledgeable and approachable.

The most pretentious professor I have ever met, and undeservedly so; highly unwilling to help and unwilling to admit that he is anything less than perfect. Avoid this class if possible. Talks in monotone, makes things up.
ugh Intro to Modern Art was horrible

Genuinely fully a miss ogynist on several occasions :( also did not make students feel safe going to him. Was especially unfortunate when boys in class wouldn't do work and it was all dumped on girls last min and he was not a good resource and did not reflect in grade.
Dr. Klaesner is a challenging professor; however, he helped connect me with my current internship. You can tell he really cares about students and wants them to succeed.

I would have considered a different major if I had known he taught the class and graded assignments this way. He clearly lacks the ability to teach effectively, and I even doubt that he fully understands the lecture material himself. The slides he used look outdated — as if they were prepared twenty years ago.

Grades assignments with near-zero basis. Lectures are fully unnecessary and more thoroughly cover personality tests and group work than the actual design process and expectations of the course. Rubrics provided for reports are terribly vague. Essentially no guidance is given by the instructors throughout the course. Basically a tech writing class.

Incredibly boring, bland, and pointless. Super condescending to students. Watching him interact (with mostly female) students makes me uncomfortable. His grading is laughable and contradictory. The "help" he gives is awful. Sad excuse for a professor at a top college. Not a surprise he is disliked by the other professors.
Dr. Klaesner is a tough professor, but he is very knowledgeable. I think you get out what ef

First, our dean has stopped him from researching. For teaching, he is very uncaring, uses mostly outdated materials, and is very condescending to students. He does not use a clear rubric and takes off points because HE thinks the project isn't good, given HIS experience. Has the lowest score in official course evalutation of the entire eng school.

Dr. Klaesner didn't care about students. What he cares about is throwing tons of criticism into students' homework. He always got ready to read his lecture slides. There was no guidance/mentoring from him for students; what he did was simply introduce some basic concepts and read his boring grading rubrics. I am VERY DISAPPOINTED with his class.

He looked so confused when our group was presenting the final presentation. 

No idea about what I learned from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His senior design class is not helpful for me to get insights into professional ways of developing an engineering product. The only few things I learned are to find a client and define the problem...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Klaesner knows ~a lot~ about circuits and electronics. He cares about the students a lot and even though he rambles a little bit, its with the intention of explaining applications of what you're learning. He also does a ton for getting students internships and is very personable if you just strike up a conversation.

Absolutely ridiculous professor. He and his TAs are extremely disrespectful to students, throwing out suggestions in very condescending ways. TAs are helpful at the very least and Dr. Klaesner is neither helpful nor respectful. I also know from my peers that no one thinks he is a good teacher and most of us agree with his absurdity.
Intro to Archaeology has a lot of material, but if you study the tests are not that hard.  Labs are very fun and a good way to boost your grade if needed.

Not easy, but fair and always tried to help you improve. Lots of study material. Lectures cool - one was in 3D - and better than the readings, which are not as important to study. Always tries hard in lecture to add current discoveries. She's good, take her.
Learned more in this intro class than any other. She works you, but is fair and gives lots of study materials for the test.

Makes no sense. She is a horrible lecturer and is a pain to listen to. Unrealistic with her grades and exams. Her class alone made me reconsider my anthropology major so that I wouldn't have to take the class

Dr. Kleutghen is an extremely harsh professor. She has little compassion for students. Additionally, many of the negative RateMyProfessor scores of her are deleted, so her score on this website is slanted more positively than it should be.

Dr. Kleutghen is overall great. She can be intimidating (especially 1 on 1 at office hours!) and it can feel like she expects you to know more than you do, but she explains things very thoroughly and wants you to understand. I have learned a LOT in her class. If you have any interest in Chinese art, absolutely take one of her courses.

Don't pay attention to the positive scores. She is known to delete negative ratings of her on rate my professor. Her score should be much much lower. She yelled at me in class and was very unprofessional.

I have never encountered a professor quite like Professor Kleutghen. Your participation mattered so much and she graded it extremely harshly. She gave around 10 hours of reading a week and expected you to understand all of it. If you don't understand the reading, good luck because your participation grade will drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Kleutghen has high expectations for 100-level class. She also took down all the course material one hour before the final exam, she requires a doctor's note for sickness, and she can be a little mean to students who misunderstand the material in class. But her lectures are stellar and she's very accessible. You just have to devote some energy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hard class, but I learnt so much about East Asian arts. Most importantly, I learned about work ethics.
Very challenging class but thought-provoking, a must take at washu
Very challenging class, require a lot of work, but very thought-provoking

Professor Kleutghen is very demanding.While she is very passionate about Chinese art and culture, her passion can sometimes morph into condescension. She is very particular without explicitly telling students her expectations for projects. If you're looking for an easy and relaxed humanities course, do not take professor Kleutghen's course.

Professor Kleutghen is amazing! She gives good lectures and constructive feedback to every test / assignments, cares about students a lot. Lots of reading to do but the class was very fun. Participation is encouraged but not graded, good for introverts like me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Has really high, strict standards. I can tell she puts in a lot of work into her lectures and course set up, but she then expects the same level of work ethic from students with homework, discussion, etc. If you're really interested in the topic, and learn best via speed note taking every lecture, you'll do great. Otherwise, you'll struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class is intense... Everything is graded and the TA's patrol the lecture hall to make sure you don't do anything against the rules of the class... not a very enjoyable experience.... Professor Kleutghen is very smart and genuinely cares about her students, but she is a tough cookie
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kleutghen is great. She's an expert in her field, and really passionate about helping her students. Most of the people who complain are ones who want this to be an easy class. If you put in the work, you'll find that the class is rewarding and inspiring. I will be taking more classes with her in the future.

Took this course for sheer interest, Professor Kleugthen is probably one of the best professors I have had at Wash U. She is very knowledgeable about the subject she teaches, gives clear lectures, and lets you know what she expects for class. <-- she expects a lot though, especially for an intro level, but worth it. Make quiz-lets twice a week!

The worst professor I have had in my life. Treats students like middle schoolers with ridiculous anti-technology and food/drink policies, with TA's at the back of a huge lecture hall sweeping the room to confiscate your belongings. Absolutely 0 compassion for students, and very pompous and arrogant about her own knowledge. Mispronounces a lot.
This is the most micromanaged lecture class I have been in. She is knowledgeable on the subject but lecture is not engaging and she does has little compassion for her students.
Professor Kleutghen is an inspiration. She is amazingly put-together and eloquent, and she is passionate about what she teaches. She is tough but fair, and expects a lot from you.
she offers helpful research strategies and has info
Terrible prof.  Rambles about random stuff most of the time.
The worst teacher I have ever had. Legitimately useless. Possibly made me dumber. Just tune her out in class, you'll have to learn everything yourself before the test anyway.

HORRIBLE!! SHOULD NEVER TEACH AGAIN! Cannot convey the simpliest info to us. We have to ask millions of questions to understand what she talking bout. Unclear about everything, which is annoying. Really accomplised lady, but bad prof. Good note: in office hrs she will explicitedly tell you what you did wrong. So you can try again next time.
no more qualified to teach than a random bum off the street- can't even convey the slightest bit of relevant information- left her classes more confused than when I entered.
No Comments
She's just so unclear.  Focuses on details and forgets to show us the big picture.  Really nit-picky about points and the bluebook.

Amazing lecturer. The course is extremely well-structured. Homeworks, readings, quizzes, and exams are deeply connected. Homeworks are thoughtful and interesting, exams are pretty fair if you studied. Lectures are pretty interesting and humorous. He knows what is real math education!

Dr. Knese is a great professor. We went slow, but I think he values depth of understanding over quantity. He always asked us if we had questions, and was willing to push a lecture off if the class was confused about a topic/proof. His office hours could sometimes be awkward and silent, but maybe that was me. Lastly, he cracks some funny jokes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Knese is an amazing professor. It was his first time teaching Math 203 and I think he nailed it. We went pretty slow in the beginning, but we started to pick up the pace throughout the semester. His homework questions aren't too bad (you can always go to his office hours for help). His exams aren't bad at all as long as you know the material.

(Took for 310, but that wasn't an option on the list) Prof Knese was awesome. As a transfer student who had already taken real analysis, I felt this class was quite difficult towards the end of the semester. However that isn't really his fault, and he did a great job engaging the class.

GK is great. His lectures are engaging, he is humorous and he genuinely cares about his students. If you want to do well in this class, you will. Make sure to finish all of the homework assignments and do the practice exams and you'll do well. Reach out to him if you have problems w anything, he's very amicable.

He's got a great sense of humor in class and lectures were pretty clear. The homeworks could be pretty tough at times, but the exams were not bad at all as long as you were comfortable with the theorems and concepts. He's a good lecturer and much better than most of the math professors I've had at WashU. Definitely would take a class with him again

He is a laid-back professor, who doesn't take himself too seriously in class. However, that doesn't make him a bad instructor. He also does well to make you understand the "why" for what you're learning, instead of just the "how". Even so, the exams are pretty fair, and grading is reasonable. I would definitely recommend 309 with him.
Very funny teacher with a great sense of humor. Enjoys talking about the "deep" ideas of mathematics. He moved the class along at a somewhat slower pace than I would have preferred though.

Dr. Knapp's class was great: U.S. War in Iraq. He gives compelling, interesting lectures and tries to get to know the students who participate in class. He has a cult following of history students who take all his classes, no matter what. He does teach important contemporary topics, so I understand. He doesn't do any grading; it is all the TA.
Knapp is the GOAT. Extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. Also very flexible with deadlines in my experience as long as you had a valid excuse. Wish he could teach all my classes.

Awesome prof - knows a lot. GWOT itself is super timely and interesting. This class is a lot of work, although worth it. You just need to know what you're getting into. 12-14 books (we would read a book for class sometimes). Oral assessments where you teach the material you had to read for class. Very rewarding, just know what you're getting into.
The best like actually the best

Incredible professor, you would not regret taking a class with Professor Knapp. Quite possibly the best professor in the history department. Brilliant, passionate, and overall, a kind and good person.
Best professor at WashU. Fantastic at giving lectures and super sharp about everything he presents you with/ 10/10 recommend

Proffesor Knapp is clearly a smart guy and is approachable when asking questions outside of class. However, this class (and I'm assuming his others) is graded almost entirely on papers. Be sure to understand the Chicago style guide for writing because he loves it and will make you use it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Professor Knapp's lectures were engaging and had lots of humor, they were fast paced and very heavy on content. No option for pass/fail, very few assignments making up entire grade. Didn't love non pro-America opinions/discussions. Not a lot of help available and was not a fan of the TAs grading. Had no pre-req's but definitely should have.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The U.S. War in Iraq 2003-2011 is the best class I have taken at WashU. Professor Knapp is provided the class with engaging lectures and it was undeniably clear he knew his stuff. The grading was done by T.A.'s who were, for the most part, wiling to help you out with thesis statements and general feedback. I had to work for an A but deff recommend
Incredible professor and fascinating subject material. Anyone interested in foreign policy needs to take one of his courses.
Professor Knapp is great, but he definitely favors some students over others. If you take his class, go to office hours!

Knapp is the GOAT. GWOT is my favorite class I ever took at WashU. Above average amount of reading but it's interesting and enjoyable. One of the few classes where I learned and remember stuff years later.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I would never take a class with this man again, worst professor I have ever had at WashU
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The US War in Iraq was one of the best classes I have ever taken at this school. The lectures can get long and there are a lot of notes, but if you pay attention, you learn a lot and the 3 papers that determine your grade are much easier. There is also a lot of reading, but it is interesting and helpful. Attendance is 10% of the grade. 10/10 class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The Global War on Terrorism is a bit like spending a semester on a CNN panel.  The discussions are based on non-academic books published for a general audience, and they don't become any more informed or insightful as the year goes on.  I imagine Dr. Knapp is great for other topics but this is clearly not his area of expertise.

Knapp is one of the university's best lecturers.  Lectures are sometimes long, but are very clear and comprehensive. A lot of reading, but the lectures often cover the same material.  Entire grade based on 3 papers, which seemed a little disconnected from lecture. Prof has TAs do the paper feedbackgrading process. Good class for those interested
He is a really good lecturer and in this class I had to write just three big paper which are not terrible at all if you listened his lectures. It was the best class ever in my college.

History of the Iraq War. This was by far the best class I have taken in college. Knapps is an expert lecturer and makes everything he talks about interesting. He does lecture to you for the entire period, but he always asks if people have questions at the end and kindly answers all. 10/10 would take again

The History of Popular Culture was an Interesting and enjoyable class. I also appreciated the format of the class, with three papers and no tests or quizzes, that allowed me to gain a more in depth understanding of the subject, tailored to my own interests.

Incredible prof. Great sense of humor, knows his stuff incredibly well, passionate about the subject. Makes his ideas clear and its easy to turn the lectures into essay theses. Must take a class with him, very cool guy.

His Cold War History class was amazing. It ignited an interest in the Cold War period that I didn't even know I had. I found him super accessible, engaging, and very well-prepared for class. This was probably my favorite class during all of undergrad. Take this class, and ask him questions after class.

Prof. Knapp is very prepared for class, but he thinks he knows everything about anything...He really thinks that he is more intelligent than 90% of the world's population when in reality he is a young, smart guy with little common sense.
Great lecturer, very interesting, and lots of fun.

I don't know about Cracks, but his Cold War class is certainly not as good. This may be due to the class size (70 kids) but his lectures often ramble, are overly self-justifying, and he often gets caught up with fairly useless questions and a lot of class is wasted. It's a good course, but everything is in the assigned reading, not his lectures.

Kristor will open your mind and teaches a very romanticized class--an idyllic one in which there is constant participation, laughter and great insight. Very witty and knowledgable about what he teaches.  Cream of the crop at Wash U and one of the best classes out there.  A hard but fair grader who forces you to delve into the material at hand.
He is an amazing professor. He comes prepared to every class and makes every lecture wonderful. I love going to class and I learned so much. He is funny, helpful and interesting. Take his class!

Wow, literally THE best professor I have had at Wash. U.  Class is exciting, edgy, and most of all..extremely organized.  There is a lot of info, but he makes it easy to follow.  Feels like you're in that ideal college class to open up your mind, read great books, etc.  Cares about students, very approachable.  Take anything he teaches

Amazing lecturer and professor.  Witty, funny, responsive, and respects his students and their opinions.  The best professor at this apathetic school...do everything you can to take this professor!  Sure, it's a lot of reading, but it will open up your mind and respect others you never thought you could.

GREAT lecturer, inspires interesting debate among students.  He's a tough grader on written assignments but you WILL learn a lot if you follow at least some of the assigned readings and pay attention in class.  GO FOR IT!
Amazing lectures. Very smart, witty, and knowledgable. Young and relates well to students. Assigns too many books, but you don't need to read them. Take his classes.

Very well-read and knowledgeable on subject material.  Lectures move quickly but are clear, well-organized and entertaining.  Knapp is young and relates well with the students.  By far the best professor I've had at Wash U!
Great class and he is a very interesting person.  He mixes things up so it's easy to follow along and hold your interest.  As long as you show an interest in the topic, he will be easy on you.

This class had such interesting topics, and I think it is especially valuable coming from an OT. Kathy is such a lovely person, and I had such a fun time in this class! There were no exams, so our grade was based on several projects throughout the semester, which made this class low-stakes and more enjoyable!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: KATHY IS THE BEST!!! Take this class

Professor Kniepmann is one of the best people I know at WashU. Disability, Quality of Life, and Community Responsibility will change your perspective and alter your way of thinking. Showing up to class is a joy and her assignments are designed to make you think. She is committed to the wellbeing of her students and is passionate about her work.

Kathy is incredible. I took class with her as a senior and loved it. As a grad student I still come back for her panels and speak. Shes kind and interested in her students and their lives. Her classes arent challenging, but they make you think and reconsider your perspectives. As a disabled woman, her disability class made me much more confident.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Kniepmann is actually an angel. EVERYONE should take a class with her.
Great person... Classes are engaging, interesting and fun. One of my best experiences at WUSTL
Kathy is a real gem!!! She is the kindest, sweetest woman ever and I highly recommend this class to anyone
Kindest woman in the world.  Kathy is a saint.

Kathy is a wonderful person and it was a pleasure to be a part of her class. Discussions were meaningful and thought-provoking, most movies were great films that were enjoyable to watch. Assignments basically ask for a summary of your reactions. Interesting class and great learning environment.

Extremely kind and intelligent professor. Not a lot of work at all, but definitely learned a lot! Class was like a nice break from my hectic day. Highly recommend taking a class with Kathy!! (Especially Disabilities in Film if you like watching movies)
Kathy is a wonderful human being and I very highly recommend her classes. I learned something, had fun while doing so and enjoyed the discussions. She's simply awesome.
Inspirational and life changing. Fascinating perspectives.
The easiest class I've taken since grade school, and yet it is interesting and meaningful
Best and nicest teacher at WashU.  Easy class while also making you feel good about yourself.  TAKE THIS CLASS!
He gives amazing lectures and focuses heavily on empirical evidence that supports the concepts we were learning. Exams aren't hard but definitely need to put some time into studying.
I think Dr. Kool's lectures are amazing! Lots of materials to take in for this class, but the exams are relatively easy. He is also makes delicious chocolate chip cookies that he brings to class.
lots of information, good lecturer

cog psy. it's fine overall as long as you put real effort in it. Course content is interesting, and this class actually inspired me to do more research in this field. Sometimes the slide went really fast, i guess he assumed everyone already read the textbook. Prof.Kool is really passionate about his field and he can pass that energy to students
I had Wouter for Cog Psych 360. He is a pretty good lecturer even though the content can get pretty boring at times. I thought the exams were fair. I never read the textbook and still did fine.

He seemed fine at first, but he wasn't that nice of a prof. He called our 1st exam "not great..." but then wouldn't use exam questions that past years had gotten all correct when making this year's exams (I wonder why the exam average was low). It didn't feel like he was trying to help us. You can't see your graded exam so idk where I lost points

I don't know why it says PSYCH 306 but the class is actually 360. IMO this class requires some real hard work. There are no homeworks but the exams really require you to put in the time to study. One lowest exam is dropped so things worked out in the end. The lectures are clearly organized and the outline is helpful.

Kool made the course seem fun at first, but quickly became unlikeable. He recapped our midterm evals and said that he could not do any of our suggestions. He also told us that he took off questions from previous exams that everyone got right. PollEv is fine if you go to class. Slides' organization so confusing. Lectures get boring really quickly.

Cog Psych has a reputation of being a hard class with terrible professors. With that in mind, Kool is a solid choice. As a lecturer, he goes fast and is a bit on the confusing side but this was his 1st time ever teaching and he improved a lot during the semester. I found the difficulty of his tests to be in line with other WU psych courses.

Really enjoyed this ballet class. Dancers are held to a certain level, so do read the syllabus and/or send her an email if you are unsure of which ballet level to take (she was very helpful over the summer when I was trying to fit a ballet class into my schedule) I definitely saw my technique improve over the semester... good experience overall!

I thought Christine was a wonderful ballet teacher!  She was able to strike a perfect balance between the strictness required for ballet, and the sweetness to make the class enjoyable.  She gives individualized attention even in large classes.  Highly recommended!
She is a very tough grader.  Only the very best dancers get A's.  When she is in a bad mood, watch out!
Will not look at you when asking her a question. Can also be incredibly unapproachable once she has made up her mind about you.

Christine is an excellent ballet teacher - she goes in sequential order with the steps and is very clear in explaining what your body needs to do with each movement. She gives us ample practice and does some body conditioning as well. Written work is pretty easy. I highly recommend this class.

Great Professor, especially for a more niche course like philosophical logic. Extremely approachable -- if you ever have any concerns about the course, I'd honestly just recommend chatting with him about them. I did so myself, and he was very receptive and accommodating. Lectures are engaging and course structure is unique but reasonable.

Rather nice man. Receptive to ideas. Unpretentious. And he treats his student with an unusual sense of dignity and often engages in the discussion over the idea itself. Democratic equality at its best.

Nic is a great prof, and introduction to philosophy. I took Business Ethics (234) with him, and had a great semester. He has 100% attendance requirements but any email ahead of time can get excused. He really cares about the topic, and is willing to talk about it. He clearly loves philosophy and is excited to get people talking. Great readings too

Nic is a goat. Philosophy isn't my main area of study, so taking a class offers a new perspective and environment compared to my other courses. He has a good sense of humor and is a genuine person who is both smart and caring. I would highly recommend taking at least one class with him during your time at WashU and getting to know him.

Dr. K is so understanding and patient. Even though attendance was mandatory and I didn't show up a lot of the time he never held it against me and was super kind about it. As long as you put effort into the class you will get a good grade.

Dude is just a 10/10 chiller. Don't get me wrong, great philosophers is not a class I enjoy, but Dr. K makes up for it. I had some really important meetings I needed to attend during class hours, and he was super understanding - something I can't say for others. I love this guy even if his class isn't my thing.

Business Ethics was by far my favorite class that i've taken. All the readings were super interesting and the workload was very easy. A quiz before every class but graded on completion, 2 short essay exams(notes/readings allowed), and 1 short paper. It's a fascinating topic and he makes discussion flow very smoothly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nic is a fun lecturer that makes class pretty engaging. The class (business ethics) was very chill, but attendance is required.

Good at philosophy, but would talk for an extended period. The course was very disorganized, and he changed the grading requirements a few times. He's a kind person, and holds great office hours, but has really weird paper requirements. His style is unique, which could be good or bad depending on the person. Overall, good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As my first philosophy course, I wasn't ready for the density of the material, but his explanations made the class possible for me. Without him walking us through each reading from before the class, I would not have gotten an A. The amount of reading tended to fluctuate, but it got harder as the semester went on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gives huge mansplainer vibes and definitely loves the sound of his own voice. But, at the same time, very thoughtful and intelligent. Also very kind and understanding.

I cannot say enough good things about Professor Koziolek. He is absolutely brilliant, but what truly sets him apart is the way he runs his class; he encourages us to openly embrace our mistakes, and is very humble in encouraging us to question and doubt the things he says. Highly recommend taking a class of his during your time at WashU.

Prof. Koziolek was a really great teacher and an interesting lecturer. The class grade depended heavily on essays, with a little bit for participation. There were quizzes on each reading, but they were graded on completion. I highly recommend going to him about the essays since they are such a big part of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best prof I've ever had. He cares about each individual student, is exceptionally kind and understanding, and facilitates learning in a non-stressful way. He's wonderfully human in the way that he understands and relates to students, creating a safe space. Not to mention absolutely brilliant. I love the guy and you'd be lucky to learn from him:)
Fantastic lecturer, extremely knowledgable, hilarious person. Talk with him outside of class just to hear what he has to sayyou will not regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nic is a super cool guy. Go to office hours - discussing things w/ him 1-on-1 is wonderful. Is very well read in philosophy and will engage you on the readings. You could probably not read in-depth and still do fine, but reading carefully made the class more engaging. Lectures can be dry sometimes, but the concepts covered are all interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Nice on teaching and grading

Professor Dan knew the material very well and was able to convey concepts learned within the course by using personal experience. He is also open to answering and clarifying questions on issues you may have during amd after each lesson.
Best person and professor ever meet! He has professional knowledge and is also a really nice person. He is very kind and friendly. Love him.
Would definitely recommend him.
Mainly group assignments with only little individual work. Good professor!
Dan has a really good teaching skill and he arrange this course and give the grade very well.
Dan is definitely one of my favorite instructors at WashU, he's easygoing and always welcomed to help. Highly recommend his class!

The teaching style worked well for me. I struggled a bit during the semester, but the professor helped me understand the material clearly when I needed help. I enjoyed being able to discuss the subject during class as an open discussion. Professor is great and I would definitely take a class taught by him again!

She is an incredibly dedicated professor who genuinely cares about her students and provides valuable, constructive feedback. She stands out as one of the top professors I've had the privilege of learning from in the Sam Fox School.

Very approachable in class, but did not give explicit critique feedback for our 2nd project and 3rd (the final) grades. Tight deadlines (e.g. 2 days), heavy assignments (e.g. have ## of iterations). The class structure depended on Becca's feedback. Becca and our TA gave 1-1 or small group feedback but sometimes ran out of time due to ~18 students.

Becca was a great, talented, and knowledgeable professor who made classes enjoyable. My only complaint was how much work was expected of us in the second half of the semester, when the workload increased quite a bit with little time. It was very stressful to manage with other classes, but I would definitely take a class with her again.
SHE IS HANDS DOWN MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR IN SFS. Her feedback is always practical and helpful; I learnt a lot from her class. She's also very caring too.

Becca is amazing! She is so nice and approachable. You will spend a lot of class time working on the projects and she is always walking around to answer questions and give feedback. She cares a lot about process work, so this is very beneficial. She also pays special attention to craft. Overall, I found her grading to be fair, if not on easier.

I love Becca! She gives really constructive feedback, and I've grown so much from her class. She's a pro in type and you'll learn a lot as a designer. She's a little tough in grading and ask a lot from students, but it's because she wants you to develop and grow. She values process more than result, so if you work hard you'll do just fine.
Really good feedback and also really nice
a great professor is knowledgeable and helpful.

Michael Koby is a respected professor,  prolific writer of law review articles and is currently Associate Dean for Graduate and International students at Washington  University in St. Louis School of Law. He is a rare and inspiring type of professor that raises the bar in legal research
Excellent professor! I would definitely take him again.
great person and professor
Prof. Koby is the best professor I have ever had.

very helpful- a million times better than most legal writing professors, who teach some ridiculous formula because it's too difficult to convey how to write well- I was very lucky to have had Koby instead
No Comments
No Comments

I could not recommend avoiding Dr. Wyckoff more. Sincerely one of the worst professors I've dealt with. Lacks any amount of clarity on assignment expectations and shows little to no interest in students' success or even course material. Lectures are boring and often useless as she reads directly from slide decks. Surprised she was hired, honestly.

The workload is a bit much, but the class is structured well and they are truly an amazing professor who cares about their students. These reviews are old, Dr. Wyckoff is both incredibly organized and knowledgeable on Water Resources; I never had them for Thermo but every prof for that class gets hate. If you prepare for exams, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really wanted to give them the benefit of the doubt, but things just kept getting worse. I have taken other courses (required) with content I was hoping/expecting they would be more knowledgeable in. However, they did not improve in their performance as a professor. They could not explain any core EECE concepts. Don't recommend :(

Extremely disorganized lectures. Unable to explain any ideas in class, making everyone confused. The problems on recitation and quizzes never reflect what they were taught during the lecture. Be prepared to teach yourself as you might be more knowledgeable than Dr. Wyckoff. This professor is definitely the worst of all in the EECE department.

I understand she came into WashU right before the semester started, but she still could have been better prepared. I seriously don't know how she got hired. The class was a mess. She didn't even know the material and couldn't read her notes or answer students' questions, which is the number 1 responsibility of a prof. AVOID AT ALL COST!

Worse professor I have ever had in my academic career and that is not an exaggeration. I'm not exactly sure how she got hired by EECE department at Washu, as she does not perform nearly as well as the other educators. She is scattered and all over the place. Her teaching style shows she does not care about the students learning. Self Taught class.

She is very nice and we understand this is her first semester at WashU, but this class was kind of a mess. She copies lecture notes incorrectly from the textbook and is not qualified to answer questions from students. She says attendance to recitation is optional, but they count towards your grade. She could improve by knowing the material better.
Takes off points for everything and anything on quizzes. If you love partial credit DO NOT TAKE.
Shes nice but simply does not know the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Better off reading the textbook on your own.

This is her first semester at WashU from teaching at UT and our class is severely underwhelmed. Imagine a professor whose teaching style is copying/reading things incorrectly from the textbook, and when you question a method or equation, getting sassed back or denied an answer. Not very available outside of class.
Hard but good. Fun!
Great prof, very

Shreyas demands a lot from her students but only because she wants them to succeed. Her workload can be A LOT (like "I want to scream cry and throw up" a lot) and she can be very honest in her feedback sometimes, but it's definitely helped me challenge myself more as an artist than I would have without her instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Shreyas is definitely one of the most intense design professors I've ever had BUT I grew so much as a result of her class. Her classes are hard because she knows what she's doing -- rarely will she give you work without reason. She doesn't give much feedback in the moment -- most feedback is from peers in crit. Difficult class but so so worth it.

Shreyas is one of the hardest teachers but in the best way possible. She is amazing artist and wants you to excel at what you do. It may come off as rude but she wants to see your best work and knows when you're not actually trying. She pushes you for your best and that's very appreciated when some professors in Sam Fox will baby you a little.
Shreyas is fun and inspirational. She can be somewhat demanding sometimes, but that's how she pushes you to learn.
Passionate, but not so caring. Well-known tough grader. Some people love her but some people find her rude.
Krone is a great person, and is so caring and kind, but his lectures probably won't teach you anything. Luckily there are no exams and labs are participation based, making this class very easy.

Prof. Krone is an amazing person. He's caring, fun, and entertaining. However, his lecture style leaves much to be desired. For someone learning statistics for the first time, his lectures are very rushed and he primarily just reads off a google doc. He teaches like you already know the jargon, which makes interpreting his lectures challenging.
Prof. Krone is a pretty decent professor with chill vibes. Not a lot to be said a bout a 1-credit engineering ethics & sustainability class; just do the work and you'll be fine.

The whole class is designed very poorly. Prof. Krone does not have real appreciation of St. Louis community nor engineering ethics. Instead, the assignments are busy work that doesn't make any sense. They are formal rather than practical, and Prof. Krone does not tend to solve this issue, making the course a suffering and hypocritical absurdity.

Prof Krone was very charasmatic, which definitely helped keep me engaged with all the jargon and technical terms involved in Stats, it could get a little dry and boring sometimes. Very understanding. Sometimes, he sits in awkward silence until someone answers his very obvious question. Not a very exciting class but not too hard either.

Professor Krone is decent. It's really easy to get an A if you get help at office hours. Krone is understanding and will let you submit work late if you have an excuse. This semester, he incorporated AI into assignments, which I felt hindered my learning. Not the best professor, but not the worst.

I feel like Krone gets a bad rep since people aren't willing to put in effort to actually try to learn. Lectures can be fast, but he always reexplains things if you ask, and there's tons of help at OH. Homework/projects are graded on accuracy, but again OH is super helpful. Also, the class is based in R so it's nice to have some coding experience.

Very nice person, bad teaching style. In a big lecture room, he just reads off of a sub-adequate word document and expects us to keep up and understand. The concepts taught are incredibly important for research, but he doesn't make it clear at all. Also hard to find material to help supplement the lack of learning on the internet.

This class should be renamed "History & Race in St Louis". Easy, boring, and I didn't learn anything worthwhile. You also get assigned a 1-semester co-op, which is a wildcard in terms of difficulty, time commitment, and relevance. The class has political undertones &the instructor didn't make me feel comfortable enough to share my dissenting views.

I have taken 4 classes with Krone now and I wish I could take more. I have had a few good profs at washu and he is absolutely one of the best. Prof Krone is so dedicated to improving the lives of students and the quality of our education at Mckelvey. You can tell he really cares. The world would be a better place w more educators like him!

This class is a joke. The professor didn't show up or left early half the time despite meeting only once per week. Krone's classroom policies and attitude give the impression that he doesn't trust his students or treat them as equals. The assignments are all meaningless busy work which makes sense bc the course doesn't teach you anything useful.
I hate statistics but I love Krone. Super funny and understanding. Projects are tough but go to his office hours and you'll be fine.

There are no exams in the class, just homework and projects which accurately reflect the lecture notes/labs. Office hours and the TAs are very helpful. Krone is super understanding and cares about his students-  he is accommodating to personal circumstances and tries hard to make class fun

Lectures can sometimes be a little fast-paced but example problems in the notes help to solidify concepts. Weekly homework can be a little tricky but you are allowed to collaborate with friends and office hours are extremely helpful. Take-home assessments can take a while to complete but if you have a good grasp on the material you should be fine.

Prof. Krone is not a good lecturer because his class is really boring and not helpful compared to his notes. However, he set the class in a proper difficulty level that matches to the lecture: there are no exams! An easy A professor and doesn't create difficulty on student's grades, but there won't be much knowledge one could gain from his class.
Professor Krone is very kind and caring. His class is also very interesting and the assignments are useful. He does not waste time with busy work. I enjoyed the class.

I heard that krone had bad rate my professor reviews and I was so hurt. I took prob stat fall 19 and I still rave about this man. He really wants his students to succeed so if you show effort and that you want to learn he will really try his best to help you. Do NOT be afraid to go to his office hours! He's super friendly and approachable.

I took Professor Krone's ethics class in FL2020 and found it very enjoyable w/ interesting content discussed. The class itself is only 1 unit, so it's not much work and you can actually get a lot of it done ahead of time. Lots of EC (related to the 2020 election) and super easy grading. Good to pair with a heavier schedule as a WashU student.

If you put in the effort to succeed, Professor Krone will help you succeed. Based on past reviews, it seems like his lectures have improved. This spring, he filled class time with helpful examples. You have to go to lecture to learn the material, but TA's help immensely with homework and practice tests are similar to the exams.

Professor Krone is a great guy, very accessible outside of class and his tests and homework are relatively easy compared to other 300-level engineering courses. Definitely would take again. Lectures are not the most interesting but this is made up for with overall ease of material in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Krone just copies a ton of writing off a piece of paper. He does not explain any concepts in a way that is understandable. Very hard to follow his class notes and his explanations are not clear. The class is not easy either. You have to teach yourself everything. Would not recommend this professor.

Very unorganized, lectures are just him reading off a piece of paper and then writing it on the board as the students write silently. Horrible at answering questions asked by students. Be prepared to teach most of this material to yourself, because you'll learn more by self teaching in 3 days than you will from going to his lectures for 5 weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures were very fast and he barely went over details. He just wrote examples and never elaborated them. He stood in front of what he wrote, so it was hard to take notes during lectures. On the other hand, his exams were very easy, and the textbook for the class is very helpful. You could do well in the class just by reading the textbook.

His lectures go by stupidly fast and are pretty hard to pay attention in (so if your calculus is not very strong, you WILL suffer). If you can't keep up with his lectures, try to use the textbook-he wrote it, and his lectures tend to pretty much just be a copy of his textbook sections. However, his understanding of the content is second-to-none.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are so bad

Avoid taking any course with Krantz at all costs. He may be a great mathematician but a horrible teacher. You can cheese the exams really easily but don't expect to actually learn anything. Most days he ends class early, stands in front of the board, and writes extremely small. He doesn't care about his students at all.

Krantz is passionate about differential equations and math as subject. He is generous when grading exams and homework, but that is unfortunately a necessity. Krantz's lectures are paced too quickly and he frequently stands in front of the bord he is writing on, not allowing to you so take notes until he's already moved on to the next section.

Krantz class is very straight forward. His lectures are very example heavy which is amazing. He isn't the most elaborate lecturer but it suffices. His exams are near identical to the practice and aren't difficult. The homework isn't too much and it covers most everything you'll need to know for exams plus some. Try and you'll succeed.

Besides being a quite potent form of anesthesia, Krantz is extremely quiet when lecturing and writes very small on the board, making it impossible to glean any information whatsoever from lecture. But he sticks to the textbook pretty well, so just read that instead of going to class.

I took Professor Krantz's Math 310 in 2018, and he was very nice and easy, but Complex Variables is a mess. He teaches rigorous complex analysis so fast and vague that nobody could follow his writing on the board, and he breaks his "tradition" of easy exams by a tricky final that is very different from all the practices. I learned very few math.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is no class at all. 5 min recorded audio for each lecture reading through his crappy lecture slides in a speed so fast that 0.5x won’t help you. Spend 15 min in “lecture” and 1 hour in hw, and you pass with A.
My message is simple: if you have to take Calculus I as a major requirement but do not like Calculus and want to get good grades, take Calculus I Extended with Professor Steven Krantz.
Exams are not hard if you've taken the practice tests, and genuinely cares for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If he's teaching 233 or 310 or anything, just go for it. You would not regret

Lectures are a little boring and moves pretty fast. Could probably just skip lecture and read the textbook as he copies his lectures straight out of the book. Funny guy though and his exams are carbon copies of the practice exam so its easy to get a good grade

Professor Krantz made calc 3 easy to learn by presenting it in understandable and bite sized portions. In addition, he often told fun and or hysterical stories about his past life or made quips in class. He was frugal with time and often ended 15 or so min early. Take Calc 3 with him if you can! It made math fun again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Krantz is honestly amazing. His lecture pace is perfect because he only tells you what you need to know. He regularly lets class out early because he's so efficient with time. Sometimes he will bless you with a joke or story. Also, his test never have surprises so if you go to class you're pretty much guaranteed an A.

Amazing teacher and very understandable and smart.  He always randomly gives us a 1-2 minute joke in the middle of lecture and is ready to answer any questions.  In order to do well on his exams just a simple run through of the practice exam will suffice.  He get's right to the point without any fluff, meaning class is usually let out in 45 minutes

Professor Krantz is a wonderful and brilliant professor -- he is extremely funny, and his exams are pretty easy as long as you pay attention in lecture.   His grading is generous.  He seems to really connect with the students.

Great teacher! Admittedly I would get lost in the lectures, as he is incredibly smart, but I wrote it all down and, come test time, I realized that I knew everything that was asked on an exam. Very reasonable exams and very helpful in office hours
Great lectures while also being one of the smartest professors here. Gives very reasonable tests. If you have the chance take his class

Really great prof! Lectures were interesting and engaging. Not really the warmest prof ever, kind of brutishly funny. Homeworks got to be incredibly difficult, but exams were ridiculously easy because he was just looking to see that you know the very basics (and he means it). Would definitely take another class with Krantz.
Great Professor, hilarious too. Best I've had at WUSTL.

Homework was longer and more difficult, but on the exams he really wanted to make sure you understood the fundamentals. He also told a lot of funny side stories in class, but they didn't take too much class time either. Everything was explained well, with theory first and simple examples afterwards.
Funny lecturer with interesting stories, can seem rude at times in class, but really a good teacher.

His class was structured very well. He built up each concept from an intuitive way to think about it to the formal, rigorous approach, with many examples along the way. He sometimes came off as a bit full of himself, even condescending. The midterms were fairly easy, but the final was harder.

Steve Krantz is awesome! He explains things really well - describing them abstractly, then using examples to make them more concrete. He thoroughly prepares you for exams. His amusing stories are certainly a plus when you have class at 9 in the morning. Definitly one of my favorite professors ;)
He is a great teacher!  Also, his jokes are quite possibly the funniest I have ever heard from anyone.  He really tries to keep you interested, and he is very intelligent!

Dry material but he has presents the material in a way that I haven't asleep yet.  Course itself can be tough, with some tricky concepts.  But he has canceled class many times in order to give students a break! Likes to joke about himself.  Exams are doable.  He tells you exactly the material to be covered on the exam.
Krantz is a great professor.  Makes a hard class much easier.  EXTREMELY flexible with homework, tests, etc.  Take the writing section if you can.

I had Dr. Krantz in the early 90s and he was hands down the best professor at Wash U.  He made Dif EQ easy to understand and told stories in class to keep our interest.  He is one of the best teachers I have ever had anywhere!  Thanks Dr. Krantz!!

Amazing professor!! I have taken all of the classes he offers, and he makes them all incredibly interesting (even while tackling tough topics). Amazing mentor and lecturer, he really cares about his students.
Professor Kundel is great!
Professor mad a very difficult topic incredibly accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's an awesome teacher and makes sure his students know the material. Amazing mentor and makes the topics he teaches even more interesting. His class is fun and focused on problem solving not boring lectures so that you can easily get a deeper understanding of the topics.

Professor Kundel is seriously the best. He makes an effort to eliminate the stressful nature of most science courses and gives students a real chance to learn in a healthy environment. He is super accommodating and caring. It really feels like he is rooting for the success of all of his students. You MUST take a course with him!

Most wonderful guy!!! So smart and willing to help, explains every concept without making you feel stupid. Such a personable guy who truly cares about his students, learning all of our names. Class format is lectures posted online, in-class: activities/clarification of material. Take this class! Midterms are straightforward.

Kundel is a good professor and he cares about his students. I think sometimes he can be unreachable which is frustrating, but overall he is a decent professor. I really enjoyed his lectures and found the content he taught to be very digestible.

One of the best professors I have had. Makes the class very enjoyable and all the grading is very fair and allows for mistakes. Exams ask detailed questions but if you are familiar with the material you will do well. Overall great and if you have to take a bio class as a requirement I would choose his class.

Dr. Kundel is a great lecturer, and honestly makes the course extremely enjoyable. He himself explains concepts clearly and is readily available outside of class for the 100's of questions that come up during the timeline of this course, especially considering the copious amounts of writing. Grading is often unclear sometimes, but the class is fun
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Combined with a great lecturing style, Kundel's slides digestibly break down content in a detailed and pattern-focused manner. Grading is fair, tests not too bad. Take home quizzes every other Thursday similar to Gen Bio, but easier. Some EC given. When one lecture didn't record properly, he went out of his way to re-record the lecture offline.

Dr. Kundel is by far one of the best professors at WashU. He is incredibly kind, knowledgeable, and gracious. Bio 1500 was just challenging enough to push me, but not so hard that it caused panic. His class structure is very clear and efficient, and his exams come straight out of his lectures and the practice exams he distributes before.

One of my favorite classes at WashU! Dr. Kundel is exceptionally caring and creates a uniquely supportive environment for exploring and learning even with challenging material. This class is very hands-on and time-intensive, but Mitch is with you every step of the way. Be aware that grading criteria for papers can be pretty vague though.

PCS is one of the easiest Bio classes at WashU, quizzes and exams are pretty easy (averages on both allowed you to get an A provided you completed extra credit survey, problem sets and poll everywhere). No HW, lots of extra credit, and problem sets had unlimited attempts so if you messed up you could just resubmit.

Best professor hands down. Made every concept super clear and easily digestable. There is alot of content but if you take it piece by piece and study a little bit everyday--golden. He was extremely kind, so passionate to help people learn, and very accessible within and outside the classroom.

PCS is definitely content heavy, but Kundel made it easy to get help outside of class and succeed in the course. Definitely take a class with him before you leave WashU. He is passionate about biology and an engaging lecturer.

Dr. Kundel is an amazing professor who changed PCS for the better. The class is super chill, which makes learning the content less stressful and more enjoyable. Exams were fair. Extra Credit is given. 92+ is an A.

Took Molecular Biology of Genetic Disease. If you don't watch the lectures outside of class, you are screwed, but they are only 20 min and help guide you through the class. He is a great teacher and super understanding for extensions. AI's are actually clueless tho.
Awesome lecturer, really cares about his students! 1500 is easy if you are willing o put in effort.
Awesome professor and really caring guy who genuinely cares about the well-being of students. Lectures are great too and it is an overall great introduction to biology.
Really nice guy. I would definitely take his course again.
Take his class! super nice lecturer and grading
Really nice guy, grading is tough, and the AIs are clueless. I could really see me and him being friends outside the classroom, he's super approachable.
Love Kundel; he is approachable, excited to teach! I would go to him for questions about biology lecture.

Easy going and great at breaking down the course material. Tests and quizzes match exactly the content in class, so as long as you put in the work by watching lectures and participating in class, you will do just fine.
Great introductory bio course with a great bio professor!

Great professor. Would take again, he is very accessible outside of class and I was usually the only one at office hours! Biology is challenging for me but he explained things without making me feel stupid and I appreciate that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: he gives lectures that you have to watch before class which explains everything clearly, then opens discussion in class to clear up any remaining questions. You can also set up office hours with him on zoom or in person, which was really helpful to me. But don't rely on anything last minute, sometimes he takes a bit to respond :D

An interesting class that is not a huge stressor grade wise. Well structured so due dates were very clear. Kundel is a very nice professor that actually enjoys what he is teaching. Sometimes a hard/picky grader but manageable.
Very helpful during class and was very approachable. Was a difficult grader but provided good feedback. The class material was very challenging but he did a great job being accessible to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mitch is the best. He's super helpful and explains things well in lab. I wish I had room to take more classes with him :(

Dr. Kundel is an amazing lab instructor. He truly cares about how his students are doing, and is more than willing to meet outside of class to discuss either lab material or lecture material. He is super helpful in lab, funny, and an overall great professor. If you can take his lab section, do it-I can't recommend him enough!
Kundel rocks. Super nice guy who loves teaching and cares about his students. He actually wants his students to learn, rather than just perform for tests. Glad I took his lab section.

Dr. Kundel taught my 2960 lab section and he did a great job. His lab lectures were clear and he was good at fielding questions clearly. He also checked in with each group several times making sure things were going well, which was nice.
Dr. Kundel is an amazing person. He is a great teacher and really cares about his students. I really enjoyed the classes he taught. 10/10

Not a class for the faint of heart. Tons of notes, and in my opinion the homework was loosely related to the exam material at best. Still, I found his lectures interesting, though not always the easiest to follow. Really nice guy, happy to explain stuff in class. If you already like astronomy I'd recommend, otherwise I'd pass.

Nice guy but not a good experience with the class. Took it on a whim because I thought it would be easy or entertaining. Lectures were so boring and hard to follow. No engagement with class. If you love solar system you might not mind this class but don't take it just for fun. I will say it seems hard at first but surprisingly easy to get an A.
You were the best! I loved taking your class and he is the best professor I've ever had!
Great Professor! One of the most empathetic and engaged professors I've had so far

Nice guy who's very knowledgable and the class is very interesting. Took class for NSM requirement. barely any homework and it's not graded harshly, but tests are the issue. The midterm and final both ask many extremely detailed and insignificant facts that he'll mention once in class and youre expected to memorize random planet densitites.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: genuinely so much better than hafer but still not all that. 2960 is a lot of memorization and not that difficult but just SO much content for each exam. its doable but hafer and kunkel do not make it any easier.
Good bio prof

read directly off slides and was not engaging. barely went to any lectures and was able to do fine by cramming every lecture slide on a cheat sheet. exams are needlessly wordy, complicated, and harshly graded. curriculum based entirely on memorization without understanding.

Kunkel clearly likes biology, which makes a world of difference when she is teaching instead of Hafer. She also doesn't read verbatim from the slides, which is nice, as it makes the class more interactive. She is rather caring and can generally answer people's questions, which is great.

No idea why her ratings are so high. She is unclear, moves extremely quickly through material, simply reads off the slides, and will have you leaving class knowing almost nothing more than you came in with. If you haven't taken bio in a while, this class is going to suck. Very difficult to take notes by hand, thanks to the bombardment of slidedecks

I found that Kunkel cared about what was being taught and that made her lectures enjoyable enough. She taught rather quickly, in my opinion, but doing the study guides and practice quizzes help get me up to speed.

I'll start with the positive. Dr. Kunkel is nice to her students. now for the negatives. In the lectures she mostly reads off of a powerpoint and it is very difficult to stay engaged during them. Grading of exams is awful and as they are worded horrendously, also asking clarifying question is not helpful. The exam average is around a C-.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The Bio 2960 lecture professors are both kind, but they just throw information at you and hope you can work enough outside of class to understand it further. Exams are fair and straightforward.
Kunkel is nicer than Hafer and seems much more approachable. She has no authority in class however and does not know how to teach a big class like 2960.

Dr. Kunkel is a very sweet person and cares about her students. However, she simply reads off the content heavy slides and doesn't explain much. This means you have to teach yourself some tricky concepts. She is active on Piazza and answers questions there in a helpful way though. Class itself can be hard, but taking AP/IB bio makes it a lot better

Really fast paced lectures, but that's not her fault; there is a lot of material to cover in Bio2960. I didn't take any high school bio, so this class has been an insane amount of work. She is very accommodating, clear, and logical. She cares a lot about her students. If you don't have any background in bio, get ready for a GRIND.

Not the best lecturer but so much better and nicer than Prof Hafer. When she can't answer a student's question (which is honestly frequent) she owns up to it and offers to look into it after class. Don't buy the textbook it's unnecessary. Class is memorization-heavy but if you take good notes you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: kunkel such a kind person. if she doesn't know the answer to a question, she'll be honest about it. very helpful during office hours and makes sure you understand the concepts. i loved her lectures because they were always very clear
Loved her as a bio professor! She always answers questions in a non-judgmental manner, and she explains the course content really well.

I vividly remember the first day of classwith palms sweating, heart racing, tears dripping down my red, blustery faceof having to stand up in the 370 seat Wrighton 100 lecture hall, everyone standing up, carrying out the biological ethics oath. Though nervous of messing up the oath, I didnt; The dna gel electrophoresis was mine now. Good prof.

Professor Kunkel is very nice. Her teaching style is clear compared to her co-lecturer, Professor Hafer. This class very test heavy. Also, you do NOT need to buy the book. You do not need to read in order to pass the class. Notes from the class are sufficient.

She explains stuff really well especially compared to everyone else that taught that class along with her. Her slides were easy to follow and in a logical order and she explained everything very thoroughly. I understood the parts of the class that she taught the best and was always relieved when it would be her turn to teach
She is very very sassy and honestly kind of mean. Hard to get help in office hours because she is not willing to explain things twice. Very boring
Make general biology very boring, but she tries (tries!) to be exciting. The material is very difficult and memorization heavy. Think 5x AP biology.  Clickers are useless (don't bother)

Plant Bio and Genetic Engineering is a great class, and I really can't recommend it enough if you like plants and genetics at all. The lectures are very clear, though sometimes a little repetitive (you will draw many many constructs). Just enough work.
