This has been the worst class I have taken at Wash U. Kunkel is a TERRIBLE teacher, and she takes a class with very interesting material and ruins it. Do not take this class. Everyone that sat around me also thought it was a terrible class. Trust me, its awful.

I'm a junior, and she's probably the best bio professor I've had so far at WU.  The first third of the course was just basic plant physiology and that wasn't really my thing, but after that the genetic engineering stuff gets very interesting.  Word of caution: some people take this class thinking it will be easier than other bio courses.  It isn't.
Very helpful and clear, not a class for people who are uniterested or ambivilent about plants

Such a nice teacher. She is really caring, and loves the subject she teaches. I highly recommend this class to anyone who has not thought about plant biology. I love animal physiology, but this class makes plants very interesting. The presentations at the end are really neat too.
plant bio is amazing. such a fun class. so useful. very well taught. take it and brave new crops (anthro)--that should be a cluster
Very helpful, explained things very well and made it easy to remember them.

Kurenok is not a great lecturer, he often covers dense and complex material in an even more complicated way. Despite that shortcoming, he is a fantastic professor. He is knowledgeable and accessible and truly wants his students to learn. His exams are graded generously, and he is a kind person. If you are lucky, he may even drop personal lore.
Very nice and kind professor and very High Score! A+!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class covers a lot of very tough material at a pretty fast pace. Kurenok's lecture notes are very well put together, but he's not very good at presenting those lecture notes in class. However, he is very knowledgeable about what he teaches and is good at answering clarifying questions. Exams are all take-home and graded VERY generously.
His lectures are not easy to follow, but he is always willing to help and guide you through the problem after class.

Professor Kurenok's lectures aren't the clearest, but he will spend plenty of time after class clarifying any points of confusion you may have. The homework prepares you well for the midterms; the difficulty of both is fair & gives you good amounts of practice with useful complex variables techniques. The class policies are transparent.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kurenok is very knowledgeable, friendly, and caring. His accent is not nearly as strong as people make it out to be. His lectures are engaging- he doesn't just write on the board or read off slides he explains the concepts well and gives good examples. His exams and assignments are fair and he is very easy to reach if you have questions.

He's so nice to his students. I once went to his office hour and it was about to end. He explained equations to me until I fully understood. At that time the office hour had past for almost half and hour. He's not native speaker so he has strong accent. However, his lecture note is super clear. He's my favorite professor.
Excellent Course!

Kurenok is a good person and an ok teacher. I can feel he likes teaching and cares about the students, though he might not be able to explain some concepts well. He has a relatively strong accent, but I'm not a native speaker and I have no problem understanding him after a week or two. Homework and exams are fair. No tricks.

Good Luck. The lecture notes are written as if you're on year 3 of your dissertation. Unless you dream of dealing with heavy heavy notation with little practicality along with homework that isn't applicable to what is going on in the class, then you're in for a treat.

He is bad at explaining. His pronunciation makes it even harder to understand. But he is nice. He tries to explain it thoroughly(tho not good) and cares about students. His exams and homework are very fair- it just asks whether u understood the basic concept or not. no big twists. Also altho his lectures are bad his lecture notes are great&clear
Really enjoyed the class it. It was definitely an easy A and he did a good job explaining concepts/giving fair exams that reflected the covered material.
Prof. Kurenok is very knowledgeable and a good teacher, but he seems to be unsure of his teaching sometimes. Tests were mostly fair, homeworks as well.

Vladimir is the professor to take if you care more about getting good grades than learning new things. His lectures are confusing, and his thick accent doesn't help. But partial credit is extremely generous, and his typed lecture notes are huge. You can often find him in his office, but getting help at office hours is usually only halfway helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He really wants students to exceed in his class, and makes a strong commitment to help you if you have difficulty understanding content. His accent can him a little tough to understand at times, but he provides clear written notes to supplement lecture. He is accessible and very helpful during his office hours, but his lectures can get confusing.

A pretty easy professor. He has a thick accent that you will need to get used to in the first few weeks. Office hours are usually very available but not always helpful. He is not the clearest instructor, but his lecture notes definitely help. If you show up to class and do the homework, you will get at least a B. Somewhat nice guy.

Professor is a nice guy, actually pretty adorable. He gives printed lecture notes before class, and doesn't take attendance. HOWEVER, his lectures are incredibly confusing. His accent is a bit difficult and he often confuses himself in lecture and does examples wrong. He also barely does any examples in class. He grades VERY easily though.

He really wants students to exceed in his class, and makes a strong commitment to help you if you have difficulty understanding content. His accent can him a little tough to understand at times, but he provides clear written notes to supplement lecture.
Very nice person. Lectures are not very clear, had to use book. But if you go to office hours he will explain things well. Exams were graded generously.

I really like him - he's a nice guy, passionate about math, adorable accent, tells funny stories, and gives life advice. I very much respect him, but his lectures do not do it for me at all - unclear, few examples, and he's not good at answering questions. I had to rely heavily on the book to understand the material. Graded the first 2 tests easily

Kurenok was a good guy. He was overall a very fair professor. If needed, go into to talk to him and he will be more than willing to offer help. While his accent may be difficult to understand, he will be more than happy to repeat himself if needed. Lectures can be dry, but looking at the book and past tests will guarantee at least a B+.
Kurenok was very helpful in answering questions in both class and office hours. Clear, well-paced, very fair exams and easy to do well if you pay attention in class and do the work.

He taught Stats for Engineers at UMSL and it was terrible.  He is hard to understand, gives poor notes, and doesn't understand student questions well enough to answer them.  My book was much more helpful that his lectures.  I tell all of my friends not to take his class.  Seems like a nice guy, but I didn't like his teaching style or communication.

I never went to class because I realized that he posted notes online and the notes online were better than the notes he wrote in class. I bet a lot of people realized this. Then he got mad and increased the difficulty of the exams because we all stopped going to class. He is very hard to understand. I think I made the right move.
Hard to understand in class and in person. Shows easiest problems in class and assigns hardest problems for homework. Tests follow hw's pretty consistently.

Prob Stats for Engineers is a pretty easy class and Kurenok seems like a nice guy, but I had a tough time understanding him.  Towards the end of the semester I just stopped paying attention in class.  Tests aren't bad though.
He is a nice person, but his lectures are useless. He never writes anything out and reads screenshots from the textbook. He never answered questions clearly and would just ramble.

It's really hard, because I genuinely like Dr. Thoroughman! He is very smart, caring, and easy to talk to! However, he just is not the greatest lecturer. Also, the class is very easy which means students really don't have to put much effort into the class to get a good grade. They need to give more in person exams and HWs and make it more difficult

I don't think I actually fully learnt any new material in his class- reads off the textbook during lecture, doesn't explain things when we try to ask him questions, and the material covered in class doesn't prepare us for homeworks/midterm quiz/final exam at all.
The BME circuits class is a joke.

Returns 0 grades. Does not answer questions at all. Refuses to write anything on the board, not even working out problems. Lectures are disjointed, eclectic, and often irrelevant. Entire course based on a random professor's lecture notes from a different school- not even a BME class. Cool guy, really passionate, good lab section, otherwise not good

I was originally excited to take the new BME circuits course but was majorly disappointed once the class began. The lectures made no sense and left me more confused than ever before. No example problems were ever worked out in class, even though our final and homework consisted of working out problems. The grading is also ambiguous.

WORST PROFESSOR IVE EVER HAD. This man belongs in a research lab, not a classroom. Im sure he knows about circuits, but he has zero inability to pass that knowledge to anyone else. He also doesn't grade homework for months!! WashU needs to seriously reconsider his teaching position. Take ESE230 instead to actually learn something. Overall terrible.

Thoroughman is the absolute worst professor Ive ever had. He rambles on about things that arent related to the material, chastises students for not knowing things he didnt teach, and throws a full-on hissy fit if someone asks him for an example of what hes talking about. I am leaving BME because of this man, and I hope WashU fires him.
super hard class but thoroughman is a really great guy who wants the best for his students.

BME220 is a very interesting class. It gave me a new perspective on the college education system while giving me no new insight on circuits. We spend 80k to for a carbon copy of another professors website. Classes consist of rambling that nobody understands. When asked for examples he aggressively refuses and short circuits. Please do not take!!!!!

DONT TAKE BME 220. That class is a joke. Just take normal circuits. Thoroughman is very vague in his lectures. Honestly you could probably learn more by reading a textbook. He teaches entirely from a webpage from another professor from Harvey Mudd. The only time anyone actually learns anything is from the labs.

He teaches the brand new bme 220 class and is an actual disaster. He cant even come up with his own notes he stole a professor from Harvey Mudds notes and refuses to accept any criticism from the class. No body has any idea whats going on. Take normal circuits.

Intro to BME is a joke. The lectures do not matter. I have attended them all and none of them relate to the material on the test. The homework also has no correlation to the test. You go in and try to bs your way through the exam and hope he likes what you wrote down.
Such a hard class, but he knows it. He's not a bad guy, but this class is meant as a weed out class. He does care about students, the material is just insane for a freshman.

This class is hard because it is meant to be hard. Be sure to use the PST leaders as much as you can on the homework because you won't make progress without them. He guides you on what to study for exams. Pay attention to the things he repeats because they will be tested. This was my hardest class of the semester, but my far the most interesting.

The most energetic lecturer I've had.  Great at engaging students, very entertaining.  Brilliant and very passionate about his portion of QP.  He's helpful with specific questions and explains CLabs well.
previous post may be ironic; he did not hold any office hours and was very unhelpful.
Very animated professor. Not entirely understandable at all times but definitely very helpful outside of class. The class itself was challenging yet interesting. Got 4 credits to spare? Take BME301A!
Hard grader

Dean LaRose is a good professor, but the course leans far too heavily on group assignments that are ambiguously worded and graded as if by an invisible rubric known only to a higher power. The course setup makes it far too easy for freeloading group members to tank your grade while contributing little more than their ID to the final submission.

This course is a complete waste of time. The speakers range widely, but most were incredibly boring. Grading is very nitpicky, with little to no feedback provided, and is not released until late December. Your grade is a mystery. Grade scale is insane (>95 for an A). The case assignment is painful, with unclear expectations and group freeriders.

Awful. The assignment instructions are painfully unclear, yet her grading is extremely nitpicky. The speakers were monotonous and added nothing that wasn't covered in orientation. The "assignments" themselves were pointless busywork. The grading scale is absurd (92 is a B+), and with such unforgiving grading-earning an A (95) is nearly impossible.

Dean LaRose is a kind lady who is more than willing to answer any question and greets everyone with a smile every class. She brought interesting, enlightening professors to enrich and immerse students in the business curriculum. Attendance was mandatory as class was once per week, and participation points were deducted if you did not attend.

Amazing guy. Can't really go wrong between him and Woodhams but I'd probably choose Lake. Biggest difference is that Lake uses an iPad but Woodhams writes on the blackboard. 

He's very funny and nice, and he has a bunch of cool colors for his iPad. "Flipped lecture" format requires paying slightly more attention.

Solid professor, very kind and helpful and great at answering questions. The class itself uses a flipped classroom format with pre-lecture videos while synchronous class time is used for solving problems, but sometimes the in-class pace is a little too fast to keep up with. Make sure to make good use of Piazza and office hours.

Kind and funny. Class time is him going through example problems, all the learning is done through textbook readings asynchronously. Clear, not super difficult. TA'd for him and he was nice to work with.

Lake is a great instructor/lecturer. Lake cares about his students and makes sure that everyone understands what is going on as we solve example problems step-by-step in class. Lake always brings a positive attitude to class and I appreciate his sense of humor. He also brought us doughnuts and lets us pick the pen color! #GalaxyPen
He is soooooo nice!!!! We can choose pen color every class! The lecture is clearly and he is a really nice teacher that don't want any one gets a B.
amazing professor that genuinely cares about his students, the content can definitely be challenging but he makes it the easiest it can possibly be
Great professor. Theory lectures can get complex/tricky, but the course content as a whole is fairly understandable.

The hardest English class I have ever taken. This dude is a mega acedmic it is sometimes hard to even understand what he says while teaching because he uses such complex language. His assignments are overly hard and confusing. He is very very smart, but almost too smart for a basic college writing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Revard is highly passionate about his work and is accessible outside of class. Although his grading can be strict, the rubric is clear, and he is flexible on due dates for most assignments. Importantly, the course has a heavy workload. Dr. Revard is also very funny, even though he may initially seem intimidating.

Professor Revard is awesome. He definitely comes off as sarcastic and even a bit intimidating, but he is very passionate about what he does and genuinely wants his students to succeed. Revard is super funny and always has a new crazy story to tell at the start of each class. His course is not an easy A, but it will make you grow as a writer.
Very tough for a mandatory college writing course, but I really enjoyed Revard as a professor. Be prepared to have work due every class and receive harsh but helpful feedback.

I was not a fan of Dr. Revard. His tangents were bizarre; he would often delve into bizarre topics such as sex, paraphernalia and politics that had nothing to do with the course. Though his feedback on essays was good, he gave the class many "busywork" assignments that weren't helpful to class success. I would opt for a different professor…
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Revard is a phenomenal professor, he's funny and engaging. His assignments are very clearly defined and fairly graded. If you want to slack off in college writing, not the class for you, but this class will improve your writing a ton if you let it. Highly recommend!!
Funniest guy ever. Knows how to teach writing. Other reviews are for people who don't work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Revard is a great P&P professor but the class is pretty work-heavy. He gives clear grading criteria and as long as you follow it and put in the effort he will be harsh but give you a good grade. I never got anything under a 93 on any daily or major assignment. Definitely show up to office hours before submitting major assignments!!!!!

While his class was comparably more work than other CW classes, Professor Revard was a great writing professor who offered insightful advice and genuinely cared for his students. I felt intellectually challenged and stimulated by the essay prompts and readings. He also has a knack for entertaining the class with his crazy stories.

This guy had the craziest stories up his sleeve, from friends who did meth, growing pot in a closet, going to court with his mom, to standing in line at an ice cream store and figuring out your sexuality. Fun to talk and listen to, in terms of class management I felt CHALLENGED for what is a mandatory class everyone has to take, but you'll survive.

Revard is unlike any teacher I've ever had. He certainly makes class interesting with his humor and oddball stories. But more importantly he is a fantastic writing teacher. Place & Perspective is very challenging, but it has definitely made me a better writer, and I attribute this to Dr. Revard. Take his class, you won't regret it.
Great professor, definitely came out of his class a better writer but a very difficult grader.

Lawrence Revard is a hard-to-place person, but in the best way possible. He was relatable and hilarious, and would tell us stories about his past. He made classes quite entertaining, which is saying a lot for a college writing course. The work load is kinda heavy though with daily assignments, but with respect to papers, he gives great feedback.

Daily assignments can feel annoying but they're pretty low stakes. Do them and you'll get the 2-3 points they're worth. Quirky personality with very interesting life stories he'll randomly share. Essay writing felt like he gave you a thesis and if you used his recommendation, you'd do well. Otherwise...idk. A ton of work imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Revard gives lots of daily assignments that make this course seem like one of the more difficult College Writing classes. However, he gives good feedback, is very informed, tells interesting stories, and will undoubtedly make you a better writer.

Dr. Revard is a great college writing professor. He's very smart and will give you thorough feedback on your assignments. There are a lot of assignments, which can make it feel a little overwhelming at times, but it definitely makes you practice your writing constantly. Overall, I believe I am a better writer after this class and highly recommend!

Revard is an exceptionally interesting person, and while he may be snarky, he's still a good natured guy (with some wild stories too). His grades are tough but fair (revisions allowed), and classes are super chill discussions. If you're looking to coast through college writing avoid him, but if you want to become a better writer, he's your man.

Prof Revard is probably one of the most interesting professors I've had at WashU. Class time is almost always low-pressure discussion with him telling a random story about his life every 10 minutes - they're fun to listen to. Overall, Revard is super chill but he will push you to become a better writer. I'd recommend him 10/10 times. Great prof!
Great professor. Super funny tangents. Very fair grading and good feedback. Don't listen to ANY of these other reviews. He's great.

Revard is a very interesting man. A lot of strange stories at the beginning of class, some funny and others quite bewildering to say the least. I did eventually come around to him tho. Although there is a lot of work, he really does help and want your writing to get better. If you're ready to put the work in, I would recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Revard is interesting. Be ready to hear weird personal monologues out of nowhere, though he means well and can actually be funny at times. While there's basically a writing assignment each day, he does want to help you become a better writer. If you talk to him about it you'll get pretty solid advice. But I'd say find an easier Writing I class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher to have, if you dont have the same view as him expect a bad grade.

I've never had a more ridiculous time in an English course. This is supposed to be your introductory course to English so you can get it out of the way for your major, whatever that may be. The grading is devastating. If you're an avid writer by heart, he will still find ways to critique your work. He complains about published research papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Revard is a great professor with a funny sense of humor and a unique way of teaching college writing to his students. But I warn you, if you suck at writing you're screwed, he expects you to know basic writing skills and wants you to have good structure and citations. If you can write decent papers and take criticism, you'll do just fine with him.

Prof. Revard is definitely a hard professor; however, I recommend him unequivocally. He'll challenge you and make you a better writer. He'll work with you as much as you want. He'll tell you where you stand. If you put in the time and really get to know him, you'll reap the rewards. He is interesting, funny, and enjoyable. Don't drop this class.

This class is pretty challenging because Revard pushes you. This is not your typical high school English/writing class. Revard is really intelligent but can sometimes be confusing. He is also really hilarious. This class took me out of my comfort zone but it was honestly worth it.
A very underrated professor, his lectures are pretty funny and he does offer good insights for papers, he's quick to call out bs if he sees it. He was pretty understanding during this whole pandemic
Professor Revard is a great professor who made me not only a better writer but also a better thinker. His teachings on logical reasoning in research and writing are invaluable for me.
Do not take his class. He is completely vague and yet he expects you to perfectly meet his expectations. Switch out of his class as quickly as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you walk in on your first day of College Writing and see that Revard is your professor, switch out faster than you can say "Here!" during attendance. That's all I have to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very harsh grader, also very vague on his criteria for grading. Seems to value papers more on whether he agrees with your opinion than on any argumentative value. Avoid him if you can

Professor Revard does not care about his students at all as he will willingly criticize them in front of the whole class. Very disrespectful to the class and a harsh grader as well. AVOID him if you can!
smart and helpful man, but RUTHLESS grader, take my advice and STAY AWAY thank me later
I loved Professor Lai's class. He was very excited to teach and gave great lectures. The class was also pretty easy, though interesting.

Rutgers Criminal Justice Research Methods. CJ majors are not math focused individuals so the fact that this class was just a stats class in disguise was BS. Professor Lai is a very sweet man but he is not cut out for teaching CJ majors who have enough trouble with math as it is. Very disorganized, unclear lectures, poor assignment management

Dr. Lai is young, sweet, and pretty funny. Grade is very straightforward, 3 (easy) homeworks, PollEverywhere participation every class, and easy multiple choice exams (average is usually 90%). Can attend class on Zoom. Lots of content overlap with Consumer Behavior (FYI for marketing students), and similar to other psych classes.
Awesome course! Professor Lai was engaging and the workload was light. Take this class!
Very engaging lecturer and deepened my interest in social psych!
Doesnt seem to trust his students at all

so funny and entertaining!! uses funny/captivating examples to help us understand concepts. wants everyone to do well. textbook reading not necessary to do well, but supplemental readings show up on tests

He is the best teacher I have ever had at WashU. He is the kindest, most understanding professor and his lectures are consistently interesting. It would be a loss for students to graduate without ever taking one of his classes. He is the reason I want to major in psychology now. Take his class and you will forever be happy that you did.

I have never rated a professor here before, but I had to say something about Prof. Lai. He's so sweet and very understanding and compassionate, makes the lecture materials very easy and accessible and is incredible at answering questions. Definitely my favorite professor in my time at Washu, and he has made the online learning experience smooth.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best lecteurs at WashU. He explains the concepts well and made the class extremely interesting. His tests are fair and the class average is around 84%. Definitely take his class.

Dr. Lai is one of the BEST lecturers I have ever had. He breaks down really complex social psych concepts down so you understand every part of them. That said, his exams are absurdly hard. Take pass/fail if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite courses taken. Attendance not mandatory, all lecture PPTs are posted. No homework, grade based entirely on two midterms + final take home essay (but easy). Readings support class lectures but you can get all the material just from PPT without having to read. Super interesting topics, super kind and caring professor and AI's.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved the content of this class and Lester is a pretty good lecturer who uses cool real-world examples to keep things relevant & interesting. Exam grading was a bit confusing and at times inconsistent, but overall a good class.

2 in class essays and 1 take home final. There's around 50 topics per exam but she gives you 18 on the exam and you choose 6 to write about 4 sentences max. Graders were pretty nice, but you have to get at least an A on every exam to get an A- in the class. Just study the topic definitions. Attendance not mandatory
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GCM was one of my favorite classes in college. You need to study for exams but it is not too hard. Content was very interesting. I learned a lot about eating disorders.

Gender, Culture, and Madness was the most interesting class I have ever taken! I looked forward to her lectures and genuinely enjoyed the readings outside of class. She is well spoken, engaging, and clearly an expert at what she does.

Dr. Lester is a good prof because she is very knowledgeable in her professions. Besides that, the slides that she uses to present the material are quite not organized, and you need to try to reorganize yourself and put some effort into making a natural flow of what the content is about. The exams consist of all short answers and essay questions.

Gender, Culture, Madness was probably one of the most interesting classes I've taken. Her slides are created more as talking points for herself instead of notes to copy down. The class was based off of in-person short answer/essay exams that were graded pretty easily. Funny and interesting prof overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has definitely changed my perspective on mental illness and the health care system. Some pretty intense books were assigned that have made me feel things I never knew I was capable of feeling,  but I immensely enjoyed the classes, 95% of the time. Sometimes we'd have some historical lectures that were boring, but otherwise, it was fun!

I went to class maybe three times this semester. Lester read off her unorganized, unprofessional powerpoints, which she then posted on blackboard. Her papers were unreasonably long, but she told you exactly what to write, which is frustrating. That being said, I got an A without reading any books and studying for about 45 minutes total.

Do not take Rebecca Lester's classes. Unless you're intrigued by unprofessional powerpoints full of incorrect spellings, abbreviations, and random unorganized chaos. The class was easy enough but she does not have anything together.

She is fabulous. Our exams were basically 6-10 pages of writing, which she graded really easily despite the considerable work that goes into them. Discussions are engaging and her work is really interesting as well.
Dr. Lester is great! I had a great time in her class. It's really interesting, and the grading is completely fair. She cares a lot about students and is fun to talk to.

I really like her as a person and a teacher, and the information covered in class is pretty interesting.  However I really don't like the tests. The mult choice are unneccessarily tricky and the other sections are graded way too harshly.  I have a C+ in this class which is my lowest grade ever in college and I do the readings.
Lester is a super nice professor w/ fascinating research.  Obviously intelligent, she needs to learn to not rely on powerpoints b/c they sort of take away from the class.
Great teacher.  Really cares about students, very clear lecturer, and extremely intelligent.

Her part of medicine and society was really interesting. We read a bunch of great books. She is really interested in her work and a pretty laid back teacher. I had a good time in this class and I would recommend medicine and society to every freshman.

Great professor who clearly shows her knowledge and interest in the subject matter. Covers an impressive amount of content in just a semester, and it is easy to come out of the class having learned a lot.

Material is almost entirely off of the slides and each lecture is crammed with material. The professor does a good job communicating these points and is very open to questions and in providing more explanation.
For Climate Change Seminar: There are no tests just projects and interesting lecutres

Took 1st year climate change seminar. Limbeck is a great prof which doesn't clock if you're just taking it for credit. Though earth sci is a slog, her explanations were really clear and she always related high level subjects back to real life. It's easy to zone out but if you make your goal actually learning instead of a grade, you'll learn a lot.

shes very sweet, knowledgeable, & flexible. interesting class only if you like dinosaurs. exams had some niche questions, but overall pretty chill if you study a decent amount. mostly memorization. slides on canvas, can be long and slightly disorganized. you will def benefit by going to class as not everything is on the slides themselves. fab hair.
She's an angel!!!!

Great professor and person. Lectures were always super fun and engaging, especially if you have a dinosaur hyperfixation. The tests are very reasonable (I finished them all within ~20 min), but there is a fair amount of memorization required, so I'd be weary if that isn't your forte. Homework can be a bit tedious at times but never difficult.

If you have a dinosaur hyper fixation/are willing to acquire one, this class is for you. Slides are posted but you need to go to lecture and take notes. There is a fair amount of memorization.

Prof. Limbeck is very sweet and a good lecturer. She always responds to questions quickly and clearly, both during class and on canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: her canvas is so well organized it had me twirling my hair. Never liked science classes until taking dinosaurs, and even though it's not her main study area, you wouldn't know it when she gives such fast informative lectures. She's also really funny and like always has the answer to your questions! cannot reccomend more.

Prof. Limbeck is a super sweet and intelligent person. I took her first-year seminar about climate change, and it was a very easy class to learn about what's happening in the world right now. I will say, though, that her classes solely consisted of lectures, which could get boring.

She's knowledgeable and kind. She will ensure you have all the information and things you need, and she's very willing to talk to students and make necessary adjustments. The class is just a very long lecture. She could benefit from a 5-minute break, an activity, a video, or something every class because it can get very monotone. Can be nitpicky.

Oh my goodness I want to pull all of my hair out during every class. She throws definitions and information at everybody in the dryest way imaginable. The exams are unclear about expectations for free response questions. Overall would tell anybody to steer clear of her.

Limbeck is a pretty passionate professor and clearly knows a lot about paleontology. However, lectures are often over 100 slides long and fairly unorganized. This class goes over a lot of material and the tests require a LOT of memorization. The only saving grace for this class is that exams are curved heavily and the homework is very light.

If you're taking the dinosaurs because it seems like an easy A, do not take it. Lectures are extremely boring, and there is a ton of material to memorize. She seems nice, but there are definitely other classes that are easier to fulfill credits.

I took her Unearthing the Science of Climate Change class. Great teacher, she really knows what she is talking about and her explanations were easy to understand. Expectations are fair and also very clear. Virtually no homework and a manageable final project. I would really recommend Dr. Limbeck and especially this class for future first-years.

Limbeck is amazing! She is a wonderful addition to the EEPS department staff. Her expectations are crystal clear and she is always available to help/explain. Super clear lectures, very little homework, and very straightforward exams. Challenging and stimulating but not overwhelming! Everyone in EEPS should take a class with her if possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor on this campus. Gives such good feedback and grades things in a reasonable to quick time frame. Would take every class with her if I could.

I actually have a very different experience with Dr. Loui compared to other commenters. The grading is somewhat weirdly scaled and not fully fleshed out in terms of what she actually wants. Could be unreceptive to perspectives different from hers.

She is an incredibly caring, energetic, and involved semester who is invested in you as a student and individual. Learning from her is very enjoyable and she will make sure you are exposed to new material and ideas in an effort to give a strong foundation for future work.

Professor Loui is such a superb professor. She's extremely kind and cares about her students. The already interesting material covered in her class is even more engaging thanks to the passion in her lectures. She's understanding, not a harsh grader, and will deliver a great small-seminar-class experience.

Dr. Loui is definitely one of my favorite professors at WashU! She cares a lot about students and is always so understanding. Lectures can definitely feel long, but the content we covered was definitely informative. There was also a lot of reading but if you get the main idea you'll do great on the assignments. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Literally one of the best profs at WashU. She really cares about you as a person and wants you to learn the material rather than memorize it. I want to take all the classes she offers!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor at WashU!!!

Dr. Loui is the best!! One of the best profs I've had at WashU. If you're thinking about taking a class w Suzanne, do it! The professor makes the class, and she made it worth it. I also learned a lot of interesting material. The best!

Environmental Humanities is a class I definitely recommend. Loui is so nice and really cares about her students. While the class may get a tad boring with lectures, she usually switched things up by doing small group discussions. Requirements are clear and assignments were very manageable.

I LOVE SUZANNE! She is truly the kindest professor who cares so much about her students and their success.The topics covered in Enviro Hum are genuinely interesting and she teaches them so so so well. The class isn't hard, but it is interesting so you will want to participate a lot. I cannot recommend taking a class with her enough.

I can't encourage you enough to take a class from Suzanne. She is a wonderful and kind human being who truly cares about her students. The topics in her enviro hum course were very interesting and lectures are inspiring. Over the course of the semester we did discussion boards, read 3 books (easy reads), wrote a few papers, and did one project.

Professor Loui is an incredible gem at WashU. I took her Environmental Humanities and Fallout courses back-to-back and wish I could take a class by her every semester! She's knowledgeable and open minded, and she cares about her students immensely. The classes are fascinating and I've learned so much from her mentorship. Take a class taught by her!

It's an engineering-level class. It's gonna be hard and a lot of work. BUT. The amount of leniency Woodhams gives you is insane. If you miss a lecture, or need to turn in an assignment late - he will help you through it. He even stayed an hour past the class time so that I could finish an in-class exam. He's so nice it's actually insane. Thank you!
I like this person fr
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. He was fun in lecture and class prepared you for exams. He sometimes was unprepared for lecture but not too often. Annoying amount of assignments but manageable.

Super nice person. Class is mostly individual, do-yourself, learning from projects out of textbook, not really much actual teaching/instruction going on. Still, you learn a lot. Weekly quiz is pretty easy, final project is fun and flexible. TAs were also great and there are lots of opportunities to get help.

Woodhams is a great guy, took statics with him. Material definitely wasn't easy, but he really cares about helping you. The structure of watching prelectures and only doing examples in lecture was annoying at first, but it makes sense because the material is so problem-solving-heavy. Also was very generous in giving back partial credit on exams.

Great person. Recently received his Doctorate! Took CAD and Numerical Methods (Matrix algebra) with him. Learned a lot about MATLAB and SolidWorks. Very knowledgeable and incredibly friendly and accessible. Nicest professor, will remember you.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Course content overall was fairly straightforward and pretty interesting at certain points. I felt the pace of the class was good. It can be a bit tricky at first to understand what the professor is explaining but there are examples and homework problems which help solidify concepts.

I learned a lot in this class and I think the course is structured well. Material can be a bit challenging at first but professor is always available to answer questions. You can usually finish the weekly homework in class if you work efficiently. Definitely recommend doing the workbook practice problems, (there are weekly quizzes).

Pretty chill; no lectures and attendance isn't mandatory, but I would recommend going to as many classes as possible. Do your work and read through the workbook and you'll be solid. I easily could've gotten a higher grade if I went to class more.

Woodhams is a great professor who actually understands the need to show students how to do different problems. Lectures are really helpful, and while the material isnt particularly easy, we would be so lost without him. Hes also just a pleasant person to be around. I wish every engineering class was taught by him.
Not really lectures, just has you run through CAD exercises to learn CAD, which I prefer because I learn by doing. Definitely a great intro to CAD and the TAs are very knowledgeable .

He doesn't lecture, he will give you ton of hw and grade really hard on it. He doesn't care about your other class. He always gives you 2HW on the same week as your 2 tests that he gives out. Very unreasonable for 2hr credit course.

Professor Woodhams is a great professor! CAD with him was straightforward and interesting- I struggled a bit on the exams, but he was very available for extra help and I was still able to get an A in the class. He's very approachable and a good lecturer.

Louie Woodhams is too pure for this world <3 Seriously though, super nice guy and CAD with him is great. Pretty easy, but you'll still learn the ropes of SolidWorks - everything a CAD class should be.

Incredibly nice guy. Always so willing to help. He explains things pretty well and gives brief, concise lectures. The homework assignments and quizzes are not too hard, but make sure you keep up and not get lazy. The exams can be a little tricky, but he lets you retake them up to an 80%. He is a great professor, definitely worth taking CAD from him

Not too easy or too hard, just a pretty typical CAD class. I almost gave a 2 for difficulty. He is a very sweet guy that loves to answer peoples questions, and his lectures are short to allow you to work on the homework. The tests are comprehensive but fair. Lots of assignments so best to keep up and get help when you need it!

He is a really great instructor. He is willing to help you with whatever you need at the drop of a hat. If you are ready to put in the work you can easily get an A as he lets you resubmit work that have errors. Some people find his tests tricky, but if you understand the sketch book you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved taking Professor Watson's class. The discussions were engaging and I enjoyed hearing her perspective, especially on her own research. She was also flexible on deadlines and listened to class feedback.

I took Dr. Watson for Philosophy of Law and she is my favorite professor I've had at WashU. She genuinely cares to get to know each of her students, and is so understanding/flexible. Her explanations of material are very clear and help explain confusing/difficult content. Also, her humor adds the perfect touch to her classes. 100% recommend.

I'd highly recommend taking a class with Professor Watson! The class is a lot of reading, and grades are based entirely on a few essays throughout the semester. However, it's definitely worth it; Prof. Watson's lectures make the material much easier to understand, and she's very flexible with deadlines. Readings are well-selected and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor Watson is great!

- Attendance isn't mandatory, but it is 10% of your grade and the in-class lectures really help you out.
- Be proactive about reaching out. Professor Watson is pretty lenient with extensions and gives good feedback on outlines; just be sure to chat with her outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would definitely recommend a class with her. The readings aren't too heavy but definitely required, as it's pretty obvious who does the readings. A couple papers make up the entire grade but you have plenty of time to write them and gives clear feedback. The grade you get depends on the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Losos is incredibly passionate about what he does and it shows. He's super friendly and is really invested in the success of his students. Also, he's one of the few professors on campus who does animal-related research and he loves discussing it. I would highly recommend this class--it was so much fun and very minimal work.

Professor Losos is great, he's super passionate about what he teaches and genuinely cares about all of his students. He made an effort to help us connect with possible internships or job opportunities after the class and I thought his class was super unique and fun.

Such a fun class and professor! It was great getting to know him and his background and talking to him about his experiences. He cares a lot about his students and provides them with lots of inspiration and knowledge, definitely take a class with him.

Dr. Losos is very accessible via email and always encourages discussion with his students. It feels like he genuinely wants to get to know his students. Research and Conservation in Zoos and Botanical Gardens was a good resource for internship and research opportunities for academic careers in biology or ecology.

Prof Losos is such a gem! Sweetest professor I had this semester. Although the semester was remote, he brought in some really interesting guest speakers. Readings and assignments are light work and are more just to help you prepare questions.

Dr. Rosa was great! He is so knowledgable on Cognitive Science and gives a great introductory class. His lectures are very easy and if you read beforehand, really help your understanding! Assignments are very easy. If you really get into the material, the class goes by so fast. Loved the class and loved his teaching!
just need to go for attendance. boring as heII but the easiest A you will get at this school. attendance, one presentation, and one paper make up your whole grade, but a super easy grader.

Luis teaches the content very well, always comes prepared, and gives good feedback on assignments. There was one big essay and one presentation, but the rest of my grade was assignments, so it was not too difficult. Lectures can be a bit monotonous at times, but he engages the class well by forcing us to talk and come up with examples.
Professor Watt is super kind and very genuine. I talked to her for extensions a few times and it was never a problem

She has a nervous energy around her for classes and is actually pretty dismissive towards students who ask questions about the lecture content. I did feel she did have a racial prejudice against international students, who she often accused of using google translate or AI to write their papers... I would wait for another professor's class to open

Professor Lori Watt is one of the best at WashU. In my mind, there are many people who simply take classes because they are easy or because they provide credit. I have taken Lori Watt because she makes learning enjoyable, accessible, and interesting. No, this is not Calc 3, but I have taken away much more from Professor Watt's teaching.

She was very nice, gives a lot of small quizzes but they're open book, and if you have questions, you can email her and she'll help you get to the right answer. We had to write two essays that had vague prompts but she's a pretty easy grader. There was a lot of reading, but lectures were pretty easy, I spaced out for most of them and did fine.

Professor Watt is a very adaptable professor, and legitimately cares about your success both in class and outside as well, letting you know about various course-related opportunities on campus. The worksheets, papers, and online quizzes were graded fairly, as was the group project presentation.
One of the nicest professors I have had. She knows her info well and is very approachable.
Great professor and great class. Best class of my freshman year.

Gives grades that are probably a letter grade lower than they should be, takes points off paperswritten answers on tests simply because it wasn't the best answer in the class. Really stupid grading system.  Mediocre lecturer. A little bit all over the place, seems a little nervous and sometimes gives responses to questions that aren't answers.

Professor Watt is such a sweetheart. She's really passionate about what she teaches. Theres a lot of reading but it's an interesting class but it's very discussion based.   I would take her if you can. She's fantastic.

Absolutely wonderful professor! While she really encourages the class to lead the discussions and for students to come to their own conclusions about the topic, she is very good at facilitating. She was by far my most helpful professor and always was willing to help students in preparing for essays or understanding classroom material. Really great!
Very interesting, very intelligent. Great professor! Take her if you can! Challenging, but worth it--you'll learn a lot!

I had great expectations for crossing borders, but this class simply falls flat.  The lectures have nothing to do with your grade.  You need a 95% to get an A, which is UNREASONABLE for a 200-level course.  TA grading is really inconsistent.

She's always seems very nervous during class, but you get use to it. Lectures are decent. Slightly hard to follow and she moves quickly through powerpoint slides often, but whatever. Apparently some students had troubles with TAs, but I thought mine was fantastic. Overall, shes a decent prof.

The subject matter was quite interesting, but she wasn't the most compelling lecturer. She seemed very nervous, but is very sweet and made an effort to learn everyone's name. The quizzes weren't bad (she gives you all the questions in advance), but the TAs mainly grade the papers and grade differently, so grades are pretty much a crap shoot.

I disliked this class. The professor was really knowledgeable and nice, but she was disorganized and nervous during lectures, which made her hard to follow. Additionally, the TAs didn't grade equally. Some TAs graded easily while other graded harshly, which I thought was totally unfair. If you can take another class, do so.

Unfortunately she is very nice, helpful, organized and clear, however she manages to let her TAs take control of the grading which leaves us students constantly disappointed. I've never worked so hard for a class in my life, never learned so much and still managed to only get a B. So frustrating! You can't get mad at her cuz she's realtively nice.
This was a boring and unorganized class, but the prof really knows her stuff and she was very helpful during office hours.
good

Amazing, nice, & sharp! In my course she was fantastically organized (by far the most organized class I've taken, previous reviews are based on a class she did for the first time).  She is energetic, excited about learning and teaching, creates a friendly environment for ideas.  Most important is her gift for clarity even re: difficult concepts.

there's no doubt that she was unorganized and boring, but i think that the class could improve if she continues to teach it over time. i like that it was broken down into areas but had a common overarching theme. the class has potential, but it just wasn't there yet.
very unclear
Bad
Teacher was very disorganized, and was teaching material she didn't seem to be familiar with.  Lectures were tough to get through.
interesting, well organized, very easy to get a good grade

Watt did not always make things clear in her lectures. The articles read for class were not discussed, and she did not seem well prepared for class. She always had so many papers in her hand that she kept flipping through while lecturing. She is very sweet, but I felt she could have been stronger.
Great professor. Very clear and very helpful. Always concerned about her students. The topics she covered were fascinating and moving. I learned a great deal.

Prof. Watt is a very knowledgeable instructor.  She made class extremely interesting.  I looked forward to her classes and her assignments were on key with what we were learning.  We had very interesting speakers and movies in class.  I learned alot.
No Comments

Watt seemed shy at first, but really opened up once the course began. Her section on Japan was her strongest, but she cares about her students and is incredibly sweet. I learned a lot about the world, and had a good time.
Amazing Prof! This was my 9 am at Penn State, but his lectures were always engaging and interesting! He truly cares about the present and future of his field as well as the students in his courses!

Lulewicz is great because he draws from his own specialties and other peoples' so we have a lot of guest lecturers. I think it's cool because it shows that, though he is very knowledgable and passionate, he also does not know everything and has students learn from many different sources. Grading is easy so don't worry, just go to class.

Jake was a super nice professor who actually cared about his students' mental health and well-being. The class is mostly composed of lecturers from other schools lecturing on what they do for research. Awesome class!

Super interesting intro class, very caring guy and if you put effort into the assignments you will get an A. Only complaint is the lectures are a little disorganized, but overall he is a very nice guy and there's very little homework. Make sure you go to the guest lectures because he does pop attendance checks. Overall really cool class and easy A!

Guest lectures are important to go to since he takes attendance at them randomly. Additionally, you are required to write about topics discussed in these guest lectures in the final assignment. Very little homework, easy A.

Amazing. Super caring and is always available if you reach out to him. World Archaeology was probably my favorite course the semester I took it -- Prof. Lulewicz makes it easy to get an A because he cares more about your effort to learn than strict deadlines, etc.
Professor Jake is my favorite professor at WashU hands down.

Jake is a really good guy who cares about the subject matter a ton. The class "Warfare and Violence" isn't a ton of work, and Jake isn't a tough grader so it's not hard to do well. Still really interesting stuff.

He said on the first day that if you try you'll get an A. However, he was stressing a lot of us out towards the end because he seemed like he might change his mind on that. There were three projects all due within two weeks of each other at the end of the semester. He said he would just give a total grade based on what he thought about your work.
Great prof. 10/10 would take intro to GIS again. Learned a lot and can use for future jobs. Wish he taught a more advanced course in GIS I could take as well.
Clear, interesting, and fun lectures. Tests are very straightforward with good study guides. Awesome professor and class.

I really liked this course. I didn't initially have a "passion" for the subject, but Professor Salas' engaging lectures and the TA lead discussion sections were really great. I highly suggest taking this course. There were a few tests and papers that were very reasonable and not there to stump the students.

Really solid professor. Greek is a tough subject but he teaches it really well and is funny to boot. It's a tough class though, so expect to study and pay attention in class but if you try and ask questions, he's a really easy grader.

i took ancient medicine w him and it was fascinating (tho i am not a classics or medicine major). he's a rly good lecturer and answers student questions v well, and also is fun and sorta dorky. tests are fair, & if you go to lecture and take good notes you def don't need to read the textbook.

He teaches a very difficult subject but explains everything clearly and writes straightforward exams. He is very engaging, clearly cares about the class and the students. Very approachable and accommodating.
Fond of puns. Gives clear guidelines on grading criteria.
Helpful, friendly, lectures are really interesting. Would absolutely take this class again!
Great professor, would definitely recommend. He understands the stuff is hard and really cares about his students. You have to work to get an A but you learn a lot in the process.

If you take Type w/ Lynne, be aware that:

- Workload is ECTREMELY heavy compared to other studios
- You will spend ALL your free time on unhelpful busywork
- Criteria are unclear/directly contradict rubric
- Announcements are posted late, even within 24 hrs of due date
- Lynne has a habit of cutting students off/giving vague, condescending answers

As a person, she seems great and kind, but as a teacher, she is harsh and a little bit mean. I felt like I was constantly being talked down to. After being told my work was great, she would give bad grades. If you have self-worth and don't want to start to hate digital art, I would highly suggest rethinking if you want to take her class.

as a person she is friendly and understanding if you communicate and have a good work ethic. but also she only gives subjective feedback and tbh doesn't have a background in type idk why she teaches the class. she always say we would do good and then would bash us in grades which she doesn't know how to publish. prepare to spend all ur printing $
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took Engr4502 with Lynnea, she's so nice and actually cares about you. Material was sort of useless and group projects were all pretty free, but that's due to the nature of "engineering leadership" and not her. Super understanding and accessible outside of class, seems to genuinely care about how you're doing. Never had to stress about this class.

Absolutely AMAZING professor. Super knowledgable about WGSS and grades super easy on papers. Definitely pretty unorganized and takes forever to grade, but seriously such a kind and amazing human being. Would 100% recommend into to WGSS with her!

I'm kinda shocked to see that people gave Brumbaugh below a 4. I took ENG 310 and 4502 with her, and I loved both. Lectures aren't super useful, but I strongly believe that to be a product of the material, rather than Brumbaugh's ability as a teacher. She's knowledgable, articulate, and the nicest professor I've had at WUSTL. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Brumbaugh is by far the best professor I have had at Wash U--she is brilliant, kind, personal, and overall a fantastic person. Her Intro to WGGS class is absolutely phenomenal, and she pushes students to think outside the box while remaining comfortable and confident in their ideas.

Nice professor. Class is very useless and takes too much time. At least two assignments per week, half of which she won't even grade. They are very confusing too. There is something different every week. Some people might find that fun but I didn't like it. Don't take this class if you have a busy semester. Your other classes deserves more time.

I didn't mind her for Tech Writing.  I enjoyed going to class because she's very nice and has a good personality, but the class itself is TOTALLY USELESS.  I learned absolutely nothing.  Doesn't explain assignments too well.  Also, she taught so many classes this semester that she clearly didn't have time to thoroughly read anything we turned in.
I enjoyed having Brumbaugh for tech writing. She was fun and pretty laid back.  Sometimes she would see the class was stressed and cancel class, etc.  Pretty easy grader too.

She was the worst professor I have ever had.  She is very inconsistent and does not explain assignments well.  I did not learn anything useful from this class.  If you can take Tech Writing with any other professor you should.  Then you might actually learn something.

This class is super easy, all you have to do is show up and she'll at least give you a B+.  She even told the class that she has never given anyone below a B+....after the first couple of weeks it is really had to get to class since it is so boring and completely useless!
Awesome teacher.  Very understanding and she gives assignments that let students be creative.  I loved her class.
No Comments

you guys are all on crazy pills.  lynnea is an awefully tough and picky grader and the class itself is more or less worthless without the virtue of being a blowoff.  i suffered all semester doing pointless projects while sitting through her haphazard lectures, and i urge you to avoid the same fate
she rocks!
GREAT class. I loved the material and the way she taught was fantastic. I learned more in that class than in any other class I have taken.  Extremely helpful material!
Brilliant teacher and her class is really great but the assignments are essentially worthless. The material is wonderful and the class is fun.
There is a lot of work, especially as you get to the end of the semester, but Lynnea is incredibly flexible and very effective in her teaching.
Incredible teacher, very helpful and knowledgeable, makes things interesting and fun, goes above and beyond
Lynnea is hands down the best teacher at Wash U. Her classes are time consuming, but very rewarding and very useful as well.  Possibly one of my favorite professors of all time
Awesome prof. Would highly recommend anything she is teaching.

She is a very very understanding and compassionate teacher. I took this class first semester freshman year and was very nervous about a lecture based class (being a science major.) I didn't talk much but did pay attention and she noticed. She understood my anxiety and accommodated. She provided a great intro to the academic side of feminism.

She's always so nice, impossible to dislike personally, and an incredibly forgiving professor--willing to accomodate students (and move due dates and such). Her class isn't hard, just a good deal of reading. The class is mostly discussion (you can get away with skipping readings if need be).
DONT TAKE HER CLASS

Lyda's a great teacher! She really cares about every students success. She's very enthusiastic and has a deap understanding of the material. To do well, read the chapters, read them again, and participate in class disscussions. Would recommend not asking questions that are answered in the syllabus. I hope to take more classes from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Expects professionalism from students, but then has "bad days". Overall she knows what she is talking about and is a good professor, but the experience has been negative. She also schedules the midterm exam for the day after fall break and makes herself available for reviews during the vacation, when many students are not in town.  Thanks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic, very knowledgable, easy on the eyes!
Lyda is gorgeous and brilliant and great in class!  It doesn't get any better!!

The most adorable teacher I've ever had. The class would go by incredibly quickly because Mme. Breakstone made it so delightful and was so energetic. I wish she taught higher level French so I could take another class with her! Very tough grader though. My As on 307 papers became equivalent to Bs graded by Breakstone.

Madame Breakstone is so adorable/enthusiatic. I received As on many papers, and I think one of the biggest reasons was that I finished ahead of time so that I could ask her questions.  She's hard in that she doesn't like the verb "etre" or any other boring verb, so you have to really expand vocab, but without making errors...really helps my french.

I specifically signed up for her section because I had heard she was great, but I hated the class!! Her grading on the papers was ridiculously tough and I couldn't please her no matter what I did. Her assignments were also very unclear.

Sweet lady/very good humored! Learned so much(esp.different tenses) Big on having people up to the board to write exercises & it surprisingly helps a lot! Hw every night-not too heavy but graded on completion. Only complaint-grading of tests:even when I studied a lot, I still got Bs. Got a B+in class but I think I deserved A for all of my hard work
This teacher is ****

Nice woman, enjoyable class, teaches you some serious french. One complaint=grading.  Never before have I complained re:hard grading, but her standards for an A were inordinate. Also her grading system rewards you for doing less. Focuses on perfection not effort, so those who write short dumb sentences win out (I tried both on tests, I know).  Eek.
She is a very difficult teacher, but she is most concerned with students showing improvement so take her advice and demonstrate it in the next assignment.

After 3 semesters and many courses, Mme. Breakstone is still the best teacher I've had at Wash U.  She cares very much for the students and does what it takes for everything to be understood.  If taking French, make sure it's with Mme. Breakstone.
Passionate

She is a really caring and helpful teacher. The class was somewhat difficult (but not nearly as difficult as the other sections). She really cares about her students, knows them all by name, and helps out whenever she can. If you are taking french, I would recommend her class.
Tons of fun!
I love Mme. Breakstone.  She is sooo nice.

Wonderful teacher. very knowledgable, speaks clearly and, when asked to clarify, explains clearly. Also, she's very, very understanding if you can't get the homework done or can't come to class.  However, assignments can be very difficult to understand, and the work load is large.
She knows her stuff, but heaven help you if you fall behind.  Also, she's a tough grader, so get all the points you can in your subsection
Great teacher - my favorite at Wash U.  A difficult grader but very helpful.

I took Modern Texts and Contexts with Professor Shipe and he is a fantastic professor! He gave great feedback on essays that truly helped me improve and write pieces I was proud of, was quick to reply to emails, and was kind and encouraging. He also made hilarious jokes and his class was a really positive environment, would recommend!

I took Modern Texts and Contexts with professor Shipe and he is a fantastic professor! He gave great feedback on essays that truly helped me write pieces I was proud of, was quick to reply to emails, and was an all around friendly and encouraging professor. His jokes were hilarious and his class had a really positive environment, would recommend!
He is easygoing and it seems like everyone gets the grade they want. He allows you to be flexible with essay topics, so you can write about anything, which makes the process a lot easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shipe is that dude. Class vibes are super chill, he is really funny and nice. Absolutely take a class with him if you can

Shipe was such an upgrade from my first-year CWP--kind and sweet. Can be awkward at times but its funny. Was always willing to meet outside of class to help you and really encouraged people to explore their writing. I felt that he graded a bit tough, but never truly harmed my grade--I think he just wants you to learn and grow and I appreciated it!

Shipe is a great lecturer and adds the perfect amount of structure to discussions. He's the Dude. He gives great feedback, and you'll do well as long as you revise based on his notes. Sometimes he'd note that I was onto something and needed to elaborate, but I had actually no clue what I was doing; however he was always accessible and understanding

Professor Shipe is one of those diamonds in the rough - he's a little awkward at times but makes it funny, he's a great listener, and I love the way he taught the material. Lots of reading but the class is structured so that if you really enjoy some material you can earn your points there. Just a really warm-hearted and down to earth professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Shipe is one of the best professors I've had so far at Wash U. The class is very reading heavy, but the books you read for this class are pretty entertaining and lead to great discussion in class. Prof Shipe gives great feedback on your comments in class and on essays and I honestly feel that this class has made me a much better writer.

Prof Shipe is a phenomenal instructor. All the novels we read in his class were fantasticbe aware though that it was a reading-heavy class, so be prepared to put in the time needed to succeed. I'd take any class he taught thoughhe was super nice, funny, and I felt that I learned a lot through the discussions that he facilitated.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was outside my major and a kind of random choice but this is honestly one of the best classes I have taken! Shipe is such a great Professor! He is hilarious leads discussions flawlessly. He is also a super fair grader and gives great feedback. I looked forward to this class every week!

Prof Shipe is the best professor I've had at Washu after 4 years. He has an uncanny ability to take all comments and use them for constructive discussion while keeping all engaged. He's funny and caring, sporting thorough knowledge about everything ranging from beer, pop culture, to sports. I've never learned more or had more fun in a class.

As a senior and writing minor, Prof. Shipe is by far the best writing professor I've had in college. He is equal parts kidding around with the frat bros and nerding out about the Bachelor. He's very intelligent and gives great feedback. Discussion is never forced, and by far my favorite class of my senior spring.

Professor Shipe combines a depth of knowledge on the subject and a generous, sensitive spirit. His sense of humor is relaxing and makes the class enjoyable, his empathy is such that your heart will be touched forever. He cares about his students to a fault, understands what most people don't. Very intelligent and very kind.

Professor Shipe combines a depth of knowledge on the subject and a generous, sensitive spirit. His sense of humor is relaxing and makes the class enjoyable, his empathy is such that you can see into his soul and be touched forever by his character.

My favorite class! I whole-heartedly recommend this freshman seminar, or any class taught by Professor Shipe. Shipe is funny and makes it easy to contribute in class discussions. He grades paper's pretty had, but if you participate in class and write fairly decent papers, you will get a fine grade. This class always put me in a great mood.
Class was so laid back and Prof Shipe was always entertaining and willing to help

He's a great teacher who really cares about his students and wants to be in the classroom. He's really funny, in an adorably awkward way, and facilitates good class discussions. He can be tough on papers, however. Overall, great!
Professor Shipe is one of the best teachers I have had in college.  His class is so enjoyable and you learn a lot.  Professor Shipe is the MAN!!!
Prof. Shipe was a great teacher, class was always entertaining!
HE DA MAN!

Matthew Shipe is one of the most hilarious  people and professors I know. Writing 1 isn't supposed to be the most fun class, but Matthew made it quite enjoyable to come to class. He cares about his students and gives good feedback on papers. I love this guy!
He was absolutely wonderful.  He made class funny, enjoyable and I actually learned a lot of abuot writing
aside from injecting humor into a subject with banal topics, Dr. Shipe is adept at fulfilling the goals of a writing class: showing that writing (and writers) has a purpose that can be appreciated.
awesome teacher! great guy! i was dreading the class but he made it not only bearable but fun! will work with students to help them... great prof!
No Comments
Amazing professor who genuine cares about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Mejia is a great professor and an even better human being. I've already taken three classes with him, and they're all worth it. One of the best professors you'll have at WashU.

Martin's lectures were very insightful and engaging, and so much of it is due to the evident passion and care he has for the material and his students. There were weekly readings that were a bit lengthy at times, but never too difficult. Overall a great instructor that I couldn't recommend more.

The coolest professor I ever had! He engages the whole classroom in the topic of discussion. Quizzes can be challenging at the beginning, but his lectures are awesome and very inspiring, so they will make studying easier. Martin is a professor who truly loves teaching. I highly recommend taking Cultures of Health in Latin America with him.

wow. 151 is peas compared to 152 where the lab reports are horrific. they give you wrong answers in office hours. you can instantly get 8 points off (out of 70) for one wrong answer. never got a grade i was happy with throughout all the lab reports. confusing material. nearly useless lectures where half of the time she doesn't even say anything...

She is very bad at teaching. The lecture is very boring and goes too slowly. While the 151 is not hard, and it does not matter if she is a good teacher, 152 is much more difficult with all the different unknowns. It is just even more challenging when she cannot explain the concepts well in 152.

Honestly. 151 was cheese, but 152 started clamping down like crazy. The AI's have occasionally given false information during lab reports, not to mention the level of precision on experiments has become significantly more challenging. The tests have become harder too, but still manageable. The abhorrence for Lutes is followed religiously by sheep.

Unprofessional attitude. Doesn't even teach the class, literally...Autry does. Class is pretty easy to learn by yourself, but the structure of the course and the amount of workload for 2 credit lab is ridiculous. Professor get's irritated easily and questions aren't answered professionally nor accurately.
When is the Quiz?

Lutes puts very little effort into the class, not preparing an actual lecture each week and just relying on old course videos and lab manual readings that you have to do outside of lecture on your own time. The structure of the class is terrible and has little consistency week to week. Overall, tests are easy but everything is learned on your own.

Has a dismissive Attitude, not helpful in person or in useless lecture. Still an easy class, but people definitely lose their interest in chemistry because of her. Don't go to class if you value your time, unless Autry is teaching.
The professor is engaging, but the class can be challenging. Use tools like unstuck ai, study sessions, and the free textbook to succeed. Attendance is required, but worth it for the support.

Avoid Lutes, take Autry instead. Dr. Lutes does not teach the material clearly at all, never responds to emails, and is extremely unprofessional. She walked out mid-lecture after a few students out of 350 kept asking about the quiz. She said she would give us all zeros on it. The whole course is unorganized. Way too much work for a 2 credit class.

I'll say this: my ADHD is bad but Dr. Lutes' is worse. She's disorganised and I found myself self-studying a lot (like for everything). I attend her lectures and they're... really bad. This class needs a new professor and a new way of teaching content.

I'm trying to keep things nice here but his class is not enjoyable... gl yall.
Extremely mean professor who gets ticked off for no reason at all. She will punish the class of 350 people if one person makes a mistake. Terrible way to run a large lab class.

As a student who wants to learn, I don understand why she doesn't have that kind of attitude to teach, and she never responds to email. Sometimes she made decision without deep consideration, and I don't think it is what a normal professor will behave. I want to be as respectful as possible so that's what I will say about her for now.

The whole class especially the first three weeks are extremely unorganized. Also Lutes crashed out during the lecture and just left the room in the middle of the lecture. I don't think this is supposed to happened in a mandatory class and it's lecture.

Abysmal Professor, horrible course outline. All of the poor reviews are accurate. She is treated badly by students, but the course structure is far too difficult and the labs are way too long. Autry is the only reason lab reports are possible and the exams were easy. Only reason I passed with an A+
