She assigns a lot of reading, some of which is last minute or not on the syllabus, but overall Dr. Mustakeem was one of the best teachers I have ever had! She is passionate and down to earth and always there if you need guidance. Take a class with her!

Dr. Mustakeem is amazing at leading discussions. She assigns a heavy reading and writing load, but she makes you WANT to complete everything. Make sure you do the reading, because she will call you out.

Great Professor who really cares about the students. He's always looking to learn from the students and wants to see us succeed. AFAS 368 was a laid back class with just presentations, a few papers, and a midterm that wasn't hard at all. If you want a guranteed A in a class and to learn something new, I would definitely take this class.
Highly recommend taking Swahili taught by Prof. Mutonya. He is a very funny and engaging professor who cares about his students. Easy to get a good grade, and not too much work.

Prof. Mutonya is by far one of my favorite teachers. I always look forward to his class. He is caring and passionate about his work. His classes are very easy and require little work. Since his classes are small, he has time to give each student the attention they need. He makes his classes very engaging and fun to be in.

Tremendous professor. I loved the layout and structure of the course - weekly reflections, a couple presentations, and a final. Gets you really into the material and being from Kenya, he reflects on personal experience to help you really understand topics. Knows everything about Africa. Also just a really great person who wants you do to well.

Very fun and kind guy. A social linguist who knows the workings of Swahili on more than just a native speaking basis. Class isn't incredibly organized, but everything he teaches is clear, and you will learn a ton. One of the happiest and nicest professors I have ever had.

Mwalimu is an interesting, caring professor. He adores Swahili, and loves to talk about both the language and the culture from which it comes. He is highly qualified and immensely interested in his students. As long as you show up, pay attention, and complete your assignments, you're almost guaranteed to do well. I highly recommend taking Swahili!

Mutonya was often very unclear on what he wanted specifically for assignments, he gave broad expectations.  Sometimes the classes were dry, but the information was interesting.  Overall, an ok class if you're looking for broad information.  There isn't any in-depth knowledge presented.  No one should receive a poor grade in the class!
Very informed Professor.  Really enjoyed his class.  Learned alot!

An amazing man. Took Swahili and Intro. to African Studies with him and decided to major in AFAS because of him. Will help find study abroad opportunities and even fin. aide for them. Makes classes very interesting. He is an amazing man and for sure is the best teacher at Wash. U.

Prof. Mutonya was the best professor I had at Wash U. He is brilliant and he loves what he teaches. I took his Kiswahili classes and his course on African Literature (which was fantastic). A top of the line teacher and human being

Really a great guy. He's Kenyan, and has that great laidback Kenyan outlook on things. Unfortunately general African Studies is not his field per se - I suspect he is much more well-versed and knowledgeable in Swahili classes. But the class is a great intro to Africa if you don't know much about it.
Great guy
No Comments
I took Swahili with him, great teacher for an uncommonly offered language, so cute and funny, he always made the class laugh-not always on purpose.  Great class.

She's amazing -- super smart, organized, and nice. Her lectures are super interesting and her slides are really well organized. She's also really funny and nice, I really enjoyed going to lecture to hear her speak. 10/10 would recommend this class and her as a professor

Dr. Mueller is wonderful. I didn't know much about anthro and she made the class very accessible to me. As long as you put in the effort you will do well! She is also hilarious and very down-to-earth.

I absolutely adored Prof. Mueller and this class. I learned an incredible amount about domestication, and she did such a great job of explaining concepts (and giving hints as to what would be on the quizzes). Highly recommend this class and professor! (she's also hilarious)

I love love love Professor Mueller. She made culture and environment a much more interesting class and changed the structure of the course to include more projects/essays that help your grade. She really tries to make class fun and engaging and her exams are not too difficult.

Natalie Mueller is absolutely amazing and I wish we could just be best friends. She was so cool, caring, chill, excited about the subject. You could tell she wanted to make the class low stakes and fun for us as long as we put in solid effort and learned something. I loved that. I learned so many interesting things about domestication. Awesome prof
I took Bio 3180 w/ Professor Mueller and learned a lot about domestication of modern species. She is very easy going and the class is chill as long as you pay attention during lectures.
Prof Mueller is an absolute GEM. Love her. Very intelligent, organized, and really cares about each individual student. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: On point. I understood most of the things he says
very good
poor clarity. He can't express himself better for students to learn. Question marks over his qualifications.
One of the best professors.
Just visit this link and see it for yourself :<a href="http://www.pansika.com/" title="Welcome to Malawi">www.pansika.com</a>
Best Law Teacher Ever, I hear you are now in malawi? Your brother is forcing you on malawians? Tell him to try joyce banda.
BORING BORING
You can't understand what he's saying, the lectures are unhelpful, and the exam is completely random.  Might as well let a random number generator create all the final grades.
I barely learned anything in his class. He has a very thick African accent, so it is very hard to understand what he is saying. He is also very slow and barely covers any material.

Mullins was a good College Writing professor. She definitely pushes your writing and I learned a lot. She wants you to succeed, so meeting with her and listening to her comments are important for getting good grades. She's kind of quirky, so class was pretty entertaining. Power and Commodity Culture topics were very interesting, good discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: While she is passionate about folklore and discussion conversations, her cackling laughter at her own jokes continues to haunt me. She poorly communicates the expectations for writing assignments and you can expect averages of a B-. She is nice about meeting one on one but its the only time youll ever learn something worth your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I honestly don't even think I can type how I feel about this class into 350 characters. However, I will say that if you do not write in a way in which she is familiar, you can expect to be shook by your grades. Good luck my friends. You're GONNA need it. Also, the questions asked during discussions can be confusing at times.

The professor was very subjective. In personal statements, she said, "your voice is too midwestern." She preferred some styles of writing, and if you did not write like that, you could expect below a C.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Willow Mullins is a great teacher and also the best person I have met here at WashU. It was a pleasure to be able to take her class and I would retake it again if I had the opportunity. She teaches writing 1 and helped make the transition from high school to college much smoother.

Professor Berg is just OK. The grading in this class was EXTREMELY unclear; our biggest assignment of the year, an essay worth 20% of our grade, had one sentece worth of instruction. We also never got the syllabus until the last week, or the grade scale. The class title and description were also not accurate to the course.
Very smart and knows what she's talking about. She's not great with technology and a bit disorganized at times but I learned a lot from her. Very important to the readings and participate in class.

Assignments were easy but she gave such specific grades (i.e. 13.6/15) and she comes off a little passive aggressive when asking for extensions. I missed a few classes due to illness and she only excused a few of them (1 was the class I missed before I registered for it) which dropped my grade. Take her class if you have to but be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Berg really cares for her students and is very much there for them. She is a very fair grader and participation does matter, but also she knows how to make a class fun if you are open and willing in class. Definitely would take again. She's the type of professor to ask you how you are doing outside of class.

Some of the lectures could be a little boring. Nancy's anti-humor was entertaining at times. Very unclear instructions at times, but Prof Berg does really care about her students and overall I enjoyed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Berg is quite awkward and, at times, difficult to have as a teacher. Her instructions can be quite ambiguous and there's a gap between what she wants and what we understand. However, it was clear by the way she weighed work, encouraged students, and listened to us that she cared about our success. Also, I promise you'll warm up to her humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Berg is a very sweet lady who puts effort into making connections with her students. She is great at facilitating discussion, sometimes lengthening segments when the discussion is rich, and open to moving on when it's lacking. She is certainly not closed-minded... she is really good at bringing multiple sides to controversial issues.

Incredibly helpful and concerned about students.  Sets high expectations for writing.  Did not find her closed minded at all and think she actually allowed us to discuss the readings however we wished, though after clarifications. Again, SUPER helpful and concerned for students.
I really enjoyed the class - prof berg was helpful outside of class and i thought my writing and reading improved. it was also fun - take lit of childhood if it's offered again.

Most boring a comparative literature class could possibly be. Most discussion was about what happened in the books we were reading. Very superficial discussion. As a person, professor seemed cold and uninterested. Overall very awkward experience. One of the worst classes I've taken at WU.

I took this class despite ominous comments; I wish I had listened. The literary discussions fail to sustain my interest or go past the surface of the text. The class often feels like a plot review. When a comment is made, she will often disagree, and does not let a discussion develop, instead letting comments hang in the air or objecting to them.

Did not find her closeminded. Found that she opened my eyes to new ways of approaching the topic/reading. I can see how someone very set in their ways would feel snubbed, but she will always listen, she just won't necessarily agree. What fun would class be if everyone agreed, though? Definitely recommended.
Close minded in a University which is known for its open intellectual exchanges.
Definitely comes into class with a set agenda, and does not want to hear an opposing opinions.  Rather close minded and difficult to approach.
No Comments
No Comments
Go to lectures as they as super helpful in succeeding in the class.

I would suggest going to all the lectures because you can feel lost just looking at the slides. He's a funny guy, and you can tell he really cares about his students. He releases all the past tests as practice tests and if you can do those you can do well in all the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are engaging and he's a really enthusiastic guy. He's always willing to help and if you understand the concepts you'll thrive.

Really funny guy. Goes on rants sometimes during lectures and isn't always the most prepared, but will always devote time to answer students' questions. The class is a little difficult and he works pretty quickly sometimes because he knows his micro, but he'll always slow down and explain if you need him to. Also lowkey gives the easiest tests.

Really great professor and funny guy. He's super into the subject so he goes on rants, and sometimes is not the the most straightforward when he explains how to calculate things. But he is very smart and knows his stuff. He's pretty accessible, puts out a lot of study materials, and made class interesting sometimes even though I kinda hate micro.

Natenzon is one of my favorite professor's at WashU. His lectures were extremely engaging in my opinion and he always listened to student feedback. I do think the class could use more TAs but he hosts some office hours and you can ask him questions right after class. If you understand the content and do all the practice exams, you will do fine!

Incredibly nice professor, really enjoyed his lectures, and I thought he was fairly good at teaching the material. However, his exams are immensely difficult, and the bi-weekly problem sets are not especially easy, either.

The difficulty of this class is overrated in my opinion. Its true that Paulo is not a very good instructor (although a nice guy), I never paid any attention to his lectures, I think online videos and self-studying are more efficient for this class, and if you do his practice exams, the actual exams are very fair and manageable.

Paulo is a fine teacher. He cares more about his academic papers than actually teaching the class. He is a nice and funny guy but not the best teacher. His class is easier than the other MEC 290 Professors, so I would still recommend it over CDC's class. The class should be fine if you have already taken MGT 100

Office hours were useful but weren't sufficient enough for me. I did not learn from his lectures. Additionally the exams were difficult. Either learn MEC290 from another prof or be prepared to devote ## hours a week to his class. Again, Paulo is probably an amiable prof to do research with but his teaching isn't accessible for beginning microecon.
Very nice professor, but the class is definitely hard. I feel like I only did well because I had taken AP Micro and Macro in high school. I would recommend taking advantage of office hours

Prof. Natenzon is a REALLY nice guy. I have nothing bad to say about him as a person at all. He really cares about his students and is super personable. Regarding the content of his class, it can be really hard to understand and I think he does not always have the best approach in lectures when trying to explain the material. Great guy, hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Clearly very intelligent, and mixes humor into his lectures. Exams can be hard but certainly aren't impossible, just study. Some say stay away, but I like him and would like to take more classes with him.

I feel like he just does not understand student learning in the slightest. He just gives the formula or idea behind an economic concept with a little explanation and then expects the students to comprehend the application of the formula or rule with absolutely zero practice.

Brilliant teacher, but failed to acknowledge the lack of knowledge many students came into the class with. Homework was too hard and took a large group to understand what to do. Test averages were extremely low, but the curve did surprise me in the end with a much better grade.
Really smart. But his exams and homework so hard!!! if you don't want too much psychological pressure, or there is high opportunity cost, just don't take it.
Great professor, easy to talk to and helpful, interesting class, not an easy A though.
I don't recommend this professor.
the most useless course
Lecture notes are hard to understand
Never take his courses
The worst professor in the world
The worst course I have ever taken.

This professor is the best CS professor I've had at WashU. He really knows his stuff and he's a good lecturer. He cares a lot about his students and he's very willing to take questions and explain concepts during lecture. But, he also expects his students to use full effort and he grades tough - prob the hardest cs class at washu.
Good class but very difficult, only take it if you are comfortable with a theory-heavy class. The tests are curved though so just do better than your peers who are also struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: cse417 is a math class through and through, anyone interested in an easier coding class should take the ESE version. The class is well organized but difficult. Raviv seems uninterested in interacting with students at all, especially undergrads, but is a good lecturer. overall one of the best and hardest classes I have taken

1. Attendance needed. Don' t provide lecture record and he will show some mathematic prove on the whiteboard, which maybe tested in exam.

2 exams. Each worth 25 of your total grade and there is a 25 points curve on the exam.

5 homework. Each worth 10% of your total grade. Each took me 2 days to finish. The grading of hw is harsh and strict.

He's a clear speaker and smart, but he is not very good at explaining concepts. The only times he gives us any intuition is for extremely basic material and when it gets a little more complicated, he goes into complex math that is direct from one of the textbooks. Unsure if that's him not understanding it either or if he just wants us to suffer:(
the worse.

I normally don't post here but since everyone is so negative I felt I needed to. This is both the hardest and the best class I have ever taken, hands down. Don't expect another easy coding class. This is a math class, there should be more prereqs, but it's fair. Raviv is very clear about this and if you want something easier just take another class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lecture slides are hard to understand, and assignments are time consuming.
Hardest thing Ever taken
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Raviv is a bad lecturer. The class material is very interesting and should lend itself to a challenging but rewarding experience. Raviv, however, rarely uses anything but his slides to explain detailed proofs and his unable to answer questions well when they arise. He then tests students on proofs that they essentially need to have memorized.

I don't know what went wrong, this course is great, but course materials does not appear on your homework, and those things will not appear on the exams, teaching you X, ask you to solve Y, and test you Z. You might never see things you learned from this class ever again. I'm not doubting this course now, I am doubting meaning of of life now.

This course is nearly impossible to do well- the homework and exams are graded harshly and beyond the scope of the lectures in my opinion. However, I did learn a lot in this course. Take another introductory machine learning course at WashU that don't cause as much stress, if you can.

Dictator. Grading scheme was based completely on his discretion and never known until it is posted on your transcript . The materials are inheritably hard, he makes it even more boring. Use TAs to talk to students and even teaches class instead of any communication attempt. Extremely difficult exams in unreasonable time. Avoid at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great potential for the class, not a great professor. The midterm mean was 62 - this exam received a 15 point curve. The final exam mean was a 67 - no curve at all. He also made the grading scale more strict - B+ was 87-91 and A- was 91-94, without any reason or mention in the syllabus (bye GPA). Take the class, but not with him.

417 was my hardest class yet and Raviv isn't the best professor I've had. But I feel like the reviews are too harsh. The course is just very math and theory-heavy for a cs class. The homework/exams go deeper than the lectures but aren't impossible if you spend time reviewing the material with the textbooks. Just know what you're getting into.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the hardest classes I've taken because it's so theoretical & math-heavy. But the class is supposed to be a theory course so I don't blame the prof for that. HW is incredibly difficult w/o attending TA hours & reading the textbook. Tests scores were low but there's a significant curve. I don't regret taking this class but didn't love it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I agree with every single word in other reviews. This class does not have practical value due to the low teaching quality, and it will damage your academic record/future jobs as it grades harshly. Please don't take this class if you don't want to live in its shadow for the rest of your college years.

Extremely difficult class, awful lecture with some impossible exams. He stated he cares about the wellbeing of students, but his course made it clear that he doesn't. Don't take this class, just don't take it, period.

Lectures cover the bare minimum outlines of a topic. Few example problems covered in class. Weekly omework assignments (50% of grade) are unjustifiably difficult in comparison and many problems are undoable without attending TA office hours which are always packed. Difficulty of midterm and final (each 25% of grade) exams are absurd for 1.5 hours.

How easy the lecture, how tough the homework. Have to study myself much much time after class. Also, the exams are extremely difficult with impossible amount of time (1.5 hr for a 6 hr test??). Getting a B+ brings me good standing in this course comparing to others but ruined my transcript! I hated CS and switched major afterwards!

Do not take with this professor unless you enjoy harming yourself, your life or your transcript. Extremely difficult tests that failed a huge percentage of class, homework is almost impossible to finish. Most importantly, I don't feel this class teaches a lot in knowledge, if I must say I learned something, then perhaps collaboration skill.
Teach rather shallowly while assigning hard homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her teaching approach seems to primarily involve reading from PowerPoint slides, which lacks logical explanations. There appears to be an issue with unfair grading in the course, and it's disappointing that feedback is unavailable. Hiring such an ineffective professor for a mandatory class has potentially impacted Olin's ranking negatively.

I would advise against selecting this professor, as she tends to solely focus on presenting her own viewpoints during class without providing precise explanations or responses to her students. It is advisable to keep your expectations low for her class. Her course evaluations tend to be irrational and unfair, resulting in unjust scores.

You can't learn anything in her class, everything has to be done by self-study, the video before the class is just narrating the concept, everything has to be done by yourself, I'm really not sure what the purpose of choosing this class is.

Had a great experience taking MKT 370 this semester. Class consists of a wide variety of deliverables and material, from tests, quizzes, in class presentations, brand challenge, participation, to guest speakers, etc. You really get out what u put in. Kinda tough grader but fair, makes the grading criteria clear. Would definitely take her class!
Ok professor, teaches good concepts but not very engaging. However, if you study, take her practice exams, and review lectures, you should be good in the class.
I'm not sure why her rating is 16% because she is hilarious and also very understanding of personal circumstances. She definitely prioritizes effort over perfection which I appreciate.

Schnurr has one of the most disorganized canvas pages I have seen, where most of the due dates were incorrect (she refused to fix any of the issues brought to her attention). The Supersite homework in the class is pretty horrible as well, and her lectures don't cover the material that is on the test.

Cannot believe that she has such a low rating, she was incredible in class, super funny, and so willing to help if you were confused about something or just wanted extra help. Great prof and person and I hope to have her again
I honestly don't know why the rating is so low, she was an amazing professor when I was there and my class even talked about how we couldn't believe how low her rating was.
Disorganized, Poorly managed department

As the head of the spanish dept you would think she knows what is going on. I had a different prof who had to step out for part of the semester, and wasnt at the same pace, so there were certain things on an exam that we hadnt done. Schnurr graded them and refused to give any grading mercy despite the fact that we handnt learned it yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly, she's as bad as the reviews seem. While she can be disorganized, she grades quickly and there's definitely cohesion when it comes to lessons. However, class is mostly speaking practice while all of the grammar or vocab work (there's a lot of it too) is done independently which isn't my style.. She's not the best, but not the worst either.

AVOID this professor. Schnurr is disorganized. She frequently forgot to post assignments on canvas, and some of her presentations had errors. Attendance is mandatory although I think she forgets to take attendance.

Incompetent. All there is to say. Takes two plus months to grade anything - in all reality the class is certain she loses everything we turn in and gives random grades depending about how she feels about you. Unbearable amount of useless homework. Extinguished any and all passion I have for learning the spanish language.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most incompetent professors I've ever had.

She's very sweet, but terrible at teaching. Don't take her class if you want to learn Spanish. She's scatterbrained (even emailed us the quiz once without even realizing) and takes forever to grade/return assignments. We went into the final not knowing what we had in the class. We had to teach ourselves all the material as well.
Awful Professor, super unorganized. She is amiable in person, but she doesnt care about teaching and her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not good at teaching. Not much more to say tbh.

I'm very shy and nervous when speaking. I only participated when she called on me--bad move. She barely goes over any literature until the day of. The oral exam is a nightmare as she didn't explain anything. The Spanish tutor is a big help until Schnurr contradicts what the tutor says. I'm a Spanish minor and I'm continuing w/ a different teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very useful class if interested in doing Business abroad. The vocabulary is incredibly useful, but she doesn't really care so it's up to you to learn. She is horrible at communicating and takes forever to grade, but I had a great time in the class. Take it with friends.

Schnurr is unlike any professor I have ever had. The class was very small, only 7 students, and she was ok with just about every excuse for a student to miss class. Loves talking about her experience and will waste an entire class hour in it. Very unclear and disorganized, takes forever to grade, but cares about student feedback for deadlines/tests
Absolutely no explanation of grades. I got a B+ in the class while getting A's on nearly every single test. Strongly dislike this woman.
Nothing special, pretty bad teacher

HORRIBLE TEACHER. STEER CLEAR. Schnurr doesn't explain anything, which makes the exams difficult. I was going to be a Spanish minor but he completely turned me away from the language. She made the class a lot harder than it should have been. Extremely disappointed with her representing the Spanish department at a school like WashU. AVOID HER.

She has good intentions; however, she is not the greatest when it comes down to wanting a solid understanding of the language. For example, I was explicitly told that any verb can be used like gustar, which is simply false. She can be funny and likes to relate to her students, but if you want to learn, this is not the best option.

A lazy, bumbling professor. She is so incompetant and she is not an easy A like everyone says. She gave me a B-, and I don't understand why. Take Braxs, Carey, or Bishop instead for oral communication, but avoid this woman--she is a nightmare.
horrible. gave me a B+. Don't know why she did. Please avoid at all costs.
Great class. It's easy and I had a lot of fun.

Although others comments about her lack of organization are decidedly true, I greatly enjoyed her Business Spanish class.  Students are expected to self-motivate to learn.  Her focus is on teaching, not grading, and if you demonstrate a growth in content and understanding and a real interest in the material you will do well.
I like her alot shes a very nice person who simply likes to converse in spanish, subtly helping build confidence in oral communication, the course i signed up for

Avoid this class. Everyone says she's a guranteed A, but I ended up w/a B although I worked very hard. I got a B because Prof Schnurr didn't like me, and in her class, grades aren't based on effort or product, but instead on whether she likes you. To make things, I didn't learn a single thing since she's so disorganized & scatterbrained.

The worst class ever. Schurr is so horrible that I don't know why she hasn't been fired. Since there's no "real" syllabus and graded assignments aren't returned until 2 months l8r, U can't know ur grade. And it's very hard to change her impression of you--if she doesn't like you @ the beginning, then she'll be biased against you 4ever. Avoid her!

If you're looking for an easy class where you do literally nothing then this class is for you.  However, if you were looking to learn something you'd better go elsewhere.  Schnurr is the absolute worst professor ever and when she actually comes to class all you do is chit chat or watch movies without any real purpose.  Everyone somehow gets an A.

Easiest class ever. Homework is never collected, exams are a joke. I think I technically failed the final, but I still got an A in the class. It is a lot of fun and a stress free class because you do nothing except watch movies. Definitely a great class if you are looking for an easy class either for requirements or for an easy A!

I had Schnurr for Spanish 101 and 102. Easy A's both of them. Just study before the exams, suck up a little, talk lots in class (which helps you practice Spanish anyway), and do the assigned exercises (which take <=10 min). She's got a cute kid and likes to trade restaurant recs. If out of things to talk about, trying those=brownie pts!

Perhaps the worst professor at WashU.  This lady is nice but completely disorganized.  Anyone trying to learn Spanish should avoid her.  Grades are a total mystery since she never returns the few assisngments that we actually do and tests are almost 100% based on the movies we watch.  I learned nothing.

Very nice and pleasant person.  Always interested in the students enjoying their assignments.  That said, she is very unorganized:  work handed-in is never seen again, she forgets about everything she has done or assigned in the previous class, and far too much time is spent watching movies in class with no discussion.

Totally disorganized and forgetful.  Don't bother doing assigned work since she'll never remember it for the next class.  Can get a bit frustrating never knowing what's going on or what your grade is being based on (since you won't do any work) but you'll come out with a good grade in the end, regardless of how little effort you put in

She's a bit crazy.  The class is completely disorganized, there is no organized syllabus (the one she passed out for the first two weeks wasn't even followed, then she just gave up).  The outline for course grading is irrelevent because she doesn't follow the assignments.  Nothing is ever handed back.  Avoid this class.

Very nice person, fairly easy class. However, she is very unorganized.  We never get quizzes or assignments back, which creates more work for us in the end. Not a very high stress class, very laid back. Most classes she just talks to us in Spanish.
A very easy class.  Watching movies is the majority of "homework", and classtime is usually spent discussing current events. Showing up every day seems to merit an A.
She is completely unorganized, but still fun in class.  You should definitely take her class.
No Comments
She's so unorganized. It's an easy A. She talks a lot of politics in Spain and Latin America, which is good if you're into that sort of thing. Sometimes you just wish she would teach you.

great teacher- definitely takes a personal interest in students and cares about their learning, doesn't go by the book but teaches more through talking and listening to spanish, which I thought was more helpful and improved my spanish speaking skills which is why I took the course in the first place

Although she takes a personal interest in her students and is passionate about Spanish, she is a lazy teacher. Her lesson plans are unorganized,and the goals for the course are unclear. Some days she will forego a lesson just to talk. She even showed us a movie that was 95% English!

Dr. Nesbit was among my favorite professors. I took a few classes with her, and loved each one. Her classes are reading-heavy, but she teaches from truly engaging works. I never felt I was doing "work." She gives students the space to play with their work and explore interesting topics. If you're a writing major, I recommend her.
She is good and very helpful. I always found her approachable
No Comments

Tarashea is definitely helpful and intelligent. She has a great personality and allows for enagaging class discussions. However, organization is not her strength. Although she did try to conduct the class in an organized fashion, we were pretty much behind on workshop for the whole semester. If you like a laid back instructor--she's great though!
Nothing much to say here. Nesse is a very caring professor and gives great feedback. Class isn't too hard, but I learned a lot.
GREAT professor. Very funny, gives interesting lectures, although they definitely drag a little at times. He really cares about his students' success.
Love Erik ! He gives you really good advice and he takes different opinions very well, and he makes classes very enjoyable!

He's a really nice and fun person, and genuinely cares about students. Not an easy class though! He makes you work for the grade - lots of reading, homework, and essays, not to mention quizzes and tests. A bit too much reading and not enough focus on the actual grammar/vocab in my opinion. He doesn't post slides online so go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: You can tell Nesse loves what he is doing because he is always very energetic and engaging in class. If you are deciding between professors, choose him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He was a hilarious and caring teacher that made lectures enjoyable.

He's so sweet and he gets really into what he's teaching. Would definitely take again!! For the essays, make sure you read over them and you're guaranteed a better grade if you go to meet with him before you turn it in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The exams in this class are very fair. He wants you to succeed and is even available outside of office hours to talk. Office hours have been extremely helpful especially on some of the harder problem sets. He posts notes and solutions to homework to canvas which are super beneficial when studying.
I think he was a solid lecturer. The class moved quickly at points but overall he was just a typical math professor.

Professor Nguyen is a sweet, funny guy and you can tell he cares about his students, but he isn't very good at teaching. His lectures were incredibly hard to follow and a lot of people, including myself, would attend other lecturers whenever possible. He also didn't cover everything on the tests in lectures, aside from reviewing the study guide.

Professor Nguyen makes jokes in class, and he is a really sweet person, but he isn't a great professor. He makes many computational and conceptual errors when he is working through problems which makes it hard to follow examples. His lectures are generally hard to follow and even harder to comprehend. Many people went to other professors' lectures

He's a pretty funny and sweet guy but not the best lecturer. Isn't that great at explaining the material, and most of my real learning came from outside the class. I found the exams to be pretty easy, though I skipped the vast majority of lectures by the end of the semester.

The other lecturers I went to (Thornton and Wick) spent significantly more time explaining the concepts of this course and for most of Nguyen's lectures it felt like he would spend about 5 minutes explaining the concept and the next 45 minutes doing practice problems with little explanation as to what he was doing. Seems nice but not a good prof

I love this man with all of my heart and I know he feels the same about each and every one of us. Just don't try to correct something super trivial or he will make you feel foolish. But he is a massive jokester and always makes us laugh and warms our hearts with his. Please take a class with this man, you will not regret it.

The man is a total genius, and it shows. His knowledge of the material is extensive, almost encyclopedic, and his ability to peel through the substance and give you a simple recitation of the law is unrivaled by any other professor I've taken. That said, he will often lose his train of thought making connections to other concepts, so follow along.
Great lecturer. Really really knows the topics and is enthusiastic about them.  Can be less helpful outside of class.
Decent prof if you can get past his elitism and recycled jokes. Straightforward presentation of material.
Class was interesting and concepts explained well.  I found the final unfairly weighted towards RAP concepts.  It comprised a far larger percentage of exam material than it did of class time.
I learned a lot and he inspired me to get my graduate in security certificate, also the other reviews are lying cuz he is a good prof and he does not normally give A+s lmao

He doesn't explain concepts very well and is very unorganized, tend to skip over slides and freestyle in class. Even if materials can be dense and long, he struggles to explain the basics. Gradings are very generous. I don't know what I learn from the course and still got an A.

Professor Zhang did have some trouble explaining some topics but I think a lot of it was due to there being so much material to be covered. Although, it is pretty obvious that he is very interested in what he teaches and is very generous in grading/extensions/extra credit.
Struggles to communicate complex ideas and hard to understand. Very unorganized class structure. Frequently misses lecture because of travel to conferences.

Great lectures! Plenty of readings outside class but as long as you get at least a synopsis you will be fine. Not a super harsh grader either. Far and away my favorite prof of the semester, she was always interesting and insightful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a kind, attentive, and passionate about the texts + open to all students' perspectives. Assigns us assignments due Sunday night for peer review in-class onTuesday- does not release the group assignments for peer review until MONDAY evening/night, causing cramming +Reading for Thursday class is way too heavy for a Tues-Thursday class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Would recommend

I would recommend the The 19th-Century Russian Novel to fulfill your Writing Intensive requirement. The books and discussions were interesting and Prof. Svobodny is a very enthusiastic instructor. Her instructions are clear and she is open to giving feedback on your essays if you share your ideas early. A good introduction to Russian Literature.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Svbodny is an absolutely wonderful professor. I've taken three literature courses with her and I wish I could take more. She provides wonderful insights, and selects great reading material. The discussion style course with the occasional lecture is the perfect formatting.

Great class. Professor Svobodny knows so much about literature, did a great job facilitating discussions and providing supplements to the readings. she's a tough but fair grader, and there were only 2 papers. A lot of reading, at least 100 pages per week- However, if you stay on top of it, it's not too bad. Take a class with her if you can!

I took Russian lit and language courses with Dr. Svobodny. She is a great professor and amazing person. If you have an interest in Russian lit, do yourself a favor and take a course with her. She knows her stuff, and will provide valuable feedback on your writing and reading analysis skills. She clearly cares about her students. Wonderful professor

I took the class Reading War and Peace but this prof offers two different Russian Lit classes a semester. She is an amazing teacher who really cares about her students and facilitates great discussions on the reading. Definitely take a class with her!
Dr. Danis has been one of my favorite professors here at WashU. He cares that everyone does well, and will go to lengths to help anyone. Definitely recommend!

Professor Danis is a really genuine guy and is passionate about Linguistics. The class isn't bad at all because there are few homeworks and he gives the exams online. I am a computer science major and was able to excel in this class easily. I would definitely take this class for a more laid back class and something fun to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His lectures can get a bit boring on occasion, but he's overall a good lecturer and clearly knows what he's talking about. Homework is all very manageable and easy. Textbook is technically required, but admittedly I did not read a single word of it, the lectures were enough to understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures were mind-numbingly boring. I like linguistics as a subject, but he makes it so tempting to skip. The grading is super easy and there is very little homework so I didn't learn much in his class. He made it so easy to skip that I didn't go at all between Thanksgiving and Christmas and got an A, I wish I had been forced to learn more.

Professor Danis has always been passionate about constructed languages and linguistics. The extra readings are inspirational and well-chosen. I walked into the class not knowing much about constructed languages, but I walked out of the class only to find myself willing to explore conlangs more.

Workload is very manageable; all quizzes are take-home, and grading criteria are clearly communicated. Prof. Danis has a somewhat monotone lecture style, but his interest in linguistics is palpable. He is extremely accessible outside of class and grades assignments quickly and fairly. Very caring and professional instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend Professor Danis to anyone who is looking for an inspirational and funny intro class. Overall the course is pretty chill and the workload is not heavy. He will introduce you very quickly to this amazing world of linguistics. You can always ask questions and discuss anything related to linguistics with him at study hall.

Super interesting class and Danis is a funny guy. He always made the 8AM entertaining by including jokes and photos of his cat on slideshows. Quizzes are take-home and open-note, but the questions can be pretty tricky. Keep up with lecture notes and ask questions during study halls, and you should be fine.

Not a fan of Danis' teaching style or course structure. A bit too dry and too few grades. No study guides or quiz resources. Tests are purposefully worded so that the answers cannot be found in the textbook, although the tests are "open note." Interesting content, but you really have to read the textbook and take notes. Don't skip.

Danis is a relaxed professor and a nice guy. Very dry disposition. You do have to take notes and learn the material but it's a pretty easy class. Interesting too, with good slides. I enjoyed it. It's not a complete freebie but it's a pretty easy class.

I had absolutely zero previous knowledge or experience with linguistics but tests aren't bad and the study guides are like practice quizzes which you can retake as many times as you want. The pace was quick and he tried hard to keep us engaged, making jokes, explaining concepts with memes and telling us stories about his new baby.

Professor Danis was great! Engaging lectures aided by memes and fun interactive participation, and he doesn't give much homework. As long as you take basic notes and skim through the textbook, you can easily get an A. This class piqued my interest in linguistics and language as a whole!

Dr. Danis was such a fantastic professor! The class was engaging with really interesting lectures and discussion. Great dad humor. You could tell Dr. Danis really was passionate about the class. Will definitely take more linguistics classes from him and HIGHLY recommend taking a class with Danis.

I really enjoyed Intro to Linguistics with Prof. Danis. His lectures aren't always the most engaging, but I learned a lot, and sometimes he throws in pictures of his cat and funny examples/videos. There are textbook readings and weekly quizzes but not a ton of work. Intro to Linguistics is a great class and definitely worth taking.
Entertaining lectures and a really caring guy. Professor Danis really made linguistics interesting to learn about. Thoughtful and meaningful class discussions. Light homework load.
Able to convey material clearly and learned a lot! Very approachable, accommodating, has clear slides, and has dry/dad humor. A great intro class overall and a survey into lots of linguistic topics.
Phonetics was interesting and professor Danis is really nice. Overall, low stress class, but you still learn a lot.
Perfect for fixed income securities. Literally makes one ready for all levels of CFA exam, fixed income section.
Hardest final exam of my life. So unnecessary.

His PPT complicates simple issues, and he has no interaction with students during class, which makes it difficult for people to listen to his class. The final exam accounts for too high a proportion of the course.
Please have some fun with Dr. Garleanu. I am sure you will like his class.
Super hard final exam with 70% of all grade. GG
Awesome professor.  You can learn advance fix income course which harder than CFA III
best class ever. taking a class with prof. catherall is a must! the nicest, most understanding, fun, and engaging professor that I have ever had. would take a class with her again in a heartbeat.

Prof. Catherall is amazing! Even though this was her first semester teaching, she had great lesson plans that were interactive and fun. Exams are not super difficult, so you get to really learn at low pressure. Definitely worth taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Catherall is awesome, she's really sweet and made learning in this class very very enjoyable and I hope to take another class with her in the future!

Every psych major should take this course.
An easy A, attendance isn't mandatory, extra credits, easy final project

100% recommend taking Psychopathology with Professor Karcher! Great lecturer, useful slides, and cares about student success. Exams also were easier than class material, I always felt over prepared after exams (in a good way).

Goated professor. Caring, accessible, and wants you to succeed. Going to be completely real here, studied max of 3 hours for each test (12 am - 4 am the day of the test) to focus on short-term memory encoding/storage, and went through 2-3 repeats of the material on the study guide as it corresponded to my notes. Ended up almost acing each test ;)

Professor Karcher is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She is a great lecturer and makes the long class periods seem short with videos, interactive portions, and personal anecdotes. I wish I could take another class with her and I thoroughly recommend this course! need to study for tests tho!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is super sweet and very knowledgeable. There is a lot of memorization but it is pretty manageable, I find her lectures to be engaging and we cover a lot of interesting topics. Definitely recommend!
Professor Karcher is an excellent lecturer, and Psych 354 has been very interesting. I found that the content has been easy to learn, and she posts exam reviews which are helpful and reliable.

Professor Karcher seems like a nice enough person, but she goes through hundreds of facts, then expects you to memorize every single one of them for a poorly designed multiple choice exam. It has twice the amount of stuff to memorize than an average psych class. Lectures are average, slides are below average. Would take with a different professor.

Professor Chakraborty is a very fair grader for the few assignments that you are graded on in this course (3 exams for 75% of the grade) and very generous and helpful during office hours for the homework. The fundamentals of the course are covered very quickly at the start, so you may get lost if you have misunderstandings in the first few weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were definitely middling but nothing unexpected. He made the first exam challenging and completely overcorrected for the following exams due to students underperforming; nice guy but failed to give me a concrete understanding of the statistics principles he tried to teach

Lectures are boring and confusing. He's a really funny guy and is really lenient with grading (sometimes too lenient), I just wish that his lectures were better. Halfway through the class I just decided to stop showing up and teaching myself the content using the textbook.

Hilarious. Loved him. Not gentle and definitely doesn't hide it when he thinks a question is stupid. Super fair grader and really wants every student to succeed. Go to lecture, he will tell you exactly what is going to be on the exam. Lectures can be boring but that's really the fault of the content. He tries to make it fun.
Extremely condescending, discourages asking questions and grades harshly/unfairly. Absolutely do not recommend.

Solid statistics class, very similar to AP stats if you took that in high school. Chakraborty wants everyone to succeed, can sometimes be hard to follow but as long as you do the textbook homework problems and understand them, you'll be good for the midterms. A final project was in place of the final exam, which was nice

I loved him. He is super passionate about the topic and his excitement made me more interested in the course. He can tend to be a bit repetitive. For the most part, his lectures cover most of the readings, but I'd probably still do them. The class is tough though because you are graded on so little.

Very good Professor!  Always enjoyed his lectures, he was very passionate about IR and pretty funny. His lectures were a little fast paced but he always explained the concepts well. Only had 3 quizzes and the lowest score was dropped. Section Participation matters!! The final wasn't anything too extreme as long as you studied.

This was one of the best classes I took and the professor genuinely cared for students. I thought Prof.'s style was engaged, funny, and thoughtful. I learned a ton and will continue in the major. Recommend.

100 points total in the class and more than half of the points in this class are free so its really easy to pass at the very least. Very reasonable and will move assignments if he feels we need more time. Lectures are fine, section is fine, there is a textbook but you don't need it just read the lectures. Very little hw. Easy class, fine teacher.

He frequently cancelled class, so I felt less prepared for the exam and assignments than I would have liked to be. It was so bad that it became a running joke in my friend group about how he never showed up. Once, he cancelled class at 1:45 am the night before because he was in Chicago (since class was at 8:30, that was less than 7 hours notice).

This class angered me. I enjoyed the subject and the professor was knowledgeable, but seemed uninterested in actually teaching. Classes were regularly cancelled (few weeks where we had all planned classes). The syllabus was constantly updated without corresponding readings being posted. Overall, interesting subject matter but execution fell short.

The material on her exam was extremely straightforward. How she made it feel so confusing with the lectures and readings I will never know. Will vouch for what the other reviewer said: she's a great person and brilliant, but her slides are disorganized and she goes on too many tangents. Exam was fun though.

Professor Norwood is fine as a person but not as a professor. Her PowerPoints were unhelpful and she was unable to answer questions that students had. One would think that after years of teaching that she would have the ability to answer simple questions. She also had a bit of a bad temper towards certain students for no reason.
a tough grader

One of the worst professors I have had in my entire academic career. Powerpoint heavy, scattered, easily irritated by student questions, and her explanations of basic tort concepts leave a lot to be desired. After cobbling together an outline from days of poor instruction, I have no idea how I will perform on her exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a great professor. At first glance, appears approachable and down to earth. I found that she was all over the place, very PowerPoint heavy, and easily intimidated by certain students. Although I received a decent grade I would never take another class with her again.

While the lectures could drag on (because she highly encouraged student participation), she was always very helpful and made sure our questions got answered.  I respect her, and enjoyed her teaching style, because  I valued hearing other's POV and their rationale. Will definitely be taking one of her other classes!

She pretty much teaches from powerpoint and doesn't know how to answer most questions asked.   She can also be quite rude, has a real attitude that doesn't really make sense in a collegial environment.  Outside of class doesn't make much time for students.  In summary, expect to take an undergraduate class with a woman who still "keeps it real."

You know, there were a few people in our class who just disliked Prof. Norwood, but I could never understand what they were talking about. Maybe it's a personality clash thing? IDK. I adored her, though. She lectures clearly. She's HILARIOUS. She answers questions. She's incredibly accessible outside of class. There's nothing not to like here.
Writes a good lecture, but cannot cope with student questions terribly well- assumes she knows what you are asking and ends up not answering the question at all.
very fun.
Her multiple choice questions are sort of out there but if you do her practice tests that helps. Awesome professor in class, never a dull moment.
very fair and understanding to students

Noa is an excellent teacher who creates an inclusive, respectful classroom. She clearly cares about student success and keeps expectations fair and consistent. While she's straightforward and real, she remains professional and ensures everyone feels comfortable participating. One of the few professors where I feel I can truly be myself.

I had Noa for Fall Freshman Hebrew. She is an amazing teacher with degrees in education. It shows; each lesson is meticulously planned out. Word of advice: keep up on your homework. It never takes more than 20 minutes max and is 1 pt for doing it. The one week extensions are not to be used on every assignment! Exams and quizzes were written.
Professor Weinberg is very funny and makes classes entertaining!

I had Noa in my first semester at WashU, and my classes with her were always the highlight of my day. She cares a ton about making class engaging and finding a way to get the material into our brains. Languages are tricky, but Noa orders the class in a way that makes a ton of sense. She cares about her students like a mother. Noa is the best!

Noa's class is one of the most difficult ones that I've taken here. She grades people at the same level even though there's a wide variety of fluency. She is open to meet with students, but not good at providing help. I took the course out of sole interest in the language but decided not to continue because her class brought me so much stress.
Noa is a great teacher, and her class is always super fun and chill. She always wants her students to succeed.
Loved my time with Professor Weinberg. She is great!
Noa is a great professor! As long as you go to class and don't fall behind on the homework you will be ok
Noa is a great professor! It is never a dull moment in her class - she manages to make even grammar fun and interesting. This is my fourth semester with her.

Noa is one of my favorite professors! She is caring, energetic and overall and amazing professor. The workload is easy, but still educational -- She wrote the book! If you want to learn Hebrew, you will. The class is really fun and I am close with the people I met there. Noa creates an amazing and inclusive environment.
Noa has made me love learning Hebrew again. I look forward to her class everyday because she creates a welcoming environment for all of her students. I am so excited to be in her class next semester.
Noa is an awesome professor. She makes class fun and engaging. She cares a lot about teaching Hebrew and all of her students.

Noa is an amazing teacher and truly wants her students to learn while also keeping class interesting. She does give a lot of homework but it definitely helps prepare you for exams. She also provides multiple opportunities for extra credit.

Noa is awesome. I have been with Noa for two semesters, and she can be tough but really cares about her students. She is always making class fun with great slideshows, and there is ample oppurtunity for extra credit!!!
She was great would take again but there is a lot of homework

Noa is the best! This is now the second Hebrew class I've taken with her and she is incredibly committed to helping students learn new concepts in a fun, conversational way. She's always willing to go above and beyond make sure each and every student succeeds, and is super helpful in office hours outside of class too. Can't recommend highly enough.
Her class is very entertaining and chill. All the tests/grading is straightforward and it is very easy to do well. Also lots of extra credit opportunities.

Noa is a great professor. I took first year modern Hebrew with her and I was amazed by how much I learned and retained, without ever feeling that the course was very difficult or too much work. Definitely would recommend taking.
She cares about her students but isn't always the best at explaining and isn't necessarily flexible.
Noa is just lovely. She really cares about her students and made learning Hebrew fun. She also created a community between all the levels of Hebrew in the department which was cool! I had a blast.
Great professor, really fun class! There is daily homework, but never too much or anything unmanageable. Definitely recommend!

Kirby is the worst professor I have ever had. He has unrealistic expectations and has encouraged us to "find" objects to use from restaurants and places near us. Which just means steal. He has been downright rude to people and makes fun of students. He likes when we tear each other down in Crit. He needs a reality check

Pros: pushes you to explore new materials provides lots of opportunities (exhibitions, conventions) actually cares about teaching you to be an artist life skills you will make pieces that you are proud of Cons: Beware, his mood can change quickly will push his own opinions on your piece Advice: Be steadfast, independent, and hardworking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. Professor is out of touch with his students, pretty much manipulating them to make what he wants, instead of what actually interests the students. Unrealistic expectations, with very vague project guidelines. This class was a waste of time and overall made me frustrated.

I lovveeee kirby; he is an inspiring proffessor. many people critize him for the difficulty of the work and his open ended assignments but that is why i liked him. he pushed us to try new media like welding and wood work - things other 3D classes didnt do. i love his sense of humor he brings to class. overall, i would love to take his class again

Noah really inspired me. He's a really charismatic instructor and kept the class from being boring. Working 3D is hard, but he really knows his stuff and I feel like I learned so much from him. Be prepared to work hard and think, but you'll feel really proud of yourself when you see what you can do! You'll do things you never thought you could

Mainly wanted to put in a good word for him: don't be scared of his review! He is more clear than other professors and offers a lot of resources to help you with your projects. His assignments are also good for portfolio pieces. He makes you make a lot of models before making the real thing: important learning tools! Cares about students' learning

Noah cares about his students, but he's just not that inspiring. He wants us to succeed, and I like him a lot for that. He tries to make class fun, but it is hard to teach 3D design to kids who are interested in Communication Design. Kirby does try his best and gives good feedback, but it would be better if he gave it earlier rather than later.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Noah Kirby is an awful person and professor. He forces students to be ruthless in critique by rewarding them for tearing their peers down. Would not recommend, he made me want to drop out of the art school and made me hate sculpture/3D work, things I had been fond of in the past.

He is a very strong artist.  I took blacksmithing, and yes you will be outside. You will work hard, and you will learn a lot. Noah doesn't go and tell people what to do, but if you ask him he will help. He critiques everyone's work in order to push them to do their best. I poured hours into the class, learned a lot, and had a great time.

Noah states he is an artist first, a teacher second. You are not a student - you are his competition. So he has no interest in helping you succeed - if so his life as an artist would be exponentially more difficult. Zero sense of art history. He will use his rank to his own advantage and grade low. Not recommended.

Noah is very helpful if you know the right way to ask for help.  A lot of times he's going to leave things open ended and you might be confused, but I think overall that's a good thing and gets you thinking.  He expects you to be very independent. He's clearly passionate about art, and is great to have one-on-on studio visits with.

I had a lot of fun with Noah. He's a great guy if you try to understand him. He's not going to give you a lot of hints but that's what art school is about-figuring things out for yourself. I wasn't happy with my grade but I really enjoyed the class overall.

Noah made the class a challenge.  He was reluctant to answer questions in any kind of detail, which often left me confused, but also taught me to think and make decisions about my work on my own.  Noah was a good instructor overall, although I didn't always enjoy the class when I was in it.

The class was really physically demanding.  I learned a lot but didn't receive any feedback during the semester.  At the end I was given a pretty harsh grade that I don't think reflected my effort.  Don't take it if you don't want to spend hours in freezing rain blacksmithing.

He was a great professor in this class, helped us understand the material and brought very insightful speakers to the lectures. I've learned a lot in his classes that were well organized and through the materials he sent for readings.
Doesn't deserve this low of a rating. He's honestly a really nice professor and approachable. His class is definitely hard, but so is almost every bme class.
Seems lazy to explain anything and expect students to know on their own

This is such a awful professor that I wouldnt recommend to anyone. 1. His lecture is vague and lacks coherent mathematical explanation. He does calculation by drawing crude lines on slide 2. His speaking style and wording make it so easy to be distracted or make a previously well understood concept hard to understand. 3. Homework has many bugs.
I don't know how to describe professor Ledbetter's teaching style without using expletives.

Bland lectures and takes no time to ensure understanding. Instead of spending time on things that matter, professor Ledbetter takes 15 minutes teaching irrelevant material learned in previous classes. Shows work of math on slides and verbally explains without ever actually working out a problem.

Is not the best lecturer; his slides badly rehash the textbook. His tests are poorly designed for the content that he teaches, and the workload he assigns is on the excessive side. Truly nothing praiseworthy here
Not a typical academic professor. Started teaching after working for many years, which brought the "real world" to the class. Much more fun, and less dry than most engineering professors.

The type of engineering professor I would expect at a top 20 university.  Clear, detailed, challenging, and helpful when you need it.  He stayed long after class sometimes to help us make sure we were ready for the homework.  The tests were always very tough, but if you did the work, you would get the grade.  Not a BS course.  I learned much.

Professor Nobs made a tough course understandable.  He was always prepared with a full lecture.  I had to work my butt off, but I learned much more than I expected at the beginning of the course.  I am actually using what I learned in this course.
Very challenging course. Would have been much more difficult without the professOr.

Extremely arrogant, thinks he knows a lot and thinks the class knows nothing. Thinks he is funny. Pretty annoying. There is no way to make the class hard, so tries to make tests as complicated as possible.
friendly, delivers well-organized lectures
Sit near the front if you want to hear.

If you don't have the backfiles you are screwed.  With the backfiles it's a pretty easy class.  Don't bother to go to class, simply do homework and practice the past tests on the backfiles.  My advice: take the course with wheeler!

Give him some credit. It's pretty amazing that at his age, he teaches almost completely from memory. The material is hard by nature. But if you go to class and process the notes, you should do fine. The book is terrible which makes classes even more important. The backfile system also helps.

His lectures are absolutely POINTLESS to go to, because you can't hear him and he'll put you to sleep with what you can hear. That's why I only went to 3 or 4. Homework wasn't too bad, tests are open note. If you don't mind skipping lectures and learning material on your own then take him.

The class was really tough, but that has a lot more to do with the material than with any sort of lack of teaching ability on Katz's part.  I thought he did a fairly decent job handling difficult material.  While he wasn't fantastic, it'd take an incredible professor to do better with this stuff.
um. after him, i started to dislike math

The best thing about the class was the availability of backfiles. They help tremendously on exams and with the homework. You learn nothing in class because he does examples that take the entire period. He is also hard to hear and understand. Take him over Wheeler just because of the backfiles.
Had him for SSM326 and SSM317.  Can't really understand what he's saying unless you're sitting in the front row.  Homework helps w/ tests.  Don't really need to go to class.
He's boring, but easy. Homeworks are pretty hard, but tests are open notes and just like the homework.
He's really nice
Homeworks are difficult and lengthy - but are worth it to learn the material.  He is really a nice guy and will help out as long as you ask.  He's kind of out there sometimes - but it's not a fault.

The guy is old as hell. He plays with a rubber band for half of the class. He seems totally out of touch with the students. Sometimes he stays up all night and comes to class wearing the same clothes!! What the hell? I agree with the back file or die comment. Good luck with the Katz.
bad, boring, confusing
good teacher, available for help, homework is relevant and helps prepare for the tests though at times a bit much
He knows his stuff.  Homeworks are challenging, which means you actually need to learn the material!
Not a terribly exciting professor, but he knows his stuff and helps you out if you ask.
GET BACKFILES or DIE!!!! At least there is a good curve, but it will suck next year without Brian as TA!
Lectures are boring and not very helpful.  He is there for one on one help but the TA should be the one teaching the class because he explains it better.  Homeworks are too hard and too long.

This was sort of a weird class. You would sit through lectures and have no idea what's going on, but the exams are so easy. The midterm was literally two problems we did in class, and he didn't change the numbers. He's a funny and chill guy.

Quantum physics is never going to be easy but I think the professor did a good job of guiding the class to understanding complicated topics. We covered many interesting real-world applications. There were lots of opportunities to ask clarifying questions and we did a lot of practice problems which helped me to digest the content better.

Some of the class lectures were a a bit fast-paced and confusing at times but if you put in the time and effort you should be able to learn the material and do well. Ogliore is accommodating and also available during office hours if you have questions. He cares about his students and also did his best to make sure we got the most out of lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Avoid!!

Never met the professor once, only interaction was a rude email response. Most of the lab AIs are super nice and provide lots of advice on lab reports. However, when the lab reports are graded, the graders look for things that above and beyond what was taught in lab. Rubric is very unclear. Must have an almost perfect lab report to receive an A.

The only interaction you will have with Professor Ogliore is by email. For the course as a whole, though, I would suggest being thorough in everything. If you think a report good enough to submit, take another 30 min to an hour to go through and be sure that everything is in the right place and that you clearly articulate everything.

Expectations for lab reports were never made clear and graders were inconsistent about how many points were deducted for the same error because there wasn't a standard rubric. A lot of this class is hoping that you get a nice grader and learning what they want based on point deductions on previous reports. Content barely aligns with 191 lecture.

Never met him once through the whole semester of the class. Grading criteria for the lab reports was never clear. He would often take points off for things that were clearly included. Reports take a significant amount of time to write despite a lack of guidance. Grading comments were often excessively rude and not helpful at all for improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: To be blunt, this class sucks. the AIs are super pushy and annoying since they think everyone chooses to take this class rather than It just being a requirement for most premeds. The grading is hard considering the sheer lack of guidelines. office hours do not help. physics AIs know nothing about the grading and are not helpful in office hours

This man is completely absent from the class he teaches. Literally never met him once but by the way he instructs the physics lab department I can't imagine he would be a good professor. This class is unnecessarily difficult and you're entirely on your own for the whole thing.
Lots of lab report. Very stupid word count policy and obscure grading criteria. The professor himself NEVER shows up during any class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ridiculous course

Interacted with Ogliore once, nice enough. The class, however, is terrible. Instructions are unclear at best, grading is inconsistent between graders and the LAI's instructions, the first midterm was difficult with little study material provided, and I hated the three hours per week in class. Try to vomit every little detail on lab reports.

Ogliore is interesting. The lab is definitely ridiculously hard but Ogliore himself is nice. I reached out twice about confusion and the first time was meh but the second time I met w him in person and he's very nice! Even reached out to me before the last test to make sure I was doing alright. I would give Ogliore a 4/5 but the class a 2/5.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I reached out to Professor Ogliore several times and each time it was unpleasant. He was not willing to help students in his class by even dropping a single lab. Lab quizzes were extremely hard. I never even saw his face once for lab and come in to help, yet he was so strict on grading. Would never want to take anything with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Physics Lab during Fall of 2021 under this professor and the lab was extremely unfair in terms of grading as a large part of your grade is based on the groups you get. There was no teaching and not enough preparation material for the Physics Post Lab Quizzes, and the Professor did not answer any of my emails.

Professor Ogliore tries very hard to accommodate his lectures to the students preparedness. Overall, he covers the topic thoroughly and makes the subject interesting! Physics will generally be hard with any professor, but I think Ogliore does a good job at it.
does not cover topics effectively. Mainly just reads off of PowerPoint slides
Ogliore is a solid professor. Very intelligent and thorough.
Ogilvie is the man... His lectures can be a little long-winded, but he is one of the nicest teachers I have had at Wash U.

Very entertaining. Positive attitude. Definately one of the kindest and most understanding professors. Class covers some interesting material. Its kind of an environmental ethics class. If you attend, and put in some effort, you will do well.

Dr Ogilvie is the coolest prof. ever. He gives tons of extra credit and will go to great lenghts to ensure that you understand. He's also very funny and cracks many jokes. I highly recommend his class. I'll probably get a B+, but I really deserve a C-considering my lack of effort--the extra credit boosted my grade. I'm gonna miss his class a lot.

Very enthusiastic and friendly instructor.  Class may appear to be heavy on the math for non-science majors, but it is definitely possible to do well on the tests regardless of previous experience in science classes.  If you attend class, you'll do fine.

Ogilvie is the definition of the disheveled Physics professor.This class involves more environmental ethics that scientific math: so non-majors are welcomed. Take advantage of his warm personality and get to know him-he is the push-over dad you never had. His tests are really hard and his TAs are harsh graders.
Great guy! he's hilarious.
Genuinely wants you to learn and will go out of his way to help you. Might be boring sometimes but excellent teacher overall.

Although sometimes boring and hard to understand, Kadan is dedicating to helping students learn.  He will re-teach and re-explain anything.  He wants to prepare students for the real world and help them get a great job.  He takes pride in that.  His tests were hard but not unfair.  The man is comical... his jokes make class.

Did not care for the group cases approach to learning.  I prefer a teacher who gives some guidance.  Diff things work for diff people though, so you never know.  I've def never been the group work type.
Can't speak. Really boring. Very bad preparation guidelines for exams.

Kadan is a great professor.  The class is really hard, but it's definitely worth it, especially if you're interviewing for I-Banking jobs.  It's not that he gives out a lot of work, the cases are hard and timeconsuming, but it's how you learn the material.  Grade distribution is very fair
