Overall good teacher.  Very clear notes and explainations.  Gives out lots of work.  Class is interesting.  Best Finance teacher I've had in the b-school.
Great teacher, give a LOT of work, explains concepts clearly, slides easily understood if you miss class, has accent but his english is very good

Class material is great.  However his teacher method is 'slide reiteration'.  Difficult to understand his accent.  Not very approachable.  Never gives out answers.  Too bad he doesn't present the material in an intersting way.
There is quite a bit of outside work, and the exams are very memorization heavy. He was pretty chill though, and seemed to be interested in what he was teaching.

Dr. Olsen is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is incredibly helpful outside of class, offering various times to ask him questions and talk about course content. Beyond this, he cares about every student's success, all while being incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about Evolution. Though difficult, I strongly recommend this class!

Prof. Olsen has been one of my favorite professors. It was a true pleasure to take this class with him. He has so much passion and love for evolution and the natural world; it's infectious! His tests can be difficult, but all the material is taken from the slides and discussion sections (review both!). I recommend this class to everyone. Take it!

At first I did not like him, but he grow on me over time. Very accessible outside of class, and he was willing to help you out by teaching you one-on-one and going over what you got wrong on exams. He is so passionate about evolution it was sweet. It was tough, but if you put in the work, you will get an A. And ask for help if you need it!

Professor Olsen is an inspiring, awesome professor. His passion for what he teaches radiates the classroom. He is so engaging and loves to see students truly grow and understand the concepts. You have to work hard for your grade, but it is very fulfilling.

Best professor I've had. It's clear from his lectures that he's passionate and excited to teach the content. He's very approachable, often willing to make time to meet outside his office hours, and he makes material easy to understand. He tries to remember everyone's name in a class of 60 people. An A is definitely possible to get if you try.

Olsen was a spectacular professor. I always looked forward to the 1.5 hour lectures, which often felt like going to a good movie. He adds the best examples to his, lectures which really makes the content clearer and more interesting. He's the first upper level science professor I've had who studies the class roster to learn all 60+ students' names.

Favourite class thus far, Professor Olsen goes above and beyond in helping students do well. Even discussion section was enjoyable and interesting. If interested in evolution at all, you should definitely take this class!
Great class. Interesting material and fair professor. Super nice. Definitely does more than the minimum.

Dr. Olsen is the man, certainly the best professor I've had at Washu. His lectures are very interesting and he explains the material clearly. Tests aren't a cakewalk, but if you study hard you will do well. He's also super helpful outside of class and is more than happy to meet with you if you need help. Take this class, you won't regret it!

I took Evolution from the first semester this Professor taught it and it was one of my favorite classes at WashU.  He is an excellent lecturer with plenty of examples that will make you appreciate the different life on this planet.  I didn't really do any of the readings, just went to class, took good notes, and studied hard for the tests.

I took Evolution with Olsen.  The class was pretty much as expected.  It was his first time teaching (Fall 2006).  He is very knowledgeable about the subject and is happy to meet with you outside of class.  The tests were kinda long and there was a lot of focus on the readings, so it is important to do them.
Great teacher, also surprisingly funny

He's fine as a professor, but it's often difficult just to parse what he's saying even in a small room and he seems content to allow students to drive lecture--which can be nice but also problematic as you walk away not really understanding what you learned in each class period.
He's soooo old. I always have trouble hearing what he is saying. Nice man, but lectures are incredibly boring. Easy grader, but I find it really hard to listen to him.

Dr. Okenfuss is a great professor. He is always willing to take a timeout during his lecture to answer questions and he clearly puts a lot of thought into his replies. His assignments and exams are very fair and he seems to be genuinely interested in his students. Would recommend taking him to anyone that is interested in Russian history.

AWESOME! Honestly, at first I was nervous because of how old he was. Don't be deterred by of this! Give it a week and you will see that he is actually a) a total genius about Russia, b) an awesome guy, really understanding, and c) has some crazy interesting anecdotes of when he visited the USSR himself. I highly recommend him as a professor! Do it!
Great professor! he is very helpful and interested in his students. Class gets slow at times but tolerable. This man is a fountain of knowledge.
No deadlines on papers, which sounds good but hurts later on. Very knowledgable about all material, but does not clearly explain what should be done on papers. Only read first 2 pages of my drafts.
Great professor - knows his stuff!
Incredibly easygoing, concerned about students, always willing to answer questions. Hands down one of the best professors at WU.

I thought he was very cool. he was interested in the subject, very knowledgable and would surprise me with the ability to field any question asked no matter how detailed or obscure. If you pay attention, you will do well.
Long lectures get boring, but he really loves the subject and you can tell.  Go see him before you turn in a paper and he'll like you, then you're all set.
Very rude to me.  Seemed unfairly biased against me, although I could not figure out why.  If you are on his good side, that is great, but I hated this class.
Here's a teacher you can tell really enjoys the subject he's teaching.  Always willing to answer questions even if it gets the class off track.
Excellent prof.  Very knowledgeable and helpful and approachable; good guy to talk with about a lot of things, really.  Highly recommended.
kind of bizarre but very nice; his 1.5-hour lectures can get boring
No Comments
the nicest professor I've ever had
very knowledgeable, good lecturer, very good with student interaction

Horrible professor. Unclear with assignments and changes them in the middle, talked down to the entire class and treated us like children and just generally all over the place. Doesnt keep track of what she assigns us and cant even remember peoples names after a whole semester.
Very talented and knows her stuff excellent teacher. Not sure why she gets such a bad rap from so many reviews.  If you do your work and pay attention you will excel in this class.

She is a truly awful teacher who assigns absolutely insane amounts of work. Her expectations are completely unrealistic and she did not help me develop any further skill whatsoever.  She is not understanding that students have other classes as well. She's very confusing and mixed up, and is very unclear about assignments. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.

Professor Oosterbaan is strict and doesn't tolerate disrespect in her classroom, but nice once you chat with her a bit. Very understanding if you're in trouble, just doesn't bend rules. Sometimes directions are a little unclear but if you ask she'll clarify. Coming away from some bad professors, it was a relief to have someone acting professional.
Very unclear, doesn't seem to keep track of students' progress, is in her own world
great professor- really nice, easy going, easy to talk to. a little confusing at times, but as a student you just have to learn how to ask the right questions.
if you get this women for drawing..try to switch out! she is unclear and makes very little sense.  will assign a specific assignment and then change her mind once you already started it.

i have never disliked a professor so much.  class is pointless, the assignments are all busywork, gives unrealistic time lines and amounts of work, changes the assignments as you work on them, and tends to behave unprofessionaly at times.  i have never been in a class before where every single person hated the teacher and hated coming to class.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES.  most mixed up person on the face of the earth.  changes her mind all the time, can't keep track of what assignments are about.  assigns pointless exercises.  can be overly harsh. has completely unreal expectations of art students. learned a thing or two from her, but overall, a terrible professor.

I was a fan of Oltmanns, and the class in general.  The information is interesting, important, and practical: it all has very pressing real world implications.  Grading fair and straightforward, and u get to drop ur lowest exam and replace the other w/ a paper if u want.  Lectures did a good job summing the heavy amount of textbook info/details.
Okay content. Really not so interesting lectures. Bad class structure. Only exams. Only take this class if you're a psych major.
this class is WORK but you will be so thankful you took it. completely changed my view on mental health. Oltmanns is a genuius
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Content was interesting, I learned more than any other class

Its the most reading I've done at Washu. Says he won't test any trivial specific details, ends up asking those specifics on the exams. Not to mention most of the 300 pg textbook is fair game, and buying the textbook is mandatory cause its linked to your grade. Oh and he wrote the textbook too if that changes anything

Exams are way too specific. Everything on the textbook can occur on the exam and that's like eight hours of reading a week. Classes are not helpful at all. You don't need to attend lectures to get good grades on exams. Just read textbook.

The other ab psych professor is much easier. In this class, it is mandatory to purchase the textbook, and to read most of its 300 pg contents. You didn't even have to buy or read the textbook in the other class. Too much time spent on this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Incredible and knowledgable professor. Changed the way I view mental health and humanity. Given a lot of chances to succeed grade-wise, as you get to substitute an exam with a paper and drop another exam. If you're on the fence about taking this class, you definitely should!

I think that Oltmann's is a terrific professor. He is personable, honest, and funny. He provides students with what they need to succeed and it is up to them how much time they want to put into it. He has a hefty extra credit opportunity which helps, also.

Textbook Heavy. Lectures not that important. Tests you on numbers and facts so memorization heavy. Harder than the other abnormal psych professors. Weekly quizzes also take a lot of time and the questions are not well constructed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Good professor, good class! Not hard to do well if you read the book and the slideshows. Drops your lowest exam grade and allows you to replace another exam with an optional paper, so lots of chances to succeed. Interesting lectures with lots of case studies and examples from his personal experience in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Totally renewed my passion for psychopathology! Highly recommend!
LEGEND
Awesome class! He has some great stories, and he does a good job of keeping class interesting.  Overall, a great guy and teacher!

He rambles a lot and doesn't seem to do anything but talk about the same cases he treated years ago. If you don't get a good TA you'll be screwed. I got the worst TA when I took his class--she was an anal control freak.

Was not interested in taking this class, but I found that I really enjoyed it. Oltmanns was really relaxed. He also has a lot of experience in his field (for example, NASA uses him to help select psychologically stable astronauts). Good stories. Class can get a little long, though, if you're not in the mood to listen to him ramble.

The lectures were not as interesting as he may have thought they were.  You can get away with not going to class, however your grade will suffer if you never show up, and you have to read the text thoroughly.  The exams are challenging, but not unbearable.

My favorite professor so far at Wash U! He is very interesting during lectures, genuine, and available to answer any questions inside and outside of class.  Professor Oltmanns has great stories from his experience in the field and is overall very helpful.  I would highly recommend taking a class with him.
No Comments
No Comments
Did two semesters of independent study with him.  He was very helpful and really easy to get along with!  He genuinely cares about his students.  I would definitely recommend him!

Frank is a great guy with a genuine passion for what he does. He is downright hilarious at points as well. The class will certainly teach you a lot about advertising and tech. You are only graded on two exams and a term paper, which sounds tough until you realize he provides more than enough questions in the study guides that make exams easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome prof and an expert in the field of advertising. Class is interesting and midterm/final are very similar to the study guides he gives beforehand. 10 page paper at the end of the class which is rough, but definitely a pretty easy class.

This class is quite easy. Almost all of the work that you need to do can be done during class with time to spare. Everything is group work though, so that can be annoying. Frank cares more about the idea for a campaign than the actual execution and he loves to give feedback, so if you ask for it, you will be in a great position.

Frank is honestly amazing! His lectures are great and he's passionate about teaching. He's also super caring and understanding. His class was not only easy but I learned a ton of super interesting stuff!

Former advertising man, really knows his stuff. Lectures are great. Material is interesting. Lots of anecdotes about his time in the industry. If you're at all interested in advertising, take one of his classes.

Probably the most content-heavy class I've ever taken at WashU, prepare for a time commitment! However, content was extremely helpful for MCAT prep, exams were never unfair though they required a lot of memorization. Dr. Osdoby is also very kind.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Speaking now as a 2nd year med student, I very much recommend taking endocrinology. Even though the information is relatively simple, theres so much that it can seem overwhelming. Keep up with it! It prepared me so much for the MCAT and has been one of the most helpful classes for med school.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was a tough class. Dr. Osdoby has a very dry lecture style and dry lecture material, so 90 minute classes test your ability to focus. His tests were fair, and he offered some extra credit, but still was v. difficult. Even so, I remember more from this class than my previous biology courses. Be ready to memorize lots of pathways.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Loved Dr. Osdoby! He offers a LOT of information which can seem overwhelming, but the exams are extremely fair and offer extra credit. He's obviously passionate about his field and always personable/ready to help.

Fun class, you learn alot! But there's so much information, I wish i took it with a friend. Class was based on 3 non-cumulative exams (no final), a paper, and 3 quizes.  He is very willing to answer questions, wish is awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class had a LOT of information in each lecture. He only gave us two exams for the semester, so there's a TON of material on each one. You'll have to cover it all to some degree for the multiple choice section, but he does let you pick which essays you want to answer. Nice guy to talk to, definitely willing to answer questions and help out.

Not all professors can make the flipped classroom work, but Dr. Weisensee can. I felt like I learned a lot in her class. She's also caring and responsive over email. That said, her class is a lot of work, especially at 8:30 in the morning. The design homeworks are quite challenging. If you stay on top of things, you will learn a lot.

This class is A LOT of work and tests your time management skills. At certain points, the deadlines seemed a bit too short and unreasonable. With that said, I think I've learned the most from this class than any other class. I found the content to be pretty interesting and the professor is very knowledgeable.

Definitely the hardest MechE class at WashU. She is a great professor, especially when you go to OH. Required course, but really make sure you review thermo and go to office hours to ensure the design homeworks go better than horrible. Sorry, this class is hard, but it's college, and it's engineering.

She underestimates how much work her design homeworks actually are and doesn't believe us when we tell her. Everyone in this class has been miserable all semester. The class would actually be super interesting if it weren't for the completely unreasonable courseload. You can't enjoy or absorb content if you are drowning in it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: super fun class! if you study (and/or took a romance language in high school), the work is very nice paced and easy.

Professor Scartoni is really friendly and definitely cares about each of his students. His feedback is constructive, and we spend each class before a test reviewing.

He spends a lot of time planning events for the Italian department, and you get extra credit for attending 3-5 (There are at least 15 events every semester).
Paolo is absolutely amazing! I recommend his class to all my friends at WashU. Seriously the best professor I've had. He will make you love Italian.

Absolutely AMAZING! Brings joy and energy to every class, making it so you look forward to going. Attendance and participation are absolutely mandatory, but that's expected for a foreign language class. Easily reachable outside of class, either by office hours or through email. Would take this class many times over if I could!
italian king

This is Paolo's first semester teaching at WashU, and he is killing it! He has truly made me fall in love with Italian because of his passion for the subject. He makes class so interesting, and he has a genuine drive to help every student understand Italian. If you're unsure about taking Italian, let this be your sign because Paolo is the best!
The arbiter of truth. His inspirational seminars on the differences between percolation and phase separation with percolation plus were certainly instrumental to my understanding of life. And love.
Nice? person but awful professor.

Everything people say about Pappu is true. No body learns everything, everyone gets A's, etc. By far the most condescending prof I've ever had. The lectures are very lofty and theoretical and he NEVER gives examples to illustrate. Even the textbook he chose is awful. Still have no idea what actually happened in that class and what I "learned."

Almost half the class attended less than half of the lectures and almost everyone ended with an A... 
No one learned anything in this class.

This class defies learning in that you don't have to understand the material well to get a good grade... just get a really good study group and memorize the test questions. Obviously, as legendary as papputine considers himself, he doesn't care a lot about students. Basically never replies to email, intimidating to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 96+ is an A while I get an A-. Can't see my final paper so I don't know whether there's a mistake. And what I know is, HE OFTEN HAS CALCULATION MISTAKES!!!
90-96 was an A-, 96-100 was an A, while 100+ was A+. The 48-hour take home final takes you ENTIRELY 48 HOURS.

Easily one of the most genuine professors I've had at WashU. Really cares about students understanding the material and wants them to do well. Go to recitation, email him questions, and you'll be alright.

Dr. Pappu is very condescending and appears non-interested in teaching. He's apparently mad that he couldn't get into med school or something (he vaguely mentioned this to one of his prior lab member)
Awful professor. Shows no respect to students when you talk to him in person.
Simply put, he doesn't really care. There's a reason that his exams are a joke. He's pretty condescending to students on multiple occasions. But, it's quite an easy A if you put in the work.
Judge it yourself. He said in front of the class that he would give an A to a student who would beat a student who unfortunately gave a wrong answer. That's a Wash U professor!!!!!!
Great Professor. Although material he teaches in this class is tough, Dr. Pappu makes tests and quizzes so easy. He is extremely helpful during his office hours too. Such an easy A class.
Great Teacher
Rohit is the best!  I love it when he uses words like "chap" and "shenanigans" and "solvophobic"!
Favorite class of college. Had a great time. Spent all of his time engaged in an open discussion with the students.

So the book for the class is extremely unhelpful. Every page is filled with numerous formulas and almost all of it is incomprehensible. Unfortunately, every lecture is drawn straight from the textbook and additional explanation is not often provided unless asked for. Overall, I did not gain an understanding of Thermodynamics from this class.
Super chill prof who cares alot about the material. Yea hes a lil disorganized but if you pay attention in class youll be alright. Super chill about deadlines too.

He's a disorganized lecturer and his nature is reflected on the tests.Tests are open note but not about grasping concepts and being able to apply examples but just specific facts glossed over throughout the course and are majority of your grade. Only take if you can take notes on everything he ever says and complete all of the extra credit.

I quite liked Dr. Parks, but I don't know if he's a great teacher or not. The class was pretty easy in my opinion, with the lion's share of the grade coming from 3 take-home, open-note quizzes that had student-written questions. Very knowledgeable and easy to follow. It's an easy, fun time, but I don't know if I've *learned* what I ought to.

Most classes consisted of him reading "current events" headlines and articles (many of which were years old) verbatim off the board. If you don't learn how to laugh through it by mid-October, you will struggle to haul yourself to class. One plus is that he was open and transparent with students about attendance and work expectations.

The class wasn't much work, but I was constantly stressed about it. Dr. Parks would ask incredibly niche questions on the exams that didn't seem to get at the important concepts. He also didn't grade anything past the first exam until right before the grading deadline, so I didn't know how I was doing at all.

Professor Parks confused me. He clearly likes the material he teaches, but he doesn't put a lot of effort into the course. The exams were take-home, open note and written by students. He almost never grades assignments in a timely manner, and doesn't post lecture material until right before an exam. I wanted more out of the course, and from him.

Lectures mostly consist of watching videos of animals. My exam grades have represented the worst grades I have received in undergrad as students generate exam questions which he seems not to read for validity before testing us on. Half of our exams test us on his own personal opinion. Bless his heart for being so kind, but the teaching isn't there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He follows no curriculum and class is a personal yap session where he talks about what he finds interesting. These random opinions will make up a majority of his exams making it hard to do well or know what to pay attention to in class. I was disappointed as I was excited to learn about the topic and instead learned what his favorite animal was.
This guy's tests were all based on the most random stuff in class, I feel like I didn't learn anything at all, and his curriculum was literally just whatever came up in his head.
Really cares about the topics, but the exam questions are based on his personal opinions.

I don't know why Prof Parks gets such a bad rap. He is obviously very passionate about what he teaches and I feel like I learned a lot from his class. Lectures are recorded, but engaging enough to attend in person. Slides are posted on Canvas (not meant to be written word for word). Exams are open-note and there are lots of fun EC opportunities!

I liked Parks and think he is a very passionate professor as well as a nice guy. However, the class is almost entirely based on three open note exams. These exams are partially based on minute often irrelevant details and often have questions with multiple or subjective answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: John Parks clearly does not know how to teach a class. His lectures are disorganized and leaves little chance to write down what is on the slides. His exams are a series of questions that are either too vague to be answered accurately or about him as a person and not about the material. He often spends most of the class on tangents.
I took this class for the second time, and he is more disorganized than last fall. I do not understand how you get worse, the more you teach.

Took it for an easy A, was very humbled. However the issue is despite Parks being a nice and engaging Professor, he makes roughly 85% of his class grade on 3-open note exams that test on small  details. Furthermore some of the multiple choice answers are subjective, and can be interpretive (especially bc the quiz q's are from student-submissions)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Parks has a lot of passion for the subject but he doesn't do well teaching it to students. The class is all lecture which are rambles of seemingly random topics. Open book exams but they're still difficult to do well on because he will test you on tiny random details or something he mentioned weeks ago for 3 minutes.

I loved animal behavior with Dr. Parks! You must go to class because he tests you on things he says in lectures (and his lectures are random tangents), but it is easy to pay attention because he tells lots of funny and interesting stories and makes the topics interesting. Open-note exams so just take notes on things he says and you will do well!

Rambles instead of lectures. If you take Environmental issues 110, he will stand up in front of the class and show you videos, talk about random things, then test you on small, unimportant details instead of themes. Does not respond to emails AT ALL. It seems easy but if you just need the requirement take something else to save ur GPA and sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: John Parks is a nice man and passionate about his subject. That said, all the other comments are true his tests are almost impossible to study for since there are not many key points. The questions of the test are of random bits of lecture or from videos we watch in class. Open note or not, the tests are very challenging and they the entire grade.

This class was a joke. Parks is obviously tenured and knows this is the easiest NSM. The class has no structure, the syllabus didn't even have a schedule, and his lectures were just random tangents. He's a really nice guy though and wants everyone to succeed, so there is a ton of extra credit. Easy A if you even sort of pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If youre taking this class for your major, take something else lol this class is so poorly organized I wish I didnt take it

This was my second class with Parks and I know that he gets a bad rap. He's disorganized and don't even try to reach out to him outside of class. But the man really cares about the environment. He's a really great guy. This class specifically was really easy, a sophomore seminar with no tests, just discussions but I learned alot. Highly recommend.

DO NOT TAKE CLASSES WITH JOHN PARKS. At first, he seems like a really nice guy. Then, you will realize that he doesn't care at all about his students. The entire grade is based off of 3 exams. None of the questions on these exams make sense; they are either from random news articles or YouTube clips. You won't learn anything, and you won't get an A

Dr. Parks is a nice guy, and he's obviously really passionate about he does, but the class was a mess. We spent most of class watching docs and discussing them- which wasn't the bad part, it was the exams. Only 3, and even open note I did horrible- the questions are vague and filled with spelling errors, and have little to do with the class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Only 3 exams. Half of the question either don't make grammatical sense, we didn't talk all the answer choices (and you have to select all that are correct), or many times it seems more than one answer could be correct for a single choice answer. Basically the material is easy but the tests are unfair and poorly written so you won't get an A.

I loved Parks as a person, obviously extremely passionate about the environment and his lectures were fun. The class is a nightmare though. We're only graded on 3 exams and random extra credit opportunities. He has yet to grade ANY of my extra credit and we're nearing the end of the semester. The exams are also really difficult. It isn't an easy A

Seems like a really nice guy, but his class is so disorganized. Grade is based on three exams, but the content of them is either not discussed in class, or a niche comment in some video you watched in months ago. Definitely easy but really messy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: John Parks is a nice guy who seems very interested in the things he teaches. However, Parks is extremely hard to reach outside of class. Don't bother reading the schedule in the syllabus, as he hardly followed it. The extra credit opportunities were basically mandatory due to the randomness of exam questions (his long tangents are tested).

He was a really nice guy! He was really aware of how hard online learning is on students and tried his best to make the class enjoyable, interesting, and not stressful. Only two mandatory exam grades but gave lots of optional extra credit. Exams were straightforward if you listened to the lectures, which were nice and flexible. Overall good class!
He was a great professor that did his best to make the class enjoyable for the students. I could tell he was passionate about the course material. Overall would recommend taking one of his classes!

Professor Parks is a fun guy and I found his class to be legitimately impactful in how I view the environment. That said, the class is a structural nightmare. We were only graded on three exams which entirely consisted of obscure questions from tangents in class rather than actual content. He also changed the syllabus and didn't respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The most ridiculous professor I've ever had. Asking students to watch totally irrelevant documentary just because he likes it. Exams test the most random information from slides. Sneakily changes syllabus without any notice. Extremely delayed feedback on exams, assignments, etc. Never checks or responds to student emails. DO NOT take this class.

Probably the most unorganized professor I've ever had. His slides have no correlation with each other and the exams test the most random information from it. Extremely delayed feedback on exams, assignments, etc. Never checks or responds to student emails. Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Parks is a super nice guy and super interested/knowledgable about Urban Ecology. He's also one of the most disorganized professors I've had. Exams were very difficult because they tested on random facts. I did well in his class and enjoyed the topic overall but was often confused or stressed by the class.

Lectures are kind of boring and goes off on random tangents that actually end up being tested. If you write down every single word he says and study for tests, you'll be fine, but not a clear grader nor lecturer. Decently interesting to listen to though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Parks is very disorganized. We were tested on things we never covered in class. He posted slides out of order and often containing 30+ extraneous slides. He moved the final up three weeks, and didn't update the syllabus. He offered extra credit, but forget to collect it. Don't take his class if you dislike working harder than the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: By far my favorite professor at WashU. So funny and really good at getting students to care about the subject. He's almost impossible to reach outside of class but his lectures (and him himself) are hilarious. Slides don't contain a lot of information other than pictures so don't skip class - just go and take notes and you'll pass.

he's helped me become even a little bit more environmentally conscious, and for that I am grateful. he is a funny lecturer, nice clear voice, not boring. highly recommend. not that difficult. pay moderate attention, go to class most of the time, and study a bit and you can get an a.
This man talks way too fast, and is inaccessible outside of class. Slow response to emails, delayed updates to course materials, no set office hours. Yikes.

Prof. Parks is a very engaging lecturer and explained his subject matter very well. The class is only graded on the three midterm exams, and you have the option to drop the final . Study well, a lot of memorization from the lectures is required and he words his questions in tricky ways. Not an easy grader but not unfair. Did end up curving a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Parks is a very funny and engaging professor. I truly enjoyed attending his lectures. So much so, that I am planning on taking two more of his courses. However, his exams were pretty difficult, so definitely study. You must attend and pay attention to every class b/c it is extremely lecture-heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is the best professor I have had at WashU so far!! He makes class really fun and interesting and is such a dad-- a very kind dad. No hw in this class; Tests are easy if you study; big curve. He is so passionate about the environment, and is a big reason why I am considering Environmental Studies as a major. Keep up contact with him!!

Although Prof. Parks is very enthusiastic about what he teaches, he goes on long tangents about irrelevant topics, which prevents him lecturing on the pertinent material. Also, his tests are difficult and very tricky (not an easy A).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He's genuinely passionate about what he teaches. Lectures are pretty interesting. Tests aren't too hard if you take good notes.

He's a funny and nice person. His lectures were interesting, but his exams were pretty unfair. They were extremely difficult, and he's not accessible to students at all.  I have emailed him for help multiple times but received no response.

I took his seminar. He is a pretty boring guy and the quality of classes is dependent on student participation. Don't take this class if you don't like participating. The field trips we went on were fun. He is a very easy grader, cool guy, but not the best teacher. I recommend this class if you're passionate about sustainability.
Just a great dude. Took his Behavioral Ecol class, and it seriously was one of my all-time favorite classes. just go to class and you'll pretty much do well
John Parks is the Indiana Jones of Environmental Studies.  TAKE his class!
Parks is by far the best professor at Wash U.  He is engaging, interesting and funny.  I looked forward to going to his class everyday and his tests are extremely fair!!!
Great Guy! Exams are pretty easy, just study whatever he writes on the board.  He has a nice curve at the end of the class. Easy A

This class is pretty much foolproof. There is no textbook, you just show up and write down exactly what he has up on the board and then study it for the exams. The movies he shows are really pretty cool, too!
Parks is great at making information crystal clear, and not knowing what material is important is virtually impossible.
I don't know how I'm the first person to rate him as a hottie.  The other comments are very accurate otherwise.

The class is really interesting - the material is pertinent to real life. Tests are DETAILED and straight out of the notes... so going to class is key but at least book reading is optional- I didn't even buy the book. Lots of memorization, but definitely doable.

Parks gives a great intro to environmental studies because he makes his lectures very clear by writing an outline on the board as he goes. He's easy to follow even if you don't know anything about environmental studies at first. He's a pretty big biology dork but it definately adds to the class more than it hurts.
fun lectures! don't have to do the readings! can't wait to take more of his classes.

Love this man.  Really fun to watch lecture.  You only have to study for tests (all from notes), and he is flexible with issues students have.  Says the word "okay" way too much, but you get used to it.  Really study your notes.

Bai cares about materials science and brings enthusiasm to this class. However, grading is inconsistent. The class is not difficult -- homework assignments come directly from textbooks, and exam questions come directly from homework. The first exam was randomly very difficult, but the second and third were easy. He's not flexible with grading.

Dr. Bai is an extraordinary lecturer. While in class, you feel like you are learning a ton. However, in hindsight, he really didn't explain the concepts that well and the problem sets that he gave were too surface-level and easy. This class is designed as a "break" from our rigorous ChemE curriculum, but I don't feel prepared for the future.

Dr. Bai makes materials science interesting. His lectures are very clear and his practice is very helpful to learn what he covers during lectures. Some materials might be confusing towards the end of the semester but he tries his best to help us understand. However, exams cover a lot so be prepared for everything.

she is a good lecturer and cares about her students. Homework is participation and there was (in my opinion) too much extra credit for a class that didn't have that hard of content to begin with. All in all it provided me some release from a tough semester

She's awesome! Definitely a tough course by nature but she really cares about all of her students' success and is super available to help during office hours or by appointment. She can go a little fast at times but overall the class the reasonably paced and the exams were a fair reflection of what was taught to us.

Dr. Zhu was a great professor for Enmath A. I learned so much in this class, and she is extremely helpful in office hours. She works through many practice problems and also provides lots of practice through the homeworks and (optional) daily textbook problems. She is also very understanding. Last part of the course was definitely a challenge tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Parsons is a great guy and genuinely cares about his students. He is very well organized and knows what he is talking about. His lectures contrary to what some say on here are not boring. However, he assigns an absurd amount of reading, I'm talking you'll never get it done type of reading.

Parsons provides an excellent class experience that inspires thought beyond the surface level. He connects disparate concepts in interesting ways and teaches content socratically through questions and discussion. Only 4 stars because his technological skills are low and he assigns a nearly insurmountable amount of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor; ask questions of him. Very big on 1-1 student access and accommodating

There is a lot of material covered in the Pre-Modern class and two cumulative exams on all of it. Since the classes were lecture-heavy, it was insanely difficult to prepare and still graded harshly. I couldn't engage much with the material bc classes would get boring, and Parsons could be condescending and disorganized. Overall, I was unimpressed.

The only reason I wouldn't take his class again is because I hate reading. Overall, he's a really good professor and will answer all of your questions! If you're interested in African history you should definitely look into taking one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Definitely reading and lecture heavy, but he has a real talent for making lectures interesting. Learned a lot and would definitely recommend him to others.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great guy and knowledgeable Professor in his field. Lectures can be very boring in his upper level classes and it is a ton of reading. Very difficult paper assignments in this particular course. He cares a lot about students and is very friendly. Easy to get a B, but the course involves a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Parsons is the greatest man to walk the face of this planet. Take as many classes as you can

Good professor; a lot of people take the class pass-fail, so often people don't pay attention. The tests and assignments are relatively easy, but he forces one topic onto you for the final paper which can make it extremely boring and unfun to do. He's a big proponent of gender equality and stuff, so he'll make you focus on it for the final project.

Parsons can be a little condescending, but he knew the subject well and always had interesting angles and topics. Never opened the textbook, did the readings but not necessary. Tests were easy memorization since the info was all online, the essays required a bit more work. Overall, engaging class and a little work but not too bad.

Knowledgeable, funny, sarcastic. Lead the whole class to engage and find the answer instead of just giving them to the students by plain lecture. Really smart guy, you can't fool him. But very nice if you make an effort to show you care. Before I knew nothing about African history but I am taking another class with him next semester.

Took his African History 1800-present seminar. He seriously knows his stuff. Makes class very engaging, pushes you to think harder, doesn't let you get away with lazy responses. Grading expectations are very reasonable. You will learn a lot from him.

He can definitely get moody. He definitely knows his stuff, but sometimes we learn random things that don't seem really important at all. Tests aren't too bad, but the memorization of people and events can get very tedious.

Know that if you take Intro to World History, you will study WW2 and only WW2. The impossible amount of readings is because they're totally unnecessary. It seems intimidating and he talks fast but the tests are really easy. He's a good teacher once you realize you don't need to know details. Make sure you show up to class and DON'T fall asleep.
Very good teaching, keeps my attention throughout class.  As others have mentioned he can be a little moody and is often very opinionated.

Dr. Parsons knows African history well, and he gives great lectures. However, he can be moody and rude--for example, he frequently cuts people off and will shut you down if you say something that he does not agree with. On the plus side, he does grade pretty easily, and he gives you everything you need for the exams beforehand.

best professor i have taken here. Not including his intro to world history, he almost never lectures, instead creating discussion among students. decent amount of reading, but usually very enjoyable. very helpful and approachable. Renowned among African history professors. I've taken one of his courses every semester in which one was offered.
A really hard class with a lot of reading but it is so worth the skill sets you develop, even more so than the understanding you gain of the issues presented.
Lots of history, but a great lecturer. He'll put you on the spot if you haven't done the reading. The group projects are hard but worthwhile.

Excellent history professor. Highly recommended. I did fine w/o doing all the readings and just comig to class. He is very good at this class and made me want to take basically anything else he might decide to teach.

A great lecturer (if you don't mind history).  The reading is ridiculously heavy, though.  I took him pass/fail, skimmed the readings, attended the fairly interesting lectures and had no problem.  In fact, I would have no problem taking him again.

great professor, interesting material, but has a group project that is absolutely deadly.  Make sure you go talk to him if you have any problems with your group or you can get screwed by the group grade.
too much readings, but he's a cool professor and i learned a lot from this class.

Parsons tried to be PC all the time.  If he isn't as clear as he wanted to be, he would correct himself.  He cared about the student's understanding but wanted to present an unbiased opinion.  My proble with this class is the TAs.  They do not know what good writing is and appraoch papers with bias.
I agree that the assigments were way too long for anyone to read.  As a result, the focus on class participation did not really work well.
The class was boring, he assigned too many readings for someone to possibly do and his attempt to involve the class was a failure.
Good professor, but doesn't teach as much as could... has students lead part of class which isn't terribly helpful.
Greatest professor I've ever met, period.
not as great as every1 thinks, but could have been worse
Professor Parsons in a great teacher.  He leads without lecturing and adds interesting anecdotes.  Also is very helpful if you dont understand an assignment.
Parsons teaches well.  He knows his stuff and takes questions from all students, even if he falls behind considerably.  He also takes answers from the whole class, not just a few students.
Really knows his stuff. Very PC, but in a good way (tip - don't say 'tribe')! His classes are always interesting and give you a new perspective on things.

Best professor I had at Wash U, and can explain African politics and history better than anyone at the school. The best thing about Parsons is that he makes sure to keep himself up to date on a subject that is constantly changing.

He's a really cool guy who knows his stuff.  The only warning I would give is that he discusses colonial history a lot and tends to get repetitive on the basics of colonialism.  But I have learned a lot from his class.
Parsons is AMAZING i would recommend him to anyone, the lectures are interesting and although his speciality is E. Africa he speaks intelligently on many subjects
great professor
Fairly PC, but humble and intelligent, a fine lecturer and a nice guy.
Dr. P is such a genuine and caring person who wants her students to succeed. 10/10 would recommend!
Dr. P is a professor who truly cares about her students' success. She's one of the most genuine professors I've met at WashU.

She is SO nice--probably my favorite professor I have had so far. The class does require work, but you can work with other students and ask IAs questions. You probably will have to put some time into it, but it doesn't feel overwhelming at all. (Also she is super good about getting student feedback and adjusting the course accordingly)

Great professor. Gives good feedback and runs the class well. Jokes around and is always willing to meet outside of class to discuss any questions. No exams, but he did grade somewhat strictly. Overall a great guy and very much knowledgable on the topics. TA grading in the class lacked feedback, but the assignments he graded did have good comments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took Morality and Markets, and Peter brought in some cool business perspectives. We also met some cool people like the CEO of PayPal. There's a lot of readings that you need to stay on top of. Most importantly, don't forget to participate! Very intriguing class that opens your eyes to incorporating morality in business/market decisions.

He is incredibly interesting, funny, and has great lectures. I loved Morality and Markets - be warned, there are a lot of books to read while you can get by not reading them. The class will be 100 times better if you do read. He does really interesting work and has funny commentary.

Excellent professor. Very energetic and engaging lecturer who manages to tie all input together. The course had a fairly heavy workload and a lot of reading, but was well designed and the work was meaningful. Definitely a class where you get what you give, and Peter was excellent.
Awesome dude
By far the best professor I've had at WashU. Incredibly engaging lecturer and fascinating class. He is a really nice, caring, and accessible professor as well. Can't recommend enough!
He is great!!!
Professor Maciak is a great teacher and awesome guy! Super funny, knowledgable, and has entertaining, interesting classes. I highly recommend taking a class with him!

Maciak was really entertaining, interesting, and chill enough that the course wasn't too stressful as a writing intensive but was still a legitimate amount of work. Maciak is super engaging and approachable and really cares about his students. Highly recommend.

Wow, I could not rave about a class more. First off, Professor Maciak is so cool and personable. Second, I had no interest in journalism prior but now I want to pursue it as a hobby. Lots of assignments but the grading is divided well, you get to engage with your classmates (feedback sessions) and overall write about what you want.

Great professor, always enjoyed being in class. Did not write a single essay in his class which, as an English major taking an English class, was incredibly surprising. Reading was about average for a Lit class.

Maciak is a great professor. Though he takes forever to grade, he is an easy grader. There are a lot of readings, but his book selections were enjoyable and easy to get through. He cares about his students, and is readily accessible outside of class. His lectures were funny and entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall a fun class! Very group-work heavy, but the texts are interesting and Maciak is a very knowledgeable guy. Great sense of humor and does his best to keep some dry topics interesting. A necessary class for the major/minor, but very doable!

His lectures are informative and he is approachable. Assignments took a very long time to grade (sometimes months), and we were sometimes assigned readings that we then didn't discuss in class. It was often difficult to figure out which readings we were going to be focusing on in class among the several assigned. But generally a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kastor is the best lecturing professor I have ever had. I learned more in this class than in all of my other classes this semester combined. However, the class requires a ton of reading that is covered in the discussion sections, and both Kastor and the TAs grade very, very harshly. Take this class if you are passionate about history.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kastor is an incredible lecturer. His lectures were engaging and entertaining, and he is incredibly likable as a person. This being said, he is a very tough grader as are his TA's. The course requires 50-100 pages of reading per week and in depth participation graded discussion sections. Lastly, there are only 4 graded items in the whole course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer! super passionate and knowledgeable, does a good job keeping the class engaged. He's also really sassy which I find pretty entertaining. Essays and exams are very tough tho, he has super specific requirements for his essays and exams including a style guideline for your writing that is sooooo picky...overall feeling humbled.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Kastor is an amazing lecturer with so much energy and knowledge about the course. However, I switched this class to auditing because of the amount of reading and work done in the class.

Amazing lecturer
The course is only based on a handful of assignments (2 essays, midterm, and final), so there is kind of hard to come back from a tough grade. Also, grading for the essays is very rough, and the criteria/expectations of the writing assignments don't match the chill vibe of the lectures. Reading was abt 20+ pages per week.

Kastor is an incredible professor and lecturer. He is so passionate on the subject. That being said, that is all class is. It is very fast-paced and he is a very tough grader, so get ready to work very hard and long on ALL assignments. But he also gives you all the resources you need to succeed. If you work hard and go to class, you will do well.

I took Americans and Their Presidents and it's been one of my favorite classes. Kastor is brilliant lectures relate to current events and are engaging. Papers were demanding with weekly discussions, but Kastor remembers you if you introduce yourself, and even reached out to make sure I was doing okay since I was a freshman in a 300 level course
Great Professor, but get ready for tough grading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Kastor was one of my favorite professors at WashU. He's erudite, kind, and brilliant. Can't recommend him highly enough. I miss him dearly.

I loved the freshman seminar called The Presidency 101. Context of class: 2016 general election, with WashU hosting the 2nd debate. Kastor brought in a reporter/radio host twice to class and we discussed American history/culture and current events. Writing papers for him was hard but I definitely learned a lot. Our class still gets together!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Kastor is one of my favorite professors at WashU.  I've taken two classes with him (Americans and Their Presidents & United States Historical Methods) and while he is a tough grader, he's definitely helped me become a better writer and has helped me grow since my freshman year

Professor Kastor (who is also my major advisor) is one of the most engaging and interesting professors I have had. I've had him twice so far (American Presidents and Historical Methods) and he's never failed to impress. Classes are very reading heavy, but mostly discussion based. Always available to talk. Pushes you to be a better writer. 10/10

Great professor, really knows his stuff. Lectures were interesting and helpful for tests and papers. Friendly and helpful outside of class. The class wasn't easy: lots of reading and challenging tests. If you're interested in American history, definitely take a class with him

Downright brilliant. Consider yourself lucky to have a rising star in history at your disposal. He's as passionate as can be about his subject and does his best to instill the same passion in his undergrads. Great sense of humor, dynamic lecturer, you flat out can't do better. You're missing out on a golden opportunity if you don't take his class.

best prof I've had. Dynamic with a good sense of humor, you'll learn a ton in his class. Hard grader but fair. Expectations for exams are clear, a lot of material but interesting and not overwhelming. Highly recommend for history majors and non-history majors alike.

Best prof at WashU.  Hilarious, engaging.  Took the intro to American history and he told the American narrative from a completely new perspective I've never seen before.  Spent a week relating the 60s cultural movement to the political movement.  AWESOME.

Kastor is the best professor I've had at Wash U so far. He's funny, his lectures are enjoyable, and the readings are interesting. If you put in the work&do the readings, you will be fine. There is a lot of reading for the course. Participation is important, but you can go the whole semester without making 1 comment. I highly recommend Kastor

Tells great stories and lectures are interesting, but it is often difficult to relate the theme he describes as important to the lecture itself. The readings are also difficult to relate to the lectures.
Kastor is amazing - get a class with him if you can.  He's quirky and often off topic, but class is entertaining and you really learn about the subject
The best professor I have ever had. He makes you think, and makes you work, but you will learn more than you can imagine. TAKE HIS CLASS
For a cl**** I had no interest in, Professor Kastor made me fall in love with the time period that he teaches about. He was my favorite history teacher at Wash U!!!!
Lectures are extremely disjointed and hard to follow.
Peter's a great professor and advisor.  Clever, smart, witty, funny, and all around nice guy.  Make sure you're prepared for class, though, as he will keep you on your toes...
take a small class

hard as anything. do your reading and you won't look stupid in class. at least he's hot, so when you feel stupid, it's all ok. the research is hard, but he will always give direction/help you if you ask

Peter is the best thing about Wash U - period. He's interesting, eager, funny and random. His history classes are the best. He can relate anything to Seinfeld episodes. He's also one half of the coolest married couple I've ever met.
One of the best professors I had in college. Learning from him was a life changing experience.
awsome teacher
The rate of speed at which he speaks reminds me of Quentin Tarentino talking about Uma Thurman. Very funny and smart.  Knows his stuff -- does extra research to bring the message home.

Not only energetic and extremely intelligent, but willing to go out of his way to help his students.  His lectures are interesting and his courses are challenging without being overpowering.  An excellent professor.
Incredible prof. Take anything that he offers. He's very smart, funny, energetic, helpful, and as he says "mean but not cruel". He expects a lot out of you, but the work is doable.
amazing guy.  sharp as a whip and fun to boot.
Incredible teacher. His lectures are very entertaining and he will go the extra mile for you if you need it.
Peter is the most underrated professor at WASH U. Awesome in class, as an advisor, and as a teacher. Get into one of his small seminar classes
Had interesting lectures even if the slides were brief yet very content -dense. Really smart guy who is very willing to answer questions in my experience and I would definitely recommend.

Love Professor Skemer! As a student who was new to STEM at the college-level, I felt very supported by both professor Smith and Skemer in Intro EEPS. Super interesting course which I would recommend to anyone interested in environmental science!
Amazing professor. Really knows what he is talking about and lectures are engaging and fun. Tests are not that hard as the class is basically memorization. Really recommend.

Taught lectures in a very clear and organized manner that communicated all necessary material for exams and homework. Shows a deep understanding of material and answers questions in class or office hours in a very succinct and clear manner. Students found him intimidating or unapproachable, but he is nice and helpful one-on-one. Grades were fair.

Absolutely loved Dr. Skemer's lectures! Always very clear, organized, and engaging. Not a light courseload - lectures are dense, and midterms are content-heavy + a cummulative final - but the professors do everything they can to support students. Interesting and fun. Great intro to EEPS, but you do have to work pretty hard for an A.

It's really sad, because the class is on an interesting subject, but it is just so unnecessarily hard. It's like the TAs try to find something wrong with every one of your answers on the tests. This is my major, yet the class makes me hate it. Worst grade I've ever gotten in college. This is why people hate STEM. Cool stuff, but horribly taught.

Took this class as many other engineers have, to fulfil the upper level science requirement. For a topic that I have zero interest in, Phil and Jen are pretty entertaining, but that's about where it ends. They said that this course isn't a memorization course... It definitely is. Make sure you take good notes because the slides are  very brief.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He gives frat boy in an endearing way. Funny and decent enough lecturer. The class content is just boring and too much for anyone to memorize, especially if you're a humanities major used to writing papers rather than memorizing types of rocks. The exam grades in this class were the lowest I've ever gotten. Difficult to access help outside class.
Great professor and class

Phil tries his best to make lectures entertaining but the real downfall of the class is the material. It is just hard to make 14 billion years of rocks interesting. Unless you want to be a geologist I would not take this class, it does not fall under an intro level course in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's definitely gives good lectures and truly knows the content, but outside of the lectures he is sort of arrogant. I feel like he teaches just to be right about something, he doesn't actually want us to learn. You can definitely tell he never struggled in a class before, and expects everyone to retain the information on the first try.

Deliberately rude, in emails and during class. Deleted Zoom recordings because he said only synchronous students present should have access to content. Very unaccommodating for COVID-19. Gave EC to photograph WashU building (only available to on-campus students) even in a fully remote class. Exams were graded arbitrarily by TAs, no clear criteria.

I had Phil for Geology Bootcamp. I loved every second of that class, mostly because of him and Alex (the other professor). The two of them were like a comedy duo, constantly cracking jokes with one another. You can tell that they're super passionate about geology and love teaching it. They're also very personable and overall fun guys.

Phil is very passionate about rocks and the environment. Even if this subject isn't your life, he will make it interesting purely based on how excited he gets during lectures. He is very straight forward and his tests are based on lectures and labs. The tests are not hard. He gives pop quizzes, but they' re usually two questions and are easy points
He's the best!
best. class. EVER.
Purchase is awesome! Very funny, extremely knowledgable, and presents some very interesting texts. Workload is totally manageable as long as you keep up with the reading. I highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Purchases Pastoral Literature class involves exclusive topics. The workload is medium, but be prepared to read.

Pastoral literature was an AMAZING course. Prof. Purchase is incredibly knowledgable and makes the class very approachable--as someone with no classics background I was bit nervous about succeeding in the class, but he always provided tons of context and background information. Great feedback, and he's just a really caring person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Fluent in Attic Greek and Latin, Doctor Purchase is knowledgeable in classics. His lecture on class is sometimes hypnotizing but at most of the time inspiring. Moreover, he is devoted to introducing his students to different activities in humanities.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Purchase is different from some of the other professors in that he really cares for his students. He's always more than willing to help, and though papers and readings can be tough, his guidance makes them easier. Highly recommend his Text and Tradition classes, and any class taught by him is bound to be excellent.

He is a very smart professor who is articulate and gives many deep insights into the books you read. There are many readings, and you have to read them, but if you send him drafts of your essays and participate in class you should do well. He is a cool guy to talk do during office hours.

Classical to Renaissance Literature - an absolutely fabulous teacher. Makes class extremely interesting and is very knowledgeable. A lot of reading assigned though, so get ready to work, but all interesting texts. He can be fairly harsh/direct in his comments on essays, but gives fairly good grades none the less. Take him if you can!!!

I absolutely love his class "An Intellectual History of Sex and Gender". The reading is initially dry, but the questions he poses opens up the text. Sometimes seminar, sometimes pseudo lecture it is always interesting as every thought that comes out of his mouth is exquisitely worded. He is sometimes vague, but clarifies any questions you pose.
Awesome guy.  Papers can be tough.  I'd suggest talking with him about your paper a week before it's due to get on the right track.

Purchase doesn't teach many non-language classes, so if you get the opportunity, take his class.  You won't regret it. He is probably the most interesting man I've met at WashU.  Very smart and funny and has a sense of humor about himself and his entire class.  Not an easy grader, but if you meet with him he'll help you out a lot.

A-mazing. Ridiculous and absurd in the best way possible. Love love love. Very knowledgeable, gives interesting lectures, leads fabulous discussions and is extremely approachable and helpful outside of class. Go talk to him, it will probably be one of the best conversations of your life.
awesome, from his designer jeans to his hair to his british accent. very knowledgeable and intelligent, leads discussions well and introduces interesting material. definitely reccomendable!

Easy concepts taught with needlessly difficult exams and a grading procedure that makes no sense. Even students who did their work and contributed to lecture discussion would struggle to succeed. Gave us a private company for our final group project, so the data we needed was mostly unavailable. Did not communicate the week leading up to the final.

Though the material wasn't extremely difficult, Colatat makes it intentionally harder than it should be. Exams are always a time crunch. He's condescending and often late. He was unresponsive for a whole week at the end of semester. The two-hour final ended up being an hour final because he was late. I would not recommend taking MGT with Colatat.

Professor Colatat's lectures were always engaging.  It was apparent that he really enjoyed teaching the material and was well prepared for class every day(even in his attire).  He's very approachable, but has (at times) tough expectations of his students.  The TAs often did a better job explaining problems than him.

Class was rather boring given the material, but he didn't really make it any more interesting. Tests not always designed well and answers to questions seemed dogmatic at times. Such arguable questions couldn't even be answered or explained well by the TAs, indicating that the class is not structured well in the first place.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Awesome professor and great class.  Group and assignment heavy, plus there is a mandatory participation aspect of the class.  Colatat is excited about the subject and dynamic, which can make a dull topic more palatable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Colatat is really passionate about what he's teaching and comes super prepared for his lectures. He tries to encourage class participation and keeps the lectures interactive. He also attempts some humor by relating things to current events or pop culture. Always dressed to impress, and an all-around good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I would take his class again. Super helpful and really passionate and nice to the students.
A bit awkward, but a solid dude. Really knows his stuff.
Prof Bayly is my personal hero. I would take a bullet for that man
Professor Bayly is such an inspiration. I hope that one day I can grow up to be as smart and successful and kind as he is.

If you can take Mechanics II a different semester, do it.  He is the worst engineering professor at Wash U.  He does go over some of the problem set questions in class, but in no way is there any teaching going on his classroom.  Copying from the book is his go-to move.  USE THE TA'S!

He is not easy but he is nice and will help if you need it.  He goes over HW problems in class before they are due.  Expect a few exams and weekly p-sets. Overall a above average engineering professor
Awful lecturer. Just rewrites equations that are in the textbook. Tests are difficult and he does not grade easily. Seems like a nice guy but I'm not so sure he is.
The single best professor I've had. Prof. Sewell leaving Wash U is nothing short of tragic. If you're lucky enough to attend whichever school hires him next, I envy you.

Amazing professor, arguably unmatched in his passion for the subject and willingness to help students understand and excel on the material. The kind of teacher that exemplifies the importance of loving what you do, his lectures are engaging and even those with limited interest in his courses should try them out

these comments are kinda overrated. i actually thought he was a little hard to listen to at times and I thought he assigned a lot of reading. not terrible by any means, definitely interesting at times, tests and papers aren't too bad, and he is willing to help outside of class, but i wouldn't say he made the class as interesting as it could've been

Sewell is an amazing professor. He does everything right and cares immensely about the material and the students in each class. He's also the most friendly and understanding prof. I've ever known. I slept through an exam and he let me retake it, no questions asked. Taking his class is a privelege.

Professor Sewell is amazing. Fun, pleasant, engaging, open to different ideas, very knowledgable. I had some questions on the final exam and he met with me for over an hour to talk them over. Take his class even if you don't think you're interested in the material.
Such a nice guy, adorable, and easy to listen to!
Absolutely wonderful. Passionate, engaging, insightful... he's truly one of the best professors at WashU.
Good teacher. Tests are fair, and class is pretty interesting. He is engaging and uses a nice combination of powerpoint, discussion, and film clips.

Very enthusiastic about the class, very knowledgeable. Lectures off of slides so can get a bit dull, but all the slides get put online. Fair grader (though the TA is not), understanding about extensions on papers. Tests are a lot to remember but nothing tricky, just memorizing the material.

Sewell is an AMAZING professor.  If you have an interest in film/tv/media, he is an absolutely phenomenal source of information.  Ive loved both of the classes I've taken with him, and do my best to take at least one with him per semester.  He makes you think about things in a totally new way.  I would recommend his class to anyone.

eh.  This course will be pretty dull unless you have a serious interest in complex/dry media theory, Sewell is kind of goofy and just wants his students to like him.  Likes to talk about current tv shows but the class focuses on much older stuff.  Doesn't take attendance often and is a fair grader.

This class was my absolute favorite so far at WashU. This was the kind of class that requires your all but also that you want to give your all to. Would highly recommend for anyone even slightly interested in acting. Participation is really important and as long as your invested and try, you'll get a good grade. She's also super sweet.

By far the most ridiculous class I've ever taken at WashU. Pileggi somehow is accessible yet extremely difficult to work with. Her lack of empathy was incredibly jarring to experience, as most of my professors have had some sort of empathy (even if they aren't outwardly kind/warm/inviting). You can read the book and she'll still grade you poorly.

Professor Pileggi is legitimately one of the best professors I've had at WashU. She is extremely engaging and knows how to get you to reach your fullest potential in her class. From someone with absolutely no acting experience, her public speaking course was extremely beneficial and encouraged me to take more classes in the Drama department.

She is literally the best. You do have to put a bit of work in, but she is so encouraging and the work is really fun and interesting that it doesn't even feel like work. She is really really great, super knowledgeable, supportive, and always willing to work with you! Best professor I've had at Wash U - hands down.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Anna Pileggi pushes you hard and expects a lot. She's so loving and wonderful and I recommend working with her if you're serious about your craft.
Absolutely the most wonderful professor and director I've had the pleasure of working with. If you are serious about acting, there's no other.
Anna is AMAZING. The best teacher I have ever had.

Amazing teacher and coach. Easily the best class I've taken at WashU. Take her class if and only if you are serious about acting.   And make sure you try very hard on papers - she does not take kindly to poorly written work.

So, I'm the second person to review Anna 10 years later.  That alone should tell you all you need to know about taking a class with her -- the impact lasts.  She's tough and caring, and she'll help you grow as an actor in ways you didn't know were possible.  10 years down the line, I think back to this class frequently, and it STILL helps.

I had Anna 10 years ago, and appreciate everything she taught me - she is one of the best teachers I had, and always gave every student as much help as they needed. When I act now, I still hear her sometimes - anyone who has her is very, very lucky.

Anna was extremely specific in her coaching and ever creative in her methods to inspire you to do your best.  She's tough, you have to work hard, but it is one of the most rewarding experiences you can have.
No Comments
Great teacher! I learned so much in this class. She asks a lot, but is always willing to help you out (with class or something else). Take her classes!
Anna is the best teacher. She is very helpful although she demands alot.  You can go to her for anything and she will be there with open arms. I love Anna and so does everyone else that meets her!!!

Pierce is so great!! His lectures are so interesting, and he is so knowledgable!! It was such a cool experience to learn from someone with so much experience and who is so respected in the field. This course was especially awesome because we had a chance to travel as a class! 10/10 would recommend this course and this professor!

Lamar is an interesting and engaging lecturer. It was great to learn from someone with as much field experience as he does. The issue with him is that he is great at explaining concepts, but when you get practice problems, it seems like he just expects you to figure it out. He is available, but his office hours are packed. Overall AMAZING professor
Lamar is an arrogant professor who doesn't teach much. He just likes to hear himself talk.
Best professor I had freshman year.
GREAT PROFESSOR! I love him

This class is kind of interesting, but it is hard for some freshmen. Make sure to read everything and print the slides before class. (Many freshmen are not prepared.) In general, the outline of this class is not very clear and many freshmen feel uncomforateble to study without a textbook.
Great professor, albeit intimidating.  Is accommodating and helpful outside of class.  Rewards those who speak up and contribute often and intelligently in class.
he makes things clear and most of all he is so SMART in the first place~

Good teacher.  Easy concepts. The class takes some getting used to, but once you figure out what is asked (especially on tests) it is quite easy.  Make sure you participate in class. Study all assignments and practice material.

I personally did not like him that much because I thought he was a bit boring. He goes off on tangents though, and those are interesting. Otherwise, GO TO REVIEW SESSION, REVIEW NOTES/READ EVERYTHING and try hard. It's a difficult class, but not impossible.
