It's a pretty tough class. It get's less difficult by the end as you begin to understand what the professor asks for. He's a great guy, and an extremely knowledgeable professor. I definitely recommend him.
very easy class. keeping with the b school tradition of not having any challenging concepts and tests are easy along with huge boosts for participation
This was my favorite class of the semester by far, I had a really great time and I am entirely confident that it was because of this professor.
Good professor. Tests are mostly trick questions and aren't very well written, but he will give points back on regrades.

His class is pretty tough, and requires work.  The tests are challenging.  But he REALLY teaches you the material, and I am pretty convinced he knows everything about everything. You can ask him any business question about any market, and he will not only have an answer, but will have a 15 minute answer.  I really recommend him,this guy is the MAN!

Lamar is the man.  He's very straightforward in his teaching and answers questions well.  He's is extremely funny, but not everyone seems to understand his humor.  His tests are very fair and the class is not especially hard.  You don't really have to do all those readings.
Great prof! Awesome lectures and a very fair grader.
No Comments
awesome prof- tough class but he explains it well and lays it out in a way that is understandable.

Professor Pierce is an incredible teacher! I highly highly suggest taking his class! All his lectures are extremely interesting and he uses class participation very well. But, don't kid yourself, management is a very tough class with tons of reading. The tests are very hard and random. He will raise grades up to a letter based on participation!!!

Omg he's such a mush. Drawing 101 was so fun with him- loved the projects. He's super understanding and kind, but also very helpful. The perspectives section was hard to get through because it was boring, but generally he gives you class time to work- didn't have much to do out of class- Expect maybe an hour per project. He's a great guy

He is ok, I think we just didn't vibe super well. He talks SO SLOW and I think is definitely more suited to teaching middle school or younger grades. He is kind of funny and can be helpful if you ask questions but otherwise critiques didn't really provide any feedback and nothing was on Canvas so instructions/due dates were often unclear.

Pike is the best. Pike is a god. He's so funny and entertaining, but very professional, organised, and helpful in critiques. He gives you a lot of freedom to draw what you want and in whatever style, and he makes you feel passionate about art. I learned a lot, had a lot of fun. You can tell he loves his job, art, and his students.

Prof pike is such an amazing professor, he gives really good feedback and is always willing to meet w/students outside of class to help them in any way possible. He is also super accommodating, where if ur unable to turn something in on time you just need to email him and explain the situation and he's super chill. Class pace is super manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Pike is extremely caring about everyones work and developmental process. He is also hilarious. The course was extremely engaging and effectively met all of the goals mentioned in the syllabus. This was my favorite class of the semester.
Super helpful and friendly. Always looking to help you improve.

2D design with Pike is great. He's really respectful and helpful to students, and makes the class bearable even to people who have no interest in it. He tells a lot of stories about his life and is just a very nice person and cares about his students' well being, not just their art. Take a class with him!
Professor Pike is very friendly and helpful. He is also open to learning new ideas from students and his main interest is helping all the students succeed.

He is an awful professor. I learned almost nothing and felt like I had wasted an entire year in his class. Looking at past comments...maybe he used to be better but now his class is useless. His teaching/learning methods and his opinions are the only ones allowed to exist in his class.Don't take this class if you actually want to learn modern Hebre

Rami is a control freak. He seems to have a sense of humor at first, but winds up getting really mad and saying "We dont have time" if you crack a joke. That being said, he usually lets out early. A lot of ppl in the class find him annoying. Overpronounces ur name. Dont take the class if you're advanced in hebrew-he will likely feel threatened.

Great teacher!! I took hebrew all of high school and didn't learn half as much as i am this year with Rami. A nice guy and fun class to be in. His style is very unique so at first I wasn't sure but I learned to really like him.

Rami is one of my favorite professors so far at WashU, and possibly ever. He's funny and engaging - I really look forward to this class. He cares about his students and wants them to do well, but he doesn't have any qualms about embarrassing you in front of the class if you don't know what you're talking about - so do your homework!
awsom!
What a sweetheart - my classmates and I still have inside jokes about our class and how funny he is - doesn't like people who skip classes
Helpful, funny, and so damn cute, "bevadai!"

I look forward to coming to his class; he has a good sense of humor, and I always feel I get my money's worth of learning out of the class.  Having the textbook means I can work ahead if I know that I have a heavy week ahead.  He also grades very fairly.
great class
i came into the class pretty ahead of everyone else, so it was pretty easy. he's a fun guy, an israeli santa clause, big and jolly.
No Comments
No Comments

A truly fantastic professor.  Long lectures can be hard to sit through, but if you care about production, what you take away from his class his invaluable.  He is the one of the sweetest people I have ever met, and cares incredibly about his students.  He pushes very hard but only to ones benefit.  The most I have ever learned in a class.

If you are incapable of accepting constructive criticism, don't take this class. However, if you want to develop as a filmmaker and learn something about the art; I highly recommend Pier. He gives just enough guidance to get you going in the right direction, but he won't do any hand holding. This was a great class.

If you are interested in creating something meaningful, Pier will help you find your voice and help develop your artistic awareness so that your piece is infused with meaning.  Also, contrary to a few comments I see, Pier is very humble and open to working with your passion.

Taught one of the greatest classes in the entire film department, highly recommended!! I'm going to take as many classes with him as I can. He was very helpful, insightful, and downright friendly. He's also friendly outside of class and always full of great information regarding film and more

Prof. Marton should not be underappreciated.  He is a wonderful resource for any student interested in film editing/production.  If you are willing as a student to seek out help when you need it, Prof. Marton will be a good match for you.  If you expect to be babied, and get an automatic A, maybe you should find a different class.  Go Pier.

Pier is obviously very invested in his students and their work. If you have a strong interest in the topic and are willing to put forth a lot of effort, you can do fine.  Pier is a nice guy, he just doesn't seem to put up with students who try to just barely get by -- Take the class if you have time to spare & an interest in the subject.

Pier's classes are great if you want to be there. If you truly love your project then Pier will help you make it that much better. If you half ass it, you'll get frustrated with how much he expects from you. Pier actually cares about his students and their projects. You'll have to work hard, but its worth it.
even if what you make isn't groundbreaking you'll get a fine grade if you show consistent effort. pier is a nice person and i liked him a lot

If I trusted the reviews here, I prob wouldn't have taken the class. Glad I didn't--one of the best classes I've taken at WU; definitely a challenge but well worth the late nights in Eads. Pier gives you the tools, but forces you to find your own voice/style. If you resent that... go do math or something else where there's only one right answer...

He is a great teacher if you are willing to go outside your comfort zone to try new techniques and think differently. .  You may feel frustrated at times becasue of the ambiguity of some assignments, but he pushes you creatively and in the end it's worth it.  If you like to know exactly what to expect it's probably not the best class to sign up for.

Pier is misunderstood.  The problem is people want to be spoon fed everything.  This is a class that urges you to find your own voice... Pier cannot hold your hand all the way through until you find it.  Yes, he's unclear, but only because there is no one

I feel obligated to defend Pier Marton against all these jokers. Yes, the class is quite challenging, but Pier does a marvelous job of delving inside the history of moving images (and their philosophical origins in semiotics) while teaching the basics of f

I had such high hopes for this class, but what a disappointment it was!  Marton's ideas are interesting to listen to, he would make a great lecturer for a philosophy of film class, but as an instructor in how to make films, he is the worst.  The entire film department at Wash U is a disappointment and lead me to transfer to another college.

OMG, this was the WORST class that I have EVER taken.  He is an awful teacher.  Not only does he load on a bunch of work but he just isn't a good teacher.  I had to take the class for a film requirement but, trust me, if its not a requirement for you, DONT TAKE IT!!!

His teaching defies this rating system.  Marton is often impossibly ambiguous and unhelpful, but these methods can be very positive (and helpful in the long run).  You have to expect something different with this class and keep an open mind.  He's an excellent teacher for the willing (and patient).

Only take this course if you have to for a Major/Minor.  He is ruthlessly arrogant, goes out of his way to make students feel insignificantly ignorant, and has an air about him that would make the Fonz seem modest.  Not to mention, the assignments are fairly pointless and overly difficult.  No good!

Arrogant, plays favorties, unfair, has unrealistic expectations, gives too much work, and does not teach well.  He values his opinion over everything else and will grade down just because he does not like something.

Philosophy of Medicine itself was incredibly interesting but sometimes when she would be explaining things it would just make it more complex and confusing than it needed to be. Lots of annoying quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She's an extremely lenient grader and offers up to 6% extra credit. Very passionate about what she teaches and easy to reach outside of class via email. No prior philosophy knowledge needed and 2/5 for amount of work required. Overall fantastic class. Highly recommend.

BiomedicalEthics. Anya is an extremely intelligent professor and a renowned scholar. She was dedicated to learning everyone's names week 1. A little quirky, sometimes distant, and will always challenge thought and push boundaries of conversation. Relevant and interesting topics. Learned a lot from her. Highly recommend taking a course with her.
Very sweet professor!
541 is as easy as 131 if you have Pless
Please remember: Take his course at ALL COSTS!

The best professor in the CSE department. Enthusiastic about what he does, and makes lectures funny and informative. Easy to follow, fun to talk to, and extremely helpful and supportive to his students. His lab is a fun environment to work at, and he is even more amazing outside of the classroom than inside.
My best professor this semester. Funny and interesting. He understands the material very well. But the course is way too easy, at least for me.

Fun, quirky teaching style. Pretty fair expectations, although problem sets can be very challenging without help. Don't miss class. Definitely shows his love for computer science and enjoys talking about his/other professors' research.
I learned more about Algs and Data Structures in this course than 241. He's SO smart and funny, I looked forward to this class every day.  Uses great analogies to help students understand.
Somehow this man makes proofs and all these weird logic statements fun! Really enjoyable class environment, not too difficult, fair grading, and surprisingly interesting/useful material.
Dr. Pless is hilarious. 240 was a fun class, but the material seemed to wander around, without being very focused.  Dr. Pless really knows his stuff though.
he can make anything sound interesting

He is such a funny great guy. The class is difficult, which kind of takes you by surprise, but he knows the material really well, and has such a quirky teaching style. This was my favorite class to attend when I took it, just because he was so cool.

His test-taking policies are awesome (open-chalkboard!), his explanations are very clear, and he is funny and good at explaining things. The only problem I had with this class is that he made it seem too easy, so I was a little shocked when it suddenly became more difficult than anticipated halfway through the semester.
Not well organized, the homeworks became pretty hard, but the lectures were easy to follow and he answers your questions if you ask.
Awesome lecturer.  Extremely clear and easy to follow explanations for everything!  Plus a quirky sense of humor.  241 with Pless is INCREDIBLE!
Maybe not the most organized, but has a really solid understanding of the material.
Funny guy and good teacher.  Homeworks can be difficult but Pless is willing to answer any questions you may have.  Take him for CS201 if you can.

Beware: "Quirky" is a good adjective. But he's got a great sense of humor, and he really, really knows his stuff- take him if possible, but only if you're going to actually participate in class. He permits (and pretty much encourages) irrelevant
Not the easiest professor to follow, and sometimes the TA didn't even know how to do the homework problems. But he's pretty entertaining and helpful.

Such a great professor. Keeps class interesting and fun. The material covered in class is great for those entering the bio or science world and has helped me in other classes. Super easy but you still learn quite a bit. Take his class if possible.

Great professor, he made the material very interesting, approachable, and applicable. The homeworks and exams were reasonable, although the grading scale is slightly harsher than average (93 is an A-). Still a great class to take. Work included 1 homework per class, 3 midterms (no final), and one short group project (mainly working by yourself)

I happen to love etymology, partly because it lets you easily remember or outright guess the meanings of even the most obscure words you might come across. That said, I think Platte is the shiiiit--he's highly engaging, helpful, and understanding. If you go to class and keep up with the easy, short (yet frequent) homeworks, you should do great.
Really interesting professor and the class has practical use. No final and the exams aren't bad at all. So glad I took this class
His class is so fun and he is genuinely nice
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really great professor. His lectures are informative and he does his best to make them interesting given pretty dry material. He loves to show video examples of weird contraptions, and sometimes a live Eagle webcam video. Tests are graded incredibly generously but you still learn a lot. He's also a very nice guy outside of class.

The goat. I loved going to class even though not strictly mandatory. He is fun to have for lecture, clearly enjoys what he does, overall a joy to learn from even if course content isn't super rigorous.

Took Machine Elements, Dynamics, and Senior Design with him. The nicest professor. Very knowledgeable and hands-on, and the classes themselves are pretty easy (and he makes them easy with how his notes are). He'll have a lot of homemade demos which is really cool.

The lectures were entertaining and engaging while providing lots of interesting/useful information. There is a lot of weekly homework for this class (coding, written, and CAD) that takes a decent amount of time to complete but it's pretty easy/straightforward.

Dr. Potter always made class fun and interesting. If you don't get an A, it's probably because you were trying not to. Easiest class in the MEMS department by far, and probably one of the most useful.

This class was by far my favorite class at WashU due to the flexibility of the class and finally being able to apply what we learned in engineering. Potter gave lots of suggestions for projects but was also open to ideas related to engineering. Grading was very simple as long as you completed all the work on time and put some effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Unmatched lectures. Extremely fascinating and engaging. You should 100% take this class!!
This is a class for film students. Easy if you aren't one, but be ready to do actual work
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor
I love this man more than my own father

SO AWESOME He is so funny and personable, it's like having a friend tell you about something they are interested in. He's down-to-earth, super caring, and doesn't think of himself as better/smarter than his students. I wasn't excited to learn about American cinema history but he actually made it really interesting. He is so cutieee

Took this class on a whim and it ended up being one of my favorites. Powers is an engaging professor, and all the films you watch are fascinating. I have no background in film studies and was able to do fine. Passionate and clearly knowledgeable in his field. Is reasonable with assignments. Lectures are all interesting and well done.

Professor Powers is great. He is super enthusiastic about every course he teaches, and is excited to help any student who asks for help. I would highly recommend taking a course with him. You will learn a lot, and if you put the work in, you will get a good grade.

Dr. Powers is absolutely my favorite professor I've had at Wash U. So much passion and his enthusiasm is infectious. Lectures are always really cool, doing the reading improves the experience and makes it easier to follow and contribute to discussion. Expects a lot of his students, fairly hard grader, but gives great feedback on how to improve.
He is a good teacher who has humor at times. Overall is a nice guy. The class is a freshman seminar and has a good amount of work. He doesn't grade too hard, but rarely gives out A's.
GOAT

Dr. Polites is an amazing professor and such a nice guy. This class was so informative and I have learned information from it that I will want to know for years to come. Take this class, you won't regret it.

I had him for Medprep. The lectures are 2 hours long, which can seem like a doozy, but he is engaging the entire time. He's so funny, and there is a lot of valuable stuff to learn. The "Ooh-Aah" lecture is probably the most engrossed I've ever been in a lecture EVER - highly recommend!

I know the student who provided the only negative comments on this site. I knew her in both in college and medical school. She was told by Dr. Polites to stop coming to class late. Of course, that's all some students need to attack a professor and course that has among the highest approval ratings in the university.
Really resourceful class. Learned a lot, definitely every considering pre-med should take this class.
AMAZING!! Such a helpful class.
DR. GREGORY POLITES IS A GOD AMONG MEN. TAKE MEDPREP
This class is literally "show up and pass" that's how it works. Polites is funny and a good lecturer. If you are considering a career in medicine, take this class.

Greg Polites is an annoying, self righteous person. He told the same stories over and over again and bores you out of being pre-med. As a current WUSM student and a former wustl undergrad, I can say that Greg Polites does NOT offer an accurate portrait of the medical school. Please do not take Med Prep.

Bad w canvas + after effects. Can't keep track of our websites and had the whole class type our names in his email every critique. I suggested he make a google doc with our websites, but he got defensive and said he "wasn't in town for the last few days". Disorganised; canvas assignments have wrong dates and prompts. Pro: easy + lots of work days

Going into his class, I was really nervous about not doing well as I am not in Sam Fox and have no experience with any of adobe. Tim made all my fears go away as he was extremely helpful, understanding, and accessible. I thought his feedback was helpful but not too harsh as he clearly just cares about seeing his students excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Through the process of creating projects, Professor Portlock actively encouraged students to give each other helpful feedback while simultaneously offering his own. He is very open to different styles and emphasized the importance of experimentation and creativity in our work, which I really appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's kinda disorganized but I think that's because he's new to WashU. Gives basic open-ended feedback (+ lots of group crits), but you can always ask for more specific feedback. He's also really open to diff. styles so he lets you do what you want. If you actively participate and ask questions before doing the project, you'll do well in his class.

Unorganized and no sense of time management. In our crits he never once got to everyone's work fully, so most of the time my feedback was "I like x, think about x," and then he'd move on. When asked 1-on-1 the feedback was more helpful, but took a long time to get out of him. All this+ knowing that you could have easily been in John's group :(

My main problems with Portlock are that he's very disorganized and that he can go weeks without discussing certain students' work. We spend hours on a drawing and he leaves very little time for critiques, often skipping over the works of many students. He's a nice guy but I can honestly say I haven't learned much since the first week of school.

Prof. Portnoy was one of the best professors I've had. He really cares about his students and the focus in class is learning, not grades. His lectures are interesting and applicable to the real world. There's a couple of essays you have to write, but he grades them fairly. There's not a ton of other homework. Overall, a wonderful prof and class.

Rob Portnoy is the BEST, though he needs to re-do the quizzes for this class. They are unbelievably random in terms of what they ask; besides that the class is pretty fair and if you use the TAs, go to office hours, put in a decent amount of time into readings/papers, you'll get what you deserve. Can't say that abt quizzes tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had Professor Portnoy for Human Resources Management and Leadership in Organizations and he is one of the best professors I've had. He makes class super interactive and engaging. It is easy to get an A if you attend class and do the few assignments so I was never concerned about my grades - only about learning, which is honestly rare and a gift
I got an A on the midterm, and an A- on the final. I got a B in the class!?  If you take this class, you're risking facing a deadly grading curve.
Great class. Very nice and caring person. interesting topics. Quite easy as long as you go to class.

Extremely easy. Very boring. Take home midterm and final. Required to keep a "learning journal" where you write about what you did in class everyday from an "HR Perspective". Almost no work. 1/20th of a finance class in terms of work. 1/5th of a marketing class. Really nice guy. Bring a laptop so you can surf the web during class.
he makes you laugh..easy but informative class.
This was the best and one of the easiest classes that I have ever taken.  If you need an upper level course, take this, you won't regret it!
He is one of the best professors ever that inspires you to learn and take interest in class material
Really nice, always allowed re-takes of take-home exams, and gave full credit. Wants people to do really well.

Professor Precup is great! I took her Honors Math 1 as my introduction to proof-based mathematics. The course is challenging, but I enjoyed it nonetheless. She lectures great and clearly, and have very inspiring OH. She organizes homework so that 1-2 problems are more difficult, and she intentionally does that to motivate students to seek for help.

Precup makes this class difficult (as it should be). Her lectures are solid and she provides good study resources, but the tests were challenging. She also left for 2 weeks in the middle of the semester, leaving us with a sub, which wasn't ideal. However, she is super nice and cares about student success.
Relates to students well and explains proofs well. She is happy to help in office hours, which are very helpful. Lots of homework which is very difficult, but collaboration is encouraged.

310 is a tough class with every professor. She's doing a fair job, but the thing is: She gives out way too much homework (I need about 2 hours just for copying with Chat's help). There's no curve on the exams, but the exams are hard and there's very little extra credit, so it's bad for your grade.

She is a great professor. I love her lectures bc she always explains idea very clearly. It is great to have her as your first proof-based class. Attend her office hour, it will be inspirational for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Precup explains things well and is so nice. Generally, the examples she goes over are easier than the ones on the quizzes but just do some extra practice outside of class and you'll be ok. The Calc II workbook is really helpful because it has practice problems and equation summary sheets. Webwork problems are a good grade booster too.
Excellent lecturer. Clearly understands material and is able to effectively communicate it. Homework and exams is challenging but certainly doable. Accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ponder's Orgo class is certainly quite challenging, but his passion for the subject, and interest in his students, is genuine and clear. While tough, Ponder is a great professor. If you are PreMed at WashU you should take his class. Grading is hard but the final distribution is quite reasonable.

Organic chemistry is definitely a class where you as a student have to rise to the occasion to understand the material. Dr. Ponder writes tough exams, but he is intentional about the exams and problem sets he creates. Ponder is accessible and very willing to help you rehash what you don't understand from lectures or from the textbook. Nice guy.

Ponder is an excellent teacher. He does a good job of covering not just what happens but WHY. My understanding of chem was greatly enhanced by the language and methods he used. If you're focused on the grade, I advise going through every chapter problem in the text. But enjoy the class too--being taught by such a good lecturer is a real privilege.

Professor Ponder is tough. His exams are not easy, but none of the material is new. He teaches you the concepts and gives you practice problems that challenge your understanding of them. His exams are a comprehensive review of all past challenges. His curve is fair with about 30% of the class receiving an A. Do all his practice sets!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Ok, his lectures are not terrible, but he just doesnt know how to teach. He especially does not know how to write exams, and he brags about that. As a result, he uses a complex grading scheme, he cannot even describe. I was truly disappointed w/ this class. (Worst in Chemistry)
One of the best lecturers Ive had at WashU- really cares about his students and an all around great professor.

I really enjoy Dr. Ponder's teaching style.  He is a great lecturer and goes slowly enough that students have time to absorb and understand the mechanisms/syntheses that they are copying from the board.  His exams are quite difficult, but his grading curve is more than fair.
Ponder is clearly very enthusiastic about his field, but he even confesses to be bad at writing exams...

I admit that I bear much of the blame for my eventual performance in the course, however, I honestly think that Ponder needs to reevaluate how he writes his tests&problem sets. They are too difficult compared to the material provided during lectures. Your mileage may vary on office hours, I often found myself more confused afterwards than before.

Lectures are pretty good, and that is where it stops.  His exams and problems sets don't make sense, and the TAs don't get them either.  He has no clue how to write tests, but at least he admits it.  He is really weird in one-on-one settings.  I stopped going to office hours.  You need a PhD in statistics to figure out his grading scheme.
Great, informative lectures, but the problem sets and exams made me PONDER dropping the course (get it?). Seriously though, this course was by far the hardest thing I've ever taken.

Good grief, hardest course I've taken that wasn't because of the professor. Fortunately, Dr. Ponder is extremely helpful and does a very good job of explaining the essentials for understanding orgo. Exams are extremely hard but graded on a generous curve, so it's really not that bad. Doing the readings/problem sets is a must
Ponder gets a bad rep, but I don't really see why.

He's a phenomenal teacher, very clear and imparts knowledge of chemistry that will last far beyond the class. He teaches a way of thinking, not just memorization of very general concepts. His exams are very difficult but the curve is extremely generous. My interest in chemistry started with his class and the way he pushed students to problem solve.

Dr. Ponder is an incredibly nice guy who is willing to get to know any student. His lectures are very informative, and he starts each one with a fun art history lesson! He truly loves this subject and is doing some amazing research - go ask him about it. His tests are very difficult, but once you learn how molecules work, they make perfect sense.

I heard horror stories about Orgo I with Ponder. Don't be afraid! He starts every lecture with a mini art history lesson, how cool. It's a challenging class, but the curve is generous and Ponder is an enthusiastic guy who clearly loves teaching orgo. By the end you will have a strong conceptual understanding of the subject.

Exams are hard but the curve is extremely generous. Pretty easy to get an A compared to other advanced chemistry courses at washu. Prof. Ponder is always available during his office hour and really helpful as well.
no.

Jay Ponder expected us to already know very difficult topics about Orgo before he even taught them to us. The gap between class material and the exams was enormous and he really knows how to shake your confidence. He doesn't understand how to relate to students or how to teach in an effective manner. Never take this with him if you have a choice.

He's a good teacher and genuinely cares about students, but there's a significant gap between the material he presents in class (or even that's presented in the book) and the concepts that are tested.  The curve makes grades turn out okay in the end, so long as you don't mind exam averages under 50% in the meantime...
He taught out of the textbook but did not teach for his exams. The gap between the in class material and the level expected on the exams was huge.

He flies through the material and does not realize the students are lying in the dust.  He clearly cares, but he does not know how to relate to the students, and he cannot write exams.  I understand this is the first time he has taught, and it showed.  He needs to take teaching classes.

Skipping the baseline levels of organic chem, expecting us to fully understand topics after one reading or example, and consistently writing tests above 80% of the class's abilities proved Jay Ponder to be the most arrogant and useless professor I have encountered. I think I would have enjoyed orgo under most other professors.

Organic chemistry can be a hard class to make interesting, but Dr. Ponder certainly tried his best to make it fun. Exams were pretty brutal, but if you studied a few days prior to the exam a B was certainly possible to obtain. Overall, Dr. Ponder was an engaging lecturer who teaches a rough class, he's a good guy.
Hard class, but he's a good teacher!

Writing intensive class, material was far-reaching and ranged from discussions of laboratory culture to the anthropology of organ donation, social media, and DNA technologies. Incredibly well-spoken, and almost frighteningly intelligent, caring and lovely professor too. Learnt a TON. She recognizes your hard work and will reward you for it.
Great class. Great lectures, interesting material. One of my favorite classes I've taken here. Dr. Song is amazing, and teaches you  a lot without making it unnecessarily difficult.

Contemporary Chinese Culture and Society was one my favorite courses I've taken so far.  Prof. Song is incredibly engaging, kind, and knowledgeable.  The class was really interesting, and though not particularly difficult  I learned a ton.  Fantastic teacher.  I'd take any class taught by her.

Professor Purdy was among my favorites at Wash U. She is absolutely brilliant and does a great job at teaching the details. You learn a lot in her class. Its also clear she cares a lot about her students both in and out of the classroom. Her class is not easy, but it is fair. You have to think to succeed.

I purposefully took this class because I'd heard such positive comments regarding Dr. Purdy. Everything I heard was a lie. She has absolutely no compassion for her students, especially during a global pandemic. The workload was ridiculous and Dr. Purdy was of no help in terms of meeting outside of class. The worst class I've ever taken at WashU.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Very interesting and relevant class, even for non-education majors. Rare that I'd say this, but tbh I enjoyed the content enough that it made the LONG reading assignments worth it. Prof has high expectations, but was always willing to help students. Relatively little writing (for a writing intensive); just two 3-pg papers and one 10-pg term paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Purdy is the smartest professor I have ever had, but with that comes high expectations. She expects you to be on the ball 100% of the time and know the readings front and back. Even though she comes off as intimidating, she is actually not as hard of a grader as you would think. This is not an easy A but you will learn SO much.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Sachs' grading criterion is clear. She made sure we understood what she was looking for in her practice mid-term exam. Also, she is very accessible during her office hours. Would take her class again if I have the opportunity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: The grading standards are unclear, and the classroom atmosphere is not good.

Prof. Sachs taught an extremely complex (and at times convoluted) subject in an accessible, clear way. Her expectations for our knowledge were always clear - we were expected to know a lot, but we knew what we were expected to know! She’s tough but fair and always supportive, and made a real to get to know us. She’s a fantastic professor!

Seminar was incredibly insightful. Should be required for every member of congress and others working on drug price policy. Deeply explores what turns out to be a nuanced world of the policies/incentives and laws related to drug development and drug pricing. Highly recommend this course even though it is hard at times and a lot of reading.
Tough, but fair, and if you answer wrong she nudges you towards the right answer. The feeling of soul-clenching terror when she cold-calls on you never stops though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nice person; bad (and cold) professor. Our grade was 50% participation and 50% papers (three overall), but the grading process was never explained (i.e. quality? quantity?). She gave no helpful feedback on papers and never explained how they were evaluated. And for a so-called "expert," she contributed very little insight into discussion. Avoid her
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Many ideas in HIST 1151 related to medical history are interesting. The course is rigorous for a 1000-level class and requires strong independent preparation. Essay expectations can feel highOverall, this course is best suited for students who are ready for a reading- and writing-intensive class.
Hard grader with no clear grading criteria.

Prof. Ramos is an amazing professor! I was initially intimidated by the long readings and the fact that there were only 4 papers. However, she was very understanding and flexible when it came to grading and due dates; The readings were interesting and thoroughly explained in class. You still have to put in work, but Ramos is always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I found physics to be rather challenging, but Dr. Ramanathan's lectures were very clear and helpful! He checks in with the class intermittently to ensure that the material is understood, and he presents numerous practice problems so that you can see the material being applied. There were also a lot of very cool physics demonstrations!
He's good at teaching especially compared to the other Physics I professors. Super nice and wants to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really encourages in class participation and teaches at a moderate pace. Always willing and excited to answer questions, very friendly and polite.
Really great
really great at explaining concepts and is always very engaging with the students, will stop and make sure to clarify any confusion.
I'm sad to see that he is not teaching Physics 192 next semester. He explains things very clearly and maintains a clear structure of the class.

Prof. Ramanathan is very kind, his lectures are sometimes slow, but overall decently engaging.Make regrade requests on exams because he usually finds a way to give you a few extra points (assuming there's some merit to your appeal). Watch that your hand doesn't go above your shoulder if you don't want to instantly be called on :)

Great lectures for a challenging physics class. Loves to answer questions, is super engaging and polite. Makes awkward eye contact with you mid lecture though. He's super interesting and I genuinely enjoy this class.

Professor Ran is a great person who truly cares about his students. He is very good and fueling in-class discussions about relevant topics. My main complaint is that at times it can be hard to understand him between his accent and the microphone. So, if you don't see that being an issue, and you benefit from discussion to learn. I would recommend.

Was Ran the best lecturer I ever had? No. Did he have very clear handwriting when writing on the board? Absolutely not. However he's one of the funniest professors I've ever had and I was always laughing in class which made it easy to be invested in his lectures. Highlight was him leading us in a Shrek sing-a-long on the last day of class.

If you work with other people on assignments and go to lectures, totally possible to get an A. Lectures are required attendance- Ran is a pretty funny lecturer, I laughed quite a bit. However, the lectures can be a bit complex or unrelated to the subject at times.
Awesome professor. Pretty clear lecturing, very fun and entertaining. Clearly cares about his students.

Lectures were pretty dry and often poorly organized. Slideshows didn't include key information, so if you didn't write down everything she said out loud, you would miss something important. Several exam questions asked about things not at all covered in class.

Doesn't record lectures, disorganized and disengaging lectures, posts lecture slides that are missing key material, review slides don't have everything, expects you to know content from textbook not covered in class, exams are hard, but just unfair bc they are terribly worded. I often get questions about material I know well wrong.

Her lectures are very disorganized and it's very unclear what you're supposed to take notes on and know. Lectures are not recorded and the slide decks posted on Canvas are missing key terms. There are no practice exams, no practice questions, and no study guide provided for exams. There is a review session, but they often miss key content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are very mundane and unengaging. She posts empty notes that are very difficult to review. Her exam prep is the bare minimum with review slides that are barely relevant to the actual exam's content. She encourages participation and has in class activities though so that's something.

I came to her office during office hours, and she looked and sounded annoyed that I was there. Why have office hours if you will be bothered by students coming by???? She clearly does not care about her students and only wishes to further her own career at our expense. If you don't want to teach and only want to research, then do that.
Her lectures were a bit boring and disorganized, and hard to take notes on. She cared about her students and was available outside of class to explain these concepts however

Thompson did not strike me as someone who wants to connect with her students. The lectures were quite boring and pretty dense. I would suggest anki for this class. Readings were a lot, and I gave up at some point. Exams were tricky, but doable (I would only study the day before). Take it with friends so you aren't bored.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was extremely hard for me. The lectures went so fast, and no videos were posted. Dr. Thompson is not understanding or friendly towards students, and is clearly at the university as a researcher. If you're interested in psychopathology, take it another semester with a different professor. The lectures are not helpful for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a Psychology major who has gotten As in all other psych classes, this class was harder than I expected. Lectures went too fast for me to keep up and readings took a long time. I could not figure out what to do in order to succeed in this class. The only reason I have an OK grade is because I had friends in the class who seemed to understand.

Pretty much your whole grade is made up of 4 50 questions MCQ exams, the questions aren't hard but they are focused on the textbook which you have to read. She records the lectures but you have to request them. She's fine but she doesn't really care about making personal connections. The TAs also grade hard on the few homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: pretty easy class and lectures were fine

Renee Thompson is not a good lecturer. She is VERY dull, passive-aggressive, and condescending. She often doesn't know how to answer students' questions during lectures and her office hours are a waste of time. Final grades aren't out yet but I've had an A- all semester. The class is easy enough if you attend the lectures and read the textbook.

Huge reason im leaving WashU. Students often triggered by class, bc the professor gave no warnings before graphic topics. Emails were not responded to, however personal they were. If you dont like a lot of reading, lectures, or multiple-choice tests, you wont get a good grade. If youre highly interested in the topics, that helps carry you through.

Good class, it's just a lecture so you pretty much have to go everyday if you want to get the material. No recorded poll everywhere and the slides are posted online. She does go through the slides pretty fast though so I would recommend taking notes on your computer or else you will fall behind. Interesting class, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class because it (like most psych classes at WashU) was very clear what was expected of you. Show up to lecture, take notes, and study textbook material, and you should be good. It was also pretty interesting. Since the requirements were really clear, this was never a class that gave me too much stress.

Thompson is a good lecturer, she tries to find videos and examples for class that are engaging and interesting to students that help you understand material. To do well in class, you must read the textbook and also go to lecture and study both. It is a great class but you must work hard to do well

Must pay close attention to lecture coz there are blanks in lecture slides you must fill out and these will be tested. Exams test a lot from textbook which she doesnt cover during lecture, so catch up with reading! Exams are not easy, assignments can be buffer but there is no reminder or announcement. Lectures are boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not a good lecturer, sometimes seem lost. But she tries to make up for it with videos and class discussion. She also gives assignments as a buffer for exams which is very nice. Her lectures could get very boring because of her teaching style and the materials are very set and structured. But try to go to class as her demonstrations could be useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She largely reads off the slides, but often throws in explanation that's not on them, so you need to go to class. The class started to get boring and monotonous toward the end since all of the lectures were structured the same, but the material is insightful and makes you more aware of stigma. Tests aren't too bad if you study and go to lecture.

Presented material in clear and concise manner. Made lectures interesting with special topics, videos, and supplementary assignments. Always available outside of class and very interested in students' feedback

Not a great lecturer, but she's funnygenuine and clearly invested and passionate about her class.  I appreciated her sensitivity to the subject of stigma towards mental illness.  Open to answering questions in class.  Tests are difficult but not unfair.  Would definitely recommend this class, but wouldn't necessarily recommend her as a prof.

She can be a little dry during lecture, but it was her first year teaching so that's understandable. She's pretty helpful if you talk to her outside of class, and if you had a problem with a test question she genuinely wants to know how to improve things in the future and help out students.

She straight up reads off the slides and doesn't post them on blackboard until 5 mins before class. Annoying, but I'll cut her some slack since this is her first class. The exams are easy other than a few misleading (or poorly written) questions. Very attractive.

She's brand new, so give her a break. Really nice during office hours. Might read from slides, but pay attention to other things she says. Exams a little tricky, but if you study a lot then you're fine. Makes assignments fun by having us watch movies or read stories. I think with experience at WashU she'll get a lot better. Just give her a chance.
Just reads from slides, tries to trick you on exams, and makes a class that should be fascinating extremely boring. I was so upset.

Raj restrict anyone to ask question previously for the class. And one time I ask a question because I am still a bit confusing about a concept. He say that this guy maybe cheat for his homework. It is a disaster for his words and make me awkword. I write my homework hand by hand. How dare he say that words!

1. too much workload
2. strict grading
3. bad temper
4. unfair, judge student who ask questions(they ask questions just because they study hard)
5. the exam is really insame, lot of work but just a few time left to finish it

The worst professor I've ever had. Teaches remotely because "it's inefficient to come to campus." He grades you on participation but requires we keep track of our own participation to "prove" they should get points. The topic is fascinating, but just get the textbook and run. 0/10.

Terrible professor, always contradicts himself and incapable of answering questions. For such an important topic in CS, he hasn't updated the materials in years. The only takeaway from this course is that I should have self-studied.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Worst ever, hates questions , same exam same homeworks every year! All about how well u squeez info into ur cheatsheet! About how fast u can answer in the exam! You won't benefit much.

 Material is not up to date

The poorest choice of professor for such an important material in cs field. Avoid him. Super long exam with very short time window. Boring lectures where he is unable to answer any question clearly, while he forces students to ask them. Flipped class, with recorded lectures and mandatory zoom Q&A sessions. Unreasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super dry and boring. Flipped classroom (watch lecture at home, go to class for Q&A). Basically, he just reads from the slides. You probably learn much more and better from reading the textbooks. Hard test. Materials are definitely interesting and stuff that every cs major should know. Too bad we can't get a better prof to do such an important job
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best courses that I have taken with this professor. Make sure to attend the class and participate. Lots of homework and labs, but really easy to do because it won't take more than two hours to do a bunch of them together. Clear grading criteria. Be aware of the exams timing and competition.

Horrible.  Unable to answer any questions in class.  Exams are ridiculously long and are given in a shortened period of time.  His explanations are vague and the best students are the ones that can fit every little detail onto their exam cheat sheets.

One of the worst profs in the CS department. Very unclear in lecture - he invites students to ask questions, but then can barely answer them. Tests on minutiae and acronyms without ensuring understanding of larger concepts (put a *lot* of detail on your cheat sheet to do well). Cuts off time on tests after 60 min. so that students won't finish...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is really patient. To do well, you need to go for every class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You have to work hard. It is a very difficult class. You can tell that the professor really want the student to do well. But there are lot things to learn in this class. You have to work hard but it is definitely worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good course for those interested in going to the industry. Will cover a collection of concepts not known to many.
It is really helpful.

Very useful course especially for people who are seeking a job in industry. I believe the professor did a lot of preparation on this course to present high quality material. With his vast knowledge and expertise in this field, you will definitely learn a lot. The grading was generous, so you don't have to worry as long as you study fair enough.
Really helpful. Especially for those who wants to go to the industry right after graduation

I think it is a great class. The professor teaches everything from the fundamental level. The homework is quite related to the teaching material, and not very hard. Overall it is a good choice to chose it as an undergraduate course.

This was one of the best courses which I ever took. I went from not knowing anything about networking to deep appreciation to the field and looking for ways to be active in this field. The exams were more than fair. In a world were any device with a battery is networked I highly recommend this class.

Studying with Dr. Jain was an amazing experience. All that you need to know to start you on networking is in this class. Jain is very knowledgeable, he cares about the students. Lectures were very interesting and the book highly recommended. Dr. Jain will explain and go over any question that you may have, I wish more prof. were like this.

Professor Jain is one of the renown experts in the field of networking. He is very knowledgeable about the material. It is difficult to convey all of the material in only 2 hour and a half lectures a week, so most of the learning comes from the textbook.

I enrolled this course in FL2010, which motivates me enroll more courses taught by this professor. I really enjoyed this course absolutely. In common sense, this course is the best one in PhD core courses. Don't hesitate to enroll this course.

Very excellent course! I can't believe why some guys rated this teacher so terrible. This course teaches us a lot. The percentage of grade is very reasonable. Best of 2 mid-exams will be chosen as your final mid-exam grade. I've never seen other Profs provide this kind of mechanism. Also, the content covered in every class is awesome.
Pretty structured professor. Very easy to follow and posts everything online

A good teacher, easy to understand and follow. Material in class is interesting and easy to understand. CSE473 is useful to understand core concepts in computer networking. I recommend others to take this course.

Good Professor.  Prof. Jain genuinely knows what he's talking about and brings industry experience to the classroom.  Grading was generous, there wasn't too much work, and overall class was pleasant and enjoyable.
It is a very good class. If you work hard, I am sure you will learn lot's of useful knowledge.
It is a very good class. If you really work hard, you can learn lot's of useful knowledge.

Pretty easy class, material was thought pretty well covered. We went thru a lot of material, and everything was covered in book too. The labs were pretty simple to do especially if you had any idea how to ssh in a terminal.
Really smart guy, simply not a good teacher. Tests and gives work on things he didn't really teach, assignments are always strangely worded and unclear, doesn't communicate well with students.

Not a good professor. Argued with students who asked questions. Tests were entirely memorization based. Lectures were not helpful, although the textbook for the class was excellent, that's where I learned 90% of the material. Confusing and tedious labs. DO NOT TAKE HIS NETWORKING CLASS, BUY THE BOOK
terrible professor. Incomprehensible. tests on random and unrelated material. mean-spirited (laughs at questions posed by students). avoid.

Great guy, the most important aspect of taking a class with him is creating a relationship with him and utilizing connections. otherwise, the material is interesting, but knowledge of the material is graded horribly on tests. attend class and participate.
So disingenuous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His grading scale is horrible, makes the class unfair. Super entertaining and interesting class though.

While admittedly some of the readings are rather dumb (you are tested on them too) and Rishe spends a lot of time bragging about his connections, the lectures are still rather engaging and he's a great guy to speak to outside of the classroom. He's very knowledgable on & caring for the subject matter. Worth taking him for any sports business class.

He grades you on dumb assignments and exams that test your sheer memorization of specific things that will likely have no value moving forwards, and then has bizarre grading criteria. He is a good lecturer but there is no material to back it up, and then we are expected to memorize like 10 different lists that say effectively the same thing.

Rishe's personality is fantastic. I never dreaded going to lecture, always felt welcomed to go to office hours, and thought he had a great sense of humor. The class was graded by very few things. The exams really did not test that much microeconomic knowledge and tested much more on arbitrary current events (was annoying). Didn't learn that much.

For Rishe's MEC 290, you don't need to know microeconomic quantitative concepts super well. He tests primarily on examples he gives in class, or applications in the textbook. He goes over things quickly in class, so I would highly recommend rewatching his classes and taking notes from that. Often gets off topic and tries to tell jokes/ anecdotes.

I was not a fan of Professor Rishe or his class. I found his explanations to be very confusing and was really not a fan of his attitude. He constantly talked about himself. Based on the class structure, you aren't tested on the concepts of micro, but rather the articles and applications he has you read outside of class. Would not recommend.

He was an absolutely fantastic professor for MEC290. He explains the concepts in a way that makes them easy to understand, and if you don't understand you can just ask and he'll be happy to help. There were no homework assignments in the class, just 2 test and 2 quizzes which all required significant studying but were very fair.

Fantastic professor. Probably one of my favorite professors at WashU. Lectures are great. He really explains the concepts in a way that is understandable. He integrates real world events and applications into the course which is super helpful. Would highly recommend.

Pat is really so great. Has good, entertaining lectures and really takes the time to get to know his students. He also is very good at making the material applicable in the real world and gives very valuable life tips for working, in the business world or otherwise.
Only professor I've ever had at WUSTL that sends out weekly emails. Extremely friendly - knows all students by name. Reasonable, nice, charismatic.  Tests are tough and packed with questions.

Never seemed prepared for class.  Talked too much about himself and not enough about sports.  Almost no economics involved with topics.  Could have covered the same amount of material in half the time.  Very boring lectures because he never stayed on topic.  I do not recommend at all.
GOod
I'd rather watch YT shorts for 24 hours
I love her

Just because you achieve as an academic does not mean you are skilled at teaching. I had to teach myself the majority of the content in this course despite attending every lecture and making a very active effort to try to learn.

decent lecturer -- the course is difficult. the homework does not help at all and is extremely time consuming. I scored slightly above average each exam (avgs in 60s) but still ended with A-. 480/600 = A- and 535/600 was an A, which is an insane gap.

Lectures didnt help much without going over the textbook, especially towards the end. Big textbook merchant! Averages usually hovered around the 50s-60s which she would consider to be a good performance. If you can, pls take heemstra for your own sake. An A- or higher is doable, but youll need to really utilize the textbook & sacrifice hella time
I think she tries her best to teach, but her lectures are difficult to understand. I learned more from glancing the textbook as well as asking AI questions from previous exams/workshop questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: heemstra or gap semester.

Just avoid her at all costs tbh. She gives practice workshop questions every week, but they're literally only 6 pages long so u can never get any practice in. Also her exams r stupid hard, with things that you've never seen before. Then she has the audacity to tell the class that the exam was easy despite the average being a 50%.

I don't understand how a teacher could be so unhelpful, given the resources of a class as big as Orgo and 3-time a week lectures. Randomly, in a help session, a small group of students were told that the AI program, which we were forced to use, was teaching us incorrect rules and mechanisms. The whole class was never informed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid her at all cost. Exams are super difficult. Went to her office hours once about an exam and tried to explain through my reasoning but she got super defensive and wouldn't let me talk...

Her lectures have improved significantly over the last few years. She is generally available and helpful during office hours. The class is difficult, but she realistically does a good job with the allotted time.
actually so bad she doesn't teach at all. avoid at all costs

Very kind and helpful if you talk to her one on one. It's clear that her expectation for students is that we teach ourselves, and lecture just goes over the main concepts (I mean hey, it does say that in the syllabus. Fair game). Get ready to read the textbook and go to office hours if you wanna do well.

Lectures are for the most part unintelligible and important concepts are mumbled or glossed over. Camping out in office hours/optional workshops is basically required if you want to get any sort of grade you'd be unashamed of. The average scores on the midterms are abysmal and she will blame it all on the students.
Genuinely could not have learned less from lectures, had to teach myself everything and then the exams were unreasonably hard. Never had a worse lecturer.

this professor just can't explain concepts clearly, maybe due to her english. she tries to explain but everytime fades into mumbling and doesn't know what she's talking about. also, a lot of memorization that is useless. why would we need to memorize pka and electronegativity values? shouldn't these be provided on the reference sheet?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Chen is amazing and I don't understand why she gets so much hate. She listens to student feedback, gives clear expectations, and is incredibly caring and supportive. She was a much better lecturer than Barnes because she stayed on topic and clearly explained mechanisms and what was needed to know for the exam.

Professor Chen is awesome. I understand how some people might find her lecture style difficult, but I think orgo in general is hard to lecture. It really takes a lot of work outside the classroom, but if you plan ahead, use your resources, and ask questions, you will be ok. Most importantly, Professor Chen really cares about her students.

I really think that Chen is over hated. As someone in section 3, I thought that she did a better job than Barnes at explaining concepts and mechanisms. She's also incredibly caring and nice and will go out of her way to try to help you.
Did not explain any concepts propely

This class is very difficult and covers a lot of material, but Dr. Chen is so caring and supportive that it makes it worth it. Her office hours are very helpful, and she always provides a detailed explanation. She puts so much effort into making sure that everyone has the resources to succeed, and it's important that you utilize them.

the material is challenging but I don't think it is because of Professor Chen. Orgo at WashU is pretty hard. But she is ready to help and willing to help you even outside her office hours. I found her helpful throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Avoid her at all costs. Has no idea how to teach, glazes over difficult concepts with no explanation, very confusing lectures. Get ready to learn on your own. Tests are difficult, some close to impossible. Class averages were in the 50-60's, that should tell you something about the her teaching abilities. Take the class with literally anyone else.

While I am aware this was Professor Chen's first semester lecturing, lecture was difficult to follow and did not adequately cover topics for exams which almost entirely make up the final grade. I found reading the textbook to be a better alternative to lecture but lead to a lot of time spent reading rather than practicing. Exam avgs were around 50

Lectures were not useful and it felt as if you had to fuse both professors together to gain some basic understanding of the concepts. Office hours were not helpful as she did not understand what students would ask her or how to explain the concepts clearly. Very frustrating to deal with and did not feel supported by the professors in the course.

I was frustrated w/ Chen a lot this semester. This was her first time lecturing, so she deserves some leniency, but some lectures were just inadequate- eg not going into depth on the things students need to know, writing mechanisms in literal silence. OH were occasionally helpful- sometimes she didn't really get what students were trying to ask tho
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: What a terrible semester. Prof Chen was as confused as we were. I tried to go to the extra sessions, but those were just as bad. No idea what grades were based on. Just plain frustrating. To go from Chem 111/112 to this felt like false advertising. I was considering Chemistry as a major...not any more.

She doesn't know how to give clear lectures and would confuse the class and herself. If the average is a less than 50 on the exam for many students than that fault is on the professor not the students regardless of how hard the class is. She doesn't know how to gives lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was satisfactory at teaching the material, but could be better at explain concepts for everyone. Lectures were very fast paced but that had more to do with the material rather than her own doing. Was helpful if you went to office hours.
Boring lectures, inconsistent exams. Lack of useful practice questions. Generally not very helpful. If I hear her say "clearlei" again I'm gonna explode on the spot.

Not a good lecturer, very unengaging and not good at explaining concepts apart from surface level. Exams deal with much more complex problems that you could only be prepared for by work outside of class. Poorly structured. If students are averaging Ds on your exams you probably aren't teaching properly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Actually the worst professor ever. Fails to even teach. Doesn't even know chemistry herself (ex: always says "apparently" when explaining concepts as if even she is surprised by what she is teaching). It is very clear she has never taught here before. Exams aren't even close to what is taught. Rude. Doesn't answer questions. Just inadequate.

Professor Mabbs was an extremely enthusiastic and dedicated lecturer. His lectures were humorous and well explained. Some lectures build on context from the textbook and readings, and he doesn't go over that in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures are very comprehensive but crammed with information. He's a great teacher with lots of experience. Definitely take advantage of PLTLs, as that is where the concepts actually came together for me. Weekly quizzes are okay and require minimal studying, but exams are pretty difficult (especially the final).

Tough exams but grading scale adjusts for it. Professor Mabbs loves teaching, is accessible outside of class, and usually lectures well. Sometimes he doesn't time lectures well so we cram material into the last five minutes and his handwriting can be suspect. Overall, he is caring, even if he can be a little intimidating to talk to one-on-one.

He truly loves chemistry but is just not a great lecturer. Sort of goes in talking like you know the stuff. He cares, though, and tries. He is just not great at teaching, especially because it's a tough subject to learn. If you're in 1701 and don't have a vast chem background, I'd recommend going to Daschbach's lectures instead.

Chem 1701 is notoriously tough, but Mabbs is accessible outside of class and usually has great lectures. Sometimes he doesn't word things well and his handwriting can be suspect but he loves teaching and times lectures very well despite the dense material.
Dr. Mabbs is awesome. Such a great lecturer who you can tell is passionate about what he's teaching. His lectures were super engaging and taught well. Tough class but definitely worth it.
Tough material, tough tests with limited time, but great lecturer and accessible after and outside of class.

Mr. Mabbs has an extremely soothing voice and acts like he genuinely cares about your learning process in the class. He takes time to answers questions when a student raises their hands and also can spend time after lecture to answer any more questions you might have about certain topics. Although the course is difficult, he gives his support.
Inspirational, Hilarious, Caring
Very personable and kind. Wanted us to understand the material and was also very helpful during office hours.
Competent communicator.

While the course is very hard but he is really nice. He is so patient that he even explained one concept for me for 40 minutes after class. But since he is a researcher so sometimes his teaching can be incomprehensible.

The test grading was obnoxiously unfair, but the tests themselves were representative of in class material. Mabbs was ok, but his lectures got stale, and if you missed one, they felt really optional onward (although participation is graded). The help-sessions are always crowded and unavailable. PLTL/online-lectures are key.

tuff but great course. mabbs is such a cute englishman. dry sense of humor helps keep things chill in class. it was nice to have 2 profs so you could hear different perspectives. so happy i took 111 over 105. do not listen to advisors, 111 is quality.

Mabbs himself is very nice. Chem111 is extremely difficult, but he is a good professor. It can be difficult to ask questions in help sessions with so many other people there, but if you can ask, he does give good explanations. Plus, I really liked how he highlighted chemists from underrepresented identities.
Tuff course but Mabbs nailed it. He is so encouraging and I would love him even if I don't end up with an A.
Prof. Mabbs was an amazing professor and made Chem 111 very enjoyable!

Best prof ever. Really appreciated how he talks about scientists from underrepresented groups and achievements. Chem111/112 is not an easy course, but his lectures are very helpful. Hardworking pays off in this course.

Dr. Mabbs is a fantastic professor. Probably the best lecturer I have ever had. The content of Chem 111 is pretty difficult, but he always kept the lectures super engaging, and I never really found myself bored. He uses the chalkboard much more than slides which facilitates note-taking very well.
Chem 111 is a total disaster, but Mabbs is awesome. He gives very clear lectures and is very personable.
I LOVE HIM
difficult class but mabbs is awesome

Best science class I've taken in a while. Mabbs teaches lectures like a continuous story and class is entertaining and easy to follow. Assessments are difficult, but the curve makes it not too hard to do well.

Mabbs, mabbs, mabbs. What a mabbulous little British man! He cares so much about his students. He's very approachable as well, and his accent legitimately makes lecture less boring. Even though Chem 111 is definitely challenging, the instructors do a great job of providing lots of extra resources to help you succeed.

It's clear that Professor mabbs is very passionate about chemistry, and that he tries his best to help students understand course content. However, his expertise sometimes does the opposite because he just uses big words to explain very simple concepts, which can leave some people confused at times.

Mabbs was a good professor. Since 111 is such a hard class, I recommend going to Daschbach for office hours because she is an even better teacher in my opinion. Still, Mabbs is very passionate and quite organized as a lecturer. Be ready to put in the work for this class, but it isn't as impossible at it seems.

lots of tests but mabbs is a good professor that is passionate in what he teaches. he goes fast and there's a lot of tests so be prepared to essentially study the whole semester past October. would recommend if u can put the time in

Mabbs was a good lecturer who left me feeling prepared for the exams. He was also accessible to students outside of class and enjoyed getting to know people who wanted to know more about chemistry. Tests were extremely challenging and constitute most of your grade, so make sure you're prepared. The class incorporates a lot of physics too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I learned so much, and even though I got a C, I didn't fully utilize the resources that were provided until the end of the semester. he is a really good lecturer, and it is really easy to take notes and to learn. I do suggest going to office hours with prof. daschbach, she is the GOAT!

Mabbs is a great professor. Chem 111 is designed to be a very different course but, with few exceptions, Prof. Mabbs did a great job explaining concepts at a reasonable pace and working through examples. HW is very light but studying is absolutely necessary to get a good grade.

Dr. Mabbs was a caring teacher with very clear grading criteria. Use the calendar to stay on top of things. He was confusing sometimes, and do not drift off or you will be lost. No fear, go back and look at the video. Go to help sessions. I like Dr. Dashback's.
Amazing lecturer, makes class very interesting but you have to pay attention constantly to do well in the class. If you like physics and need to take chem take 111.

Mabbs includes weekly chemistry in the real world segments which combine the topics learned with applications. It is really engaging and unique to this teacher. He sometimes goes through topics a bit quickly and his examples aren't very reflective of quizzes and exams. His handwriting on the board isn't very good and it can be hard to take notes

Professor Mabb's lectures are very clear and easy to follow. The tests are difficult, however there are lots of resources to prepare you for them. Overall, he's a very dedicated and nice professor and truly cares about the topics he teaches.

Professor Mabbs is such an amazing lecturer. He is able to make the topics easy to understand and interesting. He really cares and wants his students to succeed, and he is very accessible outside of class during his office hours.

Nicest and most relatable guy I've ever met, and he is always there with a smile. He'll also help you after class or during DAILY office hours. Theres so many resources to help you succeed, even if the material is hard. Daschbach on the contrary, is not a nice person, but she is very intelligent and helpful.

Professor Mabbs is the sweetest, most passionate, little British man ever. He makes the most difficult topics easy to understand, and his passion for chemistry is contagious. I came into his class thinking chemistry was hell on earth, and now I want to major in chemistry. There are so many resources, and his brilliance is very apparent.
He is an expert in teaching, providing many great insights into the principle of general chemistry.
Very good lecturer, his lectures tell a story about chemistry. He is kind and very interested in helping us succeed.

Mabbs cares about his students, but his lectures are just average. He can ramble and go in circles so they are hard to follow sometimes. That being said, if you put in the work outside of class, it's not impossible to do well.

There's no denying that the exams are really hard. That said, the class has REALLY leniant cutoffs, and as long as you average your exams to around 80% you will definitely get an A. That said, 80 is even pretty hard to get sometimes. Mabbs is really caring, but he likes to make things difficult, which made me learn a lot.

Mabbs is hard to follow in lectures. He's not good at explaining concepts clearly and often goes in circles that makes you lose focus of the key concepts. He genuinely wants his students to understand the content though, especially in office hours. Chem 106 isn't as bad as it's reputation, but you have to put in a lot work outside of lectures.

chem106 = easy material made very difficult (for no reason) with very lenient cutoffs... the HARD A was an 83 or an 84? and an A+ is 97.. like what lol. mabbs is clear in lecture but overexplains easy shit. if you have a question go to luo. before exams go to bakupog. u will overstress and learn way too much and get a 96.9 (same grade as da 83.01s!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Based on the previous reviews, I was afraid of Professor Mabbs, but having gone through Chem106 with him I know he's a very thorough and excellent professor. He is a very good lecturer, you just have to pay attention and be an active learner. He's very kind, answers questions thoroughly, and is accessible outside of class.

I think 106 was much harder than 105, but I think Mabbs handled the content well. He was a good lecturer and usually went at a good pace. He held a lot of outside review and was always available for extra help. Overall, he seemed like a good guy and a strong professor. Just keep up with the content and attend PLTL! You got this, chaps!
