if you haven't taken AP chem, this class will be HELL. Get ready to dedicate half a semester to this one single class.

Get ready to learn an entire course by yourself. Mabbs is funny, charming, and VERY CLEAR, but lacks the most important teaching skill for an introductory course: teaching you what you need to know. He stresses things that are unnecessary for exams and glosses over the most important concepts. Material presented is unorganized. Exams are RLY hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mabbs does not explain concepts very clearly during his lectures (which are also quite dry), but he is pretty helpful in help sessions. His exams are way harder than any practice sets given.

After hearing how hard chem106 was, I was terrified, but for anyone who complains about the difficulty didin't put in the amount of effort it took to do well. Of course this class is difficult, but I absolutely loved Dr Mabbs and think he did an incredible job if you sought out his help. I felt so supported by him, and it was my favorite class here

Whether you aced chem 105 or struggled in it, GOOD LUCK in 106 with Mabbs. He is terrible at explaining things and the sample questions he goes over in the worked example videos are not nearly as difficult as the exam questions. To survive this class you really must do the most and that probably isn't even enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mabbs does not always explain concepts clearly during lecture and the lectures are usually rushed. Also, the exams are much harder than the recitation worksheets and the problem sets, so it is hard to be prepared for exam questions. For this class you definitely need to go to office hours, do PLTL, and consistently review your notes.

Exams felt significantly more difficult than the work done in class. I would go into exams feeling 100% certain and confident on the material, but the exams would catch me so off guard. Especially the final, it was just tragic. Would've been helpful having practice problems that were actually similar to exams and not an easy version of the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mabbs would speed through lectures just to get through more information. He would not spend enough time on difficult concepts and then expect us to know how to solve problems related to it.

He is unclear a lot of the times during lecture, and questions on the tests are not always directly aligned to what you learned in class (but I guess this is what the large curve is attributed to). Also disorganized and takes a long time proving equations rather than giving examples similar to what we will see on assignments later on.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The jump from Chem 105 to 106 was drastic and unexpected and with a different professor, it did not help. During lectures, he does a problem on the board and you will have no clue why or how he is doing it because he never gives you any equations. He also goes super fast through lecture and you can barely read his handwriting.
Great professor. The material could have been very difficult, but he made it clear and easy.

Awesome professor. Truly cares about what he is teaching, and if students understand. Nice guy. Difficult topic though. Grading procedures are rather opaque (everything is normalized, so an A on one test does not equal an A on another).

Quantum Chemistry is a difficult subject, but Professor Mabbs does a good job of explaining the material. If you have any problems on the homeworks or anything else in the course, go to his office and he'll steer you in the right direction. Exams are pretty difficult.

Mabbs was very incoherent in his teaching method--skipping from topic to topic without clearly connecting how its relevant for something else. He was confusing and made class harder with his light writing on the board. Not a very organized guy.
Difficult class, but all the material on the exams are in the lecture notes.

This was Professor Mabbs' second year at WU, and his first year teaching. Even though he was thrown right in to Gen Chem 1, the biggest class at WU, he did a great job of keeping everything clear and interesting, competing with Prof. Buhro's section. I recommend taking 111A with Mabbs if possible. If it's worth anything, he's got an amazing accent!

Roots to Ferguson is one of the most valuable classes. You will find yourself continually applying its concepts to other classes, and the lectures are truly engaging. Professor Rosenfeld teaches at a great pace, but make sure to stay on top of the readings and material, as things are stretched out.

Great class with important material that everyone should know about, especially given how isolated WashU is. He is well spoken and always shouts at the beginning of class but like in a nonchalant way. Class is a lot of work with readings and memorization for exams but its reasonable.

Amazing professor! I am not a sociology student, but grew up in STL and this class was absolutely amazing– Jake is a great lecturer and a very caring teacher, he clearly cares so much about what he teaches. I wish he taught more classes at WashU, so I could have taken another one with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing class! Very heavy on readings but lectures were engaging and went through all of the readings in detail. Very prevalent to today's world and content about hard topics (racism, segregation, inequality) was based in evidence and delivered very well.
best class at washu hands down. must take. incredible lectures, tests were fair as long as you went to class. TAKE THIS CLASS!
Very engaging lectures!

This class was hands down one of the best I have taken in my entire time at WashU. Professor Rosenfeld is smart, funny, clear, and communicative. If you graduate WashU without taking his course on the roots of Ferguson you are objectively missing out on one of the greatest opportunities this school has to offer you.

one of the best classes and broadened my understanding so much, definitely recommend just to take this class even if it is not required. Lectures are long but information is interesting, Exams are easy but requires you take good notes. Readings are especially long in the beginning but if the subject interests you, the read is not bad

ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS AND CLASSES EVER!!!! Roots of Ferguson quite literally changed my world view and life. His lectures are captivating and I found myself constantly surprised class was over even though he has a technology ban and doesn't use slides very often. The exams are difficult, but if you go to class, you'll do great!
So amazing one of the greatest minds of our generation. engaging lecturer and I learned so much. he backs up his information with facts

LOVED this course. The lectures were engaging and I learned so much valuable information. Although the readings were heavy, my interest in the class made it easier. I would recommend this class to absolutely everyone. Rosenfeld is approachable, knowledgeable, and humorous when appropriate during class. Take lots of notes during lecture.

I took roots of ferguson first sem freshman year and I loved the class. Rosenfeld (Jake) is very knowledgeable and engaging, TAKE GOOD LECTURE NOTES but he will always repeat something if you ask.  I think everyone considering roots of ferguson should take it I enjoyed the class and learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I learned the most maybe out of any class at WashU from this. This should be a mandatory class for the whole country, and we're lucky to have it here. Rosenfeld is hilarious and keeps it serious yet light. Rare and hard to do for this topic. Just get the gist of the readings and understand the concepts and you'll be fine for the tests!
Prof. Rosenfeld is the best lecturer I have ever had. He's incredibly engaging and really knowledgable. TAKE HIS CLASS

Getting Paid was my second class with Jake. This is the stuff he's an expert on and it was really interesting. Learned a lot and enjoyed the class. He doesn't use many slides, just lectures from notes which is kind of annoying, but he'll repeat things over and over so everyone can get it. Really nice guy and cares about students. Highly recommend.

It seemed like prof rosenfeld didn’t care about this class outside of class. When he finished lectures and students still had questions he would tell students to ask the TA and then walk out. He also never was present when exams were being handed back. LECTURES NOT RECORDED, and he doesn’t help when you need to fill in notes from lecture.

Roots of Ferguson is one of the most interesting classes I've ever taken. The material is so fascinating and you learn a lot. The only catch is that your grade is based off 3 exams, so be ready to study. He lectures for all of class time, so take active notes and show up to class. Overall, a great class and it really challenges your thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Rosenfeld is really great and I really enjoyed The Roots of Ferguson. I got a lot out of the class and Prof. Rosenfeld is really interesting and knows his stuff. My only complaint was that he doesn't lecture with anything visual, just talks for an hour and a half straight which makes notetaking a challenge.

Jake is my favorite prof at WashU so far. He is lecture heavy but somehow they aren't long or boring. I have learned SO much from him and he is so knowledgeable. If you have the chance take his class!! also hes not hard on the eyes...

This class was incredibly interesting due to the fact that Rosenfeld is an incredible lecturer. It is easy to stay engaged during class (which I advise you attend). Since the class is bigger now, he relies on 3 exams for grades and they are pretty tricky and somewhat difficult to study for but all in all would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He doesn't really do presentations so you need to take good notes.  He is really interested in what hes teaching and is very engaging.  However, he doesn't really give firm directions so its always a little scary to send things in.  Also yes he's not hard on the eyes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Rosenfeld is both dynamic and extremely knowledgeable.  Tricky prompt for essays and only one test, but the readings are very manageable.  Encouraged a positive classroom environment and easily clarifies controversial topics.  i think most people in the class really appreciated the class and respected him.  also he's super hot

The only grades given in my class were two papers and a final exam. He gave some opportunities for extra credit. He is a very dynamic and enthusiastic lecturer and he really cares about his subject matter. Very willing to help. I enjoyed this class and I would take another class with him.
One of the best lecturers I've had the pleasure of listening to. Incredibly enthusiastic and engaging.
It seems sweet at first, but it is super rude. Never take her Fashion Promotion and Exhibition class. She will overassign way to much work and be super passive agressive

She tends to seek a lot of compliments and recognition from fellow students and can be quite demanding in that regard. Additionally, her rubrics for assignments often lack clarity or specificity. She is known for being a strict grader, and students who go above and beyond to gain her favor tend to receive better grades.

Course content and grading was inconsistent with the syllabus. I found that even as an experienced hand knitter with a no knowledge of machine knitting, Prof. often focused on basic skills and swatches leaving little to no time for unrealistic final projects. She taught basic concepts wrong and asked advanced students to explain regularly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a really tough grader. Exams are very difficult, especially compared to the first half of transport, and he is not clear with grading standards. Additionally, classes are disorganized and hard to follow. However, he is very accesible to students. He will stay for hours after the office hour ends to make sure students get the help they need.

Took materials science (EECE 305) with him FL24, and now he's teaching the mass transfer portion of EECE 3510. He doesn't come to class prepared, his exams are extremely unfair, his notes don't make sense and are riddled with mistakes. He needs a significant amount of improvement to be considered a good lecturer....

Took EECE 305 Material science with him and he is very bad about having clear criteria for grading- I got marked 12% off for a true/false type question. All of his written response questions offer almost no partial credit even though he claims to give students as much partial credit as possible.

Outside of class, he is a pretty normal guy, but as a professor, he doesn't really know what's going on. Grading is inconsistent from paper to paper and from section to section. It's very hard to know what he wants until it's actually graded.
It is simply not possible to convince him that his answer key is incorrect. He will defend his incorrect answers indefinitely despite all evidence to the contrary.

The class was intended to be realistic to engineering, but was more realistic to research. He never answered a question directly, and marked me off multiple times for doing something he TOLD me I could do. Basically, completely random grading with no desire to help.

Most disorganized and confusing class I have ever taken. Didn't seem to prepare lecture materials before class, frequently said contradictory statements concerning the syllabus, and gave incoherent proofs and explanations. Extremely disappointed with the complete lack of structure in the class. Had to self learn the entire course.

Prof Rodsphon is super kind and friendly towards students especially when you need help understanding the material during office hours. Invested in making sure students were learning and understanding not just specific examples but the concepts overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kind professor although awfully disorganized in general. He changed our final grades last minute after having told us that he used the wrong curving system to grade and give us feedback on all of our previous assessments but most people didn't seem to have been affected much. Easy to get a good grade as he gives solutions in class.

Very nice guy. Lectures can be a little disorganized, but if you show up regularly you should be fine. Exams were not all that hard and he is a very generous grader. Overall, great class, would take again.

Rudy is great. He is so smart & passionate about math. He teaches in a way that spreads that passion to his students. He is patient, kind, and understanding. His main goal is to help students learn. But, he expects students to have a full understanding of the concepts, not just a memorization of procedures. He is very generous with grading tho

Professor Rodsphon is a great guy. Very interesting and lighthearted, but lectures seem to be erratic at times. Also doesn't do a lot of student problem-solving, so much of the work is self-studying. Was a little behind material wise but was a very knowledgeable guy.

Rudy is a fantastic person, but a lot of the lectures seemed haphazard and unprepared. I didn't really understand a lot of his explanations and had to look at khan academy, etc. to find out what was really going on (EXPECIALLY with surface integrals)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prepares us well for exams, gets to know students well and makes the learning environment very comfortable. For multivar, he is good with the diagrams and visualizations for the multiple integrals.
One of the best professors Ive ever had. Amazing at drawing figures, which is important for Calc 3. Over all a really good guy and a good teacher.

Ruth Clark is so amazing. I wish she could be my grandma. She's pretty cut and dry, but also super funny. She constantly cracks subtle jokes in lecture. She's super accessible outside of class, so go to office hours for help or for additional laughs. She has great video lectures and problem sets. Only four 50 question multiple choice exams.

Like everyone else we moved to recorded lectures a couple weeks ago and.... I think if I could put Dr. Clark on 2.0x speed in real life I might. Her normal voice is pretty great though. Funny prof. Lots of material, but her handouts + course objectives cover pretty much everything. 4 exams, 25% each of your total grade. No homework is nice.

Incompetent professor. After 20+ years you would assume that this professor would know how to teach this course but her lectures disproportionately focus on easy material and skim over the most challenging material. Reading the textbook and watching KA videos are necessary to piece together her badly disorganized notes. Stay away from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Probably the best teacher I've ever had. Lectures with interesting material presented well, with jokes interspersed to keep them fun, and definitely the most fair grading system I've taken. Can't recommend enough!

Good sense of humor, entertaining lecturer, but taking notes in class is stressful because she says a lot of information that she does not write down. You may have to rely heavily on the textbook like I did, but that should be enough for an A. The lectures are always confusing, but the exams are straightforward.
Interesting material. Straightforward exams. Well organized.

Prof. Ruland managed to make a fascinating topic both dull and uninformative. His explicit goal was to teach us "how to read," resulting in lectures that were rambling, condescending and vague. Grading was extremely subjective; don't assume an easy A based on the lack of real coursework. Most disappointing class I've taken at Wash U.

Ruland is a nice man, but this class is horrible. The worst class I've taken here. We were still talking about the movie we watched on the first day in our last class, not because we'd come full circle, but because we never went anywhere. Students are rarely given the opportunity to speak, and choose not to because he has a set answer already.

He is deceptively profound and often lectures students on meaning and confusion of life. But when you look at the course books he has assigned, they are complete trash and second-rate literature. Many students can be fooled by his quack wisdom though. His one journal a day method is refreshing but can quickly turn into one essay a day and a pain.

Took him 3 times. First time, I had trouble staying awake. Second time, I realized what a secretly funny and interesting man he is, even if a bit monotone. Third time, understood how useful and effective his daily journal method is. Learned more about life and literature from this wise old man than I could've imagined, just took listening closely.

the class is a total and complete pain.  at first the daily journal sounds easy but it's OBNOXIOUS because although he says only a few sentences is acceptable it turns into an essay a day.  the texts are interesting but the prof is NOT.  didn't learn a thing!!!

At first the class is really interesting but then you realize that he more or less rehashes the same ideas over and over again.  The daily journal can be a pain, especially on Saturdays, but it's really not so bad.  There isn't very much discussion in class, it's mainly him talking which is a pity. Overall he's not so bad though.

While Professor Ruland's class is fairly easy, it's really rather dull.  Sitting through class each day required a lot of caffiene to stay awake!  He tends to ramble about things of little interest and doesn't really encourage student engagement.  The assignment itself--writing at least a paragraph every day--was easy, but a bit tedious.

He's really an interesting man, and the way he formulates the class not only helps you read better, but write better. You will write a paragraph every day, even on weekends, but its not that bad. He taught me a lot, and hes one of the better profs here.

I loved Prof. Ruland. If you get used to the writing in your journal every day thing, the class becomes very enjoyable. He's a very nice guy, I don't know where the horror stories come from. Take a class of his if you can deal with no essays, no tests, just writing a paragraph or so every day (including weekends.)
Awful teacher--the class is nearly impossible to sit through, and i learned nothing.
Prof. Ruland is one of the best professors in WashU's English Department. I can't imagine taking American Modernism and Postmodernism from anyone else. He's an amazing storyteller too...

ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE! i can't stress it enough: both he and the class were a waste of time. he gave me a C- for no reason--i did every assignment, met with him out of class, didn't miss classes. didn't matter, apparently; he said sometime,s he gives bad grades to people b/c he "feels like it." i fought for my grade to be changed by the department.
No Comments
I really enjoyed this class.  Ruland is a kind man with some very different teaching methods that really worked well for me, though they do not work well for everyone.

he is the worst teacher i have ever had. he seems to pride himself on making people cry and being unclear. seriously, his class is HORRIBLE. everyone bonds over hating it. don't take it. i heard not to take any english prof whose last name begins with an r, and that sounds about right...

Not an enjoyable class.  I have him for intro to literary study, and we probabl spend about a third of our class time on things relating to English.  He basically just likes to hear himself talk.  Quite a bore.

Her english sucks and lectures consist of her reading off the slides she already posts online, so attending lecture is pointless. Regular typos on the exams. Helpful outside of class and on Piazza though, and you can find all the homework and quiz answers online The class isn't that bad but you'll have to teach yourself all the material.
No idea what is she talking about.

There were significant typos on exams and the final, not the little kind of typos where you know what they were going for, but serious enough that a large portion of the final was figuring out what it even meant.
She's basically reading the slides, but her English is so poor that nobody understands what she's talking about.

Ruth Miller is the definition of a horrible professor. She clearly doesn't care about the class or her students. Her illogical, incomprehensible teaching style is almost hilariously ironic for a class on logic. The TA's for this class are also horribly unknowledgeable and inaccessible.

Miller is one of the worst professors I've had. Her lectures aren't organized, she doesn't explain topics well and she's not very helpful in answering questions. For a logic class, everything she does is in the least logical, efficient way possible, like giving us a seating assignment 5 minutes before the exam. If this class is required, good luck.

Terrible lecture and grading. The quiz and exam questions are not clear and confusing. And those questions are not really discussed in the class at all. She asked TA to do everything. She's not nice and impatient. Never want to take her class again.

She's a boring lecturer but is great at explaining things one on one. Fortunately, you don't need to attend the lectures. Everything you need to learn will be in her ppt slides and taught to you through the assignments.
Absolutely no need to go to lectures, because you'll end up trying to teach yourself everything from the book and online sources. Smart professor, awful, awful lecturer
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Not a particularly interesting lecturer but a fine professor and 332 is a decent amount of work but not particularly hard and can all be found online. No need to attend lecture
Definitely not a good lecturer. Her class is extremely boring.
Extremely heavy work load and very unclear instruction. However, don't expect to learn much from your work. You'd be better off reading a book about database than taking her class.
You will regret it if you take her class.
She is really unclear and her lectures or slides are confusing.

The lecture slides are confusing to understand, and the lecture itself doesn't help either. The exams are not reasonable; things shown up on the exams are not explicit in the lecture slides. long homework. Bad news: you have to take it as a comp sci major.

Taking this class was miserable, for the reasons mentioned by others. But she recognizes that this is a difficult course, and she grades VERY generously on account. You will probably hate this class during the semester, but keep your head up, and you'll have a decent grade by the end. Still, don't take it if you don't have to. You won't enjoy it.

I LOVE Dr. Russell.  The class wasn't too difficult but there's a good amount of logic involved.  She's crystal clear with her explanations.  She promoted good discussion and is very knowledgeable in philosophy.  I don't see what the other people are talking about, I loved her.

Expectations for test are unreasonable.  Lectures incredibly boring.  Material is entirely new to most students, but Russell makes no effort to help those who are struggling.  About 1/5 of the class dropped out after midterm, which seemed to delight her.  Don't take this class.

this was gillian's first time teaching symbolic logic... i hope it's her last, too. at least, if she continues to use the same textbook, bostock's 'intermediate logic'. lectures are hard to follow, sending you to the text, which is flat-out impossible. problem sets from text were extremely difficult. tests also very challenging. avoid if possible.

This class is SO BORING. Russell prefers you to work out the material in small groups, and when you don't know what you're talking about this is kind of difficult to do. She's very into the material though, so if you have an interest in language go for it. Grading is by means of 5 papers.

Grades were based 60% on 6 hws which were about every other week, and the other 40% was a midterm and a final. The material is not that difficult, but can be very confusing, and Russel doesn't always do the best job explaining. If you have programming experience, this class will be a joke for you.

prof. russell's intro to logic was a good course. most homeworks were very straightforward, as was the midterm, but the final was dreadful. still, take intro to logic with her if possible. covers material slowly, making it easy to grasp material even if you only attend class every other time.
Jill is extremely cute.  She's also a great professor, VERY into philosophy.
Really poor professor. Boring material, insipidly presented, then expects you to write something incredibly insightful about topics you don't care about...very poor
Prof. Russell is really nice and a very good teacher.  The Phil. of Language class material is super boring though, so unless you like mental masturbation go for something else.
Really like her class.
Lectures are a bit boring, but paying attention pays off a lot.  She takes the material pretty slowly so it's easy to follow.  Do the homeworks legitimately and you should ace the course.

She's a good, engaging lecturer who puts a lot of effort into her presentations, and is very successful in explaining tough material.  She is very tough, though, and expects a lot of originality from her students. Don't take her upper-level classes if you're not serious.
Super chill professor. Always happy to help. He cares about whether or not you care about the class. The class taught me some great concepts but can be a little boring at times.

Easy class. Someone told me the only hard assignment in this class was the Instagram one, and it was optional/extra credit this semester so the class was pretty low workload. Introductory HTML/CSS/JS and a bit of React. You do have to go (attendance is taken), but large parts of the assignments are done in class so it is basically worth it.

Easy elective, no exams... do the assignments and labs and you will get an A. Professor Tihen mostly live codes for his lectures, so it is worth going since he gives you big chunks of the assignments in class.

He's a great lecturer and goes through a ton of content in a short time frame. You definitely walk away from this class having learned a lot about web development. He's always open to helping students after class, which is really kind of him.
good elective to take.

Some of the assignments can be a bit time consuming, but the content is overall pretty easy and there are a lot of resources available to help you. It is a really practical class and many of the internships I have applied to are looking for almost this exact skill set. Professor Tihen does a lot of live coding in class, which is nice.

The workload is a little high for a lower level elective, but the actual content is extremely useful if you are looking for summer internships. Prof. Tihen is friendly and fair, but the lectures occasionally moved too fast for me and I struggled to keep up during the live coding lectures.

Sam is a pretty good professor. He can get distracted during lecture a bit but overall, the content is pretty easy. The assignments are have clear criteria and are pretty simple (minus the Instagram one).

Professor Tihen was a great Professor and was always available outside of class. This was the first class I enjoyed taking at WashU because it challenges you while the difficulty remained relatively low. I would definitely recommend taking this class if you want to learn a lot of new things and engage in something creative.

A lot of work, but not super hard. Will help after class and over Piazza, but doesn't hold office hours. TAs hold office hours but can be hit or miss. Nice guy who clearly cares, but the lectures can be dry - mostly him coding parts of the assignments, so it is worth going just for that.

Lectures are a bit boring, but the labs in class are fun. Lots of live coding sections of the assignments. Very responsive on Piazza. Daily, extremely easy quizzes - but you have to be in class. Grading can be a bit harsh on some of the assignments. Nice in person and always willing to help.

Professor Tihen was the best professor I had at WashU. He was accessible outside of class and was always willing to help. The class isn't hard if you attend lecture and stay on top of your assignments. This was the first course at WashU that I enjoyed taking because I was able to combine computer science with fun aspects of creativity.

Professor Tihen is super helpful and really cares about his students and the course material. The assignments are practical and teach skills you can actually use, but they do take a lot of time and effort. He's very responsive on Piazza and gives great feedback to help you improve. Definitely a class where you'll learn a lot if you put in the work!

Dr. Johnson is a nice and caring professor. I never took piano in my life and joined right before add/drop deadline. This class is an easy A if you put just 10 minutes of practice each day on the piano. I practiced 20 min a day and everything was a breeze. I never thought I'd be able to learn an instrument or sight read at all but did well .

Dr. Johnson is such a nice and caring professor. I never thought I'd be able to learn piano. I had never played before and joined right before add/drop deadline ended. The class is an easy A if you show up to class and show effort and you put in like 10 min a practice a day. I practiced piano 20 minutes everyday and everything was easy and fun.

Dr. Johnson is one of the most amazing professors I have ever met. She provides students (at least me) with very personalized lectures and gives us detailed feedback. No matter what your level is in piano performance, she can always make your MUS 159 and 160 class worth the effort you put in. Highly recommended!!!
Uses large words when unnecessary. Jumps around a lot during lectures making it hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not even in this college, but look at the picture. He's just a puppy, ahhw, that's so sweet.

Not the most exciting lecturer, especially at 3pm. Good comments on papers. Tough grader on exams, which were made up of quote identification alone. I'd recommend this class for the subject material, although Ancient Philosophy (L30 347C) covers a lot of the same stuff, and Brown is an AMAZING lecturer.
He's a nice guy, knows a lot, but sometimes writes ambiguous essay questions.
Pretty tough for a first semester T&T class but he's a very nice guy and pretty funny once you get over the initial intimidation
Hardest Classics prof I've had here, and I'm a Classics major
Not too difficult.  Lots of info provided in lectures, so it's not a good class if you want to skip a lot.  Grading average to generous.
I was slightly obsessed with Ryan when I was a Freshman... probably because he was the only prof I had under 50. And now he's a dad. Awwww....
Has he told you yet that he's a Rhodes Scholar?  Not yet?  Oh, he will...everyday.
No Comments
No Comments
Kinda intimidating but very interesting.
Such a kind and awesome professor!

Dr. Scott is absolutely amazing! MKT 378 is one of my favorite classes I've taken at WashU. The lectures and topics are very relevant, and she presents them in a very easy-to-understand way. The homework assignments are very straightforward and really helpful. Exams aren't hard if you study. I learned a ton from this class and enjoyed it a lot.

Professor Scott was awesome! She answers questions really well and truly does want her students to understand the material and succeed in the class. Lectures were pretty interesting and had a lot of real-world application. There's not a ton of assignments and most of them are fairly straightforward.

Professor Scott is amazing! Lectures are super interactive and fun. Homework is not much, really helpful, and fairly easy. One group project and one final exam, but lots of resources to help you succeed on them. One of my favorite classes and profs at WashU!

I LOVE SCHMIDGEN! He is a great professor, very engaging with the students and even though I took him for Early Texts (which is required), he still made the material and discussions interesting and lively. He also is very knowledgeable about the Middle Ages/17th century and sprinkled in some history throughout, which was great.
LOVED this professor! He is really encouraging and amazing at explaining concepts. I had him for Early Texts and Contexts and he was great.

Great, fun class. Prof schmidgen is funny, nice, cares about his students. The class became tight knit because of how well he encouraged discussion and kept things light. Not too tough of a grader but gives great feedback

I took Literature and Justice (first year writing seminar) with Schmidgen and it was one of my favorite classes I've had at WashU. I improved so much as a writer. Writing is a difficult subject to teach because it is so abstract, but Dr. Schmidgen does a great job breaking large intimidating assignments into manageable chunks.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Writing, Lit and Justice. he's a very eloquent speaker that allowed for cool in-class debates. However, I released he is an EXCEPTIONALLY hard grader. I don't think there weremore than one or two A-grade papers the whole semester. It made me focus really hard on all my essays, which is really tough because I took this as a required class...
Lectures are so boring, he typed them out and read from his paper (and his slides are not helpful)

Dr. Schmidgen is the head of the Literature department  yet he is one of the most approachable and helpful professors I have ever had. He is happy to read over papers or talk about your ideas during his office hours, he is very respectful of differing opinions, and he structures his class to be a collective pursuit of truth rather than a lecture.

Professor Schmigden was a great teacher, I really enjoyed his class. He gives some really insightful analysis of the books and is really involved in the class, and very passionate. He is really nice at office hours and involved with students. The topics covered during discussion are very varied and interesting. Take his class!
He's pretty much the man :) I really enjoyed his class; it was fun, easy and laid back. I would highly recommend you take a course with him if you get the opportunity. PS he wears amazing pants.

I'm sure he is a brilliant guy, but he needs to work on the pedagogy a bit.  Really intimidating and most un-helpful in class.  The expectations for his assignments were not communicated well at all.  It was really too bad - I think it could have been a great class.
No Comments
He seems very stern at first, but he is extremely helpful and patient.  He gives lots of attention to your papers, too.  Definitely my favorite professor!

He can be kind of awkward outside of class, but maybe that's just because he's German. Very intelligent, very helpful and clear in class. And he's the only professor I've ever had to put an Ikea futon in his office for his students to sit on. Really good professor.

Its very rare a prof can be very bad at lectures , give horribly difficult exams and then not even curve so the entire class suffers because the absolute scores are so low. Yet somehow Linda schilling manages to attain all three. Truly insufferable , worst prof encountered at Washu. Avoid her like the plague plz.

Professor Schilling's lectures are extremely useful. The material is challenging, but she explains it clearly, stays organized, and works through problems step-by-step in class. I don't really find her rude; often students don't engage, and when she asks questions, many stay quiet on their screens. She's an excellent professor if you pay attention.

Professor Schilling teaches at a rigorous and detailed level and is always willing to explain examples thoroughly if students ask questions. While she may seem strict, this rigor benefits learning. Complaining about memorizing formulas in a derivatives course—especially for those pursuing quant roles—is unreasonable.
In this class, really recommend to study the material meticulously and come to the lecture even though they are optional
Heavy class, get ready to be tested. But generous grader.
A lot of overreactions here. Tough class, fair final exam.

Professor Schilling is the worst teacher I've had. Idk how she's still teaching here, but her lectures are vague and high level without any explanation. Simply copy and pasted from a textbook. She doesn't respond or is vague and passive aggressive to students answering questions. She also violates her own syllabus policies. It is very hard to learn

Schilling is a difficult teacher. Her lectures are not of the highest quality, and she provides little information regarding exams. That being said, many of the ratings below are overblown; she is merely a bad teacher, not a nightmare.

Professor Schilling is the WORST professor I have ever had. She is inaccessible during crucial exam periods, shows no effort and treats students as an INCONVENIENCE, and is RUDE in response to student questions. Her lectures are incredibly disorganized and she is very unclear about what is and is not relevant to exams.
Absolute worst professor OAT. Super pissy and hates her students. Don't know how she's lecturing here at the amazing institution of WashU
Probably the worst professor I've had at WashU

Often doesn't respond to student emails with questions. Went through lecture slides in a scattered manner across several class periods one week before the final to vaguely go over what we did and didn't need to know for the exam, but laughed and refused to post a condensed list of topics or answer questions related to topics covered on the exam.

Worst professor you can see at Olin. Absolutely no response when sending her emails. TAs are not hosting any OHs. No cheatsheet on the final, but ask us to remember all the formulas. Seems to have no patience for anyone and clearly does not know what she is teaching about (all slides are copied and pasted from the textbook).
Very unreasonable expectations

She suddenly banned cheatsheets before the final despite the syllabus allowing them all semester. Her classes are hard to follow and the slides are overly dense. Prof Cai taught the first half of the course and did a wayyy better job.
It is reasonable for her to have this rating. While prof Cai Jian deserves a better rating.
Terrible. Does grading and enforce policies against the syllabus. Lectures are extremely confusing. Spent three whole lectures just pondering which parts will not be on the exam. Avoid if possible.
Confusing lectures, unclear expectations / syllabus, did not learn anything

I have no idea what this class is talking about once midterm ended and she came. No crib sheet on final and AGAINST SYLLABUS???????? I love professor Jian's part of this class but once this professor take over everything turns disastrous. WORST PROFESSOR

Professor Schilling is knowledgeable, but her lectures are unclear and her slides are overly dense. She required us to memorize about 75 slides of formulas with no exam cheatsheet, which felt like a PhD-level course than an undergrad class. She doesn't teach at a level that most of the class can understand. I would not recommend this professor.
Worst professor I have had in 4 years at WashU, basically need to be a math PhD to somewhat understand this class.
dumps more work on you than a flipped porta-potty
Worst professor within the business school. Content is hard and strict grading on completion-based assignments. Lectures are all very confusing.
No curve at all, and your grade of 75% depends on the finals
Tough final,vague lecture,strongly not recommended.
Tough final,vague lecture,strongly not recommend.

The Mid-term consists of 11 multiple choice with a time limit of 80 mins. However, the final has 4 multiple choice and 10 essay questions in only 90 minutes. The course covers stochastic, derivatives, and finally Black-Scholes. Take this course if you like to challenge yourself.
Extremely hard final exam. 90 minutes for 10 short answers and 4 multiple questions. Avoid this prof's class.

Lectures are recorded and Sellers does a good job at explaining course content. Sellers also provides lots of real-world examples which helps to better understand concepts. Grading was very generous and the professor is a cool guy!

Dr. Sellers made Fatigue & Fracture Mechanics one of the easiest courses in my college career. Homework was reviewed in class before the deadline, participation in canvas discussions was mandatory, and the only exam was a take home. It is so much easier to get excited about the material when you don't have to stress about your grade.
the best professor in the WashU I have had class with. he was born to be thermodynamic teacher.

It seems like the teacher wants you to learn and cares about his class, however, it does not come across well. When you ask a question, expect an answer designed to make you feel stupid. Don't expect any accommodations. Work equal to 3 credits for only 1 credit.

Not as brutal as other people describe. He is a pretty decent lecturer, and the TA's are moderately helpful during office hours. Homework is weekly and is very good prep for the exams, but make sure you actually think through the problems and not rush to the solutions. Participation is a grade boost. Just com in with an eager, optimistic attitude.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Sellers' high expectations and seemingly emotionless spirit make him a controversial professor in the Engineering department. But he knows his stuff really well and does his best to synthesize the material in class, so don't skip. Very hard homework questions, but they will somewhat prepare you for the very hard tests. Do not slack off.

Sellers' high expectations and seemingly emotionless attitude make him a controversial professor in the Engineering department. But he knows his stuff really well and does his best to synthesize the material in class, so don't skip. Very hard homework questions, but they will somewhat prepare you for the very hard tests. Do not slack off.

One of the greatest professors I have met. Go and study hard he will appreciate you a lot. Passionate about teaching. I have to say those who said those harsh words must have not paid enough attention to the materials

He is definitely a tough grader. Actually, an unreasonable one. He'd take points off for not stating something that wasn't explicitly asked in the questions. He does not have a clear, consistent, or organized grading criteria. It is entirely up to his discretions. Strongly not recommended.

Dr. Sellers is not just going to hand you a grade.  It is obvious he takes pride in teaching and if you are taking his class be prepared to work as hard as he does.  He has little patience for students who are not putting forth effort.  But, if you put in the effort you will leave this course with a deep understanding of the material.
Not approachable, will not give partial credit on any exams, and homework is just stupidly long.

most arrogant professor i've ever had. he thinks he's so smart and will often go on random tangents proving how smart he is, and often times makes whoever asked the question feel stupid. not a great professor, avoid at all costs

Easily the worst, meanest professor I've had at this school. Goes about his lecture with broad, unclear mathematical expressions that don't pertain much to coursework he assigns. He laughs at students who don't understand. He finds pleasure in loading on homework and seeing students struggle with exams. Avoid this guy if possible.

Some students went to every class and enjoyed his class. In my opinion, in class he tries so hard to get class participation, which is admirable. But he goes about it in a way which made me feel like he was trying to teach kindergardeners. I can't say much more because after the first 4 classes I only went to few more.

She is an interesting professor, but a hard grader who never specifies what she wants and almost seems to want students to get B's instead of A's. Exams are example heavy. She makes you take pop quizzes every class so they're just quizzes. And she takes notes on who participates every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She had the best class structure I have ever seen. Everything is clearly organized in the modules and very easy to follow. The exams are a little tough, got a D on the first one but still ended the class with an A. She emphasizes group projects a lot and is very knowledgeable. One of the best professors I have had.

Selin is nice and cares a lot about marketing, but her grading criteria was set up to where you get full points or nothing. Tests questions are also difficult so getting an A is a challenge with her (Consumer Behavior 4101 - Ohio State University)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor overall. Tries to make even the most abstract research concepts interesting, and leads lectures very well. Makes it very clear what she expects on exams and cases. Grading procedures are very demanding, but the curve makes  it bearable.

Seely is AMAZING! Taught me more about poetry in a semester than I could've hoped to learn in years! Great feedback! Patient! Totally unpretentious & personable! He's just what an academic should be: immensely knowledgeable, willing to share that knowledge, wants you to succeed & loves connecting with people. Take his class! Best decision ever!
Shane is a phenomenal prof- and absolutely brilliant.  He has an encyclopedic memory and offers everything he knows to his students.
Shane Seely is a straight boss. No questions asked.  That is all.

Best teacher at WashU, hands down. Was not looking forward to exposition (gotta love clusters) but Seely made it my favorite class. Engaging, entertaining, interesting, funny, and very smart. Fair grader, too. Definitely take exposition with him. A writing class that you actually look forward to!
The best professor I ever had in college.

Seely is amazing! His class is completely discussion based and just... fantastic. This has honestly been the best English class I've ever taken. He's got a great sense of humor and gives the class this vibrant personality that brings out the best in all of us :)
Great teacher. Wonderful sense of humor and facilitates comfortable discussion very well. Is a fair grader and will give credit for a good rewrite of a paper. Very helpful and easy to talk to.
Seely is awesome! He seemed really into the subject and encouraged input from the rest of the class. He's also a fair grader too
Awesome class...some of the most involved and engaged discussions I've ever been in. He's really passionate about the material and naturally concerned about the students. Seely is the man!
One of the best English teachers I have ever had--just an awesome guy.  If you have the chance, take his class.  He won't let you down.
Professor Seely is AWESOME.  My favorite teacher I've had at Wash U yet.  He has a great sense of humor, too.
No Comments
Very intelligent guy - always wants to help you out. Very abstract for a composition class.
loved him.  very intelligent.  not an easy grader, but a fair one.  one of the few classes that i've felt like i've actually learned from.  favorite professor i've had.
No Comments
This man is AWESOME.  Plain and simple.  He grades fairly and makes class very interesting.

He is an amazing teacher. His grading is not always easy but he makes the material interesting and keeps his students interested in the subject. He created an amazing class atmosphere filled with lively discussions.

Graebner is a difficult professor to get used to in many ways, his lectures are compelling if you're engaged with the readings. His feedback is not very helpful, but he grades pretty generously. Generally, good prof and helpful outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fr322. Near impossible to make up attendance if you had to miss. Grading was harsh, only gave out 2-4 As to the class all semester. His comments also contradicted each other sometimes. Also would warn us that we have an essay coming up but would only post the prompt the class before it was due.

Lectures about things that are in no way related to the readings. Gives unclear feedback on essays and seems to think that only his way of writing is correct. There's a reason that his classes have low registration numbers... stay away if possible.

I transferred into Graebner's French 307D section from Elizabeth Allen's a few weeks into the semester because his only had 3 students in it. The difference was stark. He is incredibly organized (which is important for me), engaged, and actually has a good French accent. He is not an easy grader, but will reliably give 95's if you put in effort.
Graebner is AWFUL!! His teaching is terrible and his grading is entirely subjective. He lectures on and on about things that are irrelevant. Waste of my time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I had the great opportunity of taking Islam, Immigrants, and the Future of European Culture" with Professor Graebner before graduating in 2007. The course was extremely well taught, and I took away understandings of contemporary European culture and ethnic politics that I still draw on today in work and personal life.

It takes a while to get into his teaching style, but he is very genuine and really cares about his students. His lectures are usually very insightful and interesting. He is a hard grader, but going into office hours and listening to his advice helps a lot.

Islam, Immigrants and the future of European culture: horrible teacher, the books and a movie were awful - lots of cursing, drinking and sex- did not represent Islam at all. Confusing and boring teacher and a hard grader. He does talk a lot about himself and how well educated he is. I would not recommend this class
Unapproachable and rude. He never stays on topic and would rather talk about himself than the books he assigns for class.
A pure egghead academic who has a very clear area of interest (North African Francophone literature), Professor Graebner is probably most helpful to the students who are similarly inclined.

Very smart guy, completely incomprehensible.  Loves to hear himself talk...harvard-educated, very impressed with himself, makes the class uninteresting and bland.   Often rants about his previous life experiences in academia, not interesting at all, cannot relate to him in an intro level IAS course.   DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE!

Great teacher. Takes a little while to get into his style, but give him a chance and he becomes very comprehensible when you do. Especially good if you go in to talk during office hours. Do the reading ahead of time and the lectures become quite interesting and insightful.
Very smart but lacks social skills. Probably a good researcher but not a good teacher.

Generally a good professor but this class is not as easy as it seems at first. At the end of the semester he springs unreasonable assignments. He expects a lot but you can learn good writing skills from him if you can ignore your ego for a little while. Not a particularly personable prof. but his heart is in the right place.

Incredible class. He's incredibly knowledgeable about all sorts of topics, and brings this knowledge into the course. He has a daily lesson plan, which made our discussions relevant and much more comprehensive than discussions I have had in similar classes. And he is VERY accessible.  He sidetracks sometimes, but it's interesting. Grading is fair.
worst prof at wash u

I really liked him and the class. He was kind of off-putting at first- uses lots of big words. But if you're willing to put aside your pride and *gasp* learn, he's excellent. I look forward to taking more classes with him
he's a tough grader,but he's fair... i liked him
the worst professor i have ever had in my entire life

Very smart man, but class gets extremely monotonous.  Very picky grader--with papers you have to meet with him if you want any chance of coming out with a decent grade. Make sure you are very interested in the class material.
No Comments

he knows the material, but seems a little picky about grading.  that is, he seems to grade more on whether he likes your style of writing in comparison to his. would re-write your sentences/paragraphs just because.

This guy is absolutely horrible! Confusing and conceited he rambles on about things that don't make sense and never gives clear definite answers on anything. He's a very picky and hard grader and boring to boot. And yes, he does wear a cape.  His class will make you want to kill yourself!
No Comments

Absolutely EVIL!!!! Reminiscient of harry potter's professor snape, right down to the cape. Don't take his class unless you enjoy confusion, boredom, and things that have absolutely no relevance or make any sense.  Not a shred of humanity, seriously.

You dont learn anything in class, so theres no point going to class. Its time for chatting about theatre stuff. You dont learn any technical things. You have to participate in a production and work on a group project, and both of them are highly time consuming and annoying. Have to spend ur weekends stuck in the backstage doing nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He would get very ill-tempered, where he yelled at students and graded unfairly, unnecessarily harsh.

The class is unorganized and the lectures are boring. There is a group project and you have to work a production which can take up to two weekends. It's quite annoying. Would not recommend unless you really need an A. It's not that its hard to get it just a lot of annoying things you have to do. Not worth it. Plus he thinks he's funny and he's not.

One of the nicest teachers I've had. Lets you out of class early lots of days and is excited to see what you're working on. Generally a really understanding guy who wants everyone to do well if the just put forth some effort. DEFINITELY recommend him!

This will probably be my most favorite class in my college career. Intro to Theater Production was wonderful. Awesome professor who loves what he does. Learned a lot. Pretty easygoing and a ton of fun. Never dreaded going to class and he made sure we knew our stuff. The actual work in the theater took lots of time but the experience was memorable.

Had him for Intro to Theat. Production. HIGHLY RECCOMMEND - favorite class of the semester. Less than a lecture than a bunch of friends talking - and noone knew each other when it started. It helps that he loves the subject. He's understanding and easygoing and tries to make sure everyone understands things. A great guy and a great teacher.

This is not the easiest intro class you will take but Professor Trent definitely makes it easy to understand. The projects will be hard to do if your group procrastinates and you may or may not end up doing most of the work so be prepared to spend time on that. The weekly HWs were challenging without PST but also very doable by yourself.
This class was traumatic.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The way he presents the material during lecture sounds like its easy and then I go to do the homework and I do not understand. Join PST or just take the sophomore make up class that no one tells you about. This class was very hard but very rewarding, and if you put in the effort, you will do well. Trent gives good feedback during office hours!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This has been one of the hardest classes for me this semester but Professor Silbaugh's passion for what he is teaching has made up for it. He genuinely cares and wants to help his students. I wish there were more opportunities for grades other than homework and midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: easiest class I have taken so far. Amazing professor. makes tough topics easy to follow. 10/10 would recommend.

Professor Silbaugh cares about what he teaches and is passionate about the subject. He's kind and honestly, a very fair grader. The course itself covers a lot of different topics and equations, which can feel overwhelming at times. Lectures can get a bit boring occasionally.

Trent is great he cares about his students and does his best to answer any questions that they have. However, the class itself is boring and the material is odd because it is only equations. Also, the homework is very difficult if you don't go to PST. They purposefully make it so you have to get external help and can't do it on your own.

Dr. Silbaugh is a great professor. Although the material is very difficult, he does a good job of teaching the basic concepts and the applications of them. The homework is very heavy, but his office hours and PST are really helpful if you're stuck on a question. His office hours for projects were really helpful, and he's overall a very nice guy.

Prof Silbaugh was a great professor. He knows that this class is extremely difficult and made sure to be very accessible and understanding, especially in office hours. Lectures sometimes feel rushed, but he makes sure to clear up any questions outside of class. Homework is very hard, but exams will raise your grade with partial credit&cheat sheet.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor silbaugh did a great job teaching this course. He was accessible in office hours and gave generous partial credit on exams, emphasizing understanding. Homework was graded pretty strictly, and would be pretty much impossible to complete without joining a weekend PST. Exams were fair, though challenging, but you can have a cheat sheet.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a solid lecturer. Despite attendance not being required, missing a class is kind of detrimental if you don't have someone to take notes and send them your way. Homework is hard, near impossible to do without PST, but fine if you are in it. Tests are infrequent and you have a cheat sheet. Interesting class (fave of sem.) and...he's lowkey hot

Professor Silbaugh is amazing--his lectures are very easy to follow and he does a great job explaining hard to understand concepts. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. The class is hard but was still my favorite of the semester.

Really nice guy and a pretty good lecturer too. Sometimes explanations were breezed over too much (esp. with the mathy stuff like mass transfer, "chained" heat transfer analogous to resistors in series, etc.), but via office hours and PST I was able to sort out problems. Really wants to help you!

He is the man of the department. I've had 5 classes with him already and will have the 6th class next semester. He truly cares about students' well-being and knows a lot about ChemE. He also give pretty good grades if you truly pay effort on the homework and assignment. He makes Reactions interesting and Unit Ops less stressful.

This was a very easy class, and the professor was amazing. She was very relatable, and in my opinion, the work was fun. She is also very understanding and lenient with deadlines if you have a valid excuse. You're guaranteed to do well if you attend every class on time, participate, and put effort into your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Great person. Follows the CWP rules. The only downside is that the large majority of the work you do is not completion-based (like some other CWP classes).Frequent work/readings, but manageable. Willing to work with you. Frustrated with the discrepancy between professors and their grading styles across the college writing classes.

Professor Siciliano is a great professor, and she really cares about her students. The timing was a bit unfortunate for the course (8:00 AM), but I ended up learning a lot and it was an overall great experience. She grades very fairly, and is good at giving clear feedback. 

Would recommend if her course! Just try to get in a later time slot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: he's awesome holding office hours fixes all problems for students

Grading system unclear, hired bad TA and did nothing with the complaints, boring class. Bro gave a final on 12/16 while I graduated on 12/14. 
AVOID BY ANY CHANCE, WORST CLASS OF MY LIFE
avoid at all cost
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've had in my 4 years. boring lectures, writes all over his own slides yet refuses to post these annotations after class. Constantly contradicts his previous word, adding quizzes or moving assignment deadlines. His teaching style does not promote learning. Unless you have a solid understanding of R already, stay away.

Not a good class for people who do not have a reasonable coding or statistics background (run now). If you need to use R in the future, this class is worth it. Chib is an expert in his field but not the best lecturer.

His lectures are terribly poor for introductory R. The class was running weeks behind schedule because he stopped class for every little software hiccup that students had. Not receptive to feedback about how the class was being run.
extremely boring. can't understand his lecture. drop this class before it is too late
You can at least get an B+ if you just turn in the assignments. He has a great research background and expertise in Bayesian. He is the coolest Indian professor i've ever met. He mad chill.
Amazing expert, terrible professor. Run away before it's too late
Extremely boring. He needs to engage the class more, and be less monotonous, most people are falling a sleep. I would not recommend him.
Amazing researcher obviously one of the tops in his field. Unfortunately he has lost his ability to teach. Poor guy
His graduate courses are amazing! Go Bayes!
No Comments
Extremely knowledgeable. Very interested in his work. Cares about the students. Easy grading.
Boring!!!
Really caring professor and easy class.

Shah Ji is incredibly welcoming! She blends comfort with learning and gives a reason to keep showing up. She's flexible, understanding, and amazing at teaching, in and out of class. She truly makes learning feel possible.

Shah Ji is the best professor I've had at WashU. She is so respectful and caring to each and every one of her students. As a non-Urdu speaker, she made me feel welcomed and created a safe learning environment. I would highly recommend anyone to take the course. She encourages everyone to do well in the course and you can def get an A in the class.

Professor Toqeer Shah is an outstanding educator who is incredibly supportive, approachable, and passionate about teaching. Her classes are engaging and thoughtfully structured, and she genuinely cares about student growth. She creates a welcoming environment that makes learning both effective and enjoyable.

Professor Shah Ji is my favorite professor at WashU. If you're thinking about signing up for any of her classes, there is no need to think further. Sign up. She redefines what it means to be a professor and cares for her students deeply.

Great class with an awesome professor! Grading was very clear and lenient. Professor Shah is so caring and is always willing to help. Class was always really fun and discussion based. Definitely learned a lot!
Awesome professor!!! love her class.

Shah Ji is by far the kindest, sweetest, and best professor I have had during my time here at WashU. I've taken Urdu I, II, and now III with her and can look back and say it was definitely my best academic decision I have made here. The class is filled with discussion and builds a beautiful environment of learning and cooperation. Highly recommend!

She really cares about the success of her students and is willing to be flexible with our different schedules to ensure that. She's empathetic and provides a space where we can all be ourselves even in our class assignments. She always makes sure that everyone is on the same page and no one is falling behind

Toqeer Shah is the type of professor that truly cares about her students and their success. Whether it's making time to work with students individually outside of class or designing activities that truly immerse students in the urdu language and associated culture, Professor Shah goes above and beyond, and is the reason I have achieved urdu fluency

Made me fall in love with reading/writing/speaking and learning Urdu! This will be third (and final level) Urdu class with her, and I wouldn't want to learn Urdu poetry from anyone else. Other than being a great professor, she's so loving and caring and passionate about what she teaches. Truly a model professor.

Dr. Shady is a great professor and really cares about her students. I took intro to migration with her, and she was amazing at lecturing and keeping the class engaged. She has a great teaching style, and you will learn a lot from this class. The tests aren't too difficult either. She is extremely knowledgeable and welcoming. I recommend this class.
Shady is a queen she's so nice and i love talking to her about politics and she makes me feel safe
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shady is fantastic. I took migration policy with her and she was great at facilitating discussions about tough topics. She is clearly very smart and does her best to bring everyone up to her level of expertise. Great class, great professor.

Dr. Shady is hands down the nicest and best political science professor I have encountered at WashU. Very knowledgeable about material with interesting lectures. Really encourages in class participation and discussion. Quizzes and exams are very easy and pulled straight from lectures. The one essay is very manageable because of how it is divided

Dr. Shady is an amazing professor, her lectures are really discussion based so I enjoyed that. She's very sweet and kind. The tests are easy to pass if you pay attention and participate in class. I recommend creating a study group and using flashcards to study. The first test was on the readings so be sure to read the first unit for sure.

I really enjoyed Professor Shady's course! Her lectures are very insightful and engaging, and it's obvious that she's very knowledgeable. She encourages participation and asks for personal experiences, which creates a comfortable and inclusive environment.Tests can be specific, but as long as you follow the slide decks you should do well.

Expects great things from you and it makes you a better student. Very knowledgeable of the topic shes teaching and understanding. Emailed me multiple times when I missed class, not in a "get here kinda way" but in a "what's going on?" kind of way. Grading and how to succeed in the class was clear. Big paper for her class, offered lots of feedback.

I found the lectures to be very enjoyable. A lot of them were discussion based but participation is not graded and she never put pressure on anyone to talk or cold called (even when the room was silent) which I appreciate. Super approachable in office hours and overall good classroom environment.

Dr. Shady did a great job teaching this new Writing Intensive course (Politics & Identity). Multiple checkpoints for the main paper of the semester helped groups stay on pace, although her feedback was sometimes contradictory for later reviews of the same content. Knowing terminology from the lectures is needed for the exams.

Her class was much harder than I expected for a 200 level class. I bombed the midterm exam (got a C) but then was forced to clutch up on the final to get an A-. Her exams are pulled straight from the slides, so just study them, which I learned a little late. There's a 10 page paper you have to write over the semester, so keep that in mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures and content are really interesting, and she has you start working on your final papers at the beginning of the semester so you don't scramble at the end, great feedback on drafts too. Tests could be extremely detailed and difficult to do well on. I studied for days for the final and still didn't feel super confident. Study early for tests!
He's a great professor who cares about students. The late coupons system works well for the homework assignments and he is very upfront with expectations for the course.

Prof. Shidal is a great professor who genuinely wants his students to succeed. Pre-recorded lectures can be a little easy to fall asleep to, but studios during class time clear up a lot of the confusion. Shidal offers pretty decent explanations to questions and is responsive on Piazza. Lab assignments are doable (get a good group for labs 4 & 5).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor with nice calm lectures. He talks pretty slowly so I would suggest watching videos on like 2x speed, but overall he is good at conveying material. Class has plenty of extra credit and you generally can ensure you get a 95+ on any lab. Exam was a bit difficult but overall I think the class was fair as it was balanced by labs.
Great professor that cares about the students.

Prof. Shidal is very knowledgeable and helpful 1-on-1. Recreation and online lectures are very boring and at times difficult to follow; felt like I was supposed to know more than I did. Labs were not too bad, but the exam was REALLY difficult, and tried to trick you on every question. My biggest advice: DO THE OPTIONAL READING and EC from day one!

Overall good professor. I think sometimes he needs to bring more enthusiasm to class. I also think he is a much stronger professor in 332S but I think hes been teaching that for longer. I generally do not recommend Computer Security so if not that class, take this professor!

Class takes up a normal/reasonable amount of time. Lecture videos, recitation, and the studios definitely help. Exam might be rough if you slack off, but it's only 17% of the grade, and there's extra credit offered on every lab. Professor Shidal is accessible outside of class and he's always willing to explain a concept further.
exam of hard

I really enjoyed this class! I think the grading is very fair and you can always submit regrade requests if anything looks weird. He genuinely cares for his students and is easily accessible outside class. The assignments can be workload heavy, even more if you have a bad group for last two labs and studios.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Challenging but good class, Jon cares about his students and will help any understanding in class. He knew my name pretty quickly, and he and his TAs all were very available and helpful. Midterm is hard, but only 17% of final grade. This class is not as hard as people say, even for someone with no real world CS experience.

Super nice, one of the only comsci profs I've had with actual helpful lectures. Very present in class and always happy to answer questions. Class was challenging but very doable and he is super available to help. Exam is tough.

shidal is rlly nice but the grading was so inconsistent bc its done all by TAs which can be annoying. if u go to shidal he will be helpful which is good tho. all the lectures r async on canvas which can be tricky if u r a procrastinator. the midterm was hard but if u stay on top of watching the videos and asking questions during studio its fine

Prof. Shidal is a great professor. His explanations are very clear if only a little drawn out. If you go to his office hours with a bug in your code he will likely find it in less than a minute and explain why you have the issue.

RMP doesn't give me the option to select CSE433 with Shidal (so putting this review under 422). But this is the second class I've taken with Shidal and he's just as caring, accessible, helpful, smart, precise, and illuminating as always. He remains my favorite prof in WashU's CS department.

Shidal is an amazing teacher. He is always available to talk to students and teaches the course really well. I left this course learning a lot and would love to be able to have him is my professor again. I recommend anyone to take a course with him if you can.

Lectures are certainly boring but mainly serve to reinforce the material presented in module recordings; they can be safely ignored during studio if you have a good understanding of the content before class. Studios themselves are super helpful and give great hands-on experience for C++ principles
A flipped class style with in-class studios. You mainly learn C++, which is not a super interesting topic. He is quite boring with the lecture, but a nice guy overall. Exam is hard but curved.

Shidal is a pretty good professor. My only complaint is that it's hard to understand his lectures in the beginning (not super good at dumbing things down) but once you understand how to code in c++, it's so much easier. Do the assignments early cause they can take some time to complete. He's really attentive to students and helps as much as he can

Best CS professor I've had so far at WashU. Genuinely cares for students. Class not super difficult, especially if you've already used C++. Assignment instructions are super clear, just need to follow those. Sometimes graders are a bit tough, but not excessively so. Can do studios asynchronously, which is nice.

The course is very straightforward and doable except for the one test which is disproportionately hard relative to the rest of the class, but it isn't that bad if you just focus on memorizing C++ syntax & understand pointers (you get a cheat sheet)

Jon is one of the best professors in the CS department. His lectures/explanations are clear, precise, and illuminating. He really understands how to make potentially daunting concepts incredibly digestible. Beyond that, he is caring, super nice, and approachable. I found 332 incredibly organized and an exceptionally valuable class.
Just a phenomenal professor and person.
Great professor. Great vibes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His CSE332 course is awesome. It's elective but I highly recommend this course.
i love jon he rules.

Shidal is knowledgeable and a good lecturer. Each class is a required studio, and sometimes a free day to catch up on studio or hw. The assignments can be large, but he will frequently accodomate for any difficulties the students may face. He is decently active on piazza. The 1 exam is the only flaw which does not suit the class. He curves it a lil

Shidal is a great professor, he is so passionate about the material and wants you to learn. The class is cool and you get to work on a variety of projects. It is very code heavy, so be ready to do a lot of coding, and it is not an easy A, he makes you work for it, but he is a great prof and loves to see you engaged, so make sure to make an effort.

Know his stuff, and seems alright as a guy. However, he is rarely around to help you and doesn't try to seem open. Lectures are informative, but the one test is easily the worst part of this class and you do not get prepared for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: After taking this class, I also TA'd for him multiple semesters. I appreciate Prof Shidal not just as a lecturer but as a mentor. If you get the chance I recommend not only the class but coming back to TA, he's a great supervisor and really values feedback both from students and TAs.
Professor Shidal is very caring in the studio and will explain everything in the easiest way to let you understand.

Professor Shidal is very accessible outside of his office hours and was willing to meet with me just about anytime I emailed him.
