He gives really thorough explanations and actually cares about you as a student. He pretty much gave everyone extensions as long as you asked in a reasonable amount of time.

Professor Shidal was a great! The recorded lectures were long but helpful. Definitely go to office hours! He walks through problems until you understand them. He was also understanding about extensions as long as you ask early. The labs get progressively harder, but not too bad! I would definitely take a class with Professor Shidal again!

Shidal's great! The class has its rough moments, but that's more my fault than his. There are online lectures, but I didn't watch them and did fine. I love going to his OH and he always answers my questions. He's willing to give an extension for labs as long as you ask in advance. Almost everyone fails the midterm but it doesn't count for much.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shidal is fantastic. He obviously cares about his students but if you do not do the work you will not do well in the class. The midterm was definitely difficult but is not worth much of the grade and he curves it pretty nicely. The recorded lectures are long and a little boring but if you watch them on 2x speed they really aren't bad.

I hate seeing Shidal slander. Obvious some of you haven't seen the rest of the WashU faculty, because Dr. Shidal is a gem. He's incredibly knowledgeable of the topics he teaches and he puts in the work before and after class to make sure everyone understands the material. Hard class but I never once felt like I wasn't given the knowledge to succeed
not great at explaining concepts, and the professor basically talks in loops. don't take his class if you want to learn

He's a nice prof. He cares about students and quickly responds to students' questions via both email and piazza. Tbh the lectures are quite boring, but the overall class structure itself is quite fair and clear (No doubt about it!). He is there to help u if u need help. The guidance and instructions are super clear. Recommend this class.
Not a good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Shidal is a caring and good professor. Although, his lectures can sometimes be boring as there is no interaction. He just talks for 45 mins or so. Studios and Labs are fairly manageable. There is only one exam, during the middle of the semester, and worth 19% or your grade. This exam is pretty tough tbh. Stay updated and study weekly
Professor Shidal was awesome this past semester. I was able to grow, not only as a student, but as a human being. I would recommend this guy again!

Very helpful during/after lecture. Willing to explain things in laymans terms if need be, but also knows how to articulate ideas using niche vocab. Helpful coding examples provided in lecture slides. Lab instructions are hard to read; would recommend reformatting them before starting labs (if you have time).
Very chill professor. Willing to help and pretty laid back. Very reasonable as well. Would recommend.

Shareshian is super kind and truly listens to student's opinions. He gives us study guide about exactly what is going to be on the exams. Exams are more about understanding than difficult calculations. He is teaching the matrix content  with the most straightforward examples possible. Even if it's 300-level math, get a good grade is not hard.

Very easy going professor, genuinely wish you could get an A for the class. He is super enthusiastic about matrix and math content in general and really listens to student's opinions. Gives us study guide on exactly what is going to be on the exam. The content might be a little abstract (this is a 300-level math class after all) but exams are easy.

This was literally the easiest class I have taken at WashU. 85% of the grade was based on exams that sometimes included high school level math and were always significantly easier than whatever the other sections were being tested on. This is the definition of a class you take if you dont need to learn the content but want an easy A.

Leaps and bounds the best professor I've had at WashU! Exams are worth 85% of your grade, but NEVER did I ever feel like he was trying to trick me––simply seeing if we had understood the material. His office hours are INCREDIBLE! I would come with so many questions and always leave incredibly relieved. His passion for the material is infectious.

The nicest professor ever. If you have to take matrix, take it with him. He genuinely wants students to understand the material and never tries to trick you, he's clear about what he expects. Go to office hours!
Shareshian is super nice. He really cares about how people do in the class and asked for feedback throughout the semester. Really helpful in office hours. Would recommend.
Very accessible during office hours and over email, always around to help!
He is awesome and willing to help. Great lectures and problem sets that help you prepare for the tests.

Super accessible outside class, very willing to help you learn what you need to learn. Do not be afraid to contact him about stuff outside class it will significantly improve how you feel over math material
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His grading system was skill based so it only allowed for you increase your grade. He was very caring when it came to making sure the class as a whole understood the math. I'm not a super big math person but this professor made it the best way possible. I think he did his best to make the class simple.

Shareshian is awesome. I had him for 131E and he was so willing to help all of us. He was always making himself available outside of class, emailing additional office hours time. He also is so passionate about teaching math, and you can really feel him light up when he is helping troubleshoot. 

Overall, great!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you have any doubts about your calc or pre-calc ability, take 131e with Shareshian. GOATed professor. Explains concepts very well, always willing to help students, genuinely cares that you do well in the class and goes out of his way to make sure things are clear with any questions you might have. Also a super nice guy.
He is awesome.

Prof. Shareshian made me personally feel like I could do math and do it well. For someone who is looking for an easy NSM credit, take Math 131E. Shareshian is easy to understand and very available to help you succeed.
One of the kindest teachers I've ever had. He really cares about his students and will do all he can to help you succeed! Definitely take a class with him if you get a chance

He teaches Linear Algebra again after 15 years. He teaches hard material in the lectures and sometimes confusing because there is not a lot of notes to support his analysis, but his tests are very easy. However, I did not set up a mindset in Linear Algebra unfortunately from his class.
Dr. Shareshian's class makes me believe I can do math and think math is something fun!

He's such a nice prof. He cares about students and tries to help out students if they struggle to understand a concept. His explanation is very clear. If you have a hard time understanding some parts, go to his office hours. He is there to help you. Also, overall class structure & grading system was super fair. 1000% recommend.

Professor Shareshian was an engaging and clear lecturer. Calc 3 can be tough, but he made it understandable and interesting. Would highly recommend going to his office hours- he's very friendly and helpful.

He's awesome! I have him for Math 310W and while it's a harder class, his lectures are really thorough and he makes it easy to understand. He's super accessible outside of class and will help walk you through homework sets you're having difficulty with. Super friendly and easy to talk to.
Gives funny and easy to follow lectures, and has reasonable expectations in the exams. Easily the best math professor at WashU.
Professor Shareshian is amazing. His lectures are interesting, and tests are easy. He answers emails quickly. No complaints.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you are going to take calc 3, take it with Shareshian. he's brilliant, a genuinely cool guy, a little quirky, and great math lecturer. also he looks like an intelligent mark ruffalo
Great professor. Take his class if your lucky enough to have the chance.
Dr Shareshian is an amazing, kind, and intelligent man. Although his tests tended to be easy, he taught thoroughly and whole-heartedly.

Yeah, lectures were probably taught at a level a bit more sophisticated than the test required, but he was amazing! He is a great lecturer with a great sense of humor and always made expectations for exams clear. I highly recommend!

John Shareshian is a great human being, good teacher, also a PING PONG GOD. IMO lectures were at a much higher level than the actual tests, don't know if this is standard at WashU or just him. Lectures are effectively optional, however it is a pleasure to watch him teach. As someone else said, 100% could be Einstein reincarnate, absolute genius.

Shareshian is an extremely caring, nice, and smart man. He gives off the typical sweet, dorky, middle aged man vibes. I personally didn't go to many lectures since you could just study off the textbook and get an A+, but the lectures I went to he was always sweet and answered my questions. The tips he gives about the tests are also accurate too.

Professor Shareshian did a great job explaining the fundamentals of calculus using simple languages. His lectures were inspiring and well prepared. He always did a few examples after introducing new concepts, which really helped learning. He gave clear explanations of what was going to be on the exams. He was also a nice man with humor.

Professor Shareshian's math 310 class might be my favorite class I've taken at WashU. This was my introduction to mathematical proofs and I actively looked forward to his class at the end of the day. He is very straightforward about what you can expect on the exams.
Shareshian is an Awesome guy. I've never met a more honest and respectful man.
Prof Shareshian is a great person who gives interesting lectures. He is just really funny in class.

This man is the smartest human I have ever crossed paths with. I am shocked that he agreed to teach the easiest math course at WashU. If someone were to say he was the second coming of Einstein, I wouldn't even question it. He explains everything so well, and has a bomb New York accent. TAKE HIS CLASS!!

If you have already taken CalcI, this class is a breeze. That being said, if you haven't taken it, the material is harder to understand the way it is presented. You definitely have to put in the work, but Shareshian truly wants you to do well. The exams are extremely fair, testing only basic knowledge through straightforward questions (no tricks!).

Dr. Shareshian cares about students very much, and puts forth a lot of effort into making sure people understand the material taught. I like that he focused his class on making sure people conceptually understood the course, but there are few example used. The book is a big help.

He hasn't taught calc 1 for like ten years, so it had been a while and it was kind of obvious. His lectures weren't always clear, especially if you hadn't taken calc before. There's 3 exams and a final, webwork, and section worksheets that make up your grade. His tests are really easy, which is nice but he also wasn't like the best professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: SO GOOD. Take 310 with him! His lectures are interesting, and he understands that not everyone is a math genius at WashU and actually starts from the basics and works up. He makes proofs fun and doable, and is also very helpful at his office hours. Exams aren't bad, and if you can do the HW you can  definitely do well on the exams.
A fantastic professor. He truly cares about the students and offers flexible office hours. He would much rather a student understand the concepts than to blatantly memorize.
Fantastic professor.  Extremely fair, demonstrates clear concern for students.  Teaches very well, explaining complex material at an accessible level.  Extremely helpful office hours.
Professor Shareshian maintained a great classroom environment, and was particularly attentive to being fair on exams. He explained the material well and was great to listen to.
An awesome professor who is really passionate about math. Makes you want to go to class even if you aren't a math person. Very intelligent, but really wants you to learn the material too.

Awesome professor! You can tell he cares about his students and takes time to make sure everyone understands what he's doing. If you get him you're very lucky and should take advantage and GO TO CLASS!
Great teacher.  Very down-to-earth and easy to understand.  Very approachable and made class interesting and easy to pay attention to.
He is one of the best math professors I have had!  When you listen to him talk, you can tell that he loves the material he's teaching.  He works very hard to make sure we understand the lessons
Absolutely great professor. Thorough and funny, he teaches you more than solving problems. So lucky I got him.
Very thorough. Very helpful. You would be very lucky to get him for sure.
I have taken him for three classes including intro to higher mathematics, 310, linear algebra, 429, and most recently combinatorics, 370.
Amazing professor who went out of his way to ensure to the students understood the material and that the grading procedures were fair. So good I chose him as my major adviser!

I would take anything w/Prof Shareshian. Lectures were fantastic, and he was over-the-top in trying to be fair when it came to exams. He's tough, but it is 310 - from what I hear, though, I can't imagine taking this course with anyone else. Definitely most worthwhile office hours I've ever been to as well, and he's welcoming about it as well.
He is a professional lecturer. Every point made are crystal clear and interesting. Very helpful (yet very hard) homework. Fair grading scheme and reasonable exams. Great class!

This man is gorgeous. Even though the class is not fun in the least, it's worth it to go to watch his teach. I'm fairly certain 310 isn't fun with any prof though, and he seems to be one of the better ones from what I hear.
SUPERNOVA

Just show up to class with a question and you'll get an A. I did other homework in the class, watched youtube, or movies as well. Just read slides right before and prepare a random question and it's easy.

Easy A professor. I did not understand anything during the lecture but still got a good grade. Only thing you have to do in class is prepare a question based on the slides and do only two TAKE HOME problem sets for entire semester. He literally said you can use your favorite AI to do the problems. It is 50% participation.
Easy class but you have to go to lectures if you want any credit, it's 50% participation.

Professor Smith is my favorite professor I had at WashU. He has been teaching for 50+ years and is incredibly knowledgeable. He is very involved in helping students succeed. There is minimal homework and reading but attendance and participation matter. I have recommended taking a class with Prof Smith to every single person. He is the best!
Please take him for an easy A, and he genuinely knows what he is talking about!!! Very passionate and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Learned a ton in a field I thought I knew about. Great guy who keeps the class simple with his explanations. All you have to do is review the lecture and ask one question about the material during class, and prepare for exams. Informative if you want to go into the major. There's a reason why his classes have massive waitlists, the secret is out
Easy class and chill professor

One of my all-time favorite professors at WashU. Very knowledgeable about his field and able to dissect any question you have about the content. All you have to do is come with questions and willing to discuss to succeed. Also the sweetest guy possible, will be the first to ask about your day outta class and how you are doing. Truly a gem.

This was the easiest class. All you have to do is come to class with a prepared question based on the slides, and he just answers it. That's basically the whole class. take for GPA boost, and ignore other rates because they are really old

I took Introduction To Global Climate Change In the 21st Century with Smith and it was, hands down, the worst class I have ever taken at WashU. Completely incoherent, expectations weren't clear, we were tested on stuff we weren't taught, HE'S A CLIMATE SKEPTIC! He said Arctic ice melt was good bc warm water is more biodiverse. Avoid at all costs.

Professor Smith is very friendly and willing to patiently answer questions. The material is interesting, although it is easy to get lost. However, as all of the taught materials are available to view outside of class, it is not difficult to do well in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class isn't interesting (unless you're passionate about ocean tides) but take it for the easy NSM A. Doesn't take attendance, uploads powerpoints/recorded lecture on blackboard, all exams/assignments are take-home and submitted via email. I stopped going to class after week 1 and was easily able to figure out the take-homes on my own.

This professor is absolutely wonderful if you like the text material, but awful if you don't have any interests in the class. He is very talky and would answer your questions very patiently. He gives classes by presenting powerpoints. He is great for the course GCC.
nice but talk really fast. knows a lot but lectures are a little boring. no textbook and attendance is optional. i got a grade a LOT higher than it should have been, which I definitely don't mind.

Great guy, but boring professor. Attendance is literally optional and you could still get an A. Extra credit for going to class though which is a plus. Take it if you need a gut, but not if you want to learn about GCC.

I took this class to fulfill a requirement because I heard it was easy. Friendly guy, content is not very stimulating, tests are harder than you would think, but in the end I got a grade that was much higher than the amount of effort I put in (and probably higher than the actual mathematical grade I had.)

Very nice guy but terrible professor.  Attending class is not mandatory but he gives extra credit quizzes.  Lectures are very unorganized and extremely boring--entire class fell asleep.  Asks very stupid questions on tests--multiple choice and T/F.  Sometimes leaves entire lectures off of his tests.  Like I said, he's nice but a bad teacher.

This class is easy as long as you study for the tests. All of the lectures and power points are online, so you don't have to go to class, although there are some extra credit pop quizzes. The lectures are usually boring, so I would not recommend going to class if you are going to fall asleep.
His tests are not as easy as I thought. But, he's a good professor.

Oceanography was as a whole a good class.  By the end it turned into more of an environmental issues class, but that's not a bad thing.  If you read the slides, you did well on the tests.  DON'T BUY THE TEXTBOOK!  It's expensive, and optional, as we found out on the second week.
If you want an "A," take this class. All you have to do is study the slides and read the book before tests and you'll be fine. Nice guy but lectures weren't pretty boring.
Great class, really underrated. Only had about 10 kids in it, but it is an easy A, and you learn a lot. Very interesting subject matter

I don't understand these ratings.  He's the nicest teacher I've ever had.  He gave our whole class A's.  Our tests were oral group exams and the final was watching "The Day AFter Tomorrow."  How much better can it get?  I learned some stuff too!

When I took this class, it was an automatic A if you showed up for everything. Didn't excuse the fact that his lectures went off on tangents, half the class fell asleep on a regular basis, and his TA seemed to know more than he did. Don't pay for the book, you won't open it.
probably the easiest class in all of college.. especially the final

Lectures were hard to follow and the tangents he went off on didnt help with the organization of the class.  However, he does show really cool videos and overall is a really really nice guy.  If you take this class with him, make sure you go to class, dont worry about doing the reading, but show up
I don't really think I learned anything...and having class at 8:30am on Monday didn't help.

On a whole, not as bad as made out to be.  It's hard to stay awake sometimes, but that could just be due to the time of the class (mid-afternoon).  The class is great if you've ever wondered exactly how the weather worked.
totally sucks.  goes off on irrelevant tangents, and is very disorganized.  tests do not accurately gauge knowledge of material.  class is a waste of time.
By far the easiest class, its an automatic A as long as you go to class and only miss one quiz.  But its ssoooo boring and you don't get to ocean's until the very end.
Nice, very funny, likable guy. Interesting and easy going class.
Best Prof. at Wash U by far.  Interesting class that is applicable to everyday life.
Nice guy and Great prof. Not too dificult. Makes classes more interesting by joking alot.
funny, sarcastic, interesting. awesome guy, i would/am taking everything he teaches
Great class.  Class time flies by and is very entertaining.
No Comments
No Comments
Great Professor, really interesting class. Very helpful outside of class, wants you to get the most out of it. Great class.
No Comments
Great professor, he really makes the class interesting and fun...makes you want to go to class.
Cunningly witty, mordantly funny remarks, makes the subject applicable and interesting.

Very interesting class.  Possibly the most applicable business class I've ever taken. While he can be sarcastic (he warned us at the beginning of the semester that he might make someone cry haha), he is so loveable and interesting you can't help but like him.

Very passionate teacher. I loved how she made jokes and also would sometimes bring treats corresponding to her lectures. The class definitely required time but if you work through the homework and can spend time studying terms prior to the class it is not difficult to succeed.
She is clearly very interested in what she had to say. She's well prepared and qualified. She has lots of jokes, explains the content well, and often brings food. You'll enjoy the class.

Prof. Jen would be one of the most amazing professors you would met throughout uni. There are plenty of extra credit opportunities and she's very friendly and interesting. Don't hesitate to take her courses.

she's an angel. presentations can be a little unfocused, but she explains content really well. a lot of info to learn for each exam, but offers so many resources/support hrs & adjusts curve/allows for corrections. slides provided & lectures recorded. interesting enough to pay attention, she's incredibly passionate. will frequently bring baked goods
Exciting lectures, and we can see she's really passionate about her field and teaching.

She cares about all her students even in a large lecture. She is super well versed in her subject area and is easily approachable with whatever questions you have. She also will bring baked goods to class so bonus there. Take her if you have any interest in our planet at all.

Knows what she is talking about. Her tests were not that difficult, as her portion of the class was not that complicated. Really enjoyed how excited she was to be there and she was so funny. Also, she bakes treats for lecture multiple times during the semester.

Best professor I have had at WashU. Made class fun and interesting. Homeworks were used to apply lecture concepts to the real-world, and tests were drawn from study guides. Always baked fun EEPS-themed treats that were related to lectures. Lectures incorporated current events and real-world topics, while still being applicable. I learned a lot.

Loved Dr. Smith! She was very knowledgable, funny, and always excited for lectures. Helpful and highly accessible outside of class. Baked cute, EEPS-themed treats for the entire class. The class/exams are challenging and content-heavy (not an easy A!) but the professors are truly excellent. Great intro to EEPS.

I went to office hours for Prof Smith's class almost every week just to do the homework assignment, and was always met with help. I took this class just as an NSM, as I don't have much interest in science at all. It was a good experience, although it is unnecessarily difficult for an intro level class.

Jen herself is great, but the class is horrible. You will have to fight for your life to get a good grade in this class. Maybe it's just the TAs grading super harshly, but damn, they turned a class for my major into something a dreaded. Jen is cute though. Milf hours. But damn what a super hard class. Avoid it if you calue GPA, or your time.

Took this class as many other engineers have, to fulfil the upper level science requirement. For a topic that I have zero interest in, Phil and Jen are pretty entertaining, but that's about where it ends. They said that this course isn't a memorization course... It definitely is. Make sure you take good notes because the slides are  very brief.

Funny and kind person. Frequently baked science-themed treats for the 100+ person class. The lectures were boring because of the subject matter. It's difficult to do well on the exams, merely due to how much material is covered -- even if you study. Office hours aren't helpful, she speaks in parables rather than answering simple questions.

I love this professor and class so much! I am so glad I took it and I learned so much about the earth. She is very enthusiastic about the material and makes the lectures less boring than they could be. Definitely recommend.

Jen is an amazing person and teacher. She tries her best to make jokes and keep the lectures entertaining. However, the class is extremely boring and you have to do alot of work for it, its 14 billion years of rock history. If you aren't interested in rocks DON'T take this class, it is not intro level. As a freshman it was not the move.

I love Jen with my whole heart. She is so funny during her lectures and cares about her students understanding the material, as is demonstrated by her out of class availability. She always bakes treats for the 100 person class on test days and is overall just an angel

Jen is so kind! She really loves her job and is genuinely excited to teach. She's a great person to get to know, she is always learning more about her field and loves engaging with students. Love love love Dr. Smith!

Prof Jen Smith is truly an amazing professor. She is on the docket to teach the updated version of Earth and the Environment renamed to EPSC202 Intro to Earth and Planetary again for the next few years. She is extremely knowledgeable and speaks about her personal experiences, brings in food, teaches creatively, and really cares for her students!
she is so enthusiastic about teaching and always uses food for demos. very passionate teacher.
She has the whole package for teaching- passionate for the subject, cares for the students, challenges them, tries to make the class interesting, etc.

Prof. Smith is probably the best professor I have had at WashU in terms of level of knowledge, excitement and personality.  She is willing to go above and beyond most professors for her students.  Paleoenvironmental Recon. was a great class, definitely recommended!
Dr Smith is fantastic. Literally changed my major to environmental studies after a week of her class.

surface processes.  not a hard class, test material from lecture, with textbook use only for clarification.  two tests, no papers.  a few optional fieldtrips!  as always, a fun, interesting professor!
an amazing teacher!   very good lecturer, excited about subject.  my favorite teacher at WashU.  classes are enjoyable and interesting.  not much work other than studying for tests.
Great, interesting class.  Actually interested me enough to change my major to EPSC.  A good amount of work, but if you like earth science, you're all set.
Great teacher, easy to understand, cool, highly recommend you take this class
No Comments
Clear, precise, animated, organized lecturer. She assigns readings, but almost all of the material comes from lecture. Down with the kids. Field trips were pretty entertaining. And she's hot.
Great professor!  I really enjoyed class and learned a lot.

makes earth science fascinating and relevant to all. nice use of a variety of disciplines in lectures (esp. archaeology), motivating, not overly didactic or hung up on small details. labs were a **** though because of lack of aid and bad TA
RAR, baby, RAR!  One hot tamale, great lectures, knows her geolizzle shiznit!
Super nice guy, there's no homework so your grade mostly relies on exams, quizzes and group projects. Exams are kind of hard, but there's a nice curve.

Don't be fooled by the couple good ratings. Im guessing the only reason he's been given good ratings is because he seems like a chill guy. Almost entire grade is determined by exams, which are terribly hard for an intro class. If you have 40+ years of acct experience you may just be able to pass the class with a C. Good luck getting email response.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very nice person, but not a great professor. Very boring lectures, which covered material rather poorly. Tests were very hard (averaged around 20-50%) and cover things never done in class. Extra difficulty associated with this approach considering there is no homework, so if you don't study past exams, you would be completely lost.

Soczek is funny and easy-going, but as a professor, there are things I wish he did differently. He responds slowly to emails (or not at all) and grades slow too (generous grader tho). Lectures are entirely off of text-heavy word documents instead of ppts, which makes it hard to follow along at times. Exams are a lot harder than practice exams.

Professor Soczek is a very nice person, lenient grader, and does a lot of fun extra credit opportunities. With that being said, Professor Soczek lectures entirely off of a Word document that is very hard to understand. I wish Professor Soczek would go over actual application examples or explain concepts in an easier way. Exams are pretty tough.

Mark really frustrated me when in his class.  His homework was extremely more difficult than his in-class examples.  

He also presents notes off of a word document, which is so hard to follow.

I have been working on his homework for 4 hours, and I'm not much further along than when I started.

I like Professor Soczek as a person, but I think there is room for improvement in lecturing. His notes for classes are very much text heavy and he does not really do examples in depth in class (he says how to do it instead of showing how to do it). He is a great man with a great sense of humor. Be prepared to self-study (as needed).

Soczek is a great professor! While lectures may not have been the most interesting (I think more attributed to the course material itself), Soczek was enthusiastic and always provided examples, whether problems or real-world cases. Not a lot of work (if at all), and a lot of extra credit. A few tough exams and a slow grader, but good professor!
Terrific professor! Extremely helpful and entertaining in class. Grades too slowly, though.

Soczek is extremely helpful when questions are asked and doesn't belittle students at all. He's an overall great guy and is willing to help students excel in their work. Be sure to ask lots of clarifying questions and have him explain methods in doing problems because it does get confusing on tests.

The lectures can get dull because of the nature of the topic but he's a funny guy and a very nice guy. He is very helpful and tries hard to answer questions. He explains things very well and he does fun activities in classes such as March Madness brackets with prizes.

I felt that the tests were unduly hard. Class lectures are all theory and the test is all application. DO THE HOMEWORK PROBLEMS and go to him for help. He's a nice guy who will definitely help you, but YOU have to go to HIM. Definitely a slow grader, but a fair grader. He tries to make the class easy for you, even though the tests are pretty hard

Class is incredibly boring and the material is not very clear.  Soczek is not very organized, often putting up practice quizzes/exams very late, and you will not have a good idea of where you should be in the book or what problems you should be working.

I really liked Soczek as a professor. He grew on me. Very nice and flexible guy who def. cared for the overall success of his students. Also learned a ton in the class. Tests were fairly difficult but Soczek prepares you well for them. Slow but generous grader. Also believes in learning for learning's sake, which is nice.

Soczek is a very knowledgable teacher.  His grasp and understanding of the material is amazing.  The man is a walking GAAP encyclopedia.  In all honesty, he is a great teacher who will do anything for his students in or out of the classroom.  He is demanding and covers a lot but he wants to prepare you for the outside world.

He's a really nice guy and a good professor. I'm not good at accounting and I actually knew very little about business when I started the class, but I learned a lot regardless of being one of the lower students in the class (I had trouble staying awake - not necessarily because of him).
Soczek is a nice guy, and a good teacher, if you can just stay awake...  (I couldn't)
This guy is a terrific professor, and he really enjoys teaching too so that helps. If you do the back-tests that he offers before exams then you are sure to do well with him.
Boring stuff. I don't like this teacher.
Soczek is awesome.  He's probably the best professor I've had in college.  His office tells all!!!
The best accounting professer at Olin.  Classes are difficult, but well explained.  Always has time available.  Little slow to return grades, but great in every other respect.
Great Professor, really nice and willing to help.
This class is impossibly hard, but he is really helpful about it.  He gives 3-5 years of back tests and is a lenient grader.
Class material okay. Soczek is annoying.
Great professor, great friend.  Games in class to cut through the work.  Give lots of back tests for studying.  Very helpful.
Very nice guy. Helps out if you go talk to him. Class a little boring though.
He is a really nice guy who will always go out of his way to help students
Lectures are reasonable, if a little fast. Luckily, there are lots of resources outside of class too. I usually still had questions.

Excellent lecturer and enthusiastic about the content. The subject material was challenging, but Prof. Song taught it in a way that was understandable with a bit of practice. The pace and workload were manageable for a class of this difficulty.

Poor scheduling and organization. When questioning the professor, they either reword your question or say, "it's like that because it is." The professor would make at least 3 mistakes a lecture; sometimes huge ones. You learn by doing, and learning differential equations in this class was like navigating a busy street with a peephole of light.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a great lecturer who taught very clear and concise. The problem with him was his grading system. 40% FINALL??? He makes all the midterms extremely easy-worth 6.66% each. Then drops the hardest test I have seen at WashU which also happens to be 40% of my grade. But again, he is a great lecturer just please fix your grading system Dr. Song.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good at explaining things, but lectures are very fast-paced and oftentimes it could be a struggle to copy things down from the board since no notes or lecture recordings are posted. Subsections are optional but great for getting more practice. The Canvas page could use a little more organization instead of having everything on a single page.

Yanli Song is a great professor who genuinely cares about his students and confirms the content makes sense to everybody. His lectures are clear and prepare students very well for the exams. All of his outfits are great, and it was extremely wholesome when he came back after his child was born during the semester and he was very excited to tell us.
I liked all the times when he wrote on the board and when he wore slippers to class!

Best math professor I've had at WashU. Explains things extremely clearly and very accessible in office hours. Homework is graded on a combination of completion and accuracy, so it's very manageable. Tests are also pretty similar to homework questions and lecture examples, so they are not too difficult. Highly recommend to to anyone!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great at explaining things. You need to go to class, but that's okay, because class is really interesting!

Song is a pretty decent professor. He teaches concepts fairly well in class but can be a bit unclear if you ask him a clarifying question. The class is only graded on homework and exams; there's very little homework, and the tests are short and not too difficult. He doesn't post any lecture notes though, so it's up to you to make class

Prof. Song really cares about making sure that every student in the lecture understands the content he goes over. 310 can get to be an abstract, confusing class at points but he always welcomed questions and answered them thoroughly, even if it took more time than he was expecting. There's really clear expectations and he wants everyone to do well.
He goes through concepts pretty thoroughly which helped me really understand the progression of the course. Do not hesitate to ask questions!

The class is difficult if you are not great at math like me. Professor Song is sweet and pretty funny. The tests are fair, and he is overall a good teacher. He is a good choice if you can learn from examples, but maybe watch videos on the topic before (or after) so you can process his examples better.

Pros: - Very straightforward/methodical - Teaches well and explains well - Very knowledgeable - Often relates back to old material Cons: - Accent (not too bad tho) - Sometimes hard to read writing (sit in front) - Lots of homework but it keeps you on track - Only way to get material is from lecture no online help - Exams are a bittricky
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Spriggs was an overall nice professor. However, his grading criteria for the essay worth 20% of the grade was not well-explained. Also, I'm not sure what he based participation grade on, because I participated in almost every class and showed up to office hours and got a participation grade below the class average.

Grades off 2 exams and a group essay he never read/gave everyone in the class the same grade within 2 % points. No rubrics. Asked group to grade each other on participation and didn't take that into account at all. A/A- cutoff is 93.6. Doesn't release slides so take in-class notes verbatim from slides. STAY AWAY AT ALL COSTS IT'S NOT WORTH IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He digresses alot in his lectures and expects you to remember readings to cite them on exams. And for the group essay he makes you add on to his own research which I found a little odd. I wish I saw the reviews he had before I took the class because I would have avoided all the work. It's a good preparation for grad school, other than that, not fun

Exams are pretty difficult and almost entirely based on memorization of the slides shared in class. It's an interesting subject, but Spriggs can be a boring lecturer and struggles to keep the class engaged. Grading is tough and there is no curve so only a handful of students receive As.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Spriggs rambles in his lectures, has uninformative slides, and grades you off of very few things (usually 2 exams and 1 group essay.) For our class, he did not do the essay and made one of the exams worth 65%. The exams are also extremely difficult and nobody got an A on the first exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Spriggs is very knowledgeable in the area of judicial politics and the Supreme Court. However, his lectures are very hard to follow and often turn into tangents, with little to no slides with information on them. The class is based on a group project and 2 exams. The 2 exams were extremely difficult for a lot of people.

Would not recommend course unless you are VERY interested in the topic - Supreme Court (Justices more so than cases). Rambles in lectures, hard to pay attention to, disorganized/unused Canvas, course grade is determined only by midterm, final, and group paper - grading criteria is unclear. Class grade distribution was:
A+ 1
A 7
A- 17
B+ 12
B 2
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of reading, tough grader, you will learn a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Spriggs is an interesting lecturer, but not a great teacher. He isn't accessible and can be obnoxious. With that said, the class wasn't too tough. The exams were pretty reasonable as long as you study the cases beforehand. Not a big fan of Spriggs, but still an interesting class.

I thought he was a pretty pretentious lecturer. Having said that, if you went to the lectures, and wrote down notes for all the court cases & just memorize them word for word (obviously know how to apply them), the tests were easy. He says he wants students to answer his questions, but he mostly answers them on his own

Great class, one of my absolute favorites.  Really interesting material and he doesn't really care if you keep up (as long as you are prepared come test day).  The paper seems overwhelming at first but go meet with him or the TA and you'll be fine.

He is a fun and smart professor, but his TA was a tough grader. Also, the curves were pretty brutal. I would recommend taking a class, such as this one PASS/FAIL. I don't know a single person who received an A with him, and this class will likely drag down your GPA.
VERY Smart professor. Extremely well structured class, no surprises. Expectations are perfectly outlined. Test is straightforward. GREAT CLASS

An excellent, well structured class.  Prof Spriggs was always willing to answer my questions in class and office hours, and was very flexible when I had to reschedule the midterm. Lots of cases and material to read for the paper but there was only one and he gave plenty of time to do it If yo're at all interested in the Supreme Court take it
Very interesting class. Definitely need to do the readings in advance. Tries to promote in-class discussions -- doesn't always work. I defintiely recommend this class to polisci majors.
Took this class way back in Fall 2024. Lecture heavy and honestly some tricky exam questions but lectures are amazing and so engaging. Highly recommend!

The best of the three Intro Psych professors by far. Great lectures, content covered in class is all that will be on the test - pretty fair questions imo. Only downside is that he doesn't post videos/slides till the night before the test, so you need to either go to lecture or get notes from a friend.

Dr. Sommers is a good lecturer, but his exam cover concepts not covered in class or the textbook. He won't provide slides, lecture videos, notes, practice exams, or other resources to aid learning. This makes succeeding in the class hard, as you're left to study mostly on your own.
His lecture is really amazing and interesting. But I guess it is important to read the textbooks. Some concepts in the exam can be mentioned in the book but not in the lecture.
Engaging, knowledgeable, enthusiastic, funny. The one thing I wish he did differently was give us review questions for the exam like the other two psych professors did.

My favorite of all of the psych professors - fascinating content and very engaging lectures. I admit to having an advantage with the midterm and exam: I did not have to study much due to my strong background in neuroscience. Overall, he was the only psych professor where I attended every lecture - for the cool neuro content and the man himself.
Exams doesnt cover what is taught.

If you are wanting a funny guy you'd like to be friends with, take a class with Dr. Sommers. If you value your education and GPA, your test grades will thank you for taking classes elsewhere. Class is extraordinarily easy, but the exams are exceptionally difficult and cover course material never discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sommers seems to be a nice guy who is good at lecturing until you take his exam, which has concepts not covered in class or the textbook. The irony of this class is that psychology encompasses fundamental principles of learning, yet Sommers WONT give you slides, lecture videos, notes, practice exams, or virtually anything to help you learn.

His lectures were indeed engaging and fun, the problem is they don't even cover half of the material tested. Operant conditioning was tested although it was supposed to be covered the week after the exam. He promised the class before the exam that it would be based on lectures. Well that was a positive punishment for me for believing him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best of the 3 intro psych professors by a long shot.

Best of the three intro psych professors. Super engaging lectures that keep you entertained and learning. 2 online quizzes during his time teaching, heavily based on the lectures so as long as you go to class you'll be fine.
I loved intro Psych with Sommers. He was so funny and very clearly outlined his expectations.  Sommers is very reasonable and clearly knows what he is doing.
Super engaging lectures. Very awesome respectable guy. Always leaves room for questions during lectures. Easy quizzes.
love him so much. Great passion for the subject

Professor Sommers is one of my favorite professors last semester. He not only explain the concepts very well, but also gives interesting anecdotes (which made the class easy to get through). Quizzes are fairly easy.

I loved Prof. Sommers, I wish he taught the whole semester instead of just the first third. Some people thought he was mean but he's just from Brooklyn and has a dry sense of humor. His slides are very bare bones so you do have to actually listen to take notes.

Sommers was my fav prof out of the three that taught. Actually enjoyed going to his lectures, he obviously knew what he was talking about and talked at a speed that allowed me to take good notes. Since they didn't release the recorded lectures until 48 before each quiz, I went to every lecture but I'm sure you don't have to. Light workload too!

Sommers is truly great at lectures, making them compelling and funny. He sounds like he knows what he's talking about, and his lectures match up well with quiz questions. He also will occasionally go on tangents that are time-wasting and entertaining. Overall, he seems like a great dude professor.

Professor Sommers for Intro to Psych was amazing, and I would highly recommend taking him when he is available for the Fall Semester again. His lectures were very straight to the point, and the way he wrote the questions on his quizzes were fair, as long as you took good notes and are engaged. I thought he answered a lot of question really good too

Really fantastic lecturer. Presented information clearly, at a good pace, and in an engaging manner. Answered students' questions in class. Quizzes for the class were challenging enough to make sure one learns the important content from the class but not overly difficult. Also, try not to procrastinate on the research credit.
Hes funny and made me want to come to class. he gots off topic easily which can be annoying but otherwise good way to start freshman year

Top notch dude. Hilarious and engaging lectures. Some other people here say the quizzes were poorly worded but I thought they were fine. 10/10 would take again. Be aware that if you're taking him for Intro to Psych then you may only have him teaching for a third of the semester.

Professor Sommers is very engaging and gives great lectures. As a few others have said on here, the quiz questions can be very confusing, but if you read carefully and know the content well the quizzes should not be a huge issue.

He's a charming lecturer who is very engaging. Good at explaining topics and cracks jokes during lecture to lighten up the mood. Quizzes varied. Oftentimes, the questions were very poorly written and extremely confusing. Good lecturer, poor design of quiz questions.
Is a nice guy and his lectures are decent. Quizzes are pretty challenging though and are worded strangely.

Very amazing professor. Contrary to another professor who taught Intro to Psych this semester, his lectures actually made sense and his quiz questions were very fair. Could get a little monotone at times but still very engaging. Definitely make the most out of your time with him before you get to the next professor.

(For Intro to psych) Sommers was solid. His lectures are clear and he teaches well. No homework/tests, only quizzes online every other week. My only complaint is that his quiz questions were sometimes poorly written/vague, but I'd recommend for Psych 100
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sommers section of the intro to psych class was really well done. His lectures were engaging and funny and he was always willing to talk to students after. The quizzes are a bit wordy and can be confusing, but if you study and go to lecture you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Engaging lecturer, loved his section of Intro to Psych!

Professor Sommers was a great lecturer for the first section of Psych100B. He was funny and nice, the material was not very difficult, and we only had 2 quizzes during his segment of the class (one every other week), both of which were take home and pretty easy.

His lectures were good but definitely read the textbook during his unit and be careful with bad wording on the quizzes because his terribly written quiz questions cost me a few points. Overall I enjoyed this class and it's not hard to do well if you take good notes and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sommer was a solid lecturer. His lecture videos were very informative and I felt like I learned a lot. Honestly, I didn't think he was very difficult assessment wise, but sometimes he wasn't the best at wording questions so you just had to read it carefully

Lecture wise, Sommers was actually a good teacher. He made the material from the readings clearer and was very engaging. HOWEVER, the wording on tests was absolutely terrible. I would avoid taking a class with him for this reason as your grade is purely based off of tests and research credit.

Professor Sommers was really fun in the first unit of Psych 100B. His lectures were fun and engaging; I always loved going to his class. The class, in general, isn't too hard, but it does give a great overview of Psych. No need to read the textbook if you go to class and take good notes. I definitely recommend it.
Good professor, he definitely likes what he teaches. Can be a bit too enthusiastic at times and speak very fast.

You have to go to lecture (plus it's easier to absorb info than just reading the book). The lectures are great though; Sommers has good humor. Reading the textbook isn't completely necessary, but it can help to read the material beforehand. None of the test questions are surprising (all MC). Go to lectures and study, and you'll be fine.

The most engaging lecturer I've had at WashU. I didn't do as well on the test as I wanted to, but it was my first psych test and I hadn't gotten a feel for WashU tests yet. Absolutely loved going and listening to his lectures.

He's hilarious! Lectures aren't recorded, so get ready to go to class and take notes, but if you keep up with your readings and pay attention, it's a great class. He's super interesting and one of my favorite professors so far. His tests get a little tricky if you don't read, but as long as you study and put in the work, an A is definitely doable.
My favorite class as a first semester freshman, I really enjoyed it even though I didn't do well on the test. He was clear, interesting and funny!

He's the man. Funny, smart, attentive, super nice and has great control over the class. Basically the perfect guy for Psych 100. I really hope I get to take another class with him. Exam was an easy A if you go to class and do the readings.

I really loved having him as a professor. His tests were a little challenging, though that's more due to the extent of the information he covers rather than the difficulty of the information he presents.
Always allows time for questions and is really helpful. Love this guy! His lectures are really interesting.
Very understandable.  Easy Class.  When he taught Psych, I got an easy A.  The other psych teachers are horrible, especially Head.  Enjoy him while you have him.

Dr. Sommers is a boss. Great intro psychology teacher. Fascinating lectures. Good tempo. He always took time to prompt the class for questions and patiently answer, despite the large, lecture hall setting. I am looking forward to future psychology classes with Dr. Sommers?a subject I never imagined I might major in prior to his course.

Professor Sommers is the complete package - nice guy, funny, makes the course material interesting. Always took time in class for questions anyone had. Make sure to keep up with the readings, though. Psych is a class that's easy to put on the backburner because there isn't any homework per se. Tests are fair but challenging. Better than Duchek IMO.
Funny guy, interesting & varied lectures.  All you could want from an intro course.  Not a blowoff.
I love that guy
Funny man, kept psych class interesting
Makes a lot of jokes, and succeeds in being funny most of the time. Interesting. Good lecturer.
interesting, amusing, great.

More challenging than you'd expect for an intro psych class, but the information is so interesting and the powerpoint presentations he uses make it much easier than it would be in a normal lecture...also very into using visuals.

sommers was awesome. seriously he is like a cult figure at wash u. he made what would have been boring material very entertaining. thought his exam was fair. his pace was a little too face tho. and don't ask him what the website is cuz he'll get mad.
boring

I enjoyed his lectures though they were a bit slow, it was worth going to class. He made the material pretty clear although his organization was a bit sloppy. I thought class was pretty good, but I was disappointed with the exam which was worded badly and the grade didn't reflect what I learned.
Nice guy, good teacher
Not as good as duchek, not as bad as lambert.
Best teacher of the 3.
very entertaining, great class
Really funny, really cool
talks too fast
No Comments

She is the worst writing 1 teacher possible! She is rude and mean, and unclear and a super tough grader for no reason! She gave me a D on my final paper and put 0 comments on the whole 12 page thing!  I don't even think she read it... She is truly a mean human being and enjoyed lowering my GPA just because she could.
shes kinda tough but an amazing and knowledgable teacher
she's awesome
Just start all your assignments early and you should be chillin
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Class is entirely project-based so you'll learn a good amount. It is quite time consuming if you're not a seasoned developer already but grading is very fair (and you have a partner)

Didn't love the way it was taught -- videos that have been recycled for years, zero lecture. Class needs to be updated on content and taught in person

Cloud Computing w/ Sproull is a great class. Sproull is kind, enthusiastic, knowledgeable, helpful, and super fair. The class is a pretty easy A and teaches you lots of incredibly relevant skills for the tech industry that CSE330 doesn't touch on. Would recommend!

todd sproull is awesome and so funny. made going to class fun and he has a lot of knowledge to share, you just have to put in the effort in this class and put in the effort to talk to him and then hes super down to help you. everyone wants u to succeed in this class. grading is very chill and straightforward.

class is a couple of projects every few weeks. they give u a lot of time for each one and tbh it takes maybe a day to learn the framework and then another day to build out the project w that framework. a lot of them build off each other too so its not an overload of information. this class made me like ui stuff and feel confident w development
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I think ppl expect this class to be easy with minimal work like the other cs classes here, but u dont learn anything this way. this class is a spot of light in a sea of darkness of poorly structured classes where u can get away with learning and doing nothing. I loved this tho and it rlly pushed me to like cs more
great class, I've never learned as much as I did in this class. class is basically office hours so help is always there. just try your hardest and you will be rewarded

Only class this semester where I enjoyed doing the homework (only projects). And all the project rubrics/expectations are online so you can see them rn. Such an awesome class, reasonable amount of work but not too difficult—you just have to put effort. You learn so much in this class! Attendance isn't mandatory but way more fun if you show up!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved coming to this class every day. I am not a cs nerd so don't think that either. it's just fun to have projects u can call your own and its fun to collaborate with other people. u gain so much experience working w in teams, debugging, and solving ur own problems which is super important in the real world. Todd is the goat.

It's a semi-self taught class, so you get what you put into it. If you want to learn a lot and make projects that you can be proud of, definitely take this class. Any problems TAs or Sproull usually can 100% fix easily because they know a lot about the frameworks. Just don't larp your time away in this class and it's cake.

This was such a fun class—some projects def take a lot of time, but if you enjoy learning by doing and talking to people you will love this class. Sproull and TAs are always willing to help and the class is very collaborative. No exams, it's def manageable as long as you don't start work late!! Easily one of my favorite classes i've taken.

His rating is not entirely his fault. The class is structured where you have 6 large projects, and class time is used for work. The class is essentially run by TAs, most of which are useless. If you set aside time for this class and complete all the work, you should get an A. However, it is a lot of work. Todd is helpful if you reach out to him

Sproull does not teach this course, his outdated lectures from 10 years ago do. If you have a good team this course is easy to succeed in and adds helpful projects to your portfolio. That said, Sproull does minimal work for this class, only take it for your personal development.

YOU MUST start on assignments early. Don't leave it up to second week for you to start on the assignment, as you wont be able to finish it. A lot of the stuff in this class seems outdated, and is probably not as useful for a cs student to learn. This class is an insane workload compared to other cs courses, only take if you need cs credits
No lecture. No studio. No exam. No discussion.

The biggest reason why people struggle in this class is they don't start early. I completed the majority of projects early on so I barely need to attend class/pay attention to the work for a semester. This would've been a great class 10 years ago when companies were still using these technologies since his videos haven't been updated since 2016.

Tough class because there isn't much downtime between labs: HW fatigue. My mental health did take a hit however the grading was a lot nicer than I realized. He's not really accessible--just go to TA office hours. I personally felt that he likes people who really get CS and not really those who struggle more, but idk. Biggest advice: start early!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you value your mental health, don't take this class. All the Wikipedia/assignments are available online with a google search, so if you want to learn the material, just self pace. The workload on top of 4 other classes is unreasonable.
If there was a 0, I would give it.

As someone with prior swe internship experience the class was easy enough imo, but i've never seen a professor so disinterested in his class. A WashU cs prof who doesn't host office hours, reply to piazza posts, or answer students questions is surprising but reflective of the cs program here. If you have no prior experience you will likely struggle

Incredibly unreasonable and inconsiderate of students' situations. Group projects were required, yet there was no way of grading individual effort and no accommodation if there were issues. And even if an incredible amount of extra work was completed he adhered to unreasonable policies. Basically has 0 respect for students.

CSE438. 4 labs (2-3 weeks each) + Final project (5 weeks) for the grade. The resources provided for each project are about half of what you need and are reused videos. Lots of outside research is needed to do each project. Each project takes anywhere from 4 to 25 hours. Some are insanely tedious and difficult, so start atleast 4 days before due.

Fantastic 48+ working hours per week makes your summer terribly fulfilled, one project per week without a second extension for any assignment with mind blowing new materials and lecture notes made decades ago.
At most 50 hours of workload per week. Significant penalties for various minor points. No late submission is allowed even with the request before the deadline.
massive work load

Isn't accommodating, thinks of his students as robots and not humans. Unwilling to help out at all with anything happening outside of the classroom, I wouldn't be surprised if he has been the cause of multiple students' depression because I know he has certainly helped mine.

Yes, 330 is a very hard and time-consuming class (esp. if you've only taken 131), but Dr. Sproull is super kind and always happy to help whenever you get stuck. He is extremely knowledgeable about web development and can solve pretty much any problem you encounter in under 5 mins. You will undoubtedly come out a better developer
Insanely smart. Class is mostly just learning yourself and A LOT of work, but most useful class I've taken yet. Highly recommend, but take it with a friend.

330 has an intense workload, but the work is valuable and the class is built for success if you put the time in. 330 covers a wide range of languages in large, interesting projects with a partner. TA OH are available several hours daily on zoom. Sproull is helpful in class, which is work time for projects. Grading criteria is very clear in rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 330S gets a bad wrap but it's the best class I've taken at WashU. There is a ton of work but it built my entire resume. You learn so much and the class isn't hard if you put the time in (the rubrics are very clear so it is easy to do well). Take the class during an easy semester to build up your CS skills. Sproull is way better than his 1.9 rating.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Seems like a friendly guy. But he doesn't teach at all. He just assigns. 

Wants you to just read the wiki. Videos do nothing. Group projects are hard to do on your own so you better know a good partner! I got stuck with a dumb one on module 3.
This is an online class, and about 10% students fail.

He'll give you 2 20-min videos every 2 weeks and expect you to complete huge 20 hr+ projects with no help. These videos are also many years old as well as the homemade wiki pages you get. How WashU prides themselves on being a top tier institute while employing professors that only teach via recycled videos and short wiki pages baffles me.
worst professor that i have ever met in my life. do avoid him at all cost. this guy does not teach plus never help solve any questions posted on piazza at all and his TA are all very unhelpful.

Dont take this class when youre taking other hard classes. There are too few TAs and sometimes you have to wait over 2 hours to get helped even if you get to TA hours early. Prerecorded lectures are also extremely unhelpful in completing projects.
Dr. Sproull is very helpful when you ask for help. However, 330 is a large class and with so many questions being asked, it can be hard to get ahold of him.
This guy is the worst. He tries so hard to act like the cool teacher but in reality hes the worst person and a genuinely terrible professor.

Todd struggles to keep tabs on the logistics of his class. I can't speak for 330S, but for 240 He was unaware that the majority of the assignments had not been graded by week 6 of the semester. He did not remedy this problem, even when asked in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Homework heavy, but materials are pretty good and helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class takes up a TON of time but it is well spent and you learn a ton of new skills. Do not take this course during a hard term because it is a lot of work, but if you have time to fit it into a lighter term I highly recommend. Excellent recorded lectures. Very in depth wikipedia style wiki provided explaining everything. Fun projects

I can't even say this professor is bad at teaching because it's pretty much non existent. I had him for both 240 and 330, and he makes everything seem like a joke. The class content is really interesting, but he is just so bad. Get ready to teach yourself EVERYTHING and spend like 15 hours a week on projects.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Has no class but all the lectures / course wiki are online. Pretty much everything you could need to know is on the course wiki. Assignments aren't "hard" but they take an extremely long time to complete ,especially because many new languages are covered. Overall a very useful class in terms of learning new things
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Really bad at teaching!

Students should carefully review the official course evaluation in previous semesters, which reveals that Todd may have a problem enforcing consistent grading systems. As other posts mentioned, it is almost like online course though it is not. So don't expect him to spend too much time on teaching or taking caring of the TA team.

Not too horrible, and the content of course itself is useful for the training of web development. But I doubt the instructor spends much time on this course like the others. The exam was graded three weeks after the submission and during that time there were no other assignments pending. Now after a month, we still havent received the grade of HW5

Todd is not always available and most of the help are from TAs. But most of TAs seem to be students who took this course before, and I highly doubt they can answer questions other than their assignments. In fact, the TA hours are messy. Rooms are not reserved like other lectures, TAs can be late, and not every one get equally amount of help.

The course is merely lumped with tutorials of different frameworks of web development, outdated. Todd cares much less about the lecture compared to instructors of other similar courses, and he wont even show up each class. Grade and regrade are significantly delayed.

Youll wait weeks to get the result of grades. You are likely to receive the grade of after submitting two more assignments, and hence the grade provides almost no insight/feedback to correct mistakes in further homeworks but rather purnishment. Regrades will not be replied, so you dont whether it is not considered or not. This is insulting.

Professor Sproull was not very helpful or knowledgeable, and pretty inaccessible. It is an entirely online class, and the best source of knowledge are the TA's. A lot of coding, but none of the material is deep or difficult. I personally will not take another class with this professor. The material is old and you can learn it by yourself.

(1) Grading are extremely slow, even compared to courses that have more students and fewer graders. (2) Roughly 15% of the overall grade has no clear rubric and is admitted by TA that different TA might give diffeerent score. (3) You can get different explanations to certain rubrics from TA, head TA and Todd Sproull. A failure of management.
The course demands a lot of work but you learn a lot. However, professor Sproull is extremely arrogant and does not help at all. Take it with someone else if possible.

This professor was easy. Everything you need to do well in the class is handed to you from him. He gives out handouts and trying to read the book is not helpful at all. The class is easy cause everything is repetitive. You do the same thing throughout the entire semester. He lets you know what exactly will be on the exams. Easy class!

Wow, there are no words to describe how useless this professor is. He relies on a plethora of handouts which are clearly older than some of the students. He's literally not able to be reasoned with. You could stand there for 20 minutes and argue with him about grading and he wouldn't give you a single point back. He is way past his prime.

2nd worst prof. I've ever had, examples are wrong, hates explaining things twice, will not change schedule for anything, can't make up quizzes, homework is full of errors, handouts are full of errors, halfway senile, can't operate equip., doesn't respond to emails, clearly neurotic and unreasonable, mentions little about tests which are 40% of grde

He has lost his marbles.  You can count on him doing half of his examples wrong and he won't know it.  Be careful, when he tells you that you won't be tested on something, you really are.  NOT helpful, and needed to retire about 10 years ago.
No Comments

She is so nice, so kind, so patient, and so caring. Although the class is not so interesting, she tells everything in detail. Easy homework, easy grading, and the exams are similar to the practice exams.

Balan was a very kind teacher who cared about her students. The class was relatively easy as long as you show up and pay attention a little bit. Practice exams are very similar to tests so master those.
really caring teacher! she always provided support and let us know exactly what we needed to know for each exam & assignment

She is wonderful! She supported me well throughout the course, making sure I understood it. I also think she really cares about what she is teaching, trying to get everyone to follow along even when they don't... beware of momentary pop quizzes (usually just based on completion for attendance check).
She is kind and willing to help. However, lectures can get very boring, and you will learn almost nothing.

She is the kindest lady, always willing to help you, and cares about her students. She is SUPER hard to hear during lectures, and the class is boring, and you will learn little to nothing. Be nice to her! She cares about students and loves statistics.
Best professor ever. She was so helpful for the final project and genuinely cares about seeing her students succeed!

Professor Balan really cares about her students. She is super helpful and supportive as long as you reach out to her. Our group struggled with the final project, and she guided us step by step for 1.5 hours. Her classes are well-explained and engaging; she has a brief wellness session before each class and offers screen breaks. Highly recommended!

Very easy class. Professor Kim made an effort to be personal and interact with students. The class was pretty disorganized and you didn't always know what assignments were or when they were due. However, in the end it was a simple class with few expectations and help was available if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Are you looking for a class where all the busywork you do gets dropped into a black hole? Look no further.
Feedback? None. 
Grades? Definitely not.
Informative and coherent lectures? You're asking for too much already.

From the bottom of my heart, don't take a class with Prof Kim. She has good intentions, but you will get nothing out of it.

Professor Kim has the most boring lectures I have ever participated in. They were actually painful to sit through. The class was not clearly structured, and professor Kim was very disorganized. The class was on writing skills, yet I learned very few tangible writing skills. Assignments are mostly boring busy work. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Intro to Pilates with Susan is one of the best classes I've taken. She makes class super fun and is super understanding of all circumstances. Whenever I couldn't make it to class, she proposed alternatives and when I wasn't feeling super energetic, she would provide an easier version of the exercise. She is simply the best!

Prof. Volkan is one of the sweetest, most nurturing professors I've had at WU. She's there for her students outside of class and makes an effort to get to know her students and form long lasting relationships. (I had her 4 years ago and we still talk and visit all the time!) Her classes are taught in a creative and challenging way. Take her class!
Professor Volkam is the best teacher i've had at wash u...you must take this course. she's the sweetest woman alive!!! AHH I LOVE HER!
LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE. period.
She is the most engaging, most interested, and most fun professor I have had yet at Wash U.  Take this class, you will learn SO much and have fun in the meanwhile.
I absolutely loved this class, probably my favorite.  She is so sweet and makes class something that you look forward to attending.  You should take this class with her if you get the chance.

My favorite class. Even if you have never taken an acting class before, I highly recommend taking one with her. While it was a 2 hour class, we always wanted it to last much longer. It was tons of fun. You bond with the class and learn a great deal about yourself. Take it if you get the chance.

I loved this class. I have no acting ability whatsoever, but she always finds something nice to say. She's a little out there, but so sweet and so much fun...i'd recommend the class to anyone. There are some assignments but as long as you do them, you will get an A.

She is one of the nicest professors on campus and truly a cool person. She prefers concise work and graded pretty easily. Her exams were easy I got an A on the midterm from just listening in class - no additional studying. Loved hearing her stories more than the class, she is so fun. There was a relaxed atmosphere in class; I never dreaded going.
Good Professor

Professor Parikh is super nice and an exciting teacher. Sometimes I felt like the lectures were unorganized but the reading material was interesting (sometimes really long though). Attendance is required, but you can finesse that if you have friends in the class to sign you in. The class felt "chaotic" at times, with not a ton of direction.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Parikh was by far my favorite professor at WashU

She's clearly a cool person, but disorganized and never seemed to have a clear plan. Lectures were just her going over the readings in depth which meant I didn't have to read them but also made class boring. It was interesting when she would open for discussion, though.

Prof assumes an unrealistic level of backgroud knowledge in lectures. Lectures sometimes dry but integrate well with the readingstests.  Exams are easy provided you learn all the termsconcepts from readinglecture. A solid but not exceptional polisci course.

As a lecturer, she's mediocre. Most people generally skip except for "project days" which are mandatory, and understandably so. She often rambles on during lectures, but makes up for it in her willingness to help students who ask questions. She's very nice, just not very clear. Tests were a breeze though.
Very good teacher. A bit disorganized but lectures are really informative and interesting.

Amazing teacher, learned an enormous amount from her. Sometimes is a bit disorganized, but the genuine caring and her enormous knowledge of the subject is always obvious. Going to office hours is amazing, she is willing to discuss any and everything about her class candidly, and you can learn SOOO much from her, highly recommended.

Professor Parikh is an engaging and passionate lecturer.  Her examples and her ability to draw students into her lectures make attending class a joy.  She is truly caring and amazingly interesting in office hours as well.  I would suggest attending class, especially because she draws most tests from lectures (which are much clearer than the book).
Most disorganized instructor ever.  Good luck following her lectures.  Can be entertaining though if you're aiming to get personal stories out of her to get off-topic.  Very easy.
She's a really fun lady and is extremely knowledgable about India and Pakistan. The Sri Lanka and Bangladesh portions of the class are pretty weak. She's a good lecturer but gets off track easily.
