Very knowledgeable in her area of expertise, but lectures lack organization. She is entertaining at times, but not always the clearest lecturer.  Her exams are relatively easy, but at times ID questions come completely out of left field. If you are fairly knowledgeable about subject material, take her- otherwise, be prepared to do all the readings.

I took comparative politics from her, but it basically became a survey of her research in India compared to the United States political system, which was marginally interesting but not so helpful when it came to the tests on the actually material.

terrible professor, gets off topic ALL the time, goes off on long tangents, repeats herself, i could have slept all semester and not missed anything, i dont understand why people seem to like her so much.  doesnt teach about relevant or educational things
Very good professor herself; unfortunately her illness has forced her to relegate many of her teaching duties to Alfred Darnell (um, yeah) and Jeff Smith (full of it).

He has a superiority complex based on potentially (most definitely) a lot of childhood trauma and feelings of inadequacy. Architecture isn't worth abusing students and promoting a low quality of life. The tortured artist schtick is played out. Truly wish for his healing but requires a lot of deep introspection and therapy.
incredibly harsh, was only in studio for the first 30 minutes of class, and expects unreasonable work within the timeframe.
Taking his class is the worst choice I've ever made in my life
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor's attitude towards students is abysmal. He expects you to do massive amounts of work which he critiques harshly and makes you feel terrible about. He often compares projects to other failed projects in architectural history which is the most embarrassing part about him considering he's not even licensed.
Though all studio members experienced with continuous working without sleeping, he threatened students with fail, and refused to make effective communications.
too much work and useless

This guy is so abusive to students.  He insults you personally, not just your work.  He will physically break your models.  I will avoid taking him again at all costs.  I did not learn much from him from a design stance because he dictates your design to you. But unfortunately I have to admit I did learn from him in an architectural sense.

Sung Ho lives in his own universe of idealized forms. His "teaching" is mostly limited to being abusive toward students. Many have complained of way over the many years. Apparently the school's devoted to his formalistic approach to architecture leaving us with a meager background in design that considers form above all else. What about people?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Poor communicator.  Degrades students, but seems to justify it in his mind.  At this level professors should be role models, and mentors, Sung Ho is not.  Yet he'll feign being hurt if you confront him, though continues to belittle students.

School doesn't have to be a boot camp to learn.  Degrades students with incessant sarcasm.  Not overly qualified, wrote a book - sure did...designs for competitions in his own firm - sure does.  Unfortunately, not licensed and has never had a building built.  If your goal in life is to become an architect who builds in reality...not recommended.
No Comments
No Comments

In my four years of college I have never had a worse worse than prof. Karunamoorthy. Lectures are very hard to follow, so no one is paying attention, or they don't show up at all. His tests are not timed appropriately, so they're really hard to finish even if you know the material. His grading is unreasonably harsh. Avoid at all costs.

Made us buy HIS OWN textbook to do homeworks. Just reads off of slides, not very clear. Literally tells us what is going to be on the exam and has open book exams. Very easy class, don't feel like I learned anything hence my low rating.

Dynamics and Vibrations itself had a lot of hard concepts but swami gave a lot of examples and practice exams to help prepare. He also gave hints on what would be on the exam so it made it easier to study for. During grading, he was very generous with partial credit so showing work was very important. Overall great class, would take again.
Great professor! She's very sweet and always makes class interesting. You can tell she really cares about her students. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Even at the very end of the day, this class was always lively and fun. Although there was a lot of homework, she was always full of energy and tried to make class enjoyable by playing games with new vocabulary or finding new and interesting ways to practice grammar. I cannot recommend more!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great professor!

Great professor. Really cares for students and offers extremely clear guidelines and expectations. She expects you to speak in Spanish, but that shouldn't be surprising. She was always upbeat and excited to teach! Definitely take her class!

Prof Swick is one of the best Spanish professors I have come across at Washington University. While she can sometimes seem a bit condescending, she is excellent at explaining the rules of Spanish grammar to non-native speakers (a skill that few foreign language professors here possess). Also, she keeps the class  busy so you are always entertained.
Professor Swick can sometimes come off as impersonal and impatient. Sometimes class is conducted in a disorderly fashion.

Sra. Swick was a great prof., definitely one of the best in the department. As someone said earlier, she is a "hidden gem." Her grading is reasonable, and she makes the class as fun and energetic as she can while we learn boring grammar. She is also super nice and approachable. I highly recommend taking her class!

Sra. Swick is awesome. Be forewarned-- she's a hard grader, so look over your essays multiple times, and when you think they're perfect, look again. As well as being funny and a sweetheart, she really helped me refine my grammar skills and is EXTREMELY approachable. Only teaching one class of 307 per semester, she is one of Wash U's hidden gems.

Sra. Swick is definitely good with helping you learn grammar. You end up doing a lot of busy work in 307, which can get boring, but Swick moves at a good pace and tries her best to keep the class somewhat interesting. She's also really nice and approachable.

She is super nice and really wants everyone to do well. Extremely reasonable grading and super nice work load. She has so much energy, really makes it easy to sit there and go over grammar and vocab 82 times without wanting to off yourself.
Señora Swick is amazing! She cares a lot about her students and it is obvious that she really wants every one in her class to actually understand the language and enjoy using it.
Senora Swick is very energetic and involved- she loves Spanish and her students. She makes class interesting and is always available for help. An excellent teacher for any beginning Spanish class.
Very energetic. Good intentions, but activities got annoying and the class often felt like high school.
Cares about students.  Her class is a lot of fun.
the material you have to learn is boring, but swick is really upbeat and funny.  always willing to help and is very friendly.
Swick is a great professor.  Her class was sooooo much fun every day...very engaging.  She's kind of all over the place, but she has a very good sense of humor...a little naughty at times!
Extremely nice and teaches in the best interest of her students.  I LOVE her.  Definitely take her class.
She's really nice, genuinely cares for her students, and keeps everything clear and moving. Definitely recommended!
Not the greatest class material, but she's really cute and nice
No Comments
Awesome prof, great enthusiasm and cares sincerely about her students.  Spanish 353 is helpful and useful without being to stressful.
I LOVE Swick!
Wonderful teacher. She is very concerned for her students and she is very organized
No Comments

As someone who had A/A+ in all other math classes, even A+ in Syring's 3200, I found Syring's 494 the most terrible class I've ever had. The test questions were impossible and completely unrelated to our homework. Plz avoid a professor who threw impossible questions at his students even in a semester when a global pandemic hit so many ppl hard

Terrible at explaining things, tests have unfair questions that are barely covered in hw/lectures. Please avoid this if possible. Most people who take this class do it bc its a major requirement, so maybe wait until literally anyone else teaches it if possible. Probably the worst professor I have had at washu

My review was taken down. Maybe I should temper my review. Well, here it goes: although sooome people may think Mr., or should I say Dr., Syring is a good Professor, I happen to think otherwise. His condescending attitude is, ummm, quite a disappointment; Im sure he cares about math, but perhaps not teaching. Period. Drop the mic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Indulges in his student's failure. Makes the hardest stats class at WashU even worse. Bad lecturing: only goes over proofs of theorems and explains them badly. Extremely hard exams: unrelated to what he teaches, involves little concepts mostly calculations (you'd be better-off being a calculator). Doesn't respond to emails. Absolutely merciless.

Worst class I've taken at WashU. Explained simple concepts in round a bout ways that left me feeling confused on the basics. Every time I asked questions in class or in office hours he was snarky and belittling. Averages for every test were at or below failing, with only a slight curve in the end. Considering taking 2200 because I learned NOTHING

Nice person overall. His lectures can be a bit repetitive as a lot of it is proving a concept for a large chunk of time. Tips: stay caught up with the material; if you need help, utilize office hours.

Syring was good at teaching but he taught from the textbook, which was not very good in my opinion. This sometimes lead to some confusion, but he was available to answer any questions. Tests were hard, but there were opportunities elsewhere to make up points. He also listened to what students had to say and incorporated feedback during the course.
Explains concepts well and writes clearly.

Syring is terrible at lecturing, he gives super basic examples then throws impossible homework questions which seem totally unrelated. The textbook he uses has horrible wording too, so it's impossible to understand what the questions are truly asking.

Long lectures, as others have mentioned, and unorganized.  Honestly he sounds like a conspiracy theorists when he spurts his theories 'no one else believes.'  Funny if you like conspiracies, but he is very knowledgeable.  Didn't know how grading worked at all, and didn't learn anything.

Long, disorganized lectures. Unclear what he wants on assignments most of the time. Readings are completely optional, and you honestly don't even need to read the Odyssey, despite the class being about that book.

Rude, unhelpful, unorganized and uninteresting. I studied for hours but he has too much information to possibly learn and doesn't clearly narrow down anything. He's retiring, but I thought I should say how much his class disappointed me.
Tends to make the student feel unimportant. Disorganized. Hard to study for tests because doesn't clarify what's most important. Likes to talk about himself.

Terrible teacher. Extremely self-absorbed, managed to find ways to talk about his own research in every single class regardless of relevance. Completely rejects any ideas that might contradict his own. Avoid.
Love this class on Egyptian art. Symeonoglou is brilliant and loves teaching. He is an outstanding professor and I highly recommend taking any of his classes.
Incredibly interesting professor. Knows the subject really well and does an amazing job making the material interesting.

Although he is a bit scatter-brained at times, I thoroughly enjoyed his lectures and I loved this class!  He is very knowledgeable and passionate about his subject.  I would highly recommend him to anyone interested in the subject, who doesn't mind a little bit of disorder.

unclear grading, no use of textbook, no test review, absolutely not available to students (ignores email), strange tests, contradictory lectures. Good luck getting clarification on anything. Stay away!!!

What a pompus ass. He is very self-absorbed and egotistical and is too busy doing research to condescend to be available for his students. He acts like he is the only one who knows anything about Greek art. Not approachable at all. I am very disappointed, since I had heard good things about him.
Probably my favorite professor at Wash U - amazing man with a wealth of information in his head and lots of theories! Go to his office hours and just listen to him talk because he is incredible.
Outstanding archaeologist and professor.  One of the world's experts on Crete, Homer, and Thera.  Take his class!
Good professor, knows what he's talking about, and has a great sense of humor. Very forgiving if you have to turn in something late.
great professor
Does not care about his students
Fun, down-to-earth professor. Great class, very interesting material.
Smart, learned, down-to-earth professor. I loved his class on the Art of the Egypt of the Pharaohs. He made it so interesting that I can not wait to visit this  ancient land!
No Comments
Great prof, would recommend her for completing the college writing requirement. Make sure to participate in discussion and do the readings or at least skim!!

Dr. Taylor is the sweetest human, and you can tell she actually cares about each and every one of her students. As long as you communicate with her, participate in class, and do your work, it's a very easy class. There are assignments due before every class (3 times a week), but they are not long/hard. Very glad to have her as my prof.

She is so awesome! I didn't get the topic I wanted for College Writing but in hindsight the prof is more important. She made class welcoming and fun and easy if you just do the discussion posts and the occasional essay. Lucky to have her for CW because other profs can be a real pain esp for a class that doesn't matter a whole lot in the end

prof. taylor is super nice and understanding. however, the only assignment she graded & left comments on was our final, which i feel was used for our final grade. there are discussion posts for the assigned reading for every class, but it's very casual. make all of the other essays & posts be ok, but try for the final. everyone got at least an a-
I didn't learn too much but the class was okay.
Taylor is great! Very kind and forgiving, really makes college writing not bad. Still haven't gotten feedback on much written work at all though

Dr. Taylor is incredibly kind and understanding. I would recommend her writing identity course for sure for college writing. However, you will get very little feedback and wont learn much most likely.
Dr. Taylor is a really supportive instructor. Her courses are intriguing and the work loads are fine. The feedback she gave is very constructive. She is a nice and easygoing person.

An outstanding professor. She is kind and caring, checking in with her students to make sure they're alright, and she only assigns a couple of larger writing assignments. Just know that there will be readings and discussion posts for each class, but they can all usually be done in under 30 minutes. Cannot recommend her class enough.
She was the kindest teacher. Very understanding and gave me an indefinite extension for no points off. Surprisingly enjoyed the class and I think she grades easy (no grades are in yet lol).

She has been one of the most lenient but also attentive professors I've ever had. She always understand when I have other things going on and always checks up on us. Discussions are well lead and I always learn a lot but it is also very low stress.
So sweet and a great, kindest teacher ever. She genuinely cares about each student.

i have dr. taylor for my college writing class (writing identity) for this semester and she is simply amazing. she's engaging and wants to hear about what we do outside of class. one time i accidentally showed up an hour early and she let me stay through that class instead of waiting for my own. plus she plays pokemon go

Prof. Taylor showed up to class late for the majority of the semester. It is the last day of finals and I have received one grade from her all semester. Nothing was graded out of the probably 10 major assignments that we had until after the last week of classes (the day before the final paper was due). She is kind, but her class is poorly organized

Let me just say that after arriving late to every single class her peer review reminded the class to "keep in mind I have two children to feed"... returned all papers super late. Only one or two essays were graded before the last week of class :(

Tough grader. Wants your paper to flow well + provide some creative insight. A b+ is a above average paper while an A-/A is an exceptional paper. Overall, nice teacher and understanding but you must put in work to get a good grade. She is very flexible to different ideas and writing styles.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Would take again

reviews.comment: Basically, writing one is boring and there isn't really anyway to get around that. Dr. Taylor is super nice and of all the writing one profs she probably gives the least amount of work. With that said, she is a hard grader and she nitpicks. If there is any flaw in your paper you best believe she will find it.

She is one of the most helpful teachers i have encountered. She also likes to push students to do their personal best. Since i love to write she really helped me reach my goals even if they exceeded the ones listed in the syllabus. She makes writing 1 enjoyable unlike many of the writing 1 teachers at wash u.
Very very straightforward homework and exams. International finance is very similar to macroeconomics, just with more exchange rate math.

International Finance by Mark Taylor was one of my favorite courses here at WashU. Absolute beast and an amazing professor. He definitely cares about his students and his assignment/exams are super manageable.

Great class. Prof. Taylor makes complex material easy to understand and all slides are accessible. He wants you to succeed in the class if you are willing to try.  If you're into international finance you could go very in-depth with the professor and the materials-- he's an international expert who's actually done the work which is cool.
I wish I had more professors like Dr. Templeton. He's incredibly smart, wise, funny, enthusiastic, and passionate.
good guy

Took his Pop Gen class. Alan is okay. Pro: He knows his stuff. Con: He doesn't teach it very clearly for students, who, being students, have not had nearly as much experience as him in the field. He made the class buy copies of the manuscript he's hoping to get published soon. Not cool.

Templeton is okay - The material is somewhat interesting, but his lectures fly above everyone's head in the room. If you've had Prob Stat, that will help. Otherwise, you wont have a clue what hes talking about half the time. He is a leader in the field but he can't bring it down to a 200 level bio class very well.
His lectures are cool, they can be dull, but usually aren't.  His tests are surprisingly easy.  He happens to be a genius at the stuff he's teaching, which really makes the class great.
Genetics Adonis!  Can't spell "dying" to save his life! Promotes the burning of large tracts of forest (Smokey the Bear is evil)!  Tells a lot of jokes in class.  What a great guy!

Alan Templeton is a genius, as well as an excellent teacher. Of course he's going to talk about his research--it's groundbreaking, as he is one of the foremost biologists in his field. If you can't appreciate this then maybe you should take biology at a community college. Better yet, don't even both

A good professor - take him if you're interested in the field. And for the critic before this - he may be arrogant, but Templeton teaches his own research because he has invented and redefined much of the field. That's a good thing, not a bad thing, dummy. You go to Wash U to learn from experts.

pass on temp. he goes way too fast and defines concepts with terms and symbols needing even more complex definitions. As for the previous post, it shouldnt be hocki ng that he originated a concept he taught us but rather expected, becuse this arrogant crackpot teaches his research as course material
So cool that all you need to succeed are his lecture slides he puts online.  I was browsing the net one time and I discovered that he originated one of the main concepts we discussed -awesome stuff.
he's incredibly boring but enjoys talking about his studies in the ozarks
Great professor, very enthusiastic.
His examples are soooo good.
No Comments
No Comments

I liked Templeton.  The class was full of unique ideas that you wouldn't be taught anywhere else.  It really redefined the way I thought about genetics.  He was sooooo refreshing after that Duncan guy...
I thought his half of the course was very interesting - I really liked it.  He's a really smart guy

funny, edgy, and entrancing guy.  His lectures were very detailed, used many different disciplines, and explained concepts well.  One of the only good uses of Powerpoint I've seen.  Definitely motivated me to do much better than expected.
Wrote his own textbook for the course, and used us as guinea pigs for it.
She is the worst. Shows blatant favoritism, grades incredibly hard, and is outright rude. If you're thinking of taking (or re-taking) Bio 2960 with her, I'd recommend against it.
She's rude to students, shows high favoritism among certain few, and is horrible at explaining information.  However, her lecture notes are good (probably because they're from another prof).

One of the worst professors. Pays no attention to what students want. Very difficult and frustrating to talk to.  Her lectures are from another professor's powerpoint slides which means she is not fully prepared to teach this course. Strong favorism among the students can be observed.

Very old instructor (not a full-time professor) who significantly lacks the capability of teaching. Very biased. She is a person who loves to get picky, and refuses to admit her own mistakes. Must be avoided.
Summer course lecturer. She is very mean and not good to teaching. I think she is still a lecturer only because of her influential husband. dont take summer bio2960

She doesn't really teach, but intro to micro isn't that difficult. She gives out a lot of extra credit and the exams are moderately difficult. However, she assigns tons of (busywork) homework that can be hard to remember to submit and you need them for your grade.

If you actually want to learn something in microeconomics, then you should choose Professor Bandy! She is really caring and completely accessible outside the lesson. She cares a lot about whether you fully understand one concept, and her lessons are really fun!

She gets a lot of hate, but she's honestly one of my favorite professors. She's funny (even though her humor seems to go over a lot of people's heads), and while some say she is hard to understand at times, if you seek 1 on 1 help things will become clear. Would skim through lecture slides before each exam and had no issues getting good grades

She's highkey funny but like nobody in my class laughed. Ultimately, if you've never taken micro before it'll be a bit challenging and you'll need to like be a good student, but Bandy is supportive and helpful.

Professor Bandy is not at all as bad as some people make her seem. She sometimes over-explains concepts, but other than that her lectures are engaging and clear. I think microeconomics can be more easily understood if you have experience in calculus and macroeconomics, but it isn't necessary. Test are extremely easy if you study.

Bandy gets a bad rep, but I didn't dislike her at all. Her class is fairly difficult, and her explanations can leave the class confused often, but she truly cares and tries her best. She is a very lively person, and she's not afraid to crack a joke. My advice is to read the module in the textbook before class so you have a better understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bandy's lectures are in-depth, though admittedly, often leave the class confused. Push through the discomfort! I think everyone in that class experiences a point where they don't understand the material: it's hard for Bandy to explain things because a lot of it IS supposed to be very intuitive. Read the textbook if you have to, most people didn't!
So funny and awesome
Poor lecturer in terms of learning, but entertaining. Tests are manageable as the grading curve is very forgiving. Lots of homework
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you have no experience with microeconomics, avoid this class at all costs. Tests are atrocious and poorly designed. They don't test you on your understanding, but rather your test taking skills. Lectures are super confusing  and useless, she explains simple concepts in the most complicated way. I should have read the reviews before signing up.

Bandy's lectures can be confusing, but she's approachable and genuinely cares about student success. The material is challenging, but using the textbook, study resources like Unstuckstudy, and attending office hours can really help. Overall, a rewarding class if you're willing to put in the work.

I wouldn't say that this class is very difficult but if you have no background in economics I would not recommend. The lectures are a bit confusing so you may end up having to teach yourself the material but outside of that she provides good extra credit opportunity.

Don't take this class with bandy if you have no experience with econ. Lectures are super unclear and exams are way too difficult. It's hard to be prepared for exams because you really never know what's going to be on them. She makes sure she's very available for questions and office hours but this still doesn't help.

Bandy is very nice, and she clearly cares a lot about teaching and wants her students to succeed. However, if you've never taken econ and want to actually learn, don't take this class with her. Lectures are useless and incredibly difficult to follow, and the only way to learn or understand anything is by reading the textbook.

I don't think she's quite as bad or as strict as her reputation makes her seem, she made a lot of jokes and was pretty accommodating. Like, she's not trying to make students miserable or make the class ridiculously hard. However, I think her lectures would be much more difficult for people who haven't taken economics before (such as AP)

Bandy clearly cares a lot about teaching, but her lectures were the opposite of good teaching. The examples were difficult to follow, and she would rarely answer student questions, instead she would interrupt the student and further confuse them. Final was very difficult. I switched the class to P/F early on. Very nice in office hours though!

Bandy's not the best lecturer by any means, but you can tell that she's passionate about teaching economics and wants her students to succeed. Extremely accessible outside of class. Her exams are definitely harder than you'd expect but they're still fair and provided a great foundation for Intermediate Micro. Overall, I think she's overhated.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was scared to take this class because Bandy has such a bad wrap. But she was a good professor, really passionate about subject matter and available to help students outside of class. Exams/quizzes were overall fair, but final was pretty rough. She also gives generous extra credit for coming to class.

Bandy always seems to get a bad rep... but she is the best teacher I had this semester. She is the funniest person and she brings such an authentic presence to each of her class.I was so scared coming in, but her class completely disproved me. The class is extremely doable and she makes her self available to her students. Don't listen to others.

Had her for micro and she was always great. Interacts with students, willing to work with you if you missed an assignment deadline, and responds very quickly to emails. Exams are tough tough, she makes you work for it. Made the final unnecessarily challenging. Attendance is optional but you do get extra credit (2% extra for missing 6 or fewer).

A character but average professor. Lectures are dry and draining, but she's enthusiastic about questions and is accessible outside class. I never took econ in HS, so there was a learning period-- I should've worked more outside class, though. Overall, I enjoyed the material and am still very happy with how I did, but Bandy has room for improvement.

I loved this professor. She was caring, funny, and made lectures really interesting. While she's not always the most articulate in explaining Microeconomic concepts, I nonetheless loved the opportunity to take her class!

Anyone who took Econ in high school will find this course easy and fair to get an A. However, if you have never taken Econ before, this class is gonna hurt you. Her final is atrocious so, hopefully try to get better grades in the first two exams. Never take this course for humanities credit, go for macro.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't let the rating deter you away from this class. Bandy is honestly a good professor. Just review the lectures after every class, and you'll be fine. The exams are super fair.

I LOVE Bandy. She is just such a lovely person. Yes, she's not the best lecturer, but she really does try her best. She is always there for her students and genuinely cares about them. If you're interested in economics PLEASE take classes with her.
Funniest professor and gives extra credit for attendance
Love Bandy. Epic class.

Bandy's Canvas has a lot of resources, she's easily accessible, and she communicates a lot through Canvas announcements, she just can't teach AT ALL; my friend who took econ in HS said that Bandy's explanations even made her confused. 

Don't take if you're only doing it for the AN credit, take macro instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty funny, wants you to do well, but she's been teaching so long she sometimes gets confused if you don't understand something right away. Lectures are fast, so I'd read the textbook either before or after. People complain about the class/exams but I felt that it was fair. Put in the time/effort to actually understand stuff and you'll be fine.

Decently funny professor and the material is not that hard, though I would not recommend you only listen to the lectures. Use online resources as well (of which there are many because this is a basic course). Sometimes the tests can be a bit confusing.

Very difficult if not experienced in econ. Don't take if you're looking for an introduction to economics. The lectures are too confusing, difficult to understand, and the textbook is unhelpful. Exams are only easy if you understand the lectures, and even after attending office hours I've left more confused. I would not recommend the clas
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Her lectures are very confusing and she talks in circles. Reading the textbook after attending the lectures only made the material harder to understand. She likes to say "Folks, this won't be on the PowerPoint or in the textbook so pay attention" :(
If you took econ in HS, this course would probably be a lot easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: comprehensive
she is just legit endless yapping

Lectures were REALLY hard to follow, don't take her if you have no econ experience. Got through the class only by common sense. She spent half the class complaining about lack of student participation and asking "why is your generation so sad? + the other half writing useless confusing examples. Extra credit for attendance was a decent cushion.

A very down to Earth professor. Despite the poor reputation, she genuinely cares for her students. Econ is not a sexy subject, as she would say, so it is understandable that class can sometimes be boring. The attendance requirement is quite lax and allows for two whole weeks of absences. Makes herself very accessible before tests!

Bandy made this class as easy as she possibly could for people (cutting a unit, pushing back due dates, etc.). She's honestly really funny, but she will demand that you participate in the lectures and sometimes is a little confusing explaining things. Plus, the slides are full of text which made it hard to take notes.

There are only two tests, which makes the course very test heavy. The lectures can be rather dry, but this is just the nature of Macroeconomics. The professor tries very hard to make class more interesting by being energetic. Study hard for tests and you will be fine.
Bandy's lectures are great, interesting, and funny. She references the textbook sometimes but you definitely don't need to buy it

Took both macro and micro with Bandy. She isn't super good at lecturing, but I appreciate the effort she puts to make sure students are engaged. I wish there had been more to cushion your grade in case you have a bad grade, but otherwise neither class was particularly difficult and definitely prepared me for upper level classes.

I thought prof Bandy was really good. She's a funny person, and lectures are informative. Also, she gave like 3% extra credit for showing up to class enough times and filling out her course eval, and she gave bonus points on the midterm and final. I don't think she deserves the rep she gets.

Attendance is not really mandatory. You can earn extra credits by attending a certain number of lectures.
She does not explain things clearly enough.

Professor Bandyopadhyay is fun to talk to but don't ever take her class unless you have already done economics. She is bad at explaining concepts and then she blames the students for not being smart enough. I like how she uses real world examples to describe things though!

You will have to purchase TopHat for this course, which is $30, in order to submit many assignments and verify attendance. Quizzes, homeworks, and exams are relatively easy with no surprises if you attend the lectures. The expensive textbook is not required.

Wish attendance hadn't affected grades because I would've learned better from reading the textbook in my own time. Lectures were unnecessarily complicated, and homework questions didn't always line up with what lecture material. I wouldn't take micro with her unless you need it for your major. The final wasn't super easy to study for.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't understand why Bandy gets so much flack. She's always on top of her email, updating canvas, sending announcements when a deadline changes, etc. Her guidelines initially seemed strict but they weren't a big deal. She makes her lectures entertaining, even if they're confusing sometimes. Plus, there's a lot of extra credit.

This class was a constant headache for my friends and me. Lectures were boring and confusing. Tests and quizzes were hard although there are lots of opportunities to earn points elsewhere. READ THE TEXTBOOK and you will get by. In the end, I would strongly advise against taking this class unless it is required for your major/minor.

sometimes her lectures don't make much sense. but a lot of the time, they do. gives a lot of extra credit / participation points it is impossible to get below a b. the very hilarious lady made my year. just do the work actually and you will be set.
Take Econ 1011 in the spring.

Although Bandy's lecture may not be one of the best at WashU, she really tries to help her students and lets her students learn. I got five on both AP Micro and Macro so this class is easy for me, but I do understand why her reputation is not good and sometimes her lecture can be very confusing.
She is a terrible lecturer and admitted to purposefully confusing students in lecture. She is impatient and makes the material more difficult than needed. The final was completely unreasonable.

Everyone failed the midterm, so she asked the class what she could differently so that students actually learn. Many students gave good feedback on what she could change to benefit us. She then told everyone that it's their own fault because the new generation is always on their phones and we are getting dumber year by year. Changed nothing.

I really liked micro with Bandy, but you have to approach her class in a certain way. I read the textbook for every chapter, which makes her lectures make a lot of sense. Her reputation isn't great, but I really think that's overblown. She takes the time to make sure each of her students understands, and her class is interesting and worth taking.
The final caught me very off guard, and her lectures are tough to follow.

Hot take: Bandy is overhated. She is a pretty terrible lecturer (I never went to class, attendance wasn't mandatory when I took ECON1011), but if you follow along with the videos she makes and her slide decks, you'll be fine. I never opened the textbook, but some people find it helpful. Stay on top of Tophat work and slide decks and you'll be fine.

Lectures are mediocre. She's a funny person but isn't the best at teaching concepts and the point of the material. Exams are somewhat difficult but don't be surprised if there is something you have never seen before on there. Best bet is to read the textbook.

Take this class at your local college/uni or take it with a different professor at WashU. Do anything and everything in your power to avoid taking a class with Bandy. Worst lecturer here, not sure how she got hired. Her explanations make you more confused. Best bet is to learn everything on your own and zone out during her lectures.
The worst teacher I ever had. The worst lectures I ever had. Please do not take this class with her.
She is such a gem in WashU professors. Take her and get your best life at WashU.

Bandy is great. I honestly think her bad ratings are exclusively from exceptionally stupid kids. This is micro econ. If you fail micro econ it is not Bandy's fault. This class is so easy that if you have any common sense you could pass with no instruction at all. That said, her lectures are great and she is hilarious.

This is a very unpopular opinion but I enjoyed Bandy's intro to Micro. The content is very easy and the work is set up for your success. I didn't buy or open the textbook and still did very well in the class. She can definitely ramble in lectures and posts notes via long videos but overall a friendly teacher that wants students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take a class with Bandy. I read the textbook and watched all her lecture videos and her midterm was still impossible. She's not good at explaining concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bandy's midterm is hard indeed, but her final is extremely easy. Go to lectures, do homework and quizzed, and go to office hours helps a lot. She may be a bit intimidating at first, but she tries to improve and she's a kind lady. Her lecture may not be clear but are not terrible. Study hard and you will get an A.

Even though she's taught this class for years, her explanation of concepts and her answers to questions were poor. If you study the homeworks, quizzes, and textbook you'll do well. The midterm this year was harder than expected, but the final was decent if you studied.

I do not recommend ever taking a class with Bandy. I had to teach myself everything because she did a poor job at teaching and would just post lecture videos to watch. Half of the grade is from 2 exams, which are much more difficult than any of the practices and are very poorly written, which I found to be very unfair. Overall, awful professor.

Prof. Bandy clearly cares about her students and does her best to make sure everyone understands the material. It was painfully clear that many people were not bothering to use the various resources she provided then proceeded to complain about their grades and bash her. She may rush or be blunt but she actively tries to accommodate students.

Not a good professor and DO NOT take her. This year she gives us tons of lecture videos to watch, which were recorded by her in 2019, but the exams are way harder than those of 2019. Her videos are just reading slides, and even make concepts much complicated to understand than just reading the textbook.
I don't know where the 5 point ratings come from. Probably from her TAs honestly. I'm sorry but she really doesn't make things learnable for studetns, and students are better off self-studying.

General Chemistry aka one of the hardest classes in WashU is not even nearly as hard as Bandy. She explains so poorly that you have to learn everything on your own, AND tests are hard If you go to her for a question, it's likely that you will be more confused than the moment you came bc she loses patience so quickly & won't take time to elaborate
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: course content isn't too bad and all lectures are posted online so class attendance isn't necessary. However, she goes out of her way to be nasty to students then talks about how her kids love her so she cant be a bad person. Ultra self-righteous so avoid conflict at all costs.

Bandy is a joke. She didnt even begin to somewhat try to teach us until over half her class failed the midterm. She now pretends to care when thats obviously not the case. At one point said if we couldnt answer a specific question, then we dont belong at WashU. I felt welcome after that!

In my personal experience, if you read the textbook (!!!) and watch the pre-recorded videos, you will do fine. You can't just waltz through the class - you have to put work in. But if you do what she tells you to do, you will be fine. Bandy has a good sense of humor but it can come off a little harsh. She cares about students though.

Horrible professor. My whole class failed the midterm because she couldn't teach or answer questions clearly. Super long tests with improperly worded questions. Takes 5 minutes just to try to figure out what she is asking.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horrible lecturer, doesn't answer questions. You leave the class feeling worse than you did before you walked in. Ridicules students for asking questions, and tells them that they have to learn it on their own. Do NOT take a class with Bandy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly the worst professor I've ever had. I've never written on Rate my Professor but feel the need to with this professor. She makes concepts unnecessarily difficult and more confusing. She moves way too quickly through concepts and never really breaks them down in an understandable way. The midterm exam was like taking the ACT.

Prof. Bandy really cares about the success of her students but is a strict grader. If you know how to look at simple graphs write out the graphs to answer the exam questions you will do fine in the class.

Lecture's are mediocre but the content is not too difficult. Just read the summary of the chapters and you'll know 90% of what you need to know. She has an abrasive personality which some might find funny and some annoying. Overall, not bad if you put in 1.5 to 3 hours a week. Not much homework either.

Professor Bandy is super fierce and aggressive and will berate you for asking questions to the point that no one does. She is not a bad human, just a bad intro to micro professor. You should get ready to use a lot of external help from TAs or the internet if you want to understand material and pass
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bandy is really funny but save yourself the torture and don't take her class. She ridicules people who ask questions during class and it is so hard to learn the material when all of the lectures are just hours of prerecorded videos and excessively long readings. This class is very exam-heavy so if you do not do well on the exams, you're screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved having Bandy as my Econ teacher! I had her for Micro and liked her so much I made sure she was my teacher for Macro as well. Very funny and always willing to help/answer questions if you ask.

Great and very funny teacher! The content of intro level classes is never that interesting so the class may feel content heavy but if you attend lectures and do the homework you should have no trouble getting an A. Bandy made the content fun and I would definitely recommend her as an Econ teacher!
Terrible professor do not take any of her classes
Bandy is possibly the worst professor known to mankind.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This teacher does not know how to teach. This year 2021 fall we are learning everything on canvas, through her recorded videos. Basically is a self-study online class, except that it's not even real time, interacting, learning. I just find it daunting to ask her question because she always seem so aggresive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She rambles off a lot during class but she tries... at least during class. Oh and do your homework.
very exam heavy with a few chances of extra credit. not a nice or understanding woman at all.

She is a pretty average professor. She basically just reads off the powerpoint slides. The class Itself is not that difficult and if you follow along with her notes and slides, then you will do well on the exams. The textbook is useful if you don't understand the lecture slides, but other than that you don't really need It.

Bandy, as students call her is really not a good teacher. There are times when she can be funny in class but most of the time I choose not to go to class because she overcomplicates and rushes through the material, expecting you to learn it on your own. She makes you read so much and watch lecture videos literally before coming to lecture. Not good
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, final is extremely easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of people don't like her, but I personally find her class amusing. She's extremely funny and wants us to succeed. Sometimes she's bad at explaining specific concepts but she will always help you in office hours. Overall, a solid professor

I definitely struggled in Bandy's class, but she does know her stuff. Her lectures can be confusing, especially if you have no prior experience in economics. A well-respected professor, for sure (nearly everyone knows her), but if you're not passionate about the subject, I would avoid sheerly due to the amount of studying expected of you.

Bandy's a tough one. I had her for Intro to Micro. While I enjoyed the content, I learned most of it through reading the textbook, because her lectures tended to be very confusing and didn't do a good job of explaining the material. She does give lots of extra credit though. I wouldn't recommend her if you have other options.

You should read the textbook to understand the content because she moves through information very fast. It is not her fault, that is just the nature of the course. You do not need to have taken Econ in high school before, but if you did not, be prepared to work. Overall, I am glad I took this class for the content I learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really am not a fan of her lectures despite her being a really solid person. Thought the class was fairly difficult until the end when I realized my grades were pretty solid. Have to study for the exams and do fairly easy homework and you'll be fine. Classic "if you don't show up it's hard, if you show up it's pretty easy" class.

Bandy is one of the sweetest professors I know. Her class is pretty easy and she has very clear grading criteria. Honestly if you show up to class, pay attention and do the readings regularly you'll be fine for the exams and quizzes. There's also tons of multiple choice problems on the internet that you can use to practice for the exams.
The hardest class Ive ever taken. The material isnt hard but she is a horrible teacher and Econ math is hard to learn from a textbook. She puts the hardest examples on the test also.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Bandyopadhyay is a solid lecturer. Attendance is extra credit. I had never taken a economics class before but am now considering a major in it. The first day of class, Bandy lays out the expectations for the class and follows them. She will grade two different ways and take the better of the two.

Her 1011 and 1021 are easy A classes, but her lectures are nonsense. Always talks about things not that relevant to class, and says "Are you with me?" when students get really bored. She does not really care if she gives good lectures. Would recommend for whoever needs social science credits, but really boring.

I found myself having to use online materials and videos and the book to actually understand the concepts because the lectures weren't helpful or clear to me. But I have no background in Econ and it didn't come super easily for me, so others may be able to understand the lectures. And there is extra credit for attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures were awful, she would get off topic then ask if everyone was still with her. No one would answer. She was not very nice either calling out individual students in large lecture halls. Once she made a student leave class because he did not know the answer to a question. Go to class for extra credit but would avoid her class if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I understand why Bandy has mixed reviews. Honestly lectures are boring, and I don't think she's outstanding at communicating the necessary material. However, she is very fair, you know what you will be tested on, and she added extra credit for attendance. She teaches the material, if you learn it you'll do well, if not she won't feel sorry for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She simply fails to explain anything and assumes that everyone understands what she is talking about. Do not take this class unless you have taken both micro and macro and have mastered the material. I can count the things I learned in class on one hand, but still go to class for the 2 percentage points of extra credit.
She's a really engaging lecturer; everyone should experience Bandy once at washu. If you go to class and do the readings, you should do fine in this class.

Honestly my favorite professor so far at WashU. She made class enjoyable and coming from someone with no economics experience in high school, I found the material straight forward even though it required some outside reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Does a poor job of teaching an introductory class. She speeds through lecture material as if students are already familiar with the info she's covering and just confuses you more. Would not recommend taking a class with her if you've never taken econ before.

She goes way too fast in class, assuming that you already know what is being taught in class. Bandy calls out students in class and forces them to ask questions. She is a bully and does not want students to do well. Bandy intimidates students and makes them feel stupid and afraid to ask for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Here's the deal. She is simply the sweetest professor who wants her students to do well, but her style of lecturing to large rooms makes it difficult to pay attention and take notes. She's extremely fair, and everything is specified in advance. You're graded 95% based on 2-3 exams, so do as well as you can on those.
She's such a mom, I love her. Grading is super clear and she offers some extra credit. She does tend to over-explain sometimes, but she's actually the nicest so just ask her to clarify.

If you're looking to learn the basics of Microeconomics in a nurturing, hand-holding setting, you've come to the wrong place! From what I've seen, the kids who are either math majors or who have had prior exposure to Economics (ex: AP Econ in high school) are the only ones who get As in the class. It's fast-paced; get ready to teach yourself.
Honestly made the class more difficult than it needed to be. Tests were difficult to prepare for and lectures were boring and drawn out.

After all of the horror stories I've heard about Bandy being unreasonable, unfair, and even cruel, I'm shocked to hear that others think she cares about the success of her students. I can't disagree more. She takes an easy subject and somehow makes it confusing. So don't take the risk - it's not worth the GPA hit - and avoid her class at all costs.

Do not take this class. The exams are difficult, unfair, and worth a huge portion if your grade. Lectures do not make sense and are extremely difficult to follow. If you have no economics background this class will be terrible. The professor is not interested in the success of the students and does not curve the exams or release the averages.

The morning of the first midterm for this course, my hometown, Santa Rosa was engulfed by the largest wildfire in CA's history. I asked if I could take the test the next day because I could not stop crying or focus. She did not allow me to do this because she said it was not an emergency. She cares very little about the wellbeing of her students
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is helpful and willing to answer question, but her class is not organized at all, even though she has some jokes. Her class was no more difficult than AP material. Even if you do not come to class(lose all attendance points) , you will still get A if you read the ppt and book.

She moves really fast through the material in lecture, so if you get confused, you better read the book, use office hours, or ask questions in class. It is not looked upon kindly if you fall behind and go to her with tons of questions before a test. Luckily, she knows her stuff, is super accessible, a funny woman and wants to see students succeed.
Just study in advance
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Probably partly due to the subject matter, but I found her lectures to be dry and hard to pay attention to. She can be funny, but that's more at the beginning of class before getting into the day's material. She drops an exam from your grade, which helps, but I found 2 out of the 3 exams to be tough.  About 4% total extra credit is available.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I'm glad I took AP Micro/Macro in high school, because it was the only way I was able to do well.  This class killed my interest in the subject. Bandy yelled at us ("Are you following me?!") as she jumped from topic to topic, skipping through slides and struggling with chalkboards.  Paying attention in lecture was painful, and I stopped attending.

Bandy is definitely a good professor, but I had to look to outside resources to hear the material a second time. She could be a lot more clear in lecture, but she cares about student learning, and she's good in Office hours. She wants you to do well, and if you put in the work, you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher. Funny at times. Knows what she is doing. The class is hard, but she tries to make it easier.

Bandy is an amazing human being, but it's really hard to pay attention to her lectures. The class is easy if you can stay awake and pay attention, but otherwise you are forced to rely on the book. She gives great life advice and says some hilarious things, but is really hard to follow when she starts drawing on the board.
Boring lectures, but is very informative.  Clearly teaches everything that she tests you on and encourages collaboration.  Overall a good teacher and an easy class.

Had her for both 1011 and 1021. Super easy classes. As a professor she's really funny and nice (kinda feisty too), but isn't the best at teaching large lectures. Her lectures are super boring but there's random attendance that's worth extra credit so go. She's really good 1:1 though, so go to her office hours for help.  Prepare to read textbook.

In my personal opinion, Bandy's lectures are not the most helpful guides to learning the material. Her lectures come straight from the textbook, but she rushes through the material quite quickly during her lectures. Reading the textbook gave me a much better grasp on the material. She gets snappy and accusatory during lecture as well

Bandy is very feisty. She does random attendance days for a grade, otherwise you could honestly get by with just the textbook and slides. I always fell asleep in her class... I struggled at first but learned to actually study; went from a C to an A-. She definitely wants to help, but can come across as kind of intimidating (in a motherly way).
Lectures are very informative! I attended all of the lectures, and never even had to open the textbook for the class.

Great person but not that great of a professor; she often overcomplicates things and either goes too fast or too slow. Lectures aren't really worth going to so you should plan on just reading the textbook. Midterms are not easy; got a 5 on AP micro but didn't do that well in her class.
Bandy was amazing. Favorite teacher I've had and tests are straight forward.
Will go out of her way to help students and is very friendly.  Lectures are long and similar to textbook.

She is very very funny, but her lectures aren't the most helpful. Good thing is you can learn everything you need to know for exams from reading the textbook/lecture slides. Shouldn't be too hard to get an A in this class as long as you read everything before the test.

Bandy is a mixed bag. She's super funny at times and can be very helpful if you seek it out (check out the online handouts for chapters!), but her lectures can be both boring and confusing. Exams aren't so bad, but reading the textbook or at least the slides is crucial.

I had her for both Intro to Micro and Intro to Macro. She's funny during class, but I only went to lecture because she took attendance as extra credit.   Most of the time I fell asleep because I was so bored.  You could really just learn everything from the textbook if you wanted to. She's not a very good teacher in lecture, but much better 1-on-1.

Bandy is possibly the best teacher I've ever had. She does everything she possible can to make sure every single student understands. Ask her for help and you will get it. Plus she's pretty hilarious sometimes.
She wasn't helpful at all and the tests were confusing.

The class is easy. Bandy's lectures are incredibly boring though. I learned all of the material by reading the book. I would never have gone to class if she hadn't occasionally taken attendance. She's an alright person, but she's bad at teaching.
Helpful, approachable, clear, and genuinely funny.

The class is not that hard. Teacher is very understanding, and her grading system is extremely fair. She likes when students ask her questions in class, and has a strange, funny sense of humor. Sometimes she isn't very clear and a little boring, but overall good

She is a really funny person and absolutely adorable. You can tell that she really cares about her students and that she wishes the classes weren't so big so that she could get to know people better. I went to her many times for help and she was always willing and helpful. Class is pretty boring but I think she did her best given the material

I took Econ 1011, 1021, and 380 all with professor Bandy. She kept most topics fairly interesting and was concerned for students. I enjoyed all three of her classes and she maintained a welcoming classroom environment. For grading, attendance is solely extra credit and grades are heavily determined by a small amount of exams.

She can be quite funny and passionate, but it doesn't make up for often-tedious classes. Sometimes I have no idea what is being discussed in class. That being said, your grade doesn't require much effort to keep up.
Very helpful. Funny too!

Better to just read textbook and not even pay attention/go to class. She basically just rushes through each chapter in class and you need to read the chapter on your own anyway. At least she's nice and tries to inject a little humor into class. Generous with extra credit also. Final was WAY easier than 2 MTs.

As hard as she tries to make students "understand" rather than "memorize," powerpoints, the textbook, and her quizzes lend absolutely no help in answering the types of questions on her examinations. Even practice exams have completely different problems than the actual exam.

She moves through material quickly and, as much as she may try, she doesn't always do a great job of explaining things. She also makes her exams much harder than her practice tests/quizzes. Powerpoints come straight from the book, yet I still found the book to be much more helpful than her lectures.
Not a fan of her teaching style, but she is pretty funny.
Extremely nice and very willing to help
Bandy is the greatest.
Awesome.
She's amazing and always willing to help. She has a fun sense of humor and makes the 1.5 hour classes go by more quickly!

As long as you read the textbook, attend class, and take note of what Bandy teaches that is not in the textbook, you will be fine.  Bandy is entertaining, helpful, and more than willing to help outside of class. Plus, extra take-home quizzes result in extra credit, which is nice. As Bandy emphasizes, make sure you UNDERSTAND, not just memorize
Professor Bandy is so good. If you need microeconomics, you should definitely take it from her. She teaches you more than just the textbook. She makes economics pertinent to all other subjects.

Bandyopadhay is an entertaining professor. She's very amiable, down-to-earth, and extremely easy to learn from. Her system is clear and student-friendly, and she's very available. A simple 15-question multiple-choice take-home quiz is given weekly, in addition to two midterms and a final. If you pay attention and/or read, you'll do well.
Take her.. she is wonderful.. to bad she is leaving WVU

You can conceivably miss all of her classes except the exam day and still pass/receive an A. However, the material was extremely foreign to me, making studying on my own was difficult... It might help a lot to go to class. Although I only went three times outside of test days, I lucked out with a C.
most boring worst teacher ever

This class is extremely easy anyway, but especially with her.  She's also super nice and quite entertaining at times.  No need to buy the book either as long as you have her notes unless you just want it.
She is a good teacher, but I didn't really unsterdand much until I read the book.
she is so funny!!! really easy gonig and honestly cares if you are understanding the lecture. go to class and read the power points for the exams. not too bad
It wasn't that bad. The test were just rediculously hard.  I didn't like this class, although she was a nice woman.

She makes it as easy as possible for you to get and A or a passing grade. She is one of the nicest teachers you will EVER have at WVU! There is absolutely NO DOUBT that if you need to take this class take it with her!!! *Not actually hot :)
Easiest class at WVU

Dr. Bandy was a great teacher. She tries her best to help you understand the concepts of economics. I thought I would get a C because of mid term grades, but ended up with an A in the class. Gives some extra credit. Definitely take her class!

She is very helpful and giving! 5% Bonus is available as long as you get 1 question right on the online quizes. Then if you bomb your tests she will count your grade from your best test score! She even lowered the grading scale. An 85 was an A, I got an 83 with the bonus.  I am more pissed at myself for letting an easy A slip away.
She does everything she can to make sure the students underatand the material. She gives extra credit, and attendance doesn't count. She is a really great teacher!
Awsome! Loved her! Easy class! Learned alot!
She definately wants you to understand the material and do well in the class. She gives 5% extra credit added to your final grade just for taking quizzes.
awesome teacher, my fave in 3 years at wvu

bandy is awesome! attendence doesnt matter, and all that does is the final exam... she usually gives 2/3 big tests and a final exam.  if your final test grade is better than your class grade, then what you got on your final is your final grade. make sense? all in all shes awesome! she gives extra credit too.
Worst teacher ever. Could not understand a word she said and didnt teach the class she just read off of power point

Horrible teacher, impossible to understand when she talks, Mock Exams dont help. very strict with grading scale. 79.44 doesn't get you a B you need the 79.5. she wont listen if you try to talk grades to her
She is a great teacher. One of my favorites at WVU. She really cares about the students and loves what she teaches. She tries to make the class fun and interesting.

She was real funny, and she seemed to have a passion to teach.  She gave lots of extra points, quiz's, study groups.  The class was way to big and testing days were crazy with all those people.  Sit near the front because people in the back talk and you can't hear her.
No Comments
boring

Very nice & helpful at all times!  Class is tough, but she gives you numerous chances to help yourself raise your gade. ex: Up to 5 pure bonus points for taking quizzes throughout semester & if you do better on the final than your 3 regular test average, your final counts as your grade.

She is the funniest woman EVER! She's a great teacher, really really wants her students to do well - will do anything she can to help. Class is hard though, you MUST work for the A. Liked her so much I'm taking her again for 202!

I thought the class was extremely easy and she's the most caring teacher on campus. I never opened my book. I got A's on every exam by reviewing each Webct quiz(which is bonus) and the mock exams for 15 minutes each. The tests are like the mock exams and overall you get 5% added for doing quizzes.
No Comments

I think Sudeshna is one of the most heart-felt teachers that I have encountered in my college experience. She is always willing to help you understand. The class isn't easy, but she will do what she can to make you understand. She tries very hard and is good at her job.

Sudeshna is an excellent teacher. If you go to her class everyday and  read a little bit,you will can do well.  You will not do well because the class is hard but her teaching makes up for it. She is very nice and easy to understand. 1 of my fav. teachers and i don't like teachers.
She's a good teacher, but if you dont have the dicipline to read and study on your own time withouht specific things being assigned don't take her
Great teacher who is always willing to help. She grades fairly and gives extra credit quizzes. Highly recommended.

If I studied and/or went to class, it would be very easy. Offers up to 5% extra credit for taking quizzes!!! If you do poorly on midterms, the final grade could be your overall, so don't worry too much. Very nice lady and easy to understand. She's definately there to help!
Bandy will go to painstaking lengths to make sure that you understand the material and explains concepts well.  She also cancels class a lot...which makes me smile.

She isnt hard to understand at all. She is a really kool lady and no one is going to be easy in econ. Its just a tough subject, but she really puts forth effort and tries to help you out. The exams are a little 2 hard but other than that she is a fun lady to take.
Funny, Easy to understand.  Notes are on powerpoint.  Gives mock exam which really helps.  Would Recommend!
Acccent was not bad.  Explains concepts well.  Fairly easy class.
She was VERY hard to understand. I don't think I would have done so poorly if the class room setting was smaller.
No Comments
(First of all... her name is spelled wrong)  I just wanted to say that she is NOT difficult to understand... her accent isn't strong at all.  Very helpful, nice, and funny.
She says the funniest stuff!!
No Comments
She is impossible to understand... in addition to her dialect. Get somebody for students to relate to!

One of the best poli sci professors at WashU. Really knowledgeable about his work and cares about student success. Classes are structured well but lots of individual work needed to keep up. Fair tests and projects; none of them are tedious or super hard. Attendance is tracked though it may not seem like it.

Professor Betz is clearly incredibly passionate about the topic and super accessible. There are so many TAs for this class and they are genuinely helpful, go to office hours if you're struggling. I would recommend the class with Betz to any poli-sci or non poli-sci student.

This class was unbelievably difficult and unorganized. It's required for the poli sci major so there's no way around it but it is tough to get through. Betz is a really nice guy but his class is terrible.
Genuinely a great guy, but his class was unbelievably disorganized.

Rating Chem 481:
Tim is smart, but he expects too much from his students. He covers multiple chapters of a textbook in 1 lecture and is ambiguous about what will be covered on the exams. The entire Biochem 1/2 series is an absolute mess and the only way to succeed is to memorize the textbook.

Professor Wencewicz brings enthusiasm and curiosity to every lecture. He is an expert in antibiotics and bioorganic chemistry, running a research lab in the field. Start the paper early and seek feedback often. Even from just attending lecture and reading the textbook, you will learn so much from this class. The paper is just the cherry on top.

Prof W is ok, but I do not think he knows how to challenge students or he does not teach us how to think about orgo. Work load was reasonable & exams were straight forward. This year was a big letdown after taking two incredible semesters of Gen Chem. I now see why so many WU students take Organic over the summer elsewhere.

Professor Wencewicz presented every reaction with excitement and was always doing his best to keep us engaged. My favorite part was at the end of every chapter, he would highlight how the reactions and processes we learned about are used in biological systems. He worked hard to be sure we understood the material and were prepared for every exam.
Really inspiring person who brings Organic Chemistry to life
Took Orgo II as well as Bioorganic Chem with him. Super nice guy, good lecturer, clear expectations. If you need to take a chem elective, take Bioorganic with him for sure.

Orgo is always hard. That said, Wencewicz gives you every opportunity to succeed.  Make sure to understand every reaction written on the board. For the final grade, he considers every individual. Did you improve throughout the semester? One bad test? etc. Finally, watching recorded lectures is way more effective than going to class.
Not very accessible outside of class but a really nice guy. Decent lecturer -- about as good as it gets for orgo. More organized than my 261 teacher

While Professor Wencewicz is not the most exciting professor, and his lectures are quite long, he is a fair test writer and sets a generous curve.  He is also very helpful in his office hours.  Reading the textbook (carefully) and doing the book problems help immensely with the exams.
His lectures are relatively boring and long.  However, his exams are very straight forward and easy if you put in the work.
Great class! I took bioorganic chemistry, and it was all based on antibiotics. There are a couple recommended textbooks, but there are also a lot of literature papers provided.

Good class. Rubrics are clear and specific. Not hard if you show up and do the work. Group project is heavily weighted and at the end of the semester. Don't wait until the last minute or the end of the semester to use the TAs. Highly recommend office hours too.

One of the worst professors I've had, told our group one thing and graded on another criteria. Two faced professor who's feedback is redundant and would never have any real improvement on the grade/project.

People who want to learn love this class. If you think you're already a good communicator, you'll hate it. Classic example: 
Student - "I'm just surprised by this grade because my high school is known for producing great academic writers." 
Prof. T - "I can tell, but I don't need an academic writer. I need a business writer."
Listen and it's great!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Full of busywork and subjective grading; unwilling to work with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Deceiving with grades, rude to students, unapproachable, and unfair. Avoid her classes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Worst professor in Olin. Terrible grader and comes off as nice but is not genuine and fair with her grading at all. Would recommend taking the course with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I'm still in this class, but I like it a lot. Prof Thomas is really engaging, and the class has tons of activities so the time goes by really quickly. You definitely need to do the prework, because she's not going to cover it in calss, and you're responsible for it.

The class itself may not be the most useful, but Staci is a fun teacher to have. She tries to make the class engaging and enjoyable. If you put the effort in, you will definitely become a more effective presenter and communicator.

What you put in is what you get out. Students who weren't satisfied with Staci were the type to think this was going to be an easy class (or that it should be). Put in the work and go to office hours if you're frustrated in the slightest.

I really liked Staci! She's very sweet and tries her best to make lectures as engaging as possible. This class helped me with my presentation skills, and the TAs as well as Staci were extremely nice! The class is very dependent on the final client project, which varies in difficulty. However, a lot of the content for the course is pretty useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst professors I have encountered at WashU. Before I took this class, I had heard from other students about her bad reputation for being unfair and fresh, but I took the course anyways. She seems to have some superiority complex over her students and talks down on them instead of trying to have a civil conversation.

She was absolutely amazing. I learned so much from her but she made it easy, digestible, and enjoyable. She loves participation and will provide so much help if you go to her office hours especially early on. She is a teacher I will never forget and am so grateful I had.

This entire class is busy work. The career unit is helpful but after that, the class essentially teaches you how to be a consultant which is annoying if that's not your thing. Be warned: the client project is a lot more work than you're expecting and you better pray for a good group. Staci is great though (if you're on her good side!)

She is very indirect with some of her comments until you see the grade in the assignment. Most of the time, it is her way or no way. The workload was ok, but a lot of it felt useless, and your grade in the final project heavily relies on who you get as teammates.
Favorite class!!!

She tells us exactly what she wants in the rubric and is super nice! I did poorly at first bc I forgot to read the rubric but once you do its an easy A tbh. a lot of writing but lots of time in class to get it done!

The course structure needs to be redesigned. You have to do a lot of busy work that has little to do with improving your networking skills and securing a job. I do not mind the considerable time commitment, but the lack of real-world relevance and highly subjective grading criteria hinder the overall experience.
My mother told me if I don't have anything to say, don't say it all…
I hate this class it is a complete waste of time and it is very time consuming. It is literally forcing us to be pretentious consultants.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: this is a 4 credit course, so the workload is heavier than other courses. Rubrics are provided, 2 TAs per class, and a willingness to meet with students whenever. If you don't pass this class, it's totally on you. There is some busy work, but it's about YOU (complete a psychometric, do your resume), so it's all helpful.

Picks favorites. You have to follow exactly what she tells you, otherwise, your grade is impacted. Very much so her way or the highway. Not too hard to do well in the class and some content was useful.
Amazing professor!!

MGT 201 is somewhat useful if you're trying to go into consulting. Otherwise, it's primarily busy work with many deliverables (a lot of writing) and a group case presentation. Professor Thomas is an engaging professor who definitely knows her stuff when it comes to communication. She encourages the use of ChatGPT, which is pretty cool.
