reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed her teaching style and feedback. Some of the work seemed unnecessary, but that's more of a complaint about the course than about the professor. While some of the things we learned were a bit redundant, some things were extremely helpful. There is a lot a lot of work for this class, but nothing too difficult.

The class was helpful at times, but then other times it was just a waste of time. Some advice and instruction was kinda annoying (how to write emails, using describing words in linkedin, etc.) There is a lot of busy work, but what you put into the class is what you'll get out of it. Staci is pretty nice and funny though so that is good.

she has a smile that kills
no seriously i thought she was going to kill me

To begin, I don't like the class itself. I feel like the assignment instructions are very unclear and the TAs (depending on who you have) can be harsh in terms of grading. Professor Thomas is a great professor but beware that the assignments in the class are very much busy work.

I can't speak for everyone with my review, but Staci was a good professor overall. I will say that I struggled to see the value in what we were learning at some points (I don't think I'll be changing how I write my emails). But some information was valuable, like that pertaining to presentations. Also, the class's workload is QUITE heavy.

Honestly the most frustrating professor I had at Olin. The information is relevant, but I would argue that some of her advice is not necessarily correct in some ways, so double check with career center. Made the class less enjoyable, and ask peers how they were successful for some of these topics as following her content can come off as overbearing

You get out of this class (and Staci) whatever you put in. Theres a ton of busy work, but the grading isn't super harsh, so as long as you put effort in you'll be fine. Staci does play favorites, but as long as you aren't on her bad side it won't be an issue. Just put in effort and participate, and your grade will work out
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst class I've ever taken at WashU. I'm a hard worker and got along with Thomas, but was still subject to borderline aggressive grading and feedback. You can't trust that her in-person feedback will be reflected in your grade. For a communications class, this had one of the most overwhelming and unhelpful canvas pages I've ever seen.

Good professor, well-structured class. Easy A if you:
1.) Do the work
2.) Show up to class
3.) Read the assignment instructions and rubrics.

The course has a Friday subsection, led by the career center, some but not all sessions are super-valuable. The client project is great practical experience. I walked away ready for the internship search.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Staci Thomas is Rude, Combative, and knows everything about everything. She likes to psychoanalyze her students in 1 on 1 meetings, which can be uncomfortable. The course has valuable information, but I would recommend getting it from another professor and definitely not from her.

Staci is undoubtedly the best professor I have had the pleasure of meeting in my time at WashU. Although there is a decent amount of homework for this class, all of the assignments are purposeful. Even though I am only halfway through the semester, I have learned more practical life skills from her than I have in any other WashU course.

Great professor. I've continued asking for her advice and guidance since I took her class in 2020. She's really helpful, and has great connections! The class teaches real-world skills, so I liked that.

Fantastic professor that legit cares about her students. Took this class in 2018, and it remains the most helpful class I had at WU. She'll help you succeed if you're struggling. One of the most popular profs at WU. "Bring your best, or just don't come." Doesn't accept excuses, late submissions, poor quality and whining. It's real-world, all day.
What is there to say about Staci Thomas except bad things?

MGT 201 is one of the most ridiculous classes in the B school so it's hard for me to evaluate staci when the class just teaches you about networking and writing emails. Staci was definitely very enthusiastic about it but I was just bored to death at 10 am during this class. TA grading also sucked.

This class broke my brain. Staci is one of the most disrespectful, combative, and untruthful people I have ever known. She runs the class like a tyrant: everything she says is right, and if you disagree in the slightest, you fail. For a College that claims to champion mental health awareness, I'm shocked she's employed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Staci Thomas is the worst professor I have ever had in my entire life, bar none. She is a rude, obnoxious person, who always has to be the smartest person in the room. Staci plays favorites too. The only people who like her are Staci's favorite students, if you're not one of them, get ready for hell.

Easily the worst professor I've ever had. Played favorites in class, terrible communicator, targeted quiet students because she didn't like them being quiet. This class played a significant role in sending me back to therapy. I have never had a professor that made my mental health worse than Staci. Avoid her at all costs.

I graduated back in 2018 and I think about Staci's class often. It was (by far!) the most useful class I have ever had. Staci is great! I remember being excited to come to class because she is that engaging. She also shows a lot of respect for her students. The key to succeeding in her class is to give her the same respect in return.

Professor Thomas cares deeply about her job. Thats the only positive thing I can say about her. Her lectures are long and boring, she picks favorites, and she grades harshly to certain students who she perceives as less interested in the material. MGT201 taught me a lot about communication, but she provides weak feedback and is a harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This course taught me life skills. I learned a million practical things, but primarily the importance of audience orientation. I've been applying her lessons in every email, every text, every report. She definitely expects you to pull your weight and look for the answers yourself before emailing her. "Be the solution, not the problem."

I love that Staci teaches us things that are so relevant and useful for the workforce. She makes class very fun and engaging, but beware of cold calling if you don't participate. Very thoughtful and cares about the class. Sometimes harsh on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Staci tries to make material that could be taught in one day stretch out over the course of a semester. She acts as if she's the smartest person in the room at all times and will give you F's if she thinks you don't care. Communication is not clear on assignments. She has given feedback that is borderline rude and unthoughtful. Never again.

Staci is great! Her lectures are engaging and she is funny. The course content is very applicable and has taught me many skills I know I will use (resume, cover letter, writing reports, general business communication). There is a good amount of group work but the class is relatively low-stress. She also makes herself available outside of class.

Makes class fun. She's tough, but really fair. No one gets a free pass, and everyone is held to the same standard without exception. The course is relaly organized well, but sometimes she jams too much info into an hour and a half. you don't need to take many notes, because it's all experiential and 100% practical.

Great professor and a great class! I wanted to go to class more. Staci is a true gem. She really wants her students to succeed and does a great job of keeping her students engaged. The group projects were, at times, challenging but in hindsight extremely helpful for what was to come. Thank you Staci!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Group project was time consuming, but the class taught so many skills that will be useful when applying for jobs. Easy A and I would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Success in the class depended too heavily on who graded you. I got lucky, but some groups received harsh and unfair criticism. Also, for a communications class, it was ironically really poorly organized/communicated. On the positive side, it was the most practical class I have ever taken. It forced me to write resumes, cover letters, etc.

Staci is extremely helpful in preparing students for future jobs and is very accessible if you want help on your resume, cover letter, or interview skills. At times she did not communicate her expectations on every assignment clearly, which can hurt your grade. Overall she is a great professor and students will benefit immensely from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Loved this class. Practical skills in a video lecture format. Classtime is more of a workshop. Integrates student suggestions into the class. An A is totally achievable but you have to show up and do the work. A bit of tough love there.

Staci is an awesome professor who cares about her students and their success.  Her class is well outlined from the start, her expectations are clear, and you will more than likely do very well.  The group project can be grueling but it's worth it.  Take MGT201 with her over ANY other professor!

Staci is amazing. Her course is the most applicable course I've had in college. She is there for her students and wants to see her students succeed. There is quite a bit of individual and group work in this course, but it is an easy A. Also, each class has 2 TA's that are also there to help.
The first PRACTICAL course I've had in college. Actually learned some life skills, and feel like I'm prepared for the job market. Not easy, but worth it.
Really cares about her students and their success. Even though her class might be more work than other MGT201 classes, I definitely learned a lot and would recommend it.
Really helpful. She wants her students to succeed, and gives you the life skills you need to do it. I really enjoyed this class.

Really interesting class.  You have the rubrics ahead of time, so you know exactly what is expected for every assignment and presentation.  This makes getting an A pretty easy.  Very enthusiastic and willing to help students succeed.
She is not fair on scoring. And she is kind of cold.
Watches for plagiarism - be careful!  Not very flexible for late homeworks.  Homeworks are not accepted after 24 hours late.  But thes not a lot of homework.
Tough, but willing to help.  One of the most useful classes I've taken  Fun, interesting atmosphere.  Get the rubric before starting homework!
High energy.  Excellent instructor.  Good focus on WHY Western speakers differ from other cultures.
Tim is very kind. His first test was really hard but he also was helpful and is passionate in the lectures
took summer 2022 for FSAP. relatable examples in lectures, clear expectations, understands student mental health, great TA and review sessions too.
THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER

I had Bono for YA Psych, and I absolutely loved him. He is an amazing lecturer and knows how to keep students engaged. You can tell he's also so passionate about what he's teaching and is always available outside of class to talk more about it. He is also relatively young and went to WashU, so he's a very relatable person. Highly recommend.

Bono is a really great teacher and person. Psych 105 was once a week and a pass/fail course. Sometimes it was awesome, but other weeks it really felt like a waste of time. Tim Bono is a great lecturer for the first three times you hear him. After that, he gets a bit repetitive. I still think his work is amazing and he's really funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a super nice guy but his classes are rehearsed and read like a semi-inspired TEDTalk. Most of the class is presenting 7 studies that all have the same conclusion so lectures can be boring. Tests are hard and you MUST do the readings. If you are a senior with nothing better to do and want some life tips, that is what this class is good for.
Interesting, easy class. I'd recommend.
He is hands-down the best lecturer at WashU. I enjoy his lectures and it feels like time flies by. His exams are tough, so get ready to study a lot and it might not pay off.
Passionate about what he teaches, so intelligent, inspiring, clear, interesting, adorable, great butt.

Tim Bono is probably the best professor I've had at Wash U.  I had him for a freshman seminar, which was about 160 people, and a lecture class, which was about 300 people.  Although the classes were large, he made sure to get to know each student individually and made class fun and engaging.
Pretty standard psychology lecture class. Talks about pretty interesting stuff, and always backs it up with some legitimate research. He's a fun guy, but I did get bored in his class occasionally.
This guy is the real deal. Incredible lecturer, funny, charismatic, and seemingly knows everyone in a 300 person class. I find myself actually looking forward to class.

I absolutely loved him. Did a summer class with him during FSAP and he was great. Energetic, told us if the book was needed and his powerpoints were always clear and he answered all our questions. He gave great examples and clips to watch. Tests were not too hard, it was always stuff we talked about. Great time with Tim!

Prof Moore is very caring of students and fun lecturer. We only have two short papers in the semester, and he has clear expectations in terms of the structures of papers (which makes the work much easier). Be ready to wear masks in class though, as the his body condition requires.

He's a really good professor and knows a lot about Roman history. While his lectures can get a bit boring, he tries to keep us all engaged and he's just a fun person to be around. If you go to his office hours his insights are really interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tim is a great human being and really knows a lot about ancient Greek and Roman music. The class is heavily based on presentations and discussions which keeps things interesting. I really learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Prof. Braver is a nice guy who really loves neuroscience, but lectures were very dense. Presentations seem like they're taken straight from an advanced neuroscience class and are far more detailed than is appropriate for a FYP.

Quizzes are no longer based on the minutiae of these slides, but that doesn't make the lectures any more comprehensible.

Professor Braver is by far the worst professor I've had in my four years at WashU. He is not understanding of unforeseen circumstances whatsoever, and he is vindictive if you confront him in any way. After an issue we had following the unexpected death of my grandfather, Braver graded me harshly and unfairly in comparison to my peers. Steer clear

Braver could be a great man outside of this class but his lectures made my brain melt (in a bad way). Extremely unclear and easily got off topic in obscure ways. The tests were so detailed on the most unimportant things. I didn't learn anything and he doesn't facilitate learning, the only way to pass is to memorize everything. very disappointing.

He single handedly gave me imposter syndrome. He speaks 100,000 miles an hour and his tests are impossible. Numerous times I was tested on things I had less than 4 words about in my notes. He says offhand comments and then makes them worth 8 points on the tests. Ridiculous professor. I want to report him to the psych department.

I was not surprised when Braver announced that this was his first time teaching MBB. He is never able to finish lectures, yet the entire test covers the 37 slides he speeds through in the last 10 minutes of class. He's a decent guy and has great experience, but doesn't know how to teach. The class itself was underwhelming as well.
He has a Tesla Model 3. He speeds through the material. Half of the slides are discussed in the last 10 minutes. None of the slides relate with one another. ��

This was my 2nd class with this professor (1st being BioPsych). I think he is a great professor! You can tell he really likes neuroscience+ research & tries sharing this interest with students. If you're interested in any of the above topics, I would highly recommend both classes!Y ou'll learn alot and be challenged, but will do well if u work hard
excellent answerer of questions and good stimulator of discussion

UGH.  I had a 4.0 in college until THIS class...my first C ever.  I thought I would love this class; as I was once a bio major.  However, it was all I could do to stay awake, and consciousness is still no guarantee you'll actually learn anything.  I learned a fair bit from the book, but the tests were lecture-based.  STAY FAR AWAY FROM THIS CLASS!

worst class ever...very boring, poorly taught, teacher doesn't seem concerned with students.  tests are difficult and covers slides not completely covered and all the info in the book.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Braver often does not finish going over the slides in his lecture notes, but still holds you responsible for the material.  In addition, tests cover book material and lecture material.  It is a lot of information at once!

Todd Braver should not teach.  I can't believe he's still teaching, when he only gets terrible evaluations.  Bio Psych was a class just not run well, run very poorly in fact.  It was pretty easy to see that this man did not care much for teaching at all, as everything done was a total mess.  Avoid!!
Boooooooooo!!!!!!!!

I've always been really interested in bio psych and was really interested in the material... until taking this class!  Horribly boring professor, tests don't always reflect how much you know, everything about it was bad.
It's a hard class and boring at times but if you are interested in the subject it's completely worthwhile.
No Comments
nice guy, horrible professor; avoid bio. psych if at all possible!; terrible!!; hard material and uninteresting lectures made a class that could've been great really awful.
Tomy Ames was such an amazing professor. This class was, for the most part, a "hands-on" learning experience. I will always remember his teaching for the rest of my career path.

Professor Tomy is a very insightful educator. In the class, he never gives out answers; instead, he lets students think hard and debate with each other, so that the classroom allows different idea to exist, but also give students a chance to cross-examine their own ideas. As long as you write with effort you will receive a decent grade.

Professor Tomy is very funny and told a lot of stories during class. There was a lot of reading but he also used podcasts and youtube videos which made things easier. Most of class was talking about the readings and debating. His grading at the beginning was easier than at the end but I also got a lot of extra credit so still ended up with an A.

I absolute love Dalla Torre. I have taken four classes with her and would take more if I could. She's also my advisor. She's extremely caring and understanding. Her course load is no different than any other language class at WashU. Highly recommend taking a class with her. She's extremely knowledgeable and passionate about her classes.

Professor Dalla Torre creates a lively classroom setting where I always felt comfortable and excited to participate in class. For language learning it's important to actively practice and I felt like the classroom facilitated this. There is VHL homework due before every class and attendance is important but this should expected for a language class

Prof Dalla Torre is not a good professor and constantly displays her arbitrary grading system she uses for oral exams and tests/quizzes where comments are unclear and unhelpful for work done. She also insinuated that one of her students was sexist because he asked a course policy question. I would avoid her as she makes claims like this frequently.

Unreasonable amount of work: online HW due before class (3x/week), 4 quizzes, 2 exams, 2 oral exams, and a final project. 

More importantly, with 50 minute classes, students could barely finish quizzes and 12-part exams left people scrambling. If you can't finish in time, she says to contact Disability Resources. Enthusiastic but very dismissive.

Trevor always made class fun and never hesitated to share their thoughts or mince words. That being said, it felt like a lot of the time students could be dismissed or made fun of for sharing their thoughts if they disagreed or had different interpretations. Engaging lectures and explained readings in a very easy-to-understand way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I got frustrated sometimes because I felt like Trevor was very dismissive of people's interpretations of readings, but this improved later on and I appreciated how understanding Trevor was. As long as there was communication it was ok to miss class or get extensions sometimes. Trevor grades also was never overly harsh with scoring.
I love Professor Trevor! They are so caring and really want you to succeed! Make sure to pay attention in class and take notes and you should be good on the exams!

Professor Trevor is great. The class is purely discussion based, so make sure you read the readings and some group projects. They assign the readings on Canvas (about 20-30 pages long). The homework assignment are weekly reflection essays, which are super short and easy. Pay attention in class and you will do well on the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this class and Prof. Trevor. They are extremely knowledgable, caring, and engaging. Classes were incredibly interesting. Participation is important but the assignments were interesting. I would take this class again in a heartbeat.
Amazing Prof. I've taken two classes with Trevor and they are both a great teacher and very understanding of the college student mindset.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very participation based. Great prof tho

Sometimes, Trevor made queer studies easy and fun, but they speak w/ long sentences, big words, & very abstract ideas. Appreciates participation, but its easy to feel like they think your contributions are stupid. Can get angry if the whole class read but doesn't understand a reading. Look up "Think, Mark, Think!" meme. They're Omniman, you're Mark

Great professor and great class. You get A as long as you work hard. The only thing is that you need to be politically correct in your paper and class discussion, so be cautious with what you say. But overall it's a great class and you get to read a lot of great readings.

Here's my issue with Trevor: she's nice and she's not a harsh grader (she gives extensions no questions asked as long as you ask her 48 hours before the due date) but she doesn't allow much room for Devil's Advocate. You can tell when she's hearing what she wants to hear and when someone's not being quite PC enough.
Great class, great professor. Changing the world one reading at a time.

Trevor's awesome. Everyone should take her intro classes, honestly. The grading seems a little rough but a lot of the overall class grade is participation, attendance, and completing some ungraded assignments consistently. Attendance is absolutely mandatory.

Professor Treitel is a good professor in the way she teaches lecture and is accessible during office hours. However, I would not take a course with her again. Too many readings, and if you fall behind, catching up is hard. Grading in the essays is way too harsh, and the feedback is inconsistent. The stress these essays cause is not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Super engaging, assignments are all relatively easy and meaningful. Office hours are always interesting and she seems like she really wants to get to know you!
The professor was great!  extremely organized and cares!  She attempts to learn everyone's name and is truly engaging!
great professor, engaging and very nice!
Really engaging and caring professor

Treitel is very passionate about what she does and is pretty clear in class. She loves to bring art into her lectures and does a pretty good job on making clear what is looking for on test. Overall a good professor!
Keeps the class engaged and interested about the topic at hand.  Extremely approachable.

She is very friendly and her lectures are generally interesting. In her World War I class, she only spent a little time on the actual military aspect of the war and WAY too much time on the home front. A lot of the readings get repeditive and seem unnecessary (nothing you couldn't figure out with common sense). A completely average professor.

Honestly the worst professor I have ever had. Clearly doesn't care about his students and always makes you feel like your questions are dumb and he doesn't have time for you. Class is all lecture based which gets quite boring and tests have surprise questions from the text. AVOID if you can.

I know a lot of people are not a fan of Trinkaus, but I think he is great teacher. Class is not mandatory but he talks about things that he doesn't put in his powerpoints that matter for tests. He is super knowledgable and prominent in his field and tells a bunch of interesting/ funny/ cute stories about his life. His classes are always my favorite

He tells a lot of stories during lecture, but if you pay attention you'll see that there's a connection between all of the stories and asides. If you're interested in human biology and anthropology I would definitely recommend. Not a difficult class, but you do have to attend lecture to know what is going on.

Trinkaus is a cool dude that is enthusiastic about his work. He knows the material extremely well and the content is very interesting if you like physical anthropology (if not, why are you in this class?). You MUST go to class to do well. He is very helpful and kind if you ask him specific questions at his office hours. One of my favorite teachers.
Very boring lectures.. exams are annoying to study for but easy if you took good notes in class. If you can, try to avoid this class.

The class is pretty easy to do well in if you go to all of the classes and take notes.  THE BIGGEST ISSUE I HAVE IS THAT HE DOESN'T LET YOU USE THE BATHROOM DURING CLASS (1.5 hrs) AND CALLS YOU OUT IF YOU DO.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLAS IF YOU HAVE A SMALL BLADDER FOR REAL.

He can get dry (when a topic is harped on too much), but the material is incredibly interesting and I learned a lot. I think about physical characteristics differently now, and I feel like the information is useful in all fields. Tests were long but not too hard, at least no multiple choice. He goes off on tangents a lot, but they're funny.
Very interesting class with lots of useful information. Thoroughly enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

Has very interesting subject material and is incredibly intelligent--but he is boring and a very bad teacher.  His tests are the most random things--a few questions that together are worth 20% of the test grade are sometimes over material he mentioned once, for only a minute or two.

Someone needs to give this guy Powerpoint for christmas cause he scribbles on the board for 1.5 hours during every lecture.  Very informative and interesting except I got carple tunnel(sp) after this one.  Needs some photos or something to spice up the lecture, I saw too many catching ZZZzzZz's.

worst class ever! do not take it!  he is very, very boring and corny with his silly jokes.  poorly taught and unconcerned with students.  however, he is very intelligent and at the top of his field with his research.
One word boring, but easy class if you can show up and listen. Material interesting so it mediates his boredom somewhat
Human Variation was the class....he's brilliant and a nice man!
Old exams WERE available for this class from 1999 on his class website for a few years back.  They didn't help much except for on the final.

Brilliant.  He is the top in his field - what else could you want?  You just need to pay attention in his class.  Pretty funny if you listen.  Sometimes he goes off on tangents..but they liven up class. Great Professor
His political views got in the way way too much for the class to be enjoyable.  He contradicted himself a lot in this class, though I know he knows his neanderthals...
so boring, rambles, gets off topic, knows his field, but not good at teaching to others, should not be a professor just because he's smart

doesn't provide study sessions or answers for old exams.  makes frequent bad jokes that range from unintelligeble to obscene.  knows a lot, class is interesting in short bursts, but also rambles circularly.  needs to use more slides and examples.
No Comments
Not the most exciting guy...but at least he knows his stuff.
Tough but fair. Gave helpful (if slightly acid) feedback on both writing style and the arguments in papers. Good storyteller, which is really helpful in a history class on a foreign culture.
Now over ten years out of my Japanese history class taught by Dr. Tsunoda, I look back at her as a dynamic lecturer and one of my greatest mentors.
Great teacher and advisor - approachable, honest, smart, tough, sincere, serious about her work and therefore yours
Her lecture always makes me fall asleep. Some papers are not quite related to Japanese history.
Unpleasant, unhelpful, not approachable

This course is simply amazing. reaqdings are great and not too long, assignements and exams fair. She's approachable especially if you don't try to just suck up and try instead to talk about serious issues in her field. Great prof. all around

Great professor. Very interesting and prepared, prrovides helpful comments on both papers and in class. She is a very brilliant thinker. To ddo bad in her class you gotta be stupid and not study. People who think she's not good are usually taking the class as a requirement. Great person to work with
Excellent professor, though some may find her informal style off-putting. She knows her stuff.
She is often a little sharp but is always intellectually honest.  If you are an idiot she will tell you so, but barring her colorful diction her comments are extremely helpful.
Tsunoda is an extremely helpful and clear professor.  The only way to do poorly in her class is to blow it off (i.e.: write a crap paper the night before)
Complete opposite of Copeland.
she said a paper "went to hell in a teacup" how helpful is that????
Evil woman.
No Comments

She reads off her slides for her lectures and bases her exams off of her slides AND student presentations, then for your assignments she will grade you super ambiguously but super strictly and take off 15%+ with the note being "some aspects could be better". She is also like 80 years old and struggling to understand basic English. She is sweet tho
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this class is atrocious. content is already pretty dry and esoteric, but Treiman somehow made it all way worse.  TONS of weekly homework essays, 60 pages of very dense weekly readings, and lectures/slides content barely even align w/ the $350 textbook. assignment prompts are convoluted and poorly explained.  btw u can't pass/fail this class.  AVOID

Dr. Treiman was terrible and uninspiring. Of course I feel awful that she had health problems, but she was absent for the entire first half of the semester. Despite having different sub professors come and teach us each week, Dr. Treiman was still the one to grade our assignments and write our tests. Get ready for a LOT of homework and hard exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: SO much work. Way too much, feels like a writing intensive course when it's not. Makes you write essays on the hundreds of pages of reading she assigns and then other essays on top of it. A ridiculous amount of work for a psychology class. You have to be participating. Took the class for three weeks and dropped- waiting for another professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Tests are difficult and WILL take the entire time to finish, but she offers lots of chances for review. Had reading quizzes every class but they were super easy, just need to skip the chapter before class. Lecture was kinda boring. Not my favorite class but not unbearable.
I enjoyed her class
seminar style class, enjoyed it and learned quite a bit
good professor, small class, knows subject matter well

She is one of the most uncaring and unhelpful professors I have ever taken a class with. Her lectures are long, but her lecture slides barely provide any information about the topics. She gives extra credit through the hw, but barely gives full marks so it ends up hurting your grade. Would never take again.
She is a female Ben Stein.  Monotone and boring and her tests cover too much in the time alotted.  Barely had time to finish the multiple choice let alone essays and fill in the blanks!
interesting topics, good class
knowledgeable professor
Professor Trieman seemed to be more focused on her research on language development than the material in the text, or the individual concerns of her students.  Perhaps she should stick to the lab?
This class is awfully boring.  She just repeats what is in the book. I didn't attend any of the classes after the first test, and I did fine.

Love the subject matter, hate the course. based on how easy the book was and how little additional info the lectures provided, everyone should've gotten A's, but that didn't happen. She's not understanding, she wouldn't let anyone take the ridiculously late final even an hr early to make a flight.
Lectures both from the book and boring.  Very clear teaching if you like to hear the same thing two or three times.  Apparently had a very traumatic childhood.

Developmental psychology sounds like fun, right?  And it could have been, but no.  Professor Treiman makes lectures painfully boring, and the tests don't always cover the material covered in class or in the book.  Becky T. definitely does not get my seal of approval.
Extremely boring, class is straight out of the book.  Like the great majority of psych classes here, not worth the time.
soooooo boring. sitting through the class is torture. ruins what could be an interesting blass. the TA was much better at explaining everything.
She just reads from the book...I could have taught the class...lazy bum
nooo goooood
She changed the grades for our course without telling anybody.. 2/3 of the way through the semester, causing many people to get lower grades than they should have.
Very knowledgeable and clear.  An interesting course. Tests and assignments are returned promptly.
Reis, Aslan, Sultan, Imparator, Onder, Kral, Baskan.
The GOAT
He is a great professor. He is a hard worker and very kind to helping his students. That was a great experience to take the course from him...

An absolute unit of a professor. If you ask for help, his response time is no less than 20 business minutes and will help you with pretty much anything, whether that be conceptual or a question about a specific question on the exam.
Great class, interesting lectures.
Great professor!
He is one of the professors I see by now. He was very nice and help a lot with each process.

Prof. Turner was a joy to have. He always comes to class with perhaps a bit over-caffeinated, however this helped those of us who were having trouble waking up ourselves. He always came prepared and you can tell he is very passionate about the material he teaches. It is quite interesting stuff! He is a bit unavailable on his trips to Central Asia.
Very good teacher, one of the best in EECE department. However, homework and some units are hard, but he is pretty reachable outside of class and willing to give extensions and help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jay was a good lecturer and obviously very enthusiastic about the course. If only enthusiasm reflected competency! The syllabus was not followed at all. He was extremely hard to reach via email or phone: it took over a month for him to actually respond to my requests for an exam regrade. The exams were not reflective of lecture materials.

Prof Turner has a super interesting job that he talks about a lot because it has to do with the class. I find it really inspirational because this is the first EECE course that has allowed me to see the potential of what I could do post-graduation. Homework is hard but he's *INCREDIBLY* helpful during office hours and you can email him too.

Professor Turner, as always in 311, gives very interesting lectures and really cares about students. His assignment is a lot but very clear expectations. I just want to give an appreciation for him after I graduate. He hesitates to use technology though. I believe the in person class might be hard.

Dr. Turner is a cool guy at the top of his field, but he was a very difficult professor this semester. He teaches Intro ChemE alongside Dr. Giammar and Turner is widely known as the more difficult professor. He writes notoriously unclear test questions that the entire class struggled to understand.
Class materials are attractive and inspiring. Jay is really a helpful and talented teacher. Though the workload is pretty big.
awesome teacher, he is available to answer questions, class is not boring at all.  take classes with this teacher, you'll like it if you're an engineer

Gives extremely clear and detailed feedback on papers, which is not something that a lot of professors are willing to do. It does take him a long time to grade papers. Provides some interesting readings, and so long as you read them and attend class, you'll do fine.

Professor was good in class. He stayed neutral with arguments and did not force people to talk or anything. When it comes to papers, he will critique your rough draft and give great notes. If you turn in a rough draft you usually get a good grade. Exam was ridiculous. Created a study guide and then used nothing from it for the actual questions.

Gotta agree with the below post-- took this class P/F and very glad I did so. Got a C- on my first essay which admittedly wasn't very good, tried a different approach on the second one and got a C+. Exams are better, but only slightly so, and focus on specifics from arguments rather than main takeaways. Pretty aggravating.

Very interesting class material, but professor was underwhelming. Took months to get exams and papers back and despite this, graded extremely harshly. His exams required ultra specific answers that nobody thought they needed to know. Nobody I know got A's in this class and he also would grade essays based on whether he agreed with your opinion.

A goofy guy, but he leads discussions well, even when people are shy to talk (or haven't read). He's not my favorite professor, but it's well worth taking Present Moral Problems with him: he'll let the debate happen, expectations are clear, and it covers important topics

This class was the most difficult course and time intensive course that I took at wash u. I was regularly spending 20+ hours per week trying to understand the reading assignments and working on the labs. That being said, Turner was very clear on the material and expectations and was very helpful outside of class to those who asked for it.

According to the TAs it was his first time teaching Intro, but still... The quiz class average near the middle of the semester was in the 40's. Your final grade can't be higher than your average quiz score, so a lot of people withdrew. He was getting so much flack from students/TAs he changed his grade scale 2 hours before the withdrawal deadline.

Awesome teacher. The material he covers is really hard, but he puts a lot of effort to make it manageable for the student. He is also available almost anytime by email, and always does his best to respond with a complete answer to help us understand. Awesome experience
Very good prof.  Quite difficult, but I really felt like I learned something after I was done.  Some friends have disagreed, but I really enjoyed his course, and have worked with him after.

Professor Schlichenmeyer has run a very chaotically organized CSE314 class for the past few years, and it unfortunately has not changed. New technologies were very poorly integrated into the class due to the professor not really understanding them himself. Feedback was nonexistent, and he was unresponsive outside class. Only take if needed for DS!

Adjunct professor so hed benefit from a stronger TA corps to support him especially with student feedback. This was the first CS class at WashU where I felt like a developer and not a toddler doing fill in the blanks. Invaluable class if u want to code professionally, DataSci/DataEng or not. it's what u make it. Make sure to get good groupmates lol

Unclear why they still have him teaching this class. It's the 4th year he is teaching the same class and he still has no idea what he is doing. There are multiple issues in every assignment requiring their deadline to be extended or dropped altogether. He does everything at the very last minute. Only take if you NEED it for your DS requirement.
nice guy. but i haven't learned anything.

Most disorganized and unprepared teacher I've ever had. Very bad work ethic and organization in terms of course planning and logistics. He's super nice and clearly knows his material, but this man would take an hour to fail to explain how to butter toast. He'd also ask a 4th grader to do calculus problems and be annoyed when they can't do it.

He is very disorganized. Homework expectations are changed after posting, and links to submit do not work. It's just a chaotic class and he doesn't explain anything so it is a lot of working on stuff on your own. Fortunately, he does allow chatGPT and CoPilot which helps but it is a time-consuming class. Just be prepared to spend a lot of time.

Maybe one of the worst professors Ive had. The longest, most difficult and ridiculous homework assignments assigned weekly, a terrible textbook with typos, a brutal grader, and an overall confusing instructor. Always made concepts seem more confusing than they were, and hes not understand of student needs. Would not recommend personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures were confusing, and content was extremely difficult. He seems to prefer putting students in their place over helping them learn. He is not really willing to help students outside of class, if you go to office hours you'll just be told to figure it out yourself. CHOOSE ANOTHER PROF IF YOU CAN.

Just whatever you do dont take a class that he teaches. He doesnt respect that students are not as knowledgeable as him and doesnt know how to explain concepts in a way that doesnt go right over students heads. Office hours are not that useful, spent about 20 hours per week on HOMEWORK. Dont do it to yourself.

Bongers was a fantastic professor and easily the best math professor I have had at WashU. He is great for people who actually want to understand math at a conceptual level in addition to learning computations. His class was difficult but if you went to class (his lectures are really helpful and well explained) and pay attention, you can do well.

Bongers gives really long homework assignments. His lectures are fine. His office hours are ok, depends on the day. Some days he will help; other days he wants you to figure it out yourself. Take home exams are very difficult. Expect to spend a lot of time on his class.

Decent professor. A little awkward at times but is clearly knowledgable about the topic and does a decent job explaining considering how complex some of the topics were. He is patient with students and tests are not easy but still fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Don't go to lecture, just watch professor Leonard on Youtube. It honestly really makes me sad to say this, Wash U is an amazing school but this was the least clear, most frustrating course I've taken here. Professor Bongers is a brilliant mathematician, but sadly, not suited to be a teacher.

calc 3 has become much harder at Wash U especially the exams - if you have the choice to take calc 2 instead, do so; bongers is sweet but goes too fast, exams are hard, sub section is a joke; if you take this course, watch professor leonard videos and don't go to class.

Dr. Bongers, in my opinion, does not explain complex math concepts with a great deal of clarity. Definitely more focused on pushing a lot of material than actually having you understand. I, trying to be as constructive as possible, recommend not taking his class because it is extremely difficult and not taught in a way conduce to understanding.
Not a good professor. Didn't even give a drop for discussion section.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hands down the best math professor I've had! His lectures are very concise, clear, and informative, combining helpful dosages of big-picture explanations and specific examples. Add on his light humor, genuine care for students, and accessibility outside of class, and he's the perfect math teacher. Kinda wish I could take more math classes now...

Great instructor who really knows his stuff and is able to effectively convey and teach mathematics. He really took student feedback into consideration, to the point where we were able to choose the specific topics he would cover during review sessions before exams. I recommend taking a class with him.
The best math professor I have had at WashU. Great dude, great lectures, and easy to learn from. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take his class and you will fall in love with maths

Amazing professor! Does such a good job of really explaining material clearly and thoroughly in class both with general and specific examples. Everything on exams has been covered in depth in class and homework problems prepare you for difficulty and grading. Incredibly helpful at office hours for homework or just a chat. Would highly recommend!

This man explains differential equations in a way that makes it make sense. He is clear, concise, provides a lot of example problems, and has a sense of humor. Honestly, he's everything I'd hope for in a math professor. Take his class if you can - math won't be a struggle if you do.
She ruined my confidence in my abilities, and made it really difficult for me to return back to architecture. Felt totally alone.

Constance's studio was the most inspiring studio I have taken at WashU. I left the studio with a comprehensive project I was proud of and a newfound interest in what I was investigating. I credit her commitment and encouragement; Constance is always available for honest and constructive feedback. It is evident she wants to see her students succeed!

Constance is a very dedicated professor. She will make sure a lot of work is produced but you will have an amazing portfolio project by the end. She pays a lot of attention to details, is very interested in film as a medium and the way it relates to architecture, and is very innovative.

Constance is perceptive to each student's interests and often roots her feedback to greater design discourses. While she may ask for more than "average", her student's work tends to be highly articulate, thorough, and impassioned. IMO, Constance is a rare researcher and educator open to mentoring students interested in exploring Ideas and growing.

Constance is one of my favorite professors at school, renowned for her innovative ideas and ability to offer each student personalized critiques and directions for their projects. She is incredibly responsible and goes out of her way to support her students. In one of her courses, she even recorded all the readings aloud, purely for our convenience

Constance is my favorite professor during school. Everyone is lucky to have her. She is so inspiring and encouraging and always brings joy and energy to the class. Her passion for teaching and architecture is priceless. I miss her class every day, it's not easy but memorable. She helped me grow so much and I will always be grateful for it.

Constance is awesome. The studio was balanced in terms of theory, design, and fabrication, and the lectures were great learning experiences that is uncommon for studio courses.

Workload is heavy, but you'll grow a lot in the end. Follow through and great projects will come out of this studio!

Constance is a truly remarkable professor. She always gives engaging lectures and thoughtful desk critiques. She made a significant impact on my learning experiences with architecture. She's always very on point with her criticism and shows love to her students. You can't help getting attracted by her charisma!

Constance was a very dedicated instructor, very inspirational and encouraging. She is also very smart and quick to understand how students think and tries her best to help with students' projects. I would take her studio again in a heartbeat.

I was in the very first 211 studio Constance had taught here at Washu and it was a wild experience.We were second years, however we were tasked to design a theater, which is quite a serious endeaver consider the program sets. We had experienced a lot of growth that semester. Constance helped me personally later on in life and I am always grateful:)

Constance is very knowledgeable and inspirational. She gives great precedent references that facilitate the design process. Her studio is indeed work-intensive, but I got so much out of it and the project really enhanced my portfolio. Come to her studio prepared! You will always get more and better feedback when you have materials to show.

In my experience with Constance as a professor, she was always on time and ready to make progress during class time. She is often available and follows through with what she says she will do. If you do take a class with her be ready to produce superior architecture work!
Too much work
Frustrating

Being in Constance's studio was difficult because it felt like both the students and the other professors were often in the dark as to what we were doing and why we were doing it. It was also very theoretical and focused on abstract representation, which was frustrating as someone more technically inclined.
Constance is great.

Constance is one of the best professors in WashU undergrad architecture. She thinks beyond the traditional limit of plans and sections. She can constantly refers to canonical works in canonical ways, thus providing useful and insightful ideas.

WOW! One of the best profs at WashU. Compassionate. Excellent communicator of ideas. Inspires great conversation. Wherever you are on the religious/ideological spectrum, you will be challenged! Not one to strawman a thinker he disagrees with, but makes every effort to represent their thought how they would want it represented--refreshing for a prof
Fantastic lectures. Extremely knowledgable. It's clear that teaching is his passion and he's skilled at it.
Spectacular lecturer, very knowledgeable about New England Puritanism and other areas of interest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable professor and can make topics that appear boring come to life. Rapport with Professor Inazu is great, and they have intellecutal discussions in class. Will not cold call on students, but you should still have done all (or most) of the readings assigned. TAs graded most papers, but I think the profs look at the final paper?
Kind professor, and the lectures are not dry.

Professor Valeri is clearly an expert in the topics he lectures on. He brings up insights that would never have occurred to most people, and explains them in a manner that makes them understandable. He also interacts well with students so you aren't always being talked at. That said, he can be a bit dry and there may be times where you get sleepy.

Valeri gave good historical insight that helped complement the legal aspects of religious freedom in America. His comments help you write the short discussion essays required for the class. Great lecturer.

Genuinely had to drop this class because I got sick and he didn't let me make up work. Clearly a smart guy with interesting things to say, but he doesn't care what students think. Not understanding, harsh grader, likes to shame students and be mean for the sake of it.

The Professor seems only very interested in what he thinks. The class structure and management are quite abysmal. Never were we were never quite on schedule, or received writing assignments in a reasonable timeframe with clear grading criteria. There is very little joy in listening to him lecture.
Performative. Positive reviews must be written by attractive women, for whom he has a particular affinity.

One of those professors you never forget. Walked into WashU a stem major, but Sherry just makes you fall in love with LIT, and now I'm walking out an English major. Very discussion-based, but Sherry makes talking easy, as he guides discussions clearly and eloquently. Minimal homework, just reading, expectantly. Truly the best at WashU. 10/10.
Unhelpful feedback.
Professor is not kind, and does not create a comfortable learning/conversational environment for students
This professor is not very kind or understanding towards his students.
VINCENT SHERRY IS THE BEST PROFESSOR AT WASHU

One of the best professors I've ever had! Super understanding about outside-of-school circumstances if you just let him know, super thought-provoking class. Workload isn't too crazy at all, and if you participate actively in discussions you'll do well. 10/10 highly recommend
He's really wonderful. I've taken two classes with him, and he's always happy to have short conferences outside of class that are always extremely helpful. I have nothing negative to say about him.
Professor Sherry augmented my sense of what is possible in an English course. I won't read poetry in the same way again! He is very funny and charming.

This one towers above the rest, literally and figuratively! He's a leaning tower of knowledge who says everything so beautifully. He completely changed the way in which I think about poetry. Take this course if you want to change the way you read. He might also change the way you speak. Brilliant. Deep. Funny too. My favorite professor thus far.

This one towers above the rest, literally and figuratively! He is a tower of knowledge and he says everything so beautifully. He completely changed the way in which I think about poetry. Take this course if you want to change the way you read. He might also change the way you speak. Brilliant. Deep. Funny too. My favorite professor thus far.

Like most well-designed courses, the harder you work the more you get out of it. Challenging, but presented so you don't have to be great at econometrics to understand and benefit. It was very  helpful professionally when designing priced-based incentives. He makes his expertise in auctions very accessible; mantra  "can we do better?"
Did two courses with him during my MBA at INSEAD. Prices and Markets and Advanced Game Theory. Awesome professor with his own style. He opened up two new worlds of wonder for our class.
His class is manageable but the lecture is extremely dull. He is fair though.

Don't even think about not reading the case studies!  He can smell it is you don't show up prepared.  If you do your work you will love his classes. Probably one of the best proffers I've had in healthcare management. He's an executive for his day job, so he expects a lot from us be he gives just as much.

He's a healthcare executive so knows his stuff, and expects you to come prepared.  He will work with you if you need it, but don't come with excuses.  Class participation is mandatory, so read the cases!!!  Kinda easy on the eyes.   Oh, there is group work so don't be surprised.

very organized and knowledgeable. Uses Harvard cases for review. no textbook needed. class participation & attendence req'd. one midterm paper and one group final presentation. Would highly recommend!

Gives good advice for the most part. I will say she is definitely more partial to more realistic art styles & photo manipulation over "cartoony" styles & didn't really care much for original characters/designs over altering existing images/characters. I enjoyed all of the projects but the third one, timelines can be a bit busy but def manageable.
Loved taking Color Systems because I received great feedback on projects-- addressed strengths AND ways to improve. So helpful for portfolio building!!

amazing teacher, she really knows what she's talking about. every crit i've received from her are spot-on and very helpful. her color unit made me understand the concept of it all so much better. though because she is so good at what she does, i feel like her expectations are pretty high. amazing class either way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wassenaar is very helpful. The projects are pretty fun and not too demanding. She gives a clear rubric on what she wants, enough class time to finish projects (though outside hours are definitely a must), and actually wants student feedback to make the class better. Definitely a good choice for 2D.

Cheryl is great! Eco art was such a fun elective to take with her. She organized the class amazingly well and knows exactly what she's talking about. She's very fair in her grading and the effort you put in is the grade you'll get (she can tell dude I don't know how). Everyone says to take a class with her and you totally should!

If you need to take 2D design, you should definitely take it with Cheryl. She is super helpful and all her assignments are meaningful. She truly knows her stuff which is why everyone respects her. The class can be challenging at times, but it is never too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a godsend - the right amount of tough and demanding, and being understanding. She expects your best work but is sensible enough to ask for only what's needed to make sure you've learnt something properly. Seems distant at first but you'll soon realize she's genuinely caring . Regrades your work if you resubmit them.

Cheryl was the best art teacher I have had so far at Wash U.  She is crazy smart and really truly knows her****.  her class is hard and pain in the ass but well worth it.  except to work really really hard but you will learn a ton.

Cheryl is tough.  She knows her****.  But she will probably extract from you EXACTLY what you need her to.  I loved this class becoz she is open to conceptual ideas while holding you to technical concepts.  She apreciates both, and understands design to an intimidating degree. Challenging to "idea" people, but worth every minute of it.
Wonderful

easy class if you are decisive and confident when it comes to your art.  nightmare if you like to waver and secondguess yourself.  class is not terribly demanding in terms skill or time if you have strong ideas.  for the most part, wassenaars class is a battle with yourself.

I have had her for a few classes now. She is awesome, yet she is not easy. Cheryl will make you work hard, and will give you an appropriate grade. Be willing to redo some work, and she will more than likely bump you up at least half a grade point.
She expanded my general awareness, while forcing me to sharpen my focus on a few, previously underattended aspects of design and my craft.  Great teacher, but a lot of projects and exercises.
No Comments
great learning expirience, very challenging, but very worth it! =)
Great subject matter, class, and teacher! Produced a lot of work. Talked a lot about the conceptual. Found art is an area art students should really explore.

Prof. Wexler was able to help me better understand content form quantum (last semester) that I often felt completely lost on. Connecting stat mech to quantum systems we previously talked about previously was revolutionary and connected so many dots in my head. Its clear he cares about teaching and making sure students understand the content.

Thank goodness I made it. The exams were unnecessarily hard, and nothing like the material in lecture or on the problem sets. He talks down to students, except for his favs. His lectures improved when there was another prof in class, then got crappy again after. I do not see I learned anything this semester.

The gap between what is covered in class/in homework vs the exams is enormous. Assigns little to no homework problems and they are far too easy. Exams are only hard because you don't know what to expect and Dr. Wexler does little to prepare you. Also very confusing to understand.

Horrible professor. Lectures are him rambling for 50 minutes with questions that cannot be answered using lecture content. Truly have no idea why he is allowed to be a professor with no knowledge of how to actually teach.

Textbook is a must have for the class - Wexler is a new teacher and lectures do not fully cover the content and are often drawn out and confusing. Homework is easy if you have the textbook, but good luck on exams.

Wexler is new, and it shows a bit. He really cares and is very nice. The course is hard, and he gave tons of derivations. So, it is extremely math/physics heavy. I don't know if it is possible, but I wished he would have provided some insights into the equations and material? I am not sure how this course helped me as a STEM major.

Dr. Wexler is an outstanding physical chemist. I especially appreciate his teaching in statistical mechanics, which is extremely thought-provoking in connecting quantum mechanics to thermodynamics. This class, together with Chem401, is mind-blowing for me throughout my sophomore year, and pchem will be part of my life from now on.

Amazing prof! Would love to take more classes with him. BCB has long lectures, but somehow they dont feel as long as they are as Jason is great at keeping you engaged and gives great explanations of the material that are suitable for advanced concepts even without many prerequisites. Exams and quizzes are pretty easy as he tells you what to expect.
Dr. Weber is an amazing lecturer and really sparked my interest in cancer biology. Highly recommend

My favorite professor I have ever had. He is so engaging and passionate about the subject, and also teaches similar material to the med and grad students. His class is awesome, even if you are a non-science person with a remote interest in cancer I would totally recommend his class!

Phenomenal professor. He explains everything very well. There's absolutely no way you can sleep in class. Lectures were engaging and not boring. There are only 2 exams but he'll let you know what to expect before exam day. Study and you'll get an A. By far the best prof in a year of science courses.
Really challenging tests, but I liked his lectures a lot.
Greg's great, would class again!
I thought he was funny,
Greg's clearly meant to be a professor.  GReat teacher!
Great to talk with after class.
He's the man!
Easy class, good teacher. Definitely recommend!
He makes you work for your grade but you learn a ton of really interesting stuff.  He has a cute sense of humor and all the girls think he is hot!!
I was dreading this required course but he made sure we understood every important topic before moving on.  Great teacher!
Greg spent a ton of time working through examples both in class and in office hours.  Hard class though, I'd have been lost without the extra help.
Really tough course but he worked through questions and homeworks with us.
Super helpful in office hours, even made time outside of schedule to meet with me and explain the reading!

Regan is definitely way strict and demanding, but she is also an awesome teacher if you let her teach you. It can feel like she's just putting you down sometimes, but she's really doing what she knows will make you grow, painfully or not. She helped me figure myself out when I hadn't even known I was confused.

I really wanted to like Regan. I think our personalities clashed a bit, and she made me seriously question whether I am meant to be an artist. (and not in a good way.) She barely EVER praises work, which made me want to do well out of fear, not love. I don't operate well under those conditions. She could however, read me like a book.

Regan is almost singlehandedly responsible for my drawing abilities, which I did not acquire until after my semester in Florence. One day she told me my markmaking was lazy. After that, I was miraculously cured of my inability to draw. Sharp as a tack. And full of great ideas when your project has come to an impasse. And she's so stylish.

Regan likes to say, at the end of 2-D, "see how much you learned even though it was so hard?".  I don't think I learned very much at all.  The projects were either not stimulating at all or had too many restrictions, and the way she guides students through the "creative process" is counteractive to creativity.  Just did not like her teaching style.

One of my absolute favorite teachers ever. Yes, OCD,& so stylish & talented and one of the nicest, friendliest people i know.She'll be in italy for 3 yrs running the art prgm,so go there! Single-handedly made me question leaving art.A wonderful advisor and friend to students.& turn stuff in on time.

I love Regan!  She is all those things, OCD, incredibly anal about matboard, and if you dont show up to a crit you can forget about your grade, but she inspires SO much creativity, and is a joy to be around for three hours a day twice a week (which is more than I can say for most professors).

I think I can sum up my experience with Regan with one story. A friend of mine broke his nose the night before a project and was due, and spent the night in the hospital. Regan took 20% off his final grade, because it wasn't in on time. This woman has no soul.

Wonderful.  As noted, extremely challenging, well dressed, and possesses a preternatural ability to determine if matte board is cut at exactly 90 degree angles.  While I gave her a low rating for clarity, I mean it in a good way: she gives you freedom.

Awesome lady, wonderful teacher, but incredibly OCD. I'm convinced that if you created the greatest masterpiece the world has ever seen and presented it to her on a piece of matboard without perfect edges, you'd get a B-.
As long as you do things exactly her way, you'll improve and come out with cool suff (P.S. - cut your matte board REALLY PRECISELY).
unbearably attractive, very distracting
Very well dressed.  Also very OCD.  But cool teacher overall
Goated, the best.

I really enjoy lectures. But grading is too friendly. We should have curves to deflate the GPA, something like only 10% A/A+, 20% A-, 20% B+. And we should increase percentage of exams in final grades. I'd prefer 80% exams in final grades, 40% for midterm and 40% for finals. Many students should just fail. They know nothing about what they learned.
Great guy, super accommodating and nice. Workload is reasonable and builds on the concepts really well. Lectures can be tedious sometimes though.

Really a gem! He is so wonderful and caring; while this was probably the easiest class for me this semester, it was also probably the class I learned the most in. Truly wish I could take more classes with him!
Super great and nice professor!

The class is lecture-based with slideshow presentations given by the professor. I think the professor does a good job of presenting information. The class is sort of what you make of it. The content is pretty interesting and I enjoyed sitting through lectures but you could probably also get a good grade in the class by not doing much.

She was very kind and the class was fairly easy. You are graded based on projects and papers but they are not difficult at all to complete if you put some effort (one of our projects got canceled too). 
The class randomly took attendance so I recommend going to classes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She says exactly what are on the slides so if you download her powerpoints you would never have to go to class. The grade consists of 2 papers and 2 "projects" where you either make a slideshow or some fake tweets and call it a day. Oh and the first assignment that was worth 5% of the grade was to draw a map. So it's very easy to do well

Amazing professor. Out of the Wild is a great class you learn a lot and its pretty much just participation and the one final paper. As long as you show up most of the time and talk a little bit you'll be set.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor. Out of the Wild was basically graded on attendance and one giant paper so if you showed up it wasn't that hard. She's very nice, funny and flexible if you want to push deadlines. Great class.

Gives really interesting lectures and really cares that her students are interested in what she's talking about. Very passionate about her field and understanding if you have to miss class. She wants you to enjoy spending time in the class and supports you in other classes as well; she recognizes that her class isn't the only one you're taking.

Professor Widder is such a reasonable person. Just communicate with her and you will do fine. Intro BME is like if Professor Widder made you carrot cake and asked you to do the dishes afterwards--a very fair amount of work for a good reward. Tests are easy and curved.

Widder is the best - so sweet and the Intro to BME class is great overall. Lectures can be a bit slow but if you are interested in the material, it's still great. Grading is a bit unclear which can be annoying, but she is generous, so it's worked out for everyone I know.

Easily the most kind and caring professor ever. Aside from being the sweetest, she's also super knowledgeable and such a fun person. I have never felt inspired to write a review on rate my professor, but she's so amazing I just want everyone to know :)

The most kind and caring professor I have ever had. She expects a lot from her students, but it is fair and she will help you as much as she can along the way, and she genuinely wants every student to succeed.

Professor Widder is one of the kindest professors I've had at WashU! She is quick to respond to emails and meet outside of class if you need help, and her lectures/overall course gives a good introduction to Python. The workload is manageable and reflect what is taught in class.
Very great and kind professor, highly recommend as a great introduction to Python & Machine Learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Widder is the sweetest person ever and is very respected in the department. She gives good lectures that are easily understood. Study guides prepare you for the test, but the study guide info wasn't explained in depth leaving students stressed and uncertain with exams. However, she is an easy grader and cares about students, so most get As/Bs.

Prof. Widder is great! However, 140's format can be a little tedious. The formatting of the homework is a little weird and the sophomore TA's also seemed to be on a bit of a power trip. But besides that, it was great!

Professor Widder makes BME enjoyable. She is extremely dedicated and caring and takes the time to grade our tests and projects all by herself. The class requires a lot of independent study but is very interesting.
Prof. Widder is the best professor I've ever had. BME is a hard major but she really makes it fun and extremely engaging.

So sweet and genuinely caring! You can always email her questions and get a quick, helpful response. She is super nice with grading and understands that our course load is extremely tough for the first semester. She even helps run an opportunity page for BME to help us find research/internships!

Widder is a sweetheart, she is sarcastic enough to keep engagement in lecture and nice enough where no one is intimated to ask questions during and after class. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. 10/10
Professor Widder is the kindest professor I have had so far. I am so excited to take Biomedical Data Science next semester!
What can I say about Dr. Widder? She is the greatest teacher ever...

I actually can't imagine the BME department functioning without Professor Widder. She singlehandedly carries the entire department on her back and every single student who interacts with her has nothing but amazing things to say about her. Truly she has made mine and everyone's experience as a BME worthwhile.

What more can I say about Dr. Widder that hasn't already been said on this forum? She is truly the greatest teacher at WashU. She makes an effort to get to know you personally if you reach out; her lectures are very well put together; she makes everyone feel like they are part of something greater. Self study will help in 140. Overall great class.

She is a wonderful educator and a splendid person. Her slides are well made and doing some self-study is definitely gonna help. However, she shines not bc of her classes but because of who she is. A true gem in BME department.

Widder is a Lebron type in the biomedical engineering department; she deeply cares about the success of her students, is often accessible for any assistance, and shares a genuine passion for the concepts she's teaching. 140 is a moderately tough class, but it is fair and sets up well for classes you'll in the future.

The GOAT, singlehandedly carries the BME department. 10/10 professor + human being. 140 was the light in the tunnel during my freshman year. Labs are super fun, lectures are very informational. Prepares you well for the second semester of BME.

BME140 was a fantastic class. It prepares you so well for other classes like Physics, Biology, etc. Widder is literally the greatest teacher to ever exist. She cares so much. So welcoming so amazing. Prof widder feels like family. WE LOVE YOU PROF WIDDER. YOU CARRY THE BME DEPARTMENT. THANK YOU FOR BEING THE BEST!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Widder is the only reason I'm still a BME at this point. QP is hell and widder was the only reason remotely passed. If you need anything just ask, any time of the day. If you show you are trying, she'll be willing to make any necessary accommodations for you. She deserves a raise, and then some! Give QP some time, ESPECIALLY the 3rd and 4th CLabs.

Professor Widder is arguably the best part of the BME department at WashU. She always makes sure you are understanding the material and cares about her students well being. I emailed her on a Friday night at 5:30 and she responded in 3 minutes, which shows her dedication to her students. Great professor, and I look forward to more classes with her!

Widder is the hidden gem of the BME department. She is what will get you through QP as a BME. Highly suggest becoming a regular at her office hours, and getting to know her better. She is a great resource to get help in both classes and just general advice.
Professor Widder made the mess that was interesting BME more bearable.

Professor Widder is one of the best professors at WashU. I had her for Themo Lab and took QP I/II with her as the lab professor and I loved having her for all of the classes. She's a professor who genuinely cares about you as a person outside of class. She's understanding about personal situations and is there for class matters or to just talk. 5/5

Not sure if it was just the class or the teacher but this could have possibly been the worst organized class I've ever taken. Was expecting an architecture theory type class but instead got a boring random lecture class that nobody needed this semester. I never learned anything and the only thing we had to do for the class was make a 5 min podcast.

Heather is a terrible teacher. She designs your project and then forces you to do that. At the same time she is so insecure that she changes her mind all the time so you are constantly redoing your work.
hard to communicate

She is a really nice person, no matter in class or out. She has an absolutely solid architectural background. She is always helpful of guiding student to complete their projects from really abstract concepts to extremely logical spaces. She is more like a translator between ideas and architecture when she teaches in school. I like her studio.

Guidance is quite scattered. Attitude seems to be to work harder than smarter. Not well grounded as a responsible practicing Architect. Do only what she asks and in the amount x10 and you will get a good grade. Knows how to see a good student, but not an innovative designer/architect.
She's willing to help at all hours.. it gets to be too much. She's much more interested in the conceptual  than the realizable. Expect to make some great physical models.

She's really good at what she does, and she expects a lot from her sudents. you have to push yourself. she's available outside of class anytime (within reason) if you only ask. she's the best prof at this school hands down.
Ken Wood is awesome! : )
Ken wood is great.

yay ken! he can be demanding, but if you truly put forth an effort, he will be helpful and understanding. kind of awkward, but a funny endearing way. He seems to give out more work than some teachers in drawing 1, but opens up the options more in drawing 2. i recommend him!

Quite easy if you have a background in math, probably would be harder if you're more of a music than a math person. Super nice guy, very interesting lectures and subject matter. Does make a number of mistakes on the board, so be aware. Highly recommend!
No Comments

Very nice man, willing to help students and shows genuine concern for their difficulties.  However, class is harder than it should be.
