Teaches class more like teaching music to math students than math to music students, would have been nice if he could have done both.  Not a horrible class though.

Very unclear, he's too smart to be teaching Calc 2. Tried going to lectures but I was even more confused afterwards, so I ended up learning everything online.  Work very hard studying for tests! Do the recommended practice problems! Webwork and past tests don't always align as well since chapters are switched around

I'm going to cut the guy some slack because it was his first year teaching Cal II but I didn't learn anything in his class. I couldn't understand the way he taught most days and math has been my strong-suit for as long as I can remember. Hopefully they put another professor in to teach such a large and important class.

Wushi isn't the best lecturer but it's definitely worth it to go to his office hours. He is very helpful 1 on 1 and he becomes so much clearer. He is open to making himself available to students and generally willing to stay past his office hours if people have more questions. Pro tip: he expects his students to have read the textbook before class.
Absolute worst professor I've ever had. Enjoy not understanding anything all semester and learning it on your own. Has colorful shirts.

Given that it's Professor Goldring's first year at WashU, he deserves credit for trying to trying to adjust to his classes' methods of learning. Though not the clearest, he genuinely cares about his students and his lectures are usually pretty easy to follow. Self-study is definitely a must, though.
I literally do not understand anything in this class. He is really unclear and uses his own language and terms to teach. What is happening?

I know he has just started his first year at WashU and it takes a little time for him to adjust to the environment. BUT, he is so good at making simple stuffs way more complicated than they're supposed to be, and in an one-hour-long lecture he could spend twenty minutes on one single problem. Self-study is needed if this course is mandatory.

Prof. Martin, while sometimes difficult to understand, is very motivated about teaching accounting. Her tests aren't the easiest, but quizzes tend to be very easy. She doesn't assign homework, but the recommended problems definitely help.

An excellent teacher. Well explained, interesting material, and fair tests. Plus if you participate in class she gives out candy. The course is curved too so that's a nice addition too. Attend class and do the practice problems and it's an easy A, regardless of what lazy B Schoolers may say.

Very nice woman, but the class did not take her seriously and she had no control. It was also hard to understand her with her accent, but what can you do. Not a terribly hard class, but it's easy to get caught not going to class and falling behind.
cant speak english

Can be hard to understand at times...lots of time wasted in class due to clarity issues. Looking over the slides in my room at night proved more useful than going to class. Go to class if you want, but it's not necessary.

I really liked prof. Martin. Her class was pretty boring, but accounting in general is pretty boring. I didn't find her very hard to understand, more that she would ask obvious and sometimes pointless questions. But in the end her tests were easier, the grades turned out well and I learned the material really well.

I was at first skeptical about how this class would unfold after reading comments from prior semesters. However, this semester was a pleasant surprise. Prof Martin is always prepared, and she finds a way to teach the material in a way that you can understand very quickly. You really only need the book for the first few chapters.
Prof. Martin is very knowledgeable and a great teacher overall...she is willing to help her students and offers plenty of opportunities for extra credit.  Strongly recommend the class...

Professor Martin may at first come off as difficult to understand, but once you really begin to talk to her you'll find out she really cares about her students and will work hard to help you succeed. She does have an accent, but I think, as long as you read the textbook, the information is still clear. She is a fair grader and nice!

This teacher shamelessly plagiarizes the work of other ACCT profs simply to minimize her own effort.  She takes PPT slides from other professors and reorganizes them so they don't appear identical; the result is an incoherent, disorderly presentation that she can't explain because she DIDN'T write it.  She is HARDLY a professor worth taking.
Impossible to understand and only writes in math shorthand.

He has a thick accent that is hard to understand at the beginning, but you eventually end up understanding everything he says.  He knows his students by name, and is willing to stick around after class for questions.  You reallized how much he tought you after you are done with the course.  You will feel lost, confused and frustated but don't give

One of those professors around which you design your schedule so that you won't have to take a class with him.  It takes a very special kind of out of touch not to realize that some of your students might have classes that require evening exams.  When facing the choice between his ME 265 section and CSE 200, take the CSE course.  Very thick accent.
Dedicated and smart, just not the clearest lecturer.  Willing to help (at least try to help).

I took organic 228 for chemistry majors at Texas A&M with Dr. Wooley. She is a great professor and really cares about her students' success. Going to her office hours frequently was hard because she was always changing the days and times, but she was always very helpful. Her exams are extremely difficult, but she curves very well. TAKE HER CLASS!

While the her teaching style is more than demanding, I think it's refreshing that she doesn't treat her students like imbeciles. She believes that all of her students are up for a challenge. That being said, be prepared to eat, sleep, and breather organic chemistry. If you like it (I DID), than you're in luck. If not, take another professor.

Dr. Wooley is one of the most amazing professors/chemists I have ever had the pleasure to to take a course from.  She is brilliant and truly personable.  And even though I did not do well in Chem251 (due to my own lack of intelligence, no doubt), I did enjoy the class tremendously.  Even the horrific chem lab.
No Comments

For 251, she was a good lecturer, although her exams were harder than they needed to be - sometimes to the point of unfairness.  For 257, she made it clear that teaching the class was not one of her priorities, and it showed in the quality of her teaching.  Overall, a brilliant scientist, but an arrogant and condescending professor.
Like people have said, kiss her butt and you get a good grade.
this woman is crazy, and the class was WAY too hard, expecially for only 2 credits.
Like many have said, sometimes pushing your nose in the crap and kissing a lot of butt is required.  Way too much effort for the credit/knowledge/grade involved.
I can honestlly say that this woman's classes have been the most miserable experiences in my life.  Too much work, too much stress for the grade and/or credit received.

She was pretty disorganized and would come in all tousled, but that can be forgiven due to her passion for teaching and concern for the students.  The class wasn't too hard and you could do well with only a good set of class notes. PLUS she's a major hottie -ay ay ay!

Assigned a ton of homework, the most of any of my classes. He's a math genius but that just makes him awful at explaining concepts in class. Exams were really hard and got more difficult as the year went along. Not much sympathy for his students either.

Not good. Hard to follow in class, and assumed we knew things that we didn't know. Homework was absurdly long. Spent so long trying to complete the homework that my studying for the tests was cut short, and so I did not do as well. Diffeq is hard enough with a good professor - Yasha just made it harder.

Took DiffEq with Yasha this past semester, exams were mainly based on practice exams but the last two were way more difficult than the first two. Gives WAY too much homework (both written and WebWork), homework sometimes took 12-15 hours to complete every week. Office hours very helpful

The GOAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAT. Mr Yang man, good times.

Professor Yang is super knowledgeable and takes time to make sure students understand WHY we are doing what we are doing

reviews.comment: I've had Yang for 309 Matrix Algebra and 132 Calc II. In Matrix, he was a fairly good lecturer and I felt the structure of his class was good for learning. There is a lot of content in the course so I can't really blame him for moving quickly. While he aimed for lowish exam averages of our grade, the grading scale was good so I thought it was fair.

The professor himself is nice, especially if you go to office hours and/or ask questions. Personally I found the class difficult but I did get progressively better throughout the semester which was nice. The lectures also follow the textbook closely. My only complaint is I wish we got solutions for all practice tests, as that would've been helpful.

Dr.Yang is not that great a lecturer but definitely a 10/10 person. Super accessible and nice during office hour. 2 Midterms each weights 15% and the final weights 40%. The first midterm is easy, but the second is kinda hard. The final exam is alright.

For Math 309. Not sure why so many 1s here, but he's a good lecturer and cared about questions in lecture. grade distro was 2 exams worth 15% each, final worth 40%. Midterm 2 was very hard, 1 was easy, and the final was in between. Nice guy and clear lecturer, worth taking his class. I will say he was pretty inconsistent at responding on piazza tho

Course content is pretty difficult, which makes lectures sometimes challenging to follow. But, Yang is very accessible during office hours and is always willing to go over any questions. Exams were quite difficult (all of our exam averages were within the D range), but Yang is generous with the curving scale.
Tough Linear Class.

Dr. Zaher is great, but the course is extremely difficult. I'd easily recommend him if the curve weren't so ridiculous, but I probably wouldn't take it again. He's super nice and inspirational, and really cares about how you do!

lectures are a little disorganized, but ultimately i'm glad i chose one sem biochemistry over 2 sem biochemistry at washu. he's caring and dedicated and truly wants us to UNDERSTAND material. exams are tough for me but not unfair. also noteworthy is that i'm NOT writing this in hightsight, am getting a B rn, and still love him. he's so enthusiastic
Worst class I have taken.  Avoid this guy at all costs.

P. Zaher is truly invested in his students, and if you take the time to go to office hours and talk to him, you'll find that he wants you to succeed. He tries to learn everybody's name (in a LECTURE class) and while his lectures can be a little disorganized, he is happy to go over things multiple times with you one-on-one.

One of the worst classes I have taken at WashU. He teaches nothing in class. He goes through lecture slides and tell us just to memorize this diagram. The diagram will be extremely complex and make no sense to the student and he will do an AWFUL job explaining. I haven't met a fellow student in the class who likes his teaching
Not a great experience with him.
torture during the pandemic. multiple answers questions are insanely difficult. A nice person but barely knew how to teach.
Jeff Zacks is the worst. A horrible, horrible person. Stay away.

After taking this class, I have no earthly idea what all the negative reviews about Zacks being "arrogant and rude" were about. I had a great experience in Zacks' class--his lectures were clear and engaging, he's very approachable, and seems like someone who genuinely cares for his students!

I generally struggle in lecture classes (especially those that involve biology or neuroscience) but Prof Zacks organizes his lectures well and does a good job of explaining them in ways that I could wrap my head around. He was very helpful (as was the TA), and friendly/approachable!
sure, his scholastic pedigree is impeccable, but he's the biggest ****bag I've ever come across
He really is as awful as everyone says.

There are several great professors in our department, many that are competent and teach well, and a few that waste everyone's time.  Jeff Zacks is at the bottom of the entire list.  He has an affected manner and seems to think that taking every opportunity to abuse students will compensate for his egregious bumbling.  Students I know all loathe him

In a class based on discussion, Prof. Zacks was awful at leading discussion. He talks for too long, capitalizing the conversation for an inappropriate amount of time. His intellectual insecurities are obvious. He has a reputation for picking favorites and handing out emotionally-charged grades. This reputation was confirmed in this class.

This teacher has no coherent teaching method and just likes to talk on and on about nothing. Very harsh grader and has little interest in helping students understand the topic. He is condescending and belittling when questions he deems unworthy are asked.

Arrogant, condescending and belittling. He has no interest in teaching or making his concepts clear. His teacher's pets are obvious. He was unhelpful and outright mean. He made sure the class knew he was from Stanford and that most of this was beneath him, especially those who needed help.

He seems knowledgeable,but this man is horrible underneath.In summary,he either favors students or humiliates them,his grading procedures are unfair,he makes you feel stupid and he doesn't even answer questions. Karma! he will get what's coming to him.

omg i could write a book on how much i hate this man, he picks on students unfairly, tries to humiliate and embarrass people, unfair and unclear grading, rude and disrespectful outside of class, has obvious teachers pets, should not be allowed to teach
VERY good teacher. lots of work, but you will leave knowing your stuff. hands down my favorite psych prof.
The best professor in the department.
he really likes it when people are late to class
He dressed extremely well and was funny.  Very clear class instruction.
Kappy

Kaplan is a nicer grader. Don't worry too much about grades in this class. His lectures I really like because he does the accounting problems with us in class. One thing I don't like is the evening tests we need to take. It ranges from 6:30pm or 7pm. Personally, around nighttime, my attention is not there, so this makes test-taking harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor and makes the course content accessible and manageable for students. Would 1000% recommend taking his section for 2620.
Dr. Kaplan was a stellar. I found his input inspiring and his energy electic. I think every student could benefit from a class with Dr. Kaplan.

He's a really nice guy and is good at teaching the subject. He brings in a lot of practice problems and examples during class and has plenty of extra problems available during review sessions or online. Tests are straightforward and very similar to the problems he gives. I would definitely recommend taking him for 2620.

clear lecturer, fair (really easy) exams, accessible even outside of office hours. goes over practice problems in class, which is very helpful for learning the material really wants to see students succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As a new professor, he is trying to do well but I'd say there is huge space for improvement. typos in examquiz;the tendency to read slides;randomly changes grading criteria sometimes comes not so prepared(but may improve after he teaches this class more)

This semester is the first time that Professor Kaplan teaches this course, but he's absolutely doing an amazing job as a new lecturer! The material is explained very clearly, and a lot of in-class practice and review sessions are provided to help us catch up. Also, he always maintains a lively class atmosphere.
Professor Kaplan is great. This class is not the most interesting or entertaining but he makes the material relatable and always applies real life problems. He also offers lots of outside help.

Works hard, expects you to work hard. Briefs can be vague and confusing, but it's her first year as a studio lead so I'll give her grace. Exposed us to a lot of intense work very fast, but I liked that because it gave us great exposure to skills for the years ahead. She has a great sense of humor if you get to know her.

Zahra could be very intimidating during the first few encounters. But throughout the semester, she proved to be a great architect, professor, and just a person in general. Very work-heavy, so get ready to work on weekends a lot. She does use some difficult terms so you should ask for clarification but her feedbacks are very detailed and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I never understood anything that we were doing or how to do it. She would explain things in the weirdest ways with lots of pretentious design words in a first semester undergrad studio. The grading criteria was never clear, when I would read the brief overviews it felt like reading a different language. Seems nice but not for new architects.

His way of teaching is very engaging and effective! I'd also add that he uses homework sets in a very smart way to supplement the topics covered in class versus the homework sets just being some annoying chore that doesn't facilitate learning and just eats up time!
It was a great class!
I highly recommend Prof. Zeng!!!

Like many have already commented, he explains things very well. But he is also an incredibly understanding professor! Whenever people in the class were facing challenges that impacted learning, he was very responsive in providing accommodations and genuinely wanted to help.

The way the prof laid out the material blows my mind. The clarity is insane and tricky topics suddenly felt trivial! Two semesters ago I took 415 with a different instructor and back then I felt getting hammered nonstop with unimportant details that only distracted from the core topics. I'm glad I dropped the course back then to retake it with him

This prof has an amazing ability to prepare very tough course material in a way where learning feels easy and even fun. Ngl he appeared scary in the beginning with his extensive knowledge of engineering and math topics, but you will be in for a treat when you start to see how personable and witty he is. He is kind of a comedian lol

Took three courses with Prof. Zeng. Definitely shaped my college trajectory, never thought I would enjoy applied math so much but he framed the subject as this fascinating puzzle I couldn't get enough of. I quite literally wouldn't have finished with the major I did without him. One of the best professors in the engineering school in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: amazing professor!
Best professor I've had so far. Very fun lectures. Taught me what it means to really know a subject.
Dedicated to the students. Extremely invested in student work and our ideas. Very knowledgeable, and definitely one of the most intelligent and well-rounded people I've ever met.

I was really proud with the work I made by the end of this class. Zeuler is a great professor who gives a ton of feedback and constructive criticism. I liked how the class was about developing habits and refining the process. Prof understood that it wasn't about the end result but instead the journey there.

Lima is an AMAZING professor. He loves teaching, and he describes himself to be an educator. It matters to him how students are connected to the classes and things he talks about. He is most inspirational in the sense that he knows a lot and is willing to share it with you. He is a man with clear eyes and spotless mind. Just love his class!
One of the best teachers in the architecture school.

The lectures and notes have many errors. Quiz and exam didn't make the questions clear. Only answers as same as his could receive credit.

Disorganized lectures and assignments. Quizzes actually are almost irrelevant to the course materials while he usually says "It's straightforward". Let's make an assumption he can do logical thinking. However, why did he make CSE514A in mess? Don't take this if it's not a required course for you.

reviews.comment: I can understand almost everything in the lecture but his quiz is not relevant to the lecture.

The course has no textbooks or other materials, just his lecture notes, but he left lots of blanks in them, saying that students will fill them in by listening to his lectures. But his lectures are so disorganized and inattractive. Also, questions in quizzes and exams are almost irrelevant to his lectures. Would not recommend.

reviews.comment: Important topic for present day software industry. Supplement the lectures with online material and attend all lectures since there may be a quiz anytime.

the worst teacher I've had in the entire engineering school. He simply does not care about undergrads. His midterm  had problems only reasonable to solve by algorithms NOT YET COVERED in the course. (Not a joke or exaggeration, we covered those algorithms like 3 weeks after the midterm). Oh, and he is just a terrible lecturer too. Very disorganized
just a really bad teacher, shouldnt be teaching. pretty cocky too.

This guys is bad. Very bad. The curriculum is mostly copied and pasted from MIT, homework and all. Zheng is horrible at teaching, often making mistakes and never correcting them. Hand waves over very complicated topics. Tried to make 25% of the class repeat until we revolted. SUPPLEMENT WITH COURSERA AND MIT OPENCOURSE Algorithms course! Good Luck

He's earnest and wants to be a good teacher, but his class notes are a mess and he spends a lot of time trying to correct his own mistakes. Class was useless. I taught myself this class entirely from the textbook. Would not recommend.
Prof. Zoes comment for papers are really helpful! Her deadline is rather flexible, too

Prof. Zoe is the best professor that I have met at Wash. U. The reading load for her class is moderate, compared with other classes in the Classics Department. Moreover, her group project assignment is really engaging, and her weekly discussion post really helps students to communicate their ideas! She provides an asynchronous option for her class!
Love Zoe so much! Incredibly passionate and knowledgeable. She does ask a lot of her students, but also is very accommodating. Maybe the most caring professor I've ever had!

Taking 193, I found this course to be contrastingly easy in comparison. The grading is very unique but much more susceptible to revisions and feedback. However, I felt that I learned a lot less in this course than 193, but 194 is a dream for someone with a strong work ethic and who wants to learn out of curiosity rather than to survive another day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor, encourages participation and answers questions well, but he is a little disconnected from the class. Sometimes he didn't know what the homework or quiz questions were about (which means the lecture was sometimes kind of unrelated to the quizzes). The class is being improved, though, so hopefully this gets better in the future.

Only bad thing to say is that the class was poorly designed. It is being improved so I hope it is better. Zu jiaoshou is a great lecturer, he makes learning physics fun and engaging. Lectures are condensed into the most important concepts you need to do the problems while the readings are to learn the intuition and physics.
I think Chong would be an awesome teacher if he put more work into the class. He is extremely funny and makes the class enjoyable.
Really funny guy and does a good job keeping the room engaged during class.  Necessary to come to class because of iclicker.

Great lectures! Professor Zu seems genuinely enthusiastic about teaching physics, even to those who aren't particularly interested in learning. Ended up watching lecture videos for most of the semester but he was definitely very personable and good at answering questions when I did attend lectures in person.
clear lectures; nice guy; easy with grading and grades; fully understand the materials; care about students' understanding and questions...

I graduated about 20 years ago. Professor Zwicker was a profound, positive influence in my life -- one of the 3 best teachers I had at any stage during my formal education, and a generous, brilliant, interesting person outside of it.  It should say enough that 20 years later a former student of his writes this review.

One of the dullest classes I've ever been in.  The paper topics were awful.  Prof Zwicker knows a lot, but it seems like he just wants you to guess what he knows and isn't really interested in hearing anything new.
Definitely the best professor I've had at WashU.  He's the reason I am majoring in English.
Brilliant professor who gives great lectures. Ok, his jokes are sometimes very subtle, and he makes you work, but he is the best of the best.
Wonderful, brilliant teacher.
this class is death. he has a fake british accent and insists upon doing his own dramatic monologue renditions of... milton. so boring, such a random grader, get out while you can
This is my advisor. He has never once made an effort to see me or advise me. He does not respond to my emails and he has made no effort to help me meet my graduation requirements.
